releases.body:
**Fixed**
- `includeCoAuthoredBy: false` is now honored in ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), so ACP clients no longer instruct the agent to add a Co-authored-by trailer to commits.
- Targeted /settings commands show the selected setting immediately
- A telemetry-disabled warning raised while resuming a session is saved to the session history, so later events no longer reference a missing parent.
- A BYOK provider key that is not a valid HTTP header value, such as key command output with a status line before the key, is no longer printed in the model error or saved in the session log.
- copilot mcp enable now fails with a clear message for a server the repository disables, instead of reporting success and changing nothing
- A prompt hook that returns an empty modifiedPrompt or modifiedTransformedPrompt no longer sends the model an empty prompt. A hook value that is ignored because it is empty or not a string now shows a warning naming the field.
- `copilot sessions import --name ""` is now rejected as an invalid name in both `--dry-run` and a real import, instead of passing the dry run and then failing with a persistence error.
- A ~/ directory in skillDirectories, COPILOT_SKILLS_DIRS or COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS now resolves to your home directory, so its skills and instructions load.
- The `.vscode/mcp.json` migration notice now appears in repository subdirectories and after `/cd` into another workspace, and no longer appears for repositories already migrated to `.mcp.json`.
- Skill and background-agent timeline entries now show sanitized, readable errors and results
- Allow /mcp enable and /mcp disable for servers granted GitHub auth at startup
- Gemini models automatically defer tools behind search when requests exceed the 512-function limit.
- Removed repository hook configs no longer block later tool calls in the same session.
- In --autopilot, background task completions that arrive after a run stops are delivered with your next message instead of being dropped.
- Collect debug logs keeps the active invocation and ignores stale completion results
- Resuming a session with an unreadable event log now reports a load error instead of not found
- Copying text on native Windows no longer changes your console code page.
- Keep the selected task visible in /tasks when long lists exceed terminal height
- Signing in to a remote MCP server whose protected resource is a bare origin such as https://mcp.example.com no longer sends the resource with an added trailing slash, which authorization servers that compare it exactly rejected.
- Write remote session handoff cleanup failures to the debug log and show a clear error when no remote session is prepared
- Keep command-mode drafts after accepted commands so you can continue typing immediately.

**Fixed**
- Empty sessions no longer flash into the session picker before disappearing
- An @file mention written inside parentheses, brackets, braces, angle brackets, quotes or backticks now attaches the file, and expands correctly in ! shell commands, instead of being silently ignored.
- Custom agents that share a built-in agent's name are no longer offered to the model as a second agent type, since delegating to that name always runs the built-in agent
- The details view in /skills, /plugin and /mcp no longer passes terminal control characters from a skill, plugin or server's metadata through to the terminal; its trust and data blocks now show them escaped.
- Wrapped lines in the `/ide` dialog now continue under their text instead of under the bullet or row number
- After choosing Go back on the startup session-in-use prompt, sessions opened later with `/resume` show the in-use warning again.
- Instruction files whose frontmatter is not valid YAML now keep an applyTo or paths list and excludeAgent, instead of applying to every file, to none, or to an agent they exclude
- A preToolUse hook that returns `"modifiedArgs": null` no longer makes the tool call fail with "Expected JSON object but got null"; null now leaves the arguments unchanged, as it does for the hook's other fields.
- Escape and Ctrl+G leave Ctrl+R reverse search in one press when it was started from a slash command, /cd path or command-mode draft, instead of clearing the draft.
- Pressing Enter on a search with no matches in the session browser or the custom agent picker, or Tab in the agent picker, no longer adds a space to the search text.
- Messages such as the /rename confirmation now show 8-bit control characters from the text they echo as spaces instead of sending them to the terminal.
- `copilot sessions import` now reports a second session header as "Only the first record may be a session header." and an unknown record type as unsupported, instead of asking for a record id and timestamp those lines never needed.
- When the editor opened with Ctrl+E in /settings saves the file and then exits with an error, the edit is now kept in a recovery file and its path is shown, instead of being deleted with a message saying the editor did not save.
- When signed out, the Issues and Pull requests tabs no longer offer a `/` search that could only fail with "Search failed."; `/` there now opens the slash-command picker, as on the Gists tab.
- Keep the /statusline dialog's preview and toggle descriptions inside its border when the sessions sidebar is open.
- The view tool now fails at once on a named pipe, socket or device instead of waiting forever for a FIFO writer, which left non-interactive runs hanging.
- Expanding a tool call with Ctrl+O now shows the values of object and array arguments instead of a `{…}` or `[N items]` placeholder, so MCP calls that take a nested parameters object can be inspected
- Command hooks receive COPILOT_HOOK_DEPTH so hook-launched sessions can stop recursive agentStop chains
- Remote HTTP MCP servers connect through proxies that require Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.

**Added** - Add opt-in session management tools and @mentions for opted-in local sessions **Improved** - Managed-account policy refresh warnings now include Policy Helper findings and clear once policy resolves **Fixed** - Reuse valid saved MCP OAuth credentials for anonymous connections and initial challenges without requiring another sign-in - On the colorblind theme, unread sessions in the Sessions sidebar and its legend are marked with * instead of the same blue dot as finished sessions. - MCP reload now reports one settled connection summary per reconciliation - Copilot Free signup completes when account setup overlaps model refreshes - Resuming an autopilot objective no longer starts a duplicate continuation prompt - /context shows updated usage details after switching models in an active session - Repository disableAllHooks continues suppressing user hooks after trusted-workspace rebuilds - Extensions no longer prompt for permission after their connection closes during initialization - Permission prompts keep your current selection when options update during loading - Entra sign-in uses the VS Code application registration again by default - Preserve typed and pasted typeahead input across later cwd loading gates - Copilot's built-in documentation tool now returns the installed CLI's own commands, flags and help topics instead of an error line about a missing README - /add-dir and /cd now accept a directory wrapped in quotes, such as a path pasted from a shell or file manager, instead of reporting that it does not exist. - Assistant replies, other rendered markdown and the expanded Read, Create, Edit and Search rows no longer pass escape sequences and control characters from their text to the terminal, so a reply or a file cannot restyle the timeline or hide its own lines - The first `@` of a session now highlights the first suggested file instead of the working directory, so Tab or Enter inserts that file. A suggestion you pick with the arrow keys still stays highlighted while results update. - The busy indicator shortens a long tool name instead of cutting off its elapsed time and output size - A `!` shell command cancelled after it printed output now shows that output once, instead of repeating it above the cancellation message. - Canvas windows no longer reappear or revert to an older URL after being closed or updated while a session is still loading - Code blocks in assistant replies keep their lines and indentation after a line that starts with a triple-backtick code span, a fence line with a language inside another code block, or indented text right after a closing fence, instead of being joined into one line. - Collapsed tool result previews no longer show a replacement character when an emoji falls where the preview is cut, and wide characters no longer overrun the preview width - The autopilot completion check label now matches the decision autopilot acts on: a reviewer verdict with non-English text right after the verdict word no longer shows as passed. - Confirmation dialogs such as "Enable autopilot mode" and "Confirm folder trust" keep their title, highlighted option and key hints on screen in a short terminal - Ctrl+U and Cmd+Backspace at the start of a prompt whose first line is empty no longer add a blank line - The terminal cursor no longer stays in an unfocused pane, such as the /config right pane after returning to the sidebar - A directory name containing escape sequences no longer restyles the session picker Location column, the footer working directory or the /session info Directory row; the path is drawn as plain text - A long name that wraps beside other text in a row, such as in /extensions manage or the /agent picker, no longer loses a character where it wraps. - The Getting started box no longer suggests /model in sessions that use a model from your own provider, where /model is not available. - HTML exports (`/export html`, `/share html`, research reports) and rich text copied with `/copy` keep inline `
` line breaks, including in table cells, instead of joining the lines - The "Agent finished" desktop notification no longer shows a reply from an earlier turn or from another session when a prompt ends without a reply of its own, such as a prompt blocked by a hook. - The /instructions picker no longer lets terminal escape sequences or line breaks in an instruction file name or plugin name restyle the list or draw extra rows. - `copilot -p --output-format json` and `copilot workflow run` no longer write 8-bit terminal control characters (C1 and DEL) from model replies, tool output or workflow results raw: they are escaped in the JSON, which parses to the same values, and `workflow run` failure messages on stderr show them as spaces. - A prompt that starts with a combining accent no longer hides the last typed character or puts the cursor one column too far right; the accent is drawn on the cell before it, as the terminal itself draws it. - `--max-ai-credits` with `NaN`, `inf` or a number too large to represent now fails with an error that names the value you typed, instead of reporting it as "null". - Local MCP servers start once per session when the first credential resolves - An MCP tool title, or tool arguments the model writes, can no longer use 8-bit control characters to erase or redraw the tool approval dialog or the timeline row - The "Agent finished" desktop notification now shows inline code such as `src/*.ts` as written, keeps spaced-out asterisks such as `2 * 3`, and no longer leaves part of a link's address behind when the address contains parentheses. - Permission prompts show the control characters in a directory or file name instead of letting its escape sequences restyle the path or its line feeds split the row - The `/permissions` picker keeps its title, the highlighted mode, the Assisted Permissions security statement and its key hints on screen on short terminals, such as 80x12 or 60x14, instead of pushing the title and the first modes above the top of the screen. - Plugin rules whose `globs` is a comma-separated string, such as `"*.ts,*.tsx"`, now apply to the files those patterns match instead of never applying. - In `-p` mode, a sub-agent's streamed reply now ends with a line break, so `--silent` no longer prints it and the main agent's answer as one line and the default output no longer glues it to the front of the task tool's row. - Typing `?` in Ctrl+R reverse search or at a permission prompt no longer opens quick help, and pressing it twice no longer leaves a stray `?` in the prompt. - `/remote on` tries again after an earlier attempt failed, instead of reporting "Remote control status: connecting." and doing nothing until the CLI is restarted. - /rename and /session rename refuse a session name with a double quote or a control character, as --name and /fork already do, instead of storing it. - A repository's .github/copilot/settings.json can no longer color, hide or add lines to the startup warning or the /settings Problems explanation that reports its invalid settings: keys and values from the file are shown escaped, and a setting's value containing a line feed is no longer shown in the Problems explanation. - Show unresolved GitHub repositories in /chronicle reindex results when some sessions cannot be synced. - copilot --resume and --continue now fail at once with the permission error when the session store cannot be read, instead of printing nothing and never exiting. - Ctrl+C closes a Ctrl+R history search without clearing the prompt you were typing or arming "ctrl+c again to exit", so pressing it twice no longer quits the CLI. - copilot sandbox ca trust --allow-host '*' now reports an invalid host rule, like other invalid hosts, instead of an unrelated masked-credential error - The /sandbox dialog now fits short terminals: it keeps its title, its tabs, the highlighted setting and its key hints on screen and scrolls the settings instead of cutting them off. - A command scheduled with /after or /every that cannot be scheduled, such as /clear or /exit, now reports in the timeline that it cannot be scheduled when it fires, instead of silently doing nothing. - With --screen-reader, /plugin, /skills and other labelled lists read their rows and their empty message instead of only the list name - Under `--screen-reader`, the "User message" label on a sent message stays on one row beside the message instead of breaking into a column of two-letter pieces, and the "Search" label in `/search` and the model picker is now separated from the text you type. - With `--screen-reader`, the session browser no longer reads the label of its Source tabs twice ("Source: source: current tab"). - With --screen-reader, the home screen no longer goes blank and stops responding in a very small terminal, such as 15 columns by 8 rows. - A search path naming the working directory with a trailing slash is now shown as the current directory instead of an empty path - /session delete refuses an unknown option such as --force with a usage error. Before, an unknown option placed before a session ID consumed the ID, and the command deleted the current session without asking. - With context management tools on, session_history search now matches the conversation text, so a query that contains a line break, a quote or a backslash finds the message it was copied from, and read_item returns the message text instead of its JSON encoding. - Escape sequences in a session name, branch or working directory no longer restyle rows in the Sessions tab and session pickers, or show up as stray text such as [31m on the Sessions sidebar cards; the text is drawn plain - /session prune and /session delete-all reject malformed days, unknown flags and stray arguments instead of deleting sessions - In /settings list editors, an item that wraps onto a second line no longer pulls its text one column left of the other items and against the selection marker - The /settings value picker no longer draws its options over each other or over its border in short terminals, and keeps the highlighted choice on screen. - /share file and /share html list a message's images as [Image: name] instead of leaving an image-only message blank, and the HTML page title comes from the first message with text - Markdown session exports (`--share`, `/share file`, `/share gist`) now show shell commands, search patterns and file paths exactly as they ran: a `*` or `__init__.py` no longer turns into italic or bold text, and a heredoc no longer becomes headings, lists or a code block that swallows the sections after it. - /share file and /share html no longer keep the quotes around a pasted output path in the file name - /share research and /share html research add .md or .html to a file path given without an extension, as /share file and /share html already do, and the saved HTML report now carries a link to open it. - Output from ! shell commands that print terminal hyperlinks or window titles, such as ls --hyperlink=always, is shown in full instead of disappearing along with every later shell result. - Shell output that redraws a progress line in place, such as `git checkout` or `curl`, now shows the line's final state inside the output once the command finishes, instead of every frame on rows outside it. - Pressing Enter on a slash command whose arguments follow a non-ASCII space, such as the ideographic space a CJK input method types, now runs the command with those arguments instead of dropping them: `/allow-all off` no longer turns Allow All on. - Tab-indented files keep their indentation in the expanded file view, in expanded grep and glob results, and in the gist details screen, instead of rendering every line at column 0. - `copilot workflow run` and `copilot -p` text output now redact `--secret-env-vars` values and recognized tokens in lines a workflow or extension logs, as the JSON output and the final result already did. - Opening /theme in a terminal 6 columns wide or narrower, or narrowing the terminal while it is open, no longer blanks and freezes the whole session - The /theme picker keeps the highlighted choice visible in short terminals by hiding the sample preview and scrolling the list. - Error messages in the timeline no longer lose their last characters, or a wrapped line ending in a path, when they nearly fill the terminal width - Timeline rows for file tools show the control characters in a file name instead of letting its escape sequences restyle the row or its line feeds split it - Todo timeline entries show the right status for updates whose title or description contains the word where - Text cut to fit the terminal, such as a setting value in `/settings`, a cell in the subagent table, or a long objective in the pinned goal panel under `--screen-reader`, now ends in an ellipsis instead of stopping mid-word, so a cut value no longer reads as a complete one. - An unquoted -p or -i prompt that contains a command name such as update, login or help now gets the quoting hint instead of a parser error about an unknown subcommand. - The /usage activity graph now places each month label over its own week in Japanese, Chinese and other locales whose month names use wide characters, instead of shifting each label further right. - In Vim mode, typing an emoji or a math letter in NORMAL mode no longer inserts it into the prompt; it is ignored like any other key that has no command. - In Vim mode, `t` and `dt` stop before an emoji or conjunct when the target character is part of it, instead of landing on it and deleting it, and `dF` deletes the whole emoji instead of splitting it. - When `web_fetch` cuts a page at its 10 MiB limit, the model is now told the page was truncated even when the cut falls inside a script, style sheet or HTML comment. - An invalid server entry in a trusted workspace `.mcp.json`, or a file that is malformed or unreadable, is now reported as an MCP warning in interactive sessions and in `copilot -p` (stderr, or a `session.warning` event with `--output-format json`) instead of the server silently missing; before, only `copilot mcp list` said why. - /worktree and /move now run after you answer "Yes" to the folder trust prompt for the current session, instead of being refused as waiting for folder trust until the folder was remembered - Page Up and Page Down move through the settings list again. - Show "Operation cancelled by user" immediately when you press Ctrl+C, without waiting for cancellation cleanup - One-line search fields keep emoji intact when moving the cursor and deleting text - Restart keeps your current /model selection after switching models in-session - /settings unset now directs hidden subagent array keys to /subagents - Resumed handoff and compaction timeline text is sanitized to prevent style injection and extra label rows. - Fix @ file picker match highlighting and path compression for case-expanding Unicode names - Keep Unicode /diff comments and cursor visible in narrow terminal panes - Show files with non-ASCII names in /diff local-changes output - Autopilot says so when it runs with limited permissions because bypass-permissions mode is disabled and assisted approval is not in effect - Tools that embed the CLI now attach to the session requested with --resume instead of a temporary one while it loads. - Connector authorization stays actionable while plugin inventory is loading - Plugin installs and uninstalls keep unrelated extension processes running in active sessions. - Keep MCP registry forms and review summaries readable by sanitizing labels and truncating on grapheme boundaries - /diff shows each file's own patch when file names include glob characters or start with a colon - Keep @ file completion suggestions open when navigating folders with spaces - Tool calls that finish after you abort now show their final completion status in the timeline - Keep tab bar arrows and visible tabs on one row in narrow ask-user forms - Fix /share messaging for sessions without a GitHub repository to clearly report creator-only access - /context correctly separates custom instructions from the system prompt - Tools run on the first prompt even when ambient GitHub login finishes after the turn starts - Pressing Ctrl+C during startup on Windows now exits cleanly and runs shutdown before the TUI mounts. - Auto model routing now preserves your selected Auto tier when account policy refreshes during startup - `copilot help config` now says `autoUpdate` defaults to off in CI environments and that non-interactive `-p` runs start with memory off unless `--enable-memory` is passed - Installing plugins from different GitHub or URL sources keeps separate cache directories. - Keep previously approved directories accessible after turning allow-all off and changing cwd - MCP servers no longer reload when plugin activation fingerprints change without changing active plugins or trust. - Retry /voice on after a voice model load failure without toggling /voice off first - Resuming a remote session locally no longer requires a clean working tree: uncommitted changes stay in place, and the branch checkout stops only if it would overwrite them - Enforce listed choices in MCP enum and multi-select prompts so tool calls submit valid values. - Non-vision models now get an explicit note when a tool returns an image that is not sent. - Reopening a settings enum editor keeps the cursor on the saved value - Terminal setup prompt defaults to No so pressing Enter on a first prompt does not change keybindings. - `copilot plugin list` shows a plugin that managed policy enables as enabled instead of `[disabled]`. - In cloud sessions, /chronicle standup now checks local history before reporting no recent activity - Browser sign-in lets you press any key to copy the sign-in link and reopen your browser. - Mouse wheel scrolls the timeline while the /ask quick question box is open - Keep Markdown table layout stable while long link URLs stream in replies - Backspace works correctly in Windows console editors opened with Ctrl+G - ACP sessions include skills from live local marketplace plugins in /skills list and available commands. - Ctrl+D while typing an answer in a question form now deletes the character under the cursor instead of declining the form and discarding the answer. - Keep winget launcher symlinks intact when running `copilot update` on Windows - Fix caret placement after rendering at the terminal's last column - Plugin uninstall on Windows now explains when another app is using a plugin file and how to resolve it. - Rejected prompt submissions are saved to command history so you can press Up Arrow to resend. - Local plugins with matching directory names now install into separate cache directories. - Keep the /settings and /agent search carets at the cursor when long queries wrap, so no query character is hidden. - Rejected working-directory changes now keep tools and shell commands in the current directory - Resuming a session no longer gets stuck as in use after a crashed process PID is reused. - Keep externally edited prompt text in a recovery file when the editor exits with an error - Submitting /ask or /btw while scrolled up keeps your place in the timeline - Pressing Enter on /quit or /exit now exits immediately while a turn is running - Running agents in /workflows now show their current activity in run details. - Install PyPI MCP registry servers with pinned package versions - MCP stdio requests fail immediately when a response exceeds the 16 MiB line limit. - Large pastes saved in the same millisecond on one session now each get their own file instead of overwriting each other. - When the session folder is deleted mid-session, a `!` shell command now says the working directory no longer exists instead of reporting `GenericFailure, No such file or directory`. - Fix URL permission prompts to keep ${VAR} placeholders in extracted URLs - Resumed renamed sessions now show the correct /share heading instead of New session - MCP servers dashboard keeps your active search and selection while startup authentication resolves - A remote session started outside a GitHub repository now says that it is not linked to one, instead of reporting success with no mention of it - Clicking or hovering a timeline entry no longer targets the entry below it when a word-wrapped line above paints more rows than its width divides into

issues.title: feature(desktop): system tray icon with clean shutdown of the background opencode-cli service (Windows)
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode Desktop spawns a persistent background service (`opencode-cli.exe`) that outlives the app window. When the desktop is closed normally (or crashes), the CLI service keeps running and loads a **stale config** (providers, `disabled_providers`, etc.) until killed — but on Windows there is no clean, first-class way to stop it:

- Closing the window does not reliably stop the service (it lingers).
- Reopening the desktop does not reload config if the stale service is still alive.
- The only workarounds are Task ManagerKill or a terminal one-liner (`Get-Process opencode-cli | Stop-Process -Name opencode-cli -Force`), which are hostile to non-developer users and risk losing nothing but being invisible.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.13 (OpenCode Desktop, latest channel)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200, win32 x64)
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1

## Real-world consequences observed today

1. Updated `disabled_providers` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` **didn't take effect after restarting the app window** because a lingering `opencode-cli.exe` (started earlier, PID kept-alive) still served `/api/provider` and `models` from its in-memory snapshot.
2. Provider list ("connect state") shown in Desktop was served by that stale process, causing confusion ("I disabled this provider, why is it still here?").
3. Full restart requires knowing that you must quit from the tray *if there were one*, then also verify/kill `opencode-cli.exe` manually — cannot be discovered from the UI.

## Requested feature

Add a **system tray icon** for OpenCode Desktop, with:

- `Quit OpenCode` — graceful shutdown that also terminates the background `opencode-cli` service (wait for exit, then fall back to terminate), so "restart Desktop to apply config" actually works;
- Optionally a status tooltip / menu showing the background service PID + version, and a "Restart background service" action;
- Windows: also consider exiting remaining child `opencode-cli` processes on app quit (or exposing the documented cleanup command in Settings).

Alternatively (lighter option): a "Cleanly quit Desktop incl. background service" button/setting in the Desktop UI. But the tray is where Windows users expect this behavior.

## Additional Context

- Related pain point (same lifecycle): after killing the CLI, next launch performs recovery/legacy-log cleanup; a tray-managed shutdown would avoid leaving half-torn-down state and stale locks (`*.bundle.lock`-style residue we've seen for long-running tools).
- Happy to test; desktop build reports 2.0.13.

issues.title: provider: api.responses.write scope error after upgrade
issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading OpenCode, a session in a project directory failed with an insufficient-permissions error saying the `api.responses.write` scope is missing. In an earlier occurrence, clearing OpenCode’s cache for the affected directory made the error go away.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.2.5 (current; version upgraded from not recorded)
- OS: Darwin 25.5.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: iTerm.app (`xterm-256color`)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest release
- Active plugins: @tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest, oh-my-openagent@latest, opencode-elf@latest, opencode-scheduler

## Reproduction

1. Upgrade OpenCode (exact previous and new versions not recorded).
2. Open or resume a session in a project directory.
3. Use the session; the specific action that first triggers the error is not yet known.

## Expected Behavior

The session should be able to request model responses after the upgrade, or provide a clear and consistent indication if the configured credentials genuinely lack a required scope.

## Actual Behavior

The session reports:

> Error: You have insufficient permissions for this operation. Missing scopes: api.responses.write. Check that you have the correct role in your organization (Reader, Writer, Owner) and project (Member, Owner), and if you're using a restricted API key, that it has the necessary scopes.

## Additional Context

Clearing OpenCode’s cache for the affected directory made the error disappear in an earlier occurrence. It is not yet known whether this workaround resolves the current occurrence, how consistently the error reproduces, or which exact action triggers it.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: agent: skill tool loops on invalid id instead of falling back
issues.body:
## Summary

When a user asks which skills are available, the agent attempts to load a skill with id `general`, which is not a valid skill id (valid ids: `caveman`, `leanrea`, `opencode`, `report`). The call fails with "Unable to load skill general", and instead of falling back to the skill list already present in context, the agent re-issues the identical failing call ~22 times in a row, never recovering. This is an agent-loop / tool-retry failure: a deterministic error result does not terminate the loop or trigger a fallback.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Windows 11 (Windows_NT 10.0.26300, win32 x64)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color (TERM_PROGRAM unset)
- Shell: Git Bash (C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe); ComSpec cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Model: ollama/lfm3-omni:2b (LFM3 Omni 2B, 32k context) — local via ollama
- Active plugins: none found in config (MCP server `convex` configured; no plugins)

## Reproduction

1. Configure and select the local model `ollama/lfm3-omni:2b` (LFM3 Omni 2B).
2. Start an opencode session with that model.
3. Ask: "what skills you have".
3. Observe the agent call `skill` with `{"id": "general"}`.
4. The tool returns `Unable to load skill general`.
5. The agent repeats the identical call many times (~22) instead of answering from context or stopping.

## Expected Behavior

The agent should not call `skill` with an id not present in the available-skills list. On a deterministic skill-load failure, the loop should terminate and fall back to the in-context skill list (or a text answer), rather than retrying the same failing call.

## Actual Behavior

Repeated `skill` tool calls with `id: "general"`, each returning `Unable to load skill general`, forming a retry storm until the session ends. No useful answer is produced.

## Additional Context

- The string `general` corresponds to an agent/subagent type, not a skill id; this likely caused the confusion.
- The available skills were already enumerated in the system context, so no tool call was necessary.
- Session export attached by user (session-02cfc45e-de13-4e23-a741-81dedf339c3c.md).
- Repro frequency: observed once from this session, specifically while using `ollama/lfm3-omni:2b`. Likely more common with small/local models that confuse agent vs. skill namespaces; not confirmed on larger models.
- Workaround: user must interrupt the session; no in-app recovery observed.

issues.title: tui: make API failures explicit and actionable

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Summary

The V2 TUI does not model API failures consistently. Many calls use the generated SDK's default `{ data, error }` result without checking `error`, turn missing data into a valid empty value, fire-and-forget a promise, or catch and discard failures. Other user-initiated failures are shown only in a five-second global toast even though the user is still inside a dialog or workflow that can render a persistent, actionable error state.

This makes transport, routing, authorization, and server errors look like legitimate empty states or successful actions. The motivating example is #36580: `/mcp` can fail while both MCP surfaces render “No MCP Servers.”

Audit baseline: `origin/dev` at `cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e` (2026-07-12). `packages/tui/src` has 109 `sdk.client` references across 24 files; only 34 request `throwOnError: true`.

## Environment

- opencode version: V2 `dev` at `cf7503687a2485621a690d18c4b0d1ff2060bc3e`
- OS: N/A — source audit
- Terminal: N/A — source audit
- Shell: N/A — source audit
- Install/channel: V2 development branch
- Active plugins: N/A — source audit

## Reproduction

1. Cause any audited endpoint to return a transport error, non-2xx response, or body without `data`.
2. Open the corresponding TUI surface or run the corresponding action.
3. Observe one of the following:
   - a legitimate empty state is rendered;
   - the dialog closes as though the action succeeded;
   - local UI state advances despite the request failing;
   - no user-visible feedback appears;
   - a transient toast appears and disappears while the failed workflow has no persistent error/retry state.

## Expected Behavior

Every API call has an explicit failure policy based on user impact:

- **Required screen/dialog data:** render a persistent error state in that surface with the actual error and retry/back controls.
- **User mutation:** keep the workflow open, preserve input, show pending/error state next to the action, and only commit optimistic state after success or roll it back.
- **Background synchronization:** preserve the last known good value, expose degraded/stale state where it affects the UI, and log structured diagnostics. Do not substitute an empty collection.
- **Best-effort side effect:** discarding an error is allowed only when the side effect is truly optional and the rationale is documented.
- **Global/session failure:** use a persistent global or session-scoped error surface when the failure affects ongoing work. Toasts remain appropriate for brief confirmations and non-blocking notices.

## Actual Behavior

### P0 — destructive or workflow-critical mutations can fail silently

- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/question.tsx:48-79` — question reply, reject, and single-answer reply are all `void` promises. The prompt can disappear via events/UI flow with no local pending/error/retry state.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx:165-186, 408-431` — allow always, reject, and allow once are fire-and-forget. The UI changes stage before success and cannot show an inline failure.
- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:190-199` — auto-approved permission replies are fire-and-forget. Failure leaves the model blocked with no visible reason.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:1058-1090` — shell and slash-command submissions are fire-and-forget. Unlike normal prompt submission, they have no error path and submission progress can remain misleading.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:413-418` — session abort is fire-and-forget after the interrupt gesture.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:562-577` — compact/summarize closes the dialog immediately and ignores failure.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:610-663` — undo swallows abort failure, fires revert without a rejection handler, rewrites the prompt, and closes the dialog before success; redo similarly fires unrevert/revert and mutates prompt state without confirmation.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/dialog-message.tsx:29-53` — message revert is fire-and-forget while prompt state is rewritten and the dialog closes.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-rename.tsx:17-27` — rename closes immediately after a fire-and-forget update.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:1018-1030` — “Background subagents” closes immediately after a fire-and-forget request.

**Treatment:** pending state in the active prompt/dialog/action, disable duplicate submission, retain user input, render the endpoint error inline, and provide retry/cancel. Do not close or mutate dependent local state until success.

### P0 — failed reads are converted into valid empty states

- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:164-168` — session list uses `data ?? []` without checking `error`.
- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:513-531` — the non-blocking bootstrap batch converts command, LSP, MCP, MCP resource, formatter, session-status, and provider-auth failures/missing data to `[]`/`{}`. One rejection also prevents `status = complete`, but the user sees no endpoint-specific state. This is the direct class behind #36580.
- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:594-650` — session messages, todo, and diff use missing data as empty values. Only `session.get` throws; partial hydration failures can erase/omit visible session state.
- `packages/tui/src/context/project.tsx:38-67` — path/project/directory responses are consumed without checking `error`; workspace list/status failures are caught to `undefined`, with failed status becoming an empty map.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-list.tsx:34-42` — both browse and search list failures are deliberately converted to `undefined`; the dialog falls back to cached sync data, so stale results are indistinguishable from a successful load.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-tag.tsx:17-26` — file-search error becomes an empty autocomplete list.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx:316-359` — file-search errors produce no options and no error state.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-skill.tsx:21-30` and `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-console-org.tsx:32-41` correctly preserve load errors for inline rendering; these should be the baseline pattern, not exceptions.

**Treatment:** typed load state (`loading | ready | stale | error`) per resource. Empty content is only valid after a successful response. Dialogs should use a locked inline error view with retry; background stores should retain last known good data and expose stale/error metadata.

### P0 — MCP errors are completely invisible

- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:519` — `/mcp` missing data becomes `{}`.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-mcp.tsx:51-69` — toggle/connect/disconnect and refresh failures only go to `console.error`; the dialog returns to a non-loading row with no explanation.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-status.tsx:53-56` — `{}` is rendered as “No MCP Servers.”
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-mcp.tsx:28-45` — `{}` becomes an empty picker.

**Treatment:** preserve MCP load/error state in sync, render “Could not load MCP servers” with details/retry in both surfaces, and render per-row mutation errors without discarding the previous status.

### P1 — workspace/project workflows swallow synchronization and safety-check errors

- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-create.tsx:80-85` — workspace sync-list and local workspace sync failures are discarded before opening selection.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-create.tsx:133-152` — post-warp bootstrap and synthetic reminder prompt failures are discarded; the function still returns success.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-create.tsx:165-175` — VCS status failure is treated as “no changes,” skipping the copy-changes safety question.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-list.tsx:84-92` — post-delete bootstrap and initial sync-list failures are discarded.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/move.tsx:117-120` — VCS status failure is treated as “no changes” before moving a session.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/move.tsx:139-152` — failure to append the synthetic directory-change reminder is discarded after moving.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-move-session.tsx:224-260` — when removal requires force, VCS status failure becomes an empty change list and the destructive confirmation continues without the evidence it intended to show.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:294-304` — workspace bootstrap failure while opening a session is caught with an empty block; the comment says the session should remain visible/non-interactive, but no degraded/non-interactive state explains why.

**Treatment:** never interpret a failed safety read as “no changes.” Show a persistent blocking error with retry/cancel. For completed primary mutations with failed follow-up sync/reminders, show a partial-success state that tells the user what succeeded and what needs retrying.

### P1 — dialog mutations use transient toasts then close or lose context

- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-list.tsx:101-169, 301-335` — create/delete/recovery failures use global toasts. The active dialog already owns the action and should retain a row/dialog error. Some nested async callbacks can also reject outside a local boundary.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-list.tsx:58-77` — delete failure uses a toast while the row has dedicated deletion state.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-create.tsx:52-69, 100-130` — adapter-load and warp failures toast; adapter-load clears the dialog before loading, so failure leaves no persistent surface.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-move-session.tsx:224-274` — project-copy deletion failures toast despite an existing stateful dialog and inline load-error pattern.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/workspace.tsx:27-46` and `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/move.tsx:30-64, 117-160` — create/move failures use toasts while the composer owns progress and destination state.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-provider.tsx:185-207, 265-283` — OAuth authorize/callback errors toast and clear the dialog. The manual code path at `321-345` already demonstrates a better inline error, though it collapses all server errors to “Invalid code.”
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-console-org.tsx:92-111` — switch-org has no local error boundary; a rejection can escape the select callback.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:468-497, 581-601` — share/unshare failures toast and close the command dialog.
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:999-1019, 1093-1118` — create-session and send-prompt failures toast; prompt input/progress should carry a durable error and retry without implying submission succeeded.

**Treatment:** put the error in the owning dialog/composer row, preserve input/selection, and offer retry. Success confirmations may remain toasts.

### P1 — fire-and-forget/read paths can reject without a boundary

- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:427-430` — LSP refresh from an event has no rejection handler.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:501-538` — both startup fork flows handle `result.data` absence but not promise rejection; the only feedback is a generic toast for a non-throwing error result.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/dialog-fork-from-timeline.tsx:22-68` and `packages/tui/src/routes/session/dialog-message.tsx:77-103` — fork assumes `data!` and has no dialog error state.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-session-list.tsx:150-169` — workspace removal in recovery has no catch around a callback that should resolve a boolean.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspace-list.tsx:89-93` — `project.workspace.sync()` is fired without handling rejection.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx`, `question.tsx`, and the mutation sites listed above use `void` as an error policy.

**Treatment:** shared mutation/task helper that requires explicit pending/success/error handling; lint/test against floating SDK promises unless annotated as best-effort.

### P1 — background/global failures are hidden or reduced to transient toasts

- `packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx:85-127` — workspace sync startup and the entire SSE loop discard errors. The user has no disconnected/reconnecting state and no last error.
- `packages/tui/src/context/data.tsx:551-564` — nine V2 location bootstrap requests use `Promise.allSettled`, but failures only reach `console.error`; downstream menus can appear empty.
- `packages/tui/src/context/kv.tsx:22-31, 54-61` — preference read/write failures only reach `console.error`; users believe changes persisted.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:1018-1028` — session execution errors are five-second global toasts. They should be attached to the affected session/turn and remain inspectable.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:1052-1067` — update failure is a toast despite originating in a modal workflow, and the actual server error is discarded.

**Treatment:** persistent connection/degraded indicator; session-scoped error cards/status; persistent settings/persistence warning; modal update failure with actual details and retry.

### P2 — error toasts lose useful details

- `packages/tui/src/ui/toast.tsx:60-78` — one global toast slot means a later toast overwrites the previous error; all errors expire after five seconds by default; non-`Error` SDK error bodies become “An unknown error has occurred.”
- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:1010-1017` — create-session error is logged to console but UI says only “Open console for more details.”
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-provider.tsx:190-194, 270-277` — raw `JSON.stringify(error)` or generic OAuth copy instead of normalized actionable details.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:921-939, 990-1014` — copy/export catches discard the actual error.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:1058-1066` — update failure discards the endpoint error.

**Treatment:** normalize generated SDK errors through `errorMessage`, retain structured details for an expandable error view, and reserve toasts for success/info or genuinely non-blocking failures.

## Recommended Design

1. Introduce a small TUI async-state model for resource and mutation ownership rather than a generic global error bus:
   - resource: `idle | loading | ready(data) | stale(data, error) | error(error)`;
   - mutation: `idle | pending | error(error)` with retry and preserved input.
2. Add reusable dialog/select error rendering (`locked`, title, normalized message, retry/back) based on the existing Skills and Console Org patterns.
3. Make required SDK calls use `{ throwOnError: true }`; require call sites to either catch into explicit UI state or propagate to an owning boundary.
4. Keep last known good background data on refresh failure. Never use `data ?? []/{}` to erase state unless the response succeeded and the schema permits absent data.
5. Add session/global degraded surfaces for SSE, bootstrap, and session execution failures.
6. Add a lint rule or focused test that rejects floating `sdk.client` promises and empty catches in `packages/tui/src`, with a documented `bestEffort(...)` escape hatch.
7. Add fault-injection tests for transport failures, non-2xx SDK results, and malformed/missing response data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `sdk.client` call in `packages/tui/src` has an explicit, reviewed error policy.
- [ ] No required read converts an SDK error/missing response into a legitimate empty state.
- [ ] No user mutation is fire-and-forget unless explicitly documented as best-effort.
- [ ] Dialog-owned failures render persistently in that dialog with retry/back and preserve input/selection.
- [ ] Composer-owned failures render persistently in the composer and preserve the unsent prompt/command.
- [ ] Session execution errors remain inspectable on the affected session/turn.
- [ ] Background refresh failures retain last known good data and expose stale/degraded state.
- [ ] SSE/workspace synchronization has a visible disconnected/reconnecting/error state.
- [ ] Error rendering preserves normalized server details; unknown structured SDK errors do not collapse to a generic message.
- [ ] Tests cover MCP status, session list/search, skills/org/project dialogs, question/permission replies, prompt/shell/command submission, rename/fork/revert/compact, workspace safety checks, and bootstrap partial failure.
- [ ] Intentionally ignored failures are wrapped in a named/documented best-effort helper and excluded from user-critical paths.

## Intentionally Best-Effort / Out of Scope

These catches should not automatically become blocking UI errors, though they should be documented or logged where useful:

- opening an external URL after the UI already displays the URL (`ui/link.tsx`, retry-action/docs links);
- renderer palette detection and theme fallback;
- temporary-file cleanup after the primary operation has already failed;
- clipboard backend probing/fallback between platform implementations;
- optional sound/attention behavior;
- reading optional local editor metadata;
- current-checkout lookup used only to highlight one row in `dialog-move-session.tsx:58-67` (already documented in code).

## Independent Cross-check Additions

A second read-only audit confirmed the list above and found several failure modes that deserve explicit tracking:

- `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:1055-1118` — prompt, shell, and command submission clears input, appends history, and may mark editor context sent without confirmed durable admission. This is stronger than a missing notification: user-authored content can appear sent while being lost. Preserve the exact prompt and attachments until admission succeeds.
- `packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx:36-39, 85-116` — the SSE retry loop only retries after normal stream completion. A request, stream, synchronization, or event-handler exception reaches the terminal empty catch and permanently ends event delivery. Isolate subscriber exceptions and catch failures inside the retry loop.
- `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:594-654` — partial messages/todo/diff failures are cached by `fullSyncedSessions`, suppressing retries for the rest of the TUI process.
- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-provider.tsx:395-415` — credential save and instance reload responses are unchecked, so the flow can report success or navigate after API failure.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:588-600` — `unshare(...).then(success)` can show false success because generated SDK API failures normally resolve as `{ error }` rather than reject.
- `packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/system/diff-viewer.tsx:114-131` — rejected diff resources default to an empty list, and the “No diff!” branch can shadow the later error branch.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx:371-385` and `packages/tui/src/plugin/slots.tsx:32-45` — plugin-host startup and slot-render failures are console-only while the TUI continues as though plugins loaded normally.
- `packages/tui/src/prompt/history.tsx` and `packages/tui/src/prompt/stash.tsx` — persistence failures are swallowed and writes are not consistently serialized. Stash failures affect user-authored drafts and need persistent dirty/error state.

The central implementation trap is the SDK's dual failure channel: API failures generally resolve in `result.error`, while transport/runtime failures reject. `try/catch` alone is not sufficient unless the call opts into `{ throwOnError: true }`.

## Additional Context

Related issue: #36580. Modal interaction work in #36302 overlaps on async dialog state, but this issue owns the broader API failure contract across bootstrap, composer, session, workspace, event, and plugin paths.

This issue is an audit/umbrella for the V2 TUI error-state contract. Fixes can land incrementally, but each child change should check off the corresponding call sites here rather than replacing one silent failure with an ephemeral toast.

issues.title: client: late history pages repopulate deleted or evicted sessions
issues.body:
### Description

An in-flight `createData().session.message.loadMore()` can publish an obsolete page after the session was deleted/evicted or its transcript was resynced. It also clears `loading` for a newer request that replaced it.

This affects the shared client transcript cache, not persisted server messages. With a real loopback HTTP fixture, deleting or evicting a session clears its 20 loaded messages, but releasing the pending older-page response puts 20 messages back. After deletion, `missing()` remains true while `message.list()` contains the old page.

A concurrent resync can lose a history boundary too: start with 40 messages, hold the older 20-message page, append a message and resync the newest 20. Releasing the old page produces 40 cached messages with the middle message absent and `more()` false.

### Plugins

None.

### OpenCode version

2.2.5, dev `1bf08ae46a91f7793c756e4ee521e37b6b554064`; Bun 1.4.4.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load a session's newest message page through `session.message.sync()`.
2. Start `session.message.loadMore()` and hold its HTTP response.
3. Deliver `session.deleted`, call `session.evict()`, or invalidate and resync with a different newest page.
4. Release the old response and await `loadMore()`.

Expected: the old request must not repopulate a cleared cache, replace the new cursor, invoke `beforePublish`, or clear a replacement request's loading state.

The ordinary delayed-page control passes. Focused regressions currently have five intended failures, including eviction followed by a new request using the same cursor, and deletion followed by a replacement with the same cursor.

The adjacent work in #57547 and #58491 changes resync-window/retention policy. This is narrower: I am preparing a guard using the existing request ownership and captured cursor, without changing those policies.

### Operating System

macOS 15.6.1 arm64.

### Terminal

Bun scripts; no live OpenCode service or model calls.

issues.title: composer: highlight slash commands so they are visually distinct from prompt text
issues.body:
### Description

In the composer, a slash command is rendered as ordinary text. In dark mode `/goal` is the same white as the prompt, so the only way to tell whether the leading text is a command or prose is the command menu or the result after submitting. This is especially confusing when the command has arguments: `/goal This is a test message.` looks like a plain sentence with a leading slash.

Claude Desktop and several TUIs render the leading command token with a distinct command color (and a subtle hover/focus state), which makes the boundary deterministic. The screenshots below compare the current OpenCode composer with Claude Desktop.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session or new-session composer.
2. Type `/goal This is a test message.` (or any built-in/custom command with an argument).
3. Observe the text. The `/goal` token has the same style as the rest of the prompt.

### Expected

- When the leading token matches a known slash command, style `/command` as a command token (color and/or subtle background), while the argument text stays normal.
- Works for built-in commands and custom commands; skills too if they become slash-triggered later.
- Unknown leading text such as `/not-a-command` stays plain, so the highlight itself signals validity.
- Caret, selection, IME composition, undo/redo, paste, and history navigation are unchanged.
- Hover/focus emphasis is welcome but optional; the minimum is a visible distinction in both light and dark themes.
- Per-command icons in the suggestion menu (Antigravity-style) are out of scope here and can be a separate enhancement.

### Actual

- The composer renders text parts as plain text nodes; only file/agent/session/skill mentions get token spans.
- Slash commands are parsed only when the prompt is submitted, so the editor has no command token to style.
- In dark mode the command and the prompt are both `--v2-text-text-base`.

### Root cause

- `packages/app/src/composer/editor/editor.tsx:495-530` (`renderComposerEditor`) creates text nodes for `type: "text"` and spans only for mentions.
- `editor.tsx:170-183`: local input intentionally skips re-rendering to preserve the caret, so a render-time token split alone would not update live.
- `packages/app/src/composer/client-slash-command.ts:9-38` and `packages/app/src/composer/model.ts:346-352` parse the command only on submit.
- The command catalog is already available at `model.ts:272-285`, so no new metadata is needed.

### Proposed fix

- Detect the leading command token from the same catalog and decorate it without replacing the contenteditable DOM:
  - Prefer the CSS Custom Highlight API (`CSS.highlights` + `::highlight(...)`) for a range-based color; it does not touch the caret, IME, or undo stack.
  - Fallback: a non-editable token span like mentions, only if it can preserve editing and backspace semantics.
- Update the highlight on input/selection and after programmatic edits; clear it for unknown commands or when the slash is not at the start.
- Use an existing syntax or accent token rather than a hardcoded blue; ensure contrast in both themes.
- Add tests for built-in/custom commands, arguments, unknown commands, backspace, IME, and RTL.

### Screenshots

Current OpenCode composer — `/goal` is plain text:

![OpenCode composer: /goal is plain text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/magiccodelab/opencode-issue-assets/main/assets/slash-0.webp)

Claude Desktop reference — the command token is highlighted:

![Claude Desktop: /goal is highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/magiccodelab/opencode-issue-assets/main/assets/slash-5.webp)

### Additional context

- Desktop and web share the composer, so this is not desktop-only.
- Environment: OpenCode Desktop v2.2.5, Windows; also reproducible in the web UI.

issues.title: ACP: slash commands execute but never stream their output
issues.body:
## Description ### User-visible symptoms Running as an ACP agent (in JetBrains Rider 2026.2): slash commands (built-in like `/init` or custom) execute, but their output is not visible in the chat. Plain prompts in the same session work normally. Another ACP agent in the same IDE does show its slash-command output, so the client's rendering path is fine. ### At the protocol level `session/prompt` replies `end_turn` immediately; no `session/update` follows for that turn. #### Example [Rider's ACP log](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/acp.html#collect-acp-logs) (`llm.agent.extended.logging=true`): ```text 20:44:23,425 → session/prompt id=5 {"prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"/my-test"}]} 20:44:23,457 ← {"stopReason":"end_turn","_meta":{}} ← 32 ms … no ACP traffic for 4 m 16 s … 20:48:39,687 → session/set_config_option id=6 ``` The command *did* run (it produced its effect). OpenCode's `session_message` table shows that the turn ran to completion after it was closed on wire: ```text seq 20 user 20:44:23.531 ← AFTER end_turn seq 21 assistant 20:44:24.281 → completed 20:44:32.895 ... seq 28 idle 20:44:32.901 outcome=succeeded ``` `my-test` was advertised in `available_commands_update` so this is the recognized-command path (not the unknown-/ fallthrough).
## OpenCode version 2.0.26
## Steps to reproduce 1. Install OpenCode as an ACP agent in Rider. I used a custom agent path. 1.1. Install OpenCode independently from Rider. 1.2. Add OpenCode as a [custom agent](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/acp.html#add-custom-agent): ```{ "default_mcp_settings": {}, "agent_servers": { "OpenCode": { "command": "full/path/to/opencode.exe", "args": ["acp"] } } } ``` 2. Run any slash command.
## Operating System Windows 10
## Suspected cause `packages/cli/src/acp/turn.ts`: ```ts yield* submit(attached, prompt) if (prompt.command) return "succeeded" as const // ← return yield* Fiber.join(events) ``` For command prompts the turn returns `succeeded` before `Fiber.join(events)`, and then the release step closes the per-turn event subscription, so no `session/update` (and no `permission.asked`) can be emitted. ### Possible fix PR #49208 (open; probably needs rebase onto current v2).

issues.title: tui: thinking/footer marquee row slides and leaves line artifacts in COSMIC Terminal (cosmic-term)
issues.body:
## Summary

In OpenCode v2.2.5 running inside COSMIC Terminal (cosmic-term), the row that
marquee-slides right-to-left while the model is thinking shifts/repaints badly
during the animation, leaving a stray horizontal line artifact below the footer
text (persisting even while idle). This looks like the remaining portion of
#23452 ("loading bar shifts window, lines in logo"): the mitigation in #33633
removed the logo animation, but the thinking/footer marquee animation still
misbehaves in cosmic-term.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5 (latest release channel)
- OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS (Ubuntu noble), kernel 7.0.11-76070011-generic, x86_64, Wayland
- Terminal: cosmic-term 1.5.0~1785465790~24.04~7daf10e and
  1.11.0~1792606905~24.04~a5e1bb5 (reproduces on both); TERM=xterm-256color,
  COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: official release
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Run the opencode TUI inside cosmic-term on Pop!_OS 24.04 (Wayland session).
2. Send a message so the thinking spinner / footer marquee row is active.
3. Observe the footer row sliding right-to-left and a horizontal line artifact
   below the footer text.

## Expected Behavior

The animated row repaints in place, and the idle screen renders with clean text
and no stray line artifact, in cosmic-term (other terminals render this
correctly, per the reports in #23452).

## Actual Behavior

During the thinking animation the footer row slides and the terminal paints a
spurious line under the text; a thin line artifact also shows below the
branding while idle. It reproduces consistently, survives terminal restarts and
resizes, and did not change across the cosmic-term 1.5.0 → 1.11.0 update.

## Additional Context

- Related: #23452 (closed: logo animation removed by #33633) and the
  cross-filed terminal-side issue pop-os/cosmic-term#789 (still open). The same
  details are being posted there as a comment.
- Workarounds tried, none helped:
  - Updated cosmic-term 1.5.0 → 1.11.0
  - Full terminal restart
  - Changed the terminal font
  - OpenCode v2.2.3+ debug-bar text-rendering controls
  - `"animations": false` in cli.json — the footer row still slides and the
    artifacts persist
- No alternative terminal was installed locally for an isolation test at the
  time of testing; everything above reproduces on the stock Pop!_OS cosmic-term.
- Happy to provide a short screen recording if it helps triaging.

issues.title: desktop: /export saves to the client machine on SSH servers — write into the workspace and show the path
issues.body:
### Description

On the Windows Desktop app connected to a server over SSH, `/export` opens the Windows save dialog and writes the file to the local machine. The session workspace is on the SSH host, so there is no way to export the session next to the project. The success toast also shows only the filename, not the chosen path, and offers no Copy action.

The JSON payload itself is already complete: `fetchSessionExport` pages through every message. This request is about the destination and the path, not the format.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect the Desktop app to a remote server over SSH.
2. Open a session and run `/export`.
3. Save the file.
4. The file appears on the Windows machine; the remote workspace is unchanged.
5. The success toast shows only the generated filename.

### Expected

- A destination choice: save into the session workspace on the server, or save to this computer.
- A workspace export writes under the session's `location.directory` (default suggestion: `.opencode/exports/<filename>`) and returns the absolute server path.
- The success UI shows the full path with a Copy action. For local saves, also offer "Show in folder".
- The default should be the workspace, matching the old cwd behavior and keeping the export next to the project.
- Filenames should keep Unicode titles instead of falling back to `ses_...`, and collisions should get a suffix rather than silently overwriting.

### Actual

- The renderer fetches the export and calls `platform.saveFile`.
- On Desktop, that opens an Electron save dialog and writes with the local `fs.writeFile`.
- The remote SSH workspace is never touched.
- `saveFile` returns only a boolean, so the app cannot display or copy the chosen path; the toast uses `filename` only.

### Root cause

- `packages/app/src/session/commands/use-session-commands.tsx:152-181`: `/export` runs entirely in the renderer and calls `saveSessionExport`.
- `packages/app/src/session/commands/export.ts:64-76`: falls back to a browser download, or calls `platform.saveFile`.
- `packages/desktop/src/main/files/index.ts:73-85`: `dialog.showSaveDialog` plus local `fs.writeFile`. It has no access to the SSH server's filesystem.
- `packages/app/src/runtime/platform/platform.tsx:79` and `packages/desktop/src/renderer/api-types.ts:44`: `saveFile` resolves to `boolean`, so the absolute path is discarded.
- `packages/app/src/session/commands/export.ts:36-49`: the filename slug only keeps `[a-z0-9_-]`, so non-ASCII titles lose their text.

### Feasibility

The server already exposes a location-scoped write: `packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:78-100` (`fs.write`), which creates parent directories and returns the absolute path. The app already uses it to upload attachments (`packages/app/src/composer/attachments/destination.ts:31`). No new protocol is required for a workspace export.

### Proposed fix

- Add a small export dialog with **Workspace (server)** and **This computer**, plus the existing JSON format (Markdown is tracked in #55542).
- For the workspace, POST the serialized content to `fs.write` with `location[directory] = session.location.directory` and `path = .opencode/exports/<filename>`, then use the returned `data.path`.
- Show the full path in a toast or result dialog with a Copy action; use `showToast({ actions })` or the existing result-dialog pattern.
- For local saves, extend the desktop save IPC to return the chosen path instead of a boolean, or add a path-returning variant.
- Default to the workspace, especially when `server.isLocal` is false.
- Treat the export as sensitive: it contains the full transcript, so use a git-ignored directory and/or restrictive permissions, and mention that in the UI.

### Additional context

- OpenCode Desktop v2.2.5 (source `1bf08ae`), Windows desktop app, SSH remote server, no third-party plugins.
- Related: #53748 (TUI exports to `/tmp` instead of cwd), #55542 (Desktop Markdown export), #49803 (Desktop/TUI slash-command parity), #58957 (remote file download in the Desktop preview).

issues.title: desktop: /export offers only JSON — expose the Markdown format the TUI already has
issues.body:
## Summary

`/export` offers a Markdown format in the TUI, but the desktop app only offers JSON. Same command, different formats depending on which client you're in.

## Current behaviour

In the TUI, `/export` presents a dialog with two formats — Markdown (human-readable, opens in `$EDITOR`) and JSON (structured, re-importable). This is described in #48105.

In the desktop app, the command palette describes `/export` as "Export the full session transcript as JSON", and no Markdown option is offered.

So a user who wants to read a conversation, or paste it somewhere, has to work in the TUI — or open the JSON and convert it by hand. For a long session that JSON is several megabytes.

## Related, and deliberately not duplicated here

This is **not** about the truncation bug. #50014 and #50732 both cover it, and the Markdown export there is built from the UI's loaded window rather than full storage. That is a separate fix with someone already on it, and this request should not compete with that work.

It does affect the desktop app equally — a desktop user exporting a long session gets whatever the TUI produces, truncated or not.

**A note on scope, offered as an observation rather than a direction:** #50014 and #50732 look like two reports of one underlying cause — the Markdown transcript being assembled from the UI's loaded window instead of from storage, which is presumably why the JSON path is unaffected. Fixing that at the source would close both issues at once. Leaving that decision to whoever is picking them up.

## Why I think it belongs in core rather than a plugin

I built a plugin that reads the session store directly and writes Markdown, which sidesteps both the format gap and the truncation. That works, but it means:

- a second, divergent implementation of session export that will drift from whatever the built-in eventually does
- users needing an extra dependency to read their own conversations

The desktop Markdown format is a parity gap, not a missing feature — the implementation already exists in this repo.

## Proposal

Expose the existing Markdown format in the desktop app's `/export`, ideally through the same format choice the TUI offers.

If there is a reason the desktop app deliberately ships JSON-only, I'd like to understand it — I couldn't find one in #48105 or elsewhere.

## Environment

- OpenCode 2.0.24 (desktop)
- Observed on the session list in the desktop app; `/export` in the command palette is described as JSON

issues.title: goal: add Copy/View full to the pill menu and keep the objective readable after Clear
issues.body:
### Description

The goal pill is the only place that shows the full goal objective, but its popover heading is clamped to three lines and the menu has no Copy or "View full" action. Clearing the goal deletes the goal state, hides the pill, and leaves the truncated timeline notice as the only record.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `/goal <long objective>`.
2. Click the `Goal` / `Goal met` pill above the composer.
3. Observe the three-line heading; try to copy the full objective or find a copy action.
4. Click `Clear`.
5. The pill disappears. The timeline still shows only `Goal: <truncated>`.

### Expected

- A Copy action copies the complete objective.
- A "View full" action or scrollable view shows the complete objective.
- Clearing the goal does not remove the only readable copy; the transcript should stay self-sufficient.
- Clear should ask for confirmation, since it is destructive.

### Actual

- The heading uses `line-clamp-3` at 11px in a 320px popover.
- The menu only offers Pause, Resume, and Clear.
- Clear removes the goal state; the full objective remains in `messages[0].text` but has no UI entry point.

### Root cause

- `packages/app/src/session/composer/plugin-pills.tsx:110-119`: generic popover header with `w-80`, `text-[11px]`, and `line-clamp-3`.
- `packages/gui-plugins/src/goal/renderer.tsx:94-112`: menu only has Pause, Resume, and Clear.
- `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts:374-383`: `clear` writes `undefined` to the goal storage.

### Additional context

Built-in goal plugin (#59437). The same objective is also hidden in the timeline; see #61332.

### Environment

- OpenCode Desktop v2.2.5 (source checkout `1bf08ae`; Desktop and web share the same `packages/app` renderer).
- Windows desktop app.
- No third-party plugins; this is the built-in goal plugin.

issues.title: goal: the initial objective disappears from the timeline after /goal
issues.body:
### Description

When `/goal <objective>` is used in a session, the objective never appears as a user message. The first timeline row is a synthetic kickoff notice rendered as one truncated line:

`Goal: 参见计划：...`

The rest of the objective cannot be read or expanded from the transcript. This makes the user's initial request look like it disappeared, especially in long sessions.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session.
2. Run `/goal <objective>` with an objective longer than one line.
3. Look at the top of the timeline.
4. Try to expand the `Goal: ...` row or find the rest of the text.

### Expected

The objective should remain readable in the session, for example as a collapsible goal card or an expandable notice with the full text. Copying it should also be possible.

### Actual

Only `Goal: <first 120 characters>` is shown, then the row is clipped by `truncate`. The full text exists in the synthetic message's `text` field, but there is no UI path to it. The session title is also replaced with the first 60 characters of the objective, so the tab and header show the same fragment.

### Root cause

- `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts:411-431` stores the objective in goal storage and creates a `synthetic` kickoff with `description: Goal: ${truncate(text, 120)}` instead of a user message.
- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/projection.ts:1179-1186` projects synthetic messages with a description as `Notice` rows.
- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/session-timeline-row.tsx:574,727-729` renders the notice as a single-line `truncate` with no expand or copy.
- `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts:404-409` overwrites the session title with `truncate(text, 60)`.

### Additional context

- A real 356-message session export has `messages[0].type === "synthetic"`, `metadata.source === "goal"`, and only one later `user` message. The initial objective is not present as a user message.
- This is the built-in goal plugin added in #59437 (v2.2.1+), not a third-party plugin.
- The goal pill also lacks a full-text or copy view; this is tracked separately.

### Environment

- OpenCode Desktop v2.2.5 (source checkout `1bf08ae`; Desktop and web share the same `packages/app` renderer).
- Windows desktop app.
