issues.title: desktop: session scroll position is lost when switching sessions and back (v2 2.0.29, Windows)
issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenCode Desktop v2 (`opencode v2.0.29`, Windows), switching from a long session to another session and then back drops the timeline to the bottom of the conversation instead of restoring the scroll position left when the session was last active. The reading position is lost on every switch.

Follow-up to #55114 (closed as not planned for Desktop 1.18.x, with the instruction to open a new issue with a v2 version if it still reproduces).

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.29 (`opencode --version`)
- OS: Windows 11 (Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0, x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: desktop app UI session (terminal environment variables are not set)
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: OpenCode Desktop, release build (v2)
- Active plugins: `oh-my-openagent@latest`

## Reproduction

1. Open a session with a long conversation (long enough that the timeline scrolls).
2. Scroll up so the viewport rests in the middle of the conversation, away from the bottom.
3. Switch to a different session.
4. Switch back to the original session.
5. Observe: the timeline is at the bottom of the conversation instead of the position left in step 2.

## Expected Behavior

The timeline should return to the scroll position left when the session was last active, and should only follow to the bottom when the user left it at the bottom (or new content is being appended).

## Actual Behavior

The timeline jumps to the bottom on every switch back. No error is shown; the previously read position must be found again by scrolling manually. Occurs consistently and does not require new messages to arrive in the session.

## Additional Context

- Previous report with the same symptom: #55114 (Desktop 1.18.34/1.18.35, macOS; closed as not planned; also confirmed there on Desktop v2 2.0.28 by another reporter).
- Earlier related reports: #42213, #45212, #35377, #44152 (desktop); #42806 (web, parent/child sessions, open).
- Earlier fix attempts closed without merging: #48125, #33875.
- Source notes from #55114: session tabs are router routes, so switching unmounts the previous session's timeline (its `scrollTop` is discarded); the timeline follow state defaults to `pinned: true`, so a remounted timeline lands at the bottom; the window-scoped tabs store persists titles/panes/closed tabs but no scroll offset or pin state.
- Frequency: 100% reproducible, any session with a scrollable timeline.
- Workarounds tried: none found; manual scrolling back each time.
- Related open requests: #54572, #53629.

issues.title: A bug where a session is automatically executed without permission.
issues.body:
## Description

I was building a desktop app (`translate-desktop`) in one project. The build was still running when I rebooted my computer.

After the reboot, I started `opencode --yolo` in a different project directory. OpenCode automatically resumed the unfinished session from the other project and continued running it. It repeatedly launched `translate-desktop` windows and interrupted my work.

I did not approve this. I also could not find a clear setting or command to disable it.

## OpenCode version(opencode TUI)

`2.2.1` (`latest` channel)

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), kernel `6.12.113+deb13-amd64`, x86_64.

### Terminal

GNOME Terminal on Wayland, `TERM=xterm-256color`, shell `/bin/bash`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long-running build in a session. The build opens a desktop app window.
2. While it is still running, reboot the computer.
3. After reboot, start `opencode --yolo` from a different project directory.
4. Do not resume anything manually.
5. The old unfinished session starts by itself and keeps launching the app.

## Expected behavior

- After a reboot, unfinished sessions should stay paused.
- OpenCode should ask before resuming, or provide a clear setting/command to disable auto-resume.

## Actual behavior

The old session resumes automatically, runs tools without my consent, and opens app windows.

## Additional context

- The issue is not the app itself. The problem is that OpenCode resumes the old session without asking.
- The background service is global, so a session from another project can be resumed even when I start OpenCode in a different directory.
- Workaround: press `Esc` to interrupt the turn before rebooting, or run `opencode service set disabled true` to use a standalone server. There is no obvious setting for this.

issues.title: [FEATURE]:Per-Session OAuth Account Isolation for OpenAI Codex
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

# Feature Request: Isolate OAuth Accounts Per Session/Tab

## Problem

When using OpenCode with the native OpenAI Codex OAuth integration, switching accounts can potentially affect other active sessions or tabs.

For example:

1. Open OpenCode in Tab 1 and authenticate using **Account A**.
2. Start a coding task in Tab 1.
3. Open another OpenCode tab (Tab 2).
4. Switch the Codex OAuth account to **Account B** in Tab 2.
5. Return to Tab 1 and continue working.

The concern is that switching the active OAuth account in Tab 2 may also change the account used by Tab 1.

This makes it difficult to work with multiple OpenAI accounts simultaneously.

## Expected Behavior

OAuth authentication should be isolated per OpenCode session or instance.

- Tab 1 should remain authenticated with Account A.
- Tab 2 should remain authenticated with Account B.
- Switching accounts in Tab 2 should not affect Tab 1.
- Existing tasks and conversations should retain their original account.
- New requests in each session should consistently use the account assigned to that session.

## Proposed Solution

Provide session-level or instance-level OAuth account isolation instead of relying exclusively on a globally shared active account.

Ideally, users should be able to:

- Authenticate multiple Codex accounts.
- Assign a specific OAuth account to each session.
- Run multiple sessions concurrently using different accounts.
- Switch accounts in one session without affecting other sessions.

## Questions

1. Is OAuth account selection currently shared globally across all OpenCode sessions?
2. Is there already a supported way to isolate Codex OAuth accounts per session?
3. If not, could this be considered as a feature enhancement?

**Use case:** Developers who have multiple OpenAI accounts and want to run parallel coding tasks using different Codex subscriptions without authentication conflicts.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: session browser tabs should be visible from non-desktop clients (web/iOS)
issues.body:
## Summary

Browser tabs opened in a session are only reachable from the desktop app. Other clients connected to the same server (web, iOS) show no tabs and cannot attach to the pane, so when I switch context away from my desk the browser state that is part of the work is gone.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (darwin arm64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: opencode-mobile-notifications

## Reproduction

1. In OpenCode Desktop, open a session and open a page in its side-panel browser (e.g. `https://example.com`).
2. Connect another client to the same server (`opencode pair`, open the link on a phone or in a browser).
3. Open the same session from that client and look at the side panel.

## Expected Behavior

The session's browser tabs are visible from any client, at least as a list with URLs so they can be opened. Ideally the page itself is viewable there, either through a remote-attach to the running pane or a server-proxied renderer.

## Actual Behavior

The other client shows no browser tabs at all. The pane is a desktop-owned Electron `WebContentsView`: a window registers as the pane's owner over `rpc.experimental.browser.control` and receives embeds by `tabID`, and only one window can own it at a time (the app surfaces `Browser control moved to another desktop window` / `browser.pane.replaced`). There is no HTTP surface for another client to attach to; the server API has no browser endpoint. The web build of the panel is limited to "Only web pages can open here", and in this test it rendered nothing.

## Additional Context

- Agent-side control already works well (`browser.tabs.open/list/close/focus`, `navigate`, `reload`, `back/forward`, `click`, `fill`, `evaluate`, `screenshot`, `console`), scoped to the session's side panel. This request is only about *other clients* being able to see or reach those tabs.
- Motivation: browser tabs are frequently part of the context needed to resume a task, so a client that cannot see them loses that context on a device switch. No sync service is implied; reading the session's stored tab list would already be useful, and a remote/proxied renderer would be ideal.
- GUI plugins cannot close this gap: they cannot add UI to the native iOS client, and they cannot claim or relay the pane to a non-desktop client.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: /handoff — continue a long session in a fresh context, without LLM re-summarization
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Long sessions eventually get noisy enough that the model starts tripping over its own history. /compact helps but keeps you in the same session; forking copies everything. What I keep wanting is a fresh session that starts with just enough to continue the work.

This has come up before — #26757 and #21760 asked for essentially this and both went stale; #40578 implemented it on top of LLM compaction and got caught by the PR cleanup bot before review. I have a small prototype of this running locally and it's been surprisingly useful. Happy to share details or a PR if the team thinks this belongs in core.

issues.title: mcp: remote server that allows anonymous tool listing never enters needs_auth; OAuth sign-in is never offered
issues.body:
## Summary
A remote OAuth MCP server that serves its tool list to anonymous connections (Google Workspace Calendar MCP at `https://calendarmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`) is reported as "connected", so OpenCode never sets `needs_auth` and never offers a sign-in affordance. Tool calls then fail with `requires a login before it can register a client`, and there is no way to reach the OAuth flow from the UI.

## Environment
- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26300 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: N/A — OpenCode Desktop
- Shell: N/A
- Install/channel: latest (Desktop)
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction
1. Configure a remote MCP server with pre-registered OAuth client credentials:
```jsonc
"google-calendar": {
  "type": "remote",
  "url": "https://calendarmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1",
  "oauth": {
    "client_id": "{file:<redacted>}",
    "client_secret": "{file:<redacted>}",
    "scope": "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.calendarlist.readonly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.freebusy https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly",
    "callback_port": 19876,
    "redirect_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:19876/callback"
  }
}
```
2. Note the server connects and exposes its 9 tools without any auth state: `mcp connected server=google-calendar tools=9`.
3. Open `/mcps` — the server shows green/connected and there is **no** authenticate/sign-in option (Desktop list rows are only enable toggles). A previously shown "Connection failed" modal had only Disable / Try again.
4. Call any tool → `MCP server "https://calendarmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1" requires a login before it can register a client` (HTTP 401, `mcp http authentication rejected`), `failed to call MCP tool`.

## Expected Behavior
A remote server that requires OAuth should enter `needs_auth` (like servers whose initial request is rejected), and `/mcps` should offer the sign-in flow. Tool calls should never dead-end with a login requirement that no UI can satisfy.

## Actual Behavior
The server stays "connected" (anonymous tool listing accepted by the gateway), the auth state is never surfaced, and the user is locked out of the OAuth flow entirely. Changing `protocol` to `auto` or `2026-07-28` does not change the behavior.

## Additional Context
- Related open issues: #53942 (server stays connected while calls fail 401), #59820 (no offline access → no refresh token), closed #44220 (calendar MCP tokens never saved).
- Workarounds tried: pre-registered OAuth client config, `protocol: auto` / `2026-07-28`, app restarts, forcing reconnect via toggle. None surface auth.
- Note: for contrast, a server whose *initial* request is rejected (e.g. GitHub's MCP when unauthenticated) correctly enters `needs_auth` — but then OpenCode selects `dcr` registration and fails with "Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration" instead of using the configured pre-registered client.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Stateless streaming inference with external history and tool declarations
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I searched for an existing request covering this complete interface. #47366 concerns per-request options on stateless text generation; #50185 concerns supplying an external executor to OpenCode, which is the opposite direction.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Expose a public, authenticated single-step streaming inference API for applications that own their own conversation history, agent loop, tool execution, and approvals, while OpenCode continues to own provider connections, credential refresh, configuration, and model resolution.

#### Current gap

Source inspected: OpenCode 2.2.5, commit ff90ed91607cabf420a369e9009539c1aa0932af.

- `@opencode/ai` already supports single-call `generate`/`stream` with full messages and tool declarations; its separate `loop` API executes tools.
- `Generate` uses `ModelResolver` and the existing authenticated provider runtime, but public `experimental.generate.text` accepts only prompt/model and returns text.
- `session.generate` uses OpenCode-owned session context and returns text. `session.prompt`, CLI run, and ACP operate on OpenCode agent sessions.
- Using `@opencode/ai` directly does not by itself reuse an installed OpenCode instance's connected accounts, configuration, and model resolution.

An external orchestrator therefore cannot currently use the complete existing provider/account machinery through the public API while retaining ownership of history and tool execution.

#### Requested contract

Extend the existing Generate owner and expose it through the official Server/client and embedded SDK surfaces; exact method naming is open for discussion.

Input:
- Explicit model reference (`providerID`, model ID, optional variant).
- System instructions and complete messages, including assistant tool calls and externally produced tool results.
- Tool declarations/JSON schemas, tool choice, and supported generation options.
- Request identity and cancellation through the existing request/stream lifecycle.

Output:
- Typed text/reasoning and tool-call stream events.
- Finish reason and usage, including cache fields when supplied by the provider.
- Existing typed authentication/model/provider errors; no silent model, account, or billing fallback.

Semantics:
- Perform one model step, without executing client tools or starting an OpenCode agent loop.
- Do not create a business Session or append to a user's session history.
- Reuse Provider/Integration/ModelResolver, supported provider hooks, credential refresh, and the existing request executor.
- Define the configuration/location and account scope explicitly. Do not export provider credentials in model/readiness responses or diagnostics (related exposure concern: #53465).
- Require only bounded request-scoped state, with cancellation and resource cleanup owned by the existing lifecycle.

#### Acceptance evidence

1. Use a connected test provider through the normal OpenCode resolver; credentials remain server-side.
2. Submit full history plus a test tool schema, receive a tool call without executing it in OpenCode, then submit an independently generated external tool result in a second request.
3. Stream normalized output and usage; cancellation terminates the request and releases resources.
4. Missing account, unavailable model/variant, and unsupported capabilities produce explicit failures.
5. No business Session/history rows are created by these calls, and unrelated sessions/configuration remain unchanged.
6. Cover the contract through the official generated client and embedded SDK using an isolated test account/environment.

Related: #39243, #47366, #50185. This requests the external-history/tool streaming contract in addition to existing text-only generation; it does not request a second agent runtime or a new credential store.

issues.title: Claude Agent: 5-hour plan limit drains ~1.8x faster because the SDK labels requests sdk-ts
issues.body:
### Description

With the Claude Agent provider, opencode uses the 5-hour Claude plan limit about 1.8x faster than the same work in Claude Code's own TUI.

opencode starts `claude` through the Agent SDK, and the SDK sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts` when it isn't already set. Requests labeled `sdk-ts`/`sdk-cli` use more of the 5-hour window for the same tokens. Weekly limits don't seem to be affected. This is tracked upstream in anthropics/claude-code#97074 (still open, with a controlled A/B test showing ~1.8x). T3 Code users measured the same thing with a custom label: 14-15 calls per 1% with `sdk-ts` vs 25-27 with any non-`sdk-*` name (pingdotgg/t3code#24649, pingdotgg/t3code#25597).

Users can't fix it from Claude Code's side either: opencode loads no `~/.claude` settings (`settingSources: []`), so the common `"env": { "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT": ... }` workaround in `settings.json` has no effect. Only exporting it in the shell before starting opencode works today.

Suggested fix: set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=opencode` next to the other variables in `ISOLATION_ENV`. The SDK keeps a value that is already set, and Claude Code keeps custom labels (it only rewrites `cli` to `sdk-cli` in `-p` mode).

_Written by Claude Opus 5.5 on behalf of @Salloxy._

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

2.2.5 / `dev` at c8a473b, Claude Code 2.1.316, Agent SDK 0.3.301

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect the Claude Agent provider with a Pro/Max subscription.
2. Run a session and look at any Claude transcript it writes under `~/.claude/projects/...`: every entry has `"entrypoint":"sdk-ts"`.
3. Compare the 5-hour usage per token with the same work in the `claude` TUI (`"entrypoint":"cli"`), or with opencode started with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=opencode` exported.

### Operating System

Windows 11

Windows Terminal

issues.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers that use `{env:VAR}` in `headers` connect on some service runs and fail on others. On failing runs the header goes out with an empty token, even though `ps eww` shows the variable set in the `opencode serve --service` process. A literal token in `headers` connects every time.

Related: #56125 (same Kagi config, closed because the maintainers could only reproduce it with the variable missing from the service) and #33853 (a commenter there also has the variable set and sees it resolve to empty).

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64)
- Terminal: Unavailable (opencode runs under T3 Code)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (`~/.opencode/bin/opencode`)
- Active plugins: @dietrichgebert/ponytail, plus local plugins ruff, pyrefly, ty, oxc

## Reproduction

The failure is intermittent. These steps produced both successes and failures:

1. Add two remote MCP servers to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` with env substitution in the auth header:
   ```jsonc
   "kagi": {
     "type": "remote",
     "url": "https://mcp.kagi.com/mcp",
     "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:KAGI_API_KEY}" }
   },
   "github": {
     "type": "remote",
     "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
     "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:GITHUB_MCP_PAT}" },
     "oauth": false
   }
   ```
2. Make sure both variables are in the background service's environment.
3. Run `opencode service restart`, start a session, and check `/mcps`.

## Expected Behavior

Both servers connect with `Authorization: Bearer <value of the variable>`.

## Actual Behavior

On a failing run, both servers fail on every connection attempt. Kagi returns 401, and opencode then tries OAuth and marks the server `needs_auth`:

```
level=WARN message="mcp http authentication rejected" status=401 server=kagi origin=https://mcp.kagi.com
level=WARN message="mcp connect failed" server=kagi status.status=needs_auth
  status.error="MCP server \"https://mcp.kagi.com/mcp\" requires a login before it can register a client"
```

GitHub fails in the same runs:

```
level=WARN message="mcp connect failed" server=github status.status=failed
  status.error="Error POSTing to endpoint: bad request: Authorization header is badly formatted (HTTP 400)"
```

Remote servers that use OAuth or no auth connect normally in those runs.

## Additional Context

- I checked the running service with `ps eww`. `KAGI_API_KEY` is set and non-empty in the `opencode serve --service` process that logged the failures.
- Kagi's `initialize` endpoint returns 401 only when the bearer is empty or missing. Any non-empty token, even `Bearer nope`, gets 200. So the 401 means opencode sent an empty token.
- GitHub's "badly formatted" 400 matches the empty `Bearer ` that #54205 found through `opencode api get /api/config`.
- Of four service runs with this config, two connected Kagi (`mcp connected server=kagi tools=2`) and two failed. Restarting opencode didn't fix it.
- A second opencode process, started by Zed, was running at the same time with the same variable set.
- Workaround: a literal token in `headers` connects every time.
- Not yet checked: `opencode api get /api/config` during a failing run, and whether it reproduces in the plain TUI outside T3 Code. I'll add both when I have them.

issues.title: [FEATURE]:Thread for updates that anxious users can subscribe to
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I'm a sort of new user. New to AI assisted coding as well. Not a heavy user. I installed opencode in mid-October and used it without ever hitting a limit and now every message hits a limit.

Most users here seem to be suffering from this with multiple threads and an attempt to collect similar problems in one thread, etc. But there is a lack of clarity.  I don't know about others but far from coding help, opencode is wasting time to simply wait around and possibly break things while trying to resolve a server-side issue.

This is not ungratefulness. Free tiers can't be choosers. But we are also potential customers if this starts working for us. And there are paid users needing the free tier as well. This is clearly not a brief problem. It's lasted through multiple updates. Users attempt to use the software, hit a limit or get started and hit a limit, then come here to see if a new solution has come up...

It would be graceful all around to simply give a daily update or similar as to what was found/investigated/is being attempted to resolve the situation, so we don't have to track individual threads for potential solutions for days on end. And if nothing has changed, then a message to simply wait, so users can get on with their lives and also not bother you.

Doesn't have to be fancy. Just a thread with "Subscribe to this thread for status updates on the limits issue" and everybody gets told in their inboxes and a lot of frustration and wasted effort is saved.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61339

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A delayed history page could refill a deleted/evicted transcript or replace the cursor from a newer resync. Its finalizer could also clear a replacement request's loading state.

Only accept each page while the request still owns its slot and the original cursor is current. Deletion releases that slot too. The finalizer only clears loading for its own request. This changes the client cache, not persisted messages or retention policy.

- `bun run test test/solid-eviction.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize --seed 61300`: 110 passed.

A real loopback HTTP fixture also confirms cleared caches stay clear and a resync keeps its newer cursor. No model calls.

Scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Root `bun run check` reaches unrelated missing workspace dependencies in this filtered install, so I cannot claim a full monorepo check. Runtime validation was on macOS arm64; Windows/Linux remain for CI.

prs.title: fix(core): rebuild a location after its directory becomes a git repo
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61009

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A location graph is cached for its whole life and resolves its Project once. Opening a folder before `git init` therefore pinned the markerless identity: `opencode session list` returned nothing because sessions were stored under the new VCS identity.

The map now records the resolved Project id. Graphs whose identity could not be pinned yet (no VCS marker, or a repository with no commit or remote, where the id is `global`) are re-resolved before the next borrow, and invalidated only when that id actually changes.

The check stays cheap and never disturbs a live Location: it probes only the location directory for `.git`/`.hg` with async fs (no upward walk), skips borrowed or retained graphs, and detaches with a deferred invalidation instead of `lifecycle.shutdown`, so running steps hand off at their boundary.

### How did you verify your code works?

New tests in `packages/core/test/location-layer.test.ts` cover the `git init` -> borrow -> first commit sequence (a `global` identity mid-way, then the commit id) and assert a borrowed location keeps its identity until released. Without the fix the first test fails with `Received: undefined`. `bun test test/location-layer.test.ts`: 26 pass, 0 fail. `bun run typecheck:tsc` passes.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix: link new Console workspaces to their Go page and show monthly Go resets
prs.body:
**Hitting a Go limit now links new Console workspaces to their Go page, and monthly limits show when they reset.**
Follow-up to #60284. Workspaces created in the new Console have `org_` IDs, and the TUI only recognised the older `wrk_` ones. Separately, every client treated a reset more than a week away as a bad header, which hid the reset date for monthly Go limits.

❌ **Before**
1. A user in an `org_` workspace hits their Go limit in the TUI.
2. ❌ The "turn on Extra Usage" link goes to the Console home instead of their workspace's Go page.
3. A user hits their monthly Go limit with 25 days left.
4. ❌ The TUI, desktop dialog, composer tray and timeline all hide when it resets.

✅ **After**
1. The link goes to `opencode.ai/console/<workspace>/go` for both `org_` and `wrk_` workspaces.
2. Reset times up to 45 days out are shown; anything later is still treated as a bad header.

```diff
- workspace id matches wrk_…            -> Go page link, else Console home
+ workspace id matches org_… or wrk_…   -> Go page link, else Console home
- reset more than 7 days away  -> hide it
+ reset more than 45 days away -> hide it
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| TUI Go link, `org_01J…` workspace | ❌ Console home | ✅ its Go page |
| TUI Go link, `wrk_…` workspace | ✅ its Go page | ✅ its Go page |
| Monthly Go limit, 25 days left (TUI, desktop, timeline) | ❌ no reset shown | ✅ reset date shown |
| Reset 60 days out | hidden | hidden |

TUI notice for a monthly limit with 25 days left in an `org_` workspace, rendered by the TUI lifecycle test harness:

❌ **Before**
```text
┃ OpenCode Go monthly usage limit reached
┃ Switch to a free model with ctrl+x m to continue.
┃
┃ Or turn on Extra Usage on your Go page to keep going now:
┃ https://opencode.ai/console
```

✅ **After**
```text
┃ OpenCode Go monthly usage limit reached
┃ Resets Nov 27, 8:00 PM. Switch to a free model with ctrl+x m to continue.
┃
┃ Or turn on Extra Usage on your Go page to keep going now:
┃ https://opencode.ai/console/org_01JXYZ7Q2M4N/go
```

The new TUI, desktop and timeline tests fail without the change. 4 test files touched, all passing. One of them also gets small spacing and object-building tidies that the changed-files lint asked for.

👀 **Read:** `packages/tui/src/util/usage-limits.ts`, the workspace pattern. It only matches letters, digits, `_` and `-`, so the ID needs no URL encoding. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Found reviewing #60284 against the Console's workspace ID and Go allowance code · no user reports</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test test/util/usage-limits.test.ts` (packages/tui): 7 pass
- `bun test --conditions=solid --isolate --preload ../ui/test/solid-jsx.ts --preload ./happydom.ts src/session/usage-exceeded-dialogs.test.ts` (packages/app): 3 pass
- `bun test src/timeline/projection.test.ts` (packages/session-ui): 25 pass

- The notice frames above: the TUI lifecycle Go-limit test, temporarily set to a monthly limit and an `org_` workspace, run once with this branch and once with `dev`'s `usage-limits.ts`

</details>

prs.title: feat(tui): add linux_clipboard_selection config for primary buffer support
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #43176
Fixes #6110
Supersedes #6370 (extends it with primary/both modes, primary-read support, and the wl-copy MIME fix)

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Reimplemented against the `v2` branch (per @simonklee's request): the v2 TUI runs on OpenTUI, whose core clipboard already supports the primary selection natively, so this PR adds a config knob on top of that support instead of hand-rolled clipboard plumbing. The v1-only `wl-copy --type text/plain` MIME workaround and manual OSC52 guards are dropped.

Adds a `linux_clipboard_selection` config option (`tui.json`):
- `clipboard`: Standard clipboard only (Ctrl+V)
- `primary`: Targets the middle-click buffer; TUI paste reads from it too
- `both`: Updates both buffers simultaneously (default)

With the default `both`, copies on Linux now **also write the primary selection** — this extends existing copy behavior rather than replacing it. On other platforms the primary write simply reports `unsupported` and is ignored.

Also documents the option in the TUI docs and adds it to the settings dialog.

### How did you verify your code works?

Built a local binary from this branch, set the option to Clipboard / Primary / Both, and verified middle-click paste picks up copies from each configured mode. `bun typecheck` and the TUI test suite pass, including new selection-routing and config tests.

prs.title: feat(opencode): restore doom loop detection as internal plugin for v2
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59339

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

This is offered for design review; I can adapt the implementation to whichever direction the team prefers.

v2 currently has no doom-loop detection: the `doom_loop` action is still accepted by the v1 config schema and rendered by the TUI, but no code produces it. The v1 detector also missed rotations, because it required three consecutive identical calls inside one assistant message.

This PR restores detection as a zero-dependency detector module plus a thin internal plugin, with no runner changes:

1. **Same-message guard** — v1's one working dimension, carried over unchanged: the same call emitted 3 times inside one assistant message asks once.
2. **Signal A** — per-signature identical-output streak (warn 3, block 6). Counting is per signature, so rotations and interleaved calls never reset it. This is the part that catches the shape v1 missed.
3. **Signal B** — line-level information novelty (warn 3/5, surgical ask at 8 only when that signature's A streak is ≥3, circuit breaker at 12). Single-line outputs are exempt.
4. **Signal C** — per-tool failure-equivalence streak (warn 4, block 6). Volatile error tokens are normalized; successes of other tools do not reset it.

Every challenge goes through the existing `doom_loop` permission ask, so intentional polling keeps an escape hatch. A user message resets only B and the breaker; A/C counters deliberately survive, so an interruption does not hand the loop a fresh counter. Memory is bounded with LRU caps and a 10k line store; state is rebuilt from durable history after a restart.

Relation to #53032: different shape — a pure module plus a thin plugin rather than runner changes. Its consecutive-only predicate does not catch rotations: running it over the 199-call incident sequence gives zero firings.

Scope: tool-call loops only. Text/reasoning loops (#15271, #46030, #46492) and harness/compaction loops (#15533, #52697) are out of scope and linked as related in the issue. AST normalization of bash inputs is deliberately deferred to keep the core zero-dependency; it can return as an optional layer if maintainers want parse capability exposed to plugins.

### How did you verify your code works?

- 66 targeted tests pass; `packages/core` typecheck is clean.
- Replayed the shipped detector against my real 199-call incident and four quantified community incidents (#47759, #45442, #50073, #50678): every incident is intercepted, and two legitimate-work negative cases behave per their adjudicated semantics. #49042 (pure-text runaway) is marked out of scope rather than claimed.
- Ran #53032's exact predicate on the same incident: zero firings.
- Cost on the incident corpus: about 0.1 ms per call, no I/O, no runtime dependencies, bounded memory.
- Interactive report with the incident timeline and call-by-call replays: https://metal-huang.github.io/opencode/doom-loop-report/

### Visual

```svg

    <!-- 通用工具调用签名 A/B/C 轮换出现，表示周期循环 -->
    <g font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="8.5">
      <text x="12" y="22" opacity="0.9">tool A(args)
        <animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.25;1;0.25" dur="2.4s" begin="0s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
      </text>
      <text x="12" y="38" opacity="0.9">tool B(args)

      </text>
      <text x="12" y="54" opacity="0.9">tool C(args)

      </text>
    </g>
```

prs.title: feat(server): add experimental job list endpoint
prs.body:
### Problem

`Job.Service` tracks active and unconsumed background `shell`, `subagent`, and `image` jobs in memory and in the `job` SQLite table until each completion notice is admitted to its owning session. Nothing exposed that registry over HTTP, so CLI and SDK callers could only observe foreground session execution (`/api/session/active`) or query location-scoped shells (`/api/shell` by directory), missing image jobs, session-scoped shell lookups, and the window between background completion and inbox wake.

### Change

I added `GET /api/experimental/job` (`client.experimental.job.list`) to expose raw unconsumed background job state without changing foreground session `idle` semantics, matching the `schedule` experimental pattern (`packages/schema/src/job.ts` subpath only, omitted from the `@opencode/schema` root barrel and `@opencode/sdk` contracts).

```diff
 packages/
 ├── schema/src/job.ts               # Job.Kind, Job.Status, Job.Time, Job.Info tagged union (subpath only)
 ├── core/src/
 │   ├── job.ts                      # exposes backgroundJobs on Job.Service
 │   ├── job/list.ts                 # merges SQLite job rows with live state.jobs
 │   └── session/background.ts       # SessionBackground.list (sessionID, kind, status, descendants)
 ├── protocol/src/groups/job.ts      # GET /api/experimental/job (experimental.job.list)
 └── server/src/handlers/job.ts      # validates sessionID and filters background jobs
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Caller["Client / CLI"] -->|"GET /api/experimental/job?sessionID=...&descendants=true"| Handler["JobHandler.list"]
  Handler --> Session["Session.get (404 if missing)"]
  Handler --> Bg["SessionBackground.list"]
  Bg --> Jobs["Job.backgroundJobs (SQLite job + live state.jobs)"]
  Bg --> Walk["Upward parentID walk (when descendants=true)"]
```

Query parameters on `GET /api/experimental/job`:

| Parameter | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `sessionID` | Filters to jobs owned by that session (`404 SessionNotFoundError` when unknown). Omit to list all unconsumed background jobs on the server. |
| `kind` | Filters to `shell`, `subagent`, or `image`. |
| `status` | Filters to `running`, `completed`, `error`, or `cancelled`. |
| `descendants` | When `true` with `sessionID`, walks `parentID` upward from active jobs so background tasks spawned inside child or grandchild subagents are included too. |

### Out of scope

prs.title: fix(cli): wait for background jobs in opencode run
prs.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60698.

### Problem

`opencode run` exited as soon as the session's first foreground step emitted `session.execution.succeeded` and `experimental.session.wait` resolved, even when background `shell`, `subagent`, or `image` jobs launched during that run were still working and would later wake the session with their results.

### Change

I updated `runNonInteractivePrompt` (`packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts`) to check `client.experimental.job.list({ sessionID, descendants: true })` before concluding a run is finished, keeping the live SSE stream open across idle boundaries with zero polling.

```diff
 on session.execution.succeeded:
-  return
+  if experimental.job.list({ sessionID, descendants: true }) is non-empty
+     or inbox / owned active sessions still have work:
+    stay on the SSE stream for the synthetic wake turn
+  return
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Run as opencode run
    participant Server as OpenCode Server
    participant Job as Background Job

    Run->>Server: event.subscribe + session.prompt
    Server-->>Run: step 1 events + session.execution.succeeded
    Run->>Server: GET /api/experimental/job?sessionID=...&descendants=true
    Server-->>Run: [running job] (stay on SSE stream)
    Job->>Server: sessions.synthetic (wakes session) -> completeBackground
    Server-->>Run: step 2 events + session.execution.succeeded
    Run->>Server: GET /api/experimental/job?sessionID=...&descendants=true
    Server-->>Run: [] (+ inbox/active empty) -> exit 0
```

Details:
- **Zero-gap handoff**: background notifiers admit `sessions.synthetic` (waking `SessionExecution`) strictly before `completeBackground` clears the job row, so checking `job.list` followed by `session.active` and `session.inbox.list` has no race window and needs no polling loop.
- **Descendant background tasks**: `descendants: true` keeps `opencode run` open when a spawned subagent still owns a running background shell or image job; once `waitingForBackground` is active, owned descendant terminal events re-run the quiescence check.
- **Ctrl-C while waiting**: `SIGINT` interrupts running background child sessions and aborts the SSE stream when the parent session is already idle, exiting cleanly with code `130`.

### Out of scope

- V1 compatibility mode (`compatibility === "v1"`), which continues to avoid V2 `/api/experimental/*` endpoints.
- Automatically terminating detached long-lived dev servers started by a prompt unless interrupted by the user.

### Verification

- `bun test test/run/noninteractive.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` in `packages/cli`: 150 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test test/import-boundaries.test.ts` in `packages/cli`: 5 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck && bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/cli`: 0 errors
- `bun run check` from root: 35/35 tasks pass

prs.title: fix(core): project error finish as a terminal assistant failure (#52378)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52378

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A subagent whose provider stream ends successfully with an explicit `error` finish reason (for example Gemini's `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`) was reported to the parent as a successful completion. The parent received `state="completed"` with "Subagent completed without a text response.", which an orchestrating session reads as a clean empty answer rather than a provider failure.

The V2 owner of this decision is `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts`. It already synthesized an assistant failure for a successful stream ending with `unknown`, but `error` never entered that branch. This change makes both finish reasons synthesize `InvalidProviderOutputError`, with the message matching the recorded reason.

Two details worth calling out:

- `unknown` keeps `classification: "incomplete-stream"` so it stays retryable and continuable exactly as before. An explicit `error` finish gets no classification, so `isRetryable` returns false and the step stays terminal instead of being retried. That split is what keeps the two paths behaving differently.
- `length` is deliberately excluded. It is a valid truncation outcome that may carry usable partial output, so it stays outside this error-only fix and remains tracked separately in #52378.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/tool-subagent.test.ts` exercises the real V2 child runner, job outcome and parent notification for both delivery modes with a synthetic error-finish event: foreground surfaces a tool execution failure, background satisfies the parent job as an error and writes `state="error"` into the notification. The empty `stop` path is kept as a control and still reports `state="completed"`. 14/14 pass.
- `bun run lint` is clean.
- Repo-wide `bun typecheck` does not complete in my environment (tsgo exceeds 300s and gets SIGTERM), so typecheck relies on CI.

prs.title: fix(acp): forward session title updates to clients via session_info_update
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56894

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`opencode acp` never told clients about generated session titles. Core generates a title after the first user message (`SessionTitle.generate`, durable event `session.renamed`), and `session/list` returns stored titles, but nothing pushed title changes mid-session. ACP clients that display dynamic session names from `session_info_update` (e.g. the ACP Pro extension) were stuck with a fallback label like `opencode - Session xxxx` until they re-listed sessions.

Changes:

- `packages/cli/src/acp/sessions.ts`: the existing global event subscription now also handles `session.renamed` and forwards it for attached sessions as `{sessionUpdate: "session_info_update", title}`. This is global rather than per-turn because title generation runs in a detached fiber that can settle after the triggering turn has ended; it also covers renames from other sources (e.g. `session/fork`). Renames for sessions the adapter does not have attached are ignored.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/service.ts`: loading, resuming, or forking a session that already carries a non-fallback title now announces it once via `session_info_update`. A titled session never triggers title generation again, so without this the client would never learn the stored title. Fallback titles (`New session - <timestamp>`) are left alone so clients can replace them on the first rename.

### How did you verify your code works?

New wire tests in `packages/cli/test/acp/session.test.ts`:

- a rename of an attached session produces a `session_info_update` with the title
- a title arriving mid-turn (through `session/prompt`) is forwarded
- renames for unattached sessions are dropped
- load/resume/fork of a titled session announces the stored title, while a fallback-titled session announces nothing

Adjusted `replay.test.ts` and the command-ordering expectations to account for the new notification. `bun test test/acp/` (104 tests), `tsc -b`, and the repo's `lint` + `typecheck` all pass.

### Screenshots / recordings

The design carries forward #60446 with a separate surface:

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in `prompt.history_scope` setting to the CLI config. `global` is the default and keeps today's behavior: Up and Down recall prompts from every session. `session` filters recall to the current session and gives each session its own cursor.

prs.title: fix(core): price Copilot long-context tiers and cache writes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52089

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

GitHub Copilot costs were undercounted badly on long sessions. In my case (#59671): a 25h session on Copilot / Claude Haiku 5.5, 348 requests, ~344K average context, OpenCode showed $1.56 when the real bill is roughly $9.34 (between $2.03 and $10.15, since Copilot picks the price tier per request by prompt size).

Two causes, both in the Copilot provider code:

1. Copilot's `/models` payload ships two price tiers (`default` and `long_context`, the latter starting above `default.max_prompt_tokens`). The builder only read the default tier.
2. The builder hardcoded cache writes to $0 (`cache_write_price` is in the payload, unread), and both usage adapters dropped `cache_write_tokens`, so cache writes weren't counted at all.

Pricing that session's totals at the ≤100K rates with free writes gives $1.5557 — cent-exact with the displayed $1.56, which is how I know exactly which rates the old code applied.

The builder now emits the write price and a context-tier cost entry, which `SessionUsage.calculateCost` already applies per request, so no calculator change was needed. The adapters map `cache_write_tokens` into `cacheWrite`. While there I replaced their hand-rolled `noCache` arithmetic with `ProviderShared.subtractTokens`/`sumTokens` like the shared protocols use: both streaming adapters left `noCache` undefined on responses without cache details, which downstream prices the entire prompt at $0, and neither clamped against broken breakdowns.

Deliberately not addressed: Copilot's own reported billed amount (#35765) and the richer `pricing` shape from #59460.

### How did you verify your code works?

New unit tests: the builder prices cache writes and emits the long-context tier entry (boundary taken from `default.max_prompt_tokens`), and keeps a model whose `long_context` object is malformed instead of dropping it from the catalog. Both streaming adapters map cache-write tokens into `cacheWrite` and keep the breakdown consistent (`nonCached + cacheRead + cacheWrite = total`). `bun run check` passes, and the `packages/core` suite has the same 4 failures as a clean `dev` checkout (all environment-related).

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Copilot session cost: displayed $1.56, actual about $9.34">
  <style>
    .bar { animation: grow 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }
    .tag { animation: fade 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }
    @keyframes grow { 0%, 15% { width: 26px } 55%, 100% { width: 142px } }
    @keyframes fade { 0%, 30% { opacity: 0 } 65%, 100% { opacity: .9 } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .bar, .tag { animation: none } }
  </style>
  <g fill="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,monospace" font-size="11">
    <text class="tag" x="12" y="11" font-size="9" opacity="0">6x undercount: tier + cache writes</text>
    <text x="12" y="27" opacity=".5">billed</text>
    <rect x="62" y="18" width="26" height="9" rx="2" opacity=".5"/>
    <text x="94" y="27" opacity=".5">$1.56</text>
    <text x="12" y="53">actual</text>
    <rect class="bar" x="62" y="44" width="142" height="9" rx="2" opacity=".9"/>
    <text x="206" y="53">$9.34</text>
  </g>
</svg>
```

prs.title: fix(core): preserve valid env substitutions during fallback
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57554

Related: #57497 and #55915. The original v1 example is already handled in v2; this fixes remaining interference between v2 fallback and supported raw/pre-escaped values.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When one Windows value needed escaping, `ConfigVariable.substitute` retried by escaping every environment value. That made raw JSON fragments outside strings invalid and changed the meaning of already escaped strings, potentially preventing an otherwise valid configuration document from loading.

Keep raw-first substitution. On fallback, scan each placeholder's original JSONC context: leave raw fragments outside strings alone and preserve already valid string contents; escape invalid string contents. Comment escaping keeps its previous behavior.

<details>
<summary>Cause, consequences and compatibility boundaries</summary>

The previous fallback used one escaping mode for the entire document. For example, `WINDOWS = C:\Users\Example` triggers fallback on `\U`; a neighboring raw `FRAGMENT = {"k":"v"}` is then escaped even though it is outside quotes, and a pre-escaped `QUOTED = a\"b` gains an unwanted literal backslash. Whether one value was valid depended on unrelated fields.

The scanner reads the original text, so replacement lengths do not invalidate offsets. The callback identifies string/comment context and checks individual string contents with the existing JSONC parser. It preserves the raw-fragment/pre-escaped compatibility introduced by #55915 and leaves the successful raw path unchanged. An integration regression also combines a raw JSON shell value with a Windows value through actual `Config.Service` loading.

**Observable compatibility tradeoff:** in a mixed configuration, a value such as `C:\temp\new` contains valid JSON escapes. Previously, if another value forced fallback, the document-wide retry escaped that value into a literal path. With this patch, it retains raw interpretation: `\t` and `\n` decode to tab/newline even during fallback. Configurations containing two Windows paths can therefore change meaning. This is now explicit for maintainer decision; the raw-only path remains unchanged. The general literal-versus-pre-escaped ambiguity is not solved, and no path heuristic or new syntax is added.

</details>

### How did you verify your code works?

```sh
# Run from packages/core
bun run script/test.ts test/config/config.test.ts --test-name-pattern=env --rerun-each=10 --max-concurrency=2
```

- Real helper/filesystem layer and actual `Config.Service` integration; synthetic values, isolated sandbox, no external service calls.
- Both affected regression cases fail on the original implementation. Corrected focused run: 30 pass / 0 fail, 80 assertions across ten repetitions.
- Full config file: original plus regressions 36 pass / 13 fail / 1 skip; corrected 38 pass / 11 fail / 1 skip. Compared failure-name sets: the same 11 ancestor-discovery failures exist in both; only the two regressions differ. The sandbox's ancestor configuration causes those existing failures.
- `git diff --check` passed.

These results were obtained with the patch on `552f867`. The patch was reapplied to `f2a34141`; the only intervening commit changes infrastructure, and neither affected source/test file changed. Tests were not rerun after that rebase.

Local runtime was Bun 1.3.11; CI should verify the pinned Bun 1.4.2. `bun run check` stopped because the minimal sandbox lacked `oxlint`; a full development install was avoided with less than 1 GB host RAM free. Full monorepo lint/typecheck is not claimed.

GitHub template/compliance checks passed. The `test`, `check` and `nix-eval` workflows currently report `action_required` before creating jobs; upstream authorization is still needed for those runs.

<details>
<summary>Review follow-up: TS2748, additional validation and evidence boundaries</summary>

The issue is labeled `reproduced`. The [issue-triage bot](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57554#issuecomment-6303673854) reproduced the project document being dropped in the CLI. Separately, the [PR review on e269c97](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57556#pullrequestreview-5592878016) reported 49/0 config tests and verified helper behavior, but found a blocking core typecheck error; its source CLI could not start because of an unrelated `react/jsx-dev-runtime` problem. These are bot-reported observations, not our end-to-end CLI test or CI results. The review is `COMMENTED`, not formal approval.

[Commit 6c07ef0](https://github.com/JoaoMarcos44/opencode/commit/6c07ef0336ce0075ddf56eca2c65d5617c4ddfae) addresses [TS2748](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57556#discussion_r4331253092). `jsonc-parser` declares `SyntaxKind` as an ambient const enum, which cannot be accessed as a runtime value with `verbatimModuleSyntax`. The scanner still determines the token and its offset; the correction reads that original token's first character (`/` for comments, `"` for strings), following the existing CLI technique. No `any`, compiler suppression, numeric token constants or dependency changes are introduced.

Targeted follow-up in an isolated sandbox, with the real `variable.ts` and filesystem helper closure:

- Minimal `bun run typecheck`: the previous source produced four TS2748 errors; the corrected source exits 0 with `verbatimModuleSyntax` and `isolatedModules`.

The [compatibility review comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57556#discussion_r4331253101) is reflected explicitly in the cause/compatibility section and in the infographic.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Permanent edge-case coverage after review</summary>

`packages/core/test/config/variable.test.ts` adds ten permanent scenarios for `ConfigVariable.substitute`, using the real filesystem layer and existing Effect test helpers:

- Raw arrays with nested JSON and scalar elements; one variable used inside and outside strings.
- Multiple placeholders in one string, escaped quote boundaries and comment markers inside strings.

The infographic now uses a Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock style. Its compatibility warning and verification limits are retained.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve undo on conflicting compaction
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57553

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A rejected manual compaction could confirm staged undo first, truncate visible history and clear redo. With messages A/B/C and undo at B, reusing A returned a conflict after deleting B/C; reusing B could incorrectly succeed because B had just been removed.

Move the undo commit into compaction admission after ID validation, under the existing session mutex. Keep it before the pending-compaction lookup and enqueue. An exact retry preserves staged undo and does not wake execution while that undo remains staged.

<details>
<summary>Cause, consequences and why the ordering matters</summary>

`Session.compact` previously published `RevertEvent.Committed` before `SessionInbox.admitCompaction` checked whether the ID already belonged to delivered or pending work. The committed event's projector removes `session_message` and `session_inbox` rows at/after the undo boundary and clears `revert`. A later conflict therefore could not preserve the original state.

The new optional `beforeAdmit` effect executes only after the existing ID checks succeed. It runs inside the existing admission mutex, before looking for a pending compaction: committing undo can remove an older pending entry, so returning an entry selected before commit would be incorrect. Exact retries return their existing admission without committing undo. The caller then reloads the session before scheduling a wake, preventing the runner from processing that pending compaction while redo remains staged.

This preserves the successful commit-before-enqueue behavior from #46383. It does not introduce a new database transaction, change public Protocol/HTTP schemas, or claim that event logs or user files were deleted.

</details>

### How did you verify your code works?

Real Session/Bus/SQLite regression tests, using the existing model/execution fixture in an isolated Windows sandbox:

```sh

bun run script/test.ts test/session-compact.test.ts --max-concurrency=2
bun run script/test.ts test/session-compact.test.ts test/session-owned.test.ts test/session-projector.test.ts test/session-runner.test.ts --max-concurrency=2
bun run script/test.ts test/session-revert.test.ts --max-concurrency=2
```

- Original implementation with the new ID regressions: 4 pass / 2 fail.
- Final compaction suite: 7 pass / 0 fail, including conflicts before/at the undo boundary, coalescing, pending-entry replacement and exact retry without an extra wake.
- Affected session suites: 275 pass / 0 fail (includes the 7 focused compaction tests). Snapshot/revert: 1 pass / 0 fail in isolation.
- `git diff --check` passed.

These results were obtained with the patch on `552f867`. The patch was reapplied to `f2a34141`; the only intervening commit changes infrastructure, and none of the affected source/test files changed. Tests were not rerun after that rebase.

Local runtime was Bun 1.3.11; CI should verify the pinned Bun 1.4.2. `bun run check` could not complete in the minimal sandbox because `oxlint` was absent; a full development install was avoided with less than 1 GB host RAM free. A snapshot run timed out under concurrent load; both original and corrected versions passed subsequent isolated runs. Full monorepo lint/typecheck is not claimed.

GitHub template/compliance checks passed. The `test`, `check` and `nix-eval` workflows currently report `action_required` before creating jobs; upstream authorization is still needed for those runs.

<details>
<summary>Issue triage and review evidence (20 Oct 2026)</summary>

The issue is labeled `reproduced`. The [issue-triage replay](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57553#issuecomment-6303660607) and the [opencode-agent review](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57555#pullrequestreview-5592873345) confirmed both ID cases. These are attributed bot-reported results, separate from our earlier local results and from CI. The review state is `COMMENTED`, not a formal approval.

The diagram distinguishes the rejected-ID path from an exact retry, and explains why pending work must be read again after undo is committed. It claims truncation of visible history/redo, not deletion of files or durable event logs.

</details>

`GET /api/info` reports `version` but nothing that identifies the **HTTP API generation**. Since 2.0 the v1 routes are gone entirely, yet a 2.x server still says `"version": "2.x.y"` — so a client that gates on semver connects happily and then fails on every call. ## Notes

`apiVersion` is optional, following the existing "optional at every level so clients still decode servers that predate a capability" convention in this schema. Absent means a pre-2.x server; treat as `1`. Purely additive — no behaviour change.

prs.title: fix(util): redact credentials in structured log output
prs.body:
## Summary

Credentials reach `log/opencode.log` verbatim. Provider errors, request spans, and tool metadata all funnel through one structured-log formatter, and any of them can carry an `Authorization` header or an API key — in practice a live `xpl_…` key was found sitting in the log file in plaintext.

## Change

- New `packages/util/src/observability/redact.ts`: redacts `Authorization: Bearer …` values, bare bearer tokens, and prefixed keys (`xpl_`, `sk-`, `ghp_`, `glpat_`, `xox…`, …), keeping the recognizable prefix so a reader can still tell *which* credential leaked without being able to use it.
- Applied once, inside the structured-log formatter, so every line written to the log file passes through it.
- Test coverage in `redact.test.ts`.

## Notes

- Scope is deliberately the log file only. Shell tool output (`shell/*.out`) also persists raw output and is a separate, more invasive change: redacting it would alter tool semantics, so it is not included here.
- This stops future leaks only. A credential that already leaked still has to be rotated.

## Verification

- `bun test src/observability/redact.test.ts` → 4 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run check` at repo root → 35/35 tasks, 0 errors.

prs.title: feat(cli): add opencode doctor
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `opencode doctor`: a read-only report of the data directory and the failure modes that are hard to see from a normal session.

Motivated by a real incident. A v1 CLI and the v2 desktop app shared one `~/.local/share/opencode`; the database ended up with a stale schema (`table session_inbox has no column named type`), the directory had grown to 1.7 GB, and every question about what was actually wrong had to be answered by hand with `sqlite3` and `grep`. `doctor` answers them in one command.

## What it reports

- global paths (data, config, cache, state, log, bin, repos, tmp)
- data directory total, plus a per-child breakdown so you can see what is large
- database, `-wal`, and `-shm` sizes
- count of orphaned temp-then-rename leftovers (`<file>.<pid>.tmp`)
- how many `opencode` executables are on `PATH`, with a warning when more than one shares the data directory (the failure mode above)

## Design

- Measurement is separated from presentation: `handlers/diagnostics.ts` does the read-only filesystem work and is unit tested; `handlers/doctor.ts` is a thin formatter.
- Standard library only (`node:fs/promises`, `node:path`, `node:os`) — no database handle, no writes, nothing created if a path is missing.

## Verification

- `bun test src/commands/handlers/diagnostics.test.ts` → 5 pass, 0 fail (16 assertions, including real temp-directory walks).
- `bun run check` at repo root → 35/35 tasks, 0 errors.
- Exercised the measurement layer against a real 800 MB data directory:

```
total        800.6 MB
database     {"size":"543.2 MB","wal":"2.5 MB","shm":"1.1 MB"}
orphaned     0
installs     1
children:
  bin             143.2 MB
  log             2.3 MB
  shell           1.4 MB
  snapshot        36.0 MB
  storage         70.5 MB
  tool-output    501.9 KB
```

**Not smoke-tested end to end through the CLI entrypoint.** `bun run dev doctor` cannot start in a fresh clone: `packages/tui/src/config/index.tsx` imports `react/jsx-dev-runtime`, which is not installed, so the entrypoint throws before command dispatch. This is pre-existing and unrelated to this change — the stock `bun run dev debug paths` fails identically on a clean `dev`. Worth confirming on CI where the TUI dependencies are present.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #57988

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

A request for a folder that no longer exists already returns 404, but booting the location saved its Project first, so the missing folder showed up in `GET /api/project` and stayed there after a restart. Existing rows for missing folders also got `time_active` bumped on every such request.

prs.title: fix(core): repair V1 global sessions left by completed imports
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #49827 for people who already upgraded.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

#56322 attributes V1 global sessions to their folder's project during the import, but only for imports that hadn't finished. Anyone who already upgraded still has those sessions under `global`, where the per-folder session lists can't find them.

This adds a one-time repair that runs in the background on server start, after the import:

```text
if the import is completed and the repair hasn't run:
    for each folder of V2 sessions still under global that came from V1:
        look up the folder's V2 project (same lookup as the import: 5s limit, stop after a timeout)
        nothing found, or it's global again -> skip
        one transaction:
            insert the project row if missing (never replace)
            set project_id + path, only where the session is still global; time_updated is kept
    mark the repair done
```

- Only touches `session_v2` rows that are still `global`, have no workspace, and also exist in the V1 `session` table. Sessions created in V2 are left alone.
- Lookups run outside transactions, and each folder is its own short transaction. If it stops partway, finished folders stay fixed and the next start does the rest.
- If the repair hits a database error it logs a warning, leaves the migration status alone, and retries next start.
- Fresh imports mark the repair done in their completion transaction, since they already attribute sessions.
- Undoable: the V1 `session` table still has the original `global` project ids.

Also points the orphan-session test at a missing folder inside its own temp dir instead of `/tmp/orphan`, which could exist on a machine.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test: a completed import with V1 global sessions in a plain folder, a git repo subfolder, a missing folder, plus a V2-native global session. Only the first two move, time_updated is kept, and the repair is marked done. Fails without the change.
- Ran the repair on a copy of a real already-migrated database (kv, project, session, session_v2 only): 346 sessions moved in about 100ms, 9 new projects, no other session column changed, no non-global session changed, 138 stayed global because their folders are gone.
- `bun run check` passes; `v1-migration` and `project` tests pass with `--rerun-each 3`.

prs.title: feat(browser-extension): add OpenCode Browser, an extension agents control over MCP
prs.body:
## What this is

OpenCode Browser is a Chromium extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Chromium, Helium, Arc) that lets AI agents use the user's real browser through the `browse` MCP tools: open and drive tabs with Playwright, take screenshots, capture network traffic, record, and hand off to the user for logins, 2FA, and payments. It has no chat UI; agents control it.

```
agent ── browse MCP (stdio) ── relay (127.0.0.1:19988) ── WebSocket ── extension ── chrome.debugger ── tabs
```

- `packages/browser-extension` – the extension: relay link, agent tab groups (collapsed, at the start of the tab strip), idle agent tabs closing after 10 minutes, a toolbar button that lets agents use the current tab (or stops them), an in-page handoff banner, and a status page (also the options page).
- `packages/browser-extension/cli` – the npm package `opencode-browser-cli` (own lockfile, outside the workspace): the relay, the `browse` MCP server, the `opencode-browser` CLI, and setup. It is Browser Control (anomalyco/browser-control 8c80ac2, MIT) ported in: renamed, on port 19988, accepting only OpenCode Browser's extension IDs.
- `execute` uses `patchright-core` (Playwright's API without enabling CDP's `Runtime` domain, which pages can detect), and agent input is human-like by default (curved mouse paths, paced keys, gliding scroll).
- Releasing is manual for now (`npm publish` in `cli/`, `bun run package` for the store zip); see the package README.

## Install, and why there's no pairing

```sh
npx opencode-browser-cli install
```

This installs the CLI, adds the `browse` MCP server to opencode's global config, and copies the extension. If an unpacked build is already connected and older, it reloads it and checks the reload took effect. It then reports which browsers and profiles have the extension, and opens the Chrome Web Store listing when none does.

There's nothing to pair: the extension connects to the local relay, which only accepts OpenCode Browser's extension IDs (store `mfnicocicmmlkpjnaffgihfjhdgjkdjg`, unpacked `afeafocngkodbmaipcngoamamfmekgfo`).

## How to test

1. `cd packages/browser-extension/cli && bun install && bun run build && node dist/cli.mjs install`
2. Load `packages/browser-extension/dist` unpacked (Developer mode → Load unpacked), or let `install` reload an already loaded copy. Its status page says Connected once an agent uses the tools.
3. From an opencode session (restart it so it picks up the `browse` MCP server):
   - `session_new`
   - `execute` with `await page.goto("https://news.ycombinator.com"); return page.title()`
   - `execute` with `return (await page.screenshot()).length`
   - `session_list`

   A new agent tab group appears at the top of the tab strip.
4. Click the toolbar button on one of your own tabs; the badge shows ON. `status` lists it as `owner=user` with its `tab=` id, for `session_adopt({ tabId })`. Click again to take the tab back.
5. `opencode-browser status` shows the relay, the extension (with its build and origin), and every tab agents can use. `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/logs/relay.log` has the details.

## What was removed, and why

Earlier revisions of this PR also had a side panel:
- a chat client for the opencode server, with a session picker;
- multi-server pairing (a connect page redeeming `opencode pair` codes);
- a per-prompt "browser context" message and a "share tab" strip;
- site scripts, browsing-history and tab-request tools, which needed approval prompts in the panel.

All of that is gone. The extension is now only the piece agents control over MCP, which keeps it small (the built extension is about 90 KB, with no UI framework) and its permissions minimal.

Removed with it:
- the `sidePanel`, `userScripts`, `contextMenus`, `activeTab`, `nativeMessaging`, `downloads` and `webNavigation` permissions, and the optional history/bookmarks/topSites/sessions permissions;
- the keyboard shortcut, the native messaging host and the opencode plugin;
- the `@opencode/ui`, `@opencode/session-ui`, `@opencode/client`, Solid and Tailwind dependencies;
- the tag-triggered publish workflow.

`install` cleans up what earlier versions set up.

## Fixed: relay crash on oversized messages

Reported with Browser Control (CLI 0.8.3, extension 0.0.25): the relay crashed with `unhandled RangeError: Max payload size exceeded (WS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE_LENGTH)` and kept crashing until the extension was reloaded.

Cause: `ws` reports an oversized frame as an `error` event on the socket. The relay had no listener for it, so Node killed the process.

Fix:
- The relay accepts messages up to 256 MiB, as Playwright does.
- It logs socket and HTTP server errors instead of crashing.
- The extension fails a single command whose result is too large, instead of sending it.

Checked on an isolated relay: a 240 MB CDP result passes, and a 260 MB client message gets a 1009 close while the relay stays up.

Also fixed while stripping it down: tab-capture recordings stopped after the first chunk, because the worker never answered the recording page's chunk messages.

## Verification

- Typecheck (extension and CLI), lint and build pass.
- Clean headless Chrome: the extension loads, the status page connects, the worker logs no errors, and the payload tests above pass.

prs.title: fix(core): keep tool calls unsettled when their terminal write fails
prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #52796 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `toolExecution` and `failTool` in `publish-llm-event.ts` mark a call settled before they publish its terminal event. If the publish fails (SQLITE_FULL in my case), the call stays settled in memory but `running` in storage, so `failUnsettledTools` skips it. The downstream missing-tool-result rejection is handled in v2.0.22 by #52421 and #52426: request normalization adds missing results and moves system updates after pending results. That protects the provider request but doesn't update the stored tool state. This PR addresses the remaining failed-write settlement problem in #52796. The fix keeps the mark synchronous, before the first yield, as the publisher's concurrency note requires. It clears the mark again if the publish fails, so the step's cleanup can still record a `Tool.Failed`. `toolExecution` now also checks for empty content before marking, because that defect left the call stranded the same way. If the retry write also fails, the step dies and the session errors. This does not fix disk exhaustion or recover the lost successful tool output. The publish and the rollback run uninterruptibly, so an interrupt after the write commits can't clear the flag and allow a second terminal event. Known limitation: when a `Tool.Success` write fails, the cleanup records the raw storage error as the tool's error, so the model sees a failure for a tool that actually ran. A dedicated "result could not be saved" message would need a typed error from `toolExecution`. I left that out to keep this PR small. The other places that set `settled` before publishing (`tool-input-error` and the hosted results) run inside the uninterruptible provider-event handler. A failed write there fails the whole step, and `settleStaleToolCalls` settles the call on the next drain. So they don't strand a call within a step, and I left them as they are. ### How did you verify your code works? Added two tests in `session-runner.test.ts`, one per path. At submission, both failed on the base branch and passed with the fix: - `Tool.Success` projection dies for a local call - tool returns `Tool.Error` and the first `Tool.Failed` projection dies Both assert that the persisted tool state becomes `error`; the second also checks that the failed terminal write is attempted twice. Their unmatched-call assertions inspect `TestLLM` requests before production request normalization, so they are not evidence of an Anthropic 400 on v2.0.22. Added two tests in `session-runner-tool-events.test.ts`: an interrupt that arrives after a `Tool.Success` or `Tool.Failed` write has committed must not let `failUnsettledTools` publish a second terminal event. Both fail without the uninterruptible wrapper. Submission validation: `bun run test` in `packages/core`: 5602 pass, 0 fail. `bun typecheck` and the pre-push `bun run check` passed. The October 6 follow-up was source inspection of v2.0.21/v2.0.22, the current upstream publisher, and the test client; tests were not rerun for this description update. ### Screenshots / recordings Not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): run Claude Code tool hooks
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #12472

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Runs the `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `SessionStart` command hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json` and `settings.local.json`, next to the existing `.claude` skills compatibility.

It is an internal plugin on the existing `tool` `execute.before` / `execute.after` hooks. Each matching hook gets the Claude Code payload on stdin (`session_id`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, plus `tool_response` after the call). Tool names are mapped to Claude Code's (`shell` -> `Bash`, `edit` -> `Edit`, ...) and `tool_input` gets `file_path` / `old_string` / `new_string` added beside the native keys, so existing matchers and scripts keep working.

- `PreToolUse` exit 2 fails the call with stderr as the tool error.
- `PreToolUse` exit 0 with JSON `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`: `deny` fails the call with `permissionDecisionReason`, `ask` shows the normal permission prompt for the call even when rules would allow it (a rule that denies still wins). The older top-level `decision: "block"` form counts as deny. `allow` is ignored on purpose, so a hook can tighten permissions but not loosen them.
- `PostToolUse` exit 2 appends stderr to the tool result. Exit 0 with JSON `decision: "block"` + `reason`, or `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, appends that text the same way.
- When several hooks match, a deny from any of them wins over an ask.
- The ask reason is the permission request `message`. The TUI permission prompt now shows a request's `message` under its title (before, only the attention notification did), with a render test in `test/cli/tui/input-scope.test.tsx`.
- `SessionStart` runs when a session is created (not for subagent sessions), with `source: "startup"` for the matcher. Its output, either `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` or plain stdout, is saved to the session as a synthetic message. A first request that starts before the hooks finish waits for them and gets the context directly.
- Any other exit code, a timeout, or a hook that fails to start is logged and does not block the tool.

What this leaves out, on purpose:

- `Stop`. There is no hook on v2 that can keep the loop going, which is #16626.
- Hooks from a project's `.claude` directory. They would run commands from a repo the user has not reviewed, and I did not want to add a trust prompt in this PR. Only the home directory settings are read.
- `SessionStart` with `source` `resume`, `clear` or `compact`. Only new sessions run it.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Tests in `test/config/claude-hooks.test.ts` run real hook commands from a temp `.claude` directory: exit 2 blocks with stderr, the stdin payload matches, exit 0/1 and non-matching matchers let the call through, `settings.local.json` is read, project `.claude` hooks are ignored, PostToolUse feedback is appended, a JSON deny blocks with its reason, and a JSON ask goes through `Permission.assert` (the evaluate hook turns allow into ask, keeps deny, and leaves other requests alone; a reject with feedback fails the call with that feedback), and SessionStart output is saved to a new top-level session, skipped for subagents, and spliced into a first request that started before it was saved.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` is clean, and the repo pre-push `bun run check` passes.
- The tests drive the plugin through a stub plugin host and a stub `Permission` service, the same way the other internal plugin tests do. I have not run it in a live session.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### What does this PR do?

Adds a `statusline` option to the TUI config. It takes a shell command; the TUI pipes session state to it as JSON on stdin and shows the first line of stdout in the prompt footer.
