prs.title: fix(gui-extensions): wait for painted frame before screenshot capture
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #52407

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`case "screenshot"` calls `Page.getLayoutMetrics` and immediately follows it with `Page.captureScreenshot`. After a client-side navigation the layout is already updated, but the compositor can still hold the previous frame, so the capture returns a stale image.

`createBrowserPage` already has a `painted()` helper (double `requestAnimationFrame` raced against a 150 ms timeout) at the bottom of this file — it is only used by the element-comment highlight path. This PR calls it before sizing the clip, so the capture waits for the next painted frame. Typical cost is one to two frames; the existing race caps the worst case at 150 ms, and this runs only after the visible-tab check above.

Honest caveat: I could not reproduce a stale frame in this environment across ~63 scenarios (isolated Electron harness, the shipped v2.0.20 app, and this branch). So this is defensive hardening that closes a timing window, not a fix for a demonstrated failure. The original report's symptom was in part page-side — see the triage comment in #52407 for details.

### Issue for this PR

Refs #36677

This PR covers the active-borrower reload lifecycle leak discussed in that issue. It does not establish that the original idle CPU loop or accumulated MCP processes are resolved.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Fix the active-borrower reload leak described by Just-Silver and underdark456. After reload replaces an RcMap entry under the same key, the old entry sees the replacement and treats itself as cached. With an infinite idle TTL, its layer scope never closes.

Patch Effect 4.0.0-rc.112 to compare entry identity when releasing: close the detached graph after its last borrower, without removing the replacement. prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Partial fix for #43818, covering the OpenAI chat protocol (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Manifest in OpenAI mode).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Gateways that bill per request (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Manifest) already return the actual USD amount as `usage.cost` in the response usage block. Opencode captured the field but dropped it, so every step was priced from token counts times the models.dev catalog rate.

That is wrong for router models (Opencode shows `$0.00` because the catalog has no price for a varying upstream; it should show the reported cost) and for OpenRouter (Opencode bills the cheapest listed endpoint; it should bill the endpoint that served the request).

This fixes the OpenAI chat protocol path. It carries `usage.cost` through the normalized `Usage` contract (`packages/ai/src/schema/events.ts`, `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`) and makes `SessionUsage.record` prefer it when it is finite and non-negative (`packages/core/src/session/usage.ts`), falling back to catalog pricing otherwise. A reported `0` stays authoritative. The step settlement now carries the raw usage (`packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts`, `step.ts`) so the reported cost reaches accounting; title and compaction already passed it.

Future PRs still need to address the Anthropic-messages path (slightly more complicated) and the other protocol mappers (open-responses, gemini, mistral-chat, bedrock-converse).

### What does this PR do?

labels.name: no-action

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I would like pi-tui to preserve line-boundary semantics through rendering and copying, so mouse selection can join soft wraps introduced by viewport width while retaining hard line breaks from the source content.
#506 describes this symptom, and #7721 attempted to track soft wraps with invisible markers. I understand the compatibility and risk concern raised when that PR was closed: custom components would also need to understand and propagate those markers.
I would therefore like to suggest a different direction: optional semantic selection metadata kept separate from display strings. Built-in components such as `Text` and `Markdown` could provide it, while components without it would naturally retain the current copy behavior. This could solve the hard-break/soft-wrap problem without requiring existing custom components to understand hidden markers.

### Why?

I can reproduce this in Kitty, Alacritty, and Ghostty: copying a response wrapped because of viewport width inserts extra newlines into the clipboard. This does not appear to be specific to one terminal.
The distinction still exists inside `wrapTextWithAnsi()`: it first separates source newlines, then creates visual wraps with `wrapSingleLine()`. However, it ultimately returns only `string[]`, so that boundary information is lost. Fullscreen selection copy later reconstructs the result with:
```ts
const text = lines.join("\n");
```
Every visual row therefore becomes a hard line break. `/copy` preserves the original full assistant message, but cannot copy an arbitrary mouse selection. The public extension API also has no access to transcript selection coordinates or the built-in copy reconstruction path.

### How?

One possible design is optional selection information associated with each visual line, for example:
```ts
interface SelectionLineProjection {
  text: string;
  joinerToPrevious?: string;
  selectableColumns?: { start: number; end: number };
}
```
The joiner could preserve a real `"\n"`, omitted whitespace, or `""` for a continuous soft wrap such as a long token or CJK text. Layout, clipping, and scrolling would propagate this sidecar without interpreting it, and fullscreen selection copy would use it to reconstruct selected text. Lines without a projection would fall back to the existing visual-row behavior.

issues.title: Nix build fails on 9c9ce85: TS2322 in github-copilot.ts (empty classifier catalog group)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Building `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47` from a Nix flake fails in `pi-workspace-packages`:

```text
src/providers/github-copilot.ts:33:3 - error TS2322: Type 'unknown[]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ProviderModel<GitHubCopilotApi>[]'.
```

Line 33 is

```ts
models: [...Object.values(GITHUB_COPILOT_MODELS), ...Object.values(GITHUB_COPILOT_CLASSIFIER_MODELS)],
```

The catalog hydrated from the pinned revision does not contain any `classifier` entry for `github-copilot`, so the key set of `ClassifierModelCatalog<TGroups, "github-copilot">` is empty and `Object.values(...)` is `unknown[]`.

This looks like the same class of problem as #10985 (stale Nix catalog pin vs. provider source): `update-model-catalog-pin.mjs --if-stale` compares hydration validity and model *groups*, not whether a provider has zero models of a type that the source code references unconditionally.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47`, `npm ci`.
2. Fetch the pinned catalog `sha256-f4dbabe79cda4b38aee4a761b23fd5eaf526ac2e28fed3c9ee86e37ca0e5d71e` and hydrate:
   `node packages/ai/scripts/hydrate-model-catalog.ts <catalog.json>`
3. `npx tsc -p packages/ai/tsconfig.build.json --noEmit`

TypeScript 7.0.2 (also `tsgo` 7.0.2 from nixpkgs) reports the error above; `npm run check:model-data` passes ("Generated model data is valid."). Only this one error is produced.

Notes from the investigation:

- The hydrated `github-copilot` data has three api groups (`anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`) and **only `chat` entries** — no `classifier` of any type.
- The live catalog (`sha256-c2cce837…`) behaves the same; the only difference against the pinned revision is one extra chat model (`gpt-6.1-terra`).
- Pulling `data-json.d.ts` (`declare module "*.json"`) into the program via a looser `exclude` does not change the error, so the JSON import already resolves to `unknown` regardless of that declaration.
- Reproducible outside Nix on Arch/NixOS with the plain npm toolchain, i.e. it is not a packaging artifact.

### Expected behavior

Either the catalog should carry at least one `github-copilot` classifier entry, or `github-copilot.ts` should not spread `GITHUB_COPILOT_CLASSIFIER_MODELS` unconditionally (the constant it reads is derived from the hydrated JSON, which may legitimately be empty).

### Version

1.5.0, revision `9c9ce8547e5a88cbe834a53e9a6d83a789d08e47`, `nix/model-catalog.json` pin `sha256-f4dbabe79cda4b38aee4a761b23fd5eaf526ac2e28fed3c9ee86e37ca0e5d71e`.

The `nix.yml` run for this commit (2026-11-02T23:57:35Z) is reported green, so the CI environment must resolve the JSON type differently — please check whether the workflow still hydrates the catalog, or runs `tsc` from the JS TypeScript 7.0.2 package rather than `tsgo`.

AI-assisted diagnosis; the reproduction commands above are mine, run on Arch Linux and on NixOS.

issues.body:
### What happened?

I run pi inside WSL2 from Windows Terminal. When the `copy-to-clipboard` function gets invoked (`/copy` or highlight to copy in tui), the text does reach the Windows clipboard, and I can paste it into Windows apps just fine. But it never shows up in Win+V windows clipboard history. This happens in both Windows Terminal and Wezterm. 



### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi inside WSL2 from Windows Terminal (or WezTerm)
2. Trigger copy-to-clipboard on any text (`/copy` or highlight to copy)
3. Open `Win+V` on Windows
4. The copied text is not in clipboard history

### Expected behavior

The copied text should appear in the Windows clipboard history (`Win+V`), in addition to the regular clipboard.

### Proposed solution

In order to populate the Windows clipboard in a way that makes it show up in `Win+V` history is to emit an OSC 52 sequence on copy. 

Pi only emits OSC 52 on remote sessions, not on WSL. I understand that this is deliberate in order to avoid terminals writing the native clipboard concurrently with the addon and very large OSC 52 payloads desynchronizing terminal rendering, but I propose that we can use the `isWSL` check and emit OSC 52 in that case. The existing `MAX_OSC52_ENCODED_LENGTH` guard should still apply so oversized copies don't trip the desync issue it's there to prevent.

I would be happy to submit a PR if the proposed solution is acceptable.

### Version

0.79.10

issues.title: Long-lived session: model confabulated user messages and tool calls absent from the session log

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# Long-lived session: model confabulated user messages and tool calls absent from the session log

## Summary

A single pi session that had been continuously reused for ~31 days (one JSONL
session file, ~146 MB, many compaction cycles) began producing assistant turns
that referenced **user messages and tool actions that never happened**:

1. The agent claimed the user had sent two screenshot messages. Grepping the
   session `.jsonl`: the quoted phrases appear **only inside assistant
   messages** — no matching user records exist anywhere in the file.
2. The agent claimed it had edited a memory/notes file. The file's mtime was
   hours old and it contained none of the claimed additions — those tool calls
   never executed.
3. When the user challenged the false history (three times), the agent doubled
   down, "quoting" the invented messages with confidence.

Everything actually applied to disk had been explicitly approved, so no damage
resulted — but the incident demonstrates that a drifted long session can act
on, and argue for, a history that does not exist.

## Why this is reportable against pi (vs. pure model behavior)

Confabulation is a model failure mode, but pi is the layer that manages
session lifetime and compaction. Today pi happily keeps a months-old,
multi-hundred-MB session running without any signal that turn-level fidelity
is degrading. Notably, pi's own session log was **exactly** the ground truth
that made this detectable — that design choice is great and should be leaned
on further.

## Suggested mitigations

- Warn when a session file exceeds a size/age threshold ("context quality may
  be degraded — consider /new; state lives in your memory files, not here").
- Optionally surface a persistent status-bar indicator when the effective
  context is heavily compacted rather than verbatim.
- Docs: recommend rotating sessions (daily/weekly), as a first-class
  recommendation alongside memory-file usage.

## Environment

- pi 1.5.0 (incident spanned a 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 update mid-session)
- Windows host, single long-lived interactive session
- Self-hosted local model provider (model name withheld)

## Reproduction

None synthetic — this arose organically from ~a month of continuous reuse with
compaction. The session `.jsonl` forensics method (grep quoted phrases vs user
records; check file mtimes vs claimed edits) is a cheap way to test any
suspected session's fidelity.

issues.title: cacheWarming "idle" stops silently once an extension handles turn_end and the context holds a custom or compaction message
issues.body:
**What happened?**
With `cacheWarming: "idle"`, the idle warm never fires in our sessions: 507 `cache_warming_decision` events since September, all at `continuationProbability: 1`, none at 0.15. `/session` shows `Inactive (conversation context changed)` right after the run settles.

Cause: `cacheContextIsCurrent` (`core/sdk.js:214-222`) checks each captured message by object identity. When any extension has a `turn_end` handler, `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` goes on to `_commitBoundaryDrafts`, which calls `_refreshFinalizedContext()` even with no drafts (`core/agent-session.js:492`, `:636`). `sessionEntryToContextMessages` (`core/session-manager.js:179-188`) builds new objects for `custom_message`, `branch_summary` and `compaction` entries on every projection. So `validateRun()` stops the warmer before any decision is emitted. Without a `turn_end` handler, idle warming works.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `note.ts`: `pi.registerCommand("note", { handler: async () => pi.sendMessage({ customType: "n", content: "x", display: true }) })` plus `pi.on("turn_end", () => {})`.
2. `pi -ne -e note.ts` on an Anthropic model, `cacheWarming: "idle"`. Run `/note`, send one prompt, wait for it to settle.
3. `/session` → `Cache Warming … Inactive (conversation context changed)`.
4. Remove the `turn_end` line → `Decision in 4m …`, and the idle decision fires.

**Expected behavior**
The idle phase compares the prefix the provider saw: compare entry ids, or memoise the projected message per entry (entries don't change after append).

**Version**
1.2.0, Linux. Same symptom as https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10700; related to https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10515.

issues.title: Editor segments the entire remaining line just to read the next character

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Moving the prompt cursor right or pressing Delete only needs the next complete display character, such as an emoji or a letter with combining marks. Instead, the editor segments the entire remaining line into an array and then uses only its first item:

```ts
const graphemes = [...this.segment(afterCursor, "grapheme")];
const firstGrapheme = graphemes[0];
```

At the start of a line containing 50,000 `a` characters, a single Right or Delete consumes all 50,000 segments, although only the first is needed. Repeated movement repeats this traversal and array allocation.

The affected reads are in `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`, in `moveCursor()` and `handleForwardDelete()`. Cursor painting has the same pattern, but its input is limited to the current visual line, so its impact is smaller.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load a single line of 50,000 `a` characters through the external editor, or directly through `Editor.setText()`.
2. Move to the line start, then press Right or Delete.
3. Instrument the segment iterator: both first-item reads consume the whole remaining text.

Use expanded text for this check: ordinary large pastes are usually folded into a paste marker and do not reproduce the same long-line case.

Measured directly against the core Editor, without extensions, with full layout unchanged: after warm-up, 41 alternating samples per version gave these median component times:

| 50,000-character line | Current | First-item reads only |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Right + render | 9.26 ms | 7.15 ms |
| Delete + render | 5.40 ms | 3.52 ms |

These are synthetic, component-level measurements, not whole-Pi key-to-screen latency. Short inputs have small absolute gains, and full-document layout work remains. Both versions passed the same 193 existing editor tests; additional Unicode and paste-marker behavior checks matched.

### Expected behavior

Consume only the first segment needed at these call sites, without expanding the entire iterator.

#### Proposed fix

Replace the three first-item reads with direct iterator consumption:

```ts
// Current: consume every segment, then take the first.
const graphemes = [...this.segment(afterCursor, "grapheme")];
const firstGrapheme = graphemes[0];

// Proposed: take only the first item.
const [firstGrapheme] = this.segment(afterCursor, "grapheme");
```

**Change only:**
- The first-item read for rightward movement in `moveCursor()`.
- The first-item read in `handleForwardDelete()`.
- The first-item read used to paint the cursor over the next character.

**Preserve:**
- The existing `this.segment()` path, so emoji, combining-character sequences, and valid paste markers remain atomic.
- Each call site's existing empty-result handling and movement, deletion, and painting behavior.
- Reads that need the complete segment list, along with wrapping and full-document layout.

**Regression checks:**
- Add counting-iterator coverage for the first-item reads, asserting that later segments are not consumed. Use consumption counts rather than timing thresholds as the regression assertion.
- Cover Right and Delete with emoji, combining characters, valid paste markers, and end-of-line behavior.
- Rerun the existing editor tests and the long-line comparison above.

This would not make the entire segmenter lazy. When valid paste markers are present, the underlying segmenter still traverses the text and builds a merged list. This change leaves that logic alone and avoids another array expansion at the call site; the ordinary-text path without valid markers can avoid consuming subsequent segments.

Related: #8029 and #4721 cover adjacent editor/layout performance work. This report is specifically about eagerly consuming the entire suffix for a first-item read; the current #8066 diff does not change these reads.

I'd be happy to submit a minimal fix and regression tests within this scope, pending maintainer approval.

### Version

Source commit `58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8`; Node.js 24.20.0; macOS.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

I'm working on my usereq pi extensions that inject a file's content into the context during requests, and occasionally I receive a 400 error after an OpenRouter request:
_**Error: 400: {"message":"This endpoint's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. However, you requested about 1049560 tokens (442154 of text input, 2749 of tool input, 604657 in the output). Please reduce the length of either one, or use the context-compression plugin to compress your prompt automatically.","code":400,"metadata":{"provider_name":null}}**_

The context sometimes slightly exceeds the maximum acceptable input size.

I haven't analyzed the issue on the pi CLI side myself, but it seems related to some kind of output budget estimation. Here is the output of the analysis:


_In the pi CLI (@earendil-works/pi-ai) the provider-request output budget is sized as contextWindow − contextEstimate − 4096, and the chars/4 context estimator under-counted the real request by 5,080 tokens — 984 tokens past the 4,096-token safety margin — so OpenRouter correctly rejected a request that exceeded its endpoint limit by 984 tokens._

_clampMaxTokensToContext fills the window up to a fixed 4,096-token margin derived from a chars/4 estimate that (a) excludes the full tool-schema payload and (b) under-counts dense markdown. Because the clamp always fills the window, the failure triggers whenever estimator error > 4,096 tokens — and that error scales with session size — which is exactly why the failures are sporadic and correlate with long sessions and large files injections._

Exact arithmetic from the log:

```
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Component                                         │ Tokens                                               │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Endpoint maximum                                  │ 1,048,576                                            │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Text input                                        │ 442,154                                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Tool input (schemas)                              │ 2,749                                                │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Requested output budget (max_tokens)              │ 604,657                                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Total requested                                   │ 1,049,560 → over by 984                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Enabled context files (31,128 + 120,665 + 41,407) │ 193,200 = 18.43% (matches the log's [18.4% context]) │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Accumulated session history (444,903 − 193,200)   │ ≈ 251,700                                            │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```
Does this make any sense to you?

Is there any workaround?

Francesco

_No response_

issues.title: Extension-registered models get no cost default; calculateCost crashes reading 'tiers'

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.99.1 (also present in earlier versions)

## Summary

Models registered by provider extensions keep `cost: undefined` at runtime. After the first streamed response, pi-ai's `calculateCost` reads `model.cost.tiers` and throws:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tiers')
```

## Root cause

- `modelFromJson` (used for `models.json` providers) defaults missing cost:
  `cost: definition.cost ?? { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }`
- `extensionModelFromDefinition` (used for `registerProvider` / `createProvider` with `fetchModels`) just spreads the definition — no cost backfill (`dist/core/provider-composer.js`).
- `calculateCost` then does `for (const tier of model.cost.tiers ?? [])`, which throws when `model.cost` itself is undefined (observed in `dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-7JGR3GZN.js` and `bedrock-converse-stream.js`).

So the invariant "every model has cost" holds for one registration path but not the other.

## Repro

Register a model without `cost` through an extension provider and run one turn; the error surfaces when usage is priced after the response. (Real-world trigger: a gateway extension whose `/v1/models` roster carries no pricing field.)

## Suggested fix

Either side closes the gap; both together are defense in depth:
1. In `extensionModelFromDefinition`, apply the same zero-cost default as `modelFromJson` (parity between registration paths).
2. In `pi-ai`'s `calculateCost`, start from `model.cost ?? { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }` so a cost-less model prices at 0 instead of crashing.

issues.title: TUI Markdown prints HTML comments as visible text
issues.body:
## What happened?

The pi-tui `Markdown` component prints `<!-- ... -->` comments verbatim. I hit it in the new "Extension Updates" notice: my release tooling keeps `<!-- USER-EDITABLE SECTION START -->` / `<!-- USER-EDITABLE SECTION END -->` markers in `CHANGELOG.md`, and both lines show up around every release entry. The markers come from my [semver-calver-release](https://github.com/cad0p/semver-calver-release/blob/b57af46335825afcbf8173a9fa0a32dbee8d1a01/release/action.yml#L279-L281) action; [pi-napkin's CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/cad0p/pi-napkin/blob/13adac98bf6137f5698841bc0442b1f986d793f0/CHANGELOG.md#L5-L13) is a real example. This is pi's own renderer on Markdown the package author wrote, not model output, so it is separate from #6454.

marked lexes comments as `html` tokens, and both the [block `html` case](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts#L717-L722) and the [inline `html` case](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts#L826-L831) push `token.raw` as plain text. Comments are meant to be invisible in rendered Markdown, so every surface using `Markdown` leaks them: the "Extension Updates" notice, "What's New", `/changelog` and assistant messages. An extension can't work around it for the notices: the [Extension Updates call site](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/10cf3264fbbb42d02f7dee45a8b19adcf9085e4e/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L897) passes no transform, so `registerMarkdownTransformer` never sees that text.

## Steps to reproduce

On 1.5.0, from the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` install directory:

```js
import { Markdown } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
const theme = new Proxy({}, { get: () => (s) => s });
const md = new Markdown("## [1.0.0]\n\n<!-- release-notes:start -->\nFixed a bug.\n\nSee <!-- todo: link --> the docs.", 0, 0, theme);
console.log(md.render(60).map((l) => l.trimEnd()).join("\n"));
```

Output:

```
[1.0.0]

<!-- release-notes:start -->
Fixed a bug.

See <!-- todo: link --> the docs.
```

In the app: give an installed extension package a `CHANGELOG.md` entry containing an HTML comment and bump its version; the comment line appears under "Extension Updates".

## Expected behavior

Comments are not shown, without leaving extra blank lines or double spaces where they were. Other inline HTML keeps rendering as text (`with <tag> markers` should still show).

I'm happy to send this with a test if you want it.

## Version

1.5.0 (code unchanged on `main` @ `10cf3264f`)

### What happened?

`sleep()` in packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts (line 182) adds an abort listener to the caller's signal and never removes it when the timer fires.  The SSE retry loop calls it on each retry (lines 446 and 471), so every retry leaves one listener on a signal the caller may reuse.

I'd like to fix it myself with a regression test.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `stream()` from openai-codex-responses with transport "sse", maxRetries: 3, your own AbortController signal, and a stub fetch that returns 429 with `retry-after: 0` three times, then a normal SSE response.
2. After result() resolves, check getEventListeners(signal, "abort").length.

Result on main 642e30b68: 3 listeners left.

### Expected behavior

No listeners left after the request finishes. The listener should be removed when the timer fires, as utils/sleep.ts does.

1.5.0 (main @ 642e30b68)

issues.body:
### What happened?

We use pi-coding-agent as headless SDK.  When the process died with `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`.

We pulled the core dump and found the heap was full of log files. When the grep gets context more than '0' it reads each matched file and splits into an array, just to print the surrounding two lines.

In our case, the agent grepped a directory of server logs, 100 MB to a few GB each, with context 2 and 12 files got loaded before the 4 GB default heap ran out. This has killed our process 10 times in the last 2 months and got auto-restarted before we noticed.

The file is core/tools/grep.ts in 'getFileLines' and 'formatBlock'.

We only use 'pi-mcp-adapter' extension, but its not the reason of this bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run below in bash to make 8 files of about 95 MB:
```
mkdir logs
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do seq 1 6000000 | sed 's/^/log line /' > logs/server$i.log; done
```

2. Below script will call grep tool with context. Save as grep-oom.mjs in the same directory (npm i @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent first):
```
import { createGrepTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
const tool = createGrepTool(process.cwd());
const r = await tool.execute("t", { pattern: "line 5999999", path: "logs", context: 2 });
console.log(r.content[0].text.split("\n").slice(0, 4).join("\n"));
```

3. Run with this:
```
node --max-old-space-size=1024 grep-oom.mjs
```

Result:
Dies in about 13 s with "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit ... JavaScript heap out of memory". One match per file, but every file is read and split whole because of context: 2.

### Expected behavior

grep with context should never be able to run the process out of memory: its memory should follow the size of the output, not the size of the files it searches. ripgrep already handles context, so grep should pass the --context N flag through and format the 'context' events from rg --json. I have a small fix, and I'd like to send it as a PR.

issues.title: Notify extensions after boundary compaction is committed

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Notify extensions when a `compaction` entry returned from `turn_end` or `agent_before_settle` is committed. Prefer extending `session_compact` to cover this supported compaction path rather than adding an API for extensions to emit core lifecycle events themselves.

### Why?

Today, `_commitBoundaryDrafts()` saves the compaction and refreshes the canonical context, but only emits the SDK’s `entry_appended`. Unlike ordinary compaction, it does not notify `pi.on("session_compact", ...)` observers.

An extension can therefore replace the conversation history without other compaction-aware extensions being notified. Consumers include providers retaining remote conversation state, extensions maintaining context-dependent caches or budgets, and compaction telemetry/UI. A concrete failure is a persistent provider connection continuing the old remote transcript after local compaction.

Consumers must instead inspect the active branch in later hooks or arrange extension-specific coordination. `pi.events.emit()` uses a separate bus and cannot reach lifecycle subscribers.

### How? (optional)

After a boundary compaction is committed and the context projection refreshed, await the notification before the next model request. Include the saved compaction entry and identify the boundary origin without misreporting it as manual, threshold, or overflow compaction. Notify once per committed compaction, never for rejected drafts. Keep existing compaction notifications unchanged.

Source-inspected on main at [`642e30b`, `_commitBoundaryDrafts()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/642e30b68930a644050794011555a04ed9027eb4/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1040-L1044).

issues.title: [fullscreen] Large transcripts re-render every frame; every resize re-emits the whole transcript (1 core saturated)

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
> 🤖 Drafted by the reporter's local pi agent from measurements we collected together; the reporter verified the repro with `pi -ne` (no extensions). Disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## What happened?

On Windows 11 / Windows Terminal / **2 logical cores**, working in a session with a large transcript
(current session file ~1.6–2.4 MB) makes the TUI stutter badly on window resize and when scrolling.

Measured inside the pi process (wrapping `process.stdout.write` + sampling `process.cpuUsage()` deltas over 5 s windows):

| Scenario | pi process CPU | stdout written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regular`, each resize 120×30 ↔ 209×51 | **5.2–5.8 s CPU per 5 s window** | **3.9–5.2 MB per resize** |
| `regular`, scrolling | 3–5 % of one core | ~10–120 KB / 5 s |
| `fullscreen`, scrolling a large transcript | **66–101 % of one core** | ~30–360 KB / 5 s |

On a 2-core machine, 66–101 % of one core is 25–50 % of the whole machine spent on the render path, which is what
shows up as stutter. Switching `tuiMode` from `fullscreen` to `regular` removes most of it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Terminal, `tuiMode: "regular"` (default), resume a session with a large transcript
   (a few thousand entries / ~1.5–2.5 MB `.jsonl`).
2. Maximise → restore → maximise the window a few times (each resize with a large transcript).
3. Observe the stutter; confirm by measuring bytes passed to `process.stdout.write` and `process.cpuUsage()` deltas.
   With `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, scrolling the same session saturates one core continuously.

## Expected behavior

Render and emit work should scale with the **visible viewport**, not with the total transcript size — both for
per-frame rendering and for resize.

## Version

pi 0.85.1, node 22.23.2, Windows 11 26100, Windows Terminal, 2 logical cores.
Only difference between the rows above is `tuiMode`.

## Additional context

- `createChatViewport()` places the transcript document inside `new ScrollView(document, { follow: "end", ... })`,
  and on resize the whole transcript appears to be re-emitted at the new width (3.9–5.2 MB per resize).
- The numbers were collected with one locally loaded panel extension that wraps `process.stdout.write` and samples
  `process.cpuUsage()`; that extension's own components render in **0.1–0.2 ms/frame** (instrumented), and the CPU burn
  also appears in windows where it renders nothing.
- Re-validated with **`pi -ne`** (no extensions): resizing with a large transcript still stutters → not extension-caused.

issues.title: Extension changelog repeats on every launch when the package version is a prerelease
issues.body:
## What happened?

The new "Extension Updates" notice shows the same entries again on every fresh launch when the installed package version has a prerelease suffix and a patch number above 0.

[`getNewEntries()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/642e30b68930a644050794011555a04ed9027eb4/packages/coding-agent/src/utils/changelog.ts#L182-L193) splits the saved version on `.`, so `0.1.5-20261020.7` becomes `["0", "1", "5-20261020", "7"]`. `Number("5-20261020")` is `NaN`, the `|| 0` turns it into 0, and the saved version is read as `0.1.0`. [`getExtensionChangelogUpdates()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/642e30b68930a644050794011555a04ed9027eb4/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts#L1384-L1429) then finds `[0.1.1]` to `[0.1.5]` newer, shows them and saves `pkg.version` again, which reads back as `0.1.0` on the next launch.

This matters for packages published on a prerelease dist-tag. Mine publish `X.Y.Z-YYYYMMDD.N` builds to `@next`, so anyone on `@next` of a package at `0.1.5` would get the same notes on every new session.

## Steps to reproduce

On 1.5.0, from a directory where the package is installed:

```js
import { getNewEntries } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/changelog.js";
const entries = [{ major: 0, minor: 1, patch: 5, content: "0.1.5" }, { major: 0, minor: 1, patch: 4, content: "0.1.4" }];
getNewEntries(entries, "0.1.5");            // []
getNewEntries(entries, "0.1.5-20261020.7"); // ["0.1.5", "0.1.4"] entries, every time
```

In the app: install a package with an extension, `version: "0.1.5-20261020.7"` and a `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [0.1.5]`, launch once to record it, then start a few fresh sessions. Launches 2 and 3 both showed the 0.1.5 and 0.1.4 notes, and the saved version stayed `0.1.5-20261020.7`.

## Expected behavior

Compare only the `major.minor.patch` part of the saved version, as already happens for the changelog headings, for example `lastVersion.split(/[-+]/)[0].split(".")`. Then `0.1.5-20261020.7` counts as `0.1.5` and nothing repeats.

I'm happy to send the one-line fix with a test if you want it.

## Version

1.5.0 (code unchanged on `main` @ `642e30b68`)

issues.title: Make skill resolution observable: a no-model skills listing (--print-skills / pi skills)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

There is no deterministic way to ask "which skills would this pi load, given this agent dir, cwd, and flags?" Today the only observable output is the `<available_skills>` block injected into a model prompt. To audit skill loading on a headless box I resorted to one-shot model calls (`pi -p "list the skills in your prompt"`) — slow, cost real inference, and the answer is itself generated (a model can misreport its own prompt).

Context: I was verifying skill curation on an offline machine (a DGX Spark seat). Confirming that `-ns --skill <dir>` suppresses auto-discovery of `~/.claude/skills` and that settings.json `-path` entries behave as documented required several paid round-trips per hypothesis.

## Proposal

A built-in listing command or flag, e.g.:

- `pi --print-skills` (or `pi skills list`) — resolves skill discovery exactly as a normal run would (same agent-dir resolution, project walk, settings, flags) and prints one entry per skill: name, source path, origin (discovered / configured / explicit `--skill` / extension), and whether it was excluded.
- `--json` for scripting.

No model call, no provider configured; pure resource resolution, like `pi`'s existing path/flag handling.

## Nice-to-have

The same output marking *why* each auto-discovered skill was or wasn't loaded (root walked, `-path` excluded, duplicate name shadowed). Half the debugging was reasoning about precedence between discovered skills and extension-provided ones.

issues.title: Settings-level control to prune auto-discovered skills (skills.disabled or skills.roots)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

Core auto-discovers skills from fixed locations (`~/.claude/skills`, `.pi/skills`, project scopes, ...). On a machine where those locations are populated for a *different* machine (we sync our full `~/.claude/skills` to an offline ARM box so the seats stay identical), most discovered skills are dead weight in the prompt, and there is no settings-level way to subtract them:

- `settings.json` → `skills: ["-<path>"]` only governs that resource array, not the auto-discovered set (verified on 1.5.0: excluded paths still appeared in `<available_skills>`).
- `PI_SKILLS_ROOTS` is an env var of a third-party extension; core ignores it.

The only working lever is CLI flags — `-ns` plus a repeated `--skill <dir>` — which works but must be threaded through every launch path (a daemon's runner script *and* a shell wrapper for interactive use). That is what we ship now, and it is brittle for ad-hoc seats.

## Proposal

A settings-level control that applies to discovered skills, e.g. either:

1. `skills.disabled: ["<path-or-glob>", ...]` subtracting from auto-discovery (same precedence rules as the resource array's `-` entries), or
2. `skills.roots: [...]` replacing the default discovery roots outright when set (mirror of the extension's `PI_SKILLS_ROOTS`, but honored by core so daemon and interactive seats agree without flag plumbing).

Either would let a synced, shared `~/.claude/skills` stay in place while each machine's settings.json says what it actually has resources for.

issues.title: Add Arabic RTL rendering to the TUI (bidirectional text, Windows Terminal)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

Arabic and Persian output in pi reads backwards in Windows Terminal. I want bidirectional rendering: reorder RTL lines into visual order before they are written, and put a line against the edge its script reads from. Behind two settings — `terminal.rtl.enabled` (default off) and `terminal.rtl.align` — so nothing changes for lines with no RTL content.

**Why?**

Windows Terminal paints cells in the order the program writes them and does not implement UAX #9 (microsoft/terminal#538, the same blocker raised in #3301). Text stored correctly in logical order therefore reads mirrored on screen: an Arabic user cannot read the transcript, and the caret in the prompt sits on the wrong side of the word being typed.

Copy, search, the saved transcript and column widths are all correct today — only the painted order is wrong. The terminal will not fix it, so the TUI can: write the visual order, keep the logical state.

**How?**

`reorderLine()` in `packages/tui/src/bidi.ts` runs one rendered line through UAX #9 (bidi-js) on grapheme clusters and returns it in visual order. Only the string written to the terminal changes; caret offsets, selection, copy, wrapping and widths stay logical. Code blocks, table borders, list markers and quote bars stay where the renderer put them, and content inside them is reordered where it is produced. Alignment follows the script that dominates the line, so `npm install ثم build the package` stays on the left.

Tests: `packages/tui/test/bidi*.test.ts` (52 tests) and `packages/coding-agent/test/rtl-settings.test.ts`. The implementation is on [rtl-bidi](https://github.com/AliQaseef/pi-rtl-bidi/tree/rtl-bidi) and the PR is [#11580](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11580), auto-closed until this issue is approved.

Screenshots (Windows Terminal, RTL on):

![Arabic reply and tool output in visual order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AliQaseef/pi-rtl-bidi/rtl-screenshots/rtl-patch/screenshots/pi_reply.png)

issues.title: OAuth refresh token lost when an RPC process is stopped during the startup catalog refresh (invalid_grant)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

My `openai` (Sign in with ChatGPT) login keeps dying with `OAuth refresh failed for openai: OpenAI OAuth token request failed (400): {"error": "invalid_grant"}`. `/login` fixes it until the token next expires while I'm not using it.

I run pi inside T3 Code, which starts `pi --mode rpc` every few minutes to check status and stops it as soon as it answers. In RPC mode pi starts the catalog refresh in the background at startup, and that also refreshes any expired OAuth credential, even though the catalog doesn't need it. If the process is stopped after the token request goes out but before the new token is written, OpenAI has already used up the old refresh token and auth.json keeps it. The SIGTERM shutdown doesn't wait for the refresh (on Windows it's a hard kill anyway). This may explain some of the "dies after idle" reports in #10377.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let the `openai` access token in auth.json expire.
2. `pi -ne --mode rpc --no-session`, send `get_state`, then SIGTERM it 200–300 ms after it answers.
3. The next request fails with invalid_grant.

Against a local token endpoint with single-use refresh tokens and ~150 ms latency, this lost the token 30 of 30 times. Stopping within 150 ms or after 350 ms never did, and neither did `--offline`.

### Expected behavior

The catalog refresh shouldn't rotate credentials it doesn't use, and shutdown should wait (with a timeout) for a refresh already in flight. Using `--offline` as a workaround for now.

### Version

1.4.0 (macOS and Windows, Node 26)

issues.title: Alacritty: multi-character IME commit is treated as bracketed paste, so slash/@ autocomplete never opens
issues.body:
## What happened

In Alacritty on macOS with a Chinese IME, slash-command and `@` file autocomplete only open when the IME commits a **single** character. Any commit of two or more characters inserts the text correctly but never opens the autocomplete list.

Reproduction pattern with pinyin input (text in the editor is always plain ASCII):

| Input | Result |
| ----- | ------ |
| `/` then commit `m` | autocomplete opens |
| `/mo` committed as one chunk | no autocomplete |
| then commit `d` (single char) | autocomplete opens for `/mod` |
| `/mode` with `de` committed as one chunk | no autocomplete |

Switching to an English keyboard input source makes all of these work. The same happens with `@` file autocomplete: a two-character IME commit closes the list instead of refreshing it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. macOS with Alacritty, Chinese IME active.
2. Run `pi`.
3. Type `/`, then type `m` and commit it with Enter. The command autocomplete opens.
4. Type `mo` and commit it as a single IME commit with Enter. The autocomplete list disappears and does not come back.
5. Type `d` and commit it. The list comes back for `/mod`.

## Expected behavior

Autocomplete should refresh for `/mo` (14 matches with default commands and installed skills) and for `/mode`.

## Actual behavior

No autocomplete list. Text is inserted correctly.

`cat -v` in the same terminal shows a clean `/mo`, which is expected: `cat` does not enable bracketed paste, so Alacritty does not wrap the commit.

## Root cause

Alacritty submits IME commits through bracketed paste. This is confirmed by the Alacritty maintainer in alacritty/alacritty#8764:

> Alacritty does submit IME text through bracketed paste mode, so my guess would be that the application is trying to be smart by detecting that and fails horribly to function properly in the process.

On the pi side, bracketed paste is enabled unconditionally at terminal start, and a single-line paste is handled by:

- cancelling any open autocomplete,
- inserting the text atomically,
- returning without any autocomplete re-trigger.

The insertion helper explicitly documents that it does not trigger autocomplete and that the caller is responsible. Since `handlePaste` returns immediately after inserting a single line, no trigger happens.

As a result, single-character IME commits take the normal key path and trigger autocomplete, while 2+ character commits take the paste path, close the list, and never re-open it.

## Suggested fix

After inserting a single-line paste, re-trigger autocomplete for the current context, or distinguish IME commits from explicit user paste. Either change keeps pasted text working and restores completion for IME commits. This is closely related to #9795 (autocomplete after single-line paste) and #4253 (multi-codepoint IME commits).

## Environment

- pi 1.3.0
- Alacritty 0.17.0 (94e7c88)
- macOS 15.8.1
- Chinese IME (pinyin input, commit by Enter)

## Related

- alacritty/alacritty#8764 (IME commits use bracketed paste)
- alacritty/alacritty#8692 (maintainer declines a terminal-side config option)
- earendil-works/pi#4253 (multi-codepoint IME commits)
- earendil-works/pi#9795 (autocomplete after single-line paste)

issues.title: Extension loader imports *.test.ts from .pi/extensions/ — a self-executing test's process.exit(0) kills the host process (took down our pi-web server twice)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

The project extension loader auto-imports **every** `*.ts`/`*.js` file directly under `<cwd>/.pi/extensions/` — including test files. Since importing a module executes its top level, a self-executing test file placed there runs its assertions (and its `process.exit()`) **inside the host process**. This took down our pi-web deployment twice today.

## What happened

A developer/agent added a plain test file next to a real extension:

```
<project>/.pi/extensions/decide.ts        ← real extension
<project>/.pi/extensions/decide.test.ts   ← self-executing test
```

`decide.test.ts` is a standard "run checks at module top level, then exit" script:

```ts
const check = (name, cond) => { console.log(cond ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL', name) ... }
// ... 9 top-level checks ...
console.log(`\n${pass} pass, ${fail} fail`)
process.exit(fail > 0 ? 1 : 0)   // ← runs on import
```

pi-web creates AgentSessions **in-process**, so the first session opened with that project cwd imported the test as an extension and `process.exit(0)` killed the entire Next.js server. Journal (twice, verbatim):

```
18:19:38 node[4472]: [pi-web] session_start dispatched to extensions for session 01a18bd6-…
18:19:45 node[4472]: PASS request_priority parses
…            (9 lines)
18:19:45 node[4472]: 9 pass, 0 fail
18:19:45 node[4472]: [pi-web] Next.js exited unexpectedly (code 0)
```

The session_start → crash delay was 2.3s / 6.3s, and the 9 check names matched the file exactly, which is how we traced it.

An extra twist: because the child reported code 0, pi-web's wrapper relayed exit 0 and systemd's `Restart=on-failure` did **not** restart the service — it stayed down until a human noticed. (An all-green test suite is the *worst* case here: a failing check would have exited 1 and auto-restarted.)

## Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` (current `main`, around line 740):

```ts
function isExtensionFile(name: string): boolean {
	return name.endsWith(".ts") || name.endsWith(".js");
}
```

`discoverExtensionsInDir()` pushes every direct `.ts`/`.js` file with no exclusion for `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` (or `_`-prefixed helper files). Test files conventionally execute at import time and call `process.exit()` — they are never valid extension entry points, and an unwary `mv`/`cp` into `.pi/extensions/` is silent until it kills a session.

## Minimal repro

```bash
mkdir -p .pi/extensions
printf 'console.log("boom"); process.exit(0);\n' > .pi/extensions/x.test.ts
pi -p "hi"   # or start any session in this cwd / open it in pi-web
# → host process exits immediately after "boom"
```

## Suggested fixes

Any of these, ideally the first:

1. **Exclude test files in discovery**: skip `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts` (and `.js`/`.mjs` variants) in `isExtensionFile()`. Cheap, matches the convention of every TS project.
2. Quarantine imports: catch/neutralize `process.exit` during extension module import (patch `process.exit` around the jiti import).
3. At minimum, log a warning when a discovered extension file matches `*.{test,spec}.*` before importing it.

## How we mitigated it locally

- Guarded the test body with `if (import.meta.main)` (inert when imported, still runnable via `bun run`).
- pi-web's wrapper (`bin/process-lifecycle.js`) now exits **1** when the Next.js child dies unexpectedly with code 0, so `Restart=on-failure` recovers.
- Filed here because the discovery-side behavior is the actual footgun.

## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0 (Node 24, Linux); behavior confirmed unchanged on current `main` (`isExtensionFile` as quoted above).
- Also reproduced via pi-web (which imports project extensions in-process when creating AgentSessions).

Error: Retry failed after 1 attempts: basispoints_tool_arguments_stalled: Tool arguments stopped making progress: consecutive whitespace outside JSON strings (output_index=1, whitespace_bytes=1024, limit_bytes=1024)

Pi should treat this as a recoverable generation failure, retry within the configured retry limit, and continue the task when recovery succeeds.

issues.title: Anthropic adapter silently drops root anyOf from custom tool schemas

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

When a custom tool parameter schema uses a root-level `anyOf`, the registered schema and Pi's argument validator retain the constraint, but the Anthropic Messages adapter silently removes it from the model-facing `input_schema`.

The emitted schema contains only `type`, `properties`, and `required`. The model therefore sees independent enums rather than the valid combinations. Runtime validation still rejects invalid calls, but the schema shown to the model no longer describes the tool contract.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a minimal extension that registers a tool with two enum properties and a root `anyOf` coupling their valid combinations.
2. Log `event.payload` from `before_provider_request`.
3. Run only that extension with `pi -ne -e ./repro.ts` and select an Anthropic model.
4. Inspect `tools[].input_schema`.

The registered schema has the `anyOf`; the outgoing Anthropic schema does not. The non-strict conversion rebuilds a legacy schema from only root `type`, `properties`, and `required`.

### Expected behavior

Preserve supported root JSON Schema constraints in the Anthropic `input_schema`. If a constraint cannot be represented by that provider, fail explicitly or document/reject it instead of silently flattening the schema.

### Version

0.84.2

prs.title: Anthropic message threads
prs.body:
Anthropic can keep a conversation on the server (message threads beta).
A request can then continue from the previous reply and send only the
new messages, instead of the whole history every turn.

pi uses this when a session id is set and caching is on. It still builds
the full request, compares it with the previous one, and only sends the
new part if nothing earlier changed.

- Default: on only for the anthropic provider on api.anthropic.com.
  Gateways that drop unknown fields would lose the conversation.
  Override with compat.supportsMessageThreads.
- If the server rejects a continuation, pi resends the full request
  as a new thread. Other errors turn threads off for the session.
- New option StreamOptions.disableContinuation. The cache warmer sets
  it so warm requests don't replace the session's thread.
- cleanupSessionResources(sessionId) frees a session's thread state.

prs.title: fix(ai): leave room for OpenRouter's input overcount when clamping max tokens
prs.body:
OpenRouter checks input + max_tokens against the context window before routing, using its own tokenizer. For prose it counted up to 12% more input tokens than the provider. pi left only 4096 tokens spare, so models whose output limit is close to the window (e.g. DeepSeek flash) were rejected with a 400, which pi then treated as a context overflow and compacted.

The default output limit now leaves 15% of the estimated input unused (at least 4096). When that would leave less than 32768 tokens of output, only the fixed 4096 margin is kept and output is capped at 32768.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): only report packages as up to date when pi update checked them
prs.body:
## Problem

#11707 prints `Packages are already up to date` whenever no package changed. In two cases that claim is false.

**1. npm left the old version installed.** Extension updates install `@latest` or the configured range. If npm resolves stale registry metadata, it reinstalls the old version and exits 0. The existing check warns, then the summary contradicts it:

```
Updating npm:foo...
npm:foo is still 1.2.0 (registry reports 1.3.0); npm registry metadata may be stale, try again in a few minutes
Packages are already up to date
```

**2. Offline mode.** With `--offline` or `PI_OFFLINE=1`, `updateConfiguredSources()` returns before checking anything, and the CLI still prints `Packages are already up to date`.

## Change

The CLI only prints "already up to date" when the update ran and printed no warning:

| Situation | Output |
|---|---|
| Packages changed | `Updated N packages:` and the list (unchanged) |
| Nothing changed, no warnings | `Packages are already up to date` (unchanged) |
| Nothing changed, a warning was printed | `No packages were updated, see the warnings above` (or `<source> was not updated, ...`) |
| Offline mode | `Skipped package updates (offline mode)` |

The CLI counts `progress` update events, which are always warnings, and does not try to map them to packages. That is deliberate: the git warning about untracked files that could not be cleaned is printed even though the commit did change, so a warning does not mean "this package was not updated".

In offline mode, `update()` still runs, so `pi update <unknown source>` still fails with "No matching package". `isOfflineModeEnabled()` is now exported from `core/package-manager.ts` (not from the package index) so the CLI uses the same check.

The changelog entry from #11707 is adjusted, since it is unreleased.

## Tests

`test/package-command-paths.test.ts`, both through `main()`:

- npm `view` reports 1.3.0 but `install` leaves 1.2.0: the stale-metadata warning is printed, then `No packages were updated, see the warnings above`, and no "up to date".
- `PI_OFFLINE=1`: `Skipped package updates (offline mode)`, no "up to date".

Both fail without the fix. `cycles project package overrides in config local mode`, `prints a pnpm metadata hint when self-update fails` and `should expand ~ in exclusion and exact patterns` fail locally on Windows, on `origin/main` as well.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): take grep context lines from ripgrep instead of reading matched files
prs.body:
When `context` is set, the grep tool read every matched file whole and split it into lines, only to print the lines around each match. Memory grew with the size of the matched files, not the output. In the issue's reproduction (8 log files of about 95 MB, one match each, `context: 2`, `--max-old-space-size=1024`), the process ran out of heap after about 10 s.

ripgrep already supports context. This change passes `--context N` to rg and formats the `context` events from its JSON output. The tool no longer opens matched files.

Details:
- After the last allowed match (`limit`), rg still sends that match's trailing context. The tool keeps those lines, then stops rg. A match inside that window is shown as a context line, as before.
- Lines past the 50 KB output cap are counted but not stored, since truncation drops them anyway. Match counts, the match-limit notice, and `details.matchLimitReached` stay as before.
- rg merges overlapping context, so lines shared by nearby matches are printed once instead of repeated per match. This is the one intended output change.
- Context lines are decoded by rg, so UTF-16 files with a BOM show correctly with context (#11423, closed as no-action). Non-UTF-8 lines and paths, which rg sends base64-encoded, are decoded too.

Breaking: `GrepOperations.readFile` is removed because nothing uses it anymore. rg always ran locally, so this hook never made grep work on a remote backend. Docs now say to override `execute()` for remote search, as the Gondolin example does. Code that passes `readFile` still runs, and the value is ignored. Only code that type-checks an object literal against `GrepOperations` fails to compile.

Known remaining differences and limits:
- Memory no longer grows with file size or match count, but a single huge matching line (tens of MB) is still buffered whole before being cut to 500 characters. That was already true for `context: 0` on main. Bounding it would mean discarding oversized rg JSON records, which is a separate change.
- In a directory search, rg stops reading a file once it finds a NUL byte, so context past that point in a text-looking file that turns binary later is omitted. main reread the file and printed it. Explicit file paths are unaffected.
- `details.truncation.totalLines`/`totalBytes` count formatted rows. With deduplicated context, or file names containing newlines, they can differ from main. No renderer or notice displays them.

**Testing**
- Issue reproduction: before, `FATAL ERROR ... JavaScript heap out of memory`. After, correct output in about 60 ms with 135 MB RSS.
- `pattern: "line", context: 3, limit: 100000` over the same 770 MB of logs reports both limit notices and peaks at 154 MB RSS.
- New tests in `test/tools.test.ts`:
  - Merged overlapping context, plus trailing context at the limit including a match inside it. Fails on main.
  - UTF-16 with context. Fails on main.
  - Truncation reported when stored output ends exactly at 50 KB. Guards the counting logic.
  - Matches still counted past the byte cap. Passes on main too; it guards against stopping rg early at the cap.
  - Huge `context` value accepted.
- All 92 tests in the file pass. `npm run check` passes.

fixes #9276

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report the installed version after npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun self-updates
prs.body:
## Problem

For npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun installs, `pi update` prints `Updated pi from <old> to <new>` using the version pi.dev advertised, without checking what the package manager actually installed. If npm resolves stale registry metadata shortly after a release, it reinstalls the old version, exits 0, and pi still reports success:

```
$ pi update --self
Updating pi with npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.6.0...
Updated pi from 1.5.0 to 1.6.0      <- 1.5.0 is still installed
```

The other two self-update paths already check:

- Managed installs: `verifyManagedRelease` runs the new release's `--version` and fails on a mismatch.
- `selfUpdateCommand` / `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND`: reads the installed version back and warns on a mismatch.

## Change

The package-manager path now uses the same check as `selfUpdateCommand`, extracted into `reportSelfUpdateResult()`:

1. If this installation's `package.json` now has the planned version (`detectInstallChange()`), report the update.
2. Otherwise read `pi --version` from PATH, which covers installs that land in another directory, e.g. a renamed package.
3. If neither reports the planned version, print the existing warning instead of `Updated pi ...`:

```
Ran npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.6.0, but `pi --version` reports 1.5.0, not 1.6.0.
```

For pnpm, a mismatch also prints the existing `pnpm store prune` hint, since stale pnpm metadata is the likely cause.

Like the `selfUpdateCommand` path, a mismatch is a warning and does not set a non-zero exit code.

## Tests

`test/package-command-paths.test.ts`:

- New: npm exits 0 but the old version stays installed -> warning, no `Updated pi from`.
- The existing npm self-update tests fake `npm` without changing anything on disk, so they now put a fake `pi` on PATH that reports the expected version. `putFakePiOnPath()` is extracted from the existing `prepareSelfUpdateCommand()` helper.

`cycles project package overrides in config local mode` and `prints a pnpm metadata hint when self-update fails` fail locally on Windows, on `origin/main` as well, independent of this change.

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): list updated packages with version changes in pi update
prs.body:
## Problem

`pi update`, `pi update --all` and `pi update --extensions` print only `Updating <source>...` progress lines and a final `Updated packages`. Users cannot see which extensions changed or to which version. Several outdated npm packages in the same scope are installed as one batch, so the progress output does not even name them.

## Change

`pi update` now prints a summary of what actually changed:

```
Updated 2 packages:
  npm:foo 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
  git:github.com/user/bar (project) abc1234 -> def5678
```

When nothing changed it prints `Packages are already up to date` (or `<source> is already up to date`).

- npm: compares the installed `package.json` version before and after the batch install. The "before" version comes from the existing `shouldUpdateNpmSource` check, so this adds no extra registry calls.
- git: compares `git rev-parse HEAD` before and after `updateGit`. Commits are shortened to 7 characters.
- Packages whose version or commit did not change are omitted, including npm installs that hit stale registry metadata (those already get the existing warning).

## API

`PackageManager.update()` still returns `Promise<void>`. `ProgressEvent.type` gains a `"result"` member. Each changed package is reported through the existing progress callback as:

```ts
{ type: "result", action: "update", source: "npm:foo", message: "npm:foo 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0" }
```

The CLI collects these messages to print the summary. A separate type keeps the existing contract that each `start` is followed by exactly one `complete` or `error` for the same source. Reusing `complete` would have produced a second `complete` for git packages and a `complete` without a `start` for batched npm packages. The only compatibility cost is for TypeScript consumers with an exhaustive `switch` on `event.type`.

## Tests

- `test/package-manager.test.ts`: npm update emits `start`, `complete`, then a `result` with `npm:example@^1.0.0 (project) 1.0.0 -> 1.2.0`; an up-to-date package emits no result.
- `test/git-update.test.ts`: git update emits a result with the old and new commit; an up-to-date clone emits no result.

`should expand ~ in exclusion and exact patterns` fails locally on Windows. It tests path resolution and is unrelated to this change.

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): add PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND and selfUpdateCommand for pi update
prs.body:
Refs #7756, #5607.

Problem: when a wrapper or another package manager provides Pi (mise, a `PNPM_HOME` wrapper such as nub, Nix), `pi update` cannot update it and prints "pi cannot self-update this installation." Users with several machines have to remember which tool updates Pi on which machine.

Example:

```sh
export PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND="mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}"
pi update
# Updating pi with mise use -g npm:@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.4.0...
# Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0
```

or in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:

```json
{ "selfUpdateCommand": ["nix", "profile", "upgrade", "pi"] }
```

Behavior:

- `pi update` still checks pi.dev first. The command runs only when a newer release exists, or with `--force`, and the release note prints first.
- Placeholders come from that release: `{packageName}`, `{version}`, `{installSpec}` (`<packageName>@<version>`). A package rename announced by pi.dev flows into them.
- `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` takes precedence and is split on whitespace (no quoting). The setting is argv, for arguments with spaces, and is read only from global settings, so a project's `.pi/settings.json` cannot inject a command.
- The configured command replaces Pi's own update logic for every install method, including installer-managed installs: it is explicit user intent.
- Exit code 0 does not prove an update. Pi reports "Updated pi from X to Y" when its own `package.json` now shows Y (in-place updates) or when `pi --version` from PATH reports Y (wrappers such as mise or Nix that install each version into a new directory). Otherwise it warns: ``Ran <cmd>, but `pi --version` reports X, not Y.``
- "cannot self-update this installation" now mentions the env var and setting.

Docs: `docs/cli.md` (new "Custom update command" section), `docs/settings.md`, `docs/environment-variables.md`, `--help` env list, regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json`.

Tests: unit tests for argv resolution and placeholders in `test/config.test.ts`; CLI tests in `test/package-command-paths.test.ts` for env precedence over the setting and the managed install, global-only setting gated by the version check, and command failure. `npm run check` passes.

Manual end-to-end check with real mise 2026.10.23 in a sandboxed HOME, running this branch as the mise-installed 1.3.0 (`PI_PACKAGE_DIR` pointing at mise's install):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}` | mise installs 1.4.0; `Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0` |
| Already 1.4.0 | `pi is already up to date (v1.4.0)`, mise not run |
| In-place `npm install -g --prefix <dir> {installSpec}` via the setting | `Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0` |
| Command `true` (exit 0, installs nothing) | ``Ran true, but `pi --version` reports 1.3.0, not 1.4.0.`` |

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): preserve indentation in rendered diffs
prs.body:
## Problem

The edit tool's intra-line renderer can drop indentation from a removed line when text is inserted before otherwise unchanged content.

For example, this input:

```diff
-83   await commitRecordingChunk({
+83   const result = await commitRecordingChunk({
```

was rendered as:

```diff
-83 await commitRecordingChunk({
+83   const result = await commitRecordingChunk({
```

`diffWords()` groups the shared leading spaces into the added segment (`"  const result = "`). The existing highlighting logic moved those spaces outside inverse styling, but only appended them to the added line.

## Solution

Extract whitespace shared by both lines before calling `diffWords()`, then initialize both rendered lines with that prefix. This preserves indentation without changing the existing word-level highlighting behavior. The existing handling for whitespace that belongs to only one side remains unchanged.

Added regression coverage for:

- insertion before indented content;
- replacement within indented content;
- keeping shared indentation outside inverse highlighting.

## Validation

- `npm run check`
- `./test.sh`
- targeted `packages/coding-agent/test/diff.test.ts` (3 tests)

prs.title: feat: release version tags on pkg.earendil.com
prs.body:
## Problem

`scripts/release.mjs` pushes `Release vX.Y.Z` and `Add [Unreleased] section…` to main in one push, then pushes the tag. CI builds only the pushed head, so the tagged release commit is never built and pkg.earendil.com has no build of a release. Example: for v1.4.0, v1.3.0 and v1.2.0 the tagged commits have Build Binaries and Nix runs, but no CI run.

Internal users want to install a release from pkg.earendil.com as soon as it is tagged, without waiting for the npm release.

## Change

- `ci.yml` also runs for `v*.*.*` tags (the pattern `nix.yml` uses), so the tagged commit is built and packed.
- `preview-packages.yml` also publishes passing CI runs of release tags: `POST /_/releases` keeps the packages for good under the tag (it never moves), then the `latest` ref moves to it. Pre-releases (`v1.2.3-rc.1`) are released without moving `latest`.
- `scripts/preview-packages.mjs publish` decides what a push run publishes (the workflow passes the run's branch and conclusion), reading the GitHub API with `fetch` before anything is uploaded. A tag push's `head_branch` is the tag's name, and a branch or tag can carry its own copy of CI, so:
  - every push run must be for a commit on main, comparing against main's resolved SHA (a bare `main` in compare would resolve to a tag named `main`);
  - a release tag must match `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$`, have passing CI (CI packs before its tests run), and point at the commit, dereferencing annotated tags, also nested;
  - other names publish nothing.

  This also closes an existing hole: a tag named `main` on an unreviewed commit could move the `main` ref.
- A release happens after the uploads and before moving refs, so `latest` never points at a failed release. The job summary lists the release's install commands.
- A passing push run whose CI artifact expired (3 days) fails with "re-run CI" instead of passing silently, so a release tag cannot go unreleased unnoticed.

## Before / after for a release

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CI of the tagged commit | none | build, test, pack |
| `pkg.earendil.com/<package>@vX.Y.Z` | 404 | kept for good |
| `…@<release sha>` | 404 | kept for good |
| `…@latest` | none | moves to each release |
| npm, binaries, pi.dev, Nix `stable` | unchanged | unchanged |
| main and PR previews | unchanged | unchanged |

Tag CI runs trigger Publish Model Catalog and Nix, which skip them (`head_branch != main`).

## Before merging

- [x] Deploy pkg.earendil.com with `POST /_/releases` (earendil-pkg `7955990`); until then a tag run fails at the release call and `latest` does not move.
- [ ] Add a ruleset restricting creation, update and deletion of `v*` tags to maintainers / the release process: a pkg release skips npm's gate and is kept for good.

## Checks

`npm run check`; `node --test scripts/preview-packages.test.mjs` (10 tests, under 2s, against a fake server for pkg.earendil.com and the GitHub API with raw API responses). Each of these mutations fails a test: bare `main` in compare, wrong API field names, no on-main check, no tag target check, one-level tag dereference, `latest` for pre-releases, unanchored or loose tag pattern, no CI conclusion check, dropping `identical`. actionlint reports only the existing `queue:` complaint.

prs.title: fix(nix): pack pi-schema from the checkout in the Nix package
prs.body:
`nix build .#pi` stopped working once pi-schema became a runtime dependency of the coding agent. It now fails with `error: attribute 'integrity' missing` in `import-npm-lock`.

The install lock (`packages/coding-agent/install-lock/package-lock.json`) points internal `@earendil-works/*` packages at registry URLs and has no `integrity` field for them. `nix/package.nix` packs each internal package from the checkout and swaps it in through `packageSourceOverrides`. `@earendil-works/pi-schema` was missing from both lists, so `importNpmLock` tried to fetch it from the registry, found no hash, and failed.

This change packs `packages/schema` in the workspace-packages derivation and adds the matching `packageSourceOverrides` entry. `build:offline` already builds `packages/schema`, so `dist` is there when the package is packed.

Testing:
- Checked that every `@earendil-works/*` entry in the install lock without `integrity` now has an override in `nix/package.nix`. Before this change pi-schema was the only one missing. After it, none are missing.
- Built `packages/schema` and ran `npm pack --dry-run` on it. The tarball includes `dist/`.
- `npm run check` passes.
- I could not run `nix build` myself. The reporter says the same change builds on aarch64-darwin and the output includes pi-schema.

Fixes #11682

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): apply context edits to branch summary input
prs.body:
When a partial assistant reply fails and automatic retry succeeds, pi appends a `context_edit` that hides the failed attempt from model context. Branch summarization (`/tree` with summarize) built its input from raw session entries through `getMessageFromEntry`, which ignored `context_edit` entries. As a result, the summarizer received the hidden attempt again. Content replacements were ignored the same way.

What the change does:
- `prepareBranchEntries` now collects the latest `context_edit` for each target in the branch.
- It applies those edits to the entries it converts, using the same `projectContextEntry` logic as the live context and compaction:
  - an omission (`replacement: null`) drops the entry;
  - a replacement swaps its content.
- `projectContextEntry` is now exported from `session-manager.ts` so both paths share it.
- The existing branch-summary behavior is unchanged: tool results are still skipped, and compaction or branch-summary entries still become summary messages.

Testing:
- Added `applies context edits to branch entries` to `test/branch-summarization.test.ts`. It covers one omitted assistant entry and one replaced assistant entry. The test fails without the change and passes with it.
- Ran `branch-summarization`, `branch-summary-extensions`, `agent-session-branching` and the compaction tests: all pass.
- `npm run check`: biome and the coding-agent checks pass. `tsc` reports 6 errors in `packages/ai` model-catalog tests, and the same 6 errors occur on unmodified `main`.
- End-to-end reproduction with the faux provider and `AgentSession`: a failed attempt, a successful retry, then `navigateTree(target, { summarize: true })`. Before the change, the summary request contained the failed attempt's text. After the change, it contains only the successful retry.

Fixes #11602

Requested by @davidbrai
