releases.name: v1.5.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Extension update changelogs**: see what changed in installed extension packages on the next fresh launch after an update. Package authors can choose the changelog path, and `collapseChangelog` condenses the notices. See [Show a changelog](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md#show-a-changelog).
- **Faster streaming**: large tool calls are parsed incrementally, and code-heavy answers and tool rows reuse highlighting and rendered Markdown instead of repeating the work on every update. See [Keep rendering responsive](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/tui.md#keep-rendering-responsive).
- **Custom self-update commands**: use `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` or `selfUpdateCommand` to update pi through a wrapper or another package manager. See [Custom update command](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md#custom-update-command).
- **GPT-6.1 Terra**: available through OpenAI, Azure OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI Codex, with tool search, mid-conversation thinking-level changes, and thinking `off`. Codex offers a 500K context window. See [Models](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md#models).

### Breaking Changes

- Tool argument validation runs on `@earendil-works/pi-schema`. TypeBox features outside JSON Schema (`Type.Refine()`, `Type.BigInt()`, `Type.Undefined()`, codecs, `Format.Set()` formats) no longer apply to tool arguments; see [Tool parameter schemas and TypeBox](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#tool-parameter-schemas-and-typebox). Plain JSON Schema tools, including MCP tools, now get the same coercion as TypeBox tools, such as converting numeric strings and wrapping a single value into an array. Validation failures the model sees list pi-schema's messages (`- path: missing`, `- limit: expected number, got string`) instead of TypeBox's (`must have required properties path`, `must be number`).

### Added

- Extension packages can now show their changelog after an update. Pi reads `pi.changelogPath` from the package's `package.json`, or `CHANGELOG.md` in the package root, and on the next fresh launch shows entries newer than the last seen version under "Extension Updates". The `collapseChangelog` setting condenses this to one line per package ([#5958](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5958), [#8790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8790))
- `pi.exec()` accepts a `maxBuffer` option that limits stdout and stderr combined, and its result has a `truncated` field that is true when output exceeded the limit ([#11360](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11360))
- Device-code login (for example GitHub Copilot) now opens the verification page and copies the code when you press Enter. Providers can turn either action off with `openBrowserOnConfirm: false` or `copyCodeOnConfirm: false` ([#9282](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9282), [#9301](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9301))
- `pi update` can update Pi through a wrapper or another package manager. Set `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` (for example `mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}`) or the global `selfUpdateCommand` setting; `pi update` runs it when pi.dev reports a newer release and fills `{packageName}`, `{version}`, and `{installSpec}` from that release. See [Custom update command](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md#custom-update-command) ([#7756](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7756), [#5607](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5607))
- Extensions can format the user's configured keybindings with `keyText()` and `keyHint()` from the tool render context and the message and entry renderer options. Importing these functions from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` can resolve the extension's own copy of the package, which does not see pi's keybindings, so hints such as `keyHint("app.tools.expand", "to expand")` rendered without the key. The docs now recommend the injected functions ([#4748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4748))
- Added persisted session-entry `messageId` and ISO `timestamp` to `MarkdownTransformContext`. They are available when rendering saved entries and undefined for live rendering ([#7952](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7952) by [@vipentti](https://github.com/vipentti))
- Added a `blocked` option to inline `ctx.ui.custom()` components so approval prompts and other custom dialogs can report that pi is waiting for user input. Overlays ignore the option. See [Custom screens and overlays](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/tui.md#use-custom-screens-and-overlays) ([#11428](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11428))
- Added `Usage.cost.totalFromProvider` to distinguish billed totals from catalog estimates in SDK and extension usage data; combined usage is marked provider-reported only when every part is ([#11178](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11178))
- Added concrete `responseModel` metadata to messages from pi-messages providers such as Radius, including when a virtual model is requested. See [AssistantMessage](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/message-types.md#assistantmessage) ([#11265](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11265))
- Added GPT-6.1 Terra for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI Codex, with tool search and mid-conversation thinking-level changes. It supports thinking `off`; Codex offers a 500K context window

### Changed

- Extensions keep importing `Type`, `Static` and `TSchema` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai`: Pi maps that import to pi-ai's compat entry plus the TypeBox it bundles, now that pi-ai itself no longer re-exports TypeBox, and its `StringEnum` there stays a TypeBox `TUnsafe<T>`. The built-in tool factories (`createReadTool()` and the others) return `TypeBoxAgentTool<typeof schema>`, which keeps `params` typed for TypeBox.
- Tightened system prompt
- `pi update` for installs from the pi.dev installer no longer passes `--min-release-age=0` to `npm ci`. The release lockfile pins every package, so the flag had no effect, and security scanners that block it stopped the update ([#11262](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11262))
- `/model` and `/scoped-models` now show a model's name next to its ID when the name adds words the ID lacks, such as a renamed `models.json` override ([#5916](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5916), [#11347](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11347))
- MCP OAuth sign-in now uses pi's Client ID Metadata Document by default when the authorization server supports it for public clients, and registers a client dynamically otherwise, like Codex, Claude Code, and opencode. Clients registered before stay in use while their redirect URI matches. The new default `oauth.clientRegistration: "auto"` registers when `clientName` or a non-default `callbackUrl` is set; `"dcr"` always registers. `pi mcp add --oauth-client-registration` sets the mode ([#11426](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11426))
- Changed the default OpenAI model from `gpt-5.5` to `gpt-6.1-sol`, including after ChatGPT sign-in when no model is selected ([#11442](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11442))
- Updated the built-in model catalog to models.dev v2. Realtime and image-only models are no longer offered as chat models; newer OpenAI and Google chat models are included

### Fixed

- Updated glob matching to prevent denial of service from amplified glob patterns.
- Fixed a saved "Do not trust" decision being ignored for projects without trust-requiring resources, for example a folder with only `AGENTS.md`. pi auto-trusted such projects, so `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` returned true and package commands treated them as trusted. A saved decision in `trust.json` now takes precedence; auto-trust applies only when no decision is saved ([#10947](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10947))
- Fixed `Shift+Enter` queueing a follow-up instead of inserting a newline in Apple Terminal setups that send `ESC` + Return. pi now checks the local Shift key state for that sequence, as it already did for plain Return; `Alt+Enter` without Shift still queues a follow-up ([#11559](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11559))
- Fixed the working status (OSC 7501) disappearing in Rex and iTerm2 during runs in regular TUI mode. Rendered messages wrote OSC 133 prompt markers to the terminal, which the terminal treats as a new shell prompt; regular mode no longer writes them ([#11519](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11519))
- Fixed compaction, branch summaries, and bug-report summaries in SDK sessions passing the stored OAuth token back to the model runtime as an explicit API key. Provider auth that treats explicit keys differently from stored OAuth now sees the OAuth login, as normal prompts do ([#11520](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11520))
- Fixed a redundant system prompt update (tools, rules) when an extension set the same active tools in a different order, for example a reversed `pi.setActiveTools()` list. Tools that stay active now keep their order and newly activated tools are appended ([#11495](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11495))
- Fixed `pi.exec()` crashing pi with `RangeError: Invalid string length` when a command printed more output than fits in a string. The default output cap is the smaller of 256 MiB and the runtime string limit; past the cap, the command is terminated and the result has `truncated: true` and a nonzero exit code ([#11360](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11360))
- Fixed `pi.exec()` never returning when a command ignored SIGTERM after a timeout or abort. pi now sends SIGKILL 5 seconds later, as intended
- Fixed `pi install` and `pi remove` adding ever deeper nested entries to the npm `package-lock.json` when the agent directory is reached through a symlink, such as `~/.pi` linked into a dotfiles repo. pi now passes the resolved real path to npm ([#11358](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11358))
- MCP sign-in now rejects authorization endpoints and other OAuth metadata URLs that are not `http:` or `https:`. Before, a malicious MCP server could supply a `file:` or custom protocol URL, which pi passed to the platform URL handler.
- Automatic `fd` and `rg` downloads no longer fetch x86-64 binaries on ARM32 and other architectures without a prebuilt release. pi now warns and recommends installing the tool with the system package manager ([#11209](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11209))
- Fixed `/model` search ranking letters scattered over an earlier part of an entry above a real match, for example `opus` listing `gpt-oss-120b` and `claude-sonnet-4.5` before `claude-opus-4.1` ([#11220](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11220), [#11296](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296))
- Fixed `/resume` search matching scattered letters anywhere in session messages and IDs, for example `1024` matching inside a session UUID. Session names and working directories still match fuzzily; IDs and message text now match only as exact substrings ([#11220](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11220), [#11024](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11024), [#11296](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296))
- Fixed HTML export showing a blank page for sessions with thousands of entries ([#11225](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11225), [#11293](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11293))
- Fixed HTML export not showing system messages: the system prompt and tools, and later section updates such as after `/reload`. `pi --export` now includes the system prompt and tools too ([#11261](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11261), [#3464](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3464), [#11290](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11290))
- Fixed aborting a bash command on macOS sometimes running the next command of a list such as `long_step; next_step`. pi now stops the process group before killing it ([#11252](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11252), [#11289](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11289))
- Fixed large streamed tool calls taking excessive CPU time and memory because every delta re-parsed the accumulated arguments. Providers and agent proxy streams now parse each delta once, grammar tools no longer copy their entire input per delta, and interactive tool renderers run at most once per frame ([#9265](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9265))
- Fixed the login dialog opening sign-in URLs that are not web URLs, and printing control characters from sign-in, device-code, and info URLs, which could end a terminal hyperlink and send escape sequences to the terminal
- Fixed `tui.select.pageUp` and `tui.select.pageDown` being ignored in slash command and file autocomplete, `/settings`, and the model, scoped models, login, fork, `/mcp`, and llama.cpp selectors. In fullscreen mode, PageUp/PageDown now move an open list or autocomplete menu instead of scrolling the transcript, and a page key bound to Ctrl+V pages autocomplete instead of pasting an image ([#7629](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7629), based on [#7680](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7680) by [@muyiyr](https://github.com/muyiyr))
- Fixed tool output and `!` command output showing the parameters of control sequences with a `<`, `=` or `>` prefix as text, for example `35;59;1M` from a mouse report `ESC[<35;59;1M` or `0;276;0c` from a terminal reply `ESC[>0;276;0c`. Text after the keypad-mode sequences `ESC=` and `ESC>` is still kept ([#11377](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11377))
- Fixed `pi -e npm:<pkg>` staying on the version from the first download. On each start and `/reload`, pi now reinstalls an `-e` npm package without an exact version when the registry has a newer matching version. `pi -e git:<repo>@<branch>` likewise stayed on its first checkout and is now fetched and reset to the branch; a commit-hash ref that is already checked out is not fetched. Offline mode and failed checks keep the cached copy ([#11375](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11375), [#11590](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11590))
- Fixed Windows paths being compared case-sensitively. When the working directory and home directory differed only in drive-letter casing (`c:\Users\me` vs `C:\Users\me`), skills in `~/.agents/skills` loaded twice, as project and user skills, and were reported as name collisions. The same mismatch also re-asked for saved project trust, hid sessions in a custom session directory from `--continue` and `/resume`, and stopped `pi remove` from matching configured local packages ([#10488](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10488))
- Fixed paths next to the home directory being shown with a broken `~` prefix, for example `/home/me2/project` shown as `~2/project` when home is `/home/me`
- Fixed `pi mcp login -l` and `pi mcp logout -l` failing with `Unknown option --local.` although `pi mcp add` and `pi mcp remove` accept `-l`. With `-l`, they now require the server to be a project server. Unknown options are now reported as typed, and a mistyped server name gets a suggestion, for example `Did you mean "gurker"?`
- Fixed `pi update` naming pnpm for installs that only live under `PNPM_HOME`, for example a wrapper under `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/`. pi said "not managed by a global pnpm install"; it now names the package manager only when that manager owns the install ([#7756](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7756))
- Fixed image paste, copy, and opening the browser for sign-in failing silently on WSL when the working directory is deep. Windows programs such as `powershell.exe` and `explorer.exe` cannot start from a directory whose `\\wsl.localhost\...` path exceeds 260 characters; pi now starts these helpers from `/` ([#11592](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11592))
- Fixed the external editor failing silently, for example when the editor command is wrong or a Windows editor cannot start from a deep WSL directory. pi now shows a status message such as `External editor exited with code 1; prompt unchanged` ([#11592](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11592))
- Fixed `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` ranking a tool below tools that only mention its name in their descriptions, for example `peekaboo app` ranking `mcp__peekaboo__app` 14th. A tool matching more of the query's words now ranks above one matching fewer, a query word in a tool's name scores more than any number of mentions in its description, a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus, and long server instructions no longer lower the scores of that server's tools ([#11331](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11331))
- Fixed `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` finding nothing for Chinese, Japanese, Thai, and other non-ASCII queries, because the tokenizer kept only ASCII letters and digits. Words in any script now match, text without spaces between words such as `搜索记录` is split into words, and canonically equivalent text such as `café` and `cafe\u0301` matches ([#10816](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10816), [#11037](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11037) by [@haoqixu](https://github.com/haoqixu))
- Fixed `pi update` stopping with `git clean -fdx failed with code 1` on Windows when another pi session had a git extension's native module or executable open. Windows cannot delete such files, so the update left the new code with the old dependencies. pi now warns, installs the dependencies anyway, and retries the clean on the next update ([#11597](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11597))
- Fixed tool rows and streamed answers highlighting the same code again on every redraw. A running codemode row highlighted its whole script on every progress update and timer tick, a complete `write` row its whole file on every update and expand toggle, a streamed `write` its first 50 lines on every delta, and a streamed answer every earlier code block on every delta. Rows now reuse their last highlighting until the code, theme, or loaded grammars change, and assistant messages keep their rendered Markdown blocks while streaming ([#10971](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10971))
- Fixed resized photos being sent as multi-megabyte PNGs even when JPEG was much smaller, causing large requests to fail or time out. Image resizing now tries the smaller encoding first ([#11551](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11551))
- Fixed `pi update --extensions` reporting success without warning when npm's stale registry metadata left a package at its old version. pi now reports the installed and expected versions ([#11536](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11536))
- Fixed skill validation warnings being labeled `[Skill conflicts]` even when there was no name collision. They are now shown under `[Skill warnings]` ([#11521](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11521))
- Fixed codemode tool descriptions including entire union and multi-line output types in every request. Object unions now summarize their fields and discriminators; other multi-line types point to `describeTool()` for the full declaration ([#11501](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11501))
- Fixed the model-scope startup notice being left in the shell after exiting fullscreen mode. It now appears inside pi's fullscreen header ([#11508](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11508))
- Fixed startup from a deleted working directory crashing with an uncaught `uv_cwd` stack trace. pi now asks the user to change to an existing directory ([#11509](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11509))
- Fixed failed session writes leaving entries in memory that were absent from disk, so later entries pointed to missing parents and resumed sessions lost earlier history and tools ([#11460](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11460))
- Fixed `/tree` branch summaries ignoring the session's thinking level, which could make reasoning models reject summary requests with an unsupported `none` effort ([#11444](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11444))
- Fixed hidden thinking with an empty hidden-thinking label still adding blank rows before answers and tool calls ([#11402](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11402))
- Fixed package installation and removal printing npm audit and funding advice, including `npm audit fix` instructions that could install a second copy of pi into the package directory ([#11409](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11409))

issues.title: Anthropic provider: JSON side queries fail with 400 on Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 (forced tool_choice not supported)

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/content-generation
labels.description: AI content generation

issues.body:
**What happens.** With an `anthropic` provider on `claude-sonnet-5-5` or `claude-opus-5-5` (Qwen Code 0.26.1), side queries that request JSON send `tool_choice: {"type": "any"}`. These models reject that:

```
400 invalid_request_error: tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.
```

Path in the 0.26.1 bundle: `runSideQuery` with a `schema` → `generateJson` → `functionCallingConfig.mode: ANY` (from #6929) → `AnthropicContentGenerator.resolveToolChoice` → `{type: "any"}`. Purposes that take this path: `permission_classifier_stage1`/`stage2`, `auto-memory-recall`, `auto-memory-forget-selection`, `session-title`, `next-speaker`, `subagent-generator`. The main agent loop never forces a tool and works.

**Reproduce (API level).** `POST /v1/messages` with `"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5"`, one tool, and `"tool_choice": {"type": "any"}` returns the 400 above. The same happens for `claude-opus-5-5`; `claude-haiku-5-5` accepts it. I confirmed the API rejection directly and traced the code path in the bundle; I haven't reproduced the classifier failure in an interactive session.

**Workaround.** A bare `"fastModel": "claude-haiku-5-5"`, declared under the same `anthropic` provider, routes side queries to a model that accepts forced tool use. In an interactive 0.26.1 session on `claude-sonnet-5-5` with it set, the permission classifier, follow-up suggestion and session-title requests went to Haiku 5.5 and all returned 200. It does not cover `subagent-generator` or `auto-memory-forget-selection`: those run on the main model whatever `fastModel` says, so they would still get the 400.

**Suggested fix.** For Claude models that reject forced tool use, send `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}` with the schema tool marked `strict: true` and named in the prompt, or use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) in `generateJson`. #13919 addresses the same problem for strict OpenAI-compatible backends.

issues.title: Auto-memory catalog pruning playbook for the >10K always-on-context warning + 2 product pitfalls

issues.body:
**Related:** #14976 (warning's CJK estimate + unactionable advice) · #14982 (open PR improving the warning) · #15826 (users asking how to make the prompt go away)

Not a new bug report — a field report on what actually moves the number on the user side, plus two product-level pitfalls we hit while doing it.

## Setup

1M-token context window, CJK-heavy usage. Every session starts with:

```
Warning: Loaded always-on context (QWEN.md context files + auto-memory) uses about 10,455 tokens,
more than 10,000 tokens — the smaller of that and 15% of this model's 1,000,000 token context window.
Consider trimming long always-loaded context or moving details into on-demand files.
```

## What the number actually is

Two auto-memory `MEMORY.md` indexes (user + project) plus QWEN.md. The memory **file bodies are never injected — only the index lines are**. Our catalogs had accumulated **174 index lines ≈ 37 KB**: closed incident records, one-off diagnosis snapshots, superseded design notes. The index is append-only in practice — a memory gets a line the day it is saved and nothing ever removes it.

Per #14976 the estimator divides chars by 4 and undercounts CJK ~2×, so a Chinese-heavy catalog is even more expensive in reality than the warning claims.

## The playbook that moved the number

1. **Extract real usage signals from transcripts.** `Relevant memory` injections are not persisted (see pitfall 2), but tool calls are: one grep for `"file_path":"…/.qwen/(memories|projects/<hash>/memory)/…"` across all session `.jsonl` files under `~/.qwen/projects/*/chats/` yields every read/write of every memory file — timestamps plus per-memory session counts, i.e. "last actively used" per memory.
2. **Combine with content-closure judgment:** merged CRs, incidents already resolved/shipped, point-in-time stats baselines, preferences superseded by a newer architecture → dead weight. Standing behavior rules (feedback) and frequently-read references stay.
3. **Pruning = two steps, both required** (see pitfall 1): remove the index lines from `MEMORY.md`, **and** move the files out of the memory tree.

Result here: 174 → 143 index lines (~37 KB → 30.5 KB), 32 entries archived, warning gone on new sessions. Growth on this repo is ~1–2 new memories per working day, so it would cross 10K again within weeks — manual playbooks don't scale, which is why the suggestions below matter.

## Pitfall 1: files archived *inside* the memory tree get re-indexed

We first moved 55 stale files to `memory/archive/` and deleted their index lines (138 → 86 lines). The auto-memory indexer then re-registered every unregistered `.md` under the memory tree — the index grew back to 141 lines, with machine-truncated descriptions differing from the originals.

Working procedure: archive to a sibling directory **outside** the tree (e.g. `memories-archive-<date>/`) *and* delete the index lines. Both steps.

Suggestion: give `memory/archive/` (or an `.archive-` prefix) opt-out semantics in the indexer, or document the behavior — right now "archiving" inside the tree silently undoes itself.

## Pitfall 2: there is no way to know which memories actually trigger

- The injected "Relevant memory" blocks never appear in transcripts, so retrieval effectiveness is unauditable. Verified on the session that received an injection: the injection preamble exists nowhere in that session's `.jsonl`.
- Every session's opening context embeds the **full catalog snapshot**, so grepping transcripts for memory filenames yields ~100% false positives — "mentioned" is indistinguishable from "loaded".
- Bulk maintenance/sync passes read every memory file at once, stamping all of them "read today" and polluting any last-read analysis.

Suggestions:

- persist per-memory `lastTriggeredAt` / trigger counts (e.g. next to `user-memory-meta.json`) and surface them in the `/memory` panel (#13396 / #14230 are natural homes);
- consider auto-aging one-off `task_summary` / incident-type memories — propose archiving entries with no trigger in N days;
- once #14982 names the memory catalog as the dominant contributor, link the warning straight to that remediation path; "Consider trimming long always-loaded context" reads as "edit your QWEN.md" and does not move the number when the catalog is the driver.

labels.name: priority/P3

labels.description: AI content generation

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support an opt-in mode where local images (read via read_file / pasted) are uploaded to a user-configured object storage (e.g. Aliyun OSS) and sent to the model as a URL (`fileData.fileUri` → `image_url.url`) instead of being embedded as base64 `inlineData` in the request body.

Concretely:
- A settings block (e.g. under `model` or a new `media`/`oss` section) where the user provides OSS endpoint / bucket / accessKey (or an upload command/script) and optional URL prefix / expiry;
- When enabled, before sending a request, qwen-code uploads each local image part to OSS and replaces the `inlineData` part with a `fileData.fileUri` pointing at the (signed) URL;
- Fall back to the current base64 inline behavior when OSS is not configured or the upload fails.

### Why is this needed?

Today local images are embedded as base64 `inlineData` (`data:<mime>;base64,...`) in the request body. With several or large images the request body grows very large and can exceed model-platform request-size limits, causing failures. Remote URLs are already passed by reference (`image_url.url`), so the only gap is local images. Uploading to user-provided OSS and passing a URL keeps the request body small and lets the platform fetch the image, matching how remote images already work.

### Additional context

- Relevant code: `packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/converter.ts` — `inlineData` → `image_url: { url: dataUrl }` (base64) vs `fileData.fileUri` → `image_url: { url: fileUri }` (by reference). The URL path already exists; this feature is about producing a URL for local images via user-configured OSS upload.
- Security: credentials must come from user config / env (never hardcoded); signed URLs with expiry preferred; the upload target is fully user-controlled.
- Related (not duplicates): #3518 (pasting images as base64/data-URL, closed), #8608 (inline image render perf).

issues.body:
## What happened

Provider-backed model with a custom id in `modelProviders.openai[]`. Both documented switches were set, per `docs/users/configuration/model-providers.md`:

```json
"capabilities": { "vision": true, "agent": true },
"generationConfig": { "modalities": { "image": true } }
```

`read_file` on a PNG attachment returned:

> Unsupported image file: "image.png". This model does not support image input. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. To handle this file, try using skills if applicable…

## Measured

- The endpoint accepted the same image over a direct OpenAI-compatible call — the model was never the problem.
- A 64x64 PNG got the identical refusal, so it wasn't size either.
- The config was correct the whole time. A restart made it take effect; `settings.json` was byte-identical before and after.

## The gap

The message is accurate about the state — the resolved route genuinely had no image modality. It just isn't actionable: it points at skills, and says nothing about the two settings that decide it or that they're read at startup. It sent me down a resize path for what was a restart.

## Ask (small)

When the placeholder fires, name the model and the field that came up empty — and if that field is set in the provider entry, say the value is resolved at startup. One line, no behaviour change.

Happy to be told this is working as intended — the message wasn't wrong, just not useful.

issues.title: feat(core): let managed installs disable the models.dev catalog refresh from settings (and honor the privacy opt-out)

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/configuration
labels.description: Configuration management

labels.name: scope/settings
labels.description: Settings and preferences

labels.name: scope/data-privacy
labels.description: Data privacy concerns

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

A settings-level way to turn off the daily models.dev catalog download, so that managed
installations can disable it from system settings.

Since #11959 (v0.25.0), every `Config` initialization calls `void refreshModelCatalog()`
(`packages/core/src/models/model-catalog-refresh.ts`), which downloads
`https://models.dev/api.json` at most once every 24 hours and caches it in
`~/.qwen/model-registry.json`. The only off switches are environment variables:
`QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=off` (stop the download) and `QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV=off`
(disable the catalog entirely).

There is currently no way to disable it from settings:

- `privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled: false` and `telemetry.enabled: false` do not affect it;
- both variables are in `PROJECT_ENV_HARDCODED_EXCLUSIONS`, and `settings.env` skips entries
  for which `isHardcodedProjectEnvExclusion(key)` is true — so setting them in the `env`
  block of the **system** settings file is silently ignored too;
- the variables therefore have to be injected into the real process environment of every
  launch path (terminal shell, launchd for the Desktop app, `.desktop` entries, Windows user
  env), which a settings-based deployment cannot guarantee.

Any of the following would work for us:

1. a settings key, e.g. `model.catalogRefresh: false` (or `model.modelsDev: "off" | "bundled" | "refresh"`),
   readable from system settings; or
2. allow `QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV` / `QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH` in the `env` block of the
   system settings file (only workspace/project scopes need the exclusion); and/or
3. skip the refresh when `privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled` is `false` — the request is not
   statistics, but users who opted out of non-essential traffic generally expect no
   third-party calls besides the configured model provider.

The bundled catalog snapshot is fine to keep using offline.

## Why is this needed?

I run managed installations behind a corporate egress policy where the only allowed
outbound destination for Qwen Code is our own OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Usage statistics,
telemetry, the CLI/Web Shell update checks and web search can already be disabled from system
settings; the catalog refresh is the one automatic third-party request on every launch that
cannot. The request itself
carries no session data, but it reveals that the machine runs Qwen Code and its IP to a third
party once a day, and in our setup the catalog adds no value (the model is a custom
deployment with explicit `contextWindowSize` in `modelProviders`).

## Additional context

- Observed on v0.26.4 (standalone, macOS); same code on `main`.
- Related: #11959 (feature), #12812 (deferred review findings), #12770 / #12844 (earlier
  privacy opt-out gaps for throwaway configs, both fixed).
- Workaround for now: a local installer patch that turns `refreshModelCatalog()` into a no-op
  in managed installs.

prs.title: fix(extensions): load extension manifests saved with a UTF-8 BOM
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extension manifests saved with a UTF-8 BOM now load. The extension manager strips a leading BOM before `JSON.parse`, the same way the LSP config and TOML readers in core already do. The CLI command loader, which re-reads the manifest for a custom `commands` path, now uses the existing `stripUtf8Bom` helper. Three other readers of the same files strip it too: the mods loader (`mods/discovery.ts` `readManifest`), the classic hook loader (`hooks/hooks.json`), and Agent Plugins v1 `plugin.json` (`getAgentPluginSchemaStatus` and `loadAgentPluginManifest`).

## Why it's needed

Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM by default (`'{"name": "bomext", "version": "1.0.0"}' | Out-File -Encoding utf8 qwen-extension.json`). `JSON.parse` throws on U+FEFF, so the extension is skipped without a warning and `qwen extensions list` says `No extensions installed.` Same class as #13595 / #13944.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`npx vitest run src/extension/extensionManager.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"` in `packages/core`, and `npx vitest run src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"` in `packages/cli`. Both new tests fail on main (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

0.26.2 on Windows 11, BOM manifest in `~/.qwen/extensions/bomext`:

```
before: No extensions installed.
after:  ✓ bomext (1.0.0)
```

Manifest without the BOM lists on both. A BOM manifest missing `name` is still skipped.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux (node:24): prettier, eslint `--max-warnings 0`, `tsc --noEmit` for core, vitest `core/src/extension` (1022 passed) and `cli/src/services` + `src/config` (2896 passed), same as main plus the 2 new tests. Windows: the new core test, `tsc --noEmit` for cli (same 3 unbuilt `@qwen-code/web-templates` errors as main), and the CLI repro above.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: low. Only a leading BOM is removed before parsing, in `qwen-extension.json`, `plugin.json`, `hooks/hooks.json` and the mods manifest reader. User-visible: extensions, Agent Plugins and hooks saved with a BOM, which were silently skipped, now load.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS. `managed-package.ts` left alone.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15785

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 做了什么

带 UTF-8 BOM 的扩展清单现在可以加载。扩展管理器在 `JSON.parse` 之前去掉开头的 BOM，与 core 中 LSP 配置和 TOML 读取器的做法相同。CLI 命令加载器会为自定义 `commands` 路径重新读取清单，现在使用已有的 `stripUtf8Bom` 辅助函数。读取同类文件的另外三处也会去掉 BOM：mods 加载器（`mods/discovery.ts` 的 `readManifest`）、经典 hook 加载器（`hooks/hooks.json`）以及 Agent Plugins v1 的 `plugin.json`（`getAgentPluginSchemaStatus` 和 `loadAgentPluginManifest`）。

## 为什么需要

Windows PowerShell 5.1 默认写入 BOM（`'{"name": "bomext", "version": "1.0.0"}' | Out-File -Encoding utf8 qwen-extension.json`）。`JSON.parse` 遇到 U+FEFF 会抛错，扩展被静默跳过，`qwen extensions list` 显示 `No extensions installed.`。与 #13595 / #13944 属于同类问题。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/core` 运行 `npx vitest run src/extension/extensionManager.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"`，在 `packages/cli` 运行 `npx vitest run src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"`。两个新测试在 main 上都失败（`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`）。

### 证据（修复前后）

prs.title: feat(web-shell): edit GitHub repository settings from the channel editor
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Three settings that decide how a GitHub Channel behaves can now be changed from the Web Shell instead of only by hand-editing `settings.json` on the daemon host: which accounts may start tasks in a given repository, whether that repository answers without an @mention, and how often the notifications API is polled.

The poll interval becomes an ordinary field on the form, filed under Connection next to the API base URL. When the group policy is an allowlist, the Access control section grows one row per allowlisted repository, each with a require-mention control and a speaker control. Typing a repository into the allowlist adds its row immediately; deleting it removes the row.

Every row starts at **Inherit**, and the option label names the value being inherited — `Inherit (require a mention)`, `Inherit (allowlist only)` — so the operator can see the effective setting without opening a file. A row left at Inherit writes no key at all, so the repository keeps following the channel-wide default and a later change to that default still reaches it.

The speaker list appears whenever the row's effective policy is an allowlist, whether the row chose it or inherited it. Under an explicit "Allowlist only" an empty list means *nobody*; under an inherited policy an empty list means *no per-repository list*, so the channel-wide one applies. The two cases are deliberately different, and the helper text says which one the row is in.

## Why it's needed

The channel-wide speaker default is `open`. Narrowing it narrows every repository at once, so the only way to restrict a single repository was the file the form does not show. The practical result is that the permissive default stays in place by inertia: an operator who wants two maintainers on one repository and everyone on another has no way to express that in the UI, and an operator who wants one repository to answer without a mention has to know the key name, the nesting, and that the value is a boolean rather than a string.

This closes the gap the previous GitHub editor PR (#16096) listed under Risk & Scope: per-repository `requireMention`, the poll interval, and per-repository sender allowlists remained editable only through `settings.json`.

The poll interval turned out to be more than a rendering gap. The daemon's stored-value guard rejects a field the platform has not declared, so before this change a GitHub Channel could not persist `pollInterval` through the management API at all — the value was reachable only by editing the file directly. Declaring the field is what makes it settable, not just visible.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open Settings → Channels → edit a GitHub Channel whose group policy is Allowlist and whose allowlist names two repositories, one of them already customized in `settings.json`. Confirm the customized row shows its stored values rather than "Inherit", and the other row names what it inherits from the channel-wide settings. The poll interval sits under Connection and shows the stored number.

Change one row's require-mention to "Answer without a mention" and its speaker policy to "Allowlist only", type two logins, and save. The stored configuration gains a boolean `requireMention: false` and a string array `allowedUsers` under that repository's key, and nothing else moves. Set both controls back to Inherit and save again: both keys disappear, and the repository inherits once more.

Now save a channel you have not touched at all. The `groups` object must come out byte-identical, including keys this form does not model (`dispatchMode`, `groupHistoryLimit`), an empty allowlist (`allowedUsers: []`, which means nobody), and a list stored with no policy beside it (which inherits the policy but overrides the members). Those last two shapes cannot be expressed by a tri-state control plus a text box, so the save compares each field against the same reading of the stored object it seeded the draft from and only writes what actually changed.

Finally, open an Email channel: its poll interval has moved from Credentials to Connection. The section map is keyed by field name, so the same setting on a second polling platform files the same way. A test pins this rather than leaving it to prose.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Captures from the repository's own visual harness: the real Web Shell in Chromium at the harness viewport (1280×800), both themes, with the daemon's HTTP layer mocked by `page.route`. The mocked daemon means the pictures prove rendering, not backend behaviour; what gets stored is covered by the unit tests below. Both arms use the **same stored channel** — two allowlisted repositories, one customized with `requireMention: false` and a two-login allowlist, one empty, and `pollInterval: 30000` — so the difference is the form, not the fixture.

The before arm was produced by reverting the five source files to the base commit and running a temporary scenario that asserts the rows and the interval field are **absent** (`toHaveCount(0)`), so the pair cannot accidentally be two pictures of the same arm. All four PNGs have distinct hashes and were verified byte-for-byte after publishing.

**Per-repository settings — dark**

| Before | After |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![Before: the GitHub channel editor with an allowlist of two repositories and only channel-wide speaker controls; the stored per-repository settings and poll interval are invisible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/01-repositories-before-dark.png) | ![After: one row per allowlisted repository, the customized one showing its explicit values and the other naming what it inherits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/07-repositories-after-dark-v3.png) |

**Per-repository settings — light**

| Before | After |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![Before, light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/03-repositories-before-light.png) | ![After, light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/08-repositories-after-light-v3.png) |

What the comparison shows:

- Before, the allowlist is a text box and the only speaker controls are channel-wide; the customized repository's `requireMention: false` and its two-login allowlist are nowhere on screen. After, each repository has its own row showing exactly those values.
- The empty repository's row reads `Inherit (allowlist only)`, naming the channel-wide policy it follows instead of silently materializing it.
- The poll interval is absent before and reads `30000` after, under Connection.

Verification commands run locally:

```text
$ cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/channels client/i18n.test.ts client/build-artifact.test.ts
Test Files  7 passed (7)
     Tests  281 passed (281)      # includes the 40 build-artifact guards, re-run against a fresh build

$ cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
Test Files  25 passed (25)
     Tests  1689 passed (1689)

$ cd packages/channels/github && npx vitest run
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  221 passed (221)

$ cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/commands/channel src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
Test Files  28 passed (28)
     Tests  700 passed (700)

$ npx eslint <changed files>            # no output
$ npx prettier --check <changed paths>  # All matched files use Prettier code style!
$ cd packages/web-shell && npm run build                 # BUILD_EXIT=0, three vite builds + tsc + notices
$ cd packages/web-shell && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit   # WEB_TSC_EXIT=0, zero output
$ cd packages/cli && npx tsc --noEmit                     # CLI_TSC_EXIT=0
$ cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test-fence.json   # SDK_TSC_EXIT=0
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-base      # BASE_BUILD_EXIT=0
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-github    # GH_BUILD_EXIT=0

$ npx playwright test --config playwright.visuals.config.ts -g "GitHub channel"
  4 passed (40.0s)
```

63 new tests: 41 on the editor state (override reading, canonical keys, exact round-trip, the two inexpressible shapes, boolean and array writing, inherit deleting the key, unmodelled-key preservation, case retyping, removal, chat platforms unaffected, the poll interval staying optional, and a five-part invariant sweep over twelve stored shapes crossed with every single-field edit and with the stored and final group policies, through the real save path) and 22 on the component (rows per repository, rows appearing as you type, inherited-value labels, speaker-input visibility both ways, row labelling for screen readers, the saved request body, the interval's section, Email's interval, and chat platforms showing no rows).

Every behavioural claim is pinned by a mutation that was introduced and then reverted from a byte-level backup. Forty-one mutations (M1–M41) across six rounds, every one killed by exactly the cases that describe it: materializing the resolved require-mention (8 cases fail), replacing the stored group object instead of merging (8), keying the draft by the stored case (1), keeping overrides for removed repositories (1), writing require-mention as a string (3), dropping the interval from the section map (1), and showing the speaker input regardless of policy (1).

The casing mutation is worth a note: the first draft of the test list did **not** kill it, because the save path lower-cases stored keys and would have preserved the settings verbatim even with a mis-keyed draft. The defect would have surfaced only as a row quietly showing "Inherit" for a repository that has stored settings. A case asserting the draft's keys are canonical was added to close that hole.

A multi-pass audit then ran over the whole diff — eight passes, open-ended and adversarial alternating, until two consecutive passes found nothing. It corrected the clamp's blast radius in four places (the getter clamps, and Email is exempt because it does not extend the base at all, not because of its own bound), changed the speaker hint from "keep the channel-wide list" to "use" because a repository storing its own list is not keeping the channel-wide one and clearing the box widens it, passed the group policy into the retained-settings alert instead of deriving it a second time, and fixed three documentation defects: a design decision that still described the superseded Critical implementation, a user-doc paragraph that contradicted the next one on what clearing an explicit allowlist does, and a files table missing nine of the PR's files. The sweep's own oracle was attacked too: its first version would have excused the round-1 Critical, and the correction is witnessed by re-running that mutation against both versions. The re-captured rows are published as `-v3` under new names; #16096's editor capture hashes identically and was left alone.

### Tested on

|     OS     |  Status   |
| :--------: | :-------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |    ✅     |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, vitest with jsdom for the component tests. The host Chromium cannot load `libatk-1.0.so.0` and `sudo` needs a password, so both visual arms ran inside a Playwright container image (Playwright 1.61.1, Chromium 1228, Node 22) with this worktree mounted, writing PNGs back to the host. Only the two GitHub editor scenarios were run, not the whole visual suite.

One environment fault is worth recording so it is not mistaken for a code fault: the first full build failed with `TS2339` for `timingSamples`, `failures`, and `hasTurnError` in files this PR never touches. The local `packages/sdk-typescript/dist` was dated Oct 31 while those properties were added to the SDK source by #16111, already in main. Rebuilding the SDK cleared them; the build then exited 0 with zero TS errors.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the editor now writes per-repository `requireMention`, `senders`, and `allowedUsers`, so a mistaken row edit changes who can drive the agent in that repository. The inherit option names the value it inherits precisely so that switching a row to "Anyone" is a visible widening rather than a silent one. Switching a row to "Anyone" keeps a stored speaker list that has names in it — inert under an open policy, and preserved so returning to an allowlist does not destroy the operator's work. An empty list is released instead, because keeping it would deny everyone while the row reads as inheriting.
- Cross-package scope: the per-repository half needs no daemon change — the store already validates all three shapes, which was measured against the real store rather than inferred from reading the validator. The poll interval does cross packages, and the review is why: an unbounded interval lets the form persist a hot loop (Node clamps a timeout past its 32-bit range to 1 ms), so number descriptors gain a `maximum` beside `exclusiveMinimum`, mirrored in the SDK types, the registry's metadata validation, the store and the editor, with GitHub declaring the same one-day ceiling Email already enforces. `PollingChannelBase` also clamps to that ceiling, so a hand-written configuration cannot hot-loop either. Of the three channels that extend it, DWS overrides the getter with a constant and Email does not extend it at all (it parses and bounds its own interval), so GitHub and GitLab are the only two the clamp reaches. Declaring the field also required an unchanged-value tolerance in both the editor and the store, so a channel storing a value the runtime tolerates (`pollInterval: 0`) is not stranded on an unrelated edit — scoped to the *range* of an unchanged finite number, because an existing contract test pins that an unchanged scalar of the wrong type is still rejected. The section map is keyed by field name, so **Email's existing poll interval moves from Credentials to Connection**; a test pins that too.
- Review history: four rounds plus a multi-pass audit. The first found one access-control defect (choosing an allowlist with an empty box persisted no list, so the runtime handed the channel-wide list back). The second found its mirror (leaving an allowlist kept the empty list, so inheritance could never return the members), a hint derived from the draft rather than from what the save writes, the unbounded interval, the stranded-channel regression, settings that outlive the policy switch, three documentation contradictions, and twelve behaviours whose tests stayed green when the behaviour was removed. All are addressed in this branch. A third round found the hint asking the projection about the current draft instead of about an empty box, row edits discarded when the policy was switched before saving, an interval ceiling that replaced previously honoured values with 60 s instead of clamping them, an alert claiming settings still apply under Disabled, a range message inventing a lower bound, and five more unwitnessed paths — all addressed the same way. Across those rounds and the audit that followed, the suite grew from 28 to 63 new tests and the mutation count from 7 to 41; the audit ran eight passes over the whole diff and its findings are reported in a separate comment. A fourth round found two access-control regressions in the branch that retains repository settings when the policy leaves Allowlist: it was gated on the stored policy, so edits made during a temporary switch were dropped on a channel that was already open; it iterated stored groups only, so a repository added during that visit was never written; and it projected one lower-cased draft onto both spellings of a conflicting alias, widening a repository nobody edited while the conflict check stayed silent. All three are fixed, each pinned by a case that asserts the admitted set and by its own mutation, and the sweep that missed them now crosses the policy dimension as well.
- Not validated / out of scope: no run against the real GitHub API — the notification payload is never fetched from github.com in this verification. Everything short of that is now measured rather than inferred: a live daemon built from this branch served the descriptor over HTTP, accepted and refused the right upserts, and the persisted configuration was fed into a real `GithubChannel` to check who the sender gate actually admits. Only the two GitHub visual scenarios ran. The channel-wide `groups["*"].requireMention` is still not editable (it is the value every row inherits, and exposing it is a separate decision), nor are `dispatchMode` or `groupHistoryLimit`. The group-policy default divergence is untouched and tracked in #16144.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No stored configuration changes meaning, and an untouched save is byte-identical. A new channel's poll interval stays absent rather than persisting the descriptor default, so the runtime keeps owning its 60-second default. Two in-flight PRs touch files this one also edits — #16117 adds unrelated fields at the end of the same GitHub descriptor and edits the same user doc, #16106 edits the same locale file — so expect a trivial rebase rather than a semantic conflict.
- Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-github-repository-settings/docs/design/github-channel-repository-settings.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-github-repository-settings/docs/design/github-channel-repository-settings.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including the compare-with-initial write rule, the eleven design decisions, constraints, risks, acceptance criteria, and the two open questions.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #16096, closing the per-repository gap it listed under Risk & Scope. Related to #16144 (the group-policy default divergence), which this PR deliberately does not change.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

决定 GitHub 渠道行为的三项设置，现在可以从 Web Shell 修改，而不必再到 daemon 宿主机上手改 `settings.json`：哪些账号可以在某个仓库里发起任务、该仓库是否无需 @ 就响应、以及多久轮询一次通知 API。

轮询间隔成为表单上的一个普通字段，归入「连接」、与 API 基础 URL 同区。当群组策略为允许列表时，「访问控制」分区会为每个已允许的仓库长出一行，各带一个「需要 @」控件与一个发言人控件。在允许列表里输入一个仓库会立刻出现它的行，删掉则行消失。

每一行都从**继承**起步，且选项标签会写明继承的是什么——`继承（需要 @）`、`继承（仅允许列表）`——操作者不必打开文件就能看见生效设置。保持在「继承」的行一个键都不写，所以该仓库继续跟随渠道级默认，之后修改那个默认仍然能到达它。

只要该行的**生效**策略是允许列表，发言人列表就会出现，无论是它自己选的还是继承来的。在显式「仅允许列表」下，空列表意味着*没有人*；在继承策略下，空列表意味着*没有按仓库的列表*，于是渠道级列表生效。这两种情况被有意区分，辅助文案会说明当前行处于哪一种。

## 为什么需要

渠道级发言人默认是 `open`。收窄它等于一次性收窄所有仓库，所以只限制单个仓库的唯一途径，就是表单不展示的那个文件。实际结果是放开的默认值靠惯性一直留在原地：想让一个仓库只给两位维护者、另一个仓库对所有人开放的操作者，在 UI 里无法表达；想让某个仓库无需 @ 就响应的操作者，则必须知道键名、嵌套层级，以及那个值是布尔而不是字符串。

这补上了上一个 GitHub 编辑器 PR（#16096）在 Risk & Scope 里列出的缺口：按仓库的 `requireMention`、轮询间隔、按仓库的发言人允许列表当时仍只能改 `settings.json`。

轮询间隔还不只是渲染缺口。daemon 的既存值守卫会拒绝平台未声明的字段，所以在本改动之前，GitHub 渠道根本无法通过管理 API 持久化 `pollInterval`——那个值只能直接改文件才碰得到。声明这个字段让它变得**可设置**，而不只是可见。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

打开 设置 → 渠道 → 编辑一个群组策略为允许列表、允许列表里有两个仓库（其中一个已在 `settings.json` 里自定义过）的 GitHub 渠道。确认已自定义的那行显示它的既存值而不是「继承」，另一行则写明它从渠道级设置继承的是什么。轮询间隔在「连接」下，显示已存的数字。

把一行的「需要 @」改成「无需 @ 也响应」、发言人策略改成「仅允许列表」，输入两个登录名，保存。落盘配置在该仓库键下多出布尔 `requireMention: false` 与字符串数组 `allowedUsers`，其它一概不动。把两个控件都改回「继承」再保存：两个键都消失，该仓库重新回到继承。

接着保存一个你完全没碰过的渠道。`groups` 对象必须逐字节不变，包括本表单不建模的键（`dispatchMode`、`groupHistoryLimit`）、空允许列表（`allowedUsers: []`，意为没有人），以及只有列表没有策略的形态（继承策略但覆盖成员）。最后这两种形态无法用「三态控件 + 文本框」表达，所以保存时会把每个字段与「生成草稿时对已存对象的同一份读取」比对，只写真正变化的部分。

最后打开一个 Email 渠道：它的轮询间隔已从「应用凭据」移到「连接」。分区映射按字段名生效，所以第二个轮询平台上的同一个设置以同样方式归类。这一点由测试钉住，而不是只写在文字里。

### 证据（改动前与改动后）

截图来自仓库自带的视觉测试装置：真实 Web Shell 在 Chromium 里渲染，视口与套件一致（1280×800），暗亮两套主题，daemon 的 HTTP 层由 `page.route` mock。因为 daemon 是 mock 的，这些图证明的是渲染，不是后端行为；真正落盘的内容由下面的单测覆盖。两臂使用**同一个已存渠道**——两个已允许仓库，一个自定义了 `requireMention: false` 与两人允许列表，一个为空，且 `pollInterval: 30000`——所以差别在表单，不在 fixture。

改动前那一臂是把五个源码文件回退到基线提交后，跑一个临时场景得到的，该场景断言这些行与间隔字段**不存在**（`toHaveCount(0)`），因此这组图不可能意外变成同一臂的两张。四张 PNG 哈希互不相同，发布后逐张做了字节级核对。

**按仓库设置 —— 暗色**

| 改动前 | 改动后 |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![改动前：GitHub 渠道编辑器里有两个仓库的允许列表，但只有渠道级发言人控件；已存的按仓库设置与轮询间隔都看不见](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/01-repositories-before-dark.png) | ![改动后：每个已允许仓库一行，已自定义的那行显示它的显式值，另一行写明它继承的是什么](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/07-repositories-after-dark-v3.png) |

**按仓库设置 —— 亮色**

| 改动前 | 改动后 |
| :----: | :---: |
| ![改动前的亮色主题](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/03-repositories-before-light.png) | ![改动后的亮色主题](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repository-settings/08-repositories-after-light-v3.png) |

对比说明了什么：

- 改动前，允许列表是一个文本框，唯一的发言人控件是渠道级的；已自定义仓库的 `requireMention: false` 与它的两人允许列表在屏幕上无处可寻。改动后，每个仓库都有自己的行，显示的正是那些值。
- 空仓库那行写着 `继承（仅允许列表）`，把它跟随的渠道级策略说出来，而不是悄悄把它物化。
- 轮询间隔改动前不存在，改动后在「连接」下显示 `30000`。

```text
Test Files  7 passed (7)

$ cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
Test Files  25 passed (25)

$ cd packages/channels/github && npx vitest run
Test Files  2 passed (2)

$ cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/commands/channel src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
Test Files  28 passed (28)

$ npx eslint <改动文件>                 # 无输出
$ npx prettier --check <改动路径>       # All matched files use Prettier code style!
$ cd packages/web-shell && npm run build                 # BUILD_EXIT=0，三个 vite 构建 + tsc + notices
$ cd packages/web-shell && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit   # WEB_TSC_EXIT=0，零输出
$ cd packages/cli && npx tsc --noEmit                     # CLI_TSC_EXIT=0
$ cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test-fence.json   # SDK_TSC_EXIT=0
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-base      # BASE_BUILD_EXIT=0
$ npm run build --workspace=@qwen-code/channel-github    # GH_BUILD_EXIT=0

$ npx playwright test --config playwright.visuals.config.ts -g "GitHub channel"
  4 passed (40.0s)
```

新增 63 条测试：41 条针对编辑器状态（覆盖读取、规范键、精确往返、两种无法表达的形态、布尔与数组写入、继承删键、未建模键保留、重打大小写、删除仓库、聊天平台不受影响、轮询间隔保持可选，以及一组五部分不变式扫描——十二种存量形态叉乘每一种单字段编辑、再叉乘存量与最终群组策略，走真实保存路径），22 条针对组件（每个仓库一行、输入即新增行、继承值标签、发言人输入两种可见性、供读屏使用的行标注、保存的请求体、间隔所在分区、Email 的间隔、以及聊天平台不显示行）。

每条行为主张都用「引入变异再从字节级备份还原」钉住。六轮共四十一个变异（M1–M41），每个都只让描述它的用例变红：物化解析后的「需要 @」（8 条失败）、用替换而非合并处理已存群组对象（8 条）、按已存大小写给草稿键（1 条）、为已删仓库保留覆盖（1 条）、把「需要 @」写成字符串（3 条）、把间隔从分区映射里去掉（1 条）、无视策略显示发言人输入（1 条）。

大小写那个变异值得一提：测试清单的初稿**没能**杀掉它，因为保存路径会把已存键小写化，即使草稿键错了也会原样保留设置。缺陷只会表现为「一个有既存设置的仓库，它的行悄悄显示『继承』」。为此补了一条断言草稿键为规范形式的用例。

随后对整个 diff 做了多轮审计——共八遍，无方向与对抗交替，直到连续两遍查不出问题。它修正了四处关于钳制影响面的表述（getter 是钳制，而 Email 豁免是因为它根本不继承该基类，不是因为它自己的上限）；把发言人提示从「沿用渠道级列表」改为「使用」，因为存着自己那份列表的仓库并不是在沿用渠道级列表，而清空输入框会放宽它；把群组策略传进保留设置告警，而不是再推导一次；并修掉三处文档缺陷：一条仍在描述被取代的 Critical 实现的设计决策、一段在「清空显式允许列表会怎样」上与下一段自相矛盾的用户文档、以及一张漏掉 PR 九个文件的文件表。扫描自己的预言也被攻击：第一版会豁免第一轮的 Critical，修正的承重性由「对两个版本重跑同一变异」见证。重出的行截图以新文件名 `-v3` 发布；#16096 的编辑器截图哈希完全一致，未作改动。

### 测试过的平台

|     OS     |  状态   |
| :--------: | :-----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅    |

### 环境（可选）

Linux，组件测试用 vitest + jsdom。宿主 Chromium 加载不了 `libatk-1.0.so.0` 且 `sudo` 需要密码，所以两臂视觉截图都在 Playwright 容器镜像里出（Playwright 1.61.1、Chromium 1228、Node 22，挂载本工作区），PNG 写回宿主机。只跑了两个 GitHub 编辑器场景，没有跑整套视觉套件。

有一个环境故障值得记录，以免被当成代码故障：第一次完整构建在本 PR 从未触碰的文件里报 `timingSamples`、`failures`、`hasTurnError` 的 `TS2339`。本机 `packages/sdk-typescript/dist` 停在 10 月 31 日，而这些属性由已在 main 的 #16111 加入 SDK 源码。重建 SDK 后清零，构建随即 exit 0、零 TS 报错。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：编辑器现在会写按仓库的 `requireMention`、`senders`、`allowedUsers`，所以一次误改行就会改变谁能在那个仓库里驱动 agent。「继承」选项之所以写明它继承的值，正是为了让把一行切到「任何人」成为一次可见的放开，而不是静默的。把一行切到「任何人」会保留其中有名字的已存发言人列表——该列表在开放策略下不起作用，保留它是为了改回允许列表时不毁掉操作者的劳动。空列表则会被释放，因为留着它会在该行读作「继承」的同时拒绝所有人。
- 跨包范围：按仓库那一半不需要改 daemon——store 本来就已校验这三种形态，这一点是对真实 store 实测出来的，而不是读校验器推断的。轮询间隔确实跨了包，而原因来自评审：无上界的间隔能让表单落盘一个热循环（Node 会把超过 32 位范围的 timeout 钳制为 1 毫秒），所以 number 描述符在 `exclusiveMinimum` 之外新增 `maximum`，并在 SDK 类型、注册表元数据校验、store 与编辑器里镜像，GitHub 声明与 Email 已在运行时强制的同一个一天花板。`PollingChannelBase` 也会钳制到该天花板，因此手写配置同样无法热循环。继承它的三个渠道里，DWS 用常量覆盖了该 getter，Email 根本不继承它（自己解析并限制间隔），所以钳制实际只作用于 GitHub 与 GitLab 两个。声明该字段还要求编辑器与 store 都加入「未变更值容忍」，这样一个存着运行时本就容忍的值（`pollInterval: 0`）的渠道不会在一次无关编辑上被困住——容忍只作用于未变更有限数字的*区间*，因为既有契约测试钉住「未变更但类型错误的标量仍要被拒绝」。分区映射按字段名生效，所以 **Email 既有的轮询间隔会从「应用凭据」移到「连接」**；这一点也有测试钉住。
- 评审历史：四轮评审加一次多遍审计。第一轮找到一处访问控制缺陷（选「仅允许列表」且输入框为空时不落盘列表，于是运行时把渠道级列表交了回来）。第二轮找到它的镜像（离开允许列表时保留了空列表，于是继承永远无法交回成员）、由草稿而非保存结果推导的提示文案、无上界的间隔、把既有渠道困住的回归、比策略活得更久的设置、三处文档矛盾，以及十二项「行为被删除后测试仍然全绿」的行为。全部已在本分支处理。第三轮又发现：提示问的是当前草稿而不是空输入框的投影、切策略后保存会丢弃行内修改、间隔上界把原本被尊重的值替换成 60 秒而不是钳制、告警在 Disabled 下仍声称设置生效、范围消息凭空造下界，以及另外五条未被见证的路径——同样全部处理。连同随后的审计，新增测试从 28 条增至 63 条、变异从 7 个增至 41 个；审计对整个 diff 跑了八遍，其发现另有一条评论报告。 第四轮在「策略离开允许列表时保留仓库设置」的分支里找到两处访问控制回归：它按存量策略把门，所以本来就是 open 的渠道上、临时切换期间做的编辑被丢弃；它只遍历已存群组，所以那次访问中新增的仓库从未被写出；它还把一份小写草稿投影到冲突别名的两个拼写上，在冲突校验静默的同时放宽了一个无人编辑的仓库。三处都已修复，各由一条断言准入集的用例与自己的变异钉住；放过它们的那组扫描现在也叉乘策略这一维。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：没有对真实 GitHub API 跑端到端——本验证从不向 github.com 取通知 payload。除此之外都已实测而非推断：用本分支构建的活 daemon 经 HTTP 下发描述符、接受与拒绝正确的 upsert，并把落盘配置喂进真实的 `GithubChannel`，核对发言人闸门究竟放行谁。只跑了两个 GitHub 视觉场景。渠道级 `groups["*"].requireMention` 仍不可编辑（它是每行继承的值，暴露它是另一个决定），`dispatchMode` 与 `groupHistoryLimit` 也同样不在本次范围内。群组策略默认值的分歧未触碰，记录在 #16144。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。已存配置的含义不变，未触碰的保存逐字节相同。新渠道的轮询间隔保持缺失，而不是持久化描述符默认值，因此 60 秒默认仍归运行时所有。有两个在途 PR 也改了本 PR 涉及的文件——#16117 在同一份 GitHub 描述符末尾加了不相关的字段并改了同一份用户文档，#16106 改了同一份语言文件——所以预期是一次平凡的 rebase，而不是语义冲突。
- 设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-github-repository-settings/docs/design/github-channel-repository-settings.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/web-shell-github-repository-settings/docs/design/github-channel-repository-settings.zh-CN.md)。两个版本完整且同步，包括「与初始读取比对」的写入规则、十一条设计决策、约束、风险、验收标准与两个待决问题。

## 关联 Issue

承接 #16096，补上它在 Risk & Scope 里列出的按仓库缺口。与 #16144（群组策略默认值分歧）相关，本 PR 有意不改那个默认值。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): show a Channel event timeline
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Channel events page to the Web Shell and the read-only route behind it. Every Channel now records what it did — the inbound messages it accepted, the ones it skipped and the machine reason for each skip, the replies it published or suppressed, its inbound task transitions, and the result of each poll — into one bounded journal per Channel. The new page shows those events as a cross-Channel timeline for the current workspace, with a Channel filter and an event-type filter, and refreshes every five seconds. Events carry routing decisions, identifiers, and errors only; message text is never written to the journal.

## Why it's needed

When a Channel does not answer a comment, the only way to find out why is to read the daemon log. The Channel management page shows configuration and a runtime badge, so an operator cannot tell from the Web Shell whether a notification was filtered by `reasonFilter`, dropped because the comment did not mention the bot, rejected by a sender gate, deduplicated, or answered but published as a suppressed comment. The publication audit, the inbound task store, and the notification cursor each answer a different question, and none of them is readable by the daemon. This gives the operator one place that answers "what did my Channels do, and why did that message produce no reply?".

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a daemon with a Channel configured, for example a GitHub Channel with `reasonFilter: ["mention"]` on a test repository, then open the Web Shell and click the new Channel events entry in the sidebar (or navigate to `/channel-events`). Pick the workspace that owns the Channel in the workspace selector — with more than one registered workspace, a Channel started in a secondary one is only reachable after selecting it.
2. Before any session exists, a notification filtered out by `reasonFilter` already appears as an `inbound` / `skipped` event with reason `reason_filter`. A comment that does not mention the bot appears with reason `mention_required`; a comment already handled in an earlier poll appears with reason `duplicate`.
3. After a mention triggers a turn, the timeline shows the accepted inbound message, the task transitions, and the publication outcome (`posting` then `posted`, or `suppressed` for the no-reply sentinel, or `failed` with the error).
4. Poll results appear as `poll` / `ok` with the notification count and duration, or `poll` / `failed` with the consecutive-error count and backoff.
5. The Channel dropdown narrows the timeline to one instance and the type buttons narrow it to one event type; both are sent to the daemon as query parameters, so a busy workspace does not have to load everything to filter it.

Route-level checks: `GET /workspace/channels/events?limit=3` returns the newest three events with `truncated: true` and `Cache-Control: no-store`; `?type=bogus`, `?limit=0`, and `?since=yesterday` return 400 with `invalid_channel_management_request`; an untrusted workspace returns 403; the same journal never appears under a different workspace's route. `channel` repeats once per instance name, because a Channel name may legally contain a comma.

Unit coverage: `cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run src/channel-events.test.ts`; `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/routes/workspace-channel-management.test.ts`; `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/channels/ChannelEventsPage.test.tsx`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: no Channel events entry exists and `GET /workspace/channels/events` is not served (an empty journal answers 404 from the SPA fallback rather than JSON).

After: the whole chain was driven end to end on a local daemon — the **real `GithubAdapter` with real Octokit over real HTTP** against a local GitHub-compatible API, a real agent turn against a local OpenAI-compatible model, and the page rendered in real Chromium over CDP. **Nothing was seeded into the journal**: every row below was written by the adapter itself. Only GitHub's servers and the model are local; no real repository, account or credential was used.

![Channel events timeline earned from real traffic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-01-en-timeline.png)

The model's reply was really published — the adapter POSTed it to the GitHub API, and the journal carries `outbound/posting` → `outbound/posted` with the session id. The type filter narrows the timeline and the request carries the filter:

![Filtered to outbound publications](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-02-en-outbound.png)

The Channel menu lists the real instance, and selecting it narrows the timeline:

![Channel menu with the real instance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-06-en-channel-menu.png)

One real poll that filtered 300 notifications writes 20 individual rows plus one counted row, so a redelivered batch cannot push the useful rows out of the page's window:

![Collapsed reason_filter row with its count](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-09-en-inbound-collapsed.png)

When the result is clipped the page says so — here over a journal that really outgrew the page's 200-row request:

![Completeness banner over real truncated data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-04-en-truncated.png)

The Chinese UI uses the same 频道 term as the existing Channels entry, and renders the collapsed count too:

![Chinese timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-05-zh-timeline.png)

![Chinese collapsed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-10-zh-collapsed.png)

The sidebar entry sits directly below Channels (the standalone shell uses the icon rail, so the entry is an activity icon with the `Channel events` label as its accessible name):

![Sidebar entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/02-sidebar-rail.png)

Measured on that real run: the page issued one journal request every 5 s while visible (3 requests over 12 s). A single real 500 from the API was absorbed by the adapter's own retry and the poll still reported `ok` with `durationMs: 1009`; three consecutive failures produced `poll/failed` with `consecutiveErrors: 1` and `backoffMs: 2000`, then recovered. A model emitting `<no-reply/>` produced `outbound/suppressed` and posted nothing; a failing publication produced `outbound/failed` carrying the API error; a failing model produced `task/failed` with `attempts: 1`; a sender outside the group allowlist produced `inbound/skipped` with `group_not_allowlisted`. Across 5,594 journal rows scanned, none contained message text. Sustained traffic really rotated the journal and it stayed bounded (`.1` at 1,048,640 bytes, files 0600, directory 0700).

The workspace-switch capture below is from the earlier seeded-journal run and is kept because it shows the two-workspace selector; the qualified route's isolation was re-checked live in the real-traffic run, where another workspace's route never returns this journal.

![Secondary workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/02-secondary-workspace-v2.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Node 24, `npm run build && npm run bundle`, `node dist/cli.js serve --require-auth` with a temporary `QWEN_HOME`, a local GitHub-compatible HTTP service and a local OpenAI-compatible model endpoint (placeholder key, no real credentials in the daemon environment), and chrome-headless-shell driven over CDP for the page assertions. Model calls were made against the local endpoint only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: one synchronous journal append per inbound, skip, task transition, and poll event, in the message path. Each record is a single JSON line, the file rotates at 1 MiB to one backup, and a write failure is swallowed into a single stderr line so diagnostics cannot break message handling. The read path is asynchronous and chunked so it cannot stall the daemon: 256 KiB per journal file, 4 MiB per request, 32 files (freshest first), 500 returned records, and anything those bounds clip sets `truncated`. A scope directory that cannot be read answers 5xx rather than an empty list. The page pauses polling while its tab is hidden. A GitHub poll that filters more than 20 notifications journals the first 20 and collapses the rest into one row carrying `detail.filtered`, because the poll cursor stays put while a task is recoverable and the same batch would otherwise be re-journaled every poll.
- Not validated / out of scope: GitHub's real servers (the full chain was exercised against a local GitHub-compatible API with the real adapter, so provider-side behaviour such as notification pagination and read-state timing is still unverified); macOS and Windows were not run locally, although rotation removes the previous backup before renaming so it does not depend on POSIX rename-onto-existing semantics. The page shows events for the resolved workspace only, not across registered workspaces.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new capability bit (the page and route are gated by the existing `channel_management`), no settings changes, and no message text is persisted.

Design: [2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.md](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/channel-events-timeline/docs/design/2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.md) / [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/channel-events-timeline/docs/design/2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.zh-CN.md).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在 Web Shell 新增「频道事件」页面及其背后的只读路由。现在每个频道都会记录自己做了什么——接收了哪些入站消息、跳过了哪些消息以及每次跳过的机器原因、发表或抑制了哪些回复、入站任务如何流转、每次轮询的结果——写入按频道划分的有界日志。新页面把当前工作区的所有频道事件展示为一条跨频道时间线，支持按频道和事件类型过滤，并每五秒刷新一次。事件只携带路由决策、标识符与错误信息，绝不写入消息正文。

## 为什么需要它

当频道没有回复某条评论时，唯一的排查方式是读 daemon 日志。频道管理页只显示配置和运行时徽标，运维人员无法从 Web Shell 判断：通知是被 `reasonFilter` 过滤了、因为评论没有 @ 机器人被丢弃、被发送方门禁拒绝、被去重跳过，还是已经回答但被抑制发表。发表审计、入站任务存储和通知游标各自回答的是不同问题，而且 daemon 都读不到。本 PR 给出一个统一入口，回答「我的频道做了什么，为什么那条消息没有回复」。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 用配置了频道的 daemon 启动，例如在测试仓库上配置 `reasonFilter: ["mention"]` 的 GitHub 频道，然后打开 Web Shell，点击侧边栏新增的频道事件入口（或直接访问 `/channel-events`）。在工作区选择器里选中拥有该频道的工作区——注册了多个工作区时，在次工作区启动的频道只有选中它之后才可见。
2. 在还没有任何会话时，被 `reasonFilter` 过滤的通知就会以 `inbound` / `skipped`、原因 `reason_filter` 出现；没有 @ 机器人的评论以 `mention_required` 出现；上一轮已处理过的评论以 `duplicate` 出现。
3. @ 触发一轮后，时间线依次出现被接收的入站消息、任务状态流转、发表结果（`posting` 后 `posted`，或 no-reply 哨兵对应的 `suppressed`，或带错误的 `failed`）。
4. 轮询结果以 `poll` / `ok`（带通知条数与耗时）或 `poll` / `failed`（带连续错误次数与退避）出现。
5. 频道下拉把时间线收窄到单个实例，类型按钮收窄到单个事件类型；两者都作为查询参数发给 daemon，繁忙工作区不必先加载全部数据再过滤。

路由级检查：`GET /workspace/channels/events?limit=3` 返回最新三条并带 `truncated: true` 与 `Cache-Control: no-store`；`?type=bogus`、`?limit=0`、`?since=yesterday` 返回 400 与 `invalid_channel_management_request`；不受信任的工作区返回 403；同一份日志绝不会出现在另一个工作区的路由下。`channel` 按实例名逐个重复传参，因为频道名允许包含逗号。

单元覆盖：`cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run src/channel-events.test.ts`；`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/routes/workspace-channel-management.test.ts`；`cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/channels/ChannelEventsPage.test.tsx`。

### 证据（改动前与改动后）

改动前：不存在频道事件入口，`GET /workspace/channels/events` 也不提供服务（空日志时该路径由 SPA 兜底返回 HTML 而不是 JSON）。

改动后：整条链路在本地 daemon 上端到端跑通——**真实 `GithubAdapter` + 真实 Octokit + 真实 HTTP** 对接本地 GitHub 兼容服务，真实 agent 回合对接本地 OpenAI 兼容模型，页面在真实 Chromium 中经 CDP 渲染。**日志没有任何预置**：下面每一行都是适配器自己写的。只有 GitHub 服务端与模型是本地的，未使用任何真实仓库、账号或凭证。

![真实流量产生的频道事件时间线](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-01-en-timeline.png)

模型的回复真的发表了——适配器把它 POST 到了 GitHub API，日志里对应 `outbound/posting` → `outbound/posted` 并带会话 id。类型过滤会收窄时间线，请求也带上过滤参数：

![过滤到出站发表](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-02-en-outbound.png)

频道菜单列出真实实例，选中后时间线收窄：

![含真实实例的频道菜单](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-06-en-channel-menu.png)

一次真实轮询过滤掉 300 条通知时，只写 20 条明细加一条计数行，因此被重复投递的批次不会把有用的行挤出页面窗口：

![带计数的合并 reason_filter 行](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-09-en-inbound-collapsed.png)

结果被裁剪时页面会明说——这里的日志确实超出了页面请求的 200 条：

![真实截断数据上的完整性横幅](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-04-en-truncated.png)

中文界面与既有「频道」入口用同一个词，合并计数同样渲染：

![中文时间线](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-05-zh-timeline.png)

![中文合并行](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/real-10-zh-collapsed.png)

侧边栏入口就在「频道」正下方（独立版 Web Shell 使用图标 rail，因此入口是活动图标，其可访问名称为 `Channel events`）：

![侧边栏入口](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/02-sidebar-rail.png)

这次真实运行的实测：页面可见时每 5 秒发起一次日志请求（12 秒内 3 次）。API 单次真实 500 被适配器自身的重试吸收，该轮仍报 `ok` 且 `durationMs: 1009`；连续三次失败则产生 `poll/failed`，带 `consecutiveErrors: 1` 与 `backoffMs: 2000`，随后恢复。模型输出 `<no-reply/>` 时产生 `outbound/suppressed` 且一条未发；发表失败产生带 API 错误的 `outbound/failed`；模型失败产生 `task/failed`（`attempts: 1`）；发送者不在群允许列表时产生 `inbound/skipped`、原因 `group_not_allowlisted`。扫描 5594 行日志，无一含消息正文。持续真实流量确实触发了轮转，且总量有界（`.1` 为 1,048,640 字节，文件 0600、目录 0700）。

下面这张工作区切换图来自更早的预置日志运行，保留它是因为它展示了双工作区选择器；带限定路由的隔离性已在真实流量运行中重新实测——另一个工作区的路由永远不会返回这份日志。

![次工作区](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/channel-events/channel-events/02-secondary-workspace-v2.png)

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

Node 24，`npm run build && npm run bundle`，`node dist/cli.js serve --require-auth` 配临时 `QWEN_HOME`，本地 GitHub 兼容 HTTP 服务与本地 OpenAI 兼容模型端点（占位 key，daemon 环境里已清除真实凭证），并用 chrome-headless-shell 经 CDP 做页面断言。模型调用只发往本地端点。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：每条入站、跳过、任务流转与轮询事件都会在消息路径上做一次同步日志追加。每条记录是单行 JSON，文件在 1 MiB 时轮转并保留一个备份，写失败会被吞掉并只打一行 stderr，因此诊断设施不会打断消息处理。读取路径是异步分块的，不会阻塞 daemon：每个日志文件 256 KiB、每次请求 4 MiB、32 个文件（最近修改优先）、最多返回 500 条，任何被这些上限裁掉的结果都会置 `truncated`。作用域目录读不到时回 5xx 而不是空列表。页面在标签页隐藏时暂停轮询。GitHub 单轮过滤超过 20 条通知时，只记前 20 条明细，其余合并为一条带 `detail.filtered` 的记录——因为只要任务仍可恢复，轮询游标就不前进，同一批通知否则会被每轮重复记录。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：GitHub 真实服务端（整条链路已用真实适配器对接本地 GitHub 兼容服务跑通，因此服务端自身行为——例如通知分页与已读状态时序——仍未验证）；本机未跑 macOS 与 Windows，但轮转先删除旧备份再重命名，不依赖 POSIX 的「重命名覆盖已存在文件」语义。页面只展示解析后工作区的事件，不跨已注册工作区汇总。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。不新增能力位（页面与路由复用既有 `channel_management` 门禁），不改设置，也不持久化消息正文。

设计文档：[2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.md](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/channel-events-timeline/docs/design/2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.md) / [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/channel-events-timeline/docs/design/2026-11-02-channel-events-timeline.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

无

</details>
