issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

Shortlist storage/spawn constraints and on-demand roster exist. The workers-view save action and operator-awareness contract are incomplete.

This is a criterion-by-criterion source reconciliation against [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). “Source complete” credits the owning implementation; it does not claim an unrun native, provider, deployment or final-distribution check. The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

- **shortlist — source complete:** toggle_fleet_model edits explicit shortlist=true rows in selected Fleet; docs describe shift-F. [fleet] models is stale wording, not a second store to implement. Carrying source: [e34f207d21](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/e34f207d2172aa0f0ca7121de433a8c6eecb7247).
- **spawn — source complete:** Off-list choice returns available routes; saved profile/manual pins remain exact; roster uses resolved spawn route preview.
- **save-in-role — implementation missing:** SubAgentsView handle_key exposes transcript/refresh/stop/Fleet navigation and scrolling, not save-in-role. Existing FleetAddModel roles action/members persistence can be reused.
- **operator-awareness — partial decision required:** Tool description instructs action=roster. Roster exposes models and saved profiles via same resolver; there is no always-visible stable fleet block, and rows cap64 with total count. Founder original request and later issue status leave the always-visible-vs-on-demand contract to reconcile.
- **reachability — implementation or field removal missing:** resolved_spawn_roster_entry still emits reachability:unverified literally. No actual probe is established by roster.
- **presentation — partial evidence missing:** Existing shortlist labels/picker are present; new worker save action does not exist, so its narrow/localized acceptance cannot pass.

**Next action:** Implement workers save-in-role using existing FleetAddModel/member writer, reconcile operator-list visibility, and remove/qualify the unverified reachability field.

Current owner: [CW-6319](https://linear.app/shannonlabs/issue/CW-6319).

Whole issue remains open. 0.10.3 is unpublished; earlier dated status below is historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.12 (filed 2026-09-06).
>
> **What remains**
> - Add 'save this model in this role' to the session workers view (`/fleet workers`, crates/tui/src/tui/views/) so a role a worker just ran on can be written to the selected fleet file via crates/tui/src/fleet/members.rs, with no second store.
> - Decide whether the operator needs the fleet model list without calling `action=roster` first; if yes, add a stable, prefix-cache-friendly block to the `agent` tool description (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs ~11205) with a snapshot test pinning order.
> - Replace the hardcoded `"reachability": "unverified"` in the roster row (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:16913) with a real reading, or drop the field.
> - Update the issue body: the shortlist lives in the fleet file as `shortlist = true` rows, not `[fleet] models`.
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Shortlist toggle shipped: `toggle_fleet_model` is 'the picker's one-key toggle' editing only explicit shortlist rows (crates/tui/src/fleet/members.rs:365-372); docs/FLEET.md:136 documents `⇧F` in `/model`, and docs/FLEET.md:123-135 documents `/fleet models`, `/fleet add`, `/fleet remove`.
> - Storage differs from the proposal: the shortlist is `shortlist = true` rows in the selected fleet file, not a `[fleet] models` config key (docs/FLEET.md:114-121, :127; crates/tui/src/fleet/identity.rs:560-613). No `[fleet] models` key exists in docs/FLEET.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md or config.example.toml at v0.10.1.
> - Spawn constraint shipped: an off-list model is refused with the list in the message — 'Requested model is outside the selected Fleet. Available routes: {choices}. Use action=roster' (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:16511-16531); ambiguity across providers is refused at :16535-16537.
> - Operator awareness shipped as an on-demand tool result, not a stable prompt block: `agent(action=roster)` returns `models` rows from `fleet_models()` plus saved `profiles` (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:11537-11563), each with route provider/model, context_window, capability_badges, cost_class (mod.rs:16901-16913).
> - Reachability is not actually checked: the roster row hardcodes `"reachability": "unverified"` (crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:16913).
> - No prompt-level fleet block: `git grep -iE 'fleet models|fleet_models|your fleet' v0.10.1 -- crates/tui/src/prompts crates/tui/src/prompts.rs crates/core/src` returns nothing.

---

## Founder direction (2026-09-06)

> we still need to make it so we are making like a shortlist of models that the user wants to be considered for sub agents — the flow from provider → model → model shortlist (that becomes the fleet models for the operator to choose from and assign roles, and then a user can choose if they want to save that model in that role) — and we want that + the manual configuration.

Plus the standing goals this serves: truly model-agnostic, cache-maxxing, and the working model being aware of every model in its fleet.

## What exists today (receipts)

- Fleet profiles already persist a provider, model, and thinking setting per role (#4137, #5042), and `roster.model_overrides()` plus `config.subagent_model_overrides()` are merged into the subagent runtime's `role_models` at launch (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs` ~11964, `tools/subagent/mod.rs` ~12914).
- `[subagents] providers.<name>` carries per-provider fan-out and budget knobs (`config.rs` ~2725) but no model list.
- The spawn `model` parameter is validated per provider (`normalize_requested_subagent_model`) but the operator is never told which concrete models it may pick; the prompt only documents `model_strength`.
- The model picker shows the live catalog per provider; there is no "consider this for the fleet" mark, so the only way to a role→model binding is editing a Fleet profile or TOML.

## Proposed flow

1. **Provider** — connected providers (exists).
2. **Model** — the live catalog for that provider (exists).
3. **Shortlist** (new) — in the model picker, a one-key toggle marks a model "fleet". Persisted as `[fleet] models = ["provider/model", ...]` in config; the same list is editable by hand. Entries are `provider/model` ids resolved through the model registry, so nothing is provider-specific.
4. **Roles** (extend) — at spawn time the operator sees the shortlist as *fleet models* and assigns one per role; the `model` parameter is constrained to the shortlist (plus the session model) and the error for an off-list model names the list. In the Agents view, a role row offers "save this model in this role", which writes the existing Fleet profile — no second store.
5. **Manual configuration** stays authoritative: `[subagents.roles.<role>] model = "provider/model"` and Fleet profiles win over the shortlist; the shortlist is what the operator may choose from when nothing is pinned.

## Operator awareness and cache

- The subagent tool description (or a stable system-prompt block) lists the fleet models with the tags the registry already knows: strength tier, context window, price class, and whether the route is currently reachable. Stable ordering, rebuilt only when the shortlist or a pin changes, so the block is prefix-cache friendly.
- When the shortlist is empty the block says so and the operator falls back to today's `model_strength` behaviour.

## Acceptance

- Toggle a model in the picker → it appears in `[fleet] models` and in `/fleet` as a fleet model; remove it → it disappears from both.
- Operator spawn with a shortlisted model succeeds on any provider; an off-list model is refused with the list in the message.
- "Save in role" from the Agents view produces the same Fleet profile a manual TOML edit would, and the next session spawns that role on that model without the operator choosing.
- The operator prompt/tool description shows every fleet model with its tags; snapshot test pins the block and its ordering.
- Narrow terminal and localized labels covered like the rest of the picker.

## Out of scope

Automatic model routing or pricing decisions (`--model auto` stays as is); provider onboarding; any change to how a single-session model is chosen.

## November 2 desktop contract preparation

The founder clarified singular **Fleet** as the configuration surface for member profiles used as sub-agents or in workflows. The desktop now presents that roster and purpose. Full member-profile editing and save-in-role acceptance remain open under P08 / CW-6319.

A bounded contract has been prepared for exact-file detail reads and revision-guarded writes. The implementation must reuse the existing profile files, identity checks, provider validation, effective roster and named Fleet store. The App Server and existing TUI draft handler must share the same content-revision guard so one editor cannot overwrite another. `SetupTransaction` currently provides atomic replacement and rollback, while an expected-content guard remains to be added to the shared writer. No canonical Engine implementation was changed by this preparation.

issues.title: [BUG] Custom openai-compatible provider: output budget clamped to the hosted-catalog ceiling (32K for qwen3.8-27b) even though the server accepts 262K — reasoning models return empty terminal stops

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [ ] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## What happened?

When a provider is configured as `kind = "openai-compatible"` in front of an
**operator-owned vLLM server** (e.g. a lab proxy), the output budget sent to the
server is clamped to the **hosted** catalog row's `limit.output` — **32768 tokens**
**for** `qwen3.8-27b` — even though the server itself accepts far more.

Verified against the real server (vLLM 0.32.0): `max_tokens = 131072`, `262144`
and `262000` are all accepted (HTTP 200, `finish_reason=stop`). The runtime still
emits `max_tokens=32768`.

With a reasoning model at `reasoning_effort: high` or `xhigh`, the model spends
the entire 32K allowance on hidden reasoning and never produces visible text. The
server returns a terminal `stop` with no answer, and the turn fails after two
retries:

> Model returned terminal stop reason `stop` with no answer or tool call
> (after 2 retries)

This makes long sub-agent tasks (reviews, planning, verification) fail reliably
end-to-end.

## Root cause (traced in the code)

1. The embedded model catalog (`crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json`)
   declares for `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`:

   ```json
   "limit": { "context": 262144, "output": 32768 }
   ```
2. `route_budget.rs::effective_max_output_tokens_for_route` intersects the
   requested cap with the compatibility cap. For a Custom provider, the
   catalog-derived `max_output` (32768) is applied, so every request goes out
   with `max_tokens=32768`.
3. The same failure shape — reasoning consuming the entire output allowance,
   zero visible text — is already documented in `route_budget.rs` for another
   route class ([#6285](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6285>)).

Custom providers are operator-owned endpoints, like the Ollama / SGLang / VLLM
routes that already have an operator-owned allowlist in
`route_declares_unknown_output_ceiling` — but **Custom itself is not in that**
**allowlist**, so a catalogued model name is still clamped by the hosted row.

## Expected behavior

For custom `openai-compatible` endpoints in front of operator-owned engines, use
the operator's real serving ceiling instead of the hosted-catalog `limit.output`:

* Add `ProviderKind::Custom` to the operator-owned allowlist in
  `route_declares_unknown_output_ceiling` (alongside Ollama / SGLang / VLLM).
* Honor the catalog's `generation_default` when present, otherwise the generic
  automatic cap.
* Keep the window-relative `ContextBudget` clamp as the hard cap (never raise
  any cap, only stop under-clamping).
* Unify the "custom" label with the existing `Unverified`/`RouteDeclaredUnknown`
  provenance so receipts stay truthful.
* Run `cargo test route_budget` (and add a regression test for the Custom route
  with a catalogued model name).

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Configure a provider:

   ```toml
   [providers.myqwen]
   kind = "openai-compatible"
   base_url = "https://your-vllm-host/api"
   model = "qwen3.8-27b"
   ```
2. Run any task at `reasoning_effort = "high"` or `"xhigh"` (e.g. a review or
   planning sub-agent).
3. Observe the repeated empty terminal stop and the failed turn.
4. Compare the emitted request (`max_tokens=32768`) with the server's accepted
   values (`262144` works).

## Environment

* **Codewhale version**: 0.10.2 (main @ 44007bf)
* **Where**: TUI + sub-agents
* **OS**: FreeBSD
* **Channel**: built from source
* **Provider / model**: custom openai-compatible → `qwen3.8-27b` (vLLM 0.32.0)

### Codewhale version 版本

Codewhale  0.10.2

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Other

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Cargo ([crates.io](<http://crates.io>))

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

*No response*

### Terminal and shell 终端

*No response*

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

## Extra notes

* Same failure class as [#6285](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6285>); related budget work: [#5518](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5518>), [#5820](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5820>), [#6540](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6540>), [#5461](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5461>).
* Workaround today: set `CODEWHALE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=262144` (env) or lower
  `reasoning_effort`.
* Optional separate change: correct the catalog `limit.output` for
  `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` (32768 → 262144) with fresh server evidence.
* I searched existing issues: no open issue or PR covers this case (searched:
  qwen, qwen3.8, 27b, empty stop, output cap, vllm ceiling, custom endpoint).

Engine packet, October 31. Trace the custom endpoint output cap from route lookup to the wire. Scope is crates/engine/src/route_budget.rs and the existing config/model catalog accessors only as needed. Verify with exact wire requests on a loopback custom route and the existing route-budget checks.

Candidate landed on Engine main 1d750e5098. With a 262144-token configured window, six ordinary CLI turns across qwen3.8-27b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b, and alibaba/qwen3.8-27b now emit 65536 automatic and 131072 explicitly requested on a custom OpenAI-compatible transport. The third spelling reproduced 32768 before the fix, while the first two already honored the larger values on this base and window. The initial scoped suite had 43/44 passes. The existing assertion for the modified provenance label was updated and its rerun passed. Real FreeBSD/vLLM reasoning output is an outstanding reporter surface.

issues.title: Upstream candidates from the app-side reuse audit (reasoning tiers, provider facts, artifact producers, MCP keys)

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Context

Pinvou is a desktop embedder that links the engine in-process (`deepseek-tui` = `codewhale-tui`) and drives it via `Op` / `Event` / `EngineConfig` / `ToolSpec`. On 2026-10-04 we ran a "reinventing-the-wheel" reuse audit (app features vs engine capabilities + internal reuse), re-verified on 2026-11-02. Four upstream candidates surfaced where **CodeWhale itself benefits** (benefits-all-embedders → upstream first per fork policy), and a search today found no existing issue or PR for any of them.

This is a summary issue to confirm approach with maintainers. **All four proposals below are pending maintainer confirmation — no implementation starts before that.**

Precedents for this issue → confirmed plan → PR flow: #81 → #82, #85, #87.

---

### U3 — Reasoning-tier capability query (effort: L; interim M)

**Today** the engine exposes only `apply_reasoning_effort` (`crates/tui/src/client.rs`, verified at line 3989 on 2026-11-02) plus internal `is_exact_*` predicates. There is no query an embedder can call to ask "which reasoning tiers does this (provider, base_url, model) support?".

As a result the tier knowledge exists three times in Pinvou, kept in sync by hand-written "aligned" comments:

1. engine predicates (`apply_reasoning_effort` / `is_exact_*`),
2. app Rust re-encoding for auxiliary calls (`pinvou3-app/src-tauri/src/features/sessions/bridge.rs`, app `core/reasoning_dialect.rs`),
3. app JS mirror (`pinvou3-app/src/features/settings/model-catalog.js`) — this copy exists only because the engine exposes no query.

Live drift example (verified 2026-11-02): `model-catalog.js` line 1001 notes the app's copy of engine facts "covers only grok-4.6 / grok-4.5, so grok-4.7 gets no tier UI" — the app has no way to know without duplicating engine internals.

**Proposal (from the audit):** expose a reasoning-tier capability query, e.g. `supported_reasoning_tiers(provider, base_url, model)`, via `codewhale-config` (and/or a Tauri command for desktop embedders). Interim M step: keep the tables but generate the JS table from engine data, with a pinned test.

### U4 — Export provider/model facts for embedders (effort: M-L)

**Today** engine-side provider/model facts live in three hand-maintained tables:

- `crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs` (verified 2026-11-02: `DEFAULT_XAI_MODEL = "grok-4.6"` at line 197),
- `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json`,
- `crates/agent/src/lib.rs` `ModelRegistry` (`pub struct ModelRegistry` at line 129).

Pinvou re-hardcodes the same facts in JS + Rust and has already drifted: app `model-catalog.js` line 97 defaults xai to `grok-4.7` vs engine `grok-4.6`; `kimi-k3` vs `k2.7-code` is double-maintained; the zai model-case is encoded in a JS comment that pins a specific engine commit.

**Proposal (from the audit):** first reconcile the engine's own three fact tables into one authority — this continues the direction of #6396 ("Catalog and pricing: finish collapsing model facts and price tables into one authority", closed) — then export a single facts surface (defaults, wire ids, aliases, case-folding) from `codewhale-config` for embedders, plus generated JS tables with pinned tests. Division of labor: the app keeps product decisions (which tier/model to preselect); the engine owns facts.

### U10 — Artifact file-producer records/events (effort: M)

**Today** `ArtifactKind` has a single variant — `pub enum ArtifactKind { ToolOutput }` (`crates/tui/src/artifacts.rs` line 25, verified 2026-11-02). The engine records tool-output spillover only and emits no events on write/patch tools.

As a result, "which files did this session produce?" is answered in Pinvou by three parallel registries: a frontend tracker, a `deliverables.rs` full-scan, and an `engine_support.rs` JSON re-parse — none of them consuming engine records.

**Proposal (from the audit):** extend `ArtifactKind` beyond `ToolOutput` (file-producer records), or emit events on write/patch tools. This collapses all three app-side registries into one source and is useful to any embedder UI.

### U11 — Export `ENGINE_OWNED_MCP_SERVER_KEYS` (effort: S)

**Today** the set of MCP server keys owned by the engine is a convention-based contract: Pinvou maintains its own copy of `ENGINE_OWNED_MCP_SERVER_KEYS` in four places (`pinvou3-app/src-tauri/src/features/marketplace/connectors.rs`, `features/marketplace/mod.rs`, `features/runtime_bundle/platform/mod.rs`, `features/runtime_bundle/platform/extraction.rs`), with lockstep tests keeping the copies pinned.

**Proposal (from the audit):** export the constant from the engine so the lockstep tests share one source of truth. Trivial size; could ride along with the next engine-side cleanup in the style of #81 → #82.

---

### Suggested sequencing (audit's order, for discussion)

Small and self-contained first: U11 → U10, then the L-scale items that need maintainer buy-in: U3, U4 (U4 starting with the engine-internal fact-table reconciliation).

File paths above were re-verified against the tree on 2026-11-02; exact line numbers may shift with `main`.

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Index-free source-navigation echoes, bounded source reads and guarded fork-prefix inheritance on the existing Engine. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; there is no replacement turn loop or indexing daemon.

**Current head:** [`7a491a9f`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/7a491a9f17474af5239eb6fb47addad4b2aa794f), incorporating upstream main [`acc47fbca`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/acc47fbcab3ea5906614aef77d15e95b7c7ddfff). The previous PR head remains an ancestor: this is a history-preserving update, not a force-push. The generated guide was rebuilt from the merged documentation rather than choosing a stale generated side.

## Implemented slice

- Revision-qualified Rust function/method references carry a path, source window and revision. Stale references are refused; guarded paging requires forward progress and retains snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust grep results can supply bounded enclosing-function references and small complete bodies. Broad/truncated searches retain their ordinary output. This is syntax evidence, not macro expansion or name/type resolution.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search. Child/scout/workflow fixtures follow the current catalog; root goal mutation remains unavailable to children while goal inspection stays discoverable.
- Source echoes remain append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Host observations, current access authority and evidence actually delivered to a model remain separate.
- Fork-prefix inheritance remains gated by matching route/model/opaque receipt and supported dialect; unsupported or changed identities take the cold path.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.
- The native read budget now survives the final Chat Completions projection for execution-matched canonical reads. Ordinary unbudgeted, mismatched and oversized results retain the wire backstop; a source-looking footer is not authority. See [`3c31b672a`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/3c31b672a).
- Finite headless turns receive a logged working-deadline notice while tools remain available. An exhausted ordinary turn can deliver its final text report without falsely becoming successful; cancellation and the distinct goal-pause contract remain intact. The existing feature row and configuration documentation are updated.

## Current verification

On the final merged source, **55 selected `codewhale-engine` library tests passed: 0 failed, 0 ignored**, using remote RCH. This is a one-package diagnostic, not a DSR repository-level gate. Selection covers native-read wire projection, stream decoding, deadline/admission/report-only fences, catalog deferral and the goal-pause contract.

The **four original subagent regressions also passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, replayed directly from that same compiled engine test executable: BM25/regex delegation discovery, independent bounded activation caches, depth-cap catalog preservation, and child goal-control discovery. These are separate from the 55-test selection, not four additional compilations. The fixtures retain cache-budget and root-goal mutation boundaries rather than restoring forbidden child tools.

The selected Cargo payload was:

```sh
RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test --locked -p codewhale-engine --lib -- \
  admission_gates:: client::chat::stream_decoder_tests:: \
  model_tool_catalog_applies_native_and_mcp_deferral \
  capability_compact_surface_defers_nonessential_core_tools \
  capability_full_surface_preserves_small_default_head \
  goal_turn_uses_goal_step_allowance_and_pauses_budget_limit_after_final_report \
  --test-threads=1
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the staged diff whitespace check, and the website facts check pass. Nine owned source/documentation paths were read back from the worker after testing and matched local bytes. This does not claim a pristine pre-compile transfer of every repository file.

The earlier TUI-checkpoint receipts are historical, not substituted for current engine verification. Full web documentation validation remains blocked locally by missing `marked`; it is not recorded as passing. No full workspace suite, full web build, native macOS/Windows acceptance or packaged-release qualification is claimed.

## Still draft: task qualification remains blocked

This stays draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). Earlier failed and incomplete comparisons remain in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898) and [the previous findings](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140); they are not replaced or pooled into a success claim.

The latest paid follow-up repaired the task but remained unqualified after an incomplete final provider stream. No treatment followed that failed control. A fresh integrated screen was then blocked **offline, before paid forwarding**: current native startup creates v3 coordinator state outside the frozen fixture's v1 startup boundary. The source-bound Linux executable exercised at the preceding integration checkpoint is not claimed as a packaged build of this final merged head.

The frozen write-boundary rule remains unchanged. A compatible, explicitly versioned startup fixture must be approved and re-admitted before fresh controls; both controls must qualify before treatment. No current-PR speedup, cost reduction, task-quality improvement, live-provider cache saving or independent quality review is claimed. Wider composition/impact-navigation work and release acceptance are not implied.

Refs #6393, CW-6439

prs.title: fix(tui): resolve /save and /load paths against the workspace
prs.body:
## What and why

`/save` took its path as written and `/load` didn't, so the two disagree. Started in one directory with `--workspace` pointing at another:

```
/save backup.json
/load backup.json
/save ~/x.json
```

Before:

```
Session saved to backup.json (ID: 4e298511)
Error: Failed to read session file: No such file or directory (os error 2)
Session saved to ~/x.json (ID: 4e298511)

launchdir/backup.json
launchdir/~/x.json
```

`backup.json` lands in the launch directory, where `/load`, which joins bare names to the workspace, can't find it. `~/x.json` creates a directory literally named `~` and reports success, with the file nowhere near home.

After:

```
Session saved to /path/to/workspace/backup.json (ID: 35a22431)
Session saved to /path/to/home/x.json (ID: 35a22431)

workspace/backup.json
home/x.json
```

`/load backup.json` now restores the session, and `/save` names the file it really wrote. Both sides now expand `~` with `expand_tilde`, as `/config` does, and join to the workspace, as `/export` does. An absolute path is unchanged.

One thing moves for `/load`: `sub/x.json` used to resolve against the launch directory because it contains a slash, and now resolves against the workspace like `/save`. Without `--workspace` those are usually the same directory.

## Issue

No-Issue: `/save` writes outside the workspace and to a literal `~` directory, and `/load` can't find what `/save` wrote; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a release build of this change and one of `main` at 7ec9fdddb in a pseudo-terminal at 110x34 with an empty HOME, a local mock OpenAI-compatible server and `--workspace` set to a second directory; the receipts and files above come from those runs, with the paths shortened. Release because a successful `/load` overflows the stack in a debug build, which isn't this change: a debug build without it does the same.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6579 of 6587 passed, with 1752 tests whose names match `save`, `load`, `session` or `commands` among them. The same eight tests fail on 7ec9fdddb without this change: `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `session_save_without_an_id_keeps_the_conversation_that_owns_the_snapshots`, `continue_recovers_legacy_checkpoint_without_removing_it`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_stderr`, `dispatch_user_message_surfaces_continued_message_submit_timeout`, `offline_queue_lifecycle_preserves_edits_and_explicit_reset` and `renamed_title_survives_next_in_memory_automatic_snapshot`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99): clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 7ec9fdddb; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: docs(harmonyos): describe how Codewhale runs there today
prs.body:
## What and why

The HarmonyOS page was mostly a record of what used to go wrong on the hmdfs user
directory: which check failed, what the old refusal message said, why that wording
named the wrong directory. A reader who just wants to run Codewhale on a HarmonyOS
PC had to work out which of those paragraphs still describe their build.

The page now describes the two supported routes and nothing else:

- **Linux subsystem** (融合开发引擎) with the ordinary Linux ARM64 build, and its
  documented platform limits.
- **Native OpenHarmony** (`aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos`): the cross-build, the
  signing step, and how the binary gets exec bits on a mount that ignores `chmod`.
- **The VS Code extension in CodeArts**: three steps, since the engine is the only
  piece that has to be built and signed for the platform.
- One table of what works on a device, and a short user-directory section that
  keeps only the facts that change a decision there (where the store lives, how to
  get strict permission checks, one driver per workspace).

`docs/INSTALL.md` gains a HarmonyOS row in the prerequisites and in the supported
platforms table, so the native arm64 tarball and its signing requirement are
visible where people look for a download. The footer that claimed the mount could
not express ownership says what is true instead: this row is the native target,
and inside the subsystem the Linux ARM64 asset is the one to use.

Both pages are rewritten in English and Simplified Chinese, section for section.

## Issue

No-Issue: documentation-only rewrite of an existing page; no tracking issue was opened for it.

## How I tested it

Documentation only — no Rust build, no device run.

- Both languages carry the same nine `##` sections and the same four tables, with
  matched column counts; every in-document anchor resolves.
- The cross-page links point at headings that exist
  (`INSTALL.md#migrating-from-npm-cargo-or-another-installation`, and its Chinese
  counterpart).
- `python3 scripts/check-readme-translations.py` and
  `scripts/check-readme-locales.sh` pass; `README.md` is not touched, so the 18
  translations stay in sync.
- The three new external links answer `200`.

One thing I could not run here: `node web/scripts/derive-facts.mjs`, because this
machine's `python3` is 3.9 and the feature-registry parser needs `tomllib`. So
`web/data/agent-docs.generated.json` still embeds the previous `INSTALL.md` text.
That file is regenerated by `release.yml` at release time and is not gated on PRs,
but it is stale until then — regenerate it if you want it in this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — not applicable: Markdown only
- [ ] `docs/features.toml` row — not applicable: no feature change

prs.title: fix(tui): stop treating dollar amounts as inline math
prs.body:
## What and why

Inline math opens at any `$` and closes at the next `$` that isn't after whitespace or before a digit, however far away, even paragraphs later. So a dollar amount that comes before a formula loses its `$`, and the paragraphs between them run together. Shell variables and amounts written `10$` go the same way. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
Basic is $5 a month and Pro is $12.

For the break-even point, solve $12m = 120$, which gives $m = 10$ months.

Some regions bill 10$ per month and 100$ per year.

At a principal of $1000 and a rate of $r$, the interest is $1000r$.

Put the tool on your path with PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH and restart the shell.
```

Before:

```
● Basic is 5 a month and Pro is $12. For the break-even point, solve $12m =
▏ 120, which gives m = 10 months.
▏
▏ Some regions bill 10per month and 100 per year.
▏
▏ At a principal of 1000 and a rate of $r, the interest is 1000r.
▏
▏ Put the tool on your path with PATH=HOME/bin:PATH and restart the shell.
```

After:

```
● Basic is $5 a month and Pro is $12.
▏
▏ For the break-even point, solve 12m = 120, which gives m = 10 months.
▏
▏ Some regions bill 10$ per month and 100$ per year.
▏
▏ At a principal of $1000 and a rate of r, the interest is 1000r.
▏
▏ Put the tool on your path with PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH and restart the shell.
```

The closing half of Pandoc's `tex_math_dollars` rule was already here; the opening half wasn't. `find_math_end` now has three more ways to say a `$` isn't math:

- It's followed by whitespace, which is that opening half. It's what `10$ per month` needed.
- The line ends before anything closes it. That isn't in Pandoc's rule, so it's stricter, but a reply has `$$` and `\[` for that, and they're unchanged.
- It reaches a `$` that opens rather than closes: one before `{`, or before a letter or digit and not right after one, a closing bracket or a narrow non-ASCII character. That's what `$1000 and a rate of $r$`, `$HOME/bin:$PATH` and `本金为$1000，利率为$r$` needed. `$n$th`, `$(n+1)$th`, `$k$-means`, `$x$个`, `$α$th` and `$25°$C` still close, and so does `$x^2$` after `\$5`.

Two of these change what counts as math: `$ x^2$` and a `$...$` split across lines now print as written.

This doesn't fix everything, because some of it is ambiguous from the text alone. `$A$B` still reads as math, since it has the same shape as `$n$th`. A formula that ends in a wide character right before a letter, like `$x个$th`, doesn't close, because `利率为$r$` has the same shape. A line that mixes `$10` and `10$` still pairs them, including a table row like `| $10 | 5$ |`.

## Issue

No-Issue: dollar amounts and shell variables lose their `$` in replies and can merge paragraphs; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at d9d168363 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x36 and 100x36 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. A further reply covered the cases named above, `$$`, `\[`, `\(`, code spans and fences, bold, and a table, on both builds at 80 columns and on this one at 50. Another covered `$α$th`, `$25°$C`, `$é$th` and the Chinese cases at 90 columns, on `main` at 8225f75b1 and this one.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6586 of 6589 passed, with the 576 tests whose names match `latex`, `math`, `markdown`, `transcript`, `message` or `history` among them. The three failures, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens` and `undo_retry_apply_path_keeps_engine_request_and_reopened_session_consistent`, fail the same way on d9d168363 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.
- `cargo clippy` with CI's flags (also on 1.99) stops at errors already on `main` at d9d168363, in `diff_render.rs` and `ui_text.rs`. With `--no-deps -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `obfuscated_if_else`, `double_must_use`, `manual_clamp` and `unnecessary_cast` allowed, it's clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on d9d168363; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): expand tabs in replies and sent messages
prs.body:
## What and why

A tab in a reply takes no room on screen, because ratatui drops control characters when it paints a line. Go and Makefile code indents with tabs, so it loses all of its indentation, and `a<TAB>b` prints as `ab`. This reply, at 80 columns, with real tabs:

````
The handler:

```go
func handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.Method != http.MethodPost {
		http.Error(w, "method not allowed", 405)
		return
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "ok")
}
```

The Makefile target:

```make
build:
	cargo build --release
	cp target/release/app bin/
```

And the output, tab-separated:

```
name	size	owner
a.txt	12	alice
```
````

Before:

```
    func handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.Method != http.MethodPost {
    http.Error(w, "method not allowed", 405)
    return
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(w, "ok")
    }
▏
▏ The Makefile target:
▏
    build:
    cargo build --release
    cp target/release/app bin/
▏
▏ And the output, tab-separated:
▏
    namesizeowner
    a.txt12alice
```

After:

```
    func handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
            if r.Method != http.MethodPost {
                    http.Error(w, "method not allowed", 405)
                    return
            }
            fmt.Fprintln(w, "ok")
    }
▏
▏ The Makefile target:
▏
    build:
            cargo build --release
            cp target/release/app bin/
▏
▏ And the output, tab-separated:
▏
    name    size    owner
    a.txt   12      alice
```

Each line now has its tabs expanded before it's parsed, at the 8-column stops `markdown_grapheme_width` already counted for wrapping. So what's painted matches what the wrapper measured, and a code line wraps at the same character as before. Everything after the parser sees spaces: `-<TAB>item` is a list item, and a table row with a tab reaches its border. Expanded, `-<TAB>-<TAB>-` looks like a list item too, so the horizontal rule check now runs before the list check; that also makes `- - -` and `* * *` rules, which print as bullets on `main`. A message you send goes through `render_plain_text`, which expands them the same way. Tool output already goes through `DisplayNormalizer` at 4-column stops; I kept 8 here because that's what the wrapper measures and what a terminal does.

A partial mouse selection now copies the spaces on screen rather than tabs, so a Makefile recipe pasted from one won't run. Selecting a whole message, `/copy` and `/export` still give the source with its tabs. `tab_line_partial_selection_copies_exact_fragment_not_whole_cells` and `tab_indented_code_fragment_copies_shifted_exact_text` pinned a tab taking no cell (#6365), so I moved their selections to the cells it takes now and changed the fragment the first one expects. The composer still hides tabs while you type; that's a separate layout and I left it.

## Issue

No-Issue: tabs in replies and sent messages aren't painted, so Go and Makefile code loses its indentation; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b8c541792 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x40 and 100x40 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. A further reply covered a tab in prose, `-<TAB>` and `1.<TAB>` items, a table cell, an inline code span, CJK before a tab, a tab-indented paragraph and a long code line, at 80 and 50 columns. Another covered rules and bullets written with tabs and spaces, at 80 columns. I also pasted a message with tabs and ran `/export` on each build; the file has the tabs on both. `/copy` reads the stored text and writes to the real clipboard, so I didn't run it.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6588 of 6589 passed, with the 722 tests whose names match `markdown`, `fence`, `indent`, `wrap`, `grapheme`, `copy`, `transcript`, `highlight`, `plain`, `list` or `rule` among them. The failure, `undo_retry_apply_path_keeps_engine_request_and_reopened_session_consistent`, fails the same way on b8c541792 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.
- `cargo clippy` with CI's flags (also on 1.99) fails on `main` at b8c541792, in files this doesn't touch: `collapsible_if` in `codewhale-engine`, `obfuscated_if_else` and `double_must_use` in `diff_render.rs`, `manual_clamp` in `ui_text.rs`, `unnecessary_cast` in `workflow_panel.rs`. With `--no-deps -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and those lints allowed, it's clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on b8c541792; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): size table columns from their content
prs.body:
## What and why Every table column gets an equal share of the terminal, whatever's in it, so a column of row numbers takes as much room as the sentence next to it, and the sentence wraps with half the row empty. This reply, at 80 columns: ``` Getting it running: | # | Step | Command | |---|---|---| | 1 | Install the dependencies | `npm install` | | 2 | Build for production | `npm run build -- --mode production` | | 3 | Start the server on port 8080 | `PORT=8080 npm start` | And the flags: | Flag | What it does | |---|---| | `--force` | Overwrite the target even if it already exists, without asking for confirmation first | | `--dry-run` | Print what would change and exit without touching anything on disk | | `-v` | Verbose output | ``` Before: ``` ┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐ │ # │ Step │ Command │ ├────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 1 │ Install the │ npm install │ │ │ dependencies │ │ │ 2 │ Build for production │ npm run build -- │ │ │ │ --mode production │ │ 3 │ Start the server on │ PORT=8080 npm start │ │ │ port 8080 │ │ └────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ ┌────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Flag │ What it does │ ├────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤ │ --force │ Overwrite the target even if it │ │ │ already exists, without asking for │ │ │ confirmation first │ │ --dry-run │ Print what would change and exit │ │ │ without touching anything on disk │ │ -v │ Verbose output │ └────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` After: ``` ┌───┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐ │ # │ Step │ Command │ ├───┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 1 │ Install the dependencies │ npm install │ │ 2 │ Build for production │ npm run build -- --mode production │ │ 3 │ Start the server on port 8080 │ PORT=8080 npm start │ └───┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘ ┌───────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Flag │ What it does │ ├───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ --force │ Overwrite the target even if it already exists, without │ │ │ asking for confirmation first │ │ --dry-run │ Print what would change and exit without touching anything │ │ │ on disk │ │ -v │ Verbose output │ └───────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` Each column now gets the width its longest row needs. When they don't all fit, the narrower columns keep what they need and the rest split what's left, so a table that fits doesn't wrap, and one where every column is long lays out as it did. A table narrower than the terminal stops at its content. Widths come from the parsed cell, so markup and link targets don't count. While a table streams, its columns resize as rows arrive. The whole table is already re-rendered until it ends, so the rows line up in every frame. A table with too many columns for the terminal still overflows, by less than it did. #7186 landed first, so I merged `main` in. A cell with `
` is measured line by line, so its column asks for the longest line and not the sum of them. ## Issue Refs #6561 (U04-m6): this is the uneven half. The narrow half isn't touched: the 4-cell floor stays, so a two-column table at width 8 still needs 15 cells. ## How I tested it - Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 8225f75b1 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x34 and 120x34 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs. Further replies on this build covered CJK cells, rows with missing or extra cells, links, long words, empty columns and a twelve-column table at 80 and 50 columns, and keycaps, flags, ZWJ emoji and combining marks at 80. I took frames while a table streamed slowly. - After the merge, a reply with `
` in two cells at 80 and 60 columns, with and without the line-by-line measure. At 80 the `Commands` column went from 34 cells to the 26 its longest line needs, and the first row went from four lines to three. At 60 there isn't room for the difference, and both render the same. The reply above renders the same on both. - `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib` on the merged head: 6579 of 6587 passed, with the same 519 tests among them. prs.title: fix(engine): read text files that start with BM as text
prs.body:
## What and why

The `read` tool treats any file starting with `BM` as a bitmap. So a note that opens with "BM25 is a ranking function" comes back as this, and the model never sees the text:

```
Read image file [image/bmp]
[Image omitted: unsupported, invalid, above the source limit, or unable to fit the 256.0 KB default delivery budget. Use read_media with a crop or higher detail if needed.]
```

The read still goes through `note_file_read`, so a later write sees the file as read when its contents never arrived. After:

```
BM25 is a ranking function
second line
```

The other image types have longer signatures in `sniff_media_type`; `BM` was the one two-byte check. A BMP header has four reserved bytes at offset 6, which encoders normally write as zero and text doesn't contain, so `primitive_image_mime` now requires those too. A real BMP gets the same refusal as before. A BMP from an encoder that writes something else there would now be read as text.

`detect_rejected_format` also matches on `BM`, but it only runs on files already being treated as images and a test pins it, so I left it.

## Issue

No-Issue: `read` returns "Image omitted" for text files that start with `BM`; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 8225f75b1 in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that calls `read` on a two-line text file starting with `BM25` and on a generated 1x1 24-bit BMP, and logged the tool results it got back. The results above come from those runs. The BMP gets the same refusal on both.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-engine --lib`: 7024 of 7046 passed, and the 22 failures are the same 22 on 8225f75b1 without this change. All are in `tools::subagent`, `client::responses`, `runtime_threads` or `session_secret_scrub`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6584 of 6587 passed. The three failures, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens` and `undo_retry_apply_path_keeps_engine_request_and_reopened_session_consistent`, fail the same way on 8225f75b1 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets`, `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-engine`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps -p codewhale-engine` with CI's flags stops at errors already on `main` at 8225f75b1, in `fleet/executor.rs`, `session_manager.rs` and `subagent/coord.rs`. With those lints, `collapsible_if` and the ones `main` trips in the TUI crates allowed, it's clean.

prs.title: fix(tui): stop math with non-ASCII text from crashing the TUI
prs.body:
## What and why

A reply with a non-ASCII character inside a LaTeX environment crashes the TUI. A saved reply does it again on `--continue`, so that session can't be reopened either. This happens in release builds and in 0.10.2. This reply is enough:

```
The piecewise function:

$$
f(x)=\begin{cases} x & \text{如果 } x>0 \\ 0 & \text{否则} \end{cases}
$$
```

Before, the process exits with status 1 and writes this to `crashes/`:

```
Location: crates/tui/src/tui/history/latex_render.rs:1312:37
Panic: start byte index 12 is not a char boundary; it is inside '如' (bytes 11..14 of string)
```

After:

```
● The piecewise function:
▏
▏ f(x)=
▏ ⎧ x,  如果 x>0
▏ ⎩ 0,  否则
```

`try_render_env` looks for `\end{...}` one byte at a time and slices the rest of the string at each step, so the first multi-byte character panics. Any of them will do: `α` or `×` typed directly into `\begin{aligned}` does it too. It now steps by whole characters.

The second crash is in the `\left`, `\right` and `\big` arms. They trim whitespace before reading the delimiter, then add its length to the untrimmed offset, so `\left 如` lands inside the character. That's also why `$\left ( x \right )$` renders as `(( x ))`; it's `( x )` now.

To look for more of these I used a throwaway test, not included, that puts `如`, `α`, `×`, `é`, a ZWJ emoji and a combining mark at every position of 41 LaTeX shapes, in each delimiter form, through `render_latex_to_string` and `render_latex_in_text`. That's 24270 inputs: two panic sites on `main`, none with this change.

`\left\{` printing a bare backslash is a separate display bug and isn't touched here. This is in the same file as #7196 but not the same lines.

## Issue

No-Issue: non-ASCII text in a LaTeX environment crashes the TUI; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a release build of `main` at 8225f75b1 and the installed 0.10.2 in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above: both panic and exit, and `--continue` on `main` panics again. A debug build of this change at 80 and 100 columns renders it, reopens it with `--continue`, and also handles `\begin{aligned}` with `α` and `×`, `\begin{pmatrix}` with Greek letters and the spaced delimiters above. An ASCII `cases` reply renders the same on both builds at 80 columns.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6584 of 6587 passed, with the 576 tests whose names match `latex`, `math`, `markdown`, `transcript`, `message` or `history` among them. The three failures, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens` and `undo_retry_apply_path_keeps_engine_request_and_reopened_session_consistent`, fail the same way on 8225f75b1 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.
- `cargo clippy` with CI's flags (also on 1.99) stops at errors already on `main` at 8225f75b1. With `--no-deps -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `obfuscated_if_else`, `double_must_use`, `manual_clamp` and `unnecessary_cast` allowed, it's clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 8225f75b1; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one

prs.title: fix(tui): decode HTML character references in replies
prs.body:
## What and why Replies print HTML character references as written: `<`, `&`, `|`, ` `. A link keeps the `&` in its target as well, so `?q=rust&page=2` opens with a parameter named `amp;page` instead of `page`. This reply, at 80 columns: ``` A few things from the page: - The function returns Result<Vec<u8>, Error> on every path. - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new - Same link with a label: [search](https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2) | Syntax | Meaning | |---|---| | a | b | a or b | | Option<T> | maybe a T | |   nested | indented | In code it stays: `&` and `<T>`. ``` Before: ``` ▏ - The function returns Result<Vec<u8>, Error> on every path. ▏ - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. ▏ - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new ▏ - Same link with a label: search ▏ ▏ │ a | b │ a or b │ ▏ │ Option<T> │ maybe a T │ ▏ │   nested │ indented │ ▏ ▏ In code it stays: & and <T>. targets: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2 ``` After: ``` ▏ - The function returns Result, Error> on every path. ▏ - Sales & Marketing owns the form, not Support & Success. ▏ - Search link: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new ▏ - Same link with a label: search ▏ ▏ │ a | b │ a or b │ ▏ │ Option │ maybe a T │ ▏ │ nested │ indented │ ▏ ▏ In code it stays: & and <T>. targets: https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2&sort=new https://example.com/search?q=rust&page=2 ``` Plain text decodes the whole run instead of stopping at each `&`, because a token boundary is a wrap point and `Vec<u8>` has to stay one word. Link labels and link targets decode too; code spans and fences don't. The result is text, so `<br>` prints as `
` and `*x*` doesn't go italic. The names are the ones `decode_html_entities` in the web scraper knows, which is in the engine crate, so tui-kit can't call it; an unknown name or `R&D;` prints as before. ` ` becomes U+00A0, so it doesn't wrap or drop at the edge of a row. A reference at the end of a bare URL stays outside it, as in GFM, so `<https://a.test>` links to `https://a.test`. A numeric reference to a control or hidden character stays as written, by the `hidden_chars` check the GitHub report tool uses, so a reply can't put ESC or a bidi override on screen this way. `escape_review_text` now escapes `&` too: that's how plugin review text stays literal, and `&` has just become markup. This touches the link arm #7182 rewrites. If #7182 lands first I'll merge `main` in. ## Issue No-Issue: HTML character references print as text in replies and leave `&` in link targets; I searched and found no issue for it ## How I tested it - Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 982c6408a in a pseudo-terminal at 80x34 and 100x34 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows and targets above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. A further reply on this build covered the cases in the two paragraphs above at 80 and 50 columns, including `\‮`, which is what `escape_review_text` now produces. I didn't run the plugin review flow itself. - `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6589 of 6589 passed, with the 685 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `link`, `wrap`, `table`, `keycap`, `transcript`, `plugin` or `url` among them. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, on 982c6408a; it merges cleanly into current `main` - [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a November 2 merge qualification: original head `07967b1f12f809f2356efa63cc29529dac33d1bf` retains the contributor history and current main. The System-note repair preserves the exact reviewed JSON argument values through Markdown/backslash preprocessing. The required Lint, Windows and npm-wrapper checks plus Safety succeeded in [run 41539492294](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/41539492294). The broader Ubuntu job remains **failed**: 19,036 passed, 46 unique failures and 33 skipped; this is not an all-green run. All 23 directly selected existing checks passed in hosted CI and the retained native integration cohort. The ordinary public renderer passed 20 comparisons. The actual macOS plugin review/confirmation journey now passes all 46 assertions: exact literal argv, stale/content/capability/prefix refusal, two-step exact-hash trust, trust remains disabled, no plugin execution, normal exit 0, real terminal EOF and owned cleanup. Its only HTTP was one owned catalog metadata GET; there were zero inference POSTs. That native journey used the integrated local 0.10.3 development build with two separately qualified incumbent fixes: the reload translation receives its required workspace, and existing interactive futures use heap boundaries to avoid a reproduced debug stack overflow. prs.title: fix(tui): render markdown images as their alt text
prs.body:
## What and why

Markdown images go through the link arm with the `!` left behind in the plain text, and a linked image, the usual badge form, is split at the image's own `]`. This reply, at 100 columns:

```
The README opens with two badges:

[![CI](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tool.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/tool)

and a screenshot: ![Main window](https://example.com/shot.png)

Wow! [Docs](https://example.com/docs) are linked too.
```

Before:

```
● The README opens with two badges:
▏
▏ ![CI](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions) ![crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/tool)
▏
▏ and a screenshot: !Main window
▏
▏ Wow! Docs are linked too.
```

`![CI` was a link to the badge image, and `](https://github.com/acme/tool/actions)` was text with the bare URL linked. After:

```
● The README opens with two badges:
▏
▏ CI crates.io
▏
▏ and a screenshot: Main window
▏
▏ Wow! Docs are linked too.
```

`CI` links to https://github.com/acme/tool/actions, `crates.io` to https://crates.io/crates/tool and `Main window` to https://example.com/shot.png.

An image now shows its alt text linked to its source, and a linked image shows its alt text linked to the outer destination, which is where a badge is meant to take you. The link arm takes an optional leading `!`, `![` ends a plain-text run, and the label and destination parsing moved into `split_markdown_link` and `split_link_destination`. Only one level of nesting is read, without recursion, so a long run of `[![` can't grow the stack. A `!` that isn't followed by a link, like `Wow!` above, prints as before.

## Issue

No-Issue: markdown images show a stray `!` and badge links print as markdown source; I searched and found no issue for it

prs.title: fix(tui): break the line at
prs.body:
## What and why A markdown table row has to fit on one source line, so `
` is how a cell holds more than one line, and models write it often. The renderer printed the tag as text. This reply, at 80 columns: ``` The retry settings, side by side: | Setting | What it does | |---|---| | `max_retries` | Default: 3
Set to 0 to turn retries off | | `backoff` | 1. Wait 1s
2. Wait 2s
3. Wait 4s | | `jitter` | Adds up to `250ms`
Only when **backoff** is on | | `
` | In code, the tag stays as it is | ``` Before: ``` │ max_retries │ Default: 3
Set to 0 to turn │ │ │ retries off │ │ backoff │ 1. Wait 1s
2. Wait 2s
3. │ │ │ Wait 4s │ │ jitter │ Adds up to 250ms
Only when │ │ │ backoff is on │ │
│ In code, the tag stays as it is │ ``` After: ``` │ max_retries │ Default: 3 │ │ │ Set to 0 to turn retries off │ │ backoff │ 1. Wait 1s │ │ │ 2. Wait 2s │ │ │ 3. Wait 4s │ │ jitter │ Adds up to 250ms │ │ │ Only when backoff is on │ │
│ In code, the tag stays as it is │ ``` `parse_inline_spans` now turns `
`, `
` and `
`, in any case, into a newline token, and the wrapper ends the row there. Because that's in the parser, `**one
two**` stays bold on both rows, and a paragraph, list item or quote breaks the same way instead of printing the tag. A trailing `
` adds no empty row, and `` or `Vec` prints and wraps as before. A table cell lays out each part straight from its tokens when they all fit, so `` ` port: 8080`
` hosts:` `` keeps the spaces from #7184; if a part doesn't fit, the whole cell goes through the wrapper, as a long cell does today. A tag inside a link label still prints as text. ## Issue No-Issue: `
` prints as text in replies, where it's the usual way to break a line in a table cell; I searched and found no issue for it ## How I tested it - Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at f77435889 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 and 100x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above; the rows above come from those runs, and 100 columns showed the same difference. Further replies on this build covered the cases in the two paragraphs above, at 80 columns. - `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 6589 of 6589 passed, with the 365 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `link`, `wrap`, `table` or `keycap` among them. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, on f77435889; it merges cleanly into current `main` - [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

issues.body:
## Summary

After an involuntary Gateway process death, background agent preparation failed with `SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired`. The affected agent then permanently refused `chat.history`, `chat.metadata`, `models.list` and progress-card requests with `UNAVAILABLE`, instructing an offline Doctor repair. The interrupted modeling request could not continue.

This report concerns recovery/admission after a refused reclamation commit, not a request to change history retention or bypass current-authority checks.

## Environment and actual observation

- Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, managed user systemd Gateway.
- Installed full-package source candidate: 2026.9.8 / `190042328f3e7d88570a388163820e4b67836c5e` (includes the separate indexed-media producer repair in #166568).
- 2026-10-07 14:44:23 UTC: systemd-oomd killed the Gateway cgroup after system memory and swap exceeded its 90% threshold. This was not a manual restart or printer operation.
- 14:44:29: systemd restarted the Gateway automatically.
- 14:45:54: HTTP listener bound; agent preparation continued in the background.
- By 14:52:29: affected-agent RPCs consistently returned the checkpoint-expired error and `Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.`
- Supported read-only `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent <affected-agent> --json` completed successfully: one target, 97 SQLite session entries, zero reported issues, no import or archival mutations. This inventory is not a full integrity certification.
- The host was heavily CPU/I/O constrained during recovery. Exact data has not been reproduced in a synthetic fixture yet.

## Source lead, not a proven complete root cause

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.ts` uses a five-second worker decision wait. A host authorization callback that observes a cell no longer in REQUESTED throws the generic checkpoint-expired error; the worker has a distinct refused-request error and settlement/rollback protocol. Current main `9bdad160d80686de5d080e4f6f128736f4831aef` still has this same commit-decision code.

Please distinguish confirmed native rollback/refusal from uncertain mutation or failed close, and investigate how a late authorization/refused request is propagated into permanent agent readiness failure. Keep live-authority, database identity, integrity and write-settlement gates intact. Raising the timeout, clearing admission state by hand, deleting sessions or changing retention would not establish the producer repair.

## Expected / actual

Expected: crash recovery either completes through the supported owner or reports a specific durable-data risk; a safely refused and rolled-back cleanup request should not misdiagnose a healthy store as irrecoverably unavailable.

Actual: the affected agent remains unavailable after startup with the checkpoint error. No conversation rows, indexes, compaction summaries or history have been edited manually; no provider/model change or guard weakening was used.

Related: #162319 contains an earlier checkpoint-expired observation during cold archival, but its main request is a retention-policy decision. This incident is startup recovery becoming a persistent agent lockout.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.
