issues.body:
### Summary

Add an optional tool to the existing ElevenLabs plugin that turns an ordered script with two selected voices into one generated dialogue MP3.

### Problem to solve

A scripted interview or podcast scene needs a relationship between each line and its speaker, together with the surrounding exchange. The [podcast_generator project](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/README.md) implements this task using batches of speaker turns. Its author explains why synthesizing each turn separately and assembling the recordings does not provide the same conversational context. That is an external implementation and reported motivation; I have not independently evaluated its audio quality.

There is also an OpenClaw-specific consumer surface: [pixcli's registry README](https://hub.openclaw.ai/shellbot/plugins/openclaw-pixcli) advertises optional dialogue and podcast tools. It is an existing alternative, not a request from its author to migrate.

The bundled ElevenLabs integration currently accepts one text and one voice per synthesis request. A speaker name written into that text does not become a second voice assignment. The requested output is a short jointly generated exchange using the operator's ElevenLabs voices, rather than an ordinary spoken assistant reply. Applicability to operators of the bundled plugin is an inference from these public workflows, not a reported OpenClaw outage.

### Proposed solution

Keep this capability inside `extensions/elevenlabs`, behind an explicitly enabled plugin tool; `elevenlabs_dialogue` is a suggested name. Use the existing optional-tool registration and manifest contracts. Do not expand the core `tts` tool or the shared speech interface.

The initial tool would accept an ordered array of nonempty `{text, voiceId}` turns, with exactly two distinct voice IDs. Generate a single bounded scene using Eleven v3 and return one MP3 artifact. Preserve turn order and inline audio tags. Reject scripts above a total of 2,000 text characters before making a request; this intentionally excludes automatic long-form episode production.

Reuse the plugin's configured authentication, runtime-resolved secrets, trusted base URL and guarded HTTP helpers for `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Use `mp3_44100_128`. Do not accept credentials, arbitrary endpoints or publication destinations in tool arguments. Keep normal tool admission, cancellation and current invocation authority. A provider error must not silently substitute another provider or turn the script into single-voice narration. Do not automatically regenerate or replay a request whose paid outcome is unknown.

Return the audio through existing media storage and tool-result/reply contracts. Artifact creation and delivery must be distinguished; do not claim delivery from a local path alone.

### Alternatives considered

- Repeated TTS calls followed by audio assembly preserve voice assignments, but each synthesis lacks the complete exchange. They remain useful when independently editable stems are the goal.
- The external Python project or a direct ElevenLabs SDK integration can already perform the vendor request; a custom OpenClaw tool can wrap that existing contract. An equivalent multi-voice operation in the current hosted ElevenLabs MCP was not established. These are valid alternatives; this proposal adds a narrowly scoped operation to an existing bundled owner, rather than claiming that OpenClaw cannot run such a workflow at all.
- pixcli already supplies dialogue tooling through its separately configured Meterkey service. Its README permits private output; it does not force public publishing. Keeping the existing ElevenLabs account and voice catalog is the distinction here, not an invented ban on other plugins.
- Other speech providers can offer dialogue, but their voices are not the selected ElevenLabs voice IDs.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: operators generating two-voice scripted scenes with the bundled ElevenLabs integration. The public projects establish the task, not the size of this population.
- Severity/urgency: an additional authoring capability; existing single-voice speech remains available. No production incident or urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Each qualifying scene needs one bounded dialogue request.
- Practical consequences: the bundled integration cannot currently express both speaker assignments in a joint synthesis. Operators use a separate integration or assemble independently generated turns. No measured time savings or quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [External batch producer](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/generate_podcast.py): `build_batches` and `generate_dialogue_batch` preserve speaker turns. Its older batch-size assumptions should not be copied.
- [ElevenLabs API contract](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert): ordered text/voice pairs produce audio. This proposal uses a smaller two-voice subset and the current short-request guidance.
- [Current bundled request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) and [plugin entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts): scalar synthesis and no dialogue tool.
- [Existing optional-tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/docs/plugins/building-plugins.md#registering-tools).
- Related [issue #165655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165655) / [PR #165656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165656) concern dialogue-model transport for a single speaking voice and phone-call socket reuse. The inspected open PR sends one text/voice pair; this proposal concerns a structured multi-voice script and an audio file.

This is static source and public-contract research. No vendor request, installed-plugin execution or listening test was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested implementation: register an optional version 2 tool in the existing plugin and declare its manifest ownership; factor reusable plugin-local credential/config and request helpers rather than copying their policy. The public factory context already supplies runtime config, provider-key resolution and `assertInvocationCurrent`; recheck current authority after awaited preparation and before the request and artifact admission. Reuse focused media-store and bounded binary-response helpers. For a finished direct reply, the existing `canDeliverSourceReply` / `details.sourceReply` contract can deliver the artifact; nested Code Mode execution remains program data under that contract.

Non-goals: real-time calls, WebSocket pooling, new v4 model support, voice cloning, speaker identification, transcription, pronunciation-dictionary management, long-script chunking, audio editing, podcast hosting, public uploads, new persistent jobs, and a generic dialogue SDK. Existing TTS defaults, personas and fallback behavior remain outside this tool's operation.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the tool explicitly enabled and usable ElevenLabs credentials, submit a short A/B/A script with two accessible voice IDs. One dialogue request preserves the three turns and both IDs, and returns a playable MP3. Confirm the supplied voice assignments with a listening test as well as the request trace; do not promise subjective quality.
- The returned artifact is usable through the actual tool/result path. A direct source reply reaches only the admitted source conversation; a nested program call returns data without an unsolicited send.
- Empty text, malformed voice ID syntax, a missing second voice, and a script over the character budget fail before the vendor request. A syntactically valid voice ID may still be unavailable to the account; surface that provider access/validation failure honestly rather than claiming local validation proves access. The disabled tool is absent from discovery. Cancellation, a retired invocation, and credential/plugin disablement do not admit a new request or publish a success artifact.
- Authentication, validation, timeout, malformed audio and size-limit failures produce an actionable error, without silent voice/provider substitution or automatic paid regeneration. Existing single-voice TTS still works with its previous defaults.

Implementer unknown. Live synthesis, real tool delivery, failure/cancellation proof and focused plugin/contract checks remain work for the eventual implementation. Maintainers should decide whether this existing-owner enhancement is worth maintaining relative to the external alternatives.

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Support native sticker search and sending in the official Zalo Personal plugin using the existing `sticker-search` and `sticker` message actions.

### Problem to solve

An OpenClaw extension author built a [patch for `@openclaw/zalouser`](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md) so group replies could include a native Zalo sticker selected by an emotion keyword. The [implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js) locates and rewrites the installed plugin's generated JavaScript, then calls `getStickers`, `getStickersDetail`, and `sendSticker` on its existing client. This is a concrete use case for sending a platform sticker object from an OpenClaw group conversation; an image attachment or emoji is a different output.

At [OpenClaw main `82c8ad576b31`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts), the plugin exposes only `react` as an additional shared message action. Its separate [`zalouser` tool](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts) accepts text, image, link, directory, profile, and status operations, with no sticker operation. Users of the official channel cannot perform this task through its supported actions.

The patch is historical, with its latest commit dated June 8, 2026. The same author's current [Setup project](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-setup/blob/0f12991d9787c1d3cf331b8b9ba1a256df2d559f/README.md) says the old integration and Sticker add-on were retired in favor of a maintained alternative channel. That is a valid solution. This request concerns supporting the same native object in the existing official channel, without maintaining a private patch or adopting another channel runtime. Current demand to migrate back to the official channel is unknown.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing `zalouser` channel action adapter; add no new core action, tool, SDK surface, credential store, or channel.

- `sticker-search`: for the selected account and an authorized group conversation, accept a bounded keyword query and return a bounded set of native sticker choices. Each choice must include a send-compatible selector carrying the native sticker ID, category ID, and type. Reuse the existing `query`, `limit`, and `stickerId`/`fileId` fields where appropriate. Exact selector encoding is a plugin implementation decision.
- `sticker`: send exactly one selected native sticker to that group using the same account/profile and existing target resolution and action authorization. Return the platform message ID and normal channel delivery result. Reject malformed selectors and unsupported targets before sending.
- Reuse the current plugin's API/session owner and cancellation/effect-boundary handling. Include the native `/api/group/sticker` POST in its dispatch tracking. Stop before submission if the admitted operation is canceled or no longer current. An ambiguous network outcome must not trigger a blind resend or a claim of confirmed delivery.

Initial scope is explicit group sticker search and send. Suggested search budget: default 5, maximum 10 choices; these are proposed resource bounds, not Zalo API limits. No automatic interpretation of `[Sticker: ...]` in ordinary text, automatic emotional replies, mention changes, sticker uploads, whole-catalog collection, or DM support is requested.

### Alternatives considered

- **Alternative channel:** [OpenClaw Zalo Connect](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-zalo-connect/blob/0e5908c6ccc00cde6f539a82fd82086fc90285de/README.md) already advertises native stickers and many other actions. It is a valid option. The remaining proposed benefit is for installations retaining the official `zalouser` channel and its current account/session owner; no claim is made that all OpenClaw users are blocked.
- **Patch the generated plugin:** the cited implementation targets generated `zalo-js-*.js` files. It expresses the exact missing behavior, but does not establish compatibility with current main. We have not executed it.
- **Skill or separate tool:** a skill can call supported tools, but cannot obtain this missing behavior from the official tool's closed action enum. A separate code plugin could own another Zalo connection or use an alternative channel's bridge; the official channel's client implementation is private. This does not establish a missing generic SDK contract.
- **Send an image, emoji, or reaction:** these remain useful existing outputs but do not send a native sticker object.

### Impact

- Affected: users who retain the official Zalo Personal channel and want native sticker replies in groups. A historical plugin patch demonstrates the task; the current affected population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: this particular output is unavailable through the official channel; text, media, and reactions remain usable. No urgent incident or quantitative severity has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Keyword-based group replies are described by the source; no usage frequency has been measured.
- Practical consequences: the documented approaches are patching generated plugin code or using a different channel. No time savings, user counts, or account-migration failure rates are claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original task and patch](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/README.md), plus [native lookup/send implementation](https://github.com/tuanminhhole/openclaw-skill-zalo-sticker-mention/blob/6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2/mentions.js), commit `6b242577111737f33b7ccf3f322dd952c7e035a2`. This is implementation evidence, not an independently observed live send.
- [Current channel action adapter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/channel.ts) and [optional tool schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/tool.ts). A pinned scan of the plugin's non-test TypeScript, JSON, and Markdown found no sticker implementation.
- The plugin already pins [`zca-js` 2.2.0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/package.json). That package's published Git revision `dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9` contains [`getStickers`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickers.ts), [`getStickersDetail`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/getStickersDetail.ts), and [`sendSticker`](https://github.com/RFS-ADRENO/zca-js/blob/dadfef18bcac53537741855c99f084152da1fad9/src/apis/sendSticker.ts). The last accepts `id`, `cateId`, and `type`, supports group targets, and returns `msgId`.
- [Shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.ts) already contain sticker search/send concepts. This is an adapter gap, not a new common contract.
- PRs [#27905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/27905) and [#29075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/29075) concern `zalo` Bot API inbound handling and emoji replies; neither supplies `zalouser` native sticker sending. Both are closed and unmerged at the research time.

Research is static. No dependency installation, external patch execution, paid service, account login, or authenticated Zalo delivery was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation entry points are the plugin's `channel.ts` action descriptor/handler, its lazy `channel.runtime.ts` exports, the private `zca-client.ts` API typing, and the existing `zalo-js.ts` API/session owner. The existing [`send-context.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-context.ts) checks cancellation and current effect authority; its message dispatch path matcher currently excludes `/sticker`. Reuse that owner and [`send-receipt.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82c8ad576b316af079a13301d0540215900be4b6/extensions/zalouser/src/send-receipt.ts) rather than introducing a second sender. These are implementation suggestions, not a claim that the change has been built.

Preserve plugin lazy loading, existing account isolation, target and access policies, credential ownership, and current delivery outcome semantics. No configuration migration, new persistent catalog, new authorization scope, or dependency upgrade is proposed. Search can return fewer choices when detail lookup is partial; it must not claim catalog completeness. The existing unofficial Zalo integration and its account/platform limitations continue to apply. No implementer has committed. Selector encoding and the exact bounded search defaults remain owner decisions.

Acceptance criteria:

1. In an authorized group conversation on a configured `zalouser` account, search a keyword, choose one returned selector, and send it through the shared message tool. Zalo displays one native sticker in that group and the tool reports its platform message ID.
2. The selected account/profile is used for lookup and send. Another configured account is not silently selected; malformed selectors and unsupported non-group targets do not issue a sticker POST.
3. Cancellation or retirement during lookup/session preparation prevents a later send. A recorded accepted send retains its ID; an uncertain outcome is not reported as confirmed or blindly retried.
4. Empty/partially unavailable search results are bounded and explicit. Existing text/media/react paths continue to work, and ordinary text containing `[Sticker: ...]` does not acquire a new side effect.

An implementer should run focused action, routing, send-context, and receipt tests, then the affected plugin checks and startup profiler. A real authorized Zalo group is needed to verify native rendering and actual transport outcomes; mocked API responses alone cannot establish that acceptance criterion.

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a multi-question `ask_user` text reply, a line numbered like the prompt (`1. Deny`) is not read as a question number: the answer is saved as `1. Deny`, bound by line position, or rejected when the question only accepts its listed options.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have an agent call `ask_user` with two questions: `ruling` (options Deny, Allow) and `authorization` (options Approved, Deferred).
2. Answer in the chat with two lines: `1. Deny` and `2. Approved`.
3. Inspect the resolved answers (`question.get`, or the tool result the agent receives).
4. Repeat with the lines reversed: `2. Approved` then `1. Deny`.

### Expected behavior

`ruling` = `Deny` and `authorization` = `Approved` for both line orders, matching `1: Deny` / `2: Approved`, which already works. A reply that answers only some questions stays rejected as incomplete (#146646).

### Actual behavior

On main (parser unchanged from `1b15b48e2f3` through `e375530e380`), the dotted prefix is not a key separator, so the lines are positional:
- `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"` and `"2. Approved"`. Built-in `ask_user` questions accept free text.
- `2. Approved\n1. Deny` is saved as `ruling = "2. Approved"` and `authorization = "1. Deny"`.
- With options-only questions (`isOther: false`), both lines normalize to nothing and the reply is rejected with `question '<id>' requires an answer`.

Separately, the single-question card text (the text block next to the option buttons, which the Telegram and Teams renderers show) lists options as `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default` under "Reply with the number, the option text, or your own answer.", so there is no number to reply with.

Correction to the first version of this issue: question ids are not the problem. `cas1_authorization: Approved` binds by id on main. The three replies I sent in the live session were each one line for a two-question card, so their rejection was the correct incomplete-answer behavior.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.4 (live session); parser behavior confirmed on main `e375530e380`

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout running as the Gateway service

### Model

Not model-dependent (reply parsing). The live session used qwen3.8-27b on a self-hosted endpoint; the reproduction used the qa-lab mock-openai provider.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> mock-openai (qa-lab) for the reproduction; live session used a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Logs

```shell
# live session, 2026-11-01, Telegram direct chat (single-line replies to a two-question card)
09:34:09 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ question.resolve 2ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=question 'cas1_authorization' requires an answer
09:34:11 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=telegram chatId=telegram:<redacted> messageId=<redacted> ... outcome=error reason=question-response-rejected
# qa-lab, main parser, reply "1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent" to a three-question card
"status":"answered","answers":{"answers":{"deploy_target":["1. Production"],"checks":["2. E2E"],"release_note":["3. Urgent"]}},"resolvedBy":"plain-text"
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: anyone answering a multi-question `ask_user` prompt by text (the docs say Discord, Slack and Telegram use readable text for these). Severity: the agent receives a wrong or prefixed answer, or the user is re-prompted. Frequency: every reply that numbers its lines with a dot. Consequence: wrong input to the waiting agent, or a timeout to `no_answer` if the user keeps answering this way.

### Additional information

Related: #173760, #173845 (guidance and reply template, open), #146646 (incomplete-answer contract). Fix: #190513.

issues.body:
# Codex harness: thread stays "claimed by active work" after turn completes, wedging the session until gateway restart

## Summary

With the Codex agent harness, a session's Codex thread is not released after a turn finishes normally. Every following message to that session fails with:

```
Codex thread <threadId> is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

The harness does not fall back (`Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend`), so the agent stops replying entirely. Restarting the gateway clears it, but the next completed turn on the new thread wedges it again.

## Environment

- OpenClaw CLI: 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), Homebrew `openclaw-cli`
- `@openclaw/codex` plugin: 2026.10.9
- `@openai/codex`: 0.160.0 (darwin-x64 app-server)
- Node: v26.13.0
- macOS 15.8.2 (x86_64), gateway under launchd (`ai.openclaw.gateway`, port 18789)
- Channel: Discord DM, agent on Codex harness (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, fallback `gpt-5.6-luna`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent on the Codex harness, bound to a Discord DM.
2. Send a message, and let the turn run tools and finish normally.
3. Send another message to the same session.

**Expected:** the second message runs a new turn on the thread.
**Actual:** it fails immediately with `is claimed by active work`. Every later message fails the same way, and each model fallback candidate fails too, until the gateway restarts.

## Evidence

The latest stuck thread is `01a19f8e-60b7-7fb1-b2ec-4689de6cc154`. Its rollout file shows the last turn ending cleanly:

```
2026-11-03T04:02:17.208Z  event_msg  task_complete  turn_id=01a19f90-5a8d-7000-8871-ed9011a6f36f
```

Three minutes later, the next inbound message was rejected:

```
2026-11-03T04:05:09.836Z  ERROR  Codex thread 01a19f8e-... is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

Around turn completion, the log also has:

```
WARN agent/embedded  codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable  reason=context_unavailable
INFO agent/embedded  codex app-server turn released after terminal dynamic tool result  tool=sessions_yield
```

The pattern repeats across gateway restarts (all times UTC, 2026-11-02 to 11-03):

| Thread | First error | Last error | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01a198bb-6040-70c1-8f60-2f24f2b70f2a | 13:30 | 01:59 | 35 |
| 01a19d4f-9fa8-7792-bc33-5b234394551a | 17:36 | 00:44 | 90 |
| 01a19f19-7e19-7430-9b32-49bc9ec81120 | 02:20 | 03:39 | 37 |
| 01a19f8e-60b7-7fb1-b2ec-4689de6cc154 | 04:05 | 05:06 | 29 |

The same error also appeared on 2026-11-01 for thread `01a198a5-3bd1-7250-af32-9f7e6d73e46d` (14 failures). Gateway restarts at 02:02, 03:44 and 03:53 UTC each cleared the wedge only until the next completed turn.

The claim doesn't appear in `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`state_leases` holds only `gateway-owner`) or in the agent's `openclaw-agent.sqlite`. It seems to live only in gateway memory, which would explain why a restart clears it. The error string comes from `@openclaw/codex/dist/.setup/thread-lifecycle-run-*.mjs` and `session-retirement-*.mjs`.

## Possibly related symptoms on the same gateway

- About 70 Codex app-server or code-mode-host processes (about 3.3 GB RSS) built up as children of the gateway within ~75 minutes of a restart. The gateway itself ran at ~150% CPU and 3 GB RSS, and CLI commands (`openclaw status`, `openclaw codex --help`) hung. After a restart, this dropped to one Codex process.
- A `memory-core` short-term workspace lock was held by a pid that no longer exists (`Timed out waiting for memory workspace lock ... held by 53114:...`).
- `memory session startup catch-up failed: Error: Agent database Worker owner is closed`.

## Related issues

- #188422: a sibling native child holds the parent, giving "claimed by active work". The shape is similar (the turn also ended through `sessions_yield`), but the stuck thread here made no native `spawn_agent` calls during its turns.
- #190932: the first dashboard reply hits the claimed-work guard on 2026.10.9. Here the first turn succeeds and every later turn fails.
- #172837, #182549, #181046: earlier claim, pin and fallback bugs.

## Suggested direction

The thread claim should be released whenever a turn reaches `task_complete`, including when settled-turn finalization hits `context_unavailable` or the turn ends through a terminal dynamic tool such as `sessions_yield`. A stale claim whose turn has already completed should also expire or be reclaimable, so the session doesn't stay dead until a restart.

issues.body:
### Summary

Please decide whether Slack should support an opt-in that makes an already-admitted, explicitly mentioned **bot-authored informational group turn** reply-optional when group silence is allowed. This asks for a product-policy decision; it does not claim the documented current requiredness is a regression.

### Problem to solve

In cooperating-bot rooms, a completion/FYI notification may explicitly mention a peer only to deliver context. The receiving agent may have nothing useful to add. A genuinely empty completed answer is still a missing required reply and can trigger recovery/error output, keeping otherwise finished exchanges alive.

Exact completed `NO_REPLY` is a different case: merged #170534 already honors deliberate token-based silence on main. This request concerns the remaining optional-completion policy, including a genuinely empty final; it does not seek to reimplement that merged fix.

### Proposed solution

Ask the Slack/runtime owners to accept or reject a backward-compatible, operator-controlled policy at the existing reply-expectation owner:

- Applies only to authorized bot senders, an admitted group/channel turn with an explicit bot mention, and resolved group silence `allow`.
- When opted in, the turn may complete silently without a forced visible-answer recovery, while ordinary useful replies still work.
- Preserve the current default. Human explicit mentions, DMs, authorized commands, `disallow`, sender access, and bot-ingress protections keep their existing contracts.
- Do not prescribe a new configuration key or implement a new public surface before the owners choose the scope. If the supported answer is to require exact `NO_REPLY` and leave truly empty explicit mentions required, please record that decision here.

### Evidence and scope

On official `openclaw@2026.10.8` (build `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; verified tarball SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`), an isolated synthetic fixture with Slack group context, `SenderIsBot: true`, `WasMentioned: true`, explicit mention provenance and group silence `allow` returns `required` from the distributed owner. The current-main owner likewise has no bot-sender exception for explicit mentions. This is source/distributed-function evidence, not a fresh live Slack incident or end-to-end model run.

Historical motivation and the original policy request: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164946#issuecomment-6266529788 . That issue is closed for its original Discord/exact-`NO_REPLY` defect. #169927 is also closed for the existing intentional-silence solution; neither closure approves this distinct truly-empty opt-in policy.

### Alternatives and related work

- Use the existing exact-`NO_REPLY` contract: already supported on main, and a valid alternative if owners reject this policy.
- #166380 changes the delivery hint only for turns that are **already optional**. It leaves explicit-mention admission required, so its merge alone does not answer this request.
- #177555 / #160750 / #160752 govern whether **untagged** bots are admitted. This request starts after explicit bot admission and does not expand sender authority.
- #164877 handles implicit-thread requiredness, not explicit bot mentions.

No private runtime patch, modified employee package or configuration change is proposed or distributed. No customer content, workspace identities or credentials are included.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Only after maintainer direction on the public contract. The behavior should stay in the existing owning path; no independent workaround is proposed.


<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
### Current decision boundary and new official beta evidence — 2026-11-02

The remaining question is a product-policy choice, not an outstanding implementation review: should an explicitly mentioned, authorized bot-authored informational group turn under silence allow be allowed to finish genuinely empty, or should it continue requiring a useful reply or deliberate exact `NO_REPLY`?

Fresh immutable **2026.10.10-beta.5** Core/Slack evidence, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still returns `required` for the synthetic explicit-bot/group-allow fixture. That is an actual imported distributed expectation-owner result; it is not a live Slack/model reproduction or a fresh empty-final completion run. The unchanged 20-case fixture is **17 PASS / 3 FAIL**, with this policy requirement distinct from the two untagged-bot admission requirements. The [published release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the artifact hashes and limited execution scope.

Current main at [`dcd73e41bd0555b1ee8a912c716332a54c7993bd`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dcd73e41bd0555b1ee8a912c716332a54c7993bd/src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts#L96) retains requiredness for explicit mentions under allow and has no bot-sender exception in that owner. The source completion policy maps required empty output to missing; that is a source inference here, not a newly executed transport or completion test.

Merged #190467, which supersedes #166380, improves the delivery hint only for turns **already classified optional**. It explicitly preserves explicit bot requests and required replies. Merged #170534's exact `NO_REPLY` handling likewise does not authorize genuinely empty explicit-mention completion. Neither adoption decides this issue.

The existing [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186514#issuecomment-6460509344) recommends retaining the exact-`NO_REPLY` contract. That recommendation is not a recorded Slack/runtime-owner rejection or acceptance. Please record the owner decision here: either accept a backward-compatible optional-empty policy, preserving human explicit requests, DMs, commands, disallow and sender access; or retain exact `NO_REPLY` as the supported deliberate-silence contract and state that genuinely empty explicit mentions remain unsupported. No new setting name or implementation is proposed before that decision.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: explicit-bot requiredness also persists in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, still returns **`required`** for the same synthetic explicitly-mentioned bot/group-allow fixture. In the unchanged20-case matrix, this remains one of **3FAIL / 17PASS**; the other two failures are the separate untagged-bot admission cases tracked by #177555. Merged #164877's two implicit-thread optional/silent cases nowPASS in stable, without deciding this explicit-mention policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) supplies the immutable package hashes and unchanged-byte checks. Scope is the actual distributed expectation-owner decision in the same isolated function/gate matrix; this adds no new live Slack/model or genuinely empty-final execution claim. The existing owner-choice question above remains unchanged: optional genuinely-empty completion versus the supported exact`NO_REPLY` contract. A bot recommendation or this distribution result does not record owner acceptance or rejection.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:end -->

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `live.transcript: true`, the voice-call plugin sends live transcript batches to the requester session. On a realtime call where the caller's speech is finalized after the assistant has started its reply, those batches repeat each assistant reply and never contain the caller's lines. The end-of-call report is correct.

This started with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602. That change keeps the caller's line ahead of the reply in the transcript, so the line is inserted before entries that have already been batched. The live batcher reads new lines by transcript index (`transcript.slice(cursor)`), so it picks up the shifted reply again and skips the inserted caller line.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the voice-call plugin with `realtime.enabled: true` and `live: { transcript: true }`, and have an agent place a call with a requester session.
2. On the call, the callee speaks and the assistant answers. The realtime provider finalizes the callee's ASR line after the reply has started, which is the case https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602 handles.
3. Read the live transcript messages in the requester session.

### Expected behavior

Each final line is delivered once, and the callee's lines are delivered as well (`Callee: …`).

### Actual behavior

Each batch repeats the previous assistant reply, and no `Callee:` line ever arrives:

```text
[live 0-1] Assistant: Friday at nine works.
[live 1-2] Assistant: Friday at nine works.
[live 2-3] Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
[live 3-4] Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
[report]   Callee: Is Friday free? / Assistant: Friday at nine works. / Callee: Can you bring the part? / Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
```

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.9 (main at f77ca8f4666)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04

### Install method

Built from source

### Model

None; the reproduction uses synthetic realtime provider events and makes no model call.

### Provider / routing chain

Twilio-style carrier media stream -> voice-call realtime handler -> call manager -> live transcript delivery -> requester session

### Additional provider/model setup details

The voice-call plugin ran in a harness:
- A real local WebSocket carrier stream fed the realtime handler.
- The realtime provider bridge emitted synthetic events: speech started, assistant reply, then the caller's final line.
- Requester-session sends were captured instead of reaching a Gateway.

### Logs

_No response_

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See "Actual behavior" above.

### Impact and severity

The requester agent asked for a live transcript to follow the call. It sees only its own side, repeated, and nothing the callee said until the end-of-call report. Affected: builds from main since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602, on realtime calls with `live.transcript` enabled, for every exchange where the caller's ASR line finalizes after the reply has started.

### Additional information

Regression on main since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602 (merged 2026-11-03); v2026.10.10 is not affected.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

While a Telegram flood wait is active, every typing action the account limiter deliberately holds back is logged at ERROR as `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (429: Too Many Requests: retry after N (flood wait active; request not sent))`. The request never reached Telegram.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Telegram bot with streaming previews in a busy group until Telegram answers a preview edit (`editMessageText` or `sendRichMessage`) with 429 `retry_after` N. The gateway logs one WARN: `telegram/flood Telegram flood control on editMessageText: all calls for this bot wait Ns; replaceable update skipped`.
2. While that wait runs, let a reply keep typing (the keepalive fires every 4 s).
3. Each held-back typing action logs `telegram/api telegram sendChatAction failed: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after N (flood wait active; request not sent))` at ERROR. Outbound typing (`sendTypingTelegram`) logs the same refusal as `telegram typing failed: ...`.

The regression test in the linked PR reproduces this on main `586f5766569` with a scripted Bot API: it fails with exactly that extra ERROR line.

### Expected behavior

A typing action the limiter held back is the designed outcome, not a failed API call:
- `account-throttler.ts` describes these responses as "Synthetic 429s for requests the limiter held back; they never reached Telegram".
- `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md` says typing runs as a replaceable request that is "skipped, not queued" during a flood wait.
- The flood wait itself is already logged once at WARN.

Real chat-action failures (a 429 from Telegram, a 400, a network error) should still log at ERROR.

### Actual behavior

- One gateway logged 11 such ERROR lines between 2026-11-03T00:30:25Z and 00:33:08Z, in two bursts (3 lines from 00:30:25Z, 8 from 00:32:58Z).
- Each burst followed a flood WARN: 00:30:23.606Z `editMessageText`, wait 12 s; 00:32:57Z `sendRichMessage`, wait 11 s.
- All 11 end in `request not sent`. No sendChatAction 429 returned by Telegram itself appears in that window.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.5 (`7e15622f37b`) with 5 local commits. Of the files on this path, the local commits change only `bot-core.ts` (request-timeout transformers), not the limiter, the logging wrapper or the typing call sites. The code path is unchanged on main `586f5766569`.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout, gateway service

### Model

Not model-specific.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (not involved; the defect is in the Telegram channel).

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

```shell
{"date":"2026-11-03T00:30:23.606Z","lvl":"WARN","0":"{\"subsystem\":\"telegram/flood\"}","1":"Telegram flood control on editMessageText: all calls for this bot wait 12s; replaceable update skipped"}
{"date":"2026-11-03T00:30:25.660Z","lvl":"ERROR","0":"{\"subsystem\":\"telegram/api\"}","1":"telegram sendChatAction failed: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 10 (flood wait active; request not sent))"}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code path on main `586f5766569`:
- `extensions/telegram/src/account-throttler.ts:76-86`: `skippedFloodResponse()` builds the synthetic 429 with `(<reason>; request not sent)`. It is returned for replaceable calls (typing) at `:105` (network edge) and `:167` (entry).
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.ts:270-278`, `bot-message-dispatch-context.ts:68-76` and `send-actions.ts:85-94` wrap chat actions in `withTelegramApiErrorLogging`.
- `extensions/telegram/src/api-logging.ts:50-57` logs every error from those calls through `telegram/api` at ERROR, including the limiter's own refusal.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Telegram bots whose replies type while the bot token is under flood control, usually triggered by streaming preview edits in groups.
- Severity: annoying. These ERROR lines are for requests that were never sent, so they trip error alerting and bury real failures. No message is lost through this path.
- Frequency: 11 lines in 2 min 43 s on one gateway. That gateway's text log holds 204 such lines (sendChatAction or typing failures ending in `request not sent`) on 19 days between 2026-10-07 and 2026-11-02 across the builds it ran in that range, 43 of them on 2026-11-01 alone. A second gateway with a quieter group load logged none since its last restart.
- Consequence: misleading ERROR logs and alert noise.

### Additional information

- Present since at least 2026-10-07 in that gateway's log; the flood gate itself shipped in #157349.
- Related: #141959 quotes these lines as evidence for a reply-loss bug; this issue is only about their log level. #190006 changes the same limiter's resend budget for final replies and does not touch logging.

issues.body:
## Summary

After two upstream `LLM idle timeout (120s)` events on provider `kimi`, the kimi plugin instance became permanently stale: every plugin-surface RPC fails with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin kimi was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.`, repeating every minute via health refresh, and never recovers without a Gateway restart.

Meanwhile, **both** direct API calls to the provider and the Gateway's own transport-layer model fetches keep succeeding — so the provider and the network path are fine; only the plugin instance handle is dead.

No config change, no `plugins reload`, no install/uninstall happened around the failure window. The only precursor is the two idle timeouts from the model API.

## Timeline (journal, 2026-11-03, CST)

Trigger — two upstream idle timeouts (transport layer):

```
12:28:45 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=kimi api=anthropic-messages model=k3.1-pro elapsedMs=119957 message=LLM idle timeout (120s): no response from model
12:30:47 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=kimi api=anthropic-messages model=k3.1-pro elapsedMs=119993 message=LLM idle timeout (120s): no response from model
```

Transport recovers on its own (12:49–12:51, multiple `status=200` responses), then at 12:53:04 the plugin-surface errors erupt:

```
12:53:04 [session-events] Session change preparation failed error="Plugin kimi was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools."
12:53:04 [gateway] Lifecycle event dispatch failed sessionKey=… error="Plugin kimi was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools."
12:53:25 [health] refresh failed: Plugin kimi was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
12:53:31 Subagent announce failed: PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin kimi was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
12:53:53 [gateway] request handler failed: PluginInstanceUnavailableError: …
12:53:53 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ models.list 16ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=PluginInstanceUnavailableError: …
```

It never self-heals — `health refresh failed` fires once per minute for 20+ minutes (35+ occurrences as of 13:14, still ongoing), `models.list` stays UNAVAILABLE.

## Layered contradiction (same minute, two layers)

Plugin-surface RPC dead, transport-layer fetch alive:

```
12:53:53 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ models.list UNAVAILABLE (PluginInstanceUnavailableError)
12:58:33 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=kimi api=anthropic-messages model=k3.1-pro-highspeed status=200 elapsedMs=3325
```

Direct API probes (bypassing the Gateway entirely, taken at 13:14 while the plugin was still stale):

```
GET  https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/models            → 200 (0.19s)
POST https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages (8-token ping, k3.1-pro-highspeed) → 200 (0.88s, normal generation)
```

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (stable), Linux x64, `systemd --user` service
- kimi provider plugin: 2026.10.8, `enabled`, config intact (checked via `openclaw plugins list` / `inspect` while stale)
- Provider config: `api: anthropic-messages`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/`
- No config hot-reload, no plugin operation, no Gateway restart in the failure window
- Plugin instance recovers only after Gateway stop→start (pending)

## Related

- #154891 — same `PluginInstanceUnavailableError` signature, but triggered by failed/rolled-back config hot-reload. Our case shows a **different trigger path** (upstream LLM idle timeout, zero config/plugin activity) reaching what looks like the same dead-instance state.
- #165970 — plugin reload tears down active model instances.
- Possibly one root cause underneath: plugin instance lifecycle not rebuilt after an abnormal-path teardown.

## Suggested direction

A provider-side transport failure (idle timeout) should not leave the plugin instance permanently unavailable. Candidates: rebuild/replace the plugin instance when its handle is detected stale (e.g. after N consecutive `health refresh failed`), or decouple provider transport failures from plugin-instance teardown entirely.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Running a Gateway update from the Control UI on Windows (Scheduled Task install) stops the task/gateway and then hangs indefinitely at stage 4/7 ("Activating"). The Scheduled Task is left Disabled, no gateway process is running, and the npm package is NOT updated. Dialog shows: "Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it." Manual recovery: `schtasks /Change /TN "OpenClaw Gateway" /ENABLE` + `openclaw gateway start`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, npm-global OpenClaw 2026.9.5, gateway managed as Scheduled Task (logon trigger).
2. Control UI → update Gateway to the newer release (target 2026.10.2).
3. Update stops the task/gateway; dialog reaches "Activating" (completed 3 of 7 stages) and spins forever. Observed on two consecutive update attempts the same day.
4. Post-mortem after killing the dialog: Scheduled Task State=Disabled; zero gateway processes; `openclaw --version` still the OLD version; gateway log contains `update.run completed` RPC entries and the line "Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it."

### Expected behavior

Activation either completes (start the new build and verify) or fails loudly with an automatic rollback that restores the previous gateway AND re-enables the Scheduled Task. The task auto-start suspension performed before the update must be symmetrically resumed on every exit path (success, failure, interruption).

### Actual behavior

- Scheduled Task left Disabled; no gateway process; package version unchanged (update never landed).
- Control UI shows an endless spinner at "Activating" with no error surfaced to the user.
- After manual task re-enable + `openclaw gateway start`, the old build runs normally; a later CLI `openclaw update --yes` completes the update successfully.

### OpenClaw version

from 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), target 2026.10.2; CLI after manual recovery still 2026.9.5 until CLI update

### Operating system

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200

### Install method

npm global; gateway via Windows Scheduled Task (logon trigger)

### Model

main agent, glm-5.3 — issue is not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

local gateway → Control UI update flow → Windows Scheduled Task service manager

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Previous gateway was not verified: automatic rollback cannot restart it.   (update dialog step detail)

# gateway log around the same window:
update.run completed actor=openclaw-control-ui device=<redacted>
Runtime: stopped (state Disabled, last run 267014, last run time 2026-10-12T04:08:57.0000000Z)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Control UI dialog screenshot available on request (Chinese locale; stage list: Requested ✓ / Validating ✓ / Preparing ✓ / Activating (spinner) / Restarting / Verifying / Done).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Windows Scheduled Task installs using the Control UI update entry.
- Severity: high — gateway left down with a hung UI; unattended machines stay down until manual CLI recovery.
- Frequency: 2/2 attempts on 2026-10-12 (both update attempts failed identically).
- Consequence: users believe an update is in progress; no error is shown; remote/unattended gateways stay offline.

### Additional information

- The same target update completed successfully via CLI (`openclaw update --yes`) immediately afterwards, including service restart — so the failure is specific to the UI-driven/service-inspection path, not the package itself.
- Historical note (separate concern, possibly already fixed): an earlier 9.x gateway self-update persisted the retired transient key `plugins.installs` into openclaw.json; the running gateway does not validate, so the next cold start failed schema validation ("Unrecognized key: installs") and the logon-triggered auto-start aborted with "Refusing to run automatic gateway startup migrations because the selected config changed during startup" — which presents as "gateway did not auto-start after reboot". 2026.10.2's CLI update did NOT reproduce the writeback, and doctor auto-migrates the key now.
- Not a duplicate per issue search before filing (searches for "fs-safe-move EPERM", "update stuck Activating", "scheduled task disabled automatic rollback").

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On main `a93c259`, a focused test shows that after a `plugins` `reloadAndResume` handoff from a Control UI-shaped turn, in a session whose recorded delivery route is Telegram, the resumed turn runs on that Telegram route: both its reply and a `message` send without a target go to the Telegram chat (a mocked test channel), although the handoff tools say they resume "in this same conversation".

### Steps to reproduce

Repeatable form: a local focused test (not committed) at main `a93c259` runs the real `plugins` tool, the real handoff and the real resumed-turn dispatch with a Control UI-shaped caller and a mocked model, on a session whose recorded route is Telegram `999`, and records what a test Telegram channel receives (results under Actual behavior; method under "Screenshots, recordings, and evidence").

Product steps, derived from source reading; not run on a live Gateway:

1. Chat with the agent in Telegram in a session that Control UI can also open (for example the main session), so that the session records the Telegram chat as its delivery route. Keep the default reply settings (no `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`).
2. Open the same session in Control UI and ask the agent to reload a plugin and continue. The agent calls `plugins` with `action: "reloadAndResume"`, as the tool description directs.
3. After the reload, the resumed turn's reply is delivered to the Telegram chat.

By source reading, `github_publish` and a self-held `sessions_send` hand off through the same helper (`handoffSessionTool`) and resume the same way.

### Expected behavior

The resumed turn continues in the conversation that handed off. For a handoff from Control UI, its reply stays in the session transcript and nothing is auto-delivered to Telegram. References:

- The handoff helper tells the model "handed off; resume with its result in this same conversation" ([`session-tool-handoff.ts` L157](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts#L157)), and the resume event text says "Continue the original task in this conversation." ([L247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts#L247)).
- The `plugins` tool description says `reloadAndResume` will "resume this same conversation with success or failure" ([`plugins-tool.ts` L137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/tools/plugins-tool.ts#L137)).
- [`docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md` L341-L343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md?plain=1#L341-L343): `reloadAndResume` "reloads and resumes the same conversation with the result".
- By source reading, exec completion notifications already return to the turn that started them: the start-time route is recorded ([`bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts` L207-L212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts#L207-L212)) and passed as the event's `deliveryContext` ([`bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` L147-L152](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts#L147-L152)), so a notification started from Control UI stays in the transcript ([`session-event-handoff.ts` L458-L462](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts#L458-L462)).

### Actual behavior

Focused test at main `a93c259` (local, not committed); the session's recorded route is Telegram `999` and its chat type `direct`; IDs are synthetic. The yielding caller has the Control UI shape (`turnSourceChannel: "webchat"`, `turnSourceTo` set to the session key) and calls `plugins` `reloadAndResume`. In the resumed turn, the mocked model first calls `message` with `action: "send"` and no target, then replies with plain text:

1. The test Telegram channel received two sends, both to `999`: the `message` send ("This must stay in the session.") and the resumed turn's reply ("Reload resume stayed in the session.").
2. The resumed turn ran with `telegram` as its message provider and originating channel and `direct` as its chat type, and the resume settled as `completed` with `delivered: true`.

By source reading, this is because the resume event is enqueued with only the captured session target and no route of its own ([`session-tool-handoff.ts` L249-L265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts#L249-L265)), so its route is the captured target's route ([`session-event-handoff.ts` L104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts#L104)), which is the session's recorded Telegram route ([`session-event-target.ts` L237](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-target.ts#L237)). The resumed turn takes its originating channel and target from that route ([`session-event-context.ts` L198-L201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.ts#L198-L201)); its final reply passes the delivery gate ([`session-event-handoff.ts` L448-L463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts#L448-L463)), and a `message` send without a target resolves to the same chat ([`message-action-normalization.ts` L26-L48](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts#L26-L48)). The `message` part also applies when the yielding turn is an internal turn whose replies are not auto-delivered and that has no recipient of its own: its resume still runs on the recorded external route.

### OpenClaw version

Focused test: main a93c259fda08 (source checkout); not checked on a release build

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64), Node 24.22.1

### Install method

Source checkout with pnpm (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile); focused test run with OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node and pnpm test on the test file with --maxWorkers=1

### Model

Not model-specific: the route is chosen when the resume is enqueued; the focused test mocks the model runner

### Provider / routing chain

N/A: the focused test makes no provider request

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# Focused test at main a93c259 with the local test case added and no production change, run alone, with one
# diagnostic line added to the test for this run to print the outcome (label shortened, fields trimmed):
# OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/tools/plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps a Control UI reload resume internal'
diagnostic {"status":"completed","delivered":true,"sends":[{"to":"999","text":"This must stay in the session."},{"to":"999","text":"Reload resume stayed in the session."}],"messageProvider":"telegram","originatingChannel":"telegram","chatType":"direct"}
# The test's assertion that the Telegram test channel's sendText was not called:
AssertionError: expected [ [ { cfg: { …(4) }, …(30) } ], …(1) ] to deeply equal []
Tests  1 failed | 20 skipped (21)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Focused test (local, not committed), at main `a93c259`:

- Real code on the path: the `plugins` tool (`createPluginsTool`), the handoff helper `handoffSessionTool` and its session-target capture, `enqueueSessionEventForHost`, the resumed turn's dispatch and its `message` tool, and reply delivery up to the channel's `sendText`.
- Mocked or injected: the `plugins.reload` Gateway method (returns at once); the model runner (it calls `message` and returns a fixed reply); the yielding caller's identity, set by the test to the Control UI shape instead of being derived from a Control UI `chat.send`; a test channel plugin registered as `telegram` with a mocked `sendText`.
- The values in Logs were printed by a diagnostic line added to the local test for that run. The same test without the diagnostic line also failed on the base, on the same `sendText` assertion.

Source reading for the Control UI caller shape: a Control UI turn's origin is `webchat` with the session key as its target ([`chat-origin-routing.ts` L113-L117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-origin-routing.ts#L113-L117)), which becomes the tool caller's `turnSourceChannel` and `turnSourceTo` ([`attempt-gateway-tools.ts` L33-L39](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-gateway-tools.ts#L33-L39)). Such a turn keeps the session's recorded external route instead of replacing it ([`session-delivery.ts` L115-L131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.ts#L115-L131)). A separate local probe (not committed) through an in-process Gateway, with a Control UI client's `chat.send` and a scripted model calling `reloadAndResume`, observed this caller shape at the handoff and the resume enqueued without a route.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: by source reading, sessions whose recorded delivery route is an external chat, when a `plugins` `reloadAndResume`, `github_publish`, or self-held `sessions_send` handoff is started from Control UI or from another internal turn with no recipient of its own, with default reply settings.
- Severity: the resumed reply goes to the session's last external chat (for example a Telegram DM or group) instead of the Control UI conversation where the user asked for it; a `message` send without a target in the resumed turn goes there too.
- Frequency: by source reading, deterministic once the handoff captures an external recorded route; the focused test failed in 2/2 base runs.
- Consequence: after a plugin reload from Control UI, the continuation appears in the external chat (in the test, two messages to `999`). Whether Control UI also shows it live was not checked.

### Additional information

- The resume is enqueued with only the captured session target ([`session-tool-handoff.ts` L249-L265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts#L249-L265)). Local history inspection found no change involving `deliveryContext` in this enqueue path since the helper was introduced.
- A handoff from an external chat resumes in that chat: an external turn records its own route on the session when it is admitted ([`session.ts` L563-L600](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93c259fda08848306354f752fd998935ede694c/src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts#L563-L600)), so the captured route is that chat.

issues.title: Sharing one GPU between a local MoE engine and media renders (mmap experts + VRAM lending) — prior art?

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

issues.body:
### Sharing one GPU between a local MoE engine and media renders — has anyone else walked this road?

I run OpenClaw on a single RTX 3090 (24 GiB) with a flash-inference MoE engine serving chat at `:8080`, and the same card doing ComfyUI work (image-to-video, interpolation, upscale). Every attempt to render kept thrashing the box or leaving the engine sluggish afterwards, so I spent a day fixing it. What actually worked:

**1. mmap the experts instead of holding an anonymous arena.**
Maps are file-backed page cache (`RssFile`), so the kernel reclaims them on its own under pressure. Anonymous maps of the same size are *not* reclaimable — freeing them requires killing the process, which turns every park/unload/reload into an expensive event.

Measured: ~42 GiB mapped as `RssFile`, but only **2.3–4.1 GiB `RssAnon`**. Full expert cache stays at 8622/8622 slots / 14 302 MiB while in use, and a full unload lands at **584 MiB GPU / 4.7 GiB RAM used, 55 GiB available**.

**2. Lend VRAM; never stop the inference server for a render.**
`POST /v1/vram {"reserve_mib":N}` shrinks the expert cache instead of stopping the server, then hands it back. Gate the render start on measured free VRAM and refuse if it doesn't materialize.

**3. Governor: full cache while in use, unload when genuinely quiet.**
Full cache while a request is in flight or quiet ≤ 120 s; full **unload** at 10 min idle (parking alone doesn't help host RAM under mmap — the process has to exit). `/v1/unload` answers 409 while any request is in flight, so it needs a detached retryer (it took 11 tries before landing). The governor must also *skip cache re-fill* when the human deliberately unloaded, otherwise the next chat message silently rebuilds everything and the feature looks broken.

**4. The render bug was memory's fault only by appearance.**
A "HD pass" that kept crashing at 2.7 GiB RAM / 576 MiB free was running frame interpolation **and** RealESRGAN ×4 on a clip that was *already* 1920×1080 @ 48 fps — upscaling to ~3328×1920 and scaling back down. Deleting those nodes: multi-minute crash → **21 s wall**, reserve need dropped from 19 000 MiB to 7 000 MiB. The workflow also hardcoded an old stage-1 input path, so it "succeeded" against the wrong source.

**Net effect:** engine decode expert-cache hit rate went from **64.7% → 93.5%**, and reload after unload went from ~38 s to effectively free (page cache survives the hold — 47 GiB buff/cache stayed put through an 18-minute unload).

### Questions for anyone who has done this already

- Are you running a MoE flash-inference server *and* ComfyUI/video work on one card? How do you arbitrate VRAM — engine-side lending like above, or an external supervisor/admission layer?
- Anyone measured **mmap'd vs resident expert memory** on 24 GiB cards? Is my "anonymous arena is the real culprit" conclusion consistent with what you've seen?
- For "keep it unloaded until I say otherwise": anyone solved the `auto_load` race (model reloads on the next inbound request and rebuilds the whole cache)? We ended up with a self-polling watchdog service; a systemd timer driving a `Type=oneshot` unit fired once and never repeated (`Active: active (elapsed)`, `Trigger: n/a`) — is there a cleaner idiom?
- Related to #128388 (resource-aware admission for self-hosted providers, closed as stale): is provider-side readiness/admission still considered out of scope for core, or is the supervisor pattern documented anywhere now?

Happy to share exact numbers, unit files, and the workflow diff if useful.
