prs.title: fix(browser): preserve upload budgets across clock corrections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

File-chooser uploads can fail after a forward wall-clock correction even though their elapsed timeout budget remains available.

## User Impact

Accepted uploads keep their completion budget when the Gateway host's wall clock changes, including with remote-browser latency. No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `performance.now()` for the upload owner's three private elapsed checks: deadline creation and remaining atomic-click/native-assignment budgets. Existing timers, authority, cancellation, settlement ordering, strict upload paths and cleanup are unchanged. The cross-process download deadline deliberately remains epoch-based because it is compared inside Chrome's `page.evaluate`; unrelated monotonic origins cannot be exchanged.

The original commit by **zhangguiping-xydt** is retained. This is the same elapsed-budget defect category as #186531, not a browser redesign or new API.

## Evidence

[Built CLI/Gateway + real Chrome before/after proof and screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191668#issuecomment-6596251678).

- Secretless Linux `node:24.22.1` Docker, built artifacts, real Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4, fresh private browser/state/profile per run, public built browser CLI and final DOM evaluation.
- Transparent CDP proxy uniformly delays browser response chunks by 30 ms, without changing native upload messages or injecting upload failures.
- Main twice: after a +60-second **process-local Date.now wall-clock step**, real `input.files.length` stays **0**. Candidate twice: it becomes **1**, with the expected synthetic filename and visible counter. No-step controls succeed on both refs in all four runs.
- This is **not a system clock jump**: Chrome's clock, the OS clock, performance.now and timers are untouched, following #190894's preload method.
- Existing deadline regression strengthened to honor the native timeout during the clock correction. Main **1 intended failure / 6 passes**; candidate **7/7 pass**. Original authority, strict-path, passive-invocation, cancellation, supersession and cleanup controls retained.
- Targeted Oxfmt/Oxlint pass. Production +3/−3 (net 0); tests +15/−18 (net −3). Removed the now-unneeded 39-line allocation; no SDK export, baseline increase or new option.
- [Inherited test-line ratchet classification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191668#issuecomment-6596256090): source CI's 223-line excess and independent 219-line witness are different prepared main snapshots. No ratchet was rerun or baseline raised; exact-head CI is reported independently.

Frozen main `09f0b0b40080c6b96bff32fae7832b3253865470`; built candidate production artifact `0ccd2e3e55fd6d3f3349d24d8a3b7634cfc915f6`. Final follow-up only consolidates tests and documents the unchanged production behavior. Main integration picked up changed browser route/profile availability used by this proof.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous private clock comparisons with no migration. Blast radius is file-chooser upload timing; download clock exchange, path authorization, cancellation and per-page cleanup remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ci): unblock allocated tests after inherited budget debt
prs.body:
Closes #191680

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fully allocated test additions failing CI because main already exceeds its effective test-line ceiling. The inherited deficit blocked #191676 despite its exact 37-line allocation.

## User Impact

Contributors can add justified regression coverage with matching allocations again. This is an internal accounting repair; no product behavior or tests change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconcile exactly **834** inherited lines at main `29e1324fa3370afb9c01486e24b857f7603ce6f4`: scalar **6,319,970 → 6,320,804**. Existing allocations remain **100,412**, so the effective ceiling becomes **6,421,216**, exactly the measured total. No speculative headroom is added.

This is the documented, operator-directed scalar-only reconciliation after auditing the missing grants. A retroactive allocation record alone would exceed the checker's credit bound because this repair adds zero test lines. The checker and that enforcement stay unchanged; no test shrinking/splitting, allocation padding, or CI exception.

The first crossing was `2a32ab046f2502654175864962c34e2033a11cae` (#191638): 48 unallocated test LF consumed the remaining two-line slack and left 46 lines of debt. Further omissions account for the full current deficit:

| Landed change | Unallocated literal test LF |
| --- | ---: |
| `2a32ab046f` — #191638, settled-wake regressions | +48 |
| `6d172664c8` — #191548, unsupported-npx diagnostic regression | +7 |
| `24aff34974` — #191604, proactive Teams delivery regressions | +170 |
| `9cf93b0833` — direct image-error diagnostics | +238 |
| `c29085dbfe` — #189887, native tool rewrite/approval regressions | +409 |

These sum to 872. The original two-line slack and subsequent 36-line reductions leave exactly **834**. Fully allocated intervening changes have zero effect on the deficit. Original before/after Git blobs were counted by literal LF using the checker's pathspecs; the result is not estimated from PR diff size.

Reported by @obviyus in #191680. No active competing maintainer repair was found before claiming this issue. Requested repair scope is this exact audited reconciliation, followed by normal green-CI landing of #191676.

## Evidence

- Actual main-push failure: [41583908048 / 125744815716](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41583908048/job/125744815716), head `29e1324f`, base `e851dbf7`: `Test lines: 6421216; ceiling: 6420382; over by: 834; net delta: +148`.
- Earlier [pinned-main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41581396479/job/125736975095): head `09f0b0b4`, 840-line deficit. The later [scheduled green job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41583880349/job/125745007092) explicitly remained 834 over and passed only because its delta was zero; that was not a budget repair.
- Literal-LF and allocation-history audit traced the crossing and every subsequent debt change. New scalar arithmetic: 6,320,804 + 100,412 = 6,421,216.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the one-line candidate against `29e1324f`, Codex P0–P2: scoped-clean, complete coverage, no findings. Simplification retained only the scalar correction.
- `git diff --check` and targeted scalar/arithmetic validation pass. No broad check, product test, staging, packaging, container, or browser ran on the production Team host. Hosted PR CI must report the tree within budget, in addition to all required checks passing, before merge.
- No CHANGELOG, dependency, protocol, or test changes. Existing tests prove the allocation enforcement; this data correction does not add a duplicate test.

prs.title: feat(plugins): reload edited bundled plugin code in development with OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Developers working on bundled plugins, such as Knowledge, have to restart the Gateway to test every edit to the plugin's server code. `openclaw plugins reload <id>` refreshes the plugin's registrations, but bundled code keeps running from the host and the reload returns `restartRequired: true`.

## User Impact

A developer can start a Node/Bun source checkout or compiled-on-disk Gateway with `OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1`. With it set, `openclaw plugins reload <id>` loads that bundled plugin's edited code from disk and returns `restartRequired: false`, with a warning that the replaced code stays in memory until restart.

**Nothing changes when the variable is unset.** Bundled code stays host-owned, and reload returns `restartRequired: true` with the existing warning. The opt-in must come from the Gateway's launch environment: there is no config key, CLI flag, RPC field or UI toggle, and config `env.vars` can't set it, so `config.patch`, agents and remote clients can't turn it on. Standalone executables (JIT, bytecode and AOT) ignore the variable and say so in the reload receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

This restores the capture path from #180466, plus the Worker host-link repairs from #181128 and #181458, but only behind the operator opt-in. It reuses the existing captured-generation, worker preparation and recovery owners, so there's no second reload subsystem.

**How this addresses the concerns behind #182403:**

- **Embedded/AOT builds have no physical files to recapture.** Standalone executables ignore the opt-in (`isStandaloneRuntimeExecutable`), keep embedded code, and return `restartRequired: true` with a warning that the variable was ignored. No filesystem discovery runs.
- **Bundled modules get a second code identity.** That never happens by default. With the opt-in, only plugins named in an explicit `plugins.reload` are recaptured: the plugin tree plus the chunks that `dist/runtime-dependency-ownership.json` lists for that plugin. Those chunks are used only by plugins, though other plugins may share them. Host, SDK and core-shared chunks still resolve to the Gateway's loaded modules, including from captured Workers.
- **Embedded provider-auth fix.** Untouched; `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-runtime.ts` isn't modified.
- **Production regressions after #180466** (#181494 setup activation, and the capture-scanner stall from #182194). The capture path can't be reached by default. Even with the opt-in it isn't used for startup, config-driven reloads (including model changes), setup modules or public surfaces, because the reload's lifecycle reason must be `reload`.

**Launch-only opt-in:** `isConfigRuntimeEnvVarAllowed` (the config env admission owner) rejects `OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`, alongside the other deployment-owned host controls. A config write can't publish it into `process.env`.

**Fix found end to end:** A bundled capture is rooted at the host package, and binding the plugin's cache root to that capture root merged the host package's cache record into the plugin's. Later cold public-surface loads, for example a web-search provider, then failed to resolve `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`. The plugin now keeps its own cache root, and a regression assertion covers it.

**Updated onto current main:** main extracted reference resolution into `plugin-generation-reference-capture.ts` and added source snapshots and captured-directory tracking. Bundled reload now plugs into the extracted resolver through one optional `linkSharedModule` hook; snapshot and directory capture are unchanged and never run on the bundled reload path.

**Env-var budget:** `config/env-var-count-budget.txt` grows from 459 to 460 for this owner-approved name.

**Accepted edge cases (documented):**
- JavaScript module graphs can't be unloaded, so each development reload keeps the previous graph until the process exits.
- If a config-driven reload later replaces a dev-reloaded plugin, it goes back to the Gateway's loaded code.
- Setup modules, public surfaces and host/SDK edits still need a restart.
- **Not yet proven:** plugin state operations (`*-operation-api` modules, for example memory-core recall) for a dev-reloaded bundled plugin. They load from the captured copy rather than the shared bundled operation capture. Knowledge has no operation APIs. Treat this as unverified until a follow-up adds a check.

## Evidence

- **Gateway reload regression** (`server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts`): unchanged main assertions still show an edited bundled helper stays `A` with `restartRequired: true`. With the opt-in, the same reload loads `B`, then `C`, with `restartRequired` absent and a sibling plugin retained. Negative control: disabling the gate makes the new assertion fail (`expected true to be undefined`).
- **Loader matrix restored from #180466** (`plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts`, 12 tests): source TS, compiled CJS/ESM, runtime overlay and denied file links, Worker shared imports across recovery, plus the WASM, directory-cycle and discarded-URL capture regressions. The new cache-root assertion fails on all 5 layout cases without the fix.
- **CommonJS shared imports:** captured CommonJS code reaches shared host modules after #185033 started routing `require` through `module.registerHooks`. Without the fix, raw `pnpm vitest run` failed the compiled-CJS and source-TS layout cases with `Cannot find module 'file:///…/shared.cjs'`; with it, all 12 pass under both runners.
- **Gate/refusal** (`bundled-plugin-dev-reload.test.ts`, `config.env-vars.test.ts`): off by default; explicit reload targets only; a mocked standalone executable ignores the variable with a warning; config `env.vars` can't publish it.
- **Isolated Gateway, end to end** (rerun on 2026-11-02 against the compiled `pnpm build:runtime` output of the tree now on current main, identical results to the earlier run; no `Cannot find module` errors in either Gateway log; separate state dir and port; the live Gateway wasn't touched). A module-evaluation marker was appended to Knowledge's plugin-owned `dist/storage-protocol-*.mjs`. Each run started with marker `A`, edited the file to `B`, then ran `openclaw plugins reload knowledge`:

```text
== CFGONLY (launch env unset; config env.vars.OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS="1")
  "restartRequired": true,
    "Bundled plugin code is owned by the running Gateway. Restart the Gateway to load updated code; rebuild first when using compiled output."
== CFGONLY markers after reload:
A main=true
== LAUNCH (OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 in the Gateway's launch environment)
  "restartRequired": false,
    "Development reload loaded knowledge from disk; replaced code stays in memory until the Gateway restarts."
== LAUNCH markers after reload:
A main=true
B main=true
```

  An earlier run with the variable fully unset matched CFGONLY. `tools.invoke knowledge_status` behaved the same in every mode afterwards. It failed for the expected reason in this test setup: the session has no memory audience.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed .ts files>
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts \
  src/plugins/bundled-plugin-dev-reload.test.ts src/config/config.env-vars.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-generation-*.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-instance-module-loader.*.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-state-operation-source.test.ts src/plugins/loader.runtime-registry.test.ts \
  src/plugins/setup-registry.lifecycle.test.ts src/plugins/public-surface-loader.test.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/facade-loader.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Changes walkthrough</summary>

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-dev-reload.ts` | Owns the opt-in, standalone refusal and receipt warning |
| `src/config/config-env-values.ts` | Config env vars can't set the launch-only opt-in |
| `src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.ts` | Restored ownership/shared-module policy; cache root |
| `src/gateway/server-plugins.ts` | Derives explicit reload targets from the lifecycle request |
| `src/plugins/lifecycle.ts` | Captured digest → dev warning; otherwise existing restart warning |
| `src/plugins/loader-module-runtime.ts`, `loader-runtime-core.ts`, `loader-types.ts` | Carry gated reload targets to the module loader |
| `src/plugins/plugin-instance-module-loader.ts` | Bundled shared path unless the gate selected the plugin |
| `src/plugins/plugin-generation-*.ts`, `plugin-native-module-loader.ts`, `plugin-module-loader-recovery.ts` | Restored #180466/#181128/#181458 capture plumbing and Worker host links |
| `src/plugins/plugin-generation-reference-capture.ts` | Optional `linkSharedModule` hook keeps host-shared chunks canonical during bundled capture |
| `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.ts` | Passes the lifecycle request instead of only its digests |
| `config/env-var-count-budget.txt` | Records the approved name (459 → 460) |
| `docs/cli/plugins/uninstall-and-update.md` | New "Development: reload edited bundled code" section |
| `docs/plugins/architecture.md`, `manage-plugins.md`, protocol, `environment.md` | Pointers to the development mode |

</details>

prs.title: fix(telegram): typing held back by a flood wait is logged as an error
prs.body:
Closes #191686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway logs an ERROR for every typing action that Telegram flood control held back, although the request was never sent.

## User Impact

User impact: during a Telegram flood wait, typing that OpenClaw deliberately skips no longer writes `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (flood wait active; request not sent)` at ERROR. A 429 that Telegram itself returns, and any other API failure, still log at ERROR. The flood wait is still logged once at WARN by `telegram/flood`. Nothing about sending changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account limiter answers a replaceable request it holds back (typing, preview updates) with a synthetic 429 whose description ends in `; request not sent)`. grammY turns that into a `GrammyError`, and `withTelegramApiErrorLogging` logged it like any API failure. The logging owner now recognizes the limiter's own refusal and skips it, for every operation it wraps, so the three typing call sites need no per-site filter. The limiter builds its description from the same exported suffix, so the mark has one definition. The error is still thrown, so typing keepalive failure counting and the chat-action cooldown behave as before.

Simplification against an earlier draft of this branch: the first version exported a predicate from the limiter and added a `shouldLog` filter at each of the three typing call sites. This version moves the decision into the logging wrapper: production change +17/-3 lines in 2 files, against +21/-2 in 4.

## Evidence

- Regression test (`api-logging.test.ts`), one case per typing call site (inbound reply, recovered forum topic, outbound `sendTypingTelegram`), through grammY's `Api`, the real account throttler and chat-action handler, and a scripted Bot API:
  - Telegram 429s a preview edit, then typing during the wait is held back.
  - After the wait, Telegram 429s typing itself, then returns a 400.
  - The test asserts that the `telegram/api` error logger receives exactly the real 429 and the 400, and that only 2 sendChatAction requests reached the network.
- `account-throttler.test.ts`: typing held back at the gate and typing held back at the network edge after the per-chat action queue both carry the `request not sent` description; Telegram's own 429 does not.
- Fail without, pass with:
  - With the suppression removed from the logger, 3 of 13 `api-logging.test.ts` cases fail, each with the extra line `telegram sendChatAction failed: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 30 (flood wait active; request not sent))` (`telegram typing failed: ...` for the outbound case).
  - With the fix, both files pass: 37 of 37.
- Consumers: the 34 Telegram test files that import a changed module or cover message context, dispatch and polling pass (633 tests). `withTelegramApiErrorLogging` has 20 call sites in the extension; no test elsewhere expects an ERROR for a held-back request (`git grep "request not sent"` finds only the throttler test).
- `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and the line-cap, assertion-safety and test-line ratchets pass against `586f5766569`. Test-line growth is 134 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-typing-flood-log-level.txt`.
- Not covered end to end: Crabline's Telegram server cannot return a flood 429 for a Bot API method, so no qa-lab scenario can reach this path, and I did not provoke real Telegram flood control on a live bot.

prs.title: improve(telegram): polling workers start faster and use half the memory
prs.body:
Closes #190889

## What Problem This Solves

Each Telegram polling account runs `getUpdates` in its own worker thread, and every worker loads the debug proxy capture store (about 1,250 modules, roughly 20 MiB of heap) even though capture is off unless `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED` is set. A Gateway with three bot accounts carries about 60 MiB for code that never runs, and every polling restart pays the import again.

## User Impact

Each Telegram polling worker holds about half the heap (42.2 → 21.9 MiB) and reaches its first successful poll in less than half the time (487 → 202 ms). With debug proxy capture enabled, the worker records `getUpdates` exchanges exactly as it does on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker imported the transport through `fetch.ts`, whose static `plugin-sdk/proxy-capture` import evaluates the capture store graph. The transport core now lives in `fetch-transport.ts` and takes the capture owner functions as an option. `fetch.ts` keeps `resolveTelegramTransport` and `resolveTelegramFetch` with the same signatures and passes the SDK functions, so main-thread callers keep capture unchanged.

The parent decides capture with the owner's `resolveDebugProxySettings().enabled` and passes it in `workerData`. Only then does the worker import `fetch.js`, after its stop listener is registered. The worker marker moves to a side-effect-free protocol module; importing it from the parent factory also pulled in `process-runtime`. The six type assertions that move with the transport now carry `// SAFETY:` comments, so the assertion baseline loses its Telegram fetch entry instead of moving it.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule written before measuring: correctness identical, evaluated modules −30% or more, retained worker heap −10 MiB or more, first poll-success wall and CPU median ≤ 1.05× and p95 ≤ 1.20×, steady CPU per poll ≤ 1.05×.

Built worker against a loopback Bot API (one empty short poll, a 20-update batch acked like the parent spool, then empty polls), 10 samples per arm, order alternating each sample, idle host (load 0.2–0.7):

```
node scripts/perf/telegram-ingress-worker-measure.mjs --build-dir <head> --compare-build-dir <base> --samples 10 --output <json>
```

| Metric (median) | main 0ce08d269ff | this branch | ratio | p95 ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Evaluated modules | 1,794 | 550 | 0.31 | 0.31 |
| Worker heap after full GC | 42.21 MiB | 21.86 MiB | 0.52 | 0.52 |
| Construction → first poll-success | 486.7 ms | 202.2 ms | 0.42 | 0.42 |
| Worker CPU to first poll-success | 483.7 ms | 199.3 ms | 0.41 | 0.45 |
| Worker CPU, 20-update batch | 4.51 ms | 2.15 ms | 0.48 | 0.30 |
| Worker CPU per steady empty poll | 3.04 ms | 2.88 ms | 0.95 | 0.94 |

Both arms send the same poll sequence (offsets `null, null, 1020`, timeouts `0, 1, 1`) and ack update 1019.

Whole Gateway, built `dist` of each checkout, booted from a copied state with three Telegram polling accounts inside a network-less sandbox (the workers stay in their poll retry loop, which keeps the import cost and drops the traffic). 5 boots per arm, order flipping each round, idle host (load 0.35–0.91). Each boot waits for `/healthz`, settles 120 s, then opens Node's inspector with `SIGUSR1`, forces a full GC in every isolate and reads `Runtime.getHeapUsage` per worker. Rule written before the run: Telegram worker heap median −10 MiB or more each, process RSS median not higher, spawn → `/healthz` median ≤ 1.10×.

| Metric (median of 5 boots) | main 0ce08d269ff | this branch | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heap per Telegram worker after full GC (3 per boot) | 42.10 MiB | 21.77 MiB | −20.3 MiB |
| All worker heaps after full GC | 726.2 MiB | 665.6 MiB | −60.6 MiB |
| Main isolate heap after full GC | 328.1 MiB | 328.3 MiB | 1.00× |
| Process RSS after 120 s settle | 1,881 MiB | 1,786 MiB | −95 MiB |
| Process RSS after forced GC | 1,751 MiB | 1,652 MiB | −99 MiB |
| Spawn → `/healthz` 200 | 7,807 ms | 7,794 ms | 1.00× |

The Telegram heap spread is under 0.03 MiB in both arms. The fifth boot of each arm had extra non-Telegram workers (29 and 27 instead of 23), which raises that boot's RSS in both arms and leaves the medians unchanged.

Capture enabled, whole Gateway: fresh state, one Telegram polling account whose `apiRoot` points at a loopback fake Bot API (first `getUpdates` empty, the second returns update 5000, then empty), network-less sandbox, one run per build:

```
openclaw proxy run -- env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<gateway state> openclaw gateway run
```

The Gateway child gets its own state dir because `proxy run` holds the owner lease of its own. The run stops after the fifth `getUpdates` (still in flight at shutdown, so four pairs are recorded); `openclaw proxy sessions --json` then lists one `proxy-run` session (34 events on this branch, 36 on main; the extra two are the sandbox's failed DNS lookups for update checks). These are the `getUpdates` rows of that session's `capture_events`, with the bot token replaced by `<token>` and the loopback `host:port` by `<fake-bot-api>`:

```
kind      method  path                                  status  stored body                          meta_json
request   POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  -       offset=none timeout=0 limit=100      {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
response  POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  200     ok=true results=0                    {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
request   POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  -       offset=none timeout=30 limit=100     {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
response  POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  200     ok=true results=1 update_ids=[5000]  {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
request   POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  -       offset=5001 timeout=30 limit=100     {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
response  POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  200     ok=true results=0                    {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
request   POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  -       offset=5001 timeout=30 limit=100     {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
response  POST    <fake-bot-api>/bot<token>/getUpdates  200     ok=true results=0                    {"subsystem":"telegram-fetch"}
```

The stored batch response is `{"ok":true,"result":[{"update_id":5000,"message":{"message_id":1,"date":1793577600,"chat":{"id":4242,"type":"private"},"from":{"id":4242,"is_bot":false,"first_name":"Proof"},"text":"capture proof"}}]}` (synthetic). Main records the same eight rows (its first two responses land in the other order), and both builds record the same 14 main-thread Telegram rows (`getMe`, `deleteWebhook`, `deleteMyCommands`, `setMyCommands`, `sendMessage`). On this branch the worker's transport records only when the worker loaded `fetch.js` from the parent's `debugProxyCapture` flag, so these rows also show that flag reaching the worker.

When the Gateway owns capture itself (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED=1` without `proxy run`), both builds record those main-thread rows and none of the worker's `getUpdates`: the worker's capture store open is refused with `Shared-state admission requires the host broker`, because `openSharedStateSqliteWorkerStore` rejects callers off the main thread. That is the same on main, and this PR does not change it.

Measured on `0ce08d269ff`, and the capture runs use the same two builds. The branch is rebased onto `fc6dff488ce` without conflicts; `0ce08d269ff..fc6dff488ce` does not touch `extensions/telegram`, `src/proxy-capture` or the proxy CLI, and the SAFETY comments and the dropped marker re-export added after the measurements do not change runtime code. The checks below were rerun on the rebased branch.

Tests: Telegram fetch, keepalive, ingress worker (factory, runtime, deadline, context) and polling session, plus `src/proxy-capture/coverage.test.ts`: 8 files, 72 tests pass. No unit case is added: the capture run above shows the parent's debug proxy setting reaching the worker and the worker recording its `getUpdates` exchanges. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm deadcode:exports`, oxlint and oxfmt pass, and the CI baseline ratchets (`check:baseline-ratchets`, max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, database worker and dialect, timeout race, mock exports) pass against the PR base `fc6dff488ce`.

Overlap: open #151923 also edits `extensions/telegram/src/fetch.ts` (dispatcher pool options). The changes are independent, but git will report a conflict for whichever lands second, and that branch moves its `fetch.ts` edits into `fetch-transport.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Diff shape</summary>

`git diff -M -B` shows `fetch.ts → fetch-transport.ts` as a 95% similar copy; the changes there are the type-only SDK import, the `debugProxyCapture` option, the early return in `captureResponse`, and `resolveTelegramFetch` moving to the new `fetch.ts`. `scripts/lib/type-assertion-guard-scope.mjs` follows the existing chained assertions to the new path, and the SAFETY comments remove the file's line from `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt`. `polling-session.test.ts` imports the marker from the protocol module.

</details>

prs.title: fix(voice-call): live transcript repeats replies and drops caller lines on realtime calls
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191688

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `live.transcript: true`, live transcript batches on a realtime call repeat the assistant's replies and never deliver the caller's lines when caller ASR finalizes after the reply has started.

This follows https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602, which sorts that late caller line ahead of the reply in the transcript.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159138

## User Impact

User impact: the requester session receives every final call line once during the call, including what the callee said. The end-of-call report is unchanged. A caller line that finalizes late arrives in the batch after the reply it prompted, so live batches can be out of dialogue order; the report stays in dialogue order.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191602, `addTranscriptEntry` sorts the transcript by timestamp. A late caller line is therefore inserted before entries that were already batched.

`observeCall` collected new lines with `transcript.slice(cursor)`. After the insert, that slice picks up the shifted reply again and never reaches the caller line.

Live delivery now records which transcript entries it has handed to a batch and sends the final entries it has not sent yet. Entries are the same objects across call snapshots within a process. The persisted cursor and the batch idempotency keys keep their meaning.

Accepted edge case: after a Gateway restart mid-call, delivery resumes from the persisted index cursor, as on main. A late caller line sorted in before that index (before the restart or in the first event after it) is not sent live, and the last delivered line is sent once more. The end-of-call report keeps the full transcript.

## Evidence

Tested at `39e0b70c8d5` (base `upstream/main` `f77ca8f4666`).

The voice-call plugin ran in a harness:
- A real local WebSocket carrier stream (Twilio-style `start` event) fed `RealtimeCallHandler`.
- The real call manager (`provider: "twilio"`, `realtime.enabled`, `reports: { enabled: true, includeTranscript: true }`, `live: { transcript: true, minIntervalMs: 20 }`) handled the call.
- Live transcript delivery was the real runtime.
- The realtime provider bridge was synthetic: for each of two exchanges it emitted speech started, the assistant reply, then the caller's final line.
- The requester-session sends were captured at the Gateway request boundary.

Both sides ran the same script.

Full captures of what the requester session received: [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-191602-live-transcript-cursor/before-live.txt), [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-191602-live-transcript-cursor/after-live.txt). In them, the `[live:…]` and `[report:…]` line prefixes and the `---` separators come from the capture harness (the end of each message's idempotency key), not from the text the session receives.

Before (base `f77ca8f4666`), excerpt:

```text
[live:0-1:0] Assistant: Friday at nine works.
[live:1-2:0] Assistant: Friday at nine works.
[live:2-3:0] Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
[live:3-4:0] Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
[report:0]   Callee: Is Friday free? / Assistant: Friday at nine works. / Callee: Can you bring the part? / Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
```

After (this PR), excerpt:

```text
[live:0-1:0] Assistant: Friday at nine works.
[live:1-2:0] Callee: Is Friday free?
[live:2-3:0] Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
[live:3-4:0] Callee: Can you bring the part?
[report:0]   Callee: Is Friday free? / Assistant: Friday at nine works. / Callee: Can you bring the part? / Assistant: Yes, I will bring it.
```

Each excerpt puts one message on a line. Left out: the `Voice call <id>, live transcript:` header of each live message, and the report's header lines (`Voice call <id>`, `Outcome`, `Duration`, `End reason`); its transcript lines are joined with ` / `.

Observed result: on the base, each reply is delivered twice and no `Callee:` line arrives live. With the fix, each final line is delivered once and both callee lines arrive. The report is the same on both sides.

The new test in `call-delivery.test.ts` sends a reply and then a caller line stamped earlier into one live batch. It expects `Callee` then `Assistant`. It fails on the base (the batch holds the reply twice) and passes with the fix.

Checks:
- touched tests `pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/call-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (8 passed) and `call-delivery-runtime.test.ts`;
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/voice-call/tsconfig.json --noEmit`;
- `oxlint --type-aware` and the format check on the changed files.

The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/voice-call/src/call-delivery.test.ts` | 10.7 s |

Test lines: `check:test-lines-ratchet` is red on this PR, as it is on main; the overage is inherited from main. The run on this head (`--base f77ca8f4666`) reports:

```text
Test lines: 6419874; ceiling: 6419651; over by: 223; net delta: +13.
```

Without this change, main at `f77ca8f4666` has 6419861 lines against a ceiling of 6419638, the same 223 over. The allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/` matches this change's +13 lines exactly. The test is needed because no existing test covers a line inserted before entries already sent in a live batch.

Simplify pass:
- The pending `lines` queue is gone; delivery state now records the entries already sent.
- Production +20/−6, tests +14/−1, plus the 2-line allocation file, against the merge base.

Not covered:
- No real carrier call or realtime provider; the bridge events are synthetic.
- No running Gateway; requester-session sends were captured at `runtime.gateway.request`.
- The restart edge case above (resume from the persisted index cursor, as on main) was not reproduced.

prs.title: fix: channel DM dismiss stays idle while pending
prs.body: Closes #147824 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where confirming **Dismiss** on a channel DM access request left the confirmation labeled “Dismiss” with no progress copy, while the request row’s **Approve** button switched to “Loading…” even though only dismissal was running. ## Why This Change Was Made The pairing owner already interlocks approve and dismiss on one busy request ID, but it did not remember which operation was in flight. That identity now travels with the busy request, and the hub queue plus confirmation dialog derive matching pending labels and accessible names from it. Pairing policy is unchanged. ## User Impact While a dismissal is pending, Dismiss shows “Dismissing…” on the dialog and the matching row action. Approve keeps its idle label. Approving still shows “Approving…” instead of a generic loading label. Failed requests still surface the error and restore the actions. ## Evidence Held `channels.pairing.dismiss` against this branch’s Control UI with the repository mocked Gateway, then read the rendered DOM. English, dark, 1440 × 1100. Google Chrome 148.0.7778.96 and Playwright 1.63.0 on Linux. Head `fe78e13f5681487768bf800a196a8ae384ab7a7d`. These captures are from this PR, not overlapping #148224. **Before** — confirmation keeps the idle verb; the row’s Approve action borrows the loading label **After** — the confirmation reports the dismissal it is running **Recovery** — a rejected dismissal restores idle Dismiss/Approve labels and shows the error **Approve pending** — Approving… on the confirmation; Dismiss stays idle Rendered values from the same Chromium sessions. The modal blurs the queue, so row labels and accessible names were read from the live DOM while the request was held: | Reading | Before (dismiss held) | After (dismiss held) | After recovery | After (approve held) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Confirmation label | `Dismiss` | `Dismissing…` | `Dismiss` | `Approving…` | | Row Approve label | `Loading…` | `Approve` | `Approve` | `Approving…` | | Row Dismiss label | `Dismiss` | `Dismissing…` | `Dismiss` | `Dismiss` | | Row Approve accessible name | `Approve 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Approve 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Approve 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Approving 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | | Row Dismiss accessible name | `Dismiss 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Dismissing 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Dismiss 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | `Dismiss 555000111 for Telegram, account Work` | | Any `Loading…` copy in the row | present | absent | absent | absent | | Dialog error | none | none | `Dismissal failed` | none | The before column is this branch with `ui/src/pages/channels/view.pairing.ts` restored to parent `78f1ce5505f` for the unfixed renderer. The after columns are head `fe78e13f568`. Overlapping https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148224 remains open and unmerged. Its CI gate is still failing (`checks-ui-e2e` 5/13 and 13/13, `check-dependencies`, `openclaw/ci-gate` on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34840179936). This PR is not closed as a duplicate while that landing path is unverified. No competing merged PR for #147824. Source-proven on current main: `pairingBusyRequestId` alone drove Approve to `common.loading` and left Dismiss/confirm idle. Focused Vitest (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/view.pairing.test.ts ui/src/lib/channels/index.test.ts`): **34 passed**, including: - dismiss in flight records `pairingBusyKind: "dismiss"` and clears it after settle - dismiss pending copy and aria on the row and confirmation; Approve stays idle - approve pending copy and aria on the row and confirmation; Dismiss stays idle - existing mutation interlock still disables sibling actions Local gates on `fe78e13f568`: - `pnpm build` passed - `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed - `tsgo:ui` and `tsgo:core:test` passed - oxfmt, oxlint, and stylelint passed on the touched files - Control UI source-mode Playwright capture on this head passed (dismiss pending, recovery, approve pending) Full `pnpm check && pnpm test` were not rerun end-to-end; the UI lanes above cover the changed contract.

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body:
Closes #190485
Related: #173760, #173845, #146646

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions.

## User Impact

User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number".

Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt.

The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string.

The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected.

## Evidence

- Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot.
- Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines).
- New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails.
- Card text from the real Telegram and Teams renderers for a single question with options: main shows `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default`; this branch shows `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text.
- `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety and test-line ratchets are clean against `1b15b48e2f3`. Test-line growth is 59 lines (the 7 parser cases of the first revision, 108 lines, are now one 5-row table), recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`.
- Not covered: no live Telegram run after the fix. The qa-lab scenario answers through `chat.send` (the same reply path Telegram text uses), because a qa-channel reply cannot reach a pending question while the turn is blocked.

prs.title: fix(ui): match NFD macOS file paths against NFC preview search queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the file preview modal's search filter fails to find files whose paths contain accented or combining characters when those paths come from macOS (NFD/decomposed Unicode) and the user types the same text in composed form (NFC).

## User Impact

User impact: on macOS, where file paths contain decomposed Unicode (e.g. `plans/resumé.md` stored as NFD), searching for `resumé` (typed as NFC) now finds the file in the preview modal. Previously the file was invisible to the search even though it was listed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter in `file-preview-modal.tsx` compared raw strings:

```ts
`${file.path}\n${file.contents}`.toLowerCase().includes(query)
```

macOS file paths use NFD (decomposed) Unicode while keyboard input is NFC (composed); the raw `includes()` check fails across the two forms. The fix canonicalizes both sides to NFC — the same approach as #188883 for the session-diff jump search (the sibling UI search site fixed yesterday). No other preview behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main, regression test only: a file with an NFD path (`plans/resumé.md`.normalize("NFD")) is invisible when searching with the NFC form of the same word:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.test.ts
 × matches NFD macOS file paths against NFC search queries
   → expected +0 to be 1
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the same file is found, and the full suite passes:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.test.ts
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Also verified: `pnpm format:check`.

prs.title: fix(agents): Fast mode unavailable for Anthropic API keys from config or environment
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native apps hide or disable the Fast mode control, and the Control UI default-model settings omit Fast, when the Anthropic API key comes from the config file (`models.providers.anthropic.apiKey`) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead of an auth profile.

## User Impact

User impact: users with an Anthropic API key in their config or environment can turn Fast on from the Android, iOS and macOS apps and choose it in the Control UI default-model settings, the same as users with an auth profile. The Control UI chat and `/fast` already worked and are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog passed the selected auth mode to provider Fast policies unchanged. That mode is `"api_key"` for an auth profile but `"api-key"` for a config or environment key, and the Anthropic Fast policy accepts only `"api_key"`, so `models.list` published no `supportsFastMode` for those keys. The fix normalizes the mode once where the host builds the policy context, using the existing normalizer that runtime choice and Doctor already use. This is the Fast-control sibling of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164556, which fixed the same mismatch for the Ultrafast picker gate.

<details>
<summary>Owner choice and alternatives</summary>

- Request construction already passes `"api_key"` for any non-OAuth Anthropic key, so only the catalog and the request disagreed. With this change, every provider policy sees one spelling, the policy cache keys on the normalized mode, and modes the normalizer does not know pass through unchanged.
- The producer keeps `"api-key"`: it is the config `auth` vocabulary that other consumers read and already normalize, so changing it there would touch each of them for no user-visible gain. Accepting both spellings in the Anthropic policy instead would push the two spellings onto every third-party policy. The Anthropic policy is the only bundled Fast policy that reads `authMode`.
- The `selectedCredential.requirement` that https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164556 used cannot replace `authMode` here: it is `"api-key"` or `"subscription"` and does not tell OAuth (no Fast) from a token (unknown).
- The plugin SDK runtime-hooks page now states that an API key reports `authMode: "api_key"` whatever its source.

</details>

## Evidence

Tested at `3625fd3292c` (base `main` at `5342923d897`).

**Gateway catalog.** For each key source, an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port, synthetic key, no provider call) answered `models.list` on the base and on this branch:

| Key source | Before `supportsFastMode` | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models.providers.anthropic.apiKey` | absent | `true` |
| same, with `auth: "api-key"` | absent | `true` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | absent | `true` |
| auth profile (`api_key`) | `true` | `true` |

Rows per source (claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-4-6 as listed): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/fast-support-before-after.txt

**Android client.** A scripted run on an Android 16 emulator, wiped before each side, with the same app build on both sides and only the Gateway checkout differing. The key was in `models.providers.anthropic.apiKey`. The script paired through "Set up manually", opened Chat with `claude-opus-4-6`, opened the Effort sheet, tapped Fast mode, and then read the session's stored `fastMode` from the Gateway state. The control checks (the model in the composer, the Fast mode row in the sheet) were met on both sides.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fast mode switch after the tap | **off** (disabled) | on |
| session `fastMode` after the tap | **unset** | `true` |

![Effort sheet after tapping Fast mode, Before (left) and After (right)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/fast-switch-before-after.png)

Full screens: [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/before-2-after-tap.png), [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261101-anthropic-fast-config-key-finding/after-2-after-tap.png).

**Tests.** The new case in `src/agents/model-fast-mode.test.ts` resolves Fast support with `selectedAuthMode: "api-key"` against the real Anthropic policy. It fails on the base (`expected undefined to be true`) and passes with the fix; the other 8 tests in the file pass on both. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

<details>
<summary>Checks, test time and review</summary>

| Test file | Local `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/model-fast-mode.test.ts` | 9 passed, wall 33.8 s | 3.92 s (Vitest duration; 5.33 s for the shard, `checks-node-changed-2`) |

- oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, the test-lines ratchet (6374242 against the 6390973 ceiling) and `git diff --check`. No `vi.mock` was added.
- Review: a local autoreview pass (Codex, reasoning medium, P0 to P2) over the full branch range `5342923d897..3625fd3292c` found no issues.

</details>

Not covered:
- The Fast request mapping itself was not exercised: native Anthropic Fast requires the public Anthropic endpoint and a real key. This change does not touch the request path, which already passed `"api_key"`.
- Only the Android emulator was run. iOS and macOS use a shared Effort control that is disabled by the same `supportsFastMode`. The Control UI default-model settings require `supportsFastMode === true` for their Auto and On options. The Control UI chat was not affected, because it falls back to a provider list when support is unknown.

prs.title: docs(telegram): correct preview streaming default from partial to progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared config reference (`docs/gateway/config-channels/personal-messaging.md`) states that Telegram preview streaming defaults to `partial`. This is incorrect: the runtime default is `progress`, and the channel-specific doc (`docs/channels/telegram/messaging.md`) already documents the correct default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime fallback for Telegram's preview stream mode is `resolveTelegramPreviewStreamMode(params, "progress")` in `extensions/telegram/src/preview-streaming.ts:10`. When no `streaming.mode` is configured, streaming is enabled with mode `progress` — not `partial`. The inline comment `(default: partial)` disagreed with both the implementation and the sibling channel doc, misleading users who relied on the documented default.

## User Impact

Users reading the shared config reference now get the correct default for `streaming.mode`. They will no longer assume Telegram sends answer previews in `partial` chunks by default when the actual default is a single `progress` message.

## Evidence

**Runtime default**
`extensions/telegram/src/preview-streaming.ts:10`
```ts
return resolveChannelPreviewStreamMode(params, "progress");
```

**Sibling channel doc (already correct)**
`docs/channels/telegram/messaging.md:77` — "(default: `progress`)"

**Docs toolchain**
- `pnpm format:docs:check` — 1,412 files, clean
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — 1,424 files, pass
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 16,216 internal links, 0 broken

**Format / lint**
- `oxfmt --check docs/gateway/config-channels/personal-messaging.md` — correct
- `git diff --check` — clean

**Proof boundary**
This is a documentation correctness fix; no CLI or runtime behavior changes. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head**
`5a69221fc282dbae12d153342e774ba0b72d2bf3`

prs.title: fix(ios): keep local device settings available without Dashboard
prs.body:
Related: #139514

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iPhone and iPad users cannot change local appearance, voice, or permission/device controls when offline, connected with Limited access, or unable to open the embedded Dashboard through native Cloudflare Access authorization.

## User Impact

Device Settings is available at the top of the native fallback and through Device in the connected-admin Settings toolbar. Local access does not grant Gateway scopes or expose credentials. Gateway administration keeps its existing gates.

**Draft — qualification incomplete:** the latest runner reports a clean tracked current-head normal Share/Watch build, 72 logical native tests, and the fixture-disabled offline UI flow passing. Strict expanded-scope SwiftLint remains failed; real OS permission completion/retirement, live Limited/Access/admin routes, physical voice, baseline-red evidence, and matched uploaded screenshots remain open. This is not validation-complete readiness.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier Dashboard consolidation intentionally removed duplicate native settings. This restores only a small local-device projection, not native copies of Gateway work pages. Native controls and the authenticated WebKit adapter share IOSDeviceSettingsActions and the existing consent, permission, snapshot, and preference owners.

No configuration keys, schemas, durability policy, dependencies, or protocol versions change. The simplify pass removed the bridge-only forwarding wrapper and kept one setting-effect implementation. The subsequent fixture-array extraction satisfies the inherited function-length gate without changing message content or suppressing the gate.

## Evidence

### Current-head runner verification

The [November 3, 03:41:57 UTC runner checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6594867082) identifies exact head `60ab831850f0bbece0229ddea32753ac227791fe`, tree `3f878be69e41d19235c0f21a9c708e738cc08b3c`, in an isolated detached checkout. The tracked tree was clean during the native and offline runs, with no production edits. These are runner-reported results, not an independent Mac replay by the coordinator. The Mac used dependencies linked from an existing prepared installation; this is **not** a new frozen-install claim.

| Check | Runner-reported result |
| --- | --- |
| Normal app, Share, and Watch build plus selected native suites | **PASS:** xcodebuild exit 0; **72 logical tests in eight suites**, zero failures, **54.349 seconds** test time. Normal Share/Watch dependencies retained; pinned Watch Rust toolchain used. |
| Fixture-disabled offline native UI | **PASS:** xcodebuild exit 0; **one test, zero failures, 39.100 seconds** on the exact current head. |
| Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 | **PASS:** zero of 12 selected files require formatting. |
| Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1, strict scope including selected tests | **FAIL:** 13 serious violations across the configured 509-file scope: six multiline-argument violations in IOSDeviceSettingsBridgeTests.swift:159–178 and seven size/style violations in OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift. No suppressions, repairs, or gate waiver. |

The eight native suites are IOSDeviceSettingsSnapshotTests, IOSDeviceSettingsBridgeTests, PermissionRequestBridgeTests, IOSPermissionInitiationTests, SettingsHubTests, SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests, OpenClawTypographyTests, and NotificationServingPreferenceTests. The xcresult device/configuration count of **84 includes parameter cases**; it is not 84 logical tests.

The offline flow launched the normal app with screenshot fixtures disabled, dismissed onboarding Close, exposed Device Settings from Gateway Offline, selected Light, checked keep-awake off/on values, left/reopened settings with Light retained, reached Open iOS Settings/Precise Location, and asserted no WebView or secure credential editor. Reuse this exact-head native/offline pass; generated-only or semantically identical test-formatting changes alone do not call for replaying the whole native run.

The normal Xcode build's lint phase consumes the source-only Swift file list, which excludes Tests/UITests. Its passing build therefore does **not** establish that the separate expanded test-inclusive strict lint scope passed.

**Lint attribution remains bounded:** the bridge test file and both checked-in lint configurations are byte-identical to the audited base, so those multiline-call inputs are inherited, not introduced by this PR. The UI file differs only by the added 46-line local-settings test; its surrounding text is unchanged and it was already large. The report does not publish the seven individual UI diagnostics or the full expanded lint invocation, so their individual rule/line attribution and minimal remedies remain unresolved. This source comparison is not an executed base-lint result and does not make the strict gate pass.

### Real notification permission probes — failed qualification attempts

The same checkpoint separately describes head plus an **uncommitted test-only method**, patch SHA-256 `1e3c551619c736882547f7ef5a0a4da011b08799d9aa0f59baafb94c5abd6a5b`, for permission exploration. The probes failed in **22.970**, **27.368**, and **27.128 seconds**: first a conditional hosted-relay consent expectation (the recording instead showed a real iOS notification prompt), then SpringBoard OS-alert lookup, then app OS-alert lookup after reinstall. The OS alert was **not successfully accepted**, and no successful post-grant assertion or scene/currentness-at-completion observation was obtained. A final notification-serving preference of false is neither a production-defect finding nor proof that post-grant effects were correctly rejected. No production behavior was changed.

### Artifact and source provenance

The runner retains raw xcresult bundles, logs, the exploratory test-only patch, and three exported offline screenshots locally. It reports visually inspecting those three **after-only** captures with no credentials visible. They are **not publicly downloadable attachments** and do not provide matched baseline/after evidence; the coordinator has not independently inspected the raw media or replayed the Mac runs. The linked comment provides accessible textual receipts and commands.

The earlier [old-head-plus-four-file-patch receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6594476902) remains historical supporting evidence (one UI test, zero failures, 36.797 seconds); the later current-head run above supersedes the previous no-native-replay limitation for the reported native/offline cases. The older [lock-contention checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6591324350) described an attempt that did not launch the build; it does not describe current lock state or negate the later completed run.

Current source publication directly advances `36c51fae3a29cb37bfbb55b43debfcf7f42572ce` to `60ab831850f0bbece0229ddea32753ac227791fe`: five revision files (+139/−96), complete PR 14 files (+637/−170). The runner's four patched source blobs matched exactly; the additional canonical inventory row retains the same voice-footer string/ID. Fixture-array content, order, IDs, and timestamps are preserved. Permission currentness is unchanged. Canonical inventory verification passes (4,575 entries, changed=false), all 46 inventory Node tests pass with one worker (2.98-second wrapper report), and source-file-list/whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 source review of that five-file revision found no actionable finding. Source preparation previously completed its own supported-runtime frozen installation; that is separate from the Mac's linked dependency setup. Historical optional release-script tests had nine passes and seven missing-Ruby ENOENT setup failures, not a passing aggregate.

The [completed current-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191524#issuecomment-6591313494) found no introduced code finding and requested further authority/visual proof. That review predates this latest checkpoint; its unresolved permission and route asks are not cleared merely by native unit tests passing.

### Review findings disposition — reproduction still required

- **Potential P2 permission-completion risk, still unqualified:** initiation requires an active scene. The new screen's ongoing predicate also requires `isVisible && scenePhase == .active`. If an actual permission callback resumes before scene reactivation, later app-owned notification preference/APNs enrollment, Health, or location-mode effects may be skipped. Source supports this ordering concern, not a confirmed general all-settings failure or authority bypass. Location polling waits for activation, whereas delegate completion can resume directly; the actual SwiftUI screen/callback ordering is the discriminating boundary, not a mutable-Boolean helper alone. The failed alert-handling probes did not reach successful post-grant observation and do not confirm this concern. No speculative production change is included.
- Preserve native consent, live-currentness checks, and WebKit admin/document guards. Local preferences must not acquire a Gateway-admin requirement. Cancellation before initiation must prevent an OS request and app effects; after initiation it cannot undo an OS grant, but retired work must reject later app-owned commits.
- **Low-priority/P3 test cleanup:** the typography token-presence smoke test is weak/redundant and is not a product/security blocker. The existing recursive audit rejects bare font overrides but permits inheritance; neither establishes complete rendered-control coverage. No unrelated cleanup is included here.

### Required local Mac proof before readiness

- Retain the reported 72-test native pass, exact-head offline UI pass, and selected SwiftFormat pass. Resolve strict SwiftLint with its exact diagnostic list and effective invocation, then complete applicable review/checks for any authorized repair; do not demand broad replays solely for generated or semantically identical test formatting.
- Observe the regression red on the baseline and green with this fix.
- Retain the proven offline flow; qualify live Limited/read-only and Access fallback, and preserve the connected-admin Dashboard route.
- Verify native consent/permission lifecycle and real-device Voice & Talk controls.
- Targeted permission case: start notifications at notDetermined with the serving preference off; enable from the actual native screen, accept the real OS prompt, and record the actual currentness predicate/scene phase at completion. After reactivation, verify the serving preference, APNs enrollment, and UI are correct without a second toggle. Contrast leaving/canceling before initiation (zero OS request/app effect) and completion after retirement (no later app-owned commit). Exercise Health/location siblings only where their callback path differs.
- Capture, inspect, sanitize, and attach matched before/after native screenshots in chat and this PR. None are supplied yet.

Potential overlap: #189938 adds Access-backed embedded Dashboard support and touches SettingsHubScreen/docs, but does not restore offline or Limited-access native local controls.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep rejected shares from reporting sent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS share sheet reporting **Sent** and dismissing its draft when the Gateway ignored an oversized message or rejected its attachments.

## User Impact

Rejected shares stay editable with an actionable error. **Sent** means the Gateway admitted the request for agent dispatch, not that the agent finished. Older Gateways cannot confirm admission: the sheet keeps the draft and asks users to check the destination session before retrying and update the Gateway. Retries are not deduplicated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `NodeEventResult` contract for explicit admission/rejection. Publish the decided receipt before an incognito session's existing accepted-work drain, without releasing actor custody or weakening connection checks. The share extension checks that receipt instead of treating RPC success as admission. No protocol/schema/config or dependency changes.

## Evidence

- **Retained authoring evidence:** audited-base handler regressions failed before the repair; the original four focused Gateway files passed 85 tests (67.60s Vitest / 71.30s wrapper including cold preparation). The final test-only async annotation subsequently passed methods/server typechecks. Original production core/test typechecks, targeted TypeScript lint/format, native i18n, docs, whitespace, line ratchets, and normal commit hooks passed. These are historical implementation receipts, not certification of the runner's later unpublished repairs/tests.
- **Retained source review/simplification:** independent Auto Review (P0–P2) was scoped-clean for tree `2b5f210c5543f8bb7eb1a314ec12ef49cf5bc7d5` after addressing early incognito response publication. The existing [ClawSweeper assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191514#issuecomment-6591138522) reports no actionable code findings for published head `a40c24d758d6d92291e25d67a8a65224148bd91b`; it predates the expanded qualification below and does not review unpublished runner changes.
- **Earlier focused runner report, kept distinct:** [@jjjhenriksen reported](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191514#issuecomment-6591412043) 88 Gateway passes across a different four-suite selection, plus OpenClawLogicTests/ShareComposeStateTests: 8 methods / 13 parameter-expanded invocations, zero failures on iOS 26.5. Those counts are not replaced by or added to the later campaign's distinct-test count.
- **Expanded Gateway campaign:** the [expanded runner report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191514#issuecomment-6594871578) records **85 distinct tests / 107 passing executions across four suites**: server-node-events 52, nodes.event 22, session-events 8, APNs registration 3. The 22-test nodes.event suite ran twice. Gateway production source was unchanged; the incognito oracle was strengthened locally to resume held work after admission, retrieve the real inherited memory-actor binding, commit a session-entry patch, and read it back. That TypeScript strengthening remains local/unpushed; mocked dispatch in this regression alone does not prove provider custody or general actor-resource release.
- **Fresh same-oracle base-red/head-green:** the [integration follow-through report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191514#issuecomment-6595213849) records a SHA256-matched strengthened nodes.event.test.ts oracle: audited base `70c99be459a77d474f19a7eed0e575449ef088e1` **4 failures / 18 passes**, published production head plus the local test-only strengthening **22 passes**, including post-admission memory-actor write/read. This is real-handler baseline proof, **not a full native baseline build/red run**.
- **Actual Photos → Share → OpenClaw client boundary:** on iOS 26.5 Simulator, the real extension passed **9/9 wire scenarios, zero failures, 397.165s**: ok:true/handled:false oversized and attachment refusals, legacy acknowledgement, malformed receipt, wrong event, RPC rejection, disconnect, held reply with the real 25-second timeout, and explicit acceptance. Rejections retained the exact draft and restored controls; acceptance was observed by dismissal and the persisted Sent event, not direct assertion of the fleeting Sent label. The fixture saw exactly nine node.event requests, one per case, with no automatic resend during the run. **These synthetic wire replies test the actual client, not server admission decisions.**
- **Actual extension → isolated production Gateway → real provider adapter → history readback:** the later integration used a fixed OpenAI-compatible SSE test endpoint, not synthetic Gateway receipts or mocked dispatch. User and assistant history were read back through the production API. The held-incognito test passed in **39.878s** while the endpoint still had one request/one pending response; only after sheet dismissal was that response released, followed by completed incognito history readback. The actual **20,001-character oversized-share test passed in 46.971s**, preserving/reconstructing the exact draft and restoring editing/Send/Cancel; provider request count did not increase. These are fixed-external-I/O integration results, **not live inference, paid-provider qualification, or a replay of all nine wire cases against the real server**.
- **Native build provenance:** normal app + Share + Watch builds passed **only with published head plus local build repairs and local test changes**: the ShareComposeState.swift redundantStaticSelf formatter correction and fixture-array extraction from AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.seedMessages to satisfy function-body lint. The runner reports task-only Rust-toolchain repair and checkout-local dependency-link isolation, leaving shared installs/toolchains unchanged. Those source/test repairs remain uncommitted/unpushed. Installed extension executable/debug-dylib hashes matched the successful build products. An initial stale-installed-binary failure and an earlier unpaired UI pass are not product verdicts or unchanged-head qualification; corrected cursor-position test assumptions retained exact text/length assertions. **Unchanged published-head normal native build qualification is not claimed.**
- **Limits retained:** targeted TypeScript typecheck/lint wrappers in the expanded run were setup-blocked by declaration custody; runtime/build success is not full typecheck/lint certification, and native pinned formatter/linter certification is not claimed here. Ambiguous-session-controller diagnostics during held incognito work remain recorded: completion/history passed, but the diagnostic is neither classified as a defect nor certified harmless. Physical-iPhone qualification was explicitly outside the operator's scope.
- **Evidence provenance/access:** all expanded results above are publicly **runner-reported by @jjjhenriksen**, not independently replayed or raw-artifact-inspected by this metadata updater. Raw screenshots/media, logs, xcresults, exact local repair patches, strengthened test sources, and integration fixture receipts remain local rather than downloadable/embedded evidence. The full patch and artifact bundle have not been supplied to this checkout; no byte-for-byte equivalence or public screenshot-completion claim is made.

## Local Runner Handoff — Keep Draft

This remains an explicitly requested **draft for qualification**, not ready for review/merge, release, or a Ready transition. The new reports materially extend the earlier logic-only evidence; the old normal-build/toolchain failure is superseded only by the disclosed **locally repaired** build result, not by an unchanged-head build pass.

The narrative identifies repair locations but is insufficient to recreate the exact tested patch. If the original patch cannot be supplied, any independently reconstructed repair needs its own fresh source-bound qualification rather than inheriting the runner's native pass.

Reconcile declaration ownership through the existing supported tooling before claiming TypeScript typecheck/lint results; do not bypass custody guards. Inspect the sanitized ambiguous-controller diagnostic before assigning a cause. Bind any eventual native rerun to the final source/test tree and installed extension hashes, and make sanitized before/after media and relevant receipts accessible for inspection. Batch source, proof, and this body before a future review refresh; **no new ClawSweeper request is made by this metadata pass**.

**Keep Draft: unpublished repair/test inputs and raw proof artifacts still need reconciliation. No Ready, merge, release, or paid/live-provider qualification is claimed or requested.**

prs.title: docs(discord): correct preview streaming default from off to progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared config reference (`docs/gateway/config-channels/community-chat.md`) states that Discord preview streaming defaults to `off` in two places. This is incorrect: the runtime default is `progress`, and the channel-specific doc (`docs/channels/discord/messaging.md`) already documents the correct default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime fallback for Discord's stream mode is `resolveChannelPreviewStreamMode(config, "progress")` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts:57`, and the doctor migration registers `defaultMode: "progress"` in `extensions/discord/src/doctor-contract.ts:31`. When no `streaming.mode` is configured, streaming is enabled with mode `progress` — not `off`. The two contradictory statements in the shared config reference were confusing users and disagree with both the implementation and the sibling channel doc.

## User Impact

Users reading the shared config reference now get the correct default. They will no longer believe Discord streaming is off by default and wonder why a live "work in progress" message appears; they now know they can set `streaming.mode: "off"` to disable it.

## Evidence

**Runtime default**
`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts:57`
```ts
const discordStreamMode = resolveChannelPreviewStreamMode(params.discordConfig, "progress");
```

**Doctor migration default**
`extensions/discord/src/doctor-contract.ts:31`
```ts
streaming: { mode: { defaultMode: "progress" } },
```

**Sibling channel doc (already correct)**
`docs/channels/discord/messaging.md:81` — "Discord preview streaming defaults to `progress`, which keeps one editable work message without tool rows."

**Docs toolchain**
- `pnpm format:docs:check` — 1,412 files, clean
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — 1,424 files, pass
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 16,216 internal links, 0 broken

**Format / lint**
- `oxfmt --check docs/gateway/config-channels/community-chat.md` — correct
- `git diff --check` — clean

**Proof boundary**
This is a documentation correctness fix; no CLI or runtime behavior changes. No runtime behavior proof applies.

**Exact head**
`03a276b60e67e79b643d0ab0b4bb7daa883a1e60`
