prs.title: chore: investigate Windows node exec pending in Code Mode (#176315)
prs.body:
Related: #176315

> **Investigation placeholder — intentionally draft, not ready for review or merge.** No implementation patch exists yet. The root cause and current-main reproduction remain unproven; no native Windows before/after result or passing regression is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows-node command submitted through Code Mode can remain pending without returning native output, an exit status, or an actionable failure, even when discovery and native Codex session listing succeed.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is for remote Windows commands to return their actual output and exit status, or a truthful denial, timeout, cancellation, or unknown-outcome result. There is no delivered behavior change yet. Authorization and unknown-outcome safeguards must remain intact; uncertain requests must not be replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #176315 reports this failure with a Linux Gateway and native Windows node running OpenClaw 2026.10.4. The failing owner has not been identified, so this draft deliberately does not propose a speculative repair.

The next step is one bounded, harmless absolute-path `codex.exe --version` probe in an isolated paired environment, using normal supported approvals. Correlate the Code Mode bridge request with exec entry, preparation, approval disposition, node invocation, native process completion, terminal-result acceptance, and Code Mode continuation. Only then select the smallest fix at the responsible boundary.

## Evidence

**Completed investigation — source analysis, not native execution:**

- Read the report and complete comments, traced the execution and result-return owners, and compared release `383c124cc32f` with inspected main `76985e4c31c4`.
- The release sets `bridgeDispatchStarted` before `runBridgeRequest`; it does not establish that exec or a Windows process started. [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af/src/agents/code-mode-state.ts#L570-L573).
- Last confirmed incident boundary: an outstanding Code Mode `bridge:callValue`. First unconfirmed boundary: entry into the nested exec implementation and node-target resolution. Later execution and return stages remain unconfirmed for that request.
- Compared #168523 (headless approval delivery), #104798 (bare-name allowlist precheck), PR #166140 (open at the October 29 inspection) (Windows shell-wrapper policy), and merged PRs #175949 and #128440 (Code Mode lifecycle repairs). Similar symptoms do not establish a shared cause or prove that this report is fixed.

**Required before this can become an implementation PR:**

- [ ] Verify actual Gateway/node builds, Node versions, transport, capabilities, and effective approval policy in the isolated test environment.
- [ ] Capture the bounded native Windows failure and its first stalled boundary; reconcile the request before any control or retry.
- [ ] Compare the equivalent supported direct node-exec path with Code Mode, keeping policy and command equivalent.
- [ ] Add a regression that fails on the base and passes with the owner-correct repair.
- [ ] Capture native Windows before/after stdout and exit delivery; verify relevant denial, error, cancellation, and disconnect cases.
- [ ] Complete targeted tests, typecheck, lint/format, and independent review; replace this draft's pending statements with exact results.

Native Windows access and an isolated paired Gateway were unavailable in the investigating session. No implementation tests were run, and no production service, approval policy, or unrelated session was changed.

Reported by @ceo633 in [#176315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176315).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6ba2f796-3a2a-4e83-976b-0e817bd5b51a)
- Implementation and verification: pending; no implementation session or patch exists yet.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop replies after their parent is deleted
prs.body:
Related: #96692; complements #119737. Compared with merged backport #180878, this draft retains observed-deletion lifecycle and per-physical-write/retry coverage; neither check and publication are atomic.

## What Problem This Solves

A threaded reply can outlive its parent. An observed parent deletion currently becomes only an informational event, so queued output, native buffered output, and files can continue publishing to a destination that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact active publishing address after an authorized deletion, without cancelling the underlying agent work. Carry that publication-only signal through deferred replies, previews, native streaming, and ordinary delivery. At the ordinary sender boundary, verify the live parent before each physical text/card send and file completion, including known-safe transport retries. Native retries and preview/final edit retries honor observed parent retirement too. Managed writers and deletion signals reach partial updates, both finalization paths, explicit rate-limit retries, and invalid-block replacement; ambiguous final-edit readback keeps the original reader. Keep earlier accepted parts and do not turn a later failure into permission to replay them.

This complements the confirmed-placement receipt work in #119737. It does not replace that PR or claim to repair every existing receipt/reconciliation inference. A parent read and Slack write are not atomic. Native streams without an observed deletion remain a separate limitation.

## User Impact

After OpenClaw observes deletion of an active reply parent, it stops publishing further output to that parent, including buffered native output. Child deletions and another workspace's matching timestamp leave unrelated publishers intact; explicit top-level sends remain supported. Ordinary threaded sends now require a readable live parent, adding bounded read requests and failing without publication when that evidence is unavailable. Workspace/listener and direct-handoff authority stay scoped to the existing delivery owner.

## Evidence

- Independent review found a native HTTP429 replay gap, and hosted review found a preview/final edit replay gap. Both are corrected in this candidate. A fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its confidence is limited by unavailable surrounding source and unrun tests, types, lint and formatting; live behavior remains unverified.
- Candidate base: `7dcc40f7addb9e45ce3e36768c505ff9cb005209`.
- Regression cases cover deletion before pending final text/file output, deferred delivery, native buffered append/stop, workspace/child isolation, queued sender release, multipart acceptance, upload completion, and identity/transport retry boundaries.
- All 23 original changed TypeScript files and the seven follow-up files passed Node syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. These do not establish type or runtime correctness.

prs.title: fix(agents): sandbox policies reject sandboxed agent runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A plugin requiring `before_agent_run` context `sandboxed === true` rejects a builtin embedded run even after the host has prepared its sandbox. Setup supplies the prepared sandbox to tools, but downstream hook context reads the original attempt parameters.

## User Impact

Policy plugins receive the sandbox state actually prepared for the current attempt. A genuinely sandboxed run can satisfy the existing policy, while preparation returning no sandbox produces `sandboxed=false` and remains blocked by that policy before model dispatch.

The assignment also overwrites a stale caller sandbox on internal attempt input. That defensive case is covered by an in-process regression; no supported normal Gateway route injecting that stale value was identified, so this PR does not claim a reproduced externally reachable policy bypass.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publish the prepared sandbox in the existing local attempt snapshot before downstream hooks consume it. The change preserves the caller's sandbox field/object and the public hook contract; it adds no new policy state, API or fallback. This is not a claim of whole-input immutability: existing finalization separately clears `input.continuation`.

Production +3 lines, tests +36, allocation metadata +2 across three files. The two added full-attempt regressions cover prepared-sandbox admission and stale-caller rejection using mocked preparation/prompt execution. CLI filesystem binding remains separate work: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163238.

## Evidence on the Reviewed Main Candidate

[Candidate-specific terminal excerpts, six Gateway results, reproduction commands, complete standalone probe and supplementary test instrumentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191205#issuecomment-6596016240).

- Tested head: `c9b74a6e9a148207996054be8d8ce2cc06de59f1`.
- Head tree: `45782131d0f23e9ea2046e9a3eb7486deecf108e`.
- Unfixed control: exact parent `ed2def8f795223f8aa49490aeb800b03be2b01c0`.
- Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, official pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, same workspace dependencies/lockfile on both sides.

These executions are specific to the main PR candidate, not the release backport. The latest moving main was not dynamically tested.

### Same full regression file on parent and head

The identical head test file was copied onto the parent without the production fix: **25 pass / 2 fail / 0 skip**, with the two expected opposite sandbox-value assertion failures (43.53s Vitest). On head: **27 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip** (24.23s).

Because the original red assertions stop before the prompt assertion, separate temporary soft-assert instrumentation recorded both hook values and prompt calls. For prepared=true/caller absent, parent reports false and makes 0 prompt calls; head reports true and makes 1. For prepared=false/stale caller present, parent reports true and makes 1 prompt call; head reports false and makes 0. Both consistent-state controls pass. These are internal mocked-preparation tests, not HTTP-provider observations. The instrumentation is included with the evidence and was removed after testing.

### Shipped Gateway + real Docker + local HTTP provider

Both exact revisions were separately built with official `qaRuntime`. The same standalone probe launches `node openclaw.mjs gateway run` and calls `gateway call agent --expect-final`, with isolated HOME/state/config, a real loaded policy plugin, a local HTTP Responses fixture, and the real builtin `exec` tool.

| Revision / sandbox / plugin policy | Hook sandboxed | HTTP requests | Observed result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Parent / on / observe | false | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Parent / on / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked by the test plugin |
| Head / on / observe | true | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Head / on / require true | true | 2 | Real exec returns `DOCKER\n/workspace`; run completes |
| Parent / off / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked before the first HTTP request |
| Head / off / require true | false | 0 | Run blocked before the first HTTP request |

The observe control establishes that the parent really runs the tool inside Docker while publishing false to the hook. The require-policy pair then demonstrates the user-visible false rejection and its repair. Blocked RPC results have `status: error` and `hook_block`; command exit code 0 is not counted as an admitted run.

**Boundary:** The strict policy is a test plugin, not a default OpenClaw policy. The real Gateway off/require test has no stale caller value. That stale-value combination is proven only at the internal attempt boundary above: public builtin entry parameters do not supply sandbox, and dispatch supplies it only to the transport-owning plugin-harness branch. No reachable Gateway stale-input bypass or private-data disclosure was reproduced. `sandboxed=true` describes prepared sandbox state, not confinement of every plugin tool, elevated exec or external CLI.

### Additional verification

- Official typed lint, oxfmt/Bun format parity and affected strict test type graph pass.
- Adjacent sandbox/hook-context/Knowledge regressions: **14/14**; existing CLI admission/reliability regressions: **150/150**.
- [Independent hosted verification](https://github.com/WangKangAandy/openclaw/actions/runs/41485974966) asserts the exact candidate SHA/tree/parent and passes official focused checks, full 27-case regression, test-line allocation and tracked-source cleanliness. Its separate workflow commit `2641c57bfdf490abe85d5c161a59531552f6e117` is not part of this PR.
- [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41487743941) succeeded on this head; inapplicable skipped jobs are not represented as executed tests.
- Local allocation-ratchet execution was blocked by an old Git lacking `git cat-file --batch -z`; only the separate hosted result is claimed for that check.

No production deployment, live platform delivery, real paid model, new real HTTP-503 fallback integration, or full release/UI build was performed for these main-candidate checks. Earlier release-backport integration remains separate historical evidence and is not used to establish this candidate's behavior.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): isolate iMessage chat.db worker admission from shared OpenClaw stores (#148750)
prs.body:
## Summary

Complementary to #148835 (startup watermark off main thread) — does **not** compete with that PR.

Even after #148835 routes `resolveIMessageStartupRowidWatermark` through `openSqliteWorkerStore`, a wedged `chat.db` native open still holds the **shared** SQLite worker broker’s serial `admissionTail` (and can pin a shared worker slot). Unrelated OpenClaw SQLite opens (sessions, delivery, etc.) then stall — gateway main thread is free, but shared storage admission is not.

## Fix

- Keep **one** `SqliteWorkerBroker` physical ownership registry; add separate `admissionTail` scheduling lanes (`shared` | `isolated`).
- **Lane-aware worker slots:** `acquireSlot(lane)` never places foreign/isolated actors on workers already serving shared stores (and vice versa), so a wedged foreign factory cannot pin shared-store I/O at a full pool.
- **Physical ownership reservation:** serialize/reserve per identity **before** awaiting worker capacity; recheck after await so concurrent cross-lane opens during retirement cannot double-create / overwrite actors.
- Expose narrow `openIsolatedSqliteWorkerStore` (existing/foreign read-only) on the isolated lane — not a second broker / create opener.
- Route iMessage receipt/`chat.db` reads in `withIMessageReceiptGuidReader` through that isolated lane.
- Shared OpenClaw admission stays responsive when a foreign open wedges; cross-lane same-file / hardlink / backend-mismatch / replaced-path ownership still applies.
- Works with #148835: when that PR lands, watermark + receipt paths both use the isolated reader.

## Evidence

Head: `9e99be375ec20195302a0b39f8a3d0d7ec865959` (rebase onto tip `main`; conflict-free / MERGEABLE).

Architecture (Claw ACCEPT): **one** physical DB ownership registry (`actors` / retained paths) with **separate scheduling lanes** (`admissionTail.shared` vs `admissionTail.isolated`) **and** lane-aware worker execution. `openIsolatedSqliteWorkerStore` is narrow **existing/foreign read-only** — not a second ordinary create opener / second broker.

Probe entrypoint/environment:
- Checkout: `kvnloo/openclaw` branch `per-1695-imessage-admission-isolation` @ `9e99be375ec20195302a0b39f8a3d0d7ec865959`
- Verify owner: openclaw verify @ `/workspace/openclaw-149233-verify` (desk pack `/workspace/openclaw-follow-2026-09-15/verify-149233/`)
- Runtime: Node 24.19.0, Linux box
- Preferred harness: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts …` — **FAIL_env OOM 137** (0/0) on host; not a leaf patch FAIL
- Focused leaf claim: `-t "keeps shared admission free"`

Leaf verify @ tip `9e99be375ec20195302a0b39f8a3d0d7ec865959` (openclaw verify):

```
-t "keeps shared admission free" → 3/3 PASS
```

Broader isolation filter (same tip): **7 PASS / 1 FAIL** flake under sibling load / 10 skipped — not a hard FAIL on the primary leaf claim.

Ordered redacted terminal trace (blocked-foreign → healthy shared I/O; prior tip probe, architecture unchanged):

```
{"tMs":3,"event":"start-blocked-foreign-open","lane":"isolated","path":"<redacted>/foreign.sqlite"}
{"tMs":9,"event":"foreign-open-dispatched","workerSeen":true}
{"tMs":990,"event":"blocked-foreign-factory-entered","marker":"<redacted>/foreign.sqlite.factory-entered"}
{"tMs":991,"event":"start-healthy-shared-open","lane":"shared","path":"<redacted>/shared-healthy.sqlite"}

```

Ready for `@clawsweeper re-review` on tip `9e99be375ec20195302a0b39f8a3d0d7ec865959`.

Closes #148750

prs.title: fix(voice-call): realtime phone consults fail on Claude CLI agents with no API key
prs.body:
Related: #188440 (this fixes the realtime consult path; the classic responder that #188440 reports is unchanged, see Gaps)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime phone consults fail with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` when the called agent runs on a CLI runtime such as `agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`.

## User Impact

User impact: a realtime Voice Call consult now runs on the agent's configured runtime, including a subscription-backed Claude CLI agent with no provider API key. Each consult is an ordinary turn of the call session, so later consults in the same call keep earlier ones, and the agent's normal tools (for example `sessions_send` to another agent) work under `toolPolicy: "owner"`. The caller stays a guest: owner-only tools stay refused, and `voice_call` stays bound to ending the current call.

The classic (non-realtime) phone responder is unchanged and still runs `runEmbeddedAgent`; see Gaps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Realtime consults called `runEmbeddedAgent`, which never selects a CLI runtime. Discord voice does not have this problem because it runs a normal agent turn (`runCommandFromIngress`). Consults now take that same path:

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` accepts `runner: "agent-turn"`: session preparation (fork, lineage, delivery) is unchanged, and the turn runs through `agentRuntime.runCommandFromIngress` as a guest. Voice Call opts in; other consult callers keep `embedded`.
- Plugin ingress: a plugin that owns no channel may admit a turn without `messageChannel`, and only as a guest. Owner elevation still requires the exact trusted plugin of the named channel. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the calling plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. Public `agentCommandFromIngress` still strips both.
- The CLI runner carries `toolBindings` into the MCP loopback grant (they already reached embedded tools), so `voice_call` keeps its active-call binding on the CLI route.
- Voice Call runs consults in its service context. Webhook handlers run outside the Gateway, and without the service's Gateway context `sessions_send` failed with "Requester provenance requires trusted in-process Gateway dispatch."

A CLI-dispatch alternative (`cliBackendDispatch` on the embedded runner) was considered and rejected: it is a one-shot helper path without session history or the requester's normal tool policy.

## Evidence

Focused tests (all new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here):

- `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts` 18/18: agent-turn consult shape (guest, `deliver: false`, one-shot thinking, bindings), and refusal of embedded tool-context adaptation.
- `src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.test.ts` 32/32: channel-less guest turn admitted; owner claim and foreign channel refused; foreign tool binding refused; bindings snapshotted.
- `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts` 5/5: `toolBindings` reach the prepared CLI run.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/{mcp-grant-context,tool-authority}.test.ts`: bindings snapshotted into the loopback grant.
- `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts` 23/23: consults run as agent turns (an embedded call throws) inside the service context; a host-forced consult (`consultPolicy: "always"`, called the way `scheduleForcedAgentConsult` calls it) runs as a guest agent turn and its owner's abort cancels the turn.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

User impact: root help stays fast for provably inert strict-JSON plugin configuration. Ambiguous or help-affecting configuration retains the existing live-config behavior.

prs.title: fix(update): report the finalize worker's exit instead of a missing result file
prs.body:
Related: #191542

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` reports `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/openclaw-update-migrated-*/result.json'` instead of the real failure when the fresh migrated finalize worker exits before writing its result.

## User Impact

User impact: when migrated update finalization fails, the update failure detail names the worker's exit (termination, exit code, signal, cleanup) instead of a missing temp file, so operators and triage see what actually failed. The outcome is unchanged: still `update-recovery-pending` with the same recovery fields, exit code 1, and no new rollback or restoration path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`continueMigratedUpdateInFreshProcess` read and parsed `result.json` before checking how the worker exited. A worker that crashed before writing the file therefore threw the read's `ENOENT`, and the existing exit check never ran. In #191542 the real cause (a PostgreSQL engine selection error, since fixed by #191547) only appeared in forwarded stderr above the misleading `ENOENT`.

The parent now checks termination, exit code and cleanup first, then reads the result. A clean exit without a readable result fails with the read error attached as its cause (malformed JSON goes through the same catch; only the missing-file case is tested). Both errors stay plain `Error`s with the existing "Update finalization did not confirm the admitted run's terminal outcome" prefix, the same class the existing exit check already throws, so callers classify them exactly as before.

One visible difference: when the worker exits unsuccessfully, the top-level failure-fact code changes from the misleading `ENOENT` to the generic `Error`, matching what the existing exit check produced. After a clean exit with no readable result, the top-level code is also `Error`, and the read's `ENOENT` stays in the detail as the cause.

The worker side is unchanged. Production diff: +16/-7 in one function. Tests: +37 lines in the owning suite, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-finalize-worker-exit.txt`.

<details><summary>Why classification and recovery are unchanged</summary>

- the only caller (`update-command.ts`) owns the ledger handoff, so `withUpdateCommandRecoveryUnwind` wraps any non-pending error in `UpdateCommandPendingRecoveryFailure`; only `UpdateCommandRecoveryPendingError` takes a different branch, and neither new error is one;
- the function's own catch still runs Windows autostart compensation with `complete(false)`;
- the reason comes from the run result (`update-recovery-pending` here), and recovery only depends on state-read contention, which neither `ENOENT` nor these errors are.

</details>

## Evidence

Every run was on macOS arm64 (Mac Studio) in an isolated checkout with isolated state; no live Gateway or user state was involved.

**Regression test, red on base and green with the fix.** `update-command-migrated.test.ts` adds two cases that drive the real `continueMigratedUpdateInFreshProcess` with a candidate worker at `<root>/dist/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.js` that writes stderr and exits without `result.json`, once with exit 3 and once with exit 0.

- Base 19aff5bfd42 plus the test: both fail with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../openclaw-update-migrated-*/result.json'`.
- With the fix: both pass (29 ms and 18 ms).

**Caller outcome, before and after.** A throwaway driver (not committed) ran the real parent inside the real `withUpdateCommandRecoveryUnwind` with the ledger handoff owned, as `update-command.ts` does:

| | base | fix |
|---|---|---|
| thrown | `UpdateCommandPendingRecoveryFailure` | `UpdateCommandPendingRecoveryFailure` |
| result.reason | `update-recovery-pending` | `update-recovery-pending` |
| result.recovery | `{"serviceRestartSafe":false,"reason":"runtime-verification-failed"}` | same |
| exit code | 1 | 1 |
| detail, worker exit 3 | `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../result.json'` | `Update finalization did not confirm the admitted run's terminal outcome: worker termination=exit, code=3, signal=null, cleanup=normal.` |
| detail, worker exit 0 | `ENOENT: ... result.json` | `...: the worker exited without a readable result. \| ENOENT: ... result.json \| ENOENT` |

**Related suites, passing with the fix.** These 8 files ran green: `update-command-migrated`, `update-command-migrated-schema`, `update-command-migrated-windows`, `update-command-recovery`, `update-cli.admission-ledger`, `update-cli.preactivation-inspection`, `update-command-post-core-admission.process` and `update-migrated-finalize.worker` (54 + 53 + 25 tests across 3 shards).

**Owning lane, `vitest.cli-process.config.ts` (66 files), run on an earlier revision with the same production code** (the final amend only reformatted the new test and lowered its line allocation from 40 to 37). 58 files passed, 3 were skipped, and 6 tests in 5 files failed. The same 5 tests in 4 of those files also fail on the unmodified base on this host:

- `gateway-backed-exit.process`: extra CLI stderr;
- `doctor-output.process`: a retained path in the output;
- `update-command-rollback`: state dir mode `0o770` vs `0o2770`;
- `sqlite-readonly-worker.compile-cache.process`: extra snapshot log lines.

The fifth file, `update-command-migrated-schema`, failed once under full-lane load and passed when run alone on both base and branch.

**`pnpm check:changed`.** Typecheck core and core tests, lint, and the ratchets passed. The dead export scan flags `scripts/ci-adaptive-select.mjs` and `scripts/ci-test-observations.mjs`, which this change does not touch (`scripts/` is identical to base); the scan was not rerun separately on base. Every other step passed, including format and `lint scripts`. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passed separately (slack 403).

**Cost.** `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 72.6 s wall, 68 s Vitest. Almost all of that is the existing suite; the two new cases add under 50 ms.

**Not covered.** No full `openclaw update` run through a real migration; the proof starts at the parent function and its recovery unwind. Windows compensation was not exercised in this proof; its path through the function's catch is unchanged.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)


## Maintainer takeover and independent review

Maintainer-directed takeover retains the contributor's exact head `07bf6a77409192b80f32bd4b1788cced2a411766` and all reported proof and failure limits above. The PR was draft, so its initial CI product jobs were skipped; it is now ready and exact-head [CI run 41582531942](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41582531942) is running. No product proof is inferred from the earlier skipped checks. No contributor code or tests ran on the production Team host.

Independent autoreview of commit `07bf6a77409192b80f32bd4b1788cced2a411766` against parent `19aff5bfd422faec3fe3aa5ccb72cb25d16becb4`, with the complete caller, recovery unwind, and result-owner context, completed scoped-clean through P2: no actionable findings. The first capture attempt stopped before reviewer launch on a missing partial-clone blob; after materializing the exact reviewed blobs, the same review route completed. Source review confirms the parent and result identity checks, pending-recovery classification, stderr forwarding, native compensation, and scratch cleanup retain their existing owners.

Simplification review required no code change: the patch reorders the existing child-success check and gives successful execution with unreadable publication a useful causal error. The two new subprocess cases protect distinct exit outcomes without a new production seam. Contributor-reported red/green evidence remains attributed above. Exact-head CI must actually execute the relevant tests and finish green before landing.

The diagnostic repair must be present in the updater parent. An older installed parent still produces its older diagnostic on the first hop; subsequent updates use the repaired parent once that package is installed. No full shipped-CLI migration/update or latest-stable upgrade matrix was run for this narrow diagnostic change.

Squash credit: Mitchell Etzel `<16581152+etzelm@users.noreply.github.com>` and steipete `<58493+steipete@users.noreply.github.com>`.

### Exact-head CI evidence and landing blocker

[Hosted node job 125740840766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41582531942/job/125740840766) independently executed the two new real-child regressions: exit 3 without a result passed in 16 ms, and exit 0 without a result passed in 11 ms. All 31 owner-suite cases passed (Vitest duration 103.09 seconds), as did the schema sibling's 21 cases and Windows compensation sibling's six cases. No contributor test ran on the production host.

The full CI gate is not green: [baseline-ratchet job 125740840649](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41582531942/job/125740840649) reports `Test lines: 6419885; ceiling: 6419675; over by: 210; net delta: +37.` CI checked merge `f156532c5a5503f3a9277f021c93944c1df1d12f`, with ordered parents main `47913a7b17cc45fe28e76e4f32c158cdf98c6763` and this PR's exact `07bf6a77409192b80f32bd4b1788cced2a411766`. The base-to-merge diff contains exactly the three reviewed files, adds 37 test lines and the matching 37 allocation, and keeps scalar `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` at 6319970. Thus the tested main base already has 6,419,848 test lines against a 6,419,638 ceiling: the same inherited 210-line debt. This PR's allocation fully covers its own delta.

Current main `e851dbf79c2c7339ac688e583e2ec3d8a3f28dc6` supplies no repair for that gate. Landing is held for fully green exact-head CI. No allocation padding, unrelated test deletion, blind main integration, CI rerun, or inherited-failure exception was selected. The remaining PostgreSQL jobs are still running; their eventual results will be recorded before closeout. The contributor's earlier local failure evidence above remains unchanged.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The remaining merge decision is whether Slack should expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current head is `c92dc8bf476cf47bc885643f4e9679386543437d`: its [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558847597) succeeds, and maintainer edits are enabled. The generated-conflict integration is recorded below; CI is not owner acceptance.

The latest [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. This integration retains11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; current-head CI supports integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: the same admission requirement remains in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, was checked with the unchanged20-case synthetic matrix: **17PASS / 3FAIL**. The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. The existing native Gateway proof retains its original binding. This paragraph updates distribution evidence only; the current PR head and compatible opt-in proposal remain unchanged. Slack-owner acceptance or rejection remains unrecorded.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:end -->
<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:end -->

## Evidence

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current integration and CI — 2026-11-03 JST

Current head: `c92dc8bf476cf47bc885643f4e9679386543437d`; prior head: `8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2`. Resolved an actual generated fingerprint conflict by a normal merge of pinned official main `634c1bfe531e782671b1a1da904819be44eee4ba`. Only native generated config metadata conflicted; the exact prior authored feature delta was retained. Automatically merged official documentation additions are bound separately. No private runtime repair, assertion relaxation or workflow rerun was added.

Native generators/checks passed with the current official allocation counter: **Test lines OK: 6415295; ceiling: 6415535; slack: 240.** The shared scalar and pre-existing allocation inputs match pinned main. A change-specific record, where present, is explained below. [Current-head required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558847597): **success**, zero failed/pending lanes at `2026-11-03T01:24:52.584377+00:00`. The same first native run was followed to terminal; historical local feature/Gateway proofs were reused only at their original heads, with zero fresh local behavior cases claimed.

The only changed prior feature-document input is an unrelated accepted official Slack read-bound paragraph; the runtime/configuration/test feature inputs remain byte-identical and the strict opt-in authored delta is retained. prs.title: fix(worker-environments): isolate a corrupt profile snapshot from the environment list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
listRows decoded every worker-environment profile snapshot with an unguarded JSON.parse. A stored "null", "{}", or truncated snapshot threw inside the row map, so one bad environment made the whole list unreadable. null and {} also passed the shape check and later crashed on profileSnapshot.project or handed undefined settings to requireWorkerProfile.

## User Impact
Gateway placement and environment reads keep returning the healthy environments when one stored snapshot is corrupt. A direct read of the bad environment fails with an error that names it.

## Why
Snapshots are written as { install, settings } before a project exists, so the decoder requires a JSON object with a settings object. It does not require project or executionMode, which are added later. List reads skip the bad row and warn. A lookup of that one id still throws.

## Evidence
src/gateway/worker-environments/store-row-codec.test.ts covers null, {}, truncated JSON, a snapshot stored before project preparation, and a list that keeps the healthy row.

Closes #180197

prs.title: fix(plugins): authenticate native MCP servers with environment-backed headers
prs.body:
Closes #184192
Related: #160244

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes PostHog and other enabled native MCP plugins sending literal environment placeholders as authentication headers, resulting in failed tool discovery.

## User Impact
Native plugin header credentials resolve from the Gateway environment using the existing config grammar. Missing or empty required variables skip the affected server with a generic diagnostic; healthy siblings remain available. Enable only plugins whose declared endpoints you trust.

## Why This Change Was Made
Resolve at the native-manifest boundary, not the shared HTTP transport: already-resolved operator config must not be interpolated twice. Reuse the config parser for escaping and defaults; leave URLs, process fields, third-party bundle formats, and operator override precedence unchanged. Manifest metadata is not mutated.

The open stacked PR #160244 already identifies this fix direction. This is a small standalone fix against current main for the independently observed released PostHog failure, with fresh regression proof. It does not replace or close that work. No inspection-only option is added because current callers do not require it.

Simplification: no new parser, state, cache, public option, or per-provider code. Necessary growth is 44 production additions/1 deletion, 91 test additions/2 deletions, and two documentation lines.

## Evidence
- Base: `b17d07fc01e0ce6efdc569d890140f1a11488239`. Two added regressions fail on unmodified production source (literal headers; missing servers retained), while nine existing tests pass.
- `corepack pnpm test src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **11 passed**. Fixed run: 26.38s wall time, 23.48s runner duration; individual new tests 2ms each. Cold compilation dominates.
- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-config.cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **14 passed**, 10.13s wall time.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json src/plugins/bundle-mcp.ts src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts`: passed, no problems in two files.
- Targeted oxfmt check, plugin-extension import boundary, one-file docs MDX check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent isolated autoreview at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Regression coverage includes expansion, escaping, fallback, unsupported syntax, one-pass substitution, unchanged URL/manifest, undefined/empty variables, sibling retention, ownership metadata, and credential-free diagnostics.

Limits: these are production-loader boundary and consumer tests, not a live PostHog test of the patched package or a full Gateway end-to-end run. Original reported live evidence is 401 through the released plugin versus 200 with direct credential initialization. No real credentials were used in the checkout. Hosted CI timing/results are pending. A first consumer command named a nonexistent auth-status test and ran no tests; the corrected existing suites above passed. The contribution guide names a retired source-boundary script; the current plugin-boundary checker passed instead.

prs.title: fix(logging): preserve stuck-session recovery classification in automation failures
prs.body:
Closes #138528

## What Problem This Solves

When the stuck-session watchdog kills a scheduled agent run because a tool call is blocked behind an approval that can never arrive, the operator only gets a generic "Check automation history for details." alert and a cause-free run-history error (`cron isolated agent run aborted`) — the real reason (`blocked_tool_call`) is thrown away one layer above the formatter. This fix carries that semantic cause through recovery into **both** the run history and the chat alert, so the operator immediately sees the run was blocked on a tool call.

- Problem: After the recovery refactor onto `watchdog.tick()`, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` stopped forwarding the attention `classification` (e.g. `blocked_tool_call`) into the outcome. The aborted outcome had no `reason`, `formatRecoveryOutcome` could not print it, and cron `finalizeCronRun` had no descriptive cause (and the chat alert reads a different field entirely).
- First attempt & review: the initial fix stored the cause in a diagnostic-owned `WeakMap` keyed by the operation. Review (ClawSweeper) found it racy (populated only after `tick()` settled, fragile instance identity, and an `object`-typed lookup that is a production TS error for the optional controller owner) and not projected into the chat alert.
- Redesign (this revision): drop the WeakMap; record the cause on the **controller-owned** `ReplyOperation` via an optional `recoveryClassification` field — the same instance cron finalization reads, so there is no separate store and no instance-identity lookup. `finalizeCronRun` surfaces it as the run-history error when no descriptive message exists, and projects it into a typed `agent-stall` `CronFailureNotificationDetail` so the chat alert renders `Cause: blocked_tool_call`.
- What changed: `diagnostic-session-recovery.ts` (request `classification` + aborted `reason`), `diagnostic-session-recovery-coordinator.ts` (forward `classification` to `recover`), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (fill `reason`, set `operation.recoveryClassification`), `session-controller.contracts.ts` (optional `recoveryClassification` field), `cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` + `run-finalize.ts` (plumb & surface in history + chat), `cron/types.ts` + `cron/failure-notification-text.ts` (new `agent-stall` detail).
- Removed: `src/sessions/session-recovery-classification.ts` (the WeakMap store).
- What did NOT change: cancellation/restart/rate-limit behavior, scheduler merge re-admission, and the `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` overload signatures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: the recovery refactor moved recovery onto `watchdog.tick()`, and the coordinator stopped forwarding the `classification` the attention layer already computed, so the formatter had nothing to surface. The classification is already available at recovery time; we thread it through the existing owners (the controller-owned operation and the typed notification contract) rather than rebuilding a cause-inference layer.

- Best fix: thread the already-computed classification (small, surgical, no abort-path behavior change). Recommended.
- Alternative: thread it through `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` -> `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` -> `handle.abort(reason)` (requiring the single-session overload to accept a reason). A prior attempt (#180212, +530/20 files) followed that broader path and was closed unmerged. This PR uses a narrower carrier on the controller-owned operation plus the typed notification detail, which avoids changing abort signatures and is far smaller.
- Risk / non-goals: `finalizeCronRun` only uses the cause when `meta.error` lacks a descriptive message. `decision.reason` (`semantic_stall`) is the fallback when no classification is supplied. Structured `errorCode`s for immediate exec denials and threading the active tool identity are intentionally out of scope.

## User Impact

Scheduled runs killed for a blocked tool call now show `blocked_tool_call` in the automation run history **and** carry that cause in the chat alert (rendered as `Cause: blocked_tool_call`), instead of a generic "Check automation history" body with a cause-free run error.

## Evidence

- `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` now sets `operation.recoveryClassification = "blocked_tool_call"` on the controller-owned operation when the aborted outcome occurs; `run.ts` reads `ownReplyOperation?.recoveryClassification` (no WeakMap, no `object`-typed lookup, no undefined-owner TS error).
- `run-finalize.ts` projects the cause into `failureNotificationDetail: { kind: "agent-stall", classification }`, and `cronFailureDetailLines` renders `Cause: blocked_tool_call` for the chat alert.
- oxlint `--type-aware --type-check` reports 0 errors/warnings across all changed files (note: `tsgo` cannot run in this worktree because the `tsrs` transitive dependency resolves through a `node_modules` symlink that escapes the checkout; full CI will type-check).
- Added/updated regression tests:
  - `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery-cause.test.ts`: classification carried as `reason`; watchdog-reason fallback; **recorded on the controller-owned operation** (`op.recoveryClassification === "blocked_tool_call"`); not recorded when recovery does not abort; formatter prints the cause; coordinator forwards `classification`.
  - `failure-notification-text.test.ts`: renders `agent-stall` as `Cause: blocked_tool_call`.

What was not tested here: the full vitest suite could not be executed in this environment (the runner flags vitest as a watch service and terminates it before results are emitted), and a real end-to-end Gateway run (blocked-tool scheduled run -> watchdog termination -> persisted history row + chat failure alert) is pending operator redacted output. CI on this PR runs the new regression tests and the existing recovery suites.

prs.title: fix: replies after a plugin reload from Control UI go to the session's last external chat
prs.body:
Closes #190980
Related: #189953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a session usually chats in Telegram and the user asks the agent in Control UI to reload a plugin and continue, the resumed reply is sent to the Telegram chat instead of continuing in Control UI.

## User Impact

User impact: a tool handoff (`plugins` `reloadAndResume`, `github_publish`, or a self-held `sessions_send`) started from Control UI, or from another internal turn with no recipient of its own, now resumes in the session transcript when the session's recorded route is an external chat. The resumed reply is no longer auto-delivered to that chat, and a `message` send without a target in the resumed turn fails with "requires a target" instead of resolving to it.

Handoffs started from an external chat, callers without a turn source, and sessions without a recorded external route enqueue the resume exactly as before. No config, schema, or permission change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Line references are at `a93c259`.

The handoff tools say they resume in the conversation that handed off: "resume with its result in this same conversation" (`src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts:157`), "resume this same conversation with success or failure" (`src/agents/tools/plugins-tool.ts:137`), and "reloads and resumes the same conversation with the result" (`docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md:341-343`). The resume event is enqueued with only the captured session target (`src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts:249-265`), so its route is the session's recorded external route (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts:104`; `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-target.ts:237`). A Control UI turn intentionally keeps that recorded route (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.ts:115-131`), so its handoff resumed in the external chat.

The handoff now enqueues the resume with `deliveryContext: { channel: "webchat" }` when all three hold:

- the yielding turn's source channel is internal: `webchat`, or an internal source hint such as `heartbeat` (`isInternalRouteContext`, `src/utils/delivery-context.shared.ts:93-98`);
- the turn has no recipient of its own: `turnSourceTo` is empty or this session's key, which is what a Control UI turn carries (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-origin-routing.ts:113-117`);
- the captured target has a recorded external route.

The existing delivery gate keeps an internal route's replies in the transcript (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts:458-462`). Exec completion notifications already pass their start-time route through the same `deliveryContext` option at enqueue (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts:207-212`; `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:147-152`). Unlike the exec route, the resume carries only `{ channel: "webchat" }`: the delivery gate keeps only `webchat` in the transcript, and an internal source hint such as `heartbeat` copied into the route would pass that gate and fail at channel delivery (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-delivery.ts:24-28`). `deliver`, the target capture, and the handoff's checks are unchanged.

The other cases keep the current enqueue:

- An external turn records its own route on the session when it is admitted (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:563-600`), so its captured route already is the conversation that handed off.
- An internal source hint with an external recipient of its own (an agent RPC turn that delivers its reply) keeps its current resume route.
- A session used only from Control UI has no recorded external route, and its resume is not delivered today; an internal route there would drop the chat type that the resumed turn now inherits from the session (`src/auto-reply/reply/effective-reply-route.ts:130-134`).

## Evidence

Focused tests on `a93c259` with this change (Node 24.22.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`); the pushed head `99c0b10e02ad` has the same production change byte-for-byte as the first commit, and its new commit changes only `plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` and the test-line allocation record.

- `src/agents/tools/plugins-reload-handoff.route.test.ts` (new), `selects the reload resume route: $id` (eight cases): the real `plugins` tool and the real `handoffSessionTool` run with `plugins.reload` and the enqueue mocked; the test reads the options passed to `enqueueSessionEventForHost`. With the session's recorded route on Telegram, three yielding turns enqueue the resume with exactly `{ channel: "webchat" }`: `webchat turn without recipient`, `Control UI turn addressed to its session` (`webchat` plus the session key), and `internal source hint` (`heartbeat`, no recipient). Five enqueue it without `deliveryContext`: `external Telegram turn` (recipient `999`), `Telegram turn without a recipient`, `caller without a turn source`, `internal hint with its own recipient` (`heartbeat` with recipient `999`), and `session without an external route` (a Control UI turn on a session used only from Control UI).
- `src/agents/tools/plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts`, `keeps a Control UI reload resume internal: $id` (the composed cases, `idle` and `queued behind another run`): a real handoff, the real `enqueueSessionEventForHost`, and the real resumed-turn dispatch and `message` tool, with the model runner and `plugins.reload` mocked. A Control UI-shaped caller hands off on a session whose recorded route is Telegram `999` (chat type `direct`); in the resumed turn the model sends a `message` without a target, then replies. Both cases assert that the test Telegram channel's `sendText` is never called, the resume settles as `completed` with `delivered: false`, the `message` send fails with "Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation", and the resumed turn runs with `webchat` as its message provider, and its dispatch has `webchat` as the originating channel and no chat type. Each case also passes when run alone (`-t`).
- `keeps a Control UI reload resume internal: queued behind another run`: a test reply operation is held active on the session when the resume is enqueued, standing in for another turn (by source reading, a queued follow-up turn takes its route from its own queued item, not from the active run: `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts:46-77`). The resume is queued as a separate follow-up turn (`deferredToActiveRun: "followup"`); before the held operation settles, the model is not called and nothing is sent. After it settles, the queued turn runs once, nothing is sent, the `message` send without a target fails, and the turn has `webchat` as its message provider and no message target (`messageTo` undefined).
- Before the fix, in the composed case (its earlier single-row form, now the `idle` row), the test Telegram channel received two sends to `999`: the `message` send ("This must stay in the session.") and the resumed reply ("Reload resume stayed in the session."). The resumed turn ran with `telegram` as its message provider and originating channel and `direct` as its chat type, and settled with `delivered: true` (printed by a diagnostic line added to the test for that run; excerpt in the linked issue).
- Before and after, and partial reverts: on the base (the production change reversed, tests unchanged), the three route cases that expect `{ channel: "webchat" }` and both composed cases fail, and the other five route cases pass; both runs exit 1, and both composed cases fail on the same `sendText` assertion (`expected [ [ { cfg: { …(4) }, …(30) } ], …(1) ] to deeply equal []`). With the change, all 22 cases in `plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` and all 8 cases in `plugins-reload-handoff.route.test.ts` pass. Each partial revert of the production change, applied alone, fails only its matching cases: enqueuing the yielding turn's own normalized source route, as exec completion notifications do, instead of `{ channel: "webchat" }` fails `Control UI turn addressed to its session`, `internal source hint`, `Telegram turn without a recipient`, and the `queued behind another run` composed case, the last on its `messageTo` assertion (`expected 'agent:main:reload-route-composed' to be undefined`: the queued turn received the session key as its message target); writing the internal source name into the route instead of `webchat` fails `internal source hint`; dropping the recorded-external-route condition fails `session without an external route`; dropping the no-own-recipient condition fails `internal hint with its own recipient`; widening the internal-channel check to any source channel fails `Telegram turn without a recipient`. The `idle` composed case, which does not assert `messageTo`, passes under all five, and the `queued behind another run` case under the other four.
- Existing tests, unchanged: `github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts` 8/8 (Duration 24.64 s), `server-plugin-reload.prepared-borrow.test.ts` 5/5 (20.43 s), `sessions-send-self-hold.test.ts` 25/25 (11.41 s), and `session-event-handoff.test.ts` 24/24 (19.40 s) pass.
- Layout: the eight route cases are in a new file because adding all new cases to `plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` would exceed the 1,000-line lint limit for test files. The composed cases stay in that file, which is on the database-worker core list (`test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, tests that need the host-owned SQLite broker, which runs in forked processes) and so runs in the `infra` Vitest project; they reuse that setup and the file's real-handoff fixture.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; base and fixed runs on the same machine at different times): `plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts`, base 20 tests: Duration 65.02 s (tests 56%, transform 37%), wall 98.2 s; with this change 22 tests: Duration 50.35 s (tests 83%, transform 10%), wall 82.0 s. The two added composed cases took 3.2 s (`idle`) and 2.4 s (`queued behind another run`); the lower total comes from less transform time, not from a cheaper file. `plugins-reload-handoff.route.test.ts`, 8 tests: Duration 12.14 s, wall 14.9 s. CI seconds (CI run 41427410355, job `checks-node-changed-2`, Bun runtime, one file per shard): `plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` (`infra` project), 22 tests: Duration 77.57 s (tests 61%, transform 33%); `plugins-reload-handoff.route.test.ts` (`agents-tools` project), 8 tests: Duration 93.44 s (transform 91%, tests 4%), and its eight reported per-test times sum to 3.85 s. The existing file was above 30 s before this change; the cases added to it are the composed ones, which prove a contract that no unit-level test can: a real tool handoff, enqueued and resumed for real, idle or queued behind another run, makes no channel send.
- Test lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/tool-handoff-resume-route.txt` records the net added test lines. The eight route cases pin which yielding turns get the internal route; the composed cases are the ones that check what the resumed turn sends.
- Size: production +12 lines in one file (`src/agents/tools/session-tool-handoff.ts`); tests +382 (209 and 173) lines in two files, plus the allocation record.
- Checks: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` (core config) on the changed files including both test files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --staged` (including the test-line and max-lines ratchets) pass. `pnpm check:changed` on the first pushed commit (`aa9147ebc77e`): 35 of 36 checks pass; the dead export scan fails, reporting unused exports in two files this change does not touch (`PendingContextEngineTurn` in `src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.ts`, `materializeSessionRepositoryWorkspaceOnGateway` in `src/gateway/session-repository-materialization.ts`); this change adds no exports. Not run: `pnpm build` (no entry-point, packaging, or lazy-loading change) and the plugin and channel contract tests (no shared plugin or channel interface change).
- Local review: `autoreview` (Codex CLI 0.164.0, engine `codex`, local mode) on base `a93c259fda08` and an uncommitted local snapshot of the full change against that base (both commits; patch SHA-256 prefix `9ea939be8686`), `--max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.9)", no P0–P2 findings; remaining findings: none. The review covered the diff and the supplied source context; it did not execute code or tests.
- Local probe (not committed): through an in-process Gateway, a Control UI client's `chat.send` turn whose scripted model calls `plugins` `reloadAndResume` reached the handoff with `turnSourceChannel: "webchat"` and `turnSourceTo` equal to the session key; the resume was enqueued with `{ channel: "webchat" }` with this change and without `deliveryContext` on the base.
- Live run, idle case (an isolated test Gateway listening only on loopback, token auth; the real model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` through a ChatGPT OAuth sign-in, with no provider API keys in the Gateway environment; Control UI in a browser; a Telegram test bot in a DM whose sender was paired as the command owner; tools: the `messaging` profile plus `plugins`, with Tool Search, Code Mode and ACP off; a local test plugin that registers one service and no tools). The base and fixed builds came from the same checkout of `99c0b10e02ad`, the base build with the production change reversed; a check of the built output found the change in the fixed build only. A message to the bot in the Telegram DM, answered there, set the main session's recorded route to the Telegram DM; that route stayed the same through the base and fixed runs below.
  - Base: in Control UI on the main session, the model called `plugins` `reloadAndResume` (result `started`, `yielded: true`). About 8 seconds after the request, the resumed reply `HANDOFF-RESUME-BASE` arrived in the Telegram DM; it also appeared in Control UI.
  - With this change: a Telegram check message got its reply in the Telegram DM. Then the same request in Control UI: about 8 seconds after it, the resumed reply `HANDOFF-RESUME-FIX` appeared in the open Control UI chat without a page reload, and it was still in the transcript after a later reload. After the reply to that check message, the Telegram DM received no bot message until another check message, sent about 7 minutes after the request, got its reply.
  - In both runs the plugin re-registered once, the resumed reply came from a separate turn after that, and there was no `message` call between the handoff and the resume.
  - Session replacement (same Gateway, this change; the test plugin's service stop was held for 4 seconds to keep the reload open): the model handed off a reload again from Control UI. About 0.12 seconds after the plugin's old service began stopping, `sessions.reset` was sent for the main session; it returned about 1.2 seconds later, before the reload returned (so before the resume could be enqueued), and the session's lifecycle revision changed. The Gateway logged `Plugin reload handoff failed: SessionDeliveryGenerationRevokedError: The original session generation no longer accepts this delivery.` No resumed reply appeared: the new session had no assistant entry (only the reset notice), no other session was updated, no run was active afterwards, the Telegram DM received nothing, and Control UI showed the new, empty session.
  - The live runs cover the idle case and did not include a `message` send without a target; the queued case and the target-less `message` send are covered by the focused tests above.
- External-chat control (same PR revision as the live run above, rebuilt for a separate isolated Gateway run): for this control only, the test Gateway used trusted-proxy auth on loopback; a local test proxy identity was granted `operator.admin` through `gateway.auth.identityScopes` (no `gateway.roles`, no device auto-approval), and the Telegram DM sender was linked to that identity's profile with `users.linkChannelIdentity`. With this setup, the model called `plugins` `reloadAndResume` on the same local plugin from the Telegram DM; the reload completed (plugin runtime generation +1) and the resumed reply `HANDOFF-EXT-LINKED` arrived in the Telegram DM about 10 seconds after the request. The call's result was `started`, `yielded: true`; the resumed reply came after the plugin re-registered once, with no `message` call between the handoff and the resume; after the request, no other bot message appeared in the Telegram DM until the test Gateway was stopped about three minutes later.
- Screenshots:
  - Control UI after the later page reload, with this change: the request, the `reloadAndResume` call, and the resumed reply `HANDOFF-RESUME-FIX`. The call is labeled "Interrupted"; in the base run the corresponding call showed the same status (that run's UI was in Chinese), and in both runs the call's result was `started`, `yielded: true`.

    ![Control UI after a page reload, with this change](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/282d4074-0010-464e-be83-3d4aab4b7880)

  - The Telegram DM during the external-chat control: the check message and its reply `HANDOFF-TG-TAIL`, then the request and the resumed reply `HANDOFF-EXT-LINKED`.

    ![The Telegram DM during the external-chat control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9dfbe4f6-05ba-4506-8990-a04f7de56180)

**Not covered:**

- Final-effect rejection after authority revocation was not run live; the session replacement case above was.
- The composed tests' Telegram channel is a test channel plugin with a mocked `sendText`, and the yielding caller's identity is set by the test to the Control UI shape rather than derived from a Control UI `chat.send` (the local Gateway probe above checked that shape); the live runs above used real Control UI and Telegram turns.
- The live run used the main session under its canonical key (`agent:main:main`) in a fresh state; a session still stored under a legacy key was not checked.
- A handoff from an external event turn still resumes on the session's recorded route. System events do not update that route (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:566`), so when the event's own route differs from it, the resume follows the recorded route, as on main.
- The route is captured when the turn hands off. If another conversation's message updates the session's recorded route while an external turn is still running, that turn's handoff resumes on the updated route, as on main.
- After this change, the resumed turn of a Control UI handoff does not carry the session's recorded chat type (for example `direct`), because its route is internal while the recorded route is external; an exec completion notification started from Control UI behaves the same today.
- `github_publish` and a self-held `sessions_send` reach the same enqueue through the helper's `run` path; their existing tests pass unchanged but set no turn source, so the new route is exercised only through `plugins` `reloadAndResume`.
- Deferred work that does not use the tool handoff, such as subagent completions, the CLI agent no-output notice, and background media generation results, keeps its current routing.

prs.title: fix(imessage): preserve literal trailing-space in configured cliPath/dbPath
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured iMessage `cliPath` or `dbPath` ending in whitespace was silently rewritten to a *different* path before use. macOS allows trailing spaces in file and directory names, so these are legitimate literal values, and the rewritten spelling is usually another real file: OpenClaw could run the wrong `imsg`, read the wrong `chat.db`, and — through the trimmed remote-host cache key — SSH-stage an attachment to one Mac while executing the RPC on another.

- Problem: the extension applied `.trim()` to configured paths at ~20 call sites, conflating "is this configured?" with "normalize this value".
- Problem, second layer: the plugin-state store trims every entry key, so the recovery cursor for a literal `chat.db ` collapsed onto its trimmed spelling and inherited a high-water measured on a different database — the exact cross-database suppression the cursor identity exists to prevent.
- Solution: blank detection now uses the SDK owner `readNonBlankString`, which returns the original bytes. Path *resolution* keeps `resolveUserPath`'s contract — `OPENCLAW_HOME` first, result absolute — through `resolveIMessageLiteralPath`, without trimming. Cursor keys hash the `(accountId, dbIdentity)` pair, so a literal identity keeps its own slot instead of collapsing onto its trimmed spelling.
- What changed: every configured-path decision point migrated together — `cli-path.ts`, `client.ts`, `send.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `probe.ts`, `actions.ts`, `chat.ts`, `channel.ts`/`channel.runtime.ts`, `setup-core.ts`, `private-api-status.ts`, `message-tool-api.ts`, `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, `cli-output.ts`, `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts`, `monitor/remote-host.ts`. Home-tilde expansion moved to a dependency-free `user-path.ts` because a bare `node` child imports it.
- What did NOT change: business normalizations that are not path identity — `HOME` lookup, shebang/echo matching, configured `remoteHost` validation — keep trimming.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner per responsibility: "blank vs. literal" belongs to the SDK string-coercion owner, not a locally invented helper. An earlier revision of this PR added a private `readLiteralPath` that was byte-identical to `readNonBlankString`; it is deleted, so there is no second implementation to drift.

The cursor key is the `#184862` digest of `JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity])`, which carries the literal bytes: an identity ending in whitespace gets its own slot instead of inheriting the high-water of its trimmed neighbour. The pre-`#184862` NUL-composite key is still adopted when read, so no operator's stored cursor moves on upgrade. (Rebased onto current main, which redesigned these keys; this branch's earlier quoting is superseded.)

Also fixed a regression this PR introduced: `send.ts` stopped capturing `shouldClose` and re-read `opts.client` in `finally`, so a mid-request options mutation could close a borrowed client. The captured flag is restored and covered by the existing custody tests.

Risk / non-goals: the local `dbPath` no longer goes through `resolveUserPath`'s trimming step; `~` expansion, the required-home cwd fallback, and absolute resolution are preserved, all pinned by tests.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a literal trailing-space `cliPath`/`dbPath` get exactly the binary and database they wrote, on the host the wrapper names. Fully-blank values are still treated as unset, so empty or absent config behaves as before. No config migration, no new option, no public SDK export, no lockfile change. A literal database that used to share a cursor row with its trimmed neighbour now keeps its own, so a high-water from the other file can no longer silence it.

## Evidence

Two real `sshd` instances on loopback (`mac-a`, `mac-b`), real `ssh`/`scp` behind wrappers that name one host each, a fake `imsg` that logs the exact bytes of its `argv` and every `--db`, a trimmed neighbour binary that must never run, and an isolated Gateway per tree. The `local` account uses the literal `cliPath`/`dbPath`, the `remote` account a literal wrapper plus a literal remote `dbPath`, the `plain` account ordinary paths.

This head (`a8bb5af`), media uploaded through the production staging path:

```console
sshd sessions: mac-b=14  mac-a=0
staged on mac-b: sha256 77db3976… == source 77db3976…
--db seen by the child: [chat.db ]   (trailing space intact)
cursor: literal db -> no since_rowid   ordinary db -> since_rowid 777
```

Same harness on `HEAD^`, the tree the shipped channel is built from (2026.10.8 ships this channel as `@openclaw/imessage`, not bundled):

```console
sshd sessions: mac-a=15  mac-b=0
staged on mac-a: sha256 77db3976…   (the upload hit the wrong Mac)
trimmed neighbour binary executed: yes
cursor: literal db -> since_rowid 888   (the trimmed neighbour's high-water)
```

Upgrade: a state dir created by `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then booted by this head — stored config bytes unchanged (same sha256), the cursor row for an unchanged identity still honoured (`since_rowid 777`), both stored rows still present, and the old trimmed-spelling row no longer reaching the literal database.

Unit suites — green with the fix, and both guards red on the base:

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  38 passed (38)
      Tests  352 passed (352)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

That cursor case and the cache case are the regression guards. On `HEAD^` the cursor readback fails with `expected 888 to be 777` — the literal database inherited the high-water of its trimmed neighbour — and the cache readback fails with `expected { trimmed: true } to deeply equal { literal: true }` because both spellings shared one entry. Other new cases: a literal-vs-trimmed `it.each` for database lookup plus blank-as-unset, an attested-binary resolve returning the literal path, a spawn assertion that the literal `cliPath` and `--db` reach the child, a remote-host case separating two wrappers by SSH destination, a CLI-output assertion that the literal `--db` bytes reach `imsg`, and a spawn-boundary case for the cwd fallback — the parent leaves `~` in place (`/srv/gateway/~/Library/Messages/chat.db`).

## Rebased Onto Current Main

The branch was rebased onto `main` and the resulting conflicts resolved; the PR is a single commit on top of current `main`, so the merge is clean. Where `main` had moved on, `main`'s newer owner won and this branch's overlapping mechanism was dropped:

- `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts` — keeps `main`'s `#184862` digest keys plus the legacy NUL-key adoption, and this branch's `readNonBlankString` path identity. The earlier whitespace-quoting encoding is gone because the digest already carries literal bytes.
- `client.ts` — combines this branch's literal-path resolution with `main`'s `remoteHost` plumbing.
- `cli-path.ts` / new `user-path.ts` — `resolveIMessageHomeDir` and `expandIMessageUserPath` now live in `user-path.ts` (a bare `node` child imports it); `cli-path.ts` re-exports them.
- `send.ts` — keeps this branch's `readNonBlankString` path semantics. The formatter splits the added import across three lines, so the file offset that growth with equivalent consolidations (one `stringValue`-based blank check replacing a hand-rolled `typeof`/`trim()` ternary, and grouped declarations) to keep the line-cap ratchet flat. No behavior change.

Verification on this head (`a8bb5af`, rebased onto `main`):

```console
$ node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --staged --base HEAD
Line-cap ratchet OK: 23 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  1 failed | 37 passed (38)
      Tests  1 failed | 356 passed (357)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
      Tests  5 passed | 1 skipped (6)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)
```

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on all 23 changed files. The single remaining imessage failure is `status.test.ts` expecting `iMessage: needs setup` while this shell renders `iMessage: 需要设置`; it reproduces on unmodified `main` in the same shell (locale-dependent), so it is not from this branch.
