Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: feat(ui): clear failed session alerts from the Subagents panel and session hovercard
prs.body:
Related: #185192, #185054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several child sessions fail or time out, each failure can only be cleared by opening that child, one at a time; the Subagents panel lists the failures but cannot acknowledge them.

## User Impact

User impact: failure alerts can be cleared in place. In the Subagents panel each unread failure has a **Mark {name} as read** control and the Failed heading has **Mark all as read** (two or more), on desktop and mobile. The session hovercard shows **Dismiss** under the hovered session’s own failure. Current main no longer folds child failures into the parent hovercard; this conflict repair preserves that behavior. Acknowledging clears the sidebar alert and hovercard notice on every surface and device, survives reload, and a later failure of the same session alerts again. Panel grouping does not change: failed runs stay listed under Failed, exactly as on main after you open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already decides whether a failure is still an alert: a failed session alerts until its read time passes its failure time, and opening the session writes that read time. These controls send the same conditional `sessions.patch { unread: false }` (fenced by `expectedSessionId` and `expectedMarkedUnreadAt`), so there is one acknowledgement shared by every surface, tab and device, and no new state, option or API.

- Controls appear only where the viewer can patch the failed session. The hovercard carries the failed session’s own sharing role and manual-unread marker, so a session-scoped owner gets Dismiss and a manually unread session is acknowledged instead of rejected as stale.
- The alert stays until the Gateway row reports the read. If the Gateway rejects the write, an error toast says so with the Gateway's reason ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. ..."), and the alert and its control stay, so the same click retries; the next successful acknowledgement replaces that toast with "Marked as read". It is a toast rather than an inline line because the hovercard can close before the reply arrives (session deletion reports its failures the same way).
- Focus: on desktop it moves to the next failure's control, then to the acknowledged row; on mobile it stays on the row. The hovercard keeps its existing focus restoration.
- Known limits: the acknowledgement is fenced to the session, not a run, so a newer failure that lands between render and click is acknowledged too (opening the session behaves the same today). While the parent conversation is open, main's existing hidden-run read for subagents can acknowledge a child whose retry fails immediately; this PR does not change that path.

## Decision for the area owner

The open question is only whether the Subagents panel and the session hovercard should offer these acknowledgement controls (per row, Mark all as read for two or more, Dismiss in the hovercard). They add no state, option, setting or API: each control sends the same conditional read receipt the Control UI already sends when you open a failed session, so the Gateway stays the single owner of "is this failure still an alert", grouping stays by run outcome exactly as on main, and declining the direction means simply not merging. Approving it on this PR is enough; nothing else depends on it.

#185054 (open, another contributor) makes the same choice for the composer failure cards that #185192 has since removed from main; this PR covers the surfaces that remain.

<details><summary>Surface inventory</summary>

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel, desktop Failed group | Lists failures, no acknowledgement | Per-row Mark as read, Mark all as read (2+); rows stay in Failed |
| Subagents panel, mobile Finished list | Failed rows with red indicator, no acknowledgement | Same controls; rows keep their Failed indicator |
| Sidebar row failure indicator (own or folded child) | Own failure via row menu Mark as read; folded child only by opening it | Cleared by any acknowledgement of the failed session |
| Session hovercard failure section | No action | Dismiss, acknowledging the failing child when folded |
| Background session toast, sidebar issues inbox, chat details tally, native roster | Unchanged | Unchanged (transient, no session failures, or counts only) |

</details>

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `isUnacknowledgedSessionFailure` (`ui/src/lib/session-attention.ts`) is the single failure-alert rule; `sessionRowAttention` and the chat pane's read acknowledgement use it instead of two copies.
- Error attention carries the failed session's `sourceSessionId`, `sourceMarkedUnreadAt` and `sourceSharingRole`, so the hovercard targets the failed session with its own fence and role.
- `canDismissSessionFailure` / `dismissSessionFailures` (`ui/src/lib/sessions/session-failure-dismissal.ts`) own the access check, the conditional write and its rejection feedback (the shared `showToast` owner with `severity: "error"`).
- The hovercard error section moved to `session-hovercard-error.tsx` to keep `session-hovercard-solid.tsx` under the file line cap.
- New copy: `chat.subagentsPanel.markFailureRead` ("Mark {name} as read") and `chat.subagentsPanel.markAllFailuresRead` ("Mark all as read"). `sessionsView.markFailureReadFailed` ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. {error}") and `sessionsView.markFailureReadDone` ("Marked as read"). The hovercard reuses `common.dismiss`.

</details>

## Evidence

### Conflict repair (2026-11-02)

Merged main `6d172664c829` into the existing contributor branch, preserving the newer hovercard layout, own-session-only error attention, and narrow Subagents panel behavior. Moved the two dismissal labels into the optional-session English catalog so the current catalog composer includes them.

- Secretless AWS Crabbox validation: 66 focused tests across four files passed; 19 bundled Chromium browser scenarios across the three affected E2E files passed.
- UI typecheck, focused formatting, English catalog verification/baseline, and targeted lint completed. Lint reports one warning on the unchanged `ViewerFacepile` expression inherited from main.
- Browser proof covers desktop/mobile acknowledgement, bulk acknowledgement, failed-write retry, hovercard dismissal, and narrow panel containment. Before/after panel screenshots were inspected.
- Independent conflict-resolution review found no P0–P2 issues, including a follow-up review of the translation relocation.
- Local ClawSweeper completed on `6d172664c829..644986a42953`. It raised two P2 feature findings: cached error attention can lack a session ID, and a fulfilled `null` patch result can replace rejection feedback with success. Both paths are unchanged from the original PR head `a9972c44f10c`; they remain follow-ups for feature review, outside this conflict-only repair. This is not a clean full-feature review or merge recommendation.
- Previous-head GitHub CI is historical evidence, not current-head validation. This update does not merge the PR.

The original evidence below predates the conflict repair. Parent-folded child failure screenshots describe the prior base, not the current behavior. Current main displays only the hovered session’s own failure.

### Real Gateway, real failed subagents (Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2)

An isolated Gateway built from this branch (`dist/` plus `dist/control-ui`, served bundle hash checked against the build) on loopback with a synthetic config. A parent turn spawns four real subagents through `sessions_spawn`; only the loopback model provider is scripted, and it rejects every child request with HTTP 400, so each child run fails through the real runtime (`status: "failed"`, `lastRunError: "LLM request rejected: Synthetic provider rejected the request | synthetic_rejection"`). No WebSocket interception; frames are observed passively. Two browser contexts are paired as two devices.

| | Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel with four real failures | ![main: Failed 4, no controls, parent row red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-panel.png) | ![branch: Mark as read per row and Mark all as read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-controls.png) |
| Parent row hovercard (child failure folded) | ![main: failure notice, no action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-hovercard.png) | ![branch: Dismiss under the child failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-hovercard-dismiss.png) |
| After acknowledging | | ![one row read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-one-read.png) ![all read: rows stay in Failed, parent row no longer red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-all-read.png) |
| Second device after reload | | ![device B: no controls, no red row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-device-b-after-reload.png) |
| Same child fails again | | ![device B sidebar alert returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-sidebar-device-b.png) ![device B panel offers Mark as read again (WebKit)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-panel-device-b-webkit.png) |

Sequence asserted in both browsers (all pass):

1. Main build: Failed 4, zero acknowledgement controls in the panel and hovercard, still 4 after reload.
2. Branch build: the hovercard on the parent row names one failed child. That child is also marked unread by hand (`sessions.patch { unread: true }`); Dismiss then sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` equal to its marker and the Gateway advances `lastReadAt`.
3. Mark as read on one row, then Mark all as read on the remaining two: controls go, all four rows stay in Failed, the parent row's red indicator clears.
4. Reload: still acknowledged. A second paired device: no controls, no red row.
5. The operator asks the parent to retry one child; the parent's real `sessions_send` runs it again and it fails again. Both devices show the red parent row with "Child session ... failed" and that one row's Mark as read control.

Captured `sessions.patch` request/response pairs for the four acknowledgements (Chromium; WebKit identical in shape):

| Child | Sent | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| folded child, manually unread | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: <its marker> }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| row control | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| Mark all as read (2) | same shape, one per child | ok, `lastReadAt` set |

Real-seam red for the hovercard fence: the same harness against the previous head of this PR sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null` for the manually unread child; the Gateway answers ok with the entry unchanged (no `lastReadAt`) and the alert stays.

### Rejected acknowledgement and retry (mocked Gateway, Playwright Chromium and WebKit 27.2)

The mock Gateway holds the first `sessions.patch` and answers it with `UNAVAILABLE: Session store unavailable`; the second click goes through. Asserted in both engines: the error toast text, the alert and control still present and enabled, a second `sessions.patch` on the same control, the alert cleared, and the error toast replaced by "Marked as read".

| | Rejected | Retried |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel (WebKit) | ![error toast, Mark as read control still on the failed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, control gone, row still in Failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-retried.png) |
| Session hovercard (Chromium) | ![error toast, sidebar row still red, Dismiss still offered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, sidebar alert cleared](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-retried.png) |

A rejection was not forced on the real Gateway: the session store would have to be broken under a running Gateway, or the row changed between render and click, which races the live row update. The retry sends the same request as the real-Gateway acknowledgements above.

### Mobile (mocked Gateway, 390px)

![mobile before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-before.png) ![mobile after marking one read: control gone, Failed indicator kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-after-one-read.png)

### Tests (macOS arm64)

Red = the new tests on the previous head's production code; green = this branch.

- `ui/src/components/session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts`, new: Dismiss on a folded child failure under `operator.sessions.write` sends that child's `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` and `expectedSessionId`. Red: Dismiss is absent (child role dropped); with broad `operator.write` it sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null`. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/lib/session-attention.test.ts`: failure stays an alert until read and alerts again later; error attention carries the source session id, marker and role. Red: source facts missing. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagents-panel.test.ts`, 2 cases: desktop controls only on unread failures the viewer can patch, exact conditional params, rows stay in Failed, focus to the next control then to the row; mobile acknowledged in place with its Failed indicator and focus on the row. Red: fail. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/components/session-hovercard.test.ts`: Dismiss renders and calls its owner only when supplied.
- Rejected write, new: `chat-subagents-panel.test.ts` (desktop and mobile) and `session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts` reject the first `sessions.patch`, then expect the error toast with the Gateway reason, the control still present and enabled, a successful second click, and "Marked as read" replacing the error. Red on the previous head: 3 fail (no toast; the rejection was swallowed). Green: pass.
- Playwright (mocked Gateway) `subagents-panel.e2e.test.ts` and `session-progress-hovercard.e2e.test.ts`, including the two new rejection cases: 19/19 pass in Chromium and 19/19 in WebKit.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, oxlint, oxfmt and stylelint on the changed files: pass.
- Full `pnpm lint`: exits 1 on 11 errors, all in files this PR does not touch (`extensions/copilot`, `extensions/knowledge`, `extensions/oc-path`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/tlon`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, `src/agents/code-mode-execution.ts`); no changed file appears in its output.

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an unambiguous choice between starting a new root chat and creating a child of the selected chat. Previously, implicit Gateway parentage could make a supposedly independent chat a child, while explicit children and grandchildren could appear at root in Threads.

## User Impact

- The sidebar header **+** starts an independent root session. There is no second, competing independent-session button.
- The selected eligible session's overflow menu offers **New child session**. Children and grandchildren retain their hierarchy in Threads.
- Existing sessions are not migrated or reparented. Connection, busy-state, write-access, and selected-parent guards remain.
- These creation actions require a Gateway supporting the new intent fields. An older Gateway gets an update-required error; the app does not silently fall back to different parentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair carries explicit child intent through creation, persisted session metadata, reset preservation, list/describe/event projection, and Android rendering. Ordinary New sends `independent: true`; child creation sends `explicitChild: true` with the selected parent. Existing upstream standalone/direct-chat behavior and visibility admission remain intact.

The public API rejects conflicting independent/parent intent and adoption of existing keys. A review-discovered edge case is also fixed: explicit child creation without a key cannot take the main-session reset shortcut and reset its parent.

This is an Android proposal, not a web Control UI `/new` change. **Maintainer acceptance of the public `sessions.create` fields and Android product behavior remains separate from this repair.** No upstream merge is requested by this update.

## Evidence

### Final conflict refresh — October 31

Latest head: `83a24f9b7ac18ea4c62e5b94a2404c22023a5c87`, integrating upstream `20cdaea4bb5fc2035949a39643ae2df413ed9f3b` with published `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321` as first parent. Normal fast-forward publication, no force push.

Upstream advanced during the preceding validation. The only new conflict was the generated Gateway predicate output: canonical regeneration preserves upstream's optional publication-review URL field alongside this PR's session intent fields. Main inspected the incremental generated diff; no handwritten repair was needed. **36 affected schema/compiled-validator tests passed**, canonical freshness and native merge hooks passed, and the exact tree/parents were verified. Prior session lifecycle, inheritance, projection, catalog, lint/types/format and Android evidence remains scoped evidence for unchanged PR-owned inputs. Earlier UI build proof is not exact-current-head clearance because upstream also changed unrelated UI files. Hosted CI remains separate.

### Preceding repair and integration — October 31

Preceding repair head: `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321`, integrating upstream `bf56514c98ecb628b406889e6d573d0485bfd53e` while preserving published `7e886928692e6897289bf66af707fb86646b0609` as its first parent. No force push.

The earlier Build dist failure was caused by a stale Control UI history-state validator after the session-row schema gained `explicitChild`. Canonical regeneration and a schema/standalone parity regression fixed it in `7e886928`: the regression failed before regeneration and passed afterward; all 29 validator tests, UI production build, scoped lint and test typechecking passed on that head.

The integration resolves the generated Gateway predicate conflict through canonical generation, preserves upstream session-creation authority and cancellation changes, and reuses the existing error-response helper to satisfy the session-creation file's line limit without changing error behavior.

- Integration validation: 17 Gateway lifecycle tests, 2 inheritance tests and 13 session-entry projection tests passed on the integration candidate. The only subsequent source edit was the equivalent catalog error-response simplification; 2 selected public-handler catalog rejection tests passed afterward (22 unrelated cases were intentionally not selected).
- Scoped Gateway lint, Gateway-server typechecking, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on the final tree. Gateway and UI generated-output freshness checks remain applicable: generator inputs and outputs did not change after those checks.
- Main independently inspected the integration's three handwritten merge owners, the final error-response change, generated-validator parity and proof applicability; no actionable integration finding remained. Earlier full-feature independent review is described below. The standalone autoreview authentication gap remains; this is not a claim of an autoreview or ClawSweeper pass on the new head.
- Earlier UI and Android build/test evidence below is scoped prior-head evidence, not a fresh full-suite run on this integration. No new APK or live-device test was performed. Hosted CI and maintainer product/API acceptance remain separate gates.

### Earlier feature repair evidence

Repair commit: `6a07b12ac85ece37ddaf80a002266969ddcd29eb`.
Integrated upstream: `54c3474691a6adc971056be145135d9146289394`. The update preserves the previously published head as its first parent; it is not a force push.

### Fresh focused validation

- **17 Gateway lifecycle tests passed**, including independent roots, explicit child/grandchild persistence and projection, reset retention, conflicting intent, and existing-key rejection. The new no-key child regression failed before the reset fix and passed afterward; it verifies a distinct child, unchanged parent entry, child metadata, and no parent-end hook.
- **2 inheritance-owner tests and 13 session-entry projection contract tests passed.**
- **69 Android tests passed**: controller creation (5), sidebar/Threads UI (2), grouping (24), and command controls (38). Production/test compilation and `:app:ktlintCheck` passed.
- Targeted TypeScript lint, Gateway-server typecheck, formatting, native-string inventory, canonical Gateway validator regeneration, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent read-only code review covered the complete candidate. Its one actionable finding—the no-key child reset path—was fixed, regression-tested, and reviewed again. The standalone autoreview CLI could not authenticate; the independent review ran through the connected coding-agent session instead. No standalone-autoreview success is claimed.
- A normal hook-enabled merge commit was created in a secretless container, with exact tree and both parents verified. Merge-mode hook behavior is not a claim that all ordinary-commit checks ran.

Gateway checks used isolated repository harnesses and the repository-supported Node/oxlint fallback because the pinned Bun runtime could not be staged in the offline proof environment. Android dependency hydration/build used a task-owned secretless container. Full hosted CI is separate; earlier failed checks belong to the old head and are not represented as cleared by these local results.

### Before / after

Inspected synthetic Compose test renders, not connected-device screenshots. The historical before image shows the redundant root action and inline child action. The repaired sidebar uses one header New action plus the selected row's overflow menu. Minor speckling in the sidebar render is a test-raster artifact; incidental navigation ordering is not the claimed change.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: redundant independent action and inline child action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-before.png) | ![After: one header New action and selected-row overflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-after.png) |

![Selected-row menu: New child session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-child-menu.png)

![Threads: Project, Child, and Grandchild remain nested; Ordinary New is a separate root](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-threads.png)

### Scope and remaining limits

No new APK installation or live Android-to-Gateway device test was performed. Public-handler and rendering tests prove the scoped boundaries, not a full deployed-version upgrade matrix. [Earlier contributor-reported device evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159159#issuecomment-5901361888) predates this candidate and is not exact-head proof. The full cross-platform suite was not rerun locally; current-head CI and maintainer review remain merge gates.

The repair uses the existing creation, lineage, projection, and reset owners rather than adding a parallel hierarchy manager. Its necessary growth is the explicit intent contract and boundary regressions; most generated-code churn is canonical predicate renumbering.

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: fix(android): parallel Claude CLI tool calls show no results in chat history
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the Android chat, a Claude CLI session in which the agent ran tools in parallel shows those calls without results after the reply, and lists each result again in a tool group of its own. This is the Android side of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/171975, which https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171976 fixed for iOS only.

## User Impact

User impact: on Android, parallel tool calls in Claude CLI sessions show as one tool group in which each call expands to its result, as on iOS.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.history` returns Claude CLI tool results for parallel calls as user rows that carry only `tool_result` blocks. Android parsed them as user turns, and the timeline's turn fence (`projectTranscriptToolActivity` in `ChatTimeline.kt`) then dropped the calls still waiting for a result before reading the row, so the results became new tool rows and the calls stayed without results.

`ChatController.parseHistory` now splits such a row into one tool result row per result, before the timeline sees it (on Android a `session.message` event only triggers a history reload, so this also covers live updates), the same place and the same rule as iOS `ingestedMessages` from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171976. Text or images on the same row stay a user row after the results. The result rows take no idempotency key, so they never match an optimistic outgoing message, and carry the result's error flag, which source previews read on result rows.

History cached on the device by an earlier app version is stored already parsed, so it shows the old rows until the next `chat.history` refresh replaces it.

## Evidence

Tested at `8ec596d6ad0` (base `upstream/main` `c8518acbb27`).

Both sides ran the Android debug app (play flavor) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway: own home, state and config, a loopback port, no provider variable (so no provider calls), its runtime built from the base and started from this branch's checkout, which changes only `apps/android`. Its main session is bound to a synthetic Claude CLI transcript with two parallel `Read` calls; `chat.history` returns the results as two user `tool_result` rows. One script drove both sides; only the installed APK differed. It opens the session, expands "Worked for 5s", then taps the call group, the first call row, and the result-only group for `notes-a.md` and its row when there is one (base only; on the fix those taps land on the open result text and change nothing). Nothing was mocked.

| Expect | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the Claude CLI turn is open (control) | met | met |
| no result has a tool group of its own | **not met** (2 groups) | met |
| the first call opens to its result | **not met** | met |
| the result of notes-a.md is on screen (control) | met (in its own group) | met (under its call) |

![Turn expanded. Before: the call group plus one result-only group per result. After: one group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-171976-android-parallel-tool-result-carrier/2-worked.png)

| Call group expanded | First call tapped | Result of notes-a.md |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: two call rows without chevrons. After: two call rows that can be opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-171976-android-parallel-tool-result-carrier/3-calls.png) | ![Before: the call does not open. After: the call opens to Alpha: the build passes.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-171976-android-parallel-tool-result-carrier/4-first-call.png) | ![Before: Alpha: the build passes. only inside a separate result-only group. After: under its call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-171976-android-parallel-tool-result-carrier/5-result.png) |

Recordings of both runs, side by side (not time-aligned): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-171976-android-parallel-tool-result-carrier/video.mp4

Observed result: on the base the calls cannot be opened, and the results appear only in separate tool groups, one per result; with the fix there is one group and each call expands to its result.

The summary line says "tool outcomes unknown" on both sides (4 before, 2 after). That label and the group title ("Read ×2" after the fix, file names before) come from the Gateway's prepared activity for these rows: Claude CLI results carry no error flag, so the Gateway marks them "Outcome unknown", and its history activity does not pair a carrier's result with its call either. That is Gateway behavior and is left to a separate change.

Checks, through Gradle: the new test `ChatControllerMessageIdentityTest.claudeCliParallelToolResultsSettleTheirCallsInOneGroup` fails on the base (one unresolved group with both calls without results, then one group per result) and passes with the fix (2.5 s in Gradle's test report when run alone, Robolectric start-up included); `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.*' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.*'`: 1483 passed, 0 failed; `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` passes.

Not covered: an emulator and a synthetic transcript only; no live Claude CLI run. Mixed rows (results plus user text) follow the split order in the code but were not reproduced on a device.

prs.title: feat(sessions): choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automatic idle or daily reset always carries the last six user/assistant messages into the new session, and there is no way to change that number. Some deployments want more continuity after a reset, others want a clean start.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `session.reset.tailMessages` (also in `resetByType` and `resetByChannel` entries) to choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps. The default stays 6, so nothing changes unless the key is set. `0` starts the new session empty. `/new` and `/reset` still always clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tail size was a constant inside the transcript selection. It is now resolved with the rest of the reset policy, so the per-type and per-channel overrides work the same way as `mode`, `atHour` and `idleMinutes`. The four places that write an automatic preserve-tail boundary pass the resolved value: the channel reply path, `openclaw agent`, the gateway agent turn and cron's stale-session rollover.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/config/zod-schema.session-config.ts`: `tailMessages` (integer, at least 0) on the reset policy object, with label and help text.
- `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts`: `SessionResetPolicy.tailMessages`, type override first, then base, then `DEFAULT_RESET_TAIL_MESSAGES = 6`.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-replay.ts` and `session-reset-boundary-event.ts`: the preserve-tail request takes an optional `tailMessages`; omitted means the default.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `session-hooks.ts`, `src/agents/command/session.ts`, `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-patch.ts`, `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-session-persist.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/session.ts`, `run-session-state.ts`: pass the resolved value. In `session-hooks.ts` the redundant `explicitReason` parameter is dropped: for explicit resets it always equalled `previousReason`, so `session.ts` does not grow.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/session.md`, `docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md`, regenerated config baseline.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `src/config/sessions/session-reset-boundary-event.test.ts`: with 4 turns, the boundary keeps from turn 2 by default, from turn 4 with `2`, from turn 1 with `10`, and nothing with `0`.
  - `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.test.ts`: default 6, base value, chat-type override, channel override, and the schema rejects `-1`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `config:docs:check`: clean.
- 44 test files that import the changed modules (sessions, reply session, agent command, gateway agent turn, cron isolated agent): 574 passed. One test, `src/cron/isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` "runs a linked current job as a child of its conversation", fails on this macOS machine identically on `main` without this change. `src/config/io.observe-recovery.test.ts` (2 tests) does the same.

Live run against a real Gateway:

- Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1. Candidate: this branch (`e8c6e67a793`), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` and installed with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz>` (`openclaw --version`: `2026.10.9 (e8c6e67)`, tgz sha256 `ecf411c1…da63`). The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, which logs every request body, so no provider key is used.
- Config: `session.reset = { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 1 }`, plus `tailMessages` per round.
- Each round: `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof-<round>` sends turns 1–4 to a fresh session, waits 80 s, then sends turn 5. The table shows the user/assistant messages the model received on turn 5, the first turn after the idle reset. Per-turn runtime-context messages are left out.

| `tailMessages` | Model input on turn 5 | Reset event |
|---|---|---|
| not set | T2, A, T3, A, T4, A, **T5** (6 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 2 |
| `2` | T4, A, **T5** (2 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 4 |
| `0` | **T5** (none kept) | `reason: idle`, no `firstKeptEntryId` |
| `20` | T1, A, T2, A, T3, A, T4, A, **T5** (all 8 kept) | `reason: idle`, `firstKeptEntryId` = turn 1 |

In every round, turn 5 stayed in the same session id and the transcript has one `reset` event between turn 4 and turn 5, so the difference comes from the reset tail and not from a new session.

The VM was purged afterwards.

prs.title: fix: prevent ACP hook failures from replaying tasks in another runtime
prs.body:
Closes #147010

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an ACP task being replayed through the ordinary agent runtime when its dispatch hook times out or throws after work may already have started.

## User Impact

When an ACP dispatch fails or times out, the turn stays owned by ACP. Interactive sessions receive an error notice instead of an automatic retry through another runtime that could duplicate work. Parent-owned ACP children remain silent so their parent retains delivery ownership. Missing hooks and hooks that explicitly decline the turn keep their existing fallback behavior, and control commands remain available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The claiming-hook API previously collapsed errors, timeouts, and explicit declines into the same unhandled result. This change preserves that distinction internally. Only an error or timeout retains ACP ownership, including for a prompt after an in-place reset, and uses the existing final-delivery path for the notice. Cancellation, private delivery, parent-owned child delivery, and already-queued final replies are respected. The change does not alter timeout budgets, missing-hook behavior, explicit-decline behavior, or provider-specific retries.

## Evidence

- At base `060e856e5f9df245d63c98990fcb47e18108c6b9`, regression cases using the public dispatcher and real plugin hook runner show that a timeout or thrown error can reach the ordinary resolver after an ACP side effect.
- With the fix, 500 focused tests pass across reply dispatch and plugin hooks. Coverage distinguishes error/timeout from missing/declined hooks and includes control commands, reset tails, cancellation, suppressed delivery, already-queued final replies, and lifecycle accounting.
- Diagnostic assertions verify one processed event and one idle transition on the failure paths.
- A guard-specific loopback run used the source Gateway and the official built `acpx` plugin. A temporary, uncommitted probe at the registered `reply_dispatch` hook boundary wrote a side-effect marker and then threw before the existing ACP runtime error handler could claim the turn. The Gateway returned the new guard notice, and the ordinary-model sentinel received zero requests:

  ```text
  [guard-proof] agent_wait={"status":"error","error":"The ACP turn did not complete. It was not retried with another runtime. Check any existing results before trying again."}
  [guard-proof] hook_side_effect=hook-started
  [guard-proof] terminal_reason=acp_dispatch_unclaimed
  [guard-proof] delivered_notice=The ACP turn did not complete. It was not retried with another runtime. Check any existing results before trying again.
  [guard-proof] ordinary_model_requests=0
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```

  The probe was removed after the run and the checkout returned to the published commit with a clean worktree. No external model or channel was invoked.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 060e856e5f9df245d63c98990fcb47e18108c6b9` passes, including core and core-test typechecks, changed-file lint, dead-export checks, and changed-lane guards.
- The same patch was rebased without conflicts onto `0347bd5ab4a84001579dadac97f542309db9d05a`. The intervening `main` commits did not touch the two implementation files. After applying review feedback for parent-owned child delivery, 89 directly targeted tests, `git diff --check`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 0347bd5ab4a84001579dadac97f542309db9d05a` pass at the rebased head.
- Full `pnpm test` was not run; the scoped suites cover this dispatch boundary.
- No external model or Telegram E2E calls were made. Production configuration and installed patches were not changed.

prs.title: fix(cli): try requested audio and video inference models first
prs.body:
Related: #176246. Earlier strict-pin proposal: #172409 by @yetval.

## What Problem This Solves

`infer audio transcribe --model provider/model` and `infer video describe --model provider/model` can silently use a configured media model instead of the requested model.

## User Impact

The requested model is tried first, and the result reports the model that succeeded. Configured media models remain fallbacks: a failed attempt can send the file to another configured provider or CLI backend. This is a draft proposal while the strict-pinning versus configured-failover contract in the linked issue remains undecided.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag was used as a conversation-model hint, which does not override configured media entries. A separate optional file-request override now reaches the existing media selector. Matching entries retain their original transport settings and credential-owner indices; a different model does not lend its model-specific settings. The configuration remains the source for fallbacks.

Reported and discussed by @yetval; this implementation was written independently of the earlier strict-pin proposal.

## Evidence

Normal CLI requests to a local compatible HTTP server now pass both audio/video explicit-model cases and both no-override controls. Five additional cases pass for an empty media-model list, an exact configured entry at index 1, provider-wide settings, and ordered HTTP 400 → configured-fallback success for audio and video. The observed endpoint, model, headers, exact request count, and JSON winner are checked independently. All commands and HTTP handlers joined without forced termination.

The resolver regressions fail before the fix (5 failures, 6 existing passes) and pass afterward. Focused file-runtime, automatic-audio, video, authority, and processing-disposition tests pass (51 total); core/test type checks, source/test typed lint, formatting, MDX, and native line/test budgets pass. The test ceiling is unchanged; 91 regression lines fit within its existing budget.

`pnpm build` passed before the final removal of a redundant local model-list alias. The equivalent simplification passed fresh P0–P2 review and affected type/lint/test checks; the final runtime build passed. Final transport evidence uses that runtime. The full SDK build evidence is reused for the unchanged public API/type additions.

These checks use synthetic audio/video, isolated state, and a local compatible HTTP server. They prove CLI routing and transport/fallback behavior; they do not establish real vendor availability or inference quality.


Latest-stable upgrade validation remains **NOT RUN**. The draft still awaits the fallback-contract decision and review of the evidence below.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable CLI/wire evidence and current-head source binding</summary>

## Inspectable local HTTP evidence

Current PR head: `7c722be663ab50739c3d074d18b22057bb460c84`. These captures use normal `pnpm openclaw infer` CLI invocations, native media adapters and a synthetic loopback HTTP server returning fixed compatible responses. No vendor model or paid API was called. This proves selection and transport behavior, not transcription/video-understanding quality.

Inputs: a 16,044-byte PCM WAV (1 channel, 16000 Hz, 16-bit) and a 31,772-byte MP4 byte-identical to tracked repository fixture `ui/src/e2e/fixtures/video-poster.mp4`. No repository provenance is asserted for the WAV. Request/media bodies, response text and credentials are omitted.

Commands preserve the actual flags; private file paths are normalized for display:

```sh
pnpm openclaw infer audio transcribe --file ./audio.wav --json
pnpm openclaw infer audio transcribe --file ./audio.wav --json --model openai/whisper-1
pnpm openclaw infer video describe --file ./video.mp4 --json
pnpm openclaw infer video describe --file ./video.mp4 --json --model moonshot/kimi-k2.6
```

### Before and after requested-model selection

These are field projections of captured wire metadata and actual CLI JSON stdout, not reconstructed raw stdout. Each row represents one data request. The explicit requests were `openai/whisper-1` and `moonshot/kimi-k2.6`.

```jsonl
{"phase":"before","case":"audio-explicit","wire":{"url":"/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"gpt-4o-transcribe"},"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-4o-transcribe"}}
{"phase":"before","case":"video-explicit","wire":{"url":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"kimi-k2.5"},"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"moonshot","model":"kimi-k2.5"}}
{"phase":"after","case":"audio-explicit","wire":{"url":"/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"whisper-1"},"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"whisper-1"}}
{"phase":"after","case":"video-explicit","wire":{"url":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"kimi-k2.6"},"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"moonshot","model":"kimi-k2.6"}}
```

All four before commands exited 0 with valid JSON; the fixture detected the two wrong-model results. No-override controls passed before and after:

| No-override case | Before wire / CLI model | After wire / CLI model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| audio-control | `gpt-4o-transcribe` / `gpt-4o-transcribe` | `gpt-4o-transcribe` / `gpt-4o-transcribe` |
| video-control | `kimi-k2.5` / `kimi-k2.5` | `kimi-k2.5` / `kimi-k2.5` |

Each no-override case made one data request, exited 0 and returned `ok:true`.

### Exact transport ownership and failure fallback

The following are actual ordered data requests. `x-fixture-route:null` means that configured-row marker was absent. All requests passed the synthetic-auth equality check; no authorization value is published. GET model-inventory requests are excluded from data-request counts.

```jsonl
{"case":"audio-no-configured-models","requests":[{"method":"POST","url":"/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"whisper-1","x-fixture-route":null,"status":200}],"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"whisper-1"}}
{"case":"audio-exact-owned-index-1","requests":[{"method":"POST","url":"/owned/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"whisper-1","x-fixture-route":"owned-slot-1","status":200}],"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"whisper-1"}}
{"case":"audio-provider-wide-row","requests":[{"method":"POST","url":"/provider-wide/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"whisper-1","x-fixture-route":"provider-wide","status":200}],"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"whisper-1"}}
{"case":"audio-explicit-400-configured-fallback","requests":[{"method":"POST","url":"/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"whisper-1","x-fixture-route":null,"status":400},{"method":"POST","url":"/fallback/v1/audio/transcriptions","model":"gpt-4o-transcribe","x-fixture-route":"configured-only","status":200}],"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-4o-transcribe"}}
{"case":"video-explicit-400-configured-fallback","requests":[{"method":"POST","url":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"kimi-k2.6","x-fixture-route":null,"status":400},{"method":"POST","url":"/fallback/v1/chat/completions","model":"kimi-k2.5","x-fixture-route":"configured-only","status":200}],"cli":{"ok":true,"provider":"moonshot","model":"kimi-k2.5"}}
```

The first three cases have exactly 1 POST each. Both fallback cases have exactly 2: the requested primary receives nonretryable HTTP 400, followed by the configured fallback receiving HTTP 200. The configured-only marker appears only on the fallback, and CLI JSON independently names that fallback as winner. prs.title: fix(acp): prevent task replay after dispatch hook failures
prs.body:
Supersedes #147018, thanks @xenaocx-dev.
Related: #147010

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ACP tasks running again through another runtime when their dispatch hook throws or times out after starting work.

## User Impact

ACP dispatch failures surface as task errors without automatically replaying possible side effects. Missing hooks and explicit declines keep their fallback behavior. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The claiming-hook owner now stops on the first ACP dispatch error, before either another hook or ordinary agent dispatch can run. An invoked hook can already have started work even without returning a claim. Pre-invocation plugin reload refusals retain their existing replacement path, and non-ACP hook failure policy is unchanged.

The simplification pass removed the redundant empty-handler early return: the shared loop already produces a declined outcome. Production growth is 13 lines for the contextual failure policy and error propagation; this avoids adding a second delivery or lifecycle owner. The 64-line regression allocation covers two public-dispatch cases and the existing ACP-decline control.

## Evidence

- Main baseline `1a74a80617cfba9f1ca7e605d80b512db834103e`: both new error/timeout cases fail because the public dispatcher swallows the error and completes; the other 23 tests pass. The relevant owner files remain byte-identical on newer main `8910654af4923408553a9af6183074f5e05ba7f8`.
- With the fix, 35 focused tests pass across `dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch-scope.test.ts`, `wired-hooks-reply-dispatch.test.ts`, and `hooks.before-dispatch.test.ts`. The two regressions use the real hook runner, two fake runtimes, and an ordinary-runtime sentinel; only the first runtime performs an effect, and dispatch rejects. Testbox: [run 41574183164](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41574183164).
- Dispatcher file wall time: 52.42s red, 41.59s green (existing suite includes a 15s final-delivery admission check and cold runtime imports). Hook-runner file: 5.40s; before-dispatch file: 0.90s. PR CI supplies broad proof and its own timings.
- Codex autoreview against the baseline plus local changes: complete, scoped-clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings. Subsequent changes only wrap formatting and strengthen the existing decline test with ACP context.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. This independently implemented regression ran on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox. No live model or channel calls were made.
- Final ACP-decline control: 9/9 pass (26.66s including a new worker generation). Touched-file oxlint reports zero warnings/errors; oxfmt passes all five touched code/docs files; `git diff --check` passes. All compilation, dependency installation, lint preparation, and Bun staging ran remotely on Testbox.
- First exact-head CI [run 41575027957](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41575027957) passed all 40 other jobs, including tests, production/test types, lint, docs, browser E2E, and boundaries. Its baseline-ratchet failure was PR-caused: the allocation parser rejects inline comments. The follow-up changes only that record to the plain scalar `64`; the canonical parser reproduces the rejection before and accepts `64` after. The failed run is retained as failed evidence; the corrected head has now passed fresh CI. This mechanical correction does not change the reviewed production code or test cases.
- Final exact-head [CI run 41575945180](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41575945180) passed all 41 jobs at `1283a19b337329fcb36aaf76b798435d37eaf714`, including the corrected baseline ratchet and aggregate gate. All PR checks are complete without failures. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Startup and SQLite schema inspection repeatedly allocate objects for data that has not changed.

## User Impact

Reduces avoidable allocation work without changing plugin selection, SQL parsing, configuration, or storage formats. No operator action is required. Whole-Gateway RSS and latency acceptance is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The materialization owner now prepares plugin policy once and refreshes it only after a plugin-section rewrite. SQLite scanning keeps its existing quote/comment rules while walking numeric positions directly. These are independent extractions from the memory investigation; this PR does not include the held catalog-worker changes in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189111.

Production delta: +18 lines (+17 for explicit original/working policy ownership; the scanner has unchanged executable LOC plus one explanatory comment). Test/support delta: +96. The ineffective raw-deny-array spy is removed; the public precedence assertions remain.

## Evidence

Validated on pinned main `2c0ab86fa416c5dc4995cf50ea24312b241da434`, candidate tree `cae6d51b8359f1717ca3ac296ad295dc5551ec08`. Fresh dependency-qualified AWS proof passed: 275 tests covering policy materialization/core/channel siblings; SQL schema parsing/contracts/facts; native iterator lifetime, node SQLite, single-statement and backup behavior; core and affected-test types, targeted lint/format, and a complete build. [AWS run evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6616ae383be0840347fbe8bdf0342293).

Independent local autoreview: scoped-clean P0–P2 on signed head `fd6dcd0a6563633fc394a58acf670e416d90a368`. [Hosted exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190283#issuecomment-6557501489) found no correctness issues. Its test suggestion is applied in signed head `8de8fff5f23827fa3480b1ab8cb19b5fddab6f9b`: remove five lines containing two redundant spies/count assertions and their comment; retain all functional assertions and the 56-to-1 work-count regression. This is the only change since the tested build, so every production blob and benchmark input remains identical. CI on the test-only head reports an unrelated main-side lint failure: `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments)` for `createDeferred<void>()` at `src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts:167–168` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41303552446/job/124840264041)). The tested merge and its main parent contain the identical failing blob; the PR does not touch that file. The classifier calls it new relative to its earlier passing main comparison. No CI rerun or merge is requested; the performance hold below remains. No build or performance rerun is needed for deleted test assertions. Test-line ratchet passed without a ceiling change.

The review's performance-table request is addressed below; the result fails the landing rule. A fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade matrix was not run: this patch changes no persisted data, config/default shape, migration, or installation contract. Compiled startup/load and the focused settings/selection tests cover the changed allocation owners.

**Do not merge: the completed comparison below fails the predeclared performance rule.**

Predeclared performance rule, before the new measurements:

- Five serial baseline/candidate pairs, independently built from pinned main and main plus only these five files; identical committed benchmark controller from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190259.
- Real compiled Gateway: 8 agents, concurrency 8, 3 turns each, 250 seeded sessions, 20 history messages of 1,024 characters, 64 probes at 100 ms, 100 updates from 2 clients, 2 history clients with burst 2, 4 subscribers, mock provider, no warmups. Same default stream cadence in both arms.
- Compiled catalog worker: 5 workspaces, 5,000 remote rows, runtime plugin, 20 task rounds; repeat with 4 providers. Separate cold request and warm request statistics; forced GC stays outside timed requests.
- Require matching functional responses and verified turn counts, fewer repeated owner operations/allocations, and no 20% worsening in any user-facing CPU, memory or latency metric. Report every worsening median and sample spread; do not claim controlled RSS savings if background inference counts differ.
- Existing isolated evidence is not whole-Gateway acceptance: unchanged five-candidate policy normalization falls from 56 calls to 1; the SQL scanner microprobe reduced sampled allocations by 94.95%. Completed compiled results are reported below.

## Compiled performance result — hold

Five AB pairs completed in [AWS run `run_0de52806d422c11ecadf1089f43bc7dd`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0de52806d422c11ecadf1089f43bc7dd), Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, m7i.xlarge, four CPUs. prs.title: fix(macos): keep Gateway auth when Tailscale exposure is turned off
prs.body:
Closes #187597 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Gateway's token, password and trusted-proxy settings are deleted when Tailscale Exposure is set to Off in the macOS Connection settings while the app is connected to its Gateway. ## User Impact After choosing Off, paired phones, other CLIs and the Control UI keep authenticating with the existing token. Before this change they were rejected after the Gateway restarted, and the Gateway ran with a new runtime-only token. ## Why This Change Was Made `TailscaleIntegrationSection.buildTailscaleConfigRoot` is the one place that maps Exposure to config. On Off it now removes only `auth.allowTailscale`, the key Serve writes, and leaves the rest of `gateway.auth` alone. The Gateway already treats a missing `allowTailscale` as false when Tailscale mode is not serve (`src/gateway/auth-resolve.ts:79-81`), so this does not widen access. The regression test goes through `saveTailscaleSettings`, the save boundary the settings view calls, with `ConfigStore` routed to its connected `config.set` path. `saveTailscaleSettings` is internal for that test, like `loadedSettings` and `applySettingsIfChanged` beside it; the builder stays private.
Root cause The original Tailscale settings (28ad475) skipped `auth` on Off. 850cbfe3698 ("route macOS remote config via gateway") replaced that with `gateway.removeValue(forKey: "auth")` without giving a reason. The connected save (`ConfigStore.saveToGateway`) sends the whole document to `config.set`, which replaces the stored config, so the deletion reached `openclaw.json`. On restart the Gateway found no token and generated a runtime-only one. The offline fallback (`saveDict(preserveExistingKeys: true)`) merges keys, so it never deleted `auth`.
## Evidence ### macOS app, connected Off save, after upgrading from the latest stable 1. `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm (latest stable) wrote the config with `openclaw config set`: token auth, `allowTailscale: true`, and `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent: 7` as an unrelated setting. Its Gateway started on that state and accepted the token. 2. The Gateway from an ad-hoc build of this branch then ran on the same state as the named profile's launchd service, and the macOS app (same build, same profile, local mode) attached to it: "Using existing gateway (pid 90862)". Exposure showed "Tailnet (Serve)"; I chose Off in the Connection window. 3. The app's own UI connection sent `config.set`; the Gateway accepted the write and restarted; the app reconnected with the same token. The config diff against what 2026.10.8 wrote is only the two intended keys. 4. After the restart: the original token is accepted; a wrong token is rejected; a request carrying only Tailscale identity headers is rejected.
Gateway log and config diff ```text 19:56:02 [ws] client connected conn=03661c35-… client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token 19:58:07 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.set 3898ms bytes=734 conn=03661c35…b1e8 19:58:13 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale) 19:58:14 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (write) 19:58:27 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting 19:58:43 [ws] client connected conn=5aba3fcf-… client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token $ diff <(jq -S . openclaw.json written by 2026.10.8) <(jq -S . openclaw.json after the app's Off save) "gateway": { "auth": { - "allowTailscale": true, "mode": "token", "token": "proof-token-187597" }, "bind": "loopback", "mode": "local", - "port": 18998 + "port": 18998, + "tailscale": { + "mode": "off" + } }, ```
Stable 2026.10.8 writes the config ```text $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.mode token $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.token proof-token-187597 $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.allowTailscale true $ openclaw config set agents.defaults.maxConcurrent 7 $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # stable 2026.10.8 Gateway {"ok":true} ```
Authority after the restart ```text $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # original shared token {"ok":true} $ openclaw gateway call health --token wrong-token unauthorized: gateway token mismatch $ curl /__openclaw__/assistant-media?meta=1 -H 'tailscale-user-login: peter' -H 'x-forwarded-for: 100.64.0.1' ... # identity headers, no token 403 (Gateway log: "observed unattributable proxy-shaped traffic from 127.0.0.1; Gateway-authenticated routes reject it") $ curl /__openclaw__/assistant-media?meta=1 -H 'authorization: Bearer proof-token-187597' 200 ```
### Main vs fix on the same connected save The same `config.get` → Off → `config.set {raw, baseHash}` sequence through the CLI against an isolated Gateway, starting from token auth plus `allowTailscale: true`. Main removes `gateway.auth`, the Gateway logs "auth token was missing. Generated a runtime token for this startup", and the original token is rejected. The fix keeps `auth.mode` and `auth.token`, removes only `allowTailscale`, and the original token still works. | main | fix | |---|---| | | |
Main output ```text $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # before {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"proof-token-187597","allowTailscale":true}} $ openclaw gateway call config.get | jq '.gateway.tailscale.mode = "off" | del(.gateway.auth)' | openclaw gateway call config.set {raw, baseHash} config.set: {"ok":true} $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # after the save {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","tailscale":{"mode":"off"}} 18:56:31 [reload] config change detected; reload (gateway.auth.mode, gateway.auth.token, gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale, meta) 18:56:32 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting 18:56:33 [gateway] auth token was missing. Generated a runtime token for this startup (not persisted) $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # same client after restart health: unauthorized: gateway token mismatch ```
Fix output ```text $ openclaw gateway call config.get | jq '.gateway.tailscale.mode = "off" | del(.gateway.auth.allowTailscale)' | openclaw gateway call config.set {raw, baseHash} config.set: {"ok":true} $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # after the save {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"proof-token-187597"},"tailscale":{"mode":"off"}} 19:01:16 [reload] config change detected; reload (gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale, meta) 19:01:17 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # same client after restart health: ok $ openclaw gateway call health --token wrong-token health: unauthorized: gateway token mismatch ```
### Swift test at the save boundary `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests`. The test loads a document with token or password auth plus `allowTailscale: true` and calls `saveTailscaleSettings(.off)` with `ConfigStore` on its connected `config.set` path. On main's logic it fails for both cases at `TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203` (`gateway["auth"]`) while `.saved` and `tailscale.mode == "off"` pass; with the fix the suite passes 10/10.
Test output ```text == MAIN logic == ✘ "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" credentials ["token": "existing-token", "mode": "token"] TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203:9 Expectation failed: gateway?["auth"] as? [String: String] == credentials ✘ "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" credentials ["mode": "password", "password": "existing-password"] TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203:9 Expectation failed: gateway?["auth"] as? [String: String] == credentials ✘ Test run with 10 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.017 seconds with 2 issues. == FIX == ✔ Test "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" with 2 test cases passed after 0.005 seconds. ✔ Test run with 10 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.051 seconds. ```
Gaps: the main-branch failure is shown on the replayed connected save and in the Swift test, not by clicking in a main build of the app. Identity-only acceptance before Off was not exercised; it needs a real Tailscale Serve front end. Gates: `git diff --check` clean. swiftformat and swiftlint were not available locally. Production delta +6/-2; test delta +38/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no config or state migration. Blast radius is Off saves from the macOS Tailscale section. Not included: Doctor recovery for hosts that already lost `auth`. That would be a Doctor change needing owner approval. Those hosts already had a new token saved by `ensureAppHostedGatewayAuth` and re-pair through the existing flow. The Serve display for Gateways with no Tailscale config is #187599.

prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with a generic credential alert when a separately managed Gateway blocks migration after an update
prs.body:
Related: #187000

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an in-place app update, the macOS app shows the generic "client credentials need recovery" alert and quits when a local Gateway it does not manage (extended-stable channel, a channel install policy, or an independently managed or write-disabled service) is still running and blocks the required credential migration.

## User Impact

User impact: the app now explains which owner keeps that Gateway's version and reports the known credential-maintenance conflict, with **Retry** / **Quit OpenClaw**. It does not infer version incompatibility from contention or unconditionally recommend an upgrade/downgrade. Resolve the reported conflict through the Gateway's management tool; change versions only if recovery identifies incompatibility. It still never stops, replaces, or migrates under such a Gateway. Credential preparation failures with any other cause keep the existing generic alert. Background (`--background-only`) launches print the same guidance and quit, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the credential migration owner knows why preparation failed, so it now marks the one case this alert explains. When a required migration's maintenance admission is refused because a process with lock role `gateway` holds the state, `prepareStartupClientCredentials` throws `ClientCredentialGatewayHeldError`, and `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` reports `error.code: "client_credentials_gateway_held"`. The app runs that command with `--json` and shows the Gateway-owner alert only for that code **and** an excluded local Gateway service. Everything else, including invalid config and the runtime-pin conflicts proposed in #191436, keeps the generic recovery alert. Legacy preparation before admission is validate-only, so the alert can accurately report stopping before the required maintenance. The earlier draft's "nothing was changed" claim for every failure is gone.

The stale-service detection from #190162 (remote primaries hosting a local Gateway) now returns one pure `admission` decision (`notHosted`, `excluded(reason)`, `admitted`), and `managedRepairGatesOpen` is derived from the new `managedRepairExclusion`, so existing gate callers behave the same.

Overlap: #191468 (merged) touches only `GatewayEndpointStore`. #191436 (open) edits `startup-client-credentials.ts` and the same docs paragraph. The overlap is textual only: its pin-migration failures are not Gateway-held, so they correctly keep the generic alert.

## Evidence

**Real CLI against a real isolated Gateway.** Private `HOME`/state/config, named profile `mgre2e`, port 34781, never the operator's Gateway:
- With `pnpm openclaw gateway run` holding state (pid 19622, role `gateway`) and a required migration (receipt device mismatch, the remount case), `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` exited 2 with `"code": "client_credentials_gateway_held"` and the contention message naming that holder.
- Same running Gateway, unrelated failure (invalid config): exit 2, **no** code (`Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config …`).
- After stopping that Gateway, the same command exited 0 with `{"ok": true}`, and the receipt returned to `complete` with the original device. This is the CLI side of **Retry**.

**Original-head regression evidence** (`c7e792e3b2d3`), red on the base and green with the fix:
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts`: "attributes a required migration refusal to the Gateway only when a gateway holds state" uses a real state-owner lock. The `gateway` case fails without the fix, and the `agent-embedded` case proves non-Gateway holders are not attributed. Suite: 22/22.
- `register.maintenance.test.ts`: the coded JSON failure envelope and exit 2. Suite: 39/39.
- Swift, private `HOME`/state/`TMPDIR`: `ClientCredentialStartupTests` (`--json` arguments, only the Gateway-held code yields `GatewayHeldError`, owner-specific recovery text) and `StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests` (the #190162 hosting matrix plus owner exclusions): 11/11.

**Original-head gates** (`c7e792e3b2d3`):
- `swift build` for the app product and the test targets passed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, oxfmt, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` all pass.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only 2 existing file-length violations in untouched files (`DashboardManager.swift`, `GatewayConnection.swift`).

**Original-head review:** local autoreview (Codex), committed range `d894035c7829..c7e792e3b2d3`, `--max-priority P2` with the owning sources as context: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings (0.88). An earlier P0-only pass was also clean.

**ClawSweeper finding follow-up** (`dddadc75e57f`):
- Removed the unsupported incompatibility diagnosis and unconditional version-change advice from the alert and docs. Receipt reconciliation after a remount can require exclusive maintenance without changing the credential layout.
- Removed the unused app-version argument and the wording-only helper test; error attribution, cancellation, and bundled-owner tests remain. No detection or service-lifecycle behavior changed.
- Current checks passed: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` (app and test targets), targeted SwiftFormat, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, docs oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.
- Native tests were not rerun on the operator desktop; the macOS guide requires OS-level isolation or a disposable runner. The earlier 11-test result above is prior-head evidence and includes the now-removed wording test. Subsequent explicitly authorized isolated native proof is recorded below.

**Native app validation on the current head (`dddadc75e57f`):**

Performed natively with explicit operator authorization, in a fresh OCM environment: separate HOME/CFFIXED_USER_HOME, state/config/profile, bundle identity, test LaunchAgent, and port 34781. No copied operator credentials or channels. A sandbox guard denied app access to the operator state and writes to operator preferences/LaunchAgents, and blocked connections to the live Gateway ports. App metadata pins the tested commit.

- Stable `2026.10.10` service: the actual app showed the owner-preserving maintenance alert with Retry / Quit. Retrying while the service held state returned to the alert without migration. After stopping only the test service, Retry completed migration; the native credential socket returned the original synthetic device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config remained unchanged.
- Compatible runtime: the test service ran the PR app's bundled runtime. A synthetic receipt device mismatch represented remount maintenance (not a real filesystem remount). The real app showed the same corrected maintenance alert without asserting version incompatibility. Retry while held returned to the alert. After stopping only this test service, Retry repaired the receipt; native credential admission preserved the original identity/keys and config.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes remained equal to their pre-test values. The live Gateway restarted independently during the interrupted agent run, so continuous PID preservation is not claimed; no test command stopped or modified that service.

**Validation findings / remaining gaps:**

- **Quit OpenClaw hangs.** Reproduced by clicking the actual recovery alert button. Process sampling shows `prepareCredentialsAndFinishLaunching` at `MenuBar.swift:421` synchronously inside `NSApplication.terminate`, whose nested termination loop prevents the main-actor cleanup from settling. The existing `requestTermination()` helper at lines 568–572 explicitly documents this hazard and schedules termination outside the main dispatch task. The hung test process required forced cleanup. This finding is not fixed by the copy-only commit.
- **Visual screenshots remain missing.** Accessibility inspection verified the actual alert text and controls, but captures are blank: `AppActivation.presentAlert` sets `alert.window.sharingType = .none` (line 146). No mockup or blank image is offered as screenshot proof; the capture restriction was not bypassed.
- Successful Retry is proved at the real app credential socket, not full chat/model connectivity. The full native suite remains CI-owned.
