prs.title: fix(ui): catch empty typing avatars in remote-draft tests
prs.body:
Closes #165045

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: remote-draft browser checks pass when the typing avatar loses its content but its frame remains visible.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The existing direct and group browser cases now reject empty or hidden avatar initials. Shipped-entry-point verification remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing remote-draft scenario owns this check. It now requires visible Owner initials with the expected text while preserving the avatar frame's absolute-position assertion. No production renderer or additional test scenario is introduced.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and scope</summary>

The original selector accepts either an avatar or its layout slot. A sized frame can remain visible after its content disappears; pending slots also hide their children without hiding the frame. The new descendant assertion checks the initials themselves, not the wrapper or accessible label. The fixture supplies Owner without an image URL. Both direct and group cases use this checkpoint; image/fallback rendering remains unchanged.

The earlier repair, #173786, was closed without merging. This change independently verifies the content-removal control on the selected base.
</details>

## Evidence

Final local checks: isolated Linux container, supported Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Chromium 156.0.8078.4. All three checkpoint controls were repeated on this runtime for both direct and group cases; the older Node 24.20.0 runs are retained separately. Base `50c3ff63fcd42100dbf0bd0ff677c759ffee3178`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Content removed; original avatar checkpoint | Direct and group both pass incorrectly with empty text and classes/role/name retained. |
| Content removed; repaired checkpoint | Both fail at the expected initials assertion. |
| Content restored; repaired checkpoint | Both pass with visible `O` initials and the placement check intact. |
| Full existing spec on base and fix | Both report 4 passed / 5 failed. The later RTL CSS matcher and browser-cleanup failures are unchanged. This is not a passing full-suite claim. |
| UI E2E typecheck | `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json`: exit 0. |
| Focused lint | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts`: exit 0. |
| Focused format | `pnpm format:check ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts`: exit 0. |
| Test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` | Exit 0. |
| Independent source/diff review | Complete, P0–P3, for the full two-file diff at `14fee5abe8df86db19134b893b78c7732a473847`: no findings. Simplification steps 1–3 and slop pass clean. |
| Worktree setup | `node scripts/worktree-setup.mjs full`: exit 0. The unchanged UI build reports an advisory chat-boot gzip overage. |

The mutation probes temporarily stop immediately after the avatar checkpoint, before unrelated later assertions. Their instrumentation is not committed. These runs exercise the existing browser suite with its fixed-response Gateway fixture; they are not real-Gateway proof. The restored checkpoint on supported Node completed in 17.00 seconds including setup; the full fixed file took 19.00 seconds wall time. CI seconds are pending.

<details>
<summary>Content-removal output</summary>

```text
base/direct: avatarContent="", legacyAssertion="passed"
base/group: avatarContent="", legacyAssertion="passed"
fix/direct and fix/group: toHaveText("O") failed; observed avatar text ""
restored/direct and restored/group: avatarContent="O", contentAssertion="passed"
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Browser-fixture controls, not real-Gateway proof</summary>

Content removed while the frame remains visible:

![Browser-fixture avatar with initials removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/def53b42-a995-464e-bd20-1f155b4f60c8)

Restored visible initials:

![Browser-fixture avatar with O initials restored](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18a4ebe8-3e87-49d0-820f-4da0ef23e516)

</details>

Production code delta +0/-0; browser-test delta +5/-1. The existing-format allocation record grants exactly the four added test lines; no test is added.

Merge risk: two-way door; the blast radius is the existing remote-draft browser assertions, not shipped application behavior.

Pending verification: real-Gateway attempts on Node 24.20.0 and supported Node 24.22.1 stopped at the executor's native child-process cleanup boundary before producing completed proof; the latter also reported watcher exhaustion. Auto Review aborted before producing a report. The completed independent source/diff assessment above is separate from that failed tool attempt and is not an Auto Review result. The full-spec failures above remain unresolved and predate this patch. The batched macOS proof run remains outstanding.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/22e87ec9-1af6-4e99-be52-ab7eb2c427df)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/edd39895)

prs.body:

Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.

Avoid implementation details such as:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes local model setup treating a reachable Llama app or Ollama service with no ready model like a missing service.



## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: users keep a clear **Set up** action for an idle local service instead of seeing a duplicate install suggestion. Existing model selections and manual setup remain unchanged.



## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Reuse the existing read-only availability hook independently of runnable-model discovery. Preserve only positive reachability in an optional result field, add the Llama availability hook through its existing discovery owner, and consume the fact in the real Models setup page.

This observes HTTP service reachability, not operating-system app installation. Protected or unknown responses do not establish absence. Ollama still considers resident models only; discovery does not pull or load models. No new configuration, migration, schema version, or model-facing tool.



## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

### Current provider artwork

The official artwork dependency is now included in this branch. These representative light/dark views use canonical manifest metadata through the production setup-option projector: **Llama app**, **Built-in local AI**, and **Ollama**, each with **Set up**. All three distinct masks decode and paint contrasting interior pixels. Captured source: 37a8bdb / tree bb65bb93; 2/2 browser cases, 18.30s wall time. Synthetic three-choice consumer proof, not full-catalog/live-service/native/inference proof. Views are naturally scrolled to the provider rows; no full-modal claim.

![Current provider artwork - light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a31869cd-d597-48c6-984c-619fb613ed54)

![Current provider artwork - dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4406fc1d-3e17-495f-9ae2-ae2c3add1158)

<details><summary>Matched icon regression — identical custom wire choices before/after</summary>

Before uses original 942ac7 production; After includes the official artwork dependency. The same initial Gateway fixture and supplied labels/actions are held constant. These custom-label controls are not the canonical default-copy preview above.

![Icon regression before - L fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4eda49f3-ae22-442d-ab7a-50f0b13ea897)

![Icon regression after - official Llama mark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2807184-50cc-4c59-980c-3ad20670baf1)

</details>

Earlier feature-flow images retain their original source and scenario labels below; they are not relabeled as current artwork proof.


- [Secretless real Gateway RPC qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41505187846): **1 file / 1 case passed, no skips**. The case covers idle, ready, protected, and unknown fixtures, preserves the configured model and config bytes/timestamps, and restricts requests to read-only discovery paths. Setup: **60.688 s**; RPC case: **9.388 s**, with the original **60 s** case deadline.
- Focused core, lifecycle, protocol, Llama, Ollama, and Control UI tests, targeted types/lint/format, and the browser setup-action case passed. Unchanged proof is reused, not relabeled as a new run.
- Fresh independent scoped P0–P3 source review: clean after repairing the fixture acquisition-retention finding.
- Browser captures use the same production UI with a synthetic service-fact transition; they are separate from the real Gateway RPC proof above.

- The schema-valid browser case passed: **1 case, no skips**, **3.018 s** case / **14.86 s** total. UI production types, direct fixture semantic checks, targeted lint/format and fresh scoped review passed.

- The real RPC/state-effect boundary requires one suite-owned Gateway fixture, rather than a cheaper helper-only test. CI test phase: **159.367 s** (including compilation/import); measured RPC case: **9.388 s**. prs.title: fix(gateway): let worker Goals reach COMMIT with current authority
prs.body:
Related: #191197 and #191621.

## What Problem This Solves

Worker Goal input can recurse through its own session-authorization guard before COMMIT, leaving the Goal uncommitted. Resume also loses the retained sharing handoff needed by later turns.

## User Impact

Authorized worker Goals reach COMMIT and continue after Resume. Revoked membership, changed session lifecycles, and revoked or reassigned placement claims still refuse the effect. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the committing transaction's target and membership facts authoritative throughout synchronous authorization, including source reentry, then restore the previous frame. Outside that frame, source reentry can use the existing published sharing owner without recursively checking its own writer guard. Resume forwards that owner's existing retained handle.

## Evidence

- Frozen main `ad1a025f8ac6d`: four of the five worker Goal cases fail before COMMIT, including a stack overflow and a claim-change hook that never runs.
- Two new membership/lifecycle regressions pass on main and fail against rejected candidate C because it accepts committing revocation facts using an older publication. Both pass with this repair. The five worker Goal cases also pass, including Resume/continuation and strict revoked/reassigned COMMIT claims (seven selected cases, 55.44s).
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `ad1a025f8ac6d` is scoped-clean at P0–P2 with explicit authorization focus: no stale-fact override, widened access, or lost live operator/placement check was found.
- Sharing/Goal owner tests plus the real isolated Gateway membership/tool-write revocation file pass 41/41 (98.17s). Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The new 30-line regression allocation protects transaction membership and lifecycle precedence. Net production growth: 16 lines. The initial lint finding (parameter reassignment) was corrected with a local binding, and the final exact patch received another clean authorization review.
- The Gateway uses synthetic model execution and real session/authorization/worker owners; this is not live provider or cold-process recovery proof. CI seconds and broad PR checks remain pending; production-host restrictions prohibit broad local suites.

prs.title: fix(msteams): DMs fail for users who have the app installed but never messaged the bot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Microsoft Teams DM to `user:<aad-object-id>` fails with `No conversation reference found for user:<id>` when the user has the app installed but has never messaged the bot. This also affects every DM recipient when `dmPolicy: "disabled"` drops inbound DMs before a reference is saved.

## User Impact

User impact: agents, cron jobs and `openclaw message send` can now start a DM with any user who has the Teams app installed. The user does not need to message the bot first. Channel and group chat sends are unchanged: they still need a stored reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

- When a user target has no stored reference, the send path now opens the personal chat with the Bot Connector (`POST /v3/conversations`, `isGroup: false`, tenant in both `tenantId` and `channelData`). It stores the returned reference, then sends through the existing path.
  - Teams returns the existing 1:1 chat if there is one, so this does not create a second chat.
  - The Connector URL comes from the configured `serviceUrl`; without one, from the account's stored references, then the public global endpoint. Each candidate must pass the existing cloud-boundary validator before any request, so a URL from another cloud is skipped.
  - The create request runs under the existing Connector handoff with the caller's delivery-authority assertion. Authority is checked again after token preparation and at HTTP submit, as for message sends (#151193). Opening the chat does not mark the message as dispatched.
- When the bot is added in personal scope (`conversationUpdate` `membersAdded`), the handler now saves the conversation reference with the builder that inbound messages use. `dmPolicy` gates inbound messages only, so it does not apply to this save.
- Docs for proactive messaging are updated to match.

## Evidence

- **Live Teams, real tenant, exact head.** The plugin's real outbound adapter (`msteamsOutbound.sendText`) ran in a standalone Node process with isolated state and no stored references. The production gateway was not touched. Target: an installed user whose DMs are dropped by `dmPolicy: "disabled"`. Redacted transport log:

  ```text
  === main
  RESULT_ERR No conversation reference found for user:<aad>. The bot must receive a message from this conversation before it can send proactively.
  === this branch, authority revoked while the token request is in flight
  TRANSPORT POST login.microsoftonline.com /<guid>/oauth2/v2.0/token
  RESULT_ERR delivery authority closed            (no Bot Connector request)
  === this branch, forced cloud=China with a stored public-cloud reference
  RESULT_ERR No conversation reference found for user:<aad>. ...   (no request of any kind)
  === this branch, normal send
  TRANSPORT POST login.microsoftonline.com /<guid>/oauth2/v2.0/token
  TRANSPORT POST smba.trafficmanager.net /teams/v3/conversations
  TRANSPORT POST smba.trafficmanager.net /teams/v3/conversations/a:<id>/activities
  RESULT_OK {"messageId":"1793674110857"}   stored: personal a:<id>
  ```

  A Microsoft Graph read of the user's 1:1 chat with the bot shows message `1793674110857` with the test text. The negative runs added no message.
- **Focused tests:**
  - `send-context.test.ts`:
    - a user target with no reference, through `sendMessageMSTeams`: create payload, stored reference, send to the new chat (global and stored-regional Connector URL);
    - a cross-cloud stored URL is skipped before any create;
    - authority closed during the lookup prevents the create.
  - `send.handoff.test.ts`: real Teams SDK client against a local Connector. Authority revoked during the token wait prevents the `POST /v3/conversations`; held authority submits it.
  - `monitor-handler.adaptive-card.test.ts`: realistic personal-install `conversationUpdate`. The reference is stored for personal scope, not for group chat.
  - Each new test fails when its guard is removed.
- Full msteams extension suite: 92 files, 951 tests pass. `oxfmt` and type-aware `oxlint` are clean.

Limits:
- The install-time save (`conversationUpdate`) is proven by tests only, not by a live install event.
- The host's core is 2026.10.7, so the live run used this branch's msteams plugin on the released 2026.10.7 plugin SDK.

## Merge danger

- **Mostly a two-way door.** A revert restores the old behavior completely. The only state written is ordinary conversation-reference rows in the existing msteams conversation store (no schema change). These rows are valid references and stay usable after a revert.
- **Blast radius:** Microsoft Teams only.
  - User-target sends that have no stored reference now call the Bot Connector to open a chat. For a user without the app installed, the error changes from "no conversation reference" to the Connector's own error.
  - The SDK client now loads before the reference lookup. A send to an unknown conversation now reads credentials before it fails.
  - Personal-scope installs now write a reference row.

prs.title: fix(gateway): give each utility fallback its own observer deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session observer runs its assessment call under a single abort timer (`SESSION_OBSERVER_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 s). That timer bounds everything inside `execute`: model preparation plus up to two `completeModel` attempts, and each attempt runs the configured `utilityModel.fallbacks` chain under the same `abortSignal` (`src/agents/utility-completion.ts:98-120` spreads the same request, including `timeoutMs: 30_000`, into every candidate).

So when the primary utility model uses its 30 s, the fallback starts with the signal already about to fire: the reporter measured the fallback chain stopped 7 ms after the primary's timeout with `caller_signal_aborted` and a 3 ms lane task. Two such failures in a row disable the observer for the run, and the notice tells the operator to add fallbacks that are already configured.

The fix sizes the one shared deadline by the configured candidate count: `30 s × (1 + fallbacks.length)`. Each candidate keeps its own unchanged 30 s call budget, and a single-model config (no fallbacks) keeps the exact 30 s bound it has today. No retry, model-selection, or notice wording changes.

Closes #191600

## Evidence

Red on the branch point, green after the change, on the reported scenario (one configured fallback):

```
$ node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts
 FAIL  ... > budgets one model call per configured utility candidate
AssertionError: expected true to be false
 ❯ src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts:231
    231|   expect(signal?.aborted).toBe(false);     // at 30 000 ms with a fallback configured
```

After the change, the same file, and the whole observer suite:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)

$ node scripts/test-projects.mts "src/gateway/session-observer*.test.ts"
 Test Files  14 passed (14)
      Tests  104 passed (104)
```

The existing `aborts stuck completions at the cap and disables the run after two failures` case still passes unchanged: with no fallbacks configured the deadline stays 30 s.

Checks:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check      # All matched files use the correct format
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 files>     # Found 0 warnings and 0 errors
$ node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts  # Test lines OK: 6417370; ceiling: 6417644
```

`scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` fails in this checkout with pre-existing dependency drift unrelated to this change (`@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` missing `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` missing `DirectoryMode`, and `string`→`number` mismatches in `src/cli`, `src/config/io.audit.ts`, `src/infra`). None of those diagnostics touch the two files in this PR.

## Surface area

- `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts`: a `resolveObserverDeadlineMs` helper (candidate count from `readUtilityModelSetting`) and the timer that consumes it. 13 added lines, 1 removed.
- `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts`: one regression case asserting the fallback still has time at 30 s and that the chain is still bounded at 60 s for one fallback.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/session-observer-fallback-deadline.txt`: 26 allocated test lines.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep secrets when a Gateway config save fails
prs.body:
Closes #187600 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS app writes `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` over channel tokens and the Gateway auth token in `openclaw.json` when a settings save (Browser toggle, Tailscale apply) reaches the Gateway but `config.set` times out or fails while the Gateway restarts. ## User Impact A failed Gateway save now fails visibly (Tailscale shows the error, the Browser toggle reverts to the saved value) and `openclaw.json` is left unchanged. Before, the save reported success and the next Gateway start failed with "Gateway auth token is a known redaction sentinel" until the user ran `openclaw doctor --fix` and re-paired devices. ## Why This Change Was Made `ConfigStore.save` now sends Gateway-loaded documents only to `config.set`, the owner that restores redacted values. Documents loaded while the Gateway was unreachable come from the unredacted file with no lease and keep the direct local write, unchanged by this PR.
Root cause `ConfigStore.load` builds the document from `config.get`, which redacts secrets in place (`src/config/redact-snapshot.ts`). On a save error that `permitsLocalFallback` allowed (a timeout, a dropped connection), the `catch` in `ConfigStore.save` passed that same root to `saveLocal` → `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict(preserveExistingKeys: true)`, whose merge lets every incoming leaf overwrite the file. `preserveGatewayAuthIfNeeded` protected only `gateway.auth`, and Tailscale passes `allowGatewayAuthMutation: true`. The save-time fallback dates from before #137502. Since that change a document without a Gateway lease is written locally before any Gateway call, so in production only lease-holding (redacted) documents reached the fallback. Removing it leaves `permitsLocalFallback` in use for `load`, which still falls back to the local file when `config.get` fails. Gateway-loaded documents also no longer reach the merge, so they no longer inline `$include` content or drop key removals. Saves of documents loaded offline are unchanged.
## Evidence ### Packaged macOS app, real `config.set` timeout Both builds were packaged ad hoc from this branch: `main` (with `ConfigStore.swift` from `upstream/main`) and this fix. Each ran under an isolated named profile in local mode. The profile's Gateway LaunchAgent ran a small WebSocket proxy in front of the real Gateway. The proxy forwards every frame and drops only `config.set` requests, so the app's own transport times out after 10 s. The config held test values `gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0002` and `channels.telegram.botToken = 123456:test-bot-token`. The trigger was the status-menu **Browser** button. Both runs started from the same config file. main: ``` 16:55:05.039Z [proxy] client req config.get 16:55:05.050Z [proxy] client req config.set 16:55:05.050Z [proxy] DROPPED config.set id=00C705DD-... 22:25:15 local: openclaw.json rewritten by the app channels.telegram.botToken = __OPENCLAW_REDACTED__ gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0002 (kept by preserveGatewayAuthIfNeeded; Tailscale apply passes allowGatewayAuthMutation: true and loses it too) browser.enabled = false ``` This branch: ``` 16:58:00.852Z [proxy] client req config.get 16:58:00.863Z [proxy] client req config.set 16:58:00.863Z [proxy] DROPPED config.set id=EF202F2C-... 16:58:11.390Z [proxy] client req config.get (menu reloads the saved value after the failed save) openclaw.json: byte-identical to the pre-click file (cmp), botToken = 123456:test-bot-token, browser.enabled = true ``` Screenshot of the main-build menu after the click: Browser shows off, matching the file. ### Offline editing The profile Gateway was stopped (port closed) and the Browser button clicked on each build. Neither build wrote the file: `browser.enabled` stayed `true`, and the menu showed "Cannot reach gateway at localhost:64313". The app logged repeated control-channel endpoint recovery during the save. The offline-load path is unchanged by this PR, and lease-less documents still go straight to `saveLocal`. Behavior with the Gateway down is the same before and after. ### Gateway and test evidence Isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, private `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, loopback port) seeded with `gateway.auth.token` and `channels.telegram.botToken`: - `openclaw gateway call config.get --json`: `hash` present, both secrets returned as `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`. - Control: `config.set` with that raw and `baseHash`, `browser.enabled` flipped: the file keeps both real values. - Consequence on main: `openclaw gateway run` on a file with the sentinel exits with `Gateway failed to start: Gateway auth token is a known redaction sentinel, not a credential. Run openclaw doctor --fix ...`. The new Swift test runs the real `ConfigStore.load`/`save` against a temp `openclaw.json`, with the `config.get` document shape and the transport's `gateway request timed out after 10000ms`. It fails on main (`didThrow`, `after == before`) and passes here. `ConfigStoreTests`, `OpenClawConfigFileTests`, `TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests`, `BrowserControlSettingTests`, `HealthStoreStateTests` and the StatusMenu descriptor/reconcile/width/summaries suites: 80 tests pass. `StatusMenuRecoveryPresentationTests` (a screenshot capture test) fails on a `#require` of the unset `OPENCLAW_TEST_MENU_CAPTURE_DIR`; it does not use `ConfigStore`. ### Upgrade from latest stable (2026.10.9) Built from the merged head `9069abec3c0` (version 2026.10.9; `ConfigStore.swift` and its test identical to `0e36b5c84cd`, where the runs above were taken). 1. `openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm wrote a fresh isolated profile and installed its Gateway as the profile's LaunchAgent. Config: `gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0004`, `channels.telegram.botToken = 123456:test-bot-token`, `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent = 4`, `messages.ackReactionScope = all`, `browser.enabled = true`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion = 2026.10.9`. 2. Update: stopped the 2026.10.9 service, ran this build's `openclaw doctor --fix` (pre-migration SQLite backups saved, state migrations applied), then installed the service from this build's runtime. Health ok. The upgraded app connected (operator and node). 3. Successful save, Browser button: `config.set` went through, and the Gateway logged `config hot reload applied (browser.enabled)`. The file now has `browser.enabled = false`, and the token, botToken, `maxConcurrent = 4` and `ackReactionScope = all` are unchanged. 4. Failed save, same Gateway behind the `config.set`-dropping proxy: three clicks, three `DROPPED config.set`, each followed by the menu's `config.get` about 10 s later. `openclaw.json` is byte-identical (`cmp`) to the file before the first click. Without step 2, the upgraded app first reported "Another OpenClaw process is using your data" because the old Gateway held the state database. That is the existing update sequence and not affected by this diff. Screenshot of the menu after the successful save: Browser off. Accepted edge: when the Gateway save fails, the Browser toggle reverts to the saved value without a message, as it already did for other save failures. The test replaces `local save can fall back to protected direct write when gateway is unavailable`, which asserted the removed behavior. Production delta +5/-12; test delta +33/-14. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the fallback with no state or config migration. Blast radius is macOS app saves of Gateway-loaded config in local mode when `config.set` fails.

prs.title: fix(logging): mask credentials carried in a nested URL
prs.body:
## Evidence

### CI integration follow-up (2026-11-02)

CI on `dffbb6741e85a2551cd98376ff698c0f7ffd7d18` exposed two missing consumers of the extracted encoded-query module: the explicit PR-wrapper source inventory and the recovery test VM's list of real modules. Both now include `redact-encoded-url`, so copied wrappers retain the import and recovery tests load the actual factory rather than an external-dependency stub. The authored evidence also now uses the template's required `## Evidence` heading.

The wrapper source-closure tests pass 3/3, and the update/restart module-outcome tests pass 19/19. These checks use the exact declared TypeScript, fs-safe and proc-safe versions installed in a task-private dependency directory; the shared installation and dependency pins are unchanged. The body passes the repository's external-PR context/evidence evaluator. On exact head `13a1f2ef0d27ffd987ee71a94db64a15e65b24df`, [CI job checks-node-changed-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41575096698/job/125717118397) passes, including `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` with 16 passed and 2 existing skips. The duplicate local provisioning run was stopped after that exact-head CI result became available; it is not counted as a local pass. The previously failing `checks-node-compact-small-2` also passes on that head. New CI remains required; this is not a claim that all repository gates pass.

### Whole-text follow-up (2026-11-02)

The previously documented encoded-URL gap in `redactSensitiveText` is now closed. Whole-text redaction reuses the same encoded-query matcher as line and record redaction. The default prefilter admits `%3D`, including when the credential name is entirely percent-encoded. The matcher follows non-credential callback values up to the existing nested-query depth bound, with offsets kept in the original input.

The regression covers ordinary and fully encoded credential names, one and two levels of callbacks, whole text, tool output, log lines, and log records. It also checks that disabling redaction leaves the text alone and that a non-credential query remains readable. Restoring the original production files makes it fail by exposing the synthetic credential.

`redact.test.ts` and `redact-byte-identity.test.ts` pass 59 tests in 2.53 seconds; the large-text security file passes another 4 tests. All 250 byte-identity samples and 468 recorded hash cases pass without modifying either fixture. Formatting and commit freshness checks pass. Tests ran through the repository wrapper with an isolated config that maps workspace imports to their actual source files, because the full repository config cannot load missing local dependencies. There are no parser/redactor stand-ins in this run.

Full repository lint/typecheck and a fresh real CLI run remain unverified. The lint wrapper fails while preparing package-boundary artifacts, and the full lint configuration cannot load `eslint-plugin-solid` from this machine's dependency install. A correctness-only Oxlint check passes, but is not presented as the full lint gate. CI and maintainer security approval are still required.

The shipped CLI traces below are historical evidence from the earlier revision. The new whole-text behavior is demonstrated through the public redaction APIs and regression tests above.

## What Problem This Solves

A credential inside a **nested** URL survives logging redaction. `URL_QUERY_VALUE` is `[^&#\s<>]*`, so in

```
https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>
```

the value of `cb` runs to the end of the string. `cb` is not a credential name, the nested `?token=` sits inside that value, and the `g` scan has already consumed past it. A direct `?token=<secret>` is masked correctly today — only the nested shape leaks.

The same leak has a percent-encoded form, the OAuth `redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D<secret>` shape, where the separators are `%3F`/`%26` and the `=` is `%3D`. No assignment grammar matches that, and net-policy's URL redactor (which *does* decode nested URLs) is not on this path.

Measured on `main` with a neutral sentinel — one that no value-shape rule recognises on its own:

```
redactSensitiveText("https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>")   -> secret in full
redactSensitiveLines(["GET https://x.test/?next=%3Ftoken%3D<secret>"])      -> secret in full
redactLogRecordForTransport({message: <same>})                             -> secret in full
```

## How It Was Found

A sentinel-secret fuzz over the production redaction entry points: credential-named assignments in 33 base names × 16 spelling mutations × 15 contexts, asserting the sentinel never survives, and only demanding redaction where the shared classifier itself calls the name a credential.

A methodology note, since it bit me: the first run used an `sk-`-prefixed sentinel, which openclaw's own value-shape rules mask on their own, hiding this gap. The numbers above use a neutral sentinel.

## Fix

Nesting is handled in the scanner, not in the grammar. `visitPair()` recurses into a value **only when that value's own name is not a credential**:

```ts
if (!isSensitiveBodyKey(key)) {
  if (kind !== "url" || depth >= MAX_NESTED_URL_QUERY_DEPTH || !token.includes("?")) {
    return;
  }
  const nested = new RegExp(URL_QUERY_PAIR, "gu");
  for (let match = nested.exec(token); match; match = nested.exec(token)) {
    const nestedPrefix = match[1] ?? "";
    const nestedKey = match[2] ?? "";
    visitPair(
      nestedKey,
      match[3] ?? "",
      valueOffset + match.index + nestedPrefix.length + nestedKey.length + 1,
      depth + 1,
    );
  }
  return;
}
```

A sensitive value still reaches `splitSecretValueForMask` + `maskToken` untouched, so the mask boundary of an actual credential is never recomputed. Only `?` can open a nested assignment, because `&` cannot appear inside a value. The depth bound mirrors net-policy's `MAX_NESTED_URL_REDACTION_DEPTH`, a fresh regex per level keeps `lastIndex` out of the recursion, and offsets are threaded through so existing original-offset coverage still lines up.

**`URL_QUERY_VALUE` is byte-identical to `main`.** An earlier revision of this PR narrowed it to end at `?`; that truncated the mask of a sensitive value that legitimately contains a raw `?` (`password=***?bravo`) and was correctly caught in review. The character classes are not touched any more, which is what makes this change strictly additive: every assignment `main` masks is still masked identically, because that branch is untouched.

One preparation rule covers the encoded form on the record and line paths, masking the value of an encoded assignment whose decoded name is a credential (reusing `isSensitiveBodyKey`). Both grammars are tempered rather than greedy, so the scan stays linear — 48 KB of back-to-back encoded pairs costs **10.6 ms**.

### Keeping a serialized edit inside its scalar

A log record is redacted by scanning its *serialized JSON*, and `URL_QUERY_VALUE` admits `"`, `:`, `,` and `}`. With no trailing `&` to stop it, a value runs past the closing quote of its own scalar, and the capture was applied to every token it overlapped:

```
{"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>","level":"info"}
  ->  {"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=***","***":"***"}
```

`level` is destroyed, key and value both. `src/logging/redact-json.ts` now clamps a serialized capture to the scalar it starts in:

```ts
const firstIndex = firstIntersectingToken(tokens, capture.start);
for (let index = firstIndex; index < tokens.length; index += 1) {
  …
  if (!batch && index > firstIndex) {
    break;
  }
```

The `","` between two scalars belongs to the JSON, not to any URL or form body. Line **batches** are excluded, because there the tokens are lines of one text and a capture legitimately spans several.

**This defect is not introduced by the nested scan — `main` has it today.** A top-level credential that ends the message is enough (`{"message":"https://x.test/?token=opaque-short","level":"info"}` → `"***":"***"` on `main`), and the repo's own baseline records it: 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` store `"***":"***"` where `"level":"info"` belongs, both from the *encoded form* grammar (`client%5Fsecret=`). What the nested scan changes is the reach — on `main` nested callbacks are skipped entirely, which is the leak this PR fixes — so the fix belongs on the path, not on the symptom.

## Historical evidence — shipped entry points

The real CLI, built from the earlier revision and run as a process with stdout piped. The *before* column is the same CLI with `src/logging/redact.ts` replaced by `upstream/main`'s copy and a forced rebuild; nothing else differs. Synthetic credential `nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij`, hosts under the reserved `.test` TLD.

**Gateway log tail** (`openclaw logs --limit 200 --plain`, reading the configured file log):

```
# main
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3Dnested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2

# this head
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=***&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D***&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2
```

**Plain console output** (`openclaw config validate` echoes a rejected value as `got: "<value>"` through `console.error` → `redactSensitiveText`):

| case | `main` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| nested, plain | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij` | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested…ghij` |
| nested, percent-encoded | leaks | **unchanged — still leaks** |
| top level | `?access_token=nested…ghij` | `?access_token=nested…ghij` |

The top-level row is the control: `main` already masks it, so redaction was running over these lines before this PR. The only thing that changes is nesting. The masked nested value takes `maskToken`'s own partial `nested…ghij` shape, identical to the top-level shape for the same value.

## Encoded whole-text gap

The gap described in the earlier console table is fixed by the follow-up above. That table remains historical evidence of the previous revision rather than a result from the current head.

## Earlier checks (Node 24)

```
src/logging/redact.test.ts                 -> 58 passed
src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts   -> 3 passed
src/logging (whole directory, 64 files)    -> 716 of 716 passed, 0 failures
oxlint, oxfmt --check on the changed files -> clean
run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json         -> exit 0
```

**Recorded-corpus changes, stated explicitly:** 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` are re-recorded, because they had stored `"***":"***"` in place of `"level":"info"` — the corruption described above. Their masked `message` bytes are **byte-identical**; only the clobbered sibling field is restored. The other 248 entries and all 468 `redact-prefilter-fixture.json` hashes are untouched, verified by replaying all 250 samples and confirming exactly 2 differ and both only in that field. The reason is recorded in a comment in the test file so the deviation from "byte-identical to the pre-fix implementation" is not silent.

New cases: the two `?password=alpha?bravo` regressions, a top-level/nested mask-parity assertion, the plain nested URL through the whole-text path, a nested URL with no credential staying byte-for-byte readable, the percent-encoded nested query through the line-batch path, and a record-path case asserting that a mask with no trailing `&` leaves its sibling fields intact (red on base: `expected undefined to be 'info'`).

Companion PR: #176526 fixes the same class of leak in `packages/net-policy` (URL redactor, nested URL behind leading text). The two are independent — this path does not call that redactor.

This touches a security-sensitive file, so it will need a maintainer `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve Talk operator identity across invocation guards
prs.body:
Related: #191197. Replaces the rejected source-identity approach in #191616.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat-backed Talk consultations lose the original operator source identity when session authorization adds an invocation guard.

## User Impact

Talk keeps the authenticated operator identity while independent invocations retain separate authorization and revocation. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate canonical source comparison from invocation ownership. Keep invocation ownership in queued-input keys, narrowed authority copies, and subagent completion cohorts so one invocation cannot substitute for another.

## Evidence

- Frozen main `ad1a025f8ac6d`: real Gateway Talk RPC source parity and the extended operator regression fail at source comparison. With the repair, the named Talk/capture/reconnect/reply/admitted suites pass 112 tests in 119.20s.
- Final operator-role, queue-authority, prefix-stability and self-hold files pass 78 tests in 65.60s. Completion custody passes 67 tests in 70.73s, including distinct invocation owners in both mixed and cancellation-only cohorts. The mixed regression failed against the first candidate before its completion comparison was repaired.
- Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. New regression allocation: 34 lines to protect canonical identity, independent keys and completion custody. Net production growth: 11 lines.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `ad1a025f8ac6d` is scoped-clean at P0–P2 with an explicit authorization focus. Its initial P1 completion-batching finding was fixed and reviewed again. No accepted findings remain.
- Tests use synthetic execution with real Gateway/session/authority owners; this is not live voice-provider proof. The named Talk file exceeds 30 seconds because it exercises isolated Gateway RPC and SQLite custody. CI seconds and broad PR checks are pending; production-host restrictions prohibit broad local suites.

prs.title: fix(install): npx openclaw exits 1 with no message on an unsupported Node
prs.body:
Closes #191546
Related: #185966

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `npx openclaw` exits 1 with no explanation when Node is below the package's floor.

## User Impact

User impact: someone trying OpenClaw through `npx` on an old Node sees which Node versions are supported and where to get one. The command still exits 1.

This applies only under `npx`, meaning `npm_command=exec`. `npm install -g`, updates and every other install path keep the preinstall rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

`npm exec` hides lifecycle output and the failure itself, so the preinstall message never reaches the user. An `npx` install is a throwaway copy that replaces no working release, so when `npm_command` is `exec`, and only then, the preinstall script lets it finish. The launcher then reports the runtime through its existing check, and tries its existing Node recovery first.

**This is a workaround for npm hiding script failures, not a fix for that behavior.** It depends on npm setting `npm_command=exec`. A runner that sets anything else gets no change: if it hides script output too, its failure stays silent.

## Evidence

Node 22.22.0 in a clean macOS VM. First block: unpatched 2026.10.9 prints nothing. Second block: the same release with this branch's preinstall script and its imports prints the requirement.

![npx before and after on Node 22.22.0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7152757-4a67-47cc-a498-33a91accd2f5)

Tests: `test/scripts/preinstall-package-manager-warning.test.ts` passes 37 of 37. Without the fix, 1 of 37 fails on the `npm_command=exec` case. The same test keeps asserting exit 1 for a plain install.

Not tested:

- `pnpm dlx`, `yarn dlx` and `bunx`.
- An `npx` run of a package built from this branch. The live run used the published 2026.10.9 package with the changed script swapped in.
- Node versions below 22.22.0, Windows and Linux.
- The launcher's private runtime install offer on an interactive terminal.
- Typecheck was not run, and `oxlint` crashed on the linked dependencies used for local testing. Local review and CI have not run.

prs.title: fix(update): repair loops on its own error when a crashed update also left a pending package step
prs.body:
Closes #184893

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` fails with "Another update executor owns this installation ... run `openclaw update repair` to settle it", and every later update stays blocked, when a cancelled updater exited while a package update step it had prepared was still pending.

## User Impact

Repair now settles both leftovers in one run: the unused package preparation closes as `publication-not-started` (the installed package and launchers stay unchanged), the cancelled update custody is released, and the next `openclaw update` is admitted. Before, repair told the user to run repair, and every repair refused the same way.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repair settled the pending package step first, and that settlement asked for fresh update admission. The cancelled custody refuses fresh admission by design, and repair only replaces that custody with its own claim in a later step, so it never got there.

Repair now takes its claim first and settles the package step under it. Finalization already runs repair's maintenance under the same claim, so this adds no new authority. Settlement keeps its own executor admission when no claim is held (ordinary repair with no leftover custody, and the update command's own settlement).

Scope of the claim: repair holds it for both kinds of leftover lock it settles, the cancelled custody of a crashed updater (lease version 4) and an older dead owner it reclaims (version 2 triage or legacy update child). A dead triage owner refuses fresh admission the same way (existing test "repair reclaims a root handoff owner"), so a pending package step settles under the claim there too. Legacy update children go through the same path but are not separately tested, and no test combines either older kind with a pending package step.

Known edge: an earlier macOS Gateway keeps its own lease store. When the custody sits there, repair's claim lives in that store rather than the one the package step recorded; settlement still checks the recorded lease database identity, and admission in the current store stays fenced by the earlier store's check (#185002). Low risk, not separately tested.

Unchanged: when the custody cannot be settled yet (its updater or descendants still live, or the grace period has not passed), repair still refuses as before; the next repair settles both once the custody is free.

## Evidence

<!-- t2-custody-verification:start -->
**Takeover verification — head `02846bc0f286d9579ea48c8fb78229d8c9c50660`, rebased onto `95fa337a11e90a2f6882b6489664992a66ae28b6`.** All three contributor commits retain Sukhdeep Johar as author. No additional source changes were needed after source review, simplification, and independent review.

- **Red on pinned main:** the two changed regression files produce exactly 3 failures and 12 passes. Combined repair repeats the retained-v4 custody refusal; both lost-claim rows reach reporting instead of refusing. Runner wall time: 127.27s.
- **Green on rebased head:** all 380 tests pass across 21 focused files, including the six repair/recovery files (115 tests, 248.48s runner wall time) and all remaining consumers of the changed lifetime fixture plus repair siblings (265 tests, 311.70s).
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted repository oxlint, oxfmt on all six changed files, and `git diff --check` pass. The changed cancellation file takes 82.95s of test time (the combined regression is 12.58s); it proves real SIGKILL/process identity, SQLite custody and registered CLI recovery that a cheaper helper test cannot establish. The retirement file takes 3.72s. Net test/fixture lines remain zero. CI-specific timing for these files was not collected.
- **Isolation:** fresh secretless Crabbox AWS lease; no hydration, instance role, or Tailscale. IMDSv2 credentials endpoint returned 404 before code execution; full head SHA verified; HOME/state isolated under private `/tmp`. [Red/green and checks run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3978dcd3363aaf533c32764f81987a84), [fixture consumers and repair siblings](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0ec894ccbcf7213a5c39f9e38b244118). Initial baseline setup failed before tests because a shared root dependency link omitted plugin-local packages; installing its unchanged frozen dependencies resolved setup.
- **Independent review:** Codex autoreview of the complete rebased range `95fa337a11e..02846bc0f28`, with unchanged repair, executor, publication, and authority owner context, is `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 with no findings. This was static review.
- **CI:** [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41068168212) is attached and **red** in [PostgreSQL conformance (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41068168212/job/124106104307). The same test (`whole-archive PostgreSQL restore`, captured config alias case), `ConfigMutationConflictError: included config target changed since last load`, and `src/config/io.write-safety.ts:76` stack also fail in [scheduled main run 41063477930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41063477930/job/124089262163). Those backup/config paths are unchanged here. The failure classifier initially matched only the job name; the test/error/stack comparison above independently confirms the inherited failure. CI is now terminal with only this root failure and its aggregate failed; other applicable jobs passed. The T2 continuation explicitly authorizes the supported native inherited-failure exception for this exact head. The recorded CI remains red; no CI rerun was requested.

The installed-package and stable-upgrade evidence below is the contributor's supplied prior-head evidence; those campaigns were not independently repeated in this takeover. Independent current-head proof exercised the registered CLI and its real process/SQLite recovery boundary. No schema, config, protocol, public SDK, dependency, or changelog changes.
<!-- t2-custody-verification:end -->

**Regression through the registered `openclaw update repair` CLI**, `update-repair-cancellation.test.ts` "repair settles cancelled custody together with an unused package preparation". A real updater process prepares the package step, cancels, and dies by SIGKILL (the existing crash fixture), leaving a version 4 lease family of 4 rows and a `prepared` journal. The only synthetic piece is the inert sealed helper the journal records, as in the existing package activation tests.

- On `main` (b0966db1204): repair exits 1 with "Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner …, lease version 4, …). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it."; all 4 custody rows remain; the next admission is refused the same way.
- With this change: repair exits 0 (`status: "ok"`), reports "previous package update operation … closed as publication-not-started. The original package and launchers remain unchanged.", leaves 0 custody rows and no pending package step, and the next admission succeeds.
- The 6 existing cases in that file pass on both, including the failed and deferred repair cases that keep the claim.

**A lost claim changes nothing.** `package-update-activation-retirement.test.ts` "preserves damaged unused helper|candidate while settling an unpublished preparation" now first settles under a repair claim whose check throws: settlement rejects with that error before any report (the case's later call count proves none ran), and the journal stays `prepared`; the ordinary settlement then proceeds as before. On `main` the claim is ignored and settlement proceeds, so both rows fail.

**Bench run (isolated container with an init process, main `b0966db1204` vs this head):** the two changed test files give main 3 failures, exactly the new checks (both lost-claim rows and the combined repair case), and this change 15/15. Without an init process the container's first shell does not reap the SIGKILLed test updater, so repair sees "Handoff descendants remain live or unverified" and the existing crash cases fail on both refs alike; that is a property of the container, not of this change.

**Checks.** The 48 test files that import the repair command or package activation pass (702 tests); `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files. Net test lines against the merge base: 0. The repeated retained-custody and settled-custody report checks in `update-repair-cancellation.test.ts` moved into two helpers, the earlier-Gateway store setup into a third, and the inert sealed-helper mock is now exported from the activation lifetime fixture; every assertion is kept. Re-proof after the consolidation on the bench (one tree at a time, init process): `main` fails exactly the 3 new checks (both lost-claim rows and the combined repair case, for the bug's reasons), this branch 15/15; on the Mac the 15 test files that use the changed fixture pass except 5 pre-existing child-process cases in `package-update-activation-lifetime.test.ts` that need a built sealed helper and fail the same way on the previous head.

**Live proof with a real installed package** (isolated bench, Debian container with an init process, Node 26). Both refs were packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (`main` at 6bd45e1ba98, and this branch at 2eec3e631d5 merged onto it; the later commit 1fb2a67ded6 changes test files only), installed with npm, and updated with `openclaw update --tag <newer local package> --timeout 1800`. The update ran under libfaketime with a timestamp file. The moment its package activation journal reached `prepared`, the clock was advanced by 1800 s, so the update's own deadline expired inside the step between preparation and publication (where a real install stops and drains the Gateway; in the container that step takes well under a second, which is why the clock had to move). The real deadline cancelled the update: "Package activation was refused and its prepared publication could not be retired. | Update activation exceeded its 1799-second budget." It recorded cancelled custody (lease version 4) while the journal stayed `prepared`, and a watcher sent SIGKILL the instant that row appeared, like a crash during cancellation cleanup. State after the crash on every lane: 1 custody row (version 4), journal `prepared`, no leftover or zombie processes. Later commands ran on the same advanced clock: +31 min for the next update, +80 min for repair and the final update, past the 45-minute custody grace. Repair's process census refuses inside a detected container by design ("Host process visibility cannot be established from this container"), so each lane removed the Docker marker before starting; the install's processes all live in that container's own PID namespace, which shares nothing.

- On `main` (3 lanes, all alike): next update exit 1, "Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner …, lease version 4, …). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it."; repair exit 1 with that same message, twice; the custody row and the pending package step remain; the final update exit 1 with the same message. That is the reported loop.
- With this change (1 lane): next update exit 1 with the same refusal (unchanged); repair exit 0 and "previous package update operation … closed as publication-not-started. The original package and launchers remain unchanged."; afterwards 0 custody rows and no pending package step; a second repair exit 0; the final update exit 0 and installed the newer package.
- Boundary, with this change and without the kill (1 lane): the same cancelled update, left to exit on its own, released its custody itself ("Cancellation settled before recovery"; 0 rows, journal `prepared`), and the next update recovered the package step and finished (exit 0). The loop needs the updater to die after recording its cancellation, which is the crashed updater the issue describes.
- Not counted: in rounds of six lanes at once, some updates stalled at the candidate Gateway start-up check before reaching the package step and never produced the state; the three-lane `main` round had no stalls.

Earlier live attempts, for the record: a plain kill (TERM, then KILL) at `prepared` never records cancelled custody; the next update reclaims the dead owner and recovers the package step on both refs. Only the deadline writes cancelled custody. Git-checkout installs do not create a package step, so they cannot reach this path.

### Live run

Captured lane summaries (timestamps are the bench's real clock; `<prefix>` is the npm prefix of the install). `main`:

```
[20:49:04] installed version 2026.10.8 -> target 2026.10.9
2026-10-28T20:52:49.642Z phase prepared
2026-10-28T20:52:49.642Z clock jumped +1800
[20:52:49] cancelled custody recorded 180s after start; update killed: {"key":"<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw","rows":1}
[20:52:51] update exit 137
[20:52:51] lease rows after crash: [{"root":"<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw","version":4}]
[20:52:51] journal phase after crash: [{"phase":"prepared"}]
[20:52:53] next update exit 1
Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner c78f50d7-12f7-4664-924c-24f40c42b100, lease version 4, last activity 2026-10-28T21:22:49.661Z). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it.
[20:52:56] repair 1 exit 1
Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner c78f50d7-12f7-4664-924c-24f40c42b100, lease version 4, last activity 2026-10-28T21:22:49.661Z). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it.
[20:52:58] repair 2 exit 1
Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner c78f50d7-12f7-4664-924c-24f40c42b100, lease version 4, last activity 2026-10-28T21:22:49.661Z). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it.
[20:52:58] lease rows after repair: [{"root":"<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw","version":4}]
[20:52:58] pending journal after repair: 1
[20:53:00] final update exit 1
Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner c78f50d7-12f7-4664-924c-24f40c42b100, lease version 4, last activity 2026-10-28T21:22:49.661Z). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it.
[20:53:00] installed version now: OpenClaw 2026.10.8
```

With this change:

```
[20:24:50] installed version 2026.10.8 -> target 2026.10.9
2026-10-28T20:31:20.878Z phase prepared
2026-10-28T20:31:20.878Z clock jumped +1800
[20:31:20] cancelled custody recorded 318s after start; update killed: {"key":"<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw","rows":1}
[20:31:23] update exit 137
Package activation was refused and its prepared publication could not be retired. | Update activation exceeded its 1799.779133255-second budget.
[20:31:23] lease rows after crash: [{"root":"<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw","version":4}]
[20:31:23] journal phase after crash: [{"phase":"prepared"}]
[20:31:25] next update exit 1
Another update executor owns this installation. It retains cancelled update custody (owner 2c3812d9-6faa-4ea5-a6ad-aee53724c049, lease version 4, last activity 2026-10-28T21:01:20.905Z). If that update has exited, run openclaw update repair to settle it.
[20:36:51] repair 1 exit 0
"status": "ok"
closed as publication-not-started
[20:38:09] repair 2 exit 0
[20:38:09] lease rows after repair: []
[20:38:09] pending journal after repair: 0
[20:45:13] final update exit 0
[20:45:13] installed version now: OpenClaw 2026.10.9
```

### Upgrade from the latest stable release with existing settings and data

Stored data: this change touches no schema, journal, lease row, report or config format. It changes the order of two steps in repair and adds an in-process `owner` option to settlement; everything written to disk is written by the same code as before.

Run (same bench, 2 lanes alike): the published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (npm `latest`, build dc2523e) was installed from the registry, given a config with user settings (`plugins.enabled=false`, `update.channel=stable`, `agents.defaults.model`, `gateway.port`) and a workspace file, then updated to this branch's package (2026.10.9) with `openclaw update --tag <local package>`; `openclaw update repair` ran twice on the upgraded install; a final `openclaw update` ran; then the data was checked.

```
[21:02:29] openclaw --version: OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) (installed from openclaw@2026.10.8)
[21:02:32] config validate before update exit 0
[21:09:40] next update exit 0
[21:10:42] repair 1 exit 0
[21:11:42] repair 2 exit 0
[21:11:42] pending journal after repair: 0
[21:13:04] final update exit 0
[21:13:04] installed version now: OpenClaw 2026.10.9
[21:13:06] config validate after exit 0
[21:13:07] workspace seed readable: seeded before update 2026-10-28T21:02:29
[21:13:07] state files after: 16; missing from before: 0
```

prs.title: fix(telegram): message effects are silently dropped when effectId is set
prs.body:
Closes #191644

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram messages arrive without the requested animation, and without any error, when the agent sends them with `effectId`.

## User Impact

User impact: in a private chat, `message` send with a numeric `effectId` (for example `5104841245755180586`, 🔥) now plays that Telegram message effect once, on the first message of the send: text, rich, media, album, or location. A send with `effectId` to a group, supergroup, channel or `@username` target now fails before anything is sent. So does a non-numeric value such as an iMessage effect name. In both cases the error says how to fix the call. Sends without `effectId` are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared message tool advertises `effectId` / `effect` on every send. The Telegram send action and the prepared presentation/location path never read it, and nothing in the plugin set Bot API `message_effect_id`.

The change validates the value once at the action boundary: it must be a numeric id, and the target must be a private chat. The value then rides in `channelData.telegram` to the Telegram send owner, which applies it. It stays on every attempt until Telegram accepts the first message, shared fallbacks included: rich to plain, quote, caption, photo to document, album to single photos, voice to text. Follow-up chunks and album items don't repeat it. The send owner checks the resolved chat id again, so a payload from another producer can't send the field to a group. The streaming reply funnel doesn't take effects, so no recovery predicate changes, and both funnels still degrade the same way.

Effects ride on `send` rather than on the iMessage-style `sendWithEffect` action because Telegram accepts them on every content type, not only text.

Not included:
- A name-to-id map. The Bot API has no method to list effects, and community lists disagree on some ids (❤️).
- Effects on the `sticker` and `poll` actions, which still ignore `effectId`.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests, red on `main`, green with the fix.**
  - `extensions/telegram/src/send.message-effect.telegram-http.test.ts` (new) drives the registered Telegram send action, the prepared presentation and location routes, and a direct payload over the real HTTP Bot API fixture:
    - private text: `sendMessage` gets `message_effect_id`
    - private media with caption overflow: `sendPhoto` gets it, the follow-up `sendMessage` doesn't
    - rich account with a `RICH_MESSAGE_URL_INVALID` 400: both `sendRichMessage` and the plain fallback `sendMessage` get it
    - prepared presentation: `sendMessage` gets it
    - prepared location: `sendLocation` gets it
    - group payload from another producer (negative control): no `message_effect_id`, and the send still succeeds
  - `action-runtime.test.ts`, "rejects invalid external send input before network delivery": two new rows, `effectId: "confetti"` and a group target (`-1001`) with a numeric id. Both reject, and no HTTP request is made.
  - `channel-actions.contract.test.ts`: the prepared path rejects `effectId` for `-1001`, `-1001:topic:42` and `@somechannel` targets before delivery.
- **Red runs.**
  - All three test files against `main`'s production code (`5b482e2d3e4c`): `action-runtime.test.ts` 2 failed / 38 (both rows: the send resolves instead of rejecting). HTTP and contract files 8 failed / 21: the five private HTTP cases get `message_effect_id: undefined`, and the three contract rows resolve. The group-producer case passes on `main`, as it should.
  - The second commit's rows against the first commit's code: 1 failed / 38 in `action-runtime.test.ts` and 3 failed / 15 in `channel-actions.contract.test.ts`, each because the promise resolved instead of rejecting.
  - Negative control: turning off the send-owner chat check fails only the group-producer case (`message_effect_id: "5104841245755180586"` reaches `sendMessage`), 1 failed / 6.
- **Green runs on the branch head.** `action-runtime.test.ts` 38/38. `send.message-effect.telegram-http.test.ts` with `channel-actions.contract.test.ts` 21/21. `action-runtime.test.ts` runs under `test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`, where it is routed; the Telegram config doesn't pick it up. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed files, and the pre-commit hook passed on the head commit.
- **Live** (not run yet; to be filled in before leaving draft). The same change runs on a 2026.10.9 gateway as a local patch, in a private chat with the bot:
  - a text send with `effectId=5104841245755180586`;
  - the same send to a private-chat topic target (`<chat>:topic:<id>`);
  - a presentation or media send.

  Proof will be the effect in the client and `effect_id` / `message.effect` on the delivered message. Negative control: a send with `effectId` to a negative chat id or an `@username` target returns the private-chat error and makes no Bot API request.
- **Gaps.**
  - Full `tsgo`, `pnpm check:changed` and the full extension lane weren't run locally because of host memory limits; PR CI runs them.
  - The Telegram Test Server e2e (`.agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot`) wasn't run because its shared credentials aren't available to me.
  - Whether clients render effects in private-chat topics isn't documented by the Bot API; the live check above covers it.

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(agents): cache drop warnings blame max_completion_tokens when only the output cap changed
prs.body:
Closes #191648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped` warnings blame `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens` when the prompt prefix is unchanged and only the per-request output cap moved.

## User Impact

User impact: on Chat Completions routes, a cache drop with an unchanged prompt prefix now reads `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix` with `providerPrefix=prefix-match`, so the warning points at the provider instead of an OpenClaw request change that did not happen. Prompt, tool, message and other parameter changes are still attributed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Chat Completions transport clamps `max_completion_tokens` (or `max_tokens`) to the remaining context budget on most requests (`openai-completions-params.ts:511`). `describeProviderPrefix()` compared every tracked request parameter, so the cap alone turned `prefix-match` into `parameters:max_completion_tokens`. An output cap bounds the completion; it does not change the prompt tokens a prefix cache keys on.

The parameter comparison now leaves out `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`:
- A cap-only change keeps `prefix-match`.
- When something else changed as well, the warning names only that: `parameters:temperature`, or `system`.

`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md` and `docs/logging.md` say so.

Accepted edge case: if the cap changed and the only other difference is the JSON key order of the remaining parameters, the `order` signal is not reported.

## Evidence

- Production (details in #191648): on two hosts running a 2026.10.10-beta.5 based build, all 66 and all 83 drops labeled `parameters:max_completion_tokens` had equal `prefixHash` and `routeHash`. 35 and 17 of them went to 0 cached tokens.
- Unit: one new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` with 5 cases:
  - `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` alone -> unchanged prefix.
  - Cap plus `temperature` -> `parameters:temperature`.
  - Cap plus changed instructions -> `system`.
  - On base `19aff5bfd42` all 5 fail. The received values are `provider-input-change:parameters:max_tokens`, `...:max_completion_tokens`, `...:max_output_tokens`, `parameters:temperature+max_completion_tokens` and `system,parameters:max_completion_tokens`. With the fix the file passes 22/22.
- Consumers: 14 test files that use the observer pass (276 tests).
- End to end: an isolated `openclaw agent --local` turn against a scripted local Chat Completions server. Request 1 makes a tool call with 22560 cached tokens; request 2 reports 0. The bodies differ only by the two appended messages and `max_completion_tokens` (44468 -> 41385).
  - Base build: `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens ... providerPrefix=parameters:max_completion_tokens`
  - This branch: `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix ... providerPrefix=prefix-match`
- Checks:
  - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files pass.
  - The line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass against the base (test-line slack 410, no allocation needed).
  - The new cases run in 1-2 ms each. The file takes 52.9 s with `--maxWorkers=1`, mostly the existing retention test and transform.
- Not covered: a live provider run. The qa-lab mock serves only Responses and Messages and reports no cached tokens, so it cannot produce a cache drop.

prs.title: fix(telegram): disabled buttons render as active and stay clickable
prs.body:
Closes #191645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram button marked `disabled: true` stays clickable when it is sent through the `message` tool's `edit` action or in a reply payload delivered through the Telegram reply dispatcher, and turns into an `Actions:` text line instead of a button on core presentation delivery.

## User Impact

User impact: agents and plugins can show inert buttons on Telegram, for example "✓ Selected" after a choice or an action that is temporarily unavailable. The label stays in the keyboard, tapping it does nothing, and no callback reaches the agent or plugin. On core presentation sends, a disabled button now appears in the keyboard instead of as an `Actions:` line in the message text. Buttons without `disabled`, or with `disabled: false`, are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram Bot API 10.3 added a native disabled inline button (`InlineKeyboardButton.disabled`). The Telegram renderer now maps `disabled: true` to that button type instead of a callback, URL or Mini App button, so no `callback_data` is sent for it. Telegram also advertises `supportsDisabled`, so core presentation adaptation keeps disabled buttons as native controls, per the presentation contract in `docs/plugins/message-presentation.md` (Discord does the same since #84312). The disabled branch runs after action validation, so a disabled button still needs a valid action, as the normalizer already requires.

Accepted edge cases:
- A disabled button whose action Telegram could not encode (callback data over 64 bytes, a Mini App button outside a private chat) now renders as a disabled button instead of a text line; it never sends anything, so there is nothing left to encode.
- A control-only reply whose buttons are all disabled keeps the existing "Choose an option." anchor text.
- In a managed multi-select keyboard, the toggle re-render keeps only callback buttons, so a disabled button disappears after the first toggle, as URL buttons already do.
- Telegram does not document how clients that predate disabled buttons render them; with no `callback_data`, a tap cannot produce a callback on any client.

## Evidence

- Regression test at the Bot API HTTP boundary (`outbound-adapter.telegram-http.test.ts`, "keeps disabled presentation buttons visible and inert on action send, edit, and payload send"): one keyboard with an active button (`disabled: false`, negative control) and a disabled one, sent through the Telegram `send` action, the markup-only `edit` action, and the registered payload send.
  - Before the fix (base 5b482e2d3e4c): `send` and `edit` emitted `{"text":"✓ Staging","callback_data":"env|staging"}`; the payload send dropped the button from `reply_markup` and put `✓ Staging` in the text.
  - After the fix: all three emit `[{"text":"Deploy","callback_data":"env|prod"},{"text":"✓ Staging","disabled":{}}]` and the label is not repeated in the text.
- Focused tests on aaf0d4bb315c: `outbound-adapter.telegram-http.test.ts` 35 passed, `action-runtime.test.ts` 36 passed (both in the `extension-database-workers` project), `lane-delivery.presentation.test.ts` + `button-types.test.ts` + `interactive-fallback.test.ts` 45 passed.
- `lane-delivery.presentation.test.ts`: the streamed-final case from #155088 ("unsupported control labels remain present exactly once") used a disabled button as its example of a control Telegram cannot render. Telegram renders it now, so the case uses an over-limit callback instead, which Telegram still cannot encode; the assertions are unchanged.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` on touched files and `git diff --check`: clean. A full typecheck was not run locally; CI covers it.
- Live Telegram client check: _to be added. Before/after screenshots of the keyboard, a tap on the disabled button producing no callback or agent turn, and an `edit` with a styled disabled button accepted by the Bot API._
- Gap: the Telegram Test Server e2e skill (`.agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot`) was not available to me. The reply-dispatcher path is covered through the shared button renderer, not end to end.
- Related: #169504 touches the same files for typed callback ownership; the only overlap is an adjacent line in `docs/channels/telegram/rich-messages.md`.
