prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: feat(onboarding): keep the Gateway running after Quick Start
prs.body: Closes #191453 ## What Problem This Solves Quick start runs the Gateway only in the foreground of the onboarding terminal. Closing that terminal stops the agent, and the dashboard shows "Reconnecting…". ## Why This Change Was Made - Quick start asks **Keep OpenClaw running in the background?** (default yes) after inference is verified. Yes installs the service through the existing setup path and opens the dashboard. No keeps the foreground Gateway. - The question is skipped where a service would not last or cannot be managed, and the Gateway stays in the foreground: - Temporary runs: `npx`, `pnpm dlx`, or anything under the temp directory. A service pointing into those copies breaks when they are evicted, which is why Quick start was foreground-only (#134221). - Hosts the installer refuses: Nix mode, a non-default install identity, an external supervisor. - Platforms with no service manager, and Linux without user systemd. ## User Impact - Fresh interactive onboarding from a durable install keeps its agent after the terminal closes, and the service starts at login. This is default-on. - `npx openclaw@latest` behaves as it did. Custom setup and non-interactive onboarding are unchanged. - Docs that described Quick start as foreground-only match the new flow. ## Known limits - `npx` users do not get the background service from Quick start. Giving them one needs a durable install, as `resolveDurableNodeEntrypoint` does for the node host. That is a follow-up. - The same `_npx` risk exists on paths this PR does not touch: `npx` plus Custom setup, classic Quick start, and `npx openclaw gateway install`. - If the service fails or is not reachable in time, Quick start uses the Custom setup failure path (error note, then setup chat) and does not host a foreground Gateway. `setup-apply` reports both as `failed`, and a foreground Gateway would collide with a service that is still starting. Setup stays resumable. - On Linux, accepting can reach the existing linger step, which may ask for sudo under the progress spinner. Custom setup behaves the same. On timeout, setup reports the manual command and installs the service. ## Evidence macOS 26.6 VM, real `openclaw onboard` from a packed build of this commit, with a local stub OpenAI-compatible model and a made-up key. `@openclaw/ai` was overlaid from the same commit because the published package is older. Global install: the question appears after inference is verified. Accepting installs the LaunchAgent and reports the Gateway running. The dashboard opens. After Terminal quit, the Gateway kept the same pid and the dashboard returned 200. A real `npx` run from the npm exec cache skips the question and installs no service. The foreground Gateway served the dashboard. Tests: 56 passed across guided onboarding, the new gate test, wizard locale parity, and service setup. The Quick start and gate regressions fail without the production change. `pnpm tsgo:core` and format passed. Not run: Linux and Windows service install, `pnpm dlx` and `bunx` onboarding end to end, answering No in the VM.

## What Problem This Solves

Ollama only refused the exact hostname `metadata.google.internal`. A configured base URL such as `http://169.254.169.254` still built an SSRF policy with `allowPrivateNetwork: true` and sent `Authorization: Bearer`. Private LAN and loopback addresses stay allowed.

## Evidence

On this branch, `buildOllamaBaseUrlSsrFPolicy` returns no policy for metadata names, link-local addresses, and the cloud metadata addresses `100.100.100.200` and `fd00:ec2::254`. `127.0.0.1` and `192.168.1.10` still pin to that hostname with private network access.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/provider-models.test.ts -t "buildOllamaBaseUrlSsrFPolicy"
 ✓ rejects empty, invalid, metadata, or link-local base URL http://169.254.169.254 1ms
```

prs.title: fix(lsp): keep unconfirmed session cleanup discoverable for later sweeps
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #190989: `disposeSession()` cached a rejected disposal promise and unconditionally removed the session from the global `activeBundleLspSessions` registry in `finally`. When `closeOwnedStdioProcess()` could not confirm descendant extinction, the rejected promise stayed cached (every later `disposeSession()` returned the same rejection without retrying) and the session was dropped from the global set — so a subsequent `disposeAllBundleLspRuntimes()` sweep visited nothing and reported a clean close, while the process tree may still have been alive.

## Root cause

`src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`:

- `disposeSession()` stores the disposal promise in `session.disposal`. A rejected promise is cached, so later disposes return the same rejection instead of retrying.
- The `finally` block unconditionally ran `activeBundleLspSessions.delete(session)`, even when `closeOwnedStdioProcess()` threw (extinction not confirmed).
- `disposeAllBundleLspRuntimes()` only visits `activeBundleLspSessions`, so a failed session became invisible to later global sweeps. `disposeSessions()` uses `Promise.allSettled()` and only records a cleanup-failure counter, so the caller saw a resolved `dispose()`.

## Fix

Only remove a session from the active registry when its process-tree shutdown was **confirmed**:

```ts
let cleanupConfirmed = false;
try {
  await closeOwnedStdioProcess(session.process, {...});
  cleanupConfirmed = true;
} catch (error) {
  recordAgentCleanupFailure();
  logWarn(...);
  throw error;
} finally {
  if (cleanupConfirmed) {
    activeBundleLspSessions.delete(session);
  }
}
```

A session whose cleanup could not be confirmed stays visible so later global sweeps observe the uncertainty through the existing cleanup contract (`recordAgentCleanupFailure` → `createAgentCleanupScope().outcome === "uncertain"`). The cached disposal promise still prevents blindly re-running a terminal process owner — no stale-owner signaling, no duplicate `dispose()` calls on the process adapter.

## Evidence

### Before (red, on base)

New regression `keeps failed cleanup discoverable for a later global sweep` fails on current main:

```
expected 'closed' to be 'uncertain'
```

A runtime disposal that cannot confirm extinction reports `uncertain` through its own scope, but the subsequent global sweep sees no session and reports `closed` — the process tree may still be alive while the sweep silently drops it.

### After (green, on this branch)

- `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts` — 22 passed (incl. the new regression: first scope `uncertain`, then the global sweep also `uncertain`, `child.dispose` called exactly once)
- `src/agents/run-cleanup-timeout.test.ts` — 4 passed

### Successful cleanup still closes and removes

The existing suite (`closes retained and pending requests while joining repeated descendant cleanup`, `records uncertain cleanup without descendant settlement`) still passes: confirmed cleanup deletes the session as before, `child.dispose` stays at one call.

## Shipped-entry-point proof (real global sweep)

Driven through the production entry points (`createBundleLspToolRuntime` → `disposeAllBundleLspRuntimes` → real `createAgentCleanupScope` receipt), with an LSP child injected at the real `createOwnedStdioProcess` boundary that completes the `initialize` handshake but rejects `waitForExtinction` — the same failure shape `closeOwnedStdioProcess()` throws when descendant extinction cannot be certified. Terminal output:

```
== shipped-entry LSP cleanup proof ==
1. creating bundle LSP runtime through the production entry point
   -> spawned LSP session, exposed tools: 0
2. after runtime.dispose(): first cleanup scope outcome = uncertain
3. after disposeAllBundleLspRuntimes(): sweep scope outcome = uncertain
4. retired process adapter dispose() calls = 1
== end proof ==
```

This shows the repair end to end:
- A runtime disposal that cannot confirm descendant shutdown reports `uncertain` through its own cleanup scope (existing behavior).
- A **later global sweep still observes the uncertainty** (`uncertain`, not a silent `closed`) — the failed session is no longer dropped from the active registry.
- The retired process owner is **not signaled again**: the process adapter's `dispose()` is called exactly once (no blind retry of a terminal owner).

## What was tested

Local (all green):

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/run-cleanup-timeout.test.ts` — 26 passed
- oxlint `--type-aware` (CI 293 rules), CI format check (`run-format.mts`), mock-exports ratchet (6406 → 6406, no drift), assertion-safety ratchet, `git diff --check` — all clean

## What was not tested

- `src/process/owned-stdio.real.test.ts` (`drains protocol output and shutdown diagnostics...`): the local sandbox cannot certify kernel descendant extinction for real spawned children (no sticky-bit temp root, restricted process supervisor), so it fails on pristine main for environmental reasons (verified by stash on the same base). It runs on CI.
- Real Windows process-tree survival was not reproduced locally; the regression models the rejected-close failure shape via the `waitForExtinction` boundary per the issue's reproducer, which is the same failure `closeOwnedStdioProcess()` throws when extinction cannot be certified.

prs.title: fix(android): keep Talk replies in the selected conversation
prs.body:
Related: #167879, #167881 (separate Gateway authority concerns)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: starting Talk from a selected Android conversation sends consultations and their replies to the phone's default conversation instead.

## User Impact

Talk starts in the chat the user selected. Browsing another chat or refreshing the default session does not redirect an active call; stopping and reopening Talk uses the newly selected chat. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the selected conversation before asynchronous microphone retirement and keep that destination in the existing Talk manager for the enabled call. Relay creation, chat sends, completion observation and history use the same binding. Standalone push-to-talk retains its default-session behavior.

This is an Android routing fix, not another Gateway authority change. The original spoken keyword test appeared successful because the agent searched a different conversation; inspecting the actual destination revealed the bug.

## Evidence

- On upstream base `012d92f5378129cb35b0d39c079374cfbd2bd437`, the new production-entry-point regression failed: expected the selected conversation, received the node default. It exercises `NodeRuntime` through observed Gateway `talk.session.create` requests, including a selection/default change during startup and stop/reopen into a second chat.
- The equivalent fix was installed in a custom 2026.10.6 Android build. The user reported that the complete keyword/follow-up/stop-reopen retest passed using REDBIRD. This is user-reported live evidence for that build, not an independently correlated transcript or a separate network-handover test on this upstream head.
- Simplification: reuse the existing capture/session owners and test fixture; no new coordinator, schema or retry loop. Production delta: +18/-7 lines; test delta: +47/-1 lines.
- Fresh independent native source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CLI AutoReview was unavailable: Codex authentication returned 401, and the supported Claude fallback was not installed. No successful AutoReview result is claimed.
- The regression observes outgoing routing and stop/reopen behavior; microphone-retirement ordering, native history fallback, and PTT behavior were source-reviewed. It does not independently exercise a blocked microphone-retirement barrier or a real network reconnect.
- Current candidate: `:app:ktlintCheck` passed; `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest` passed **152 tests** (112 Talk + 40 agent-selection), zero failures/errors/skips. This includes the formerly failing routing regression. Kotlin/Java debug and test compilation passed as part of that run.

prs.title: fix(ios): retain screenshot CPU attribution after sampling gaps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing CPU attribution in iOS screenshot diagnostics when a process is new or the previous process scan timed out. Such processes were ranked as idle even while the host was CPU-bound.

## User Impact

Operators can identify CPU-heavy simulator services after sampling gaps. Screenshot behavior and release admission are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read macOS recent CPU utilization from the existing once-per-minute process scan and use it to rank the bounded process and group output. Preserve the separate interval measurements, including their null values without a previous observation. No extra probes, subprocesses, timers, or exported process names are added. The documented recent estimate is a decaying average, not an instantaneous share of host CPU.

## Evidence

- Regression fixture reproduces first-observation and post-timeout omissions before the fix; all 9 collector tests pass afterward using the pinned Bun runtime (0.327 seconds test time).
- Native macOS collector smoke completed: process scan took 40 ms, sanitized process rows included recent CPU estimates while interval CPU remained null.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, format, syntax, diff, and test-line ratchet passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `65dfe23a008b` to head `bd21ea977bbd`: complete, high confidence, no actionable correctness or security findings. Source review was read-only; execution evidence above was collected separately.
- [Hosted CI run 41554242472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554242472): iPhone, iPad, and Watch capture all succeeded; collector workload exited 0 after 791 seconds. The complete CI run, including screenshot evidence reduction, passed. No release upload was performed.
- Hosted diagnostics contain 48 samples, seven successful process scans, and five process-probe timeouts. Recent CPU estimates remain available in recovered capture scans where interval CPU is null. The collector used 0.463 seconds of Node CPU and peaked at 52.4 MB RSS (native probes excluded).
- Phone/tablet capture samples showed saturated host CPU with normal memory pressure. Named background-service estimates include simulator `diagnosticd` at 22.9–61.3%, `intelligencecontextd` at 93.1%, and `amsengagementd` at 91.6%; these are decaying estimates and identify investigation targets rather than proving a safe service-disable optimization.

The author simplification pass retained the existing collector owner and sampling lifecycle. Net growth: 10 production lines, 29 regression-test lines, and 6 documentation lines. The scoped test-line allocation covers the new high-CPU/low-RSS process across first, changed-PID, and recovered observations. `apps/ios/fastlane/SETUP.md` documents the new field and its limits.

prs.title: fix(ios): finish Watch runtime cleanup before screenshot repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS screenshot CI stopping before Watch capture when an unavailable runtime still has a downloaded asset and CoreSimulator only partially deletes its registration.

## User Impact

Screenshot repair can reuse the downloaded signed runtime and finish its existing targeted cleanup. If the cached package is missing, download recovery remains available. Capture content, assertions, one-active-simulator policy, and headroom gates are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing fallback DMG before retirement instead of downloading another alias for the same asset. When Apple reports that it removed the registration without reclaiming the MobileAsset, wait up to two minutes for re-registration before the existing single targeted deletion retry. A briefly empty inventory no longer means cleanup succeeded. Ambiguous registrations, retained assets, and unverified imports still fail explicitly; there are no extra deletion attempts or service restarts.

`apps/ios/VERSIONING.md` documents this repair ordering and bounded wait.

## Evidence

- Baseline CI run 41550465949 passed iPhone and iPad captures but stopped before Watch creation. Its log shows partial deletion (SimDiskImageError code 30), an empty inventory immediately after scan-and-mount, and a replacement subsequently stuck deleting.
- The screenshot lifecycle fixture reproduces the retained asset plus temporarily empty inventory. Before the complete fix it failed with `old MobileAsset was not reclaimed`; afterward all 16 Fastlane gate tests pass (0.841 seconds test time). A distinct never-re-registering case stops before capture/import. A missing-package regression failed with `expected one runtime DMG, found 0` before the availability check and passes after it.
- Targeted test typecheck, lint, Ruby syntax, format, diff, and exact test-line ratchet passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `65dfe23a008b` to head `36fc8455444c`: complete, high confidence, no actionable correctness or security findings after the missing-package issue was fixed. Source review was read-only; execution evidence above was collected separately.
- [Hosted CI run 41554982416](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554982416): iPhone, iPad, and Watch capture all succeeded; workload exited 0 after 789 seconds with one active simulator. The log confirms clone, targeted retirement, signed-DMG import, and a mounted `Verified` replacement.
- This hosted run did not encounter partial-deletion code 30 or an unavailable registration, so the newly repaired intermittent branch remains covered by the lifecycle regression, not directly reproduced by this hosted run. The complete CI run, including screenshot evidence reduction, passed. The separate advisory iOS Periphery workflow also passed. No store or TestFlight upload was performed.

The author simplification pass extends the existing runtime repair owner and fixture; it adds no independent repair path. Net growth: 17 production lines, 28 regression-test lines, and 9 documentation lines. The scoped allocation covers preservation, missing-package recovery, and delayed or missing re-registration after partial deletion.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): avoid unnecessary state copies and orphaned snapshots
prs.body:
Related: #190761, #190918, #188009, #191054

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway lease inspection copies the whole state database when its recorded owner cannot be verified. Separately, delivered inspection snapshots and transient update/Doctor roots can outlive their creator, including while a surviving command is still writing into them.

## User Impact

Both current-owner readers now use the existing read-only committed-state connection for dead, unknown, and live owners. Reading a lease grants no takeover or write authority. Only a top-level native hot rollback-journal error retains the existing private recovery exception, preserving source bytes.

Inspection snapshots retain cleanup custody outside their creator. Transient update/Doctor roots share a surviving owner with their inspection commands; retirement joins those commands before removing files. Durable restore/recovery staging keeps its existing lifetime. Native extinction and filesystem cleanup failure remain separate facts, so residual cleanup stays visible and retryable. Only exclusively busy-file cleanup qualifies for the existing deferral policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's existing maintenance state now owns one lazy inspection-command broker across admission and repair callbacks. Every inspection still has an independent temporary root and native resource claim, retired immediately after use. Generation children borrow only the root explicitly provided by their actual command owner; standalone and historical-driver calls retain their own custody. No global cache or idle timer is added.

Named database-port operations and standalone generation/backup commands reuse staging transport within their existing read-only operation scope. Verification consumes already-private captured artifacts directly; published sources retain isolated reads. Redundant metadata captures and the private verification fallback-copy helper are removed. Command cancellation composes the enclosing owner and explicit signals.

Broker/resource launchers resolve through the retained updater generation after package replacement. Its finalizer closes command scopes even when uncertain Doctor cleanup deliberately skips normal release. Closure joins admitted async callbacks before sealing staging admission, then joins native resources; unresolved claims still retain runtime code.

No schema, configuration option, dependency, result cache, or public protocol change. The no-reflink transfer policy comes from already-merged #188009. RPC-only startup already bypasses state admission on the inspected baseline: **the exact reported production RPC-to-snapshot chain was not reproduced**, and this PR does not claim otherwise.

## Evidence

The production-shaped synthetic fixture contains a 12.9 GB state DB, a 35 GiB agent DB, 10,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files. No production data or live deployment is used. Two A/A controls precede five serial counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs. Acceptance requires the same unknown-owner result, snapshot children 1→0, and no greater than 20% owner-metric regression. Committed workload: `scripts/perf/gateway-owner-read-measure.mts`.

| Synchronous owner read | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot children | 1 | 0 |
| Median wall | 11,787.987 ms | 12.609 ms |
| p95/max wall, five samples | 13,182.135 ms | 13.713 ms |
| Median caller CPU | 1,161.245 ms | 13.507 ms |
| Median sampled V8 allocation | 4,704,688 B | 1,766,112 B |

Measurements use macOS/APFS, not Btrfs/FIEMAP. Imports and subprocess native work are excluded from caller CPU/allocation. These measurements precede integration; the ordinary direct-read implementation is unchanged.

- Real isolated `gateway call sessions.list` probes before one minute, during a child write transaction, and after its SIGKILL observe zero copies on baseline and candidate. Built CLI probes also produce zero readonly children/directories/owner reads for authenticated success and missing-credential guidance. The unverifiable-owner hook is armed but never reached.
- Dead/unknown-owner regressions fail on valid baselines and pass across both readers. Lease tests 50/50 and daemon/update consumers 38/38 pass. A spilled-transaction/SIGKILL fixture exercises native error 776, private recovery, retirement, and unchanged source DB/journal bytes.
- Creator SIGKILL leaves a 2 MiB orphan on the baseline and retires it after repair. Snapshot/native-owner proof passes 180 tests with one platform skip; quota/retry 48/48; generation/lease consumers 120/120. These overlapping suites are not a cumulative total.
- Node/Bun current/legacy command proof covers creator death, no premature removal, cancellation, output stop classification, and source preservation. Published 2026.10.9 inspection compatibility passes in both directions; this is not full updater activation proof.
- Current maintenance repair passes Node lifecycle 12/12, Bun lifecycle 14/14, Doctor settlement/reclamation/continuation 50/50, and migration-refusal 2/2. Real six-database SQLite and physical-generation commands start one staging worker standalone and zero under their parent owner, leave source bytes unchanged, and retire all temporary roots. Both parent-owned rows fail before their respective repair.
- The existing retained-runtime regression covers an unused scope and an admitted callback paused before its first command. A separate bounded pre-fix probe exits 13 with unsettled top-level await; the fix exits 0 after runtime release. Package-replacement and surviving-command cleanup remain covered.

## Doctor performance acceptance remains open

The repeated Doctor timeouts in [run 41556231999](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41556231999), head `1ccb2e6b`, exposed branch-caused amplification. Comparison uses actual tested merge `73373869` and its exact main parent `0cbdb482`, private Linux ARM64 Docker, Node 24.22.1, 4 CPUs/16 GiB, synthetic SQLite fixtures, the original three-case order and 120-second deadlines. This is not the hosted Ubuntu x64 concurrent shard, and the hosted timeout was not reproduced locally. No inherited waiver is claimed.

Before repair, repeated A/A observations show the same 30 metadata and 30 generation commands per damaged-identity migration, but 62 added broker starts. Metadata migration takes 29.240/30.125 seconds versus main 11.843/11.059; key-material migration 30.992/30.349 versus 11.729/10.834. Across the complete three-case flow, broker starts are 159 versus main 1, and generation-child staging starts are 77 versus 0.

The first narrow migration-scope repair leaves direct fresh-schema preparation uncovered and fails acceptance. The final maintenance-owner repair reduces the complete flow to **14 broker starts and zero generation-child staging starts**, preserving all 86 metadata and 86 generation commands. Every selected case passes. A contemporaneous exact-main control still establishes the following regression:

| Flow | Exact main wall / total CPU | Current repair wall / total CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh migration helper, including admission and settlement | 3.374 / 4.108 s | 4.707 / 5.586 s |
| Fresh rollback | 1.812 / 2.220 s | 3.006 / 3.716 s |
| Metadata full migration | 12.699 / 14.147 s | 12.119 / 14.668 s |
| Key-material full migration | 11.591 / 13.618 s | 11.458 / 13.758 s |
| Whole fresh case, wall only | 7.367 s | 10.084 s |
| Whole metadata case, wall only | 20.112 s | 21.847 s |
| Whole key-material case, wall only | 18.199 s | 20.066 s |

CPU is container cgroup CPU sampled at 100 ms, including descendants and worker threads. Preparation is excluded. The fresh migration's two remaining brokers serve admission/repair and final settlement after resources close. A bounded CPU profile shows substantial module-loading work but does not establish which imports explain the branch-specific delta; no speculative import refactor follows from it.

The prewritten rule requires stable results, rollback, source bytes and cleanup; fewer unnecessary starts; and no material wall/CPU regression. **The fresh case is 36.9% slower and fresh rollback CPU is 67.4% higher. The 20% stop rule was triggered, so five-pair qualification was not started. These measurements have not been accepted or waived. Landing remains held for explicit owner acceptance of this measured tradeoff, in addition to exact-head CI.**

## Other CI and local findings

Previous repairs preserve original assertions and deadlines: discovery images retire before another copy; native command environments materialize before MessagePort transfer; copied runtime fixtures include the broker; teardown joins native owners before removing HOME. Private verification copies and repeated generation custodians were removed after measured work-count regressions. The final mixed-port Linux samples are 33.689/32.499 seconds versus exact-parent 34.574, with host staging starts reduced 33→4. The ordered PostgreSQL recovery file passes all five cases; its final recovery sample is 62.483 seconds versus adjacent control 63.644, with starts 18→4 and all 26 required exports unchanged. An earlier identical candidate's unexplained 141.041-second sample is retained; no deadline increase is included.

The original-service fixture used PID 4242 while consulting real process ancestry. Controlled collision reproduces the refusal; selecting a synthetic PID outside observed ancestry fixes it without production changes or weaker assertions. Node service tests 48/48 and handoff tests 14/14 pass. Actual CI ancestry was not captured.

Run 41556231999 also reports a UI renderer target crash before assertions. The exact-merge seven-case UI file passes locally, and UI/config/lock inputs match its main parent. This does not prove the concurrent Linux environment. No UI patch or rerun was made. Earlier UI failures from #191292 are repaired on main by #191371; the separate compaction unused-export failure was fixed identically here and on main (`9039ceb4`). No changed module is UI-imported.

Investigated local failures remain recorded: two Bun child startups trap in macOS `pthread_jit_write_protect_np`, while their Node counterparts pass; a macOS-only native PR provisioning test exceeds its unchanged 120-second deadline despite all six provisioners exiting successfully (248.397 seconds combined). Linux CI skips that provisioning case. Neither failure is relabeled as fixed or covered by an inherited-CI exception. Native review retains `tests.result: fail` and the investigations.

Fresh isolated Codex review of the maintenance repair is scoped-clean P2, no actionable findings. The final `pnpm check:changed --base 1ccb2e6bb1fd9273cdd37a191903fb981dff301c --timed` exits 0 with every gate passing. Its preceding run identified one test-only export; the helper is now private and tests use the production scope factory. Those changed tests pass under Node (3/3) and Bun (5/5). Maintenance follow-up head `6e0abf3c64e9eea37199431ab3887d59c9d95eec` passes [CI run 41569257012](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41569257012): 75 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failures, including all three PostgreSQL conformance and all seven UI e2e shards. Native review validation and preparation completed for that exact head. The measured performance tradeoff above remains unaccepted; no merge or auto-merge request has been submitted.

## Size and boundaries

Against pinned integrated main `a9e6314d`, production grows 699 lines, including 129 in this maintenance follow-up. Growth implements surviving cleanup custody, native command settlement, retained-runtime ownership and explicit operation lifetimes; lease-only behavior is net −1. Superseded cleanup paths, redundant copies and metadata captures, and obsolete synchronous test fault injection are removed. The follow-up adds 86 test lines and three documentation lines. No schema, retention-policy, credential, or live-service changes are included.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid copying state for unverifiable owner reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Current Gateway owner lease reads copy the entire state database when the recorded owner is dead or unverifiable, even though reading committed ownership requires no write authority.

## User Impact

Lifecycle and service inspection can read the current lease through the existing native read-only connection without staging a database image. A raw SQLite hot-rollback-journal recovery refusal still uses private recovery; explicit artifact-preserving and schema-admission scopes retain their existing behavior. No schema, configuration, or cache changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the owner-verification prerequisite at the lease-read boundary. Both synchronous and asynchronous reads preserve cancellation, admission and cleanup failures. Only a top-level SQLite extended result 776 permits private recovery, so a cleanup aggregate cannot authorize a retry.

This is the focused lease-read split from #191281. Creator-death staging custody, command custody and lifetime changes are deferred because their maintenance performance cost was not accepted. Runtime production delta is −1 line; the separate reproducible measurement script adds 91 lines. The 57 added test lines protect the previously missing dead/unverifiable no-copy behavior and actual crash-journal recovery; the separate allocation records that necessity without changing the shared budget.

## Evidence

The dead and unverifiable-owner regressions both fail on exact main parent `ab35e1f7326b25135e529c7cb5cc09ce6487e07b`: each invokes snapshot preparation. With the fix, all 50 lease tests pass, including a real spilled transaction killed with SIGKILL: the committed lease is recovered privately and source DB/journal bytes remain unchanged. Full test-file run: 50.99 s including fresh compiler preparation; test time approximately 16 s. All 38 affected service/update tests pass (34.25 s across two test shards). Changed-file checks completed: all gates pass except the inherited script unused-export scan described below. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

Retained production-shaped synthetic benchmark: 12.9 GB state DB, 35 GiB largest agent DB, eight agents, 10,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files (1.18 GB). Two A/A baseline controls (23.933/18.709 s), then five serial counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs. Workload: `scripts/perf/gateway-owner-read-measure.mts`.

| Owner metric (median) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall | 11,787.987 ms | 12.609 ms |
| Caller CPU | 1,161.245 ms | 13.507 ms |
| Sampled V8 allocation | 4,704,688 B | 1,766,112 B |
| Snapshot children per read | 1 | 0 |

Maximum wall among the five pairs: 13,182.135→13.713 ms. Measurements used macOS/APFS, not Btrfs/FIEMAP; imports and native subprocess CPU/allocation are excluded. The ordinary direct-read implementation is unchanged through integration and this split; these are retained measurements, not a fresh benchmark of the new main parent.

The exact reported RPC-to-copy chain remains unreproduced. Earlier real isolated Gateway calls in the first minute, during a child-held write transaction, and after that child's SIGKILL produced zero snapshot children/directories on both baseline and candidate; passive RPC bootstrap already bypassed preflight. This PR fixes the separately reproduced owner-read defect and makes no claim to identify the original artifact creator. Fixtures contain synthetic data only.


`pnpm check:changed` exits 1 solely on three unrelated script entrypoint exports. The exact owner scan reproduces all three on clean exact main parent `ab35e1f7326b25135e529c7cb5cc09ce6487e07b`, without resolution errors. Introducers: `ci-test-observations.mjs:main` — `586f5766569997816efdf795eaaf535f552627a7` (#191226); `ci-adaptive-select.mjs:main` — `1e964bb21464edd8613c9102581a6be899c985f3` (#191228); `ci-adaptive-costs.mjs:main` — `8f8ffc232db9459809136ce2022c90ab8122791f` (#191229). Each adds its exported entrypoint; files are unchanged since introduction. This is a newly discovered main regression requiring owner repair, not a green gate or ignored noise. No corresponding files or consumers change here. Format, core/scripts lint, core/scripts/all core-test typechecks, database ratchets, production/full-tree Knip scans and every other changed-file check pass.

prs.title: fix: reduce memory pressure during gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup can exhaust memory before its first diagnostic sample or model request on constrained hosts.

## User Impact

Startup pressure handling can reclaim idle credential and discovery workers, and selected startup paths load less unrelated code. This is an incremental improvement: the packaged 1 GiB trial now reaches readiness but still OOMs afterward. The 1 GiB and 512 MiB targets remain open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check memory pressure every second under the existing heartbeat owner, including constrained process headroom that RSS alone misses. Preserve the existing pressure thresholds and diagnostic schema. Restore idle-worker retirement, route startup reads and source-free publication restart through their existing lazy owners, and keep PostgreSQL heartbeat code behind its selected-backend boundary in the shipped worker. Preserve source authority, database admission, committed receipts, lease renewal and cancellation behavior.

## Evidence

- Causal red/green regressions cover pressure publication, real-worker retirement/recreation, selected startup read imports, publication restart, heartbeat loading and the production build graph. The late-startup change passed 197 tests across 13 files; the final packaging change passed 51 tests across 4 files. Affected formatting, lint and type checks passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `8051834a3ded5bc2a566c0fecbe98ad66b6f2555..289bac8250c3ce021ed59d0bc30771a011e52691` and `289bac8250c3ce021ed59d0bc30771a011e52691..fb2654d317af6bba59f4b23243cd51969ac6f2b9`: patch correct, no actionable findings, security clear. Independent source and packaging review also passed.
- Exact final ARM64 shipping build and retained-package metadata, emitted startup graph and heartbeat lazy-edge checks passed. The shipped heartbeat entry is 28,537 bytes; its PostgreSQL engine/runtime remains dynamically loaded.
- **Known failure:** exact final packaged 1 GiB trial reached readiness at about 30 seconds, then the service was OOM-killed before the real-model marker or soak completed. Limits remained 768 MiB service, 256 MiB heap, 1 CPU and no swap. Native result remains runtime-nonpass; the classifier retained UNKNOWN because the service cgroup was unavailable after the OOM. No 1 GiB PASS is claimed, and conditional 512 MiB testing was not run. Temporary credentials and containers were removed, and the lease was released.

Landing these reviewed fixes incrementally leaves constrained-RAM acceptance as a follow-up. Exact published-head CI is still required before merge.

prs.title: refactor(update): require the admitted package target
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The package updater repeats destination discovery after admission, although every production caller already supplies the admitted target.

## User Impact

No user-visible change is intended. Package staging and activation keep the selected manager and destination; Git updates, malformed-config previews, and managed-service recovery retain their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Require the admitted target in the package runner; delete fallback discovery and unused `honorPackageRoot` transport. Root policy stays in the canonical resolver. Package execution requires a target; Git execution may carry one for retention. Package result mode reads that admitted manager directly.

Production: +84/-99 (net -15). Tests/support: +39/-11 (net +28), adapting existing fixtures; no new test cases. Most changed lines come from reindenting the initialization factory.

## Evidence

- Final source: `bcc46bca989a569f831bcd45cf13b5000cb9c49d`. [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667) tests merge `ab7926c9a9bb15b99f46643633fa7c30a3ded8ac`, whose parents are main `f75bd97cda9f6d330cb2967a5816aa5af31e1f9c` and this source head. The full run passed, including all planned type stripes and PostgreSQL conformance jobs.
- Passing focused CI: [staging/admission and database retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691136541), [package/Git execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691136399), [real package staging and Doctor-failure rollback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691136638), [original-service recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691136387), and [artifact cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691136421).
- Corrected [CLI test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691798280) and [infra test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566737667/job/125691798220) pass. The first CI run identified three fixtures omitting the now-required target; those fixtures now supply their selected destination.
- Local `git diff --check`, targeted oxfmt 0.74.0, and Node 26.13.0 syntax checks pass. Dependency sharing refused an escaping workspace link; Testbox refused the sparse checkout before runner allocation. Execution/type proof comes from PR CI.
- History audit: all 16 recorded staging callers from 2026.9.5 through 2026.10.9 pass the resolved target. The staging export, compatibility bridge, retained artifact, once-only continuation, and cleanup remain.
- Independent autoreview of the original production cut (`c54e463cfc97dc85fa43ad0405609472fda945bc`) was scoped clean (P0–P3). Separate read-only reviews covered the fixture corrections and final manager read. A final local refresh refused the credential-named fixture under its sensitive-filename guard; the guard was not bypassed. [Final hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191608#issuecomment-6594304815) covers the full final head and reports no findings or before-merge code changes. Its missing installed-behavior proof is supplied by the acceptance run below.
- The ordinary CI published-driver job was skipped. A separate [Package Acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41569568104), with source and trusted harness pinned to the final head, supplies fresh-profile onboarding and latest-stable installed-upgrade proof. Both lanes passed. The upgrade completed on its first attempt in 1167 seconds; package identity, Doctor, config/state survival, Gateway HTTP probes, and RPC status passed. Restart mode was manual. Candidate `openclaw@2026.10.9` (SHA-256 `49c7669ade49b6280cc2a96d1bc620ab9ffecb3af61dee9380cd711880ccbc30`) upgrades the baseline resolved at runtime as `openclaw@2026.10.8`. This is isolated Linux package/Gateway proof; no operator installation was updated.
- Three PostgreSQL cases were skipped in the regular credential suite; the separate conformance jobs passed. No claim that those exact skipped cases ran there.

prs.title: fix(agents): a Claude 5-hour limit reply shows generic failure copy instead of the reset time
prs.body:
Related: #190750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a run that exhausts a subscription's usage window ends with `The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.` — even when the provider's own reply states when the window resets, and even when that reset is days away.

## User Impact

User impact: when a usage window is used up and no fallback model is left to run, the chat now carries the provider's bounded wording with its reset time (`You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm`) instead of advice to retry in a few minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported symptom had two independent causes, and the second one is why the first alone is not enough.

**1. The window was not recognized.** `PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE` accepted only calendar windows — `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` — plus their Chinese equivalents. Rolling windows (`5-hour`, `hourly`) describe the same condition with the same reset hint but did not match, so `isPeriodicUsageLimitErrorMessage` answered false for the Claude CLI reply. `retry-evidence.ts` already ORs this predicate next to its own long-window check, so extending the one owner of this concept also makes hour-shaped windows count as long-window retry evidence.

The pattern stays narrow on purpose: the window token has to lead the word `limit` (`hourly limit`, `5-hour limit`, `24 hour limit`). Unrelated durations such as `request timeout after 2 hours` or `The limit is 2 hours` still do not match.

**2. The quota copy was unreachable from the terminal reply.** `buildExternalRunFailureReply` is the single renderer every channel uses for a failed run. It consults the quota copy path only after rate-limit retries are exhausted, and `resolveReplyFailoverFacts` — which supplies `requestFailureText` — never consulted it at all. So a quota that names its reset time fell through to `renderAssistantRequestFailureCopy`, whose `rate_limit` entry is the fixed "try again in a few minutes" sentence. That affected calendar windows too: on current `main`, a weekly quota with an explicit reset date renders as "try again in a few minutes" through the same function, which is wrong by days.

`resolveReplyFailoverFacts` now forwards the quota renderer's output when the failure text names a periodic usage window. That renderer already sanitizes and bounds the provider line, so no raw provider text is introduced here; a plain `429 slow down` still gets the existing generic copy.

## Evidence

### The shipped reply renderer, before and after

`buildExternalRunFailureReply` is the function that produces the text any channel sends. Same call, same input, `includeDetails: false`:

Before (current `main`):

```text
in : 429 You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.

in : 429 You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.

in : 429 You are being rate limited, slow down
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.
```

After:

```text
in : 429 You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm
out: ⚠️ You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm

in : 429 You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC
out: ⚠️ You have reached your weekly limit; resets Monday 09:00 UTC

in : 429 You are being rate limited, slow down
out: ⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.
```

The second row is a defect on current `main` that this change also fixes: a calendar-window quota whose reset is days away was telling the user to retry in a few minutes. The third row is the deliberate non-goal — a rate limit that names no window keeps its existing copy.

### The committed regressions fail without the fix

`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`, with `request-error-facts.ts` reverted and the new tests kept:

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "subscription usage window"
  Tests  1 failed | 21 skipped (22)
  expected '⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.' to equal '⚠️ You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm'
```

With the fix in place:

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  22 passed (22)
```

### Classification before / after

Judged with the exported function on the same strings.

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm` | false | **true** |
| `5-hour limit reached ∙ resets 11pm` | false | **true** |
| `hourly limit reached` | false | **true** |
| `24 hour limit exceeded` | false | **true** |
| `You have reached your weekly limit` | true | true |
| `daily usage limit exceeded` | true | true |
| `402 Payment Required: Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted` | true | true |
| `已达到 Token Plan 用量上限` | true | true |
| `request timeout after 2 hours` | false | false |
| `The limit is 2 hours` | false | false |
| `rate limit 5 requests per hour` | false | false |

### Checks run

```text
vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts --maxWorkers=1                -> 22 passed
vitest run src/agents/failover/user-copy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1                                   -> 25 passed
vitest run src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts \
           src/agents/failover/retry-evidence.test.ts \
           src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts --maxWorkers=1              -> 125 passed
oxfmt --check (all four touched files)                                                            -> clean
```

### Gaps

This is not a Discord replay. The proof runs the shipped reply renderer that every channel calls, with the same function and inputs a channel failure produces, and shows the rendered text changing; it does not stand up a Discord client. The sanitizer remains the second gate — copy without a reset time is still replaced with the generic message, which is existing intended behaviour and is why the new assertions pin the reset hint rather than the raw provider text.

`#172065` (open) changes failover behaviour when a fallback candidate exists. This PR covers the surface that remains when none does, so the two are complementary rather than overlapping.

prs.title: feat(claws): add local packages through the gateway and preserve setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Integrations cannot add a converted local Claw package through a running gateway: the gateway Add API only accepts ClawHub coordinates, while an offline writer cannot mutate live gateway state.

## User Impact

An admin-authorized client can plan and add an absolute local package path on the gateway host. Installation uses the existing Claw checks, lifecycle, plugin consent, integrity validation, and rollback. Retrying an installation that rolled back before agent creation preserves its first-run instructions. Imported memory and skills no longer cause the first turn to discard custom setup instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source adapter feeds the existing Add owner:

```text
local package or ClawHub coordinate
  → resolve and inspect
  → plan + integrity check
  → native Add lifecycle
```

Local planning and application require `operator.admin`. Remote clients must transfer their package to the gateway host first. Rollback retires the existing workspace setup state along with a workspace it created and removed.

## Evidence

- Before: local source payload rejected by the gateway schema. After: an actual handler test installs instructions, the exact avatar bytes, and `BOOTSTRAP.md` as an ordinary agent.
- Before: failed Add → rollback → retry reports complete but omits `BOOTSTRAP.md`. After: the same actual-handler regression preserves the setup file.
- Regression coverage follows native Add through first-turn workspace preparation: imported memory and skills preserve a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md`; stock-template cleanup and explicit completion retain their existing behavior.
- Focused plan/apply, authorization, stale-source, schema, plugin handoff, and stateless rollback tests pass. Core type graphs, boundary checks, targeted lint and formatting pass.
- The full build passes, including CLI startup and plugin SDK export checks.
- Live isolated gateway proof at combined stack head `e33e4d5ca2b`: a fresh Stalk Bot installation completed a real agent turn with all 236 characters of custom setup instructions and 3,459 characters of memory injected without truncation. The setup file remains after the turn.
- Real WebSocket authorization regression passes for local packages: admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and real device-token revocation at the pre-effect gate prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The catalog positive control remains covered. No authority predicate is mocked; assertions cover agent configuration, installed-plugin records, and extension directories.
- Final setup regression and existing workspace sibling cases: 53 tests passed. Final runtime build passed; private workspace-logic changes do not alter the declaration/SDK export surface checked by the preceding full build.

**Merge risk:** reversible code change; affects the Claw Add source boundary and cleanup of newly created workspaces. Existing ClawHub behavior remains covered.

Prior-head CI blocker: the unchanged updater mock check also fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710); the [native classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992603758/job/117280609263) marks it pre-existing. That aggregate remains red; no exception or unrelated fix is included. The conflict-only stack restack onto `acd27635` preserves all three core patches exactly; current-head CI must run separately.

Additional private-QA full-build check: SDK declarations exceed the private testing budget. An isolated captured-main build produces the same 456 public-reachable declaration files byte-for-byte (5,440,829 bytes versus the 5,340,536-byte cap). No budget change or unrelated repair is included. Runtime/UI artifacts were generated; the full command is recorded as failed.

Compatibility evidence is scoped to the existing state contract and production boundaries. Compared directly with `v2026.10.4`, setup state remains version 1, `WorkspaceSetupState` fields are identical, and the complete `workspace_setup_state` SQL definition is byte-identical. The PR changes no persisted schema or config format. Existing completed state skips reconciliation; rollback cleanup only retires a newly created, uncommitted workspace. The 48 passing workspace cases plus 5 native Add cases cover retained completed timestamps/content, stock cleanup, concurrent completion, custom pending setup, and explicit completion. This is not a claim that a full product upgrade was executed.

Paired saved runtime proof: before the setup fix (`5ffb1320fcc`), `bootstrapExists=false` and `bootstrapInjected=false`; after (`e33e4d5ca2b`), `BOOTSTRAP.md` injected 236/236 characters without truncation and remained present after the turn. The baseline predates the fix; it is not an exact current-merge-base replay.

## Main refresh (2026-10-27)

prs.title: feat(migrate): add native agent and cron import effects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Migration providers need to create additional agents and scheduled prompts without bypassing native lifecycle or scheduler ownership. This adds lazy migration SDK operations that require the admitted offline state owner and reject onboarding staging.

```text
migration apply (final state, offline owner)
  createMigrationAgent → native createAgent → exact retry or conflict
  applyMigrationCronJob → native CronService.add → exact retry or conflict
```

Existing agents and changed jobs are preserved. Migration explicitly refuses held-store restoration; the exact agent reuse path runs after deletion/recovery gates; cron import does not start the scheduler. This is the lower capability layer for Grok configuration migration, tracked in [CLAW-1180](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-1180/import-grok-bot-configuration-through-the-migration-framework).

## User Impact

Migration providers can preserve multi-agent setups and scheduled prompts through OpenClaw’s native owners. Existing agent creation behavior is unchanged unless the provider explicitly requests exact-state reuse.

## Why This Change Was Made

Grok configuration migration needs agent creation and cron insertion after onboarding promotion, under the admitted offline state owner. These shared operations keep lifecycle and scheduler writes out of provider-specific code. The dependent provider is [#178769](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178769).

## Evidence

- **Before:** the native migration boundary regression failed with `createMigrationAgent is not a function`.
  **After:** targeted agent creation, native migration-agent and cron tests pass, including stale/cancelled ownership, staging refusal, retries, conflicts, and no scheduler execution. Core/SDK/agent test typegraphs, targeted lint, formatting and SDK export checks pass; full candidate build passes.
- The dependent provider's real-owner integration additionally exercises existing-state preservation and saved-plan recovery; its confirmed-only scope excludes credential copying. No unrelated agent or cron writer was introduced.
- The exact committed Plugin SDK API comparison passes: migration-runtime remains an existing host-local-only facade, so the published compatibility surface is unchanged. Broad local gates report inherited line-count, shard-budget and agentsapi unused-export failures; all affected paths are unchanged against the captured base. No unrelated baseline was relaxed.

- Hosted CI exposed a type-only back-edge in the existing-agent result helper and duplicate cron helper export names. The native-layer correction removes the back-edge, gives implementation functions distinct names, and tests cron through the provider facade. Both exact failing guards now pass locally, with 26 affected native tests, core types, formatting and scoped type-aware lint.

- **Recovery review regression:** before the fix, an imported definition returned `existing` and cleared a recovery hold. With `restorePaths: []`, both matching and conflicting definitions preserve the hold, config, and held database bytes until explicit recovery. Agent/cron SDK tests pass (3 tests, 70.10s wrapper / 25.02s Vitest under host load), with SDK test types and two-file lint.
- **Final-effect authority proof:** releasing the real offline owner while native workspace preparation is paused returns an SDK error and leaves config unchanged, with no agent/session database or provenance. Only the already-created empty directory remains. This proves the composed agent boundary; no new direct late-revocation cron case or published-driver upgrade was run.


- Final combined head `12dcad3075c` builds successfully in 4m22s (existing UI gzip warning retained). Native head: `73ca0a4d30b`. The rebuilt CLI selects only `stalk-setup` by name, emits all six curated integration paths, and plans no secret actions. Real Stalk repeat apply completes with 25 migrated, 12 skipped, no errors/conflicts, and a verified backup; all 19 skill bodies, 9 exported memories, and instructions remain intact, with one memory import block.

Review coordination: the local stack owner handles repairs and propagation between these dependent branches. ClawSweeper's current contract says repair/merge execution lanes are retired. ClawSweeper review is requested on the updated heads; neither PR is claimed merge-ready while live-account qualification and hosted checks remain pending.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Code can be reverted; completed migrations retain their created state and use the migration framework's backup for restoration.

**Blast Radius:** Migration

The new SDK operations admit effects only under the selected offline owner. Existing createAgent callers retain their current behavior; reuse is opt-in.

## What Problem This Solves

Add Grok Bot to the existing one-time migration workflow used by Hermes, accepting local/account sources, offline snapshots, recipes, and marketplace/share URLs.

```text
source → preview + backup → native agents / workspace / supported config
                         → explicit skipped items and integration setup guidance
```

## User Impact

Imports owned-agent identity/icons, instructions, skills, complete explicitly exported memory, timezone, supported disabled cron jobs, and compatible disabled MCP connection definitions. Supports fresh onboarding and standalone migration into existing state with conflicts and repeat-apply handling.

Credentials are not copied, even with `--include-secrets`. Private cloud memory is not requested, and partial memory is skipped, including recovery from an older saved plan. Grok sign-in is used only to read source definitions. Known plugin IDs receive curated setup guidance for AgentMail, X/xurl, Gmail/Sheets/gog, Slack, and manual Salesforce MCP. No automatic plugin installation or drop-in tool parity is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requested product is configuration migration rather than individual Claw packages. Patrick further narrowed scope to verified transfers and explicit handling of unsupported content. This uses the existing detect/plan/apply owners rather than a parallel importer.

Depends on [native migration capabilities #178768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178768). Replaces the product direction of [the earlier URL-to-Claw importer #174960](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174960). Scope and proof are tracked in [CLAW-1180](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-1180/import-grok-bot-configuration-through-the-migration-framework).

## Evidence

- **Before:** new boundary regressions fail because credentials are still planned, partial memory is still copied, and hosted private memory is requested. Default token-only discovery cannot reopen its source on apply. Imported skills cannot be selected by their names.
  **After:** 22 focused tests pass across source/provider/integration boundaries and the real migration/config/agent/cron owners (48.80s wrapper wall time). Credentials are omitted, complete memory and existing state are preserved, partial memory and old credential actions are rejected, source discovery round-trips, and the actual CLI selector accepts `Research`.
- **Plugin installation:** the official `clawhub:@agentmail/agentmail@0.2.1` package installed successfully in the stopped isolated OCM environment; required dependencies are present. Inspection confirms explicit `enabled=false`, `activated=false`, `status=disabled`. `--no-enable` preserves defaults rather than forcing disable, so the setup guide now includes `plugins disable agentmail`. No sign-in or mail operation was performed.
- Real-owner integration verifies multi-agent creation, icons, instructions, memory, skills, timezone, disabled MCP/cron, conflicts, repeat apply, and saved-plan recovery. It does not execute external integrations or schedulers.
- Earlier real built-CLI Stalk proof: 28 migrated, 9 manual/skipped, zero errors/conflicts, verified backup; all 9 exported memory entries and 19 skill bodies retained exactly. Stalk completed a real local Ollama turn and displayed its imported purple avatar. The current native-migration screenshot is attached to CLAW-1180; screenshots on the older PR show a different Claw-package flow and are not proof of these migration effects.
- Extension production/test types and root integration types pass. Scoped lint and candidate build receipts are recorded with the final revision below. Broad pre-existing line-count, graph-budget, and agentsapi unused-export findings were not waived or modified.

- Final combined head `12dcad3075c` builds successfully in 4m22s (existing UI gzip warning retained). Native head: `73ca0a4d30b`. The rebuilt CLI selects only `stalk-setup` by name, emits all six curated integration paths, and plans no secret actions. Real Stalk repeat apply completes with 25 migrated, 12 skipped, no errors/conflicts, and a verified backup; all 19 skill bodies, 9 exported memories, and instructions remain intact, with one memory import block.

Live owned-account qualification remains blocked by the MacBook's Grok Keychain item denying SSH access. The local cache contains metadata including rooms, not full bots. No account-wide completeness or integration execution claim is made; private memory is now deliberately outside hosted import scope. Source conversations were not read and no messages were sent.

Review repairs are owned by the local stack coordinator. ClawSweeper's current guidance says repair/merge execution lanes are retired; review is requested after coherent stack updates. Nothing is merged or activated in personal state.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Code can be reverted; imported state uses the migration framework's verified backup for restoration. Source Grok data is unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** Migration

Hosted definitions depend on Grok's current private API and source sign-in. Schedules and connections remain disabled until their tool scope, authorization, and delivery are reviewed.

prs.title: feat(claws): import Grok bot recipes, URLs, and owned bots
prs.body:
> **Direction update:** The requested product is now a Hermes-style one-time configuration migration. Its replacement implementation is [#178769](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178769), built on [#178768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178768). This PR retains the earlier individual-Claw implementation and proof as history; its generic local-install dependency [#174959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174959) is independent.

## What Problem This Solves

Users cannot turn a Grok Bot recipe, share URL, or marketplace bot into an OpenClaw Claw, including its instructions and appearance.

## User Impact

Adds the bundled `grok-bot` CLI and conversational import skill. Complete recipes preserve supplied instructions, memory, full skill bodies, name/avatar, getting-started instructions, routines, and integration requirements. Packages can be converted offline and installed through the running gateway's native Claw Add flow.

`--all` imports available content from the signed-in account's owned bots. These results are explicitly **partial**: Grok's available owner read APIs do not expose complete memories or original integration requirements. Both omissions are recorded in results and installed setup notes. Rooms and teammates' bots are excluded.

Routines remain disabled, and integrations require explicit setup. Source conversations and credentials are not migrated. macOS account reuse uses the active Grok Bot account and normal Keychain access on explicit request; an environment token is also supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

```text
recipe JSON / share or marketplace URL / owned-bot roster
  → source reader with explicit completeness
  → portable Claw package
  → native gateway plan/apply
```

Grok-specific translation and authentication stay in the plugin. The generic local-package Add capability is supplied by the preceding stack layer. Marketplace summaries are never substituted for full recipes.

## Evidence

- Before: the marketplace URL was treated as a local path and returned `read_failed`.
- After: the real Stalk Bot URL converted 9 memories, 19 full skills, 3 routine definitions, and 6 integration requirements. Native installation and a real agent turn succeeded. Its full 3,459-character `MEMORY.md` was loaded without truncation.
- At `e33e4d5ca2b`, a fresh native installation and real local-model turn succeeded; the correct Stalk Bot name and source avatar rendered in the running Control UI. Source and installed screenshots are attached below.
- First-run context proof: all 236 characters of the custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` and all 3,459 characters of `MEMORY.md` were injected without truncation, with all 19 imported skills advertised. The setup file still exists after the turn.
- Smoke-test limit: the small local model answered but did not follow the requested setup-file read/quotation. The package records the correct six integration requirements; a completed setup conversation and external integration execution were not qualified.
- Generated config baseline increases by exactly 21 standard `plugins.entries.grok-bot-import` nodes, with no bespoke config options. Removing those nodes reproduces the previous hashes exactly; core/channel budgets are unchanged. Plugin inventory/reference pages are generator-owned.
- Full build (including SDK exports/declarations) passed; final runtime rebuild passed at `e33e4d5ca2b`. The final native first-run fix passed 53 gateway/workspace tests, types, lint, format, and independent review.
- Before the conflict-only restack, follow-up `7fd50ddca6e` passes the exact CI type-aware lint, production typecheck, converter tests (6/6), cycle check, assertion ratchet, formatting and diff checks. It removes a type-only cycle, documents existing object guards, and safely narrows filesystem errors.
- Focused auth/cache, source selection, account filtering, partial-source reporting, converter/native-package, photo, and installation failure tests pass; targeted type, lint, and formatting checks pass.
- Restacked onto captured main `acd27635` to resolve a real stack merge conflict in generated configuration fingerprints. Range-diff confirms all five runtime/behavior commits are patch-identical; only the generated combined/core hash context changes. Prior runtime and focused-check evidence is retained with its original revision; current-head CI is tracked separately.
- Source authorization: 21 focused source/client/import tests pass, including HTTP 401/403 rejection before any package output or gateway call, and exclusion of teammates/rooms/nonowners before per-bot reads. A canonical CLI call with a synthetic invalid token reached the real roster API, received HTTP 401, exited 1, and created no export directory. This proves invalid-token rejection; no real credential was revoked.
- Gateway authorization: the existing real WebSocket/native Add test now covers local paths. Admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and actual device-token revocation during dependency installation prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The test passes; no authority mock replaces the Gateway checks. Staging/temporary writes are outside that final-effect assertion.
- Additional private-QA build scope: runtime/UI artifacts were generated, but the full command exits 1 on the private-QA SDK size budget. A separate captured-main build produces the exact same 456 public declaration files (all per-path SHA-256 hashes equal), 5,440,829 bytes versus a 5,340,536-byte cap. This failure is inherited; no budget was changed.
- Production local discovery succeeded against Grok Bot 0.70.2, finding one account and 11 cached roster entries (including rooms). No credentials or network calls are needed for local-only discovery.
- Final live owned-bot account qualification is pending a normal Keychain unlock after 1Password approval timeouts. No source writes were performed. Owner API schemas and the complete marketplace download were separately verified against the current Grok app.

**Merge risk:** reversible plugin addition. Grok's app/API formats are not a published compatibility contract; incompatible responses fail visibly. Imported instructions may reference Grok-specific capabilities that need OpenClaw equivalents.
