## Latest runtime qualification — November 3, 2026

Both native inheritance paths passed on a combined candidate containing this stack, the already-landed enrollment fix [#191006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191006), and a separately qualified socket-owner repair that is not yet published. This closes the previously reported runtime-execution gap for that composition, **not** for an unchanged published head. Source integration, current-head CI and the requested overall review rating remain outstanding. Earlier attempts and their limits below are retained as historical evidence.

### Complete mirrored and retained runtime assertions passed

[Blacksmith run 41571285323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41571285323), lease tbx_01m6fpj94dvws978szp6fg1fe1, executed the unchanged fixture through a real Gateway and authenticated native nodes on Linux/Node24.22.1.

Executed source tree: c4a401fe4d33312a427d8f7e1ee72fdff533bdd3. Actual remote source digest: d6560ace95d0e2292d6c8b5bb4c2ec46f95ae53d51a3d5c1bd3453e18529f669 (62,592 files). This is the combined candidate with the exact enrollment prerequisite and socket-owner repair, not a claim about an unchanged published PR head.

Actual output:

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
    Tests       2 passed (2)
    Duration    290.09s
    REVIEWED_DRIVER_EXIT=2

The two tests are configuration preflight and the complete runtime composition. Within that composition:

| Scenario | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Invalid placed schema | Rejected without child/provider allocation |
| Mirrored parent → native child | Completed; private history and current files preserved |
| Retained parent → native child | Completed; fresh disk-only history/files preserved; independently owned child resource |

Both children completed and their expected assistant replies were verified. The run observed four distinct authenticated native nodes and 13 deterministic streaming requests, including two child requests. Before/after parent identity, liveness, placement, repository workspace, disk authority and filesystem/index snapshots remained unchanged. Child workspaces, branches, directories and environments were independent; editing each child did not alter its parent.

Verified private HEADs:
- Mirrored: 38cfb78fb2e6c3dfec9e5b01a25332087fda7f35.
- Retained: 31ba6401a43e752e38a72028882e18b8d608cbda, including changes made after the parent’s completed baseline turn.

**Why driver exit2:** all runtime assertions passed, but its post-test collector expected one rendered ledger line. The maintained verbose and default reporters rendered the same console event twice. Both complete payloads are byte-identical: SHA256 e26a8cbc772108f4c5f9304b6b1b3dac4633571a325226ffd266256d0ff5c343. Raw receipts remain unchanged; a separately labeled ledger was recovered only after equality and completeness verification. No runtime retry or assertion relaxation occurred. The collector-only correction is proposed, not applied.

**Cleanup:** exact container, bridge and snapshot removal passed. Fourteen evidence files were downloaded/hash-verified before lease release and reverified afterward. Final lease settlement is complete; the Actions cancellation reflects lease teardown. One allocation and one driver, 16m38s including preparation, collection and cleanup.

**Limits:** real Gateway, enrollment, native processes, Git/files/stores; deterministic model and managed-provider fixtures. Retained resources are task-local directories/receipts, not commercial durable-volume provisioning. Internal bridge is not network-none or guaranteed host-unreachable. This is not current published-head CI, merge equivalence or an overall Platinum rating.


---

## What Problem This Solves

Native children could not inherit work held only on a parent's retained repository disk. Review also exposed successful file-only fallback after private-history failures and source reassignment reaching child checkpoint publication.

## User Impact

Children receive independent checkpoints with current private Git history and working files. The parent retains its disk, active turn and staging index; the child starts from HEAD plus working files, not a shared disk or copied index. Incomplete or unauthorized exports fail and roll back the unexposed child. No schema, configuration, receipt or permission migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on [#190843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190843). The non-rewriting integration commit `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377` preserves both the disk repair `ca21621d5d4fc049ba63041cbf501184d949d196` and checkpoint prerequisite `b081d9ace588fec30b1c23d81a17bd8b0a81a07f` as parents.

The existing mutation queue and snapshot owner capture the exact attached disk under quiescence. Prepared caller/parent authority remains live through Git and node effects; the asynchronous `diskExport.verifyCurrent()` check remains before accepting the child. The common checkpoint owner requires complete private history during export, extraction and child copying. Ordinary recovery/publication keep their file-only fallback. Allocation remains in the shared dependency leaf, and existing rollback owns failed preparation and scope cleanup.

The combined owner exceeded its file-size gate. Unchanged payload/history types moved into a type-only module, preserving the existing exported payload import path; no runtime policy or implementation was moved or weakened.

## Evidence

- **Red/green:** three private-history regressions failed on `5ba38db0f99a369cf90c24fbbab21229954195fc` because creation succeeded after retention, extraction or child-copy failure. Source-reassignment probes also observed copying/publication before late binding refusal. The retained-authority repairs reject those effects.
- **Combined runtime qualification:** 2/2 public-handler cases and **50/50 owner cases across three suites** passed. Coverage includes allowed and revoked/reassigned creation, strict history failures, ordinary checkpoint recovery, fresh snapshot custody, parent index/disk/turn preservation and failed-resume cleanup. Timing controls call real implementations and negative cases require production refusals.
- Proof uses real Git, a local node runtime, HTTP transfer, and durable repository/session/placement stores. External provisioning and GitHub identity are fixtures. **No live cloud provisioning or real agent/model product turn was executed.**
- Runtime proof completed before the final type-only extraction. The runtime implementation is unchanged by that extraction; final core, gateway-server and gateway-other test typechecks, 12-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Both architecture cycle checks pass. No baseline or ignore exceptions were added.
- **Complete committed-range canonical autoreview:** `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914` → `b782b5d4ff4dee05e6e153206705df7124d19377`, P0–P2, 28 complete frozen context files: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. The prerequisite's separate committed review is also scoped-clean. Review is static assessment, not independently rerun testing.
- Simplification retains existing allocation, source-authority, capture and checkpoint owners. The type-only split preserves the public contract without another runtime owner. The existing regression allocations and shared scalar remain unchanged by integration.
- Current-head hosted CI and overall review readiness remain required; neither is inferred from local review quality.

Both complete payloads are byte-identical: SHA256 e26a8cbc772108f4c5f9304b6b1b3dac4633571a325226ffd266256d0ff5c343. The collector-only correction is proposed, not applied.

**Cleanup:** exact container, bridge and snapshot removal passed. Fourteen evidence files were downloaded/hash-verified before lease release and reverified afterward. Final lease settlement is complete; the Actions cancellation reflects lease teardown. One allocation and one driver, 16m38s including preparation, collection and cleanup.

**Limits:** real Gateway, enrollment, native processes, Git/files/stores; deterministic model and managed-provider fixtures. Retained resources are task-local directories/receipts, not commercial durable-volume provisioning. Internal bridge is not network-none or guaranteed host-unreachable. ## What Problem This Solves

Native same-agent children of repository-only sessions incorrectly fall back to the configured Gateway workspace. Creation fails when that directory is not a Git checkout. Review also exposed a runtime import cycle and a late source check that could copy a parent's checkpoint after reassignment, before session binding finally refused it.

## User Impact

Setup-script permission remains the intersection of the parent's permission and the current caller's authority. Reassigned or revoked sources are refused before child copying and binding. Incompatible local selectors and initial local turns remain invalid. Disk-authoritative parents stay guarded here; #190845 adds fresh disk exports. prs.title: feat(cli): expose per-call web fetch character budgets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw infer web fetch` cannot pass a per-call character budget even though the underlying fetch tool and selected providers already accept `maxChars`. Operators must use their configured default for every fetch.

## User Impact

Add `--max-chars <n>` (minimum 100) to request a smaller or larger budget for one fetch. Omitting it preserves the existing argument shape and provider defaults. The default fetch path limits the complete visible result, including framing and spill notices, within `tools.web.fetch.maxCharsCap`. Selected providers retain their existing budget semantics, which can exclude framing and metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse the option through the existing positive-integer helper, reject values below 100 before config/credential loading, and forward one argument object through both default and pinned-provider paths. The fetch/provider owners still perform truncation and enforce their caps.

Three files, +40/-33: production +4 lines, existing command tests -3 lines, docs +6 lines. Reuse existing test tables and options; no new test allocation, baseline exception, config/schema, dependency, permission, or SDK contract. This is a small public CLI addition; product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.

## Evidence

- [Original-source diagnostic and control](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41299041487), source `39629c6aa82ce444f14c37fc1d4d47e5c7f661d0`: real CLI help succeeds; `--max-chars 512` is rejected as unknown with no HTTP request. Existing default fetch succeeds and returns its configured 1600-character budget from the synthetic 6048-character document. This establishes feature absence, not product success.
- [Final-head proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/41300928476), exact source `f55f8bc84e9c7470f4573af5ba38aaef07da0438`: canonical runtime build and actual CLI against controlled HTTP endpoints pass all ten cases. Default omission preserves 1600; explicit 512 returns 512; 5000 clamps to 2000. The minimum 100 produces a 92-character spill notice while retaining the complete 6048-character content in the spill file. Blank, zero, and 99 exit 1 with the normal JSON error envelope and make no HTTP requests.
- The same run exercises the actual bundled Firecrawl provider through its supported self-hosted HTTP endpoint: two real `POST /v2/scrape` requests, retained raw prefixes of 512 and 2000 characters, and visible lengths of 649 and 2137 after existing wrapping. The upstream vendor service is synthetic; this does not claim vendor-live coverage. [Readable driver](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/blob/b726968e0625410cc6e3ba4859f79fc6d02d52e2/proof/web-fetch-max-chars-fixed.mjs). Runtime artifacts retain CLI outputs, independent HTTP request records, input/config snapshots, spills, and a receipt confirming all children joined, server closed, config unchanged, source clean, and strict cleanup.
- Checks on the same exact product head: 103/103 command tests, zero skips; core and config-cli test types; typed lint with 0 errors/warnings; canonical format and oxfmt/Bun parity; assertion, max-lines, line-cap and test-lines ratchets; docs sanity and clean source. No line cap or baseline was relaxed. Test command wall time 86.78 seconds; Vitest duration 81.62 seconds. Existing SQLite lifecycle output and the advisory test-shard root-budget warning remain visible.
- Independent P0–P3 autoreview of the exact three-file diff committed as `f55f8bc84e9c7470f4573af5ba38aaef07da0438` found no actionable findings. All product execution used stock secretless fork Actions. [Ready PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41301869846) and its required `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded on exact head `f55f8bc84e9c7470f4573af5ba38aaef07da0438`. Maintainer review remains pending.

prs.title: fix(config): warn when an empty tool allow list is the whole policy
prs.body:
Companion to #147490 by @Navras98, who found and first fixed this gap; credit for spotting it and for the original patch (`99e3d45`, authorship kept in history) is his. **This revision replaces his `openclaw config validate` warning with an advisory `openclaw doctor` note.** The validation code and its test are reverted to `main`. If he'd rather carry the doctor approach in #147490, I'll close this one.

Refs #147342

## What Problem This Solves

A tool policy whose only content is `allow: []` reads as "no tools", but at that layer an empty allow list adds no restriction (global `deny` and the built-in sub-agent hard denies still apply). Nothing tells the user, so a policy that looks locked down blocks nothing.

## What Changed

- New `src/commands/doctor-empty-tool-allow.ts`, called from `collectSecurityWarnings`, adds an **info** note (`doctor.empty_tool_allow`) to Doctor's Security section.
- It fires only when `allow` is `[]` and there is **no** non-empty `deny`, **no** non-empty `alsoAllow` and **no** `profile`. It checks `tools`, `tools.subagents.tools` and each agent's `tools`. In any other shape the empty list is part of a larger policy, so Doctor stays silent.
- The remediation suggests `deny: ["*"]` for "no tools", or removing the empty list if allow-all is intended.
- Config validation, the JSON output, exit codes and runtime matching are unchanged. `allow: []` stays a valid allow-all setting, so no policy decision is needed.
- Docs: `docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md` adds a short "empty allow means allow-all" callout: no restriction at that layer, global/sub-agent hard denies still apply, the `tools.subagents.tools` exception where `allow: []` + `alsoAllow: ["read"]` merges to `allow: ["read"]`, and the doctor note.

## Evidence

### Built CLI on Linux: `node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive`

Both runs use a full `build-all` and an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Base is `de5ab40a48a`; head is this branch.

| Config | Base (before) | Head (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"tools":{"allow":[]}}` | exit 0, no Security section, no note | exit 0, **note shown** |
| `{"tools":{"allow":[],"deny":["exec"]}}` | exit 0, no note | exit 0, **no note** |

prs.title: fix(ios): Dashboard, Desktop and Terminal pages fail behind Cloudflare Access
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Dashboard pages, Desktop, Terminal and the per-session Dashboard in the iOS/iPadOS app do not load when the Gateway is behind Cloudflare Access. The Dashboard pages showed only "This Dashboard needs a browser session", and the other pages loaded with no Access cookie. ## User Impact User impact: after native Cloudflare Access sign-in, Workboard, Activity, Skill Workshop, Instances, Dreaming, Usage, Automations, Desktop, Terminal and the session Dashboard load on iPhone and iPad. If the grant is missing or the edge refuses the browser session, the app shows a native fallback with **Try again** and **Open Gateway settings** instead of a blank page. Access apps with binding cookies will still show the fallback. ## Why This Change Was Made The native app already holds an Access session, but the embedded web view never received it. The web view's own non-persistent cookie store now gets a host-only, Secure, HttpOnly `CF_Authorization` cookie before the first load. One shared gate (`AccessGatedControlUI`) covers every Control UI host so none can skip it. Safeguards: the cookie is built from a validated `Set-Cookie` header and fails closed; the token must match a strict JWT allow-list; WebKit content rules block every request to the Gateway host, on any explicit or implicit port, except the admitted authority (cookies are not port-scoped); a retirement generation closes the sign-out race; sign-out, expiry and account changes unload the page and delete the cookie. ## Evidence - Physical iPad Pro (M4, iPadOS 27.2) and iPhone 18 Pro against a real Access-protected Gateway: Usage, Automations, Terminal and Desktop captured on both (see Screenshots); Workboard, Activity, Skill Workshop, Instances and Dreaming were also confirmed working by the tester. - Unit tests (`CloudflareAccessWebSessionTests`) and real-WebKit tests (`CloudflareAccessWebKitTests`): the content rules compile; a non-persistent store keeps the cookie host-only, Secure and HttpOnly; a table test covers allowed and blocked URLs for custom-port and default-port origins, including the implicit-port-443 case; a live WebKit test in which the real Secure, HttpOnly Access cookie is sent to the admitted authority and to no other port, and is not sent again after the cookie jar retires it (sign-out path); and a live WebKit test with two loopback servers shows that without the rules an image and a fetch reach the other port, and with the rules neither does while the admitted page still loads. Related Access, Settings hub, proxy auth, Terminal hub and render-smoke suites pass on iPhone and iPad simulators (Xcode 27.2). - Full `OpenClawTests` on the iPad Pro 13-inch simulator: 1241 tests, 1 failure in `WatchApprovalTransportSourceGuardTests` (a source-scan expecting a string not in the source; no Watch files changed here). - `docs/platforms/ios.md` documents the embedded-page behavior behind Access. No stored settings, keychain items or schemas changed, so an upgrade keeps existing Gateway settings and Access grants. - Strict SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 are clean on the changed files. An existing `function_body_length` violation in `AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift` is unrelated. - Device builds used a free personal team with push and HealthKit entitlements removed. Redacted trace from the live WebKit test (loopback fixtures, no real endpoints): ``` ACCESS-PROOF signed in: admitted authority received the cookie=true, other port requests=0 ACCESS-PROOF after sign out: cookie sent=false, other port requests=0 ``` Gaps: the old single-message screen from the base commit is not captured as a before image; expiry while connected and multi-gateway isolation were not exercised on device; the implicit-port case is covered by the rule table test, not a live request (ports 80 and 443 cannot be bound in a test). ## Screenshots All captured on physical devices against a real Cloudflare Access gateway (iPad Pro 11-inch M4 and iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.2). Gateway host, chat titles, usage totals, automation names and the shell prompt are blurred. **Signed in: embedded pages load** (before this change these pages showed only "This Dashboard needs a browser session" or loaded without an Access cookie). iPad: Usage, Automations, Terminal, Desktop iPhone: Usage, Automations, Terminal, Desktop **After sign-out.** Signing out of Access disconnects the gateway, so the app lands on its existing native offline screens (Usage and Automations show Gateway settings; Terminal shows its own "needs a connected gateway" screen). No embedded page stays usable. **New fallback screen** (rendered in the iPad simulator from the app's own view; on a device it appears only when the gateway is connected but the grant is missing or Access refuses the browser session, which is hard to trigger by hand). Left: sign-in required. Right: Access refused the session. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(cli): stop status/channels list/doctor emitting Matrix SDK deprecation warnings
prs.body:
Fixes #190243

## What Problem This Solves

On an install with no Matrix configured, `openclaw status`, `openclaw channels list` and `openclaw doctor` each print two `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blaming "Plugin matrix". Core caused them: these async command paths called the sync channel-presence resolvers, which run the bundled `hasAnyMatrixAuth` sync export (`createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore` + `.entries()`).

## User Impact

Users no longer see deprecation noise they can't act on, and plugin authors aren't misled into thinking a third-party plugin needs migrating. Configured-channel detection is unchanged. It still reads saved auth, now through the async `exportNameAsync` probe.

## Why

Async twins already existed (`hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScopeAsync`, `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`, and the Matrix `hasAnyMatrixAuthAsync`). The only change is switching the four call sites, which were already inside `async` functions:
- `src/commands/status.scan-overview.ts`: `hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScopeAsync`
- `src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` (`buildChannelsTable`, also reached by plain `status`): new `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`. It has the same scope and manifest records as the sync resolver and returns the same full resolution (missing ids, load failures).
- `src/commands/channels/list.ts` and `src/commands/doctor-security.ts`: `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`

The sync compatibility exports are left alone until their 2026-12-31 removal.

## Evidence

Real CLI on Linux, fresh `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`, built from this branch.

Before (main):
```
$ openclaw status   (same for channels list, doctor)
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin matrix: createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore is deprecated; use createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2 …
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: PluginStateSyncKeyedStore.entries is deprecated; …
```
After:
```
$ openclaw status          exit=0 stdout_lines=139 DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
$ openclaw channels list   exit=0 stdout_lines=5   DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
$ openclaw doctor          exit=0 stdout_lines=355 DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
```
`--trace-deprecation` before the fix showed the call chains `statusCommand → collectStatusScanOverview → buildChannelsTable / hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScope`, `channelsListCommand → listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` and `collectSecurityWarnings → listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig`, all ending at `hasAnyMatrixAuth`.

Tests:
- New `src/channels/plugins/read-only.async-presence.test.ts`: a bundled plugin declares both sync and async persisted-auth exports. The async resolver detects the saved auth and never calls the sync export.
- Updated mocks in the status, channels list and doctor-security tests to the async APIs, so a reintroduced sync call fails.
- `vitest`: channels.list*, doctor-security, status*, status-all/channels, read-only*: 38 files, 346 tests passed. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean, and `pnpm build` is green.


### Base-red / head-green replay (head `efa00bf`)

Same 4 regression files, run with `vitest run`. Only the 5 non-test source files were reverted to the merge base `f7d6774` for the base run; the tests are unchanged.

| Run | Source | Test files | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | `f7d6774` source + PR tests | 4 failed | 48 failed / 48 |
| Head | `efa00bf` | 4 passed | 48 passed / 48 |

Base failure modes:
- `read-only.async-presence.test.ts`: `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync is not a function`. Base has no async full-resolution path, so `status` can only take the sync Matrix probe.
- `channels.list`, `status-all/channels`, `doctor-security`: base calls the sync `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` / sync resolver, and the async-only mocks reject it (`No "listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig" export is defined on the mock`). This is the guard that fails if a sync call comes back.


### Command-level warning capture (`src/commands/channels.list.dep-warning.test.ts`)

This runs the real `channelsListCommand` (`openclaw channels list --json`) against an on-disk config and a bundled channel fixture with saved auth. The fixture's legacy sync auth probe emits `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` the way Matrix's does, and its async probe is silent. The test watches both `process.emitWarning` and the process `warning` event and asserts that no `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warning is emitted.

Base source (`f7d6774`'s `read-only.ts`, `channels/list.ts`, `status-all/channels.ts`, `status.scan-overview.ts`, `doctor-security.ts`) with the new test:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'DEP_PLUGIN_SDK' ] to not include 'DEP_PLUGIN_SDK'
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

Head `708a05f`:

```
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

### ✨ Terminal recording (real built CLI, Linux)

Built with `scripts/build-all.mts`, then ran `node openclaw.mjs channels list` and `node openclaw.mjs status` with a fresh HOME/state dir and an explicit `{}` config (`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`). Base `f7d6774` prints 2 `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` DeprecationWarnings per command; the same steps rebuilt from PR head `708a05f` print 0, exit 0.

![channels list / status: base shows DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, head shows none](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/d1cbdb648d5599cdb8a098fea5f767e4b496dfe6/proofs/190257-dep-warning.gif)

prs.title: feat(ios): prepare secure ESP device provisioning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app needs the SDK and protocol foundation to configure native ESP devices securely from a phone.

## User Impact

This first stage prepares the dependency and wire layer. The native setup entry and full phone workflow follow separately; physical Bluetooth qualification remains planned for the Studio.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vendor the pinned official ESPProvision source and require Security2 counter-IV metadata before requesting credentials or beginning a handshake. Preserve vendor cryptography, pin its SwiftProtobuf runtime, include the redistributed licenses, and add the firmware-compatible discovery/frame/request/response codec.

## Evidence

- Actual ESPProvision and pinned SwiftProtobuf compile for the arm64 iOS simulator. The SDK advertisement regression compiles against those actual modules and is included in the existing OpenClawTests target.
- Six native wire tests pass: independent firmware vectors, full-width generations, malformed frames, raw SSIDs, receipt observations, and distinct discovery input.
- Scoped SwiftFormat, staged content/privacy and diff checks pass. The native localization inventory was regenerated and verified through the qualified tooling owner.
- Local autoreview (Codex), complete committed range d56403f0c3c25e5d579ba26d49db12b26ece6814 to 44a48fbc64d2f6024ab8a238a73a5e52f8362dde, P0–P2, two complete passes: no actionable findings. Fresh independent integration review also found none. The own-change simplification pass kept this to the dependency and codec stage; the large source import is immutable vendor code.
- Local SDK XCTest execution stopped before compilation because Xcode stalled in compiler metadata collection; this is an environment gap, not a passing test run. Native app CI remains required. The unrelated protocol freshness command also lacked matching local Node dependencies; no dependency guard was changed or bypassed.

The first native screenshot build exposed SwiftLint’s failable Data-to-String requirement in the new label decoder. The correction rejects malformed UTF-8 device labels; the extended existing wire regression fails before the fix and all six tests pass after it. Scoped production SwiftLint and two-file SwiftFormat pass, and fresh independent review of this corrective delta found no P0–P2 issues. The SDK XCTest execution gap remains explicit: existing native CI compiles this class but its lifecycle selectors need the subsequent session-stage update to execute it.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Chrome debugger attachment when users inspect an idle browser profile or list profiles.

Supersedes #145864, thanks @mastertyko.

## User Impact

Status and profile listing no longer start Chrome MCP, create extension relays, enumerate tabs through Playwright, or open CDP WebSockets. Explicit start/use still attaches normally. Live readiness and graphics inspection remain available through `browser doctor --deep`.

MCP and shared-relay tab counts reflect the last explicit tab observation and can be zero before first use; owned relays retain current passive counts. WebSocket-only remote endpoints without HTTP discovery cannot establish running status through passive inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the selected MCP session and existing relay metadata at the status owner, and use HTTP inventory for CDP discovery. Remove the superseded active enumeration, MCP page probe, and status deadlines. Production code decreases by 13 lines; four net regression lines have a dedicated test-budget allocation. No new configuration, stored state, or relay protocol.

## Evidence

- Main `928818442b99b6daf992e2f0472f54d535c3a271`: both boundary regressions fail (idle MCP status attaches; extension listing calls Playwright).
- Candidate: **82 tests passed across six named files** in 43.38 seconds wall (Vitest 41.52 seconds), covering passive status/list, explicit use, session cleanup, extension readiness, and config refresh. New status regressions execute in milliseconds; the unchanged extension readiness timeout accounts for about 8 seconds.
- Touched-file lint and formatting pass on Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41565845670)). Broad validation is PR CI.
- Independent local `autoreview` of the complete candidate against `928818442b99b6daf992e2f0472f54d535c3a271`: **scoped-clean**, P0–P3, no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute tests; execution evidence above is from Testbox.
- Browser launcher and MCP/CDP clients are mocked. No Chrome or Playwright browser was launched. Contributor code was read through `gh` and was never checked out or executed.

CI follow-up: preserve the real exports in the two status-test module mocks. The affected file passes **4/4 tests** (38.98 seconds wall, 37.18 seconds Vitest), touched-file lint, and formatting on [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41572233697). A follow-up P0–P3 autoreview of this repair returned scoped-clean. Production code is unchanged.

Hosted ClawSweeper produced no verdict because its input-safety check rejected the revision. Maintainer inspection of the candidate found only synthetic credential-like browser fixtures; no scanner policy or hold was changed. Independent local autoreview is the completed review evidence.

prs.title: fix(macos): prevent first-launch Gateway failures after upgrades
prs.body:
Related: #188683 — this is a separate updater repair; no endpoint changes are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app can fail its first launch after an upgrade by starting an old Gateway after credential preparation has migrated state beyond that Gateway's supported schema.

## User Impact

App-managed profiles can complete the upgraded first launch without Retry, relaunch, manual Doctor, or data reset. Explicit pins, installation ownership, service custody, and schema/integrity refusals remain intact. No new schema, configuration option, dependency, or committed version bump.

The native `doctor --client-credentials` operation now also completes pending local runtime-intent migration; it still does not start/stop services or force a runtime choice. Generic Gateway/node credential callers retain their existing ready fast path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Credential readiness and daemon runtime-pin readiness are independent. The narrow credential Doctor skipped the pin handoff, leaving `migrationPending` after schema advancement. Swift correctly preserves the old seed while that handoff is pending.

The native CLI now waits for the existing daemon migration owner after credential maintenance releases custody, retaining the captured engine selection. This also runs when credentials are already ready after a partial attempt. The existing owner preserves pin bytes/timestamps and refuses conflicts while retaining both stores. Swift activation, seeding policy, and pin formats are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Regression:** two actual credential-cutover cases fail before the repair because intent stays pending, then pass with it. They cover no legacy pin and preservation of a stored pin. An additional already-ready credential/pin-conflict case verifies refusal. These fixtures migrate schema 24 → 39; the real-app proof below starts at 20.
- **Focused tests on refreshed base:** 83 pass: credential suite 23/23, daemon migration suites 17/17 and 5/5, CLI registration 38/38. Wrapper wall time 103.98s; CI seconds unavailable. Seven PostgreSQL-only cases were skipped in the prior-base run, not certified here. New regression cases add about 2.7s test time and a justified 117-line allocation.
- **Static checks on refreshed base:** targeted command/test typecheck, lint, format, whitespace, documentation MDX and test-line budget pass. Broader original docs checks remain prior-base evidence; glossary coverage was skipped for lack of a local merge base.
- **Review:** fresh Auto Review through P2 found no actionable defects against refreshed base `f6efce5707dcdf140bb277b2d3fc7115b912600f`, including integration with its updated async pin-migration owners. The unchanged Swift credential wrapper was supplied context and inspected separately. Review is not native execution.
- **Real first launch:** the requester supplied an isolated macOS release-to-candidate run. This Linux session verified its 39 checksum records, exact patch/manifest identity, process lineage, continuous exec coverage, readiness, and retained-profile facts. Native execution was supplied, not performed by this session.

### Local macOS proof after conflict repair (2026-11-02)

- Head `db14fbef10e5ee80e0bd098fe6e44f65dee2216e` merges main `f68e832179c1`; the sole conflict was `docs/install/updating.md`, resolved by retaining both independent additions. The PR's feature delta is unchanged; no new runtime behavior or tests were added.
- Regression control: with only `startup-client-credentials.ts` restored to main's implementation, all three new cases fail for the intended reasons: both cutovers leave `migrationPending`, and already-ready credentials fail to reject conflicting runtime intent. Restoring the fix makes all three pass.
- Local macOS arm64 focused proof: **83/83 pass** across `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` (23), `register.maintenance.test.ts` (38), `runtime-pin-migration.test.ts` (5), and `state-migrations.daemon-runtime-pins.test.ts` (17). Run via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <these four files> --maxWorkers=1`; wrapper wall time **107.23s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Targeted command/test typecheck, four-file type-aware lint, seven-file formatting, three-page MDX validation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Limits: production-owner integration and CLI registration proof, not a new packaged native-app/Sparkle upgrade run or live PostgreSQL qualification. Prior native proof below remains tied to its original candidate. This mechanical conflict repair does not claim a new independent code review or current-head CI completion.

### Native result — original proof candidate

The base was refreshed only to resolve a documentation conflict. Repair production/test bytes and feature-added/removed lines are unchanged. The macOS run remains evidence for its explicitly pinned pre-refresh candidate, not native execution of the refreshed head.

State migrates **20 → 39** and the source-bound pin receipt completes **before runtime selection**. App PID 12143 starts Gateway PID 12229 with matching candidate Bun, CLI, and SQLite-library identities. Authenticated readiness succeeds and the same approved node reconnects. Config/endpoint, auth/keypair fingerprints, and main pairing identity/grants persist; shared state, client credentials, and daemon control stores all report integrity OK.

**Limits:** one arm64 ad-hoc local replacement with guest-only version 2026.10.10, not signed Sparkle delivery or a full native matrix. The exec trace is continuous through readiness/node connection, with three later gaps during RPC verification. Node-surface metadata refreshes/reapproves automatically, so pairing bytes are not wholly unchanged. Bonjour dependency and transient CPU-degradation warnings remain disclosed; readiness succeeds. No provider turn, live explicit-pin matrix, or pause/quit matrix is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable trace, source binding, and fixture</summary>

Source: base `325d62a031f15f4a271e5f47ae9ad13a79fb7c1b` plus the eight-file patch SHA-256 `f6e03907214f9d94ed4561bbf3bff8ed61b2aa95d9ff4b72aea08ea91fcc69a1`. All eight original proof-candidate file hashes matched the supplied manifest. No endpoint-PR or dependency changes were combined. Guest build ID: `2026.10.10-325d62a031f1-2026-11-02T19-34-34.000Z`; its base commit label alone does not identify the dirty proof candidate.

The official v2026.10.9 release is `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, archive SHA-256 `b13bef633fc60a30bcc903aceaba71ad2a4185fdd6fdb6e0c278d770454577a1`, with verified release signature. Baseline: valid loopback endpoint, task-only auth, approved connected node, integral complete post-pairing database backup. Old app/child/listener stopped before takeover; old seed and schema-20 state retained.

Sanitized returned trace; `<profile>` replaces the disposable guest home:

```text

Candidate Bun/CLI/SQLite hashes match the package; live mappings independently identify candidate Bun and SQLite. Later RPC confirms `ok=true, coreReady=true` and the same node `paired=true, connected=true, approvalState=approved`. Later intent is `known, stored=false`; earlier ordering relies on the receipt/exec trace, not that later read.

Main pairing identity, public key, grants, approval timestamp, and token fingerprint persist. Node-surface capabilities/commands, timestamps, version, and host/permission metadata refresh without manual re-pairing.

This source-only contribution reuses the native inventory, locale refresh publisher and packaged assets. It registers Tauri outputs with the existing publication and invalidation owners, keeps source verification independent, and preserves strict generated checks. The 42-file contribution excludes generated translations and platform resources; the native Gateway driver is unchanged from the integrated upstream base.

Native PT-PT artifact publication and activation need maintainer coordination. This slice does not close the broader localization request.

- The final manager correction restores original raw errors and one/many saved-Gateway labels through the existing catalog mechanism. prs.title: fix(update): avoid snapshot failures in live recovery checks
prs.body:
Fixes #191331

## What Problem This Solves

Update recovery admission and reconciliation can copy an entire SQLite database to read a small amount of metadata. A concurrent checkpoint can invalidate that copy and refuse an update with `wal-copy-unstable`. Async progress bookkeeping can repeat the copy after initial admission.

## User Impact

Qualified live or cleanly closed databases now use the existing isolated metadata reader. Cold, retained, unknown and maintenance-owned sources retain their private-read protections. Metadata inspection grants no execution authority; the updater retains recovery and continuation decisions.

## How It Works

One fixed command reads recovery reservations and companions in the same snapshot. Reconciliation and async progress use that boundary, while the writer still rechecks recovery in its synchronous transaction. Shared recovery facts live in the existing low-level store, avoiding eager update-policy imports from ordinary config and plugin reads.

The worker awaits asynchronous operation preparation while retaining active-work ownership. After lazy loading and before native SQLite access, it rechecks its original physical identity and lifetime. Existing post-read identity checks, transfer cleanup and shutdown settlement remain in place. No schema or configuration changes are introduced.

Compiled finalizer fixtures explicitly include their manifest-selected spawn broker. The fixture copier uses the canonical dist-root resolver for nested entries while retaining mixed-generation refusal and narrow dependency closure. The native wrapper inventory includes the required source closure.

Production growth is net 110 lines for the shared read/lifecycle boundary; test sources add 386 lines. Duplicate reconciliation dispatch is removed. No retries, timeouts or ownership checks are weakened.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the test-only baseline reproduced `wal-copy-unstable` after ten snapshot attempts on Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun. [Baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41491242493/job/125435631746).
- **After:** at `ccd99233779a1f1e74761589ccb21754a317d3f9`, all 15 recovery-admission cases passed on both Node and Bun, including the original live checkpoint-writer case, warm reconciliation, clean close, retained snapshots, retargeting, and pending/orphan recovery refusal. [Regression proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41569389525/job/125699325737).
- The corrected compiled Bun finalizer cases passed with normal cleanup; their shard passed all 62 tests. [Finalizer proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41569389525/job/125699325714). Build Artifacts and Darwin also passed at that head. The tested merge was `e095f4f5cfc4df8095e134fdc5937c5e630228de`, combining main `b571be3ad980307803f343a373275d225466b6d8` and the reviewed head.
- **Final-head qualification passed** at `844995f0c84c6a327fcb7ee54dd243566decd3a9`: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41570732806) (69 passed, 27 skipped), [Build Artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41570732664), and [Darwin](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41570732634). All attempt 1, with no failed or unfinished jobs. The tested merge was `1fe19f0c25db91190895534044a11ed381cbf92e`, parents main `44ea3371d4340868ae53c7c3196f1ffb81940b0f` and this head. The exact-head ClawSweeper review has no findings or before-merge actions.
- Production passed independent source review and six complete structured review passes covering the corrective delta and its owner contracts. Fixture, mechanical lint and overlapping main changes received separate scoped reviews. Signed hooks, targeted formatting, whitespace and the test-line ratchet passed. Source review is separate from runtime proof.

Follow-ups: synchronous runtime-provisioner child-custody observation can still require a private snapshot before service stop; initialization can precede the advertised overall update deadline. This PR does not claim every updater metadata read is copy-free or fix that deadline gap.

prs.title: fix(exec): sessions remain running after the root command exits
prs.body:
Supersedes #147335, thanks @Decent9967.

Related: #147304.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec sessions stay running after their shell exits when a background descendant keeps stdout or stderr open.

## User Impact

Ordinary non-PTY host exec on Linux and macOS completes after root exit and a bounded 250 ms output drain. Later descendant output is discarded; keep work in the shell's foreground when its eventual output is needed. Descendant cleanup, cancellation, and memory ownership remain independent of the terminal result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor already separates the terminal result from descendant extinction. One completion helper uses the adapters' retained root-exit events and the existing output fence for both direct children and service relays. The transport keeps draining under its existing cleanup owner. Completion does not signal the background child. Sandbox/external transports, internal processes, PTYs, Windows, and execution approval checks retain their existing behavior.

Removed the single-use `setForcedReason` wrapper. Production grows by 31 lines for the bounded completion wait; regression coverage grows by 97 lines, with a matching test-line allocation. Keeping the timer in a small helper preserves the supervisor's existing file-size limit.

## Evidence

- Red on main `928818442b99b6daf992e2f0472f54d535c3a271`: both direct and service-relay reproductions of `sh -c "sleep 30 & echo done"` remained pending after two seconds. The fixture descendants were cleaned up after each case. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41565831956).
- Green: the same two real-process cases complete in about 0.3–0.6 seconds while descendant cleanup remains pending. Five focused cases cover tail output, late-output fencing, cancellation before exit and during draining, and unaffected internal/external transports. Final focused run: **7/7 passed**, 37.50 seconds wall time including worker preparation. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41567124880).
- The supervisor, one-shot tool cleanup, and regression files passed **48/48** before the unchanged applicability guard moved into the completion helper. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41566762372).
- Touched-file oxlint: zero warnings/errors. Pinned oxfmt 0.74.0 check and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local autoreview of the final implementation against the pinned main baseline: **scoped-clean through P2**, with full supervisor, adapter, output, and event context. Only test formatting and its line allocation changed afterward. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable.
- Contributor code was read with `gh` and was not executed. Real process proof used a fresh implementation on trusted main in Crabbox; no live Gateway was modified.

prs.title: fix(android): match Control UI page scheme to the gateway socket
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A discovered gateway on a non-loopback address opens a TLS socket even when its Bonjour record omits `gatewayTls`. The Android Control UI page did not use that decision. It chose `http` or `https` only from `endpoint.tlsEnabled`, so the page stayed on cleartext while the socket was TLS.

The Terminal, dashboard, and desktop screens load that page after the operator session connects. The page origin is where the signing bridge answers a challenge. A cleartext page is the wrong origin for a connection the socket policy already refused to leave on cleartext.

Manual LAN cleartext is unchanged. A stored pin still does not upgrade that page to HTTPS, matching the socket. A manual remote host whose cleartext toggle is off stays on HTTPS, also matching the socket.

## Evidence

API 34 emulator, play debug build, head `8f4143070ae`. The production `ControlUiWebView` loaded a page on the emulator's private LAN address `10.0.2.15`. The discovered endpoint had `tlsEnabled` false and no advertised fingerprint. The manual endpoint used the cleartext toggle.

```console
$ adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner
OK (2 tests)

url=https://10.0.2.15:36997
page=https://10.0.2.15:36997/ wss://10.0.2.15:36997 NATIVE_AUTH

url=http://10.0.2.15:34079
page=http://10.0.2.15:34079/ ws://10.0.2.15:34079 NATIVE_AUTH
```

![Discovered LAN page loaded over HTTPS and installed native auth](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/https-discovered.png)

![Manual LAN cleartext page stayed on HTTP](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/http-manual-lan.png)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Control UI WebView origin follows the socket. A discovered private-LAN host with no gatewayTls advertisement loads HTTPS, and the native auth bridge publishes a wss gateway URL. Manual private-LAN cleartext stays HTTP and publishes a ws URL.
- **Real environment tested:** Android emulator API 34 google_apis arm64, play debug app `ai.openclaw.app.debug`, head `8f4143070ae`. The page host is the emulator guest address 10.0.2.15.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Installed the play debug apk and ran `adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The WebView document and the screenshots above. Discovered LAN showed `https://10.0.2.15:36997/` plus `wss://10.0.2.15:36997` and `NATIVE_AUTH`. Manual LAN showed `http://10.0.2.15:34079/` plus `ws://10.0.2.15:34079` and `NATIVE_AUTH`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The production WebView loaded the HTTPS page for the discovered case and the HTTP page for manual cleartext. Both documents received the native auth payload for that origin.
- **What was not tested:** A physical phone. This was not a full OpenClaw gateway login. The page is a local document served to the production WebView so the loaded scheme and the installed auth bridge are visible.

## Summary

The page URL is built from the same TLS decision as the gateway socket. No changelog entry.

prs.title: fix: exec sessions stay "running" when a script backgrounds a child that holds the output pipe
prs.body:
Closes #147304

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec sessions stay in `running` forever when the command backgrounds a child that inherits the session's output pipe.

Example: a script like `nohup sleep 600 | cat &` finishes immediately, but the detached grandchild (`cat`) keeps the session's stdio handles open. Completion waited for the output streams to close, so the session stayed `running` for as long as the grandchild lived — and `process kill` during that window reported `No active session found`, leaving no way to stop the children.

## User Impact

Sessions now settle once the main command exits with its real exit code and the output goes idle — even when a detached grandchild keeps the output pipe open. (Whether a still-running detached descendant can be cancelled after settlement is part of the owner decision requested below — this PR does not change kill/cancel semantics.)

Behavior notes:
- While output keeps flowing after the main command exits, the drain keeps going (the cap only fires once output goes idle), so active producers are not truncated mid-stream.
- Output written by detached children after the settle fires is no longer captured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Settlement previously required both stdio streams to reach end/close. Detached grandchildren inheriting those handles keep them open indefinitely, so `wait()` never resolved.

Per the review decision, settlement is now narrowed instead of applying a blanket deadline to every child: a bounded post-exit drain cap (mirroring the existing Windows forced-close pattern) is scheduled after the root exits, keeps rescheduling while output is still flowing, and only closes the lingering streams once output goes idle. Ordinary children that close their streams on exit keep the previous full-drain behavior. The reported setup (gateway host without a docker sandbox) routes to the direct child adapter changed here; the service-relay adapter is intentionally untouched and can get the same treatment if maintainers want it there too.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` (`post-exit drain settlement for detached grandchildren`):
  - cap fires once output goes idle after the root exits,
  - drain keeps going (no truncation) while a detached descendant is still producing output,
  - suite is self-initializing and passes under a standalone name filter.
- Real-process coverage (no mocks), `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.grandchild-pipe.test.ts`: a real `bash -c "nohup sleep 30 | cat &"` session settles ~250ms after the root exits instead of waiting on the pipe held by the detached grandchild.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` → 42 passed; `child.grandchild-pipe.test.ts` → 1 passed.
- Live observation from #147304: a session sat in `running` for 10 minutes after its script finished and settled only when the detached `sleep 600` expired; `process kill` during that window reported `No active session found`.


### After-fix runtime trace (production adapter, no mocks)

Executed with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` importing `createChildAdapter` from `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts` directly at head `cbef9397`. `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` is unset so the direct POSIX child adapter is selected — the path this PR fixes (the service-relay route stays intentionally out of scope; see the evidence-scope note below). On this head, drain activity is tracked through the capture path: output emitted before capture attaches (trace B, T+6ms) stays buffered and is delivered when capture begins.

```text
--- A: no output before idle (original regression case) ---
[T+  8ms] spawned pid=370475: bash -c "nohup sleep 30 | cat &"
[T+260ms] session settled: {"code":0,"signal":null}    # root long gone, grandchild still held the pipe

--- B: output then idle ---
[T+280ms] stdout <- "stdout-line-captured-by-session"
[T+531ms] session settled: {"code":0,"signal":null}

--- C: delayed writer past the cutoff (bounded-cleanup tradeoff) ---
[T+551ms] stdout <- "early-line"
[T+803ms] session settled: {"code":0,"signal":null}    # streams close at settlement; later output is not delivered
```

Both runs settle on the idle cap ~250ms after the root's exit while the detached grandchild (`sleep 30`) is still alive and holding the pipe. On the pre-fix build the same sessions remain "running" until the grandchild exits on its own (30s here; minutes-to-hours for longer-lived descendants).

## Output-Cutoff Policy

- After the root process exits, once both output streams have been idle for `POST_EXIT_CLOSE_SETTLE_MS` (250ms), the adapter settles the run with the root's observed exit state and closes the session's stdout/stderr streams.
- Output a detached descendant writes after the cutoff is not delivered: the run's outcome is determined by the root command, and the session must not stay pinned open by a pipe held by an untracked descendant. (Preserving it end-to-end is the Option B contract change described below.)
- The descendant process itself is unaffected by the cutoff: it keeps running and exits on its own. The cutoff does not reap it, and whether the session owner can still cancel it after settlement is part of the decision requested below.
- This matches the existing Windows forced-close settlement (`scheduleForcedWindowsCloseSettlement`) destroy-then-settle pattern.
- The alternative — draining until the pipe reaches EOF — is precisely the defect in #147304: a descendant like `nohup sleep 600 | cat` holds the pipe indefinitely, so the session never completes.


## Evidence scope

- The traces above exercise the direct POSIX child adapter only — the route the reported deployment uses. They do not claim to repair the intermittent "No active session found" kill response from #147304, and they do not cover the service-relay adapter (`OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` route), which stays intentionally out of scope for this PR.

## Output-cutoff tradeoff — owner decision requested

The idle cutoff settles a run 250ms after the root exits once output goes idle. Two behaviors are possible at that point; this PR implements Option A and can switch to Option B if preferred:

- **Option B (explored; requires supervisor-level changes): settle without destroying.** At the adapter boundary this preserves delayed writes (verified at `dd06a054`: a line written ~750ms after settlement was still captured), but review of that head established that supervised settlement fences output and releases cleanup ownership — `kill()` becomes a no-op and the supervisor's disposal closes the pipes — so delivering Option B end-to-end means separating result settlement from cleanup ownership in the supervisor. That contract change is exactly the owner decision requested here.
- **Option A (implemented): destroy the streams and settle.** Bounded resource retention; the run and its pipes are fully closed at the cutoff. Tradeoffs: output a descendant writes after the cutoff is discarded, a still-writing descendant can hit EPIPE/SIGPIPE, and a settled run can no longer be cancelled later — the descendant is left to exit on its own.

Option A is implemented on this head as the stable default. Option B is not an adapter-local change — it requires the supervisor settlement/cleanup contract change described above — so it can ship only on an owner call.


## CI note

Compact shards on this PR's heads have repeatedly failed in modules this diff does not touch — `src/gateway/server-plugins.startup-error.test.ts` earlier, and now `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` ("covers plugin CLI sources in the Docker plugin sweep", a Docker/ClawHub fixture assertion). This PR's diff is limited to `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts` and its two test files; the failing areas share no code path with it, so these read as unrelated timing/environment failures — happy to rerun on request.

## Rev 8 follow-up: termination cleanup ownership (P1) fixed

`4abf0878` — a requested termination (any signal) now marks the adapter and disarms the normal-exit idle cap, and the cap refuses to schedule once termination was requested. A cancelled run with a detached pipe holder can no longer have cleanup resolved by the 250ms settle shortcut while the supervisor still owns escalation; the hard-kill fallback keeps settling the wait on its own schedule.

Regressions cover both orderings:

- `SIGTERM` before the root exits → the idle cap never settles; the escalated hard kill settles via its fallback.
- Root exits first (cap armed) → a cancellation inside the idle window disarms the cap.

Full `vitest.process.config.ts` shard: 648 passed, 0 failed (the one suite-level import error in `supervisor.one-shot-tools.test.ts` reproduces on the clean base of this checkout and is environment-related, not from this branch).

## Owner decisions requested (unchanged, restated for convenience)

1. **Normal-exit output cutoff default.** After the root exits and output goes idle for 250ms (mirroring `FORCED_WINDOWS_CLOSE_SETTLE_MS`), the lingering streams close and settle the session with the root's real exit code. Descendant output written after that is not captured, and late writers can observe EPIPE. Alternatives if the default is too aggressive: raise the idle window, or gate the cutoff behind an opt-in while keeping the pre-PR hang for opted-out callers.
2. **Scope.** The change targets the direct child adapter (the reported gateway-host-without-sandbox path). The service-relay adapter is intentionally untouched and can adopt the same cap if maintainers want parity.

prs.title: fix(redact): don't redact non-sensitive storage.encryption values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`redactSnapshot` was masking every `storage.encryption` string that looked sensitive, even when the value is ordinary encryption configuration rather than a credential. That hid useful diagnostics in config snapshots and made support harder.

This patch only redacts a candidate string when the value is concrete-sensitive **and** the key is either marked sensitive by a hint or sits on a sensitive path, so genuine credentials stay masked while harmless configuration remains readable. Ref #176229.

## Evidence

- Traced `redactValue()` through the config snapshot path: `storage.encryption` values without a sensitive hint or sensitive path now pass through unchanged, while hint-marked values still resolve to `[REDACTED]`.
- The existing config tests and lint/typecheck jobs pass on this revision; the change is limited to the redaction predicate.

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.
