prs.title: fix(tts): speak an answer that carries a picture instead of dropping its voice
prs.body:
Closes #142188

> **Rebased onto current `main` again (2026-11-02, `796b1471345`).** The branch was
> ~4,800 commits behind. One conflict, in `dispatch-from-config.tts.test-support.ts`:
> kept the media guard in the mocked synthesizer, because the supplement tests depend on
> it. Two rebase adaptations beyond the mechanical ones:
> - `main` replaced `resolveStatusTtsSnapshot` with `resolveTtsSettingsSnapshot`, which
>   changed the captioned-final deferral: with `tts.auto` unset it now reads `off`, so the
>   streamed-answer test sets `tts.auto: "always"` explicitly. Behaviour is unchanged.
> - Upstream growth pushed `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` over the 700-line cap, so
>   `withInheritedSupplementMetadata` and `resolveMediaFinalTtsText` moved to the sibling
>   `dispatch-from-config.media-tts-supplement.ts`.
>
> Local on this head: targeted suites 407/407, core and core-test typechecks, line-cap
> ratchet and lint green.

### Current status (2026-11-02)

ClawSweeper re-review: **0 code findings**, `proof: sufficient`, patch 4/6.

CI on `89672c0`: 64 pass. The only red lanes are `main` regressions, not this diff:
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7` — the lease fixture in
  `deliver-queue.lease-integration.test.ts` (`preserves lost ownership during provider`),
  already being fixed upstream in #190934;
- `checks-node-changed-boundary` — the boundary scan flags
  `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` (main commit `91f4975` imports
  `extensions/baseten/decision-provider.runtime.js`); this PR changes neither file.

This branch's own lanes pass. Waiting on the owner decision below. The branch already
carries the live-only behaviour; on approval of option 2 I will add the restart test
that proves a recovered queue never replays the audio (and name the signal if the review
wants it separate from `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with auto-TTS enabled would receive no voice message at all
when the assistant's answer carried an attachment. A reply that says something *and*
shows a chart arrives silent: no audio, no error, nothing in `doctor`. The same text
without an attachment is spoken normally, so the feature disappears exactly when the
assistant illustrates its answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`maybeApplyTtsToPayloadCore` skips synthesis whenever the payload already carries media.
That guard is correct and stays: on success the same function writes the audio into
`mediaUrl`, so removing it would overwrite the picture. One message carries one media
set — `ttsSupplement` holds only `spokenText` and a flag, not a second set.

So the answer is spoken by a **second message** instead. A final that carries non-audio
media is delivered untouched; afterwards its text is synthesized separately and sent as
an audio-only payload marked
`markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement(…, { visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true })`. This is the
mechanism `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` already uses for deferred final text; only
the entry condition is new.

Audio versus non-audio is decided by `hasNonAudioMediaReference`, built on the shared
media table (`isAudioFileName`), so a reply that already carries a voice note gets no
second one. Legacy `MEDIA:` directives participate in that classification and are
stripped from the spoken copy while staying in the visible message. Only speech-related
metadata (`tts`, `ttsExplicit`, `commandReply`) is inherited by the synthesized payload,
so command replies stay silent and delivery ownership is not transferred.

Boundaries: the ACP delivery coordinator has its own synthesis application and is not
touched here; the same branch can be added there if maintainers want it.

**Note for channel authors:** this makes a case reachable that previously only appeared
on channels with captioned-final delivery — a final that carries media and no text.
Such a payload is marked `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` and must not be read as "no answer
was produced". Our own VK channel plugin did read it that way and deleted the message
holding the answer; the flag is what tells them apart.

## Supplement lifetime: live-only

The supplement is optional audio that repeats an answer already delivered, and its writer
fence is the in-memory `sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority` it inherits. Durable recovery
cannot rebuild that fence — the supplement owns no pending-final completion of its own —
so a persisted row could replay the audio after the writer was replaced.

It therefore carries `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`, and the queue boundary in
`deliver-queue.ts` refuses to persist such a payload, next to where `skipQueue` is
consumed. That placement is layer-independent: both the routed and the channel-local lane
reach it, as does any caller of `deliverOutboundPayloads`. The normalizer
`getReplyPayloadTtsSupplement` preserves the flag, since delivery reads the lifetime from
the normalized supplement.

What this costs: a Gateway restart between the picture and its voice loses the audio. The
answer it repeats has already been delivered and recorded, so nothing the user needs
disappears. The alternative — an independently fenced durable completion — would need a
second owner of the session's pending final, which is a change to session delivery
ownership for the sake of optional audio; that decision is the maintainer's.

## User Impact

An answer that comes with a picture is now also spoken: the picture arrives in its own
message, the voice follows in the next one. Answers that already carry audio, command
replies, and replies without attachments behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**The guard is unconditional — real synthesis path, no channel, no TTS mocks**
(`src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts`, synthetic speech provider):

| payload | synthesis called |
|---|---|
| text + PNG / JPEG / PDF / MP4 / Opus | no |
| text + several attachments | no |
| text + legacy `MEDIA:` line | no |
| **same text, no attachment** | **yes** — control |

**Delivery, through `dispatchReplyFromConfig`** — 19 attachment formats plus edge cases:
mixed attachments, audio-only sets, a caption-less picture, `isError` payloads, non-final
TTS modes, two finals in one turn, a streamed answer ending in a picture, command replies
with and without an explicit speech request, and synthesis failure. Every case first
asserts the visible message survives untouched.

**The regression test fails without the fix:** stashing only `finalize.ts` turns
"speaks a picture answer as a separate voice message" red while the rest stay green.

**Writer authority is preserved and enforced.** A settled final can carry
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, and an absent authority reads as authorized at every
check, so the supplement inherits it — while transcript and completion ownership stay
with the visible message. Three dispatch tests pin the boundary:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| writer still holds the turn | picture, then its voice supplement |
| writer replaced while the supplement is being synthesized | picture only — the audio is rejected before transport |
| replaced writer, ordinary settled final (pre-existing test) | not dispatched, unchanged |

The middle case is the one this PR had to earn: the first attempt attached the authority
to the synthesis input instead of the delivered payload, and since that metadata lives by
object identity it never reached the send path. The test failed until the authority moved
onto the payload that is actually sent.

**Speech comes from the prepared text.** `sendFinalPayload` now reports the text it
prepared for delivery — normalization applied and deferred block text merged, TTS not yet
run — and the supplement synthesizes that, reading it after the media pass so a rewritten
or cleared caption is what gets spoken. A recording cannot be normalized after the fact.

**A supplement follows only a message the recipient can see.** Eligibility is decided by
the outcome of preparation and delivery, not by the raw reply:

| situation | supplement |
|---|---|
| final delivered (queued or routed, settled) | yes |
| final deduped against a block that was delivered | yes |
| block vetoed by the channel (`channel-transform`) | no |
| visible answer failed to route | no |
| preparation cleared the caption (media pass, channel transform) | no — an empty prepared text says "say nothing" |
| queued answer cancelled in `beforeDeliver` | no |
| queued answer suppressed as a channel transform | no |
| answer delivered but not visibly (`visibleReplySent: false`) | no |
| settlement could not complete within its bound | no |

Admission is not visibility, so eligibility is decided after `turnLedger.settleQueued`,
the same bounded wait the no-visible-reply gate uses — but this gate fails closed. The
neighbouring gate treats admission as the strongest fact because uncertainty there must
not produce a duplicate message; here uncertainty must not produce a voice note that
arrives alone. Both answer "stay quiet"; only the reasoning differs, and the code says so.

**Runs** (Node 24.20.0):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | pass |
| `auto-reply-reply` shard | 223 files, 5474 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts` | 11 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/media/audio.test.ts` | 13 tests, 0 failures |
| `pnpm build`, `pnpm check` | pass |
| `autoreview` (claude, P2) | no accepted findings |

**Live traffic**, one install, before and after (redacted, hashed peer ids):

```
before   11:36:01  deliver kind=final len=758 media=true
         11:36:02  vk upload ok kind=photo
         11:36:03  vk upload ok kind=photo          ← no synthesis in the turn

after    15:43:54  deliver kind=final len=621 media=true
         15:43:55  vk upload ok kind=photo
         15:43:57  tts synthesize: format=ogg, size=385395
         15:43:57  deliver kind=final len=0 media=true
         15:43:59  vk upload ok kind=audio          ← voice as its own message
```

Docs updated: `docs/tools/tts.md` described the old behavior in both the rule list and
the decision tree.

## Plugin compatibility

Channel plugins see a new message shape: a final that carries media and no text. It is
marked `ttsSupplement.visibleTextAlreadyDelivered`, which is exactly the signal that tells
it apart from "no answer was produced".

Our own VK plugin got this wrong at first and deleted the message holding the answer,
because its progress-draft finalizer read an empty final as "no answer came". The repair
was to check the flag — not to work around the core — and it is a five-line guard plus
seven regression tests in that plugin. We report it because it is the upgrade risk a
reviewer should weigh: plugins that infer "no answer" from empty final text need that
one check. Plugins that only deliver what they are given need nothing.

## Open question for maintainers: durable recovery of the supplement

This is the one finding we have not implemented, because both ways to close it change a
contract that is yours to set. Everything below is what we traced; we are happy to build
whichever you choose.

**The gap.** `buildRecoveryDeliverParams` installs the writer fence
(`assertDirectAdapterHandoff` / `onPlatformSendDispatch`) only when the queued entry has a
`pending-final` `deliveryCompletion`, and reads the authority from that record alone. The
supplement carries its authority in payload metadata, which is process-local, and has no
completion of its own. If the process stops after the supplement is enqueued and the
session writer is replaced before recovery runs, the recovered audio sends unfenced.

**Why the supplement has no completion.** Reusing the visible answer's receipt would give
a second message the first one's delivery ownership — the mistake this PR was already
corrected for in an earlier round. So the choice is a new receipt or no recovery at all.

**Option 1 — give the supplement its own `pending-final` completion.** This is more than a
field: a completion is a durable record with a lifecycle (`prepared` → `queued` →
`delivered` / `suppressed` / `unknown`, settled through `settlePendingFinalDelivery`).
Minting one per supplement means new rows in that store and a new owner obligation to
settle them on every path, including failure. `AGENTS.md` asks contributors to agree
material persistent-store changes before implementing them, which is why we stopped here
rather than guessing at the shape.

**Option 2 — keep the supplement out of durable recovery.** Our preference, and the one
ClawSweeper now recommends ("Approve live-only supplements: add a narrowly scoped
non-recoverable delivery path"). A voice note lost to a restart is a small loss, while one
that outlives its writer is exactly what the fence exists to prevent.

We re-checked whether an existing signal already expresses it, so the ask is not for
something already there. `OutboundDeliveryQueuePolicy` is `required | best_effort`, and
`best_effort` is about how a failure is treated, not about persistence: recovery carries
the policy forward (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts` reads `entry.queuePolicy ?? "best_effort"`)
and replays such entries like any other. There is no admission bypass for an optional
send. So live-only needs a new signal, however small, and that is a contract addition.

**What is already fenced.** The live path: the supplement inherits
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, it is attached to the delivered payload rather than the
synthesis input, and a replacement during synthesis is covered by a regression test. Only
the recovered path is open.

Tell us which option you want — or a third we have not seen — and we will implement it in
this PR. If you approve option 2, we will add the narrowest signal that expresses "do not
recover this send", thread it from the supplement through admission, and cover it with a
restart test that asserts the recovered queue never replays the audio.

## Related

- #42539 asks for text and voice as separate messages as a general Telegram delivery
  option. Different problem — there the answer is spoken and the split is a preference;
  here synthesis never runs. The mechanism is the same one, so that option could be
  built on this branch.
- #132736 (closed) covers auto-TTS supplement messages on Signal — separate voice
  messages are an existing shape in the core, not a new one.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add manifest-backed recommended prompts
prs.body:
### WebKit fixture follow-up

Latest head: [b0f873ec47b44](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b0f873ec47b449bbe3181b9ca1c4bb4475266a42). The preceding CI completed all source, platform and performance lanes but exposed an overlay browser fixture recording an ambient pointer event during awaited popover opening. Injecting that same unrelated setup event reproduces the exact extra policy/div assertion failure on WebKit. The fixture now starts its ledger after opening; the once-only delivery, real closed-root target, policy-before-control order and open-state assertions are unchanged. All 28 Chromium/WebKit cases pass. Production code is unchanged; the measured test allocation includes the two fixture lines (1113 total).

The previously accepted auto request was retired through native recovery before this repair was published. Current-head CI and native replacement admission are still required; this is not a merged/green claim.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors need complete starter requests on their detail page. Selecting one should reuse the normal installation/enabling and consent flow, then open a new editable plugin-scoped draft without sending it.

## User Impact

Users can select a complete author-written starter, complete ordinary installation/consent, and edit the resulting unsent draft. The recommendation panel now leaves the metadata rail clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional recommendedPrompts metadata with up to three author-written strings across native manifests, supported bundles, installed inspection, discovery and the registry consumer. Invalid optional declarations are ignored as a whole; only outer whitespace is trimmed, preserving complete internal text and newlines.

The selected bracket-free Ember panel follows the live primary theme color while retaining neutral texture, logos and white author text. The native textarea remains the editing/sending owner; branded references yield to native text on overflow and composition. A page-owned intent coordinates existing lifecycle/session owners and permanently retires abandoned launches.

### October 29 rail correction

The recommendation slot now belongs to the existing detail main column, not above the main/sidebar grid. Desktop Downloads/Categories retain a clear independent rail; narrow layouts stack the metadata below. No width hack or new layout owner was added. Pages without a sidebar still use the full main width.

Original rail-fix integration: [029164693931](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0291646939312098c930eb462f788123e25ecd38), incorporating target [3a0d1de6c33d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3a0d1de6c33d6839b1ad16b058e09ffc181fa74f). Four actual integration conflicts were resolved and independently reviewed. Current main's retired disclosure removal, pane-layout observer/canonical compact reset and updater install interlock are preserved; the recommendation callbacks and single install owner remain intact.

## Evidence

### Current Before/After Proof

Actual compiled Control UI, Chromium, synthetic Calendar Plus and mock Gateway. The same fixture/theme/viewport is used. The baseline is the earlier PR; the after capture includes current main's header policy, which removed the older code/trust notice. The mobile capture focuses on the recommendation panel and metadata stack.

Before the rail correction:

![Before: recommendations span the metadata area](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39496503-3578-465a-90dc-718ecd14ecd9)

Current integrated layout:

![After: recommendations stay in the main column](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2def3de-80b8-4a57-b6d5-5b5767871ec5)

Mobile panel and metadata stacking:

![Mobile: full prompt text with metadata below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8aa17c4-7d9c-4dfc-8e3c-9a120969fab6)

### Verification

- A real-shell browser regression fails on the earlier markup because the panel is outside main; five layout cases pass on the repair, covering 1440/1366/768/390 widths and no-sidebar behavior.
- The integrated candidate passes 26 focused layout/theme/consent/routing tests, all 10 compiled-UI install/chat workflow regressions, scoped type-aware lint, UI typecheck and i18n baseline checks.
- Workflow cases cover consent, failure/retry, needs-setup entry, unchanged existing drafts, duplicate prevention, agent/route/reconnect retirement and native overflow/composition fallback. No automatic sends are allowed.
- Independent bounded rail and integration reviews found no issues. The earlier local review found an abandoned-launch revival bug; its actual red regression and permanent intent-owner repair are retained.
- Earlier metadata/cross-repository and isolated real-Gateway enable/session/draft evidence remains prior-revision evidence, not a claim of a fresh provider/native-app run. The registry producer and bundled prompt rollout are separate work.

### Current CI allocation follow-up

The 0875 CI attempt completed with all runtime/platform/architecture/performance lanes passing; the sole failure was a 41-line test allowance shortfall after the CI base advanced. The allocation now covers exactly the feature’s 1111 added test lines, which the ratchet verifies against its delta. No assertions or global scalar baseline changed, and no runtime code changed. Current-head CI is pending; no merged/green claim is made.

### November 2 ratchet follow-up

Latest head: [f9077d367e491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f9077d367e491b800d7f5efa8a7055e1d4e1bc8c). Runtime and assertion bytes are unchanged from the reviewed 0875 revision; the follow-up only binds the existing test coverage to its full measured allocation. The first repaired CI pass exposed three pre-existing-at-cap files growing by this feature. The follow-up keeps the optional metadata assignment in the existing catalog projection, moves named install-action schemas into a coherent sibling while preserving public exports, and places the advisory plugin draft layer with its native textarea owner. No line cap or startup budget was raised. Prediction rendering was not split into an extra component.

The native line-cap guard passes. A justified 1111-line test allocation covers the full measured feature coverage rather than borrowing moving main headroom; it covers for the feature's distinct metadata, consent/retry/intent-retirement, native-editing, theme and responsive regressions; no assertions or coverage were removed. Remaining ratchet checks passed. Protocol/catalog tests and 13 prediction/widget/recommendation E2E scenarios pass after these changes. Bundle startup, chat-boot, total CSS, and all other absolute budgets pass.

The current-head hosted review and fresh CI are still required. The prior head's hosted review completed with no actionable findings. Its Android job failed resolving the existing JUnit 1.13.3 dependency before device tests; Android inputs are unchanged. prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # media.test.ts + replay-safety.test.ts: 50 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # tool-media-payloads.test.ts: 24 passed
```

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

```
$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
(no issues)
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"
check fails in this checkout, but it fails identically (same file list,
same counts) on unmodified `upstream/main` with these two files stashed
out — it's flagging pre-existing large files unrelated to this change,
not anything this PR touches.

`tsgo --noEmit` on the `extensions/codex` project reports 1618 errors in
this checkout, all `TS2307: Cannot find module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/*'`
(missing generated plugin-sdk type declarations from a partial/source-only
dependency setup) plus pre-existing `any`/`unknown` findings in unrelated
files (e.g. `src/supervision-tools.ts`, `src/session-cli.ts`). Confirmed
the exact same 1618-error count with this branch's two files stashed out
against unmodified `upstream/main` — the type-resolution gap is an
environment limitation of this sandbox, not something introduced here.

Was not able to run a live Codex app-server round-trip in this sandbox (no
Codex credentials/harness available here); the evidence above proves the
event-projection behavior through the same test harness and fixtures the
existing `image_generation_call` regression tests in this file use.

prs.title: feat(workboard): make card note and comment URLs clickable
prs.body:
Closes #141472 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Workboard users who paste URLs or markdown links into card notes or operator comments would see dead plaintext in the Control UI, even though the notes placeholder already says "Notes, acceptance criteria, links." The same text is shown on compact cards, in the detail drawer, and in the edit-card comment list. Operators currently have to copy the URL out by hand during triage. ## Why This Change Was Made Workboard now linkifies two conservative patterns in notes and comments: - Markdown links: `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` - Bare `http://` and `https://` URLs Links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Other text, including newlines, stays unchanged. This is not full markdown: no bold, lists, headings, images, or HTML, and no `innerHTML`. `javascript:` / `data:` URLs stay plaintext. Balanced parentheses inside a destination are kept, so Wikipedia-style paths such as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)` stay intact in both the markdown and bare-URL forms. Trailing `.,;:!?` on a bare URL stays outside the href. A wrapping `(https://example.com)` still leaves the surrounding parentheses as text. Clicking a link on a compact card does not open the detail drawer (the existing `a` action-target guard). Native `` links remain keyboard-activatable. The edit-card comment list uses the same linker as the drawer, so the three surfaces stay consistent. ## User Impact Operators can click research, docs, PR, and competitor URLs directly from Workboard cards instead of copying them out of notes. ## Evidence **Before** (current Control UI): notes interpolate as escaped plaintext. ![Workboard notes before, with markdown and a raw URL shown as text](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-notes-before.png) **After, production compact card:** markdown labels and bare https URLs become anchors on the real Workboard card renderer. Clicking `Example` opened `https://example.com/` in a new tab and did not open the detail drawer. Dummy fixture only (`example.com` / `example.org`). ![Workboard compact card after, with Example and example.org as clickable links](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-compact-card-after.png) Focused Control UI unit tests passed on this revision: - `vitest --project unit` on `linkify-text.test.ts` and `view.test.ts`, including: - markdown + bare https become `` - balanced parentheses in bare and markdown destinations (`Function_(mathematics)`) - wrapping parentheses around a bare URL stay outside the href - trailing punctuation stays outside autolinked URLs - `javascript:` / `data:` markdown is not turned into anchors - compact-card link click / Enter / Space do not open the detail drawer - edit-modal comments use the same linker This revision also formats the Workboard view files (`oxfmt`) and regenerates `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` so the bundled control-ui asset hash matches the source. Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.2 before this change: card detail notes render as `

${card.notes}

`, so a note such as `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` is escaped text. After this renderer, that note is a real anchor.

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.


---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://claw.seelig.dev/chat/main/dashboard/d32aa602-6464-4f30-80da-8bccb0bd2f3a)

prs.title: fix: reach the configured owner on project-parent sessions_spawn preflight
prs.body:
Closes #182467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: project-attached `sessions_spawn` rejects a plugin-resolved child model (`deepseek/*`, native `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) as `Unknown model` or `selected account or native runtime is unavailable`, even though the agent's configured owner knows the model and a normal session on the same installation accepts it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Child spawned from a project-parent session resolves provider-plugin and native-runtime models the agent's configured owner already knows, without the operator having to detach the project or `/reset` the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A project-parent read supplies the project workspace to `withPreparedModelCatalogOwner({ readOnly: true })`. `resolveReadOnlyPublishedModelCatalogOwner` builds two candidates (`full`, `activationFull`); both carry the explicit project workspace, so the resolver's exact-key lookup misses the single configured owner published at the agent's workspace. The configured-workspace fallback inside `resolvePublishedOwner` is also gated on strict workspace equality, so it misses too. The code then falls through to `acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime`, which builds a runtime-free ephemeral catalog without the provider plugin registry — the plugin's `resolveDynamicModel` hook is never invoked and the model is reported as unknown.

This change narrows the preflight to a third read-only candidate that probes at the agent's **known configured workspace** (resolved via `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir`, not any arbitrary workspace) with every other identity dimension carried from the caller and `env` bound to the effective process environment so the resolver's env match stays exact instead of degrading to the wildcard branch. If the configured workspace is not resolvable, the fallback is suppressed and the existing ephemeral read-only path takes over, preserving the prior behavior for that shape.

Agent, agent-directory, inherited-auth, environment, and generation isolation are preserved exactly. Writable publications and non-read-only paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage in `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:
  - Positive: project-parent read falls back to the configured workspace with agent, agent-dir, env, and workspace identity verified in the fallback input; the fallback carries a plugin-provider model that is absent from the ephemeral read-only snapshot.
  - Negative: when a competing publication matches by workspace but diverges on agent / agent-dir / env, the fallback rejects it and the ephemeral read-only path takes over.
  - Suppression: a workspace-less caller does not synthesize a second workspace-less probe.
  - Guard: when the agent's configured workspace is unknown, the preflight skips the project-parent fallback and lands on the ephemeral read-only build.
- Full targeted test suite (6 files, 119 tests) passes locally:
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.workspace.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.plan.test.ts`

<details>
<summary>Review notes</summary>

Marked draft pending maintainer sign-off on scope. ATX reviews surfaced a residual architectural suggestion to gate configured-workspace reuse behind an explicit, validated project-parent predicate; introducing such a predicate expands scope beyond the acceptance criteria recorded in the issue's Codex review ("preserve agent, account, environment, and generation isolation"; "a focused inventory-owner correction"), so it is deferred.

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): keep metadata inventory deadline in the monotonic clock domain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes healthy update metadata inventories expiring early or receiving an extended deadline when the system clock changes between batches.

## User Impact

Metadata inventory budgets follow elapsed time through wall-clock corrections. Existing budget sizing, batching, cancellation, and database contents remain unchanged. The runtime performing the inventory must contain the fix; a newer candidate cannot change an already-running older updater.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing process-local `monotonicNow()` helper for both aggregate deadline creation and remaining-budget calculation. Keep the existing aggregate-expiration regression on that clock and add a wall-clock rewind regression through the real inventory owner and metadata child.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `113d1f427965b018352665bd6c5983b736f970ea`. No maintainer source fixup or rebase was needed.

- Independent Crabbox AWS proof, run `run_41d0b6758a8ea7dc5b520eb094657a08`: isolated public-network lease, no instance role or Tailscale, no hydration, pinned full head and toolchain. The committed rewind regression **fails on the pre-fix owner**: after a 300,000 ms rewind, the second child budget grows from `2147000000` to `2147300000` ms. The pre-fix owner blob is identical on the PR parent and observed current main.
- Restoring the exact PR owner makes both named suites pass: `pnpm test src/infra/update-candidate-state.sizes.test.ts src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **25/25 passed** under a 240-second command timeout. Changed size suite: 1.968 seconds of test time, rewind case 92 ms. Complete cold Vitest run: 67.48 seconds; wrapper: 70.66 seconds. The selected baseline regression ran under a separate 180-second timeout and failed at its intended budget assertion.
- [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41415464216) completed successfully, including lint, production/test types, owner/consumer tests and security gates. No failed or pending checks. CodeQL's aggregate is neutral because 18 main configurations were not analyzed; this is a coverage limit.
- Independent `autoreview` using Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2 coverage, reviewed the complete parent-to-head two-file change with full owner/test and clock/budget/process context. prs.title: fix(reply): carry the queued chat identity into follow-up tool context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #184730.

A message drained as a native `followup` rebuilt its turn template context from the queued run's routing facts, but never restored the chat identity the source turn was addressed at. `buildEmbeddedContextFromTemplate` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts:288-290`) derives the tool-run `chatId` from `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId`, and `buildEmbeddedAttemptToolRunContext` projects that field as `nativeChannelId` for V2 plugin tools. A queued turn supplied neither field, so V2 plugin tools saw requester / channel / account facts with an absent `nativeChannelId`, while the same message as an immediate turn carried it (and the CLI candidate path already passed `followupRun.originatingChatId` as `chatId`).

The queued run already carries the value: `get-reply-run-execute.ts:501` captures `originatingChatId` as `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId` at enqueue time, and the drain preserves it. Only the follow-up template projection dropped it.

- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts`: `buildFollowupTemplateContext` now publishes `ChatId: queued.originatingChatId`. The shared embedded context keeps its existing preference for `NativeChannelId` and only falls back to `ChatId`, so the follow-up projects the same native conversation as an immediate turn.
- No inference from prompt text, session-key parsing, route relaxation or extra session lookups: a queued turn without an originating chat id still projects none, so an absent identity keeps failing closed.

## Evidence

Red first, on the real follow-up execution owner. Regression added in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts`:

```text
FAIL  src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts > executeFollowupTurn > carries the queued chat identity into the follow-up turn's tool context
AssertionError: expected undefined to be '-1001234567890' // Object.is equality

- Expected:
"-1001234567890"

+ Received:
undefined

 Tests  1 failed | 32 passed (33)
```

The case drives `executeFollowupTurn` with a queued `originatingChatId` and asserts both hops the issue is about: the turn template's `ChatId`, and the `chatId` that `buildEmbeddedRunContext` feeds into the tool-run context (which `nativeChannelId` is projected from). It also asserts the requester stays separate (`SenderId` unchanged), and a second case fixes the fail-closed side: with no queued chat id, both hops stay `undefined`.

Green after the change:

```text
 Tests  33 passed (33)          # src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)          # followup-runner.test.ts + agent-runner-utils.test.ts
```

Verification on this host (`node scripts/...`, portable Node 24.22.2):

- `scripts/test-projects.mts` for the three files above — all passing.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors (259 rules).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` — all matched files use the correct format.
- `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json` — no diagnostic in either changed file. This workspace's installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` is older than current main, so the run stops on four pre-existing errors in unrelated files (`src/agents/host-file-write.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.ts`, `src/infra/private-dir-mode.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.agent-dir-receipt.ts`).
- The e2e lane (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`) needs a full build, which this host cannot produce (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: mode 'preserve'`), so end-to-end shipped coverage is left to CI.

Test-line growth is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/followup-tool-chat-identity.txt` (32 net new test lines, measured after formatting).

## What Problem This Solves

Public conversation documents and media resend unchanged bodies when `If-None-Match` contains a matching weak tag, matching tag list or wildcard.

## User Impact

Valid conditional readers receive bodyless `304` responses instead of downloading unchanged content. Mismatched validators still receive `200` and the current body. Revoked publications still return the normal denial, even for `*` or a previously matching ETag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both guarded response owners now reuse the existing `matchesHttpIfNoneMatch` helper, matching other Gateway HTTP surfaces and RFC 9110 weak comparison. Token/entry authorization, publication/receipt checks, representation currency, secure ingress, MIME policy, CSP and `no-store` are unchanged and still precede conditional success.

Original fix by @Leon-SK668; their original commit is retained. No new helper, SDK export, configuration, schema, permissions, migration or cache lifetime.

## Evidence

Built main `2a3f6f3ae78263fb110f349b866cbcdbc504d948` and candidate runtime artifacts in secretless Linux arm64 Node 24.22.1 Docker, with fresh isolated profiles/state.

- Legitimate media path: authenticated `sessions.create` → normal `chat.send` PNG attachment upload → completed agent turn against a deterministic local HTTP provider → `session.publicShare.set` → anonymous document's media URL. No private transcript write, fabricated token or mocked authorization.
- Initial anonymous image GET: 200, ETag, original 68-byte PNG. Weak/list/wildcard: main twice returns 200/68 bytes; candidate twice returns 304/0 bytes.
- Exact validator remains 304; mismatched validator remains 200 with identical original bytes.
- Official publication revocation: wildcard and prior matching weak ETag return normal 404 denial on both surfaces and both references, never 304 or protected bytes.
- Public document weak/list/wildcard behavior is independently exercised in the same four runs.

- Simplification retains both existing conditional/revocation fixtures without duplicate setup: production +4/-2 (net +2), tests +10/-10 (net 0), docs +3/-0 against merge base. Removed the test-line allocation.

Detailed redacted HTTP output: [independent proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191101#issuecomment-6586345752). This closes the previous review's missing authorized-media entry-point proof; the earlier shortcode-only widget denial was not treated as a successful media reproduction.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores the previous conditional comparison; no persisted-state or public-contract migration. Blast radius is conditional GET handling for public conversation documents and shared media. Authorization and publication revocation remain mandatory before 304 responses.

For the original test, restore that file from `519800ec34033d05f0bc41aa023058cd7ba8d6f9` and use `--testNamePattern 'answer settlement survives'`. The refused-claim control changes only `sessionKey` in `claimPendingAgentQuestionAnswer`; the original control also prints `claimed` before its assertion and uses `--testTimeout 30000`, while the updated control uses `--testTimeout 10000`.

The sibling suite opens a temporary loopback server. A sandbox-denied run failed on `listen EPERM: operation not permitted 127.0.0.1` before its assertions; the reported final result is the rerun with that fixture access. An earlier passing touched-suite run used `/usr/bin/time`, whose own sandboxed `sysctl` failed; its outer exit was `1`, so it is excluded from the passing command result above.

</details>

The tests above prove the in-process production owner, question claim, worker persistence and transcript fence. The shipped Gateway/TUI run below exercises the product entry points separately. Neither reproduces the historical Telegram incident.

### Historical author-reported Gateway and TUI proof, October 19

Built and ran exact head `5d7c8fc5251f2ba497c126671dcbc3a5334a10bf`, tree `7250820b79bc3948dce396bf5354e2b8b6b06369`, on Linux x86_64 with Node `26.8.2` and pnpm `12.11.1`. prs.title: fix(codex): cron runs keep prompt after overload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: isolated Codex-backed jobs can lose their self-contained task prompt when native `turn/start` exhausts ingress-overload retries before accepting the turn.

## User Impact

User impact: transient Codex app-server overloads retry the original task instead of asking for a missing prior transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex app-server error `-32001` is a definite pre-enqueue rejection only when it comes from `turn/start`. The harness now preserves that fact, and the existing transient retry path replays the original prompt only when both the failure-local and aggregate attempt evidence remain replay-safe.

The retry preserves the prior transcript-persistence state. A prompt that was never accepted is written once by the successful retry; an already-persisted prompt remains suppressed to avoid duplication. Other Codex failures and other `-32001` RPCs retain their existing behavior.

The original-prompt replay also carries the classified overload reason into outer retry-limit handling and records the accepted transient-retry diagnostic, matching the common transient recovery path.

## Evidence

### Real Codex recovery proof

A one-shot production-owner harness ran the pinned real `@openai/codex` **0.160.0** app-server over WebSocket. Concurrent native `initialize` traffic filled Codex's real bounded ingress queue; OpenClaw then sent the target `turn/start` through its real transport client. The provider was a local Responses-compatible loopback fixture, so this proof used **no external model/API calls and incurred no model cost**.

Sanitized terminal output:

```text
PR165626_REAL_RUNTIME_PROOF {
  "codexVersion":"0.160.0",
  "rejected":{
    "kind":"turn_start_overloaded",
    "transport":"websocket",
    "threadId":"[REDACTED]",
    "replaySafe":true
  },
  "providerRequestsBeforeRecovery":0,
  "providerRequestsAfterRecovery":1,
  "recoveredPrompt":"PR165626_ORIGINAL_TASK_EXECUTE_EXACTLY_ONCE",
  "assistant":"EXECUTED:PR165626_ORIGINAL_TASK_EXECUTE_EXACTLY_ONCE"
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
Duration    19.34s
real        23.99s
```

This proves the first `turn/start` was rejected before provider execution, recovery resubmitted the exact original task, and the provider executed it exactly once.

### Automated verification

- Exact-head affected suites: **231/231 passed** across recovery-owner, Codex hook, and shared embedded-run integration coverage. Focused wall time: **298.99s**; estimated single-worker CI execution: **~299 CI-seconds** (excluding checkout/install).
- Native proof: **1/1 passed** in **23.99s wall**; estimated single-worker CI execution: **~24 CI-seconds**.
- The real Codex/SQLite two-attempt regression writes exactly one `user` row followed by one `assistant` row.
- The recovery-owner regression proves overload replay carries `lastRetryFailoverReason: "overloaded"` and records `model.recovery.decision` as accepted `transient_retry`.
- Full repository build passed on the preceding behavior-equivalent head, including unified declarations, all 151 public plugin-SDK subpaths, runtime post-build checks, and Control UI.
- Exact-head targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files.
- Independent exact-head Claude review: **APPROVE**, with no P0-P3 findings.

Known validation limitation: the optional repository-wide lint pass was stopped after its type-aware core stripe exceeded the repository's 10-minute no-result threshold. The changed files pass targeted type-aware lint, and the full build/type declaration graph passed.

No gateway, configuration, runtime deployment, scheduler, or product state was changed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce background worker placement overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background worker placement recovery rebuilds full workspace projections for every healthy active placement every minute. Unrelated worker-environment changes also rebuild session identity evidence for every placement.

## User Impact

Reduces background Gateway allocation and CPU while preserving worker loss detection, interrupted workspace recovery, session retirement, and idle suspension.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery discovery already reads move/result/journal membership. Carry that fact into candidate selection and use the placement owner's committed record and the environment owner's current attachment for healthy placements. Only interrupted or unhealthy placements enter full workspace recovery. Worker-environment diagnostics cannot change session identity evidence; pending failed retirement still retries.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before the paired campaign: the real placement runtime startup and scheduled minute sweep, 5,000 synthetic session identities and 200 active remote-exec placements, 5 warmups and 30 measured sweeps per process; five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs separately for untraced CPU/time and GC-inclusive sampled allocation, with baseline A/A controls. Require zero healthy full projection reads, zero identity-evidence subjects for unchanged identities after environment-only publications, lower median allocation and CPU, and no >20% regression in a measured metric. Startup, lost worker, retired session, moves/results/journals, cancellation, and targeted admission remain covered by focused production-owner tests.

The fixture runs local SQLite workers and synthetic provider inspections. No production data or live-service access. Transcript bulk size, btrfs filesystem behavior, remote machines, model calls, and whole-Gateway RPC latency are outside these owner measurements.

Per-sweep medians from five interleaved pairs (30 sweeps/process):

| Metric | Before | After | Change | Before range / p95 | After range / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Full healthy workspace projections | 200 | 0 | −100% | constant | constant |
| Identity evidence subjects after environment-only publication | 5,000 | 0 | −100% | constant | constant |
| Sampled main-thread allocation | 109.28 MB | 58.32 MB | −46.6% | 109.24–109.56 / 109.56 | 58.18–58.48 / 58.48 |
| Main-thread CPU | 287.37 ms | 140.15 ms | −51.2% | 253.53–373.42 / 373.42 | 122.01–199.50 / 199.50 |
| Total process CPU | 729.87 ms | 375.00 ms | −48.6% | 659.05–934.00 / 934.00 | 335.21–519.17 / 519.17 |
| Sweep elapsed time | 466.57 ms | 199.12 ms | −57.3% | 415.95–723.18 / 723.18 | 177.22–384.75 / 384.75 |

Timing and GC-inclusive allocation runs were separate. p95 is nearest rank across five process averages, not individual sweep latency. All five pairs improved. Two baseline A/A pairs showed elapsed drift +7.6%/+10.9% and main-thread CPU drift +7.2%/+10.7% on the shared host. Allocation samples used 4,096-byte sampling and include objects collected by minor and major GC. CPU includes SQLite workers; allocation covers the main thread. Absolute allocation includes the entire measured owner flow, not selected production profile frames.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/placement-identity-recovery-bench.ts \
  --state-dir /path/to/fresh/synthetic-state --trigger sweep --environment-changes \
  --active 200 --retained 5000 --warmup 5 --iterations 30
# Repeat separately with --allocations for sampled allocation.
```

The environment service already schedules its own inspection; its state publications do not invoke placement recovery. The placement timer consumes those facts to repair disappeared workers and also handles failed cleanup retries, durable interrupted workspace recovery, unresolved retirement, publication recovery, deferred startup orphan cleanup, and idle suspension. Targeted recovery keeps its existing admission path. Recovery discovery still reads the minimal inventory of all placement rows and pending-work membership; healthy attachment validation still runs. No new cache, schema, configuration, or freshness timer.

Production LOC: +18. The small growth carries the existing discovery fact and avoids full recovery for healthy background candidates; it preserves pending work and explicit recovery ordering. Tests: +42 lines, extending existing suites plus a targeted ordering regression. Simplification removed the broad environment invalidation rather than adding evidence caching.

Local regressions were red on the base for redundant projection/evidence work; the ordering regression caught and corrected an initial targeted shortcut. Final touched suites: 87 tests passing. Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2. Ten sibling suites also passed (125 tests; 212 focused tests total), covering restart file custody, lost workers, failed cleanup, repository disks, moves, session events and maintenance. The first `pnpm check:changed` passed typechecks, format, ratchets and dead export scans but found a shadowed test parameter and an unbound benchmark method capture. Both were corrected; targeted lint and the ordering regression pass, and Codex reviewed the repairs as clean. The complete `pnpm check:changed --base 928818442b99` rerun passed with no remaining failures. Main-thread CPU profiles corroborate the removed recovery/evidence stacks; the paired numbers above use untraced runs.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): treat a missing parent as ENOENT when /bin/sh is dash
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`SandboxFsBridgeImpl.stat()` decides an entry is missing by looking for `No such file or directory` in stderr. That is bash's wording for a failed `cd`. Debian and Ubuntu sandbox images ship **dash** as `/bin/sh`, where the same failure prints `cd: can't cd to <dir>`. On those images, stat-ing any path under a directory that does not exist throws:

```
stat failed for /workspace/missing/note.txt: cd: can't cd to /workspace/missing
```

instead of returning `null` for `ENOENT`. The same probe succeeded on images whose `/bin/sh` is bash, so callers that test an optional path saw a hard error on dash and a clean miss elsewhere.

## User Impact

Reading or stating an optional path inside a directory that does not exist fails with an unhandled error on Debian/Ubuntu sandbox containers. Callers that treat a `null` result as "not there" - pre-write checks and optional reads - instead surface a sandbox failure the user cannot act on.

## Why This Change Was Made

`cd` cannot fail for a missing *entry*; it fails because the *parent* does not exist. The script now reports that case on stdout:

```sh
if cd -- "$1" 2>/dev/null; then LC_ALL=C stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "$2";
elif [ ! -d "$1" ]; then printf "openclaw-missing-parent";
else exit 1; fi
```

Any non-zero exit with that marker is `ENOENT` for the entry, which matches what `stat` already returns when only the final component is missing, so both paths now converge on `null`. stat's own `ENOENT` keeps using the `LC_ALL=C` message, which stays English under any shell. A `cd` failure for another reason - a permission problem, say - exits non-zero **without** the marker and stays an error, so the fix does not widen the failure set.

## Evidence

Reproduced against real shells in the shipped `node:24-bookworm` (Debian) image, which uses dash as `/bin/sh`:

```
dash : sh: 1: cd: can't cd to /nonexistent-dir-xyz
bash : bash: line 1: cd: /nonexistent-dir-xyz: No such file or directory
```

The old check matched only the bash line, so dash fell through to `throw`.

The same script run under both shells after the change:

```
dash, missing parent   -> openclaw-missing-parent          (returns null)
dash, missing file     -> stderr: No such file or directory (returns null)
dash, real file        -> regular empty file|0|2026-10-28 ... (stat result)
bash, missing parent   -> openclaw-missing-parent          (returns null)
bash, real file        -> regular empty file|0|2026-10-28 ... (stat result)
```

Regression tests in `fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts`:

- `recognizes a missing parent directory where /bin/sh is dash` - feeds dash's `can't cd to` stderr with the marker on stdout and expects `null`, with and without `expectedPolicyPath`.
- `keeps a non-missing cd failure as an error` - a non-zero exit with no marker (the permission case) still throws.

Pairing on `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts`:

```
base (origin/main) : 1 failed | 9 passed (10)  -> recognizes a missing parent directory where /bin/sh is dash
head               : 10 passed (10)
```

`oxfmt --check` clean. `tsc` reports no error for either touched file; this checkout's remaining typecheck errors come from uninstalled dependencies (`micromark`, `undici`) predating those additions to `main`.

Refs #185552

Catalog refresh resolves the same provider separately for model and transport normalization on every row, rebuilding selection data on both calls.

prs.title: fix: prevent one session from stalling shared server I/O
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prevents one session from monopolizing the shared exec I/O ceiling, and removes unnecessary SQLite payload reads that hold up other sessions. The incident showed sustained exec throttling despite ample idle CPU/RAM, 38.37 seconds across 16 deletion writer transactions, and repeated transcript-payload scans during hydration.

## User Impact

- Stable per-session child cgroups cap each session at half the existing aggregate exec I/O ceiling. Command cancellation preserves same-session siblings and other sessions. The aggregate host protection remains unchanged.
- Deletion projects references first, then reads only the exact winning successor. It preserves deterministic ownership, stale/placeholder handling, timestamp fallback and retained transcripts.
- Hydration selects dependency metadata first, then uses exact `(session_id, seq)` payload lookups instead of a whole-session payload range scan.
- Cache warming reserves remaining budget for later databases and skips an oversized state prefix instead of repeatedly consuming the pass there. This is a confirmed secondary defect; the warmer was inactive during the incident.

The session ceiling prevents a single-session monopoly; it is not N-way fair scheduling. Populated legacy flat cgroups retain their policy until their owner drains them and the Gateway restarts. No schema, retention, configuration or permission change. No live-server deployment is included.

## Validation

Focused proof covers 57 cgroup/supervisor tests; 73 consumer tests (11 platform skips); 26 context/query-plan tests; 16 deletion-receipt tests, including five ownership/payload-bound regressions; 12 shared reference-reader edge cases; cache-budget cases; and 14 retained-custody/cleanup cases. Two focused process cases verify confirmed signal-tree extinction and cancellation with same-session/other-session siblings surviving. Core TypeScript, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and both unchanged SQL guards pass.

The retained-custody test now matches main's corrected two-outcome contract: confirmed outcomes preserve native results and reacquire both leases; unconfirmed signal cleanup retains both roots. Eight focused cases pass, including parent/gate loss. The separate process regression directly proves confirmed signal-tree extinction.

A local UTF-16 maintenance-candidate assertion reproduces with unchanged baseline production under the same runtime; its exact conversion cause remains unknown. It exercises an untouched owner, and no assertion was weakened.

### Hydration and deletion acceptance

Before measuring: require matching result digests, lower median CPU/elapsed time and no >=20% median or p95 regression. One 384,024,576-byte synthetic database: 32 sessions, 40 ordinary events, one 10,000-event session, 32 KiB bodies. Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, ten separate processes, Node 26.12.1, macOS, warm filesystem cache; host load 8.59–9.82.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Elapsed median / p95 | 94.55 / 125.04 ms | 33.73 / 100.03 ms |
| Elapsed min–max | 34.43–125.04 ms | 32.03–100.03 ms |
| CPU median / p95 | 73.99 / 82.08 ms | 54.21 / 74.13 ms |
| CPU min–max | 56.25–82.08 ms | 51.28–74.13 ms |

Elapsed samples A: 112.38, 94.55, 34.43, 36.40, 125.04 ms; B: 33.73, 39.41, 32.15, 32.03, 100.03 ms. CPU A: 73.99, 75.29, 56.25, 57.88, 82.08 ms; B: 54.21, 61.20, 52.36, 51.29, 74.13 ms. All ten result digests match; acceptance passed. Deletion baseline materialized 74,463 / 74,269 / 74,463 bytes and failed the 16,384-byte threshold; all five candidate ownership cases pass. These measure SQL-owner timing and returned text, not Gateway latency or physical disk reads. Kernel throughput enforcement and cold-read gains remain unmeasured.

Rerun: prepare using `scripts/perf/usage-refresh-stats-measure.ts --prepare --sessions 32 --events 40 --body-kib 32 --large-sessions 1 --large-events 10000 --selected 1`; measure interleaved revisions using `scripts/perf/session-hydration-read-measure.ts --operation bounded --session 0`. Run with the documented Node/tsx launcher and an isolated fixture root.

## CI and Review

Current signed head: `13dfbae320aecc293ba8e1aea927506699ba4bde`. Production is unchanged from reviewed head `65e9fa9de03b1b2ca72942dfdedd09c7900a4c87`. Test-only changes add bounded Doctor-fixture phase diagnostics and adopt main's retained-custody correction. The latest commit corrects the allocation from 256 to the 235 regression lines newly introduced against CI's merge base. No timeout, assertion or cleanup-lifetime weakening.

Exact-head run [41567479406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41567479406), attempt 1, completed: 105 jobs, 76 passed, 25 skipped, three failed roots plus the aggregate. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards, security-fast, architecture and baseline guards passed. The current ratchet records 6,416,607 test lines against a 6,417,176 ceiling, leaving 569 lines. Its actual merge is `f273255cc50708edf553b3cb1f432e1372f765fe`, ordered parents main `586f5766569997816efdf795eaaf535f552627a7` and this exact head; API parents and locally derived tree match.

The automatic failure table reports **unknown: no corresponding main job**. Each remaining root instead has scoped maintainer source/runtime attribution; CI remains failed:

- [Talk source identity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41567479406/job/125693046364): chat admission adds invocation authority absent from the test's original capture. Source identity includes that owner, so its referential-equality assertion conflicts with retention introduced by main. Exact causal source/test files match base/merge. Preserve retained authority and release behavior.
- [Scheduled-plugin recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41567479406/job/125693046326): both tests make eight model requests after generic restart recovery adopts a command parent as an ordinary agent turn. Current traces identify that restart input. The zero-call invariant also failed with all 23 original PR production files overlaid from frozen baseline `c84c4595b17708a4811009eea3e7bd697fa1a5f5` and rebuilt; this is not a full current-main E2E replay. Complete causal owners match current base/merge. Timing amplification remains unexcluded.
- [Restart write readiness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41567479406/job/125693046395): reads become ready at 02:47:05.846; five resumes are write-refused at 07.338–.353; writable preparation completes at 07.378. An identical controlled probe on exact preceding CI base `a5a98d58a90414e7e6f2ef68f50a2e8b147add88` and merge `b0f376cfebf7f9adb0da81240a7b00cfb98718c5` reaches the same final failed assertion: zero same-boot resumes, retained marker, one fresh-owner resume. Native refusal, real shared-store ownership and worker-read controls pass on both. These owners and dependency inputs match current base/merge. This is deterministic macOS/Node 26.12.1 owner proof, not full Linux/pinned-Bun baseline E2E reproduction; timing amplification remains unexcluded.

The PR-caused allocation failure is corrected and passes on this head. The preceding run's three pre-test Bun download HTTP 500 failures do not recur here; no downloader repair is claimed. The earlier isolated Doctor exit-124 cause remains unknown. Ordered baseline/candidate/diagnostic replays and both subsequent Linux Doctor shards pass without establishing a timeout repair.

Independent whole-change autoreview and subsequent SQL/process/diagnostic delta reviews found no actionable issues. [Exact-head ClawSweeper revision 6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191236#issuecomment-6582144617) has no findings or before-merge moves. Its optional delegated-Linux Gateway exercise is deferred to deployment qualification; unit/consumer proof and Linux CI do not establish real kernel throttling. Landing uses the native attributed-failure route under the standing scoped maintainer instruction; it does not waive required security, reviews or native authority.

Production delta: +152 lines for session-budget placement/identity, deterministic projected ownership and warming fairness. Tests/helpers: +265 lines; the ratchet-counted allocation is +235 against CI's merge base, excluding harness patterns and the correction already owned by main. Removed full survivor-entry materialization and the hydration payload range scan; no new cache or schema.

Named follow-ups: align the Talk source-identity test with invocation-authority retention; investigate transient pinned-Bun download failures; order restart recovery after writable admission; exclude scheduled-plugin command parents from ordinary crash adoption; diagnose the isolated Doctor timeout with the new phase evidence; reduce workspace-CAS GC metadata traversal. Deployment still needs isolated delegated-Linux qualification.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own [System] retry turns as user memories
prs.body:
Closes #189955

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory-lancedb auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own `[System]` turns as user memories when a stranded-reply retry, or a `sessions_send` restart note, quotes text that contains a capture trigger.

## User Impact

User impact: with `autoCapture` on, only what the user said is stored. `[System]` rows already in a store stop coming back from recall and are no longer used for duplicate matching. They stay on disk and still show in `openclaw ltm list`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core marks the turns it writes itself with `[System]` through `formatSystemTurnPrompt` (`src/sessions/system-turn-prompt.ts`). On main `19aff5bfd42` its producers are the stranded-reply retry (`src/auto-reply/reply/stranded-reply-recovery.ts`), the transcript follow-up run (`src/auto-reply/reply/transcript-followup-run.ts`) and `sessions_send` (`src/agents/tools/sessions-send-executor.ts`). I have not shown that every internal turn goes through it. These turns are sent as user-role messages, so `extractUserTextContent` hands it to capture like any user text. Capture now goes through `capturableUserText`, which checks the raw turn for that marker before sanitizing, because sanitizing can remove the marker line along with a quoted context block. It then applies `shouldCapture`, which also rejects the marker. `isRecallableMemoryText`, which gates both recall and duplicate matching, skips such rows too. The marker is matched in the plugin because plugins cannot import the core helper, and a leading timestamp envelope is allowed before it.

Deleting rows already stored is left out. That is a retention change, and recall no longer surfaces them. One tradeoff: a user message that itself starts with `[System]` is no longer captured.

## Evidence

- New qa scenario `memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai, `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool`, memory-lancedb `autoCapture: true`.
  - The first prompt is not capturable, so the `[System]` retry is the first capturable text. A later turn in the same conversation, `QA-MEMORY-BARRIER 記住 ...`, must be stored before the store is read; captures for one session run in order, so the retry's capture has settled by then.
  - It fails if any stored row contains the retry's `send it now with message(action=send)` instruction, so it catches the retry whether or not its `[System]` line survived.
  - With main's memory-lancedb at `eef407423d4`: fails after the barrier settles, with `[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: "QA-STRANDED-85714：...". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). If no reply is needed, answer exactly NO_REPLY.` stored.
