prs.title: fix(doctor): 2026.10.10 update refuses when an imported audit archive lost its sanitized companion (backport #186998)
prs.body:
Related: #186974
Backport of #186998 (`4a0ab0928cc`) to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on 2026.10.10 betas, `openclaw doctor --fix`, and so an update, refuses at the `audit-logs` migration and blocks every later repair when an already-imported legacy config-audit archive is re-detected and its sanitized companion is gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a 2026.10.10 update on a host in that state finishes instead of refusing and rolling back. Real unimported records still refuse with the backup-restoration guidance, as on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186998 fixed this on main on 10-28, after `release/2026.10.10` was cut. It is not in beta.4, beta.5 or the branch tip `1cdcfc00d84`, by ancestry and by subject. The production change and docs here have the same patch-id as main's (`051fd155b6deec28`), and the release branch's two audit source files are identical to beta.4's, so they apply as is.

main refactored both audit test files after the cut. This keeps the release branch's `state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts` and adds main's two missing-companion cases to `state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts`. It also adds a case for the shape I hit (same bytes, size and mtime under a new file identity), and a Doctor-runner case for the other half of the rule: an unimported record with the companion gone still refuses.

## Evidence

- **Hit on a real 2026.10.10-beta.4 update on one of my macOS gateways (2026-10-31 04:07Z).** Doctor ran 434 s and exited 1:
  ```
  Failing check audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated
  Failing check managed-outgoing-images (blocked-by-prior-refusal): Migration step "managed-outgoing-images" was not run because prior step "audit-logs" refused execution.
  ```
  `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` were blocked the same way, and the update rolled back.
- **Cause, read-only on that host's state.** The raw-archive checkpoint (`migration.legacy-audit-raw`) records `dev 16777231, ino 19235396, size 478022, recordCount 0`. The file now reads `dev 16777230` with the same inode, size and mtime, and `config-audit.jsonl.migrated.sanitized` does not exist. Only the device number moved, so detection stopped matching and the step refused although nothing remained to import.
- The same production change on the same data: with #186998 carried onto beta.4 (same patch-id as this PR), doctor on that host logged `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left ~/.openclaw/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, ran every later step, and the update finished with rc 0 at 07:30Z.
- Installed-package upgrade, latest stable (npm `openclaw@2026.10.9`, `8b18b55`) to this branch's build at `23e85739821`. Run with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `--profile upgradeproof` and port 29789, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` each time. No launchd label or LaunchAgent was added on the host.
  1. 2026.10.9 on a seeded legacy `logs/config-audit.jsonl` of 3 `config.write` records: exit 0, `Migrated config audit log -> shared SQLite state (3 new row(s))`. Afterwards the raw archive's sha256 is `f6cc44861440c55a…`, the checkpoint reads `ino 185071743, size 423, recordCount 0`, the `config-audit` history holds 5 rows (the 3 legacy rows hash to `ab40ca823113eea8…`), and `openclaw.json` hashes to `2ccd48ad6b26cc54…`.
  2. The raw archive is copied beside itself and renamed over (ino `185071743` -> `185071842`, same size and mtime_ns), and the sanitized companion is removed.
  3. 2026.10.9 again: exit 1. `audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, and `managed-outgoing-images`, `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` are blocked by the prior refusal.
  4. This branch on the same state: exit 0, `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left <state>/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, and `Doctor complete.` A second run: exit 0, the same skip.
  5. After steps 3, 4 and 5, every value from step 1 is unchanged: the raw sha256, the checkpoint row, the 5 history rows with the same legacy hash, and the `openclaw.json` hash.
  6. This branch's `doctor --lint` over that state ran 39 checks. Its 3 findings are environment warnings (browser cookie import, a Codex route for the default model, no gateway auth token); none concern state or migrations.
- Tests on this branch at `23e85739821` (Node 26.12.1):
  - `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 52 passed, 0 failed.
  - Control: with `state-migrations.audit-logs.ts` and `state-migrations.audit-sanitized.ts` reverted to the branch tip, 4 failed and 10 passed in `audit-skips`. The three skip cases get `outcome: "refused"` with `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, the message from the real host. The refusal case gets that same undifferentiated message instead of `the raw archive contains unimported records`.
  - The refusal case also checks that nothing is imported and that the raw bytes and checkpoint are unchanged.
  - `pnpm tsgo:all` exited 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
- Gap: a unit test cannot move `st_dev`, so the moved-file case changes the inode instead. The copy is written beside the original and renamed over it, so it cannot reuse the inode. The test asserts the premise: a different inode with the same size and mtime.

prs.title: feat(ci): estimate test selection savings and model costs
prs.body:
Stack: depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191228, following https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191226. Review this PR against its stacked base.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191191

## What Problem This Solves

Skipped test counts do not reveal net CI savings after setup, full-run audits, decision-model calls and billing rounding.

## User Impact

Operators can estimate runner time, allocated CPU minutes, list cost and model tokens separately in JSON and Markdown. Shadow mode reports its added overhead; unknown prices and workflow latency remain unknown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scenario model preserves fixed setup, weights full audits, and rounds each possible execution before averaging. It handles explicit whole-job elimination, input/output token prices, and negative savings. Rates and assumptions are caller-supplied; results are projections, not invoice promises.

This is the final layer of the initial adaptive CI stack. Enabling skips or adopting a paid service remains a separate decision.

## Evidence

- Seven cost/CLI tests pass through the normal repository runner (1.70 s Vitest duration, 3.92 s shard wall time).
- Full-stack tooling typecheck, scoped typed lint and pinned formatting pass. Production and full-tree unused-file scans each report zero entries.
- Independent review and local ClawSweeper reviewed the original cost layer and its fixture-typing repair without actionable findings.
- The final restack changed commit history only: its source tree is identical to the validated stack. Exact-head GitHub CI remains the broad merge gate.

Reports distinguish projections from observed savings. Fixed setup, full-run audits, per-execution billing rounding, selector overhead and provider input/output tokens are accounted for separately. Unknown prices and critical-path latency stay unknown; shadow mode claims no test-execution savings.

prs.title: fix(telegram): large media sends time out after 30 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #112116 (closed, covered the unhandled rejection after a media upload timeout, not the deadline itself)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a large video or document sent to Telegram fails with `Network request for 'sendVideo' failed!` after 30 seconds when the file needs longer than that to upload.

## User Impact

Media sends get a deadline that grows with the file instead of a flat 30 s. An upload keeps its current guard until its transfer estimate outgrows it (30 MiB for the 30 s methods), and the longest guard is 30 minutes. Operators have no knob for this today: `timeoutSeconds` is in `RETIRED_TUNING_KEYS` (`extensions/telegram/src/doctor-contract.ts:29`), and neither client passes a timeout to `createTelegramClientFetch`.

Tradeoff that needs a maintainer call: the account throttler runs one request at a time per chat, and in a group one at a time across all of its forum topics (`GroupRequestScheduler.drain` in `account-throttler.ts`). A slow upload now holds the requests queued behind it in that chat for as long as its guard, up to 30 minutes, where today they wait at most the 30 s guard (60 s for albums) for it to fail. Other chats are not held.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveTelegramRequestTimeoutMs` gives `sendvideo`, `senddocument`, `sendphoto`, `sendanimation`, `sendaudio` and `sendvoice` a fixed 30_000 ms, and `sendmediagroup` gets the 60_000 ms default. Pinned main `2e7668b2eaad` still uses that table. The Bot API answers an upload with the sent Message, so the response cannot arrive before the file has been uploaded, and a big enough file always loses.

The resolver now takes an optional upload size and returns the larger of the table value and `ceil(bytes / 2 MiB/s)` seconds plus 15 s, capped at 30 minutes. 2 MiB/s is an assumed floor, not a measurement.

The size comes from the InputFile that `prepareTelegramOutboundMedia` builds (recorded in a WeakMap); direct sends, reply media and albums all take their files from it. A grammY transformer installed inside the account throttler, in both `send-context.ts` and `bot-core.ts`, reads the size off the payload (including `sendMediaGroup`'s `media[]`) and hands it to the client fetch through AsyncLocalStorage. I did not take the size from the caller's async context because the throttler runs queued requests from its own drain loop. In a probe on an earlier base, a second request enqueued under its own AsyncLocalStorage value ran under the first request's value, for both a group chat and a private chat.

Two more timers sat under that guard. grammY 1.46.0 races every call against one client timer, `options.timeoutSeconds ?? 500` (`out/core/client.js:77`), with no per-call override, and neither client set it. undici waits `headersTimeout` for response headers, `300e3` by default (`lib/dispatcher/client.js:319` in 8.12.3, the version main pins as of 2026-11-03; it was line 317 in 8.11.2 when this was written), and refreshes that timer when a streamed body ends, so it counts from the end of the upload. A self-hosted Bot API server answers only after it has relayed the file to Telegram. Both clients now set grammY's `timeoutSeconds`, and the Telegram dispatchers set `headersTimeout`, to 1860 s (the 30-minute cap plus 60 s), so the per-method guard is the deadline. Every other consumer of the Telegram transport keeps a shorter deadline of its own (getUpdates 45 s, file downloads 120 s to headers, probes through `fetchWithTimeout`).

## Current revision and fixture repair

Head: [`44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737), tree `8abfeb27059dab4f917a1818a34a495c1e303af3`.

This fixture-only commit disables persisted thread bindings in the upload-deadline fixture and registers `bot.stop()` for cleanup. The real bot, send stack and all four upload assertions remain. Upstream #175379 deliberately acquires runtime when thread bindings start; the upload fixture does not initialize that unrelated runtime. Production binding behavior is unchanged.

The preceding head `0afce1f7d17e08adbf2d3818122e9ebb6420cecd` merged main `2e7668b2eaad12171ef4421b68286de6063b7e77`, retaining main's one-argument account-throttler constructor and the upload transformer before the throttler. The sequential transformer/WeakMap/context test requested removed in [the review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151923#issuecomment-5733461410) is removed; the four independent size-boundary cases remain.

[Previous-head CI 40121818105](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121818105) finished with 27 successful jobs, 31 skipped and two failures: the Telegram job failed both polling-bot rows with `Telegram runtime not initialized` before their upload assertions, and the aggregate gate propagated that failure. The four boundary cases, two other send cases and loopback case passed.

## Evidence

### Upgrade from the latest stable release, Telegram settings preserved

Isolated state dir on macOS (Node 24.22.1), everything on loopback. Telegram was a local Bot API stand-in reached through `channels.telegram.apiRoot`, the same override a self-hosted Bot API uses. It records every call; it is not Telegram.

1. Published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (npm `latest` when this ran on 2026-10-27; `latest` is now 2026.10.10 and the upgrade leg was not re-run from it; build `dc2523e5a5c7`) on a fresh state dir: `config validate` exit 0, Gateway polled and consumed update 41, `message send --media <1 MiB zip> --force-document` returned `messageId` 5001, Gateway exit 0. Stored Telegram state: `telegram.update-offsets` `lastUpdateId: 41`, plus sent-message, message-cache and bot-info rows.
2. This head (`44411bc979e3`, tree `8abfeb27059d`) on the same state dir: `config validate` exit 0. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exit 0; its changes are main's database migrations and one derived `groupAllowFrom`, nothing from this PR. All 11 Telegram keys kept their values (`enabled`, `botToken`, `apiRoot`, `dmPolicy`, `allowFrom`, `groupPolicy`, `defaultTo`, `linkPreview`, `silentErrorReplies`, `streaming`, `mediaMaxMb`). The Gateway's first `getUpdates` asked for offset 42, so update 41 was not replayed; it consumed update 42 (`lastUpdateId` 41 -> 42), delivered a 100 MiB document, and exited 0.
3. The same two phases from `2026.10.7` (build `157d8c2bc3ea`, `latest` on 2026-10-26) gave the same result.

Fresh install: this head on an empty state dir with the same config started, polled, and delivered the 100 MiB document below.

### Large upload, main vs this head

Same harness. The stand-in reads uploads at 2 MiB/s, the PR's assumed floor, so a 104,857,720-byte zip takes about 50 s: longer than main's 30 s guard, shorter than this head's guard for that size (66 s by the PR's formula). `mediaMaxMb: 2000` as a self-hosted Bot API operator would set it; at the default 100 MiB cap the file is refused before upload (`file exceeds limit of 104857600 bytes`).

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main `2e7668b2eaad` (merge base) | `sendDocument` aborted at 30.7 s after 64,578,089 bytes; `OutboundDeliveryError: Network request for 'sendDocument' failed!` |
| this head, fresh state | delivered: 104,858,286 bytes in 50.0 s, `message_id` 5001 |
| this head, upgraded from 2026.10.8 | delivered: 104,858,286 bytes in 50.0 s, `message_id` 5001 |

This is the reported failure and its fix through the real CLI, Gateway and Telegram send path. It does not deliver an approximately 893 MiB file to Telegram through a self-hosted Bot API; that run is still open.

### Fixture validation

A separate Linux x64 runner tested the exact published tree using Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependencies, Vitest 5.0.5 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. Lockfile SHA-256: `21592b379203de7ecd8661cfd6e412daf6546f94b203f28c314579db20f76594`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Upload-deadline fixture | Four cases passed; 122.03 s. |
| Independent size boundaries plus loopback transport | Five cases passed; 105.10 s. |
| Restore only the upload fixture from `0afce1f7`, same environment | Exactly the 100 MiB and 1 GiB polling rows failed with the runtime-initialization error; both send rows passed; 125.27 s. |
| Boundary and loopback controls after reversal | All five passed; 129.37 s. |
| Restoration | Exact candidate tree restored; validation processes and allocation drained. |

```sh
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-timeout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-real-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Tested fixture SHA-256: `142a7e49383fc875bed18b2774b39bb862f77c363680890bf953bf54a90ab530`. Validation receipt SHA-256: `181295d70e37bcc0cb488ed9c0728241e315881072b5041d1a6cb6e10663425c`. Independent source review found no actionable issue in this fixture change.

These are fixture results. The loopback case uses a 64 KiB payload tagged with a larger upload size and a fake clock. It proves timer ordering through the local transport; it does not deliver an approximately 893 MiB file to Telegram.

## Historical product regression evidence

At `34a6f9e42fb`, the three upload files and neighboring bot/fetch suites passed 94 cases. Replacing only the four production wiring files with main `4db022470af6` caused all four upload fixture cases and the loopback case to abort at 30,000 ms. Earlier timer probes distinguished grammY's 500-second client deadline and undici's response-header deadline. These remain historical evidence, not a current-head live-platform result.

## Remaining gates

[CI 40138561883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138561883) completed successfully for this head: 29 jobs passed and 31 skipped. Its merge checkout `bd77e2ea717464e780e0a5777fa21633727576ff` has parents main `418aafaae7e8d13792b9095c010a114ca4e058ea` and this head; the upload fixture is byte-identical. All four upload cases, four size-boundary cases and the loopback case passed. The latest dependency, security and aggregate statuses are success ([status publisher 40139326205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139326205)).

The later PR-context check rejected the previous body because its validation heading did not start with `Evidence`. This body restores that required heading. The product and live-proof gates below remain open.

- Maintainer acceptance of the assumed 2 MiB/s budget and up-to-30-minute per-chat wait remains open.
- Not a merge gate: ClawSweeper's review of this head (Revision 12, 2026-10-28) accepts the proof above and no longer asks for the approximately 893 MiB send through a self-hosted Bot API. It would still be the strongest proof, and no live upload or two-bot run was performed.
- The 2 MiB/s floor remains an assumption. Loopback and fake-clock results do not establish real transfer rates.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop default view from re-adding static rows after accepted discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #191360: Gateway model pickers (Discord `/model`, Control UI) kept listing retired `qwen-token-plan` models after live account discovery succeeded.

`prepareModelCatalogView` merges `snapshot.staticEntries` (manifest seed rows + hosted-catalog rows) back into the **default** view whenever the visibility policy allows them, without consulting discovery outcomes. The CLI `--all` / `--provider` view selects `all` and skips that merge, so the CLI and the Gateway disagreed.

## Root cause

Per the maintainer's guidance (kksingh069), the correct signal is `snapshot.acceptedDiscoveryOrigins`, not `status === "ready"` (a failed refresh would bring retired rows back because publication keeps last-good inventory) and not `listedModelIds` (qwen goes through `buildOpenAICompatibleLiveProviderCatalog`, which only sets `modelIdCatalog`).

`acceptedDiscoveryOrigins` covers ready-now plus retained-last-good, and leaves out failed-with-no-history, which is exactly where fallback rows should still show.

## Fix

In `src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts`, `prepareModelCatalogView` now builds the set of providers with accepted discovery origins (using the same `createPreparedModelCatalogProviderNormalizer` that publication uses, so aliases match), and for the **default** view:

- A provider with an accepted discovery origin keeps only its **explicitly configured** static rows (`policy.configuredKeys`) or the **retained model** (`retainedKey`) — the purely automatic static fallback rows are no longer reintroduced.
- A provider **without** an accepted discovery origin (pending, or failed-with-no-history) keeps the previous fallback behavior unchanged.
- The **configured** view path is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before (red, on base `a5a98d58a90`)

`prepareModelCatalogView` appended every static fallback row in the default view:

```ts
const include =
  params.view === "configured"
    ? policy.configuredKeys.has(key) || key === retainedKey
    : policy.allows({ provider: entry.provider, model: entry.id });
```

With an unrestricted policy (`allowAny`), `policy.allows()` returns `true` for all static rows, so retired manifest seed (`qwen3.6-plus`, `kimi-k2.5`, ...) and hosted-catalog rows (`glm-5.1`, `kimi-k2.6`, ...) reappear in the Gateway's default listing after a successful discovery — matching the reported 21 models (13 live + 8 retired).

### After (green, on this branch)

The same scenario now produces only the discovered rows for the provider. Regression coverage in `src/agents/model-catalog-view.test.ts` (`describe("accepted discovery owns picker membership")`):

1. **No reintroduction** — a discovered provider's static fallback rows are dropped from the default view; an unrelated provider without accepted discovery keeps its fallback.
2. **Explicit configured refs preserved** — `agents.defaults.models["custom/hosted-retired"]` still surfaces for a discovered provider.
3. **Retained model preserved** — the retained model stays listed for a discovered provider.
4. **No accepted discovery → fallback kept** — `acceptedDiscoveryOrigins: []` keeps the previous behavior.

### refresh-fails-after-success case

Covered by design: publication keeps `acceptedDiscoveryOrigins` = ready-now + retained-last-good (see `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.ts:332`), so a failed refresh after an earlier success keeps the provider in the accepted set and its static fallback rows stay suppressed. A `status === "ready"`-only check would have gotten this wrong; the fix keys on the origins set, not on outcome status.

## What was tested

Local (all green):

- `pnpm test src/agents/model-catalog-view.test.ts` — 27 passed (incl. 4 new regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.account-access.test.ts` — 23 passed
- `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts src/commands/models/list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` — 15 passed
- `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.configured-catalog.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` — 47 passed
- `test:gateway` (gateway-methods shard): `models-list-result.configured-static.test.ts` (7 passed, 1 env-blocked), `models-list-result.cli-runtime-availability.test.ts` + `models-list-result.plugin-runtime.test.ts` — 49 passed
- oxlint `--type-aware` (CI 293 rules), CI format check (`run-format.mts`), mock-exports ratchet (6409 → 6409, no drift), assertion-safety ratchet — all clean

## What was not tested

- `models-auth-login.catalog.integration.test.ts` and `models-list.remote-catalog.integration.test.ts` (gateway-database-workers shard): the local sandbox has no sticky-bit-protected temp root (`/` is group/world writable without sticky), so these integration tests fail on pristine main for environmental reasons (verified by stash on the same base). They exercise the full discovery→publication→list flow and will run on CI.
- Live provider call against the Token Plan endpoint was not made (no key in this sandbox); the failing-path source reproduction and regression tests establish the defect per ClawSweeper's review guidance.

prs.title: fix: retain WebChat participants when reply admission is busy
prs.body:
Related: #185225

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing participant attribution when an authenticated WebChat input is persisted while another reply operation already owns the session admission slot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy admission completion path already has the resolved session target and prepared authenticated participant. It now records that participant through the existing owner, guarded by the transcript recorder's persisted-input state. Restart recovery remains outside this PR.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`
- Result: **1 test passed**.
- The proof starts a real local Gateway with a temporary SQLite state directory and a loopback OpenAI Responses fixture.
- Alice and Bob use separate authenticated WebChat profiles. The test records Bob's `sessions.list` result before admission, while Alice holds the provider response, and after admission releases.
- Before and during busy admission, Bob's Involving me query excludes the shared session. After busy completion, the same query contains exactly one session and Bob's profile is present in `people`.
- Before releasing Alice's held provider response, Bob's `agent.wait` remains `pending` or `timeout`, provider request count remains exactly `1`, and Bob's session is absent from discovery. The proof logs this as `busyBeforeRelease` and `providerRequestsBeforeRelease`.
- Replaying Bob's exact idempotency key returns the same run id and does not increase provider request count.
- Base/head regression evidence: on base `e990b80e`, the focused busy-admission regression failed `1/1`; on the PR head before this Gateway proof, the same focused regression passed `1/1` and persisted the profile participant.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, `pnpm exec oxlint test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The current main test-lines budget and justification are preserved; no dependency or lockfile changes are included.

Redacted terminal trace from the Gateway proof:

```text
real local Gateway / authenticated WebChat
aliceProfileId: <redacted>
bobProfileId: <redacted>
beforeBusy: []
duringBusy: []
busyBeforeRelease: timeout
providerRequestsBeforeRelease: 1
afterBusy: ["agent:qa:pr185353-<redacted>"]
duplicateRunId: <same as busyRunId>
providerRequestsAfterBusy: <unchanged after duplicate>
persistedUserMessages: 2
```

The proof records the busy checkpoint before releasing Alice's held provider response; `timeout` is the bounded `agent.wait` result proving Bob's run had not completed yet.

The proof uses only local fixtures and loopback services. It does not require Android, a cloud account, an external endpoint, or an external model provider.

prs.title: test: cover seeded reply-marker retention across private completion
prs.body:
Related: #173650

## What Problem This Solves

The existing tests did not check whether a requester's already-persisted final-delivery marker survives a transcript-only private subagent completion. This PR covers that constructed retention scenario.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This does not fix the missed user update in #173650 or reproduce its obligation lifecycle from spawn through settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test drives the announcement, requester-command and tool-policy owners, with an outstanding `pendingFinalDelivery` marker supplied by the fixture. It checks the private instruction, effective tool availability, marker retention and absence of a requester-visible delivery receipt.

My earlier claim that the issue review settled the historical cause as model follow-through was wrong. That distinction remains unresolved. Retaining a seeded marker does not establish whether the reported owed update ever acquired that marker or how its registry obligation was settled. The test header at `ae52c5a61701` already states this limit; the description now does too.

## Evidence

**Shipped Gateway run, October 26, at `ae52c5a61701a6fa959280f4600a05632eae0b60`.** This PR changes only 3 test files, so the Gateway that ran is the production code of base `3e0475a199e5877f1b5e0c086437ef1fedd3b693`. Built on macOS arm64 with Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build qaRuntime`; `dist/index.js` SHA-256 `2338a25698b877d2e7321c901ffff4fcab827eb100809251a3ed17bd3314e47b`. Each run had its own throwaway HOME, state and config, and started `node dist/index.js gateway run --bind loopback`. The real Telegram plugin polled a loopback Bot API stub, and the model was a loopback scripted Responses provider. No session state was seeded. No credentials or external endpoints were used.

The script follows #173650. One Telegram DM asks for a background read. The requester calls `sessions_spawn` with `completionTarget: "parent"` and replies "I'll relay the result here the moment it lands." The child returns `PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a`. In the private completion turn the scripted model replies with text and calls no tool.

Run 1: every `sendMessage` answers HTTP 500. 18:25:03 to 18:29:31 UTC, 8 of 8 checks passed. Harness output, IDs shortened:

```text
18:28:26 provider: requester turn -> sessions_spawn {"task":"PR175029-CHILD-TASK Reply with exactly PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a.","label":"pr175029-bounded-read","runtime":"subagent","completionTarget":"parent","context":"isolated"}
18:28:32 provider: requester continuation -> final text "PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands."
18:28:39 db: at requester sendMessage, markers=[{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","intentId":"18c42769-...","kind":"replayable","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"queued"}]}]
18:28:39 telegram: sendMessage #1 answered 500 text="PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands."
18:28:47 db: before child release, markers=[{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","intentId":"18c42769-...","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"unknown"}]}]
18:29:02 provider: private completion turn; tools=49 message=true; replying transcript-only, no tool call
18:29:18 db: after completion agent:main:main pendingFinalDelivery={"kind":"replayable","text":"PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands.","intentId":"18c42769-...","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"unknown"}],...}
18:29:18 db: subagent_runs 2c6a2378-... completionTarget=parent expectsCompletionMessage=true completion.required=true delivery={"status":"delivered","disposition":"delivered",...}
18:29:18 PASS: The same marker (intentId) is still outstanding after the private completion
18:29:18 PASS: Marker contents are unchanged by the private completion
18:29:18 PASS: No channel send carried the private completion's final text
18:29:19 db: message_tool_run_outcomes rows=0; session_input_completions rows=1
18:29:20 db: requester transcript seq=11 role=assistant text="PR175029-RELAY Recorded privately: the child returned PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a."
18:29:20 telegram: sendMessage calls total=2 texts=["PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands.","I couldn't deliver my reply. Please ask again."]
18:29:31 harness: done in 268.4s; 8/8 checks passed
```

- Marker creation: the requester's own turn persisted the `replayable` marker for its promise. It read `queued` when the send reached Telegram and `unknown` after the 500.
- Tool availability: the private completion request offered 49 tools, `message` among them, and carried `SUBAGENT_PRIVATE_COMPLETION_INSTRUCTION` ("Your final reply stays internal ... send it through an available, permitted messaging tool") plus the ledger line `outcome=ok; delivery=pending; requester_continuation=none`.
- Retention: the marker read just before the child was released and the marker read after the completion settled are identical, intent `18c42769` with delivery `83ee452c` still `unknown`.
- Delivery facts: the registry recorded the completion `delivered` with `completion.required=true`. `session_input_completions` has one row for `announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:...` with `status=ok`, `stopReason=stop`. `message_tool_run_outcomes` has 0 rows. The completion's text is transcript row 11 and was never sent. The only channel sends were the failed promise and the Telegram fallback notice, which also got a 500.

Run 2, control: every `sendMessage` succeeds. 18:29:31 to 18:31:11 UTC, 7 of 7 checks passed. The marker was present (`queued`) when the promise reached Telegram and was gone at the first read 0.7 s later. The private completion created no marker. The registry, `session_input_completions`, `message_tool_run_outcomes` and transcript facts match run 1, with one channel send in total.

So the scenario the new test pins now comes from the shipped Gateway instead of a fixture: a marker the requester created is retained, and not settled, by a transcript-only private completion that had `message` available. This does not reproduce #173650. There the promise was delivered and nothing was outstanding when the completion arrived, and here the no-send is scripted, not a model decision. I have not rerun this on current main.

Harness `proof-175029.mts` (Telegram stub, scripted provider and the database reads), SHA-256 `5fd7bbd867dad06164b2a62949224730843c3c9f299c44c8483cb60b11d52b6a`. Raw harness logs: run 1 SHA-256 `b1affd848176a44d17aaaceaa270226975fe9c2d9274b1aed14c949d34249928`, run 2 `544ec768ee7b6375b286fb9e935d49183e1b72dc9935cb28148c275c474c6f19`. Both Gateways exited 0 on SIGTERM.

**What the test covers.** The test calls real `runSubagentAnnounceFlow`, `agentCommandFromGatewayIngress` and `runAgentAttempt`. The Gateway method is an in-process adapter, the embedded model result is scripted, and tool factories are shared fast stubs. It seeds both `pendingFinalDelivery` and child spawn lineage. The three cases check:

- A verified private-completion handoff derives its origin-sensitive private instruction from the announce owner, permits `message` through the real policy pipeline, retains the same prepared marker, and returns `delivered: true` without `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered`.
- An operator `tools.deny: ["message"]` excludes `message` while retaining other tools and the marker.
- An unconsumed delegated handoff disables tools while retaining the marker.

The related existing private-text fixture asserts `deliver: false`, `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "automatic"`, no `sendMessage` call and no visible-final receipt. The new test is registered on the forked database-worker route.

**Historical validation, not a rerun of the current head:** at `778eafe7da02`, the new file passed 3 tests in each of 3 runs; announcement delivery passed 145; marker tests passed 5. Database-worker registry passed 12 at `58aeae3de18f`. Mutation controls failed when the parent instruction mapping or retained-tools policy was removed, and the deny case failed when global policy was skipped. These controls show sensitivity to those boundaries, not reproduction of the historical incident.

**Prior-head CI (before this adaptation):** [CI run 39845293165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39845293165) completed successfully on CI merge `bfe4f403a373a480e866faf2b4af7442e4c0bcbe` (`ae52c5a61701` merged into base `67408f3f5422043acbf3fa5fae641567119c8455`). [Changed-1 job 120057533859](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39845293165/job/120057533859) records 3/3 private-completion obligation tests and 124/124 announcement-delivery tests. The dependency-review, security-sensitive-review and ci-gate commit statuses also report success from [gate run 39846815916](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39846815916).

**Compatibility adaptation and focused validation (October 29).** #182124 replaced the exported constant with `buildSubagentPrivateCompletionInstruction(requesterOrigin)`. The fixture now asserts the expected instruction as an independent literal and exercises the origin-sensitive path. Production behavior is unchanged.

The qualified source is tree `c9d281d8e85c1a124e1b4e02ce50c901bb9a122a` on base `4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d`, with Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0`, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` and the frozen lockfile. Focused checks cover 150 distinct passing cases: 3 private-completion cases, 135 related announcement cases and 12 database-worker registry cases. Scoped lint, formatting, whitespace checks and the agents-root/agents-sessions test typechecks passed.

Reintroducing the removed export fails only at the fixture with TS2724. Replacing the requester origin passed to the private-instruction builder with `undefined` produces exactly the intended retention-case failure, with the other 2 cases passing. After restoring the source, the full three-case command passed and exited 0 in 99.08 seconds, including wrapper verification and cleanup; the supervisor confirmed source restoration and no remaining owned processes. Repeated confirmation cases are not added to the 150 total. Origin-negative log SHA-256: `d287960b9214e78c579212e96022715b40d90bb560711e6e88c475cf8bf4bf00`; restored-command log: `6ed67a655c0ab884cfe893871f2af65a5b8d7c6c4ac3dda38772a8c0a459af6c`. Interrupted attempts remain recorded as incomplete; their printed passes are not used as completed wrapper proof.

Reproduce the focused runtime and type checks with the pinned runtimes and dependencies:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.private-completion-obligation.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental
```

Correction, 2026-11-03: an earlier version said current production creates only transport-only markers. That was wrong. The reply-runner path creates a `replayable` marker whenever the final has text (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result.ts:328` and `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-input-admission.ts:151` on main `19aff5bfd42`). Only the agent-command path is transport-only (`src/agents/pending-final-delivery-marker.ts:118`). So the replayable marker this fixture seeds is a production shape, and the October 26 run log above shows one (`"kind":"replayable"`). The October 26 Gateway proof above remains tied to its historical base; no current-base unseeded marker lifecycle or live Telegram proof is claimed. The historical model no-send decision remains unresolved.

Before publication, main `1dca2e5bcb91d3d42895112f78a7a2d325b95e84` still lacked the new fixture; the related announcement test was unchanged and the registry insertion merged cleanly. This scoped check does not establish runtime success on that newer base. Published head: `d9258a5eb295fd1e8b66ef6abac2e3a7adfdab05`. [Fresh CI run 40956446253](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40956446253) completed successfully: 35 jobs passed and 30 were skipped, with no failures. It tested merge `6debea727f3075db0d858485539288e01c8679e0`, combining this head with upstream `9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb`. [Changed-test job 123738414902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40956446253/job/123738414902) records 3/3 private-completion cases and 110/110 announcement-delivery cases, both with exit 0. The PR's Checks tab remains the source for other workflow and review statuses.

**Incident evidence, 2026.10.3:** [the incident follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173650#issuecomment-6323508739) records build `1ecf113bef64`, the actual private instruction and a permitted `message` tool, a promised user update, registry delivery recorded as delivered, and no corresponding send. The shipped run above shows the same registry and outcome-table facts on this head with a scripted no-send; it does not establish why the 2026.10.3 model did not send.

prs.title: improve(auto-reply): name the model whose connection failed
prs.body:
Closes #191299

## What Problem This Solves

When a model call fails to connect, the reply says "Couldn't connect to the AI service." (#168247) but not which model. With a fallback chain or several providers, the user can't tell which endpoint is down without the gateway logs.

## User Impact

User impact: the connection-failure reply starts with the failing model, e.g. `⚠️ gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. ...`. The rest of #168247's copy is unchanged, including the completed-work caution. A failure without a provider or model reads exactly as before, and raw error text stays hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveReplyFailoverFacts` already has the failover error's provider and model; the connection copy just didn't use them. It now prefixes the copy with the failing model through `modelKey`, which keeps a model id that already carries its provider as is (`openrouter/auto` is not doubled). Terminal replies and incomplete-turn replies both read `requestFailureText`, so both get the name.

When the error carries fallback attempts, the name comes only from the attempts whose own error is a connection failure, joined with ", " when there are several. A chain summary keeps the last attempt's model while its message joins every attempt's error, so taking the top-level model would blame a backup that connected and then timed out (ClawSweeper's P2 on the first head).

This partly reverses #163381 (#163368), which removed provider details from default errors to keep them short. For a connection failure, though, the failing model is the next recovery step (which server to check), not a diagnostic. Only the connection copy changes; rate-limit, auth and server-error replies are untouched. If maintainers want to keep #163381's rule here too, closing this is fine.

## Evidence

- New qa scenario `connection-failure-reply-names-model` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai with the provider's `baseUrl` set to `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, so every model call is refused. It sends a DM and reads the terminal reply from the bus. The reply is `isError`, so it is read directly rather than through the failure-aware transport waits, the same way `a2a-allowlist-denied-cross-agent-send` reads its expected warning.
  - main at `70c93a29f17` (this PR's base): fails with `unexpected connection-failure reply: ⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. ...`
  - This branch at `a798fb3485e` (the scenario now requires two distinct named models before "request failed"): passes with `reply: ⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna, mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: Couldn't connect to the AI service. Check your connection, then try again. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow`. Check the conversation for any completed work before trying again.` qa-lab configures `gpt-5.6-luna-alt` as the fallback, both on the refused provider, so this is the real fallback-chain path, and both refused models are named. The first head named only the last one: with its `request-error-facts.ts`, the scenario fails on `⚠️ mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt request failed: ...`.
  - Command: `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario connection-failure-reply-names-model --concurrency 1 --fast`, after `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`: 22 passed.
  - "names the model whose connection failed" covers the named copy, a provider-prefixed model id, and the unchanged copy without facts. With main's `request-error-facts.ts` it fails with `Received: "⚠️ Couldn't connect to the AI service. ..."`.
  - "names only the fallback attempts that failed to connect" builds the error with the real `throwFallbackFailureSummary`: the primary is refused and the backup times out, then both are refused. With the first head's code it fails with `Received: "⚠️ backup/llama3.3 request failed: Couldn't connect ..."`.
- 34 related test files at `e40cb6903e0`: 1,053 passed, 0 failed. They are the 13 that assert this copy or call `resolveReplyFailoverFacts` (`agent-runner-failure-reply`, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e`, `incomplete-turn*`, `settled-turn-finalization*`, `payloads.errors`, `session-lifecycle-run-failure`, `server-methods`, `assistant-error-format` and others), plus `model-fallback*` and `agent-terminal-snapshot`.
- qa-lab scenario catalog tests (19 files): 145 passed, run at `fc2d656c3bc`. The scenario file is unchanged since.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exits 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Gap: the end-to-end proof is mock-openai against a closed local port. The refused-then-timed-out chain is covered by the unit test only; I did not build an end-to-end case for it. My fork runs the same naming on two bots with local models; I have not captured a live provider outage with this exact build.

prs.title: fix(talk): Talk chat shows the MEDIA file path instead of the image when a voice consult returns media
prs.body:
Closes #189542

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during realtime Talk, an image the agent returns appears as a raw `MEDIA:` file path instead of the image, and a reply that is only an image makes the voice stall on "one moment".

## User Impact

User impact: images and other files the agent returns during a Talk call now appear as attachments in the Talk chat, like normal chat. The path is not spoken. An image-only reply gets a short spoken acknowledgement instead of a stall, and if the attachment is refused, the voice says so instead of claiming it was shared. Phone, Meet, and FaceTime voice calls are unchanged.

Wording for maintainers: "I've put that in the chat." when the attachment lands, and "I couldn't put that in the chat." when it is refused. Happy to change either.

## Why This Change Was Made

The voice consult kept only the reply text and dropped its media. It now hands the answer's media, while the run is still registered, to the same Gateway attachment path normal agent replies use (`finalizeAgentRunMedia`), so the session's media-access rules and sensitive-media handling apply. `finalizeAgentRunMedia` now also reports whether an attachment actually landed; Gateway agent finals ignore that value. Speech still uses the reply text, which the runner has already cleaned of `MEDIA:` lines. Cancelling during attachment staging still ends the call turn as a cancellation, and delivery failures log a generic warning without file paths.

The delivery hook is internal to Gateway Talk, and the public realtime-voice SDK surface is unchanged. `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, which the plugin SDK re-exports from `src/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice.ts`, keeps exactly its `main` signature and calls the internal `consultRealtimeVoiceAgentWithAnswerMedia`. Only Gateway Talk calls that internal function, and it is the only one that accepts `deliverAnswerMedia`. Proof: the public declaration is identical to `main`, `src/plugin-sdk/` is unchanged, and `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base main --head HEAD` reports no Plugin SDK API changes. Phone, Meet, FaceTime, and third-party plugin callers are unaffected.

Live clients receive the consult message as it streams, and the attachment through the follow-up history refresh (`sessions.changed`), the same timing as Gateway agent finals. A live client may briefly show the `MEDIA:` line until that refresh.

## Evidence

Addresses ClawSweeper's "Before merge" items:

1. **Authority-chain proof at the media boundary.** `src/gateway/server.talk-consult-history.test.ts` drives the new Talk delivery callback into the real `finalizeAgentRunMedia`, chat history, and managed attachment owners (model faked; driver in `server.talk-consult-media.test-support.ts`). A spy on the media file opener (`fs.promises.open`) records whether the file is read. Revocations run inside a gate in media preparation, after admission and before any media read.
   - **Allowed media** (direct and relay, captioned and media-only): one managed image in `chat.history`, no raw path, exact speech, and the relay completion claim still succeeds.
   - **Out-of-scope media** in a workspace-only session (a file in an outside directory, and a workspace symlink escaping to it): never opened, no attachment, only the existing attachment-failed notice. Speech is the caption or "I couldn't put that in the chat."
   - **Revoked during staging** (relay Talk stops; relay completion claim settled by another owner; session reset): no file opened, no attachment, speech is the no-answer fallback, the relay claim returns false, and warnings are generic.
   - **Direct consult after hang-up** keeps delivering, matching its retained answer (existing behavior: "retains the direct answer when the call closes").
   - **Each guard is real:**
     - Disabling the Talk completion predicate makes the Talk-stops and claim-settled cases read the file.
     - Disabling the finalizer's session predicate makes the reset case read it.
     - The path normalizer and the local-root check stop outside files independently: the test goes red only with both disabled.
     - The media store's no-symlink open also refuses symlinks.
2. **Retained completion authority at media effects.** The callback passes only the consult's own run, session, abort signal, and completion-custody predicate. Media reads follow the session's read-tool policy, as in normal chat (every Gateway Talk caller has `read`). The tests above show that revoked or reassigned authority cannot read or attach media.
3. **Merge risk:** covered by item 1.

Found and fixed while proving this: a refused media-only reply used to say "I've put that in the chat." (red before the fix: `expected { text: 'I've put that in the chat.' } to deeply equal …`).

**Other regressions,** red on `main` and green here: "delivers {direct,relay} {captioned,media-only} consult media to Talk chat". The relay cases drive the reported gateway-relay path (`runPrompt` after adopted completion claims). `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts` checks four things:
- media is delivered before the run releases;
- cancellation during delivery stays a cancellation;
- delivery failures log no path;
- callers without a delivery hook keep today's fallback.

**Checks:** focused suites pass (history 30, runtime 19, agent-run-media 17, tool 8, and 159 across client-gateway-control, relay, and requester-final). `pnpm tsgo:core` and the gateway-server and other test typecheck shards are clean. Scoped oxlint and oxfmt are clean, and the test-line ratchet passes.

**Test cost:** `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts` takes 32.5s warm locally vs 25.9s on `main`. Only this full-Gateway layer proves history, attachments, relay claims, and revocation together.

**Still outstanding:** a redacted live Android gateway-relay Talk capture with a real model (captioned and media-only attachments, history reload, clean speech, and a following voice turn).

**Known follow-up:** the `talk.client.toolCall` path gives an empty tool result for media-only finals.

prs.title: fix(update): avoid redundant offline Doctor inspections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Offline Doctor copied every SQLite database merely to inspect reclamation mode, including already-incremental databases after readers and writers had drained. It now uses the existing immutable reader when there is no rollback journal and the WAL is absent or empty. Sources with recovery content retain artifact-preserving snapshots. Conversion, integrity, maintenance authority, identity, cancellation and space checks remain.

The synchronous integrity worker also now forwards the migration owner's existing `schemaOnly` option, matching asynchronous transport. Explicit FULL verification remains full, and QUICK never becomes a FULL-integrity receipt. This separately proven transport defect does not contribute to the measured native-update speedup: that path already uses asynchronous schema-only requests.

The stopped backup only copies, normalizes journals, syncs and hashes checkpointed sources; it is not reusable full SQLite-integrity proof. No backup semantics or migration validation changed. Transcript labels have no durable clean fact across updates, so no cross-deploy skip or new cache was added.

## Impact and measurement

Production delta is **+14 lines** (+24/−10): nine preserve the recovery branch while selecting immutable reads; five formatted lines forward one existing option. Tests and the exact instrumentation suppression inventory add 66 lines, with a separate allocation. Benchmark tooling adds 540 lines for reproducible fixture and native-copy/hash/durability attribution. No schema, config option, production sidecar, cache or new owner.

Five serial interleaved pairs passed, following two clean A/A controls. All ten runs preserve canonical content and pass schema verification without delivery repairs or admission warnings.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Ratio of medians Δ | Median paired Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Reclamation phase, s | 54.832 | 7.451 | -86.41% | -87.76% |
| Migration/Doctor + cleanup, s | 409.689 | 362.739 | -11.46% | -9.43% |
| Caller CPU, s | 113.366 | 105.372 | -7.05% | -0.65% |
| Sampled V8 allocation, GB | 6.201 | 6.130 | -1.15% | -1.19% |

Reclamation range: 52.71–93.78 s before, 6.57–8.31 s after. Total range: 385.15–474.91 s before, 348.26–442.61 s after. Every paired total improved; no total/CPU/allocation pair exceeded the 20% regression threshold. A/A totals were 508.11/483.16 s, reclamation 90.16/58.41 s, CPU 118.87/123.60 s, allocation 6.195/6.187 GB. Controls stay separate from pairs. Unchanged upstream phases vary; their shifts are not attributed to this patch. Maximum RSS median rose 5.04% with overlapping ranges and nearly identical maxima.

Baseline: `941f173975b3b43f7367c14f495ff61040af6469`. Reviewed candidate: `c7130f0b4839482f021f60b4ce26386bd500c709`. Each serial run uses a fresh synthetic fixture with 11.5 GiB shared state, a 35 GiB largest agent, seven agents, 10,003 canonical sessions and 62,000 workspace files (~1.1 GB), all incremental. The real native migration/Doctor command and CLI cleanup run with identical CPU-profile/allocation-sampling flags. Totals exclude package installation, service activation and post-start verification.

Large payload resides in a filler table, so this measures full-file work rather than 35 GiB of transcript or foreign-key content. The local filesystem is warm APFS, not btrfs; these are not deployment-outage forecasts. The full reclamation phase retains drains and lease-admission shared-state inspection. The regression proves zero target-inspection snapshots on checkpointed stores; the full-flow observer does not count every snapshot call. Bundled plugins are disabled by the existing workload, leaving an optional plugin-health warning while requested SQLite/session phases execute.

Initial controls with noncanonical delivery entries were rejected for clean-deployment acceptance: they triggered 10,003 legitimate repairs and subsequent resource-retirement warnings. The fixture now uses the existing normalization owner only for the clean deployment shape; the legacy benchmark shape is unchanged. Tiny and full-size clean controls have zero delivery repairs/admission warnings. Rejected controls are not pooled with accepted samples.

The unchanged stopped-snapshot microprobe ran two controls on 12.38 GB and 37.68 GB files. Native SHA-256 accounted for **99.78–99.85%** of combined owner time; APFS cloning took 0.53–1.07 ms per file, durability flushes 7.75–36.13 ms, and SQLite normalization/close 2.33–3.93 ms. No source checkpoint was needed. Independent source hashes and identities stayed unchanged. Source-oracle reads warm the cache and are outside owner timing; this does not apportion another filesystem's backup duration.

## Evidence

- Reclamation regression fails on base by preparing three snapshots during a no-op pass. Candidate reclamation/compaction: **17/17**. Real WAL-only mode truth and unchanged source artifacts are covered.
- Integrity regression fails on base by scanning unrelated damaged payload pages. Candidate workers: **25/25**. Damaged schema metadata and explicit FULL still fail; QUICK never publishes FULL proof.
- Both full builds pass. `pnpm check:changed` completed; its benchmark type/lint issues were repaired. Final full scripts typegraph, targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, suppression inventory **14/14** and test-line ratchet pass.
- Fresh complete **Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2**; current-head hosted Codex review has no findings.
- [Exact-head CI 41558974780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41558974780) is green at `c7130f0b4839482f021f60b4ce26386bd500c709`. Earlier CI found a lane-owned suppression-inventory omission; the exact receiver-forwarding/restoration exceptions were documented, replayed and reviewed before the final push. No inherited-CI exception is used.
- [Published-updater acceptance 41555116238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41555116238), attempt 2, passes: published `openclaw@2026.10.9` installs candidate build `fd1c8db63df3`, automatic migration and survival checks pass, and the Gateway starts and serves health/readiness/status. This is the manual-restart base scenario. Candidate production code is identical to final `c7130f0b4839`; later changes are benchmark/test tooling. Attempt 1 failed before product execution due runner disk exhaustion; only failed jobs were retried once for that diagnosed infrastructure failure.

**Unrelated local main regression:** the production unused-export scan reports `MEMORY_PROVENANCE_CHECK_ID` in `doctor-memory-provenance.ts`. It reproduces on exact base `941f173975b3b43f7367c14f495ff61040af6469`; commit `53a06f68e7297e78c065ca8ac526944d28113efa` introduced the exported constant with only a test consumer. prs.title: fix(imessage): fail closed when pairing store read fails
prs.body:
Fixes #191457

## What Problem This Solves

When the iMessage pairing store cannot be read, shared ingress currently converts the rejection into an empty stored allowlist. A pairing-policy DM whose sender is only known from that store then looks unpaired, so the sender receives a pairing challenge while the durable claim is not retried.

This change makes a pairing-store failure fail closed: the inbound dispatch owner sees the error, logs it, and can retry after the store recovers. Configured allowlist entries and access groups still admit their senders without reading the store.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared ingress helper now supports an opt-in `throwOnStoreReadError`; iMessage enables it only for reads that are actually required for admission. iMessage first checks whether the sender is already admitted by the configured allowlist or access groups. If yes, the store is not read at all. If no, the store read is allowed to throw instead of becoming `[]`.

This keeps open DMs, configured allowlist DMs, groups, and already-configured senders on the existing path. Only iMessage opts into propagation; other explicit readers retain the existing empty-list fallback. It does not add a new pairing owner or change stored data.

## User Impact

A transient pairing-store outage no longer sends a misleading pairing challenge to an already-paired sender, and the inbound claim is left retryable. Configured senders continue to deliver normally during the outage.

## Evidence

Focused iMessage decision tests:

```text
$ node scripts/test-projects.mts \
    extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts \
    extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       27 passed (27)
```

Regression behavior:

```text
before: failed read -> { kind: "pairing", senderId: "+15555550123" }
after:  failed read -> rejects with "pairing store unavailable"
```

Not tested: a real iMessage transport/store outage, or the configured-sender skip as a separate unit fixture. The proof covers the shared inbound-decision failure path; the production monitor now calls the same admission helper and lets a store error reach its existing inbound dispatch error path. Existing configured-allowlist gating tests remain green.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Traced the shared ingress store catch into the iMessage decision, added an opt-in failure propagation path, and covered both fail-closed and configured-sender behavior with focused tests.

Related: #187893
## What Problem This Solves

Parent sessions miss child approval events and reconnect replay when `session.store` points to a custom store.

## User Impact

Authorized parent subscribers receive their child's approval updates with custom stores. Existing recipient authorization and registry-parent precedence remain unchanged; no configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audience resolver used the metadata reader without its configured store locator. Pass the existing per-agent store resolver into that reader. The production change is two lines; the remaining changes prove the configured-store, registry and actual Gateway boundaries.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway runtime capture — outside Vitest

The missing shipped-entry gate is now exercised through the **normal package binary**, built independently from the parent and current PR commits. No Vitest, test-helper server startup, mocked audience/authorization, source imports or server-constructor calls were used. A separate Node observer imports the **built public** `dist/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.js` `GatewayClient` and uses real authenticated WebSocket connections and public RPCs.

|---|---|---|
| Original failure | `4fb684e294e27aed927548aaf64d2a7b8ba4696f`; `2026.10.9-4fb684e294e2-2026-10-31T23-19-58.960Z` | `false / false / false`, after all setup and positive controls passed |

Each run has its own private0700 HOME, config, client credentials, Gateway state, workspace, caches and loopback listener. Normal token authentication and device pairing remain enabled. Configuration is admitted by the normal CLI validator before launch; `session.store` points to `<RUN_ROOT>/custom-{agentId}/sessions.json`. Three equal-authority CLI clients isolate session routing. Public `sessions.create` and `sessions.describe` establish the actual stored child→parent metadata before approval registration. The unrelated subscription first receives its **own** pending and denied-terminal approval, then excludes the child's live events and pending replay while the child request remains pending. All resolutions are `deny`; no executor RPC, model call or external provider send is made. This is ordinary session projection proof, not separate-user resource authorization.

<details>
<summary>Exact build/launch commands and normal RPC flow</summary>

Paths and ephemeral endpoints below are placeholders for the task-owned builds and private per-run directories; no operator Gateway/service or production configuration is used.

prs.title: fix(slack): honor configured silence for implicit thread follow-ups
prs.body:
Related: #141556. Complements #141957; bot admission is separate (#160750 / #160752).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unwanted missing-reply notices when an unmentioned Slack thread follow-up returns `NO_REPLY` despite `surfaces.slack.silentReply.group: "allow"`.

## User Impact

Implicit reply-to-bot and participated-thread follow-ups can honor configured group silence. Explicit mentions, native slash commands, direct chats, unknown mention provenance, and default/disallowed group silence retain required replies. No configuration or stored-data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack records implicit thread admission as `WasMentioned: true` with `MentionSource: "implicit_thread"`. The existing requiredness owner now distinguishes that from an explicit request before applying the existing silence policy.

#141957 preserves authored silence in the output collector; it does not change this input classification and cannot make a required implicit-thread turn optional. This PR does not alter its scope.

Thanks to @shannon0430 for the fix and @zabealbe for the report. Sarah's #164848 changes another paragraph in the shared documentation; its tool-history and startup-context behavior is unchanged. No overlap with Pash/Sarah behavior changes.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and bundled Slack plugin in a secretless Node 24 Docker container, using a mock Slack Web API/Socket Mode boundary and a scripted Responses model returning `NO_REPLY`. Baseline rebuilt with the unchanged expectation owner at `344b71032447521feaff383f619667801dff6d83`; all other production sources in that comparison were identical. After integrating current main, the candidate was rebuilt and the same three cases rerun at `d07875a25badfee5d5a0878e27605ceb3caa9b04`.

| Input, with group silence allowed | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unmentioned reply to bot-authored thread root | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice | 1 model request; 0 replies; completed/idle |
| Explicit bot mention in thread | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice |
| Native `/openclaw` invocation | 2 model requests; 1 failure response | 2 model requests; 1 failure response |

Captured boundary output (synthetic identifiers omitted):

```text
baseline: implicit modelCalls=2
baseline: reply="Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again."
candidate: implicit modelCalls=1 replies=[]
candidate: message dispatch completed ... outcome=completed
candidate: session state ... new=idle reason="run_completed" queueDepth=0
candidate: explicit mention modelCalls=2 failureNotices=1
candidate: native slash modelCalls=2 failureResponses=1
```

The implicit completion was observed in the Gateway lifecycle log, not inferred only from a quiet interval. Explicit mention failure was posted to the original thread; the native slash failure used its response URL. Both are expected negative controls, not successful-answer evidence. This is isolated channel-boundary proof, not live Slack or real-provider proof.

Focused checks: 24 tests passed across the reply expectation and existing failure-reply suites (9.31 seconds Vitest duration). Reverting only the owner made the implicit-allow regression fail (`expected required to be optional`), while the six boundary cases passed. Changed TypeScript passed Oxlint; the regression file was formatted with Oxfmt.

Simplified contributor coverage from 86 to 32 lines: removed the synthetic admission pipeline and duplicated downstream completion assertions, retaining the actual policy regression and distinct safeguards. Against the merge base: production +3/-1, tests +32/-0, documentation +1/-1. The two net production lines carry and consume existing provenance in the existing owner; no new mechanism is needed.

### Telegram Test Server proof

Also ran the built Gateway and Telegram plugin at this exact head through the checkout's Telegram E2E runner, with a Convex-leased QA user and SUT bot, actual TDLib Test Server delivery, `surfaces.telegram.silentReply.group: "allow"`, and a scripted Responses provider. A proof-only recorder extension replied to the observed bot-authored root (its TDLib message identity was checked), rather than replying to the user's seed. The baseline rebuilt only the unchanged main expectation owner.

Captured, redacted native timeline:

```text
HEAD:
  4.396s  SUT: P164877_TG_ROOT
  4.613s  user: unmentioned reply to that SUT root
          primary model requests=1; terminal outcome=completed; no SUT message
 50.505s  user: explicit @SUT mention
 52.068s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error

BASE:
  4.581s  SUT: P164877_TG_ROOT
  4.785s  user: unmentioned reply to that SUT root
  6.580s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error
 50.309s  user: explicit @SUT mention
 51.978s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error
```

Both 105-second recordings completed. Request counts above are the primary agent's `gpt-5.5` Responses requests, correlated with its three inbound turns; auxiliary memory requests are excluded. The implicit head turn reached the model and completed, so its silence was not a dropped input. The successful proof lease was released, private credential and TDLib state removed, and both Gateways stopped. Raw identities remain only in private proof; no live production Telegram or real model-provider claim.

CI on this head is blocked by an inherited failure in [checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38485509739/job/115598538462): `tombstones a redelivered source whose recovery claim is already terminal` receives `UNAVAILABLE: Session facts are unavailable; retry the request` at the session-authorization assertion. The same focused case fails identically on clean main `c8111aba15e` and this head, before the reply runner is invoked. No CI rerun or replacement push was requested.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; reverting fully restores prior behavior. Blast radius is group/channel requests with implicit-thread provenance and an explicitly allowed silence policy; explicit requests and other channels' ordinary mention classifications remain unchanged.

prs.body:
Stack: depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191226. Review this PR against its stacked base. Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191229.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191191

## What Problem This Solves

We need to compare affected-test recommendations against full execution before allowing any CI test skips.

## User Impact

Operators can generate a shadow plan with per-file reasons while the scheduled inventory remains complete. Nothing consumes the candidate plan as permission to skip tests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selector combines a current inventory and diff with compatible baseline observations. Global or unmapped changes, stale context, audits, missing history and incomplete evidence retain tests. Optional model recommendations can add tests but cannot remove graph selections.

The caller supplies the complete inventory, diff, and provenance. The command makes no model calls. This is the middle layer of the adaptive CI stack.

## Evidence

- Eleven selection tests pass through the repository-selected unit-fast runner on the merged observation base (774 ms Vitest duration, 2.57 s shard wall time).
- The full tooling test typecheck, scoped typed lint and pinned formatting pass. Production and full-tree unused-file scans each report zero entries.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper reviews of the original layer and final typing repair found no actionable issue. Restacking preserved the implementation; only parent annotation context changed.
- Exact-head GitHub CI remains the broad merge gate.

The planner always returns the full execution inventory. Candidate omissions are advisory; model recommendations can only add candidates. This PR does not wire test skipping into CI.

Firecrawl-backed web fetch reports the original source URL as `finalUrl` after a redirect, even when Firecrawl supplies the resolved destination in `metadata.url`. This gives callers incorrect attribution.

## What Changed

Prefer the existing normalized `metadata.url` in the post-response result projection, before the existing sourceURL/data.url/requested-URL fallbacks. The requested `url` remains unchanged. No request, fetch guard, normalizer, credential policy, API or configuration changes.

## Evidence

Head: `69b1663924ed6cef50dffa8907e6a3bcd3234354`.

[Built CLI before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189425#issuecomment-6592886256): clean main and candidate builds in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker, normal `infer web fetch --provider firecrawl` against a faithful local Firecrawl API fixture. For sourceURL A and resolved metadata.url B, main reports finalUrl A twice; candidate reports B twice. No-redirect, missing metadata.url and invalid-protocol fallback controls stay A on both refs; HTTP 503 stays exit 1. All 20 requests preserve the same method, endpoint, complete JSON body and synthetic auth header across refs. No paid hosted service was used; the fixture proves response projection, not Firecrawl's redirect engine.

Source trace confirms the changed value is only post-response output and is not fed back into a fetch guard. The direct transport's separate finalUrl variable is unchanged. Current main was merged because #190706 modified this owner; all contributor commits are preserved.

The regression is consolidated into the existing payload suite, retaining hostile metadata fallback coverage with no net test growth. It fails on main for the incorrect final URL and passes on candidate. Candidate payload/tool suites: 61 tests passed, 29.92 s Vitest / 32.10 s runner including cold compilation; changed payload test execution approximately 0.1 s. Focused Oxfmt, Oxlint and whitespace checks passed.

Whole-PR deltas: production +1/-0, tests +4/-4 (net 0), docs +2/-0. The separate HTTP fixture and test-growth allocation are removed; the shipped CLI proof covers those transport/result controls.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores previous result selection; no state migration or persistence changes. Blast radius is Firecrawl fetch result attribution when metadata contains a usable resolved URL. Network requests and SSRF guards remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix: degraded-summary warning never appears when context overflow triggers compaction
prs.body:
Closes #191590

## What Problem This Solves

When context overflow triggers a recovery compaction that commits a degraded or refused summary, the recovery end event drops the recorded `qualityDegraded` and `summaryRefused` facts. The existing notice consumer consequently reports normal completion (`notifyUser: true`) or nothing (`false`) instead of its mandatory context-loss warning.

This is a distinct producer bug from the Telegram delivery repair in #191516.

## Change and User Impact

Read the committed recovery result through the existing `parseCompactionDetails` owner and carry its existing quality/refusal facts on the end event, matching the in-session producer. Users receive the existing degraded-summary warning regardless of routine notice opt-in. The parser, consumer, warning text, notifyUser and compaction selection/commit policy are unchanged. No new API, configuration, schema, model prompt or warning wording.

The same producer serves overflow, budget-precheck and timeout recovery. Only overflow recovery was exercised end to end here.

Contributor masatohoshino's original commit is preserved. The regression is consolidated into the existing recovery boundary case, retaining the locked model/auth/fallback/cache/overflow assertions. Redundant attempt-fixture overrides disappeared; the owner only consumes its promptCache. Production delta: **+17/-9 = +8**; test delta: **+18/-19 = -1**, no allocation record or shared scalar change.

## Evidence

Exact head: `7f315e432193bdf4c7df234a850de3757951f16e`; main baseline: `a5a98d58a90414e7e6f2ef68f50a2e8b147add88`.

[Real Telegram Test Server userbot proof, before/after timelines, healthy controls and lease cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191592#issuecomment-6594147510).

Built Gateway in official node:24.22.1 Docker, deterministic localhost model, actual Test Server Bot API and TDLib userbot. A real context-overflow HTTP error drives core's natural recovery compaction; inadequate model summaries fail its actual quality audit and commit degraded provenance. The model never emits warning text. All cases keep the safeguard quality audit enabled.

- Main twice with `notifyUser: true`: normal completion instead of warning; twice with false: no compaction notice.
- Exact head twice per setting: the existing warning before exactly one final, surviving native progress-card deletion.
- Healthy main/head controls: normal start/completion, no warning.
- All ten fresh Gateways shut down cleanly; ten leases released; private credential payload and restored scratch checked absent.

Focused regression suite: **9/9 pass** on head, **8 pass / 1 fail** on main because both event facts are missing. Vitest duration: head 28.71s (tests 1%), main 19.99s. Paired command wall time 77.57s; most cost is cold transformation, not added test execution. Focused oxfmt/oxlint and both builds pass. Broad validation belongs to PR CI.

The contributor's earlier fake Bot API evidence is superseded by the real Test Server captures above. The proof-only runner loader handles lease ownership and task profiles; its NODE_OPTIONS is stripped from the Gateway child, so no product runtime preload or source injection. No paid provider or personal Gateway.

## Boundaries and Merge Risk

Small synthetic history completed compaction without token reduction; no reduction is claimed. Native proof covers degraded wording, not refusal wording; the consolidated regression verifies both qualityDegraded and summaryRefused on the producer event. Budget-precheck and timeout recovery were not separately runtime exercised. No visual/screenshot claim is made.

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous event shape; this patch adds no persisted state or migration. Blast radius is recovery-compaction notices across consumers; an incorrect fact could suppress or spuriously select the existing context-loss warning. Healthy controls guard against a false warning, while compaction policy and final-answer behavior remain unchanged.
