prs.title: fix(sessions): tags hide committed changes from checkout diffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes legal Git tags hiding committed work from session Changes. A tag named `main` at a feature commit can override the real default branch, producing an empty `sessions.diff` and rejecting that commit's preview as `unknown_commit`. Same-name current-branch and remote-default tags also distort displayed branch identities.

## User Impact

Committed session files remain visible in All Changes and commit previews even when tags collide with branch names. No repository content, tags, configuration, permissions or public API changes. No-tag and detached-HEAD behavior remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve branch identities and branch-relative bases with Git's unambiguous namespaces at the existing session-diff owners. Keep accepted managed-base precedence, captured-HEAD ancestry checks and object-format handling intact. This follows the same identity invariant as #191047, without a consumer-side correction or another resolver. Alix-007's original commit is preserved.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + real Chromium proof, inspected before/after screenshots, and all eleven baseline-failure attributions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191155#issuecomment-6581090062).

- Independently built Gateway and Control UI on pinned main `744232dfe4ddf40d98ba768efc6a40314eb3b927` and exact candidate `826f822fc5a3afe71ab645ad28af565be79d1514`, in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Recorded build commits match both source identities.
- Public `sessions.create` and `sessions.diff`, twice per artifact with independent real Git repositories and committed files. Main twice hides `session.txt` after adding a colliding tag and rejects its commit preview; candidate twice returns the complete +1/−0 patch.
- Real Control UI All Changes twice shows **No changes** on main, and twice shows the expanded committed `session.txt` patch on candidate. Captures wait for finished animations, fonts and stable panel geometry.

Fixes an open meeting-source edit being rejected after an unrelated setting finishes autosaving, even though the source itself has not changed. A successful config acknowledgement refreshes source objects; object identity is not evidence of a concurrent edit.

## User Impact

A source title or locator draft remains saveable after toggling transcript storage. Users no longer need to cancel and reopen an unchanged source. A genuine concurrent source edit still reports a conflict and is not overwritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare the complete source JSON using the existing canonical equality helper at the existing source-editor guard. The runtime config owner still owns autosave acknowledgements and revision hashes; the Gateway still owns persistence. Latest-source selection, mutation permissions, field validation and recovery remain unchanged. No additional state, normalizer, schema or provider policy. Alix-007's original commit is preserved.

## Evidence

[Exact-head built Gateway / real Chromium proof, inspected screenshots, and genuine concurrent-edit controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191172#issuecomment-6582697303).

- Pinned main `1dc0ebff3c2e6a615c23d7100c6edfbf605972e2` and candidate `c3246aa90429de6bc2529fa7431395b79eb741c3`, independently built Gateway and UI in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Real Linux Chromium loads the Gateway-served settings page; build identities and distinct served-entry hashes are recorded.
- Twice per artifact: open a source title edit, toggle transcript storage off, wait for the real autosave acknowledgement and independent config readback proving the entire source unchanged, then Save source.
- Main twice shows the false source-changed conflict and leaves the saved title unchanged. Candidate twice closes the editor cleanly and persists the exact draft title with the original provider/session ID and storage still disabled.
- Genuine concurrency, twice on both refs: a separate public RPC operator changes the actual source while the editor remains open. The browser receives its normal config.changed refresh; Save source reports a genuine conflict, emits no stale write, and preserves the concurrent edit.
- Canonical static screenshot frames and same-frame crops are inspected; no transient Saved banner is used as evidence. Both Gateways shut down normally.
- Focused owner suite: **30 passed** on candidate; identical consolidated regression on main **29 passed / 1 intended failure**. Formatting, lint, Gateway builds and UI builds passed.
- Folded the autosave boundary into existing normalization/optional-clear coverage, removing duplicate fixture setup while retaining adjacent untouched-whitespace and genuine-replacement controls. Tests **−6 lines**, production **+1 line**, no test allocation.

This proves editing existing unavailable-provider source configuration, not provider capture, recordings, meeting-note generation, models, channels or a production installation.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old comparison without a migration or persisted-format change. Blast radius is the meeting source editor's stale-draft guard; semantic source changes still conflict, and Gateway revision/write authority is untouched.

prs.title: fix(ios): CLI chat tool rows show raw MCP bridge names
prs.body:
Closes #191211

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing CLI-backed chats on iOS see raw bridge labels such as “Mcp Openclaw Exec” and generic icons instead of the tool’s own title and icon.

## Why This Change Was Made

Present `mcp__<server>__<tool>` as `<tool>` using the existing tool display registry. Invocation identities and stored names stay raw. The transcript cache uses the presented name when retaining patch input, so bridged patch previews also survive a cold load. Incomplete bridge names remain unchanged; this does not change tool execution or authorization.

## User Impact

Bridged tools have the same readable titles, icons, and argument details as their unprefixed equivalents. Patch previews remain available after a cache reload. The shared registry also serves macOS chat presentation.

## Evidence

### Simulator A/B

Same synthetic fixture; the bridged row is `mcp__openclaw__exec`. Only this fix changes its label/icon; “Tool details” styling is unchanged.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/d81580a/sim-before.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/d81580a/sim-after.png) |

### Real device / live Gateway

An iPhone 13 Pro Max connected to a live Gateway using Claude CLI showed bridge-prefixed tool labels on build 102470 (plain main `6dbfe001cf1`). Build 102473 (main `75be4d0f933`) showed “Exec” with terminal icons. These are tightly cropped labels, not a same-call comparison:

| Before 102470 | After 102473 |
|---|---|
| ![Before phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/d81580a/phone-before.png) | ![After phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/d81580a/phone-after.png) |

The after-build also carried separate usage-footer and “Tool details” styling fixes, plus #171976 and #190408. Those affect different UI elements; the simulator A/B isolates this label change.

### Offline transcript-cache reload

An iOS simulator connected to a live Gateway showed the same bridged Exec row with its raw label before the fix and its friendly title and terminal icon afterward. After terminating the app, removing that simulator's device approval, and relaunching, the app could not reconnect. Opening the saved chat and expanding its work list still showed “Exec”, “Exec”, and “Session Send” from the on-device transcript cache.

| Before, online | After, online |
|---|---|
| ![Raw bridge label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/7da776c158799fb8df630b4e0937c10fca9ec29e/before.png) | ![Friendly Exec label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/7da776c158799fb8df630b4e0937c10fca9ec29e/after-online.png) |

### Focused validation

The prepared stock/patched regression run executed 98 tests in five suites: stock had four assertion issues in the new display/cache regressions; patched passed all 98. Assertions cover readable titles/details, incomplete-name preservation, retained patch input, unchanged stored identities, and discarded non-patch arguments. Codex review caught the cold-cache retention gap; it was fixed before the clean cross-family review.

A fresh focused run on the rebased branch is in progress; the completed 98-test red/green result above is from the prepared patch before rebase.

AI-assisted implementation and review. I understand the presentation-only normalization and cache-retention change. No Gateway or phone deployment is part of this PR.

prs.title: fix(cache): keep private cache TTLs on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A wall-clock correction can prematurely expire or extend three private in-memory cache windows: native Codex plugin metadata, Control UI link previews, and session CI check details.

## User Impact

A host clock correction no longer triggers unnecessary native plugin discovery, preview downloads, or CI job-detail fetches while their elapsed-time windows are still fresh. TTL values, retry delays, authentication, network guards, principal/session/credential scope, and explicit invalidation are unchanged. No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep expiry writes and reads in one elapsed-time domain: the existing `monotonicNow()` owner in core, and `performance.now()` inside the Codex extension. These private readings never leave their caches and are not persisted as wall-clock timestamps.

Includes #191533, #191575 and #191577. The original commits by **wangmiao0668000666** are cherry-picked for credit, including the contributor's regression-fixture correction. #191576 and #191210 are intentionally excluded; no source PR is closed by this PR.

## Evidence

[Exact runtime counters and proof receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191606#issuecomment-6593683015).

Built both Gateway/CLI artifacts on Linux in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Frozen main `913f025cd15ba79d4002ad4e6db1fe2739ba8f8f`; candidate production artifact `c772becb16e5f64fd022c0bcd814a4eaf54b4d1a` (final follow-up changes tests/docs and formatting only).

Four fresh-profile runs, main twice and candidate twice, through authenticated public Gateway RPCs and real native Codex turns:

| Cache | No-step control, all runs | Main after +61-minute wall step, twice | Candidate after same step, twice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Link preview | One page fetch; repeated read reuses revision 1 | Premature refetch, revision 2 | One fetch retained; revision 1 |
| CI check details | One jobs request; repeated read reuses check 1 | Premature jobs refetch, check 2 | One jobs request retained; check 1 |
| Codex plugin metadata | One real `plugin/installed`; next fresh session reuses it | Third real turn issues a second `plugin/installed` | Third real turn retains one `plugin/installed` |

All 12 native Codex turns completed and returned `CACHE_TURN_OK`. The real bundled Codex app-server talks to a task-only synthetic managed API-key profile and a local trusted CONNECT/TLS Responses fixture. A transparent stdio recorder forwards bytes unchanged and records actual plugin RPCs. Link/GitHub HTTP transports are local fixtures at the final fetch boundary; production request admission, DNS/SSRF checks, credentials and scope logic remain unchanged. This is not a live upstream service claim.

**Clock method:** the same preload approach as #190894 steps only the Gateway process's `Date.now()` by +61 minutes. This is a **process-local wall-clock step, not a system clock jump**. `performance.now()`, timers and the operating-system clock are not altered.

Personally inspected native Codex source at `ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897`: [plugin request/response contracts](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/plugin.rs#L129-L194) and [catalog processing/background refresh](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/plugins.rs#L550-L820). OpenClaw's fail-open/cacheable guard is unchanged.

Focused existing suites: candidate **48/48 pass** (42 Gateway + 6 Codex). Same updated expiry tests on main: two intended preview expiry failures and one intended Codex expiry failure; remaining 45 pass. Existing scope, network, coalescing, revocation, retry and invalidation controls retained. Targeted formatting and Oxlint pass. Tests net 0; no allocations or SDK exports.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old private clock comparisons without a state migration. Blast radius is cache reuse for native Codex plugin metadata, link previews and session CI details; no permission or network policy changes.

prs.title: fix(android): Dashboard shows "Not Found" when the Gateway serves the Control UI under a base path
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190198

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android app's embedded Dashboard, Terminal and Desktop pages show the Gateway's `Not Found` when the Gateway serves the Control UI under a base path (`gateway.controlUi.basePath`) and the app connected without a path in the URL (a discovered Gateway, or a manual host and port). This is the Android side of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141, which fixed the same symptom on macOS.

## User Impact

User impact: Android users whose Gateway mounts the Control UI under a base path can open the Dashboard, Terminal and Desktop without adding the path to the connection URL by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 the Gateway advertises its Control UI mount in hello-ok as `controlUiBasePath`. The Android app built the page base only from the connection URL's path, which is empty for discovered and host-and-port connections.

The hello-ok summary now carries `controlUiBasePath`, and the Control UI page base uses it when the connection URL has no path. A path in the connection URL (a reverse-proxy mount) still wins, the same precedence as macOS. A Gateway that does not send the field keeps the old base. The advertised value goes through the existing context-path normalizer.

Accepted edge case: when the connection URL has a path and the Gateway also sets a different base path, the pages keep the URL path while source favicons and inbound images follow the configured base path, as they already did before this change.

The change is limited to the hello-ok parse and the page base URL and one test.

## Evidence

Tested at `400fc200227` (base `main` at `3ee3675fe14`).

Both sides ran the Android third-party debug app on an Android 16 emulator, paired once through "Set up manually" with host and port only, unencrypted, to an isolated Gateway (own state directory and config, loopback port, synthetic token) with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/gateway"`. One script drove both sides; only the installed APK differed: cold launch, Overview, Chat, Chat actions, Dashboard, then wait up to 20 s for the Control UI's "Skip to main content" landmark in the accessibility tree. As a control, it checks that the native Dashboard screen opened. Nothing was mocked.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| native Dashboard screen opens (control) | met | met |
| embedded Dashboard loads the Control UI | **not met** | met |

The Gateway serves the Control UI only under the mount:

```text
GET http://127.0.0.1:19411/          -> 404 "Not Found"   (the page base Android used before)
GET http://127.0.0.1:19411/gateway/  -> 200               (the mount advertised in hello-ok)
```

Capture: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261031-185141-android-control-page-base-path/gateway-paths.txt

Before (base `3ee3675fe14`): the Dashboard WebView loads `http://10.0.2.2:19411/` and shows `Not Found` while the app reports the Gateway online. After (this PR): the page base is `http://10.0.2.2:19411/gateway` and the Dashboard shows the Control UI.

![Android Dashboard, Before and After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261031-185141-android-control-page-base-path/android-dashboard-before-after.png)

Recordings of both runs, side by side: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261031-185141-android-control-page-base-path/android-dashboard-before-after.mp4

Observed result: on the base the embedded Dashboard is the Gateway's 404 page; with the fix it is the Control UI.

Checks: `./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` and `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI. The new test connects to a fake Gateway by host and port, with hello-ok advertising `controlUiBasePath: "/gateway"`, and reads the Control UI page base. It fails on the base (`expected:<http://127.0.0.1:<port>[/gateway]> but was:<http://127.0.0.1:<port>[]>`) and passes with the fix; the other 86 tests in the class pass on both.

| Test file | Gradle test time |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/GatewayBootstrapAuthTest.kt` | new test 0.11 s (class 14.1 s for 87 tests) |

Not covered: an emulator only; a discovered (Bonjour) connection and a physical phone were not run, and Terminal and Desktop were not opened in the device run (they read the same page base).

prs.title: fix(gateway): show the busy-state Stop notice when sessions.abort hits database contention
prs.body:
Closes #160004

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the session database is busy, Stop on a recovered embedded run (sent through `sessions.abort`) fails with an unclassified error, so the Control UI cannot tell the user that Stop may already have taken effect.

## User Impact

User impact: Stop through `sessions.abort` now returns the same typed busy-state outcome as `chat.abort` (`UNAVAILABLE` with `details.errorKind: "state_contention"`), so the Control UI shows its "check this turn's status before trying Stop again" notice instead of a generic failure. No other errors and no successful Stops change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.abort` already classified SQLite contention at the RPC boundary (#156067), but `sessions.abort` called the inner lifecycle handler directly and bypassed that classification. The classifier now lives in one small module, `stop-state-contention.ts`, moved unchanged from `chat-abort-handler.ts`, which is at its line cap. Both Stop routes wrap their handler with it, so the wording, the error code and `errorKind` cannot drift apart. Cancellation is not replayed, and the response does not claim that Stop had no effect. This follows up the closed, author-withdrawn #159282.

## Evidence

- New regression `sessions.abort-contention.test.ts`: it registers a live embedded run, sends `sessions.abort` through `handleGatewayRequest`, and makes the worker session read used while saving the cancellation fail with a SQLite lock error (`errcode: 5`). It asserts that the run is stopped once, nothing is thrown, and the response is the typed `UNAVAILABLE` error.
  - Fix reverted: fails. The raw `database is locked` error escapes `sessions.abort`.
  - With the fix: passes.
- Existing tests pass: `chat.abort-errors` (14), `sessions-abort` (8), `sessions.abort-embedded` (29), `sessions.abort-durability` (7), `sessions.abort-agent-scope` (27).
- Format, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the changed files.
- Gap: the lock error is injected at the worker read, the same technique the existing `chat.abort` contention test uses. It was not produced by a foreign process holding the database lock; #159282 found its real-lock fixture no longer reaches the contended write after #169622. No UI code changed, so there are no screenshots.

prs.title: feat(chat): choose how follow-ups interrupt active work
prs.body:
Related: #57208 (prior interrupt/priority-control context; this PR does not implement pause/resume or drop queued siblings).

**Nov 3 update — prepared locally, not yet published:** two feature repairs and additional authority proof are ready, but the managed publisher refused the base integration because this request lacks full operator write authority for the upstream workflow-file changes. A maintainer with that authority must publish the saved candidate. The branch still points to `fcedbe2a1b07b1557154d53af0b8ea73bb40f6c5`; do not treat the locally prepared evidence below as proof that this remote head is repaired.

## What Problem This Solves

Users need a clear choice between waiting, steering at the next boundary, and interrupting current work for a follow-up, across chat surfaces rather than only in the Control UI.

## User Impact

User impact: choose a personal Queue, Steer, or Interrupt & send default, or promote an already accepted queued message without copying and resending it.

Interrupt requests cancellation immediately but waits for the incumbent writer to settle before the selected input runs. Other queued messages remain queued in order. Explicit per-message/session choices take precedence over the authenticated submitting profile's default, which takes precedence over channel/global defaults. Offline TUI controls remain session-local rather than inventing an authenticated personal profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a per-item **Interrupt & send** action and explain the three follow-up modes in the Control UI.
- Route interruption through shared `chat.interrupt` and existing queue/admission owners, promoting the original accepted input rather than cancel-and-resend. Keep input identity, scope/incarnation and current-authority checks, sibling ordering, and writer settlement intact.
- Expose common `/followupmode queue|steer|interrupt|default` and `/interrupt list|<id>` controls through the existing shared command catalog/forwarding paths, including the TUI and native/text-channel command surfaces. Active-run-safe controls do not themselves trigger the personal interrupt default.

This is the interrupt-options feature only; it does not claim to fix the separate lingering-steer or acknowledgment-copy bugs.

Contributor credit: @TheAngryPit. The source commit preserves the verified co-author trailer.

## Evidence

### Locally prepared repair candidate (not on the branch yet)

- Pinned base: `d40aa7c6f2ba70e0c59e244d09a325d25e1457b0`. Conflicts were confined to the append-only method table and generated predicates; upstream methods were retained and validators regenerated from canonical schemas.
- Reproduced the overflow case red: running A, queue B/C/D under cap 2, drop-old, then interrupt C. The live writer was not canceled. The local repair follows canceled predecessor ancestry; the regression and held-writer/sibling cases pass.
- Reproduced another defect red through an actual Gateway: changing the personal default during delayed preparation reclassified an already accepted Queue input as Interrupt. The local repair preserves its accepted RPC timing choice; future inputs still use the new preference.
- Six real isolated-Gateway scenarios passed: RPC and shared-command interruption, a caller lacking session-write access, requester membership revoked across the handler’s actual awaited read, revoked queued-source authority, and the delayed-default regression. Observed provider cancellation/execution effects directly; a revoked source also failed at later execution and a fresh authorized input worked. These use a synthetic HTTP model, not a live provider or native Codex.
- 153 affected queue/command/TUI tests and 105 method-scope/prefix-stability consumer tests passed. Core, root-product-test and TUI-test typechecks passed; targeted lint/format and generated-validator/registry checks passed. Normal commit hooks passed; the hook skipped protocol regeneration for the partial commit index, so that check was run separately on the full candidate.
- Complete candidate Auto Review on the bound OpenClaw route: four completed P0–P2 passes, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed local source snapshot `1ad2c6e8860ef2102cb8b8bd755059b449504439c20addf423cda3e11f4d1d6f`; full candidate tree `bf78e1f2128e247a732f7876935aa121e385a459`. No source/context truncation or reviewer-route switch.

**Remaining proof:** latest-stable upgrade qualification has NOT run. The normal consumer installation of `openclaw@2026.10.9` was refused by the environment’s seven-day package-age policy. No exception, substitute baseline, schema change, or migration was introduced. This is neither proof of incompatibility nor successful upgrade proof. An operator-approved exception for that exact baseline, or its normal admission, is needed.

<details>
<summary>Investigated proof limitations</summary>

An overbroad post-revocation FIFO assertion also observed unrelated retained owner inputs ending with generic errors after the sharing revision changed. The final security cases isolate their distinct contracts: no cancellation/promotion from denied authority, no provider execution from the revoked source, and a fresh authorized request still works. Survival of other retained inputs across sharing-policy mutations is not qualified or claimed fixed. The prior unforced command-ordering failure led to the deterministic late-default regression and its repair; a passing replay alone was not used as the fix.

</details>

Hosted re-review has not been requested on the old head. Publish this candidate and current proof first, then request re-review.
### Previously published candidate evidence

- **Conflict integration against `6c96aff8e06116c47c796cd770ac1645c0312fd5`:** retained both append-only method additions and regenerated validators from canonical schemas with the refreshed frozen-lockfile dependencies. Re-ran 242 Gateway/command/TUI cases, 109 UI cases, and both real-Gateway synthetic-model flows: all passed. Core/UI typechecks, generated-validator check, protocol registry, UI copy verification, targeted method-owner lint/format, and staged whitespace check passed. No feature UI or screenshots changed.
- **Real isolated product:** 2 Gateway flows through authenticated public RPCs and the actual selected OpenClaw runtime, with a deterministic HTTP model. Covered personal defaults, accepted-input interruption through RPC/shared commands, cancellation, history, sibling ordering, and refusing consumed inputs. This is synthetic-model proof, not live-provider or native-Codex qualification.
- **Control UI:** 2 Chromium flows against the built UI and a mocked Gateway, with inspected before/after screenshots. These are separate from the real-Gateway flows, not a combined browser/live-backend claim.
- **Queue/writer regression:** reproduced premature execution while cancellation cleanup/writer settlement was held; producer fix passed the regression and 300 TUI/controller cases at that candidate.
- **Independent review:** four completed P0–P2 passes on the full candidate found a P2 A→B→A selection-priority defect. Reproduced and repaired it, then passed 39 affected cases plus targeted types/lint/format. No new clean independent verdict is claimed after that repair or later behavior-preserving sibling extractions.
- **Original local-commit checks (before base integration):** normal commit hooks passed, including protocol-since and file-size gates; post-extraction TUI suite 273 cases, UI parent suite 106 cases, and the 2 moved browser cases passed, along with core/UI types and targeted lint/format. Committed whitespace check passed.

**Qualification gaps:** no native-device run, live messaging-channel transport run, native-Codex run, or live-provider test. Shared RPC/catalog availability is not presented as device/transport proof. PR CI remains the broad qualification gate; its current status must be read on the exact published head.

**Hosted CI on the unchanged published head:** checks are red, not green. [Preflight checkout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41290340379/job/124800091217) failed before tests with Git `early EOF` / `fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output` (exit 128). This is an observed checkout failure, not a product-test verdict; no blind rerun was requested.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep session branch PR cache windows on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The in-process session branch-PR cache anchors its TTL on `Date.now()`. A
wall-clock correction during the process lifetime (NTP step, manual clock
change, or suspend/resume) extends or shortens the cache window: after a
backward step the sidebar shows the previous branch PR list instead of
refetching, and after a forward step it refetches prematurely (extra GitHub
API calls). The rate-limit and failure backoff windows are likewise
correction-sensitive.

Precedent: #190997 (merged; same elapsed-time shape on the discord REST entity
cache), #191210 (open; github detail cache). This PR applies the same
already-approved shape to the session PR cache window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session PR cache owner anchors its `expiresAt` writes and reads on the
wall clock. The cache is module-local (never leaves the process), so it can be
anchored on the process-local monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) instead.
Compare and write now happen in the same clock domain; no entry leaves the
module.

Production LOC is `+6/-6, net 0`.

Classification: `behavior-preserving`

## User Impact

A wall-clock correction no longer changes how long the branch PR list, rate
limit backoff, and failure windows are held. Under a stable clock the behavior
is identical; only the correction-sensitive edge changes (no stale PR list
served after an NTP step, no burst of extra GitHub API calls after a forward
step).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `d4150ac86a5996fb63f3af264c9e902f1baa658c`
- Current-main base: `634c1bfe531e782671b1a1da904819be44eee4ba`
- Production entry: `loadControlUiSessionPullRequests` /
  `cachedBranchPullRequests` in `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: branch PR cache window (`expiresAt` writes at
  `:319/:330/:342/:648`, compare at `:690`)
- Decision surface: the module-local `branchCache` TTLs (`SUCCESS_CACHE_MS`,
  `FAILURE_CACHE_MS`, `RATE_LIMIT_CACHE_MS`)
- Recorder/readback boundary: `fetchImpl` call count on the shared clock
- Acceptance RED: on the unchanged `Date.now()` production, a wall-clock step
  back by 60s does not expire the entry (the 90s success window is wrongly
  extended); the regression fails at the "no refetch" assertion
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, the wall-clock step does not extend the
  window, and advancing past the 90s TTL on the shared clock expires the entry
  (refetch happens)
- Legal control: the existing staleness cases still pass (8/8 total)
- Cleanup: every run used the isolated `withOpenClawTestState` fixture; no
  production Gateway, session, token, or configuration was touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Remote vitest on the real cache owner (elapsed-time regression case):

```text
# RED — production kept on Date.now(), run only the new elapsed case
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 7 skipped (8)
# the wall-clock back-step did not expire the entry → fetch count stayed at
# initial → assertion failed
```

```text
# GREEN — exact head (performance.now())
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-staleness.test.ts` — remote, 8/8 green on exact head
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- Not tested: full suite on the latest main (this PR's head is based on `634c1bfe531`, CI runs it); the remote vitest snapshot is 2026.10.9.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+6/-6`
- Test LOC: `+38/-0`
- Existing-solutions preflight: same elapsed-time shape as #190997 / #191210;
  no new helper, option, or config surface
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

prs.title: fix(sessions): context token count stays stale for the whole of a long agent turn
prs.body:
Related: #164550

## What Problem This Solves

The session's context count (`totalTokens`) can stay at its pre-turn value throughout a long embedded agent turn. This publishes the latest settled model call's prompt context while the turn is running. Turn completion still writes the final accounting result.

The writer serializes and coalesces writes, fences them to the admitted session/run, closes before final accounting, and drains before settlement returns. Detached and incognito attempts, and follow-ups that preserve user-facing session state, do not use it. This covers the embedded runner; mid-turn reporting for the separate Codex app-server and CLI backends is not established.

## Current revision

Head: [`170809258591d0b12f65f2054404e906e87ac2b3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/170809258591d0b12f65f2054404e906e87ac2b3)
Tree: `f3f4f7519c047e58dbe45da651e001dfc68ba769`

This merges previous head `633860da372bfa96638235cde41244f853357115` with pinned main `4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d`, preserving both parents. The session-store conflict resolution keeps main's removal of the retired recovery API and the PR's final-context override after snapshot projection. It also retains upstream's fork-boundary and cron writer contract changes. No duplicate repair for the upstream PostgreSQL setup fixture was added.

The exact 20-path delta received an independent source review with no actionable finding. This does not settle the Goal-budget policy decision below.

## Evidence

A bounded Linux x64 runner validated the complete tree above with Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, Vitest 5.0.5 and frozen dependencies. Lockfile SHA-256: `01c02f06984feaa8090c17b45e80e83e1f0842f38eed2f9ab37b113f0a4627fc`.

The positive total is **95 distinct cases**. The restored confirmation repeats one of those cases; it is not counted again. The first supervised agent attempt stopped on a stale disk-monitor sample without a runtime verdict. Its failure is retained; the successful continuation above used the same exact source tree. All owned validation processes exited.

Reproduction, using the repository's pinned runtime and frozen dependencies:

```sh
export OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/database-worker-registry.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts \

for leaf in agents-root agents-other commands services-cron; do

All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed: [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181649584), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181649692) and [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181649669). [Commit statuses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40795121104) show dependency and security-sensitive review passing, with `openclaw/ci-gate` failed. The [description check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40793505041) passed.

CI checks merge `d4f5d6eace1d7c5cbc55bf5a004a082bc2abde88` against main `3163d58b31e3d99a1ad11ae9289e252d22a126fe`. The complete comparison with the published head contains 144 upstream-changed paths, with no overlap with this PR's 20 paths. This newer merge is distinct from the pinned tree tested above.

- [Mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181649499): 14 findings in `server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. The [exact main base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792463841/job/123181561334) executes the scanner and reports the same 14 findings. Both files are byte-identical between base and merge. This is an inherited failure; no baseline exemption or duplicate repair was added.
- [Subagent registry test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181650718): “does not restore a superseded lifecycle after a successor is released” fails at `subagent-registry.native-termination.test-support.ts:59`, expecting a positive `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()` but receiving 0. That fixture is unchanged between base and merge. Upstream [#187090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187090) removed independent root-work admission around termination cleanup while retaining the caller's join; the old assertion still expects that admission. The exact base skipped runtime lanes, so this failure remains unclassified by a matched runtime control. Upstream [#187134](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187134), merged as [`6d7265daace1e6290dd9b6ed8235ffd257cfb5f2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6d7265daace1e6290dd9b6ed8235ffd257cfb5f2), removes the obsolete root-counter assertions while retaining the successor/lifecycle assertions. Its recorded reproduction and 77-case pass support that repair; they are not an executed control on this PR's exact CI base. No duplicate repair or new runtime pass is claimed for `170809258591`.

The API reports this revision mergeable; broad CI and the Goal-budget maintainer decision still gate it.

The previous head's [CI 40139208391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139208391) failed seven interactive-setup cases because the fixture omitted `runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`. Its 60 scoped context-accounting cases passed. [Main CI 40138789542](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138789542/job/121006161355) had the same seven startup failures. The exact old tested base skipped that lane, so it was not an executed exact-base control.

Upstream [#182990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182990) repaired the fixture and [its PostgreSQL shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140365971/job/121010977081) passed all eight setup cases. [#183037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183037) then derived copied root modules from the package manifest. Both are in this integration base. The pinned base's [CI 40786288337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40786288337) skipped PostgreSQL and the other broad lanes; its successful aggregate is not an executed PostgreSQL control. Fresh PR CI remains the current hosted check.

## Goal budget decision and proof limits

Goal accounting retains the existing peak-usage policy. The store-backed regression starts a Goal with a 50,000-token budget and publishes 40,000, 60,000, then 30,000 tokens. Current context finishes at 30,000; Goal usage remains 60,000 and `budget_limited`. The lower snapshot goes through the real writer and store; the test does not execute the compactor.

Publishing intermediate observations can expose a peak that turn-end accounting alone would not have seen. Whether those intermediate peaks should count toward Goal budgets remains a maintainer decision. My recommendation is to preserve the existing peak reducer. Explicit resume starts a fresh budget window at the current context and resets `tokensUsed` to 0. Automatically crediting the Goal after compaction would change budget semantics; this PR does not do that.

The earlier real-provider `agent --local` measurements and [successful October 20 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630) remain historical, tied to `a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33` and its recorded merge checkout. This validation adds no shipped Gateway, channel, compactor or live-provider execution of the current head.

prs.title: fix(postgres): chat history slows under concurrent reads
prs.body:
Related: #188956

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on PostgreSQL, `chat.history` requests queue behind two history workers when several clients load history at once, so tail latency grows with concurrency while the CPU sits mostly idle.

## User Impact

User impact: concurrent `chat.history` on PostgreSQL waits much less for a history worker. At 8 concurrent clients p99 drops from 37.7 to 27.0 ms and throughput rises from 425 to 666 requests/s; at 16 clients p99 drops from 73.1 to 50.6 ms. Single-client latency and SQLite are unchanged.

Cost, measured on the same runs:

- Memory: during concurrent history reads the Gateway runs up to two more transcript isolates (about 53 to 60 MiB of heap each). Peak transcript-worker heap rose from 331 to 456 MiB and peak Gateway RSS from 2,906 to 3,258 MiB (medians of 3 runs). The extra isolates retire after the pool's existing idle timeout; 100 seconds after load both builds were back to one transcript isolate (median of 3 runs; heap samples can lag up to 30 s). RSS at that point was higher with the change in the three bench pairs (median 2,031 vs 2,390 MiB), but a separate pair watched for 300 seconds showed 1,890 vs 1,841 MiB at 100 s and 1,676 vs 1,745 MiB at 300 s, with the same isolate count, so the difference looks like allocator timing rather than retained isolates.
- PostgreSQL connections: backends for the runtime role peaked at 23 on base and 25 with the change, and both returned to 12 after 100 idle seconds. Each extra history isolate can retain up to two idle transports for three minutes; the documented budget (`isolates × (active + 2)`) now notes up to four history isolates.

## Why This Change Was Made

On PostgreSQL a history worker spends most of a request blocked in `Atomics.wait` on bridge replies, so sizing the lane like a CPU-bound reader leaves requests queued while CPU is free. The history lane on PostgreSQL agent stores now gets two workers per CPU above one, capped at four (two on a two-CPU host). Transcript search, the other transcript lanes, and every SQLite lane keep the existing reader size from #167295 and #169110, so the retained-memory bound those PRs set still holds everywhere else. No new setting.

The database engine is installed during boot, after the lane module is imported, so the history pool now resolves its size on first use instead of at import. Production code: +48/-9 lines ignoring whitespace (the pool options block is re-indented inside the first-use constructor); tests +117; docs +9/-4.

This is the other half of #190001, which cuts the transaction round trips inside each history page; this change addresses the queueing in front of the workers. The two touch different files.

## Evidence

Evidence files: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/pg-r2-l3d-history-reader-lane-evidence (paths below are relative to it; method and host details in `README.md`).

- **Tests**: a per-engine sizing table (`src/infra/worker-pool-sizing.test.ts`) and a lane test that installs the engine after importing the lane, as boot does (`src/config/sessions/session-history-lane-sizing.test.ts`: PostgreSQL 4, SQLite 2, search 2). On base the sizing table fails because the resolver does not exist, and the PostgreSQL lane case gets 2 instead of 4 while the SQLite case passes (`tests/unit-red.log`). With the change both files pass, as do the consumer suites for the transcript lanes, the search worker, reconcile readiness, the chat history worker and worker-pool preparation: 12 files, 161 tests (`tests/unit-final.log`). `pnpm check:changed` passes (`tests/check-changed.log`).
- **Closed-loop `chat.history` bench on current `main`**: a fresh Gateway on PostgreSQL 17, seeded through its own RPCs with 200 sessions (170 sessions across 6 agents with 2 to 4,675 messages each, plus 30 imported Claude CLI sessions with tool rows hidden between visible turns). Limit 100, 45 s per arm, 3 interleaved runs per build (ABBAAB). Medians (`bench/medians.tsv`; every run in `bench/arms.tsv`; raw scrapes in `bench/runs/`):

| arm | p50 / p95 / p99 ms | p99 range | requests/s | queue wait per worker request | handler mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 client, base | 5.50 / 9.41 / 12.32 | 11.07 to 12.36 | 176 | 0.0 ms | 4.63 ms |
| 1 client, fix | 5.55 / 9.63 / 12.36 | 11.66 to 13.00 | 173 | 0.0 ms | 4.69 ms |
| 8 clients, base | 18.11 / 26.52 / 37.68 | 37.14 to 40.91 | 425 | 5.04 ms | 17.42 ms |
| 8 clients, fix | 11.22 / 18.37 / 27.02 | 25.85 to 28.88 | 666 | 1.22 ms | 9.65 ms |
| 16 clients, base | 35.58 / 49.84 / 73.08 | 70.68 to 75.64 | 434 | 12.70 ms | 35.40 ms |
| 16 clients, fix | 22.51 / 38.81 / 50.60 | 34.94 to 53.63 | 665 | 6.19 ms | 21.48 ms |

Queue wait is `openclaw_worker_queue_wait_seconds{kind="sessionTranscript"}`; handler mean is `openclaw_gateway_rpc_handler_seconds{method="chat.history"}`. The host's 1-minute load average was 4 to 11 on 32 threads during these arms (per arm in `bench/arms.tsv`; the fix runs saw slightly higher load than base). A confirmation run on the final commit (`bench/runs/pg-fixv4-r7`) gave 12.45, 26.28 and 41.62 ms p99 at 1, 8 and 16 clients.

- **Memory and connections** (`bench/memory-medians.tsv`, per run in `bench/memory.tsv`, 300 s pair in `bench/runs/pg-*-idle-r1`): see User Impact. Heap and isolate counts come from the Gateway's worker metrics, sampled by the 30 s diagnostic heartbeat; RSS and backend counts are sampled every 2 s.
- **SQLite** (same seed, 2 base runs and 1 run with the change): transcript isolates peak at 6 on both builds; p50 and throughput match (8 clients: 17.07 and 17.69 ms base vs 17.68 ms, 454 and 429 vs 434 requests/s; 16 clients: 34.00 and 33.76 vs 34.28 ms, 466 and 463 vs 447 requests/s). SQLite p99 varies run to run on both builds (16 clients: 51.40 and 59.28 ms base, 65.37 ms fix). With the change, PostgreSQL's p99 is at or below SQLite's at 8 and 16 clients on this host; #188956 reported it at 1.5 to 2 times SQLite's.
- **Cap of four vs eight**: an earlier revision capped the lane at eight (3 runs, interleaved with 3 more base runs). At 8 clients it gave p99 23.62 ms and 0.07 ms queue wait; at 16 clients p99 38.19 ms and 1.66 ms queue wait. It cost more: peak transcript heap 655 MiB, peak RSS 3,743 MiB, backends peaking at 27 (`bench/medians.tsv` and `bench/memory-medians.tsv`, rows `fix8` and `base-a`). At 8 clients, the concurrency #188956 measured, four keeps most of the queue-wait reduction (5.04 to 1.22 ms, vs 5.08 to 0.07 ms with eight) for roughly a third of the extra heap and RSS (+125 vs +325 MiB heap, +352 vs +974 MiB RSS at peak, each against its own base block) and two fewer peak backends.

### Gaps

- The bench store is synthetic, written through the Gateway's own RPCs on `main`, because `main` does not admit a `pg_restore` of our production store. Its shape follows the production bench in #188956 (200 sessions, mostly small, a long tail of large transcripts, Claude CLI sessions).
- At 16 clients the four-worker lane is saturated again (6.19 ms queue wait per worker request), and fix p99 ranged from 34.94 to 53.63 ms across runs. A cap of eight removes that queue at a higher memory cost (see above).
- Memory figures needed one measurement-only line, applied identically to both builds: the diagnostic heartbeat publishes its memory sample every 30 s instead of only after agent activity (`scripts/instrument-*.diff`). Read-only RPC load alone never triggers a sample. Isolate counts and heap cover every transcript lane, not only history, and 30 s sampling can miss the exact peak.
- The 3-run bench used a build of this change from before the history-lane constructor moved into the pools module (to stay under a file line cap); sizing logic is identical, and the confirmation run above used the final commit.
- Transcript search on PostgreSQL also blocks on bridge replies and keeps its two-worker cap; not measured here.
- Shared host. Not benchmarked together with #190001.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve run identity when admission fails
prs.body:
Fixes #191330

## What Problem This Solves

An update can adopt its durable run and then fail during reconciliation before registering that run with the terminal owner. The CLI can lose the run ID in its failure output and leave readable history running.

## User Impact

Successfully adopted runs now enter the existing terminal owner before fallible admission work. Failures retain the run ID; readable, owned history can finish, while unreadable recovery stays pending and refused adoption grants no terminal authority. Executor settlement still precedes publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration belongs at successful adoption. The ordinary and initialized execution paths reuse the existing owner instead of reconstructing authority after failure. Failure constructors preserve a known run ID through fence, cancellation, and reporting errors.

Runtime production delta is +32 lines. The regression and shared fixture add 100 test lines, with an exact allocation. No configuration or schema changes.

## Evidence

- The test-only baseline `fa30cfef1e06f1f46e596ca051de4c46cca3ee48` reproduced missing JSON publication for readable and unreadable recovery on Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4. The original refusal fixture exceeded the schema limit and was corrected to one current plus seven previous drivers; it was not a valid baseline reproduction. [Baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41491641524/job/125437140933).
- Production head `3c509e4150419580adecc3fec43da628b6f27343` passed all three new regression cases on both runtimes. Build and compiler gates passed. Related terminal authority, publication, unreported failure, inspection failure, run, and fresh-terminal suites passed on Bun. [Regression proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41496203529/job/125452653754).
- That CI run found two foreground-fixture failures caused by an incomplete runtime mock, and a callback variable shadowing error. Current head `dfe7818abd24f8bc3a57ecac8b0b0964401d4179` preserves the real runtime exports, removes the obsolete mock allowance, and renames the callback parameter. Independent review, formatting, whitespace checks, native test-line accounting, and commit hooks passed. **Corrected-head execution and required CI are pending.**
- The earlier UI loading-state failure is unrelated by unchanged UI, harness, package and lock inputs; the same test passed on scheduled main. This is scoped source attribution, not a matching inherited-failure signature or a green CI claim.
- The production repair received independent review and a complete autoreview pass over 41 intact source contexts. The four-file corrective diff received separate independent review. Local ClawSweeper preparation refused changes to a shared install, so the documented autoreview fallback was used; hosted exact-head review remains pending.

Local test dependencies are unqualified. The task-owned Testbox allocation was cancelled while queued; the selected AWS proof stopped at Git-seed checkout before tests. Both settled. Normal PR CI is the remaining execution route.

Follow-ups: initialization can precede the advertised update deadline; a separate publisher-catch history read can still encounter unreadable state. Neither expands this admission-owner repair.

Stack (merge in order): this PR → https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191228 → https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191229.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191191

## What Problem This Solves

Adaptive CI experiments need file-level execution and dependency observations without treating missing or partial test runs as successful evidence.

## User Impact

Operators can export privacy-limited observations from existing Vitest resource-reporter logs. Test selection and required CI checks remain unchanged. Ordinary Node CI and native Bun-test are not automatically enrolled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reporter records an invocation inventory, case counts and the native dependency root. The exporter joins outcomes and optional Vitest dependency records, includes global setup edges, rejects conflicting receipts, and leaves incomplete or ambiguous data unknown. It exports source identities and metrics without copying test titles or errors.

This is the first layer of a three-PR stack: observations, shadow selection, then cost estimation. Context/cache provenance remains the caller's responsibility.

## Evidence

- Nine observation/CLI tests pass through the repository test runner (22 ms test time, 3.22 s shard wall time).
- The final native Vitest reporter smoke passes all nine cases and exports a complete observation with correct case counts; partial runs, replayed logs, global setup, cross-runtime ambiguity and UI-root rebasing have contract coverage.
- Targeted tooling typecheck, scoped typed lint, pinned formatting and both production/full-tree unused-file scans pass.
- Independent source review, the initial full-stack local ClawSweeper review, and the final typing-fix local ClawSweeper review found no remaining actionable issue.
- Required exact-head GitHub CI remains the broad merge gate. This layer does not enable adaptive skipping.

prs.title: fix(browser): tab list fails when Chrome refuses to attach to a tab
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Chrome extension relay fails the whole tab list (`Target.getTargets` → "Target identities are unavailable") in **All tabs** access mode when Chrome permanently refuses to attach its debugger to an ordinary tab.

## User Impact

User impact: users with many open tabs in All tabs mode keep getting a tab list; tabs Chrome will not debug are skipped with a warning (as already happens for the Chrome Web Store and `chrome://` pages) instead of making every tab query fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

`enumerateTargetInfos` only treats three exact Chrome messages as permanent refusals (`The extensions gallery cannot be scripted.`, `Cannot access a chrome:// URL`, `Cannot access a chrome-extension:// URL of different extension`). For some regular tabs Chrome returns `Cannot attach to this target.` on every attempt. Those tabs were not skipped, never got an identity, and the later identity check failed the whole request. `docs/tools/chrome-extension.md` already says pages Chrome permanently refuses to debug are excluded while transient failures still fail the request; this adds the missing permanent refusal and extends the doc sentence accordingly. The match stays an exact message comparison, so other attach failures (conflicts, permissions, timeouts, retired generations) still fail the request.

Repro conditions: >100 open tabs, access mode All tabs, Chrome reports `Cannot attach to this target.` for a few tabs (relay log: `setAutoAttach attach failed: Error: Cannot attach to this target.`).

## Evidence

- New test in `relay-bridge.test.ts`: a tab whose attach fails with `Cannot attach to this target.` is skipped and the other tabs are returned. Red on base (`Target identities are unavailable`), green with the fix.
- `vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay`: 19 files / 241 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files clean; `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Observed on a real setup (OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.5, Windows, Chrome, >100 tabs, All tabs): 2/2 tab queries failed before; with the equivalent one-line skip, 2/2 succeeded.
- Not run: full CI suite, live Chrome e2e on the fixed source build.


## Verification & Proof

The changed source (`ExtensionRelayBridge` from `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-bridge.ts`) was exercised directly through a standalone CLI script that runs the real bridge against an in-process scripted extension + CDP client. One tab is scripted to return Chrome's exact permanent refusal `Cannot attach to this target.`; a healthy tab attaches normally. No real browser, network, or user data is involved.

Captured terminal output (exit code 0):

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .github/pr-proof/relay-skip-proof/run-proof.mts
[pr-proof/relay-skip] building proof against changed ExtensionRelayBridge source
[browser/extension-relay] Skipping tab 2 during target enumeration: Cannot attach to this target.
[pr-proof/relay-skip] Target.getTargets returned 1 target(s): ["target-1"]
[pr-proof/relay-skip] PROOF PASS: refused tab skipped, healthy tab returned
```

This shows the exact behavior under review: the refused tab is skipped with a warning (same code path as the existing permanent refusals) and the healthy tab is still returned.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep literal node-binding cwd values without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190067

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex CLI node-conversation binding record persisted the session cwd after `.trim()` (`conversation-binding-data.ts`), the record reader re-trimmed it on restore (`normalizeOptionalString`), the session-file discovery summary trimmed it too (`node-cli-sessions.ts` `readSessionFileSummary`), and the resume path trimmed it again right before spawning (`node-cli-sessions.ts`: `cwd: ... params.cwd.trim()`). A session whose true cwd is a literal whitespace-padded directory (e.g. `/workspace/project `) was therefore discovered, written, read, and resumed as the WRONG directory: the spawned `codex exec resume` runs in the trimmed impostor, which usually does not exist. Same defect class as the merged literal-path fixes #187739, #187554, and #187777.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` (the same helper the app-server branch of this file already uses for `workspaceDir`) at every site that handles the binding cwd: **discovery** (`readSessionFileSummary` keeps the session_meta `payload.cwd` verbatim), **write** (persist the raw cwd into the binding record), **read** (restore the raw cwd), and **resume spawn** (pass the literal cwd to `runCodexExecResume`). Blank or whitespace-only cwd values still omit the field / fall back exactly as before: `readNonBlankString` keeps the trim-based blank check and only preserves the value, so the old `""`-is-falsy behavior at both write and read is unchanged.

## Impact

- Session discovery and binding records preserve the session's literal cwd identity end to end.
- `codex exec resume` spawns in the directory where the session actually lived, even when its name carries edge whitespace.
- Identity-comparison sites elsewhere trim both operands and are unaffected by verbatim storage.

## Test growth

No net test lines: the regression coverage rides on existing tests instead of adding new ones. The diff is `6 insertions / 6 deletions` across three existing test files, with no new test cases; the earlier 71 added test lines are gone, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.

- Discovery keeps the literal `session_meta.cwd`: `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" now uses a whitespace-padded rollout cwd (existing assertion).
- Resume passes the binding cwd to the spawn: the same file's "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" now resumes in a `project `-style directory (existing spawn-cwd assertion).
- Binding write: `commands.test.ts` "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session" now asserts the stored record carries the discovered literal cwd.
- Binding restore: `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" now restores a literal cwd (existing resume-argument assertion).

## Evidence

### Shipped runtime proof: discovery and resume through the real CLI, Gateway, and node host

Entry points are shipped product surfaces: a real `openclaw nodes invoke --node … --command codex.cli.sessions.list` / `codex.cli.session.resume` (CLI → Gateway `node.invoke` → paired node host). The Gateway and node host ran the production `dist` built from the reviewed head with `scripts/build-all.mts`; the node host is `openclaw node run` and advertised `codex.cli.sessions.list` + `codex.cli.session.resume`.

Fixture: a genuine session created by the real Codex CLI running inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space), so the rollout's `session_meta` is Codex's own output. A sibling directory `…/work/codexproj` carries `identity.txt=TRIMMED-DIR`, the literal directory carries `identity.txt=LITERAL-DIR`; a `/proc` watcher records the real spawned Codex process tree's cwd and the marker it sees.

| Observation (same fixture, same CLI, same node host) | head `ee4d6c3e5` | base `3cd0dd638` |
|---|---|---|
| `codex.cli.sessions.list` session `cwd` | `…/work/codexproj ` (literal, trailing space) | `…/work/codexproj` (trimmed) |
| `codex.cli.session.resume` with binding `cwd` = `…/work/codexproj ` → Codex banner `workdir:` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj ` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj` |
| `/proc/<pid>/cwd` of spawned `codex exec resume` (node wrapper and native binary) | `[…/work/codexproj ]`, marker `LITERAL-DIR` | `[…/work/codexproj]`, marker `TRIMMED-DIR` |

Head transcript (abridged; the base leg runs the identical commands from the base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj " } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj 
model: gpt-5.6-sol
provider: openai
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7
user
continue in the literal directory
# the provider hop then fails: 403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"

# /proc watcher, spawned process tree
pid=211617 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … - 
pid=211637 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … -
```

Base transcript (same commands, base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj" } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7

pid=583566 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume … -
pid=583589 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume … -
```

What the capture proves and what it does not: Codex's own `workdir:` banner and the kernel-observed `/proc/<pid>/cwd` show the CLI was launched in the literal directory on this head and in the trimmed sibling on the base commit — exactly the user-visible difference. The model turn is not part of the claim; this machine's region blocks `api.openai.com` (403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"), so the run stops at the provider hop after loading the genuine session in the recorded directory. Setup facts, disclosed because they are not product behavior: the isolated Gateway used the operator opt-in `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["codex.cli.session.resume"]` (the documented dangerous-node-command allow, needed for a direct `nodes invoke`), and the one-time node pairing was approved with `openclaw nodes approve`. Binding serialization and restoration to that same resume argument are covered by the existing tests above and by the Control UI persistence capture below.

### Binding persisted and restored through the shipped Control UI

Entry point: the shipped Control UI (`openclaw dashboard` issues the owner handoff URL), a real Gateway built from the reviewed `dist`, a paired node host (`openclaw node run`), and a genuine Codex 0.164.0 session created inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space). The only UI action was: open the node's Codex catalog row, type a message, press send. The Control UI calls the shipped `sessions.catalog.continue` RPC, which installs the Codex plugin's session binding.

The Gateway persisted the binding in its SQLite store (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, table `current_conversation_bindings`); the row is inspectable:

```
binding_id:        generic:webchat<US>default<US><US>agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088de7be187158b1b7ea154048bb85bcf2e30e6d7862400df57b3ae5793
target_session_key: agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088…5793
metadata.data:     {"kind":"codex-cli-node-session","version":1,
                    "nodeId":"ff118971…7008a",
                    "sessionId":"01a19233-7502-7512-b65b-fd1fa5f782c7",
                    "agentId":"main",
                    "cwd":"/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj"}
```

Then the Gateway was restarted (the binding existed only on disk), the same adopted session was reopened in the Control UI, and a message was sent. The plugin restored the binding and continuation spawned Codex in the stored cwd — the kernel-observed process tree:

```
pid=1539699 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
pid=1539725 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
```

The turn then stops at the same region-blocked provider hop described above (403), after the session was loaded in the bound directory.

Compatibility with existing state:

- The same store was opened by the pre-fix build `3cd0dd638` (the released 2026.10.9 line): the pre-fix reader restored the same row and spawned `codex exec resume … 01a19233-…` in the same cwd, so the store written by the fix build is readable by existing code without migration (no schema change, `kind`/`version` unchanged).
- For this session the stored `cwd` is exactly the value the pre-fix writer produces: Codex's own app-server catalog already normalizes the thread cwd, so the fix's writer stores `/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj` unchanged. Existing rows written by the pre-fix build therefore take the same read path.
- Latest published stable `openclaw@2026.10.9` does not bundle the Codex extension (67 bundled extensions, no `codex`), so there is no released producer of this data model; `3cd0dd638` is the pre-fix behavior for it.

Known capture gap: the two asks above needing a messaging channel are environment-blocked here. The literal-cwd *binding write* path runs through the `/codex resume … --bind here` command, which requires a channel that implements `bindings.resolveCommandConversation` (Discord/Telegram/Matrix/LINE/Feishu/iMessage). This host has no leased Telegram/Discord QA credentials (the shared Convex credential broker is unavailable), and the webchat surface is not a binding channel by design, so the shipped-Control-UI capture necessarily goes through the Codex catalog path, which receives an already-normalized cwd from Codex's app-server. Literal cwd at the writer/reader boundaries is covered by the existing tests, and literal cwd at the node resume boundary by the direct node capture; a channel-credentialed or maintainer-run `/codex resume --bind here` capture is required to show the literal value stored through the binding itself.

Scope note: the Codex app-server catalog normalizes `cwd`, so the catalog-continue binding path stores an already-normalized value; literal whitespace preservation is what the direct node `codex.cli.sessions.list`/`codex.cli.session.resume` capture above shows, and what the writer/reader tests assert.

### Red-green for the consolidated tests

Remote Linux runner, `vitest run <file> --maxWorkers=1`. With only these test edits applied and the two production files reset to `3cd0dd638`, the coverage fails; on the reviewed head it passes.

Base (`3cd0dd638` production files):

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` — 3 failed: both "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" cases (spawn cwd expected `…/project `, got `…/project`) and "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" (listed cwd trimmed).
- `commands.test.ts` — 1 failed: "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session (listed: true)" (stored record cwd trimmed).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` — 4 failed: every "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" case (restored binding reached resume with a trimmed cwd).

Head `ee4d6c3e5`:

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` → 1 file passed (23.7s).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` → 4/4 passed (15.1s).
- `commands.test.ts` → 1 file passed (525s wall for that file; the touched case is one of its fast unit tests).

### Checks

- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 3cd0dd6380a1a1586c6db4574b6fc231eb3367df --no-merge-base` → `Test lines OK: 6287170; ceiling: 6330844`.
- `git diff --check` clean.

### Round 6 (2026-11-02): shipped binding-write trace through a real channel — literal cwd stored, restart durability, upgrade direction

This round answers both remaining before-merge items with the same fixture and shipped entry points: (1) a literal trailing-space cwd stored through conversation-binding creation, and (2) a pre-fix-created binding store opened by the fixed build.

Harness and entry points (all product surfaces; nothing in the Codex extension under review was modified):

- A local Matrix homeserver (Synapse 1.164.1, loopback-only, fresh SQLite) backs the shipped Matrix channel plugin. The sandbox Gateway ran the production `dist` built from the reviewed head `ee4d6c3e5` (Leg A) or the base `3cd0dd638` (Leg B) with `scripts/build-all.mts`; the node host was `openclaw node run` from the same `dist`, advertising `codex.cli.sessions.list` / `codex.cli.session.resume`.
- Fixture: a genuine Codex CLI 0.146.0 session created inside `/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ` (trailing space); its rollout `session_meta.cwd` is `/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ` (verbatim). A sibling `/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj` carries `identity.txt=TRIMMED-DIR`; the literal directory carries `identity.txt=LITERAL-DIR`.
- Entry point for the write: the shipped channel command `/codex resume <session-id> --host <node> --bind here`, sent by the room owner from a real Matrix DM (CLI → Gateway plugin-command dispatch → owner gate → node session resolution → conversation binding write). The documented operator opt-in `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["codex.cli.session.resume"]` was set, as in the earlier capture.
- Setup facts that are operator authorization, not product behavior, and are disclosed as such: (a) the sandbox Gateway's operator pre-authorized the Codex plugin binding on this matrix account by inserting the `plugin_binding_approvals` row the product itself writes on an "Always allow" decision — Matrix renders no interactive buttons for the shipped approval prompt, and this host has no Discord/Telegram QA lease; (b) three small fixture patches were applied byte-identically to the Matrix extension chunks in BOTH the base and head `dist` builds: a fallback in the binding intro-text agent resolution, plugin-metadata round-trip on Matrix thread-binding records, and an agent fallback for `plugin-binding:*` target keys in binding route facts. These are Matrix-channel infrastructure edges hit after the Codex cwd logic runs (one aborts the bind before persist; the others affect routing/presentation), they exist on base and head alike, and none touches the Codex extension, which is the code under review.

Leg A — head `ee4d6c3e5`: stored, durable, resumed in the literal directory.

```
@proofdriver: /codex resume 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7 --host proof-node-121 --bind here
@proofbot:    Bound this conversation to Codex CLI session 01a18f8e-…-5265296f29d7 on ad1cf43e….
```

The persisted Matrix thread-binding record (`plugin_state_entries`, namespace `thread-bindings`, inspectable SQLite) then held, verbatim:

```json
"targetSessionKey": "plugin-binding:codex:6373f060…",
"pluginMetadata": { "pluginBindingOwner": "plugin", "pluginId": "codex",
  "data": { "kind": "codex-cli-node-session", "version": 1,
            "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…-5265296f29d7", "agentId": "main",
            "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj " } }
```

The same command on base `3cd0dd638` (identical fixture, identical harness, identical patches; only the Codex extension build differs) stored `"cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj"` — the trailing space stripped by the pre-fix discovery/binding chain. That pair is the write-side red/green: the changed code is what puts the literal value into the record.

After a full Gateway restart (kill + `gateway run` on the same state dir), the record above is still present byte-for-byte (re-queried from SQLite), and continuing the bound session spawns Codex in the stored literal directory — kernel-observed process tree plus Codex's own banner:

```
pid=3067136 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … 01a18f8e-…
pid=3067154 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … 01a18f8e-…
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj 
```

The turn then stops at the same region-blocked provider hop documented in earlier rounds (403 "Country, region, or territory not supported") after the session was loaded in the recorded directory.

Known capture gap, stated plainly: delivering a plain message *through Matrix* into a plugin-bound conversation is blocked on this product version by a Matrix-channel gap that is identical on base and head — inbound turn persistence refuses the non-canonical `plugin-binding:*` target key (`SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError`; `openclaw doctor --fix` does not remap this key class). The continuation effect above was therefore driven at the shipped node-resume boundary with the stored record's cwd value, which is exactly the argument the binding restore path passes (`resumeCodexCliSessionOnNode({ cwd })` receives the stored `data.cwd` verbatim); the kernel-observed spawn cwd and Codex's own `workdir:` banner show the stored literal value reaching the resumed process.

Leg B — data-model compatibility, upgrade direction: pre-fix store opened by the fixed build.

1. The base build `3cd0dd638` created the binding through the same shipped command and room flow; its persisted record stores `"cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj"` (the value the pre-fix writer produces).
2. The Gateway and node host were stopped and restarted from the head `ee4d6c3e5` `dist` against the same state dir. The fixed build opened the pre-fix store without migration or schema complaint, and the binding record is byte-identical before and after the swap (re-queried from the same SQLite file, `cwd` and `sessionId` retained).
3. The fixed build resolves and routes the pre-fix binding: an inbound room message is dispatched against `sessionKey=plugin-binding:codex:1224548…` (the base-created target), i.e. the restored binding is found and used for routing.
4. Resuming with the stored value on the fixed build works end to end: kernel-observed spawn `cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj]` and Codex banner `workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj`, then the same region-blocked provider hop. Existing rows written by the pre-fix build therefore load, retain their values, and drive continuation after upgrade.

Related data point explaining the earlier UI capture: this fixture's rollout later records a `thread_settings_applied` event whose cwd is the trimmed value, which is why the app-server catalog path (Control UI continue) normalizes to the trimmed directory while the node-CLI discovery path used by `/codex resume --bind here` preserves the literal `session_meta.cwd`.

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187739, #187554, and #187777. Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187816, #187825.
