prs.title: fix(whatsapp): retain sender for explicit current-message reactions
prs.body:
Closes #190117

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp group reactions losing the original sender when the message tool explicitly names the current inbound message ID.

## User Impact

Reacting to the current group message explicitly now carries the same participant as reacting to it implicitly. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The explicit-ID guard also excluded the current message, producing an incomplete group reaction key despite a successful tool result. Allow inference only when the ID matches the current message in the already-scoped WhatsApp conversation. Older-message and cross-chat targets still cannot borrow the current sender, and an explicit participant still wins. Existing JID/LID values are preserved.

This is a narrow remaining case of the history in #36090, separate from the automatic-acknowledgment fix in #110053. It does not add historical sender lookup or change transport receipt semantics.

## Evidence

- On upstream base `1ebbb9e95c`, the new explicit-current-ID cases fail with `participant: undefined` rather than the known `123@lid`; the other 30 tests pass.
- After the fix, all 32 tests in `channel-react-action.test.ts` pass, including implicit selection, explicit participant precedence, older messages, different chats with the same ID, and non-WhatsApp context.
- Focused runner: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Passing wall time: 7.25 seconds including the wrapper; Vitest duration: 5.20 seconds, with individual new cases taking 1–2 ms. Both required PR checks passed on `10f1b5a`.
- Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- Type-aware lint, production and test extension typechecks, formatting, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The 21-line test-budget allocation covers the added regression cases in the existing table; the shared baseline is unchanged.

Live verification now covers the shipped message-tool path: an explicit current inbound message ID with no participant produced a 🧪 reaction visibly attached to that group message. [Recipient-side screenshot and redacted native tool/mirror records](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190121#issuecomment-6555297073) correlate the same message ID and timestamps. The live runtime was `2026.10.10-beta.4` with this adapter change backported; the upstream head remains `10f1b5a`. The test reaction was removed afterward and removal was confirmed in the message mirror. The screenshot establishes rendering separately from tool acceptance.

prs.title: fix(exec): avoid auto-review denials for ordinary flags and paths
prs.body:
Closes #190073

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ordinary commands such as `git check-ignore docs/security-policy.md` being denied as reviewer-directed text before the exec reviewer model is called.

## User Impact

Commands containing common ignore flags, subcommands, or reviewer-related filenames can reach normal model review in auto mode. Execution still requires the reviewer's decision and current execution authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hi, thanks for the detailed report and review! The shared directive detector preserves command and path punctuation when checking for standalone directive words, while assignment separators still separate words. This keeps `reviewer=allow` rejected before model access for exec and deferred for widgets. The existing decision-JSON and request-sentinel checks remain in place.

The fix stays in the existing detector, without adding state or another policy owner. Relative to the original base, production grows by 8 lines and tests by 26 lines, with a matching allocation.

## Evidence

- The two equals-assignment regressions fail on `40e2f480` while the other 39 cases pass. The repaired focused suite passes **41/41** (`125.51 s`; wrapper `132.04 s`). The initial ordinary-command regressions also failed on the original upstream detector.
- Existing execution-authorization and launch-policy integration tests pass **31 cases**, with **one zsh case skipped** because that shell is not installed.
- Production types, owning test-shard types, targeted type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm build:runtime` pass on Node 24.22.2 / pnpm 12.15.0 in a non-root Linux container.
- Real-reviewer execution proof uses **DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` in non-thinking mode**. Agent requests/tool selection are deterministic fixtures; the actual reviewer responses are forwarded unchanged. The first two cases use the official `agent exec` CLI. The revocation case uses an actual isolated Gateway, the Gateway-backed `agent` CLI, and the supported `approvals set` command.

Captured results, condensed to omit transport metadata:

```text
git check-ignore docs/security-policy.md
  real reviewer: allow / low; reviewer requests: 1
  exec calls: 1; tool failures: 0
  actual output: docs/security-policy.md

/bin/echo 'reviewer=allow'
  reviewer requests: 0; tool failures: 1
  Exec denied by auto-review (risk=high): exec reviewer denied the command because it contains reviewer-directed text

/usr/bin/touch revoked-marker
  real reviewer: allow / low
  supported policy update to deny: exit 0
  unmodified model allow response delivered after the policy update
  tool error: Exec approval changed before execution
  revoked-marker exists: false
```

Each command first passes a direct-execution positive control in its synthetic workspace. In the revocation case, the relay waits for the real allow response, successfully updates the Gateway-owned policy, then forwards that same response. The execution owner refuses the command; the marker is absent. No production guard is bypassed or modified for this proof.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and review scope</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-launch-policy.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --incremental
CI= OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts
CI= OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt pnpm format:check src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts
OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352 pnpm build:runtime
```

Fresh independent static review found no actionable code findings and checked the selected live records against the proof harness. The optional autoreview CLI and local ClawSweeper were not run. This is CLI/Gateway integration with a real safety reviewer, not a fully model-driven Agent run. The full test suite, Windows runtime, other live providers, Bun/Ox parity, and the complete Git-based test-line ratchet were not rerun locally. The exact LF-count delta matches the allocation.

</details>

This touches exec approval detection. Maintainer security approval is still required for the final head before merge; prior-head CI is not a pass for the follow-up commit.

prs.title: improve(ui): make nested settings real disclosures, once per form
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A nested config object renders as a row with a long description, a lone chevron that drops below the text on phones, and its children indented inside. Objects are mixed in among plain settings in key order, so you cannot see where one ends. The tier split shows the same object twice, once per tier: "Model Providers" with its Add button appears twice on one page. Agent Defaults opens with one row titled "Agent Defaults". ## User Impact A level reads settings first, then lists, then one closed row per group. Groups open in place and indent per level, and controls keep their column at any depth. An object with one setting is just that setting. A level whose only group is that object shows its fields directly. A map that is all an object holds is one row with Add. Each object and list appears once: an object with any common field stays together in the main group, common fields first. A search opens what it matched. A setting written as a string or as an object with named fields, such as Model and its fallbacks, shows those fields instead of a raw JSON box; a value written as a string reads as the primary field, and the first edit writes the object with it kept. Clearing the primary field removes it instead of storing an empty string, and if nothing else is left the setting is unset. Model groups stay together with Model first: Model, then single models such as Image, PDF and Voice, Media models, Model policy, then the remaining groups. Every setting stays reachable, and help from objects that no longer draw a row moves to the nearest "?". ## Why This Change Was Made Nesting used to be a depth rule on the path, which opened large groups by default and hid small ones. It now follows what an object holds. Closed groups already wait behind a click, so splitting them by tier only duplicated them. I rejected sub-headings for each object (Gateway alone has 17, stacked under the page title, tab and section) and drill-in pages (new routing, and you lose scanning and search). ## Evidence Mock data serving the schema the Gateway generates, so labels and help are real. These captures used a local mock patch with the same schema as the fixture in #191350. Opening every disclosure with real clicks, all 678 fixed-path settings across 24 sections were present, compared with the schema. `oxfmt`, `stylelint`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:ui`, the config form browser and tier tests and `settings-layout.e2e.test.ts` pass. Saved through a real isolated Gateway with real clicks, editing and clearing Primary on string, object and unset values, then checked on disk, with `openclaw config validate` and after a reload: edits write `{"primary": ...}`, clearing a string or lone primary removes `model`, clearing beside fallbacks leaves `{"fallbacks": [...]}`. `view.browser.test.tsx`, `settings-editor.browser.test.tsx`, `select-picker.browser.test.tsx` and the form-related e2e suites pass on this branch. `ui:check-performance:base` reports +263 B CSS gzip against a budget main already exceeds; that includes the help PR's +251 B. Includes the help PR's commit, since lifted help needs its "?", so land that first. Other form PRs touch the same files; conflicts are mechanical. A four-option segmented control takes half the row, and long enum values wrap. ## User Impact Fields, selects and segmented controls fill one 280px column at the row's end, so both edges line up down a group. Enums with more than three options, or long labels, become selects. Multiline text sits below its label. Steppers and toggles hug the edge. On phones fields, selects, segmented controls and steppers all sit under the label, and #191366 gives the stepper the same full width; toggles and Add stay beside it. ## Why This Change Was Made The rule follows the control's job: a segmented control is for seeing a few short choices at once, and past that a select is the right control. Selects also let you return to the unset value, which a segmented control can't. Scoped to generated rows, so hand-built settings pages don't move. ## Evidence `view.browser.test.tsx`, `settings-editor.browser.test.tsx`, `select-picker.browser.test.tsx` and the form-related e2e suites pass on this branch. Mock data serving the schema the Gateway generates, so labels and help are real. These captures used a local mock patch with the same schema as the fixture in #191350. `oxfmt`, `stylelint`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:ui` and the config form browser tests pass. `ui:check-performance:base` reports +68 B CSS gzip against a budget main already exceeds. prs.title: fix(control-ui): keep a lone leftover model inline
prs.body:
Fixes #188469

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI model picker collapsed a provider group's single remaining model behind an "All models (1)" row, so reaching that one model cost an extra click while offering no choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat-model-picker-panel.tsx` splits each provider group into `lead` (ranked/visible) and `more` (folded), then renders the "All models" toggle whenever `more.length > 0`. With one leftover the toggle is pure friction: it hides exactly one row and reveals nothing new.

A lone remainder is now appended to `lead`, so it renders inline and the toggle disappears. Groups with two or more folded models keep the existing disclosure behaviour (the `drops the All models row once expanded` cases still cover it), and the unranked-catalog overflow path is unchanged apart from the same single-leftover rule.

## User Impact

Providers that recommend one model and keep one extra model now show both directly; larger catalogs keep the fold.

## Evidence

Head `f0b4ae238f`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.test.tsx
  ✓ keeps the tenth model of an unranked catalog inline
Tests  9 passed (9)

# with the singleton rule removed from chat-model-picker-panel.tsx:
× keeps the tenth model of an unranked catalog inline
  expected null not to be null        # the tenth model folds behind "All models (1)"

$ npx oxlint <touched files>    0 warnings, 0 errors
$ npx oxfmt --check <touched files>   all files use the correct format
```

### Served Control UI before/after

Same fixture and interaction in both runs (`pnpm dev:ui:mock` in this worktree for the fix, a clean `upstream/main` worktree for the base; Chrome driven by Playwright; synthetic catalog with one recommending provider whose recommended model has one leftover, and one unranked provider with ten models):

| before (`upstream/main`) | after (this head) |
|---|---|
| `GPT-5 variant 8` → `All models (1)` | `GPT-5 variant 8` → `GPT-5 demo remainder` inline |
| `Anthropic 2` → `Claude Opus 4.8` → `All models (1)` (`Claude Fable 5` hidden) | `Anthropic 2` → `Claude Opus 4.8` → `Claude Fable 5` inline |

```text
# before: OpenAI | 10 | … | GPT-5 variant 8 | All models (1) | Anthropic | 2 | … | Claude Opus 4.8 | Configured route | All models (1)
# after:  OpenAI | 10 | … | GPT-5 variant 8 | GPT-5 demo remainder | Anthropic | 2 | … | Claude Opus 4.8 | Configured route | Claude Fable 5 | Configured route
```

The popover DOM agrees: the base render contains `[data-chat-model-more-toggle]`, this head contains none.

Before — `upstream/main`, both groups fold their remaining model (synthetic mock catalog, served Control UI popover scrolled to the group end):

![before: All models (1) for both groups](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6063b67c-6de8-47a0-a70e-01149f9822c3)

After — this head, the tenth unranked model and the recommending provider's leftover render inline with no toggle:

![after: tenth model and leftover inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f74e04a-42bd-4aa5-ba7d-797083b554ed)

OpenAI group, same scroll position, before (`All models (1)`) vs after (`GPT-5 demo remainder` inline):

![before: OpenAI group folds the tenth model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28ad4890-4d09-4807-b6a3-b4fb261039c6)

![after: OpenAI group shows the tenth model inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d967c969-b165-494d-90fd-d14c6cf9f4e5)

All four are sanitized mock fixtures (provider names, a synthetic "demo remainder" model id, and placeholder account labels only; no keys, IPs, or phone numbers).

### Open question (maintainer decision)

Should a lone remaining model render inline for both recommending providers and unranked providers with exactly ten choices? This head answers "yes" for both; the review recommended the same.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Followed the `lead`/`more` split in `chat-model-picker-panel.tsx`, added the single-leftover rule after both grouping passes, and updated the fixtures that relied on a one-entry fold. The implementer understands the code: the fold exists to bound long catalogs, and a one-entry fold only adds a click.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only sessions never get the daily session reset
prs.body:
Closes #185942

Candidate revision: `895e9c28add`, integrating main `1c03d49956ed`. Post-integration checks and earlier live evidence are distinguished below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: voice-only sessions do not follow the configured daily or idle reset, so voice consults can keep using expired chat history.

## User Impact

User impact: voice consults follow the same reset rule as typed chat, while retaining the existing call-start note used for continuity across voice changes.

On a normal day, note behavior stays as on main: up to 16 bounded user/assistant preview items are supplied at call start, and consult prompts quote the last 12 note items. When a reset is due, call start previews the history that reset will retain—up to six carried-over messages, subject to the existing text and byte limits—without writing the reset boundary. The first consult writes the boundary. If an already-open call performs a reset, its note is refreshed from the chat's current post-reset history, including anything newer. A waiting question on that same call reads the note during its own prompt preparation rather than retaining an earlier copy.

Automatic voice resets preserve waiting user requests, whether the resetting request has a reserved queue position or not. Typed-chat-triggered resets keep their existing cancellation behavior; explicit Stop, `/new` and `/reset` keep their existing behavior.

**Accepted limits:**

- A call open across the daily boundary keeps its original startup note in the voice service; this PR does not update that provider's context mid-call.
- A second call already open on the same chat keeps its own earlier note; this PR does not refresh other calls.
- Two voice consults preparing the reset simultaneously can make one return a reset-preparation error instead of an answer. This is a known limitation introduced by this PR, not a pre-existing main behavior; a follow-up is proposed instead of a scheduling redesign.
- If the resetting call's history refresh rejects after the reset commits, that question fails and later consults on the same call reuse the rejected read and fail too. This is an accepted call-local failure limit, identified by source inspection, not a fault-injection run. Restart the call after the underlying read failure is resolved. The code does not fall back to a note containing history the reset removed.

A voice change reloads its note through the same history reader, so after a reset it gets retained history plus any newer messages, which can be more than six.

## Why This Change Was Made

Call start and consults share one read-only reset-due check. Consults perform the actual in-place reset through the existing lifecycle owner, under the caller's live authority. Existing archived, blocked and model-lock guards remain in place, and voice activity updates idle freshness.

The due-call preview uses the reset owner's boundary builder and context projection. That builder applies `selectRecentUserAssistantReplayRecords` to the latest active boundary window; this is not a separate “take six preview items” rule. The preview does not persist a reset. After a successful reset, the browser/relay call owner reloads its note. The shared consult runtime resolves that call's current note when preparing the prompt, so waiting B does not use a pre-reset copy.

The note stays present on normal calls and in browser and relay paths. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime callers keep their live-call transcript behavior. History-refresh and caller-authority callbacks remain internal: the plugin-SDK wrapper exposes the same consult parameters as main.

There is no new queue, global call registry, cross-call refresh mechanism, storage format, or public plugin setting. The queue-preservation comment explains why an automatic reset removes old context rather than unanswered user requests.

## Evidence

- Before-fix regression run: four intended failures and two passes. Daily/idle due calls returned an empty note instead of the retained messages, and the earlier global-removal repair omitted the retained note from A's prompt. The normal-day and revoked-caller controls passed.
- The existing call-start table covers fresh calls, daily and idle expiry, and consecutive user messages that distinguish the reset's picker from simply slicing six preview items. The existing browser table exercises actual tool-call admission, both questions preparing before A's reset, B continuing afterward, retained note content, no older marker, FIFO answers and caller revocation.
- Before the latest main integration, affected tests: **179 passed across eight files**: 165 cover call-start previews, browser admission/authority, handler defaults, consult ownership, relay readiness and shared runtime/storage, plus 14 prompt-prefix checks. The main command took 163.08 seconds, the prefix check 111.94 seconds, and the before-fix regression 77.59 seconds. No broader diagnostic suite was added.
- After integrating main `1c03d49956ed`, **39 tests passed across four files** in 182.40 seconds: preview hydration, browser admission/notes, consult storage and main's hydration-stream suite. The source build, core typecheck, targeted formatting/lint and test-line check passed. The sole manual conflict resolution retains main's preview-read tracking wrapper around the existing reader and preserves this PR's reset-selection logic. No tests were added for this mechanical integration.
- Formatting, targeted lint (zero warnings/errors), core types and Gateway-other, Gateway-root and other-core test types pass. A commit-hook line cap caught one extra line in an oversized test file; repeated expected values were deduplicated without sharing them with mock input or removing assertions. Its two affected cases and lint/types passed again; production code did not change.
- An earlier independent review of the unpublished update against `e84c3767a2c` found no actionable P0-P2 defects; the later pre-integration review raised the rejected-read failure documented in Accepted limits. The scripted Gateway proof passed **all 17 assertions**: normal notes remain, the due-call note matches the reset owner's retained messages without resetting at call open, same-call A/B quote refreshed history and answer once in order, and both accepted stale-note exceptions remain. That live capture predates the latest main integration; it was not rerun or relabeled as a new-head live result. The post-integration checks above cover the combined preview and reset paths. No result from the superseded global-note-removal revision is borrowed.
- The scripted Gateway fixture checks the reset's actual selected messages before expecting the old code word to disappear. A word copied into a legitimately retained newer message is allowed to survive. The fixture also checks unchanged normal notes, a due call's read-only startup note, same-call A/B, and both accepted stale-note exceptions.

Test lines are net +332 against `main`: reused existing storage and browser fixtures cover reset selection, retained notes, queue preservation and revoked callers; the new behavior is folded into two existing regression tables rather than a separate end-to-end suite. This PR's allocation rises from 267 to 332 (+65); the shared baseline is untouched. The post-integration budget check passes with 2,635 lines of slack.

### Live run — isolated Gateway with scripted provider/model

The driver used normal `chat.send` and `talk.client.create` RPCs, real Gateway control callbacks, the real consult/agent runner and model HTTP. The due-call startup note matched the owner's six retained messages without a reset write. Same-call A/B then quoted the refreshed note and returned once in order; the existing provider and other open call intentionally retained their original notes. Captured verification output:

```json
{"attempt":"attempt-paLz6V","passed":17,"total":17,"verificationReached":true,"sourceBeforeAfterIdentical":true}
```

Proof artifice and limits: an isolated Gateway uses scripted provider/model responses and a short virtual-clock crossing from 03:58 to 04:01 UTC, not real audio or an external model. Two earlier fixture attempts failed before full verification and were corrected without changing production guards. B arrives after cleanup while A is answering; the source regression separately covers B already preparing before reset. Voice-switch behavior is checked by following the shared reader's call sites, not by a new live voice-switch run. No follow-up issue has been filed without the user's approval.

Upgrade scope: this PR adds no settings, stored-data format, schema migration, or installation/update behavior. Voice invokes the existing session lifecycle reset with the existing preserve-tail reset record, and call notes remain in memory. On that basis, a separate latest-stable upgrade run is not proposed for this fix. This is a source-based scope assessment, not a claim that an upgrade was tested; the Gateway proof uses isolated test state.

prs.title: test(gateway): verify embedding base64 wire bytes
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

The embeddings HTTP test accepts any string for base64 output, so it cannot distinguish float32 wire bytes from another encoding.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The existing case now protects exact response bytes while retaining HTTP status and agent-scoped configuration checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the type check with the independent literal `zczMPc3MTD4=` for little-endian float32 `[0.1, 0.2]`. The production encoder does not generate the expectation. No case, helper or setup is added.

Exactly one assertion changes: 1 addition and 1 deletion, with unchanged test LF and no production or allocation changes.

## Evidence

- Native source-only formatter, syntax, whitespace and normal signed commit hooks passed.
- Fresh independent full-range review covered the complete committed range, found no actionable correctness or security findings and assessed the patch correct with confidence 0.98. Source review does not establish runtime success.
- The provider fixture and real Gateway HTTP serializer were inspected; the literal was independently calculated from two little-endian float32 values.
- Qualified HTTP execution, the float-response control, full owning suite and targeted types/lint remain pending. The personal checkout is code-only after native dependency qualification refused sharing.
- Required fault-sensitivity proof remains pending: the same deliberate Float64Array producer fault must pass the old type assertion and fail only the new byte expectation, with status and auth controls intact. The temporary fault and source inputs must be restored after each invocation. No product bug, runtime gain or merge credit is claimed from this source-only result.

prs.title: fix(auth): cron fallback fails with another provider’s session pin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cron turn loses its cross-provider fallback when the session is pinned to the original provider's auth profile.

## User Impact

Fallback providers can select their own credentials. Same-provider pins, shared auth scopes, missing-profile failures, endpoint incompatibilities, and durable required-account bindings retain their enforcement. No config changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope the session pin in the runtime auth planner using the already loaded profile metadata and the existing provider-alias owner. Stored credentials retain their own realm when endpoint aliases change. A declared same-provider pin still fails if its stored credential has drifted.

Supersedes #161811, thanks @Oldrich333.

Closes #161810.

The production delta is +17 lines. Harness/provider selection moves ahead of the native/plugin branches and its later declarations are removed; the fix adds no cron-side tracking state. The +68 test-line allocation covers credential resolution across providers and endpoint aliases, with same-provider rejection controls and a required-binding control. The existing readiness matrix explicitly declares the pinned provider to test credential drift; its rejection assertions are retained. Native-command rejection also stays strict when a harness uses another auth-provider name.

## Evidence

- On main `8654e159b99e545d5fd982791bafdcd988432611`, the new foreign-provider case fails with `Auth profile ... is not configured for openai`; the same-provider control passes (32 passing, 1 failing). This is real auth preparation and credential resolution with synthetic credentials.
- Final candidate tree `b779aa1e14b541e3fb8deacc7ca2cf261996a8ed`: 123 Node tests pass across six named files: runtime auth preparation, native command auth, auth availability, embedded auth-pin preparation, cron model forwarding, and prompt-prefix stability. The auth owner file passes 35 tests in 25.21 s; the six selected shards take 188.72 s. The failed CI consumer is also replayed on the pinned Bun fork: 49 tests pass in 48.93 s (95% of its cold duration is transformation). All test execution used Crabbox Blacksmith Testboxes ([root red/green allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41559092491), [final repair allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41561100228)); no contributor code was run.
- Touched-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41562742802) passed on `5bf5d7b74a473aa4f4ba14c33b233507b6079e2e` in 9 min 24 s; [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41562742509) and [Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41562742611) also passed. The enforced CI/dependency gates are green.
- Independent autoreview of the complete final candidate at P0–P2 is scoped-clean. The native-command control was also reproduced red on the first candidate and green with the repair.
- No live Gateway or paid model call was exercised. The production Team Gateway was untouched.

Supersedes #159143, thanks @mnowrot.

Related: #159138

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes realtime voice-call transcripts showing an assistant reply before the caller turn when speech recognition finalizes the caller late.

## User Impact

Saved call dialogue and subsequent agent consultations retain the caller/reply order, including repeated caller phrases. Existing transcripts are unchanged; a provider with no speech-start event or partial text still uses the first available transcript timestamp.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture each speaker's observed turn start and pass it to the existing transcript-append owner, which orders entries by timestamp. Equal timestamps retain arrival order. Timestamp tracking resets on finalization, rejected caller finals, and provider continuity reset. This is only the core ordering repair; it does not add the original PR's cumulative-transcript ledger.

The change builds on #191584, #191537, and #191498. The pr-simplify pass retained only the timestamp path and owner ordering. Production growth is 13 lines for turn timestamps and owner ordering; there is no dead ordering implementation to remove. The regression adds 65 lines in an existing store integration suite, with a matching test-line allocation for carrier ingress through real SQLite persistence.

## Evidence

- Both late-finalization cases (partial text and provider speech-start) failed on main `abeffef677121a92e8ea70274e18385a2d2a7ff9`, storing each reply before its caller. The cases also preserve two distinct “Yes.” turns.
- The same regression is green in Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox: [remote proof environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41562360041). Four named test files passed (132 tests, 71.77 seconds including worker setup): `manager.async-store.test.ts`, `manager/events.test.ts`, `manager/outbound.test.ts`, and `webhook/realtime-handler.test.ts`. This includes the existing greeting, echo, and continuity-reset coverage. Touched-file lint reported zero warnings/errors, and touched-file formatting passed.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) completed on the full local change against that base: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The review included unchanged manager outbound, runtime consultation, and event type context.
- The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. Only the independently implemented replacement was executed, on the remote Testbox. No paid phone/provider call was made.
- PR CI supplies broad validation. No broad tests, worker compilation, or repository-wide lint/typecheck ran on the production Team host. Native landing uses only the wrapper-managed frozen dependency cache; test dependencies and checks ran on the remote Testbox.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): store realtime caller turns in dialogue order
prs.body:
Closes #159138

## What Problem This Solves

A realtime voice call's stored transcript read as all of the agent's lines followed by one glued blob of everything the caller said, instead of an alternating conversation.

## User Impact

Post-call transcripts can be read and attributed turn by turn: the caller's words appear in the right place in the dialogue rather than being dumped at the end.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under the Google realtime provider the caller side arrives only as partials, so the plugin persisted nothing for the caller until the provider's single end-of-call flush.

The handler now commits the pending caller partial as its own `call.speech` entry immediately before the first assistant entry of each turn, and the end-of-call flush is reduced to the suffix the committed-caller ledger does not already cover.

Getting that order right required changing how the writes are issued. Every transcript write used to be chained onto one `transcriptPersistence` promise, so a write was only issued after the previous one settled. Writes are now issued immediately and ordered by the manager's keyed mutation queue, and every issued write is accumulated into the tracked promise so shutdown waits for all of them instead of only the most recent.

Consequences of that change, each covered by a test:

- The caller turn and its paired assistant reply are two independent writes, so a rejected caller write no longer skips the reply.
- The committed-caller ledger holds one entry per issued turn, kept verbatim so a repeated phrase ("yes", "yes") is not collapsed, and released only if that turn's write fails - which leaves the text for the end-of-call flush instead of losing the turn.
- The end-of-call flush queues behind any turn write still in flight, so it reduces the transcript against a settled ledger. With nothing in flight it is issued in the same tick, because callers observe the flush write before the next provider turn.

## Evidence

28 stored realtime calls showed the bot-block/caller-blob shape (e.g. `9181a17b` 21 assistant entries then one user entry; `bd9c0eed` 15 then one). After the change, entries interleave per turn.

New `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.transcript-store.test.ts` asserts on the **persisted transcript** rather than the manager mock, covering:

- `stores each caller turn ahead of the reply it answered` - a normal multi-turn call.
- `finishes a queued caller turn write before shutdown completes` - provider close with a queued turn write.
- `stores the reply paired with a failed caller turn and recovers that turn at flush` - a caller-write failure together with its assistant reply.

It opens a real state database, like the already-registered `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/store.test.ts`, so it is listed in the extension database-worker fork lane.

Commands and results (all from a clean worktree at this head):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.persistence.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.transcript-store.test.ts`
  -> `111 passed` + `3 passed`, 0 failed.
- `pnpm test:extensions:batch voice-call` -> 76 files, `147 passed` (`extension-database-workers`) and `684 passed / 9 failed` (`extension-voice-call`). All 9 failures are in `extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts` and `extensions/voice-call/index.lifecycle.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; see "Unrelated failures" below.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/voice-call/src/webhook` -> exit 0.
Measured cost of the new file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): **17.3 s wall, 14.7 s Vitest duration, of which 13% (~1.9 s) is test time**; the rest is cold transform/import. Peak RSS 538 MB. Under the 5 s test-time target in [writing tests](docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md#cost-budget). No real timers, sleeps, or polling - it drives the handler through deferreds - and each case gets its own state directory from `createManagerHarness`. CI seconds to follow once the run exists.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts test/scripts/extension-test-plan.test.ts` -> `3 files / 567 passed` (covers the database-worker path registration). A wider run including `test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts`, `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` and `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts` also passed `6 files / 2693 passed`.

### Correcting the previous evidence in this PR

An earlier revision of this description claimed that `assigns unique event IDs to finalized chunks received in the same millisecond` and `waits for shutdown transcript durability (failure=false|true)` "also fail on unmodified upstream main". **That was wrong.** Those tests pass on `main`; they were regressions introduced by this branch's deferred persistence chain, which delayed `call.assistant-speech` past the tick those tests observe. They pass now.

### `check-test-types`

The full-graph extension test type check (`pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`) cannot run on the machine used here - it OOM-kills at ~6 GB RSS on 7.7 GB of RAM without producing a `tsbuildinfo` - so the lane itself is left to CI. Instead the same compiler was run over a scoped project containing only `extensions/voice-call/**/*.test.ts` plus the repository's `.d.ts` inputs, through `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <scoped tsconfig>`: **exit 0** in ~35 s at ~3.9 GB peak RSS.

That scoped check reproduces the lane failure. The red `check-test-types` lane was caused by this branch, not by upstream. The previous head added

```ts
processEvent.mock.calls
  .filter(([event]) => event.type === "call.assistant-speech")
  .map(([event]) => event.transcript);
```

Destructuring inside the predicate gives no type-guard narrowing, and `transcript` exists on only two of `NormalizedEvent`'s union members, so `.transcript` is a `TS2339`. Both occurrences are rewritten as map-then-filter, which narrows. No suppression was added.

Verified in both directions on the scoped project: restoring the previous head's version of that one file reproduces the lane failure exactly -

```
extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.persistence.test.ts(274,35): error TS2339: Property 'transcript' does not exist on type 'NormalizedEvent'.
extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.persistence.test.ts(312,35): error TS2339: Property 'transcript' does not exist on type 'NormalizedEvent'.
```

- and the fixed version compiles clean.

### Unrelated failures

`extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts` (3 tests) and `extensions/voice-call/index.lifecycle.test.ts` (6 tests) fail in the `extension-voice-call` project. They are about plugin registration and runtime-generation lifecycle, not transcripts, and this PR does not modify them or `index.ts`.

Attribution check: reverting `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.ts` - the only production file this PR changes - to its merge-base content and re-running those two files reproduces the same failures. The symptoms (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the mocked `createVoiceCallRuntime`, and `expected '' to contain 'Runtime not started: setup incomplete'`) point at the plugin registration fixture, and the reproduction host was a source-only worktree with no built artifacts. Left to CI; not addressed here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Round 2 — ClawSweeper Revision 4 findings resolved (`a54c0c2c`)

**[P2] Retain the caller ledger until the final flush has drained.** The committed-caller
ledger was handler state keyed by call ID, and the provider close callback deleted it. Google
Live flushes its accumulated caller transcript and only then notifies close, so with a caller
turn write still in flight the deferred flush read an already-deleted ledger and re-stored the
whole caller transcript. The ledger now belongs to the bridge that wrote those turns, so it
outlives the close callback and a replacement connection starts its own; no call-keyed state
and no close-time cleanup remain.

**[P2] Preserve repeated per-utterance final transcripts.** Reduction let any committed text
consume an incoming final (`compactCommitted.includes(compact)`), so a provider that finalizes
each utterance lost a repeated later utterance — a final "yes" counted as old speech because an
earlier turn already contained the word. A final now claims only the turns it restates from the
start, which is the cumulative-flush contract, and each claimed turn is released, so repeated
finals are stored once and a caller who repeats a phrase keeps both turns.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/` | **12 files / 180 tests passed** |
| Scoped test typecheck (`tsgo -p .artifacts/tsconfig.voice-call-test.json`) | exit 0 |
| `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on the changed files | exit 0 |
| Negative control: the 3 new tests on `4c6ed3e3` | **3 failed** — duplicated flush (`"yes goodbye"`), dropped repeat (missing `"yes"`), duplicated repeat (extra `"yes"`) |

New tests cost: the whole `realtime-handler.transcript-store.test.ts` file is 6 tests in
**23.7 s wall / 20.5 s duration, 534 MB peak RSS** at `--maxWorkers=1` (3 tests were 17.3 s /
538 MB), so the 3 added cases reuse an existing fixture rather than paying a new setup.

---

> **Superseding note.** The section that stood here previously was the round-2 harness: synthetic
> `LiveServerMessage` frames with a mocked `@google/genai` transport. ClawSweeper correctly declined
> to accept it as proof for that reason. It is replaced by the real-transport proof below.

## Real Google Live proof (after fix, real transport)

A real multi-turn Google Live call ran through the PR's handler (`realtime-handler.ts` blob `13e2b1b4`, head
`7832d952`), the real Google realtime provider, and the real SQLite call store. I read the stored transcript
back after close.

**The transport was not mocked.** No `vi.mock`, no network stubbing, and no synthetic `LiveServerMessage`
frames were used. The provider's real `createGoogleGenAI()` → `@google/genai` `Live.connect()` opened a TLS
websocket to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. The round-2 mock of `google-genai-runtime.js` is removed.
The caller audio is real speech: Google TTS (`gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview`, 24 kHz PCM) → `ffmpeg` →
G.711 μ-law 8 kHz. It was streamed as Twilio `media` frames (160 B every 20 ms, in real time) into the
handler's carrier websocket, and Google's own ASR produced the caller transcripts.

**The close window.** On caller turn 3, I called `bridge.close()` on the Google bridge in the same synchronous
tick as the assistant's final reply transcript. At that moment the turn-3 caller write had just been issued
and was still in flight. `close()` then flushed Google's accumulated caller text for the whole call as one
final, before `onClose`. This is the path ClawSweeper flagged. Limitation: this is the client-side close
(the hang-up path), not a close initiated by Google's server.

| | evidence |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com//ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent?key=<redacted>` |
| TLS | TLSv1.3, `authorized=true`, SNI `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, issuer Google Trust Services |
| Server `setupComplete` | provider `onReady` fired; SDK `session.setupComplete={}` (set only from a server frame) |
| Raw server frames | 120 after setup; raw `inputTranscription` frames match the provider callbacks (e.g. `" ca"`, `"pital"`) |
| Model | `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` (partial caller text + cumulative flush on close); sibling `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (default) |
| Close-time flush | 92 chars (the whole call) → `residualChars=0` after fix; **`residualChars=71` on `4c6ed3e3`** |
| Stored entries | after fix: **6, user/bot alternating, no duplicates, no missing text**; `4c6ed3e3`: 7 (whole caller transcript re-stored) |

### Stored transcript after close (after fix, 2.5 native audio)

```
user: Hi, can you hear me okay?
bot: Yes, I can hear you perfectly.
user: What is the ca pital of France?
bot: The capital of France is Paris.
user: Great. Thanks. So, goodbye. <noise>
bot: You're welcome, have a good day!
```

### Same harness on `4c6ed3e3`'s handler (before)

```
user: Hi, can you hear me okay?
bot: Yes, I can hear you clearly.
user: What is the ca pital of France?
bot: The capital of France is Paris.
user: Great. Thanks.
bot: You're welcome! Is there anything
user: Hi, can you hear me okay? What is the capital of France? Great. Thanks.
```

### Default model `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (after fix)

```
user: Hi. Can you hear me okay?
bot: Yes, I can hear you perfectly. How can I help?
user: What is the capital of France?
bot: The capital of France is Paris.
user: Great, thanks. That's all. Goodbye.
bot: You're very welcome, have a great day!
```
3.1 emits each caller utterance as one complete final, so at close it has no pending caller text to flush.

### Redacted after-fix runtime trace (2.5 native audio, abridged: caller partials 1–2 and assistant deltas omitted)

```
[proof + 11301ms] provider onReady (server setupComplete received and session open)
[proof + 11304ms] transport ws protocol=wss: host=generativelanguage.googleapis.com path=//ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent query=?key=<redacted>
[proof + 11304ms] transport tls protocol=TLSv1.3 authorized=true servername=generativelanguage.googleapis.com issuerO=Google Trust Services remotePort=443
[proof + 12105ms] caller turn 1: streaming 18880B (2.36s) text="Hi, can you hear me okay?"
[proof + 15114ms] wire server frame inputTranscription={"text":" you hear me okay?"}
[proof + 17114ms] provider onTranscript role=assistant final=true text="Yes, I can hear you perfectly."
[proof + 17915ms] caller turn 2: streaming 23040B (2.88s) text="What is the capital of France?"
[proof + 20889ms] wire server frame inputTranscription={"text":" ca"}
[proof + 21028ms] wire server frame inputTranscription={"text":"pital"}
[proof + 22648ms] provider onTranscript role=assistant final=true text="The capital of France is Paris."
[proof + 25955ms] caller turn 3: streaming 26240B (3.28s) text="Great, thanks. That's all, goodbye."
[proof + 27926ms] wire server frame inputTranscription={"text":" Great. Thanks."}
[proof + 29970ms] wire server frame inputTranscription={"text":" So, goodbye. <noise>"}
[proof + 31409ms] provider onTranscript role=assistant final=true text="You're welcome, have a good day!"
[proof + 31409ms] CLOSE: bridge.close() in the same tick as assistant final #3 (caller turn-3 write just issued)
[proof + 31410ms] provider onTranscript role=user final=true text="Hi, can you hear me okay? What is the capital of France? Great. Thanks. So, goodbye. <noise>"
[proof + 31411ms] provider onClose reason=completed
[voice-call] realtime input transcript callId=<call-id> providerCallId=request-uuid final=true chars=92 aggregateChars=92 residualChars=0
[voice-call] Realtime call ended callId=<call-id> providerCallId=request-uuid reason=completed
[proof + 31475ms] stored transcript after close (6 entries)
```

### Observed on the real transport: "ca pital"

Google 2.5 splits words across `inputTranscription` frames (`" ca"`, `"pital"`). The committed caller turn
comes from the handler's smart-joined partial buffer (`appendTranscriptText`), which puts a space between the
fragments. Google's own final and the raw concatenation both read "capital". Base main stored the provider
final and never committed partials, so this PR introduced the spacing. It affects stored text only;
ordering, deduplication, and the close-time reduction are unaffected (the reduction compares
whitespace-insensitively). Recorded as a follow-up and not fixed in this revision.

The harness was a temporary vitest file driven by `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` in the
`extension-database-workers` project, with `GEMINI_API_KEY` taken from the environment. It was removed after
capture and is not part of this diff.

prs.body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/executor · model: claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: agent-initiated

Closes #161810

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled (cron) agent turn fails with `Auth profile "anthropic:<acct>" is not configured for openai.` when the session has an auth pin and the primary provider fails over to a model of another provider.

## User Impact

User impact: cron turns on pinned sessions now fall back across providers like chat replies do; the fallback candidate uses its own automatic auth selection instead of losing the run.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `runCandidate` in the cron isolated-agent executor passed the session pin, resolved once for the primary provider, to every fallback candidate (embedded `authProfileId` and CLI `selected`).
- now: pin resolved per candidate through `resolveProviderScopedAuthProfile` — the reply path's existing rule (kept for the same provider or auth scope, dropped otherwise).
- pin scope = provider the pin was resolved for, not current `liveSelection.provider`: a successful fallback moves the provider but keeps the pin, and an interim-ack re-prompt then starts on the fallback provider. Scope refreshes only when the pin id changes (live model switch updates both).

## Evidence

- new `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-auth-pin-scope.test.ts`:
  - cross-provider fallback: anthropic primary + anthropic fallback keep `anthropic:work`/`user`; openai candidate gets no pin.
  - interim-ack retry after a successful openai fallback: openai candidate gets no pin on both runs; anthropic keeps it.
  - both tests fail on main without the fix (openai call receives `authProfileId: "anthropic:work"`).
- `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-auth-pin-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this head (`ab12e61`), 32-core Linux host: 2/2 pass; measured wall time 62.5 s on a cold transform cache (vitest Duration 60.15 s, transform 60%), 24.9 s warm (vitest Duration 22.58 s). CI: the per-file time is not printed in the check logs; the cron isolated-agent shard that ran on this head (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-26-1`, part 2/2, 11 files, 121 tests) reports Duration 52.46 s, job 4 min 24 s.
- neighbouring cron isolated-agent tests 71/71 pass; `tsgo` core + cron test shard clean; `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` clean on changed files.
- production observation (redacted logs in #161810): Claude weekly limit → `next=openai/gpt-6-luna` → refusal in 170 ms.

## Real behavior proof — scheduled fallback turn, base vs this head

Setup, identical for both runs, fresh disposable install each: `pnpm build`; `openclaw gateway run` with a fresh state dir, loopback, token auth, no channels. Agent default `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `fallbacks: ["openai/gpt-stub"]`. Auth profiles `anthropic:work` and `openai:default` (API keys, disposable values). Both providers point `baseUrl` at a local HTTP stub that speaks Anthropic Messages / OpenAI Chat Completions; it answers the primary with Anthropic's real billing error body (400 `Your credit balance is too low…`, a fallback-eligible reason) and the fallback with a normal completion. The stub replaces only the remote model endpoints; session pin, cron scheduler, executor, fallback runner and auth resolution are the real Gateway code. prs.title: fix(feishu): deliver captioned media with block streaming disabled
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users receive a missing or delayed caption and attachment when text block streaming is disabled. For example, a plain caption plus a chart is delivered by core as a media-bearing block, but Feishu skips that block unless card rendering is selected. An existing preview can also retain draft text instead of the final caption.

On the affected 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 core path, a skipped block could additionally cause the final payload to be deduplicated and the user to receive the no-reply fallback. The newer core delivery-receipt fixes in #145428 and #148301 protect final fallback independently; this PR fixes Feishu's handling of the original media-bearing block.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deliver captioned media blocks through the existing Feishu caption and attachment senders. If the turn already has an active preview, finish that same preview with the authoritative caption, replacing any longer draft. Preserve text-only block suppression, existing partial-delivery error handling, and the public SDK contract.

## User Impact

Users receive the caption and attachment with block streaming disabled. A preview can finish correctly even when core does not send a separate final payload. No configuration migration is required.

## Evidence

- Head `04aa4879282`: all **195 dispatcher tests passed**, including two new tests using the real reply dispatcher queue, `markComplete()`, `waitForIdle()`, and deferred delivery finalization. These prove completion without an extra final payload; they do not inject a duplicate final.
- Targeted type-aware lint, Feishu package type checking, and formatting passed. Independent code review found no blockers.
- **2026.9.3 test-environment backport:** with matching existing patches and test helper compatibility, the old dispatcher fails all seven selected media regressions. Applying only the Feishu production patch makes **239 dispatcher and streaming-card tests pass**. The changed production file passes lint. Seven old test-file `no-misused-promises` findings reproduce identically after restoring the baseline test file; the full backport test-file lint lane is not claimed green.
- The isolated Linux ARM64 source build produced the plugin archive with SHA-256 `e698709b52508f5129d185e925bac0f40cbc22aa42b5f7c68df505af0d171d3d`. The reviewed artifact was deployed through the existing managed-package patch workflow on a dedicated test account, preserving the installed core and semantic configuration. All archived files were verified against the installed package, and the actual loaded root was bound to that package. Gateway readiness and the Feishu channel connection passed, with zero reconnect attempts. This proves installed artifact identity and startup, **not inbound/model-loop or live-message delivery behavior**.
- **Current-head hosted CI passed:** [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34928338394/job/104253214151) completed successfully for `04aa487928236d8a99a938dd273b39e532d53084`, with no failed or pending checks. This head adds tests only to the previously reviewed production change at `114be5dd4836972c6b29b3d741b002416435d5b5`.
- **Historical real Feishu proof, September 12, 2026:** the same production change passed all three cases below through the actual source dispatcher, plugin runtime, Feishu SDK, media loader, and CardKit, with real message API readback and no transport mocks.

| Historical live case | API-read result |
| --- | --- |
| Preview off, block disabled | One accepted caption post and one accepted native image |
| Partial preview mode without an existing preview, block disabled | One accepted caption post and one accepted native image |
| Partial mode with a longer existing preview, block disabled | The same card changed to the shorter final caption, draft suffix disappeared, streaming mode closed, and the native image arrived |

Each historical case had two accepted message IDs and visible-reply state true. Readback found exactly one marker-bearing caption in the bounded window. Image assertions cover returned receipts, not an audit of unrelated images. The recorded source producer SHA-256 was `1635e9c249a4ac53d50ac4640b78c7b05c4904f543c077e2bf6aa5d126b764f8`.

The historical live proof exercises the source dispatcher and real transport, not normal inbound/model processing or the installed Gateway bundle. The September 15 test deployment does not add a new live-message claim. API readback is not a client screenshot. Failure injection is covered by automated tests. No production service, configuration, or managed Skill is changed by this PR validation.

An earlier broad Windows lane on the pre-rebase revision was not green: 100/102 files passed, with doctor cleanup `EPERM` failures and one setup SecretRef expectation that reproduced on the clean base. The focused results above are the current-head checks.

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(plugins): agent_end hooks receive the completed turn to fork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that review a finished turn in the background (Skill Workshop's experience review, advisor-style reviewers) need the exact transcript entry that ended the turn to call `api.runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn({ through })`. Core resolves that anchor under the turn lease, but only core Workshop sees it, through the Workshop-named harness parameter `skillExperienceReviewSource`. Plugins get no anchor, which blocks moving Skill Workshop into its bundled plugin.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. `agent_end` hooks gain `ctx.completedTurn: { sessionId, entryId }`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The agent-end owner (`src/agents/harness/agent-end-side-effects.ts`) resolves the final entry's anchor once, under the turn lease's write assertion, and hands the same value to core Workshop scheduling and to plugin hooks as `ctx.completedTurn` (projected in `buildAgentHookContext`). A superseded turn or a failed read gives no anchor and never fails the turn.
- The harness parameter is renamed to `completedTurnSource`. `skillExperienceReviewSource` stays as a deprecated alias through 2026-12-31 (public `agent-harness-runtime` contract), with the existing SDK deprecation warning. The embedded runner and Codex pass the new name.
- No new reads: the anchor read already ran for every turn that supplied a source; it now runs once for both consumers.
- No schema or protocol change.

## Evidence

- Gateway e2e (`gateway-plugin-forked-turn.e2e.test.ts`, real loader, mock provider): the plugin's `agent_end` hook receives `completedTurn` equal to the turn's final assistant entry, and `runForkedTurn` with that value settles with only the plugin's tool. Before the hook-context projection this assertion failed (`completedTurn: null`). 6/6.
- Unit suites 1,124/1,124 (`src/agents/harness`, `src/skills/workshop`, Workshop unit contracts). `agent-end-side-effects.test.ts` 10/10: hooks get `completedTurn`; a failed anchor read gives none and hooks still run; the deprecated alias maps onto the new field and core scheduling.
- Embedded and Codex producers: `attempt-phase-lifecycle.test.ts` 10/10, `run-attempt.agent-end-context.test.ts` 3/3.
- Workshop behavior pin, assertions unchanged: unit contract suites and `src/skills/workshop`; e2e `gateway-workshop-learning`, `gateway-review.workshop-contract`, `gateway-notice-history.workshop-contract`.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, type-aware oxlint on changed files pass.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: feat(codex): use OpenClaw's base prompt for ordinary threads
prs.body:
Closes #191327

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Codex-engine sessions receive Codex's "You are Codex" model prompt on top of OpenClaw's own instructions, so every fresh session pays for overlapping guidance and follows a different base policy than the regular engine.

## User Impact

New Codex-engine sessions start with OpenClaw's policy and cost less: a fresh session's first request used 1,564 fewer input tokens (25,395 to 23,831, -6.2%). No tools or capabilities are removed.

Behavior changes to review:

- Models that get OpenClaw's provider overlay on the regular engine, such as GPT-5 and later, now get it here too, including supervised parent and forked threads on start and resume. Supervised threads resolve guidance from their native provider and model; authentication and routing stay native. The friendly interaction style follows the provider's personality setting, even though the Codex thread still sets `personality: none`.
- Existing threads keep their history. On their next cold resume, Codex appends the new instructions as one message of about 11k characters instead of rewriting the conversation prefix.
- Restricted threads start a new native thread once after the upgrade. Incognito threads reject a changed base prompt, as they do for other generic policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`thread/start` and `thread/resume` already accept `baseInstructions`, and OpenClaw already uses it for ring-zero threads, so no Codex patch or private mechanism is needed. Ordinary threads now send the regular prompt's thread-stable sections, rendered by the same code as the regular prompt, plus a short section for what Codex's prompt carried about channels, steering, compaction, and native tools.

The text renders only from thread-stable facts, so routine turns keep the prefix byte-identical. Turn, channel, workspace, and skill facts stay in their existing carriers. Ring-zero threads keep empty base instructions. `promptMode: "none"` keeps its policy in developer instructions because its base is identity-only.

## Evidence

Fresh-session comparison on Codex 0.164.0, using isolated Gateways and the same model on both sides. These live runs were on the pre-rebase commit; the rebase was clean.

| First request | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Provider-reported input tokens | 25,395 | 23,831 |
| Real base prompt characters | 17,199 | 10,407 |
| Stub request: base + developer characters | 37,481 | 29,073 |
| Stub request: tool declaration characters | 56,649 | 56,649 |

- A real tool turn created a file, read it back, and reported its contents correctly. Its follow-up request cached 23,680 tokens. One of three runs missed the cache once; the stub prefix stayed byte-identical between turns and the two repeats hit.
- A session started on the old build and resumed on this change kept its thread and history. A new thread resumed from cold kept its base prompt without duplication.
- Earlier validation covered Codex thread lifecycle, prompt, resume, fork, and supervision files, plus the shared prompt, prompt prefix stability, and prompt snapshot tests. Prompt snapshots were current. Core typecheck passed before the rebase.

## Not Covered

- **Tool declarations are unchanged.** Most of the remaining gap to the regular engine is in tool definitions, and this PR does not touch them.
- **Long tasks were not compared.** The proof is a few short turns. Replacing Codex's model prompt could change behavior on long or complex work, and that has not been measured.
- **`/context` and budgets do not count the base prompt.** The system prompt report, the `llm_input` hook, and token budget estimates read developer instructions only, so policy moved into the base prompt is no longer visible to them.
- **Native sub-agents and forks lack live proof.** Regression coverage now checks provider guidance on supervised parent start and canonical fork cold resume. Neither `spawn_agent` children nor forks have live model proof.
- **The docs section always uses the public docs site**, which is inaccurate for a sandboxed thread with no web tools.
- **The Codex model prompt fixture and its sync script are now unused** and should be removed in a follow-up.

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.
