prs.title: fix(ios): preserve blocked shares for native chat import
prs.body:
## Draft repair handoff — native requalification pending

This approved Save → manual app open → explicit review/import feature remains **Draft**, not merge-ready. This source repair addresses the concrete review and local Mac runner findings below; earlier-head native results do not qualify the updated candidate.

## Problem and solution

OpenClaw Share blocks documents, videos, unprepared images, and selections exceeding its three-image direct-send limit. **Save to OpenClaw** preserves original text and every readable selected file for manual app opening and explicit review/import into the captured Gateway, agent, and session. Existing drafts are never replaced; saving and importing never send automatically. The native Files/image preparation owner handles complete-batch staging and current Gateway budgets.

## Repairs in this update

- **P1 omission accounting:** preservation still gathers all original text, but only providers represented in the direct-send draft count as included. Two distinct unnamed paragraphs, three pure URLs, or extra URLs with an occupied text slot cannot silently disappear while Send stays available. Regressions exercise extraction → composition → block/control resolution. A separate duplicate plain-text URL remains supported and is covered by the existing mirrored-URL test.
- **P2 unavailable recovery:** blocked-share guidance now reflects Save availability. Missing destinations ask the user to open OpenClaw, select the intended Gateway/chat, and share again; a destination-read error is visible instead of swallowed. Send remains blocked.
- **Inbox alias repair:** SQLite receives a native POSIX-canonical directory path from the existing canonical-path owner, with the fixed database filename appended as a string. SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW remains enabled and still rejects a symlink at the database file. A real-owner regression covers ancestor aliases, reopening the same inbox, and database-file symlink rejection. No schema/data-format migration, existing app-private database change, permission relaxation, or retention change is introduced.
- Manually wrapped introduced long production lines. This is not a passing pinned SwiftFormat/SwiftLint receipt.

## Approved bounds and cleanup

The separate protected, backup-excluded App Group SQLite inbox owns original bytes and metadata atomically: 48-hour expiry, at most 50 shares and 50 attachments across the inbox, 48 MiB aggregate text/attachment payloads, and 128 KiB text/share. Expired rows are inaccessible and deleted on the next access, including foreground. Explicit discard or successful complete composer staging deletes the inbox copy; failed import/cancelled review retains it. Temporary files are removed on operation exit, with OS temporary-storage cleanup after interruption. Successful staging uses the existing in-memory composer lifetime. No JSON state, credential export, app-private database relocation, or automatic outbox insertion.

## Evidence

- Exact published repair head: 600202745b6df54fa0abf4b147cbb127fbffcc40; tree cab4aa8111cded120568eaa0e26024975241dfa0. All native tests for this exact head remain UNRUN; the prior two inbox failures are not demonstrated fixed until actual tests run. Remote prior head: 23a7e7d8f6cb5fa4f3d6cbdf3313e340a082cfed; prior tree b43be5b1b5c81522aa96ba2d26c37b3a1c2886bc.
- docs:list and diff whitespace checks passed locally. Supplemental SQLite execution confirms unchanged table/FK layouts after DDL wrapping, binary payload round-trip, and expiry cascade. These are not Swift/iOS integration results.
- Fresh whole-candidate independent static Auto Review, P0–P2, updated tree above: scoped-clean/exit 0. The unchanged canonicalPath helper implementation was not independently supplied to that review; its changed call site and new tests were reviewed. Native runtime behavior remains unverified.
- Author simplify pass keeps one inbox owner, existing direct-draft accounting and shared attachment preparation; no alternate upload path, new storage contract, or speculative refactor.

## Prior-head Mac runner results — not updated-candidate proof

See [native qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191527#issuecomment-6591647813), pinned to the prior head above:

- 16 logic tests across 3 Share suites and 20 attachment-consumer tests passed.
- Both original inbox tests failed with unavailable. The runner reported SQLite NOFOLLOW failure on Foundation-preserved temporary-path aliases. An unmodified owner passed a separate nonsymlink-path macOS oracle; this was not iOS App Group proof or evidence of app-private chat-database corruption.
- Pinned SwiftFormat failed on 6 production files. SwiftLint reported 55 serious violations with introduced and preexisting findings mixed; not all 55 are attributed to this PR.
- Normal app build with embedded Watch failed at SwiftFormat. Successful Watch Rust slices did not establish app-build success.

## Remaining qualification

This Linux checkout has no native Swift/Xcode, pinned SwiftFormat, or SwiftLint. Updated regressions, red-on-prior-head/green-on-repair execution, affected consumer checks, pinned format/lint, full normal app build, real Photos/Files Share invocation, App Group save/reopen/import, upgrade/existing-state compatibility proof, and inspected sanitized before/after screenshots remain pending. No gates are waived and no local device/host allocation or live-state change was performed. Retain Draft for the coordinated Mac runner handoff.

## Credit

Co-authored-by: jjjhenriksen <179184921+jjjhenriksen@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep MCP App confirm previews surrogate-safe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI MCP App confirm strip truncates `decision.text` with a raw UTF-16 `slice(0, 200)`. When an emoji straddles unit 200, the preview keeps a lone high surrogate and Chromium renders a replacement character next to the ellipsis.

Path: `ui/src/components/mcp-app-confirm-solid.tsx` (message and file confirms from App Bridge `sendMessage` / open-file).

Prior attempt: #167108 (closed without merge for missing Control UI evidence).

## User Impact

An MCP App that sends a long user message whose text has an emoji just past the 200-unit cap no longer shows a broken glyph in the “Send this message to the assistant?” preview.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the display cap through the shared surrogate-safe helper `truncateUtf16Safe`, matching the existing Control UI pattern (`usage/view-details`, `session-run-terminal`, `draft-title`, …). The 200-unit contract and ellipsis stay the same; only the cut becomes code-point aligned.

## Evidence

### Reachability

`dispatchMcpAppMessage` builds the confirm preview from the full App message content (join of text/title blocks). The only wire bound is an 8 MiB JSON cap — no 200-unit pre-trim. A production App `sendMessage` with `199 × "a" + "🚀" + tail` therefore reaches this strip.

### Real Solid component before/after (same mounted `McpAppConfirmation`)

Input: `a×199 + 🚀 + b×40` (UTF-16 241, code points 240).

| | wellFormed | lone surrogate | utf16 length | tail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `slice(0,200)` | false | true | 201 | `a a U+D83D U+2026` |
| fix `truncateUtf16Safe` | true | false | 200 | `a a a U+2026` |

Unit test (committed) is red on base / green with this fix: `keeps a boundary emoji whole in the truncated message preview`.

### Chromium before/after (product confirm CSS, same truncate contract)

Base:

![base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/mcp-confirm-surrogate/evidence/mcp-confirm-surrogate/confirm-preview-base.png)

Fix:

![fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/mcp-confirm-surrogate/evidence/mcp-confirm-surrogate/confirm-preview-fix.png)

Focused test:

- `ui/src/components/mcp-app-confirm-solid.test.tsx`

Related: #167108

prs.title: fix(update): preserve dirty checkouts by installing dev separately
prs.body:
Installer support: #147677. Windows launcher support: #147653.

Depends on #147621. Part of #144836's smaller follow-ups.

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit `openclaw update --channel dev` currently refuses a dirty Git checkout. For verified npm-linked installs on macOS and Linux, stage a fresh checkout and move the invoking npm exposure through the existing update transaction. Preserve the original checkout and local edits; retain rollback and report the settled runtime for recovery and triage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind admission to the actual npm launcher and prefix. Recheck launcher ownership before activation, reject custom/replaced launchers, and avoid selecting an unrelated globally installed package manager. Honor an empty `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`; otherwise choose a fresh default destination. Keep JSON output machine-readable.

## User Impact

Local edits stay in the original checkout while the managed dev installation updates separately. This requires the running updater to contain this change; selecting a newer target cannot retrofit an older updater that already refuses the dirty checkout. Install a version containing this fix through an existing supported installation path first.

## Evidence

Current repair integrates main `1f01f4944d45` and reuses its package activation, source staging, recovery, and schema-admission owners. Relocation admission lives in one target-preparation helper; the original checkout stays untouched and launcher ownership is checked again before activation. No new persistence format or configuration is introduced.

Current local proof: four targeted suites passed, 111 tests total (Git service, update execution, shared command runner, Git snapshot admission). Core production typechecking and targeted lint passed. The candidate diff passes `git diff --check`. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues in the supplied code diff; surrounding transaction/integrity implementations were not included in its isolated bundle. Historical counts below are not current-head CI evidence. Exact-head CI must complete after publication.

Earlier production-path CLI fixtures covered dirty-checkout preservation, npm launcher movement, package state, and custom-launcher refusal. Those unchanged-input results are retained; no new full managed-service end-to-end run was performed in this repair.

The service transition reuses the existing package-to-Git owner. Existing CLI/service tests cover refreshing the owned service to the settled root, preserving foreign services, and restarting the original root after rollback. The new filesystem relocation cases run with restart disabled, so a full managed-service relocation/rollback run remains unqualified.

This slice covers npm-linked POSIX installs. Canonical installer wrappers and Windows launcher support follow separately; no native Windows or full-service rollback proof is claimed here.




### CI follow-up: type-import cycle

The architecture job on `06bbc302d05c` exposed a type-only cycle through the Git update implementation, recovery, and execution contracts. Moved the unchanged `GitInstallRelocation` contract into a leaf type module and migrated all three consumers; runtime behavior is unchanged. The Madge cycle check now reports zero cycles, and core typechecking passes. Prior behavioral proof remains applicable; new exact-head CI is pending.

prs.title: fix: TUI startup fails after update rewrites chunks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local TUI sessions loading stale or missing `dist` chunks while `openclaw update` replaces the installed runtime.

## Root Cause and Owner

Package/Git activation mutates a live installation while TUI code loads lazily. The update transaction owns quiescence; TUI startup owns waiting before importing the mutable graph.

## Canonical Fix

- Give each installation a stable process identity and an ownership-checked update gate.
- Discover POSIX and Windows TUI/updater launches, including legacy titles, Node flags, and case-insensitive Windows executable names.
- Revalidate ownership immediately before SIGTERM/SIGKILL; never signal foreign, ambiguous, or reclassified processes.
- Honor the TUI's complete configurable shutdown deadline while finishing immediately when clients exit.
- Hold each affected installation gate through activation, finalization, rollback, and migrated continuation.
- Route production TUI entries through one lazy startup boundary, loading mutable chunks only after the gate clears.
- Publish TUI process identity while the cleared startup gate is still held, so an updater cannot scan between admission and discoverability.
- Relaunch standalone TUI commands from the updated installation, while nested onboarding/system-agent entries unwind their owning cleanup instead of replaying the parent command.
- Preserve main's ordinary `openclaw` CLI title; only running TUI identity is installation-scoped.
- Keep internally entered Windows TUIs discoverable through a lifecycle-owned companion marker.

## Scope Cleanup

The branch remains scoped to the update/TUI coordination owner. Unrelated Doctor mutation/docs work, output-helper extraction, environment bypasses, duplicate normalization, and test-only production exports were removed. No config, schema, protocol, or dependency changes.

## User Impact

Open local TUI clients quiesce before installed runtime files change. Unverifiable, surviving, other-account, or competing updater processes produce visible refusal/retry guidance. A standalone TUI that waits through replacement relaunches from the installed runtime before loading chunks; nested entries finish their resource cleanup without restarting onboarding or setup.

## Current repair validation

Integrated main `1f01f4944d45` and moved TUI gate acquisition into the current activation execution owner, retaining release through finalization/recovery. The gate callback is wired through affected execution fixtures. The process-title regression now restores normal writable process state instead of leaving a read-only spy behind.

- 53 focused process/gate tests and core production typechecking passed.
- Acceptance consumer shards passed 11, 6, and 99 tests. The preaction suite initially failed because of test cleanup; after fixing that fixture, all 21 preaction tests passed.
- Final targeted lint and CLI-update test typechecking passed; candidate diff whitespace check passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in the supplied code diff. The isolated review did not include complete surrounding process-discovery/respawn implementations; its result is scoped, not a replacement for integration proof.
- Exact-head CI is pending after publication. No new native Windows, published-upgrade, or full-service live proof was performed for this port.

### CI follow-up repair

- Await the asynchronous respawn owner so spawn failures reach the TUI caller instead of becoming an unhandled rejection and leaving it waiting forever. The regression fails without the await (120-second timeout) and passes with it.
- Preserve real exports in partial mocks, supply the missing activation-gate callback in the credential fixture, and prune two obsolete mock-baseline entries; no new baseline exemptions.
- All 75 focused TUI/system-agent/execution tests passed. The final consumer run passed all three shards: TUI gate, Git snapshot (5 tests), and post-update repair (46 tests).
- CLI-update and infra test typechecks, targeted lint/format, mock-export check, and diff whitespace check passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of these repairs found no actionable issues, with the full TUI gate and respawn owners provided.
- The documented per-change test allocation is 1,540 net lines against `1f01f4944d45`, covering installation-scoped process/signal authority, startup admission, nested cleanup, and updater consumers. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged; the test-line check passes.
- New exact-head CI is pending. Existing live/platform proof limitations above remain.

## Historical evidence (prior head, not current-head proof)

The following evidence belongs to the previous branch revision. References to “exact head” in this historical record do not describe the current repair:


- Exact head: `71f13ba23c442e26c2d34fe08349a237984483d5`; rebased onto `65d5066c6e901d64e57c2786956132862816fe27`.
- Exact-head formatting and 84 focused updater tests pass locally. Exact-head hosted CI is green end to end, including the published-driver upgrade from `2026.9.8` through activation, restart, readiness, and running-version verification.
- The published-driver harness-only adjustment refreshes the synthetic relabeled package content inventory and compares its installed build identity exactly. It changes no product persistent-data contract and requires no migration or compatibility shim.
- Exact-head acceptance verification passed 219 tests across process discovery, installation revision detection, TUI gate publication and withdrawal, update execution, setup finalization, remote onboarding, and system-agent handoffs.
- The rebased exact-head 219-test acceptance suite passes.
- The Windows discovery regression covers mixed-case direct, Node, entrypoint, and companion executable names. Native CIM proof confirmed that `CreationDate` supplies a stable serialized process-start identity on Windows.
- Fresh independent review found and repaired the cross-account startup/activation race, provisional Windows companion and process-title leakage, and the lock-release ordering hole. Publication withdrawal now completes inside the lock before an updater can acquire it.
- The exact-head ClawSweeper P1 for releasing the gate before discoverability is addressed by that serialized handoff; focused tests assert publication occurs before lock release.
- Remote guided onboarding now uses the nested gated TUI path, preserving its in-process credentials and parent cleanup instead of replaying onboarding after replacement.
- Startup lock contention now counts as replacement only when updater discovery confirms an active announcement; concurrent TUI startup continues normally.
- The prior ClawSweeper four-file acceptance suite passed 59 tests; the exact-head focused suites and `pnpm check:changed` also pass.
- Hosted `docker-seed-e2e` passed the published-upgrade survivor from `openclaw.9.5` to candidate `2026.9.6`: update outcome `success`, restart source `baseline-update`, and survival assertions passed. The sanitized proof is retained in [artifact 11072797868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36654764127/artifacts/11072797868).
- Real-process macOS proof from the prior exact head identified and stopped an installation-suffixed Node TUI only after signal-time ownership revalidation; the rebase preserved that patch byte-for-byte.
- Native Windows 11 proof used the exact candidate head in a disposable Parallels VM. Update activation discovered companion PID 9228 and refused with close-and-retry guidance while leaving `2026.9.6 (6d07622)` installed. After closing the companion, the identical command completed successfully to published `2026.9.7`. The VM was restored to its pristine snapshot and stopped.
- The Windows observation exposed a 6.5-minute delay before refusal. Exact head now performs a read-only companion preflight before candidate validation, while retaining the authoritative fail-closed activation gate.
- Fresh independent review found and repaired nested-startup edge cases: process-title cleanup, republishing discoverability after waiting, and continuing a nested TUI when an updater aborts without replacing the installation. Accepted follow-up findings now hash runtime build metadata so same-HEAD/same-version rebuilds count as replacement, publish a POSIX parent-PID marker so short argv capacity cannot hide a live TUI, compare revisions even when replacement finishes before lock acquisition, and return an explicit updated outcome to setup, remote onboarding, and system-agent owners. Interrupted nested launches now give the operator an updated-CLI recovery command instead of exiting silently. The final review found no additional working-tree P0-P2 defects.
- Exact head binds each termination decision to PID plus process-start identity and revalidates both before SIGTERM and SIGKILL. Real-child tests prove that a reassigned PID or foreign-account reclassification receives no final signal. POSIX discovery fixes the `ps lstart` locale to `C` for deterministic parsing.
- POSIX announcement authority additionally requires the marker's live PPID and UID to match the advertised parent before discovery can grant signal authority. A real detached orphan marker aimed at another live process is rejected by production discovery; the termination owner records zero signals and the target remains alive.
- Runtime revision identity falls back to the loaded `dist/entry.js` owner when optional build metadata is absent, preventing repeated nested-TUI respawn while still detecting replacement.

## Rollout Decision

Maintainer decision: accept the first-upgrade limitation for this PR. An already-installed updater cannot retroactively acquire the new handshake, so operators should close local TUI sessions before the first affected `openclaw update`. Once both updater and TUI include this change, subsequent updates use the coordinated gate.

## Platform Policy Decision

Maintainer decision: retain conservative refusal. Known Windows companions are rejected early with actionable close-and-retry guidance. Discovery failure in the early advisory probe defers to the authoritative activation gate; discovery failure at that gate remains fail-closed because the updater cannot prove that replacing the installation is safe. Native Windows close-and-retry proof confirms the recovery path.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep submitted text when chat switching interrupts delivery
prs.body:
Related: #165515, #190416. This is ordinary live-text delivery recovery; the local slash-command repairs remain separate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: submitted text can disappear when switching chats, agents, or Gateways interrupts native iOS message delivery.

## User Impact

Keep the original submission recoverable without overwriting newer drafts or automatically resending a message whose delivery is uncertain. If recovery storage is full or unavailable during a handoff, the original presentation stays in copy-only recovery: copy any needed text before choosing **Clear recovered text and continue**.

**Draft for the explicitly requested local Mac/iOS runner handoff—not ready for review or merge. Native behavior and the new recovery UI are not yet qualified.**

## Why This Change Was Made

- Recover against the captured conversation/composer key and revision, rather than whichever chat is currently displayed.
- Distinguish interrupted pre-live admission, successful durable capture, known-unsent failures, and ambiguous delivery. Ambiguous delivery retains its warning and manual-review path; reconnect does not blindly replay it.
- Revoke a replaced presentation's transport immediately, while the existing owner retains any text that could not enter the outbox. The fallback pane is copy-only; its explicit Clear action releases local recovery without sending or cancelling Gateway work.
- Retire only the matching captured draft after durable acceptance, including after detachment, and preserve newer original/destination drafts. Defer new-session actions while recovery owns the presentation.

No new manager, storage backend, schema, configuration option, dependency, or universal replay mechanism.

prs.title: fix(openai): Codex login says manual entry is required while browser sign-in still works
prs.body:
Closes #191553
Related: #80963

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex login says it switched to manual entry about 16 seconds in while the browser sign-in is still working, and says it is waiting for the browser when the callback port is unavailable.

## User Impact

User impact: someone taking longer than 16 seconds to sign in sees `Still waiting for the browser. Finish signing in there, or paste the redirect URL below.` If the browser finishes after that, the terminal confirms `OpenAI OAuth complete`.

When the callback port cannot be used, the login no longer waits for a callback that cannot arrive. It asks straight away and says why: `OpenClaw could not use localhost:1455, so the browser cannot finish sign-in here. Sign in there, then paste the redirect URL from its address bar below.`

When the callback is listening, the flow, its 16-second timing and the paste prompt stay the same, and only the messages differ.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser callback keeps racing the paste prompt, so the prompt is an extra way to finish, not a change of mode. The timer stays because the prompt is the way out when a callback can never arrive. The misleading `callback_timeout` log line is removed. A completion line is added because the progress line has already ended by the time the prompt opens.

The login already learns when its callback server fails to bind. That result goes to the local fallback, so the wording follows what happened and no separate port check is needed. Any bind failure takes this path, so the message says `could not use` instead of assuming another process holds the port.

## Evidence

Live in a clean macOS VM:

- At the offer, the terminal showed the new `Still waiting for the browser` line and the paste prompt.
- A callback sent 2 seconds later was answered with HTTP 200, and the login moved on to OpenAI's token exchange.
- The callback used a made-up code, so OpenAI's HTTP 401 was the expected result.

Unpatched 2026.10.9 gave the same callback and exchange result under the `Manual OAuth entry required` wording. That shows the listening case changes words, not behavior.

Tests: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` passes 40 of 40, including a test that holds port 1455 with a real listener. Without the wording change, 1 of 39 fails; without the unavailable-port change, 1 of 40 fails. `src/plugins/provider-openai-chatgpt-oauth.test.ts` passes 4 of 4, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/error-text.test.ts` passes 11 of 11 on the wording commit.

Not tested:

- A real sign-in, so `OpenAI OAuth complete` after a live browser finish is covered by the unit test only.
- Whether the confirmation line renders cleanly as the prompt closes, for the same reason.
- Login through a running Gateway. That path failed in the test overlay, so it was not exercised.
- Remote and VPS login, which this change does not touch. With the port unavailable there, the note saying sign-in may finish automatically stays wrong.
- The unavailable-port path in a live run or with a real browser. It is covered by the unit test against a real occupied port. What the browser shows depends on what holds the port.
- Windows and Linux.
- A package built from this branch. The live run overlaid a runtime-only build on the 2026.10.9 package, with some dependencies added by hand.
- Typecheck was not run, and `oxlint` crashed on the linked dependencies used for local testing. Local review and CI have not run.

#80971 proposed a port check before opening the browser and was closed unmerged. This change still opens the browser, because the address bar is where the redirect URL comes from.

prs.body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: buffered Voice Wake recognition can survive a chat or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Pending wake commands and buffered results from the old capture are discarded when the destination changes; fresh listening can resume through the existing admission gates.

**Draft for local Mac runner validation. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing:** that separate change is already proposed in #165515. No configuration, dependency, protocol, or data migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route invalidation now reuses VoiceWakeManager’s existing recognition generation, capture teardown, and command cancellation instead of canceling only the pending send. Internal recognition start/teardown retain a cancellation-only helper to avoid recursive teardown.

On the pinned main baseline, Watch-started Talk can retain another chat’s key after Talk stops. Phone focus changing to that same key would otherwise skip invalidation because Talk already targets it. prs.title: fix(ui): add Cloudflare Access logout to account menu
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators behind Cloudflare Access had no browser logout action in OpenClaw. Clearing local OpenClaw credentials (“Forget this browser”) does not revoke Cloudflare’s Access cookie, so the next request can authenticate immediately again.

## User Impact

When the authenticated ingress is recognized as Cloudflare Access, the lower-left user menu now shows **Log out**. The action warns that Cloudflare signs the browser out across all Access-protected applications, then navigates to Cloudflare’s fixed origin-relative `/cdn-cgi/access/logout` endpoint. GitHub sign-in and connected OpenClaw accounts remain unchanged.

The row is hidden for non-Cloudflare authentication and UI development proxy sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep ingress logout separate from OpenClaw account/device disconnection.
- Put the action in the account menu where operators expect logout.
- Expose only a fixed typed bootstrap capability; the browser rejects arbitrary providers or URLs.
- Keep the endpoint outside any configured Control UI base path.

Cloudflare documents that user logout applies across Access-protected applications: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/access-settings/session-management/#log-out-as-a-user

## Evidence

### UI proof

Before (capability absent):

![Account menu before Cloudflare logout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3d1812f-e959-458c-91b0-baf8009aff83)

After (Cloudflare logout at the bottom of the lower-left user menu):

![Account menu with Cloudflare logout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bc14eae-fb37-4faa-ab84-cc8b76ed3200)

Confirmation warns about global Cloudflare Access scope:

![Cloudflare logout confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cce305b0-6c29-4be5-b26c-e24ddb7414b6)

### Proof revision provenance — checked September 30, 2026

The recorded candidate `a43e36d4a76b5e953b5d15ca2dc28f288488f128` already contains the account-menu action and the **Log out everywhere** confirmation; it is not the earlier Profile-page implementation. All **14 files changed by this PR** have identical Git blob IDs at that recorded revision and current head `eadc8373b6c37ea90beff37b8fdf2b5f2b9902ed`. The head changes do not alter the recorded logout implementation. This is source-equivalence evidence, not a claim that full current-head CI or a new live run was performed.

The existing 6.72-second recording was downloaded and inspected: approximately 1.5s shows the account menu, 2.0s shows the explicit cross-application confirmation, and 3.0s onward shows Cloudflare Access login with “You successfully logged out.” The redacted network trace below supplies the endpoint/redirect diagnostics; the video alone does not expose request headers or establish the Gateway authentication boundary. As already noted, this proof supplied the fixed bootstrap capability to the candidate UI and did not deploy the candidate Gateway.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** accepting Cloudflare’s cross-application logout scope is distinct from the implementation/proof review. This evidence clarification does not claim or substitute for that approval.

### Real-origin interaction recording and diagnostics

The reviewed candidate UI at `a43e36d4a76` was loaded in an isolated managed browser at the real `https://solver.solvely.net` origin with an authenticated Cloudflare Access session. Because the branch is not deployed, the proof harness supplied the candidate's exact fixed bootstrap capability to the candidate browser runtime; the Cloudflare cookie, logout endpoint, redirect chain, and login response were real and were not mocked or intercepted.

The recording shows the candidate confirmation action, clicking **Log out everywhere**, and the browser returning to Cloudflare Access login:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b509aaf5-637d-4709-99f4-f4ca1ea92069

Real-origin confirmation:

![Candidate confirmation at the real protected origin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/019a4ce5-48e5-4b58-8619-eb9558120019)

Login required after logout:

![Cloudflare Access login required after logout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee056951-7340-4100-8242-4caaacb240d4)

Redacted browser network diagnostics (cookies, authorization headers, and OAuth state omitted):

```text
GET https://solver.solvely.net/cdn-cgi/access/logout
302 -> https://solvely.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/solver.solvely.net

GET https://solvely.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/solver.solvely.net
```

prs.title: fix(google): rename Python-keyword tool parameter names for Gemini function calling
prs.body:
<!-- Closes #143176 -->
Closes #143176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `gemini-2.5-flash` on Vertex AI with the `coding` (or `full`) tool profile would experience total tool-calling failure — `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL: print(default_api.<tool>(...))` — whenever the built-in `automations` or `memory_get` tool was present in the declared tool list, even when calling a completely unrelated tool like `read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gemini's function-calling implementation appears to render tool signatures internally as Python `def name(param, ...)` declarations. `automations` has an `in` parameter (for its `next_check` action) and `memory_get` has a `from` parameter — both Python hard keywords, both invalid as Python parameter names. When either is present anywhere in the declared tool list, the model abandons structured function calling for the entire turn rather than just failing on that one tool.

The fix reversibly renames any JSON Schema property (and matching `required` entry) named after a Python hard keyword to `name__oc_kw` before the tool declarations reach Gemini, and renames it back the moment a function-call response comes in — scoped to `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts`'s shared `convertGoogleTools` (outgoing) and function-call-parsing (incoming) code, so it covers both `google-generative-ai` and `google-vertex`. The actual tool implementation never sees the rename in either direction. Non-goal: this doesn't touch Python *soft* keywords (e.g. `match`), since those are valid Python parameter names and weren't part of the confirmed failure mode.

## User Impact

Tool calls to `read`, `write`, `web_search`, or any other tool now succeed normally even when `automations` or `memory_get` are also in the declared tool set. Previously this combination made tool-calling fail unconditionally on affected models/transports.

## Evidence

Bisected a live captured Vertex AI request (system instruction, `thinkingConfig`, and all 35 function declarations from the `coding` tool profile, replayed via direct `generateContent` calls) down to a single `in` property on `automations`:

| Request variant | `finishReason` |
| --- | --- |
| Full captured request, unmodified | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Remove `thinkingConfig` | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Remove `systemInstruction` | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Only the `read` tool declared (drop other 34) | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |
| All 35 tools, `automations.in` renamed to `in_` | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |
| All 35 tools, `automations.in` removed | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |

Verified the shipped fix end-to-end against the real Vertex API through the actual CLI (`openclaw agent exec`, fresh state dir each run):
- Before: `read` tool call on a fresh session reliably failed with `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL: print(default_api.read(path='...'))` when `automations`/`memory_get` were in the tool list.
- After: `read` succeeds with a correctly structured call; `automations` itself, called with `action=next_check, in="30m"`, reaches the tool implementation as `{"action":"next_check","in":"30m"}` (confirming the reverse-mapping restores the original key), and fails only on its own legitimate business-logic check (`next_check is only available to the currently running job`) rather than a malformed call.

Added two unit tests to `extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts` covering the outgoing rename (`renames Python-keyword tool parameter names before sending to Gemini`, plus a `leaves non-keyword tool parameter names untouched` control) and the incoming reverse-mapping (`restores the original property name when the model echoes back a renamed Python-keyword argument`), following the file's existing `buildGoogleGenerativeAiParams`/`buildSseResponse`+`runGeminiStreamResult` test patterns.

I wasn't able to run the full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` locally (sandboxed environment without pnpm/corepack and outside the repo's supported Node engine range) — relying on CI for the full suite, plus the live-API bisection and end-to-end CLI verification above for functional confidence.

- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does — I bisected the root cause empirically against the live Vertex API before writing the fix, and it maps directly onto the change (Python-keyword rename/unrename at the schema boundary).

Supersedes #143178, thanks @HighervGround.

Related: #143176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gemini tool calling when a declared parameter is a Python keyword such as `from`, `class`, or `lambda`.

## User Impact

Google and Vertex tools retain their original parameter names at execution. Existing suffix names and nested user data remain intact. This replacement includes only the Google parameter repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared Google converter chooses unused underscore aliases for declared top-level keyword parameters, restores returned arguments, and reapplies the aliases during signed history replay. GenerateContent, Vertex, Interactions, and explicit prompt caches use the same mapping. Cached requests retain canonical schemas for decoding while omitting cached declarations from the outgoing request.

The duplicate prompt-cache declaration builder is removed. Necessary production growth implements collision-safe schema-based mapping across the existing transports; there is no new cache, setting, persistence format, or dependency.

prs.title: fix: iOS reconnects keep replaying rejected push registrations
prs.body:
Related: #120241

## What Problem This Solves

Official iOS apps can reconnect successfully while continuing to reuse relay enrollment that APNs rejected with `410 Unregistered`, leaving alerts and background wakes unavailable.

## User Impact

This proposes bounded, registration-scoped recovery and an in-app retry path without reinstalling or re-pairing. Permission, successful publication, and delivery health remain separate: renewed/published registration is explicitly **delivery unverified**.

**Draft — not ready to merge.** Maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, native Swift build/test/format checks, before/after UI screenshots, and signed official-device receipt testing remain outstanding. This PR does **not** establish that notification delivery is restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway preserves typed relay rejection on the existing registration owner. Republishing the same enrollment cannot erase the rejection merely by advancing its timestamp. Test pushes, wakes, and approval sends share the rejection-recording path; a stale result cannot poison a replacement enrollment.
- iOS consumes the existing authenticated `node.event` result, requests a current APNs token, and forces fresh relay enrollment for one automatic recovery cycle per unchanged token/scope. The existing publication flow serializes overlapping callbacks; failures stop automatic renewal and expose **Retry notification setup** in Diagnostics.
- Scoped Keychain enrollment caches retain rejected enrollment and consumed budgets across relaunches and Gateway switches. A matching shipped singleton is moved only after its scoped copy is saved. A new handle alone does not reset the budget; explicit manual retry or a changed token can authorize another attempt.
- Direct APNs behavior and unrelated registrations, pairings, Gateway credentials, and App Attest keys are preserved. No new RPC, configuration option, dependency, or version bump. Missing-registration #146791 is not folded into this fix.

## Evidence

The primary regression failed before the production change for the intended reason: after a fixed relay `410 Unregistered` response, store reconstruction and unchanged enrollment republication had no retained `relayRejection`. The seven existing store tests passed on that baseline.

| Local check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Push transport/store suites | 49 passed; direct APNs, relay request behavior and healthy controls covered |
| Final store + read-kernel suites | 12 passed, including rejection/reopen/republication, fresh admission of an older-state copy, replacement protection and unaffected peer/direct registrations; 45.31s command wall / 5.02s Vitest |
| Gateway event/registration/push sibling suites | 79 passed; final modified event suite rerun: 54 passed, 64.02s command wall / 58.14s Vitest (mostly compiler/import setup) |
| Production and targeted infra/Gateway test typechecks | Passed |
| Scoped production/test lint; touched TS/JSON/Markdown formatting; whitespace | Passed |
| Kysely/PostgreSQL generation and SQLite catalog checks | Passed; generated outputs verified |
| Staged test-line budget | Passed; isolated allocation of 112 net TS regression/fixture lines |

Native Swift regressions are added for cached rejection, reconstruction, same-token renewal, repeated attempts/manual retry, **A → B → A enrollment counts**, changed-token renewal, direct transport, and matching-only legacy-cache migration. They have **not been executed** here. The Linux sandbox has no Xcode/Swift toolchain; `pnpm format:swift ios` also refused because pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 is absent. No real device received a test push.

<details>
<summary>Review, persistence contract, and remaining qualification</summary>

**Review:** Local Auto Review, P0–P2, completed all four batches against base `bf35e054b0062c64e5577b165a3ae629adc3d2d0` and final candidate tree `cca63b6b6d1a2c7d6ceeb703fbaaaf83c455483c` with no remaining findings. Earlier findings about scope eviction resetting/bypassing recovery were addressed with per-scope enrollment persistence and an enrollment-count regression. This is static review, not human maintainer acceptance or native/device proof. The simplification pass retained one registration owner and removed redundant enrollment-flight bookkeeping; the complete token/publication cycle is serialized at its existing caller.

**Proposed persistent contract:** One nullable `relay_rejection_reason TEXT` column on `apns_registrations`, through existing same-version additive admission; null means no recorded rejection, not verified health. The affected SQL operation is an additive column change, with no row backfill or new index. SQLite STRICT admission may inspect existing rows; production-scale upgrade timing has not been measured. The existing database migration/backup owner is unchanged; no new backup mechanism is introduced. A compatible pre-change shared-state backup and matching runtime are required for rollback qualification. The test uses a closed, isolated older-state copy, not a released-binary upgrade.

Keychain cache/retry state is scoped by installation, Gateway identity, relay origin, environment, profile, proof policy and topic; records persist across scope switches and replace only that scope's enrollment. Matching legacy singleton migration leaves other bindings untouched and removes the singleton only after a scoped save. App Attest state is not reset. This persistence/retention/rollback contract still needs maintainer acceptance before merge.

**Before ready/merge:**
- Run the native build, focused Swift tests and pinned native format/lint checks; inspect and attach sanitized before/after Diagnostics screenshots in chat and this PR.
- Reproduce on the affected signed official device and compare token reacquisition alone, fresh enrollment with unchanged token, and the combined path. Re-establish the rejected baseline between experiments; verify actual alert receipt and background wake, not just APNs 200/publication/a different handle. Do not target unrelated devices.
- Qualify the hosted relay's enrollment identity semantics. If fresh enrollment returns an identical handle/grant, this candidate conservatively retains Gateway rejection; actual renewal semantics and the smallest successful recovery remain unproven.
- Complete latest-stable upgrade/rollback and supported-backend qualification. Live PostgreSQL migration and production-fleet upgrade cost were not tested.
- Obtain maintainer contract/security review and applicable CI. CI seconds are not available yet; no hosted review or merge was requested.

</details>

- @TheAngryPit

prs.title: fix(cli): match infer web --provider ids case-insensitively
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw infer web search --provider <id>` and `openclaw infer web fetch --provider <id>` reject a valid provider id when its casing differs from the plugin id. `--provider Brave` fails with `Unknown web_search provider "Brave".` and `--provider Firecrawl` fails with `web.fetch provider "Firecrawl" is not available`, even though the same command already treats the value case-insensitively everywhere else: its own secret scoping lowercases the flag, the web search plugin loader lowercases it to pick which plugin to load, and `tools.web.search.provider` / `tools.web.fetch.provider` in config are matched case-insensitively (config validation was aligned with that in #177836). A script or a user typing the provider name the way the docs and UI label it gets a hard failure instead of a provider call.

## Root cause
`src/cli/capability-cli/web.ts` passes the raw flag value through to the runtimes:

```ts
// before
const provider = opts.provider as string | undefined;
...
return runWebSearch({ config: cfg, providerId: provider, args: { query, count: limit, limit } });
...
const resolved = resolveWebFetchDefinition({ config: cfg, providerId: provider });
```

`runWebSearch` loads the plugin using `normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(providerId)` (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`), so the Brave plugin is loaded, but the explicit-selection guard then compares the raw value against the loaded ids (`providers.some((entry) => entry.id === explicitProviderId)`) and throws. `resolveWebFetchDefinition` looks the raw value up with `providers.find((entry) => entry.id === providerId)` and returns null. Every bundled web search and fetch provider id is lowercase (`brave`, `firecrawl`, `duckduckgo`, `tavily`, `exa`, `perplexity`, `searxng`, ...), so any other casing can never match.

## Fix
Normalize the flag once where the CLI reads it, for both subcommands:

```ts
// after
const provider =
  opts.provider === undefined ? undefined : normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(opts.provider);
```

The lowercased id then flows into secret scoping, `runWebSearch`, and `resolveWebFetchDefinition`, so all three steps of the command agree on one provider id.

## Why this is the right boundary
The `--provider` flag is the only caller that hands an explicit, user-typed provider id to these runtimes: the agent `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools select providers from config or runtime metadata (already lowercased), and the Gateway search test RPC passes ids it got from the provider status list. Normalizing untrusted CLI input once at the trust boundary matches the sibling `infer tts convert --provider`, which runs the flag through `normalizeSpeechProviderId` before calling its runtime. Behavior for lowercase ids is unchanged, an omitted flag still means automatic selection, and an unknown provider still fails with the same error (now naming the lowercased id).

## Verification
- New `src/cli/capability-cli.web-provider.test.ts` drives `infer web search --provider Brave` and `infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl` through the real command registration and asserts the runtimes receive `brave` and `firecrawl`. Both cases fail on pristine main (the raw `Brave` / `Firecrawl` reaches the runtime) and pass with the patch (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/capability-cli.web-provider.test.ts`).
- The existing `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` suite (102 cases, including the web search/fetch provider SecretRef and dispatch cases) passes with the patch.
- `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw infer web search --provider Brave` and `openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl` failed with an unknown or unavailable provider error because the flag was compared case-sensitively against lowercase plugin ids.
Real environment tested: The real CLI run from source with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` (fresh empty state, default config), `BRAVE_API_KEY` and `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` unset, on pristine main 52e113b095d and on this patch with identical inputs. The real bundled Brave and Firecrawl plugins were loaded; nothing was stubbed. The Brave call stops at its own missing-key check before any network request; the Firecrawl fetch makes one real request for https://example.com.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<fresh> HOME=<fresh> node --import tsx src/entry.ts infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<fresh> HOME=<fresh> node --import tsx src/entry.ts infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json`
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 52e113b095d)
$ openclaw infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown web_search provider \"Brave\"."
  }
}
exit=1
$ openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "web.fetch provider \"Firecrawl\" is not available; check it with `openclaw infer web providers`."
  }
}
exit=1

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ openclaw infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "brave",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "result": {
        "error": "missing_brave_api_key",
        "message": "web_search (brave) needs a Brave Search API key. Run `openclaw configure --section web` to store it, or set BRAVE_API_KEY in the Gateway environment. ...",
        "docs": "https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web"
      }
    }
  ],
  "error": "missing_brave_api_key"
}
exit=1
$ openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.fetch",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "firecrawl",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "result": {
        "url": "https://example.com",
        "finalUrl": "https://example.com",
        "status": 200,
        "extractor": "firecrawl",
        ...
```
Observed result after fix: The mixed-case `--provider` now reaches the selected provider: search is dispatched to `brave` (which then reports its own missing API key, the same result the lowercase `--provider brave` gives on main) and fetch is served by `firecrawl` with HTTP 200, instead of both commands failing before any provider runs.
What was not tested: No Brave API key was configured, so a successful Brave search response was not exercised; other web providers were not run individually; full build not run.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: synchronous Codex hook notifications emitted for an owned native child are dropped because the foreground projector only accepts its own thread and the native child monitor does not admit hook notification methods.

## User Impact

Operators and trajectory consumers can observe SubagentStart and SubagentStop hook runs for an already-owned native child under the child canonical native run identity, including while a follow-up native turn is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native child monitor now admits hook/started and hook/completed, routes only notifications whose thread is an already-registered child, and sends them through the existing hook payload projector. Pending turns no longer hide the current child from hook observation, while turn completion handling remains unchanged. Hook observations remain diagnostic events; they do not create ownership, change child lifecycle, or participate in completion delivery. The projector now accepts the narrowed hook-method union directly, satisfying the assertion-safety ratchet.

prs.title: fix(agents): failed sandbox setup leaves containers running
prs.body:
Closes #143685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session-scoped Docker or Podman sandbox stays running and registered until prune when a native agent attempt fails after creating it but before dispatch, so repeated failed runs pile up one idle container per isolated session.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed setup now removes the container it created. Containers that already existed, were adopted by another run, or reached dispatch keep running for reuse. Agent- and shared-scope sandboxes, managed worktrees, SSH, and plugin backends behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the earlier design, which inferred ownership from registry absence. Rollback authority now comes only from the container lifecycle owner:

- Under its per-name lock, after publishing a freshly created generation, the lifecycle records a setup allocation bound to the engine target and the immutable container ID.
- Every later admission, replacement, or removal turn for that name revokes it before acting, so adopted, pre-existing, and replacement generations are never retired.
- The attempt hands the allocation off immediately before the execution phase. Any earlier failure (mount inspection, registry publish, browser setup, workspace guards, tool and session-runtime preparation) retires it in the attempt's `finally`, on the same lock, by ID. Removal is bounded to 30s and revalidates the Podman target first. Management removal intent and revoked-authority generations are kept, matching the existing failed-allocation policy.
- Only session-scoped generations are recorded. Agent and shared scopes are adopted by the next run instead of accumulating, so rolling them back would only turn reuse into a rebuild.
- The attempt scope reaches the lifecycle through AsyncLocalStorage around setup, so the plugin SDK `resolveSandboxContext` contract is unchanged. Registry changes stay on the `sandboxRegistry.write` worker path. Rollback failures are logged and never replace the attempt's own error.

Known limits:
- Ownership is process-local, like existing Docker allocation, so a second OpenClaw process adopting the same session container during setup is not detected.
- A deterministic pre-dispatch failure with model fallbacks recreates the session container for each candidate instead of leaving one behind.
- The browser container and the plugin-harness setup path keep today's behavior; both are follow-ups.

## Evidence

Real Docker 29.7.2 (linux/arm64) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `debian:bookworm-slim`, session scope, and a read-only workspace plus `requireWritableSandbox`, so `runEmbeddedAttempt` fails in setup after its container exists. Events come from `docker events`; final state from `docker ps -a` and the registry.

| Case | `main` (46fc2e34f) | This branch (f486fbc3b) |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh container, setup fails | created; still running, registry row kept | created, then destroyed; no container, no row |
| Container existed before the attempt | kept | kept |
| Another provisioner adopted it while the attempt was still allocating | n/a | kept (row `ready`) |
| Setup handed off at dispatch, rollback afterwards | n/a | kept |

<details>
<summary>Terminal output (temporary harness, not committed)</summary>


The adopter waits until the attempt's container exists, then queues behind the attempt's 3s `setupCommand`, so it adopts before the attempt fails. All proof containers and state were removed afterwards.

This output is from `1d75263f8`; re-running the harness on `f486fbc3b` gave the same results.

</details>

**Admitted operator lease (real Docker, `f486fbc3b`).** The run is admitted through `prepareAgentRunAdmission(...).admit("embedded")` with a host-issued authority that has an access grant, source, live signal, and `retain`, so the container gets private source custody.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Lease stays live, setup fails | container created, then destroyed; registry row removed; lease retain count unchanged |
| Access revoked after allocation, before rollback | revocation stop kills it (`Exited (137)`); rollback keeps the writable layer and the registry row |

<details>
<summary>Terminal output</summary>

```text
[leased] admitted operator lease live, setup fails
  docker events: create oc-proof-workspace-5d69fca9e4d25097ae49137ec079a2aa, destroy oc-proof-workspace-5d69fca9e4d25097ae49137ec079a2aa

```

Docker has no awaited target probe, so revocation landing *during* target validation can only happen on Podman (next table).

</details>

**Podman, admitted operator lease (real Podman 6.1.2 client, 6.1.3 machine, linux/arm64, `f486fbc3b`).** Same admission and authority as above, `backend: "podman"`, state and workspace under the machine's `/Users` share.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Lease live, native setup fails (`runEmbeddedAttempt`) | container created on the machine target, then removed; no container, no registry row |
| Active connection switched to `podman-machine-default-root` before rollback | rollback refused with "The active Podman connection changed…"; container still running, row kept |
| Access revoked while the rollback's own `podman info` target probe is pending | rollback keeps the generation; the revocation stop then kills it (`Exited (137)`); row kept |

<details>
<summary>Terminal output</summary>

```text
[podman] live lease, native setup fails
  outcome: attempt rejected: sandbox workspace is not read-write; collection review skipped
  containers: (none)
  registry: (none)
[podman] active connection reassigned before rollback
  outcome: rollback refused: The active Podman connection changed after this sandbox runtime was created. Restore the original Podman target before inspecting, executing, or removing the runtime.
  containers: oc-proof-podman-workspace-6c9b02bbdcb6ec44726d02337232eb23 running (Up 1 second)
  registry: oc-proof-podman-workspace-6c9b02bbdcb6ec44726d02337232eb23 backend=podman state=-
[podman] target probe started; revoking operator access now
[podman] access revoked during the rollback target probe
  outcome: rollback resolved
  containers: oc-proof-podman-workspace-3992a719711c8bf9bffcfc4091d8d953 exited (Exited (137) Less than a second ago)
  registry: oc-proof-podman-workspace-3992a719711c8bf9bffcfc4091d8d953 backend=podman state=-
```

To land the revocation inside the probe deterministically, a proof-only `podman` shim on `PATH` holds one armed `podman info` call for 2s and then runs the real binary with unchanged arguments. All other calls go straight to the real binary, and OpenClaw's own probe timeout is 5s. The harness revokes access as soon as that probe starts. The connection switch and container listing use the real Podman CLI, and the default connection was restored after the case. A second full run gave the same results. All proof containers and state were removed afterwards.

</details>

Tests, with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time (the new cases add about 2s of test time in total):

- `src/agents/sandbox/docker.access-lifetime.test.ts` (16s, 33 tests), driving real `ensureSandboxContainer` turns on the real lifecycle queue against a fixture engine:
  - Rollback removes only its own generation on the reserved-setup, plain-publish, and management-removal-intent paths.
  - It keeps generations that were adopted while queued, removed, replaced, pre-existing, handed off, revoked, managed-worktree, agent-scope, or shared-scope.
  - A failed removal rejects and keeps both the generation and its registry row.
- `src/agents/sandbox/docker.config-hash-recreate.test.ts`, with an admitted operator authority:
  - Podman rollback removes through the original local target while access is live.
  - After the active connection moves to a machine, it refuses, with no `rm` and no registry change.
  - When access is revoked while the target probe is pending, it keeps the generation and its row. Removing the post-probe recheck fails exactly this case.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.cwd-split.test.ts` (17s, 9 tests):
  - Setup and tool-preparation failures retire the allocation.
  - Dispatch hands off before the first prompt.
  - A failing rollback leaves the attempt's original error intact.

Removing each guard fails exactly the cases that cover it. The guards are custody revocation on admission and on removal, the session-scope filter, revoked-authority retention, the managed-worktree exclusion, Podman revalidation, the hand-off, the `finally` rollback, and the rollback `catch`.

Other checks:
- `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox` (737 passed) and `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run` (2823 passed) are green.
- `pnpm tsgo`, a typecheck of the changed test files, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm deadcode:full`, and oxlint/oxfmt on the changed files pass.
- `pnpm build` passed on the pre-review revision. The review fixes add only an import from `podman-runtime.ts`, which `docker.ts` already imports from.
- An independent review found these issues, all addressed: unbounded removal, rollback of reusable scopes, missing Podman revalidation, and test gaps. ClawSweeper's revision-3 P1 (operator revocation not rechecked after the Podman target probe) is fixed in `f486fbc3b`.

Gaps:
- Full `pnpm lint` on this 8 GB laptop timed out in two stripes. It also reported a `max-lines` error in `src/plugins/doctor-contract-registry.ts`, which this branch does not touch; the file is 781 lines on `main`.
- Rollback custody is process-local, like existing Docker allocation. A second OpenClaw process that adopts the same session container during setup is not detected. Closing that gap needs cross-process locking on Docker/Podman ensure, which is a maintainer decision and out of scope here.

prs.title: fix(ios): show agent pictures and enlarge Duo side controls
prs.body:
Closes #191539

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent profile pictures appearing as initials in the native iOS picker, agent list, and chat toolbar even when the same agent has a picture on desktop.

## User Impact

Existing inline and Gateway-served agent pictures now appear in those iOS views. Agents without a readable picture keep their emoji or initials and status indicator. In a phone side toolbar, the sidebar, agent, and actions artwork is 30% larger with 52-point tap targets; horizontal toolbar sizes stay unchanged. Raw SVG pictures still fall back to emoji or initials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native views only consumed badge text. They now use the existing agent identity image, including workspace identity lookup when the roster omits it. Image loading reuses the shared source policy and authenticated Gateway resource loader, with bounded decoding and route-scoped invalidation. The chat presentation retains its selected image while a response is pinned.

Colin encouraged the agent-picture scope in the iOS Discord thread on November 2.

### Duo toolbar sizing rationale

The larger artwork is a visual-proportion and usability refinement for the Duo's native side-toolbar area. On the physical device, the original fixed-size glyphs looked small beside the nearby system status indicators. The intent is to make the sidebar, agent/status, and actions controls easier to recognize and better balanced within that area.

The artwork is 30% larger, with 52-point tap targets that contain the enlarged controls. This adjustment follows the actual vertical phone-toolbar environment rather than screen dimensions; standard horizontal iPhone toolbars retain their existing artwork and 44-point targets. Brian checked the result on the closed and unfolded Duo and confirmed that the size feels right and all three controls work.

[Apple's Duo guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-iphone-duo#Vertical-controls) supports native side placement, safe-area-aware layout, and consistent control ordering across poses. The 30% enlargement and 52-point targets are our tested design proposal, not Apple-prescribed dimensions or a requirement to match system status icons. Available space varies by pose, so the system continues to own placement and overflow.

**iOS owner decision requested:** Accept the Duo sizing refinement, or request an adjustment before merge. The earlier encouragement for agent pictures is not being presented as approval of these sizing values.

The current base also failed the normal iOS SwiftLint build step because a review-demo fixture exceeded the function-length limit. Two unchanged fixture branches were extracted into helpers to unblock the build. Their existing UI tests pass.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on a physical iPhone Duo: Sparx had a picture on desktop and initials on iOS before the fix.
- Installed the signed development build on the same Duo. Brian confirmed the picture matches desktop, initials remain for an agent without a picture, switching back restores the photo, and the unfolded view looks correct.
- Full signed iOS build passed, including normal SwiftFormat and SwiftLint phases.
- 29 focused avatar, sidebar, and typography tests passed on a standard iPhone 17 Pro simulator running iOS 27.0. The two existing UI tests covering the extracted review-demo fixtures passed on the earlier avatar-only snapshot; those fixture bytes are unchanged.
- Brian confirmed the final toolbar size on the physical Duo, closed and unfolded, and verified the sidebar, agent/status, and actions controls all open normally. The built app also retains the standard horizontal toolbar on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator.
- The final Duo toolbar UI test passed on iOS 27.1: visible artwork, minimum target bounds, status popover behavior, and the actions-to-Settings flow.
- Native i18n verification passed with no inventory changes. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent static review of the complete local patch by a separate task agent found no remaining actionable findings. This is not a ClawSweeper verdict or maintainer approval. Avatar commit `4aacaf360ec` and the subsequent four-file toolbar delta `73fe783e0f3` received separate independent passes with no remaining actionable findings. Source hashes and local test results are retained for the final committed range.

Before and after below are matching crops of native physical-device screenshots. Only the avatar control is retained so private chat and Gateway details are excluded. No avatar pixels were generated or modified.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native iOS avatar before: initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6353f10b-0f4c-4720-901e-7f804435053d) | ![Native iOS avatar after: configured photo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ca0aaa7-5f4e-4bf8-944f-6f53b64f6fc3) |

The toolbar comparison below uses matching crops from the same native offline Duo fixture before and after the sizing change. The physical Duo interaction check is reported separately above.

| Toolbar before | Toolbar after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Duo side toolbar before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7763da45-0fea-441f-8391-e439762fa3b9) | ![Duo side toolbar after: larger controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf1c1740-f095-4e71-917d-c014b36894d0) |

### Wider toolbar proportion comparison

These matching 1398 × 1450 crops retain the full screen width and show the toolbar beside the chat and system status icons. They come from the same native offline Duo fixture as the close-ups above, with identical crop bounds and no resizing. The chat scroll position differs slightly; the toolbar and surrounding UI retain their original scale. Only synthetic demo content is included. Physical-device checks are reported separately above.

| Wider view before | Wider view after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Duo toolbar before, with screen context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fc680d6-f371-4581-b5d5-8c58b3c13d72) | ![Duo toolbar after, with screen context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05cc0664-dabc-41e7-8c87-89c2edd13149) |

The physical picture path was exercised against the existing Gateway. Raw SVG rendering is outside this patch; unsupported or unreadable images use the existing fallback. The side-control sizing is a small refinement of Apple’s adaptive toolbar: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-iphone-duo. No app release or App Store submission is included.

The standard iPhone UI automation runner stalled before starting the test and was stopped after diagnosis. The app itself launched and rendered its horizontal toolbar normally; this is visual inspection rather than a passing standard-iPhone UI automation result.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): remove containers when backend preparation fails
prs.body:
Supersedes #143755, thanks @aishwary-dongre.
Related: #143685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a newly created Docker or Podman sandbox stays running when backend preparation fails after its container has started.

## User Impact

User impact: failed provisioning removes its newly allocated container and registry entry while preserving the original error. Reused containers and the existing revoked-access retention policy are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep backend mount inspection, filesystem bridge loading, and persistent-generation preparation inside the existing container lifecycle lock and cleanup boundary. This reuses immutable-ID cleanup and consolidates the duplicated allocation result; it adds no rollback tracker or attempt-wide custody protocol.

This is a bounded provisioning repair. Failures after a completed backend is returned to agent-attempt preparation remain follow-up work under #143685. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

Production delta: +37 lines, including the typed internal preparation callback; most of the backend diff is indentation. Duplicate allocation-result construction was removed. Tests grow by 22 lines, covered by the dedicated regression allocation record.

## Evidence

- Reviewed current main at `9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d`, existing cleanup from #150713, and the recent Podman timeout fix #188770. The remaining leak was the backend inspection after the lifecycle returned.
- On Blacksmith Testbox, the new fake-runtime regression is red on main: create=1, start=1, remove=0 after backend inspection fails. With this fix, the same regression removes the fresh allocation, preserves a reused runtime, and propagates the exact original error object.
- 73 focused tests pass across `docker.access-lifetime.test.ts`, `docker.partial-create-cleanup.test.ts`, `docker-backend.test.ts`, and `dependency-template.test.ts`. The four-file run took 68.86s command wall time; one stale mock-call expectation was corrected, and its 33-test backend file passes in 41.47s command wall time. Wall time was dominated by transforms. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551266696).
- The two affected Gateway checkpoint cases and both cleanup regression cases pass on a fresh Testbox lease (51.40s command wall across two named files). [Repair proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41553715386). The Gateway fixture now reuses actual backend metadata and retains its checkpoint assertions.
- Touched-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass for all five touched TypeScript files. Broad [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554659146) passes for `1fd3a6d` (603s workflow elapsed), including the final Gateway fixture and core test typechecking. Both required CI-gate projections are green.
- Independent P2 Codex review accepted the corrected working-tree implementation; its two index-only findings were resolved by staging those exact fixture repairs before committing `1fd3a6d`. No additional code findings were identified. The production change is unchanged from the initial scoped-clean review. Hosted review’s two fixture findings (required session key and Gateway callback adaptation) are fixed in `1fd3a6d`. The local ClawSweeper CLI was unavailable.

All container operations in this proof use a fake engine. No Docker/Podman runtime or contributor code was executed. Live-container behavior was not tested.

prs.title: fix(cron): carry the failure-alert delivery outcome in repair briefs
prs.body:
Related: #186990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a channel-less gateway, a failing automation's operator alert cannot be delivered — the delivery failure (`Channel is required (no configured channels detected)`) is recorded only in job state fields, while the repair brief injected into the owner conversation says just `No failure alert was sent.` The operator's only visible signal omits the reason, and nothing points at the state that explains it.

## User Impact

User impact: the repair brief now carries the last failure-alert delivery outcome from job state — the recorded status and reason when a delivery failed (for the reporter's case: `not-delivered: Channel is required (no configured channels detected).`), the fact of delivery when it succeeded, and the original bare sentence when no attempt was recorded. The recurring variant keeps its consecutiveErrors counter, so each brief states both how many runs failed and why the operator alert is missing. This is the report's Expected second branch ("the repair brief carries the delivery-failure fact itself").

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildCronFailureRepairBrief` hard-coded `No failure alert was sent.` in both variants with no access to the delivery trace that `failureNotificationDeliveryFromJobState` already resolves from job state. The brief is the operator's only visible signal on a channel-less gateway, so the delivery-failure fact belongs in it. Because the streak's brief is emitted before its alert is attempted, the existing in-app fallback notice (the other operator surface) also carries the settled outcome when the delivery settles as not-delivered — rendered through the same bounded untrusted-data boundary.

## Evidence

- New `src/cron/service/failure-repair-brief.test.ts`: the bare sentence is preserved when no delivery attempt exists; an embedded transport error stays escaped inside its untrusted data block; a delivered alert is stated instead of the negative claim; the terminal one-shot variant includes the delivery state alongside the disabled notice.
- Service-level regression carries the prior settled outcome into the streak's repair brief; the fallback regression proves the settled reason reaches the in-app fallback notice and **fails on the pre-fix revision** (`9f4c836c69e`) and passes on head.
- Consumer suites `failure-alerts.outcome/persistence/account-routing` + brief suite: 37/37 green on head `c26ca18d10b`.
- **Real behavior proof — live channel-less Gateway** (revision 7): a real `openclaw gateway` at head `c26ca18d10b`, started on an isolated state dir with no `channels` config (`OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`), ran real automations through the shipped cron scheduler, transport, and session-event queue (nothing stubbed). The shipped transport settled a failure alert as `not-delivered` with `Channel is required (no configured channels detected)…`, and the next incident's **repair brief reached the owner conversation carrying that settled outcome and reason** — as did the in-app fallback notice on a scheduled failure. Outputs are the Gateway CLI's job state, run history, and the agent's `transcript_events` table: [revision 7 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188022#issuecomment-6541887935).

## Risk and Compatibility

- Error-string composition only; no delivery, scheduling, or incident-state change. The deduplication semantics are unchanged: the existing `!repair` push condition keeps one counted brief per incident (`consecutiveErrors` in the text is the counter the report asks for), so this change cannot increase brief frequency.
- The report's Expected offers "either" a doctor/status-line item **or** this brief wording; either branch satisfies it, and this PR takes the brief wording. The doctor/status-line branch is carried separately by #188946 / #189881 against `src/commands/doctor/cron/*` and `docs/cli/doctor/checks.md` — files this PR does not touch, so the two land independently.
- **Route selection is not in scope, and #189947 stays open.** #189947 (P1, `impact: security`) reports that failure alerts for `delivery: { mode: "announce", target: "owner" }` automations resolve the session's last route instead of the owner DM. This PR only composes the outcome of *whichever* route was chosen into the operator text — `failure-alerts.ts` passes the prior settled delivery through, `notification-dispatch.ts` appends the rendered note to the existing fallback text, `timer-outcomes.ts` captures it before the per-cycle reset. No target, channel, or recipient resolution changes, so this PR is not the resolution of that report; the report stays open until the route-selection work lands.
- **Different surface from #190598** (landed on main as `266002c36`, "let scheduled jobs read their own delivery receipts"): that work decides whether a scheduled job may *pull* its own run receipts and message IDs through the cron tool (`src/cron/delivery.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/*`, `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-runs.ts`). This PR writes the settled outcome into text the operator sees without asking (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts`, `notification-dispatch.ts`, `timer-outcomes.ts`, `failure-repair-brief.ts`). None of the seven files here were touched by it — main-side commits against this PR's seven paths since `c26ca18d10b` number 0 — so the two are additive, and a pull-based receipt reader leaves the un-asked-for signal in this PR still needed.
- **Merge order with #189953** (the owner-target route-selection work for that report): both PRs now carry `proof: sufficient` / `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look` — #189953 moved there at 2026-11-02T04:01Z and its two `merge-risk` labels were dropped in the same pass — so there is no proof-based tiebreaker left and either order is defensible on priority (P1 there, P2 here).
