prs.title: fix(memory): recover indexing after embedding request timeouts
prs.body:
Supersedes #144488, thanks @Finn763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes memory indexing repeatedly sending the same oversized request after the embedding watchdog expires, leaving the indexing pass incomplete on a slow provider.

## User Impact

Indexing retries smaller requests after a watchdog timeout. A single input that still times out fails visibly. Query deadlines and provider-owned timeout defaults stay unchanged; no configuration or reindex is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing batch policy now splits a watchdog timeout immediately instead of spending three attempts on the same payload. Existing network retries, cancellation, malformed-response handling, ordering, and cache publication keep their owners.

Main already includes #167891 (603f60a38cfe658f3b9f1aee509595f39dc4540e), which removed the independent HTTP timeout and bounded deep probes. Sync cleanup also releases the pending promise and preserves dirty work after failure. The remaining defect is batch convergence, not a permanently latched sync. We are declining a new timeout setting: automatic recovery fits the existing provider-owned timeout contract without another public control.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 41552993820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552993820) passed on 3ad47b920f306e84a8f2d7055836b6a66fae25d7, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. No inherited-failure exception was needed.
- Hosted ClawSweeper review of that same head found no actionable findings or before-merge requirements; it notes the disclosed live CLI/transport proof gap.

- On main 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, the new manager regression fails for both text and structured batches with `MEMORY_EMBEDDING_OPERATION_FAILED`; the 24 existing manager cases pass.
- Blacksmith Testbox [41551644742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551644742): both affected suites pass, 85 tests. The real manager watchdog aborts requests of sizes 3 and 2, then returns all three vectors in order through singleton requests, with no unchanged-payload retry or provider degradation. Existing policy tests retain network retries and single-input stopping behavior.
- After a typed abort-error fixture correction: 26/26 manager cases pass again, touched-file type-aware lint reports zero warnings/errors, formatting passes, and `git diff --check` is clean. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate against 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, P0–P2: scoped-clean. The subsequent typed fixture rejection was inspected manually; production is unchanged.
- The focused two-file run takes 30.62 seconds including worker preparation; the final manager-only rerun takes 38.49 seconds. Test bodies take under one second. New watchdog cases use fake timers. The successful `checks-node-changed` CI job takes 298 seconds including shared setup.

Proof uses a synthetic provider through the production manager watchdog and split policy. Real single-core llama.cpp hardware and a live agent turn were not exercised. Contributor code was read with gh only and was never checked out or executed.

Simplification: one existing policy owner, no new state, helper, setting, or SDK surface. Production +5/−1 (net +4); no dead or duplicate production code in this narrow owner could be safely removed. Tests grow 30 lines for the missing watchdog recovery boundary, covered by a separate allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(memory): make the embedding request timeout configurable and recoverable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw memory status --index` aborts a local embedding request at a fixed wall clock that no user setting can raise, so a slow-but-healthy provider (llama.cpp on a single-core VM at roughly 10 tokens/s) stalls the memory index permanently: the same oversized batch times out on every run, the run ends with the remaining files unindexed, and a global undici dispatcher cannot change it because the abort never reaches undici.

### Root cause

The ~300s abort is OpenClaw's own per-request watchdog, not an HTTP/undici timeout:

- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts:185` (`runEmbeddingOperationWithTimeout`) races the provider call against its own `setTimeout` + `AbortController`, so `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout` overrides on a global dispatcher have no effect.
- The budget comes from `resolveEmbeddingTimeoutMs` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts:138`), which prefers the provider's `inlineQueryTimeoutMs` / `inlineBatchTimeoutMs`. The llama.cpp provider hardcodes `5 * 60_000` (query, the ~300s the reporter saw) and `10 * 60_000` (batch) at `extensions/llama-cpp/src/embedding-provider.ts:224-225`; core falls back to the same numbers at `manager-embedding-ops.ts:78-80`, and `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts:489` does the same for remote providers.
- A config seam existed but was never wired: the batch branch already honoured `configuredBatchTimeoutSeconds`, while its only writer, `src/agents/memory-search.ts:337`, hardcoded `embeddingBatchTimeoutSeconds: undefined`. No `memory.search` key existed and the docs only said "Concurrency, polling, and timeout behavior are provider-owned".
- A watchdog timeout also matched the transport-retry regex (`timed out`), so the identical oversized request was resent until the failure budget ran out, and `isSplittableMemoryEmbeddingBatchError` did not recognise the watchdog message, so the batch was never split.

### Fix

- New `memory.search.embeddingTimeoutSeconds` (with the usual `agents.entries.<id>.memory.search` override), documented in `docs/reference/memory-config.md`. It overrides the per-request embedding watchdog for both index batches and queries. Unset means today's provider-owned budgets, so existing installs keep their behaviour.
- Timeout errors now name the request: `memory embeddings batch timed out after 1s (provider=local, model=..., items=8)`.
- A watchdog timeout is no longer resent unchanged. The index path treats it as splittable, so the batch is halved and retried, which lets a slow provider converge; embeddings that already completed stay in the embedding cache.

## Evidence

Root-cause location (file:line): `manager-embedding-ops.ts:138,185` (watchdog + budget resolution), `extensions/llama-cpp/src/embedding-provider.ts:224-225` (hardcoded 5/10 minute budgets), `src/agents/memory-search.ts:337` (dead config seam), `docs/reference/memory-config.md` (provider-owned timeout claim).

Regression test drives the real watchdog with a fake slow provider (a batch that never resolves), injecting a 1s budget instead of waiting out the 300s/600s defaults:

- Red before the fix: the manager test with `embeddingTimeoutSeconds: 1` failed and reproduced `memory embeddings batch timed out after 600s` (the provider default), plus the 2 new config-wiring tests returned `undefined`.
- Green after the fix: 23/23 in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.retry.test.ts`.
- Sabotage 1 (drop the config read): the 2 config tests fail again with `undefined`.
- Sabotage 2 (drop the watchdog guard from the retry/split policy): exactly the split-recovery test fails (1 failed / 22 passed).

## Verification

Each command run on its own in this worktree:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.retry.test.ts` → 1 file, 23 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` → 45 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` → 49 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` → 159 passed (help/label parity, tier coverage, curated leaf snapshot)
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --write` then `--check` → OK; config-surface budget ratcheted core 2421 → 2423
- `npx oxlint <changed files>` and `npx oxfmt --check <changed files>` → clean

Not exercised here: a live repro against real single-core llama.cpp hardware, and throughput-adaptive batch sizing (the third "and/or" in the report).

Fixes #144263

---

# PR #144488 — real embedding-client evidence: timeout → smaller-request recovery → indexing progress

Repo: `openclaw/openclaw`, worktree `D:/code/wt-oc-144263`, branch `fix/oc-144263-descr`.
Revisions: **after** = `b188dbae2b1` (PR head, clean tree); **before** = parent revision
`aec4f9b09b5` checked out for the PR's source files only (tests/docs stay at HEAD, per review scope).
Nothing was pushed and the PR was not modified; the worktree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) before and after.

## What PR #144488 changes (from `git diff aec4f9b09b5 HEAD`)

- `memory.search.embeddingTimeoutSeconds` is a new setting: strict zod schema + labels/help,
  per-agent override, wired through `resolveSyncConfig()` into `settings.sync.embeddingTimeoutSeconds`
  (`src/config/zod-schema.memory-search.ts`, `src/agents/memory-search.ts`, `schema.labels/help`).
- `resolveEmbeddingTimeoutMs()` now lets the operator budget win over provider-owned budgets for
  query **and** batch (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts`).
- Timeout errors name the request: `(provider=…, model=…, items=…)`.
- A watchdog timeout is treated as **splittable** (`isSplittableMemoryEmbeddingBatchError`) and is not
  retried unchanged (`resolveMemoryEmbeddingRetryBudget`) — the index halves the batch instead
  (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.ts`).

Before, the seam was dead: `resolveSyncConfig()` hardcoded `embeddingBatchTimeoutSeconds: undefined`,
timeouts fell back to the provider budget, and a timed-out batch matched the *retryable transport*
regex, so it was resent identically until the attempts budget ran out — the index stayed incomplete.

## Why this satisfies "real embedding-client trace"

The PR's own tests still drive the watchdog/splitter through a fake provider with `vi.useFakeTimers()`.
This run instead puts the **real** OpenAI-compatible embedding client
(`src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts`, real `fetch` over real sockets) in front of a
**local HTTP** OpenAI-compatible server, with **wall-clock** timers, and exercises the real
`embedBatchWithRetry` → real watchdog → real splitter → real `embedChunksInBatches` loop.

Server behaviour models a saturated single-core local embedding server: requests with > 2 items never
finish in time; requests with ≤ 2 items answer in ~50 ms. Operator setting under test: **1 s**.

```bash
  src/agents/memory-search.ts src/config/schema.help.models.ts \
  src/config/schema.labels.ts src/config/zod-schema.memory-search.ts
node "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\ocproof-144488.mjs" --side=before --timeout-seconds=1
git -C D:/code/wt-oc-144263 checkout HEAD -- \
  extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts \

  src/config/schema.labels.ts src/config/zod-schema.memory-search.ts
git -C D:/code/wt-oc-144263 status --porcelain                  # empty
```

The driver bundles the scenario with the checkout's own `esbuild` + `tsconfig` paths and prints the
per-file SHA-256 of the exercised sources, so each log identifies the revision it ran against.

`ocproof-144488.{before,after}.results.json`; scratch in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\ocproof-144488.tmp\`.

prs.title: fix(update): tolerate ENOTDIR in plugin code link targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` aborts the whole plugin capture when a plugin code link's target cannot be resolved because its path traverses a regular file, instead of recording that binding as unresolvable.

- Problem: `targetIdentity()` (`src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-code-links.ts:18`) maps "the target cannot be resolved" to `target: null`, exactly as its comment documents. A dangling link has two shapes — the target is absent (`ENOENT`), or its path traverses a regular file (`ENOTDIR`) — and the allowlist stopped at `ENOENT` and `ELOOP`, so `ENOTDIR` reached `throw error`. Both exported owners failed instead of recording the fact: `captureUpdateCandidatePluginCodeLink()` (line 34, via `onCodeLink` at `update-candidate-plugin-tree-links.ts:239`) and `assertUpdateCandidatePluginCodeLink()` (line 51, the doctor rehearsal check at `src/commands/doctor-update-rehearsal-paths.ts:64`, where raw `ENOTDIR` replaces its `Copied plugin code link changed` classification).
- Solution: add `ENOTDIR` to the errnos that mean "unresolvable target".
- Diff: one line — the allowlist becomes the canonical `["ENOENT", "ENOTDIR", "ELOOP"].some(...)` — plus a regression case folded into the existing `update-candidate-plugin-tree.test.ts` suite. Schema, `target: null` contract, rethrow for other errnos, both call sites and the update/doctor flows are unchanged; no new helper, no signature change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already settled this judgement: #190879 extended the same two-errno allowlist to `["ENOENT", "ENOTDIR", "ELOOP"].some(...)` at `src/infra/json-file.ts:28`, as did `src/commands/cleanup-utils.ts:349`. This sibling guard was never updated; kept inline like #190879, with no shared `errno.ts` owner.

Same defect shape as #191056 (`ignoreUnresolvedPluginLink`, the neighbouring helper) but independent — different file, function and contract (`target: null` vs `undefined`), zero diff overlap — and the two are *ordered*: in the store below the shipped update dies in the inventory stage, that PR's guard, before reaching this capture. `origin/main` (`0b36305eb71`) still carries both narrow allowlists; neither repair is superseded.

Risk is bounded: only `ENOTDIR` changes, from a hard failure to the documented `target: null`; `EACCES` and friends still propagate.

## User Impact

A plugin whose tree contains a code link pointing through a regular file — a replaced package directory, a stale alias from an earlier update, a partially swapped runtime tree — makes `openclaw update` fail during the plugin capture, and retrying cannot help because the link stays on disk. After this change the capture and the `openclaw doctor --fix` rehearsal handle it the way they already handle a dangling or looping link: recorded as unresolvable, capture continues, update proceeds.

## Evidence

Real `openclaw update` on a native Linux runner (GitHub Actions `ubuntu-24.04`, Node 24.22.1), from the **published latest stable** `2026.10.9` to the **published beta** `2026.10.10-beta.5`, through the shipped entry as `scripts/e2e/lib/plugin-update/corrupt-update-scenario.sh` uses it (`openclaw update --channel beta --tag <target> --yes --no-restart --timeout 1500 --json`). One plugin via `plugins.load.paths`, its `plugin-code-link` a symlink to `blocker/nested` with `blocker` a regular file — `realpath errno = ENOTDIR syscall = stat`.

Both arms carry #191056's traversal line (driver *and* staged target), so one line — this PR's — separates them:

```
RED  arm=paired-only, run 41453358607 — code chunk as published (ENOENT || ELOOP):
  update_exit=1 elapsed_s=141  status=failed  reason=candidate-snapshot-failed
    State snapshot failed (exit): ENOTDIR; after 0.975 seconds during plugin snapshot for $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
    ENOTDIR: not a directory, stat '$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/openclaw-update-canary-RIzF92/extensions/proof-plugin/plugin-code-link'
  enotdir_reported=6  inventory_stage_hits=0  capture_stage_hits=2
  installed_after=OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)  version_advanced=no
GREEN arm=paired-fix, run 41453372902 — same image, same store, this PR's line added:
  update_exit=0 elapsed_s=377  status=succeeded  60 steps completed, 2 skipped
  installed_after=OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.5 (7e15622)  version_advanced=yes
  enotdir_reported=0  capture_stage_hits=0
  settings_preserved=yes   # gateway port/mode/bind, plugins.load.paths, agents.defaults.workspace, logging.level
  state_fingerprint_before_sha=4c6299fc1e6866d1…  after_sha=4c6299fc1e6866d1…   # payload, marker, the link
  link_still_on_disk=blocker/nested   blocker_still_on_disk=yes
```

Stage label attributes the failure: without #191056's line the run dies in `plugin inventory`; widened, it reaches `plugin snapshot`, where the failing `stat` under `.update-captures/…canary-RIzF92` is `targetIdentity()`'s `realpathSync`. The driver is otherwise the published release (`dist/postinstall-content-inventory.json` recomputed). Rig: `gh workflow run plugin-code-link-enotdir.yml -f arm=paired-only|paired-fix` (private repo).

The regression case drives the exported owner over a real link, no mocks, each row asserting the errno Node actually reports before `target: null`; the ELOOP fixture is now a real cycle (`loop-a ↔ loop-b`), closing the duplicate-ELOOP finding:

```
Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 27 passed | 2 skipped (29)
# allowlist reverted to the shipped ["ENOENT", "ELOOP"]
× records a plugin code link whose target resolves with ENOTDIR as unresolvable
  Serialized Error: { errno: -20, code: 'ENOTDIR', syscall: 'stat', path: '/tmp/unresolved-code-link-XvtoL1/plugin-code-link' }
# ["ENOENT", "ENOTDIR"] — the ELOOP row guards ELOOP, not a second ENOENT
× records a plugin code link whose target resolves with ELOOP as unresolvable
  Serialized Error: { errno: -40, code: 'ELOOP', syscall: 'stat', path: '/tmp/unresolved-code-link-lzkXXP/plugin-code-link' }
```

`run-format.mts --check` and `oxlint` are clean on both files; typecheck is CI's — the changed expression already compiles at `src/infra/json-file.ts:28`.

prs.title: improve(backup): omit Codex diagnostics from restart checkpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local-companion restart checkpoints unnecessarily capture Codex’s changing diagnostic SQLite log database and its companions.

## User Impact

Local-companion capture omits only the activated Codex plugin’s managed agent-home `logs_2.sqlite` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`. Full backups and unrelated same-name files remain unchanged. Codex state, credentials, session rollouts, and other databases remain preserved. Omitted diagnostic history is not recovered; Codex recreates the log store.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep vendor policy in Codex manifest `backupResources` and add an optional generic `local-companion` profile selector to the existing planner. No global filename exclusion, extra policy owner, schema/version change, or template-exclusion option is introduced. Native backup safety and source-preservation behavior remain intact.

The native contract was inspected in [Codex 8f73cde](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4): `codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs:29,59-65,146-148,297-310` separates logs from durable databases and recreates missing stores with WAL; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/logs.rs:3-57` records bounded diagnostic/feedback history. OpenClaw’s managed-home owner is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:7-42`. Custom external Codex/sqlite homes are intentionally not inferred.

## Evidence

- Standalone head: `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`, directly parented by baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`. Mechanically separated from `1346e4f6f80911f634b77a212aead087089e1143`; no dependency on template-option commit `84f84f4e818851746b93a78e0a29bcf5b652bc8d`. Eleven files have byte-identical added/deleted lines; the remaining archive-create call only expands the baseline formatting to pass `localCompanion`.
- Fresh standalone proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-local-companion.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-backup-resources.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with a unique filesystem cache: **27 passed**, three files, **44.74s** including compiler preparation. Companion create/verify/restore test **237ms** (runner **7.67s**); plugin declaration runner **3.04s**; inventory runner **1.14s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Real archive creation, verification, and restore preserve diagnostic source bytes, state/auth/rollout bytes, a similarly named sibling, unrelated same-name database, client credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors while omitting declared diagnostics. Full-archive resource selection retains the diagnostics.
- Targeted `run-tsgo` passed for all eight changed TypeScript files and their import closure; `run-oxlint` passed all eight; formatter check passed eight TypeScript files and two docs; both docs passed MDX validation; Codex manifest JSON parsed and formatter stdin output was byte-identical; `git diff --check` passed.
- Reused original red proof: the same companion regression reached real restore and failed because `logs_2.sqlite` existed instead of returning `ENOENT`. Reused broader original lane proof: **73 passed, 1 Windows-only skipped**, **131.44s**. These are original reviewed-lane results, not new-head broad-suite results.
- Reused canonical autoreview: P0–P3, complete original local candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. That review included both independent original changes; this separation changes only context and removes the unrelated template change, so no substantive re-review was required. No claim of a new standalone autoreview run.
- Simplify: one profile conditional in the existing resource planner; no new vendor code in core or duplicate exclusion owner. Production TypeScript **+34/-6**, manifest **+24**, tests **+72/-3**, docs **+13**, allocation **+2**. The 69-line test allocation covers one archive/restore regression and independent metadata-profile admission/deduplication contracts.
- Earlier harness proof used a PostgreSQL discovery fixture. The additional exact-head compiled-CLI proof below uses real PostgreSQL and actual plugin discovery. No real-agent inference, upgrade, Windows or PostgreSQL-disconnection scenario is claimed.

## Main integration and refreshed validation

Integrated official main `2777468d26e5f21455b67591a045a40c770aee13` with an ordinary merge, preserving the original Codex head `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`. New head: `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`.

The two conflicts were additive option forwarding in `backup-shared.ts` and `backup-create.ts`. Both `localCompanion` and `excludeWorktreeTemplates` remain supported together. Registered template selection still belongs to the native registry, and exclusion precedence still belongs to the existing resource planner. No new policy owner, schema, version, or configuration option was introduced by this integration.

Fresh proof on the exact committed tree:

- **32 tests passed across four files**: combined companion/template archive creation, verification and restore; compiled CLI template/full backup behavior; native resource inventory; manifest admission and deduplication. Runner wall time **71.00s**, including worker preparation; shard wall times **29.62s / 1.17s / 3.26s**. The existing template CLI case took **5.411s**, and the companion case **0.246s**. CI seconds for this head are not yet available.
- Real lower-level planning discovers activated Codex metadata and registered templates together, omits both regenerable resources, and retains nested agent/credential owners. The archive-level test drives both options through real traversal/verification/restore and checks original source bytes. Its PostgreSQL discovery remains the existing explicit synthetic boundary; it is not fresh live-PostgreSQL proof.
- Two existing cases were extended, with no extra test case or product boot. A separate **36-line allocation** accounts exactly for this composition regression coverage; the original 69-line allocation and shared baseline remain unchanged.
- Targeted commands and infra typecheck leaves, lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent **P0–P3 review** of the complete candidate against the pinned main base completed **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings. The committed tree exactly matches the reviewed tree.

### Prior runtime proof remains correctly scoped

The real compiled-CLI/PostgreSQL 17.11 run remains evidence for original head `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`: all eight CLI invocations passed; ordinary full archives retained all four diagnostics, companion archives omitted them, and companion restore preserved durable Codex content, local credential data, and PostgreSQL anchor identity. This was not relabeled as a new-head execution.

The Codex manifest, manifest parser, activated-plugin discovery, PostgreSQL discovery adapter, archive verifier entrypoint, and restore module are byte-unchanged from that run. Incoming main adds template registry/resource plumbing and a template manifest option, plus an equivalent manifest-path expression and a remote-namespace error import relocation. This is not a claim that the whole runtime dependency closure is identical. Fresh combined tests cover the changed option/planning and archive/manifest surfaces. Existing runtime-proof limits remain: synthetic Codex payloads, no live Codex conversation or restored Gateway activation, and no separately severed-PostgreSQL test.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Additional runtime evidence

Exact candidate `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`: compiled CLI plus real PostgreSQL 17.11 completed eight CLI invocations, all exit 0, including Doctor, native database port, ordinary full backup, local-companion create, verification, and staged restore. Actual activated Codex manifest discovery omitted `logs_2.sqlite` and its WAL/SHM/journal companions from the companion archive; the ordinary full archive retained all four.

Restoration preserved Codex state, synthetic credentials and rollout bytes, a similarly named backup and an unrelated same-name file. PostgreSQL anchor/store/namespace, metadata and sentinel data were preserved. One E2E passed; fixture lint passed. Task containers and snapshot were positively confirmed absent. No production change.

Limits: synthetic Codex payloads, not a live Codex conversation. Shared PostgreSQL state was populated; other portable families were selected but unused. Full archive was inspected/verified, not restored. No restored Gateway activation or separately disconnected-PostgreSQL verification.

### Captured CLI output

Actual output with only fixture paths redacted; omitted fields marked.

— backup create --local-companion --verify (exit 0)
```text
  "localCompanion": true,
  "verified": true,
... (other fields omitted)
    {
      "kind": "plugin resource",
      "sourcePath": "<state-fixture>/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite",
      "displayPath": "$OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite",
      "reason": "regenerable"
    },
    {
      "kind": "plugin resource",
      "sourcePath": "<state-fixture>/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-journal",
      "displayPath": "$OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-journal",
      "reason": "regenerable"
    },
    {
      "kind": "plugin resource",
      "sourcePath": "<state-fixture>/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-shm",
      "displayPath": "$OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-shm",
      "reason": "regenerable"
    },
    {
      "kind": "plugin resource",
      "sourcePath": "<state-fixture>/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-wal",
      "displayPath": "$OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite-wal",
      "reason": "regenerable"
    },
```

## Investigated UI CI failure and bounded replay

The original [UI E2E failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41422704713/job/125202451410) remains unresolved: Chromium reported `keyboard.press: Target crashed` in `new-session-page.responsive-welcome.e2e.test.ts:165`, “keeps phone setup compact with 2 agents.” The job displayed 5/7, but its recorded command executed shard **5/6 with four workers**. Its executed merge was `acc670a76cf53736398652c6314380472de9427a` (main parent `419d0c53118045c5a48e80c6743454f2726c67fd`, this PR head `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`). Retained original artifacts contained only progress metadata, not a renderer crash dump. Zero recorded cgroup OOM events do not identify another cause.

After the earlier four-file Node 26 replay passed, a bounded [full historical-shard diagnostic replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554166719) on November 3 used **Node 24.22.1**, pinned pnpm 12.15.0 / Vitest 5.0.5 / Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4, four actual CPUs, and the native sequencer's exact **138 original project/file members from 834 include patterns**. Historical application/test inputs and assertions were preserved; a reviewed task-only context-lifecycle/CDP observer overlay was added.

- **138 files and 537 tests passed**, zero unhandled errors, **467.59s**. The former failing two-agent case passed in 5.665s; all seven responsive-welcome cases passed.
- Verified replay source tree: `65e183652ffd319ad7802d6958ce8166384d87b7`; transport carrier: `b9442fbd081b934b18bd72e90813a9abb3f5ea9f`. These identify the instrumented historical merge, not a new PR commit.
- The observer armed before application execution, recorded 1,602 target-created and 1,602 target-destroyed events, and recorded **zero renderer-crash events**. No crash status/error code exists to infer. The flush barrier completed; observer and browser exited 0; the journal closed.
- Test, payload and wrapper exits were 0. Artifacts were downloaded and hash-verified before exact lease teardown; final remote settlement is complete. The backing Actions run's cancellation is normal one-shot Testbox cleanup, not the test result.
- Retained private evidence archive SHA-256: `10ab66b6143954501e591e132a9a11017963561203e8dab0780145b73c6ae2e9`; 40-file evidence manifest SHA-256: `ba49cfb5ecfc3fc9448ee1b38be8dd4fac5818a5fc4e64ad420e7647b15097fe`.

**Interpretation:** the original renderer failure was not reproduced, not fixed or classified as infrastructure/inherited. Original cache contents, concurrent interleaving, cgroup scope and the diagnostic overlay differ. This replay does **not** replace current-head PR CI or clear its failed gate. No product repair, CI rerun, weakened assertion, timeout extension or repeated replay is claimed.

prs.title: docs(workboard): document card field limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Workboard "Card fields" table describes `labels` only as "free-form strings", so users do not learn that each label is capped at 40 characters or that labels beyond the first 12 are dropped without an error; title, notes, `parents`, and `skills` limits are not documented either.

## User Impact

User impact: operators and agents writing cards can see the enforced limits up front instead of discovering them through a failed create or a silently shortened label list. No behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The table now lists the limits the Workboard store already enforces: `title` up to 180 characters (required), `notes` up to 4000, labels up to 40 characters each with only the first 12 distinct labels kept, and up to 20 entries for `parents` (120 characters each) and `skills` (80 characters each) on card creation. Only `docs/plugins/workboard.md` changes; translations are generated elsewhere.

Question for maintainers: should more than 12 labels be rejected like the other caps instead of being shortened silently? This PR only documents the current behavior.

## Evidence

Values are taken from the validators (`normalizeTitle`, `normalizeNotes` and `normalizeStringList` in `extensions/workboard/src/store-normalizers.ts`, `normalizeCappedStringList` in `extensions/workboard/src/store-string-lists.ts`) and checked live against an isolated test Gateway built from this branch (`2a8d393b9be`, on top of `cff88c2d21d`, own state directory, loopback port, 2026-10-14 17:06–17:08 UTC):

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| label with 40 characters | card created, label stored (40 chars), rc 0 |
| label with 41 characters | rejected: `labels must be 40 characters or fewer.`, rc 1 |
| 13 labels `l01…l13` | card created, 12 labels stored (`l13` dropped), rc 0 |
| labels `x,x,y` | card created with `["x","y"]` |
| title with 180 / 181 characters | created / `title must be 180 characters or fewer.` |
| notes with 4000 / 4001 characters | created / `notes must be 4000 characters or fewer.` |
| `skills`: 20 entries / 21 entries | created / `skills supports at most 20 entries.` |
| `skills`: entry with 80 / 81 characters | created / `skills must be 80 characters or fewer (got 81).` |
| `parents`: 21 entries | `parents supports at most 20 entries.` |
| `parents`: entry with 121 characters | `parents must be 120 characters or fewer (got 121).` |

Labels, title, and notes were created with `openclaw workboard create`; `skills` and `parents` with `openclaw gateway call workboard.cards.create`.

Docs checks on this branch (VPS, Node 24.21.0): `pnpm format:docs:check` (48 s), `pnpm lint:docs` (23 s, 0 issues), `pnpm docs:check-mdx` (18 s), `pnpm docs:check-links` (23 s, 0 broken), `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` (9 s), `pnpm lint:templates`, `pnpm changelog:check`, `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary`: all pass. `oxfmt --check docs/plugins/workboard.md` passes.

<details>
<summary>Unrelated failures in optional docs checks</summary>

`pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports two missing fragments in other pages (`gateway/config-tools.md:60`, `releases/2026.10.1.md:849`), and `pnpm docs:spellcheck` reports words in `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime/hooks.md` and `docs/channels/x.md`. Neither touches this change.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep background work visible while chat waits
prs.body:
Related: #182684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

## User Impact

The existing compact footer keeps its claw, elapsed time, and separate subagent/command counts visible, including in bubble mode. Counts open the existing Subagents and Processes panels. Detached services do not keep an idle conversation looking busy, and unavailable command observations are labeled rather than presented as zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the selected minimal-footer design without restoring the removed delegation tracker or per-worker narration. Command classification comes from the execution owner's retained request ownership, not command-name or output heuristics. The visible conversation shares the existing process observation with the panels.

Counts cover reconnectable background exec processes, not every foreground tool or OS process. Truncated inventories show a lower bound with "+". Older workers lacking ownership metadata remain inspectable in Processes but do not acquire an inferred busy signal. No execution, cancellation, retention, or permission behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Missing-claw regression fails on the original in flat and bubble modes and passes with the fix.
- Producer regression fails on the original and passes with task-owned, explicitly detached, unknown-owner, and terminal command cases.
- 60 focused UI tests and 7 producer tests pass. Production UI and affected chat-test typechecks pass; scoped lint, styles, controller guards, and formatting pass.
- Five browser flows pass, covering subagent waiting/resumption, one and 12 workers, command-only work, detached services, unavailable reads, reconnect, completion, and existing panel navigation. Deterministic Gateway fixtures exercise the actual running Control UI; the producer regression exercises real ownership with external process I/O fixed.
- [Inspected before/after screenshots and the command-only state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185241#issuecomment-6430583591), embedded in the linked proof comment. The representative before/after pair was also delivered in the originating chat.

Focused UI proof took 15.45 seconds of Vitest time / 25.06 seconds wall; browser proof took 81.28 seconds including its production build. Producer proof took 71.97 seconds wall, mostly compiled-worker preparation; its new regression took 465 ms. CI timing is pending.

Initial broad ui/tsconfig.json validation also reported existing unrelated native-desktop and quota-diagnostics test errors; the proper production UI and scoped chat-test lanes pass. No claim of a passing broad test typecheck is made.

Independent review found a reconnect uncertainty bug in the first candidate; it was repaired and added to the browser regression. The final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Prompt indexing and row-content dependency computation were moved intact to their existing owners to respect the projection module's line limit. No new process manager or polling loop is introduced. The publisher's metadata-only commit has the same source tree as the tested and reviewed candidate.

Worked on by: @steipete

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d56dcb22-4fa6-4e67-9e48-b268811190ee)

prs.title: fix(update): tolerate ENOTDIR when resolving plugin links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` aborts the whole plugin-tree capture when a recorded plugin link resolves through a regular file, instead of skipping that one link.

- Two guards decide "this plugin link cannot be resolved", and both stopped at `ENOENT`/`ELOOP`:
  - `ignoreUnresolvedPluginLink` (`src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-tree-links.ts:22`) — every link read during inventory (`:117`, `update-candidate-plugin-tree.ts:203`, `:342`, `:369`);
  - `targetIdentity` (`src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-code-links.ts:26`) — copied-link identity recording, which the shipped candidate copy performs: `src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts:715` passes `onCodeLink` into `verifyUpdateCandidatePluginTree`, so every copied symlink goes through `captureUpdateCandidatePluginCodeLink`.
- Those are not the only ways a link fails to resolve: when an intermediate component of a target is a regular file, the kernel reports `ENOTDIR`. Measured here: `ln -s ./blocker/nested link` with `blocker` a regular file → `realpathSync`/`statSync` `ENOTDIR`, `readlinkSync` ok. Both guards rethrew it, so one unresolvable link failed the update — at inventory, and with only the inventory guard widened, at the copy/identity stage.
- Fix: accept `ENOTDIR` in both guards (one line each, in the canonical form), plus one regression that follows the same link through inventory, private candidate copy, and identity recording.
- Unchanged: the contract for every other errno (`EACCES` still propagates), the inventory call sites, the nullable `target` already used for dangling links (no schema change), and the update flow. No new helper, no signature change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository already treats "this link cannot be resolved" as exactly those three errnos — `["ENOENT", "ENOTDIR", "ELOOP"].some((code) => hasNodeErrorCode(error, code))` at `src/infra/json-file.ts:28` (`loadJsonFileThroughSymlink`, extended to `ENOTDIR` by #190879), `src/infra/update-capture-paths.ts:94`, `src/commands/cleanup-utils.ts:349`. Grepping the update family leaves only these two link-classification guards this narrow (the others are path-absence guards on locators, which must stay loud), which is why the repair covers both: otherwise the reported failure merely moves from inventory to copied-link verification. I did not add a shared `isUnresolvableLinkError` owner to `src/infra/errno.ts` — the family is small and #190879 landed the same judgement inline.

Behavior changes only for `ENOTDIR`, and it becomes what the guards already do for a dangling or looping link: inventory falls back to the recorded target or skips the entry, and identity records the binding as unresolvable (`target: null`). That stays detectable — `assertUpdateCandidatePluginCodeLink` recomputes `targetIdentity` and compares, so a link that later becomes reachable is still reported as `Copied plugin code link changed` — and the escape check `assertUpdateCandidatePluginLinkTarget` still runs before capture, so a link resolving outside the private state root is still refused.

## User Impact

A plugin tree with a link whose target path traverses a regular file — a plugin directory replaced by a file, a stale `node_modules` alias recorded by a previous update, a partially swapped runtime tree — currently makes `openclaw update` fail hard, and no retry clears it because the bad link stays on disk. The capture now tolerates that link the way it tolerates a dangling or looping one, and the update continues; `ENOENT`/`ELOOP` handling is unchanged and other errnos still fail loudly.

## Evidence

Regression through the production boundary (`src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-tree.test.ts`): `fixture()` now passes `onCodeLink` into `copyUpdateCandidatePluginTrees`, so each row creates the link shape in the source tree, pins the errno `realpathSync` really reports, and asserts the copy records exactly one unresolvable binding — its copied path and its stored link.

RED — each row against the guard that owns it, one revert at a time:

| reverted | failing row | where it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| both guards (pinned `origin/main`) | `ENOTDIR` | inventory: `ENOTDIR, realpath '…/source/plugin-link'` |
| `targetIdentity` only | `ENOTDIR` | copied-link identity: `ENOTDIR, stat '…/snapshot/plugin/plugin-link'` |
| `ELOOP` dropped from both | `ELOOP` | inventory: `ELOOP, realpath '…/source/plugin-link'` |

The third row is why the loop fixture self-references (`plugin-link -> plugin-link`): a chain to an absent file reports `ENOENT` and stays green with `ELOOP` handling removed.

GREEN: `Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 48 passed | 3 skipped (51)` across `update-candidate-plugin-tree.test.ts`, `update-candidate-plugin-tree.scale.test.ts`, `update-candidate-state.test.ts`.

Raw terminal output — real temp filesystem, no mocks, driving the shipped functions the candidate copy uses (`prepareUpdateCandidatePluginTrees` → `copyUpdateCandidatePluginTrees` with `onCodeLink` → `assertUpdateCandidatePluginCodeLink`) with `blocker` (regular file) + `plugin-link -> blocker/nested`:

```
# widened guards (this PR)
[shape] realpath errno=ENOTDIR syscall=stat
[inventory] OK entries=directory:source,file:blocker,file:payload.txt,symlink:plugin-link
[copy] OK copied-link facts=1
[identity] link=plugin-link -> blocker/nested target=null
[recheck] every recorded binding still matches the copied tree
[result] update candidate plugin capture completed; stored link bytes=inventoried plugin bytes
# inventory guard widened only
Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, stat '/tmp/pr191056-proof-ZXglBP/snapshot/plugin/plugin-link'
# both guards as shipped today (main)
Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, realpath '/tmp/pr191056-proof-ulhIJR/source/plugin-link'
```

Static checks: format `run-format.mts --check` clean; `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on the changed files → 0 warnings/0 errors; ratchet → `Test lines OK: 6394197; ceiling: 6404307`. Typecheck runs in CI (`check-prod-types`); both changed expressions are byte-for-byte the form already compiling at `src/infra/json-file.ts:28`.

## Maintainer verification

The reviewed three-file product change is preserved in signed head `c16c9844024491270c312efe63a342c305aafb5e`. This integrates pinned main `bf35e054b0062c64e5577b165a3ae629adc3d2d0`, including the existing PostgreSQL orphan-inventory isolation repair [e68dfaf78a587](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e68dfaf78a587b8be63168e397fc52290ea3eff0) (#190918). The previous [PostgreSQL conformance failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41446017953/job/125280113776) lost a sibling restore namespace between the before/after inventories; the integrated main repair places that suite in its own database. No timeout or assertion was relaxed, and no new unrelated repair was added.

Fresh Codex autoreview covered the complete product delta and full owning source/tests at tree `10978c20b2a40cdcfbb671fab9b39d42fd996f4b`: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. That exact tree is the signed head above. Runtime proof comes from exact-head PR CI; no local contributor code was executed. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41549657762) completed successfully at `c16c9844024491270c312efe63a342c305aafb5e`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. The [combined gate and security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552691329) also succeeded. Final observation: 62 passing checks, 56 planned skips, zero failing, cancelled, or pending checks.

Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the fix and regression.

prs.title: feat: configure chat attachment file and message size limits
prs.body:
Related: #166757

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot configure incoming chat document size limits independently of media processing budgets.

## User Impact

The new attachment controls are **additional to**, not a replacement for, the existing media option:

- `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb` stays available and active for incoming **images, audio, and video only**. It does not cap PDFs, text, archives, or other documents. Media files must satisfy both the media cap and the general attachment cap; documents use only the attachment caps.

- `attachments.maxFileMb` — **Maximum attachment size**, default 20 MiB per file.
- `attachments.maxTotalMb` — **Maximum total attachment size per message**, default the larger of 20 MiB and the per-file cap.
- All incoming chat files, including media and duplicate entries, count toward the decoded total. The server rejects an oversized batch before attachment preparation/storage.
- Doctor preserves the old inherited file cap when the new field is absent, retaining explicit attachment settings, media settings, and retention.

The approximately 18.56 MiB WebSocket decoded batch ceiling remains. This does not add streaming uploads or change every channel/outbound document contract. **Not release-qualified:** installed latest-stable upgrade and external live-model proof remain unrun. A real isolated Gateway/agent flow with a deterministic provider now passes.

For example: with media set to 5 MiB, per-file attachments to 10 MiB, and the message total to 15 MiB, an 8 MiB PDF is permitted but an 8 MiB video is rejected. Two 8 MiB PDFs exceed the total. Classification is based on sniffed content, not merely the filename or supplied MIME type.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends the existing attachment policy/parser and config schema rather than adding a second upload owner. Chat, session, agent/node, companion, worker-transfer, handshake and Control UI consumers use the separate budgets. New labels/help expose the actual scope and MiB units; retention is unchanged.

Simplification retained one policy owner, one batch preflight and the existing Doctor writer, with no new transport, persistence system, or permanent document-limit fallback to mediaMaxMb.

## Evidence

### Follow-up conflict refresh — November 3 (head `e31bf2773ba5`)

- Current-head selected CI completed successfully at 00:47 UTC: [CI gate job 125652907801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552445624/job/125652907801), run `41552445624`, head `e31bf2773ba579da160c6bcd4e60e807f88a8279`. Its complete log records success for every selected group, including PostgreSQL conformance; `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false` and `ALLOW_COALESCED_IOS=false`. Unselected/skipped groups are not claimed as executed proof.
- The previous head `6f4c9d372a84` passed its full selected CI gate, as linked below. Main then advanced and produced new conflicts, so that CI result remains prior-head evidence rather than being relabeled as current-head CI.
- Integrated main at `941f173975b3b43f7367c14f495ff61040af6469` without rewriting existing PR history. Again, the only textual conflicts were the generated config-baseline counts/hashes; canonical generation and verification both pass. Core count 2587 is base 2585 plus the two attachment fields; channel/plugin counts remain 4003/4938.
- All feature production and test blobs are unchanged from the previously reviewed/tested tree. The only other original PR paths changed by integration are upstream handshake documentation and wrapper-inventory additions. Upstream config IO changed, so all 43 selected Doctor migration/safety tests were rerun and passed, along with the Doctor test typecheck and diff checks.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the complete candidate against that exact base returned scoped-clean through P2. This conflict repair adds no production or test machinery.
- Published tree `e4e84822d4c779cac841abbbaf06368380bc62ba` exactly matches the reviewed/tested index tree. The final 38-file PR delta contains no task cache artifacts; all introduced commit credits were checked.
- GitHub reported this head as conflict-free at publication. Its selected CI result is verified above; final applicable security/review qualification remains separate. The installed latest-stable upgrade and external live-model proof gaps remain open; no merge or 6/6 claim is made.

### Conflict refresh — November 2 (head `6f4c9d372a84`)

- Current-head CI subsequently completed successfully: [CI gate job 125631681732](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41546086136/job/125631681732), run `41546086136`, head `6f4c9d372a84d5a5feb098fe800fb33a11762c06`, completed November 2 at 23:55 UTC. Its complete log records success for every selected job group, with `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false`; skipped groups remain skipped, not executed proof. Current-head CI-gate, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses also read back as passing. The bounded PR checks list is truncated, so its partial counts are not used as a complete inventory.

The result retains the two attachment options (core 2586 versus base 2584), the existing media option, and upstream channel/plugin surfaces (4003/4938). No handwritten hash resolution or policy exception.
- All eight selected attachment parser/policy, MIME, client admission/video, and Doctor migration/safety test files passed on this refreshed candidate. Doctor and UI E2E test typechecks and diff checks passed.
- Independent Auto Review of the complete candidate against that exact base returned scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. Simplification added no new production or test machinery for this repair.

A document larger than the media cap is accepted, appears in history, and its original bytes are retained. The standard runtime build and test command completed successfully.

The regression failed before adding this migration to the existing automatic-repair admission, then passed with exact original backup, retained media/TTL, and second-run idempotence. ### Media-only correction

- Image/audio/video cap regressions failed on the previous implementation and passed after restoring `mediaMaxMb` as a media-only admission constraint. A document above that cap still passes its independent attachment limits.
- 98 focused tests passed: parser/policy (51), MIME sniffing (5), client admission/video preparation (42), including worker-backed preparation and accepted noncanonical Base64 padding.
- Core/UI production typechecks, Gateway root/method test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and 3 changed-doc MDX checks passed. Protocol and native projections regenerated through their owners.
- Independent review identified only the stale staged policy; staged content was updated to the reviewed working-tree correction and verified. No other actionable P0–P2 issue was reported.
- These changes affect limit enforcement/preflight, not settings layout; existing rendered-control evidence remains below.
- Prior-head CI failures in `check-test-types-core-1` and `checks-node-compact-small-1` were subsequently diagnosed from Actions job logs and repaired as described above.

### Earlier implementation evidence

- New mixed-batch and duplicate-file aggregate regressions failed on the original parser and passed with the implementation.
- Focused parser/policy, migration/schema, chat admission/staging, node, worker transfer, UI admission and reload tests passed on the original implementation candidate.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, docs MDX/link/config-example checks passed on that candidate. Protocol/native artifacts and config-doc baselines were regenerated through their owners.
- Independent Auto Review found no actionable P0–P2 findings on the original candidate.
- Integrated main at `f2f8500facc1eb80a7bc68e8335133675c32b17f`, preserved its newer deferred-staging/cancellation owner, and regenerated config baselines. Refreshed-base migration tests (6), parser/policy/chat-admission tests (56), and rendered settings E2E (1) passed; reconciled core/UI typechecks and targeted lint passed. Earlier node/worker/UI-admission/reload results remain prior-base evidence. Those results are evidence for that earlier head, not the latest correction's CI.
- Public screenshot URLs were fetched without authentication and their SHA-256 digests matched the inspected images.
- Rendered Control UI browser test verified both numeric values are saved to the correct config keys. Screenshots below use the real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway response, not a live-model claim.

### Before

prs.title: fix(ios): chat screen ignores every tap while reconnecting to an unreachable gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the iPhone chat screen ignores every tap when the app keeps retrying a saved gateway that no longer answers. Closes #191449 ## User Impact User impact: while the app is stuck on "Connecting", you can still open the sidebar, tap the status chip, or go to Chat actions > Gateway settings to rescan or change the gateway address. Before this, the only ways out were getting the old address to answer again or reinstalling the app. ## Why This Change Was Made The chat tab applied its gateway handoff guard (`.disabled(isGatewayTransitionPending)`) to its whole content, toolbar included. An automatic reconnect counts as a pending handoff for as long as its preflight keeps retrying, and against an unreachable host that retry never ends (the backoff caps at 30 s). So every control that could fix the connection got disabled along with the chat. The guard now covers only the chat surface and the actions that write through the chat owner: New chat in worktree, New session options (button and sheet), and the model controls. The toolbar stays enabled. That matches the persistent sidebar layout, where the sidebar sits outside this view and already works during a handoff. One thing I left alone: during that same retry the composer stays disabled too, even though its placeholder says "sends when connected". Whether an automatic retry to the same gateway should count as a handoff at all seems like a controller call, so I'll leave that to you.
Trace - `ChatProTab.body` applied `.disabled(self.isGatewayTransitionPending)` to `content`, which carries `.toolbar { ... }`. - `isGatewayTransitionPending` includes `GatewayConnectionController.hasPendingConnectionHandoff`, which is true while `pendingAutoConnectGeneration != nil`. - `startAutoConnect` with `userInitiated: false` awaits `prepareGatewayIngress`, which loops on recoverable network errors (`while true`, backoff starting at 1 s and doubling to 30 s). The generation only clears when that task ends. - That retry only runs while no gateway config is active (`canRetryAutomatically` checks `activeGatewayConnectConfig == nil`). So it shows up on a cold launch against a saved gateway that no longer answers. - The existing test `automatic preflight retries without gaining browser authority` already shows the pending state staying true across a retry delay.
## Evidence - I hit this on iOS app 2026.10.50 with Gateway 2026.10.8 over `wss` with a pinned self-signed certificate. After the gateway host's DHCP address changed, chat sat on "Connecting" with a "Disconnected / not connected" banner, and nothing on screen responded. - New UI test `GatewayConnectionStateUITests.testToolbarStaysUsableWhileReconnectingToUnreachableGateway` saves a manual gateway at `192.0.2.10` (TEST-NET-1, so it never answers) and waits for "Gateway: Connecting". It checks that the composer is still disabled, that Show Sidebar, the status chip, and Chat actions are enabled, and that Chat actions opens Gateway settings. Against `main`'s `ChatProTab.swift` it fails with 4 failures (all three controls disabled, and Gateway settings never shows up). On this branch it passes. - A hosted test in `ChatTypingFocusTests` can't see SwiftUI toolbar items (no accessibility elements, and `isEnabled` is always true), so I went with a UI test. - CI won't run it, since the iOS lanes only run listed UI tests. Happy to add it to one of those lists if you want it there. To run it locally: ``` xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=' -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/GatewayConnectionStateUITests/testToolbarStaysUsableWhileReconnectingToUnreachableGateway ``` - On Xcode 27.2 with the iOS 27.2 simulator, the app builds and `ChatTypingFocusTests` passes (5 tests). `RootTabsSourceGuardTests` and `OpenClawTypographyTests` passed too (28 tests in 3 suites), on a run before I dropped my earlier source-text test. - SwiftFormat flagged the indent on two comment lines in `ChatProTab.swift`, so that fix is a separate style commit. - Local review: I couldn't run the autoreview helper in my setup, so I had the diff reviewed separately. No P0 or P1 findings. The one P2 was about that earlier source-text test, which the UI test replaces. Before (`main`): stuck on "Disconnected", and nothing on screen responds. After (this branch): while the app keeps retrying, Chat actions opens and Gateway settings is available.

prs.title: fix: stop completed session writes retaining request data
prs.body:
Related: #184512 and #184513. This is the separately reproduced lifetime prerequisite; invitation activation remains scoped to #184515.

## What Problem This Solves

Completed SQLite session requests can retain callbacks and captured input after their work ends.

## User Impact

Completed requests release their captures while reusable workers remain available. Accepted runs retain the caller’s live authorization, cancellation and settlement custody. Stored data, configuration and SDK-facing contracts are unchanged; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release ended writer borrows and finished callback, context and cursor bindings without discarding committed facts, receipts, attachments or cleanup failures. Persistent generation, retirement-reader and client callbacks capture their narrow owner instead of the initiating request.

Allocate only the MessageChannel carrier outside the request context, then restore the original captured owner for event and synchronous delivery. Transfer canonical sharing assertions through the existing retained operator lifetime, including final-reference and failed-handoff cleanup. No new manager, cache, schema, role grant or raised ceiling.

## Evidence

- Untouched pinned main d934b070 reproduces nine GC assertions. Counterfactual Node tests distinguish carrier collection from correct original-owner delivery; accepted writes and post-await refusal remain required.
- Source-bound qualification passed 29 Node suites / 374 tests and five pinned-Bun suites / 66 tests. The retained-sharing qualification passed 323 Node tests and 26 pinned-Bun tests; valid completed results were explicitly reused across recovery, not presented as newly rerun suites.
- Integration with main 94e2e06b passed all static gates and six targeted Node suites / 63 tests, including both RPC entry points, queued handoff, prefix stability and the three immutable Gateway replay cases. Generated inventory was regenerated through its owner; all tracked source entries were verified.
- Fresh exact-head AWS proof (b4688e2e vs94e2e06b): both clean full builds and all static gates passed; 14 owner suites / 178 tests and all three head Gateway cases passed, zero pending. The fresh base retained only the two designated regression failures as strict negative controls—not a green base or CI exception. Evidence packaging was recovered by complete copy/hash verification without rerunning tests.
- Independent local Codex autoreview of the final integrated range was scoped-clean at P0–P2 in all six passes, fallback and web search disabled; the published b4688e2e tree is byte-identical to the reviewed and scoped-qualified source. Earlier original lifetime and Node correction reviews remain recorded for their unchanged inputs.
- Exact-head CI [41551637161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551637161) succeeded on attempt 1; the native rollup watcher returned GREEN. The [current-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191197#issuecomment-6581537041) completed with no findings. No CI exception, approval submission or rerun was used.

Gateway proof uses authenticated synthetic participants, deterministic provider HTTP replay, existing membership RPCs and awaited close/start on the same files/configuration. It is not live inference, public invitation activation, or cold-process/crash durability.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only relay Talk sessions stay untitled after the user speaks
prs.body:
Fixes #191531

## What Problem This Solves

A fresh voice-only Talk session remains untitled when realtime voice runs over the Gateway relay. Direct/client-owned Talk already schedules automatic titles after committed user speech (#190613), but the relay writer bypasses that helper.

## User Impact

Eligible relay Talk sessions now receive the same automatic title from the first usable spoken task. Existing titles are preserved, ineligible session keys remain unchanged, and direct Talk retains its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing private Talk transcript/title helper with the existing relay append operation and retained writer. The helper captures the session identity, commits the transcript, then schedules the existing background title policy. Client/native callers keep their default append operation. No new title owner, public SDK API, configuration, retry policy or migration.

prs.title: fix(telegram): compaction notices never reach the chat in progress streaming mode
prs.body:
Closes #191515

## What problem this solves

Telegram's default `streaming.mode: "progress"` holds ordinary answer-lane blocks until the final reply. Existing compaction notice blocks were held too, then replaced by the final; merely exempting the hold would still put notices into the progress card that is deleted afterward.

## Change and user impact

In progress mode only, deliver `isCompactionNotice` block payloads as standalone messages through the existing sender. No new text, API, default, opt-in or global normalization. Routine start/completion notices remain governed by existing `compaction.notifyUser`; warnings already emitted by core use the same flagged path. Non-progress delivery remains unchanged.

Contributor masatohoshino's original commit is retained. The added regression was folded into the existing compaction lifecycle case without dropping its ordered phase, final acceptance or card-retirement assertions. Test-line delta against main: **+7/-10 = -3**. Production change: the original 11 added lines.

Accepted existing behavior: a delivered notice counts as a visible reply even if no answer follows, matching mode off rather than emitting an empty-reply fallback.

## Evidence

Head: `6dd9b0c0737f53d0e8e39eba99a667ecd1d82e6f`. Main baseline: `535cf43388e7d4b63e1c14754e1fa84a40889136`.

[Sanitized real Telegram Test Server userbot evidence, timelines, controls, isolation and release receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191516#issuecomment-6592022379).

Built Gateway in official node:24.22.1 Docker, actual Telegram Test Server Bot API + TDLib userbot, Convex-leased credentials, deterministic localhost OpenAI-compatible provider. Two seed turns followed by a real context-overflow HTTP error drive core's natural compaction summary and pending-turn retry. The provider does not emit compaction notices.

- Main progress mode twice: neither standalone notice; one final answer and native progress-card deletion per run.
- Exact head progress mode twice: existing start + completion notices before the single final, with both notice IDs surviving native progress-card deletion.
- Non-progress (`off`) main/head controls: unchanged two notices and single final.
- All six fresh Gateways shut down cleanly. All leases released; private payload and restored credential scratch checked absent. No paid provider or personal Gateway.

Focused checks: 20/20 lifecycle HTTP tests pass; the consolidated regression fails on main because the notice is absent. Focused oxfmt and oxlint pass; both builds pass. Broader checks are left to PR CI.

## Boundaries

Core logged completed compaction without token reduction; token reduction is not claimed. Runtime proof exercises routine start/completion notices, not degraded/context-bounded warning text; the existing degraded notice payload is covered by the consolidated HTTP regression together with ordinary interim-prose suppression. Partial and block modes were not exercised or changed. This is native message/lifecycle evidence, not a Telegram visual/screenshot claim.

The contributor's earlier fake Bot API proof is superseded by the real Test Server proof above. Two initial native setup captures with fixture request-classification errors are retained and excluded; the accepted six-case matrix uses one corrected fixture. The proof-only runner loader handles lease ownership and isolated profiles only, and its NODE_OPTIONS is stripped from the Gateway child; no product runtime preload or source injection.

prs.title: fix(android): place terminal question summaries in transcript order
prs.body:
Fixes #186494

## What Problem This Solves

On Android, a terminal question card (answered, answered elsewhere, expired, cancelled, or unavailable secret/API prompt) stays pinned in the composer dock above the composer. `/reset` shows "Session reset" in the timeline but does not clear those cards; only force-stopping the app removes them.

- Problem: `PreparedChatHistory.buildTimeline` appends every `questions` entry at the reverse-layout bottom (the composer dock) regardless of status, and `clearQuestions()` is not wired to session reset.
- Solution: only `Pending` / `Submitting` prompts own the dock via `ChatQuestionPrompt.isLiveDockPrompt()`; terminal prompts insert into the timeline by `createdAtMs` relative to message and divider timestamps.
- Changed: `ChatQuestion.kt`, `ChatTimeline.kt` (`SystemDivider.timestampMs`, ordered terminal flush), and `ChatTimelineTest.kt` regressions for newer-message ordering and session reset.
- Not changed: live prompt behavior, draft/secret clearing, gateway question lifecycle, or non-Android clients.

## User Impact

Expired or already-answered secret prompts no longer stick above the composer after the turn or after `/reset`. Pending and submitting prompts still dock so the user can answer them. Retained terminal summaries stay in the transcript at the point they belonged, instead of floating as stale cards over new messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #186494 reproduces on a real device: an expired `secrets request` card remains after `/reset` and only a force-stop clears it. Root cause is unconditional bottom docking of all questions plus reset not applying `clearQuestions()` on the main timeline. Placing terminal cards by time matches how the timeline already orders messages and reset/compaction dividers, so the fix needs no new reset side channel and keeps one owner for question dock policy (`isLiveDockPrompt`).

## Evidence

- Local: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` (worktree base `2d8b054eab1`, Node 26.12.1, Android SDK 37.0) — BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
  - `ChatTimelineTest` 25/25 failures=0 errors=0, including new:
    - `terminalQuestionPlaysBesideNewerMessagesInsteadOfDocking`
    - `sessionResetLeavesAnsweredSummaryAboveDividerNotInDock`
  - `ChatQuestionTest` 39/0, `ChatQuestionDraftLayoutTest` (bundled in same run), `ChatWorkedSummaryTest` 24/0, `ChatReaderScrollControllerTest` 23/0, `SidebarAttentionTest` green after prefetching Robolectric `android-all-instrumented` jars (earlier `initializationError` was maven fetch, not assertions).
- Red on base (by construction): base `buildTimeline` always docks every question at index 0; without `isLiveDockPrompt` / timestamp insert the two new assertions cannot hold.
- Scope: 3 files, +169 / −6; no protocol/schema/config changes.
- No device screen recording in this PR; pure timeline-order unit coverage is the cheap real entry for this layout bug. Real-Gateway e2e is not run on PRs (`run_ui_real_gateway=!isPr`).

## Merge Danger

- Reverse-layout index 0 remains the live dock edge; only `Pending`/`Submitting` stay there. If a future status is added and forgets `isLiveDockPrompt`, it would fall into the terminal path (timeline insert) rather than the dock.
- Terminal flush uses message/divider `timestampMs`; rows without a timestamp skip the flush for that row and any leftover terminal prompts land at the oldest end after the loop — acceptable for missing-clock rows, could mis-order if timestamps are non-monotonic.
- Does not clear question state on Gateway `/reset`; it only stops presenting terminal cards in the dock. Full `clearQuestions()` wiring remains a possible follow-up if retained summaries should also disappear from the transcript after reset.

prs.title: fix(onboard): Quick start disappears after Ctrl-C during a first run
prs.body:
Closes #191549
Related: #191454

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the rerun after a cancelled first run skips Quick start and continues in Custom setup.

## User Impact

User impact: someone who presses Ctrl-C early in Quick start gets the same **How would you like to start?** choice on the next `openclaw` run. Installs with authored config are still treated as configured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two things made an unfinished install look configured: the session catalog opt-out the config writer stamps on its first write, and the implicit agent roster that read-time migrations add. Onboarding classifies the pre-migration config, as `agent-team.ts` already does, and the classifier ignores a `plugins` block holding only that stamp. It reuses the existing `isNativeSessionCatalogOptOutOnly` check from the owner of the stamp.

## Evidence

Fresh macOS VM: Quick start chosen, Ctrl-C at the next prompt, `openclaw` run again. The config holds `meta`, `plugins` and `wizard`, and Quick start is offered.

![Quick start offered on the rerun](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ee44f8a-93b0-495f-9cc8-0c723598cdb9)

The test fixture uses the config shape captured from a real interrupted run.

Tests:

- `src/cli/fresh-install-config.test.ts`: 6 of 6 pass. Without the fix, 2 of 6 fail.
- `src/cli/run-main.bare-root.test.ts`: 21 of 21 pass.
- `src/commands/onboard-guided.quickstart.test.ts` and `onboard-guided.custodian.test.ts`: 30 of 30 pass.

Known gap: pressing Ctrl-C after an AI connection is saved writes more config and a pending setup receipt. From reading the code, that rerun still resumes in Custom setup. This change does not address it.

Accepted edge case: a config holding only the same opt-out stamp, written by hand, counts as unconfigured because it is identical to the stamp.

Not tested:

- A Quick start finished through to the Gateway on the rerun. No model was configured.
- Ctrl-C at any prompt other than the one directly after choosing Quick start.
- Windows and Linux.
- `agent-team.ts`, which also calls the changed classifier, and the other `onboard-guided` test files. No agent-team test ran.
- A package built from this branch. The live run overlaid a runtime-only build of this branch's fix on the 2026.10.9 package, with some dependencies added by hand.
- Typecheck was not run, and `oxlint` crashed on the linked dependencies used for local testing. Local review and CI have not run.

This branch merges cleanly with the head of #191454 at the time of writing; both edit `src/commands/onboard-guided.ts`.

prs.title: fix(agents): recover dispatch after a temporary credential-store read failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A temporary failure to read an agent's credential store can keep later requests blocked after the store becomes readable. In a real Gateway, a completed turn also leaves a run owner beside the configured owner, so retrying only singleton publications misses the ordinary case.

## User Impact

A new request can recover the agent's current credentials without restarting the Gateway or rerunning an earlier turn. Revoked credentials remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dispatch asks the existing publication queue to retry the original atomic component when it contains one configured owner and only retained run owners for the same agent. Every member must still have the same generation and original read failure. Concurrent requests share the rebuild; another failed read imposes the existing five-second retry cooldown. Cross-agent components keep their existing refusal behavior. There is no background retry, persistent-state change, or turn replay.

This is a narrow October backport; current main has a broader recovery implementation.

## Evidence

The SQLite contention test uses the real read worker. The additional Gateway fixture covers a completed turn followed by a failed credential publication, credential rotation, concurrent dispatch, and reply delivery. It uses real SQLite credentials, Gateway RPCs and a local HTTP model provider; only the scoped unreadable-row outcome is injected.

The exact fixture fails on October 1072c072 with an unpublished runtime owner. The corrected candidate sends both concurrent requests with current credential B. Credential A is used only before the failure; a healthy sibling uses its own C. Revoked and wrong-agent requests fail before any provider HTTP call.

Validation: 34 runtime/Gateway regression tests and 27 cron authorization tests passed, as did native core/core-test typechecks and focused lint.

Live Slack dual-upgrade and 30-minute staging acceptance remain pending. These local results do not claim that deployment verification is complete.

The CI timeout-race check also found an extra wall-clock timeout in the new fixture. The fixture now follows the owning test cancellation signal; the native ratchet, focused lint and the same Gateway case pass. Runtime code is unchanged by this test-only follow-up.
