prs.title: fix(sandbox): avoid slow builder removal during turn setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow first-turn sandbox setup when the container engine takes tens of seconds to remove a disposable dependency builder. Related: #191487.

## User Impact

Prepared workspaces become available once their dependency builder has stopped, without waiting for physical container removal. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer writes a host-mounted template. Publication requires stopping every writer, but does not require deleting the stopped container. Retirement now fences restart and proves termination using the immutable engine ID before returning. The existing sandbox registry and serial housekeeping owner retain removal work, retry failures with visible logging, recover interrupted builders on startup, and drain accepted installation/removal work at shutdown. Runtime-use custody excludes active installers from sweeping.

Production code grows by 132 lines for stop proof, generation ownership, and shutdown/crash recovery. This reuses the existing lifecycle and durable registry rather than adding a queue, cache, or schema. Physical engine cleanup still happens; its cost moves off the preparation path.

## Evidence

[Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41546464910) at `09796578809fcc6847629ae90ea3d0e37c35cdea`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Local independent Codex review is clean after repairing its shutdown-finalizer finding; hosted Codex review also completed without findings.

The regression fails on exact parent `e72b356459b1708372f48f6668dfadb42435f850` with `preparation waited for builder removal`. The candidate passes 80 focused tests plus 24 registry-read tests. Coverage includes concurrent prepares, serial disposal, failed-removal retry, startup recovery with ordinary pruning disabled, and shutdown during installation. Final mock hygiene changes passed all nine affected tests, targeted types, formatting, and the mock-export guard.

`pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. Its patch-caused mock guard failure was repaired and two obsolete baseline entries removed. The remaining local dead-export failure reproduces on the exact main parent: unused `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` in `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`, introduced by `af4c6a1be1c804dabb2616e8c01b0e3176bfad94` (#191285), which removed its last external consumer. This is an inherited main regression, not a passing local check.

### Authority review follow-up

ClawSweeper reported no concrete code finding and requested stale-authority evidence. The completed proof already includes `prune.test.ts`'s "rejects hosted custody released during registry inspection before runtime removal" (no backend removal or registry deletion after release), plus `registry-read.test.ts`'s retirement-authority replacement/unknown-write cases and replaced-reservation rejection. These are the existing owning contracts reused by deferred and startup cleanup.

Source audit confirms the new helper checks state admission, the live host owner, and the exact registry generation after awaited work ([dependency-template.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/09796578809fcc6847629ae90ea3d0e37c35cdea/src/agents/sandbox/dependency-template.ts#L130)). The synchronous guard is supplied to both `kill` and the existing exact-generation removal path, reaching the final engine command boundary ([container-engine.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/09796578809fcc6847629ae90ea3d0e37c35cdea/src/agents/sandbox/container-engine.ts#L175)). Persisted cleanup intent does not supply fresh authority. The lifecycle regression separately covers startup recovery and accepted-work shutdown. This is combined owner-contract test and source evidence, not a claim that the process fixture injected every authority failure.

### Measurements

A process-backed fake Podman sleeps 36 seconds on removal while exercising the real preparation, filesystem, registry, startup, and shutdown owners. The workload contains 62,002 files (1,181,100,067 bytes) and 10,001 synthetic sessions. Two A/A controls precede five interleaved A/B pairs; a separate CPU-profile arm is excluded from timing statistics. Acceptance was recorded before the first sample: zero awaited removals, at least 30 seconds lower fresh-prepare median, identical bytes, serial cleanup, and zero survivors; investigate adverse metrics above 20%.

| Fresh prepare metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time | 66.871 / 84.220 s | 23.381 / 28.134 s |
| Reconcile | 62.464 / 76.625 s | 20.147 / 25.465 s |
| Builder retirement | 36.257 / 36.290 s | 0.166 / 0.184 s |
| Main-thread CPU | 0.982 / 1.432 s | 0.657 / 0.793 s |
| Node process CPU, including workers | 34.813 / 45.667 s | 27.671 / 34.244 s |
| Main-thread allocation | 379.537 / 385.769 MiB | 313.485 / 331.128 MiB |
| Physical removals awaited | 1 | 0 |

With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. Fresh wall ranges were 61.156–84.220 s versus 20.592–28.134 s. A/A fresh times were 97.941 and 113.768 s under higher host load. Attribute approximately **36.1 seconds** to the eliminated removal wait, not the entire observed 43.5-second median improvement. CPU excludes external Git/Python processes; allocation covers the main V8 isolate. The separate whole-script native profile includes setup/verification and is not a before/after CPU comparison.

All 13 arms produced the same complete byte/type/symlink fingerprint, each created and eventually removed one builder, maximum removal concurrency was one, and shutdown left zero survivors. Every candidate returned with a stopped builder and removal outstanding. A separate actual process interruption left one stopped builder; fresh-process startup recovered it to zero (40.548 s including the injected 36-second removal).

Warm results are mixed and remain visible: sibling creation median 13.211 → 13.814 s, p95 16.904 → 34.455 s; sibling reuse median 6.082 → 5.315 s, p95 9.423 → 20.246 s. Both candidate maxima came from the same run. Physical removal had finished at least 8.9 seconds before the sibling phase; unchanged synchronization/manifest work and unchanged operation counts accounted for the delay, while host load rose 16 → 25 → 28 and event-loop delay increased. Other four candidate sibling creation samples were 11.836–13.949 s and reuse samples 4.866–5.687 s. The observations are consistent with environmental contention, but do not independently prove its cause or establish improved warm tails; no samples were discarded or rerun to replace the outliers.

The fixture uses APFS and a synthetic engine, not actual rootless Podman/btrfs. The synthetic agent database is about 8 MB, not 35 GiB. No production data or live deployment was used. Real engine resource contention after deferral remains a deployment qualification gap.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the fixture</summary>

Use separate baseline/candidate source roots and fresh output directories; run arms serially and interleaved.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --source-root "$SOURCE_ROOT" --output "$FIXTURE_OUTPUT" \
  --mode preparation --serial-turns --fresh-only --owner-switch \
  --acceleration --sandbox-backend podman --fake-builder-removal-ms 36000 \
  --files 62000 --file-bytes 19050 --requests 1 --burst 1
```

The committed fixture also supports `--crash-builder` and `--recover-builder` for process-interruption recovery. All eight changed production files in the frozen candidate match the published head byte-for-byte.

</details>

prs.title: fix(discord): channels named in non-Latin script resolve to a different channel
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord channel configured or looked up by a name without ASCII letters or digits (for example "чат") resolves to a different channel, so its per-channel settings, including its tool policy, apply to the wrong channel.

## User Impact

User impact: guild channels named in Cyrillic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean and other non-Latin scripts now resolve to the channel with that name, at Gateway startup and in `openclaw channels resolve`. A name that matches no channel stays unresolved instead of taking another channel's ID, and so does a key made only of emoji or punctuation. The live directory search returns only matching channels for a non-Latin query. ASCII keys resolve exactly as before, to the same channel IDs, including `general` for a channel named "общий-general" and "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts". The channel label in agent context for an emoji-prefixed name such as "⚠️-alerts" becomes `#alerts` instead of keeping the emoji's variation selector.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord channel name matching used an ASCII-only slug, which turns every non-Latin name into an empty string, so all such names matched each other and the first one in API order won. At startup the configured entry (mention gating, system prompt, tool policy) is then bound to that channel's ID.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187148 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188003 fixed the same class of problem for directory searches by comparing lowercase NFC text. Discord already has a Unicode-aware slug for channel labels, `normalizeDiscordDisplaySlug` (NFC, lowercase, keeps letters, marks and digits of any script). Channel resolution and the live directory search now use it for keys with letters outside ASCII, and resolution refuses an empty slug, as guild name matching already does.

For the review's Decision needed, this implements Preserve existing ASCII selection: ASCII keys keep the ASCII-only match (`extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts:156-160`), so every existing ASCII key binds the same channel ID as before. A resolved name key is bound to its channel ID (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829), and that binding is what keeps other channels and threads with the same name from using the key's policy; changing which channel an ASCII key binds, or leaving it unbound, would move or widen its policy on upgrade. A key with other letters (Japanese letters followed by `-ops`) never matches by its Latin part, which on the base bound it to a channel named `ops`.

The slug now drops emoji variation selectors and the keycap mark (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/allow-list.ts:88-91`). They are combining marks, so the slug kept them: emoji-only names such as "⚠️" and "❗️" both slugged to the selector and matched each other. Now they slug to "" and are refused.

## Evidence

Head `7a984a8f337` (base `upstream/main` `f9257898216`). The Gateway runs below are at `1fca9f16ee6`; the later commits change only tests and the test-line allocation. All data is synthetic: no real Discord account or token, no provider key.

### Real Gateway, message in, tool call, reply out

Each run started an isolated Gateway (`openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured`) with its own state directory, config and synthetic bot token, inside `unshare -rn` (loopback only). Discord was Crabline's local Discord server (REST and Gateway WebSocket) behind a small proxy that names its channels and lists the guild's channels for startup resolution. The model was a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in: on each turn it asks for `exec` with `echo tool-ran-<probe>`, whether or not `exec` was offered, and replies with the tool output once one arrives, so the Gateway's own tool gate decides. `tools.exec.mode` is `full` so a granted `exec` runs without a human approval; the only command ever run is that `echo`.

Guild: новости …10, чат …20, general …30, a thread named "чат" in новости …50 and one in general …60. Config: `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, guild `tools.deny: ["exec"]`, key `чат` = `{ requireMention: false, tools: { allow: ["exec", "read"] } }`, key `general` = `{ requireMention: false }`. One message was sent into each channel or thread.

Startup log, base:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000010 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:новости; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

This PR:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000020 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:чат; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

| Target | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| чат …20 | admitted; `exec` not offered (13 tools); the turn stops on "unknown tool" | `exec` offered (5 tools) and run; reply `ack probe-chat tool-ran-probe-chat` |
| новости …10 | `exec` offered and run; reply `ack probe-news tool-ran-probe-news` | dropped, no model turn |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` offered and run (inherits новости) | dropped |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Key `чат` removed | чат, новости and the новости thread dropped; general and its thread without `exec` | same |
| Policy moved to key `новости` | новости and its thread run `exec`; чат dropped | same |

With this PR, `exec` ran only in чат; no other channel or thread, including the two threads named "чат", got it. On the base it ran in новости and in the thread under it.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

The same config and guild ran on the latest stable release (`openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm with `@openclaw/discord@2026.10.9` installed by `openclaw plugins install`). It resolves чат to новости like the base. The thread rows differ from the base because 2026.10.9 predates https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829, so threads still match keys by name:

| Target | 2026.10.9 |
| --- | --- |
| чат …20 | `exec` run |
| новости …10 | admitted (the `чат` key resolves to it), `exec` not offered |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` run |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` run |

The config hash was the same before and after the run. Then this branch ran on that state directory and config: `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the agent database (schema 25 to 38) and changed no `channels.discord` setting. The Gateway (with the branch's bundled Discord plugin, which overrides the installed npm copy) logged the same "channels resolved" line as above and gave the same rows as "After": `exec` ran only in чат, and neither thread named "чат" got it.

### Tests

The case in `resolve-channels.test.ts` and the non-Latin query in `directory-live.test.ts` fail on the base and pass on this branch; the other 14 tests in the two files pass on both. CI seconds at this head (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`, run 41167432249): 46 ms for `resolve-channels.test.ts` and 33 ms for `directory-live.test.ts`, each the sum of the file's per-test times, since the log has no per-file total.

Checks at `7a984a8f337`: the two touched test files and `provider.allowlist.test.ts` (the startup channel-binding tests, with the resolver mocked), oxlint and format check on the changed files, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

The test-lines ratchet failed on the previous CI run because the base was already over its ceiling. This PR's net test lines (+40) are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/discord-unicode-channel-resolution.txt`; they are the regression tests above.

<details>
<summary>Per-case test notes, CLI and directory search, local timing</summary>

`resolve-channels.test.ts` "matches channel names by their letters in any script" covers a non-Latin name, a missing non-Latin name, "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts", `general` for "общий-general", `ops` for the first channel whose ASCII letters are "ops" ("чат-ops", as on the base), a Japanese `-ops` key that stays unresolved, and an emoji-only key "⚠️" that stays unresolved next to a "❗️" channel. Without the selector strip the "⚠️" key binds "❗️" and the test fails.

CLI and directory search at `458bd869c7f`, same synthetic guild (новости …01, чат …02, general …03):

```text
$ openclaw channels resolve --channel discord --kind group --json "900000000000000001/чат"
before: "id": "910000000000000001", "name": "новости"
after:  "id": "910000000000000002", "name": "чат"

$ openclaw directory groups list --channel discord --query чат --json
after: channel:910000000000000002 "чат"   (новости and general are not returned)
```

A single local run with `--maxWorkers=1` at `7a984a8f337`:

| Test file | Tests | Wall (Vitest duration) | CI seconds (run 41167432249) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.test.ts` | 10 | 6.9 s (4.7 s) | 0.046 s |
| `extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts` | 6 | 7.0 s (4.8 s) | 0.033 s |

</details>

Not covered: a real Discord guild. Messages went through Crabline's local Discord server, not Discord itself; the shared Discord end-to-end lane leases a QA guild with one fixed text channel and cannot hold the non-Latin channels this needs. The upgrade run used this branch from a source checkout on the 2026.10.9 state, not a packaged release.

Left for a follow-up: guild names are still matched on the ASCII-only slug, so a guild name that mixes scripts matches by its Latin part alone, and a guild name written only in non-Latin script does not resolve by name at all (it fails closed and never binds another guild). That behavior predates this change and is not touched here. A directory query made only of emoji or punctuation still returns every channel, as every non-Latin query did on the base.

prs.title: feat: support attended-session permission defaults
prs.body:
## Problem

Attended users cannot choose a per-agent creation permission default without repeating it on every request. A New Session picker must also show that creation default accurately, rather than label configured Full Access as Read Only.

## Change

Add opt-in `agents.entries.<agentId>.newSessionPermissionMode` using the existing creation and caller-classification owners. Explicit request modes win. It applies only to fresh, directly attended, profiled operator sessions—not existing sessions, forks, catalog sessions, autonomous runs, or delegated callers. `full` still requires current `operator.admin`.

Expose the attended creation default separately in agent metadata and New Session. Existing-session Default remains based on its existing tool-policy contract. Selection is extracted from the oversized creation service; the independent final-write permission guard remains. Replacing a pending default before persistence produces a structured retryable refusal, not an uncaught exception. No schema migration or existing-session permission rewrite.

## Evidence

Candidate: e7e3c078af1d371fed33af21797fb5ef35faa689; complete feature base 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914. The repair is atop 7395524be33e2031f7567a0df600a5195ed55f93, independently of durable creation.

The following repair and screenshot results were executed on `de78e430a40cdd82c575633eb75b383bca892a68`; they remain stamped to that head. Current-head conflict integration and input-equivalent reuse are qualified separately below.

- Registered public Gateway handler and actual persistence owners: **37 passed**. Configured Full persists for an authorized admin; current admin revocation and replacement of a pending default refuse at the final writer. Non-admin/delegated controls do not escalate. Existing production-written implicit and Guarded session records remain unchanged.
- Agent-list metadata regression failed on the reviewed head and passed after repair. All 69 original session-utils tests passed before coherent extraction; the resulting focused permission projection suite passed 2/2.
- Native network-isolated Chromium production-UI proof: the before capture reproduces incorrect **Default (Read Only)**; after shows **Default (Full Access)**. Existing sessions still show **Default (Read Only)**, and choosing Default omits permissionMode. Test body 2.53s; suite 19.24s; container absence confirmed. Inspected synthetic before/after artifacts contain no live account or credential data.
- Config documentation baseline regenerated and verified. Core/Gateway-test/UI types, protocol generation including Swift/Kotlin contracts, targeted lint/format, UI controller guard, line/test budgets and whitespace checks passed. The creation service is below its original 1,089-count allowance; no allowance increase. The 212-line test allocation covers distinct security, presentation and compatibility regressions.
- Fresh independent local P0–P2 review of the complete repair against 7395524: scoped-clean. Unchanged final-persistence implementation was not supplied to that review; the production-owner proofs above cover that boundary behaviorally.

Retained actual Gateway + CLI evidence on 7395524: genuine authenticated-profile connection, workspace inheritance, explicit Guarded precedence, and sessions.describe persisted readback. This was an isolated real Gateway, not a mocked handler, using the maintained rootless runner. No model inference was needed for creation metadata.

Sanitized prior process-runner output:

```text
[vitest:isolated] preflight Node v26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Chromium OK
✓ test/permission-default-qualification.e2e.test.ts > qualifies attended permission defaults through an isolated Gateway 14605ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
Duration    53.65s
[vitest:isolated] exit=0; container absence confirmed
```

## Qualification limits

A latest-stable binary install-over was not executed. Existing-data compatibility was tested with production-written records created before enabling this optional default. The earlier actual Gateway CLI proof was not rerun for the metadata/picker repair. Current-head CI and hosted review remain independent gates.

Cold host transforms dominate local costs: permission projection 605.52s wall; authority 499.81s wall. Failed setup attempts and the final corrected native UI run are retained in the proof record; no guard, test timeout, or expected result was weakened.

## Conflict-refresh evidence (2026-11-02)

- Preserved published history with merge commit 1711c66f2a0c09438940cc1fd285a5b0650e2975: first parent de78e430a40cdd82c575633eb75b383bca892a68, second parent official main 2777468d26e5f21455b67591a045a40c770aee13. Only actual conflicts were generated configuration baseline counts and hashes; regenerated through config:docs:gen, then config:docs:check passed. No feature implementation was changed during conflict resolution.
- Focused registered-handler/real-persistence rerun: 9/9 permission cases passed (28 unrelated authority-suite cases intentionally not rerun), covering explicit override, non-admin and autonomous non-escalation, authorized Full plus linked-account persistence, final-write admin revocation/default replacement refusal, and existing implicit/Guarded sessions. Metadata projection: 2/2 passed.
- Core, UI, Gateway-root-test and Gateway-server-test typechecks passed. Targeted merged-source lint/format and whitespace checks passed. Test-line budget passed with the ordinary default comparator.
- Fresh local autoreview of the complete 20-file feature delta against 2777468d26e5f21455b67591a045a40c770aee13: P0–P2 scoped-clean, one complete pass. Included unchanged operator/device/request authority and final persistence implementation context. The committed tree equals the reviewed snapshot. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review remains with the publishing owner.
- Existing native production-UI screenshots remain evidence for the permission picker, not a new final-head capture. The New Session owner, picker/menu, submission contract, English permission labels, related styles, protocol metadata and Solid/compiler dependencies are unchanged. Incoming UI changes affect loading-frame scroll retention, sidebar/session menus, channel pairing, thinking claims, workshop settings, retry timing, translations and the outer chat corner; none changes the settled permission menu binding shown by those captures. No full UI rebuild or screenshot rerun was performed.

Validation limitation: the ordinary default line-cap ratchet compared against the checkout's pre-existing origin/main e5a541828cd6f916c259e945bcd11b999b76159a and failed on incoming main's ui/src/e2e/session-management.sidebar.e2e.test.ts (1000 -> 1001 counted lines). That file is byte-identical to the pinned official main and was changed by upstream ba87a52ad8487d6fcbca68a57db74140f07e8b05, not this feature. The unchanged ratchet against the exact integrated main passes (16 source files). No allowance, hook, or guard was changed; default failure is retained as inherited evidence, not called green. Current-head hosted CI remains a separate gate; the local inherited failure is not a claimed CI pass.

### Follow-up: current permission-picker presentation

Commit 19b70ffc7a14bb753ba9bf2fd0e0da1ff78c6e6a updates only the attended-permission E2E regression. Accepted main now labels the trigger with the effective mode: “Read only” for the existing session and “Full access” for attended creation. The test verifies Agent default is selected before any menu interaction can change it, and still requires sessions.create to omit permissionMode. No production permission, presentation or authorization behavior changed.

#### Source-bound qualification

The real Chromium/production Control UI test used published head 0dd76e989b1b3c8c9ca8dccb81c0fcae6cfab2f9 integrated with pinned main 0267ad034a06799d11267dcd21aff5bc63ce76c3. Unpatched integrated tree: 0f8b4a73957a59455ca638055f1832b8f09dd871. With the exact committed test patch: 0c1f0a5ec2d485298c97fedd5250396b49be96cd. This distinguishes integrated-source proof from the original branch's older presentation.

- Before: **1 expected failure**, at the stale trigger-label assertion—received Read only, expected Default (Read Only).
- After: **1/1 passed**, including existing/new effective modes, inherited Default selection and creation-request omission; **0 pending**.
- Permission-picker sibling: **6/6 passed**, **0 pending**.
- Owning UI E2E typecheck, targeted lint, canonical format and whitespace checks passed. The compiler artifact includes the changed test.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the exact test-only patch was clean; the committed file matches the reviewed/tested bytes.

Observed flow:

    existing: Read only
    creation: Full access
    creationRequestHasPermissionMode: false

Execution used the repository-selected Crabbox 0.80.0 AWS small route, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, the repository-pinned Bun fork and Chromium 1248. Source/result/log artifacts were collected and hashed before release, reread afterward, and exact compute cleanup independently confirmed.

#### Separate CI failure attribution

A bounded, fresh-cache Chromium cohort ran the original disabled-menu case plus its initial concurrent chat-details/composer files: **63/63 passed across 3 files**, **0 pending**. The disabled-explanation case executed. This is not an explanation or fix for the original CI failure, and it does not establish inheritance; full-shard timing/order remains different. The earlier appearance-tooltip failure also retains its original unknown attribution.

Earlier setup failures are preserved separately, not counted as red/green proof. Prior stable-data, authority and screenshot evidence remains bound to its original revisions. Current-head hosted CI and review/rating are still required before landing.

### Sign-in CI fixture isolation

Follow-up e7e3c078af1d371fed33af21797fb5ef35faa689 adds only the existing models.catalogRefresh.enabled:false setting and an ownership comment to the first-sign-in integration fixture. It prevents an unrelated hosted catalog poller from contaminating the strict transport oracle. All sign-in, activation, credential-persistence, ownership and revocation assertions remain unchanged. No production or permission-picker behavior changes.

A controlled experiment exercised the real TLS/WebSocket flow and actual scheduled catalog callback through an entered/release/settled barrier at the existing lifecycle boundary—not fabricated requests or a filtered oracle:

| Source / proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original tested merge, callback released between original snapshot and assertion | 1 intended failure; actual catalog fetch changed [] to [catalog URL] |
| Same source and barrier, with two-line fixture isolation | 1/1 passed, zero failed/pending; callback settled without fetching |
| Exact final candidate without diagnostic instrumentation | 1/1 passed, zero failed/pending; complete sign-in/activation/revocation case |

Observed controlled-RED receipt:
~~~json
{"job":"update.remote-model-catalog","catalogRuns":1,"before":[],"after":["https://catalog.openclaw.ai/models/v2/catalog.json"]}
~~~
With the fixture setting, both original foreign-owner checkpoints recorded catalogRuns:1, before:[], after:[], and the remainder of the original case passed.

Final candidate test body:27.534s; Vitest:72.49s; canonical runtime preparation separate. Node24.22.1 orchestrated the pinned Bun runtime on isolated AWSsmall8CPU/~16GB; original CI used~32GB. Targeted formatting, lint, owning Gateway-root test types, test-line/line-cap ratchets and whitespace passed. Fresh independent P0-P2 review was scoped-clean. Committed tree b9f03c882c48413644522e52b89dd7117284abf8 exactly matches reviewed and qualified source.

The first controller stopped after valid RED because its parser expected a diff URL in JSON that Bun Vitest emitted only in the raw log. The retained stack, unchanged assertion and explicit witness were reconciled without rerunning RED; a bounded green-only continuation completed remaining qualification. Both task-owned leases independently verified released/cleanup complete, with retained hashes checked after teardown.

Evidence limit: this proves and fixes fixture susceptibility under a controlled real callback schedule; it does not recreate original CI timing or establish a permission-default production regression. Earlier natural base/merge passes remain non-reproduction evidence, not an inherited/flaky verdict. Existing UI screenshots and stable-data/authority proof retain their original source identities; they were not rerun or relabeled. New-head CI and hosted review remain required publication gates.

## Credits

Requested and co-authored by Galin Iliev (@galiniliev).

## Permission picker proof

Synthetic production-UI captures: new-session Default now shows the configured creation mode; existing-session Default remains unchanged.

Before:

![Before: new-session picker incorrectly shows Default (Read Only)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38ef49ad-824f-4807-bbcd-ce6070f50885)

After:

![After: new-session picker correctly shows Default (Full Access)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/000688e1-0c58-4866-95be-f3d9fce3576c)

## Canonical test ownership repair

Candidate `0dd76e989b1b3c8c9ca8dccb81c0fcae6cfab2f9` adds one ordering-only commit on `1711c66f2a0c09438940cc1fd285a5b0650e2975`. It moves the existing permission projection test after the deleted-agent test in the canonical database-worker registry. The registered set, pool, exclusions, assertions, and permission runtime/UI are unchanged.

- Reproduced the exact eight ownership failures before editing (8 failed, 2 passed).
- The unchanged ownership suite and three direct routing/configuration consumer suites now pass: **363 tests across 4 files**, 236.84 s wrapper.
- Correct caller typecheck leaves, targeted lint/format, syntax and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent local autoreview against `1711c66f2a0c09438940cc1fd285a5b0650e2975`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings. Static review; tests were executed separately.

The separate Chromium appearance-tooltip CI failure was not reproduced: its entire unchanged browser file passed **17/17** locally. Relevant appearance/tooltip/helper/configuration/dependency inputs match pinned main. This does not establish the original CI focus/load/order cause or prove it fixed; full-shard conditions were not reproduced. The original failure remains recorded, with no UI edit or timeout/expectation relaxation. Existing published permission screenshots retain their original provenance. Current-head CI remains a required gate.

## Latest-stable stored-data compatibility

Qualified released **v2026.10.9** source (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, agent schema 25) against candidate `0dd76e989b1b3c8c9ca8dccb81c0fcae6cfab2f9` (agent schema 39; package version still 2026.10.9). This is **source-owner storage qualification, not a binary install-over**.

- Reused the admitted, clean released source and a private copy of its immutable image. The released canonical synchronous session writer emitted three synthetic, parser-valid records: implicit permission mode, Guarded, and Read Only. The released config reader validated the old configuration without the new setting.
- The candidate maintenance lease and actual schema owner upgraded the copy **25 → 39**, preserving all four original session-entry JSON records byte-for-byte, the three retained pending inputs, cache sentinel, and configuration bytes.
- With a newly created current profile and current admin role—not restored historical credentials or roles—13 requests through the registered public Gateway dispatcher exercised existing-session describe/adoption and fresh creation. Enabling `agents.entries.main.newSessionPermissionMode: "full"` through the actual config writer left old implicit/Guarded/Read Only permissions unchanged. Fresh direct attended creation with omitted permissionMode persisted Full; an explicit Read Only selection still won.
- Existing IDs/labels and the nonpermission config sentinels (`session.dmScope`, `messages.ackReaction`) survived. Closing/reopening the persistence owner and separately inspecting the saved SQLite image confirmed all five tested permission outcomes.

prs.title: fix(ui): Android agent browser says tab unavailable after a cold start
prs.body:
Closes #187645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android chat **Agent browser** card shows "This tab is no longer available. Select another tab." and then stays empty, while the agent keeps working in that tab, when a cold start reuses Chrome's startup tab.

## User Impact

The Android Agent browser card shows the agent's tab on cold starts too. Closed or stopped tabs still show as unavailable, and the card still never switches to a different tab. The fix ships in the Gateway's bundled Control UI; the Android app is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android card is a WebView of the Gateway's `/focus/browser` page for the tool result's exact tab (`ChatBrowserCard.kt` `chatBrowserUrl()`). Since #159891, `GET /tabs` from a session-scoped panel returns only tabs the session tracked (opened by `open` or from its panel) plus tabs the request references. The chat side panel references the tabs in its transcript through `sessionTabs`. `BrowserDocument` sent the session scope but never referenced its own fixed tab. So when the session hadn't tracked the tab, the list came back empty and the panel reported it unavailable. For example, a cold `navigate` reuses Chrome's startup tab instead of opening one.

`BrowserDocument` now passes its fixed tab as the referenced tab, using the existing `tabScope.referencedTabs` contract. No Gateway, registry, or storage change.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and alternatives</summary>

- `ui/src/components/browser/browser-document.tsx` mounted `BrowserPanelHost` with `sessionKey` and `fixedTab` but no `sessionTabs`. So `bindBrowserRequestClient` sent `tabScope: { sessionKey, referencedTabs: [] }` on `GET /tabs`.
- `extensions/browser/src/gateway/browser-request.ts` keeps only `tracked ∪ referenced` tabs for a scoped list. The fixed-tab filter in `browser-panel-snapshot.ts` then found nothing. `selectTab` raised `browser.tabUnavailable`, and later refreshes left the view empty. Because the selection runs once per tab identity, and the Android card only reloads when the `targetId` changes, nothing tries again during the run.
- Tracking the tab at the producer would make the session own Chrome's startup tab, and session cleanup would close it. References exist for tabs a session used without opening them.
- Retrying, or falling back to the first available tab (the issue's suggestion), would conflict with the exact-tab contract in `docs/platforms/android.md`. The web panel has no 2-second retry. It works because it already references its transcript tabs.
- The intermittency fits the agent choosing `navigate` (reuses the untracked startup tab) or `open` (creates a tracked tab) on a cold browser. I reproduced both paths directly through `/tools/invoke`, not with a live model.

</details>

## Evidence

I built current main and the candidate, then ran an isolated Gateway (temp state, loopback port, headless managed `openclaw` profile). For each run I stopped the browser, called `POST /tools/invoke` with `browser` `navigate` and no `open`, and loaded the result's `/focus/browser?sessionKey=agent:main:main&target=host&profile=openclaw&targetId=<tool-result targetId>` URL: the same page the Android card embeds.

- Main: the page shows "Browser request failed: This tab is no longer available. Select another tab." for a tab that exists. (Screenshot: main, cold navigate)
- Candidate, same steps: the page renders the tab. (Screenshot: candidate, cold navigate)
- Control on the candidate: a tab created with `open` still renders.
- Edge case on the candidate: after closing the referenced tab while another session tab stays open, the page still shows the tab as unavailable and does not switch to the other tab.

Gateway readback on main for the cold-navigate tab, via `openclaw gateway call browser.request`:

```text
GET /tabs (unscoped)                                    -> tabs: [C09EA5A3… "Repro page"]
GET /tabs tabScope {sessionKey, referencedTabs: []}     -> tabs: []      <- what the focus page sent
GET /tabs tabScope {sessionKey, referencedTabs: [C09E…]} -> tabs: [C09EA5A3… "Repro page"]
```

<details>
<summary>Tests and gates</summary>

- New `browser-document.tab-scope.test.tsx` mounts the real `BrowserDocumentContent` and `BrowserPanelHost` against a Gateway stub that lists an untracked tab only when it is referenced. It fails on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 'browser.request', …(1) ]`, no screenshot of the fixed tab) and passes on the candidate.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser/browser-document.tab-scope.test.tsx ui/src/components/browser/browser-document.test.tsx ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-dashboard.test.ts ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-route.test.ts`: 4 files, 16 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, format, and the i18n and controller guards passed. It reported a line-cap ratchet failure in `src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; the ratchet compared against an older fork `main`. The run timed out on my machine during the deprecated-API guard, which then passed when run on its own.
- `pnpm ui:build` reports the existing CSS and chat-boot budget overages on main as well (chat boot JS gzip 1251.0 KiB on main, 1250.8 KiB here).

</details>

Not covered: a physical Android handset. The card loads this Gateway page in a WebView and needs no app change.

Production delta +7/-0; test delta +77/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the tab list of the embedded `/focus/browser` page; the chat side panel, the Browser dock and dashboards are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(voice): Discord controls and phone consults fail with PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
Related: #189036

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm) requested and guided this repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/91bf5c8e-90b2-4f50-a7b4-fd877499b08b)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord voice active-run controls and realtime phone-call agent consultations fail when agent storage uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

The two bundled voice surfaces can use PostgreSQL-backed agent stores while retaining model-selection locks, current speaker/call authority, and the existing synchronous SDK contracts. No configuration, schema, migration, or permission-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both consumers still reached synchronous session-entry reads on the Gateway thread, which PostgreSQL intentionally refuses.

- Expose the existing worker-backed model-lock check as an additive async SDK helper, reuse its existing candidate selection/predicate, and await it in voice-call before fast-context lookup and before returning its result. Recheck the live call after each wait.
- Allow asynchronous caller-policy preparation in the existing run controller and migrate Discord to it. Preparation repeats for each injection admission; a separate live caller assertion remains at enqueue and cancellation effects, including the legacy key-selected path.
- Preserve the synchronous helper/callback and released dependency-adapter contracts; no synchronous fallback is selected after a worker failure.

This is distinct from @ceckert's #189036: that PR owns the four Gateway Talk surfaces and explicitly excludes these bundled SDK consumers. This PR leaves those Gateway callers untouched and does not import that branch. Both touch the shared run controller; whichever lands second must reconcile that common owner without duplicating its implementation or dropping either set of live guards.

The private async lock check is consolidated rather than adding another lock owner. Production changes are +58/-22 lines; no new manager, cache, or storage owner is introduced. The 242 net test lines cover the distinct consumer lifetime, worker-failure, model-lock, fingerprint and final-cancellation boundaries and are recorded in their own test-line allocation.

## Evidence

### Actual product and storage boundary

Built the clean baseline `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0` and the candidate with the canonical `pnpm build`, on Node 24.20.0. All six changed production blobs remain unchanged since the candidate product proof; later adjustments only prepare runtime config in the cancellation-test fixture and migrate the root Discord integration assertion.

The disposable Gateway used real PostgreSQL 17.11 agent storage (`database.engine: sqlite`, `database.families.agent.engine: postgres`). A signed synthetic Twilio webhook issued the one-use stream URL; a carrier WebSocket sent documented start/media frames through the real voice-call server and bundled OpenAI Realtime bridge. Local Realtime WebSocket and model SSE protocol fixtures supplied synthetic transcript/tool output and a deterministic model response. The actual OpenClaw agent turn, session controller, storage, public history RPC and shutdown ran normally. No paid provider traffic or live Team state was used.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean baseline, PostgreSQL | Final tool result contains `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`; zero agent-model requests. |
| Candidate, PostgreSQL | One agent-model request; final tool result contains `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER`; authenticated `chat.history` returns that assistant answer. |
| Independent PostgreSQL read after clean Gateway shutdown | `assistant_rows=1`, `marker_answers=1`. |
| Candidate, SQLite control | Same signed-carrier flow returns `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER` with one model request; clean shutdown. |

A separate source-bound probe runs the real registered voice-call consult handler and the actual Discord voice consumer/public controller against real PostgreSQL session reads. Both baseline consumers refuse at their synchronous session reader; both migrated consumers pass on PostgreSQL and SQLite. The Discord backend is a synthetic guarded run attached through the real controller, not a real Discord transport. A separate Gateway-role probe confirms the deprecated synchronous PostgreSQL read still throws the original main-thread guard.

Limits: the carrier is a simulator, and Realtime/model responses are protocol fixtures. This does not claim real Twilio/Discord server operation, microphone capture, speech recognition/synthesis quality, or commercial model inference.

### Regressions and checks

- With the original six production files temporarily restored, the three new run-control regressions fail for the intended behavior: allowed async-policy steering does not reach the backend, and cancellation proceeds instead of honoring the revoked caller. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; the complete stop/control suite passes 12 tests.
- New consumer cases deny use after speaker revocation, session/call replacement or closure, worker failure, and a model lock applied during fast-context preparation. Existing synchronous callback/dependency-adapter cases remain covered. The synchronous model-lock helper and dependency-adapter type are byte-identical to the baseline.
- Shared Talk/control suites: 52 tests passed. Discord voice runtime e2e: 27 tests passed in both configured runs. Prompt-prefix stability: 14 tests passed. Voice-call runtime: 26 tests passed. The exact six-file Discord shard replay printed 169 tests passed.
- Core/extension production types, owning core/extension test-type graphs, targeted typed lint, formatting, SDK export/declaration generation, mock-export, line-cap and test-line checks pass. Full canonical build passed with bounded native thread pools after an initial local process-limit failure.
- Exact-head CI caught one missed root Discord integration assertion of the old callback shape. Reproduced locally (2 failures), migrated its expected async callback/live guard, and reran the complete file: 8 passed, exit 0 (13.19 s including preparation). A repository-wide callback search found no other unmigrated Discord expectations; legacy Gateway/synchronous SDK tests remain unchanged.
- Native Auto Review: complete local candidate against `9c22cf86`, through P2, **scoped-clean**, no findings. It reviewed code/context, not execution.

One larger run observed `realtime-turns.test.ts > treats a bare wake name as an activation for the next realtime transcript` fail before agent dispatch. An unchanged-code exact-shard replay printed all 169 Discord and 26 voice-call tests passed, but exec finalization failed during a transient stopped-container incident. No fix or clean terminal exit is claimed for that replay, and baseline attribution of the original wake-name failure remains unconfirmed. The separate control/prefix run subsequently completed with exit 0 after the sandbox recovered.

New-case files reuse existing suites rather than adding a cold suite/job: individual new cases take 1–2 ms in the consumer output; the voice-call file completed in 7.52 s wall, and the control/prefix command in 62.55 s including compilation/preparation. Exact-head CI for `d783c53ce3d87fdf4fb69130909dd9b7f3fae5da` passed [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41267798066/job/124735928893): no failed or timed-out jobs, all selected prerequisites succeeded, and `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false`. The formerly failing root integration shard is green.

prs.title: fix(hooks): resolve mapping header templates case-insensitively
prs.body:
## Summary
Hook mapping templates that reference a request header with its canonical capitalization render empty. A mapping such as `textTemplate: "GitHub event={{headers.X-GitHub-Event}}"` receives a request that carries `X-GitHub-Event: push`, yet the rendered wake text is `GitHub event=`. HTTP header names are case-insensitive and senders document them in mixed case (`X-GitHub-Event`, `X-Gitlab-Event`, `Stripe-Signature`), so copying the name from the sender's docs silently drops the value. When the header is the only template content, the request is rejected with `400 hook mapping requires text`, and a `sessionKey` templated only from a header is rejected as rendering empty.

## Root cause
`normalizeHookHeaders` in `src/gateway/hooks.ts` lowercases every header name before the mapping context is built, but `resolveTemplateExpr` in `src/gateway/hooks-mapping.ts` looks the header up with the name exactly as written in the template:

```ts
// before
if (expr.startsWith("headers.")) {
  return getByPath(ctx.headers, expr.slice("headers.".length));
}
```

Only an all-lowercase template name (`{{headers.x-github-event}}`) can match the lowercased map; any other spelling resolves to `undefined` and renders as an empty string.

## Fix
Normalize the template's header name with the same helper the request handler uses for the header map:

```ts
// after
if (expr.startsWith("headers.")) {
  return getByPath(ctx.headers, normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(expr.slice("headers.".length)));
}
```

## Why this is the right boundary
The header map is produced lowercase by `normalizeHookHeaders`, and `resolveTemplateExpr` is the single place where mapping templates read headers (text, message, name, sessionKey, to, model and thinking all render through it), so normalizing the lookup key there makes every templated field agree with the producer. Lowercase templates, which the docs show (`{{headers.x-event-type}}`), resolve exactly as before. `payload.*` and `query.*` lookups stay case-sensitive because JSON keys and query parameters are case-sensitive. Transforms are unaffected: they already receive the same lowercased `headers` object.

## Verification
- `src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts`: new case "resolves header templates case-insensitively" maps `{{headers.X-GitHub-Event}} {{headers.x-github-delivery}}` against a lowercased header map and asserts the wake text is `push d-1`. It fails on pristine main (the event value renders empty) and passes with the patch; the full file passes (24 cases).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A hook mapping template that names a request header in mixed case (`{{headers.X-GitHub-Event}}`) rendered empty even though the request carried that header.
Real environment tested: Real gateway started from source with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run` (loopback, token auth, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), with `hooks.enabled: true` and one mapping `{ id: "github", match: { path: "github" }, action: "wake", wakeMode: "now", textTemplate: "GitHub event={{headers.X-GitHub-Event}} delivery={{headers.X-GitHub-Delivery}}" }`, driven with curl over HTTP. The rendered wake text was read back from the real agent SQLite store the gateway wrote. Pristine main 74d1342d3ac first, then this patch with identical config and request. Nothing was stubbed; no model provider credentials were configured, so the queued wake turn itself fails at provider sign-in after the text is recorded.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'`, then stop the gateway and run `sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 74d1342d3ac)
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'
{"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
HTTP 200
$ sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"
agent:main:main|GitHub event= delivery=

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'
{"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
HTTP 200
$ sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"
agent:main:main|GitHub event=push delivery=7f3c-42
```
Observed result after fix: The wake text the gateway recorded for the main session changes from `GitHub event= delivery=` on main to `GitHub event=push delivery=7f3c-42` with the patch; the header values from the request now reach the mapped template.
What was not tested: No live model provider turn (no credentials configured); agent-action mappings with header-templated `sessionKey`, `to` or `model` were not booted live, though they render through the same function; full build not run. Some bundled plugins failed to load in the from-source gateway because of a local dependency resolution issue unrelated to hooks, which does not touch the hooks HTTP path.

prs.title: fix(sessions): cold PostgreSQL conversations fail after idle readers close
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cold transcript writes and restoration-dependent operations failing on PostgreSQL after the Gateway's cached native reader retires.

## User Impact

Cold conversations no longer depend on a boot-admitted main-thread database connection. SQLite, native maintenance, source checks, writer ordering, cancellation and commit settlement retain their existing contracts. No configuration, schema, durability, retention or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the agent database's existing worker execution generation for cold restoration. Preserve the ordinary committed display notification as well as the separate facts-only receipt publication; reopening historical archives must still refresh readers.

The author simplification pass kept one owner and no new connection, fallback, cache or API. Production is net −1 line. The new real-engine regression and adjusted native-publication fixture add exactly 142 test lines, with matching scoped allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

Qualified locally on **Node 26.12.1 and real PostgreSQL 17.11** with SQLite controls; all state, services and model traffic were disposable and local.

- **Base red, fixed green:** a Gateway-role main process with no host compatibility reader restores a real cold archive, preserves the original rows and rewrite generation, publishes one ordinary display notification, then appends and reads subsequent messages. The base throws “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker”.
- **Built Gateway RPC:** the warm baseline initially succeeds because startup retains a reader. A fixture explicitly invokes that production reader owner's idle cleanup—not a shortened production timeout or a natural 30-minute wait. After observing native readers **1→0**, base chat.inject refuses with the same guard and makes zero provider requests. The final build succeeds, retains original history, completes a real agent turn through a deterministic loopback HTTP model, survives a new-process restart, and completes a later turn: **two actual model HTTP requests**. No Team data or paid provider was used. An initial fixture signal collided with the Gateway restart signal; the corrected non-restart stimulus was rerun on both base and final source.
- **86 focused tests passed across six files**, covering both engines, publication, cancellation, stale source/owner checks, missing/corrupt archives, reopen and parent-fork consumers. Final command wall time: **119.6 seconds**, including compilation/wrappers. The two-case conformance file runs in about 5–6 seconds of test time; hosted CI time is not yet available.
- Production and affected infra/session test typechecks, scoped lint/format, whitespace, exact test-line allocation and database worker ratchet passed. The inventory remains **168→168 T1** calls; this is not a whole-Gateway SQL or performance claim.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review, complete local candidate against 9c22cf86, P0–P2: scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed the supplied diff/source context, not an independent test execution.

**CI follow-up:** [Initial exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266454178/job/124730545714) caught an obsolete incomplete-mock exemption for the fixture removed here. The same failure reproduced locally. Removing precisely that one exemption makes the mock-factory ratchet pass; no exemption was added or broadened. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of this one-line follow-up is scoped-clean. Runtime/test source and the built-product proof are unchanged; the updated head requires its own CI.

### Inspectable shipped-runtime capture

Re-ran the same local shipped-Gateway flow with actual whitelisted RPC, reader-owner and received HTTP-request observations recorded below. This is **metadata/evidence only**: the full tracked index equals published head `e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` (`git diff --cached --exit-code e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` exited 0), and `git diff --exit-code` exited 0.

The maintained `createOpenClawTestInstance` starts `dist/index.js`; that working-tree runtime was built with `pnpm build:runtime`. The native publisher preserves the guest Git HEAD, so the retained build stamp correctly says base `9c22cf86`, `inputsClean:false`, **not** the published commit. prs.title: fix(voice-call): ignore echoed caller transcripts during playback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes phantom caller turns when realtime transcription returns the assistant's own words during carrier playback.

Supersedes #159145, thanks @mnowrot. Related: #159140.

## User Impact

Unconfirmed playback echo no longer enters caller history or independently starts a host-forced agent consultation. Callers can still interrupt through the existing local speech threshold or provider barge-in.

This filters host caller turns. Realtime providers still receive every inbound audio frame and own their VAD, transcripts and responses; provider-side echo interruptions and transcripts arriving after the tail remain outside this fix. Quiet overlapping speech without a barge-in indication can be ignored during the window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing audio controller admits caller partials/finals only after detected caller speech, a provider interruption, or expiration of carrier playback plus a 400 ms tail. Carrier timing accumulates successfully sent audio even after the local pacing queue drains. An admitted partial remains eligible through its final, and finalization consumes that admission.

The original blanket masking of local barge-in is not retained because it also prevents genuine caller interruption. No config, provider implementation or SDK contract changes. The Deepgram UtteranceEnd fix in #191498 is untouched.

Production delta: +34/-1, net +33 lines for the carrier deadline and turn-admission state in existing owners. The simplify pass found no dead or duplicate owner path that could safely offset this necessary growth. The separate 43-line regression allocation covers the broken behavior and both interruption owners without new test scaffolding.

## Evidence

- Current-main negative control: base `77fadc09500839734b3a148646e54358dfc6df3d`, real handler and carrier WebSocket, quiet injected media followed by STT returning `Hello, how can I help you today?`. Expected no caller turn; main instead emitted that exact `call.speech` transcript. One regression failed for the intended reason.
- After the fix: 53/53 focused handler/pacer/audio-controller tests passed; the expanded handler/lifecycle/call-control run passed 75/75. The final two-case regression covers playback, the 400 ms tail, post-tail caller speech, local/provider barge-in and renewed playback. Runs used [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41546147614), lease `tbx_01m6f9nvc3hc0jsbxfdmh3dpjd`.
- Focused test wrapper wall time: 26.43 s for the first three named files, 21.01 s for the expanded three-file run (17.79 s Vitest duration, including transforms/setup). [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41547848762) succeeded with no failed jobs. The two added regression cases took 22 ms (local barge-in) and 18 ms (provider barge-in) in CI.
- Touched-file lint: all four TypeScript files passed. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local autoreview through the shared helper, Codex, P0–P3: `scoped-clean`, no findings against the logical patch based on `77fadc095008`. Subsequent edits only applied formatter output and adjusted the regression-line allocation to match.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. This is a credited reimplementation. No PSTN/live-provider proof is claimed. Focused tests, their dependency install and artifact builds ran remotely. Native landing used only scripts/pr’s managed, lockfile-keyed dependency cache locally, under the authorized exception; the production Gateway was untouched.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): stop assistant echo from being taken as caller speech
prs.body:
Refs #159140 — this PR fixes the **plugin-side** echo barge-in. The provider-side (Google VAD) echo interruption and the provider-committed echo transcript remain open in the linked issue. The current-head real-call observation is below; the ownership decision is in the decision comment on this PR.

## What problem this solves

The realtime handler's local RMS gate counted any inbound energy as caller speech. Assistant audio that leaks back through the line (echo) therefore armed the gate, which cancelled the agent's own turn mid-sentence and could store caller lines the caller never said. Reported in #159140.

## What this change does

`RealtimeAudioPacer.getPlayoutEndsAt()` projects the paced stream clock onto `Date.now()`, so the handler knows when the assistant's audio has actually reached the line. While paced audio is queued, or within a 400 ms tail after the last outbound chunk (`ASSISTANT_SPEECH_TAIL_MS`), the local RMS gate is fed `rms 0`, so it cannot arm `handleBargeIn`. Inbound audio is still forwarded to the realtime provider, so provider-owned barge-in is untouched. Once the window closes, the gate behaves exactly as it does on the merge base.

## Scope — what this change does not do

- It cannot stop the realtime provider from raising its own interruption from line echo. On the observed head, Google's server-side VAD (provider defaults) interrupted the greeting 9–10 times per call on echo alone.
- It cannot stop the provider from committing a transcription of that echo as a `user:` turn, so the phantom caller transcript persists. Both remain open in #159140 — **this PR does not close it.**
- On a bridge with no provider-owned barge-in, a genuine caller who speaks over the assistant is not interrupted by the local gate until the paced queue and the 400 ms tail finish. That is a deliberate, measured trade-off, put to the maintainers in the decision comment on this PR.

## Evidence

The current-head real-call observation (below) measured the local gate going from 12 echo-driven detections at −12 dB on the merge base to 0 on this head, with genuine caller turns still delivered and the post-window fallback intact. The redacted per-frame traces, the harness and the per-scenario numbers are in the observation section below.

---

## Revision 5: reduced to the change the observation supports

Head: `9b0e825a4bc37ce6c08a361e499737e43906fb8a` `fix(voice-call): mask local barge-in while assistant audio plays out`. It is one commit on top of `a6ec34f7`, pushed as a fast-forward.

### Why
The real-call observation on `2181c268` showed two things:
- The learned echo floor only delayed the false local barge-in, by 170–800 ms into each playback segment.
- The phantom-transcript guard never fired, because the provider delivers the final `inputTranscription` after the line has gone quiet.

Only `b918ba3c` had zero echo barge-ins at −12 dB, and that commit fully masked the local gate while assistant audio was active. This revision keeps that masking and drops everything else.

### What remains
- `RealtimeAudioPacer.getPlayoutEndsAt()` projects the paced stream clock onto `Date.now()` and is clamped on clear or close. Together with `ASSISTANT_SPEECH_TAIL_MS = 400`, it defines the window: assistant audio is active while `hasPendingAudio() || now < playoutEndsAt + 400 ms`.
- While the window is open, the local RMS gate is fed rms 0, so it cannot fire `handleBargeIn`. Inbound audio is still forwarded to the provider, so provider-side barge-in is untouched.
- Once the window closes, the gate behaves as it does on the merge base.
- Transcript emission is back to the merge-base form. A code comment explains why the host must not drop provider-committed turns.

### What was removed and why
These were removed:
- the constants `ECHO_OVERLAP_MARGIN`, `ECHO_AMBIGUITY_MARGIN`, `ECHO_BASELINE_SMOOTHING`, `ECHO_FLOOR_MIN_SAMPLES` and `PHANTOM_GUARD_MIN_RMS`
- the state `echoBaselineRms/Samples`, `maxEchoInputRms`, `maxRecentInputRms` and `callerAudioSinceTranscript`
- the helper `resetInputAccounting`
- the per-segment floor reset
- the `realtime phantom transcript suppressed` branch
- the ambiguous-overlap logic

The floor did not stop echo barge-in; it only postponed it. The phantom guard never fired on a real call. Both added complexity with no observed benefit.

**The phantom-transcript symptom is not fixed by this PR.** The provider drives it: the provider commits the final input transcription after playout has ended. It remains open as a follow-up.

Diff vs merge base `7ff7042d`: 4 files, +261/−46. Production code accounts for +33/−1 of that (`realtime-handler.ts` +16/−1, `realtime-audio-pacer.ts` +17); the rest is tests. For comparison, the diff was +469/−36 at `a6ec34f7`. Diff vs `a6ec34f7`: 3 files, +182/−400.

### Test-contract change (pending Voice Call owner approval)
Three existing `realtime-handler.test.ts` cases asserted that the local gate barges in on loud input while assistant audio is still playing out, or within 400 ms of playout ending. Issue #159140 reports exactly that behaviour as the bug: echo of the agent's own audio arms the local barge-in gate and cancels the agent's turn. The level gate cannot tell echo from the caller, so those assertions encoded the defect. Each test keeps its intent under the new contract:

| Test (old name → new name) | Intent kept | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `keeps local barge-in fallback for providers without speech-started events` → `masks local barge-in during playout and keeps the fallback for providers without speech-started events` | For providers without speech-started events, the local gate owns barge-in | Loud frames during playout now assert no `handleBargeIn` and no `clear`. After the window, a second burst asserts the original cancelled turn, `clear`, `handleBargeIn({ audioPlaybackActive: true })`, and `output.audio.done` on the cancelled turn. |
| `lets a session bridge override provider-level barge-in capabilities` → `... once playout ends` | A bridge with `handlesInputAudioBargeIn: false` hands barge-in to the local gate | A loud frame during playout does not barge in. After the window, the override still produces the cancelled turn, `clear`, and `handleBargeIn({ audioPlaybackActive: true })`. |
| `clears remote playback after local pacing and output state have finished` → `clears remote playback after paced playout and output state have finished` | After `response.done` and playout, the local gate clears remote playback | The caller frames are now delivered 1 s later on the wall clock, past playout and the 400 ms tail. The assertions are unchanged: `handleBargeIn({ audioPlaybackActive: false })`, exactly one extra `clear`, and no `turn.cancelled`. |

Only `Date` is faked (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })`), so no real sleeps are added. The socket, the pacer timers and `vi.waitFor` all stay on real timers.

### Trade-off
While a provider's local gate owns barge-in (no speech-started events, or a bridge override), a caller can no longer interrupt through the local gate during assistant playout or its 400 ms tail. The provider still receives every inbound frame. Barge-in by providers that own it (speech-started events) is unaffected. We accept this because a false barge-in on echo cancels the agent's own turn. That is the reported and observed failure, and it happens far more often than a genuine interruption during playout.

### Lanes (on `9b0e825a`, run via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs run …`)
| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `realtime-handler.test.ts` + `realtime-handler.persistence.test.ts` | 2 files, 84/84 pass |
| All 12 `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/*.test.ts` files (explicit list) | 12 files, 175/175 pass |
| `realtime-handler.echo-guard.test.ts` | 4/4 pass |
| `npx oxlint --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/voice-call/src/webhook` | exit 0 |
| `npx oxfmt --check` (4 touched files) | clean |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

Not run: `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` (it runs out of memory on the 7.7 GB host) and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (it refuses the external dependency links). No real-call proof was captured on this head.

### Negative control (current tests, merge-base handler `7ff7042d`)
- `realtime-handler.echo-guard.test.ts`: 4 of 4 fail. Each failure is `handleBargeIn` called once, which means echo barge-in fires.
- Updated `realtime-handler.test.ts` cases: both masking cases fail. The `clears remote playback` case passes, as expected, because it exercises post-window behaviour that the merge base shares.
- The handler source was restored byte-identical afterwards.

---

### Real-call observation on head `9b0e825a` (Revision 6)

**What this is:** This is a real Google Live provider session with real speech audio, running through the real
`RealtimeCallHandler` and a real carrier WebSocket. The line echo is simulated at the media-frame level. It is not
a PSTN/telephony call.

**Setup:**
- Head: `9b0e825a`, `realtime-handler.ts` blob `6894b015`. Contrast: merge base `7ff7042d`, blob `a8bdb29d`.
- Transport: `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` over `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (TLSv1.3,
  `authorized=true`, server `setupComplete`), with no mocks. Raw `inputTranscription` wire frames matched the provider
  callbacks 1:1.
- Local barge-in armed: `supportsBargeIn: true`, `handlesInputAudioBargeIn: false`.
- Caller audio: Google TTS → `ffmpeg … -f mulaw` → 20 ms frames.
- Echo: outbound audio at −12 or −18 dB with a 40 ms delay.
- Each row is one live call.

| Scenario | Local speech detections / clears | Google VAD interrupts (→ clears) | `turn.cancelled` | Caller turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A echo-only −12 dB, merge base | **12 / 12** | 9 (8) | 20 | — (echo committed as `user:`) |
| A echo-only −12 dB, head | **0 / 0** | 10 (10) | 10 | — (echo committed as `user:`) |
| A echo-only −18 dB, head | **0 / 0** | 9 (9) | 9 | — (echo committed as `user:`) |
| B caller overlaps playout, head | **0 / 0** during 2023 ms of overlap | 2 (2), first 2033 ms after caller onset | 2 | delivered and answered |
| C caller after playout + 400 ms tail, head | **1 / 1**, 292 ms after caller onset | 2 (1) | 1 | delivered |

**What this shows:**
- **The local echo barge-in is fixed.** It went from 12 to 0 at −12 dB, and was 0 at −18 dB.
- **Echo still cancels turns in this setup.** Google's server-side VAD, left at the provider defaults, interrupts on
  the echo 9–10 times per greeting. Google's transcription of the echo is still committed as a `user:` turn while
  the caller is silent. The mask removes only the host's barge-ins on echo.
- **Genuine caller turns are delivered.** In B and C, the question was committed and answered. Echo words
  ("Hello.", "the capital.") were merged into the delivered turn.
- **Measured cost (the P1).** In B, the caller was about 12 dB louder than the echo (voiced RMS 0.169 vs 0.043). They
  spoke over the assistant for 2023 ms, and the local gate never fired. Only Google's VAD stopped playback, 2.03 s
  after caller onset. A bridge without provider barge-in would have kept playing until the queue and the 400 ms tail
  finished. While assistant audio plays, the local gate does not interrupt. Interruption is deferred until playout
  ends; it is not removed (C: the gate fired 292 ms after onset once the window closed).

**Not exercised:** a PSTN or acoustic echo path, a bridge with no provider VAD (the B conclusion for such bridges is
inferred), other providers or models, and repeat runs.
