prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: fix(update): preserve recovery errors and async triage callbacks
prs.body:
Related: #189713

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failed-update recovery can lose its uncertain-cleanup classification, and bridged failure triage can lose its asynchronously resolved installation root.

Addresses the [cleanup-error P1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189713#discussion_r4433091379) and [async-callback P2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189713#discussion_r4433091386) left in the merged worker bridge.

## User Impact

User impact: recovery retains the signal that a child may still be writing, so existing callers can preserve artifacts and settlement safeguards. Triage receives the resolved installation root or the actual callback failure instead of silently receiving `undefined`.

The candidate package must contain this fix. Released updaters importing its generated recovery bridges receive it without changes to the installed driver. No schema, configuration, authority, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bridge now transports the canonical cleanup marker and non-enumerable error chains, including aggregate errors. Callback promises settle on the caller thread before the synchronously waiting worker is notified; synchronous live checks retain their value/throw semantics.

The simplification pass kept both fixes in the existing transport owner: no new manager, public API, or recovery policy. Production delta is +39/-22 lines. Two regression tests add 58 lines, with a matching scoped test-line allocation because existing tests did not exercise worker-originated cleanup errors or asynchronous callback settlement.

## Evidence

### CI lint correction, 2026-11-02

Head `c48073960f1f646ed9572d269c7d499392526b47` fixes the PR-caused `typescript(no-misused-promises)` error from [check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41536973876/job/125592814990). The message listener is synchronous and dispatches the existing asynchronous callback handler, matching the worker-side pattern. Callback fulfillment/rejection handling and reply-before-wake ordering are unchanged; no suppression was added.

- Exact-head [CI check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41545047018/job/125619696033) passed on `c48073960f1f`; the overall CI run was still in progress when this evidence was recorded.
- The previous single-file lint invocation did not report this error; it is not used as proof for this correction.
- All 4 existing real-worker bridge tests pass (358 ms test execution; 37.98 s wrapper including compilation/cleanup). Tooling-test typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent review of the +4/-1 correction found no substantive issues. Local ClawSweeper committed-range review (`8e24ce385cd8` → `c48073960f1f`) completed with no actionable correctness or security findings; source review only.

### Original repair evidence (`8e24ce385cd8`)

- Both new regressions fail on base `d6510f3c7e6c`: cleanup marker arrives as `undefined`; asynchronous root arrives as `undefined`.
- With the fix, 140 tests across `update-compat-isolated-bridge`, `update-compat-external-bindings`, `update-compat-cleanup`, and `runtime-postbuild` pass. These include real Node worker transport, generated compatibility modules, dependency-cache isolation, direct/cause/aggregate cleanup errors, asynchronous file I/O and rejection identity, synchronous revocation, frozen requester state, argument write-back, and returned callbacks.
- Changed test file: 4 tests in 325 ms; full four-file run: 54.74 s including cold worker compilation. CI duration is not yet available.
- Scoped lint, tooling-test typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent P0–P2 source review: no actionable findings.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review (`d6510f3c7e6c` → `8e24ce385cd8`): complete; no actionable correctness or security findings. This was source review, not an additional runtime test.
- Test-line ratchet passes with the scoped 58-line allocation.

Scope limits: this is worker-boundary and generated-bridge proof, not a new full published-release upgrade or live Doctor run. It does not resolve or claim proof for the separate Doctor final-write authority-handoff concern in #189713. Initial worktree check attempts hit dependency setup failures; a private frozen install was prepared before the successful suite run.

Maintainer acceptance evidence (head `c48073960f1f646ed9572d269c7d499392526b47`):

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn
prs.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

prs.title: fix: show guest avatars and resolve owner filter names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes initials-only people and raw profile UUIDs for guests, consistently across first-party displays of verified Gateway people—not just the Owners filter.

Reported by **Holger Gruenhagen**.

## User Impact

- One presentation rule: saved display name → verified GitHub login → privacy-safe shortened Person label. Editable names remain unchanged; the shared-owner special identity stays distinct.
- One canonical authenticated image route for account cards/footer, compact person shortcuts, online/offline People, chat participants and mentions, sharing, owner selectors, profile views and person-reference cards. Directory consumers no longer suppress host-account photos.
- Uploaded OpenClaw photos win; the existing shared-owner host photo remains supported; verified GitHub precedes Gravatar. Unlinked channel/remote identities and agent/session glyphs remain separate—no guessed identity links.

Image access is an authenticated, exact-profile-ID read. It does **not** grant directory enumeration, emails, roles or private account metadata. No configuration, schema or data migration is required. This PR does not deploy the team server.

## Implementation

Reuse the resident profile and worker-read owners. Remove upload-only projection gates and the avatar endpoint's directory-scope coupling. Keep source selection behind the Gateway, using the existing bounded HTTP cache. GitHub URLs are constructed by the verified identity owner; requests reject redirects and retain time/size limits. Raw-profile UI adapters share the same small name formatter; editable profile fields are not rewritten.

The retired upload-only flag is removed from all consumers, including performance scripts. Added production logic is the shared name formatter, native-reader enrichment and verified-provider image selection—not a second identity resolver. The dedicated test-line allocation covers 445 net regression lines, including the expanded browser flow and two real HTTP revocation cases.

## Review findings addressed before this update

- **Live device revocation:** use the existing asynchronous authority revalidator after image preparation and immediately before disclosure. Real HTTP regressions for uploaded and GitHub-backed images failed with HTTP 200 after revocation before the fix, and now return HTTP 401 without image bytes or ETag. The same paired session-only device first successfully reads another person's image.
- **Consumer failures:** update the GitHub identity test to distinguish presentation fallback from raw nullable saved names, and Session Share fixtures to expect canonical images only for explicitly linked local identities. Both suites pass.
- **Script type failure:** remove the retired projection flag from all three performance-script consumers; script typecheck passes.

## Evidence and coverage

- Production-bundle Chromium test passes (7.66 s test / 47.21 s total): account card/footer and menu, chat People owner/participant photos, compact pinned-person shortcut, Owners option and selected label, retained owner ID, and no users.list request. Distinct image dimensions assert that photos belong to the correct people.
- Original Owners regression fails on base a1f8d7f5251a744516da84d85bbe35b78f343e0c with the raw UUID; candidate source restored afterward.
- Final avatar/authentication suites: **70 tests passed** (68.10 s wall), including the new red/green device-revocation regressions, existing config rotation, upload precedence and conditional-response coverage.
- Expanded sharing suites: **17 tests passed**; affected UI consumers: **66 passed** (combined 65.62 s wall). Sidebar/person-reference siblings: **48 passed**; prompt-prefix stability: **14 passed** (combined 73.87 s wall). Resident-profile suite, GitHub identity suite, Session Share integration and owner/filter suites also passed. Counts are separate runs, not a claim of unique aggregate coverage.
- Core, UI and script source typechecks, eight touched test-type lanes and the Session Share test-type lane pass. Targeted lint, staged formatting, diff whitespace, zero import cycles and test-line budget pass.
- Anonymous GitHub avatar contract: HTTP 200, image/png, 27,761 bytes, no redirect. Enterprise hosts were not live-tested.

prs.title: fix(auth): show inherited order after clearing agent override
prs.body:
Closes #154510

Alternative to #154587. That patch redirects `clear` to the shared write owner, which leaves the selected agent's local override intact and changes the inherited order for sibling agents. This PR keeps the per-agent mutation contract and fixes the misleading diagnostics instead.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `models auth order clear` reports config/round-robin fallback when a migrated shared order is still active.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can see when `clear` exposes an inherited shared auth order, including its source in text and JSON output, without changing account priority for other agents.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command already clears only the selected agent's local override. After shared auth-state migration, an inherited shared order can therefore remain effective and continue to take precedence over config. The command now reloads the effective store after clearing, labels inherited shared order in `get`, and documents that behavior.

The storage-backed regression exercises the real persistence boundary: it seeds a shared order, sets and clears a main-agent local override, verifies the local state is removed, verifies the shared order remains effective, and verifies a sibling agent is unaffected.

## Evidence

- Real CLI proof used an isolated Node 24 container, a real private-loopback Gateway, generic profiles, and the built `dist/index.js` entry point. No command/config/targeting/Gateway-refresh mocks were used.
- The real `set -> get -> clear -> get -> sibling get` sequence completed in 27.427s. Both mutating commands completed without a Gateway refresh warning.
- `pnpm test src/commands/models/auth-order.persistence.test.ts src/commands/models/auth-order.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 files / 56 tests passed in 50.93s.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --stripe 4/5 --concurrency 2`: passed (same core-test stripe that covers the changed persistence test).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth-order.persistence.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Redacted output from the real CLI run:

```text
$ openclaw models auth order set --agent main --provider openai profile-B profile-A
Auth profile order override: profile-B, profile-A

$ openclaw models auth order get --agent main --provider openai --json
order: [profile-B, profile-A]
orderSource: agent

$ openclaw models auth order clear --agent main --provider openai
Auth profile order override cleared; inherited shared order remains active: profile-A, profile-B.

$ openclaw models auth order get --agent main --provider openai --json
order: [profile-A, profile-B]
orderSource: shared

$ openclaw models auth order get --agent worker --provider openai --json
order: [profile-A, profile-B]
orderSource: shared
```

The final sibling read confirms that clearing `main` removed only its local override and did not mutate the shared order inherited by `worker`.

prs.title: fix(cli-runner): keep fresh and resumed Claude CLI runs on one session lane
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A claude-cli turn and the next inbound turn for the *same* session could own two different serialization lanes. `resolveCliRunQueueKey` keyed a resumed run on the CLI session id (`claude-cli:session:<id>`) but a fresh run — a recovery retry, or any turn whose CLI session id is not available yet — on the conversation owner (`claude-cli:owner:<ownerKey>`). Different lanes means no mutual exclusion, so a fresh `claude -p` process without `--resume` can be spawned while the session's previous CLI process is still running, which is the coexistence in #144137's `ps` output (PID 25087, no `--resume`, started 11:17; PID 25213 with `--resume 6faa51d1-...`, started 11:18; both alive). The context-free process answers on the channel while the session's own transcript only carries the resumed conversation, which is the shape of "delivered to the user but absent from `sessions_history`".

The change: for `claude-cli`, the conversation owner is the lane for fresh and resumed runs alike; the CLI session id stays as the fallback when no owner identity exists. A fresh run therefore queues behind the session's in-flight run and re-checks its own admission before spawning, so a turn that was superseded while it waited never starts a CLI process.

- `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts:85-95` — lane resolution (`owner:` now precedes `session:`)
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts:255-263` — lane inputs (`cliSessionId: useResume ? resolvedSessionId : undefined`); `execute.ts:654` is the `enqueueCliRun` that wraps the process execution
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts:276-294` — the supervisor spawn this lane guards

## Evidence

Windows 11, this worktree. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` cannot run here (junctioned `node_modules` escapes the checkout), so the unwrapped binaries were used for the gates below. The lane test drives the real `executePreparedCliRun`, the real `KeyedAsyncQueue` lane and the real process supervisor, with the child adapter doubled (as the neighbouring `execute.pending-cancellation.test.ts` does).

1. Red, fix reverted at byte level (sha256 checked before/after):

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.cli-run-lane.test.ts
```
```
FAIL ... queues a fresh run behind the session's in-flight resumed process
AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1 // Object.is equality
FAIL ... never spawns a queued fresh run whose own turn is gone
AssertionError: expected [ { pid: 1234, …(10) }, …(1) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
Tests  2 failed (2)
```

2. Green, fix applied: same command → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 2 passed (2)`.

3. Sabotage of the mechanism itself (`enqueueCliRun` bypassing `KeyedAsyncQueue`) → both lane tests red again (`expected 2 to be 1`, `length of 1 but got 2`); file restored to the byte-identical sha256.

4. Real fake-CLI process probe, `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.watchdog-tree.real.test.ts` (3/3 runs passed): a fake CLI spawns a subprocess descendant, prints one line and then goes silent; the watchdog reports `no-output-timeout`, both the CLI root and its descendant are gone, and no stdout/stderr chunk is delivered after settlement.

5. Neighbour sanity (`src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts`): 43 failed | 61 passed both with and without this patch, with the same failure signatures (32 × `EPERM` temp-dir cleanup, plus `CLI backend executable could not be resolved`). Those are this-box environment failures, not lane behaviour.

## Verification

- Lane regression tests: red without the fix, green with it (commands above).
- Two independent sabotages turn the shipped tests red; both source files restored to byte-identical sha256 (`helpers.ts` unchanged at `eab89219f3ed12eced8c2dc77990dc7d0a2b0f14cc182b5453fa5241c27d6927` across all reverts).
- `node node_modules/oxlint/bin/oxlint` on the four touched files: exit 0. `node node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check` on the same four: clean.
- Scope boundary: this removes the concurrent admission of a fresh CLI run beside the session's in-flight run, which is the coexistence the report's process list shows. It deliberately does not make `--resume` a delivery-authorization rule. A fresh CLI process still has no supervisor scope key (`buildCliSupervisorScopeKey` returns `undefined` without a CLI session id, `src/agents/cli-runner/reliability.ts:120-132`), so a successor still cannot evict a process the host has already abandoned; that remains a follow-up.
- Not verified in this worktree: `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.pending-cancellation.test.ts` cannot load (`Cannot find package 'commander'` from the junctioned `node_modules`), so it was not exercised.

Partial fix for #144137. The closing keyword is intentionally not used.


---

**Resubmission note:** the earlier PR for this branch was auto-closed by `openclaw-barnacle` under the repository's 20-active-PR limit (`r: too-many-prs`) — a queue-depth rule, not a review outcome. The active queue has been pruned, and this is the identical commit resubmitted verbatim; the previous PR's comments are still there for reference.

---

ClawSweeper requirement addressed:

> the changed `executePreparedCliRun` queue path is exercised with a **mocked child adapter**,

  compiled/loaded by the repository's tsx loader) — the same entry point the CLI runner uses.
- The process supervisor is the real `getProcessSupervisor()` from `src/process/supervisor`
  (`executeDeps.getProcessSupervisor`'s production default). **No supervisor double and no mocked

  test the reviewer objected to; this harness does not import it).

prs.title: improve: scope iOS screenshot dependency setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Main CI screenshot capture restores the general pnpm store and installs unrelated workspace packages before building native screenshots.

## User Impact

No app behavior changes. Screenshot CI uses a smaller dependency setup while retaining cold project generation, all three device families, and the existing capture assertions and evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing frozen Mermaid workspace filter and disable the broad dependency install/cache for this job. pnpm still retains root dependencies needed by native helpers. Watch RTC and Swift package download caches stay unchanged; no new cache or dependency manifest is introduced. Store Release is outside this change.

## Evidence

- Cold XcodeGen preparation passed with the scoped install and normal lifecycle scripts: existing version/file-list helpers, TLS fixture generation, Mermaid source build/resource copying, and generated Xcode project.
- Workflow lint (pinned actionlint and zizmor), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All ten required macOS workflow/native-cache/launch test files passed: 1,143 tests passed, 10 skipped. The evidence suite initially lacked broader plugin test dependencies; after a test-only full install its targeted rerun passed (10 tests). The screenshot cold-project proof above used only the scoped install.
- Full local ClawSweeper correctness/security review completed with no actionable findings against base `1f5b1d10c403bb5c5e0a3ead9b342be3a4444180` and snapshot `b3a9d40404e84cbe283a70af4ed84da825b739f4`. The published commit has the identical tree (`defc33ddd227f375e6cfd23b16975a24ecf2a642`). Runtime/performance proof was outside that read-only review.

### Acceptance rule recorded before hosted candidate execution

Accept when the capture job's general pnpm-store archive restore count is zero, the frozen install selects only the Mermaid workspace closure (with pnpm's retained root dependencies), and hosted capture plus evidence reduction succeeds for iPhone, iPad, and Watch without changing capture behavior. Compare dependency work counts using the same package manifests/lockfile. Historical timing is context only; no controlled end-to-end speedup is claimed.

### Matched-base dependency work counts

Five serial, interleaved baseline/candidate installs used identical package manifests and lockfile, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, fresh task-owned node_modules, and a task-owned local store. Workloads were the committed shared `install-dependencies.sh` and the candidate workflow's exact install run block. Store warmth was mixed; this compares work counts, not download or elapsed-time performance.

| Per install | Baseline, all five samples | Candidate, all five samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Selected workspace projects reported by pnpm | 207 | 2 |
| Installed packages | 1,478 | 945 |

The filter retains root dependencies. It removes 533 package installations (36.1%) without adding a dependency projection. The capture job no longer requests the general pnpm-store archive. No end-to-end speedup percentage is claimed.

PR CI deliberately omits screenshot capture for workflow-only changes. [Dedicated screenshot qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41543926874) runs only the existing preflight, capture, and reducer jobs, with parsed job semantics verified identical to this candidate. It checks out `88a3bd069721d34d5047694da6fc11c93d156920`; the temporary proof workflow branch is separate from this PR. No release upload is involved. **Passed:** preflight, iPhone/iPad/Watch capture, and the final evidence reducer. Logs confirm the scoped install added 945 packages and the capture job skipped the general pnpm-store restore (zero archive transfers). Node setup took 2 seconds and the install 17 seconds in this single hosted run; these are observations, not a controlled timing comparison. Pinning the PR source separately from the temporary workflow made this a frozen-target run, so native-cache restores were skipped and the cold native build path was exercised.

[PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41543463457) also completed successfully; the exact-head CI gate is green.

prs.title: fix(memory): report curated memory files excluded by provenance
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent silently loses its root `MEMORY.md` or `USER.md` from automatic context when the file's memory provenance is recorded as `untrusted`, and nothing in the Gateway log, Doctor, or docs tells the operator.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see a Gateway warning the first time a curated memory file is excluded by provenance (once per file and process, not per turn), and plain `openclaw doctor` lists the excluded file with the time and session of its last recorded tracked write.

Affected: every agent whose root `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, or personal `users/<profile-id>/USER.md` is classified `untrusted` by the active memory runtime, with default settings. The issue thread has field reports from about ten installations on 2026.9.x to 2026.10.9; on one host the exclusion went unnoticed for six days.

This PR does not change classification and adds no way to clear quarantine. Both need the owner-review decision that is still open in 153426 (`needs-product-decision`). It only makes the existing exclusion visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The classified branch of `resolveIneligibleAutomaticMemoryFiles` already drops these files but, unlike the error and `unsupported` branches, never calls `warn`. The provenance ledger keeps one row per file and overwrites time and session on every tracked write, so by the time someone looks, the row often names a later, unrelated write. The clawsweeper review on 153426 recommends addressing exclusion diagnostics separately from the recovery contract.

- Bootstrap: one warning per excluded file, workspace, and origin class per process, reusing the existing bounded bootstrap dedupe set.
- Doctor: new check `core/doctor/memory-provenance`. It asks the same classifier the bootstrap gate uses (`classifyActiveMemoryWorkspacePaths`), so it reports only files that are actually excluded (nothing when no memory runtime is active). It names the last recorded tracked write and says that this is not necessarily the write that quarantined the file. Category `fix-now`, because `recommended` findings are hidden from normal Doctor output.
- Docs: `concepts/memory-provenance` gains "Freeform edits and quarantine": a shell or external edit leaves the record stale, so the next tracked write records `untrusted`. Doctor pages and `concepts/memory` describe how to detect the exclusion.

## Evidence

Live check on an isolated test Gateway (loopback, own state dir and port, `memory-core` enabled), source 2026.10.9 main `9e64fc4ab76`. Both builds were made on macOS (Crabbox) and run on Linux x64. The `untrusted` record was produced through the real ratchet, not written by hand: tracked owner write, untracked append (as a shell edit would do), tracked owner write against the stale hash → `originClass: "untrusted"`. Then `/context list` in two new sessions, and Doctor.

| | Base `9e64fc4ab76` | This PR (build of `b1422310be1`) |
|---|---|---|
| `/context list`, workspace has `MEMORY.md` | injected: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md` (no `MEMORY.md`) | same files (classification unchanged) |
| Gateway log lines `excluding …` | 0 | 1 for two sessions: `excluding MEMORY.md from automatic memory context: memory provenance is untrusted; run \`openclaw doctor\` for the last recorded write (sessionKey=agent:main:proof-fix-a)` |
| `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-provenance --json` | `Unknown health check id` | 1 warning: file, `untrusted`, last tracked write `2026-10-31T14:19:33.782Z`, session `agent:main:dashboard:owner-later`, "not necessarily the write that quarantined the file" |
| plain `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | — | finding listed under `Fix now:` with location and docs link |
| model or CLI runs during the check | 0 | 0 |

The last commit (`df868e897b3`) only rewords the Doctor `fixHint` so it does not point at a recovery path that the docs do not describe. It was not part of the live build.

**Upgrade check, latest stable → this PR** (same isolated test state). Step 1 runs the installed `2026.10.9` (`8b18b5578f6`, a package copy). The `untrusted` record is seeded with 2026.10.9's own provenance module, because the store layer changed after 10.9 (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168478 ). Step 2 runs this PR's build `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (the update path), then its Gateway on the same state.

| | 2026.10.9 | after PR `doctor --fix` | after PR Gateway run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` sha256 | `7f0193599f75d737` / `07b7171a92a857c2` | unchanged | unchanged |
| provenance row `MEMORY.md` | `untrusted`, `observedAt` 1793456373782, `agent:main:dashboard:owner-later`, hash `7f0193599f75d737` | unchanged | unchanged |
| `/context list` injected | `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md` | – | same |
| log `excluding …` | 0 | – | 1 (`excluding MEMORY.md from automatic memory context: memory provenance is untrusted; …`) |
| Doctor `core/doctor/memory-provenance` | unknown check id | finding printed | 1 warning, last write `2026-10-31T14:19:33.782Z`, `agent:main:dashboard:owner-later` |

The config file changed only through migrations that already exist on main (`meta.migrations.modelPolicyAllowlist` and `utilityModelSeparation`, `agents.defaults.modelPolicy`, `plugins.entries.anthropic`, `skills.entries`, `wizard`). This PR adds no config writes, and its check only reads state. I did not separately run a base-main upgrade to confirm that the same config diff appears without this PR.

<details><summary>Test gateway output (sanitized)</summary>

```text
--- seed
after tracked owner write: {"originClass":"agent","observedAt":1792946400000,"sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:owner-first"}
after shell edit + tracked owner write: {"originClass":"untrusted","observedAt":1793456373782,"sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:owner-later"}

--- base: gateway log lines containing 'excluding' (count 0)
--- base: doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-provenance --json
{"ok": false, "checksRun": 0, "checksSkipped": 71}
{"checkId": "core/doctor/lint-selection", "severity": "error", "message": "Unknown health check id selected by --only: core/doctor/memory-provenance."}

--- fix: gateway log lines containing 'excluding' (count 1)
2026-10-31T19:53:50.105Z WARN | excluding MEMORY.md from automatic memory context: memory provenance is untrusted; run `openclaw doctor` for the last recorded write (sessionKey=agent:main:proof-fix-a)
--- fix: doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-provenance --json
{"ok": false, "checksRun": 1, "checksSkipped": 71}
{"checkId": "core/doctor/memory-provenance", "severity": "warning", "message": "MEMORY.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-10-31T14:19:33.782Z, session agent:main:dashboard:owner-later. The record names only the latest tracked write, not necessarily the write that quarantined the file.", "path": "<test>/ws/main/MEMORY.md"}

--- fix: plain doctor --non-interactive (excerpt)
Fix now:
- MEMORY.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-10-31T14:19:33.782Z, session agent:main:dashboard:owner-later. The record names only the latest tracked write, not necessarily the write that quarantined the file.
  Location: <test>/ws/main/MEMORY.md
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/memory-provenance
```

</details>

Tests (Mac mini via Crabbox, `--maxWorkers=1`):

- `src/commands/doctor-memory-provenance.test.ts` (new, real provenance store; classifier stands in for the host fallback), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts` (new case: one warning across two runs), `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-health.update-scope.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-lint.state-isolation.test.ts`: 150 tests passed, 152 s. Earlier round also `bootstrap-files.remote`, `memory-artifact-provenance`, `doctor-lint.sqlite-preservation`: passed.
- Reverse check: the new bootstrap test against the unchanged source fails (`reports a provenance exclusion once per file across runs`).
- `tsgo` on the changed test files, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `check-test-mock-exports`, `format:docs:check`, `docs:check-mdx`, `lint:docs`, `docs:check-links`: clean.

Gaps: no model turn was run. Bootstrap was exercised through `/context list`, which resolves the same bootstrap context without calling the model. Personal `USER.md` exclusion is covered by a unit test only. `codex review` ran twice; both rounds' findings are addressed here.

prs.body:
Related: #162164 — this is the separate Profile-management slice for channel identity links.

Current head [`9d439202f1fa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9d439202f1fa32df9ce4fe19aebc1db0f3ba3293) resolves the November 2 main-integration conflicts on the existing branch. GitHub reports it mergeable. Current-head [canonical CI 41520993713](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41520993713) completed successfully for this exact head, and the effective CI gate passed. The earlier link to run 41520984221 identifies Security Review, not the runtime CI workflow. Previous browser evidence retains its original revision. Maintainer product/design acceptance remains separate.

Previous head [`28be4999545`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/28be49995457d748ac2254985deba504b5517c18) addresses the remaining duplicate preference-test request. All 61 retained Profile, preference, channel-link and authority cases passed in the isolated fixture. [Canonical CI 41016616774](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41016616774) passed. [Review 20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164607#issuecomment-5974524801) confirms that the author request is resolved, finds no actionable defect and is waiting on the maintainer's product/design decision. Overall remains 3/6, proof 5/6 and patch quality 4/6. Prior integration and Gateway/browser/storage evidence below retain their original revisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

## Work sessions

- Original discussion with @TheAngryPit. Work-session reference retained in the local evidence packet.
- Implementation and verification. Work-session reference retained in the local evidence packet.

## Evidence

### Current-head review - November 2, Review 21

[ClawSweeper Review 21](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164607#issuecomment-5974524801) completed on exact head `9d439202f1fa32df9ce4fe19aebc1db0f3ba3293` at 2026-11-02 23:40:53 UTC. It records zero actionable findings, no security finding and no concrete simplification defect. Proof confidence is Diamond (5/6, with media proof); patch quality is 4/6 and overall readiness remains 3/6 because product/design acceptance is unresolved. The two displayed before-merge checklist entries describe that same owner decision, not two source defects. The [re-review acknowledgment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164607#issuecomment-6591208782) confirms completion; no additional review was requested.

**Maintainer decision needed:** Should Profile expose administrator-entered channel identity links for the authenticated personal profile alongside verified Discord linking? The reviewer recommends accepting the focused, current-profile-only administrator interface with its explicit external-account-ownership disclaimer. This recommendation is not maintainer approval. Canonical CI and the effective gate are passing; the completed author proof and its revision boundaries remain recorded below. No merge or deployment is authorized or claimed.

### Conflict refresh - November 2, `9d439202f1fa`

Integrated pinned main `0a6aaf50f6c5c4e906dd906dd52b9539e4bf93be` into published head `28be49995457d748ac2254985deba504b5517c18` through the existing-PR publisher, without rebasing or replacing the contributor branch. The only conflict file was `profile-page.tsx`: retain main's refresh-label attributes and initial identity-readiness boundary, while retaining the channel-mutation busy guard and the channel section as its sibling. No feature, backend, schema, permission, workflow or live-service change was added. The existing ProfileState remains the authority owner; avatar, locale and preference-test consolidations remain.

The repository test wrapper passed all **105 cases across eight affected Profile suites** in a fresh secretless sandbox, using the pinned Bun fork. Production UI and UI-pages test typechecks passed. Ten-file formatting and type-aware lint passed with no diagnostics; staged whitespace checks passed. Simplification and comment audit added no new state, adapter, test, comment or suppression. The published PR still has the same 14 contribution paths and +1,939/-25 lines against main; the complete available patches preserve the same added/deleted feature lines. Two large API patch excerpts are truncated, so this is not a complete blob-equivalence claim.

A frozen complete-candidate Auto Review against that exact main at P0–P3 returned scoped-clean with no findings (bound OpenClaw engine). It checked the integration and state/authority reconciliation; it did not independently execute the reported tests or current browser behavior, and unchanged dependency contracts were unavailable. The first review preparation stopped on a task-generated binary Bun cache before reviewer execution; removing only that transient cache admitted the unchanged source candidate.

This conflict-only resolution adds no rendered feature behavior, so no new screenshot campaign or dedicated Gateway/browser workflow was started. Historical QA `40713289565` remains evidence for product `d605a139` and baseline `d5f7d57`, not this head. Current-head [canonical CI 41520993713](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41520993713) completed successfully for `9d439202f1fa32df9ce4fe19aebc1db0f3ba3293`; the effective CI, dependency and security-sensitive status contexts passed. The only non-success item in the bounded latest check snapshot was a canceled PR-context/evidence job, not a failed product test. No merge or deployment was performed.

### Preference-test consolidation - October 30, `28be4999545`

Removed the five duplicate co-author consent cases from the main Profile suite. The unchanged dedicated preference suite retains the same five inputs, preference get/set keys, UI outcomes, persistence and no-reload assertions. This restores the consolidation intent of [#184413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184413). Distinct preference lifecycle, rollback, authority and channel-link cases remain. Only one test file changed, with 79 fewer lines; production code is unchanged.

The canonical wrapper passed all 61 tests across the four retained suites on Node 24.22.1 with normal frozen dependencies. One-file formatting and type-aware lint passed with zero lint warnings/errors. Existing Solid diagnostics were preserved.

The unchanged desktop layout case from the prior failed CI passed once on its exact main baseline `910069e` and once on its executed merge `12b7b2b`, using pinned Chromium 1248. Both local wrappers used their normal Node fallback after pinned Bun staging failed offline. These results do not establish hosted runtime parity, a flake or a repair of [the prior hosted failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40983294988). No assertion, wait, CSS or workflow change was made. Canonical CI passed on this head. Review 20 resolves the test-consolidation request and records no actionable code finding; its sole remaining before-merge item is maintainer product/design acceptance. The previous hosted failure's cause remains unproven despite the new successful CI.

### Test deduplication - October 30, `92c7dcea650`

Removed the duplicate avatar and locale test files requested in [Review 18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164607#issuecomment-5974524801). Their nine expanded cases remain in the existing Profile suite. Four distinct assertions were retained there. ### Inspected pre-patch/after Profile comparison

The same synthetic personal identity and fixture were run against independently built real Gateways: [baseline 37259530484](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37259530484) at `e87ab44327c049ca6454550addb4a314048ee2fb`, and [candidate 37259532201](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37259532201) at `ae51861738ec9a3095388a3ff64ba4a2a6220095`. Both passed. Later changes through `f9081de0` were test-support repairs, not Profile production changes; this does not relabel the older runtime receipt.

| ![Baseline Profile identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dc45cbd-de36-4058-a367-876362216db2) | ![Candidate Profile identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5144751f-4be1-41f2-bd27-63413b56f340) |

![Candidate Channel accounts form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/011fe81c-e8d5-40a0-b1c9-db06a117bf16)

The actual seven captures were inspected, including the loaded Identity section and visibly framed candidate controls. There is no community invitation, no CSS/DOM alteration or cropped substitute. The name and email are synthetic. Avatar color and asynchronously loaded agent-sidebar content differ incidentally; this is not a pixel-identical comparison. Fixture/config hashes are identical between runs. The fork-only QA harness is `2ccc4eb272367e5ff97bc361df409355649f419f`, standard Ubuntu24.04, without secrets.

### Real link persistence remains separately demonstrated

[The earlier exact-head run 37251209191](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191) at `a8706622fd5df1741b2fe51db6f0aef4e20cd52b` passed actual Profile add → fresh reload → remove → fresh reload against real Gateway storage. Its inspected, visibly framed captures remain embedded below. This is separate from the pre-patch/after appearance comparison; neither relies on mocked persistence.

The UI consumes the existing Core link/unlink contract. **No stored-data schema or migration is introduced.** This is not installed-old-version upgrade proof, external-account control, automatic actor/memory projection, another person's live sign-in, or a change to Shared owner authority.

<details>
<summary>Existing persistence captures and earlier regression receipts</summary>

Historical behavior head `a8706622fd5df1741b2fe51db6f0aef4e20cd52b`.

### Actual Profile link persistence at this head

[Secretless standard-Ubuntu QA run 37251209191](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191) passed the incumbent production-browser/real-Gateway Profile E2E at that exact product SHA. The workflow was pinned separately to `0914994356f4ce56342b11f0052bcfb40d20d27e`; Node24.21.0, pnpm12.5.1. Receipt: `test_exit=0`, 90 seconds; [artifact11319934937](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37251209191/artifacts/11319934937) contains the receipt and five actual PNGs.

The browser adds the synthetic channel link, reloads the page and sees the same row, removes it, then reloads again and sees the empty list. The linked section is in frame in each capture; the canonical invitation-dismissal preference is set before rendering. No mocked RPC response or fabricated storage write supplies these results.

The PR adds no stored-data format or migration; it consumes the existing Core link/unlink contract. This run is not installed-old-version migration proof. That revision's CI needed subsequent fixture/format repairs. Historical canonical CI is linked above; this narrow QA run is not proof of the current Solid head.

### Earlier persisted browser/Gateway behavior at `108cfaf`

The production browser UI at `108cfaf564b3eb5485b9ba3f88aaeeee8bc130e6` was exercised against a real task-owned Gateway. The nine recorded checks passed: initial empty list; UI link success; link persistence after reload; duplicate conflict rejection; preservation of the conflicting input; UI unlink success; unlink persistence after reload; exclusion of the Shared Gateway Owner as a UI target; and rejection of a direct attempt to link that owner.

Observed requests used the existing `users.listChannelIdentities`, `users.linkChannelIdentity` and `users.unlinkChannelIdentity` methods. The direct shared-owner attempt returned `INVALID_REQUEST` with the existing explanation that the shared owner profile cannot be merged and personal sign-in is required. The served candidate bundle matched SHA-256 `6f0dc35ffa69bf03039690eaee4ed05b4c8450405c0832b25e9672c8fe081465`; the retained result JSON has SHA-256 `87280f35559a09ec7c903471cb4a369d745c763c52d22545f42edbf96fd7584f`.

The default lint preparation timed out after 300 seconds; an additional broad boundary-listing attempt exhausted memory. Neither is claimed passing. No rule or budget was relaxed.

## Publication blocker — do not review or merge this comparison
The managed publisher targeted `main` rather than the intended `extended-stable/2026.9.33`, producing an unrelated 3,242-file comparison. The published tree is byte-identical to locally validated candidate `9e53c299cb2175132dc697229c250bbc30b2d5a4`; its diff against the intended base is exactly four files, +88/-14. Base correction through an authorized workflow is required before review. The publisher also appended empty commit `2069e5e49a016b98548882b0113d3dd3712f7643` without the requested co-author trailer; the implementation commit preserves it. Keep draft; no qualification is claimed for the current `main` comparison.

## Summary
Bounded dependency repair based on extended-stable/2026.9.33 at e93b50ad2400871616c2e6588d57488dba94ecad. This is a local package adaptation, not an OpenClaw cherry-pick.

- music-metadata 11.15.0 → 11.16.0 for Matrix and the Baileys-scoped runtime dependency: rejects malformed MP4 sample entries and unsafe EBML lengths.
- nodemailer 10.0.10 → 10.1.4 only below mailauth and mailparser: preserves inbound sender/address boundaries.
- Adds four isolated regression cases. Actual pnpm 12.15.0 lock regeneration changes only these two package versions and their selectors/importer/snapshots.

## Reachability and upstream provenance
Matrix send/media.ts calls parseBuffer on supplied media; IMAP watcher calls simpleParser before sender-gate admission. Baseline malicious input reproduces the affected behavior.

Music fixes: GHSA-f94x-6692-553q and GHSA-5gfj-9q3v-qfp3. Upstream Borewit <Borewit@users.noreply.github.com>: music-metadata commits 90a7d52c69e921a0b019592d887acd97b1c8b8a5, 163f013364ac9fc8dd0c3987433cd065a615af58, 2d14dc1f7391a94235948a0b823155538f69b3df (PRs 2734/2735).

Mail fixes: GHSA-8c8m-p3m8-cjg8, GHSA-m943-m63m-w62w, GHSA-85x2-q946-cp5h, GHSA-4ffr-jq9g-5ffx, GHSA-g73g-hqqh-jr95. Upstream Andris Reinman <andris@reinman.eu>: Nodemailer commits 0a8761762ac78f2db2ba37f712f2a52a404ce011, 1cd57d2b8c49dff048c21cdbafdb54439a7f07e2, a502247555fd81773eac337486781f3b6008e16a, b5a896fcb02df1628329d7cd665ca08490b14b56, ee35f5745658bf46952651fa53207255e9dc3406. Exact patch headers and release artifact provenance verified locally.

## Validation
- Baseline frozen installation + identical regression script: 4/4 fail as expected (sender spoof, quoted delimiter spoof, bounded child MP4 OOM, EBML unsafe allocation).
- Fixed frozen installation + `node scripts/test-security-runtime-parsers.mjs`: 4/4 pass; committed head rechecked.
- Owning-project Matrix media and IMAP watcher/sender-gate tests: 45 pass across 3 files / 2 shards.
- Focused repository lint, formatting, syntax, diff checks: pass.
- Production audit contains no remaining music-metadata/nodemailer advisories; 22 unrelated residual advisories remain. This is not a clean full-tree audit.

## Scope and gates
Hono/ip-address/qs/MCP/re2js excluded without the affected reachable API prerequisites; undici per-advisory source/trigger proof remains follow-up. No fast-uri or smol-toml changes. Stable/beta music versions already fixed; their newer nodemailer parser advisories still require separately based candidates.

**Keep DRAFT.** Full independent canonical review and hosted checks are not yet complete. No RFR, merge, tag, or release approval is claimed.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: fix: visitor limit updates stall active Gateway runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: changing Visitor Access limits queues a full plugin replacement behind active agent turns, failing readiness and delaying new runs.

## User Impact

`maxVisitors` and `defaultTtlDays` changes take effect in place, including for newly prepared turns. Existing grants keep their authority and expiry. Cloudflare settings and explicit reloads retain exclusive replacement. No new configuration option, SDK contract, cache, or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visitor Access declares its numeric settings through the existing hot-reload contract and reads them from committed runtime config. The loader lends its retained Gateway service only when the requesting run's plugin settings match that committed config. Pending edits, different scopes, and original-but-now-stale settings cannot borrow incompatible service state; source, manifest, activation, and scope checks remain intact.

Config writes also stop injecting managed cleanup into explicit unset paths. Canonical cleanup still removes managed install metadata, while audit records stop claiming an absent `plugins.installs` field changed on every write.

Exclusive replacement remains bounded and deferred when retained work cannot settle. Visitor Access keeps one owner of its shared policy mutation queue; numeric edits bypass that replacement entirely.

## Evidence

Five fresh-process baseline/candidate pairs used an actual Gateway, Control UI `config.patch` RPC, eleven held agent turns, and 33 retained references per sample. Every actual agent DB preserved 5,000 seeded sessions; the shared synthetic workspace contained 62,000 files / 1.116 GB. Both arms use the same final host core with old/new plugin sources, isolating the plugin config contract.

| RPC attempt window, median / sampled p95 | Baseline: drain failure | Candidate: applied live |
|---|---:|---:|
| Elapsed ms | 60,311.9 / 60,331.7 | 96.1 / 111.2 |
| Process CPU ms | 4,487.2 / 4,979.1 | 253.7 / 274.8 |
| Sampled allocation MiB | 211.8 / 221.3 | 27.7 / 28.6 |

Readiness failures: **2,939/2,945 → 0/6**. All candidates retained the same instance and exposed the new limit to a new turn while old turns stayed held; new-turn observation was 272.6 / 306.8 ms. No sample emitted a restart signal. All ten explicit generation replacements waited for held work and completed after release. Separate installed-package proof edited a captured dependency, observed its new callback output after retry, and preserved the original write and sibling service.

Ten unchanged-write A/A controls per arm measured wall time 6.31 / 191.29 → 7.23 / 189.64 ms; process CPU 36.96 / 519.81 → 46.99 / 518.27 ms; sampled allocation 2.85 / 89.38 → 3.04 / 91.57 MiB. The A/A CPU median increased **27.1%** amid large lazy-compilation/background-work outliers; no isolated no-op CPU improvement is claimed.

These are failed blocked windows versus successful updates, including readiness polling and background work. Allocation estimates cover the main isolate; process CPU includes workers. Startup/warmup are excluded. The deterministic local model, APFS host, and ~221 MiB seeded DB do not establish live-vendor, btrfs, or 35 GiB scaling. With five changed samples per arm, sampled p95 is the observed maximum. Reproduction is committed in `scripts/perf/plugin-config-reload-gateway.ts`; bundled native code requires fresh processes for source comparisons.

Focused red/green regressions cover stale limits, service borrowing, scoped rejection, and audit paths. Visitor suites: 71 passed; config owner/siblings: 112; planner: 29; prepared/loader borrowing: 15. Existing deferred-drain/handoff/overlap cases and the external source-refresh case pass. Full build and `pnpm check:changed --timed` passed; benchmark repairs passed scoped checks and independent review.

CI exposed three startup-fixture failures caused by omitted committed-config publication. The fixture now follows real startup order without changing production guards or assertions; all 18 startup/borrowing tests pass. The repair passed lint, affected typecheck, the test-line allocation check, and independent Codex review. Exact-head [CI 41542951503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41542951503) passed on `8a9da665e13cfd7f90336946bffbe26990b88299`, including the aggregate gate. The prior failures were PR-caused, not inherited; no CI exception or rerun was used. Merged as `535cf43388e7d4b63e1c14754e1fa84a40889136`.

Independent Codex autoreview at P2 found no remaining actionable findings after the scoped borrowing repair and proof corrections. Runtime production delta is **+26 lines**: live limit policy/reads +13, redundant cleanup −4, committed borrowing +17. The growth enforces those two ownership contracts. Tests add 168 lines; the reproducible benchmark adds 562 tooling lines. Release notes remain release-owned.
