prs.title: fix(codex): pass /v1/responses client functions to the Codex runtime
prs.body:
Closes #113318

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Codex runtime, caller functions sent as `tools` to `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions` are never shown to the model. With a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` the request then fails with HTTP 502 (`tool_choice required a <name> tool call, but the agent did not produce one`); with an optional `tool_choice` the model can only answer in prose.

## User Impact

User impact: callers can pass their own functions, including a pinned `tool_choice`, to an agent on the Codex runtime and get the call back, the same as on the built-in runtime: a `function_call` output item on `/v1/responses`, or `choices[].message.tool_calls` on `/v1/chat/completions`. OpenClaw does not run these functions; the caller does. When a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` is still not satisfied, the request fails with the same 502 as before; optional-tool requests may still return prose.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP endpoint already hands caller functions to the run as `clientTools`, and the built-in runtime turns them into delegated tools. The Codex runtime builds its own tool list and left them out, so the model only saw OpenClaw's tools and answered in prose.

This adds a harness adapter, `createAgentHarnessClientTools`, next to the built-in runtime's `toClientToolDefinitions`. The built-in runtime keeps using `toClientToolDefinitions`. The new adapter reuses the same delegated-tool contract and its supporting helpers:
- the shared delegated pending result;
- the attempt's `toolsAllow` cap;
- the existing name-conflict error, which the endpoint maps to HTTP 400;
- the same eligibility: no client functions when tools are disabled, for memory runs, or for a model without tool support;
- source order for parallel calls: Codex reserves each call's slot when it arrives, before hooks run.

Codex adds these tools to the thread's dynamic tools. The existing bridge wraps them with the usual hooks, and their terminal result uses the existing terminal-tool release to stop the native turn, so Codex makes no second model request. The recorded calls go back as the attempt's `clientToolCalls`, which the shared runner already turns into each endpoint's tool-call output.

Accepted edge cases:
- A Codex-supervised thread keeps its saved native tool declarations and cannot add caller functions; with a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` such a request still fails with the existing 502.
- Like `sessions_yield`, the stop is a native interrupt, so Codex may record an interruption marker after the call. Changing the function set between requests on one session is a dynamic-tool change and is handled like any other.

The reporter's fork PR (hddms-matt-bot/openclaw#1) took a similar direction on older source; this change was written against current `main` and reuses the existing delegated-tool and terminal-release owners instead of a Codex-only delegation path.

Maintainer decision: this adds `createAgentHarnessClientTools` to the private harness SDK subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-tool-runtime` (documented in the harness attempt-runtime page). If the owner prefers another surface, the Codex side only needs the tools, the reserve call and the recorded calls.

## Evidence

- New regression tests, red on `main` and green with the fix:
  - `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts`: a client function is declared to Codex, its call returns `clientToolCalls`, the turn is interrupted, and no OpenClaw tool runs. On `main`: fails ("expected [ 'managed_task' ] to include 'submit_probe_result'").
  - The same Codex file also checks that no client function is declared when tools are disabled or the model cannot call tools (a guard; it passes on `main` too).
  - `agent-tool-definition-adapter.test.ts`: the harness helper applies `toolsAllow`, keeps the model's order when a later call finishes first, and raises the shared conflict error. On `main`: fails (helper missing).
- Focused files pass with the fix (Codex dynamic tools 19, adapter 29, adapter fires-once, `openresponses-http.test.ts`).
- Core, core-test, extension and extension-test typechecks, lint and format pass on the changed files; `check:changed` and the baseline ratchets pass except checks that could not run offline on the test machine (listed below).
- Test lines are net +96 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-responses-client-tools.txt`: one Codex boundary test and one two-case eligibility table that reuses the existing run-attempt harness (`startTool`, `createStartedThreadHarness`) and one short helper test in the existing conflict-check block.

### Real Gateway proof with a real model

Tested revisions: base `6c298cb69d8` (`main`) and fix `066157068b1`. The PR head `5ec4cd4a5f5` differs from the tested fix only by the test-line allocation record.

An isolated Gateway built from the tree, the real Codex app-server (`@openai/codex` 0.164.0) and the real OpenAI model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` on the Codex runtime. The request is the reporter's: `/v1/responses`, `tools: [submit_probe_result]`, pinned `tool_choice`, `stream: false`; a new session per request.

| Tree | Requests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 2 | 2 × HTTP 502 `tool_choice required a submit_probe_result tool call, but the agent did not produce one`, no output items |
| fix `066157068b1` | 3 | 3 × HTTP 200, one `function_call` `submit_probe_result` `{"greeting":"Hello"}`, status `completed` |

```
[6c298cb69d8] RUN1 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 140686/363
[6c298cb69d8] RUN2 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 161571/348
[066157068b1] RUN1 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/41
[066157068b1] RUN2 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/53
[066157068b1] RUN3 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/48
```

On `main` the model spent several steps (about 140k input tokens) looking for a function it could not see, then the Gateway failed closed. With the fix the turn ends at the call: one model step, and the function is returned to the caller instead of being run.

### Gateway proof with a scripted model (more cases)

The same Gateway and Codex app-server with a local fake model that calls a function only if Codex lists it (otherwise it answers "Hello" in prose):

| Run | HTTP | Output | Model saw the function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v2026.7.1-1` (reporter's release) | 502, same error | none | n/a (that release's mock does not record tools) |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 502, same error | none | no |
| fix `066157068b1` | 200 | `function_call submit_probe_result` | yes |
| fix, same session, different function | 200 | `function_call submit_other_result` | only the new one |
| fix, same session, no functions | 200 | message "Hello" | none left over |

With the fix, the fake model received one request per call and no `function_call_output`, so OpenClaw did not run the function.

Proof artifice: the second table uses a scripted local model endpoint; the first table uses a real OpenAI model.

Proof gap: the streaming (`stream: true`) path and `/v1/chat/completions` were not run live; they share the same attempt result. `check:changed` checks that need network on the test machine (Bun format/lint comparison, `knip`) and the SQLite worker ratchet (no `rg` in the container) could not run there; CI runs them.

prs.title: improve(ui): redesign MCP settings around each server
prs.body: Stacked on #191359: land that first. This PR targets main, so its diff includes #191359 until then. Best after #191354, which reports autosave. ## What Problem This Solves Settings > MCP didn't answer what people come for. Four count rows sat on top and asked for nothing. Each server row repeated its config as a word ("Enabled") next to a boxed CLI command, a Disable button and a trash icon. "Is it working?" and "what tools does it have?" had no answer on the page. Editing went through a flat form further down that mixed every server's fields, showed "MCP Server Enabled" as off for servers that were on, and turned arguments into "Args #1 Required" rows. ## User Impact The page is now the list of servers. - Each row has the name, what it runs, what the current session knows about it, and an on/off switch. - Opening a row, one at a time, shows its tools, the fields that apply to that kind of server, Remove in the danger variant, and its terminal command, inset so it's clear where a server ends. Arguments are one per line. OAuth is a switch, and Sign in appears when it's on. - Add server opens a dialog, with errors inside it. - MCP Apps is one switch under Settings. Advanced settings and the remaining commands are collapsed in the shared disclosure. `login` and `probe` now sit with each server. - The existing "Edits save automatically" line is gone, since autosave reports itself in #191354. Its reload fact moved to the "?" beside Add server. ## Why This Change Was Made Row, panel and status are one shape, so this stays one PR: a split would leave an interim page that still can't say whether a server is working. It replaces #191259 and #191262, since the row they restyle no longer exists. Status comes from `tools.effective`, read once per connection and session, because a read can hold the Gateway for seconds. A server saved differently since that read shows no status until the next one. That RPC only reports what the current session's catalog already holds, so the words stay within that: - **Tools listed:** this session has tools from the server. - **No tools:** the session has none from it. The panel says it may be failing, may need sign-in or may have none, and gives the probe command. - **Not connected yet:** no agent run has used it in this session. - **Failing:** only when the Gateway returns an `mcp-server-diagnostic` notice. - No status: the session can't be read. **"Failing" has only been seen with mock data.** On a real Gateway, servers that logged `failed to start server` (a missing binary, a closed port) returned no diagnostic through `tools.effective`, so they read "No tools". Detecting failure needs a per-server health RPC, which doesn't exist: `openclaw mcp probe` is CLI-only. This PR adds no RPC. New English strings are committed without translations, so `ui:i18n:check` reports fallback drift until the locale refresh workflow runs after merge. ## Evidence Checked on an isolated real Gateway against its config file: editing arguments, toggling both ways, adding, a duplicate name, renaming, removing and the OAuth switch. Environment values stayed redacted on screen. Sign-in itself wasn't run against an OAuth server. Several runs on this loaded machine hit Gateway main-thread stalls of up to 29 s after an MCP save, unrelated to the page's reads and with the cause not found. On the final commit the OAuth switch wrote both ways for three cycles with Sign in following it, and again after a reconnect with nothing pending. If a stall drops the connection just as a save goes out, the save still reaches the file but its acknowledgement is lost, and the shared autosave layer stops writing until someone acts: "Settings changed elsewhere" with Reload after a form save, "Autosave paused after reconnect" with Save after a list write. This PR doesn't change that layer. Empty, many servers, long values, "Failing", add errors and CRT were checked with mock data. Page PRs branch from main, so the phone image shows today's top bar until the header PR lands. | Before, mock data | After, real Gateway | | --- | --- | | | | | After, 390 px, real Gateway | After, CRT, mock data ("Failing" comes from the mock) | | --- | --- | | | |

prs.title: fix(channels): match canonically equivalent Unicode in directory queries
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainers may push to this branch to finish or adjust the change; "Allow edits by maintainers" stays enabled. The touched pair is one production file plus its existing test file, so a maintainer can re-point or narrow it without rebasing anything else.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

- **Land-ready**: comparison-only fix inside the single owner of config-driven directory query matching; shipped-CLI base/head receipt covering both canonical directions plus controls; `+3/-2` production in one file, `+31` in the existing test file, zero new files, zero config/schema/auth/storage surface.
- **Alternatives considered**: (a) patch each channel lister instead — rejected, nine config-driven listers funnel through this one helper and would re-derive the same predicate; (b) rewrite stored config keys to NFC — rejected, that mutates user data and no sibling PR did it; (c) do nothing — rejected, the sibling directory filters already landed this predicate, so the shared helper is the remaining inconsistency.
- **Scope**: `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts` + `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts`. No `plugin-sdk` export-list change (`scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json` untouched), no lockfile change.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query "<NFD #café>" --json` returns `[]` even though `channels.irc.groups["#café"]` is configured. The config-driven directory filter lowercases both operands and never normalizes Unicode, so a decomposed (NFD) query misses a composed (NFC) key — and the reverse misses too. The same predicate covers every config-driven directory listing: `irc`, `line`, `reef`, `signal`, `telegram`, `zalo`, `zalouser`, plus the config halves of `feishu`, `matrix`, `discord`, `slack` and `msteams`.

Precedent: #187148 (merged, same shape in the feishu/slack/telegram local filters), #188003, #187199, #187611, #189131, #189360. This PR only swaps the point — those siblings never reached the shared helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` is the single owner of config-driven directory query matching. It now normalizes both operands to NFC after lowercasing, so composed and decomposed spellings compare equal. Stored ids, returned entries and spelling, `limit`, empty-query behavior and non-matching queries are unchanged. No validator, option, config key, schema, dependency or persistence change; the `plugin-sdk` export list is untouched.

Production LOC is `+3/-2` (one file).

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

An operator who types or pastes `#café` in either Unicode form now gets their configured group back from `directory groups list` instead of an empty list. Same-form queries and non-matching queries behave exactly as before, and accent folding is **not** introduced (`#cafe` still misses `#café`).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `a9086c35ec2cef06c279155869d157b390b702ef`
- Current-main RED baseline: `87396e72d2474de52693866212c305c0a0ef9f13`
- Production entry: real source CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query <text> --json` (argv/command tree identical to the packaged CLI), Node 24.22.1 in a `lexiflow-all` container
- Canonical owner exercised: `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` in `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:20-25`
- Decision surface: `--query` on `directory groups|peers list` for config-driven channels; fixture is a generated `channels.irc.groups` keyed by channel name
- Recorder/readback boundary: JSON envelope (`[]` vs `[{kind,id,name}]`) plus process exit code; fixture strings printed as code points
- Acceptance RED: unchanged baseline returns `[]` for both cross-form directions while both same-form controls return the entry
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head returns the original entry for both cross-form directions; controls byte-identical to base
- Legal controls: composed×composed and UPPERCASE×composed return the entry on both revisions; the unit suite additionally proves no accent folding
- Cleanup: each run used a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under a disposable container `HOME`, deleted after the run. No production Gateway, session, channel, token or user config was touched.

### BEFORE / AFTER

Fixture bytes (verified on both revisions, `distinct: true`): composed `23 63 61 66 e9` · decomposed `23 63 61 66 65 301`.

| Direction | Base `87396e72d24` | Head `a9086c35ec2` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| composed key × decomposed query | `[]` (exit 0) | `[{ "kind":"group", "id":"#café", "name":"#café" }]` (exit 0) |
| decomposed key × composed query | `[]` (exit 0) | same entry (exit 0) |
| composed key × composed query (control) | same entry | same entry |
| composed key × UPPERCASE query (control) | same entry | same entry |

The failure shape is a silently empty result, not a non-zero exit: the CLI succeeds and reports zero matches.

```text
RED  base 87396e72d24 — composed key × decomposed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#cafe<e + U+0301>' --json
[]
exit=0
RED  base — decomposed key × composed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#café' --json
[]
exit=0
RED  base — control, composed key × composed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#café' --json
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]
exit=0
```

```text
GREEN head a9086c35ec2 — composed key × decomposed query
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0
GREEN head — decomposed key × composed query
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0
GREEN head — controls (composed x composed, UPPERCASE x composed)
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0   (both, byte-identical to base)
```

No empty-argv token is involved in this change.

Unit receipt on the same two trees (Node 24.22.1, `--maxWorkers=1`):

```text
RED  Tests  2 failed | 7 passed (9)   exit 1
     AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [{ kind: 'group', id: '#café' }]
     src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts:79
GREEN Tests  9 passed (9)             exit 0
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — RED `2 failed | 7 passed` (exit 1); GREEN `9 passed` (exit 0)
- sibling `src/channels/plugins/directory-adapters.test.ts` — `4 passed`; sibling `extensions/feishu/src/directory.test.ts` — `29 passed`
- `oxfmt --check <the two files>` — "All matched files use the correct format" (exit 0)
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <the two files>` — `0 warnings, 0 errors`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — 8 errors on the **pristine baseline and on head, sorted lists byte-identical (`diff` empty)**: all 8 are tree-local dependency drift (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.26.13` installed vs `0.27.0` required by `pnpm-lock.yaml` at base, plus missing `@noble/hashes`). Zero errors in either touched file.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet` (same algorithm) — total `6,361,886` vs ceiling `6,382,193` (baseline `6,319,970` + allocations `62,223`) → slack `20,307`; `+17` test lines, no new allocation needed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested: full repository suites (only the touched file plus its two directory siblings ran); per-channel live network directory lookups for slack/discord/mattermost/telegram (they inherit this predicate but were not re-proven against their servers); macOS/Windows hosts; a fully installed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` typecheck — blocked by the tree-local drift above, so the baseline-diff method is used instead.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+3/-2` · Test LOC: `+31/-0` · Files: 2 · New files: 0
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/string-coerce` plus `String.prototype.normalize`; no new helper, validator, option, dependency or export.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: **none** — comparison-time only, no stored value rewritten, no lockfile change.

### Compatibility note (`merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`)

Written for the review label; the API surface and its contract are untouched:

- `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` ships through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/directory-runtime`, and this changes **matching behavior only**: signatures, export list, ordering, `limit`, and returned identifier bytes are unchanged. The shipped-surface gate (`plugin-sdk:surface-report --check`) fails only on removals/budgets and the export list is identical; `check-source-contracts` is green on this head.
- On composed (NFC) stored keys — the common case — the change is **pure widening**: every query that matched on base still matches (enumerated over all raw substrings of six composed keys: 0 losses), and canonically equivalent queries in the other form now hit; same-form controls return byte-identical entries.
- Accepted edge case: a raw fragment that stops before a combining mark (e.g. `cafe` typed against a key stored decomposed) previously matched **only because that key happened to be NFD**; it now behaves exactly like a composed key always did. Verified for every raw-substring fragment of decomposed keys: `base(NFC form of the key, q) ≡ head(NFD key, q)`, 0 exceptions. Any form of the full name matches on both key forms.
- Precedent: the identical two-sided `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...).normalize("NFC")` idiom already merged in `extensions/feishu/src/directory.ts:45`, `extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.ts:92`, `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts:82`, `extensions/matrix/src/directory-live.ts:146`, and `src/cron/service/ops-read.ts:208`.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:21` | query operand normalized to NFC | comparison-only; widens to canonical equivalents only, never to different text |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:25` | id operand normalized to NFC | same; returned id bytes unchanged |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts:64-93` | 2 direction cases + 3 controls | test-only |

Consumer fan-out: `listDirectoryEntriesFromSources` → the config listers of `irc`/`line`/`reef`/`signal`/`telegram`/`zalo`/`zalouser` and the config halves of `feishu`/`matrix`/`discord`/`slack`/`msteams`; also re-exported as `openclaw/plugin-sdk/directory-runtime`.

Proof recorded 2026-11-01 (UTC).

prs.title: fix(codex): name the incompatible setting when a thread binding refuses rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #135310. This revision reapplies the diagnostic fix to the current staged-replacement lifecycle after merging main at `a45979ee0f76`. It does not restore the old lifecycle implementation.

Nine incompatibility checks currently report only `rotating a stale thread binding` when native ownership refuses replacement. If replacement is permitted but its later compare-and-swap fails, the diagnostic instead loses the cause as `committing a fresh thread`.

## User Impact

The refusal identifies the changed setting: runtime identity, MCP configuration, web search, context-engine binding, user MCP configuration, network proxy configuration, plugin app configuration, dynamic tool loading mode, or dynamic tool catalog. The same staged cause also reaches a later replacement commit conflict.

Thread ownership and recovery behavior do not change. The existing guard, expected predecessor thread ID, mutation ordering, inventory preservation, subscription release, and rejection cleanup are unchanged. A genuinely fresh start without a staged replacement retains its existing conflict message.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rotateStaleBinding` supplies the specific diagnostic operation. `stageBindingReplacement` captures it with the predecessor and passes it through the existing start context to `startFreshCodexThread`. The value is diagnostic metadata, not an authorization or configuration input. Other already-specific staging reasons also survive the commit boundary. The generic reason after an actually failed stale-thread resume remains generic.

The previous synthetic ownership regression now lives in the assignment-rotation suite rather than growing the oversized binding test file. A separate real-binary test is registered with the existing database-worker test owner.

## Evidence

All evidence below is from this revision's local run, Linux x64, Node 24.21.0. Commands run serially in memory-limited units.

### Before and after

With main's production code, the ownership regression and replacement-CAS regression both fail specifically because the operation is too generic. An additional test against the pinned **real Codex 0.160.0 app-server** reproduces the later conflict:

```text
Expected: Codex thread binding changed while changing its dynamic tool loading mode: <thread-id>
Received: Codex thread binding changed while committing a fresh thread: <thread-id>
```

The temporary thread ID is replaced above. After the fix, all 10 tests in the assignment-rotation and new native-diagnostic suites pass, including the real-binary test.

The real-binary test starts actual native threads through the production OpenClaw lifecycle and persists the original binding through its SQLite store. It injects only a failed replacement-commit result. It verifies the specific conflict, unchanged original binding, still-readable predecessor thread, expected predecessor ID in the mutation, and deletion of only the uncommitted replacement. The native check passed in 1425 ms within the final suite run.

### Verification

Final local verification on `116130492c085a37108bab211d087cd61acfb113` is green:

- **287 tests in 9 files**, two sequential shards, 151.788 s wall time:

  ```bash
  pnpm test \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.configured-mcp-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.app-inventory.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.adoption.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.native.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.rotation-cause.native.test.ts \
    --maxWorkers=1
  ```

- `npx oxlint --type-aware` on all five changed TypeScript files: zero warnings and errors. The repository's SDK boundary declaration preparation was required first.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: exit 0, 330.074 s. This is the full production extensions graph, not the incomplete raw package graph.
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base a45979ee0f7635a4bf9918a8ea648e6d0a415e51`: pass.
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base a45979ee0f7635a4bf9918a8ea648e6d0a415e51`: pass.
- `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs`, `oxfmt --check` on all six changed files, and `git diff --check`: pass.

The local merge commit preserves the exact tested file tree. Publication is a normal fast-forward push from the previously published PR head, not a force push.

### Proof boundaries

- The real-binary test uses fresh temporary homes and state, an allowlisted child environment, a non-authenticated loopback-only provider configuration, and no model inference. It verifies that no auth file exists. No operator credentials or production state are copied.
- The commit failure is fault-injected. This is real native thread creation and cleanup, not evidence of a naturally occurring concurrent production race.
- The early native-ownership refusal is covered by a synthetic ownership fixture. This is **not** an account-backed, fully adopted supervised-session reproduction or a packaged-Gateway/UI proof.
- The pinned dependency contract was checked directly: [Codex 0.160.0 dynamic tool declarations](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs). Namespaced functions carry `type: function`; `defer_loading` is serialized as `deferLoading`.

Maintainer question on the outstanding proof request: does this isolated real-binary lifecycle proof, together with the ownership and preservation regressions, suffice for this diagnostic-only change, or is a fully adopted supervised-session reproduction still required before merge?

prs.title: fix: Talk repeats the gateway password when voice starts
prs.body:
Closes #172403

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: mobile Talk shows `Realtime WebRTC setup failed (401)` and repeats the gateway password prompt when the Control UI is opened through a reverse proxy that uses HTTP basic auth.

## User Impact

User impact: a signed-in browser session can start Talk without the offer request occupying `Authorization`. Re-entering the gateway password is no longer required to get the reservation token past the proxy.

Native clients that already send `Authorization: Bearer` keep working. Direct `api.openai.com` offers still send that bearer token and do not send the reservation header.

## Why This Change Was Made

Talk posted the single-use reservation as `Authorization: Bearer` on every offer, including `/plugins/openai/realtime/calls`. The proxy uses that same header for the gateway password, so it can answer 401 before the gateway sees the reservation. The browser then shows its password dialog again, and a script-set `Authorization` header keeps the cached password from replacing the bearer token.

Gateway-origin offers now send the reservation in `X-OpenClaw-Realtime-Token`, leave `Authorization` unset, and use credentialed fetch so the browser can attach the cached basic credentials. The offer route accepts that header or the existing bearer token. Its own 401 does not send `WWW-Authenticate`. CORS allows the new header and credentialed browser origins.

Exempting the offer path from the proxy's password check is not this fix.

## Evidence

- Control UI offer tests: a gateway-relative offer and a same-origin absolute offer send `X-OpenClaw-Realtime-Token` and no `Authorization`; a direct `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` offer still sends `Authorization: Bearer` and does not include credentials. `webrtc.test.ts` still passes.
- Offer route tests: `Authorization: Basic` plus the reservation header returns the SDP answer; basic auth alone returns `401` `Invalid or expired realtime session token` with no `WWW-Authenticate`. Preflight allows `X-OpenClaw-Realtime-Token` and credentialed CORS.
- Not replayed in mobile Chrome against the live gateway. The live gateway was left untouched.

prs.title: fix(xai): xAI OAuth calls fail with HTTP 426 on the Grok proxy
prs.body:
Related: #147728

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: xAI OAuth inference and the Control UI connection check fail with HTTP 426 when the Grok proxy requires CLI version 1.0.13 or later. A missing header is reported as version (none); OpenClaw's own version string is rejected the same way.

## User Impact

User impact: subscription probes, utility completions, and billing snapshots send the proxy's advertised floor instead of omitting the header or sending the OpenClaw version. A later proxy floor bump will require updating the constant. Image, speech, and realtime calls that use the separate user-agent helper are unchanged. This does not update a running gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

`models.probe` and other tool-less completions use `prepareSimpleCompletionModel`, which only calls `wrapSimpleCompletionStreamFn`. The xAI plugin did not register that hook, so those requests never reached the Grok header wrapper. Agent turns passed `pluginApi.runtime.version` into the wrapper, and an empty value skipped the headers entirely. Billing still advertised 1.0.4.

One constant, 1.0.13, is now sent from the agent wrapper, a new simple-completion wrapper (headers plus payload compatibility only), and the billing client. #153396 adds the simple-completion wrapper but still forwards the OpenClaw version, so it would still 426.

## Evidence

On OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.3, 2026-10-21: a successful OAuth refresh was followed the same second by `models.probe`'s grok-4.7 fetch status=426 elapsedMs=151, "Your Grok CLI version (none) is outdated. Please update to version 1.0.13 or later". The probe returned in 4063ms. A fresh device login saved the profile, then the same fetch 426'd again in 154ms. The local grok binary is not consulted.

Focused vitest (`test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts`, `--maxWorkers=1`): `extensions/xai/stream.test.ts`, `usage.test.ts`, `server-compaction.test.ts`, and `index.test.ts`. 4 files, 64 tests, all passed. That includes the new simple-completion cases, the proxy header expectation of 1.0.13, the billing header tests, and server-compaction proxy-header equality. The three existing public-API payload-boundary tests time out at 10s when several run together; each is about 7.5s of `streamSimple` against the public API, and they passed in this serial run.

### Maintainer verification — 2026-10-24

The refreshed head `e8d25f92614312c16b781f3d82f96bf00708cabc` passed 72 tests across `index.test.ts`, `stream.test.ts`, and `server-compaction.test.ts` on a disposable secretless AWS runner. Billing coverage now lives in `index.test.ts`; the deleted `usage.test.ts` was not restored.

Targeted typechecking found TS2322 in both newly added simple-completion tests. Commit `e275f2684548a2b5be1476b5afaa94a22c6c3f91` fixes only their annotations to use the already imported nullable `ModelRequestHeaders` contract. The exact corrected file passed targeted typechecking, lint and formatting. Runtime code and assertions are unchanged. Independent review found no additional P0–P2 defects.

The corrected stream suite passed 15 cases, including both new simple-completion cases, but its three existing 10-second Responses payload-boundary cases timed out. Those same cases passed in the earlier 72-test run. This is retained as an unresolved intermittent failure, not claimed repaired or silently waived.

**Still draft / not merge-ready:** no Grok OAuth credential was available for authenticated probe, agent, utility-completion and billing acceptance proof. Mocked header assertions do not establish live proxy acceptance. Required exact-head CI and live proof remain outstanding.

prs.title: refactor(decisions): streamline OpenAI distribution decoding
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI and ClawRouter distribution decoding repeats each item’s record check and copies every distribution before checking whether any probability is positive.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Result values, wire/rubric ordering, malformed-response rejection, refusals and usage retain their existing semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrow each distribution item once and retain the positive-probability fact during the existing loop. Keep the Map, membership and duplicate checks unchanged; reject cardinality before all-zero distributions.

Extend the existing provider-wire table for primitive entries, unknown/missing labels and all-zero choice/score responses. The score case also protects resetting the positive flag between questions. A literal key-order expectation protects wire insertion order. These26 additional test lines require the matching allocation.

## Evidence

Node syntax, native formatting, whitespace, normal signed commit hooks and the LF ratchet passed. Fresh full-range local review found no actionable defects.

Production size is unchanged. Source-level targets are2N→N record checks and1→0 temporary distribution copies; these are not measured runtime gains.

Qualified native execution passed151 cases across the OpenAI and ClawRouter provider suites, ClawRouter integration, V1/V2 runtime and compatibility suites in92.934s. Actual test carriers were the pinned Bun fork, observed by executable identity/hash; Node26.13 was orchestration. Both owning typegraphs passed(14.188s/25.977s), and production/test typed lints passed(156.607s/19.668s). All30 frozen input hashes, sourceHEAD/binding/private dependencies and install evidence were independently verified unchanged after explicit handback; all owned PIDs settled. Individual file walls were not emitted; project durations and case timings are retained separately.

prs.body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

Related: #186066 (parent #186050; prerequisite #186065). Complements #188494 without duplicating its USER.md/bootstrap changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Proposes person-scoped project Knowledge sharing between two explicitly authorized agents without granting a scoped specialist an ungranted personal space.

## User Impact

With the documented restricted embedded-runtime profile, A and B can publish/read the same project record revision and evidence. Personal record bodies, IDs, titles, record counts, evidence, standing indexes and automatic-recall candidates remain outside the specialist’s enabled retrieval paths. Revocation is persisted and rechecked for warmed leases/references and after restart.

**Permission/upgrade proposal:** verified direct requesters now need an explicit person/agent grant rather than falling back to agent-private or conversation knowledge. Existing records are not migrated or reclassified automatically. Unprofiled legacy audiences keep their legacy partitions and cannot traverse person-space directories. This is a reviewable proposal, not a claim of upstream architecture acceptance.

**Required boundary:** the qualified profile allows exactly eight Knowledge record/evidence tools, disables automatic workspace bootstrap/code mode/tool search, and excludes raw filesystem/execution/admin/cross-session history and globally numbered Knowledge History/Recent/revision APIs. Those history sequence identifiers are not represented as private activity counts. Workspace-file import is excluded; person-bound `knowledge_attach_file` also refuses host-workspace reads. Broader tools, bootstrap inputs, providers and native harnesses require separate qualification. There is no OS tenant-isolation or erasure claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse host-minted memory audiences and live authority. The authority owner separately attests requester provenance: unattributed system execution derived from a session owner/creator cannot become a person binding. Genuine roots and validated continuations retain the fact; the existing private recovery snapshot preserves it without turning older/unclassified execution state into a requester.
- Reuse named agent-store membership and the Knowledge registry/publication lane. An operator-only grant selects one store-local space per `(profileId, agent)` against the current binding. No union search or model-controlled store/scope selector.
- Resolve tools, provider search/get/health/candidates, evidence and standing indexes through the restrictive principal. Reuse the scope-key owner for storage/index/receipt/evidence paths and include the partition in standing-index cache identity.
- Check the original administrator inside the registry SQLite transaction, after lock admission and immediately before a permission write; grant changes are compare-and-set.

prs.body:
Related: #181078

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent turns abort with "Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current" when a worker borrows the agent database receipt while its own cache still holds the receipt that was retired before a reopen.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent database being retired and reopened (execution cleanup, idle close followed by a reopen with the integrity gate) no longer drops canonical readiness for the Gateway, so held session reader continuations stay valid and turns are not aborted. Genuine readiness demotions (owner invalidation, pending validation, a child handing back a receipt after the parent revoked) still refuse exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`adoptOpenClawAgentDatabaseValidation` is called in two directions. On the parent, a mutation worker hands its receipt back (`handoff`); everywhere else a worker borrows a receipt the parent owns and keeps publishing (`borrow`). Both took the same path: when the local cache entry for the path was revoked, the function cleared `canonicalReady` on the received receipt and invalidated the local predecessor. For a borrower those cells belong to the parent. A reader worker that still caches the retired predecessor from before a reopen therefore cleared the owner's readiness for every isolate, and every held reader continuation became stale at once.

The function now takes an explicit `direction: "borrow" | "handoff"`. `handoff` keeps the existing recertification guard unchanged. `borrow` only replaces the borrower's local entry and no longer writes the owner's cells. The parameter is required at every call site, so a future child-to-parent caller cannot silently skip the guard. No reader refusal changed (`isReaderContinuationLive`, the worker in-read check and the host final check reject what they rejected before) and nothing catches or retries at the turn level.

The first commit only moves `isOpenClawAgentCanonicalStoreEmpty` next to `assertCanonicalSessionValidationSchema`, because `openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.ts` is at its line cap; it has no behavior change.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof (details, excerpts and caveats in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191488#issuecomment-6590996396; redacted transcripts, harness and verdict JSON in https://gist.github.com/Moxysmuse/e39f0b2d500907c5a819ab5c3a5526be):

- **Shipped Gateway + CLI, 2026.10.9 in docker, 12 rounds per image** (turn 1 → owner retires the receipt and closes its handle → turn 2 reopens and publishes a successor): the official image fails 5/12 turns with `Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current` (`UNAVAILABLE`) and the successor's shared `canonicalReady` dips 1→0 in 12/12 rounds; the same image with this fix fails 0/12 and returns the complete reply every time, with no cell changes. The retirement is a disclosed test-only preload calling the shipped `invalidateOpenClawAgentDatabaseValidation` + `closeMaintenanceAgentDatabase`.
- **Gateway built from this PR head vs its base**, `openclaw agent` over the Gateway WS, reopen through the integrity gate: with the #167739 fallback both complete (no turn-level red on main). With the fallback skipped for a revoked local entry (the 10.9 shape), base clears the owner's live `canonicalReady` 1→0 six times in 3 runs, head keeps 1 in 9/9 borrow-over-revoked adopts; every turn 2 returns the complete reply.
- **Production 2026.10.8/10.9**: 5 of 9 turns admitted within 1.5 s after an integrity gate failed with this error before the fix; 0 failures since the same fix was deployed (window still short, will be updated).

Tests:

- New unit case in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts` ("lowers received canonical readiness over a retired local entry only on borrow/handoff"): a local entry names a retired predecessor, then a successor receipt is adopted.
  - On `main` (9e295ec3146) without the fix the borrow case fails: `expected +0 to be 1`. With the fix all 53 tests in the file pass (`pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 9.4 s wall).
  - The handoff case still lowers readiness, and the existing "does not revive revoked canonical proof on cold integrity admission by adopt" case passes `"handoff"` and still fails without it.
- Validation-cache, canonical-validation, readonly-scope, agent-db admission/worker, reader-continuation, sqlite-worker-request, entry-read worker and transcript-worker-reader suites pass; `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt and `check-line-cap-ratchet` are clean.
- Field evidence (2026.10.7–2026.10.9 Docker Gateway, stacks captured with a `--require` preload, see #181078): all 10 turn-fatal incidents came 50–320 ms after the agent database was reopened through the integrity gate (`revoked` / `dirty-receipt`); none of 14 turns without a preceding gate failed. A worker-thread regression on v2026.10.9 (real projection worker borrows V0, owner retires and reopens to V1, a database-addressed request carries V1 to that worker) fails 3/3 with this exact error and passes with the same change.
- On `main` and `v2026.10.10-beta.5` that worker-level scenario already passes without this change, because the admission fallback from #167739 refreshes the worker's local entry before `adopt` runs. The unit case above shows the owner-cell write is still reachable on `main` whenever the borrower's local entry is revoked, so this keeps the owner as the only writer of its shared cells.

<details>
<summary>Adjacent paths not changed here</summary>

- The reuse branch of `setOpenClawAgentDatabaseValidation` can lower an existing receipt's shared `canonicalReady` from 1 to 0 on a healthy re-publication when no persisted canonical receipt exists.
- `rememberReaderAdmission` revokes every held continuation on any re-admission, even a value-identical one; that widens the impact of a demotion but does not cause one.

</details>

prs.title: fix(install): installer gives wrong PATH advice when Homebrew's Node is too old
prs.body:
Closes #191412
Related: #70411

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `install.sh` tells macOS users to change their PATH when Homebrew's `node` is simply older than OpenClaw requires.

## User Impact

User impact: the installer reports the Homebrew version it found and the required range, and gives the command that fixes it: `brew update && brew upgrade node`. This case appears when Homebrew auto-update is off, for example with `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check runs after Homebrew's node is placed first on PATH, so a rejected runtime can only be Homebrew's own. The PATH advice could not help and could not be correct at that point, so it is replaced. The installer does not run `brew update` itself, which keeps the user's Homebrew setting intact.

## Evidence

Run live on macOS with a stale Homebrew formula cache and `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`:

- Without this change: `Node.js v26 was installed but this shell is using v26.10.0`, followed by PATH advice.
- With this change: `Homebrew node v26.10.0 does not meet OpenClaw's Node.js requirement (>=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1)`, followed by `Run 'brew update && brew upgrade node', then rerun the installer.`
- Running `brew upgrade node` moved the guest to v26.13.0, confirming the advice works.

Tests: new case in `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` fails without the fix and passes with it. Two unrelated quoting tests fail on macOS with and without this change, and also on unmodified `main`: `gives a working PATH remedy after a writable npm prefix with quoted prefix` and `prints a literal-safe direct PATH remedy for zsh`. `oxlint` on the test file is clean.

`shellcheck -S warning -e SC1091` on `scripts/install.sh` reports one warning, `DOWNLOADER` at line 156, on a line this change does not touch.

Review: local autoreview with the Claude engine (`claude-opus-5-5`, Codex CLI not available) on base `4c451a77c`, head `1d414037e`, default priority scope: patch correct, no findings.

Maintainer acceptance evidence (head `1727b28958632929c8b78d95cf591a26f1fef366`):

- Fresh local `$autoreview`, committed range `4c451a77c68be7e6e24b4900bf22ef1022ef3a9a` → `1727b28958632929c8b78d95cf591a26f1fef366`, P0–P2: complete, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Full installer and installer-test source supplied; source review only.
- Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538569014) passed changed tests, lint, production/test types and `openclaw/ci-gate`. [Installer CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538569225) passed, including [macOS installer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538569225/job/125596962458); dependency and security-sensitive gates passed.
- The contributor's macOS stale-keg before/after evidence above covers the reported failure. Maintainer validation reused hosted CI; no contributor code or runtime tests were executed on the production host.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

prs.title: fix(sessions): replay creation requests across Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

Process-local `sessions.create` idempotency loses the original binding when the Gateway restarts. Retrying can create another session and repeat preparation or its initial turn.

## Change

Atomically persist the existing optional idempotency key's namespaced fingerprint and original key/session ID/lifecycle revision with the session row. The existing passive history reader resolves receipts before label/resource preparation. Current requester, sharing, scopes and lifecycle authority still gate replay; stored authorization only restricts replay and never restores authority. Deleted/reset incarnations are refused, including same-ID resets. Renaming the original does not break replay when another session takes its former label.

The five-minute retry window remains. Replay does not allocate a worker, prepare a workspace or resend the initial message. Restart replay returns `creationReplayed: true` and `runStarted: false`: no new turn started, not a claim about completion of the original work. Inspect the original session for recovery. Incognito stays memory-only. No default-agent, SQLite-only, caller-generated-ID or purpose restriction is added.

Agent schema 39→40 uses the existing SQLite/PostgreSQL migration, backup, witness and historical-port owners. The PostgreSQL schema-40 migration also adopts two deletion indexes expressly deferred by its generator; predecessor sealed catalogs retain their exact original contracts. State schema 39 and resource/disk authority contracts are unchanged. No payload backfill or fork retention columns. Rollback requires the pre-upgrade backup and matching binary.

## Current candidate evidence

Head: ea0c33beeb895a6a566e5a981a4ddf8e27b0c990. Base: 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914. Independent of attended permissions and offline ports.

The following complete-feature results were executed on repair head `ad51a9143047d2ca47dd9b51a491f0befde1c7c6`; unchanged runtime, migration and generated-artifact inputs are reused. The new three-file generator follow-up is qualified separately below.

- **41 focused native cases passed:** public replay/label reuse/reset refusal, requester revocation and membership removal after live authorization, cancellation's structured FORBIDDEN response, protocol, migrations and passive import boundaries. The revocation cases first prove an authorized replay and then assert refusal without metadata disclosure.
- **Real PostgreSQL 17.11:** native worker receipt close/reopen and competing-row rollback pass in the normal host-broker lane. SQLite migration commit/rollback and historical restoration pass. Frozen SQLite schema-27/28 SQL and PostgreSQL schema-35 digest tests pass without changing their expectations.
- Provisioning consumers: **15 passed, 3 unchanged environment-gated skips**. Wrapper inventory, extracted package aliases and retained Darwin dependency inputs: 3 passed through the supported isolated Node runner; container absence confirmed. Missing module registrations, passive-reader dependencies and broker test placement are repaired at their owners.
- Targeted tooling/Gateway/infra types, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generated-schema verification, Kysely structural guard, line cap, whitespace and exact 631-line test allocation passed. Commit bytes match the qualified source.
- Fresh independent local review of the complete candidate against the base: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**. Static review, not independent execution of the reported tests.

Actual authorization proof excerpts:

```text
PASS durable replay requester revoked after live authorization: no session metadata disclosed
PASS durable replay membership revoked after live authorization: no session metadata disclosed
```

## Process and upgrade evidence

Earlier actual two-process Gateway proof uses a non-default agent, the real agent runtime and deterministic local Responses I/O: persisted first turn, changed PID on restart, original identity after label reuse, no duplicate model call, successful subsequent turn, and reset refusal. It predates final mechanical relocations and these integration repairs; the current owner-boundary proofs cover the changed contracts. This is not live-provider inference.

Actual runner result: one process-restart test passed in 31992ms; wrapper 126.16s.

Latest-stable source compatibility: v2026.10.9/8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41 produced a schema 25 image through its released schema owner. The candidate's real maintenance/migration path upgraded it to 40, preserved all 3 pending states/message JSON, original session-entry bytes, cache and settings, and read a newly written receipt after close/reopen. The producer image hash stayed unchanged. Test 12.600s; wrapper 348.56s, dominated by cold transform/I/O.

That fixture used synthetic data validated by the released entry/configuration readers. It proves source-owner migration compatibility—not package install-over or a released-UI transcript. No package release-age policy was bypassed.

## Integration qualification

Native three-way composition was clean with port head `5d4dc9755af68e99a916ca2e8524df139c919919` and attended-permission head `de78e430a40cdd82c575633eb75b383bca892a68`. Twenty selected cases qualified the combined public permission/replay boundaries, schema 39/40 descriptors, first-use completion, recovery-envelope retirement and real PostgreSQL receipt writer. A native private-copy port also preserved the creation receipt and original session identity. No functional dependency requires stacking these PRs.

The extra port fixture initially lacked `updatedAt` in its synthetic session row; the canonical reader correctly refused it. Correcting that fixture alone produced the receipt-preservation pass. Product source was unchanged. Earlier cold setup timeouts remain recorded; subsequent prepared-worker qualification did not weaken timeouts or guards.

## Scope and remaining gates

Production/tooling delta excluding generated files: 793 added/186 removed lines; tests 654 added/23 removed. Necessary growth is the atomic receipt, replay authority and two-engine migration/compatibility boundary—not a parallel runtime or allocation manager. The repair deletes the retired generator exception and broad reader dependencies rather than adding alternatives.

Current-head CI, hosted review and landing remain separate gates. The three platform-gated provisioning cases were not exercised locally. No merge is claimed here.

## Generator CI repair evidence

Candidate: `b039bdb311e11b6369757899a779eabd7a594d94`, based on published head `ad51a9143047d2ca47dd9b51a491f0befde1c7c6`.

The sole nonaggregate failure in CI run `41415625394` was an obsolete generator assertion: it still expected PostgreSQL to defer the two deletion indexes under schema 39. The authorized schema-40 migration now adopts those indexes. The original assertion was reproduced locally with the same two extra index definitions before editing.

The existing test now verifies both indexes appear in generated SQL and the runtime artifact. The unused omission exemption was removed; its producer was already retired. No runtime session behavior, schema migration, generated artifact, expected historical digest, skip, or timeout changed. The test-line allocation decreased from 636 to 631.

- Complete generator suite: **23 passed**, 24.83 s wrapper.
- Unchanged schema-39/40 descriptor and frozen PostgreSQL schema-35 digest checks: **3 passed**, 75.50 s wrapper.
- Tooling typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generated-artifact verification, whitespace and test-line budget passed.
- Fresh local autoreview of the complete three-file follow-up against `ad51a9143047d2ca47dd9b51a491f0befde1c7c6`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings. Static review, not an independent execution of the tests. The earlier complete-feature review and runtime/process/database evidence retain their stated scope.

Current-head hosted CI and review remain separate gates; these are local qualification results.

## Response-authority repair and final process qualification

Candidate: `ea0c33beeb895a6a566e5a981a4ddf8e27b0c990`, parent `b039bdb311e11b6369757899a779eabd7a594d94`. The final results below qualify this exact committed tree; earlier proof above retains its stated source scope.

### Replay response authority and receipt binding

- Retain the existing requester, sharing, and lifecycle sources until the actual response callback. Revalidate synchronously there, after the idempotency owner's awaits, and release afterward.
- Reuse a warm cached payload only when its key, session ID, and lifecycle revision match the receipt being authorized. When an expired receipt has been replaced, project that new authorized receipt instead of returning the old cached session. This does not rerun creation, allocate another worker, change retention, or add an authorization/cache owner.
- This follow-up leaves the previously qualified agent-schema 40 / shared-state-schema 39 migration unchanged.

### Final qualification

The full candidate tree was verified identical across all 62,593 indexed entries: `f5d7f3a4128b71698259bf1c300c4c3f65ecf967`.

```text
Canonical qaRuntime build + private QA + declarations: PASS (exit 0)
Gateway consumers: 3 files, 51/51 tests PASS
Actual process replay E2E: 1/1 PASS
Test-line budget: 6,386,599 / 6,399,693 PASS (13,094 slack)
```

- Cold and warm membership-removal regressions reproduced disclosure before the response-lifetime fix and now return the native participation refusal without a replay payload.
- The replacement-receipt regression reproduced an old cached key/session ID being returned after a real replacement creation. Both generated-session and same-ID/reset variants now pass. Only the persisted expiry deadline is advanced by the fixture; identities, receipts, reset, authorization, and replay use their real owners.
- The unchanged process E2E used a nondefault agent and two genuine Gateway processes on retained state. Replay preserved original identity despite label reuse, reported no new kickoff, and kept provider requests at **1 → 1**. A subsequent turn completed (**1 → 2**), history remained readable, and reset refused the prior incarnation.
- Core and Gateway-test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet passed. Fresh independent **P0–P2 review of the complete candidate** was scoped-clean.

The build and tests ran in rootless, network-none isolation with Node 26.12.1 and native pnpm 12.15.0. An authentic task-private Git snapshot retained the unchanged provenance guard; all three producer-written build identities matched its real fixture HEAD. That fixture commit is test provenance, not an upstream revision. Both owned containers are confirmed absent.

The provider was deterministic and local, not live-provider inference. A hosting restart interrupted an earlier build with SIGTERM; its evidence was preserved and the canonical build completed normally on resumption. The already-successful exact-source budget receipt was reused rather than rerun.

### Preserved CI uncertainty

The earlier historical-import Doctor CI failure hit its unchanged 90-second process guard. The unchanged 18-file selector subsequently passed all 186 cases on both Node 26.12.1 and the CI's Node 24.22.1, but the original cause remains unknown—not claimed fixed or inherited. No timeout or assertion was relaxed. Current-head CI and hosted review remain publication/landing gates; this evidence does not claim a rating or remote CI success.

## Independent corroboration

[Linux2010's independent report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190862#issuecomment-6585685027), posted November 2, 2026, reports four failing handoff-window/replacement-receipt cases on `b039bdb311e` (17 other cases passed) and all 21 cases passing on `ea0c33beeb8` with the same overlaid tests. This is externally reported corroboration; the report was read, but its raw run artifacts were not independently verified here. It is not a hosted readiness rating or live-provider proof.

## Credits

Requested and co-authored by Galin Iliev (@galiniliev).

prs.title: feat(sessions): split deleted archive retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` previously applied the same age cutoff to both reset and deleted transcript archives. This adds `session.maintenance.deletedArchiveRetention` as an independent duration-or-`false` control.

When omitted, `deletedArchiveRetention` inherits `resetArchiveRetention` for backward compatibility. An explicit duration or `false` overrides it independently. Both settings age archive artifacts; they do not age retained SQLite reset history or transcript rows.

## Implementation

- Resolves independent deleted/reset rules from configuration.
- Applies those rules through legacy file-backed maintenance, cron reaping, and ordinary SQLite maintenance.
- Ordinary SQLite maintenance runs archive cleanup even when no session rows are removed.
- Removes a derived archive file before deleting its published SQLite recovery row; failed file cleanup leaves the recovery row intact.
- Preserves inherited deleted retention for older resolved-maintenance callers while retaining explicit disablement.
- Fences archive-row pruning against maintenance-owner invalidation before and inside each SQLite writer callback.
- Updates schema help, examples, and session-management documentation.

## Evidence
- Exact pushed head: `5460eaf7b0ab2221938f1b7a4dbfc052e69d9588`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused runtime command:
  `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-retention.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-writer.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.archive-retention.test.ts src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.fix-missing.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  Result: **4 test files passed, 22 tests passed**.
- The unmocked integration proof loads a real config file and exercises both paths:
  - a fresh configured store is initialized (`configuredFreshStore: true`);
  - an existing configured store is maintained with independent cutoffs (`configuredExistingStore: true`);
  - the expired deleted archive file and its SQLite recovery row are absent after cleanup (`deletedArchiveFile: false`, `deletedArchiveRow: false` — `false` here means absent);
  - the reset archive remains (`resetArchiveFile: true`).
- The focused tests additionally prove inherited retention for older resolved callers, explicit `false` disablement, ordinary SQLite archive cleanup with no session removals, maintenance-owner invalidation without reopening the store, file-before-row deletion ordering, and lifecycle-deletion failure recovery.
- This proof is on the exact pushed head above; no claim is made that it resolves the separate current-base merge conflict or pending maintainer acceptance.
## Known Gate

This change affects persistent retention and upgrade behavior. Maintainer acceptance of the independent retention contract, ordinary-maintenance deletion timing, and the accessor cleanup boundary remains required before merge.

## Worked on by

- Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen)

prs.title: fix(ui): keep pre-final assistant text visible after a completed turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users chatting in the Control UI WebChat would watch a long assistant reply disappear once the turn completed, leaving only a short closing message visible, when the agent ran on an `openai-completions` transport and a tool call followed the reply text.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openai-completions` transports retag already-streamed answer text as commentary once a tool call follows it. The WebChat's completed-turn grouping then folded that text behind the "worked for" row together with the tool activity, so the substantive reply vanished from view.

The fix changes `chat-thread-grouping` to fold only tool groups and text-less assistant groups when a turn completes. Assistant groups that carry text stay visible regardless of how the transport phased them.

## User Impact

Long replies that precede a tool call remain visible after the turn completes. Tool activity still collapses as before.

## Evidence

New cases in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` and `chat-thread.test.ts` cover a text-bearing commentary group before a tool call, a text-less group, and the existing tool-only collapse.

Focused runs on this branch (rebased on current `main`):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-grouping.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts
  Test Files  2 passed (2)   Tests  277 passed (277)
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>   # clean
```

Observed originally on the 2026.9.2 release with an `openai-completions` transport in the WebChat.

prs.title: feat: gate personal instructions on private session audience
prs.body:
Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps automatically selected personal USER.md content and canonical personal-instructions chat operations out of shared or unverified initial audiences, without replacing the existing human-profile registry, Settings editor, or session profile-selection rules.

## User Impact

This review proposal contains three bounded improvements:

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the selected personal file. The final common filter also withholds personal-marked/origin hook entries. Shared defaults and existing allowlists remain intact.
2. The personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set operations with known group/channel origins or execution targets. Both actions return content; both are checked before file access or mutation.
3. Initial delivery also requires committed host sharing facts: an existing creator-private **Draft**, no public share, and a canonical creator matching the selected profile (bootstrap) or authenticated editor (chat tool). Shared/read-only/suggest, foreign-creator, and unverified audiences withhold the overlay or direct chat operations to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**. Distinct delegated origin and execution sessions must both qualify. A direct label alone is insufficient.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** Session selection remains assigned human owner, otherwise authenticated human creator; a new sender does not replace it. The authenticated editor remains separate from that selection. Canonical aliases and immutable creator stamps stay with their existing owners.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** These checks cover initial loader delivery and the canonical file handler's response/write boundary. Admission is not retained through every provider submission, tool-history append, or native thread. Widening an already-used private conversation can expose prior context or generated responses. Generic file/shell/native capabilities, inferred-to-file confinement, Knowledge/LCM audience admission, and retained history remain unqualified. Trusted administrators/host access are not hostile tenants. This is proposed narrowing for owner review, not upstream design acceptance. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small admission composes the existing profile catalog and retained session-sharing facts; no second registry, cache, SQL schema, configuration, public SDK contract, or model-supplied identity/audience argument is introduced. The existing public-share fact now participates in the internal sharing projection and its invalidation. Bootstrap checks after reads and hooks; the personal-file owner composes audience checks with its existing requester/role/agent and safe-writer pre-mutation assertion.

Author simplification retained one profile/file owner and one session-facts owner, rather than another authorization manager. Against base `194b10349b12ee8480e3837b2c90f28803f362cd`: production +179/−22 (net +157), tests +462/−21 (net +441), docs +421/−7. Necessary growth is the bounded admission, its two consumers, and owning-boundary regressions. The larger proposal remains documentation, not speculative Knowledge/history/permission implementation. Test budget passes without allocation or baseline changes.

## Evidence for this follow-up

Published head: `aa13a00d8f2e861f6496b27639ebfb9cbb2f0731`; ready for review, with the broader privacy scenario still incomplete. Remote verification found all **13 expected changed paths**, without evidence files or dependency caches. The commit retains the requested human co-author credit.

- **Red → green:** the shared-web bootstrap regression originally exposed Alice's personal content after the session became shared. Committed Draft/sharing/public-link/creator facts now control delivery; no private overlay is admitted merely because chat type is direct. A public share added during a bootstrap hook invalidates the prepared release.
- **51 Gateway tests passed across two files**: 50 production tool → in-process dispatch → handler → guarded filesystem cases, plus the real isolated Gateway two-person Settings fixture. The tool suite uses synthetic admitted authority/mocked profile facts with real committed session rows. Shared web audiences, foreign creator, shared origin/private execution, and audience changes before read release or final write are denied. The real WebSocket fixture independently verifies each authenticated person's own file, other-file/shared-file denial, and final role/merge revocation. This is not a live-model/group-channel pass.
- **19/19 affected personal/remote bootstrap cases passed** in the final consumer rerun (13.36 s wrapper), including profile ordering, aliases, budgets, group/cron/subagent exclusion, metadata admission/revocation, and remote file provenance. The remote transport executes locally and does not qualify a remote-worker or native runtime.
- Other unchanged consumers passed in the broader invocation: memory provenance **4**, sharing-projection lifecycle **8**, collected-turn selection **2**, prompt-prefix stability **14**. That invocation executed eight files, with 96 passes and two fixture failures; it was not a clean whole-run pass. The fixtures were corrected at their owners: asynchronous cleanup drains SQLite borrowers before closing, and the remote provenance mock classifies the requested personal paths after supplying real session config. The affected 19-case rerun above is the repair proof; no second whole-flow rerun is claimed.
- An explicit **agents-support carrier run passed 5/5** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/harness/workspace-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The mixed-path invocation had not executed that suite. These are rendering/carrier tests with a mocked bootstrap producer, not native execution or audience-isolation E2E.
- Core, Gateway-methods, agents-root and remote/agents-other TypeScript checks passed. Scoped type-aware lint, targeted formatting, two-document MDX compilation, whitespace and exact-base staged test-line ratchet passed (24,614 lines of slack; no exception). Lint's missing braces were fixed, not suppressed.
- Fresh bound Auto Review inspected the full staged candidate and complete owner source context against the exact base: **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**. It did not execute tests. The old hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime head. Current-head CI is separate and is not claimed green here.

## Dependencies and owner decisions still required

- **Knowledge:** #186455 is agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. Separate PR #189822 at `ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4` proposes person/agent grants selecting **one space**, not a private-plus-shared union; it disables bootstrap and excludes broad file/execution/history capabilities in its qualified profile. Do not duplicate that lane. Its current body reports an executed installed Knowledge–LosslessClaw 1.2.0 save/compact/restart/grep/evidence/replay fixture—new bounded #186065 evidence, not merely source. Those are its author's reported results, not this PR's execution; the shared-owner continuity fixture and separate P/Q cases do not prove the combined person-private/shared history scenario. It remains unmerged/proposed.
- **Host/profile owners:** accept or revise this Draft-only initial-delivery rule, then define run/provider/tool-history lifetime admission and safe handling when a conversation that already contains personal context is shared. Do not silently rewrite history or reassign personalization.
- **Knowledge/LCM owners:** settle private-plus-shared person/audience grants and supported explicit-ID/delegated expansion authority, with pinned installed-version proof. Knowledge remains the durable record/evidence owner; LosslessClaw remains history/compaction owner. No private LCM database reader is added.
- **File/sandbox/harness owners:** choose and qualify a capability profile where every enabled direct read/write/exec/native route respects personal roots and inferred records cannot overwrite user-authored instructions. Prompt filtering or a read-only mount is not that boundary.
- **Runtime qualification:** real-model embedded and generic CLI execution, native Codex, delegated history, ACP, realtime, remote-worker, and Windows E2E remain untested here. No Gateway, local remote-file adapter, carrier, or prefix pass transfers to those paths. Keep the complete two-person fixture open pending these contracts and proofs. No merge, auto-merge, or deployment is requested.

Implementation proposal and named owner map: [authenticated profile audience](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aa13a00d8f2e861f6496b27639ebfb9cbb2f0731/docs/architecture/authenticated-profile-audience.md).

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier-revision evidence and publication history (not current-head qualification)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

**This draft contains two bounded runtime improvements:**

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the automatically selected personal file. The common post-hook filter also withholds personal-marked or personal-origin entries. Shared defaults and existing subagent/cron allowlists remain intact.
