Both operations return profile content, so both are checked before file access or mutation. A group-origin request cannot evade this check by executing in another session; a direct-origin request cannot use a group execution target. The error points to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** No new model-supplied audience/profile parameter, registry, SDK contract, configuration, or schema is introduced. Session-selected owner/creator and authenticated editor remain separate. Host-resolved direct chat type retains precedence over a same-session group-looking key. This deliberately narrows chat-tool availability in known groups/channels and remains a draft for owner review—not a claim of upstream design acceptance.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** Direct/unknown/shared-web audiences, generic filesystem/native paths, previously delivered history, person-private Knowledge grants, LCM expansion, and inference-to-file confinement remain unchanged or unqualified. #186455 grants agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. ## Why This Change Was Made

The additional tool-result check belongs in the existing users.personalFile owner, where current requester/role/agent, hash conflict, cancellation and final-write assertions already run. It consumes the host's existing requester origin and execution key, not model arguments or another identity manager. Production delta against refreshed base: +43/-11 (net +32). Regression delta: +167 lines across the two existing owner suites. Existing test-line budget passes without an allocation or baseline change. The wider architecture and implementation proposal stays clearly separated from these two implemented slices.

## Evidence

Base: `194b10349b12ee8480e3837b2c90f28803f362cd`. Current head: `7c4889ba5130d3bf074aab481e0aff0abc5b74f4`. All eight published file blobs match the validated local bytes; no task evidence or dependency caches are in the current diff.

### Current tool-result follow-up

The final matrix covers authoritative group/channel origin, origin-key fallback, execution-key fallback, group-origin delegation, and direct-origin execution in a group; denied operations open no filesystem root and leave Alice, Bob, and shared files unchanged. A same-session authoritative direct override still succeeds.
- **60 tests passed across three files**: the 45-case personal-file/chat-tool suite, real isolated Gateway session-only self-edit fixture, and 14 prompt-prefix tests. The combined command took 59.13 s including compilation. A lint-required simplification of the test table preserved all cases; the final 45-case owner suite rerun passed in 12.00 s including compilation (about 0.9 s of test cases).
- The tool fixture uses the production tool → in-process dispatcher → handler → safe filesystem path, with synthetic admitted authority/profile state. Separately, the real isolated Gateway fixture confirms both authenticated people retain Settings self-edit access and role/merge revocation protection. It is not a live group-channel/model test, and captured-origin test cases are not a native delegation E2E pass.
- Core and Gateway-methods test TypeScript checks, scoped oxlint, targeted oxfmt, two-document MDX compilation, exact-base test-line ratchet, and diff whitespace checks pass. The first follow-up lint found an inefficient test-fixture map/spread; the fixture was simplified rather than suppressing the rule. Final lint and typing ran serially and exited 0.

It inspected source/tests but did not execute them. The subsequent fixture-table rewrite was mechanical and rerun green. The earlier hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime code.

The unchanged bootstrap slice previously passed 58 tests across seven files. Those results remain scoped to that slice, not a second execution of the full combined feature. Neither a common-loader pass nor a synthetic caller-origin case transfers to another harness. The complete two-person Knowledge–LosslessClaw save/compact/restart/recall/direct-file-denial scenario remains unqualified. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): queued turn re-compacts a small context when preflight accounting is refused
prs.body:
Related: #140819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a busy chat session would compact its context again on the very next queued turn, even though the context was far below the compaction budget. Each spurious pass spent minutes summarizing, appended another summary on top of the previous one, blocked the queued message behind the session lane, failed that queued message with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded`, and surfaced another "Context compacted" card. On one Signal session this repeated four times in fourteen minutes; three of the four ran against a context of roughly 84k, 120k, and 91k tokens against a 252k budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token-triggered preflight compaction committed the compaction to the transcript inside the queued compactor's session-lane task, but recorded the session-row accounting (count, `totalTokens`, byte latch) only after that task returned and the lane was released. A run waiting on the lane claims the session writer as its first lane write, so the accounting compare-and-swap was correctly refused, the row kept its pre-compaction fresh total, and the next preflight projected pressure from that stale total and compacted again. The queued compactor already exposes a host commit callback that runs while the lane and writer fence are still held; the Codex transcript-byte path used it and the token path did not. This change routes accounting through that callback for every runtime, and supplies the transcript-settled callback for byte-triggered compaction on every runtime so the byte latch keeps measuring the post-maintenance transcript. Nothing about the writer, lifecycle, or session guards changes: a writer that replaces the row before the host commit is still refused, and the after-return path remains only for compactors that emit no host commit.

Non-goals: no retry against a replacement writer, no schema or config change, no change to projection inputs or context limits.

## User Impact

After a preflight compaction, the session's recorded context and compaction count match the transcript, so the following queued turn no longer re-compacts a small context, the queued message is delivered instead of failing, and users stop seeing back-to-back "Context compacted" cards for a session that was not over budget.

## Evidence

- Regression test `lands before a run waiting on the session lane claims the writer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`) models the queued-execution contract against a real SQLite session store: successor acceptance and host commit inside the lane, then a replacement writer claim once the compactor returns. Red/green on this head: with the pre-change `agent-runner-memory.ts` from `upstream/main` swapped in, that test fails with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded` thrown from `recordCompactionAccounting` (1 failed, 125 passed); with the change it passes, the count and `totalTokens` land, the replacement writer's claim is intact, accounting runs exactly once, and the next preflight does not compact again.
- Guard test `does not account against a writer that replaced the row before the host commit` keeps the newer-writer protection on the in-lane path.
- The byte-latch test now runs for both the Codex and the embedded runtime and asserts the persisted latch right after the first compaction equals the settled (post-maintenance) transcript size. The embedded case would fail if the settled-latch callback were supplied only for Codex, because the in-lane host commit measures the pre-maintenance size.
- Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one invocation): `agent-runner-memory` (126), `session-updates.lifecycle` (17), `compact.queued-successor` (25), `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens` (7), `agent-runner-execution-compaction` (14), `commands-compact.lifecycle` (8): 197 passed. `compact.queued-successor` already pins that `onHostCompactionCommitted` is awaited before the checkpoint and maintenance steps.
- Changed-path gate on this head (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`): all 29 checks pass, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, dead-export scan, and import-cycle check; `git diff --check` is clean. A second red check confirms the byte-latch asymmetry: with the settled-latch callback supplied only for Codex, the embedded case fails (`activeBytes` 314 persisted instead of the settled 186).
- Production correlation (sanitized, from the reporter's gateway): each refused accounting was preceded by `lane wait exceeded` on the same session lane 50 to 330 ms before the accounting error, and the one compaction with no lane waiter recorded its accounting normally. Effective harness was `openclaw`; the model route was an OpenAI subscription Responses route.
- Independent review: repository `autoreview` helper on the Claude engine (`claude-fable-5-1`, xhigh), branch mode against `upstream/main`, P2 threshold: `scoped-clean`, no findings. An earlier Codex-engine autoreview of the pre-amend commit (P1 threshold) and an adversarial read-only concurrency review of the diff and tests were also clean at P0/P1; that review's P2 notes (byte-latch timing on non-Codex byte triggers, comment precision, two test-fidelity cleanups) are addressed in this head.

Known gap: this is a source-only repair validated with focused tests; it has not been applied to a live Gateway. The branch includes a merge of current `upstream/main`; upstream did not touch the changed files.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.

This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.

- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.

The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: feat(plugins): prepare automation tools and preserve runtime defaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automation can be approved or saved with a tool selection that omits a configured default, then fail when its instructions need that tool. Plugins also need a supported way to prepare the selection against the creating turn's executable permissions before requesting approval.

## User Impact

`ctx.prepareCronToolSelection` prepares the concrete selection before approval, and the approval-submission callback retains the original proposal and current authority through the handoff. Embedded runs bind this preparation to their completed tool capture after policy filtering and schema quarantine; preparation before capture or after generation retirement is rejected.

Configured `cron.defaultTools` also extends nonempty effective selections during isolated agent-turn execution for existing and new jobs, without rewriting saved payloads, approvals, or run identity. Normal downstream permission and execution-target checks still apply. Saved `toolsAllowMode: "exact"` opts out durably; `"defaults"` resets that choice. An explicit empty selection remains tool-less, and schedule/name-only edits preserve copied selections. A mode-only reset reloads the current job, prepares its tools before approval, and uses its current configuration revision when saving.

**This remains a draft; full acceptance is incomplete.** Native selected-model tool availability and live consumer qualification remain open. A supported custom-model configuration can expose no shell while the existing native projection infers `read`/`exec`; a partial native bridge list is not proof of the full callable tool set. Session-target runtime default projection remains separate. This change does not add a producer capability API or establish live scheduled `read` execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callbacks reuse default selection, creator authority, plugin admission, and invocation lifetime. Approval keeps its opaque proposal unchanged and carries the prepared selection and mode separately; native persistence checks both. Unresolved configured MCP authority cannot be certified complete merely because app discovery succeeded. Existing policy owners retain their authority checks, and the temporary run projection never changes saved state.

Current main already supplies the Windows pnpm fallback fix (#190727); conflict reconciliation reuses that hook implementation and removes this branch's duplicate route.

## Evidence

- A subsequent main advance to `f9c2c4528e6c3111a01b3411eeab33af2ed38db2` conflicted only in compiled Gateway predicates. Merged it and regenerated through the owner; canonical check passed. Comparing all 566 exported predicate AST signatures after resolving interned functions and regex references found only the intended `isCronAddParams`/`isCronUpdateParams` changes against that main. No prompt/config inputs conflicted, so those checks were not repeated.
- Merged main `a9e6314da7ff4cd96d559ffdfc551837c1a90294` to resolve current conflicts. Reconciliation retains main's canonical execution-schema owner (#185581), including schema copy behavior, alongside denied-tool metadata; uses main's live runtime config selector (#189202) once before defaults-aware preflight; and retains main's provider-hook native bindings. Fresh independent review found no blocker.
- On the merged source, canonical Gateway validator, config baseline, and prompt snapshot checks passed. Config counts match main (2,584 core / 4,003 channel / 4,938 plugin), with unchanged channel/plugin hashes. Direct owner-boundary proof passed canonical schema retention/copy for denied unbound tools and declared-schema precedence. The Vitest wrapper stopped before execution at its sparse Control UI bootstrap dependency; no merged-source Vitest pass or full-CI qualification is claimed.
- Current source: `707a6ded349c09a2776d7fd4670c130e3e2754e1`. Independent source review covered runtime defaults, durable opt-out/reset, opaque approval submission, revision-bound preparation, and native persistence.
- Full CI [41536362996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41536362996) tests predecessor `dfc0526158122a908e83c1cfc7e51eec79514c33`, verified by preflight against trusted workflow `d894035c7829ab46e9ffde0561b87d89b6737f13`. Production types, both core test-type stripes, general test types, cron core and isolated-agent shards passed; new payload-merge mode/default regression cases passed under Node and Bun. This run remains in progress with failures and does not qualify the newer generated repair head or replace native PR merge admission.
- Current-head generated repairs address that run's stale prompt snapshots and Gateway predicates. Canonical snapshot and Gateway validator checks passed locally. The Gateway generator now emits portable forward-slash declaration imports on Windows; POSIX output is unchanged, and both path cases passed. The compiled declarations are byte-identical to the prior source. The large predicate diff is schema-function interning/renumbering around the new exact/defaults mode; independent review compared its reduced semantic delta.
- Remaining manual CI failures include the cron caller-revocation timeout (Node 932/933; Bun 933/933), plus other source failures and a Matrix package postinstall HTTP 500 that prevented one shard from running. Passing Bun does not repair Node. The new config-help translation key also fails ordinary manual Control UI i18n parity; repository policy assigns locale/fallback metadata refresh to the postmerge locale owner, so generated locale files are excluded from this source PR. No gate waiver or passing full-CI verdict is claimed.
- Predecessor CI [41465985162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41465985162) tested `a7d44274c866acd7dc423fba1c6766d61f8d32bc` and failed 18 source jobs. The corresponding Bun cron and plugin-update shards passed, which does not repair the Node failures.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

Closes #190640

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp reconnects fill the agent's 20-entry system event queue, so later notices are dropped.

## User Impact

User impact: the queue holds only the latest WhatsApp connection state per account.

## Why This Change Was Made

## Evidence

Real `monitorWebChannel` and system-event queue, 12 reconnects, e2e lane (`vitest.e2e.config.ts`):

```
main: x keeps one connection notice queued across reconnects
  AssertionError: expected [ Array(20) ] to deeply equal [ 'WhatsApp gateway connected.' ]
  (20 alternating "connected" / "disconnected (status 499)" notices)
fix:  ok keeps one connection notice queued across reconnects
  queue is ["WhatsApp gateway connected."]; a later "hook finished" event is accepted
```

`tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` is set, when the room is stored in `m.direct`, when a recent invite was promoted, or when opted-in per-room recovery allows it.

## Evidence

On commit `567572f5adc51a` the direct-room tracker refuses an unnamed two-member room before the cache seeds, and it still accepts `is_direct` and `m.direct`. The QA harness sets the Matrix wildcard group to accept a reply without a mention, because those smoke rooms are groups now.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
```

prs.title: Fix update command refusing all runs on managerless Linux hosts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux hosts without a systemd user session (Docker dev containers, Codespaces, WSL without systemd), every `openclaw` command was refused whenever runtime artifacts needed rebuilding - on the first run and after any edit under `src/`:

```
Local runtime artifact publication failed: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified. Run `openclaw gateway status --deep`, stop the affected Gateway with `openclaw gateway stop`, ...
Caused by: ServiceInspectionError: No supported service manager detected.
```

No Gateway was ever installed or started on such hosts, so there is nothing running to protect.

Root cause: `withGatewayRuntimeArtifactPublication` calls `readGatewayServiceState(...)` with `requireEffective: true`. The strict read path runs read-binding admission before the absence proof, and on a managerless host admission throws `ServiceInspectionError("service-manager-unavailable")` - so the existing absent fast path (which already falls through to lock/port checks) is never reached.

## Fix

In `readGatewayServiceState`: when strict read-binding admission fails with `service-manager-unavailable`, adopt the daemon's absent state (`missingUnit: true`, `not-loaded`, `running: false`) **only** when two affirmative facts hold - no runtime selector (`!isGatewayServiceEnv`) and no installed unit definition in either scope (`findInstalledSystemdGatewayScope === null`, a pure file-system scan with no native calls). A missing manager alone cannot prove absence (it also covers a missing `systemctl` where an installed-but-uninspectable unit may use its own state directory and port), so anything inconclusive keeps the original refusal.

## Evidence

- The regression test reproduces the exact refusal on main (`UpdatePreMutationError` caused by `service-manager-unavailable`) and passes on the branch; `service-absence.test.ts` gains a positive managerless case and a planted-user-unit refusal case (14/14 in that file)
- Live verification in a managerless dev container: with no unit planted, strict reads now return the absent state and publication falls through to the active-lock and port checks; with a user unit planted at the same profile, the strict read keeps refusing - the installed-but-uninspectable case
- Diagnostics from the affected container: `/run/systemd` exists (`/run/systemd/system` does not), `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset, `systemctl`/`busctl` present, no `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw*` units; `isSystemdServiceAbsent()` returns false there because the complete-runtime-directory-absent requirement defeats it - the fact that stops the existing absence proof
- `oxlint` clean on changed files; review discussion and environment-independent test pinning in cc0bd2142a / 8d3b2fabbd

Fixes #190061

prs.title: fix(sessions): CJK transcript searches return zero results
prs.body:
Refs #140736 — the issue stays open as the tracking item for the broader CJK recall half, so this PR should not auto-close it.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users searching session transcripts in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean got zero results even for text that is clearly in the history. A query like `会议` matches nothing while English queries over the same sessions work.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session_transcript_fts` is created with `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, which keeps a whole run of Han/Kana/Hangul as a single token (nothing to split on), so no exact-phrase term can address text inside such a run. Migrating the index schema would force a full rebuild for every existing agent, so this takes the query-side path instead: when `MATCH` returns zero rows and the query contains a CJK run, only the CJK-run terms are retried with `LIKE` (escaped, AND-combined); non-CJK terms stay on the exact-word `MATCH` path so a mixed query like `会议 cat` cannot widen into a substring match. Same session filter, `needs_rebuild` exclusion, ordering and `LIMIT + 1` as before.

The fallback only fires on a zero-hit query, so it stays off every normally served path.

Scope note: this is the zero-hit mitigation only. The issue's partial-recall half (CJK runs that the tokenizer *did* index but rank poorly) is untouched and the issue stays the tracking item for it.

## User Impact

CJK transcript searches return hits, with excerpts anchored on the matched term instead of the start of the message, and mixed-language queries keep their word-matching semantics.

## Evidence

- New cases in `session-transcript-search.test.ts`: CJK fallback hit with multi-term AND, session-scoped filtering, a non-CJK zero-hit query staying on the MATCH path, a late-message excerpt regression (60 filler words + CJK at the end — fails on the previous head), and a mixed-language false-positive regression (`scattered` must not satisfy `cat` — fails on the previous head).
- Focused runs: session-transcript-search 20/20, embedded-gateway-stub 22/22; oxfmt/oxlint clean; assertion-safety ratchet passes locally (`check-assertion-safety-ratchet --base origin/main`).

### Real-behavior proof (gateway `sessions.search`, no mocks)

Driven against a real agent SQLite store in an isolated state dir through the real gateway handler body (validation → scoping → visibility → `searchSessionTranscripts` → respond). Seeded via the production `appendTranscriptMessage` write path. Before = previous head `c3d52ffc`, after = this head.

After fix, query `会议` (late message: 60 filler words then `明天开会议讨论排期，重点是预算评审`):

```json
{
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main",
  "sessionId": "proof-late",
  "role": "user",
  "snippet": "… word37 word38 … word59 明天开会议讨论排期，重点是预算评审",
  "score": 0
}
```

Before fix, same query: the excerpt started at token zero and lost the match entirely — `"snippet": "word0 word1 … word47 … "` with no `会议` visible.

Mixed-language check, query `会议 cat` against a transcript `明天开会议讨论 scattered plans`:

- after fix: `{"results": []}` (no substring false positive on "scattered")
- before fix: returned that transcript (`%cat%` matched the substring)

Cost note on the zero-hit scan: the measured ~2ms was on a 2,000-row store seeded through the real write path, worst case (all-CJK query misses everything). The scan is linear in scanned rows, so latency scales with store size; whether that tradeoff is acceptable as an interim mitigation on much larger stores is exactly the owner decision tracked in the review.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes independent Canvas document clients being unable to honor the Gateway's effective embed ceiling when their paired-device/profile connection cannot use the separate Control UI HTTP bootstrap.

The observable defect is missing policy metadata: authenticated `canvas.document.view` and `canvas.document.preview` return document bytes and sandbox routing, but omit the active `strict | scripts | trusted` ceiling. This PR does not claim that a Windows renderer already consumed the field or that a permissive-rendering exploit was demonstrated.

## User Impact

<!--

Independent clients can read optional `embedSandbox` alongside the document over their existing authenticated RPC connection, without adding an HTTP credential exchange or falling back to a shared token.

This value is a **ceiling, not a permission grant**. Clients must apply any stricter local/content/preview policy; missing or unknown values require strict fallback. Older Gateways remain usable with that fallback. No new RPC, protocol bump, authentication/scope change, origin/CSP relaxation, native renderer or Dashboard substitution is introduced. Client adoption remains separate work.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--

in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.

The existing HTTP bootstrap knows the effective ceiling, but WebSocket profile/identity grants cannot simply be reused as HTTP admission. The narrow fix extends the shared Canvas response and uses the existing bootstrap presentation resolver. After the document/sandbox await, the existing owner revalidates authority and samples one active config snapshot for both sandbox origin and policy, including the default `scripts`.

The schema owns the optional three-mode type; the bootstrap type derives from it. Existing HTML byte limits, persisted-session receipt authorization, host isolation and returned HTML remain unchanged.

At upstream main [`6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb) (2026-10-29), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/canvas.ts:21-26` and `src/gateway/server-methods/canvas.ts:78-86` still lack this field. The contract is not superseded there. Main's handler has since been refactored; these historical tests are not a claim that the branch has been rebased or tested against that new main.

## Evidence

### Review status — 2026-11-02

Open, non-draft, and mergeable at unchanged head `f4997ebbe449861e68a20329657d226e83e9f7a1`. [ClawSweeper’s completed exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180520#issuecomment-6339077137) reports **no code findings**, with platinum-hermit proof and patch quality; overall gold-shrimp reflects the outstanding owner decision on the optional independent-client contract, not an introduced code defect. The [October 29 CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40904823998) is **failed, not running**. Inspected failures:

- [UI shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40904823998/job/123557506738): `chat-comment-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` timed out waiting for an assistant-media attachment response.

The run's failure classifier marked the jobs new because the comparison-main jobs passed; this is **not** a claim of matching baseline signatures. The [latest completed scheduled main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41500791219) also remains red (UI shards 1/4 and Node compact-small shards 4/42). Under the requested hold-off while main has unrelated failures, no rebase or green-chasing rerun was performed. CI remains a visible unresolved integration limitation; review readiness is not merge approval.

No source changes were needed for this readiness cleanup. The owner decision on supporting the optional client contract remains for review, before any merge.

### Exact source and before/after regression

**Ready for review, not merge-approved.** Unchanged head: `f4997ebbe449861e68a20329657d226e83e9f7a1`, tree `19e73baea7c7b2c7b2e4bc24f28cde8ed8095eac`. prs.title: fix(sessions): find CJK text inside transcript words
prs.body:
Related: #140736

Supersedes #143127, thanks @holny

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session transcript searches returning no results for interior Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text, such as `会议` in an unspaced sentence.

## User Impact

After a word search misses, CJK terms can find literal substrings with excerpts around the match. Other terms retain native word, punctuation, symbol, and prefix semantics. The retry scans selected transcript text; narrow the session selection for large histories. Queries that already return hits keep their existing behavior, so broader partial recall remains tracked by #140736.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `unicode61` index treats an unspaced CJK run as one token. A native SQLite probe also found zero `trigram` MATCH hits for the reported two-character query. A query-side retry handles short terms while retaining persisted indexes and avoiding a startup rebuild or schema migration.

Both retrieval attempts execute inline in the existing worker kernel and share filters, active-branch exclusion, ordering, limits, and hydration. Substring-only scans filter mapped sessions before reading text. Residual terms use native word parsers: SQLite probes one bounded query row in a private in-memory FTS5 index built by the existing schema owner, and PostgreSQL uses its native simple parser. This preserves meaningful indexed Unicode symbols without restoring handwritten separator ranges.

Production growth is +102 lines, including the native parser probe needed to preserve the recent punctuation contract. There was no safe pre-existing dead/duplicate owner code to offset this; retrieval retains one query. The 36 regression-test lines extend existing fixtures across both engines.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`: all 5 new CJK cases failed with empty hits; all 15 existing cases passed.
- Residual-punctuation regression red on `dfa2276f7ddefbcb4ac4dca3900bf25893c7306b`: `会议 -` returned no hits, with the other 19 owner cases passing.
- SQLite owner proof on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **20/20 passed**, wrapper **66.59s**, Vitest **64.25s**. Includes punctuation-only remainders and an indexed 🦞 positive/negative control.
- Real PostgreSQL product flow on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-test-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/session-search-product.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **4/4 passed**, wrapper **68.93s**, Vitest **66.16s**. Adds CJK punctuation, mixed-word, and missing-word checks. Existing real-worker fixtures and backend setup account for the file wall times.
- These focused commands ran on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox, lease `tbx_01m6f5bxrp176pqjkh0wzcgb5j` ([lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41535859930)); both exited 0 before lease shutdown. Touched-file oxfmt and type-aware oxlint passed with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Final schema-owner reuse: existing `buildSqliteMemoryBodyFtsSchema` supplies the private probe, with no new dialect SQL definition. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6f6xv0f6g16cwx241yt89mv` ([workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539705281)): SQLite **20/20 passed**, wrapper **76.96s**, Vitest **74.48s**; touched-file format/type-aware lint passed. PostgreSQL inputs are unchanged from the real-backend proof above.
- Final complete-change Codex autoreview at P0–P3, with SQL adapters and the worker entry point supplied as context: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The ClawSweeper punctuation finding is addressed by native token probing and the regressions above. Exact-head [CI run 41540347074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41540347074) completed successfully for `3528e6c7db8a5b00b018905b94c2146290cab2c3`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, the full selected test plan, types, lint, build, and architecture/baseline checks. No inherited-failure exception was needed.
- Contributor source was read only with `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. No standalone live Gateway/model session was run. Proof exercises production transcript writes, real SQLite/workers, and a real PostgreSQL product-flow fixture.

No Team deployment is part of this change.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep pending bind approvals on elapsed time
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainer edits are enabled on this branch: feel free to rebase, adjust wording, split the rewritten deadline case differently, or land it directly without waiting for another round from me.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

**Decision requested (not an approval claim):** this PR moves the pending plugin-binding approval deadline onto elapsed time. It touches an approval/authority boundary, so it needs an owner decision rather than a claim that it is pre-approved. The ClawSweeper `Recommendation` quoted in the review is an **advisory design suggestion, not a contract approval** — it was written by the review bot, and no maintainer has recorded a decision on this direction.

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | the 30-minute decision window is measured on elapsed time; a wall-clock jump neither collapses nor extends it | none beyond the 2-line production change |
| **Decline and close** | keep the wall-clock read gate | a `+40 min` clock jump deletes a pending approval the operator has not answered; the next tap returns `expired` even though real time remained |

**Why this needs a decision:** the change is behavior-preserving under an uncorrected clock (the window still closes after 30 real minutes, by whichever of the two authorities fires first), and it aligns the read gate with the entry's own `setTimeout` authority. But because it changes when an *approval* is considered expired after a host clock correction, the approval/security owner should sign off rather than have this land on a bot recommendation alone.

**Rationale for the proposed direction**

- **Owner:** `src/plugins/conversation-binding-pending.ts` is the sole owner of the pending-approval map (`Symbol.for("openclaw.pluginBindingPendingRequests")`); every write, reset and read of the deadline lives in this one file (`set` :52, timeout :47-49, cap eviction :55-61, read-side expiry :69-74). One import + two comparisons switch the clock domain; no second module reads the field.
- **No contract change:** the entry type is private to the file (not exported), `expiresAtMonotonic` is never persisted, serialized, logged or shown to users (`buildApprovalMessage` and `buildPluginBindingResolvedText` print no timestamps), so the reading is process-local by construction — exactly what `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` documents.
- **Matches the entry's own authority:** each pending entry is already deleted by a real `setTimeout(..., 30 * 60_000)` (:47-49), which measures real elapsed time. The read-side gate was the only measurement in a different domain; it now agrees with the timeout that ultimately governs the same entry.
- **Proof is deterministic and cheap:** four regression cases (success with binding write, requester restriction, standing-grant write, elapsed deadline), base red / head green on the same pinned host, plus a 6-run real-entry clock-step matrix; the suite runs in 49.8s on Node 24.22.1.

**Alternatives considered**

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | the 30-minute decision window is measured on elapsed time; a wall-clock jump neither collapses nor extends it | none beyond the 2-line production change |
| Keep `Date.now()` and document it | no code change | a `+40 min` jump (laptop resume, NTP step, VM restore) deletes a pending approval the operator has not answered yet; the next tap returns `expired` even though minutes of real time remained |
| Drop the read-side gate and rely on `setTimeout` alone | removes the wall-clock read | gives up the "deadline check is authoritative even when the event loop has not dispatched the timer" property that the existing suite explicitly asserts |

**Scope statement:** 2 files, +85/−9; production change is one import, one field rename, two comparisons plus a doc comment. No new option, validator, config key, schema, persistence or shared API. No other approval, exec-deadline or channel clock site is touched.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

The pending plugin-conversation-binding approval map measures its 30-minute decision window on the host wall clock while the same entry's own timeout runs on real elapsed time:

- `+40 min` wall-clock correction (laptop resume, NTP step, VM restore) while an approval is pending: the read-side gate `Date.now() >= entry.expiresAtMs` fires immediately, the entry is deleted, and the operator's next tap on **Allow once / Deny** returns `{ status: "expired" }` → *"That plugin bind approval expired. Retry the bind command."* — on Slack and Telegram this is the **first** wall-clock guard the tap meets (both channels parse the custom id directly; no earlier registry), even though the entry's own 30-minute timeout has barely started.
- `−40 min` correction: the gate goes lax while the timeout stays real, so the two expiry authorities disagree until the timer fires.

Precedent: [#190997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190997) (merged 2026-11-02, same motif) kept the Discord REST entity cache on elapsed time, and [#190894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190894) moved probe timings and cache windows across ~20 sites onto `performance.now()` / `monotonicNow()`. This PR applies the same shape to the pending-approval deadline.

**Honest scope limit:** on **Discord**, a tap first meets the 30-minute component registry (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/components-registry.ts:17,154-161`, wall clock) — that earlier guard expires the button before this map is consulted, so Discord behavior is unchanged by this PR. Slack and Telegram have no such registry, so the pending map is the first guard there. The exec-approval windows this comment mirrors (`src/infra/exec-approvals-core.ts:266` etc.) are still wall-clock; this PR deliberately does not touch them — it only aligns this map's read gate with the timeout that already governs the same entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

`addPendingPluginBindingRequest` now stores `expiresAtMonotonic = monotonicNow() + TTL` and `takePluginBindingRequestForApproval` compares it with `monotonicNow()`. Both readings are process-local, the field never leaves this file, and the real `setTimeout` (which already measures elapsed time) is unchanged. Nothing else moves: the TTL stays `30 * 60_000`, the 512-entry oldest-first cap still evicts by insertion order (no clock), the global-singleton lifecycle reset is untouched, and no option/validator/config/persistence is added.

Production LOC is `+6/−4` (import, field rename + doc comment, two comparisons).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — it completes the elapsed-time cutover the same-entry timeout already implements.

## User Impact

A pending plugin binding approval now survives a wall-clock correction: the operator who receives a bind prompt and answers it after a laptop resume still gets a real decision (approve/deny) instead of an `expired` error requiring the whole bind flow to be restarted. With no clock correction nothing changes — the window still closes after 30 real minutes, by whichever of the two authorities fires first.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `5882d40178b7805a9eb863d89118680e6d7596e7`
- Current-main RED baseline: `d56403f0c3c25e5d579ba26d49db12b26ece6814` (production code untouched; only the rewritten + new test case applied)
  - `src/plugins/conversation-binding-pending.ts` md5 `42706ea54658af95cda3a9373ac4e3f1` (base) → `94f395839fdb872950624bb88656392d` (head)
  - `src/plugins/conversation-binding.test.ts` md5 `e47b4f84b743d913d39fb02b65067404` (base) → `2906fd85a77246410415fd0389a67415` (base + rewritten/new cases / head)
- Production entry: `addPendingPluginBindingRequest` / `takePluginBindingRequestForApproval` in `src/plugins/conversation-binding-pending.ts:42,66`, reached from `resolvePluginConversationBindingApproval` (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.ts:546`)
- Recorder/readback boundary: probe prints `take=request|undefined`; test asserts the resolved approval status object
- Harness: frozen preload sha256 `b5036740d672d736703befc16087c9f9619a0d96ab54c5b17cdf65992d3e0991` (patches **only** `Date.now`, applied 200 ms after the probe's marker file — i.e. after the entry exists), probe sha256 `85f313ca4660b29e90376937cff5b39eec36260a24b94ce50e38b4a22bf30604`, same bytes on both runs, secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker on the pinned test host, loopback only, no credentials

### Inspectable RED → GREEN traces

RED — current main + only the new/rewritten tests (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/conversation-binding.test.ts`, 49.30s):

```text
× fails closed when a pending bind approval reaches its 30-minute deadline
  → expected { status: 'approved', …(3) } to deeply equal { status: 'expired' }
× keeps a pending bind approval actionable across a forward wall-clock step
  → expected { status: 'expired' } to match object { status: 'approved' }
× preserves requester restrictions across a forward wall-clock step
  → expected { status: 'expired' } to match object { status: 'approved' }
× persists an allow-always grant across a forward wall-clock step
  → expected { status: 'expired' } to match object { status: 'approved' }
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  4 failed | 19 passed (23)
```

GREEN — exact head (same command, `94f395839fdb872950624bb88656392d` pending-owner md5 and `2906fd85a77246410415fd0389a67415` test md5 verified in-tree before the run):

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
  Duration  49.82s
```

Real-entry clock-step matrix (frozen preload + probe, 6 runs, exit 0 each):

| Scenario | base (wall gate) | head (elapsed gate) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no-step control | `take=request` | `take=request` |
| `−40 min` step (no wait needed) | `take=request` | `take=request` |
| `+40 min` step after entry exists | **`take=undefined` (approval dropped)** | **`take=request` (window held)** |

### Authority-chain proof (added for the review's real-behavior request)

The shipped channel callbacks all funnel into the same resolver, and this proof runs **through that resolver to the final effect** — the binding-service write and the standing-grant row — not the pending map alone:

- Slack `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/interactions.block-actions.ts:161`, Discord `extensions/discord/src/monitor/agent-components.plugin-interactive.ts:104`, Telegram `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-router-controls.ts:432`

Terminal output mapped to the review's requested controls (base = wall gate, head = elapsed gate; commands and traces above):

| Review control | Test | base (RED) | head (GREEN) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| intended requester succeeds after a forward clock step **with binding write** | `keeps a pending bind approval actionable across a forward wall-clock step` | `expected { status: 'expired' } to match { status: 'approved' }` (gate fired, no write) | `approved`; `sessionBindingState.bind` called exactly once |
| consumed request produces no further write | same test, second approve | — (already red on the success assertion) | `expired`; bind stays 1; grant rows `[]` |
| another requester produces no binding/grant write, entry preserved | `preserves requester restrictions across a forward wall-clock step` | red at the correct-requester success assertion | wrong sender `expired` + bind 0 + rows `[]`, then correct sender `approved` + bind 1 |
| standing-grant write survives the step | `persists an allow-always grant across a forward wall-clock step` | `expected { status: 'expired' } to match { status: 'approved' }` | row `{account_id:"isolated", channel:"discord", plugin_id:"codex", plugin_root:"/plugins/codex-a"}` persisted |

prs.title: fix(agents): keep Claude CLI replies after many large tool results
prs.body:
Related: #150132, #153545

## What Problem This Solves

A tool-heavy Claude CLI turn can lose its final reply with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters` even though most of those characters are discarded tool-result payloads. Claude supplies a preview in `message.content` and echoes full output in `tool_use_result`; the parser hands payloads to consumers and keeps only the tool ID.

Charge pure tool-result records for retained IDs, metadata, unknown fields, whitespace and frames, but discount a conservative lower bound of the discarded payloads' wire size. Numbers count as one character during re-encoding so compact wire literals cannot erase retained charges. Mixed records and payloads too deep to re-serialize keep raw accounting. Per-line limits, ordinary frame limits, deadlines, auth, public APIs and model-facing text are unchanged.

Preserves @RTapiador's three original commits. Simplification removes temporary block/map/spread arrays and skips redundant child-payload measurement. Regression coverage is consolidated into the existing framing owner rather than adding a duplicate suite.

## Evidence

[Inspectable Linux shipped-entry output and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166127#issuecomment-6590762723), exact candidate `47d7ecf0b49fd600b346021176b4a04947978903` versus main `573fd8c1f005293d662890b7aad888ad7643edf5`:

- Source-built `openclaw agent exec`, bundled Anthropic plugin, **native Claude Code 2.1.288**, Node **24.22.1** secretless Linux Docker. Synthetic managed profile and #188069 trusted-CA CONNECT route to a local Claude protocol fixture; no paid provider key or TLS verification bypass.
- Fixture requests 72 real MCP `exec` calls, each emitting **120,000 characters** of line-oriented filler under default limits. This is a character count, not a claimed tokenizer measurement.
- **Main 2/2:** budget error, empty final reply; 67 large results completed before cancellation. **Candidate 2/2:** all 72 tools completed with zero failures and final reply delivered; native full-result payloads totaled **8,749,800** encoded characters per run.
- Short runs pass **2/2 per build** unchanged. Retained-ID negative controls still hit the unchanged budget **2/2 per build**. Plugin-claimed tool records still charge full raw payload/padding in focused controls.
- Focused parser suites **69/69**, changed TypeScript lint clean; identical discarded-text regression fails on main. Numeric re-encoding, mixed records, metadata, padding, raw lines, frames, deep fallback, child attribution and retained snapshots remain covered.
- Whole PR delta: production **+43/-1 (44 gross)**, tests **net −19**, docs +3.

## Merge danger

**Two-way door:** revert restores the old accounting; no storage/configuration/schema or public API migration. Blast radius is Claude stream-json tool-result accounting. An excessive discount could weaken retained-output bounds, so only pure tool-result payloads qualify and the line/frame, mixed-record, metadata, padding and conservative-number guards remain active. Custom plugin-claimed records bypass the discount and retain full raw charging.

prs.title: fix(macos): WIP — Launch at Login reports success after launchctl fails
prs.body:
Related: #127613

**WIP — the native API compatibility correction is published; fresh native CI is pending. Browser visual proof is available, but native execution, actual settings/upgrade proof, and full SourceKit-backed lint remain incomplete. Not ready for review or merge.**

## What Problem This Solves

Launch at Login could report success after launchctl failed; waiting for that operation inside the settings queue also prevented a newer Off choice from superseding an unfinished enable.

## User Impact

Failed changes reconcile the toggle and surface recovery guidance. A later login choice can reach the existing launch-agent owner before older work activates the app. Loaded-job refresh and disabling future autostart still leave the running app alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch-agent owner checks required command statuses, stops on failure, restores the previous plist when activation fails, and publishes only its current intent's outcome.

The continuation at `ef351f748081480fe9981bef2680eb88637cf984` separates validated FIFO admission from reply completion. AppState reserves the login intent synchronously, before returning its completion task; the existing request queue retains and cancels deferred replies without blocking later admissions. Ordinary requests retain their previous serialization and consent behavior. Errors are associated with their own intent rather than read from a later request's shared error state.

The follow-up at `511d29078844175382e98b7fa3701b96e10ad75f` names the deferred entry point `enqueueAdmission`, rather than overloading `enqueue`. This removes an observed iOS compile ambiguity while preserving existing `enqueue { … } onCancel: { … }` callers and their FIFO behavior. The shared cancellation fixture now exercises that legacy call shape and immediate reply retirement.

This preserves [#145451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145451)'s synchronous intent reservation, serialized launch-agent writes, and stale-hydration protection. No bridge wire keys, stored-data schema, configuration, dependencies, or upstream CI were changed.

## Evidence

- **Current source:** `511d29078844175382e98b7fa3701b96e10ad75f`, published as roboclaw-bot. Its complete tree matches the reviewed candidate. Independent automatic review of the complete 11-file candidate found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This is static review, not Swift compilation or runtime proof.
