prs.title: fix(cli): config get spends ~200 ms on an unused schema for agents, channels and plugins paths
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176318

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config get` for paths under `agents`, `channels` or `plugins` spends about 200 ms per call building the full config form schema, which it never reads when the value exists.

## User Impact

User impact: `config get` on those paths returns about 190 ms (18%) faster in the measured setup, with byte-identical output, redaction and exit codes. Not-found paths still print the same "valid but unset" or "Unknown config path" message.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175818 moved the Gateway's redaction-only readers to the lighter `buildConfigRedactionHints`, which merges sensitivity metadata without building or tier-resolving the form schema. The CLI reader `runConfigGet` was left on `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry`: it used `.uiHints` for redaction and `.schema` only for the not-found message.

- `runtime-schema.ts` gains `buildRuntimeConfigRedactionHintsFromRegistry`, the hint-only sibling of `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry` over the same registry metadata.
- `runConfigGet` redacts with it and builds the full schema only when the path is not found.
- The Doctor report for externally managed config (`reportDoctorExternalConfigRepairs`) had the same shape and uses the same hint builder.

Redaction reads only `sensitive` and the URL-sensitivity tag. The full schema's hints carry 110 more keys with those fields than the redaction-only hints (bundled registry, 171 plugins). They come from the presentation passes over the merged schema, which copy a matching hint onto the schema paths they visit (for example the `source`/`provider`/`id` fields of SecretRef inputs). A schema-shaped value built at each of those 110 paths redacts identically with both hint sets.

## Evidence

Tested at `0f23ad6c8dc` (base `upstream/main` `94fa98bfd93`).

Built CLI (`pnpm build:runtime`, `node openclaw.mjs config get <path>`, Node 24, Ubuntu 22.04) under an allowlisted environment with an isolated home and no network. Config: default plus `agents.defaults.model`, a synthetic `channels.discord.token` and a synthetic `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey`. Nothing faked.

Before (base `94fa98bfd93`):

```text
wall time, 10 runs each (ms)
gateway.mode           838 846 844 838 847 843 841 840 841 834   (control: no plugin schema)
agents.defaults.model  1067 1059 1073 1058 1066 1063 1065 1072 1066 1050

CPU profile, config get agents.defaults.model (main thread 1,024 ms), inclusive
  222.5 ms  runConfigGet
  209.8 ms  buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry
  206.6 ms  buildConfigSchemaCore
    4.2 ms  redactConfigObject
```

After (this PR):

```text
wall time, 10 runs each (ms)
gateway.mode           846 839 848 839 834 844 840 845 834 843   (control: unchanged)
agents.defaults.model  868 865 873 866 874 869 869 882 865 870

CPU profile, config get agents.defaults.model (main thread 833 ms), inclusive
   41.4 ms  runConfigGet
   31.8 ms  buildRuntimeConfigRedactionHintsFromRegistry
   29.7 ms  buildConfigRedactionHints
    2.1 ms  redactConfigObject
  (buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry not called)
```

Observed result: found values drop from 1,050–1,073 ms to 865–882 ms while the control stays at 834–848 ms. Stdout, stderr and exit codes are byte-identical between base and branch on 11 paths: `gateway.mode`, `agents.defaults.model`, `agents --json`, `channels.discord.token`, `channels.discord --json`, `plugins.entries.tavily --json`, `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` (both secrets print `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`), and the not-found paths `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, `agents.defaults.nope`, `plugins.entries.nope`, `channels.nope --json`.

Tests: the existing redaction case in `config-cli.integration.test.ts` (SecretRef ids, core and plugin schema-sensitive fields) now also asserts that `buildRuntimeConfigSchemaFromRegistry` is not called. The fail-closed case now injects its failure into the hint builder that found values use. Run on the base and this branch, both fail on the base (the schema builder is called 4 times; the hint builder does not exist yet) and pass here, with the other 25 tests in the file passing on both.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve secret store results when cleanup fails
prs.body:
Closes #127544 (reported by @steipete).

## What Problem This Solves

Offline `secrets store` mutations can commit successfully and then exit `1` without a completion message when an independent expired-entry purge fails. A multi-name removal also stops before its remaining requested names.

## User Impact

Successful local `set`, `rm` and `import` commands keep their completion result and exit `0` when only retention cleanup fails. They emit one warning on stderr per command, including a multi-name removal. Primary mutation and ownership failures retain their failure behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR proposes **success with a cleanup warning** for the exit-contract choice in the issue, matching the existing Gateway's best-effort retention cleanup. It remains a proposal for maintainer review. The catch surrounds only the independent purge; it does not encompass the authoritative mutation, current-owner check, resource settlement or Gateway runtime refresh.

The existing command-output wrapper owns warning deduplication, and every mutation caller supplies that command's reporter. No storage implementation, transaction boundary, retention period, schema, version or public configuration is changed. The necessary production growth is 21 lines for outcome separation and command-scoped reporting; no new manager or exported test seam is introduced.

## Evidence

Validation base: `cdf14a50f59a5abe5ce3df008d3141e9e789f2cc`. The reviewed and validated file bytes were committed unchanged as `b928d1c4cfa979e8bed514c178c7039021f80f90`.

- **Real CLI/SQLite before:** a disposable expired tombstone was created with normal CLI writes under a fixture clock. An external Node preload rejected only the expiry kernel's native `DELETE ... deleted_at_ms < ...` preparation; the product schema was untouched. Actual `set` and two-entry `import` values were readable in independent CLI processes, yet both commands exited `1` with no success message. A two-name `rm` committed its first removal, then exited `1` before the second. This normal CLI reproduction took **73.82s**.
- **Real CLI/SQLite after:** with the same purge fault still observed at the native statement boundary, all three commands exit `0` with their normal completion and **one** cleanup warning. Both removal targets are absent, the set value is `debug`, and both imported values match. An independent primary-INSERT failure still exits `1`, emits no completion and leaves no value. All owned CLI process groups drained; **88.44s**. Private HOME/state/PID/network namespaces were used; no operator Gateway, external model or paid resource was used.
- **Committed regression:** the four selected cases were **3 intended failures / 1 primary-failure control pass** before the fix. The complete changed CLI suite is now **21 passed**; **112.96s wrapper wall / 102.10s Vitest**, mostly compiler/import preparation. The existing Gateway purge-failure/reload contract also passes (**1 selected case**, 11 unrelated cases filtered out); its handler still returns the committed result after purge failure.
- **Checks:** scoped production and test-consumer types, canonical typed lint, formatting, MDX, whitespace and line/max-line/test-line ratchets pass. The separate allocation is exactly **42 net new test lines**; the shared scalar is unchanged. Native test budget is **6,364,033 / 6,383,792**, leaving **19,759** lines.
- **Independent review:** canonical `autoreview`, Codex, P0–P2, **scoped-clean** for the source/test/docs. Its sensitive-filename filter omitted the public allocation text; that two-line metadata record was independently checked against its staged blob and actual +42 LF delta, with no findings. The filter was retained.

Recorded after-fix child-process stdout/stderr excerpts follow. Only ANSI color and private fixture paths/addresses are redacted; these are captured streams, not reconstructed command results. Values below are synthetic, non-secret env entries.

<details>
<summary>Actual CLI output with the purge fault active, plus the primary-failure control</summary>

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store set LOG_LEVEL --kind env --value debug
stdout:
Stored LOG_LEVEL (env).

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store set LOG_LEVEL --kind env --value debug
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store rm REMOVE_ONE REMOVE_TWO --yes
stdout:
Removed 2 team store entries.

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store rm REMOVE_ONE REMOVE_TWO --yes
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store import --from <fixture.env> --yes
stdout:
Imported 2 team store entries.

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store import --from <fixture.env> --yes
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store set REJECTED_VALUE --kind env --value never
stdout:

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store set REJECTED_VALUE --kind env --value never
synthetic primary-insert unavailable
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

exit=1
```

</details>

Actual Node **24.22.1** / pnpm **12.15.0** satisfy this branch. The frozen installation's physical runtime lock matches the branch. Normal CLI build checks passed before and after; an initial offline build could not fetch lock-pinned native assets, so the trusted build populated its verified public package cache first. The CLI fault proof itself remained network-isolated.

This proves the Linux offline CLI reporting contract and real persisted mutations under a bounded injected cleanup failure. It is not a released-version upgrade/rollback, macOS/Windows or provider/model test. Gateway routing and its required runtime-refresh failure semantics are unchanged and remain distinct from retention cleanup.

prs.title: fix(update): PostgreSQL rollback retries fail after a recoverable refusal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL update rollback fails with `EEXIST` on every retry after a recoverable refusal before database publication.

## User Impact

User impact: after correcting the reported obstruction, operators can retry the same native `update restore --backup-root` request. Earlier recovery preparations, original PostgreSQL namespaces, current update history, and existing publication/authority checks remain intact. No schema, configuration, durability, or retention-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each attempt needs a fresh anchor destination. Add an attempt UUID to the existing recovery artifact name rather than overwriting or trusting an earlier preparation. The existing backup/recovery owner still owns those artifacts; no new lifecycle manager or cleanup policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Real baseline RED before the production edit:** built source `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, isolated PostgreSQL 18.6, actual Gateway readiness, Workboard CLI creation, and persisted native migration receipt. A task-owned `.migrated-<runId>` obstruction caused the intended prepublication refusal. Removing only that obstruction and retrying the same receipt failed at `COPYFILE_EXCL` with `EEXIST`. Original anchor/store and namespace remained intact. Full run: 54.17 seconds. This initial product reproduction used Node 24.20.0; final proof below uses the supported runtime.
- **Real fixed product flow:** reviewed working-tree build on Node **26.12.1**, PostgreSQL **18.6**; no mocked transport or storage. Same request: obstruction refused, obstruction removed, retry returned `status: restored`. The retained Workboard card and store UUID matched; the new anchor pointed at a verified fresh namespace; original namespace survived; SQLite audit AUTOINCREMENT high-watermark **5000** and exact current update-history rows were preserved. Real `workboard list --json` returned the card, and the restored Gateway reached `/readyz` ready. All task-owned children joined. **89.36 seconds**. Workboard has no PostgreSQL identity sequence; the explicit allocation oracle is the SQLite companion store, not an invented PG sequence.
- **Committed regression path:** the extended existing PostgreSQL backup integration case is RED on unchanged production base at the intended `EEXIST`, then GREEN with the fix. It retains binary/large-integer canonical data and exact-state restore checks. New test growth: **12 lines**, separately allocated; no additional fixture/boot. Base wrapper 65.49 seconds; fixed backup case 19.44 seconds.
- **Affected siblings:** **36 tests passed in 3 files**, including SQLite generation/refusal, interrupted-publication retention, current-history preservation, live authority, local credential, and native update retry/config recovery controls. Full fixed wrapper **284.36 seconds**, including worker preparation. Targeted production-core and infra-test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, line-budget ratchet, docs inventory, and whitespace checks passed.
- **Build:** supported `pnpm build:runtime` completed, **97.48 seconds**. This ran on the reviewed prepublication working-tree snapshot, not a subsequently created Git commit. The tested production owner SHA-256 is `7e92a49f9e88e1b9621fc37a1af868b73fc5a9ccdca157b5f8b9f749ee66f96a`; both build stamps bind the selected base plus their recorded input signatures. Current main `02b28c9d0b5ae329b07a1e758c9cfca8f1798bca` has byte-identical restore-owner source to the selected base. The published production owner at `ef4f16f4c253f84d951d79bc26d3904bd034bb49` was independently fetched and matches the tested SHA-256 above.
- **Fresh independent Auto Review:** complete local candidate against `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, P0–P2, source context for restore/backup/native CLI and SQLite controls: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Source assessment; reviewer did not rerun tests.
- **New mature published-data compatibility proof (not latest stable):** normal npm installation of exact `openclaw@2026.10.7` passed the unchanged seven-day age policy; the installed binary reports `2026.10.7 (157d8c2)`, matching first-party tag commit `157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e`. Its real Gateway created a durable session, persisted an injected transcript without inference (`runStarted:false`), and wrote `USER.md` through its RPC. Published SQLite schemas **state 20 / agent 25** upgraded through the candidate native protocol to **37 / 39**; the candidate Gateway loaded the same transcript and retained timezone, workspace, auth selection and exact user-file bytes. Native rollback restored **20 / 25**; the actual published Gateway restarted and read the retained transcript and settings. After re-upgrade, a real SQLite Workboard card was ported to PostgreSQL, the synthetic obstruction refused publication, and the same receipt successfully retried after removing only that obstruction. Final candidate Gateway history, Workboard rows/store UUID, original PostgreSQL namespace and settings remained intact. **148.95 seconds; all children joined; no mocked storage/transport, no model calls.** The released Gateway briefly advertised `agent-database-inspection-pending`; the harness followed that specific retryable readiness response before checking history. The first harness attempt stopped at that readiness response and is not counted as a passing run.
- **Latest-stable published-data compatibility — PASS:** exact published **2026.10.9 (8b18b55)**, installed from npm in a disposable prefix, then the already-built candidate at the unchanged production SHA-256 above. Node **26.12.1**, PostgreSQL **18.6**, **178.49 seconds**. The actual released Gateway created a persistent session/transcript without inference (`runStarted:false`) and wrote `USER.md`. Native candidate `update migrate --backup-root` upgraded published SQLite schemas **state 20 / agent 25 → 37 / 39**. The candidate Gateway read the transcript. Native `update restore --backup-root` restored **20 / 25**, and the actual published 2026.10.9 Gateway restarted and read the original transcript. Timezone, workspace setting, auth selection and exact user-file bytes survived each boundary. Re-upgrade and native `update finish` succeeded. Then actual `database port --family workboard --to postgres` ported a SQLite card; a task-owned publication obstruction refused recovery; removing only that obstruction let the **same persisted receipt** retry successfully. Final candidate Gateway history, PG card/store UUID, original namespace and settings matched. All children joined. The released history endpoint briefly returned its advertised retryable `agent-database-inspection-pending`; the harness waited only for that specific response. This exercises installed-release/native-upgrade/native-rollback/released-Gateway compatibility, not a managed package-swap installer.
- **Narrow, human-authorized installation exception:** the ordinary seven-day age guard initially refused the Oct. 29 release. The requester subsequently authorized test-only exceptions for **only `openclaw@2026.10.9` and `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.9`**. Before installation, registry ownership, expected SHA-512 integrity, official release tag/build identity and registry SLSA provenance were checked. Both provenance subjects bind first-party publication tooling commit `ee860ffb31039c05bacacd3387c05649c0ea7033` (merged official [#187565](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187565)); Git ancestry to current official main was verified. The product build separately binds release commit `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` and official release [#187583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187583); that maintenance-release commit was not falsely treated as a main ancestor. Exact top-level manifest pins and every matching lock entry/integrity were checked **before executing the released binary**. `npm audit signatures` passed: **493 verified registry signatures, 150 verified attestations**. All other dependencies retained the seven-day guard; existing install-script approvals were unchanged (unapproved scripts were not run). No global/workspace config or persistent exception file was changed. Disposable installation removed after proof; selected lock/build metadata and sanitized results retained locally. The earlier accidentally reconciled prefix stayed quarantined and supplied no proof.

<details>
<summary>Latest-stable proof commands and sanitized terminal result</summary>

Task-owned Node 26.12.1 and npm cache were used. Only the two literal additional package names were exempted, with exact version pins; existing Codex exclusions were preserved:

```sh
npm install --prefix .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/stable-2026.10.9-authorized-exact \
  --save-exact --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund --min-release-age=7 \
  --min-release-age-exclude='@openai/codex' --min-release-age-exclude='@openai/codex-*' \
  --min-release-age-exclude='openclaw' --min-release-age-exclude='@openclaw/ai' \
  openclaw@2026.10.9 @openclaw/ai@2026.10.9
npm audit signatures --prefix .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/stable-2026.10.9-authorized-exact
.openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/tools/node-v26.12.1-linux-x64/bin/node \
  .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/published-latest-proof.mjs latest-upgrade-1
```

The local harness invoked the installed public CLI directly for the released baseline and `pnpm openclaw` for the built candidate; it asserted produced state, not CLI exit codes alone:

```text
EXACT_RELEASE_PIN_VERIFIED version=2026.10.9 commit=8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41
published Gateway ready; session.runStarted=false; injected transcript and user file persisted
published schemas: state=20 agent=25
candidate-upgrade: exit=0; candidate Gateway ready; schemas: state=37 agent=39
candidate-rollback: exit=0; published Gateway ready; original transcript/settings read back
PUBLISHED_BASELINE_UPGRADE_ROLLBACK_DATA_SETTINGS_PASS
candidate-reupgrade: exit=0; candidate-accept: exit=0
port-workboard: exit=0; capture-pg-update: exit=0
pg-restore-obstructed: exit=1 (expected publication refusal); original anchor unchanged
pg-restore-retry: exit=0 (same receipt, only owned obstruction removed)
COMPATIBILITY_PROOF_PASS publishedVersion=2026.10.9 latestStable=true
  publishedTranscript=true settings=true userFile=true pgCard=true
  storeId=true originalNamespace=true sameReceiptRetry=true
ALL_PROOF_CHILDREN_JOINED
```

No model calls, live Team state, cloud resources or credentials were used. Production source/head and maturity policy remained unchanged by this proof.

</details>

- **Exact-head CI:** `ef4f16f4c253f84d951d79bc26d3904bd034bb49` passed all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41263453372/job/124726369419). No code or head change was made for this new proof. Current main `72cab24990b3746574ac83e3d73c79530b8cc198` retains byte-identical pre-fix restore-owner source.

Simplification: production **+2 net lines**, regression **+12**; one allocation decision stays with its existing owner. Existing conservative retention of earlier recovery preparations is unchanged.

Worked on by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

prs.title: improve: reduce PostgreSQL agent removal latency
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removing an agent incurs repeated avoidable database work when the gateway uses PostgreSQL, increasing single-agent removal latency.

## User Impact

Agent removal spends less time checking deletion authority. A delayed check also refuses journal ownership changes before returning to its caller. There is no public RPC, configuration, or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`agentDeletion.assertCurrent` currently opens a write transaction even though it only checks authority. Use the existing lease verifier and deletion-journal predicate without that transaction, retaining live operation admission and a final durable lease verification. After the worker reply, the lifecycle owner checks its existing live lease and committed-journal authority before resolving. Retire, fence, finish, rollback, and purge mutations retain their guarded transactions and final-effect checks.

## Evidence

### Upstream `agents.delete` on PostgreSQL

Built the upstream source tree that became `7a83bcd4768dfde3f991f5f3385c4b9e17ff6cfb` (base `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`) with `pnpm build:docker`. Exercised the real loopback Gateway WebSocket RPC against disposable PostgreSQL 17, with seven synthetic agents and one seeded session/message per agent. Each deletion requested `deleteFiles: true`.

| Measurement | Original authority transaction | Optimized authority check |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median warm RPC latency | 9,241.65 ms | 7,784.57 ms |
| Median SQL statements observed during RPC | 840 | 695 |
| Cold first RPC | 9,484.88 ms | 7,924.05 ms |

**15.8% lower median latency in this workload.** Both variants removed the target from the roster, refused writes from its old session, removed its workspace, kept the surviving agent writable, and allowed recreation with empty active history.

This is a controlled operation toggle, not two pristine checkout builds: both variants use the same built upstream tree and the new final host fence; the baseline restores only `agentDeletion.assertCurrent` to its original `guarded(..., () => undefined)` handler. No batch RPC or downstream `agents.detach` endpoint is involved in these measurements.

The final pair ran sequentially after local build/check/review work completed. Each boot performed six deletions; the first cold call was excluded from the five warm samples. A loopback TCP relay injected 5 ms in each database direction only during the measured RPC. SQL totals include fixture background statements observed during the RPC. These are synthetic local measurements, not production RTT or a production speedup guarantee. The full reported 25–40 second production delay remains unexplained.

<details>
<summary>Raw warm output</summary>

```text
original ms:  9309.24, 9151.42, 9110.64, 9301.61, 9241.65
optimized ms: 7831.06, 7784.57, 7599.33, 7803.42, 7739.55
original SQL calls:  840, 844, 840, 840, 849
optimized SQL calls: 695, 699, 694, 695, 695
```

</details>

### PostgreSQL final-effect custody proof

Used the same upstream `agents.delete` RPC and source tree in a separate disposable runtime, with a diagnostic pause immediately before the existing purge call. After the gateway reached that pause, a fixture client changed exactly one PostgreSQL authority row, then released the pause. Instrumentation added no authority check or alternate cleanup path. Trace probes watched the existing purge commit, archive publication, and Trash boundaries.

```text
expired lease:
  agents.delete -> OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST (lease loss: expired)
  original session retained; retirement archive rows = 0
  original workspace and agent anchor retained
  destructive-boundary trace = []

superseded journal operation_id, same lease retained:
  agents.delete -> Agent traveler0 deletion no longer owns database cleanup.
  original session retained; retirement archive rows = 0
  original workspace and agent anchor retained
  destructive-boundary trace = []
```

The positive deletion run above proves the ordinary path reaches cleanup; these negative runs prove revocation is rejected before that cleanup. They exercise revocation before the first purge, not every possible instruction-level interleaving. The temporary diagnostic harness is not part of this PR.

### Delayed-reply regression and checks

Extended the existing real-worker late-reply test to commit journal handoff, completion, or rollback after the worker read and before reply delivery. All three cases **failed on the original PR head** because the promise resolved successfully. With the existing final journal guard checked before resolution, all four cases (including scope closure) pass. This protects the lifecycle result boundary after the worker's database read or transaction has ended.

- **47 lifecycle and deletion-cleanup tests pass**; 78.30 s wrapper wall time, 44.71 s Vitest duration. The changed lifecycle file runs 22 cases, with 12.76 s summed test-body time. It uses real worker admission and commit publication; no new production test seam or sleep was added.
- Core typecheck, type-aware lint of the three touched source/test files, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent local Codex autoreview of the complete candidate: no actionable P0–P2 findings. An initial sandboxed invocation could not reach the service; the completed public-source review is the result reported here.
- [Current-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41531539590) on `7a83bcd4768dfde3f991f5f3385c4b9e17ff6cfb`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- [ClawSweeper follow-up review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191463#issuecomment-6589024083) reviewed the same head: no findings, proof sufficient, ready for maintainer review; the previous security and merge-risk attention items are cleared.
- The dedicated 22-line test allocation covers net growth from the three newly reproduced stale-journal reply cases; it does not change the shared test budget scalar.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.test.ts src/state/agent-deletion-cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.ts src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.test.ts src/state/agent-deletion.worker.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.ts src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.test.ts src/state/agent-deletion.worker.ts
pnpm build:docker
git diff --check
```

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Three serialized Workboard mock tests still seed an empty tasks array that the actual installer never reads.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. All five declarations/seven cases, rows, assertions, clocks and state checks remain. Production and public contracts stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the three unused private seed fields. These seeds enter the installer as serialized strings, so the shared typed builder contract stays intact. Three fewer test lines; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Official untouched baseline, clean candidate and exact published native proof: seven cases pass without skips.
- Throwing getters installed after serialization observe zero tasks reads in original/candidate runs, both passing seven. Injecting an actual installer read rejects all seven at the getter.
- Disabling actual appearance clearing fails the retained icon-absence keeper in both original/candidate runs, each with six passes. The installer is byte-restored and temporary getter wrappers are removed.
- Every removal scan phase completed. The production dependency and unused-export scans report the identical pre-existing loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts export on the untouched base; the other phases pass. The inherited local failure is recorded without suppression.

prs.title: fix(infra): keep the launchd recovery budget on elapsed time
prs.body:
Related to #186484

## What Problem This Solves

When the host clock is corrected during a macOS service update (NTP step, VM pause/resume, manual change), the recovery wait was measured against that jumpy clock — it either ran far past the configured timeout or expired early and refused a healthy `launchctl` restart. The recovery budget now counts elapsed time, so a clock correction no longer stretches or cancels the wait.

- **Problem**: the handoff recovery loop seeded and consumed its budget with `Date.now()` — `const deadline = Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs`, the loop gate `Date.now() < deadline`, and `deadline - Date.now()` sleeps. Every one of those is process-local elapsed time.
- **Solution**: seed the budget with `performance.now()`, gate the loop on `remainingMs() > 0`, and recompute an epoch deadline for each command.
- **What did NOT change**: spawn deadlines stay epoch-valued (they cross the parent-exit process contract) and persisted timestamps (`serviceStoppedAtMs` / `serviceDowntimeMs`) keep reading `Date.now()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

A duration was being measured with a calendar clock. `performance.now()` is monotonic per process and is the convention #186484 already established for the sibling handoff budgets; the launchd recovery loop was the one path that fix left untouched. `process.hrtime.bigint()` was rejected as needlessly low-level. The parent-exit deadline is created in the parent process, so comparing it against `performance.now()` would mix clock domains — deliberately out of scope, along with the persisted downtime stamp.

## User Impact

Self-updating macOS deployments no longer risk a stuck or aborted `launchctl` recovery when the system clock is adjusted mid-update. No configuration or user-facing behavior changes; recovery still honors `recoveryTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Current head `d7393133dfc3`.

### 1) Real `launchctl` recovery, both clock directions (macOS-14 runner)

Run [41479112671](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41479112671). The shipped `MANAGED_HANDOFF_COMMAND_SOURCE` + `MANAGED_HANDOFF_RECOVERY_SOURCE` strings are assembled byte-identically into the detached helper, which drives production `restoreGatewayService()` against a real bootstrapped `gui/501/com.openclaw.proofrecovery` job with a real child PID — genuine `launchctl bootstrap` / `enable` / `print` / `kickstart`. A preload rewrites `Date.now()` (never `performance.now()`) after the budget is seeded, standing in for an NTP correction mid-recovery. Same fixture in every row; only the budget arithmetic differs.

| clock step | budget | recovery result | wall time | real `launchctl print` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| **+60 s** (30 s timeout) | pre-fix `Date.now()` | `restored=false`, loop truncated, `enable` refused | 12 ms | 1 |
| **+60 s** (30 s timeout) | post-fix `performance.now()` | `restored=true`, readiness + runtime identity verified | 63 ms | 3 |
| **−60 s** (4 s timeout, old generation still live) | pre-fix `Date.now()` | polled far past the budget | 63 973 ms | 126 |
| **−60 s** (4 s timeout, old generation still live) | post-fix `performance.now()` | stopped at the budget | 4 003 ms | 9 |

```
[setup] bootstrap -> code=0
[helper] RESULT restored=true wallElapsedMs=63      VERDICT PASS: FIXED restored=true bounded
[helper] RESULT restored=false wallElapsedMs=12     VERDICT PASS: OLD restored=false (loop truncated by forward step)
[helper] RESULT restored=false wallElapsedMs=4003   launchctlPrints=9   VERDICT PASS: FIXED stopped at the monotonic budget
[helper] RESULT restored=false wallElapsedMs=63973  launchctlPrints=126 VERDICT PASS: OLD polled 63973ms — budget stretched by the -60000ms wall-clock step
```

Forward step: post-fix keeps the budget intact so `enable` returns 0 and the fresh PID is observed; pre-fix collapses `deadline - Date.now()` to ≤0 and `runServiceCommand` refuses with `code=1`. Backward step: both rows end `restored=false` (the pre-update PID is still live, so the shipped stale-generation branch keeps polling) — the discriminator is how long: 4 003 ms against a 4 s budget versus 63 973 ms.

### 2) Installed `openclaw update` v2026.10.9 → this head (macOS-14)

Run [41535809313](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41535809313). `openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm runs as a real LaunchAgent (`gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`); `openclaw update --yes --tag 2026.10.10` installs the package built from `d7393133` and hands the service back through launchd.

```
driver=OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55) pre_pid=4397 pre_health=200
phaseB_update_exit=0 status=succeeded after=OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (d739313)
phaseB_health=200 service_pid=21374   (new launchd generation; was pid 4397)
phaseB_marker=MARKER-macos-186831 workspace=workspace-macos-186831 data={"keep":"me","record":42}
phaseB_settings=mode=local port=19031 token_sha256_12=f0aba0d36788   (before = after)
installed_monotonic_budget_files=0 → 1   VERDICT=PASS settingsIntact=yes dataIntact=yes
```

The update's doctor rewrites `openclaw.json`, so retention checks the settings the service reads — gateway mode, port, auth-token fingerprint — plus the seeded marker, workspace note and data file. Run [41523853093](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/41523853093) drives the project's own `published-driver-update` survivor cell against the same head build (buildId `…-release-8b18b5578f66` → `…-d7393133dfc3`), `phase=finished`, `readyz=200`, durable session read back after the swap.

### 3) Regression test (base-red / head-green)

`update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts` runs the embedded command source in a VM with independent `Date` and `performance` objects, steps the wall clock **+1h** then **−2h** mid-budget, and asserts the remaining budget stays `180_000` ms while `commandDeadlineAt()` keeps tracking the live wall clock. Fails against the origin/main implementation (`1 failed | 10 passed`), passes with the fix (`11 passed`). `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and the CI type-check / lint shards are green; `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched.

prs.title: fix(signal): bound the monitor drain so teardown cannot hang
prs.body:
Fixes #191401

## What Problem This Solves

Stopping the Gateway, or restarting the Signal channel, could wait forever. `createSignalMonitorTaskRunner().waitForIdle()` looped while `inFlight` was non-empty with no deadline, and the Signal teardown `finally` awaits it (`Promise.all([stopDaemon(), monitorTaskRunner.waitForIdle()])`). One inbound receive or reply that never settles therefore pinned the whole teardown.

- Problem: the drain loop had no bound, so one stuck task blocked Gateway stop.
- Solution: each drain round resolves against a 30 s window; when the window expires the runner logs what is still in flight and lets teardown continue.
- Changed: `extensions/signal/src/monitor.ts` (bounded drain, exported runner, `SIGNAL_IDLE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS`), plus a focused test file.
- Not changed: `runTask` tracking, teardown ordering, daemon stop, and what happens to the leftover task — it keeps running, as the issue asks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue already fixed the contract in #141305 (closed for inactivity, not rejected): a bounded idle window, leftover work logged and left running, an accepted ingress claim stays queued, and a reply that resolves after the window does not send. This change implements that contract at the owner it names, without widening it: the loop simply gets a deadline per round, so work that drains normally still drains fully.

The window is a named constant and a runner parameter rather than a literal, so the shipped 30 s value is visible at the call site and the test can exercise the expiry without waiting 30 s.

## User Impact

Gateway stop and Signal channel restart now return after a bounded window even when a receive or reply is stuck, and the log names the window and the number of tasks left in flight. Normal shutdown still waits for in-flight work to finish.

## Evidence

Bidirectional, with the module export kept so the comparison is about the loop and not an import error:

```text
# old unbounded loop restored (export kept)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor.task-runner.test.ts
→ FAIL: Test timed out in 120000ms   (the reported hang, reproduced)

# with the fix
→ 4 passed  (stuck task returns after the window and logs; drained work does not log;
             work that settles inside the window is still awaited; window stays 30 s)

# existing Signal monitor suites
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor
→ 79 passed (5 files)

./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files> → 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

Not tested: a live `monitorSignalProvider` run against a real signal-cli with a held reply, which is what #141305 captured. The bounded loop is exercised directly, and the teardown call site is unchanged.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Read the current loop and its teardown caller on main, confirmed the closed repair PR carried an accepted contract rather than a rejected one, and wrote the failing test first by reproducing the hang with the old loop. The implementer understands the code: teardown must not be unbounded, and a stuck receive is reported rather than waited on.

prs.title: perf: gateway startup takes minutes when an installed plugin ships a large dependency tree
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway cold start takes 130-160 s when a configured, already-enabled plugin is installed from npm with a large dependency tree.

Measured on a copy of a real state directory (1.6 GB agent DB, schema v21, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`):

| startup step | boot 1 | boot 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config.snapshot.auto-enable` | 99.4 s | 95.0 s |
| `config.auth.secrets-activate` | 15.7 s | 18.5 s |
| `startup.maintenance` | 12.1 s | 10.3 s |
| `database-readiness` | 7.4 s | 9.5 s |
| total to `starting HTTP server...` | 131 s | 137 s |

Inside that step: `detectPluginAutoEnableCandidates` 102 s, of which
`resolveConfiguredPluginAutoEnableCandidates` 98.9 s, of which
`resolvePluginSetupAutoEnableReasons(["browser", "acpx", "xai"])` 86.6 s. Per
plugin: `acpx` **67.6 s** and returns `[]`; `browser` 437 ms; `xai` 0 ms.

## User Impact

Users with an already-enabled npm-installed plugin no longer wait ~87 s of
startup work for auto-enable candidates that are discarded. On the reproduced
state, `resolveConfiguredPluginAutoEnableCandidates` drops from **98,909 ms to
759 ms**, with no change to which plugins are enabled.

One visible behavior change: a skipped id no longer produces an
`autoEnabledReasons` entry, so the "auto-enabled X because ..." startup log line
no longer appears for a plugin the user had already enabled explicitly.
Activation provenance is unaffected — an explicit
`plugins.entries.<id>.enabled: true` outranks `autoEnabledReason`.

No config migration, no new state, no user action required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### How this was found

This came out of one plugin's install tree, not out of reading the detection
code. `@openclaw/acpx` is an npm-installed plugin whose project `node_modules`
holds 8,589 files / 655 MB, because it embeds an ACP runtime and depends on the
Claude Agent SDK platform packages and the Codex ACP adapter. Loading that
plugin's setup module just to answer a question materialization then discards
costs 54.6 s of dependency-tree capture, against 270 ms to actually read the
module (plain `import()`: 259 ms).

The rule, not the plugin, is what is wrong: **any** npm-installed plugin whose
dependency tree is that large pays the same cost for a probe result that cannot
change enablement. `acpx` is simply the clearest example, and the one that made a
130-160 s cold start visible. The filter therefore targets the general condition
(probe result provably unused) rather than adding a plugin-specific carve-out.

The probe is expensive because loading an npm plugin's setup module captures its
whole dependency tree as a generation artifact.

`resolveConfiguredPluginAutoEnableCandidates` already filters the ids it hands to
`resolvePluginSetupAutoEnableReasons`. That filter now also skips ids whose
candidate materialization cannot use, reusing the predicates that own those rules.

Skipped ids fall into two classes, because removing a candidate does not only
affect that id:

- **Denied and explicitly disabled ids** are dropped everywhere in
  materialization, including prefer-over ordering
  (`shouldSkipPreferredPluginAutoEnable` ignores exactly these ids), so their
  candidate can be skipped outright.
- **Already-enabled ids** still participate in prefer-over ordering: their
  candidate suppresses the ids they prefer over. Skipping them is gated on
  `pluginDeclaresPreferOver` (`plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.ts`), so a plugin
  that declares a preference keeps producing its candidate.

Channel-backed ids keep probing. Materialization resolves them through
`channels.<id>.enabled` and `resolveAutoEnableChannelId`, which can decide a
channel still needs enabling even when `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled` is set, so
an entry-only check would be wrong there.

Two related paths are intentionally out of scope:

- `resolvePluginAutoEnableReadiness` (`configMayNeedPluginAutoEnable`) still
  probes the unfiltered id list. It has no manifest registry, so it cannot apply
  the prefer-over guard safely; it only reaches the probe when the config has no
  `plugins.entries.<id>.config` at all.
- Probes that cost time but change nothing: plugins disabled globally or under a
  doctor diagnostic, workspace-origin plugins (dropped from the candidate list
  before materialization), and channel-backed ids whose `channels.<id>.enabled`
  already matches. Left out to keep the skipped set exactly provable.

## Evidence

- `bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader` 54,578 ms vs `loadModule` 270 ms vs
  `import()` 259 ms for the same `acpx` setup module.
- `resolvePluginSetupAutoEnableReasons(["browser","acpx","xai"])` = 86,603 ms,
  with `acpx` returning `[]`.
- `config.snapshot.auto-enable` = 95-118 s of a 130-160 s boot.
- `resolveConfiguredPluginAutoEnableCandidates` 98,909 ms -> 759 ms with the
  filter applied, measured against the same state copy.

Tests in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.setup-probe.test.ts` (a sibling file because
`plugin-auto-enable.core.test.ts` is already over its line cap and the ratchet
rejects growth):

- New: an already-enabled plugin id and a denied id are not probed; a
  not-yet-enabled id still is.
- New guard: an enabled plugin that a restrictive `plugins.allow` excludes is
  still probed, and its probe is what keeps it in `plugins.allow`.
- New guard: an enabled plugin that prefers over another candidate is still
  probed, so prefer-over ordering survives the skip.

Checked against the pre-fix tree:

```
skips probes ...: AssertionError: expected [ 'acpx', 'browser', 'denied-plugin' ] to not include 'acpx'
still probes ... prefers over another candidate: passes pre-fix, fails when the prefer-over guard is removed
still probes ... restrictive allowlist excludes: passes pre-fix (preservation guard)
```

New file: 3 passed, wall time
`pnpm test src/config/plugin-auto-enable.setup-probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
= 31.2 s on this host. With the other four `plugin-auto-enable` suites:
118 passed, 1 failed (the unrelated symlink fixture failure listed below).

Also green on this host: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files,
`pnpm tsgo:core`, and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main`.

Rebased onto current `main` (pnpm 12.5.0, `tsgo:core` clean) after main refactored
`plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts` and inlined the already-enabled check in
`materialize.ts`. The fix keeps the same three predicates; the only rebase
adjustment was dropping a cosmetic de-duplication inside the materialization loop
that main had already inlined.

Two failures are unrelated to this change and predate it on this host:

- `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts` >
  `reads external catalog files through a symlink` fails while building its
  fixture (`fs.symlinkSync` returns `EPERM` on this Windows host), before
  reaching any auto-enable logic; it fails identically on the unmodified tree.
- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-19` fails in
  `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.output-fidelity.native.test.ts`
  ("Expected native command execution"), a native Codex app-server output-fidelity
  test that needs a matching native binary. This diff only touches
  `src/config/plugin-auto-enable*`, and the failure could not be reproduced here
  because it requires the native Codex app-server. Not investigated further.

`pnpm check:changed` also aborts in its `conflict markers` lane here because
corepack invokes pnpm 11.25.0 while `package.json` requires 12.4.0, so the lanes
it would run were executed individually.

prs.title: fix(deepgram): answer calls when noise prevents endpointing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers hear no response when background noise prevents Deepgram endpointing from completing their confirmed speech.

Supersedes #158226, thanks @Weiming-Hu. Credit also preserves @weiming, the other human commit-author identity in the original PR.

## User Impact

Deepgram can complete confirmed caller speech on its provider-detected word gap while the call remains open. A long pause can split a thought into separate turns. This fallback requires interim results and endpointing at most 5000 ms; other configurations retain their existing behavior. No new settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main only completes open turns on `speech_final` or `from_finalize`; its fallback timer is close-only. Enable `utterance_end_ms` using the existing endpointing value (minimum 1000 ms), flush confirmed text on valid `UtteranceEnd`, and ignore the provider's stale `-1` sentinel. Provisional text is never promoted to a completed transcript.

This deliberately revisits the endpointing-only choice in 73b0312e525126200e1ac83c632166112eed16f7 to address the reported noisy-call stall. Deepgram documents the [word-gap behavior and limits](https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/utterance-end). The original PR's new idle-flush option, watchdogs, and retry machinery are omitted.

Production delta: +9 lines net (+14/-5). Removed the single-use `clearFinalizeFallback` wrapper and kept its cancellation in the turn owner. Test delta: +14 lines; the separate allocation covers the stalled-turn, stale-event, and duplicate-terminal regressions.

## Evidence

- Fake Deepgram stream through the real WebSocket session: red against main `054516fb8e11f06358bab0ab2b90d5313c4ac6fb` (confirmed text plus `UtteranceEnd` produced `[]` instead of `["a"]`); green after the fix, **15/15** tests. Existing close, reconnect, bounds, and provisional-gap cases also pass.
- [Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41537201489): named file `extensions/deepgram/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts`; red wrapper wall 48.52 s, green 39.32 s (Vitest 36.77 s, mostly cold worker compilation). [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538807625) passed on the replacement head in 15m32s wall time across the planned jobs; an individual-file CI timing was not exposed in the retrieved logs.
- Touched-file type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors, exit 0. Touched-file oxfmt check: exit 0. `git diff --check`: pass.
- Autoreview of the complete local candidate against the pinned main above, with full Deepgram owner/test and Voice Call consumer context: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191498#issuecomment-6590379983) also found no actionable findings and recorded the same live-call proof limitation.
- Contributor code was read with `gh` only and was never checked out or executed. No live Deepgram/carrier call was run; this proves the event-stream boundary, not acoustic behavior or an absent provider event. PR CI supplies broad proof; no broad checks ran on the Team host.

prs.title: fix: skip discarded plugin setup captures during startup
prs.body:
Supersedes #154885, thanks @unknowbug.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway startup captures a large installed plugin dependency tree just to run an auto-enable probe whose result is discarded for an already-enabled plugin.

## User Impact

Already-enabled non-channel plugins avoid unnecessary setup capture. Probes still run when channel enablement, a restrictive allowlist, or preference ordering can change selection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generation capture copies and hashes declared dependency packages to retain immutable source and resources. The auto-enable owner now filters satisfied selections before requesting that work, and readiness stays on metadata. Capture containment, symlink, hardlink, receipt, and native-admission checks remain with their existing owners.

The shared filter serves both asynchronous preparation and candidate detection. Removed the redundant xAI-specific collector and repeated configured-entry checks. Production delta: +3 lines; the remaining growth connects the filter to both callers.

## Evidence

- Main `054516fb8e11f06358bab0ab2b90d5313c4ac6fb`: the synthetic real-capture regression fails with **17 dependency files captured, expected 0**.
- Fixed: both already-enabled paths capture **0 dependency files and 0 original bytes**. Pending enablement, allowlist repair, preference metadata, and channel-backed controls still capture all **17** fixture files.
- **72 tests passed** across the five named auto-enable files on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41537703095). The new regression covers the production setup/auto-enable composition without mocking capture; its 90 lines have an exact test-line allocation.
- Touched-file formatting and typed lint passed. The new file passed all 6 cases in **1.51 s test time / 42.41 s wrapper wall time**, including 34.36 s of uncached worker preparation. This real capture boundary needs the worker path; all compilation ran remotely. In [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539239220/job/125599567015), the same 6 cases passed in **5.19 s Vitest duration / 7.15 s wrapper wall time**.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the local snapshot committed as `d0c6dcba8973c` against base `054516fb8e11f` completed **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. [Full PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539239220) completed successfully for this exact head (62 jobs completed, no failures), and [security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539239023) passed. No Gateway startup timing was run on the production host; this proves the discarded-probe optimization, not total startup latency for plugins that need execution.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

prs.title: fix(compaction): preserve active request provenance
prs.body:
## Problem

Compaction could replace the active human request with a later internal observation, or revive completed human work during an independent internal run. The first revision also rejected a second recovery after the production semantic-window reader archived the original admitted request.

## Solution

- Carry the admitted request boundary from the runtime through AgentSession into core compaction, with explicit unresolved/none/legacy-inference selection.
- Centralize recorded-source attribution for summary input, preserved excerpts, and token accounting. Clear stale generated pending asks without rewriting unrelated summary sections.
- When a **processed** request is outside the current semantic window, reuse the existing bounded checkpoint request. Newer human steering wins; internal updates preserve that request or authoritative none. Missing **unprocessed** admitted input still rejects.
- Reuse the existing compaction checkpoint; no new persisted state, configuration, or schema. Replace the redundant in-memory mapping test with persisted, repeated-recovery coverage.

This is an independent remediation related to #178477, with credit to @dmitryvostryakov for the original report and implementation. Request provenance remains separate from general model-quality concerns.

## Verification

- **Base red:** all three repeated-recovery cases fail at `a085f281e904` with `invalid_session: Compaction cannot find the admitted request.` on the second recovery.
- **Exact head:** `a9c37408306168b27b2b777de4e9165e0c9eb76b`, based on main `3523ef6747820e3253442a633dc09888c4cdf5fe`. Both commits are patch-identical to the published pre-rebase revision; no conflicts or new behavior changes.
- **Live exact-head E2E:** built the shipped CLI from this head and ran it with a private state/config/workspace, a token-authenticated loopback Gateway, and a real `openai-responses` request to `gpt-6.1-sol` through an explicit embedded-runtime provider route.
  1. `openclaw agent --local` admitted `RQ-180214-EMBEDDED` (`review the patch and do not deploy it`) and the live model returned exactly `ACK-RQ-180214-EMBEDDED`.
  2. `openclaw sessions compact` crossed the production Gateway RPC and live summarizer path. It compacted 15,191 tokens and retained both the marker and the no-deploy request in the generated summary.
  3. After that compaction, a second shipped-CLI turn added newer human steering `RQ-180214-STEER`; the live model returned exactly `ACK-RQ-180214-STEER`.
  4. A second Gateway compaction succeeded at 15,318 tokens. Its summary retained the prior checkpoint request and selected the newer steering under `Original Request`, including the no-deploy constraint.
  5. `chat.history` on the isolated Gateway recorded two successful `proof-openai/gpt-6.1-sol` model completions and two compaction records, with no pending inputs; the final session runtime was `openclaw`.
- **Persisted internal-update proof:** the committed regression reopens through production `SessionManager.openAsync(..., { compaction: true })`, verifies the original request is absent from the semantic window, and completes a second automatic compaction. Human request survives internal updates; authoritative internal selection remains none; newer human steering supersedes the checkpoint request. Missing pending input still rejects.
- **Current-head focused proof:** 96 tests passed across eight files, including persisted repeated recovery, compaction provenance and request selection, registered safeguards, runtime recovery, and host seed handling.
- Focused lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed on the rebased tree. The mock-export ratchet was the failing check in the prior CI run.
- The prior repair's independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean; unchanged patches retain that review. Earlier core, agents-sessions tests, and Plugin SDK test TypeScript checks passed.
- The live proof deliberately did not fabricate an inter-session source: the Gateway rejected CLI-exec attempts that would lose `sessions_send` attribution. That branch remains covered by the persisted production integration test above.

## Scope

Ready-for-review preparation only. Do not merge or backport.

prs.title: fix(agents): derive the legacy model allowlist from the authored config
prs.body:
Closes #191215

## What Problem This Solves

On a config with no `meta.migrations.modelPolicyAllowlist` marker and no `agents.defaults.modelPolicy`, `computeModelPolicyAllowlist` read the keys of `agents.defaults.models` as a legacy model allowlist. The Anthropic extension injects entries into that map at runtime to set `cacheRetention: "short"`, so an operator who never authored any model settings ends up with an accidental allowlist, and every explicit override outside it fails with `model not allowed`.

## User Impact

Runtime-injected model metadata no longer counts as an authored allowlist, so an explicit override such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` is admitted. An operator-authored `agents.defaults.models` map keeps its exact legacy restriction; the injected keys are excluded from it and no other ref changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Fix policy derivation at the authored-to-runtime boundary." The legacy refs are now resolved from the authored config source instead of the runtime config, through the existing `projectConfigOntoRuntimeSourceSnapshot` owner.

`computeAuthoredModelPolicyAllowlist` lives beside the legacy-allowlist detection it wraps (`src/config/model-policy-allowlist-migration.ts`, well under its line cap), so `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` — a grandfathered over-cap file where any growth fails `check:line-cap-ratchet` — ends up one line shorter than main. `resolveConfiguredModelPolicyAllow` calls the helper in a single line.

## Evidence

### Resolver-level red/green

![A/B proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191215/proof-191215.png)

The harness performs the production Gateway publication — `readConfigFileSnapshot()` then `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot(runtimeConfig, sourceConfig)`, exactly what `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts` does — for an isolated config, then asks the real `resolveConfiguredModelPolicyAllow` what it resolves. One variable differs between runs (this change).

| authored config | authored `agents.defaults.models` | runtime keys | main resolved policy | this branch resolved policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no model map authored (the report) | `[]` | 4 (3 injected) | 4 refs — accidental allowlist | `[]` — unrestricted |
| authored legacy model map | 2 | 5 (3 injected) | 5 refs — authored + injected | the 2 authored refs |

### Shipped Gateway end-to-end (live A/B)

![Live Gateway A/B and v2026.10.9 upgrade](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191434/live-gateway-proof.png)

Every row below is one real turn through the shipped entry point: isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `openclaw gateway run`, then `openclaw agent --model … --json`. A deterministic local provider records each model POST, so **0 POSTs** means the override stopped before provider I/O. Anthropic runtime defaults were active in every row (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set), injecting three keys into `agents.defaults.models`.

`branch` is head `62ed4f4c887`. `main` is the same tree with only the two changed source files reverted (`git apply -R`) and rebuilt; `grep -c computeAuthoredModelPolicyAllowlist dist/*.mjs` returns 0 for that build and 1 for the branch build.

| authored config | requested override | branch | main (PR reverted) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no model map (reported case) | `proof/proof-model` | allowed, 1 POST | denied, 0 POSTs |
| no model map (control: injected provider still works) | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` | allowed, 1 POST | allowed, 1 POST |
| legacy map `{anthropic/claude-opus-4-8}` | `proof/proof-model` | denied, 0 POSTs | denied, 0 POSTs |
| legacy map `{anthropic/claude-opus-4-8}` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (injected, not authored) | denied, 0 POSTs | allowed, 1 POST |
| per-agent `agents.entries.ops.modelPolicy.allow=[anthropic/claude-opus-4-8]` | `proof/proof-model` | denied, 0 POSTs | denied, 0 POSTs |
| map removed again, same session after hot reload | `proof/proof-model` | allowed, 1 POST | denied, 0 POSTs |

What this covers:

- **Admission for a model outside the injected set:** with no authored map, the override reaches provider dispatch on this branch and is refused on main.
- **Authored default restriction still enforced before provider I/O:** with the authored legacy map, `proof/proof-model` is denied on both sides and the provider log stays empty.
- **Per-agent restriction still enforced before provider I/O:** agent `ops` with an explicit `modelPolicy.allow` is denied with 0 provider POSTs.
- **Injected keys no longer widen an authored restriction:** `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` is a runtime-injected key, not an authored one; this branch denies it, main admits it and dispatches.
- **Policy tightening across reload for a retained consumer:** the same session `proof-a` is allowed before the map is authored and denied after the hot reload; removing the map again admits it on this branch. Reloads are the Gateway's own config watcher (`config change detected` → `config hot reload applied`).

Raw Gateway lines:

```
res ✗ agent ... Model override "proof/proof-model" is not allowed for agent "main" by agents.defaults.models. Add "proof/proof-model" or "proof/*" to agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow...
res ✗ agent ... Model override "proof/proof-model" is not allowed for agent "ops" by agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow...
res ✓ agent 1854ms runId=ede478aa... payload "PROOF-PROVIDER-RESPONSE"
```

### v2026.10.9 upgrade with existing data

The released `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI (build `8b18b55`) authored three configs; the released Gateway answered the turns first, then the copied state directory was loaded by this branch.

| config authored by v2026.10.9 | stable: proof | stable: injected anthropic | branch: proof | branch: injected anthropic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| marked legacy map (written by `config set agents.defaults.models`) | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 | allowed, 1 |
| explicit `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow=[anthropic/claude-opus-4-8]` | denied, 0 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 |
| pre-marker legacy map, hand-authored old install | denied, 0 | allowed, 1 | denied, 0 | denied, 0 |

- Marked and explicit configs behave identically before and after the branch loads them; their policy fields are unchanged.
- The pre-marker legacy config keeps its authored restriction (proof model denied). The injected Anthropic key is the only behavior change: admitted by 2026.10.9, denied by this branch.
- Existing stored data loads: the released state used agent DB **schema 25**, current main requires **39**. The documented `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the copied state on all three configs (exit 0). For the pre-marker legacy config, doctor materialized `modelPolicy.allow=["anthropic/claude-opus-4-8"]` with `marker=true` — the authored ref only, no injected keys.

Local harness (not committed; temporary directory): `run-cases.sh branch|main` drives section 1, `run-upgrade.sh` drives section 2. Both start isolated Gateways, call `openclaw agent`, and count provider POSTs from the local endpoint's request log.

### Gates

Red/green unit coverage in `src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` ("derives the legacy allowlist from the authored config"): both cases fail against main's `model-selection-shared.ts` and pass with this change. Full suite: 55 passed. `src/config/io.meta.test.ts`: 10 passed. Local gates against `upstream/main`: oxfmt, oxlint, `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (slack 2748). CI, `ci-gate`, and security review are green on `62ed4f4c887`.

## What was not tested

- No real Anthropic/OpenAI account or model key is available on this machine. The proof provider is a deterministic local endpoint speaking OpenAI Completions and Anthropic Messages; policy admission, dispatch, hot reload, and the upgrade path are the real shipped code paths, but model output quality is not under test.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): expose dependency cleanup in slow preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh sandbox preparation can spend a long time retiring a disposable dependency builder, while slow-chat diagnostics report only the enclosing reconciliation/template preparation time.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish dependency installation and container removal from checkout, template cloning, manifest scanning, publication, and cleanup in slow-chat detail. This change adds attribution; it does not change reconciliation results or promise a latency reduction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing template publication contract waits for the dependency builder to retire before publishing its files. Fixed timing names at the existing owners expose that wait without changing cleanup, authority checks, storage, configuration, or caching. The production addition is 39 lines. Documentation explains inclusive timings and distinguishes dependency-builder retirement from obsolete-template retirement.

The existing preparation benchmark can now exercise dependency templates with a real container, thousands of sibling worktree registrations, and public-source fixtures containing symlinks. It checks reconciled file bytes and link targets independently and rejects accelerated fresh runs without template-application evidence.

## Evidence

- Five focused owner suites: 37 tests passed. The final dependency lifecycle suite passed all 6 cases after test-only simplification. The updated test fails 5 lifecycle cases against the exact original production implementation because retirement timing is absent; the identity-only case remains green.
- Targeted lint, formatting, scripts typecheck, symlink-fixture equality, and independent Codex review passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base f6ccc9fa37169d9cf84744e7fc584f7bf24a7819`: every check passed except production Knip's unused `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` export in `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`. This reproduces on that exact main parent. Introducing commit af4c6a1be1c804dabb2616e8c01b0e3176bfad94 / #191285 removed the last external production caller but retained the export. This is an existing main regression, not a passing check. This PR changes no UI-imported module.
- All four serial diagnostic runs passed with identical file/link fingerprints: 62,927 entries, 718 MB of normalized source bytes, 2,000 actual sibling Git worktrees, a real Docker builder, and full equality of both fresh projections. The candidate records dependency retirement independently (280 ms locally), plus checkout, template, scan and publication stages.

| Observation | Cold-template fresh | Warm-template fresh |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A/A baseline 1 | 31.80 s | 13.40 s |
| A/A baseline 2 | 28.71 s | 14.50 s |
| Final baseline | 32.34 s | 13.58 s |
| Candidate | 31.30 s | 16.19 s |

The final cold-template pair measured Node main/process CPU 1.390/34.007→1.301/32.653 s and main-heap allocation 447.3→445.8 MB. These are individual exploratory observations, not statistical performance acceptance: the warm-template candidate was slower, and no speedup is claimed. Local APFS/Docker, a synthetic single-commit repository and an 8-MB agent database do not qualify Linux/Podman/btrfs, full Git history, cold OS page cache, or a 35-GiB database. The local builder lacks pnpm (exit 127), exercising source-only fallback rather than partial-install cleanup.

Exact-head [CI run 41535024833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41535024833) passed: 55 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failures or reruns, including both UI E2E shards and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

prs.title: improve(ui): report the running Gateway's network exposure
prs.body:
Stacked on #191467.

## What Problem This Solves

Privacy & Security can't say how exposed a Gateway really is. `--bind`, `--host` and `--tailscale` set the running process apart from its config file, and nothing reported them, so a Gateway listening on every interface looked the same as one on loopback.

`authMode` had the same gap. It was computed from config and environment without the startup override, so `--auth none` over a config with a token reported Token.

## User Impact

Admins see what the Gateway is running with, whatever config says:

| Running Gateway | Network access |
| --- | --- |
| Loopback | This device only, with a green dot |
| `0.0.0.0` or `::` | All interfaces, warning dot without auth |
| Tailnet address | Tailnet, with the address |
| Any other address | Custom host, with the address |
| Tailscale Serve | Tailnet, through Tailscale Serve |
| Tailscale Funnel | Public internet, warning dot |
| Older Gateway | The configured value, no dot (unchanged from #191467) |

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot gains two optional fields beside `authMode`, for `operator.admin` only, like `configPath` and `stateDir`: `bindHost` and `tailscaleMode`. Both are needed, and the page requires both. Tailscale keeps a loopback bind, so the bind alone would show "This device only" on a Gateway published through Funnel.

The fields are optional and additive, so `PROTOCOL_VERSION` doesn't change. Older clients are unaffected: the TypeScript clients don't check the hello snapshot against the closed schema, and the Swift and Android decoders ignore unknown keys. `protocol:check` and `gateway:validators:gen` confirm the generated output is in step.

`bindHost` is the resolved address rather than the bind mode, because `auto` can land on either side and `--host` has no mode at all. `0.0.0.0` reads "All interfaces" rather than "Local network", because on a machine with a public address it isn't local. A loopback Gateway reached from another host still reads Remote, since a proxy or tunnel in front of it isn't "this device only".

`authMode` now comes from the auth this connection was actually checked against, which includes the startup override. That restores the green dot on Gateway auth, but only beside `bindHost` and `tailscaleMode`, which is how the page knows the Gateway is new enough for `authMode` to be true. Older Gateways keep the plain value from #191467.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on an isolated port and state with synthetic secrets. The hello frame is what the browser received, and listening addresses are from `lsof`:

| Started with | Listening | Hello | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Silent config, `--bind lan` | `*` | `bindHost: 0.0.0.0` | All interfaces, Token with green dot |
| Silent config | `127.0.0.1`, `::1` | `bindHost: 127.0.0.1` | This device only, Token with green dot |
| Config `lan`, `--bind loopback` | `127.0.0.1`, `::1` | `bindHost: 127.0.0.1` | This device only |
| Config `lan` | `*` | `bindHost: 0.0.0.0` | All interfaces, Password with green dot |
| Config with a token, `--auth none` | `127.0.0.1`, `::1` | `authMode: none` | None with warning dot |
| Silent config, `--bind lan`, Gateway built before this change | `*` | no new fields | Default and Token, no dots |

Tailscale states are unit-tested only, since running them would change the machine's real Tailscale state. Admin-only delivery is unit-tested. Checks: `protocol:check`, `gateway:validators:gen`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, the hello, health-state and connection tests, and the page's unit, browser and e2e tests, plus `ui:check-performance:base`.

**Before: `--bind lan`, silent config, viewed over loopback.**

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daf57042-aa56-441d-ba1a-2856f4341f5e)

**After, the same Gateway.**

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b31d54fc-bab2-454e-b22d-113997600f72)

**After, the same config with no flag.**

![After, no flag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64e6969a-a43d-4cb5-bf98-4e4c0dd50aab)

**After, CRT at 390, `--bind lan`.**

![After, CRT at 390](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/017f8ae4-7c12-4cbe-9e96-fed9c9584c40)
