prs.title: fix(cron): owner-targeted automation failure alerts go to the last chat, not the owner
prs.body:
Closes #189947

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failure alerts for automations with `delivery.target: "owner"`, such as heartbeats migrated by Doctor, go to the job session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient instead of the owner DM, or fail with `Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>` when neither exists.

## User Impact

User impact: for owner-targeted automations without an alert-specific route, failure alerts, including the auto-disable alert when it is sent on that route, now go to the same owner DM as the automation's own delivery.

- **No identifiable owner, or DMs blocked.** When no owner can be identified (for example DMs open with `allowFrom: ["*"]` and no `commands.ownerAllowFrom`), or `delivery.directPolicy: "block"` is set, the alert is now recorded as Not delivered and the existing in-app fallback notification is queued; the automation's own delivery does not send in these cases either. Previously such an alert could go directly to the job session's last conversation, such as another DM sender, or, when the session had no last conversation, to the channel's `defaultTo` recipient. To keep receiving these alerts directly, set `commands.ownerAllowFrom` (for an unidentified owner), or configure an explicit failure-alert recipient (`failureAlert.to`, `delivery.failureDestination.to`, or `cron.failureAlert.to`).
- **In-app fallback.** When an alert on an owner-targeted route, or on a route with `directPolicy: "block"`, is recorded as Not delivered, its in-app fallback now stays in the session: the fallback turn runs in the job's delivery session (the agent's main session for an isolated job without a session key) and is recorded there, but its reply is not delivered automatically, and the turn has no current external conversation for implicit sends. Before, the fallback turn's reply could be delivered to the session's last conversation.
- **Alert-specific settings.** A `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` in the job's `failureAlert`, in `delivery.failureDestination`, or in global `cron.failureAlert` keeps its configured routing and does not inherit owner targeting.
- **Jobs that are not owner-targeted.** An alert that inherits the job's primary route now also honors its `delivery.directPolicy: "block"`: when the session's last conversation is a DM, the alert is blocked and recorded as Not delivered, as the job's own delivery to that DM is. A Not delivered alert on such a route also keeps its in-app fallback in the session, as above.
- **Upgrade.** When an alert newly inherits the owner target and the job already has an open failure incident with the same cause, the job may alert once more after the cooldown through the owner route. Repair-first handling and the auto-disable alert keep their existing timing. No config or schema change; existing jobs' `delivery.target` and `delivery.directPolicy` now also apply to their inherited failure alerts and to those alerts' in-app fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

With no alert-specific route, the failure-alert route comes from the job's primary announce target, the last tier of the documented route order ([`delivery.md` L163-L167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L163-L167)). Owner targeting (`target`, `directPolicy`) was added to the cron delivery plan in #179387; the alert-route projection carries channel, recipient, account, and thread only. Without `target`, the Gateway alert sender resolved the alert as an ordinary channel delivery (`channel: "last"` for the Doctor and setup shape) and did not reach the owner resolver that the automation's own delivery uses.

The alert route now carries `target` and `directPolicy` when it inherits the primary route and no alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` is set in the job's `failureAlert`, `delivery.failureDestination`, or global `cron.failureAlert`. The dispatcher and the Gateway alert sender pass both fields to the existing `resolveDeliveryTarget`; owner resolution itself is unchanged. This follows the documented owner contract: owner delivery "does not follow the last group conversation or guess a recipient when owner identity is ambiguous" ([L118-L122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L118-L122)), and a missing owner route is recorded "without falling back to the last conversation" ([L124-L126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L124-L126)); see also [`troubleshooting.md` L60](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting.md?plain=1#L60) and [`heartbeat.md` L171-L172](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/gateway/heartbeat.md?plain=1#L171-L172). The route-order section of `delivery.md` now adds: "When this tier applies, failure alerts keep the primary target's owner targeting and `directPolicy`."

For owner-targeted jobs without an alert-specific route, the external alert send now resolves only a positively identified owner DM, or records Not delivered; it no longer resolves the session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient.

A Not delivered alert queues the in-app fallback: a session event that runs a turn with the alert text in the job's delivery session. That turn's reply follows the session's stored route, its last conversation, and this path does not check the owner target, `directPolicy`, or `allowFrom`. When an alert whose route carries the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"` is recorded as Not delivered, the fallback is now queued with `deliver: false` and an internal delivery context (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`), the combination `sessions_send` already uses for the agent turn it starts ([`sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts` L67-L77](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts#L67-L77)). Either setting alone keeps the turn's own reply, including an error reply such as an authentication failure, from being delivered automatically. The internal context also leaves the turn without a current external conversation, so a `message` send without an explicit target is rejected (`This turn has no current conversation`). `deliver: false` is also inherited when a tool in the fallback run hands off a session event, so that follow-up turn's own reply is not delivered automatically either; this PR does not change how a `message` send without a target resolves in that follow-up turn (see Not covered). The fallback turn still runs and is recorded in the session, so the documented in-app fallback remains. `delivery.md` now adds after its fallback paragraph: "When an alert on an owner-targeted route or a route with `directPolicy: "block"` is recorded as Not delivered, its fallback turn stays in-session: it is not delivered automatically and has no current external conversation for implicit sends."

The condition includes `directPolicy: "block"` because this PR also carries `directPolicy` on the inherited routes of jobs that are not owner-targeted. When a remembered recipient fails the channel's outbound check against `allowFrom`, implicit delivery switches to the first `allowFrom` entry ([`delivery-target.ts` L347-L359](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts#L347-L359)), and the DM block is checked after that switch ([L501-L513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts#L501-L513)); WhatsApp's outbound resolver rejects DM recipients outside `allowFrom` ([`resolve-outbound-target.ts` L29-L37](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/extensions/whatsapp/src/resolve-outbound-target.ts#L29-L37)). On such a channel, an inherited alert with `directPolicy: "block"` used to go to the first `allowFrom` entry; it is now blocked, and its fallback reply, which is not checked against `allowFrom`, would otherwise go to the session's last conversation, which the alert did not reach before. Explicit alert routes and required-delivery alerts do not inherit `directPolicy`, so their fallback is unchanged.

The route is computed per failure and not stored. The stored incident signature gains the target only when an alert inherits it, so a move from the session's last conversation to the owner counts as a changed destination ([L159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L159)). `directPolicy` is not part of the signature, and the signatures of all other jobs, including owner-targeted jobs with an alert-specific route, are byte-for-byte unchanged. There is no schema migration; `failureAlertIncident.signature` is the stored state whose comparison changes.

Unchanged: the owner resolver, alert-specific routes, repair-first escalation, the in-app fallback for routes without the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"`, the settlement of a blocked DM alert as Not delivered, and notices that do not use the alert route.

<details>
<summary>Which notifications use the failure-alert route</summary>

Every failure-alert intent takes its route from the same `resolveFailureAlert` result.

| Notification | Uses the failure-alert route | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Execution-failure alert (threshold and cooldown) | Yes | Inherits `target` and `directPolicy` with the primary route |
| Auto-disable alert for a recurring job, when an alert route is enabled | Yes | Same |
| Terminal one-shot failure alert, also used as the fallback of a repair request | Yes | Same |
| Required-delivery failure alert | Only through an alternate failure destination | Unchanged: explicit destination, no inheritance |
| Owner-conversation repair request | No: a turn in the owner conversation | Unchanged |
| Auto-disable notice when no alert route is enabled | No: in-app notice | Unchanged |
| In-app fallback after Not delivered | No | Alert route with the owner target or `directPolicy: "block"`: the fallback turn stays in the session; other routes unchanged |
| "Did not start" notice | No: session notice | Unchanged |
| Alert with no Gateway alert sender | No: goes straight to the in-app queue | Unchanged |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Alert destination before and after, by configuration</summary>

Owner-targeted job with no alert-specific route unless noted. Not delivered queues the in-app fallback notification in every row. "Before" is for a job whose alert follows its session's route; for an isolated job without a session key whose agent main session has a last conversation, the base refuses that inherited route (`Refusing implicit isolated cron delivery`), records Not delivered, and the fallback turn's reply goes to that last conversation instead. "Alert-sender test" is the new Gateway test, "fallback test" `src/cron/service.failure-alert-fallback.test.ts` (fallback only, after a stubbed Not delivered settlement), "resolver test" the existing `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`, "producer test" `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts`, and "live run" the isolated Gateway run in Evidence.

| Owner identity and session state | Before | After | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner identified; last conversation is the owner DM | Owner DM | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; last conversation is another DM | That DM | Owner DM | Alert-sender test |
| Owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Owner DM | Alert-sender test (session fixture); live run |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, no channel `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Owner DM | Alert-sender test; live log (before) |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, channel `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; `directPolicy: "block"` | The session's last route | Not delivered (`dm-blocked`); fallback stays in the session | Alert-sender test (rejection, nothing sent); producer test; fallback test; live run |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; fallback test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; live run |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, no `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Resolver test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Not delivered (`no-route`); fallback stays in the session | Source reading |
| Not owner-targeted; `channel: "last"`, `directPolicy: "block"`, last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (DM blocked); fallback stays in the session | Producer test; fallback test; source reading |
| Any job with an alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` | Configured route | Configured route | Producer test (`accountId` at each level, job-level `channel`); source reading for `to` |

</details>

## Evidence

Live, isolated Gateway: a Gateway on loopback with only a Telegram test bot configured. `session.groupScope: "main"` makes a private test group (the owner and the bot only) the main session's last conversation, and `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` keeps the owner's DMs out of the main session; after every trigger, the main session's last conversation was checked again and was still the group. The bot was a group administrator, so it received group messages, and `channels.telegram.joinIntro` was `false`. The owner is identified through `openclaw pairing approve` (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`). The jobs are isolated agent-turn automations created with `openclaw automations add --delivery-target owner` (plus `--direct-policy block` for the blocked-DM jobs and `--session-key agent:main:main` for one job), with threshold 1 and cooldowns set through `openclaw automations edit`, and triggered with `openclaw automations run`. The Gateway had no valid model credentials, only a deliberately invalid model-provider API key (`automations add` requires an authentication source for the model), so every run failed with the provider's authentication error (`401 invalid_api_key`, cause `auth`). The same state was read and written in turn by the base `f47669efcec2`, the first revision `4697df95fb0c`, and the candidate `c4e527ec0c63`.

- Owner DM instead of the group: on the base, the owner-targeted job's alert was refused (`Refusing implicit isolated cron delivery`) and recorded as Not delivered, and its fallback turn's reply, an authentication-failure message (`⚠️ Couldn't sign in …`), was posted in the test group; for the job with `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`, the alert itself (`Automation "<session-key job>" failed 1 times`, `Cause: auth`) was recorded as delivered and posted in the group. The owner's DM received no alert during the base runs. Candidate, same state and same jobs: the owner-targeted job's alert was recorded as delivered, the owner's Telegram DM received `Automation "<owner-targeted job>" failed 2 times` (`Cause: auth`), and the test group received nothing; the same for the `sessionKey` job.
- Owner-route rejection and the fallback: on the first revision, an owner job with `directPolicy: "block"` and an owner job run after the owner entry was removed settled Not delivered, with delivery errors `Owner delivery unavailable (dm-blocked)` and `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` respectively; each fallback turn ran in the main session and posted the authentication-failure message in the test group. On the candidate, the same two cases settled the same way, each fallback turn ran in the main session, and the test group received nothing.
- State written by the base build: the candidate Gateway started on the state written by the base build and listed all eight jobs that the base build's CLI had created; five of them, compared field by field, read back with the delivery and alert settings that the base build had stored. The owner-targeted job's base run had opened a failure incident for the same cause; on the candidate, its next failure after the cooldown alerted once more through the owner route (the delivered alert above, `failed 2 times`), as described under Upgrade. A second failure of the delivered owner-targeted job, after its one-minute cooldown, was not alerted again (same incident signature). An owner job with an explicit alert `channel`, whose incident the base build opened, was not alerted after its cooldown. An owner job still inside the cooldown recorded by the base build was not alerted. The no-owner and blocked-DM jobs above were also created by the base build's CLI; on the candidate, their alerts were rejected under the new owner and `directPolicy` handling.
- Before the fix: on 2026-10-30, a heartbeat that appears to have been migrated by Doctor failed once on a live Gateway and its failure alert was not delivered (`cron: failure alert delivery failed`, `MessageActionDeniedError: Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>`); the job row was not read. The linked issue has this log and a reproduction at the base through the same Gateway alert sender.

Focused tests on `f47669efcec2` with this change (Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, Vitest on Node, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`); the pushed head `c4e527ec0c63` has the same changes.

- `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` (extended), producer and dispatch: an owner-targeted primary route passes `target` and `directPolicy` to the alert route, including the channel-less delivery that Doctor and setup write and with an announce-only global alert config; the dispatcher forwards both fields to the Gateway alert sender. An `accountId` at each of the three alert-route levels, an explicit alert `channel`, and a webhook alert without a URL keep their own routing without the owner target. An open incident alerts again after the cooldown when its destination changes to the owner; an incident signature computed by the base code for a non-owner route still deduplicates; changing only `directPolicy` does not reopen an incident.
- `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` (new): the alert route from the real `resolveFailureAlert` goes to the real Gateway alert sender (`sendGatewayCronFailureAlert`) and the real `resolveDeliveryTarget`, including its owner branch. An owner-targeted alert is sent to the owner DM (the final send's target is `111`) and settles as delivered when the session has no last conversation, has another DM, or has a group as its last conversation. With `directPolicy: "block"` and a DM last conversation, the alert is rejected with `Owner delivery unavailable (dm-blocked)` and nothing is sent. Mocked: session-store reads (the last conversation is a fixture), channel selection, and the final send (`sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`); the channel is a generic test plugin registered as `telegram`. Owner identity uses the test plugin's `user:` form; the linked issue's reproduction used a Telegram-style plugin with numeric IDs.
- `src/cron/service.failure-alert-fallback.test.ts` (new), the fallback after a Not delivered alert, using a fixture shared with the existing notification test (`src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test-support.ts`, new): a real `CronService` run fails, the route from the real `resolveFailureAlert` goes to the dispatcher, and after the alert send settles Not delivered the fallback is queued through the real Gateway cron target resolver (`createGatewayCronTargetResolver`) and runs as a real session-event turn in `agent:main:main`, whose stored route is Telegram recipient `999`; session-event admission and execution, the `message` tool, and the transcript are real. Mocked: the job's own run (it returns an error), the Gateway alert send (it records Not delivered for the route it receives, so the owner resolver does not run in this file), model output (`runEmbeddedAgent`), and the channel's final `sendText`; the channel is a generic test plugin registered as `telegram`. Cases:
  - "keeps an owner no-route fallback in the session": owner-targeted, the model replies normally; the turn completes with that reply, the session transcript contains the alert text, and nothing is sent.
  - "does not derive an external target for an implicit message send": owner-targeted, the model calls `message` with `action: "send"` and no target; the tool rejects with `Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`, the turn ends `failed`, and nothing is sent.
  - "does not silence the next ordinary inbound turn": after an owner-targeted fallback turn that sent nothing, an ordinary inbound event in the same session with the Telegram route is delivered to `999`.
  - "An owner blocked authentication error stays in the session.": owner-targeted with `directPolicy: "block"`, the model returns an error reply (`isError`, "Authentication failed."); the turn ends `failed`, and nothing is sent.
  - "A non-owner fallback still delivers to the configured conversation.": control, explicit Telegram recipient `999` without block; the fallback reply is sent (one send).
  - "A blocked non-owner fallback stays in the session.": explicit Telegram recipient `999` with `directPolicy: "block"`; the turn completes, and nothing is sent.
  - "A fallback-derived session event stays in the session.": inside an owner-targeted fallback turn, a session-event target is captured under a Gateway tool-caller identity bound to that turn's registered run, as in the existing "retains store, route and producer limits across lookup" case of `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.test.ts`. The captured target carries `deliver: false`; a `tool_handoff` session event queued with it runs (`executionStarted: true`; its model replies normally) and settles with `delivered: false` and `deliveryAttempted: false`, and nothing is sent.
- `src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` (changed): its setup moved into the shared fixture with the same two-agent configuration; its four cases, their names, and their assertions are unchanged.
- `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.persistence.test.ts` (one case added), stored incidents across a reload: three jobs fail with the same cause and each opens a failure incident that is saved to the cron store: a job with `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "last" }`, an owner-targeted job with an explicit alert `channel`, and a non-owner job with `channel: "last"`. The first job's delivery is then changed to `target: "owner"` and saved, and a new service state is loaded from the same store after the cooldown. On the next failure with the same cause, only that job alerts, and its alert route carries `target: "owner"`; the other two stay deduplicated. The stored signatures here are written by the new code for routes without a target, the same form the base code writes for an owner-targeted job; this is in-process evidence, not a store written by an earlier build. The cross-build check is in the live run above.
- Owner-route rejections: the owner branch's outcome for a missing owner (and for a blocked owner DM) is covered by the existing resolver tests in `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`. By source reading, the alert sender throws on a failed resolution and the rejected send settles as Not delivered; rejected alert sends for other causes are covered in `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`. The live run above shows both rejections settling as Not delivered through the alert sender.

The four `service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` cases and the added persistence case pass on both. With the change: 7, 4, and 13 (the persistence file) passed.

**Not covered:**

- In tests, the owner-route rejection and the fallback are covered separately: the Gateway test asserts the blocked-owner rejection and that nothing is sent, and the fallback test starts from a stubbed alert send that settles Not delivered. prs.title: fix(ui): preserve chat setting clicks during history refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A background transcript refresh can disable chat settings between mouse-down and mouse-up, dropping a Daybreak switch click. Scheduled [CI run 41528240484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41528240484) exposed the unchecked switch remaining checked with no preference patch sent.

## User Impact

Chat settings stay responsive during a background refresh of the current conversation. Initial loading, replacement sessions, and reconnects retain their loading protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer now treats history as ready when the existing accepted-history owner still matches the selected session. The Gateway, connection, session identity, and write-admission checks remain in place. No new state, retries, sleeps, timeout increases, or weaker assertions.

## Evidence

- A native mouse-down → session event → held history request → mouse-up regression fails on base `94e2e06be0d` and passes with the fix. It verifies both the switch and the Standard preference patch before releasing history.
- All six Daybreak entitlement scenarios pass: 19.08s test time, 89.12s including build; the gesture case is 3.00s. Browser proof is necessary for native disabled-input activation.
- All 60 tests in four affected session-control/history consumer files pass, including permission and connection-replacement checks.
- Original `chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` desktop case passes against the rebuilt UI: 11.85s case, 46.49s runner. Served asset bytes match the build. The unchanged original case also passed; the new regression deterministically reproduces the background-refresh condition.
- UI production and E2E-chat typechecks, scoped lint/format, test-line budget, and diff checks pass. Existing advisory UI build-size warnings also occur on the unchanged baseline.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete candidate against `94e2e06be0d`, through P2: no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the hosted review has acknowledged and queued the PR.

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the stream-start output count
prs.body:
Related: #148603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the output count Claude Code reports when a model call starts (usually 1 to 5 tokens) instead of the call's real output, so `lastCallUsage`, and the live usage of single-call turns, undercount output.

## User Impact

User impact: for `claude-cli` turns, `lastCallUsage` now carries each call's real output count. Single-call turns (most plain replies) now show the right output tokens in `sessions.list`, `/status`, reply usage footers and cron run records, because their live usage is that call. Context sizing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's `assistant` snapshots repeat the usage from the start of their call. The final output count arrives only in that call's `stream_event` `message_delta`, which the stream parser never read (the gap listed under "Not in scope" in #148682 and in the 10-29 ClawSweeper summary on #148603). The parser now keeps each parent call's `message_start` usage and applies that call's `message_delta` output count to it. It merges into that call snapshot rather than the parser's latest usage, because a background agent's records (`task_progress` totals, subagent snapshots) can arrive in the middle of a parent call, and mixing them would under-size context. `message_delta` records with `parent_tool_use_id` (subagents) are ignored. Only the output count is taken from the delta, so a delta that reports only `output_tokens` still works.

This is the second remaining gap on #148603. The first one (live usage uses the latest call rather than the whole turn) is covered by the open #187118; the two changes touch different code and do not depend on each other. With both merged, `usage` is the whole turn and `lastCallUsage` is the latest call, with its real output.

## Evidence

- Tests in `src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts`, red on base `92b32cadcc3` and green with the fix:
  - The existing reparse test of the real Claude Code 2.1 capture `test/fixtures/cli/claude-2.1-thinking-progress.jsonl` pinned `usage.output` at 5 (the snapshot value). It now expects 534, the capture's `message_delta` and `result` value.
  - The real subagent capture `claude-2.1-subagent-forwarding.jsonl`: the last parent call's usage is now output 66 (its `message_delta`), not 4.
  - A new synthetic test: a `message_delta` with only `output_tokens` updates the call started by `message_start`, a background `task_progress` usage record in the middle of the call does not leak into it, and a subagent `message_delta` is ignored.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot dismiss the read-only Gateway notice, so it stays above every page after they have read it.

## User Impact

The banner has a Dismiss button. This browser remembers the choice for this Gateway across reloads. A changed notice appears again. Read-only configuration enforcement stays in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing dismissible callout and Gateway-scoped browser preferences. Store the acknowledged notice content locally; the Gateway configuration remains authoritative. No new persistence helper or server setting is introduced.

## Evidence

### Current rebase — November 2, 2026

All three production feature modules remain byte-identical to the previously reviewed/tested feature. Mrunal's authorship and Sally's coauthor credit are preserved. The branch was updated with an exact lease against the prior remote head, not an unguarded force push.

**Local checks pass. Fresh exact-head GitHub CI remains authoritative for merge readiness; no GitHub merge has been performed.**

- **22/22 shell tests pass** on the rebased source (6.25s test execution; 7.39s runner).
- **4/4 mobile floating-header browser tests pass**, including the previously failing full-title assertion at 320px, the narrower truncation case, connection-notice stability, and desktop sibling. Fresh production UI build; 16.29s including preparation, 19.78s runner. No cases skipped.
- UI types, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Test-line ratchet: **6,409,714 / 6,412,107**.
- Canonical performance comparison passes: `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 68e6772de3e55c0734efad6b40306d6115f8fd6e`. Both production builds use Node v26.12.1, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.2, shared third-party dependencies, and normalized build identity; **945 finalized sidecars verified**.

prs.title: fix(tools): preserve allowlist warnings after silent probes
prs.body:
Related: #146408.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing unknown-allowlist warnings when a silent tool-availability query runs before agent tools are assembled.

## User Impact

Operators receive the existing diagnostic once. Allow/deny filtering, filter callbacks and audit reporting retain their behavior. No configuration migration is needed. Maintainer security approval is still required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing policy pipeline records a warning key only when a reporting callback exists. Silent callers omit that callback; MCP adapters preserve it when supplied. The shared bounded cache remains the warning owner.

This normal integration of main `9701d0ff` retains the canonical asynchronous Workshop availability owner. It also removes discarded reporters from the new availability and memory-preflight callers, so the migration cannot silently consume warnings again. Retired Workshop stand-ins remain removed. Main includes @steipete's canonical [#187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) mock-isolation repair with its original authorship and history.

## Evidence

Current head `72772b88394b5b8dc41f32d450dee76b78424b62`, tree `2fdec8529b73060d25ff76ba5e097aad582d233e`; normal merge parents `ec40d0ab` and `9701d0ff`.

- **Before → after:** the real public config-only availability query allows `read`, blocks `write` and stays silent. Before removing the two new discarded reporters, the following real async tool assembly fails: expected one diagnostic, observed zero. After the repair, two assemblies both return only `read` and produce exactly one matching warning in total.
- **Current focused proof:** 80 cases pass across eight files: seven complete owner/sibling files (75 cases), plus five selected memory-preflight cases; the other ten memory cases were not selected. This includes silent→reporting deduplication, eviction, deny/filter/audit controls, final effective policy, availability queries, Workshop and `/learn`.
- **Current checks:** production types, a canonical-settings consumer covering the eight test entry files, type-aware source and test lint, formatting and whitespace pass. Actual Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 satisfy the branch requirements. Package, lock and workspace-manifest blobs match the already reconciled frozen installation; no authored dependency change is included.
- **Budget and size:** native staged check against `9701d0ff` passes at **6,409,805 / 6,412,136**, slack **2,331**. The complete proposal is production **−9** lines and tests **+58**; the maintenance extension adds ten test lines. No scalar, allocation, ignore, timeout or assertion relaxation is used.
- **Cost:** the complete four-case assembly file takes **169.48 s wrapper wall / 160.37 s Vitest duration**; native preparation is 83.82 s and test bodies total 1.008 s, including 0.804 s for the warning regression. The real query plus tool construction is needed to catch discarded reporters in migrated callers; the unit pipeline alone misses this failure. New-head CI seconds are pending.
- **Independent review:** fresh full 15-file local autoreview through Codex, P0–P2, two complete partitions, scoped-clean against main `9701d0ff`; the final commit tree matches the reviewed candidate. Static review did not rerun tests and does not grant maintainer approval.

New-head broad CI and enforced approvals remain separate. Earlier exact-head [CI 40860213436](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40860213436) succeeded for `ec40d0ab`; that is prior-head evidence. Current scoped checks do not certify installed upgrade, Windows, Bun, a real provider or an operator Gateway.

<details>
<summary>Earlier proof and failures retain their original source scope</summary>

- Original official-main `d704d3b` with the regression overlaid failed through real asynchronous tool assembly: one expected warning, zero observed. The isolated `b3b5173f` public `pnpm openclaw agent exec` run used private state and local HTTP/SSE fixtures; its terminal warning and fallback result are not a rerun on this head.
- [CI 40789900799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40789900799) failed 14 existing mock factories. The exact reconstructed merge/base comparison identified the canonical main repair retained above; this PR adds no mock exemption. Native classification remained “new / matching main job passed, selected scope not compared.”
- [CI 40741017809](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40741017809) exceeded its then-current test-line ceiling by 595 at net +48; that failed scope is retained. Current native budget success uses the base and counts stated above, without increasing a grant.
- Earlier [CI 40417533408](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40417533408) failed a Bun Gateway `agent.wait` lifecycle assertion. An official-main job showed the same signature, but its root cause was not established; later green CI does not prove a repair. The earlier package-boundary declaration preparation timeout is also retained as an unsuccessful attempt at its original scope.

</details>

prs.title: fix(macos): resolve typed gateway auth refs
prs.body:
Closes #128171

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app could not authenticate to a local Gateway when `gateway.auth.token` or `gateway.auth.password` used a typed env SecretRef. The Gateway supports those inputs, but the native endpoint store previously handled only strings.

## What Changed

- Resolve supported typed env SecretRefs from the actual Gateway LaunchAgent environment, with the app environment as fallback.
- Enforce the configured env provider and allowlist; malformed, unsupported, denied, or unresolved refs fail closed.
- Keep configured refs authoritative over same-surface ambient fallbacks.
- Match Core's implicit-mode behavior: two configured token/password inputs remain ambiguous; a concrete opposite-side fallback suppresses typed-ref materialization; after materialization, password is inferred before token.
- Match Core startup when a typed local password coexists with `gateway.remote.token`: the local password wins unless an ambient Gateway token causes Core to leave that password ref inactive; when token auth is active, preserve LaunchAgent-token precedence before the remote-token fallback.
- Pass only the selected credential into the native Gateway handshake.

## User Impact

Users can keep local Gateway credentials in supported typed environment SecretRefs without breaking the macOS app connection. Invalid or disallowed references remain fail-closed, and the native app follows the same token/password selection behavior as Core.

## Evidence

### Current evidence refresh, 2026-10-28

Current public head is `3481ca33a1bf69a445814f0c620e12719c78f947` (tree `f9061f44fb6a5815d8ab0e0f3a5391a9cac3a758`). Its merge preserves `c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513` and integrates main `9a5581b4ce230381e3f200a62be4cdbe78e41c19`. GitHub blob identities confirm that both PR-owned Swift files are unchanged from `c17b72d353`. Contributor credit and the prior source and native evidence below remain attached to their stated revisions.

[Canonical CI run 40678248294](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40678248294) and its CI gate succeeded for head `3481ca33a1bf69a445814f0c620e12719c78f947`. This run contains 5 successful and 38 skipped jobs. Both macOS Swift phases and the iOS build phase were skipped. [macOS and shared Periphery run 40678248230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40678248230) completed seven selected jobs successfully, including both shared-kit producers and the intersection; the iOS dead-code scan was skipped. Skipped native tests and successful static scans do not establish packaged-app authentication.

No new native run or fresh ClawSweeper verdict is claimed. The durable review below remains bound to `ff41c754`, and the shorthand correction at `c17b72d353` remains a source disposition. Exact-current-head focused tests, packaged-app coverage of the later remote-fallback combinations, and a stable-release upgrade retaining existing shorthand settings remain required. Historical native runs, the beta2 port, and earlier CI are preserved below and are not relabeled as current-head proof.

### Historical evidence status refresh, 2026-10-27

At that refresh, the public head was `c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513`. The [completed CI run 39411875583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) succeeded on tested merge `44577cf085aada61cbbfb40cbbd236c63a28518a`, combining this head with main `d8c96213c5cf40295863fb5fb6d347e1f9caf6b7`. Its unique job inventory contains **5 successful and 37 skipped jobs**, with no failures or pending jobs. These are this run's jobs, not a sum of duplicate check/status surfaces; skipped jobs are not passing runtime proof.

The [exact delta since reviewed head ff41c754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/ff41c754d9d4aa8a70bf2da9422ade5047d11c9c...c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513) changes only the endpoint source and its test file. `configuredInput` now classifies trimmed shorthand through `envSecretRefName` before auth-surface selection, and the existing handshake matrix adds both `$GW_PASSWORD` and `${GW_PASSWORD}` with the available service token. This addresses the source change requested by the earlier P1 finding and preserves the original shorthand/fallback intent. It is a source disposition, not a new exact-head ClawSweeper verdict or packaged-app result.

The [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128175#issuecomment-5385443900) explicitly says maintaining Swift/Core parity alone does not require another product decision. Earlier parity-approval language below records historical status and is superseded on that point. Maintainer acceptance remains outstanding. **Packaged-app proof for the later remote-fallback combinations and a stable-release upgrade retaining existing shorthand settings remain unproven.** The beta2-port test evidence below is not relabeled as current-head packaged-app proof. Earlier pending-CI statements are historical and superseded only by the completed run identified here. No new runtime test, whole-current-tree review, or upgrade demonstration is claimed by this refresh.


### Historical follow-up, 2026-10-20

Follow-up head: [c17b72d353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513).

- Classify the existing `$NAME` and `${NAME}` shorthand forms as references before implicit auth-mode selection. A missing password reference no longer suppresses an available service token. Explicit modes and malformed or literal values keep their existing paths.
- The two-file follow-up passed scoped P0–P3 Codex review with no actionable findings. This is source review, not runtime proof.
- The equivalent fix was compiled in the beta2 native integration. Its 13 credential-test functions passed in a deny-default OS sandbox, including the handshake matrix with both new shorthand cases. Strict SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. This is synthetic proof of the beta2 port, not an exact-head packaged-app run or real Keychain, GUI, identity, or upgrade proof.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) started automatically after the push; no completed verdict is claimed here. Maintainer parity and acceptance decisions remain open.

### Historical candidate evidence

Current PR candidate: `1ad4bcb852b2266950eea45c077ee023e1a42358`, merged with current `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `1e13fc8abcd942ca398a89ca5560da11a1d46c41`. GitHub confirms the PR is OPEN and the head/base match those revisions. The branch is `MERGEABLE` (no content conflict), but the merge state is BLOCKED by required CI. The PR delta against current main is limited to `GatewayEndpointStore.swift` and `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` (+118/-8 production, +477/-1 tests).

- The prior exact-head CI run found a SwiftFormat `conditionalAssignment` style error before compilation. The follow-up changes only the expression form and is being validated in current-head CI.
- Scoped Codex autoreview on this exact head returned `scoped-clean` at P2 with no findings (confidence 0.76). Its report used the selected diff and supplied Core auth sources; it does not claim runtime verification. The report is preserved in the task-local review artifacts.
- ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and reported no actionable code or security findings. It marked merge blocked pending the macOS auth owner's decision on the ongoing Swift/Core credential-selection parity contract, and notes there is no fresh packaged-app runtime demonstration for the remote-token fallback.
- Exact-head GitHub CI run [36282160728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282160728) completed with the `macos-swift (tests)` job cancelled while its Swift test step was running; no Swift test result is available. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failed solely because the selected `macos-swift` check was cancelled. Preflight, `security-fast`, `native-i18n`, all three macOS Node shards, Swift lint, `macos-swift (packages)`, shared OpenClawKit scans, macOS Periphery, OpenGrep, actionlint, changed-path scan, and security review passed. The iOS Periphery scan was skipped by scope.
- A rerun was requested for the cancelled job, but GitHub refused it with `Must have admin rights to Repository`. The Swift test verdict and aggregate CI gate therefore require a repository admin to rerun.
- `git diff --check` passes. This Windows host has no Swift toolchain, so native Swift execution relies on exact-head GitHub CI.
- The app-to-Gateway runtime proof below was performed on the earlier candidate `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`. It is historical evidence and does not demonstrate the added remote-token fallback cases on the current candidate.

Native validation on 2026-09-04:

Validated candidate: `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`.

The main refresh preserves @TheAngryPit's original repair, @CassieMei's carried
auth-mode and precedence corrections, and all five contributor commits. Its sole
content conflict was two independent insertions in the endpoint store; both the
typed-reference resolver and main's source-snapshot helper are retained.

### Before

[Native baseline run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33910257814)
used unchanged production main `606d9ab82afdb28ebaad33896e41811b96ad87c7`.
The actual ad-hoc packaged app sent no token for a supported typed custom env
reference that the healthy managed local Gateway could resolve. It received
`token_missing`. A fresh literal-token control authenticated as `openclaw-macos`
and completed `config.get`.

### After

[Exact-candidate native run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33916513675)
reconstructed and checked the exact candidate tree/commit, verified its signature,
built the real app through the normal package script, and installed each real
local service through `gateway install --wrapper`. The wrapper supplied normal
diagnostics and, only in the app-env fallback cases, the service's synthetic env
value. Every case used fresh synthetic profile/pairing state.

| Cases | Native result |
| --- | --- |
| Service-only typed token and password | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |
| Different app/service values for one ref, both modes | Service value selected; completed `config.get` |
| Supported app-env fallback, both modes | Service snapshot lacks the ref value; completed `config.get` |
| Explicit modes with inactive opposite refs | Correct active credential; completed `config.get` |
| Typed token + ambient password; typed password + ambient token | Same password/token selection as Core; completed `config.get` |
| Denied and unresolved active refs, both modes | No credential sent despite a valid ambient fallback; no protected request completed |
| All four rejected setups corrected and relaunched | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |

The protocol evidence correlates `openclaw-macos`, mode `ui`, to successful
protected responses on the same connections. Separate Control UI traffic is not
used as a substitute. Rejected-ref probes kept the server healthy with the
existing reload-off option; no auth or pairing policy was relaxed. The corrected
setups connect normally.

- `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`: 83 tests passed on the exact candidate, including
  provider/allowlist rules, handshake auth, legacy strings and lifecycle siblings.
- All 14 managed services were uninstalled/unloaded, all app phases stopped, and
  all synthetic Keychains were deleted successfully.
- The earlier obscured screenshots are not counted as visual auth evidence.
- Native proof does not replace the fresh independent review or required PR CI.

### Prior ClawSweeper finding and current scope

The fresh ClawSweeper finding was checked against Gateway startup at the exact
Core revision it reviewed. Startup's `hasGatewayTokenCandidate` excludes
`gateway.remote.token`, so a typed local password ref is materialized when no
ambient/local token candidate suppresses it; after materialization Core infers
password mode before token. The native selector and connect-frame regression
now preserve that password. If an ambient Gateway token is present, Core leaves
the password ref inactive and the native selector uses the token surface.

Against current main, the production delta is +118/-8 and the test delta is
+477/-1. The added native code
implements the existing typed-env contract; it adds no configuration option,
policy, schema, remote-auth behavior, or file/exec/store-ref support. Keep the
native/Core parity cases aligned when the shared auth contract changes.

The material below is retained contributor history at its stated inputs, not a
replacement for this current baseline and exact-candidate proof.

## Historical contributor evidence

Historical contributor head: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`

The native proof was built from the exact two-file PR patch (`patch-id 7040be749e604bbda4f9be0b44ed15605a058bd9`) over frozen base `9d79bf3f8c5f18f7c35d028d57402f5085659640`.

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` — 75/75 passed on Apple Silicon macOS.
- SwiftFormat with `config/swiftformat` — 0/2 files require formatting.
- SwiftLint 0.65.1 with `config/swiftlint.yml` — 0 violations.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full ad-hoc `OpenClaw.app` package build completed; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed.
- Real isolated app-to-Gateway proof passed on port 19791: the Gateway service and app process received different synthetic values for the same typed token ref; the app selected the Gateway service value, authenticated, and completed a real `config.get` response.
- Both isolated proof PIDs stopped afterward; the installed app remained running and no operator Gateway, config, Keychain, or PortGuardian state was changed.

### Review finding and vanilla verification

ClawSweeper correctly identified that the previous selector returned no credential for mixed typed-ref/ambient cases. Before changing it, the current Core Gateway was exercised directly in two isolated profiles:

- typed token ref + ambient password: Core marked the typed token surface inactive and started with password auth;
- typed password ref + ambient token: Core marked the typed password surface inactive and started with token auth.

The native selector and regression expectations now reproduce those observed Core outcomes rather than introducing an independent token/password policy.

### Fail-before evidence

- The original typed-ref handshake cases failed before the SecretRef implementation.
- Active-mode regression cases failed before mode filtering.
- The service-vs-app conflict initially selected the stale app value before LaunchAgent precedence was corrected.
- The two mixed inferred-mode cases returned no credential before `4e35b1caf03`; both now match the isolated Core runtime outcomes.

## Historical current-main revalidation (2026-09-03)

- Current `openclaw/openclaw:main`: `9d6f5d218884b00a50746353c40170f5ab46e4db`.
- Exact PR head preserved: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/remotes/audit/pr128175` completed cleanly.
- The change is not superseded: current main resolves literal strings and legacy `$ENV`/`${ENV}` string forms, but still lacks the typed SecretRef object flow and matching credential-selection semantics covered by this PR.
- Current product checks are complete. The earlier red `PR context and evidence` result was caused by malformed heading presentation; this body restores the authored sections explicitly.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, and review this change. The final diff and proof were inspected against current Core behavior.
