prs.title: improve(ios): reuse built test specification for screenshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release screenshot capture reopens the Xcode project and resolves its package graph for each iPhone or iPad after the lane has already built its test products.

## User Impact

No intended change to screenshots or release admission. This experiment tests whether reusing the fresh build’s test specification reduces capture overhead. It is not qualified for landing yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the generated `.xctestrun` directly to `test-without-building`, keeping it beside its build products so its relative paths remain valid. Require exactly one fresh specification before creating a simulator. The same four test identities, independent app launches, first-attempt requirement, result verification, and simulator cleanup remain in place. No new cache or fallback is added.

## Evidence

### Preregistered screening rule

Before any benchmark dispatch:

- Frozen baseline: `21e7ad20d3e5f56ddaefdb44b59a2716d5ea05da`; candidate is the reviewed head of this PR.
- Run one baseline followed by one candidate, serially, on fresh `xcode-27-xlarge` hosts using iOS Store Release with `operation=screenshots`, `resource_diagnostics=false`, and `startup_probe=false`. This is screenshot-only; no upload.
- Both frozen benchmark refs receive identical temporary workflow instrumentation: iPhone only, Watch omitted, existing Spotlight indexing disable retained, raw Xcode logs/results retained, and before/after host capacity recorded. These harness edits are excluded from this PR.
- Preserve four exact screenshot tests, four fresh nonempty PNGs, independent app launches/terminations, one capture attempt, and one active simulator. Inspect images and results.
- Primary work count: capture-side `Resolve Package Graph` passes (expected 1 → 0). Measure build, boot/inventory, status-bar/headroom, capture wall time, test-suite time, overhead outside the suite, and complete capture-step time; record image/Xcode/CPU/RAM and host load.
- A promising screen requires reduced capture wall time and overhead with no lost contract. Stop and investigate failure, host/image mismatch, or any measured timing regression of at least 20%; retain failed samples rather than replacing them.
- One pair is preliminary evidence, not median/p95 performance qualification or merge approval. A larger campaign requires a subsequent decision.

### Focused validation

- Existing Fastlane fixture extended for missing/ambiguous fresh specifications and their handoff to capture: baseline red; candidate 16 tests pass (0.81 seconds test time, 2.24 seconds complete runner wall time). The draft PR does not select this test lane, so its CI test seconds are unavailable; native workflow timings are recorded below.
- Ruby syntax, formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. Targeted lint and the applicable test-script typecheck pass; test-line ratchet passes.
- Simplification: project reopening and capture-side project/scheme/configuration/DerivedData arguments removed. Production delta: +2 lines; existing test delta: +14 lines, allocated exactly for specification prerequisite and handoff coverage; shared scalar unchanged.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review completed with no actionable correctness/security findings: base `21e7ad20d3e5f56ddaefdb44b59a2716d5ea05da`, head `d6d64a9eb7144c949b9d4cf440291990cd5ec294`, high reasoning, full local range (no filtered/smoke mode). Native captures were not run by the reviewer.
- Identical benchmark harness passes `scripts/check-workflows.mts` (actionlint, zizmor, and repository guards). Frozen baseline `246a44dd964f94a06bfd322b9dbfa4ee18b55d69`; frozen candidate `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12`. The one-pair hosted screen is complete; results below.

PR #189040 remains parked and is not part of this experiment. The merged TestFlight readback repair will be observed on the next scheduled run; no additional upload is triggered here.


### Screen result: inconclusive; do not land

Both [baseline run 41483351609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41483351609) and [candidate run 41485352258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41485352258) succeeded on attempt 1. No uploads, reruns, or replacement samples. Their `ios-screenshots-<run>-1` artifacts retain raw capture/build logs, the result bundle, PNGs, phase diagnostics, and capture ledger for 14 days.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Capture package-graph resolutions | 1 | 0 | removed |
| Build | 235.05 s | 249.28 s | +6.1% |
| Boot + inventory | 81.12 s | 89.46 s | +10.3% |
| Boot status | 48.91 s | 42.51 s | −13.1% |
| Simulator inventory | 32.20 s | 46.94 s | **+45.8%** |
| Headroom gate | 10.14 s | 10.13 s | −0.1% |
| Status-bar override | 10.80 s | 2.82 s | −73.9% |
| Capture wall time | 174.72 s | 151.06 s | −13.5% |
| Four-test suite | 85.202 s | 130.180 s | **+52.8%** |
| Capture overhead outside suite | 89.518 s | 20.880 s | −76.7% |
| Complete build/capture step | 531 s | 523 s | −1.5% |

This is one sample per arm: no median/p95 or tail claim. The intended work disappeared and overhead fell, but the preregistered 20% stop threshold was crossed for suite and inventory time. No further benchmark dispatches were made. This is not a passing performance qualification.

Contract checks: the canonical result verifier independently confirmed exactly the four expected tests passed once in each result bundle; both logs contain four app launches and four terminations; both capture ledgers record one successful attempt; active simulator count never exceeded one and returned to zero after cleanup. All four 1320×2868 PNGs were inspected and are byte-for-byte and pixel-for-pixel identical across arms.

Matched runner image: `xcode-27-arm64`, version `20261026.0314.1`, provisioner `20261021.618` in westus. Matched observed host identity: macOS 27.0.1 (`26A434`), Xcode 27.1 (`27A9275`), 5 logical CPUs, 15,032,385,536 bytes RAM (14 GiB), iPhone 18 Pro Max / iOS 27.0 (`24A434`) / arm64. Fresh host uptimes were about 3 minutes at the pre-capture snapshot. One-minute load averages before/after were 6.84/412.94 baseline and 10.94/292.38 candidate. Compressor pages at the end were 35,698/51,696; swap-in/out counters remained zero in both snapshots. These snapshots do not establish peak resource use or the cause of a delay.

#### Investigation of the stop thresholds

| Test | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Agent | 23.835 s | 23.342 s |
| Chat | 25.834 s | 73.606 s |
| Control | 14.421 s | 13.180 s |
| Settings | 21.113 s | 20.052 s |

The chat trace has the same operation sequence and no additional capture attempt. `typeText("focus")` reaches the next operation in about 0.64 s baseline / 0.87 s candidate. The candidate then spends 3–6 seconds on repeated element lookups, interrupt checks, and transcript coordinate queries after typing/clearing. The region from the first value lookup after typing to the diagram/window check takes 3.42 s baseline versus 53.56 s candidate. The other three tests are slightly faster in the candidate. No bootstrap-failure, connection-timeout, or stalled-wait markers were recorded.

The slower simulator inventory check ran before the changed capture invocation, in the unchanged admission path. The pair locates these delays but does not determine whether the changed invocation indirectly affects chat accessibility timing or whether a transient runtime/resource condition caused it. Do not label the slowdown an unrelated flake from this evidence. Next investigation should target that accessibility-query window before a larger paired campaign; preserve the existing typing/focus/empty-composer assertions.

Draft PR checks settled successfully (actionlint, label, scope detection, and resolution); broad native PR CI was skipped for the draft. Local focused checks and independent review remain as recorded above. PR #189040 remains unmerged. The next scheduled TestFlight observation remains pending; no extra upload was started.

### Bounded accessibility diagnostic (preregistered)

Before a diagnostic dispatch, preserve the original inconclusive screen above. Run one screenshot-only diagnostic from the frozen candidate harness with unchanged app/test source, exact four tests, independent launches, first-attempt verification, and simulator cleanup. Temporary instrumentation stays on a separate benchmark ref and is excluded from this PR.

The named unknown is whether the post-typing accessibility-query delay is dominated by app layout/CPU work, XCTest or accessibility IPC, or wider simulator resource contention. Incremental reads observe the existing raw Xcode log without changing its output plumbing. Only during the chat test, collect 1 Hz CPU/RSS/state for processes verified to belong to the task simulator, plus cheap host CPU/memory counters. A post-typing output gap over 2 seconds triggers at most four one-second stack samples, with bounded command deadlines and no retries. Log arrival gaps are triggers only: buffering can produce them. Record each observation's wall time and failures, and retain only sanitized fixed-role events, process measurements, and call stacks. No arguments, paths, message text, UI hierarchy, or raw sample headers are exported.

Success means obtaining valid bounded observations during the real chat window while preserving the screenshot contract. A reproduced slowdown must be attributed using the process/stacks and corresponding XCTest activities; a fast run is only absence of reproduction. Instrumented timings cannot replace the baseline/candidate samples or qualify this performance change. No upload, merge, full paired campaign, assertion weakening, or timeout/retry increase is authorized by this diagnostic.

Diagnostic harness validation: frozen temporary ref `bench/ios-ax-diagnostic`, head `44fcbc3149de1831d4edb5e11efd5a7a9804f0f0`, based on the frozen candidate harness. App and test source are unchanged. Pinned workflow checks, syntax/format/whitespace checks, and focused resource-safety lint pass. Full ordinary lint was unavailable in this scratch worktree because its linked dependency layout is unsupported by declaration preparation and lacks the Solid lint plugin; no full-lint success is claimed. Synthetic and disposable-child checks cover simulator custody, sanitized output, sample caps, observation budget, cancellation, missing native exit callbacks, and preservation of a failed workload's exit code. The original resource wrapper is retained and will be disabled through the existing dispatch input.

The initial local review identified wrapper removal and unbounded observer shutdown; both were repaired. Final local ClawSweeper full committed-range review completed at high reasoning with no actionable correctness/security findings, base `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12`, head `44fcbc3149de1831d4edb5e11efd5a7a9804f0f0`. The observer checkpoints sanitized output on termination and bounds native-command settlement independently of exit notification. If the OS refuses a native child's exit, it records unconfirmed fixed-role PIDs; disposable hosted runner cleanup owns that exceptional case. The outer workflow also bounds observer shutdown. Hosted diagnostic dispatch is next; runtime attribution remains pending.

### First diagnostic result: screenshot contract passed; sampling unavailable

[Run 41490602971](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41490602971), attempt 1, succeeded in 9m42s on frozen diagnostic head `44fcbc3149de1831d4edb5e11efd5a7a9804f0f0`. The upload job was skipped. The canonical result verifier independently confirms four exact tests passed once, with four launches/terminations, one capture attempt, one active simulator, and successful shutdown/deletion to zero. The same runner image, OS, Xcode, CPU count and RAM as the original screen were observed.

Agent/Chat/Control/Settings durations were 20.627/41.406/14.425/18.679 seconds. Chat first typing begins at 24.80 seconds, versus 17.78 baseline and 15.36 candidate. The first post-typing value lookup to window check is 9.36 seconds, versus 3.42/53.56 seconds originally. Delays are present before typing, and the prolonged candidate transcript-query window did not recur in this run. This is neither a replacement sample nor evidence that an app defect was fixed.

The first full process-list command timed out after 2181.98 ms, before typing. It was terminated without exit confirmation; PID 23925 in the artifact is that observer command, not the app. The collector disabled subsequent process polling within its observation budget, retained the exact timeout outcome, and took zero stack samples. Its secondary disabled-reason label says unavailable; the detailed observation correctly says timeout. Therefore the diagnostic did **not** attribute the original slowdown. A single host snapshot (load average 225.47, about 216 MiB free of 14 GiB) is consistent with contention but proves neither CPU nor memory starvation; reclaimable macOS cache is not represented by free-memory alone.

Three screenshots are byte-identical to baseline, including Chat. Control was visually inspected: only 48 RGB pixels differ, by at most one channel value, around the Settings-button edge. No visible layout/content change. Raw logs, result bundle, PNGs, capture ledger, phases, and sanitized probe output remain in `ios-screenshots-41490602971-1` for 14 days. No raw sample files were exported.

### Follow-up diagnostic rule: eliminate process discovery

The named instrumentation failure above warrants one changed diagnostic, not a blind replay. Preserve that run and the original benchmark pair. Replace full-host enumeration with an app-produced PID receipt and the existing runner PID header. On the temporary diagnostic ref only, the debug simulator app writes fixed role, its own PID, and simulator UUID once at chat launch, through the existing Fastlane cache bridge; the UITest only supplies the path. Existing assertions, selectors, independent launches, first-attempt verification and simulator cleanup remain intact. The receipt and process checks never export content, arguments, or paths.

Use separate single-PID queries, verify executable/name/UUID and simulator parent, and freshly recheck identity before sampling. Remove full-host/service enumeration. An optional CPU-observation failure disables that role's polling without disabling host counters or independently verified app/runner samples. Retain the same two bounded sample rounds/four-command cap, deadlines, sanitized egress and bounded shutdown. This reduces diagnostic coverage of other services; app/runner stacks are the initial attribution boundary. Record observer CPU/RSS and command wall times. No claim of benchmark comparability is made for the receipt-instrumented app.

Before hosted dispatch, a task-owned ordinary simulator app proved the host Fastlane-cache receipt bridge and exact helper identity/sample path: 5.706 ms identity validation, 1638 ms sample, 16 sanitized frames, and joined sampler children. The first tiny fixture lacked the required scene lifecycle and crashed before executing receipt code; its crash report identified that fixture defect, and the corrected scene-based fixture passed. The task-owned simulator and receipt directory were deleted. Synthetic checks cover missing/wrong-UUID receipts, exact single-PID selection, sample caps, CPU-observation independence and cancellation. Focused Swift formatting passes; strict SwiftLint reports the same seven existing UITest-file violations as frozen source (including existing 2502-line file debt, temporarily 2511). No lint exception or passing full-lint claim is introduced. Workflow checks pass. Independent full-range review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings against base `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12` and diagnostic head `3773409c8eb738bd8525015f2495aef4b84357fa`. The revised harness remains excluded from this production PR.

### Follow-up diagnostic result

[Run 41494305259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41494305259), attempt 1 at diagnostic head `3773409c8eb738bd8525015f2495aef4b84357fa`, succeeded in 9m35s on the same recorded runner image, OS, Xcode, capacity, and simulator runtime as the original screen. Qualification and upload were skipped. The canonical result verifier confirms all four exact tests passed once, with four independent app launches/terminations, one successful capture attempt, at most one active simulator, and successful shutdown/deletion to zero.

Agent/Chat/Control/Settings took 19.491/56.173/13.321/20.543 seconds. Chat typing starts at 40.460 seconds; the first post-typing value lookup is at 45.045 and the window check at 52.266: 7.221 seconds, compared with 3.422/53.557 seconds in the original baseline/candidate. Delays occur before typing, including readiness, input lookup, and keyboard queries. The original prolonged post-typing window did not recur; this diagnostic does not replace either performance sample or qualify the production change.

Explicit process targeting worked: both simulator identities verified, all 55 single-PID observations succeeded, no roles were disabled or missing, and no native child remained unjoined. The app accumulated 5.10 CPU seconds over 50.205 observed seconds (10.2% of one core); the runner accumulated 0.93 seconds over 54.178 seconds (1.7%). Around the delayed input lookup, the app accumulated only 0.13 CPU seconds over a 5.668-second observation span. This does not support sustained CPU spinning in either observed process; it does not locate blocked work or identify another process responsible for delays. App/runner peak observed RSS was approximately 503/330 MiB. The Node observer itself accumulated 435 ms of CPU across its lifetime, ending at about 19 MiB RSS; this excludes native child CPU. Its 55 process observations consumed 14.16 seconds of command wall time in the background, and observer perturbation is not ruled out.

One post-typing output gap triggered app and runner stack samples. Both commands exceeded their 3.5-second deadlines and settled at about 3.6 seconds; neither yielded exported stacks. All sampler children joined and observer shutdown completed. No stack-level attribution is available, and identical sampling failures will not be blindly retried.

All 37 derived host CPU intervals report 100%; raw idle/total deltas were not retained, so real zero-idle cannot be distinguished from host/VM accounting behavior. Treat this metric as unvalidated. Load averages rise substantially and free memory varies, but neither identifies a culprit or proves memory starvation. The before/after VM snapshots report no swap-ins or swap-outs.

Control, Agent, and Settings PNGs are byte-identical to the original baseline. The chat image was visually inspected: 485 RGB pixels differ, maximum channel delta 2/255, confined to the composer region; no visible content or layout change. An independent evidence audit confirmed the CPU/timing interpretation and its limits. The original benchmark verdict remains inconclusive. The temporary diagnostic code is excluded from this PR, which remains draft.

The next useful diagnostic, if pursuing attribution, is a temporary bounded app-owned main-queue heartbeat and editor/layout counters with phase timestamps, locally validated before another hosted run. This would distinguish app responsiveness from automation delays without another native stack-sampler retry. No further run has been dispatched.

### App-owned responsiveness diagnostic rule

Before the next hosted dispatch, replace native process polling/sampling with a temporary Debug iOS-simulator helper started only for the chat screenshot process. It writes fixed event names, clocks, and seven editor counters; never text, UI hierarchy, URLs, or stack headers. A serial background writer ticks once per second for at most 120 seconds/120 ticks. At most one main-queue heartbeat may be pending. Each acknowledgment records execution time on main separately from later writer delivery and includes an immutable counter snapshot. Counter measurements cover updateUIView, fitting size, deferred interaction updates, accepted native text changes, focus begin/end, and native layout. Durations are inclusive wall time, not CPU, and nested durations overlap.

Local acceptance: compile the exact helper/editor under Swift 6 strict concurrency; exercise actual native insertion/deletion and editor layout in a disposable simulator fixture; independently timestamp a deliberate main-thread pause and verify background ticks continue while the main acknowledgment is delayed; verify the disabled gate writes nothing. This validates the observer, not the project screenshot path or a performance fix.

After local proof and full-range independent review, run one screenshot-only hosted diagnostic with resource timeline and startup probe disabled. Preserve the exact four tests, their assertions, separate app launches, first-attempt verification, and simulator cleanup. Verify result and PNG differences before interpreting timing. Do not treat this as another benchmark sample or replace the original screen.

Interpretation: compare XCTest activity timestamps against heartbeat execution, background tick gaps, snapshot age, callback counts, recursion depth, and maximum elapsed time. Background progress with a late main acknowledgment establishes a main-queue progress gap; a stale snapshot during that gap does not establish lack of app work. Prompt main acknowledgment during a slow AX query narrows the cause toward automation/service latency, without excluding all app subsystems. Writer scheduling/delivery delays remain separate, and observer perturbation is not ruled out. Flag heartbeat delays over one second and callback elapsed times over 100 ms for investigation, not as new screenshot pass/fail rules. No native sampler retries, process enumeration, timeout increases, new caches, or weakened assertions are introduced.

All instrumentation remains on the separate diagnostic branch and must be removed after the investigation. This production PR remains unchanged and draft. Local validation passed at diagnostic head `1624f251f6c99a82803d98e381cd67cdc8d40b9c`; full-range local ClawSweeper review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings against base `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12` and head `1624f251f6c99a82803d98e381cd67cdc8d40b9c` (complete, no filtered/smoke scope). [Run 41497980432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41497980432) was canceled during checkout, before build or capture, after source inspection identified a measurement bias: heartbeat request time preceded a log write. No screenshot result was produced; the always-run artifact step reported no files after cancellation. Qualification and upload were skipped. Diagnostic head `aea19aa22113a53c4aaa16765a2de2ac01bcae23` moves request time immediately before main dispatch, after the write, so writer time cannot masquerade as main-queue latency. Exact-source local revalidation passed with the corrected timestamp: native editing/layout/focus/enablement passed, all counters balanced at depth zero, and the disabled gate wrote no metrics. During an independently timestamped 2202.47 ms main-thread pause, two background ticks continued and one heartbeat waited 1387.07 ms from enqueue to execution; writer delivery was measured separately at 100.25 ms. The local simulator was deleted. A fresh full-range local ClawSweeper review completed with no actionable correctness/security findings against base `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12` and head `aea19aa22113a53c4aaa16765a2de2ac01bcae23`. [Corrected-head screenshot-only run 41498606519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41498606519) completed successfully at that exact reviewed head, attempt 1, with resource timeline and startup probe disabled. Results follow. The exact helper and editor compiled under Swift 6 strict concurrency and ran in a disposable simulator fixture. Native insert/delete binding, layout, focus, and enablement passed. An independently timestamped 2202.57 ms main-thread pause produced three background ticks and exactly one pending heartbeat recovery: main latency 2162.44 ms, writer delivery 3.43 ms. All seven counters were exercised, balanced, and ended at depth zero. Removing the screenshot argument produced no metrics file while the same native fixture passed. Source hashes matched before/after; the task simulator was shut down and deleted. This proves the observer mechanism locally, not the project screenshot path or a performance fix. Pinned SwiftFormat and workflow checks passed. Strict SwiftLint reports the same seven existing UITest violations; it reports no new helper/editor/app violations.

### App-owned responsiveness diagnostic result

Run 41498606519 succeeded in 11m10s. Qualification and upload were skipped. The canonical result verifier confirms all four exact tests passed once, with four independent launches/terminations, one successful capture attempt, at most one active simulator, and shutdown/deletion to zero. All four PNGs are byte-identical to the original baseline. The recorded runner image/provisioner, macOS, Xcode, CPU/memory capacity, and iPhone runtime match the original screen.

Agent/Chat/Control/Settings took 23.224/27.533/13.314/20.634 seconds. The severe original post-typing window did not recur: first value lookup at 20.844 seconds to Window at 23.778 was 2.934 seconds, versus 3.422/53.557 originally. Build took 284.41 seconds and boot plus inventory 107.34 seconds (inventory 61.48), versus 223.15/62.02 seconds in the preceding targeted-process diagnostic; capture took 115.87 versus 134.96 seconds. The longer overall run is concentrated before the instrumented app starts. These are diagnostic observations, not additional benchmark arms or performance qualification.

The app exported 44 records over 22.09 seconds, including 20 main heartbeats. Median main-queue latency was 0.036 ms; maximum was 1421.42 ms. The two delays over one second both precede native typing: launch/idle waiting at 3.461–4.883 seconds, and keyboard checking at 16.763–17.785. Native text callbacks begin at 20.580 seconds. Median writer delivery was 0.207 ms, maximum 389.82 ms; main execution and later writer delivery were kept distinct. Background tick intervals ranged from 616 to 1328 ms. The observed wall-clock/uptime offset spread was under 0.01 ms.

A remaining slow input lookup spans 17.792–20.444 seconds. During that interval, main heartbeats execute at 18.958 and 19.574 seconds with 0.016/0.035 ms enqueue-to-execution latency, while editor counters remain unchanged. Their records reach the writer 197.9/389.8 ms later. This lookup was therefore not one continuous app-main blockage; the probe does not establish which automation or accessibility-service operation delayed it.

All seven instrumented counters are balanced in the final snapshot, with maximum same-site depth one:

| Callback | Completed calls | Maximum inclusive wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| updateUIView | 28 | 0.034 ms |
| sizeThatFits | 120 | 0.318 ms |
| Deferred interaction update | 13 | 0.025 ms |
| Accepted native text change | 10 | 0.228 ms |
| Focus began | 1 | 0.060 ms |
| Focus ended | 1 | 0.014 ms |
| Native layoutSubviews | 12 | 0.126 ms |

Fitting, native text callbacks, and native layout total 5.815/0.898/0.932 ms respectively. Inclusive callback durations can overlap and are not CPU measurements. This supports no runaway or expensive instrumented editor path in this run. One-hertz sampling misses shorter bursts; these counters do not cover all app, accessibility, keyboard, or rendering work. No app fix or attribution of the original severe stall is justified. An independent evidence audit confirmed this interpretation.

The original performance verdict remains inconclusive. The clean production candidate remains unchanged at `d6d64a9eb7144c949b9d4cf440291990cd5ec294`, with all temporary diagnostics excluded, and this PR remains draft. Preserve the original samples and use the clean candidate for any subsequent evaluation. Do not expand diagnostics without a new observed need. No merge or release upload was performed.

### Clean five-pair campaign (preregistered before dispatch)

The user approved returning to the clean production candidate after the bounded diagnostic investigation. Preserve the original inconclusive pair and every diagnostic above separately; none is replaced or counted toward this campaign.

- Run five additional fresh-host pairs in serial ABAB order, baseline then candidate, with no overlap. Frozen baseline benchmark head: `246a44dd964f94a06bfd322b9dbfa4ee18b55d69`; frozen candidate benchmark head: `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12`. Production candidate remains `d6d64a9eb7144c949b9d4cf440291990cd5ec294`.
- Dispatch the committed identical benchmark workload through `ios-store-release.yml`, `operation=screenshots`, `resource_diagnostics=false`, `startup_probe=false`. This retains the iPhone-only harness, Spotlight disable, raw logs/results, and host-capacity snapshots. No app/runner observer instrumentation, uploads, retries, timeout changes, assertion changes, or replacement samples.
- Verify attempt 1, exact frozen source, matched actual runner image/OS/Xcode/CPU/RAM/runtime, four exact tests passing once, four independent launches/terminations, four fresh nonempty images, one active simulator at most, and cleanup to zero. Compare PNGs to the original baseline; inspect any differences before interpreting performance.
- Record capture package-resolution count, build, boot plus inventory, boot status, simulator inventory, headroom, status-bar override, capture wall time, four-test suite duration (sum of the four test durations), capture overhead outside that suite, complete build/capture-step time, and individual test durations. Record before/after host load and VM counters; these are snapshots, not peak-resource attribution.
- **Pair-by-pair stop:** after each completed pair and before another dispatch, stop and investigate any failed contract, host/image mismatch, or candidate timing at least 20% slower than its paired baseline in any recorded timing cell, including individual tests. Do not discard the sample, substitute another, or reinterpret the threshold as aggregate-only. A failed baseline or run also stops dispatch. Retain all evidence and record the reason.
- If all five pairs complete without a stop, report each pair plus per-arm median, descriptive nearest-rank p95, and range. A useful result must remove capture-side package resolution (1 to 0), reduce median capture wall time and median capture overhead, preserve every screenshot contract, and hold or improve the other end-to-end metrics. Any worsening needs explicit owner acceptance; this campaign does not authorize it. Five samples per arm cannot support a strong tail-latency claim.
- Decide whether the clean candidate has repeatable measurable benefit or should be closed. Do not merge or trigger a release/upload in this campaign.

Campaign stopped after the first additional pair under the preregistered failure rule. No second pair or replacement sample was dispatched. Results follow.

### Clean campaign result: stopped after pair 1; unqualified

[Baseline 41501186092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41501186092) succeeded on attempt 1 at frozen head `246a44dd964f94a06bfd322b9dbfa4ee18b55d69`. [Candidate 41502980635](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41502980635) failed on attempt 1 at frozen head `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12`. Both qualification and upload jobs were skipped. The campaign stopped immediately after this pair; pairs 2–5 were not dispatched. The original screen and all diagnostic samples remain separate and unchanged. There were no reruns, discarded samples, uploads, or merges.

Capture-side package resolutions were again 1 baseline / 0 candidate. Observed times follow. **The candidate failed its screenshot contract, so its shorter overhead is not a passing performance result and these are not equivalent successful workloads.**

| Metric | Baseline | Failed candidate | Observed change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Build | 235.000 s | 257.740 s | +9.7% |
| Boot + inventory | 74.860 s | 78.820 s | +5.3% |
| Boot status | 43.710 s | 48.290 s | +10.5% |
| Simulator inventory | 31.150 s | 30.520 s | -2.0% |
| Headroom gate | 10.130 s | 10.130 s | +0.0% |
| Status-bar override | 10.610 s | 3.520 s | -66.8% |
| Capture wall time | 149.850 s | 156.930 s | +4.7% |
| Four-test duration sum | 120.531 s | 130.100 s | +7.9% |
| Capture wall minus four-test duration sum | 29.319 s | 26.830 s | -8.5% |
| Complete build/capture step | 497.000 s | 524.000 s | +5.4% |
| Agent test | 19.278 s | 25.100 s | +30.2% |
| Chat test | 68.618 s | 70.259 s | +2.4% |
| Control test | 13.373 s | 14.131 s | +5.7% |
| Settings test | 19.262 s | 20.610 s | +7.0% |

Suite is the sum of the four rounded per-test durations, including the failed test for this observation. The native suite aggregate can differ by 0.001 seconds because of rounding. Agent also crossed the pair-by-pair timing stop (+30.2%). Complete step time was 497 → 524 seconds (+5.4%). No median/p95 or repeatable-benefit claim is supported by this stopped campaign.

The same image/provisioner, region, OS, Xcode, actual CPU/RAM, and simulator runtime as the original screen were verified: `xcode-27-arm64` / `20261026.0314.1`, provisioner `20261021.618`, westus; macOS 27.0.1 (`26A434`), Xcode 27.1 (`27A9275`), 5 logical CPUs, 15,032,385,536 bytes RAM, iPhone 18 Pro Max / iOS 27.0 (`24A434`) / arm64. Both hosts had about three minutes uptime before capture. One-minute load averages before/after were 5.54/279.14 baseline and 15.59/362.28 candidate. Compressor pages after capture were 46,662/46,020; swap-in/out counters remained zero. These snapshots do not establish a specific resource-starvation cause.

Baseline contract: the canonical result verifier confirms exactly four expected tests passed once. Four launches and terminations, one successful attempt, at most one active simulator, and cleanup to zero were verified. All four PNGs are byte-identical to the original baseline. Baseline Chat took 68.618 seconds, showing that substantial automation delays also occur with the unchanged project-based invocation; that does not establish that the candidate has no timing effect.

Candidate contract: build, headroom, boot, and status-bar stages succeeded. Exactly four tests ran once; Agent, Control, and Settings passed. Chat failed at the unchanged `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:145` assertion waiting for the `Mermaid diagram` button. Four launches/terminations and one failed attempt were retained; shutdown and deletion succeeded to zero. The canonical result verifier rejects the failed bundle as expected. No final PNG set was exported, so there is no passing candidate image comparison.

#### Failure investigation from retained evidence

The recording and failure hierarchy establish an actual renderer fallback: the fixture diagram's source and options are visible beside “Diagram temporarily unavailable. Use the menu to retry, or read and copy its source.” The recording shows “Rendering diagram…” initially and the unavailable fallback at the explicitly extracted 35-second frame, before the `typeText("focus")` activity starts at 38.49 seconds (native event synthesis begins at 43.23 seconds). The failure therefore precedes typing, clearing, and transcript dismissal; it is not an offscreen-only or missing-fixture explanation. The initial readiness check does not wait for the diagram itself.

`ChatMermaidBlockView` displays this fallback after a retryable renderer failure, covering busy, unavailable, timed out, invalid result, and retryable JavaScript errors. `ChatMermaidRenderer` has a 20-second watchdog spanning document loading, JavaScript rendering, and snapshotting, but the retained evidence does not log which category or phase failed. Navigation, WebContent termination, JavaScript invocation, and snapshot errors also reach this fallback. The build log shows Mermaid assets copied into the package resource bundle and app; it does not prove runtime load success. No specific crash or resource-starvation attribution is established. A longer XCTest wait cannot recover this terminal state without a changed request or explicit Retry.

A read-only comparison against current main `024e7b34f6dbd1a86c942cef8dccc6e47947bb7b` found both renderer and block-view owner files byte-identical to this frozen source. That is source evidence, not a failing current-main replay. An independent source/evidence audit confirmed those limits. The invocation change is not proven causal or exonerated. No app/editor change, timeout increase, assertion weakening, retry, or new instrumentation was made. Raw logs, results, diagnostics, and the failed-test recording remain in the two run artifacts (`ios-screenshots-<run>-1`, 14-day retention).

**Decision:** this PR has not demonstrated repeatable benefit and must not be marked ready or landed. Keep it draft while evaluating whether the renderer failure merits a separate repair; do not spend the remaining benchmark pairs without a new, evidence-based campaign decision. Closing the optimization is reasonable if that separate investigation is not pursued. The smallest useful follow-up diagnostic would record only renderer-owned fixed failure category, phase, origin, and elapsed time, excluding diagram source, SVG, and raw error text.


### Preregistered Mermaid diagnostic (separate temporary branch)

The clean candidate failure is still unexplained. Run exactly one screenshot-only diagnostic from frozen `bench/ios-mermaid-diagnostic` commit `27f313b2549a482e1c762312a5a72001ab013e23`, based on the failed clean candidate `304f2a6b40d75331b3ced572d6d3bf09ff40be12`. These temporary changes are excluded from this PR. The stopped performance campaign stays stopped; this diagnostic is neither another benchmark pair nor a replacement sample.

- Use the same iPhone-only frozen harness on `xcode-27-xlarge`, `operation=screenshots`, `resource_diagnostics=false`, and `startup_probe=false`. Preserve the four exact tests, assertions, independent launches/terminations, first capture attempt, one active simulator, and cleanup. Keep Spotlight indexing disabled. - Instrument the actual native Mermaid owner only in DEBUG iOS simulator screenshot mode. - Local mechanism proof passed against the exact final renderer/helper: real bundled WebKit render and snapshot, unchanged native-watchdog timeout with a controlled no-response fixture asset, cancellation, disabled diagnostics, invalid request, and the 64-record cap. Fixed schema, contiguous sequences, and absence of a private sentinel were checked. The fixture did not alter production assets or native timeout behavior; its simulator was shut down and deleted. The initial diagnostic dispatch [41507724416](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41507724416) remained pending behind the unrelated scheduled release's workflow-wide lock. [Diagnostic run 41516206705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41516206705) completed successfully on attempt 1 at frozen diagnostic SHA `2c6a5c1a9cf6569db40fd3b5c268f4975e8ab095`. ## Transcript coordinate diagnostic (one run, preregistered)

The successful Mermaid diagnostic's legacy activity finish timestamps show 22.625 seconds in three nested transcript accessibility queries inside a 25.253-second synthesis activity (89.6%). The temporary experiment resolves the unchanged (0.99, 0.05) transcript gutter point once and re-roots the same point to the application coordinate, subtracting the application origin. Run [41520999583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41520999583), attempt 1, completed successfully on exact diagnostic SHA `4f889c6279fcc661bf9793d13dd12f4d125cdafb`.

The complete renderer observer has 13 contiguous records and both started jobs have terminal events. prs.title: improve(ui): rethink Privacy & Security around what's exposed and what agents can do
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Privacy & Security should say how exposed this Gateway is, what agents can do, and who approved what. Instead it reported two things that were false on a real Gateway:

- **Gateway auth said "unknown"** on a Gateway using token auth. The row read the config file, which is silent when the credential comes from the environment, while the Gateway reports its real mode at connect.
- **Exec policy said "allowlist"** on a Gateway where `exec.approvals.get` resolves to `security: full, ask: off`, so commands run without asking. The row hard-coded a stricter fallback, ignored `tools.exec.mode`, and ignored host approvals.

The structure hid the rest: "Security" appeared twice, one group mixed facts, a toggle and a pairing button, nothing said where the Gateway could be reached from, Available tools showed no selection when the profile was unset, and its help text suggested choosing Full. The two tabs each held a heading and a triangle, because every setting behind them is advanced.

## User Impact

One page, no tabs, read top to bottom:

- **Access:** Gateway auth, Network access, and Devices. Each opens the page that changes it.
- **Agents:** Exec policy with what it means, Available tools, Browser tools, and Approvals.
- **Approval forwarding** and **Policies:** each setting is one row that opens in place. Settings with a switch show Enabled or Disabled and open with the switch first.

Available tools is now a select with Default as a real choice, and every option gets one factual line, so none reads as the recommended one. Pair device moves to Devices, where the same button already is. Old `?section=approvals` links still land on the section.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auth now reads what the Gateway reports at connect, falling back to config only when it doesn't report one. That report can miss a startup `--auth`, so the row states the mode without a reassuring dot and only warns about no auth. Exec policy is `tools.exec` intersected with host approvals, which is how the Gateway enforces it. A value that can't be known says Unknown rather than guessing.

Network access can only repeat what config asks for, because the Gateway doesn't report its bind and `--bind` or `--tailscale` leave config untouched. So it shows the configured value, says a startup flag can override it, and never reassures. An unset bind reads Default rather than Loopback, because the default differs in containers. Reaching a loopback-bound Gateway from another host reads as Remote, with that host named. #191486 makes the Gateway report it.

Exec policy stays read-only here. Writing `mode` beside legacy `security` and `ask` values fails config validation, so its row opens Devices, where Exec approvals live. Warnings mark only no auth and Tailscale Funnel, and are the only dots these rows can show, because a false alarm costs little and false reassurance doesn't; Full is stated plainly, with no prompt either way.

Overlap with open PRs: this replaces the Security hunks of #191409, #191411 and #191419. The Advanced disclosure in #191359 no longer appears on this page. #191189 and #191244 are untouched and this page links to them. Generated field labels stay Title Case until #191352.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on an isolated port and state, synthetic secrets, real clicks, checked against the config file: select to Coding and back to Default, Browser tools off and on, forwarding on, every row's destination, the old deep link, host approvals tightening Exec policy to Ask, and the Gateway stopping under the open page. A Gateway started with `--bind lan` and a silent config, confirmed listening on all interfaces, reads Default with no dot when viewed over loopback. A real Gateway refuses to bind to the LAN without auth, so that state is unit-tested only. Tailscale states and read-only scopes come from the mock, since Tailscale modes would change the machine's real Tailscale state. prs.title: fix(ios): avoid slow keyboard dismissal during screenshots
prs.body:
Related: #191282

## What Problem This Solves

Release screenshot capture can spend tens of seconds resolving the chat transcript while tapping its gutter to dismiss the keyboard.

## User Impact

This changes only screenshot-test automation. App behavior and the captured screen stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the existing gutter point once, then tap that point relative to the application origin. This removes repeated transcript lookup during event synthesis. The fixture stays stationary between resolution and tapping; the normalized target remains `(0.99, 0.05)`.

Typing, the empty composer, keyboard dismissal, a closed diagram preview, and a visible, hittable Mermaid diagram are still asserted. No assertion, timeout, retry, fixture, or app code changes. Only the existing UITest changes: eight lines added, two removed. Temporary diagnostics and the separate `.xctestrun` experiment are excluded.

## Evidence

- Focused Swift 6 simulator typecheck, repository SwiftFormat, and `git diff --check` pass. Strict SwiftLint retains the same seven existing violations as the pinned base; no exceptions added.
- Earlier instrumented observation, not proof of this clean branch: [baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41516206705) versus [coordinate diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41520999583). Transcript lookups inside synthesis fell from three (22.625 s) to zero; the complete gutter sequence, including up-front resolution, changed from 28.888 s to 2.407 s. Chat changed from 79.930 s to 53.242 s. These are single-run observations, not a general performance benchmark or percentile claim.
- Native translation verification passed unchanged after installing this checkout’s frozen dependencies independently.
- Full local ClawSweeper review, high reasoning, completed with no findings. Base `68e6772de3e55c0734efad6b40306d6115f8fd6e`; reviewed snapshot `4f60e7f9ae74c481c57961f41e6bbfa06df333ff`, with the same source tree as published head `f183c01514b02ba71b53bcadd0c2272414076232`.
- Clean-branch screenshot proof passed in [ordinary PR CI 41526948652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526948652), attempt 1. Both downloaded xcresult bundles independently pass the canonical verifier: all four release screenshot tests passed exactly once on iPhone and iPad. Watch capture and the evidence reducer also passed.

Validation rule, recorded before clean-branch execution: use the ordinary PR `ios-screenshots` job, which runs the shared `pnpm ios:screenshots` command without an upload. Require all four release screenshot tests to pass once on both iPhone and iPad, fresh valid screenshots, one capture attempt per family, and simulator cleanup. The ordinary job also captures Watch. Record the tested checkout SHA and PR head separately. A failed run requires diagnosis; do not retry solely for green. This is functional validation of the extracted fix, not a restart of the stopped performance campaign.

The earlier Mermaid fallback remains a separate unexplained failure; this PR does not claim to fix it.


## Clean-branch validation result

PR head: `f183c01514b02ba71b53bcadd0c2272414076232`. Tested merge checkout and workflow SHA: `e2b32aa974e8567de36893613b690cf13ecf7afe` (includes that PR head). Xcode 27.1 (`27A9275`), Fastlane 2.241.1, Node v24.22.1. Run `41526948652`, attempt 1.

- iPhone 18 Pro Max: all four exact screenshot tests passed once; one successful capture attempt; four PNGs, 1320×2868.
- iPad Pro 13-inch (M5): all four exact screenshot tests passed once; one successful capture attempt; four PNGs, 2064×2752.
- Apple Watch Ultra 3: capture passed; one PNG, 422×514.
- All nine PNGs match the evidence manifest hashes and pass local signature, chunk CRC, compressed-data, and dimension verification. Both downloaded xcresult bundles passed `node scripts/ios-screenshot-evidence.mjs verify --xcresult …`. The CI collector/reducer validated the capture-attempt records and exact artifact union.
- Every recorded phase succeeded. Both XCTest captures recorded four test starts and no instruments connection timeout, runner bootstrap failure, or stalled wait. Maximum recorded active simulator count was one; shutdown and deletion returned to zero after each of the three families.
- CI settled on this head: 22 current checks passed, 43 skipped, no pending or failed checks. This includes main CI, screenshots, the evidence reducer, native translation verification, security checks, and the completed Periphery reports/scans. The hosted ClawSweeper review also reported no actionable findings.

The run uses the ordinary screenshot lane without temporary renderer/activity instrumentation or `.xctestrun` changes. This validates the clean extracted interaction on both device families; it does not establish a general speedup or explain the separate earlier Mermaid fallback. No rerun, store upload, merge, or performance-campaign restart was performed. The screenshot and diagnostic artifacts have 14-day retention under this run.

Retained run evidence: [screenshots, both xcresult bundles, and canonical manifest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526948652/artifacts/13181880930); [phase and resource diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41526948652/artifacts/13181880702). prs.title: fix(doctor): await inspection snapshots and native repair phases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can start a synchronous SQLite snapshot from lint, inspection, migration, or a later native repair guard. Large databases then block signal handling and leave expensive images behind. Chrislro’s stack sample in #178359 identified the parent blocked in node::SyncProcessRunner.

## User Impact

The candidate awaits snapshot preparation and repair observations, carries cancellation through worker cleanup, and checks free space when inspection needs a private image. Current admission reads are consumed in the synchronous frame that performs a service, configuration, credential, or database effect, with existing physical ownership and final native checks retained.

Core #190788 already supplies platform boot provenance, cancellation and capacity protection. This PR completes the coupled caller cutover and guards unexpected cold synchronous preparation. Private CURRENT images compare the complete captured family before admission. Unknown provenance still requires the conservative integrity gate. No schema, public configuration, protocol version, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

Assembled head8bd6391d72f4697da9f5378753f8ce6fa9e326b8 includes main714490716002d24b939817366f277872b6ea2825 and the late Reader/Process fixes. Main’s bounded restart recovery and FIFO readiness behavior is preserved; both conflict resolutions received independent source review and exact-file static checks.

Canonical autoreview through P2 passed the individual stages, the complete current-admission candidate (two passes at b7d4b161), and the NOCOW child-join correction. Whole assembled-range review and runtime qualification remain pending. The current source-derived selection contains809 named owner files, all84 standing state-migration files, three agent-admission files and six critical CLI/Doctor flows. Selection is not passing-test evidence.

Remaining work before landing: a valid legacy-v2 quarantine generation can still request a synchronous target fingerprint through an async native-opening path. That owner/caller path is being completed; deliberate public synchronous calls retain visible refusal. Current-head cancellation, capacity guards, repair/upgrade flows, named owners, strict export scans, final integration review and fully green exact-head CI are required before merge.

Prior guard-only CI exposed cold admission failures. Process0f diagnostics locate its first writable restart stall after the config-snapshot callback; they do not prove native restart entered. These failures remain recorded, without inferred repair claims.

Simplification removed the full-file/decoded-row admission cache, moved the unrelated ClawRouter diagnostic outside this PR, and replaced ten intermediate allocation records with one exact2458-LF allocation across130 changed test/support files. Each post-await native phase prepares and consumes fresh owner facts.

Refs #178359, #187900, #185879. Credit @chrislro for the determining stack sample: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639. Not yet released.

releases.name: openclaw 2026.10.10
releases.body:
## 2026.10.10

### Highlights

- Backup safety: secret-redacted Git backups now cover PostgreSQL exports and omit identified bundled-plugin credentials, webhook tokens, and credential blobs while preserving nonsecret plugin state. (#174698, #186953) Thanks @RomneyDa, @art22s, and @jlapenna.
- Codex: the managed native CLI is upgraded to 0.164.0 with matching protocol projection and platform packages. (#181823) Thanks @joshavant and @RomneyDa.
- Node compatibility: installs and updates work again on Node `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`; Node 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 remains the security recommendation, and Node 26 workers no longer abort when stdin is a file. (#186589, #187516) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Gateway streaming: replies containing tool-call XML or long HTML ending at a partial tag no longer stall the Gateway. (#181397, #180765) Thanks @RomneyDa and @JasonBuildAI.
- Delegated work: subagent continuations, restart recovery, inline completion, and paused-parent result custody are substantially more reliable. (#185386, #181373, #184022, #181933, #182587) Thanks @RomneyDa, @SC-10749, @sukhdeepjohar, @Patrick-Erichsen, @BorClaw, and @jalehman.
- Cloud and desktop sessions: local desktop onboarding, repository-aware cloud environments, and moving sessions between local and cloud are now first-class workflows. (#169522, #169512, #169568, #170862, #171690)
- Cron: missed slots with stale stored next-run times are no longer dropped. (#179928) Thanks @andrewbowlds, @RomneyDa, and @shakkernerd.

### Changes

- Control UI: a new architecture, compact navigation rail, native Solid overlays and tabs, wide-chat details, and persistent New conversation access modernize the primary session workspace. (#100024, #168325, #169128, #170707, #170771) Thanks @shakkernerd and @VACInc.
- Mobile nodes: Android adds system, photos, contacts, calendar, and motion capabilities, while iOS gains an authenticated background presence beacon. (#29398, #73330) Thanks @obviyus.
- MCP apps: plugin apps can run across conversations and workspace files through a principal-bound relay. (#161747, #168233)
- Cloud environments: verified Node toolchains, repository recipes, saved profiles, startup progress, repository grouping, and local-to-cloud session moves streamline cloud execution. (#170796, #170862, #170875, #170895, #170892, #171690)
- Database engine: PostgreSQL stores can survive backups and updates, with shared state-engine selection, schema-drift checks, migrations, and an experimental Workboard store. (#170828, #172265, #171962, #169214)
- Local models: managed llama.cpp OCR, vision, and embedding-only setup join automatic first-run inference selection and provider wait-time reporting. (#148193, #170153, #169628, #170369) Thanks @duyufansh2008, @dh-js, and @RomneyDa.
- Plugin runtime control: plugins can fork live context for background side questions, steer active runs, and override model fallbacks per run. (#170146, #170152, #168893) Thanks @obviyus, @dwty11, and @RomneyDa.
- Automations: MCP events can trigger automations, and session hovercards expose attached schedules. (#165399, #172240)
- Desktop onboarding: Windows and Tauri apps can start with local Gateways, while fresh macOS installs enter guided dashboard setup. (#169522, #169512, #169568)
- Secrets UX: secure-entry prompts can reveal values on demand, and setup grants can scope credential egress. (#169925, #170810) Thanks @jacobtomlinson.
- Sessions: sessions can run in existing folders on paired devices and optionally target conversation threads through `sessions_send`. (#169722, #168846) Thanks @obviyus and @VACInc.
- Diagnostics: message and run spans can export prompts and final answers, with GC metrics attributed by kind and worker. (#156603, #171923) Thanks @ryan-dyer-sp.

### Fixes

- Backup security: apply `--exclude-secrets` to PostgreSQL Git exports and redact identified bundled-plugin tokens, OAuth credentials, signing keys, webhook tokens, hosted-media bearer records, and credential blobs. Existing Git history is not rewritten; affected integrations must sign in or register again after restoring a redacted backup. (#174698, #186953) Thanks @RomneyDa, @art22s, and @jlapenna.
- Security boundaries: keep unresolved Teams allowlists restrictive, refuse embedded Control UI auth on pinned Android Gateway connections, audit symlinked workspace skill roots, omit credentials from rejected search endpoints, and reject malformed credential input. (#184989, #180843, #182384, #182534, #167251) Thanks @eleqtrizit, @RomneyDa, @dineshsuthar123, and @Alix-007.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

## WhatsApp connection fails with outdated client (405) due to Neonize version constraint

### Description

WhatsApp connection fails with the following error:

```text
whatsmeow.Client ERROR - Client outdated (405) connect failure
client version: 2.3000.1042386815
```

### Environment
- Nanobot: 0.4.0
- Python: 3.14.8
- Neonize: 0.4.3.post0
- OS: Linux

### Root cause

The WhatsApp manifest at:

`nanobot/channels/whatsapp/manifest.py`

contains the following dependency constraint:

```python
"neonize>=0.4.3.post0,<0.5.0",
```

Additionally, Nanobot automatically reinstalls the optional WhatsApp dependencies on gateway startup, downgrading manually upgraded Neonize versions.

### Workaround

I modified the dependency constraint to:

```python
"neonize>=0.5.2",
```

Then installed Neonize 0.5.2:

```bash
pipx runpip nanobot-ai install --upgrade neonize==0.5.2
```

After this change, WhatsApp connected successfully.

### Expected behavior

Nanobot should allow a compatible, updated Neonize version to be installed and should not automatically downgrade it on every gateway startup.

Please consider updating the Neonize dependency constraint and testing compatibility with newer versions.

### Steps to Reproduce

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Nanobot 0.4.0 using pipx.
2. Enable the WhatsApp channel in the Nanobot configuration.
3. Start the Nanobot gateway.
4. Wait for the WhatsApp connection attempt.
5. Observe the following error:

```text
whatsmeow.Client ERROR - Client outdated (405) connect failure
client version: 2.3000.1042386815
```

6. Check the gateway log and notice that Nanobot automatically installs Neonize with the constraint `neonize>=0.4.3.post0,<0.5.0`.
7. Manually upgrade Neonize to 0.5.2 and update the dependency constraint in `manifest.py`.
8. Restart the gateway.

**Result:** WhatsApp connects successfully after upgrading Neonize to 0.5.2.

### Expected Behavior

### Expected Behavior

Nanobot should use a compatible and up-to-date Neonize version to maintain a successful WhatsApp connection.

issues.title: WhatsApp: missing native libmagic is reported as missing plugin dependencies
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`_load_neonize()` in [`nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/main/nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py#L83-L101) groups `import magic`, Neonize imports, and magic API validation under a single `ImportError` handler. When the Python `magic` wrapper is installed but cannot load the native `libmagic` shared library, the resulting error is:

```
WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp
```

This is misleading because:
1. The WhatsApp plugin dependencies **are** installed — `python-magic` and `neonize` are both present.
2. The actual problem is a missing **native system library** (`libmagic.dylib` / `libmagic.so`), which `nanobot plugins enable whatsapp` does not install.
3. The user has no way to distinguish between missing Python packages, a missing native library, or an incompatible `magic` API from the error message alone.

### Root Cause

The `try/except ImportError` block at [runtime.py:88–101](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/main/nanobot/channels/whatsapp/runtime.py#L88-L101) catches all `ImportError` variants uniformly:

```python
def _load_neonize() -> _NeonizeAPI:
    global _NEONIZE_API
    if _NEONIZE_API is not None:
        return _NEONIZE_API

    try:
        import magic
        from neonize.aioze.client import NewAClient
        from neonize.aioze.events import ConnectedEv, DisconnectedEv, MessageEv, PairStatusEv
        from neonize.utils.jid import build_jid

        detect_mime = getattr(magic, "from_file", None)
        detect_buffer = getattr(magic, "from_buffer", None)
        if not callable(detect_mime) or not callable(detect_buffer):
            raise ImportError("python-magic does not expose from_file/from_buffer")
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp"
        ) from exc
```

When `python-magic` is installed but `libmagic` (the native C library) is not available, `import magic` succeeds but the first call to `magic.from_file()` or `magic.from_buffer()` raises an `ImportError` or `OSError` depending on the `python-magic` version. In some versions, the native-library load happens at import time and raises `ImportError` directly — which is caught by the blanket handler and misreported as missing plugin dependencies.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install nanobot with WhatsApp plugin enabled: `nanobot plugins enable whatsapp`
2. Ensure `python-magic` and `neonize` are installed (`pip show python-magic neonize` both succeed)
3. Remove or make unavailable the native `libmagic` library (e.g., on macOS: `brew uninstall libmagic` or rename `/opt/homebrew/lib/libmagic.dylib`)
4. Start nanobot or trigger any WhatsApp media operation that invokes `_load_neonize()`
5. Observe the error message

## Expected Behavior

The error should distinguish between at least these failure modes with actionable guidance:

| Failure | Expected diagnostic |
|---|---|
| Neonize Python package missing | `"Neonize not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp"` |
| `python-magic` wrapper missing | `"python-magic not installed. Run: pip install python-magic"` |
| Wrapper present, native `libmagic` unavailable | `"Native libmagic library not found. Install it with your system package manager (e.g., brew install libmagic on macOS, apt install libmagic1 on Debian/Ubuntu)"` |
| Incompatible `magic` module (missing `from_file`/`from_buffer`) | `"Installed magic module does not expose the expected API. Ensure python-magic (not python-magic-bin or file-magic) is installed"` |

Each error should preserve the original exception cause via exception chaining (`raise ... from exc`).

## Relevant Logs

```shell
# Simulated reproduction — python-magic installed, libmagic native library absent
$ python -c "import magic; magic.from_file(__file__)"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ImportError: failed to find libmagic.  Check your installation

# Actual nanobot error surfaced to user:
RuntimeError: WhatsApp dependencies not installed. Run: nanobot plugins enable whatsapp
```

## Environment

- **nanobot Version:** 0.4.0
- **Python Version:** 3.13.2
- **Operating System:** macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- **Channel / Platform:** WhatsApp
- **LLM Provider:** (any — issue is in channel dependency initialization, not provider)
- **Model:** N/A

## Additional Context

- The original exception chain is preserved (`from exc`), but the user-facing message does not surface it — users see only the `RuntimeError` text.
- Lazy optional dependency loading should be preserved: importing non-WhatsApp code must not require `libmagic` or `neonize`.
- The fix should not replace byte-level MIME sniffing with `mimetypes` filename guessing, as that is not equivalent for buffers, extensionless files, or files with misleading extensions.
- Existing `_NEONIZE_API` caching behavior should remain intact.
- Setup/troubleshooting docs should be updated to distinguish Python package vs. native system library requirements with platform-specific installation guidance.

issues.title: Linear setup cancellation reports cancelled after authorization has completed
issues.body:
## Bug Description

Linear setup can return cancelled after saving the installation. This happens when cancel waits for poll's completion lock during token exchange, or arrives after a successful poll. The browser shows cancellation while the workspace remains authorized.

I reproduced this through LinearConnectStore.handle with the real LinearClient, mocked HTTP responses, and a temporary SQLite store. The test requires no live Linear account.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an isolated checkout of source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603` with the development and Linear channel dependencies.
2. Copy [the regression test file](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/blob/f3793d791701bf44f75acbdc9a1c30f3c44a0855/nanobot/channels/linear/tests/test_connect_cancel.py) to `nanobot/channels/linear/tests/test_connect_cancel.py`, keeping `nanobot/channels/linear/connect.py` unchanged.
3. Run the two result-replay cases:

```text
python -m pytest nanobot/channels/linear/tests/test_connect_cancel.py -k replays_completed -q
```

The fixture starts setup and completes the OAuth callback. It pauses token exchange during poll, optionally queues cancel behind the completion lock, then allows exchange to finish. It compares the results and checks the saved installation.

Both result-replay cases fail on this upstream revision and pass with the candidate fix.

## Expected Behavior

While the setup result is retained, cancel should return success if authorization has completed. Pending authorization should still cancel normally. Expiry and shutdown should clear the setup cache. Disconnecting an installed workspace remains a separate operation.

## Relevant Logs

The test observes:

```text
poll.status:             succeeded
cancel.status:           cancelled
installation persisted: true
```

Poll and cancel should return the same success payload while the setup session is retained.

## Environment

- nanobot version: source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603`.
- Python: 3.12.13.
- Operating system: Windows.
- Channel / platform: Linear connection setup used by WebUI.
- LLM provider / model: not involved.
- Browser / connection: backend reproduction; no real browser or OAuth account used.

## Additional Context

A [candidate fix is available in my fork](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/commit/f3793d791701bf44f75acbdc9a1c30f3c44a0855). It is one commit on the upstream revision above and changes two files. It reuses the completion lock to return a copy of the cached success result and keeps lifecycle cleanup separate. The Linear suite passed 145 cases, including six new regressions, and 64 related WebUI settings tests passed. Changed-file Ruff and BasedPyright checks passed.

Please advise how you would prefer to incorporate the fix under the current contribution policy.

issues.title: Required Codex compaction can fall through to generation during image retry
issues.body:
## Bug Description

If required Codex compaction fails on a request containing images, the image-removal retry clears native conversation state and rebuilds ProviderCallContext without compaction_input_budget. It then sends an ordinary generation request before compaction has succeeded.

I reproduced this through both public retry APIs, streaming and non-streaming, with a simulated HTTP 400 unsupported_value error. The reproduction uses mocked transport calls.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an isolated checkout of source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603` with the repository's development dependencies.
2. Copy [the regression test file](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/blob/5e04de932d9ea3ac209c2f1f7e967bc6ee27b695/tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py) to `tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py`, keeping `nanobot/providers/base.py` unchanged.
3. Run:

```text
python -m pytest tests/providers/test_openai_codex_provider.py -k image_retry_cannot_bypass_required_compaction -q
```

The fixture creates resumable Responses state with a pending image message and a compaction_input_budget. It rejects the first transport call and records the submission types. The required-budget cases cover both entry points.

On this upstream revision, the two required-budget cases fail and the two optional-budget controls pass. All four pass with the candidate fix.

## Expected Behavior

Return the compaction failure with its provider-state recovery signal. Image repair should respect the required budget and continue working for calls without that requirement.

## Relevant Logs

The test records:

```text
Required budget, current affected behavior: ["compaction", "generation"]
Required budget, expected behavior:         ["compaction"]
No required budget, compatibility control:  ["generation", "generation"]
```

## Environment

- nanobot version: source revision `384b7638307e5c9279286df78ace5759311ea603`.
- Python: 3.12.13.
- Operating system: Windows.
- Channel / platform: provider retry API; not channel-specific.
- LLM provider: openai_codex.
- Model: gpt-5.6-sol in the fixture; HTTP requests are mocked.
- Browser / connection: not applicable to this reproduction.

## Additional Context

The field is lost in LLMProvider._retry_without_images in `nanobot/providers/base.py`. A [candidate fix is available in my fork](https://github.com/KDB-Wind/nanobot/commit/5e04de932d9ea3ac209c2f1f7e967bc6ee27b695). It is one commit on the upstream revision above and changes two files. Related provider retry, Codex, and runner fallback tests passed: 200, including the four regression cases. Changed-file Ruff and BasedPyright checks passed.

Please advise how you would prefer to incorporate the fix under the current contribution policy.

issues.title: [Bug] strip_think removes literal think-tag examples inside fenced code blocks
issues.body:
### Bug Description

`strip_think()` removes complete `<think>...</think>` pairs even when they are literal XML examples inside a Markdown fenced code block. This changes the code example, rather than only removing model reasoning.

Related: #3004 addressed truncation caused by an **unclosed** tag appearing mid-message. This report covers a **closed pair inside a fenced code block**, which still reproduces on the source commit below. The first complete-block substitution in `strip_think()` matches the pair without checking Markdown context.

### Steps to Reproduce

Checked source: `8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9`.

From an environment with nanobot dependencies installed, import the helper from that checkout and run:

```python
from nanobot.utils.helpers import strip_think

text = "Example XML:\n```xml\n<think>keep this literal example</think>\n```"
print(repr(strip_think(text)))
assert strip_think(text) == text
```

I executed this against the cloned source, with the checkout placed first on `sys.path`.

### Expected Behavior

The fenced XML example remains intact, including `keep this literal example`. Actual reasoning blocks outside user-visible examples should continue to be handled normally.

### Actual Behavior

The helper returns:

```text
'Example XML:\n```xml\n\n```'
```

The assertion fails because the entire literal tag pair and its contents are deleted.

### Logs / Error Messages

```text
literal_preserved = False
```

### nanobot Version

Source checkout at `8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9`; `pyproject.toml` version: `0.4.0`.

### Python Version

3.12.13

### Operating System

Windows, PowerShell 7.6.5

### Channel / Platform

Helper-level local Python reproduction. The same helper is referenced by message delivery and memory code; an end-to-end chat session was not tested.

### LLM Provider / Model

Not applicable: no provider request or credentials are needed for this reproduction.

### Additional Context

Source: https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9/nanobot/utils/helpers.py#L170

A regression test covering fenced literal tags would help distinguish this case from actual reasoning removal. This report was prepared with an automated assistant; the production helper import and reproduction were executed locally.

prs.title: refactor(goal): isolate sustained-goal continuation policy
prs.body:
## Summary

Contributes to NAN-392.

Move sustained Goal authorization and continuation decisions behind a narrow execution-policy boundary, and assemble the built-in feature consistently for the Gateway, CLI, and SDK. The core retains input consumption, model/tool execution, iteration budgets, queue admission, persistence, delivery, and Stop.

## Mechanisms replaced

- Replace separate finalization, budget-output, and next-turn eligibility checks with one boundary decision. Input draining now handles real input only; it no longer selects continuation actions or communicates budget state through drain flags and tuple fields.
- Replace the command-to-runner `turn_scopes` chain with the execution scope's actual-consumption notification for initial and injected input. Remove the obsolete fields, arguments, and scope-entry path.
- Replace the queued message's encoded ticket and the separate TurnContext request/receipt plus mutable delivery pending flag with one `ContinuationHandoff`, shared by the inbox and delivery. Save failure, Stop, and rejected admission use the same withdrawal operation; pending status is derived from that owner.
- Use one committed snapshot for continuation admission: core checks generation and the Goal policy checks goal identity and rounds without another store read. Transaction-time and post-queue checks remain because they guard different time boundaries.
- Centralize terminal lifecycle publication in delivery and drain accepted publication on cancellation. Remove the loop's separate completion flag and outer cancellation path; cancellation while waiting for recovery admission or capacity still settles the dequeued handoff.

The existing turn scheduler, FIFO positions, iteration limit and 12-continuation allowance, generation guards, checkpoint/recovery behavior, and Stop semantics are retained. This does not introduce a new run/slice scheduler, alter NAN-129's tool-exposure/no-active-goal behavior, or change the UI protocol. Goal WebSocket formatting remains in the presentation adapter.

The follow-up from `25ad9b62` removes 327 production lines and adds 282, including the handoff owner. This count is supplementary; the replacements above define the architectural outcome.

## Verification

Current verified source: `160b5d439a47665229cdb9f774776287373be500`.

- 366 focused regressions passed on Windows/Python 3.13.7 across input priority, Goal state/authorization, runner behavior, queued continuation admission, cancellation, delivery, and recovery.
- Two real isolated Gateway/WebSocket scenarios passed with a synthetic local model: multi-turn continuation, and Stop while the handoff save is pending followed by an independent input. These are not browser tests.
- Deterministic regressions reproduced and then fixed cancellation during recovery admission, failed continuation admission reads, and cancellation during publication of an interrupted completion. Existing rollback-error and queue cleanup assertions remain intact.
- Touched-file Ruff, focused strict Basedpyright, Python import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full remote CI for the new head is pending. Earlier-head CI is not counted as validation of this follow-up.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): update Neonize for current clients
prs.body:
## Why

WhatsApp can reject the older client bundled with Neonize 0.4.3.post0 as outdated. The current `<0.5.0` constraint also causes gateway startup to replace a manually installed newer version with an older version. The reporter confirmed that 0.5.2 connected in their environment.

## What changed

- Require `neonize>=0.5.2,<1.0.0`, allowing the current 0.10.0 release as well as 0.5.2.
- Cover old-version upgrades and preservation of compatible versions, including 0.10.0, in the startup dependency check.
- Credit @edualbercas for the report and verified workaround.

## Tradeoffs

The broader range allows later 0.x releases without requiring a nanobot update, but future Neonize API changes could still require compatibility work. The 1.0 boundary remains excluded. Neonize 0.5.2 and 0.10.0 publish platform-specific wheels rather than a universal wheel.

## Blast Radius

Enabled WhatsApp channels with an older Neonize installation will install a supported newer dependency at startup. An already compatible installation is left unchanged; it is not automatically upgraded to the latest version. Other channels are unchanged.

## Verification

- Windows, Python 3.14, Neonize 0.10.0: `python -m pytest nanobot/channels/whatsapp/tests/test_whatsapp_channel.py::test_startup_preserves_compatible_neonize tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_optional_dependency_metadata_for_enable tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_manager_installs_manifest_dependencies_before_loading_enabled_channel tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py::test_manager_reports_dependency_install_failure_as_runtime_failure -q` — 6 passed. The 0.10.0 startup regression case failed against the earlier `<0.6.0` bound before this update.
- On an earlier PR snapshot, 54 focused tests passed with Neonize 0.10.0, including the SDK-internal callback test since removed. The actual SDK loaded, its call signatures accepted the adapter's usage, and synthetic QR and connected events reached the registered handlers. These were isolated compatibility checks, not a real WhatsApp login. `uv pip check` passed for the test environment.
- Earlier on the initial PR snapshot, the focused suite passed 53 cases with Neonize 0.5.2.
- An isolated, unauthenticated connection attempt with 0.5.2 could not reach `web.whatsapp.com` from this machine and timed out before a QR code. Real account pairing, existing-session reconnection, message/media delivery, and proxy behavior remain to be verified; the reporter's successful connection is not an independent test here.
- Full cross-platform verification is delegated to CI.

Fixes #6544
