prs.title: fix(providers): keep parallel tool calls apart when the stream omits index
prs.body:
Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API streams parallel tool calls without `tool_calls[].index`: each call arrives whole (id, name and arguments) in its own chunk, and the turn ends with `finish_reason: "stop"`. `_parse_chunks` falls back to the call's position inside its chunk when `index` is missing. That's 0 for every one of these chunks, so all the calls of a turn land in one buffer: the id and name of the last call win, and the arguments are concatenated.

Replaying a captured `gemini-3.5-flash` stream with two parallel `get_weather` calls through the `openai` client and `_parse_chunks`:

```
before: call_4234487 get_weather '{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"Tokyo"}'
after:  call_4234484 get_weather {'city': 'Paris'}
        call_4234487 get_weather {'city': 'Tokyo'}
```

### Change

A delta without `index` now starts a new call when it carries an id different from the current call's id, or a name on an id-less call that already has one. Anything else is appended to the current call, so providers that stream unindexed argument fragments keep working. Deltas that do carry `index` are handled as before.

### Tests

- `test_parse_chunks_keeps_parallel_calls_without_index_apart`: the two-call Gemini shape from the capture (thought signature shortened). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `test_parse_chunks_appends_unindexed_fragments_to_the_last_call`: id-less argument fragments still join the current call.
- `tests/providers` plus `tests/agent/test_gemini_thought_signature.py`: 1464 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/`: clean.

This change was made with Claude Code; the tests above were run on the branch to check it.

`MCPToolWrapper._render_call_result` handles text and image blocks and passes every other content block through `str(block)`. MCP tools also return embedded resources, resource links and audio. For those the model sees pydantic reprs, for example:

```
type='resource' resource=TextResourceContents(uri=AnyUrl('repo://octo/demo/README.md'), mimeType='text/markdown', meta=None, text="# Demo\n\nIt's a readme.") annotations=None meta=None
```

github/github-mcp-server's `get_file_contents` returns file bodies this way (an `EmbeddedResource` next to a short text message, or a `ResourceLink` for files of 1 MB or more). For a binary file or an audio block the repr includes the whole base64 payload, which goes straight into the tool result and the context. The docstring of `_render_call_result` already says base64 must not be forwarded for images; the sibling `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` renders the same resource types as their text or `[Binary resource: N bytes]`.

## Fix

In `_render_call_result`:

- `EmbeddedResource` with text contents renders as its text; with blob contents as `[Binary resource: N bytes]`, the wording `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` uses.
- `AudioContent` renders as `[Audio content: N bytes]`.
- `ResourceLink` renders as `[MCP Resource] <description or name>` plus its URI, the format `MCPResourceWrapper` uses for its tool description.

Image handling is unchanged, including image blobs inside an `EmbeddedResource`, which still become artifacts. A `ResourceLink` is rendered without its `mimeType` and `size`. As in `MCPResourceWrapper`, `N` is the length of the base64 string.

## Tests

- New `test_execute_renders_resource_blocks_as_text` and `test_execute_keeps_binary_payloads_out_of_result`, built from real `mcp.types` objects. On main both fail with the reprs above (the second shows `blob='JVBERi0xLjcK'` in the result); with the fix they pass. The fake `mcp.types` fixture gains the three real types the renderer now checks.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py`: 117 passed. `tests/tools/`: 1171 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `mcp.py`.

Not changed: `MCPPromptWrapper.execute` has the same `str()` fallback for prompt messages; that can be a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(runtime): preserve recovery history and prevent unsafe MCP replays
prs.body:
## Why

Interrupted turns can lose earlier completed tool rounds or persist the same recovery batch twice. Separately, an MCP connection loss can replay an operation whose outcome is unknown, resource/prompt errors can be recorded as successes, and a crashed gateway can exit successfully after cleanup. This PR addresses all four issues together.

Resolves NAN-183
Resolves NAN-393
Resolves NAN-394
Resolves NAN-395

## What changed

| Issue | Change and focused acceptance coverage |
| --- | --- |
| [NAN-183](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-183) | Every checkpoint retains the complete preceding turn delta, projected through the existing persistence rules. Recovery restores completed rounds and atomically acknowledges consumed follow-ups. New-input admission rereads committed state after the real cancellation handoff. Tests cover A completed/B interrupted, later completed and final-response checkpoints, normal completion without duplicates, Stop versus shutdown/reopened SQLite, Continue, and new input cancelling active recovery. Pending tool results explicitly report an unknown outcome. Existing temporary-session, generation, transaction and Dismiss tests remain passing. |
| [NAN-393](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-393) | Separate connection recovery before submission from replay after submission. Unknown/non-idempotent calls return a structured unknown-outcome warning after transport loss without resubmission. Explicit read-only/idempotent declarations permit the existing bounded retry policy; resource/prompt reads retain their policy. Tests perform the fake side effect before losing the response and cover later independent requests, safe recovery, cancellation, timeout, rendering and privacy. |
| [NAN-394](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-394) | Ordinary startup and runtime exceptions both exit 1 after the existing cleanup. Real isolated Windows CLI subprocesses verify a runtime-task exception after healthy startup, diagnostics, cleanup, released claims/ports, and normal stop returning 0. Separate isolated startup-failure and background restart/stop probes also passed. No supervisor policy changes. |
| [NAN-395](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-395) | Resource/prompt wrappers return `ToolResult.error` unchanged. Production registry, executor and Runner tests verify error events/hooks, exclusion from successful `tools_used`, and preservation of valid successful text beginning with `Error`. |

### Independent-review follow-up

- Reconnect now adopts the rediscovered replay declaration as well as the session. Each request attempt binds both together. If an already-started operation reconnects to a definition that is no longer explicitly safe, it stops before submitting to that replacement; later independent calls also use the updated contract.
- Cumulative checkpoints are uncommitted deltas, and committing them clears the checkpoint in the same transaction. Their recovery no longer infers prior submission from equal text. Legacy single-batch overlap handling remains supported. The interrupted Runner/SQLite test now checks distinct input IDs with identical content/timestamps and the follow-up journal after reopening storage.
- Updated the MCP privacy/proxy test fixtures exposed by the old CI run: connection-failure tests fail the pre-submit ping, while retry tests explicitly declare their genuinely read-only operations. Original privacy, proxy routing and submission-count assertions are retained or strengthened; no production configuration, timeout or fallback changes were used to conceal failures.

## Scope

One PR targeting `main`, based on `8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9`. This PR delivers the final fixes for the four linked issues. It does not change or revive #4650, extend other historical issues, or change production instances. Independent code review found no remaining blockers on the current head. The platform/end-to-end acceptance gaps below remain open; no formal GitHub approval has been submitted.

## Tradeoffs

With reconnect enabled, a non-replayable MCP tool uses one pre-submit ping. That adds a round trip within the existing per-attempt timeout, without increasing retries or timeout limits. Safe-replay annotations are server declarations, not client-enforced deduplication. Recovery checkpoints retain the unfinished turn's full delta rather than incrementally committing transcript rows; checkpoint size therefore grows with that unfinished turn.

## Verification

- Current head `20b62f4225a76fbd78cb82b1a632406a2ec865bf`: **286 targeted MCP/runtime/privacy/proxy tests passed in 3.37s**, with changed-file Ruff, MCP strict type checking and diff checks passing. The preceding head `35438b3e2` passed 510 targeted checks and its full remote CI. Its recovery/gateway implementation is unchanged by this final timeout clarification.
- The two review regressions were reproduced on the previous head: **3 failed / 2 passed**, then **5 passed** after correction (also included in the 510 current-head checks). The safe-to-unknown/unsafe cases now stop before the fresh call, and equal-text interrupted follow-ups retain all input IDs and are acknowledged only with the restored history.
- Changed-file Ruff and `git diff --check`: passed. Python import boundaries: passed, 13 rules / 216 files. Targeted strict checks on `mcp.py` and `session/recovery.py`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Earlier baseline comparisons reproduced lost A/history, duplicate C after real AgentLoop cancellation, duplicate simulated MCP submissions, lost resource/prompt error markers, and the real gateway subprocess incorrectly exiting 0 after a runtime exception.
- Retained Windows CLI evidence on `98f0c0b0`: runtime crash **exit 1**, explicit stop **exit 0**, with actual cleanup and released claims/ports. Earlier isolated startup **exit 1** and controlled background restart/stop **exit 0** evidence is also retained. The gateway lifecycle code is unchanged; these probes used no configured MCP server or pending recovery session. They were not rerun for this follow-up.
- Previous-head CI [41399422222](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41399422222): Python 3.11 failed **7 tests / 11190 passed / 80 skipped** at merge checkout `2ed530ee047ca30efdef18f8f0d47469c3184a4d` (head `98f0c0b0`, base `8b37976d3`). The seven failures were in the MCP fixtures updated above; the corresponding local files now pass all 44 cases. The old run is not a validation pass.
- Current-head CI [41413127473](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41413127473) **completed successfully: all 15 jobs passed**, including Windows, browser, native acceptance and CI required. The tested merge checkout `f16660b7ecb07b93fb5cd94cd1ca9c535ce0e715` has exactly base `8b37976d3` and current head `20b62f422` as its parents. This is current-head CI, not inherited results from [41401598874](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41401598874).
- Independent incremental review of the current head found no new code blockers. Its separate preflight/submitted timeout and real-cancellation probes confirmed zero preflight submissions, one submitted effect with structured unknown outcome on timeout, and cancellation propagation without replay. This was a code-review result, not a formal GitHub approval or completion of all issue acceptance.

### Live Codex follow-up

Used the production Codex provider with `openai-codex/gpt-6-luna` (`reasoning_effort=max`) through the existing HTTP proxy, with existing OAuth loaded read-only and TLS verification enabled. Only synthetic inputs were sent. Production AgentLoop/Runner, RecoveryCoordinator, SessionState/SQLite, MCPProvider and MCP SDK were exercised against a task-owned real HTTP JSON-RPC service; its external effects were only synthetic local records.

- Separate runtime processes interrupted and restored a real two-round prepare/submit task, then Continue used a read-only status check. The original prepared ticket and exactly one submitted record were retained.
- New input cancelled an active recovery/status request; its replacement answer completed, with unique assistant/tool IDs and no repeated submission.
- Stop retained identical-text inputs with separate IDs. Continuing the existing job reported the prepared ticket and one committed submission. Some runs encountered actual Codex connection failures and were completed through the product's Continue path, not by replaying side effects.
- An MCP tool rediscovered without its prior idempotent declaration was not called again for the original operation. A separate new operation committed once, lost its actual HTTP response, and produced an unknown-outcome error; Luna answered `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` without resubmitting.
- Actual resource/prompt MCP errors reached error hooks/events, neither appeared in successful `tools_used`, and Luna correctly described both failures.

This exposed one additional gap: the MCP SDK can surface an aborted post-commit HTTP response as a timeout. The final commit reports an unknown outcome for a timed-out **already-started non-replayable call**, while pre-submit timeouts retain their existing meaning. Neither timeout retries nor budgets changed. Its focused regression failed 1 of 4 cases before the fix; all cases pass afterward.

### Remaining acceptance

**Actual macOS launchd failure/restart behavior is unverified** because this host is Windows. The live Codex runs used isolated runtime process restarts and real local HTTP MCP with synthetic effects, not a browser/full-gateway restart flow or third-party business service. Intermittent proxy/Codex ConnectErrors, a WebSocket teardown callback error, and SDK late-response ClosedResourceError diagnostics were retained; no broader connection-stability claim is made. No proxy settings, shared instances, credentials or TLS verification were changed. Current-head code review has no remaining blockers and configured CI has passed. The unverified scenarios above remain disclosed verification limits. The PR remains Draft.

prs.title: fix(webui): avoid remounting outgoing conversations
prs.body:
## Why

Switching away from a conversation with file diffs can block the main thread by rebuilding the conversation being left. The session-keyed results wrapper introduced in #6443 remounts `ThreadMessages` before the stream hook hands over its messages, so the outgoing diff DOM and synchronous layout measurements run again.

## What changed

- Retain the outgoing transcript until its messages actually hand over. Derive `messagesKey` from the stream's existing message scope and key only the transcript subtree on that owner, leaving the viewport/composer and selection-time scroll behavior intact.
- Reset all transcript-local state on real ownership changes, including activity overrides, message menus and nested disclosures. Keep the independent session-owned subtask disclosure reset.
- Cover outgoing diff reinsertion, cached A → fork → A isolation with shared turn IDs, direct subtask disclosure resets and the history-only consumer.

## Scope

This fixes redundant work when leaving a conversation. It does not change history loading, cache/replay policy, transport contracts, diff highlighting, or offscreen rendering.

## Verification

- The original baseline fails outgoing-node identity and diff reinsertion checks. The initial PR revision also reproduced an activity disclosure leaking into a cached fork with shared history IDs; that regression now passes alongside the original performance regression.
- Focused unit suites for viewport, subtask disclosures, stream/history hooks and temporary-chat navigation: **259 passed**.
- History browser verification: **10 passed**, covering outgoing diff retention, cached fork state reset, live/history reconciliation, desktop/mobile pagination and canceling an in-progress history pull.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Full-project validation is delegated to remote CI.

### Controlled performance comparison

Production-built real `ThreadShell`, synthetic HTTP/WebSocket data, Windows Chrome 156 headless, 1440 × 800, no CPU throttling. Heavy conversation: 20 file diffs × 120 lines (about 68,000 live DOM nodes); target: a short conversation. Three interleaved batches per build, one warm-up round trip excluded per batch, **12 measured switches per direction per build**. No other task-owned test/build ran during the reported comparison.

| Heavy → short | Baseline | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Click interaction median | 772 ms | 248 ms |
| Click interaction range | 688–848 ms | 224–328 ms |
| Processing median | 692 ms | 206 ms |
| Outgoing diffs reinserted per switch | 20 | 0 |

The median click interaction fell by **68%** in this workload. Rendering an incoming heavy conversation remains expensive: automation-observed content-ready medians were 1.401 s / 1.528 s, with maxima 1.714 s / 1.767 s (baseline / fix). That incoming-content median was about 9% higher in these runs; the PR does not claim parity for heavy entry or that every switch is below 200 ms. These numbers were remeasured after the ownership-isolation fix. The original private recording is not included.

Resolves NAN-396

prs.title: fix(agent): skip _streamed flag for tool_error and empty_final_respon…
prs.body:
When a tool fails with fatal_error (e.g. safety guard blocks a command), the runner sets stop_reason="tool_error" and returns error content. However, _process_message still sets _streamed=True on the OutboundMessage because "tool_error" was not in the exclusion set. The consumer then discards the error content via the _streamed continue path, making the error invisible to the user.

Similarly, when the LLM returns only thinking tags and no visible content, strip_think filters everything, zero _stream_delta messages are emitted, but stop_reason="empty_final_response" still gets _streamed=True, causing the empty-but-valid response to be silently dropped.

This extends the existing exclusion set (which already covers "ask_user" and "error") to also cover "tool_error" and "empty_final_response" — these stop reasons indicate content was NOT actually streamed to the user, so the consumer must process them through the normal display path.

issues.title: `__release_date__` is a hardcoded constant: v0.22.5 (published 2026-10-23) displays 2026.9.24
issues.body:
Since the version line moved from CalVer to semver (`scripts/releases/versioning.py` seeds at `SEED = "0.21.5"`), releases bump the version but nothing updates `hermes_cli/__init__.py:5`, which still holds the literal written by the `chore: release v0.21.5 (2026.9.24)` commit:

```python
__release_date__ = "2026.9.24"
```

## Actual behavior

```
$ hermes --version
Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24) · stable · local bf0203a794a0
```

But `v0.22.5` was published 2026-10-23 (release `published_at: 2026-10-23T05:28:45Z`, tag `v0.22.5` created `2026-10-23 05:28:40 +0000`, tag commit dated Thu Oct 22 18:43:45 2026 -0700). The displayed date is ~4 weeks stale and does not match the release it labels.

## Expected behavior

The date shown next to the version should be the release date of that version.

## Why it propagates

Every consumer imports the same constant, so one stale literal reaches all surfaces:

- `hermes_cli/banner.py:70,226` — TUI welcome banner
- `hermes_cli/cli_render.py:926,929` — CLI render
- `hermes_cli/_startup_fast.py:200,203` — `hermes --version`
- `agent/legacy_cli.py:30,36` — legacy `--version`
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:27,525` — status API `release_date`
- `tui_gateway/server.py:1615,1618` and `gateway/session_local_inventory.py:179,181` — session info `release_date`

No logic depends on the value (display-only), so nothing fails loudly — it just reports the wrong date indefinitely.

## Suggested fix

Derive it at release time rather than hand-maintaining a literal: the `chore: release vX.Y.Z (...)` commit and the release pipeline already know the tag date, so stamp `__release_date__` from the tag/commit in the same step that bumps `__version__`. A minimal fallback would be to add a CI check that fails when `__release_date__` disagrees with the tagged release date, so the next semver bump cannot silently drift again.

## Environment

- Version: v0.22.5, install method `git`, commit `bf0203a794a0`
- Python 3.14.9, Linux (WSL)

Local workaround applied (will be swept by the updater's autostash on the next `hermes update`, hence reporting upstream): set `__release_date__ = "2026.10.23"`.

issues.title: doctor flags Hermes's own package-manager cache (~/.hermes/cache/uv) as unpruned task files and tells users to delete it

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### What happens

On any install where Hermes's package manager has run, `hermes doctor` raises a warning telling the user to move or delete Hermes's **own** package-manager cache:

```
⚠ ~/.hermes/cache/uv/ is 1.4 GB and outside every pruner (only cache/scratch/ and cache/terminal/ are reaped) — move task files under cache/scratch/<task>/ or delete it
```

That directory is not task residue. It is the package manager's uv cache, created and managed by `pm/packages.py::uv_cache_dir()` → `get_default_hermes_root() / "cache" / "uv"`. Following the advice is harmful:

- **Deleting it** just forces full re-downloads on the next install/`uv sync`.
- **Moving it under `cache/scratch/<task>/`** breaks the warm-cache path — the `uv_cache_dir()` docstring says the seeded machine cache is what makes `uv sync --offline` near-free after updates (probed 0.4 s warm vs 1.2 s cold), and the scratch pruner reaps entries after 24 h idle, so a parked cache there would get deleted anyway.

Since the cache is only ever pruned by uv itself and grows with normal use, every active machine above the 1 GB threshold gets a **permanent false warning** on every `hermes doctor` run, plus the same entry in `hermes doctor --fix` flows.

### Root cause

`unpruned_cache_hogs()` in `hermes_cli/doctor_state.py` exempts only:

```python
_PRUNED_CACHE_DIRS = frozenset({"scratch", "terminal"})
```

`cache/uv` is a permanent, self-managed dependency cache, so it can never satisfy the warning's own advice ("move it into the pruned dirs or delete it").

### Repro

1. Install Hermes and let the package manager run once (any plugin install / update seeds it).
2. Let `~/.hermes/cache/uv` exceed 1 GB (happens with normal use).
3. `hermes doctor` → the warning above.

Observed on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, checkout at `7cadfaa` (current `main`), uv cache at 1.4 GB.

### Suggested fix

Exclude the package manager's own cache from `unpruned_cache_hogs()` — ideally by importing `uv_cache_dir()` from `pm.packages` and skipping that resolved path (name-matching `"uv"` in `_PRUNED_CACHE_DIRS` also works but silently re-breaks if the PM cache location moves). Alternatively, report it as an `✓`/info line ("package-manager cache, self-pruned by uv") instead of a warning.

issues.title: [Bug] Provider name collisions make endpoint selection order-dependent and mix built-in/custom credential identities
issues.body:
## Summary

Upstream follow-up to the already-public provider credential-mixing report in [hermes-webui#8690](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/8690). [WebUI PR #8775](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/8775) refuses ambiguous provider names in its guarded paths; it does not repair the Agent resolver used by the CLI and gateway.

Two records can claim the same selector: a built-in `providers.<builtin>` row and a named `providers['custom:<builtin>']` row. Endpoint selection is order-dependent, while credential selection can identify a different row. The public report records the resulting pair as **the named record's URL plus the built-in record's key**, including when the two records have different credentials.

This concerns operator-configured providers, not a claim that an unauthenticated caller can edit the configuration. No real credentials, deployment URLs or new exploit payloads are included here.

## Root cause

Current-source inspection at Agent main `d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359`:

- `hermes_cli.runtime_provider._select_named_custom_provider` is now implemented in [`runtime_provider_custom.py:232–257`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359/hermes_cli/runtime_provider_custom.py#L232-L257). Its [`_match_new_style_provider`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359/hermes_cli/runtime_provider_custom.py#L148-L180) iterates `providers.items()` and returns the first matching entry. [`custom_provider_aliases`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359/hermes_cli/providers.py#L523-L536) lets the built-in and `custom:<builtin>` records claim overlapping names.
- The `custom:<builtin>` pool is seeded through [`_get_custom_provider_config`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359/agent/credential_pool.py#L551-L556), which removes `custom:` and selects the entry named `<builtin>`. [`_seed_custom_pool`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d7572ceda754b888216c212691e1b2301ebe0359/agent/credential_pool.py#L2929-L2943) then seeds that row's credential. In the reported `openai` case, the built-in row owns `custom:openai`; the named `custom:openai` row's separate legacy pool is `custom:custom:openai`.
- The existing entry-scoped pool filter returns `custom:`-prefixed pools unchanged, so its presence alone is not proof that these two record identities are separated.

The real-Agent, socket-blocked reproduction and version observations are in the linked WebUI report and mitigation PR. This filing rechecks current source; it does not claim a new end-to-end execution against the pinned main commit.

## Expected behavior / fix direction

Resolve the selected record once, and keep its endpoint, credential source and pool identity together. Bare built-in and explicit `custom:<builtin>` selectors must either resolve unambiguously to their own record or fail closed before client construction. Reordering the mapping must not change the result. Sorting the records or adding a warning alone would not repair the identity collision.

Give the built-in row and named custom row distinct credential identities, including when loading existing pools. Do not silently reuse a foreign row's credential during legacy-pool migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test both record orders with distinct synthetic endpoints and keys, for bare built-in and explicit `custom:<builtin>` selection.
- [ ] Assert the final URL/key/pool tuple, not just the selected provider string; reject an ambiguous request before any network call.
- [ ] Cover config-seeded and already-populated pools, with and without ambient built-in credentials.
- [ ] Exercise CLI and gateway resolution, and expose the same identity guarantee to auxiliary clients and URL-bearing model aliases.
- [ ] Use isolated configuration/auth stores, synthetic credentials and blocked outbound sockets in regression tests.

Related but different: #9315 concerns same-URL custom entries overriding an explicit key; PR #43178 adds built-in-shadowing diagnostics. This issue is the overlapping selector plus pool-record identity case described above.

issues.title: Feature: agent-loop hook for guarded decision reuse (skip already-decided model callbacks)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Feature: agent-loop hook for guarded decision reuse (skip already-decided model callbacks)

### Summary

Request an **optional hook in the agent loop** that lets a plugin (1) observe every tool receipt and (2), when a declared guard is satisfied by *observed* state, pre-fill the next tool call and **skip the model call entirely** — executing through the normal tool path and minting an auditable certificate.

This is the mechanism from [HarnessMM (arXiv:2610.32813)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813) ("Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency", THU + MSRA). The paper has no official code; I built an independent implementation in my own Rust harness and measured it. Filing here because **the current plugin API cannot express this** — this issue documents the gap and the measured upside.

### Why the current plugin API can't do it

`register_tool` and friends let a plugin *add* things for the model to call. But decision reuse needs the opposite: *subtract* a model call after observing a tool receipt. That requires a hook at exactly one place in the loop:

```
tool results arrive → [HOOK: receipts observed; if guard hit → execute
stored literal action via normal tool path, skip model call] → next model call
```

A plugin doing only the authoring half (a `declare_edg`-style tool) without the substitution half actually **loses money** — the model pays tokens to declare actions that are then never reused (see measurements below, round 1).

### What I measured (independent implementation, 2 A/B rounds)

Setup: my own Rust agent harness, Qwen3.8-27B local, 4 mini coding tasks (write module → run test → report), arms differ only in instruction + runtime switch. Physical model calls and provider-reported tokens from usage stats; substitutions counted by an append-only certificate ledger.

| Round | Arm | Success | Model calls | Total tokens | Certified substitutions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | off | 4/4 | 19 | 25.5k | 0 |
| 1 | on (tool-authored) | 4/4 | 15 (-21%) | 28.1k (**+10%**) | 4 |
| 2 | off | 4/4 | 21 | 136.3k | 0 |
| 2 | on (tool-authored) | 4/4 | 11 (-48%) | 75.5k (**-45%**) | 5 |
| 2 | on (inline block) | 4/4 | 12 | 80.0k (-41%) | 0 |

Three honest findings:

1. **Round 1 reproduces the paper's substitution paradox** (their App. D.8): authoring tax > callbacks saved on short tasks. The mechanism alone is not free money.
2. **Round 2's -45% is mostly a *behavioral* effect** of the authoring instruction ("only declare actions you have already fully decided"), which halved exploratory tool calls (21 → 11). Only 5 of the ~10 avoided calls were mechanical substitutions. This mirrors the paper's own clean ablation (GDR alone: 26.91%) vs its headline 87.93% (mechanism + context compression + tuning stacked).
3. Inline declaration via a fenced text block conflicts with streaming tool-call assembly (0 substitutions) — if pursued, it needs a structured side-channel.

So the realistic value proposition for Hermes is twofold: (a) a cheap **prompt-level** win that needs no hook at all ("plan fully before acting" instructions), and (b) a **mechanism-level** win for callback-heavy workloads (long review-fix loops, benchmark/delegation rounds) that does need this hook.

### Proposed API sketch (deliberately minimal)

```python
def register_loop_observer(self, observer) -> None:
    ...
```

An observer receives `(tool_name, ok, output)` after every tool execution (cheap, always-on — receipts are facts), and may return a `PrefilledCall(tool, args)` that the loop executes through the **same registry and approval gate as a model-issued call**, then synthesizes the assistant tool_call/tool_result pair so provider message-pairing stays intact. Every skip increments a counter surfaced in run stats (`certified_bypasses`), so token-savings claims stay auditable against physical call counts.

Safety properties worth keeping from the paper (I implemented and tested these):

- **Literal closure** — declared action args must be concrete JSON (no `${...}` placeholders) at declaration time; otherwise you'd be certifying a guess, not a decision.
- **Observation-only guards** — guards read receipts/filesystem state, never model output; unknown guard → defer to the model (failure is bounded: one extra call).
- **Substituted actions go through the same approval gate** — a substitution skips the *model*, never the *safety*.

### Alternatives considered

- **Prompt-only**: gets the behavioral win (the larger effect) with zero code, but no mechanical substitution for callback-heavy loops. Worth doing regardless; doesn't replace the hook.
- **MCP**: MCP servers can add tools but sit outside the loop; same structural gap as `register_tool`.
- **Context-engine plugins** (`register_context_engine`): operate on prompt content, not on the call/ receipt boundary.

### Implementation reference

I have a working standalone implementation (protocol spec + dependency-free Rust core, 12 unit tests, integration guide with the transcript-pairing invariant) that I plan to open-source; happy to link once public, or share privately with maintainers. The integration is genuinely small when the hook exists: bank + guards + certificate ledger ≈ 400 lines.

### Estimated effort

The loop change is a well-scoped hook point + counter surfacing; the authoring tool and guard logic can live entirely in a plugin once the hook exists. I'd be up for contributing the plugin side if there's maintainer interest in the hook.

issues.body:
**Pain cluster from the weekly pain miner** (Discord support, Oct 25 – Nov 1 2026). **Class: UX GAP.**

## The friction

The failure the user sees is a generic card; the actionable cause sits in a log or a debug bundle. Six support threads this week each needed a staff member to open a diagnostics bundle to find a one-line cause the product already knew.

| Thread | Shown to user | Actual cause (found by staff in logs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1566161955310403635 (Desktop, local model) | "The AI service rejected the request / custom did not accept how this request was built" | `HTTP 400: model 'Phi-4-mini-instruct.Q8_0' not found` on the local llama server |
| 1565048145044316390 (Desktop-mac, SSH VPS) | "Hermes couldn't finish this reply. Something went wrong while Hermes was replying." | SSH tunnel died after Mac sleep; remote backend exited `idle for 903s with no client` (`no warm backend`, ECONNREFUSED) |
| 1565386450399133787 (Desktop 0.21.5) | "Hermes hit an internal problem starting this reply…" | `ValueError`: compression model context < 64,000 (fallback picked an 8k model) |
| 1565652972610781284 (CLI 0.22.5) | "Your request was not processed. Send it again…" | fallback route 401 `invalid_api_key`, then 404 model not found |
| 1566481029517152256 (Desktop-Win, Ollama) | "Provider has been unresponsive … for 5 consecutive stale attempts" | ~204k-token session sent to a local 27B model; fix was `/new`, the message doesn't mention context size |
| 1565398640959164506 / 1565745168102199417 (Win Store) | "Gateway inaccessible (service_identity_unverified)" | one reason code for four different checks; the child exit code/output is dropped (see #146763) |

Same shape on GitHub this week: #147563 ("Gateway connection failed; no local fallback" when the model provider is unreachable), #147503 (bare `permission_denied` on first message), #146730 (misleading permission error on large paste), #146527 (bulk delete → generic error); older #119105.

Verified on `origin/main` c7c7e0fa92f4: `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en_error_layers.ts` gateway/runtime layer bodies are the fixed "Hermes hit an internal problem starting this reply…" text, with no slot for the underlying message.

## Proposed fix

1. Every error card (Desktop) and failure notice (CLI/gateway) carries one plain line of the real cause when one is known: the provider status + message for provider/endpoint layers, the exception message for runtime layers, "connection to <host> lost" for transport.
2. Known causes get a specific remedy line: model not found on a local server → "pick a model the server has loaded"; stale-attempt breaker on a large context → "this conversation is N tokens; try /compress or /new" (open PR #143134 covers part of this, SALVAGE CANDIDATE); SSH backend idle exit → "reconnecting to <host>…" instead of a failure card.
3. Related open PRs worth landing with it: #105486 / #72637 (error names the actual summarizer route), #128875 (Desktop restart errors with cause).

Distinct from #87789 (Smart App Control) and #144562 (agent self-repair). Filed by the weekly user-pain miner (ledger: hermes-user-pain-miner).

issues.title: [Bug]: `hermes update` cannot finish PM dependency sync — a virtual plugin workspace member's own extra (`dev = pytest>=8,<9`) is locked against the core dev group (`pytest==9.1.1`)

issues.body:
**Summary**

On this host every PM dependency sync now fails, so `hermes update` can no longer finish and each command prints the failure in front of its own output. The resolver failure is not caused by anything in the core tree — it is caused by an **enabled third-party plugin's test-only extra**:

```text
hermes: source-update completion failed: venv: uv lock exited 1: es for split (markers:
  │ python_full_version == '3.14.*' and sys_platform != 'android'):
  ╰─▶ Because hermes-agent:dev depends on pytest==9.1.1 and
      hermes-plugin-hermes-structured-aux-models-d14fd6dc950ced4d[dev]
      depends on pytest>=8,<9, we can conclude that
      hermes-plugin-hermes-structured-aux-models-d14fd6dc950ced4d[dev] and
      hermes-agent:dev are incompatible.
      And because your workspace requires hermes-agent:dev and
      hermes-plugin-hermes-structured-aux-models-d14fd6dc950ced4d[dev], we can
      conclude that your workspace's requirements are unsatisfiable. — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

**Why it happens**

`pm/workspace.py::_workspace_member()` copies the plugin into `<gen>/plugin-sources/<key>` and, for a **virtual** member (no `[build-system]`, `tool.uv.package` not `true`), rewrites `[project].name` to `hermes-plugin-<key>` — but the member's `[project.optional-dependencies]` survives the rewrite:

```toml
# ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-structured-aux-models/pyproject.toml (verbatim, abridged)
[project]
name = "hermes-structured-aux-models"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8,<9"]     # the plugin's own test extra; nothing in PM installs it
```

uv locks every workspace member's extras and dependency groups, so that test-only pin becomes a requirement of the whole workspace and is resolved against the core's `[dependency-groups] dev` (`pytest==9.1.1`, pyproject.toml:539) — unsatisfiable. The plugin's extra is never installed by PM (it exists so the plugin's own suite can run in its own repo), yet it can wedge the core install's lock.

**Minimal reproduction** (`uv 0.12.3`, the PM-managed uv at `~/.hermes/tools/uv-0.12.3-linux-x64/uv`)

Root:

```toml
[project]
name = "hermes-agent"
version = "0.0.0"
requires-python = ">=3.14,<3.15"
dependencies = []

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["plugin-sources/*"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest==9.1.1"]
```

Member (the shape PM generates for a virtual plugin):

```toml
[project]
name = "hermes-plugin-p1-abc123"
version = "0.0.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8,<9"]

[tool.uv]
package = false
```

- `uv lock` → exit 1, exactly the PM text above (`hermes-plugin-p1-abc123[dev]` in place of the real key).
- Delete only the member's `[project.optional-dependencies]` → `Resolved 8 packages in 412ms`, exit 0.

**Evidence from the real install**

- `~/.hermes/logs/update_receipts/latest.json` — `"kind": "sync"`, `"outcome": "failed"`, step `dependency-sync` → `ResolutionConflict: venv: uv lock exited 1 …`
- `~/.hermes/logs/update_receipts/update_20260926_153913_569965_8b6c3dddffb94492bb794ea9c134ba02.json` — the desktop `hermes update`: step `historical_takeover` → `historical takeover preparation failed: venv: uv lock exited 1 …`; `~/.hermes/logs/desktop-update-handoff.log:2326` `Update preparation failed: venv: uv lock exited 1 …` at `2026-09-26T15:39:13+0800`.
- Afterwards every `hermes <cmd>` prints `hermes: source-update completion failed: …; running with the previous dependencies — run hermes update to finish it` (e.g. `hermes mcp list`, `hermes plugins list`).

**Environment**

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+3247.gd0288be (2026.9.24), `HEAD d0288be5b3` == `origin/main`; git/source install on Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64.
- PM: uv 0.12.3, managed Python 3.14.7; the legacy venv still serving is CPython 3.11.15 (`.venv` rebuild is what the takeover was attempting).
- Plugin: `hermes-structured-aux-models` (git checkout of `trajectoire-ai/hermes-structured-aux-models@86e646a`, catalog entry `plugin-catalog/hermes-structured-aux-models.yaml`), listed in `plugins.enabled`.

**Fix direction**

A virtual (metadata-only) member's extras/groups are meaningless to the composed workspace, and PM already rewrites that member's name and dependency list — so it could equally drop `[project.optional-dependencies]` / `[dependency-groups]` for virtual members (or lock with member extras excluded). Separately: a single plugin's own pin should not be able to make the core lock unsatisfiable — an unresolvable plugin extra is worth a loud per-plugin diagnostic and a skip, not a dead `hermes update`.

Same surface as #122148 / #122270 (a plugin's `pyproject.toml` breaking dependency sync), different trigger: not a missing `[project]` table, but a member extra that resolves *against* the core's dev group.

# Desktop in-app browser: USB-C YubiKey passkey authentication fails while system browser succeeds

## User-reported reproduction

1. Register a FIDO2 YubiKey passkey with Pocket ID (tested server version 2.17.0) using its stable HTTPS hostname.
2. Connect the YubiKey via USB-C; the key uses a FIDO2 PIN.
3. Open the same Pocket ID login page in Hermes Desktop's adjacent in-app browser/preview.
4. Click Authenticate and attempt security-key authentication.
5. No FIDO2 PIN prompt appears inside Hermes. The application reports that authentication was cancelled or timed out. User confirms this still reproduces after updating to client `v0.21.5+6232`, backend `v0.21.5`.
6. Open the same site outside Hermes in a regular browser and use the same YubiKey: authentication succeeds.

## Expected

The in-app browser should complete supported USB security-key WebAuthn ceremonies, or clearly communicate the limitation and offer an external-browser fallback.

## Observed scope and limitations

This is user-reported, not independently reproduced with the physical key by the agent. It concerns an external USB-C security key, not merely Touch ID/iCloud platform passkeys. No PIN prompt appears inside Hermes (confirmed by the user after updating). The precise DOMException and timing have not been captured. Root cause is not established.

## Environment still needed

- Screenshot-confirmed Hermes Desktop client: `v0.21.5+6232`; connected backend: `v0.21.5`. Electron version remains unknown. User confirms the same failure after this update.
- Operating system/version.
- Exact YubiKey model/firmware if available.
- Normal browser name/version.

No PIN, credentials, tokens or private hostnames should be included.

## Related upstream work

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/89602 — open in-app browser platform-passkey issue; USB security-key success was not established there.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/42448 — older desktop OIDC embedded-login issue.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/67920 — system-browser native gateway sign-in; does not by itself fix arbitrary in-app browsing.

issues.body:
> *Drafted with an AI assistant; posted by the account owner.*

### Bug Description

The Bot Desktop's Browser (dock icon) launches Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=0`. In Chrome that flag alone sets `navigator.webdriver = true`, so sites that check it refuse a human login on the Bot Screen:

- Google sign-in answers the identifier step with "Couldn't sign you in. This browser or app may not be secure" (`accounts.google.com/v3/signin/rejected`).
- dash.cloudflare.com fails its Turnstile check ("There was a problem with verification").

This breaks the documented handoff flow, where the human logs in on the Bot Screen and the bot continues in the same profile. Google logins already saved in the profile also end up signed out.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `hermes computer-use screen start`, then open the Browser from the dock.
2. Open `https://accounts.google.com/`, type any address, press Next.
3. Or open `https://dash.cloudflare.com/login`.

Same result with throwaway profiles on the same display (Chrome 154.0.8037.57, Linux):

| Launch flags | `navigator.webdriver` | Cloudflare login | Google identifier step |
|---|---|---|---|
| dock flags as shipped | `true` | "There was a problem with verification" | `/signin/rejected` |
| no debugging port | `false` | n/a | n/a |
| dock flags + `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` | `false` | normal form | normal flow |

### Expected Behavior

A human can log in to Google and Cloudflare on the Bot Screen, as the takeover flow intends.

### Actual Behavior

Both refuse the browser as automated.

### Affected Component

Tools (`tools/bot_desktop/browser.py`, `dock_argv`)

### Operating System

Ubuntu (Linux 6.8), VPS, Xvnc display

### Hermes Version

Installed checkout `8a33891bdd` (2026-10-07); `origin/main` `21ede8a41b` (2026-10-13) still launches with only `--remote-debugging-port=0`.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`dock_argv` passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` so the bot can attach, and that flag turns on Blink's `AutomationControlled` feature. The repo already works around this for the same reason in `plugins/google_meet/meet_bot.py` (`--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`).

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` to `dock_argv`, next to `--remote-debugging-port=0`. CDP attach keeps working (measured). The same may apply to `_REAL_PROFILE_CHROME_FLAGS` in `tools/browser_tool_real_profile.py`, which uses the same port flag on the user's real profile.

issues.title: Evaluation request: shadow-mode pre-call check for a2a_call / a2a_discover (free; one ask, the last)
issues.body:
I opened #107908 in September to list AG's preflight in the MCP catalog; this is a different, smaller ask and the last one. Hermes's A2A toolset is the cleanest case of an agent meeting an arbitrary URL at runtime (`a2a_call` on any endpoint, `a2a_orchestrate` fan-out) with ground truth in `a2a_audit.jsonl`. We have a free, keyless check — `GET /preflight?url=` — that separates "HTTP 200" from "a working A2A/MCP endpoint", verifies card signatures and reports what it could not test. What we do not have is any independent evidence that it improves a decision; our own tests prove capability, nothing more.

Would one Hermes operator run it in shadow mode as a `pre_tool_call` plugin (observe-only, no blocking) for ~30 unfamiliar-endpoint calls and report outcomes, including every case where it was wrong? Unnecessary refusals in a fan-out are exactly the mistake we want measured. Recorded: endpoint URL, verdict, timing, one outcome record; no task content. Onboarding: `artifacts/evaluation-2026-10-14/PARTICIPANT-ONBOARDING.md` (https://github.com/AgentTanuki/agent-guild/blob/main/artifacts/evaluation-2026-10-14/PARTICIPANT-ONBOARDING.md). No reply needed if not relevant.

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows x64: node-pre-gyp not found during npm ci on get-windows, update retries forever ('source update tail not finished')
issues.body:
### Bug Description

On Windows x64, `hermes update` (and every subsequent `hermes` invocation) fails to finish the Node-dependencies build step for `apps/desktop`/`ui-tui`/`web`, because the child `npm ci` process cannot resolve `node-pre-gyp` on PATH while building `get-windows`. The failure leaves a `source-completion-pending` marker that is retried on every CLI launch, so `hermes update`, `hermes status`, and `hermes gateway ensure` all keep reporting `"source-update completion failed: an update is still running"` and gateway calls return `{"reason_code":"update_paused","state":"draining"}` indefinitely, even though the update itself already applied (`"Already up to date! [detached @ f0d94882e8]"`) and the gateway is otherwise running fine.

This looks distinct from #134246 (that one is Windows ARM64, MSBuild failing during a real native build). Here the architecture is x64, prebuilt bindings should exist for `get-windows`, and the failure is that the `node-pre-gyp` command itself is not found — a PATH problem in the npm ci child process, not a build-toolchain problem. `node-pre-gyp.cmd` does exist on disk at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\.bin\node-pre-gyp.cmd`, it's just not visible to the process that `npm ci` spawns for `get-windows`'s install script.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows 11 x64 with an existing Hermes install, run `hermes update` (or just `hermes status` / any CLI command) while a prior update's Node-dependency build step is pending.
2. The updater runs `node-deps.mjs --workspace ui-tui --workspace web --workspace apps/desktop` (and, after failing, retries without `apps/desktop`).
3. `npm ci` runs `get-windows`'s install script, which calls `node-pre-gyp install --fallback-to-build`.
4. The spawn fails with `'node-pre-gyp' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.` even though the script resolves and runs other local binaries fine; `npm ci` exits 1.
5. The CLI writes `installs/<id>/source-completion-pending` = `source update tail not finished` and increments `source-completion-attempts`. Every later `hermes` invocation re-attempts the same failing build step and prints the "update still running" message instead of running normally.

### Expected Behavior

- `node-pre-gyp` (present in `node_modules/.bin`) should be resolvable by the `npm ci` postinstall step on Windows x64, so the native dependency build succeeds (or fails soft like `stage-native-deps.mjs` does for the ARM64 case in #134246).
- A failed Desktop/web Node-dependency build step should not block ordinary CLI/gateway commands indefinitely with "update still running" / `update_paused` — the CLI (chat, gateway, profiles) already works correctly despite this failure.

### Actual Behavior

```
→ Preparing Node dependencies...
...
npm error code 1
npm error path %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\get-windows
npm error command failed
npm error command C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c node-pre-gyp install --fallback-to-build
npm error 'node-pre-gyp' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
npm error operable program or batch file.
...
  ⚠ Node dependencies failed: ...
  Desktop app build owed: Node dependencies failed
  ⚠ Update follow-up 'build' did not finish: Node dependencies: ... (the next launch or `hermes update` retries it)
```

Subsequent commands:
```
> hermes gateway ensure --profile <profile>
hermes: source-update completion failed: an update is still running; wait for it to exit, then relaunch Hermes; running with the previous dependencies — run `hermes update` to finish it
{"client_code_sha":"f0d94882e89ab8d4098b5bb2f166adfb9ee0a0ab","detail":null,"endpoint":null,"reason_code":"update_paused","state":"draining"}
```

Meanwhile `gateway_state.json` shows the gateway actually running fine and serving all profiles (`"gateway_state":"running"`), so the "update still running" messaging is misleading — the only thing actually stuck is the Desktop/web native-module build retry.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation (updater, Node-dependency build step)

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro, x64 (build 26300)

### Python Version

Hermes-managed: Python 3.14.9+20261021 (win32-x64)

### Hermes Version

0.22.6, sha f0d94882e89ab8d4098b5bb2f166adfb9ee0a0ab, channel stable

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

Node: Hermes-managed node-26.12.1-win32-x64, npm 12.0.2. `get-windows` install fails under both `--workspace apps/desktop --workspace ui-tui --workspace web` and the fallback retry `--workspace ui-tui --workspace web` (without desktop), so `get-windows` appears to be a shared dependency of `ui-tui`/`web`, not just the desktop app.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Likely the custody/elevation wrapper that `hermes update` uses to run `npm ci` in a Windows Job Object (a short Python script using `ctypes`/`subprocess.Popen` to assign the child to a job and resume it) does not pass through a PATH that includes the npm-local `node_modules\.bin`, so `node-pre-gyp`'s shell-resolved invocation from `get-windows`'s install script fails to resolve even though the binary is present on disk.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: Packaged Chromium is still Chrome 145.0.7632.6
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The Chromium package in `pm/lock.json` is still `1208+145.0.7632.6`. That build is from about 17 January 2026. Chrome stable is 156.0.8078.80.

The public Chrome 156 fixes landed in 156.0.8078.73. The reports are CVE-2026-118306, CVE-2026-118331, CVE-2026-118348, and CVE-2026-118344. Playwright 1.64 still bundles Chromium 156.0.8078.4, so bumping the Playwright package does not pick up the patched browser.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `pm/lock.json` and read the `chromium` version.

## Expected Behavior

The packaged browser is a Chrome for Testing build at or above 156.0.8078.73. The store directory is `chromium-1248`, which is the revision Playwright 1.64 looks up.

## Actual Behavior

The lock pins `1208+145.0.7632.6`.

## Affected Component

Setup / Installation, and the browser tool.

## Proposed Fix

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/148342 pins Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.80 and keeps the store directory at `chromium-1248`. linux-arm64 downloads that same build. Playwright stays at 1.64.0.

When checking out a specific release tag (e.g. `git checkout v0.22.2`), `get_version_info()` in `hermes_cli/version_info.py` returns the wrong base version. It reports `0.21.5+12940.gd923a5e` instead of `0.22.2`.

## Root Cause

`_git_version_info()` uses `git tag --merged HEAD --list "v[0-9]*"` which returns **all ancestor tags** (v0.21.5, v0.21.6, ..., v0.22.2). The `max()` correctly selects `0.22.2` as `base_version`, but the subsequent distance calculation uses the wrong reference, resulting in a display version of `0.21.5+12940.gd923a5e`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `git checkout v0.22.2` (detached HEAD on release tag)
2. Run `hermes --version` or check the dashboard
3. **Expected**: `v0.22.2`
4. **Actual**: `v0.21.5+12940.gd923a5e`

## Fix

Use `git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD` first to detect when HEAD is exactly on a release tag. If it matches, use that tag as `base_version` with `distance=0`. Fall back to the existing `--merged` logic only when not on an exact tag.

## Environment
- OS: Linux (Debian 12, ARM64)
- Install method: git
- Version: v0.22.2 (detached HEAD)

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows Desktop kills its own `hermes gateway ensure` at the fixed 75 s deadline while launch preparation runs an owed source-update tail, so every boot restarts the tail (gateway-ensure counterpart of #138248)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

labels.name: desktop/connection
labels.description: The desktop app reaching its Hermes backend: starting, stopping or restarting the local backend proc

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On Windows, the Desktop boots a local profile by running `hermes gateway ensure` (`runGatewayEnsure` in `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts`) and kills that client after a fixed 75 s: `GATEWAY_ENSURE_PROTOCOL_DEADLINE_MS` (60 s) plus `GATEWAY_ENSURE_CLIENT_GRACE_MS` (15 s). The 60 s is the ensure verb's own startup deadline. But the verb never starts while launch preparation owes work. `hermes_bootstrap.py` calls `venv_sync.prepare_launch()` for every command, and the only gateway command it exempts is `gateway status` (`_is_read_only_gateway_status`). When dependencies are stale or `source-completion-pending` is armed, `prepare_launch` takes the update marker and runs the dependency sync and/or `source_completion.py --finish-update --desktop` (TUI and web builds) before `gateway ensure` runs. That can take longer than 75 s, and then the Desktop kills the client mid-tail.

The kill also stops the tail. On Windows the completion child is bound to the lock owner's kill-on-close job. So every attempt starts the same work again and leaves a dead update marker for the next boot to reclaim. A killed run is also never counted by `_record_completion_attempt`, which only runs on a non-zero tail exit, so the #122206 backoff never engages. In our case the loop ended on the fourth attempt, which finished the tail in about 33 s, most likely because the killed attempts had left warm build caches.

This is the `gateway ensure` counterpart of #138248. Its fix (#138251) arms a grace period in `backend-ready.ts` for the `hermes serve` port-announcement wait. The ensure client has no completion grace at all. It also keeps only the last stderr line, so the user sees "Update Hermes or check the profile, then retry." while Hermes is busy updating itself.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows, git/source install on the PM-managed runtime, packaged Desktop, at 774a49c5b4. Main at 7e9eb8d9a3 has no changes to `local-gateway.ts` or `venv_sync.py` since then.
2. Leave the checkout's source ahead of its dependency generation. We hit this with a `git merge origin/main --no-commit` (about 830 upstream commits, lockfiles changed) that was left uncommitted, with no sync or rebuild afterwards. An interrupted `hermes update` or any armed `source-completion-pending` takes the same launch path.
3. Close and relaunch the Desktop.

### Expected Behavior

The Desktop waits while launch preparation finishes the update, then attaches. A boot that is busy finishing an update is not reported as a failure.

### Actual Behavior

`desktop.log` (local time +09:00, paths trimmed):

```
18:13:19.450 [boot] Using Hermes at <install root>
18:14:34.473 [boot] Desktop boot failed: hermes gateway ensure produced no result (exit 7): hermes gateway ensure timed out. Update Hermes or check the profile, then retry.
18:14:35.133 [updates] dead update marker: script helper says reclaimed
18:14:37.066 [boot] Using Hermes at <install root>
18:15:52.162 [boot] Desktop boot failed: hermes gateway ensure produced no result (exit 7): hermes gateway ensure timed out. ...
18:15:53.731 [updates] dead update marker: script helper says reclaimed
18:15:56.092 [boot] Using Hermes at <install root>
18:17:11.103 [boot] Desktop boot failed: hermes gateway ensure produced no result (exit 7): hermes gateway ensure timed out. ...
18:17:11.138 [renderer error:main] Hermes couldn't start: ...
18:17:11.571 [updates] dead update marker: script helper says reclaimed
18:17:13.535 [boot] Using Hermes at <install root>
18:18:06.063 [boot] Hermes gateway is ready
```

Each failed attempt is 75.0–75.1 s from "Using Hermes" to the failure.

Other evidence from the same window:

- `logs/update_receipts/pm_20261017T091424Z-sync-….json` is a `kind: sync` receipt from 09:14:05 to 09:14:24 UTC (18:14:05 to 18:14:24 local), `outcome: ok`. That is the first attempt's dependency sync. The client was killed 10 s after it committed.
- `desktop-update-handoff.log` has `marker-op reclaim: removed a dead update marker` at 18:14:35, 18:15:53 and 18:17:11, one per killed attempt.
- No gateway started during attempts 1–3. `gateway-starts.log` and `gateway-exit-diag.log` have no entry between the previous day and 18:17:52.
- During attempt 4 the TUI dist was written at 18:17:26, the web dist at 18:17:36 and `install-stamp.json` at 18:17:46. The gateway started at 18:17:52 and was ready at 18:18:06.

After we committed the merge, rebuilt the Desktop and restarted the gateway, a relaunch reached "Hermes gateway is ready" in 12 s.

### Root Cause

From the code at 774a49c5b4:

- `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts:10-11, 35`: the timeout is fixed at `60_000 + 15_000`, after which the client is killed. Line 41 keeps only the last 4 KB of stderr, and lines 136–138 show only its last line.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (around 12227): boot calls `ensureLocalGateway(() => runGatewayEnsure(...))` with no `beforeEnsure` and no awareness of an update tail. The update-marker gate runs before the client spawns (our log shows `no update marker` at 18:13:16), but the client then becomes the update owner.
- `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:413`: under `not current or pending.is_file()`, `prepare_launch` acquires the update marker and calls `_finish_source_update`. That function prints its banners to stderr (lines 509 and 524) and runs the tail inside the lock owner's kill-on-close job (comment at line 540).
- `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:555`: a killed run never reaches `_record_completion_attempt`.

### Suggested Fix

Any one of these would break the loop:

1. In `runGatewayEnsure`, re-arm the deadline while stderr shows the `finishing an interrupted source update` or `completing source-update dependencies` banner, as #122206 and #138251 do for `waitForDashboardPort`. The regex from #138251 could be shared.
2. Or let `gateway ensure` answer first. When `prepare_launch` owes a tail for an `ensure` command, it could emit a protocol verdict such as `{"state":"starting","reason_code":"completing_update"}` before the tail, and the Desktop could keep polling as it does for `starting`.
3. Separately, count a killed or interrupted tail as an attempt, or stamp the pending marker with its owner as #127284 proposes. Then a deadline that is always too short cannot loop without bound.

Related: #138248 and #138251 (the same failure on the `hermes serve` port wait), #127284 (a killed tail strands the marker), #139132 (sync-stage failures bypass the counter, and marker reclaim leaves the obligation in place).

### Affected Component

Other (Desktop boot / `hermes gateway ensure`, Windows)

### Debug Report

Not attached. `hermes debug share` uploads config and logs, so the relevant excerpts are inline instead.

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300

### Python Version

3.14.7 (managed runtime)

### Hermes Version

v0.22.1 (git 774a49c5b4 merged into a local branch). The local commits do not touch `local-gateway.ts`, `main.ts`, `venv_sync.py`, `source_completion.py`, `hermes_bootstrap.py` or the update lock.

issues.title: [Feature]: Mobile app (iOS/Android beta) has no i18n — ship the same 17-language UI the Desktop and web dashboard already have
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

The Hermes mobile beta (iOS TestFlight and Android builds) is English-only. Settings offers Look & Feel (appearance / canvas / font), Chat, Behavior and About — there is no language entry anywhere in the app, and the UI strings appear to be compiled in English only. Every other Hermes surface already has an i18n layer: the CLI/TUI ship 17 bundled `locales/<lang>.yaml` catalogs, the Desktop app bundles its translations, and the web dashboard has `web/src/i18n/<lang>.ts` with a language picker.

For a non-English user this is the single biggest gap in the mobile beta. The practical effect is that people install third-party clients just to get a localized UI: `Hy4ri/hermes-mobile` (Android) ships `values-zh` (1858 of 1914 strings) plus Settings → Language, and `2winter-dev/iHermes` ships zh/en. A user whose only requirement is a Chinese interface currently has no way to satisfy it in the official app, so the official app loses that user on day one.

### Proposed Solution

Reuse the catalogs that already exist rather than adding a fourth translation pipeline:

1. **Catalogs** — `locales/<lang>.yaml` (core, 17 ids: `en, af, ar, de, es, fr, ga, hu, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant`) and `web/src/i18n/<lang>.ts` for the UI-side copy. The shared helpers in `apps/shared/src/i18n.ts` (`LOCALE_ENDONYMS`, `RTL_LOCALES`, `mergeTranslations`, `formatPositional`) exist precisely so desktop and web pickers cannot disagree on a language's native name — a mobile surface should consume the same endonyms and catalogs instead of introducing its own.
2. **Initial locale** — follow the device locale on first launch (the platform equivalent of `navigator.language`), then persist an explicit pick per device. This matches the existing behaviour of the web dashboard (`localStorage` key `hermes-locale`) and Desktop (`display.language` in `config.yaml`).
3. **Picker** — Settings → Language, listing endonyms (简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, 한국어, …), mirroring the Desktop picker. Untranslated keys fall back to English so a partial catalog is still shippable.
4. **RTL** — `ar` is already in `RTL_LOCALES`; the mobile layout should flip the same way the Desktop does. There is already an RTL-related report against the iOS build (#147338), so the mirroring path exists.

If full coverage is too large for a beta cycle, ship the picker plus the top locales first (`zh`, `zh-hant`, `ja`, `ko`, `es`) with English fallback, then widen.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Point users at the web dashboard.** It does have a language picker, but the switcher is hidden below 640px and the locale always defaults to English — see #114648, still open. That is exactly the viewport the mobile app targets, so this is not a workaround for phone users.
- **Leave it to third-party clients.** They already cover this (see above), which is an argument for shipping it in the official app rather than against.

### Feature Type

Other — mobile app UI / internationalization.

### Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor).

### Additional context

Verified against `main` today: `locales/` contains 17 bundled catalogs, `web/src/i18n/` contains the same 17 locale modules, and `apps/shared/src/i18n.ts` exports the endonym/RTL helpers used by both the Desktop and web pickers. Requested by a Chinese-speaking user (简体中文) who is otherwise using the official beta.

issues.title: [Bug]: tool_describe with MCP $ref causes HTTP 400 on custom OpenAI-compatible Gemini routes
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When routing Gemini models (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash`) through `custom_providers` using OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`api_mode: chat_completions`, via gateways such as AxonHub, OneAPI, LiteLLM, 9router), invoking `tool_describe` on MCP tools that contain `$defs` references (such as FastMCP / Pydantic models with `"$ref": "#/$defs/..."`, e.g. Oxide MCP's `terminals_open`) causes upstream Gemini to abort with:

```
HTTP 400: The referenced name '#/$defs/TerminalOpenSource' in function_response.response does not match to a display_name in the function_response.parts.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible gateway in `config.yaml` under `custom_providers` routing to a Google Gemini model.
2. Enable an MCP server whose tools define parameters using `$defs` and `$ref` (e.g. Oxide MCP, or any FastMCP tool with nested models).
3. Start a chat turn that searches for and describes that MCP tool via `tool_describe`.
4. `tool_describe` returns the tool's parameter schema containing `{"$ref": "#/$defs/..."}`.
5. In the next turn, the agent sends the tool result message to the gateway.
6. The gateway converts the tool response into Gemini's native `functionResponse.response`.
7. Google Gemini server rejects the request with HTTP 400 because `"$ref"` is interpreted as an inline part pointer into `function_response.parts`.

### Expected Behavior

Tool schemas returned by `tool_describe` or tool result messages in general should not emit raw `"$ref"` keys that trigger Gemini's multimodal parts validator when replayed across OpenAI-compatible routes.

### Actual Behavior

The request fails with a non-retryable 400 `BadRequestError`, halting the agent turn.

### Affected Component

- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)
- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Platform

N/A (CLI only) / Desktop

### Operating System

Windows 11 (also affects Linux/macOS)

### Python Version

3.14.9 / 3.11+

### Hermes Version

0.22.6 (commit f0d94882e8)

### Root Cause Analysis

In PR #93393, an opaque-text fallback `_looks_like_json_schema(parsed)` was added to `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py` to prevent this exact Google Gemini 400 error.

However:
1. That check **only executes** when using the native `gemini` provider (`provider: gemini`).
2. When users route Gemini through `custom_providers` with `api_mode: chat_completions` (OpenAI format), requests go through `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` and `chat_completion_helpers.py`.
3. In `tools/tool_search.py:dispatch_tool_describe()`, parameter schemas from the tool registry are serialized directly with raw `"$ref"`.
4. FastMCP/Pydantic tool schemas registered in `tools/mcp_tool_schema.py` retain `"$ref"` when normalized via `_rewrite_local_refs()`.
5. Upstream OpenAI-to-Gemini translation proxies parse the tool response JSON and forward `"$ref"` inside `functionResponse.response`, causing Gemini to reject the turn.

### Proposed Fix

1. **In `tools/mcp_tool_schema.py: _rewrite_local_refs()`**:
   Rename `$ref` to `_ref` during schema normalization so MCP schemas in the registry never carry naked `$ref`:
   ```python
   ref = normalized.pop("$ref", normalized.get("_ref"))
   if ref is not None:
       if isinstance(ref, str) and ref.startswith("#/definitions/"):
           ref = "#/$defs/" + ref[len("#/definitions/"):]
       normalized["_ref"] = ref
   ```
2. **In `tools/tool_search.py: dispatch_tool_describe()`**:
   Sanitize the JSON output of described tools:
   ```python
   return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False).replace('"$ref":', '"_ref":')
   ```
3. **In `agent/transports/chat_completions.py: _sanitize_message()`**:
   Add a wire-level safety net for tool messages:
   ```python
   if msg.get("role") == "tool":
       content = msg.get("content")
       if isinstance(content, str) and '"$ref":' in content:
           out_msg["content"] = content.replace('"$ref":', '"_ref":')
           remapped = True
   ```

issues.title: QQ: standalone send path hardcodes msg_type=0, so Markdown never renders

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working
