issues.body:
## Summary

The standalone (non-gateway) QQ send path hard-codes plain text, so Markdown pushed by scripts
never renders in the QQ client — while the same Markdown sent as a chat reply *does* render.

## Reproduction

1. Prepare a file containing Markdown:

   ```markdown
   # Title
   **bold** and a > quote
   ```

2. Send it through the CLI path:

   ```bash
   hermes send --to qqbot --file brief.md
   ```

3. The QQ client shows the literal `#`, `**` and `>` characters.

Sending the identical content directly against the QQ Open Platform REST API with `msg_type: 2`
renders correctly (verified end-to-end), so the platform supports it — the CLI path just never
asks for Markdown.

## Where

`tools/send_message_senders.py`, `_qqbot_send_text_message()` (~line 709 on `main`):

```python
payload = {"content": (message or "")[:4000], "msg_type": 0}
```

The gateway adapter takes a different path and does the right thing —
`gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py`, `_build_text_body()` (~line 1511):

```python
if self._markdown_support:
    return {"markdown": {"content": text}, "msg_type": MSG_TYPE_MARKDOWN, "msg_seq": msg_seq}
```

with `self._markdown_support = bool(extra.get("markdown_support", True))` (default `True`).

So a reply typed into a chat renders, while a cron/script push of the same content does not —
the two paths disagree.

## Expected

The standalone path should honour the same `markdown_support` setting as the adapter: send
`msg_type: 2` with `markdown.content` when enabled, and fall back to `msg_type: 0` (optionally
stripping Markdown) when disabled.

## Extra

`(message or "")[:4000]` also truncates silently — an over-long message loses its tail with no
error. Failing loudly, or splitting, would be safer.

## Environment

Hermes Agent v0.21.1 (2026.9.7). QQ Open Platform side: custom Markdown is available to all bots
in C2C and group scenes (no template approval needed), and a 4000-character Markdown message is
accepted and rendered in full (verified).

issues.title: Desktop: after long tasks Enter reaches backend but user bubble is not rendered and text remains in composer

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
## Bug Description

After a long-running Desktop conversation or a long tool/task turn, pressing **Enter** can submit the text to the backend while the Desktop UI fails to complete the visible submit transition:

- the user message does **not** appear in the rendered chat thread;
- the same text remains (or is restored) in the composer input;
- from the user's perspective, Enter did nothing;
- fully restarting Hermes Desktop restores normal behavior.

This is narrower than a completely frozen composer. The renderer remains present and the text is editable, but the submit/render/draft states disagree.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop on macOS.
2. Use one conversation for a long period, including long-running tool/task turns.
3. After a long turn, type a follow-up message in the composer.
4. Press Enter.
5. Observe:
   - the text remains in the composer;
   - no corresponding user bubble appears in the chat thread;
   - the user cannot tell that the backend received the prompt.
6. Quit and restart Hermes Desktop.
7. Observe that composer submission/rendering works normally again.

## Expected Behavior

On Enter, exactly one of these visible outcomes should occur atomically:

1. Accepted: clear the composer and immediately render the optimistic user bubble; or
2. Queued: clear/move the text into a visible queued-message row; or
3. Rejected: retain the draft and show a visible send error, without also persisting the prompt as an accepted user message.

The backend transcript, renderer thread, optimistic message state, and composer draft must agree.

## Actual Behavior

The local reproduction produced a split state:

- Backend `agent.log` recorded a new `conversation turn` containing the submitted text.
- `state.db` contains the durable user message.
- Desktop did not render the new user bubble.
- The text remained/restored in the composer.
- Restarting Hermes Desktop cleared the bad volatile UI state and normal sending resumed.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- App: Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 / local source build
- Platform: `desktop`
- Affected session: long-running, tool-heavy session
- Restart recovery: **yes**

## Local Evidence (sanitized)

Affected local session: `20260721_145818_192531`

At the time of inspection:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| messages | ~172 |
| tool calls | ~83 |
| cumulative input tokens | ~9.6M |
| compacted state for the reported user message | false |

### Backend received the prompt

`agent.log` contains:

```text
[20260721_145818_192531] agent.turn_context: conversation turn:
session=20260721_145818_192531
model=grok-4.5 provider=custom platform=desktop history=150
msg='[submitted follow-up describing the Desktop input/render problem]'
```

Immediately afterward, the provider request failed (first 429 retries, then a 400):

```text
API call failed ... HTTP 429: upstream quota exhausted
...
API call failed ... HTTP 400: Upstream error: 400
```

### Durable transcript also contains it

A sanitized `state.db` query found the submitted text as an active, uncompacted user message:

```text
role=user
active=1
compacted=0
content_length=93
```

So Enter was not merely swallowed before RPC. The backend accepted/persisted the user turn, while the Desktop renderer/composer did not show the corresponding accepted state.

## Relevant Desktop Submit Path

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.ts`:

1. `submitDraft()` clears the draft and dispatches `onSubmit(...)`.
2. `dispatchSubmit()` restores the text into the composer whenever `onSubmit` resolves `false` or throws:

```ts
Promise.resolve(onSubmit(...))
  .then(accepted => accepted === false ? restore() : clearSessionDraft(...))
  .catch(restore)
```

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/submit.ts`:

1. Seeds an optimistic user message before `prompt.submit`.
2. The backend can persist/start the conversation turn.
3. A downstream model/provider failure makes the submit path return `false` and causes the composer draft to be restored.

The expected optimistic bubble should still make the accepted user turn visible. In the reproduction, it did not render, producing a contradictory UI: durable user message + restored composer text + no visible user bubble.

Restart recovery strongly suggests stale renderer/session-store state rather than permanent transcript corruption.

## Classification / Related Issues

Related but not an exact duplicate:

- #68467 — long tool-heavy sessions can freeze the Desktop composer/thread entirely.
- #63290 — meta issue for Desktop composer DOM / `draftRef` / AUI state divergence.
- #44978 — busy/interrupt paths can leave the composer without a recoverable visible state.
- #63210 / #63574 — first Enter in a new chat remains in input (reported fixed on current main); this report occurs **after long-running existing-session work**, and the backend did receive/persist the turn.

This report is specifically:

> existing long-running session + Enter reaches backend/durable DB + user bubble is not rendered + text remains/restores in composer + Desktop restart recovers.

## Proposed Fix Direction

1. Introduce an explicit submit transaction state keyed by a stable client message id.
2. Once the backend acknowledges/persists the user turn, never restore it as an unsent draft solely because the subsequent model call fails.
3. Keep the optimistic user bubble visible and append a separate assistant/provider error bubble.
4. Reconcile renderer state from the durable transcript after `prompt.submit` error/timeout before deciding to restore the draft.
5. If the same client message id already exists durably, clear the composer instead of restoring duplicate text.
6. Add a regression test for:
   - long existing session;
   - optimistic user insert;
   - backend accepts/persists prompt;
   - provider fails afterward;
   - user bubble remains visible;
   - composer stays cleared;
   - remount/restart is not required.
7. Add a renderer recovery path that rehydrates the active session when message state and draft state contradict each other.

## Workaround

Fully quit and restart Hermes Desktop. This restores normal composer behavior in the observed case.

## Privacy

No API keys or full transcript are attached. The prompt text and endpoint credentials are omitted/redacted; only state transitions and aggregate metrics are included.

issues.title: prompt_surface.py render fails on macOS: sys.platform is pinned before zoneinfo and psutil load
issues.body:
## What happens

On macOS, `python scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py render` exits 1 on unmodified `main` (`2d11905f79`):

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_sysconfigdata__linux_darwin'
```

So a contributor on a Mac cannot regenerate the snapshot that `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` checks. The only check left is CI, after the push, as noted in passing on #145883.

## Cause

`_pin_environment()` sets `sys.platform = "linux"` for the skills index `platforms:` gate, and only then imports `hermes_time`. Two modules pick a platform-specific module when they are first imported, so after the pin they pick the Linux one:

- `hermes_time` imports `zoneinfo`, which calls `sysconfig.get_config_var("TZPATH")`. `sysconfig` builds its data-module name from `sys.platform` and the real multiarch, which gives `_sysconfigdata__linux_darwin`, a module that does not exist.
- If `sysconfig` is loaded first, the render gets further and then fails importing `psutil`. `psutil` picks its backend from `sys.platform` (`psutil._pslinux`, then `_psutil_linux`).

On Linux the pin changes nothing, so CI never hits this.

## Fix

Load those modules before the pin, while `sys.platform` still has its real value:

```python
    # zoneinfo (through sysconfig) and psutil pick platform-specific modules when first imported:
    # load them before the pin, or the render dies on macOS.
    import sysconfig
    import zoneinfo  # noqa: F401
    import psutil  # noqa: F401
    sysconfig.get_config_vars()
    sys.platform = "linux"  # skills index ``platforms:`` gate
```

I checked this on macOS with CPython 3.14.9 against `main` `2d11905f79`. With these three modules loaded before the pin, `render --out <dir>` succeeds. Its output is byte-identical to the committed `tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/`: every surface prompt, every tool schema, and `surfaces.json`. Every later `sys.platform` read still sees the pin, so the bytes do not change.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a self-hosted gateway reached over HTTPS (Tailscale Serve, `webapp.public_url` set), the **Hermes mobile app (Android beta)** can complete Nous sign-in and still leave the user staring at a **gateway error page in the browser**:

```
{"detail":"Invalid code: Portal rejected token request: invalid_grant"}
```

The gateway log shows the sequence: one successful upstream exchange that mints the native one-time code (`native_code_issued`), then **~700 ms later a second `GET /auth/callback` with the already-consumed Portal code**, which fails and is the response the visible browser tab renders. The app itself finishes the flow a moment later (`native_token_success` → `ws_ticket_minted`), so the failure is a *losing duplicate tab*, but from the user's point of view sign-in looks broken and there is no way to tell whether to retry.

It is intermittent: an earlier attempt in the same session showed the duplicate, a later attempt did not.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.5+1115.g930e5ed` (2026.9.24), Windows 11 host, git install.
- Gateway serving webapp+dashboard on `127.0.0.1:9120`, published as `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net` via `tailscale serve` (tailnet only, TLS terminated by Tailscale).
- `webapp.public_url` = the Tailscale HTTPS origin; `dashboard.public_url` unset.
- Dashboard auth providers active at the time: `nous` (OAuth) **and** `basic` (`dashboard.basic_auth`) — the app's provider probe correctly listed both.
- Client: Hermes mobile app Android beta distributed at NousCon NYC (2026-10-31 build); exact version string not captured.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the mobile app: `Add Instance` → **Direct**, Address = `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net`, Method = **Browser**.
2. Complete the Nous Portal sign-in in the system browser.
3. Portal redirects back to `<origin>/auth/callback?code=…&state=…`.

### Expected

Either a "signed in, return to the app" page, or a silent redirect — never an error page for a flow that actually succeeded.

### Actual

The browser shows `{"detail":"Invalid code: Portal rejected token request: invalid_grant"}` (HTTP 400), the app briefly appears to fail, and the connection only becomes usable on a later retry.

### Evidence (gateway `logs/dashboard-auth.log`, UTC, identifiers redacted)

Failing attempt — the pair of callbacks is 697 ms apart:

```
00:26:43  native_authorize_start  nous   <phone-ip>
00:26:58  login_success           nous   <phone-ip>     # Portal code exchanged OK
00:26:58  native_code_issued      nous   <phone-ip>     # one-time code handed to the app
00:26:58  login_failure           nous   invalid_code   # SECOND /auth/callback, same code
```

Retry that worked (single callback):

```
00:28:53  native_authorize_start  nous   <phone-ip>
00:28:54  login_success           nous   <phone-ip>
00:28:54  native_code_issued      nous   <phone-ip>
00:29:04  native_token_success    nous   <phone-ip>
00:29:05  ws_ticket_minted        nous   <phone-ip>
```

`invalid_grant` is Portal rejecting the *second* redemption of a one-time authorization code; the gateway's own error path is `InvalidCodeError` → `_http(400, f"Invalid code: {e}")` in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py::auth_callback`. The code itself is single-use by construction (`native_flow.complete_pending` consumes the pending broker entry; `_CODE_TTL_SECONDS = 120`).

### Hypothesis

The native flow (RFC 8252) expects exactly one `/auth/callback`. The Android client appears to open the authorize URL in more than one browsing context (Custom Tab + webview, or a retried navigation), so the Portal redirect is followed twice; the second one lands on `/auth/callback` after the first already consumed the code, and its 400 is what the user sees. Because `_clear_pkce` runs on the first response, the duplicate can also surface as `missing PKCE state cookie` depending on which context wins the race.

If the second call sometimes wins instead of the first, the *app* would end up without a code at all — which would make this more than cosmetic.

### Suggested fix

Make the duplicate callback harmless: keep a short-lived (`_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`) map of `broker_state → already-issued target` and, when a callback arrives for a `broker_state` whose pending entry was already consumed, respond `200` with a "Sign-in complete — return to the app" page (or 302 to the same target) instead of exchanging the consumed code and rendering `invalid_grant`. Same for the `/auth/native/token` replay path (`invalid_code_or_pkce`).

### Workaround

- Retry once; the app usually connects.
- Or use the app's **Password** method against `dashboard.basic_auth`, which avoids the browser flow entirely.

issues.body:
# Desktop folder picker + Projects on a REMOTE gateway: client-side paths, ENOENT, and a bad breadcrumb

**Reported by:** Bernard Heuse
**Date:** 2026-10-01
**Component:** Hermes Desktop (`apps/desktop`) — Projects, right-sidebar file picker, remote (registry) connections
**Versions:** desktop client `v0.21.5+4536`, backend `v0.21.5` (upstream `ea114c3e`, 2026.9.24)
**Platform:** Windows 11 both sides (desktop client and gateway backend)

---

## Topology (where this was observed)

| Role | Machine | Windows account | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop app (client) | `the client laptop` | `bheus` | app data under `C:\Users\bheus\AppData\Local\hermes\...` |
| Gateway + agent (backend) | `the gateway host` / `<gateway-lan-ip>` | `Bernard Heuse` | `HERMES_HOME` + `projects.db` live here; real repos in `C:\Users\Bernard Heuse\PycharmProjects\` and `E:\Data\Projects\` |

The desktop app connects to `the gateway host` as a **Remote gateway**. Sessions, projects, files and terminals are therefore supposed to be read from `the gateway host`.

---

## Summary

With a remote gateway, **"Open folder as project…" can end up associating a folder that belongs to the client machine, not to the machine the agent runs on** — and the folder picker itself can be *seeded* with such a client-side path, fail to read it on the backend, and then block the one button that would let the user continue.

Two distinct defects are involved:

1. **Seed path leak / no side validation.** `pickProjectFolder()` seeds the picker from the **connected backend** (`GET /api/fs/default-cwd`), and `/api/fs/default-cwd` returns the backend's config value `terminal.cwd` when that path is a directory *on the backend*. That config value can carry a **client-side path** (here `C:\Users\bheus\PycharmProjects`, a `the client laptop` path, present in the backend's `config.yaml`). Nothing validates that a folder submitted via the Command Center's "Open folder as project — <path>" row is meaningful on the backend either, so a project row can be created on the backend whose primary folder is a path that belongs to the client machine.

2. **Picker error state is a dead end.** When the seeded/read folder cannot be read on the backend, the dialog shows `Could not read this folder (ENOENT).` and **disables "Select folder"** while the error is displayed. The breadcrumb is computed by splitting the path on `/`, so a Windows path (`C:\Users\...`) yields no segments and the breadcrumb renders only `/` — the user cannot see where they are, and the obvious action (Select) is greyed out.

Verified artifact of defect 1 on the backend:

```
$ hermes project show pycharmprojects          # created from the desktop on the remote client
pycharmprojects  [p_9ce5f2da]
  name:    PycharmProjects
  primary: C:\Users\bheus\PycharmProjects      # <- client-side path, registered on `the gateway host`
  folders:
    * C:\Users\bheus\PycharmProjects
```

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Client (`the client laptop`, account `bheus`) → **Settings → Gateways → Remote gateway** → `the gateway host` (`<gateway-lan-ip>`). Sessions/projects come from `the gateway host`.
2. On `the gateway host`, have `terminal.cwd` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` point at a path that exists for the **client** account (here: `C:\Users\bheus\PycharmProjects`).
3. On the client, open the folder picker: **⌘/Ctrl+O**, Command Center → *Open folder as project…*, or right-sidebar **Files → Change working directory**.
4. The dialog **"Choose remote folder"** ("Browse folders on the connected backend") opens at that path.
5. `GET /api/fs/list?path=C%3A%5CUsers%5Cbheus%5CPycharmProjects` on `the gateway host` answers `{entries: [], error: "ENOENT"}`.
6. UI: red **"Could not read this folder (ENOENT)."**, folder list shows only `..`, breadcrumb shows only `/` (see screenshot), **"Select folder" disabled**.

## Observed

- The picker is seeded with a path that only makes sense on the client (or on a *different* account of the same box), and the read fails on the backend.
- `ENOENT` is displayed as-is; there is no "this folder does not exist on the gateway / pick another" affordance, no fallback to the gateway's home, and no way to type an absolute path inside the dialog.
- "Select folder" is disabled exactly while the error is shown, so the dialog cannot be used to recover from its own bad seed.
- Breadcrumb is unusable for Windows paths.
- A project can be created on the backend with a client-machine folder (artifact above), which later shows an unrelated/empty tree and breaks `Reveal in filetree` expectations.

## Expected

- The picker should only ever be seeded with a path that is valid **on the backend**; if the configured `terminal.cwd` doesn't exist there, fall back to the backend's home (or its process cwd) **and say so** instead of showing a raw `ENOENT`.
- The dialog should allow typing/pasting an absolute path and should never disable its primary action on a read error (allow navigation away).
- Breadcrumb/crumb computation should be path-flavour aware (handle `C:\...`, `\\server\share`, mixed separators) instead of splitting on `/` only.
- A folder submitted for a project on a **remote** connection should be validated against the gateway (and a client-looking path — e.g. one that resolves to a different home than the gateway's — should be rejected with a clear message).

## Code pointers (upstream `ea114c3e`)

| Location | What it does |
|---|---|
| `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts:1534` | `pickProjectFolder()` → `selectDesktopPaths({ defaultPath: (await desktopDefaultCwd())?.cwd, directories: true })`; `openFolderAsProject(dir)` at `:1550` uses a supplied path with no side validation |
| `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts:45` | `isDesktopFsRemoteMode()` = `$connection.get()?.mode === 'remote'` — the single switch between gateway FS and the local Electron bridge |
| `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts:162` | `desktopDefaultCwd()` → remote only → `GET /api/fs/default-cwd` |
| `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts:226` | `selectDesktopPaths()` → remote picker only when remote **and** `directories`; otherwise the native OS dialog; returns `[]` silently when no remote picker is mounted |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/files/remote-picker.tsx:57,94,262,277` | picker state; `setError(result.error)`; renders `unreadableBody(error)`; `disabled={newFolderName !== null \|\| Boolean(error)}` on the Select button |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/files/remote-picker.tsx:19,120` | `parentDir()` / crumb builder split the path on `/` — backslash Windows paths produce a single, wrong crumb |
| `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:649` | `GET /api/fs/list` → `os.scandir` → `OSError` mapped to a raw code (`ENOENT`) |
| `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:790` + `hermes_cli/web_server_files.py:232` | `fs_default_cwd()` → `_fs_default_cwd()`: returns config `terminal.cwd` when `is_dir()` **on the backend**, else `Path.cwd()` of the backend process |

## Workarounds

- On the **gateway machine**, point `terminal.cwd` at a directory that exists *there* (`hermes config set terminal.cwd "<path on the gateway>"`), so the picker seeds on a readable folder.
- Create the project from the **agent side** (the agent runs on the gateway, so its `projects.db` and paths are backend-side): `hermes project create "<name>" "<path> <path> ..."` (multi-folder) — no picker involved.
- In the Command Center, pasting an absolute path gives an *Open folder as project — <path>* row that bypasses the picker entirely (use a **gateway** path).

## Notes

- Local (non-remote) connections are unaffected: they take the native OS dialog (`selectDesktopPaths` early-returns to `desktop.selectPaths`).
- A folder can belong to only one project, so re-pointing a project at another directory requires removing/archiving the previous owner first.

issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS, `hermes update` can hang forever right after `→ Fetching updates...`, with 0% CPU. The updater's main thread is blocked writing to the stdin of its `git cat-file --batch` child, and that child is blocked writing its stdout back. Both pipes are full, so the two processes wait on each other forever. The `timeout=120` passed to `run_git` never fires, because the parent is stuck inside a blocking `write()` syscall rather than in the `communicate()` select loop.

Seen 5 times on two Macs: on Oct 11 and Oct 13 on one, and on three consecutive runs on Oct 14 on the other (3 out of 3 that day). Killing only the `git cat-file --batch` child unblocks it: the updater then runs to completion normally (receipt `outcome: success`, Desktop app rebuilt and installed).

## Environment

- Hermes v0.22.0 (`e06df9c2ea`) on one Mac, v0.21.6 → v0.21.7 on the other. Same hang on both.
- macOS 27.0 and 27.0.1, Apple silicon
- git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)
- Managed Python 3.14.7 (`~/.hermes/tools/python-3.14.7…`)
- Git checkout, `remote.origin.partialclonefilter=blob:none`, not shallow, about 0.4M to 1.0M packed objects
- Happens both when run interactively in Terminal (`hermes update`) and when run unattended (`hermes update --yes`)

## Process state while hung (macOS `sample`)

Updater (python3.14), main thread:

```
Py_RunMain → _PyEval_Vector → _TAIL_CALL_CALL_BUILTIN_FAST
  → os_write → _Py_write_impl → write   (libsystem_kernel)   [blocked]
```

The only other Python thread is the `_monitor` thread, idle in `SimpleQueue.get`.

Child, `git -c gc.autoDetach=false -c maintenance.auto=false cat-file --batch`:

```
batch_object_write → stream_blob → odb_stream_blob_to_fd → write_in_full → xwrite → write   [blocked]
```

`lsof` shows git's fd 0, 1 and 2 are pipes to the updater; the updater has no network sockets open. This is local, not a stalled fetch.

## Likely call site

`stream_blob` means git is streaming **blob** contents, which points to `hermes_cli/update_cmd_commit.py::read_target_files()`:

```python
cp = run_git(git_cmd, ["cat-file", "--batch"], cwd=str(root), input=request, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
```

It is reached from `target_syntax_error()` (the pre-move syntax preflight, via `update_cmd_git.py` / `_refuse_before_commit_point`) and from the recovery-closure read at `update_cmd_commit.py:256`. No new progress line is printed between `Fetching updates...` and this preflight, so the hang looks like a fetch hang.

On macOS outside a Windows update, `update_custody.run()` is a plain `subprocess.run(..., input=..., capture_output=True, timeout=...)`, so this is CPython's POSIX `_communicate()` path.

## Hypothesis (not confirmed)

POSIX `_communicate()` writes `input` in `select.PIPE_BUF` (512-byte) chunks to a blocking stdin pipe whenever the selector reports it writable. If the kqueue selector reports a pipe writable with fewer than 512 bytes free, a 512-byte write is atomic under POSIX and blocks. The loop then never gets back to draining stdout. Meanwhile git has already filled stdout with large blob contents and blocks too. One thing doesn't fit, which is why this is unconfirmed: the request is only about 1 to 2 KB, so the stdin pipe shouldn't be full unless the pipe buffer is much smaller than the 16 KB `lsof` reports. On one machine, the same `cat-file --batch` calls run in isolation finished in under 3 seconds.

## Possible fixes

- Don't stream full blob contents through a pipe that is also being written: feed `cat-file --batch` from a temporary file (`stdin=open(tmpfile)`), or read each blob with `cat-file blob <oid>` or `--batch-command` with explicit flushes.
- Or write stdin from a separate thread, so stdout and stderr are always being drained.
- Either way, a watchdog that kills the child on the wall-clock timeout, independent of the parent's syscall state, would make the existing `TimeoutExpired` handling ("Syntax preflight skipped") actually fire.

## Workaround

While `hermes update` is stuck, in another terminal run:

```
pkill -f "cat-file --batch"
```

The updater then continues and finishes on its own.

Related but different: #124794 (recursive fetch process trees on tree:0 clones with git < 2.44).

prs.title: fix(pm): a virtual plugin's own-extra references follow its workspace rename
prs.body:
PM gives a plugin with no build backend a unique `hermes-plugin-…` name inside the update workspace, but the plugin's own `myplugin[runtime]` line kept the old name. So uv went looking for a different package called `myplugin`, which either failed the update and switched the plugin off, or quietly installed whatever package already had that name, and the plugin's extra never got installed.

**Stacked on #148199 (merge after it).** This branch starts at #148199's head `855180ba214`, because that PR adds the self-reference extras closure this fix has to stay in step with. The diff to review is the single top commit.

## Before / after (real `pm.sync_venv(explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)`, scratch HOME, pinned Python 3.14 PBS)

The fixture is a virtual plugin (no `[build-system]`) with `dependencies = ["pyjokes==0.6.0", "<own name>[runtime]"]` and `runtime = ["pyfiglet==1.0.2"]`.

| leg | own name not on any index (`probe-selfref`) | own name served by PyPI (`six`) | control (no self-reference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `45219aa35c2` | lock fails: `there are no versions of probe-selfref[runtime] and hermes-plugin-probe-absent-… depends on probe-selfref[runtime]`, then `⚠ Disabled plugin 'probe-absent'` (moved to `plugins.disabled`) | sync OK, member keeps `"six[runtime]"`, **pyfiglet not installed** | n/a |
| #148199 head `855180ba214` | same lock failure, plugin disabled | same: `"six[runtime]"`, pyfiglet not installed | sync OK, pyjokes + pyfiglet installed |
| this PR | sync OK, plugin stays enabled; member has `"hermes-plugin-probe-absent-…[runtime]"`; pyjokes 0.6.0 + pyfiglet 1.0.2 installed | sync OK; `"hermes-plugin-probe-pypi-…[runtime]"`; pyfiglet 1.0.2 installed | unchanged: sync OK, pyjokes + pyfiglet installed |

## Change

- `pm/workspace.py`: new `_rename_virtual_member` renames the project and every reference to its own declared name (matched with `canonicalize_name`) in `dependencies`, `optional-dependencies` and `tool.uv.conflicts` `package` entries. Extras, specifiers and markers are kept as written; only the leading name changes. It runs before #148199's `_runtime_member_metadata`, so `_selected_member_extras` follows the renamed references (installed vs. named-only extras still work, including marker-false ones). Buildable members (with a build backend or `tool.uv.package = true`) keep their declared name and are not touched.
- Docs: one sentence in `package-management.md`.

## Tests

- `test_virtual_plugin_self_reference_installs_its_own_extra_after_the_rename`: a real offline `uv lock` + `uv sync`. On base the environment gets `other_dep` (the stale self-reference resolved from the index) and no `chosen_dep` (the extra). It passes on head.
- `test_virtual_plugin_self_references_follow_the_rename_everywhere`: checks that extras, markers, conflicts and the extras closure stay intact.
- Both fail on `855180ba214` and pass on head. `tests/pm/test_workspace.py`, `test_member_selection.py`, `test_environment_build.py` and `test_plugin_declarations.py` give 65 passed. Runs came from a `git ls-files` copy under a fake HOME.

## Infographic

![virtual-plugin-self-reference](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0ea4d/p8rW-qaKJhIYmAlfW5uEz_ka2w2RFB.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): align macOS window controls with a taller header
prs.body:
## Problem
The native traffic lights share a compact 34-pixel header with the toolbar. Upstream now uses a 12-point left inset, which this PR retains. The adjacent toolbar also has a separate OS-version-specific vertical nudge. This crowds the header and separates the native controls from the toolbar centerline.

## Change
- Use a 44-CSS-pixel native macOS header while retaining the upstream 12-point left inset.
- Share title-bar metrics between Electron and renderer layout.
- Keep native traffic lights centered in the header at each page scale; preserve their native size.
- Convert native coordinates to CSS pixels and reserve the native cluster's width correctly under zoom.
- Remove the separate vertical nudge. Keep Sessions/Bots below the native-controls band.
- Keep non-macOS and browser-hosted header heights unchanged.

The explicit native position is retained because the app scales its custom header. This is not a claim that Apple specifies these exact coordinates.

## Verification
- The native Electron regression fails on the base (34-pixel sidebar offset instead of the proposed 44-pixel band).
- Native macOS E2E passes at 50%, 80%, 100%, and 125% page scale, checks toolbar/native-controls center alignment and horizontal clearance, and enters/exits fullscreen.
- Inspected native window captures, including the actual traffic lights (not renderer-only screenshots).
- 26 related component/unit tests, production desktop build, renderer and Electron type checks, changed-file ESLint, and all 14 `scripts/check` checks pass.
- Used an isolated test profile and a mock inference provider. No personal conversations were used.

Not tested on pre-Tahoe macOS. This PR does not change sidebar tab widths or remove the duplicate sidebar collapse arrow; that is a separate PR.

prs.title: fix(kanban): opt-in protocol retry holds instead of permanent sticky block (#108927)
prs.body:
## Problem

Fixes #108927. The kanban circuit breaker treats a worker that exits cleanly without a kanban
transition (a protocol violation) like any other failure. After `failure_limit` (3) attempts it
sticky-blocks the card for good. When the cause is transient infrastructure (a gateway disconnect,
or a provider wall that clears an hour later), nothing retries the card after the cause clears.

## Change

- Opt-in config `kanban.protocol_violation_actions` (default `{}`), shaped
  `{board_slug: {assignee_profile: "block" | "defer"}}`. A missing or invalid policy keeps today's
  sticky-block behaviour exactly.
- When `defer` is configured and protocol exhaustion is reached, one transaction keeps the crashed
  run, moves the task to `scheduled`, and records a `protocol_retry_held` event plus a
  `task_retry_holds` row. Default behaviour and every other failure kind are unchanged.
- Fenced public APIs in `hermes_cli.kanban_db`: `get_retry_hold`, `adopt_protocol_failure` (CAS on
  failed run id, failure event id and body sha256), and resume and retire through a single-use hold
  token, recorded in `task_retry_hold_resolutions`.
- Bounded, runtime-owned route provenance on the failure record (`cli_single_query.py`,
  `hermes_state_usage.py`). Unknown values are explicit; auxiliary calls, credentials and URLs are
  excluded.
- New logic lives in a sibling `kanban_retry_holds`; the facades only gain call sites.

## Tests

- Red on the base: `test_opted_in_protocol_exhaustion_creates_one_scheduled_hold` saw `blocked`
  instead of `scheduled` after three clean exits.
- Hold creation failing midway rolls back and keeps the sticky block; the existing streak
  regression tests follow the helper.
- Local focused A/B against the previous base: candidate 2,157 passed / 0 failed, base 1,837
  passed / 0 failed. In both legs the only problem was the runner's 600 s per-file timeout on an
  overloaded host. The timed-out roundtrip file passes alone (331 tests).
- A later local run, on a heavily loaded host, had 8 setup errors in
  `tests/test_native_codex_app_server_faults.py` (gateway connection setup) that I have not
  classified. CI on this exact head is the comparison.

## Not verified

- An A/B against the current `main`. The branch is 33 commits behind and merges cleanly

prs.title: fix(matrix): make the E2EE dependency closure an opt-in [matrix-e2ee] extra
prs.body:
### Problem

`[matrix]` — the extra PM syncs for the Matrix gateway — pinned `mautrix[encryption]==0.21.1` on Linux unconditionally, which pulls `python-olm`. That package is archived (last release 3.2.16, Nov 2023) and its newest wheels are cp37–cp312; Hermes runs Python 3.14, so **every** deployment — every OS, every architecture — builds a C++ extension from sdist. E2EE, meanwhile, is off unless it is asked for: `MATRIX_E2EE_MODE` defaults to `off`, legacy `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION` is unset, and the adapter is explicitly designed to degrade to a plain client without `mautrix[encryption]`.

So the *default* Matrix deployment pays for a disabled feature:

- **Hosts without a compiler** (the common case on a fresh machine): the update's dependency step fails every run and never converges:

```
✗ Installing Python dependencies failed; last 78 lines of output:
    Building python-olm==3.2.16
    × Failed to build `python-olm==3.2.16`
    error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'clang++'
  ⚠ Could not install matrix for configured features: venv: uv sync exited 1
  ⚠ Configured features whose dependencies are still missing — the gateway will fail to load them on restart:
    - Matrix: pip install 'mautrix[encryption]'
```

- **Silencing that costs disk:** llvm-18 + clang + cmake — **~690 MB** measured on a Debian box — installed to compile a crypto library for a bot that will never use it.
- **Resource-limited hosts pay the most.** On an aarch64 NanoPi R3S (1.9 GB RAM, SD-card storage) with the `matrix` extra selected, the same build shows up in its update log (`× Failed to build python-olm==3.2.16`, `⚠ Could not install matrix for configured features`), and where it does succeed it is a from-sdist C++ compile on a 2 GB board, re-run whenever the uv cache misses or is pruned. A device that cannot compile at all has to add a toolchain (build-essential or clang — hundreds of MB on a small SD card) to make `hermes update` stop erroring. Absolute artifact sizes are small (2.7 MB sdist, ~10 MB build tree, 224 KB installed); the build *requirement* on constrained hardware is the real cost.
- **It never converges:** this is not a transient failure. The dependency stays unbuildable until a compiler exists, so every `hermes update` re-downloads, re-attempts the build and re-prints the warning — for a feature that is switched off.

### Rebased onto `upstream/main` @ `f0d94882` (2026-11-02)

Upstream has since shipped the adjacent fix: `[matrix]`'s own deps now carry `sys_platform == 'linux'` markers, so the win/darwin bundle lanes stop building `python-olm`, and the macOS/Windows half of #132820 is addressed. The Linux half this PR is about is not: a Linux host still resolves the encryption closure for a feature that is off by default — `[matrix]` and `[matrix-e2ee]` are not split, nothing installs the closure on demand, and the adapter still tells the operator to `pip install 'mautrix[encryption]'` by hand (`_E2EE_INSTALL_HINT`). Two conflicts came from that upstream change; both were resolved by keeping upstream's markers and rationale and adding this PR's extra on top, so no upstream line was dropped.

### Change

Extras are static in `pyproject.toml`, so "use E2EE or not" has to be expressed as *which extras are selected*. The encryption closure moves into its own opt-in extra, selected by the existing config knob:

| Deployment | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=off` (default) | python-olm resolved and built | plain SDK only — no compiler, no crypto dep |
| `MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=optional` / `required` | python-olm resolved and built | `[matrix-e2ee]` installed on demand |

- **`pyproject.toml`** — `[matrix]` keeps the plain SDK (`mautrix`, `asyncpg`, `aiosqlite`, `aiohttp-socks`, `aiohttp`); new `[matrix-e2ee]` carries `mautrix[encryption]==0.21.1`, gated `sys_platform == 'linux'` in `[tool.hermes.extras-platforms]` and listed in `[tool.hermes] opt-in-extras` so no `[all]`/`--all-extras` build ever resolves it. The Linux-only markers upstream added to `[matrix]` itself are kept unchanged; this PR only moves the encryption closure out of it.
- **`plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`** — `_ensure_e2ee_deps()` installs `[matrix-e2ee]` only when `_resolve_e2ee_mode() != "off"` (best-effort: a failure stays a warning in `optional` mode and stays fail-closed in `required`); `matrix_deps_present()` (the passive probe) now reports not-ready for a `required`-mode deployment whose closure is missing; `_extra_names()` declares `["matrix"]` or `["matrix", "matrix-e2ee"]` for the updater; `interactive_setup()` prepares the extra when the operator answers yes to the E2EE question; the install hint becomes `hermes pm install --extra matrix-e2ee`.
- **`gateway/platform_registry.py`** — new optional `PlatformEntry.extra_names_fn: Callable[[], Sequence[str]] | None` (None falls back to `[name]`) so a platform can declare config-dependent extras.
- **`hermes_cli/main_install_repair.py`** — configured-features rows carry a *tuple* of extras and a row is only considered resolved when all of its extras installed (`sync_venv` unions with recorded extras, so `[matrix]`'s asyncpg/aiosqlite stay).
- **`pm/extras.py`** — `ANCHORS["matrix-e2ee"] = "olm"`.
- **`Dockerfile`** — the image bakes `--extra matrix --extra matrix-e2ee`, preserving encrypted-room support in published containers.
- **Docs** — `matrix.md` (en + zh-Hans) E2EE requirements/fallback sections.
- **`uv.lock`** — regenerated with `hermes pm lock`; the diff is the new extra plus uv re-serializing `[options.exclude-newer-package]`. No package version changes.

### Migration

Nothing to do. E2EE-off deployments already ran the plain client. E2EE deployments get `[matrix-e2ee]` at the next gateway start (`ensure_matrix_deps`) and proactively from the update's configured-features pass; `hermes setup` installs it when E2EE is enabled. `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION=true` still maps to `required`.

### Verification

- **Install graph, pre- vs post-change** (scratch copy of `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`, `uv sync --extra matrix --dry-run --no-install-project`):
  - before: `Would download 25 packages`, `Would install 83 packages`, `+ python-olm==3.2.16`
  - after: `Would download 21 packages`, `Would install 79 packages`, no `python-olm`
  - after, `--extra matrix-e2ee` and `--extra matrix --extra matrix-e2ee`: python-olm still planned (83 installs) — E2EE is intact.
- **Lockfile**: `uv.lock` regenerated with uv **0.12.13** (the version pinned in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`), so `uv lock --check` passes on this branch. Content delta is only the mautrix split (`mautrix` under `matrix`, `mautrix[encryption]` under `matrix-e2ee`) plus `matrix-e2ee` in `provides-extras`; no package versions change. The lock's `revision` goes 5 → 3 and `default-groups = []` disappears, because 0.12.13 serialises the older format while `main`'s lock was written by a newer uv — stated here rather than left for a reviewer to spot in the diff.
- **Plugin registration** (`3306fe658b`): `register()` no longer passes `allowed_users_env=` / `allow_all_env=` inline — `**gateway_env.AUTHZ` is the single source. The inline pair collided with the dict (upstream added it after this branch's shape), and `register_platform()` raised `got multiple values for keyword argument 'allowed_users_env'`; the plugin loader swallowed it, so Matrix never entered `platform_registry` and the updater skipped it as `entry is None`. Verified with a stub ctx: 28 kwargs registered, both authz values present. Nothing in the suite calls `register()`, which is why the first push shipped it broken.
- **Tests** (head `3306fe65`, install venv python, `PYTHONPATH=.`, `-p no:cacheprovider`): `tests/gateway/test_matrix_deps_rebind.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_missing_configured_deps.py` + `tests/test_project_metadata.py` → **18 passed, 2 failed, 2 errors**. Control on a clean worktree of `upstream/main` @ `f0d94882` with the same interpreter: **identical 2 failed + 2 errors** (8 passed), so those four are environmental and not this PR — two `test_matrix_deps_rebind` cases assume `mautrix` is uninstalled while the test venv has the real package, and the two `test_update_missing_configured_deps` errors are the `isolated_python` fixture refusing Python 3.11.15 against the repo's `==3.14.*` requirement. Net effect of the branch: **+10 passing tests, zero new failures**. The full suite still needs a PM-built env (`pm.build_env --out .venv --group dev --group test`); CI runs it.

### Not in scope

- Relaxing the Linux-only gate on `[matrix]`: with the crypto closure gone, plain Matrix plausibly builds on Windows/macOS too, but that is a platform-support decision (tests currently assert Matrix is hidden on Windows) and deserves its own change.
- Dropping the libolm/build-toolchain packages from the Docker image: only `[matrix-e2ee]` needs them now.

prs.title: fix(pm): lock plugin workspaces with root-named deps and non-default groups
prs.body:
## Summary

`hermes plugins install <plugin> --yes-deps` fails to lock the generated plugin workspace for any plugin whose dependency tables name the core package (live repro: the `honcho` catalog plugin). Two independent bugs in the workspace member snapshot:

1. **Missing workspace source for root-named deps.** A member declaring `hermes-agent @ git+…` (e.g. in `[dependency-groups]`) generated a workspace where that name had no `[tool.uv.sources]` entry, and uv rejects the lock: *"is included as a workspace member, but is missing an entry in tool.uv.sources"*. Fix: `_core_project_name()` resolves the root project name from the core source and `_bind_root_named_dependency()` binds such deps to `{ workspace = true }`.
2. **Non-default dependency-groups poison the solve.** uv locks *every* group of every workspace member, but PM only ever syncs default groups. Honcho's `test` group pins `pytest-asyncio==1.3.0` while core `dev` pins `1.4.0` — unsatisfiable. Fix: member snapshots keep only the default PEP 735 groups (`tool.uv.default-groups`, default `["dev"]`); non-default groups are stripped.

## Test plan

- New regression test `test_member_group_or_extra_naming_the_root_gets_a_workspace_source` reproduces both failure modes (red on base, green after fix).
- `tests/pm/test_member_selection.py` call sites updated for the new `core_source` parameter of `_workspace_member`.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/test_workspace.py tests/pm/test_member_selection.py` green; `python scripts/check` clean (14 checks, 0 blocking/advisory).
- Full `tests/pm/` failure profile unchanged vs base (pre-existing host issues only).
- Live end-to-end: `hermes plugins install honcho --yes-deps` against the real core source now locks, syncs and reports installed.

prs.title: fix(pm): strip optional-dependencies and dependency-groups from virtual workspace members
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #123864.

When preparing a virtual (metadata-only) workspace member in `pm/workspace.py::_workspace_member()`, `[project.optional-dependencies]` and `[dependency-groups]` are now stripped from the member's `pyproject.toml`. 

Virtual plugin workspace members are metadata-only bridges: their internal test extras (e.g. `dev = ["pytest>=8,<9"]`) and dependency groups exist only for running their own repository test suites and are never installed by PM. However, `uv lock` attempts to lock all workspace member extras, which caused resolution conflicts with core `[dependency-groups] dev` pins (e.g. `pytest==9.1.1`). Stripping these tables for virtual members prevents third-party plugin test extras from wedging the composed workspace resolution during `hermes update`.

## Test Plan
- Added `test_virtual_member_strips_optional_dependencies_and_dependency_groups` in `tests/pm/test_member_selection.py`.

prs.title: fix(pm): plugin dev/test extras and dependency groups no longer fail the update lock (salvage #138071)
prs.body:
A plugin's test-only pins (for example `dev = ["httpx<0.28"]`) were being solved together with Hermes's own pins, so one that disagreed with a core pin made the whole dependency lock fail and `hermes update` switched the plugin off. PM never installs those pins, so they now stay out of the lock: the plugin keeps working and its real runtime dependencies are installed.

Salvages #138071 (dependency-groups, by @hteo1337; cherry-picked, authorship kept, its `handoffs/STATUS.md` dropped) and widens it to optional-dependency extras, which is the case in #123864 / #123960.

## Before / after (real `pm.sync_venv(explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)`, scratch HOME, real uv)

Core pins `httpx[socks]==0.28.1`. Each plugin depends on `pyjokes==0.6.0`.

| Plugin pyproject | main @ 45219aa | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| extra `dev = ["httpx<0.28"]` | **evicted**: `disabled_by_update: probe-extra … hermes-plugin-probe-extra-…[dev] depends on httpx<0.28 … unsatisfiable`; pyjokes not installed | enabled; pyjokes 0.6.0 installed; no `<0.28` in uv.lock |
| groups `dev = ["httpx<0.28"]`, `test = ["httpx<0.27"]` | **evicted** (`…:dev depends on httpx<0.28`) | enabled; pyjokes installed; no `<0.2x` in lock |
| buildable (hatchling) + extra `dev` + extra `figlet` + group `lint` | **evicted** (`probe-buildable … httpx<0.28`) | enabled; package `probe_buildable-1.0.0` built and installed; pyjokes installed |
| `sync_venv(["figlet"])` with extras `figlet = ["pyfiglet==1.0.2"]` + `dev = ["httpx<0.28"]` | **sync raised** `ResolutionConflict … uv lock exited 1` | OK; pyfiglet 1.0.2 **installed** (selected plugin extra still works); dev pin absent |
| control (no extras/groups) | enabled, pyjokes installed | identical |

## What changed

`pm/workspace.py::_runtime_member_metadata` shapes the generated member snapshot (the plugin's own files are untouched):

- **dependency-groups, `tool.uv.dev-dependencies`, `default-groups`** — dropped (from #138071). Verified with uv 0.12.3 and 0.13.5: core's `default-groups = []` applies workspace-wide, so `uv sync --all-packages` never installs a member's groups.
- **optional-dependencies** — keeps only the extras this generation selects (`uv sync --extra NAME` applies the name to every member declaring it, so `hermes pm install --extra <plugin extra>` keeps working), plus extras the plugin's own requirements name (`plugin[runtime]`, closed transitively). Everything else (`dev`, `test`, `lint` …) is dropped.
- `tool.uv.conflicts` entries pointing at removed groups/extras are dropped.

The selected extras are already part of the environment stamp, so a different selection produces a new generation with the matching snapshot. Repair replays the recorded snapshot unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_plugin_local_groups_do_not_constrain_runtime_workspace` (from #138071; now locks with the extra it expects to keep selected)
- `test_unselected_plugin_extras_do_not_constrain_runtime_workspace` — a `dev` extra pinning `base-dep==2.0` against core's `base-dep==1.0` locks, and the extra is kept once selected
- `test_plugin_extras_its_own_requirements_name_stay_in_the_snapshot` — buildable member, `Plugin_Member[Runtime]` → `runtime` → `extra-io` kept, `dev` dropped

All three red on main's `pm/workspace.py`, green here. `tests/pm` full run (from a tree copy, fake HOME): main 1018 passed / 1 failed, head 1021 passed / same 1 failed (`test_cold_runtime_e2e[python3.11]`, host env). `scripts/check --only health` clean.

## Not covered

- Extras a plugin declares as `dynamic` (computed by its build backend) cannot be filtered statically.
- One plugin depending on *another* plugin's extra (`other-plugin[feat]`) is not followed.
- A plugin whose pyproject has only groups/extras (no dependencies) still counts as a member asking consent (`pm/plugin_declarations.py`, owned by #148191); it now installs nothing.

## Infographic

![plugin-test-pins-stay-out-of-the-lock](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0e92b/nnW_wAAlOOGm1tIaSOHbO_HIWGHeQl.png)

prs.title: catalog: tabella 2.0.3 — bootstrap fix, dependency remediation, ODT table fix
prs.body:
SHA bump for tabella 2.0.3: `449e754` → `4a9a47a` (release-lane merge commit; tagged `2.0.3`).

**Why a release rather than a routine bump.** Two defects shipped in 2.0.2 that a new user met immediately, plus a data-loss bug:

- **The default install did not bootstrap.** With `PLUGIN_DATA` unset, first run returned `~/.venvs/docs/bin/python` while `scripts/setup.sh` created `~/.venvs/docs/venv/bin/python`; the re-exec check silently skipped and every tool failed to import. One resolver owns the path now, and CI runs a cold-bootstrap job (empty `HOME`, no `PLUGIN_DATA`) that imports every documented dependency through the interpreter the bootstrap returns.
- **Three vulnerable dependencies, two pinned out of their own fixes:** pillow 12.3.0 → 13.0.0 (59 advisories), weasyprint 69.0 → 70.0 (EPS→Ghostscript RCE, SSRF), brotli 1.2.0 → 1.2.1 (OOB write). The EPS path was reachable through `data:` URIs, which the fetcher previously allowed unconditionally; it now allowlists image/font types and refuses PostScript payloads by magic number under any label, so the property survives a future weasyprint regression. `scripts/relock.py` regenerates the hash lock in one command.
- **ODT tables lost every cell value** behind `{"success": true}`; values are written now and ragged input no longer drops cells.

**Range being adopted** (`449e754..4a9a47a`, 2 commits plus the release-lane merge): a pytest lane on every PR (54 tests), the bootstrap fix, the dependency remediation, the ODT fix, and version surfaces aligned at 2.0.3.

**Verification:** `pytest` and cold-`bootstrap` jobs green on the release head; `windows-smoke` green on the same tree (five lanes, including pdf-from-html through WeasyPrint 70 with the new hash lock); PyPI `tabella-docs` 2.0.3 published; `validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes.

Two independent review rounds preceded the release. Each finding was reproduced before it was fixed and re-tested after; the second round caught that the first PostScript sniffer decoded differently from the consumer and let three wrappers through, which is why the check is now byte-exact and covered by tests.

Note: this touches only `sha` and `version`. The description rewrite is a separate open PR (#141476); whichever merges second will need a trivial rebase.

Adds Hermes Flow to the community plugin catalog. It reconstructs recorded Hermes session metadata as a local graph and terminal tree, and can compare runs against an editable trusted-path baseline.

prs.title: fix(pm): pin Chromium to Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.80
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Chromium Hermes ships was Chrome for Testing 145.0.7632.6, directory `chromium-1208`. That build is from about 17 January 2026. Current stable is 156.0.8078.80.

This pin moves the packaged browser to 156.0.8078.80 and names the store directory `chromium-1248`. Playwright 1.64.0 stays at 1.64.0. It finds a browser by that directory name and does not check the Chrome patch number. Its own Chromium is 156.0.8078.4, which is older than the 156.0.8078.73 stable update, so a Playwright bump would not land on the patched build.

The 156.0.8078.73 stable update fixed these public Chrome bugs. All four are rated Critical.

- CVE-2026-118306: memory corruption in FileSystem. A crafted HTML page could run code outside the sandbox.
- CVE-2026-118331: improper input validation in FileAPI.
- CVE-2026-118348: improper input validation in Skia.
- CVE-2026-118344: use after free in Layout.

These reports are already public. This is a pin bump, not a Hermes advisory.

linux-arm64 used to come from Playwright's revision mirror. The mirror build for revision 1248 is still 156.0.8078.4. Chrome for Testing now publishes linux-arm64, so that target downloads 156.0.8078.80 with the others. The archive is `chrome-linux-arm64/chrome`. The desktop sandbox probe matches `chrome-linux*/chrome`, which covers that path and the older `chrome-linux` and `chrome-linux64` layouts.

prs.title: fix(aux): resolve a named custom provider key_env from the profile .env
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Aux resolves a named custom provider's `key_env` credential through `_scoped_key_env()` → `get_secret()`. When the task's secret scope is empty or bound to a foreign profile, `serves_routed_profile()` is true and the scope deliberately refuses the `os.environ` fallback and returns its default `""` — even though the profile's `.env` is the very file that scope was built from. The key therefore reads as absent, `resolve_provider_client()` logs

```
resolve_provider_client: named custom provider 'newapi' has no resolvable api_key — request will be sent with placeholder no-key-required and will 401 on auth-required endpoints
```

and the request goes out with the literal `no-key-required`, which 401s on any auth-required endpoint. In a gateway this fires from the vision auto-detect probe at every start (issue #86446).

This PR reads the profile `.env` with the canonical tokenizer (`load_env_file`) before giving up. That is the same parser the scope is built from, memoised on the file's bytes, and total — an absent/unreadable file yields `{}` rather than raising, so no credential is ever invented and the placeholder path is unchanged.

The credential ladder also moves to `agent/auxiliary_custom_key.py` (re-exported from `auxiliary_client`) — `auxiliary_client.py` is already over its line cap, and `scripts/check` blocks any growth there. Behaviour and precedence are otherwise identical.

## Related Issue

Fixes #86446

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/auxiliary_custom_key.py` (new) — `profile_dotenv_key()` plus the moved `_named_custom_api_key()` ladder (inline `api_key` → `key_env` → `key_cmd` → credential pool → placeholder).
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` — imports `_named_custom_api_key` from the new module (public name unchanged, existing imports/tests keep working); net −30 lines.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py` — new `TestNamedCustomKeyEnvDotenvFallback` (3 tests: `.env` fallback, bound-scope precedence, unchanged placeholder).

## How to Test

Reproduce before the fix — under an empty scope plus multiplex, a `key_env` that only the profile `.env` defines resolves to the placeholder:

```python
from agent import secret_scope as ss
from agent.auxiliary_client import _named_custom_api_key

ss.set_secret_scope({}, profile_home="/home/you/.hermes")   # empty scope, as aux sees at startup
ss.set_multiplex_context(True)
entry = {"name": "newapi", "base_url": "https://newapi.example/v1", "key_env": "NEW_API_KEY"}
print(_named_custom_api_key(entry, "newapi", entry["base_url"]))
# before: no-key-required        after: the value defined in ~/.hermes/.env
```

Regression tests:

```
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py -k DotenvFallback
```

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(kanban): name the missing skill and profile when a card cannot boot
prs.body:
## Problem

A Kanban card's `skills` resolve from the **assignee profile's** own skill tree, but nothing said so at either end of the handoff:

- `kanban_create` stored `skills` unvalidated, so a typo — or a skill that only lives in the creator's profile — produced a card that could never run;
- the boot check raised a bare `ValueError('kanban_skills_unavailable')`;
- the submitter ignored what the run had recorded and printed `Kanban owner refused: Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner`.

In a live deployment a card naming one skill that only another profile carried burned its whole dispatch-failure budget (four runs, ~7 s each) with only the opaque transport message visible. The actual cause never left a profile log.

## Fix

1. **Self-describing boot failure.** `gateway/session_kanban._run_task_turns` raises `KanbanSkillsUnavailable` naming every missing skill and the assignee profile:

   `kanban_skills_unavailable: home-assistant-operations missing on profile 'fabro'`

   `_run_worker_turns` records that composed text on the attempt's `worker_result` event, so it reaches `task_runs.error` as well as the submitter's console line. Only this engine-composed message is persisted — never arbitrary runtime exception text, which can carry credentials.

2. **Validate at creation.** `hermes_cli/kanban_skills.py` is the one resolver for "can the assignee profile load this?" (its own skill roots, no creator project dirs, plugin skills skipped). Both the `kanban_create` tool and `hermes kanban create` refuse the card with a non-zero exit naming the skill and profile; no card is created. A resolver *failure* is logged, never fatal: the boot check still reports what the worker cannot load.

3. **Stop swallowing the reason.** `kanban_worker_client._exit_code` reads the attempt's `worker_result` before falling back on the receipt. When the run recorded a failure, the submitter raises/prints that text (`Kanban execution failed: kanban_skills_unavailable: …`) instead of "execution unknown". The console prefix is now `Kanban dispatch failed:`, not the misleading `Kanban owner refused:`.

## Decision: an all-missing skill list remains a hard boot failure

A worker that silently runs without the instructions its card demanded would execute the task against the wrong assumptions and report success — worse than a named boot error. With fix 1 in place the error names what to install and where. A *partially* resolvable list is unchanged: the turn runs with the skills that loaded.

## Verification

**RED on base `bfa652fa`** (tests copied unchanged onto a clean base clone): 4 files, 16 passed, **6 failed** — exactly the six new behaviour tests:
```
FAILED tests/gateway/test_kanban_skills_unavailable.py (2)
FAILED tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_create_skills_validation.py (2)
FAILED tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_recorded_failure.py (1)
FAILED tests/gateway/test_session_kanban.py::test_real_dispatcher_names_missing_skills_in_the_run_error (1)
```
The E2E failure's recorded run error on base is literally the incident text:
`... Kanban owner refused: Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner`

**GREEN on the pushed head** (fresh clone of the branch, outside any worktree/home override):

- focused: `4 files, 22 tests passed` — includes the E2E through the real dispatcher, owner, managed worker and submitter;
- kanban engine sweep (`tests/**/*kanban*.py`): `145 files, 1000 tests passed, 1 failed, 28 skipped`.
  The one failure is `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, which fails identically on base `bfa652fa` (reproduced there: `1 failed, 54 deselected`) and is untouched by this diff.
- real CLI:
  ```
  $ hermes kanban create "PROBE" --assignee adapter --skill nowhere-skill
  kanban: profile 'adapter' cannot load skill(s) 'nowhere-skill': not in that profile's skill tree, …
  [exit 2]
  $ hermes kanban list
  (no matching tasks)
  $ hermes kanban create "VALID" --assignee adapter --skill good-skill
  Created t_…  (ready, assignee=adapter)   [exit 0]
  ```
- `scripts/check --only health --base <upstream main>`: 11 files, 0 blocking, 0 advisory; `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.

## Merge notes

- Two commits on top of `main` at `bfa652fa` (rebased; no unrelated commit carried over).
- Rebased over the newer owner-retry/`_await_receipt` refactor in `kanban_worker_client.py`: the recorded-error logic lives in `_exit_code`, the single place a fresh or reconnected receipt settles. The retry/backoff semantics are untouched.
- PR only — no deploy, and the running deployment was not modified.

prs.title: feat(prompt): one short sentence before tool work where interim text reaches the user
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Where Hermes delivers interim assistant text, the agent gets one short line in the stable tier of its system prompt. Concretely, that is when `interim_assistant_callback` is set at the time the prompt is first built. The line tells the model that text written before a tool call is shown at once, and asks for one plain sentence of intent before tool work, in the same response as the calls.

```
Text you write before a tool call is shown to the user right away, while the tools run. Before tool work, write one
short plain sentence saying what you are about to do, then make the tool calls in the same response; on longer work,
add a one-line update when you find something, change course or get blocked. One line per batch of tool work, not
narration of each call.
```

### Why

On messaging platforms the gateway already posts any text in a tool-call message as an interim message (`agent/turn_tool_round.py` → `_emit_interim_assistant_message`, gated by `display.interim_assistant_messages`). Nothing tells the model so, and the identity says "no narrating tool calls the user can see". Models without a native commentary channel therefore stay silent until the turn ends, which can take minutes when tools are slow. The user sees only the gateway's tool-progress line.

**Measured on one production profile** (Claude Opus 5.5, Telegram), counting tool turns whose first tool-call message carried text:

| Condition | Tool turns with a sentence before the tools |
|---|---|
| No instruction (4 days of real traffic) | **0 of 69** |
| A system-prompt line like this one (first hours after deploy, real traffic plus two test turns) | 3 of 4; both turns longer than 15 s (287 s and 345 s) had one |

**Offline, on a replica of a real slow lookup turn:**

| Prompt | Turns with a sentence before the tools |
|---|---|
| A variant that let the model skip "a single quick lookup" | 0 of 6 |
| Without that exception | 4 of 6 |

That is why this text has no lookup exception.

Anthropic's Opus 5.5 prompting guide recommends this lever: a one-line statement of intent before the first tool call.

### Where it applies

The gate is the existing callback, checked when the prompt is built. The gateway already resolves `display.interim_assistant_messages` per platform into that callback, including the Mattermost opt-in, webhook off, heartbeat off and `-q`/`-z`.

**Gets the line:**
- Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, WhatsApp, Feishu;
- low-tier platforms when an operator turns interim messages on;
- interactive CLI through the gateway route;
- TUI and desktop;
- `api_server` `/v1/runs` and `/v1/responses`.

**Does not:**
- cron, curator, delegate subagents (they have no callback);
- platforms with interim messages off;
- sessions whose prompt is first built on a webhook or heartbeat turn (no callback at that build).

**Caveats:**
- ACP and streaming chat/completions show text through deltas and have no callback, so they do not get the line. That is the safe direction.
- The prompt is stored per session, so a setting change takes effect at the next rebuild, as for any other prompt input.

### Details

- **Placement:** a separate constant appended at the end of `_guidance_parts`. Existing stable-tier bytes keep their order, and `DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY` and SOUL.md are untouched. This does not overlap #112073, which edits the identity line.
- **No new config key:** the line follows `display.interim_assistant_messages`, which already decides whether the callback exists.
- **TUI:** the TUI clears the callback between turns, and a live `/model` switch rebuilds and persists the prompt between turns (`tui_gateway/server.py` `_persist_live_session_system_prompt`). That rebuild now runs inside `interim_preamble_surface(...)`, a context manager over a `ContextVar` set from the session's interim setting. The gate accepts it, so a model switch does not drop the line. The live callback is never touched, because a heartbeat or loop turn can start on another thread while the switch runs. The value is context-local, so overlapping rebuilds cannot see each other's value.
- **Prompt surface:** a new `telegram-interim.claude` row renders Telegram with the callback set, so the line appears in the reviewed snapshot. The existing nine surfaces are byte-identical.

## Related Issue

Refs #112057. This addresses the "model writes nothing during long tool loops" half of that issue, on every surface that shows interim text, without editing the identity line that #112073 changes.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/prompt_builder.py`: new `INTERIM_PREAMBLE_GUIDANCE` constant.
- `agent/system_prompt.py`: `_guidance_parts` appends the line when `interim_assistant_callback` is set, or inside the new `interim_preamble_surface()` context manager.
- `tui_gateway/server.py`: `_persist_live_session_system_prompt` builds inside `interim_preamble_surface(_load_interim_assistant_messages())`.
- `scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py` and `tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/`: new `telegram-interim.claude` surface. The other nine are byte-identical.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/prompt-assembly.md` and `.github/workflows/prompt-surface-diff.yml`: describe the new surface.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py` and the new `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_interim_guidance.py`.

## How to Test

1. `pytest -q tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py -k interim tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_interim_guidance.py`
2. `python scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py render`. Only `telegram-interim.claude` differs from the `telegram.claude` render: one extra stable-tier line.
3. On a gateway platform with `display.interim_assistant_messages` on, ask for something that needs tools. The first tool-call message carries one short sentence, which arrives as an interim message before the tools finish.

- `tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py`: the line is present with tools and a callback, and inside `interim_preamble_surface(True)`. It is absent with no callback, with no tools, and for a delegate-style agent.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_interim_guidance.py` (new file, so the large server test file does not grow): a between-turns persist includes the line when interim messages are on and leaves it out when they are off, without leaving a callback or flag set.
- Each new test was checked red with its guarded code reverted.
- Locally (macOS, Python 3.14): `tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py`, `tests/agent/test_run_agent.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`, the new TUI test file, `tests/agent/test_coding_worktree_note.py` and `tests/agent/test_compaction_prompt_rebuild.py` pass, 1010 tests. `python scripts/check` passes, with 0 blocking code-health findings.
- `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` cannot run on macOS: the render pins `sys.platform = "linux"`, and the sysconfig import fails, on main too. The fixtures were regenerated with the same child environment after pre-loading sysconfig and psutil. That render reproduces main's committed fixtures byte for byte, and on this branch it changes only the new row and `surfaces.json`. Linux CI runs the real check.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (ran the touched and adjacent files: 1010 passed)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes

### Documentation & Housekeeping
