prs.title: fix(pm): leave out a carried extra that no longer builds instead of failing every update
prs.body:
When Hermes moves an old install onto its package manager, it re-installs the optional features the old setup had. If one of those features cannot be built on your machine (Matrix's encryption library needs CMake and a C++ compiler), the update used to fail, and every later `hermes update` tried the same thing and failed again; now the update leaves that one feature out, finishes, and tells you the command to add it back.

**Stacked on #148194** (`fix/pm-extras-optout`): this reuses its declined-extras record and `hermes pm install --extra` opt-back-in, so review/merge #148194 first; GitHub shows this PR's diff against `main` until then (only the top commit is new).

## Before / after (real `hermes update` dependency step, live)

Scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, a `git archive` of each tree, an old-style in-tree `venv/` holding Matrix and FAL packages, and a `cmake` on `PATH` that always fails, so python-olm's build fails for real. Both legs drive the real `hermes_cli.venv_sync._sync_source_dependencies` (the legacy migration → `pm.sync_venv(..., explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)` through the PM worker), then the same step again as the next update would.

| Step | `main` (45219aa35c2) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1. first PM sync | `Failed to build python-olm==3.2.16` → **sync fails**, no `facts.json` written | python-olm fails, then `⚠ Left the optional 'matrix' extra out of this update: Hermes carried it over from the old venv, and it no longer builds on this machine (the build output is above). Everything else is installed. Once that is fixed, run `hermes pm install --extra matrix` to add it back.` → **SYNC OK**, recorded extras `['all', 'fal']` (fal, which builds, is still carried) |
| 2. next update | old venv rescanned, `legacy_selection: ['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, **fails the same way** (forever) | **SYNC OK in 2.2 s**, nothing rebuilt; a rescan of the old venv gives `['all', 'fal']` |
| 3. `pm.sync_venv(explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)` | (stuck on step 1) | `sync ok`, environment unchanged |
| 4. `hermes pm install --extra matrix` (still broken cmake) | fails, exit 1 | **still fails loudly, exit 1**: an extra you ask for is never left out quietly |
| 5. `hermes pm install --extra matrix` (cmake fixed) | — | `✓ venv +matrix`, extras `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, `declined-extras.json` back to `[]` |

`declined-extras.json` after step 1: `{"schema": 1, "declined": ["matrix"], "left_out_by_update": {"matrix": "it no longer builds on this machine"}}`.

## What changed

- `pm.sync_venv(..., carried=[...])`: names the entries of `extras` that were carried over from the old venv, not asked for. Only both legacy callers pass it (`venv_sync._sync_source_dependencies` and the historical `_update_takeover.prepare`), and only when something beyond `[all]` was carried.
- `pm/carried_extras.py` (new): when the sync fails with a build or resolver verdict, it checks that core plus the requested extras build without the carried ones (if not, the original error is raised). Then it re-adds each carried extra on top of what fits, the same way plugin eviction does. Then it syncs without the ones that fail, all under the same lock and receipt.
- A build verdict is recorded in #148194's declined-extras record with a reason, so the next scan of the old venv skips it. A lazy first-use refusal names that reason ("an update left 'matrix' out because it no longer builds on this machine") instead of a `--without` the user never ran. A carried extra that fails only for the moment (download or tooling error on its trials) is never dropped: the sync fails before publishing, so the next update re-scans the old venv and retries it (review round 2). The notice goes to stderr and into the sync receipt.
- `pm/environment.py`: the streamed uv tail now keeps the `The build backend returned an error` marker. python-olm's traceback runs well past the 2000-character tail, so on `main` a native build failure was classed as a fetch error, not a `BuildFailure`. That also kept plugin eviction from ever seeing a plugin's native build failure as a verdict. One-line hunk in a file the cxx-compiler lane touches elsewhere (`managed_environment`), so no overlap.
- `committed_venv` docstring: PM never deletes the in-tree venv (it said it did).
- Docs: `website/docs/reference/package-management.md` § Optional Python dependencies.

## Related

- #122429 (open, @whyyagswhy) adds a matrix-only C++-compiler preflight that **fails** the takeover earlier. This PR takes the opposite approach for the whole class (any carried extra, any build cause): the update completes without the extra. That PR's review also notes the preflight never fires once facts exist. Nothing there was cherry-picked; credit for the diagnosis (#122402).

## Tests

- `tests/pm/test_carried_extras.py` (new, 3 cases): a carried extra that cannot build is left out, recorded with its reason and reported, and the next sync rebuilds nothing; a requested extra or broken core still raises `BuildFailure` and records nothing. Red on #148194's head (3 failed), green here.
- `tests/pm/test_environment_build.py::test_streaming_bounds_memory_without_losing_failure_class`: new `"The build backend returned an error"` case, red on base, green here.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` (fake HOME, `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`): tests/pm/{test_carried_extras, test_declined_extras, test_extras, test_environment_build, test_lazy_install_policy, test_install_extra, test_worker_publication, test_plugin_survival_contract}.py, tests/hermes_cli/{test_venv_sync, test_venv_sync_currency, test_old_updater_takeover, test_update_launch_completion, test_borrowed_home_launch, test_launch_relaunch_loop, test_update_completion_lease, test_update_completion_process, test_update_post_commit_followups, test_update_zip_completion, test_update_missing_configured_deps}.py, tests/ci/test_update_ci_routing.py, tests/ci/test_update_transitive_routing.py: all pass.
- `python scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Infographic

![Before: every update re-carries matrix and fails. After: matrix is left out, recorded, and the update completes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0e980/sxe4JzFLVd5thoR_Y_sXv_FREFjOaI.png)



### Review round 2 (head 7e2de8e26de, restacked on #148194 f8672c8993c)

Independent review: a carried extra whose per-extra trials failed transiently was left out of the published selection with no record; those facts end the legacy re-scan, so it was lost for good. Fix (`pm.carried_extras.refuse_transient`): a transient trial result is not a verdict, so the sync fails before publishing, naming the extra; the next update re-scans and retries it. Chosen over a pending-retry record because the old venv scan already is the retry source as long as no facts are written, so no new state is needed. Build verdicts are still left out and recorded as before.

| Reviewer's live probe (real uv, carried `matrix` fixture: build failure, then its source temporarily missing; next update in a fresh process after the source returns) | 6348568d8c5 | 7e2de8e26de |
|---|---|---|
| first update | publishes `['all']`, declined `[]` | fails: `the extras ['matrix'] Hermes carried over from the old venv could not be prepared`, nothing published |
| next update | requests `None`, stays `['all']`, import fails | requests `['all', 'matrix']`, records it, import succeeds |

New test `test_a_carried_extra_that_fails_for_the_moment_is_retried_by_the_next_update`: red on 6348568d8c5, green here. The inherited configured-repair race is fixed by the base (probe on this head: declined `['feishu']`, recorded `['all']`). 27 PM/update files, 405 passed.

prs.title: perf(skills): stop rescanning the library on every keystroke and skill load
prs.body:
## Summary

Every slash-completion keystroke and every `skill_view` call re-walked and
re-parsed the entire skills library. Each of these costs is proportional to
library size, and they are paid *per operation* — on the first keystroke of
every conversation, again on every TTL refresh, and again every time an agent
loads a skill:

- A cold `command_catalog` walked every directory under every search root and
  parsed the frontmatter of every `SKILL.md` it found — in a large library,
  tens of thousands of `scandir` calls and thousands of YAML documents per
  scan. Concurrent first-keystrokes (one per open session) each ran the full
  scan, serializing into a multi-second worst case.
- A warm `skill_view(name)` — loading one skill — re-parsed **every** SKILL.md
  frontmatter in the library and rglob'd all search roots, *on every
  invocation*, to locate a single file.

This series makes the scan **single-flight**, deduplicates the freshness
signature within a request, reuses one YAML parse per file, treats a directory
that owns a `SKILL.md` as a scan leaf, scores completion items once, and locates
skills from cached catalog rows instead of a library re-parse. Per-operation
work drops from *O(library)* to *O(1)* amortized (TTL refresh still pays a
scan, but of a tree the walk no longer over-traverses).

**Measured on one large real-world library (frozen copy, three search roots,
same interpreter, interleaved A/B; every pass benchmarked at its own commit):**

| cell | before | after | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold `command_catalog` | 1,121 ms | 612 ms | **−45%** |
| cold first keystroke `/pro` | 490 ms | 184 ms | **−62%** |
| warm catalog (p50) | 123 ms | 22 ms | **−82%** |
| TTL-expiry catalog refresh | 414 ms | 167 ms | **−60%** |
| concurrent cold keystrokes ×6, worst | 5,823 ms | 267 ms | **−95%** |
| warm `skill_view` (p50) | 296 ms | 171 ms | **−42%** |
| peak allocations, cold catalog | 7 MB | 4 MB | −43% |
| directory visits per cold pass | — | — | **−87%** |
| YAML parses per cold pass | — | — | −50% |

Smaller libraries see smaller absolute numbers and the same structural change:
no per-keystroke rescan, no per-view re-parse, and no phantom commands, at any
size. Output parity was verified against a golden capture (catalog pairs,
completion results for a query battery) before/after each pass: identical
except the phantom commands discussed under *Behavior change*.

## Why the cost exists (per commit)

Each commit is one lever, red→green tested, and was benchmarked in isolation.
Directory visits and YAML parses are indexed to base = 1.00× so the table shows
where each lever lands regardless of library size:

| cell | base | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6 | P7 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cold catalog (ms) | 1,121 | 1,070 | 951 | 816 | 778 | 754 | 640 | 612 |
| cold keystroke `/pro` (ms) | 490 | 495 | 443 | 332 | 295 | 292 | 184 | 184 |
| warm catalog (ms) | 123 | 132 | 80 | 74 | 71 | 69 | 23 | 22 |
| TTL catalog (ms) | 414 | 363 | 309 | 289 | 271 | 249 | 186 | 167 |
| 6-conc cold, max (ms) | 5,823 | 588 | 547 | 455 | 392 | 331 | 260 | 267 |
| directory visits (×base) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.62 | 0.57 | 0.51 | 0.51 | 0.13 | 0.13 |
| YAML parses (×base) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 |

The catalog contents change only at P6 — by exactly the nested support files
(see *Behavior change*).

1. **`perf(skills): single-flight concurrent catalog scans (P1)`** — concurrent
   first-keystrokes each ran the full scan. One flight now serves all waiters
   (the 5.8 s → 0.6 s row). Also fixes a race: a scan still in flight when
   invalidation hit could publish stale results.
2. **`perf(skills): one directory-signature walk per completion RPC (P2)`** —
   one keystroke computed the freshness signature up to 3× (gate, scan,
   catalog); a request-scoped memo now computes it once.
3. **`perf(skills): register slash commands from catalog rows (parse-once)
   (P3)`** — command registration re-parsed every SKILL.md even though the
   catalog scan had just parsed it. Rows are reused (the parses 1.00× → 0.50×
   drop).
4. **`perf(yaml): one safe parser per thread in hermes_yaml (P4)`** — ruamel
   parser construction was per-load; now thread-local.
5. **`perf(slash): score each completion item once; memoize tokenization
   (P5)`** — fuzzy tokenization was recomputed per keystroke per item.
6. **`perf(skills): skill directories are scan leaves (P6)`** — the walk and
   the signature stopped descending into directories that own a `SKILL.md`
   (behavior change, next section). The biggest structural lever: directory
   visits 0.51× → 0.13×, warm catalog 69 → 23 ms (the TTL-gate signature walk
   shrinks with the tree).
7. **`perf(skills): locate a skill by cached catalog rows (P7)`** —
   `skill_view(name)` matched candidates by re-parsing every SKILL.md
   frontmatter and rglobbing each root per invocation; it now matches the
   cached catalog rows (path + name, disabled/hidden included so locate sees
   the same universe as before). Only the viewed file parses.

## Behavior change: a skill's own tree is support content, not more skills

**Before:** the SKILL.md walk descended into every skill directory, so a
`SKILL.md` nested under another skill — under `references/`, `scripts/`,
`evals/`, `fixtures/`, a vendored copy — was indexed as a top-level command.

**After:** a directory that owns a `SKILL.md` is a leaf; the scan does not
descend. The commands that disappear are exactly those nested support files.

Why this is the right semantic:

- **The spec says so.** [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/specification):
  "A skill directory may contain any files and directories beyond the required
  `SKILL.md`." Support material is arbitrary by design; it is not a skill tree.
- **The old behavior produced phantom commands.** A nested SKILL.md surfaced as
  a user-facing slash command — while `skill_view` already *refused* to serve
  it (shadowed by its parent). Users saw menu entries that fail on invoke.
  Repro in `tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py`: on base, the catalog
  contains the nested demo skill and `skill_view` of it returns "not found";
  on this branch both agree it doesn't exist.
- **Upstream already treats skill-owned trees as non-indexable, piecewise.**
  `_is_package_owned_markdown` refuses flat `<name>.md` files owned by an
  ancestor skill; `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` prunes known artifact dirs, and open
  PRs keep extending that list (#122646, #138397, #98536). The leaf rule ends
  that treadmill for everything *inside* a skill — no enumeration can be
  complete, because the spec lets a skill contain anything.
- **The waste dominates the delta.** In the measured library, roughly one
  SKILL.md in ten lives inside another skill, and nearly all of those were
  already invisible in command resolution (shadowed) — the walk and the YAML
  parse were pure cost. Only the few that leaked into commands change visible
  behavior, and those are the phantoms above.
- **Most of the walked tree is inside skills.** Support trees (references,
  scripts, evals, fixtures, vendored material) made up the large majority of
  directories under the search roots; pruning at leaves cut directory visits
  several-fold. The semantics and the cost point the same way.

This benefits any skill that carries its own material — test fixtures, worked
examples, vendored copies — which today either pollutes users' command menus
or forces authors to keep support material outside the skill directory.

Root-level artifact dirs (an artifact folder *next to* skills, not inside one)
are **not** covered by the leaf rule — #138397/#122646/#98536 remain needed and
are complementary.

## Measurement setup

- A frozen copy of a large real-world skills library: three search roots, on
  the order of a thousand SKILL.md files, including nested support files.
- Interleaved A/B on one machine/interpreter (macOS arm64); each pass
  benchmarked at its own commit via detached worktrees. Cold = fresh caches;
  warm = steady-state; TTL = expiry refresh; conc = 6 threads racing a cold
  catalog.
- Parity: golden capture of `command_catalog()` + `slash_completions()` for a
  query battery, compared per pass.
- The structural claims — per-operation cost is O(library) before and
  amortized O(1) after; nested support files indexed as commands — are
  size-independent; the tables above are one library's instantiation of them.

## Verification

- Every pass landed red→green: the test fails on base, passes on the pass's
  commit (`test_skill_scan_singleflight`, `test_skill_signature_scope`,
  `test_skill_parse_once`, `test_skill_leaf_dirs`,
  `test_skill_leaf_boundary`, `test_skill_view_locate_cache`, …).
- `tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py` fails on current `main` with the
  phantom-command assertion and passes on this branch.
- Full skills/slash surface: 51 files, 584 tests passed (5 pre-existing
  `home_io_guard` failures reproduce identically on base in the same layout —
  worktree git-dir artifact, not this change).
- `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean over all touched files.
- `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py` passes (no new config keys or commands).
  `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` fails identically on base in this
  environment (PM runtime sysconfig artifact); no prompt or tool-schema
  surface is touched by this stack.

## Future work (out of scope, measured)

- The legacy flat-`<name>.md` lookup still rglobs each root in full — the
  dominant share of the residual warm `skill_view` cost. Pruning that walk at
  skill leaves and at `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` would cut it and close the same
  phantom-candidate class #138397 fixes for root-level dirs.
- The freshness signature still walks the (now several-fold smaller) tree once
  per completion RPC, and up to 3× per `skill_view`; a short time-boxed memo
  would collapse those.
- Fuzzy scoring of the full item set is the largest remaining per-keystroke
  cost after the signature gate (tokenization is memoized by P5; scoring is
  inherently per-query).

## Related

- #145430 (desktop catalog filtering) is the renderer-side mirror of this
  work — complementary layers; together they cover keystroke → render.
- #108506 bounds the *curator* scan the same way (`tools/skill_usage.py`) —
  sibling, no file overlap.
- #138397, #122646, #98536: root-level artifact-dir exclusions; complementary
  (the leaf rule only covers dirs inside a skill).
- #141217 / #144319 / #142427: `skill_view` use-accounting and dedup
  semantics; different concerns, same entry point — this stack changes
  locate/scan cost only, not accounting.

## Test plan for reviewers

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_skill_scan_singleflight.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_signature_scope.py tests/agent/test_skill_parse_once.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_dirs.py tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_view_locate_cache.py tests/agent/test_skill_commands.py
# phantom-command repro on main vs branch:
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py
```

Platforms tested: macOS (arm64, Apple Silicon). The touched paths are
`os.scandir`/`pathlib` walks and ruamel reuse — no platform-conditional code
added; Linux/Windows CI should exercise the same paths.

### PR shape (for discussion)

Filed as one series because the levers compose into one claim ("discovery and
serving must not rescan the library") and the ladder above is the evidence.
If maintainers prefer, P6 (the leaf semantic) splits cleanly into its own PR —
it is the only behavior change; P1–P5, P7 are pure-cost passes that hold
parity on either side of it.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: update tirith to 0.1.1
prs.body:
## Catalog SHA update: tirith0.1.0 →0.1.1

This is a **new SHA-update PR**, following the catalog's human-reviewed update policy. It does not change any workflow, core code, trust tier, capability declaration or dependency floor.

- Previous reviewed pin: `e6482ffa5df5bafd872c51c71c152a02c27917d8` (initial catalog entry in #139437).
- New released pin: `42862b4e49cc5a46985973d982e2bf3969ad724f`; plugin version **0.1.1**.
- [Source comparison](https://github.com/sheeki03/hermes-plugin-tirith/compare/e6482ffa5df5bafd872c51c71c152a02c27917d8...42862b4e49cc5a46985973d982e2bf3969ad724f) · [release](https://github.com/sheeki03/hermes-plugin-tirith/releases/tag/v0.1.1) · [full changelog](https://github.com/sheeki03/hermes-plugin-tirith/blob/42862b4e49cc5a46985973d982e2bf3969ad724f/tirith/CHANGELOG.md#011).

## Changes being adopted

- Preserve multiline background shell-input state and approval behavior.
- Resolve the actual Hermes session directory on0.22.3+ and keep pending-directory approvals for batched commands, including process-substitution redirections before `cd`.
- Bound binary startup/checks by the host hook deadline, preserve fail-closed approvals and reduce repeated informational lookup warnings.
- Restore README rendering from this reviewed pin and remove the0.1.0 gateway-directory known issue now fixed. Keep the Hermes0.21.5 duplicate built-in-check warning.

## Disclosure and compatibility

The plugin invokes the user's installed **tirith >=0.5.0**, with commands on stdin. It never downloads, installs or updates the binary. Tirith logs locally and, unless offline is configured, can refresh its signed threat database, query OSV.dev/deps.dev/ecosyste.ms, download CISA KEV and use Google Safe Browsing only when the user supplied a key. The plugin remains fail closed; critical findings are refused and required approvals go through Hermes. It registers only `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call` and `transform_tool_result`; no tools, middleware, declared environment credentials or Python dependencies are added. Minimum Hermes remains **0.21.5**. Existing limits and offline threat-database prerequisites are documented in the pinned README.

## Verification

- Current upstream structural validator: this catalog file passes with **no errors or warnings**.
- Actual Hermes0.22.5 CLI installed the exact released pin into a clean isolated home. `plugins validate --install-deps` passed (security scan: safe; capabilities match), and `plugins doctor --ci tirith` passed.
- The installed plugin, using the published npm tirith0.5.0 native binary, allowed a benign command, blocked pipe-to-shell and critical metadata access, and required pending-directory approval for both process-substitution redirect cases. Proposed unsafe commands were not executed.
- [Final PR CI](https://github.com/sheeki03/hermes-plugin-tirith/actions/runs/41581207072) and [merged-main CI](https://github.com/sheeki03/hermes-plugin-tirith/actions/runs/41581670880):24 successful jobs each across unit, loader/approval, lint and catalog validation; dispatch-only real-tirith CI is expected to skip on those events. Real released-binary behavior was exercised separately above.
- Local hook suite:305 passed. Both new consumer-visible cwd regressions failed before the correction and passed after it; focused re-review approved the repair.

The owner submits this update for upstream maintainer review and merge. Existing catalog installations remain at the previous pin until that review completes.

prs.title: catalog: mediarag 0.1.20 — macOS support, banner image, one-sentence description
prs.body:
Updates the `mediarag` catalog entry from 0.1.19 to 0.1.20. Five field changes, nothing else.

**`sha` / `version` → `7dc0b6b` / `0.1.20`.** The release that makes the claims below true: macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon) and Windows now run the engine in CI, model-backed — both lanes bootstrap the q4 towers and run an end-to-end smoke that ingests a markdown file and a PNG, embeds, searches, and asserts a decodable thumbnail comes back.

**`platforms: [linux, macos, windows]`.** Previously `[linux, windows]`, which hid macOS from the listing entirely. macOS is arm64-only: `onnxruntime` 1.29 and `torch` 2.15 publish no x86_64 macOS wheels, and the arm64 wheels declare `macosx_14_0` — hence macOS 14 as the floor, not a preference. The same release fixes a first-run bug where a cold cache populated by pinned-revision download had no `refs/main`, so the processor failed to load while every file sat on disk.

**`image`.** Was absent, so the plugin page hero was empty and link previews had no art. Points at `assets/banner.jpg` (1568×672, 265 KB) at the same commit as `sha`, so it cannot drift from the pinned tree.

**`description`.** Replaced with a one-sentence summary plus the existing disclosure, and the disclosure's download figure corrected from ~285 MB to ~480 MB — measured 505 MB on a clean cache (174 MB text + 109 MB vision + 189 MB audio towers + 32 MB tokenizer). The 285 MB figure was wrong in the current entry and in the 0.1.19 README; an independent pre-merge review caught it, and shipping a figure the release itself corrects would be incoherent. Disclosures are unchanged in substance — subprocess adapters, user-supplied URL fetches, the Raindrop token, and the optional `uv` bootstrap are all still stated.

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on the changed entry: **OK: 1 file(s) valid**
- Pinned source resolves: `plugin.yaml` at `7dc0b6b` reports `version: 0.1.20` and `platforms: [linux, macos, windows]`
- Banner URL returns `200 image/jpeg`, 264952 bytes
- Release CI on `7dc0b6b`: Linux suite ✓, Windows (model-backed + e2e smoke) ✓, macOS 14 arm64 (model-backed + e2e smoke) ✓
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/mediarag/0.1.20/

## What does this PR do?

Documents **[Nexusyn](https://nexusyn.ai)** on the memory-providers page, following the **Memori precedent** for out-of-tree providers.

Per [CONTRIBUTING.md — Memory Providers: Ship as a Standalone Plugin](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), the provider itself lives in its own repo — [nexusyn/hermes-nexusyn](https://github.com/nexusyn/hermes-nexusyn), installable today with `pip install hermes-nexusyn` + `hermes-nexusyn install` (copies into `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/nexusyn/`, picked up by the existing user-dir discovery).

> ℹ️ Earlier revisions of this PR added the provider in-tree under `plugins/memory/nexusyn/`; that was against the contribution policy (thanks, review bot) and has been removed. The implementation, tests and setup docs moved to the standalone repo. This PR is now **docs-only** — no core code changes.

Nexusyn in one line: multi-tenant memory engine with hybrid retrieval (vector + FTS + reranking), per-agent attribution, project scoping, and server-side distillation of raw memories into wiki/lessons/decisions. The plugin implements the `MemoryProvider` ABC: background prefetch, session-digest or per-turn sync, built-in memory mirroring, 4 tools, read-only in cron/subagent contexts.

prs.title: feat(memory): add on_skill_write hook to MemoryProvider ABC and bridge
prs.body:
## Problem

External memory providers (Honcho, Hindsight, Mem0, OpenViking, etc.) can mirror built-in `memory` tool writes via the `on_memory_write` hook, but there is no equivalent hook for `skill_manage` writes. Providers miss skill creation, editing, and file writes -- a blind spot in the agent observable behavior.

## Solution

Add the missing `on_skill_write` bridge following the same pattern as `on_memory_write`:

### MemoryProvider ABC
- Add `on_skill_write(action, name, content, metadata=None)` optional hook

### MemoryManager
- `on_skill_write()` -- notify external providers when skill_manage writes
- `notify_skill_tool_write()` -- bridge gated on committed (non-staged, successful) writes and mutating actions only
- Action-aware payload mapping: `create`/`edit` -> `content`, `patch` -> `new_string`, `write_file` -> `file_content`; `delete`/`remove_file` carry no content. Supporting-file identity (`file_path`) and the replaced patch text (`old_string`) are preserved as metadata.
- `_MIRRORED_SKILL_ACTIONS` -- {create, edit, patch, delete, write_file, remove_file}

### Executor wiring
- Both executor paths (sequential dispatch in `agent/tool_executor.py` and the concurrent `invoke_tool`) mirror skill_manage writes through a shared helper, `mirror_skill_write_to_memory_providers`.

### Approval replay
- Writes staged by the `skills.write_approval` gate are (correctly) not mirrored at staging time -- but approval later calls `apply_skill_pending()` directly, bypassing the agent-loop bridge. `_apply_one` in `hermes_cli/write_approval_commands.py` now notifies the manager after a successful replay (CLI passes the live agent's manager; the gateway passes the cached agent's manager when one exists), with `execution_context: "approval_replay"` provenance. Best-effort: provider failures never break the approval.

### Provenance
- `build_memory_write_metadata` gains a `tool_name` param so skill events carry `tool_name="skill_manage"` instead of `"memory"`.

### Docs
- The full `on_skill_write` contract (per-action payload mapping, metadata keys, committed-only gating, approval-replay provenance) is documented in `website/docs/developer-guide/memory-provider-plugin.md`.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_skill_write_bridge.py` -- action->payload mapping for every mutating action, staged/failed-write gating, non-mutating actions ignored, metadata plumbing, provider-exception isolation.
- `tests/tools/test_write_approval.py` -- approval-replay mirroring (create + patch argument shapes), failed replays don't notify, approval works without a manager, provider failure doesn't fail the approval.

## Design

Follows existing on_memory_write architecture exactly. Backward compatible: providers ignore unknown hooks by default.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add recall (Recall by Polign memory provider)
prs.body:
## What

Adds `plugin-catalog/recall.yaml`: Recall by Polign as a memory provider, from
https://github.com/Polign/polign, subdir `plugins/hermes`, pinned at `262dd0ef37c2d01267b72c37ed1010921ccca6ac`.

Recall is a corrective memory where a new statement replaces the old one; while keeping
the history intact. The memory can be read with as-of at any time in the past so the user can 
go back to the belief in the past. The provider puts relevant memories in front of each turn 
(each with the date stated and what it replaced), sends each completed turn for extraction in the
background, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes, and registers five tools
(`recall_search`, `recall_profile`, `recall_remember`, `recall_forget`,
`recall_history`).

Memory lives in a local database under the profile by default, with nothing
to configure; or in a `recall serve` the user runs (`RECALL_URL` and
`RECALL_API_KEY`); or in a database the user chooses (`RECALL_BACKEND`,
`RECALL_BACKEND_URL`).

## Submitter

Polign owns the repository (rule 5).

## Capabilities

No plugin tools, hooks or middleware beyond the memory provider surface. No
required environment variables: with none set, memory is local. `requires_env`
is empty for that reason, as mem0's entry is.

## Disclosure

- Each turn goes to the extraction model the profile names: `anthropic:*` with
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `openai:*` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or a local
  `ollama:*` model. With `extract_model: none`, text is kept as written and
  nothing leaves the machine.
- On first use with the local database, the `recall` binary downloads
  `polign-server` (about 80 MB) from dl.polign.com and verifies it against a
  SHA-256 built into the binary. This is a one-time dependency fetch, not a
  self-updater: the plugin never replaces its own files (rule 3).
- The one Python dependency, `polign-recall`, is pinned `>=0.24.0,<1`.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests` in the plugin directory: unit tests over a fake client with
  the Hermes modules stubbed, and an integration test on the real `recall`
  binary with a local database under a temporary profile.
- `hermes plugins validate` was not run locally; the admission check in CI covers it.

## Release note

Added the Recall by Polign memory provider to the plugin catalog.

prs.title: fix(web): keyless Exa web_extract returns the whole page and marks pages Exa cut (#146558, salvage #146585)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keyless Exa `web_extract` now returns the whole page instead of the first 3,000 characters. When a page is longer than the 2,000,000 characters Hermes requests, the model's text now starts with `[Exa returned only the first 2,000,000 characters of this page; the rest of the page was not fetched.]`, so a cut page no longer passes for a whole one.

This salvages #146585 by @heyseere: its commit is cherry-picked unchanged with authorship preserved, and this PR completes the fix.

**Root cause.** `exa_extract_keyless` called the hosted `web_fetch_exa` tool without `maxCharacters`. The tool defaults to 3,000 (`tools/list`: "Maximum characters to extract per page (default: 3000)"), cuts mid-word, and marks nothing. Hermes read the fragment as a complete page: `error: null`, no `[TRUNCATED]` footer. Keyless is also the rescue path for keyed installs, so a keyed failure (for example `Payment Required: Insufficient credits`) lands here too.

**Why #146585 alone is not enough.** Sending `maxCharacters` fixes pages up to 2,000,000 characters. Longer pages are still cut silently, and the existing footer then reports the cut length as the page's total. On the issue's own repro (`llms-full.txt`, 6,013,598 chars), the model is told "of 2,000,026 total clean characters … the file is the complete page", and the "tail" it is shown comes from the middle of the file.

| Live `web_extract`, keyless Exa, via `model_tools.handle_function_call` (temp `HERMES_HOME` with `web.backend: exa`, no web keys, N=1 per leg) | main | #146585 only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8,179-char page (pinned [`apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/557254faa24ef5d86f67595c4c64dc61644d0f68/apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md)) | 3,147 chars ending `tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_sl`; no footer | 8,297 chars, whole page | 8,297 chars, whole page, no notice |
| 6,013,598-char page ([`llms-full.txt`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms-full.txt)) | 3,076 chars, no footer | footer "of 2,000,026 total clean characters"; no sign the page continues | first line is the notice; head+tail footer follows; cut logged |

This PR's column was verified through the real dispatcher on this branch, based on main `114b5cd633`. The main and #146585 columns are prior measurements supplied for this fix at `6059d35108`; `keyless_mcp.py` is unchanged on main since. Exa returns a page's real length rather than padding to the request, so the 8k page costs the same at `maxCharacters` 50,000 or 2,000,000. The model still sees at most `char_limit`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #146558
Salvages #146585 (@heyseere); commit 1 is cherry-picked as-is.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/web/keyless_mcp.py`:
  - Commit 1 (#146585): `exa_extract_keyless` sends `maxCharacters: MAX_STORED_TEXT_CHARS`.
  - Commit 2: the request size becomes `_EXA_FETCH_MAX_CHARACTERS`, and `_exa_page_was_cut` reports when the page body (after the `# Title` / `URL:` header) filled the request. A cut page gets the leading notice and an info log line.
  - Why the notice leads: so the head+tail window and the stored copy's 2M cap both keep it.
  - Why detection counts UTF-16 code units with 64 chars of slack: Exa counts `maxCharacters` in UTF-16 units and trims trailing whitespace, so a 2M request on `llms-full.txt` returned 1,999,950 Python chars.
- `tests/plugins/web/test_exa_keyless_page_length.py` (new; placement per `tests/AGENTS.md` and `plugins/AGENTS.md` § Tests): one invariant test per fix, both red on `origin/main`.
  - **Setup:** both run `web_extract` through real plugin discovery, with `web.backend: exa` written to the isolated `HERMES_HOME`'s `config.yaml`.
  - **What is faked:** only the network. `requests.post` to Exa's endpoint answers like the deployed tool: an SSE envelope, the page cut at `maxCharacters` UTF-16 units (3,000 when omitted), trailing whitespace trimmed, no marker. The SSRF DNS check is stubbed.
  - **Fixture:** a page with markers on both sides of 3,000 chars, plus emoji, so Exa's cut lands short of the request in Python characters.
  - **Tests:** `test_text_past_3000_chars_reaches_the_model` (fix 1) and `test_page_exa_cut_is_flagged_to_the_model` (fix 2). The second includes emoji so the cut falls short of the request when measured in Python characters. The separate mutation check was not rerun for this PR.
- `tests/tools/test_web_keyless_fallback.py`: commit 2 drops commit 1's call-arguments test. The first test above covers the same invariant through real discovery, in the directory the rules require.

Not taken:
- **A mid-token heuristic** (suggested on the issue): plenty of pages legitimately end mid-word, so it is noisy. Filling the request is conclusive now that the request is always stated.
- **A smaller request:** head+tail needs the page's real end, and 2M is the store cap Hermes already applies.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/web/test_exa_keyless_page_length.py` against three versions of `keyless_mcp.py`:
   - from `origin/main`: 2 failed;
   - commit 1 only: 1 failed (the cut-signal test), 1 passed;
   - this branch: 2 passed.
2. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/web/ tests/tools/test_web_keyless_fallback.py tests/tools/test_web_keyless_rescue.py tests/tools/test_web_extract_robustness.py`: 121 passed. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks, ok.
3. Live: set `web.backend: exa`, leave `EXA_API_KEY` unset, and `web_extract` the two URLs in the table.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (salvages #146585; #147484 edits other hunks of the same file)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (the related suites above passed; the full suite is still running locally with `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 4`)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6.2 (Apple Silicon), Python 3.14.9

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A

- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

prs.title: feat(skill): add tool-audit — agent self-monitoring for tool execution patterns
prs.body:
## Summary

New bundled skill: **tool-audit** — an operator-facing, read-only audit of one session's tool usage, grounded in the canonical SQLite session store.

Rebuilt per the sweeper review (see review reply for the point-by-point mapping).

## What it reports

`scripts/tool_audit.py` opens `state.db` read-only (SQLite `mode=ro`, the same pattern as `SessionDB(read_only=True)`) and correlates assistant `tool_calls` entries with tool-role rows by `tool_call_id`:

| Metric | Source |
|--------|--------|
| calls | `messages.tool_calls` JSON on assistant rows |
| results | tool-role rows matched by `tool_call_id` |
| orphaned | calls with no matching result row |
| errors | matched results whose JSON payload has a truthy `error` key — the same rule as `model_tools._tool_result_observer_fields` |

Uncorrelated results (call compacted away) are counted separately, never attributed to a tool.

**Deliberately not reported:** latency / success rates. Per-call `duration_ms` only exists in the in-process `post_tool_call` observer hook and is never persisted, so the report claims exactly what the store can prove — nothing more.

## Design

- `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/tool-audit/SKILL.md` with required frontmatter (description 58 chars, modern section order, contributor-first author credit)
- Profile-aware store resolution: `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` when importable, stdlib fallback otherwise (same pattern as `google-workspace/scripts/_hermes_home.py`)
- Session resolution: `--session` (id or unique prefix) → `$HERMES_SESSION_ID` → latest session; ambiguous prefixes fail instead of guessing
- Cross-platform, stdlib-only script; `platforms: [linux, macos, windows]`

## Files

```
skills/autonomous-ai-agents/tool-audit/SKILL.md
skills/autonomous-ai-agents/tool-audit/scripts/tool_audit.py
tests/skills/test_tool_audit_skill.py
```

## Testing

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_tool_audit_skill.py -q` — 11 tests: bundled-discovery via the real `_discover_bundled_skills` scanner, frontmatter hardlines, ID-correlated metrics against a fixture `state.db`, error-rule parity with the runtime observer, read-only URI enforcement, and session resolution.

prs.title: fix(pm): `pm install --without EXTRA` drops a carried extra (matrix) and keeps it dropped
prs.body:
Hermes copies the optional features it finds in an old pre-PM install (Matrix, for example) into the new dependency setup, and then reinstalls them on every update, with no way to say "I don't want that one". Now `hermes pm install --without matrix` removes it and keeps it removed, and `hermes pm install --extra matrix` brings it back.

## Before / after (real runs, scratch `HERMES_HOME`, `git archive` trees, old-style `venv/` holding the matrix + fal anchors)

| Step | `origin/main` (ea4fda7db4a) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1. first PM sync (`venv_sync._sync_source_dependencies`, the real legacy migration) | `legacy_selection: ['all', 'fal', 'matrix']` → recorded `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, mautrix installed | same |
| 2. `hermes pm install --without matrix` | `✗ --without accepts only optional default packages (chromium, cua-driver); not matrix` | `✓ venv ✓ chromium ✓ cua-driver`, exit 0 |
| 3. update's sync (`pm.sync_venv(explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)`) | recorded `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, mautrix installed | recorded `['all', 'fal']`, new generation without mautrix, `fal_client` kept |
| 3b. old venv re-scanned (facts.json moved aside) | `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']` | `['all', 'fal']` |
| 4. `hermes pm install --extra matrix`, then the update's sync | n/a | recorded `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, mautrix installed, decline record emptied |

The reporter's harder case also reproduces on main without the CMake workaround used above: on this host (CMake 4.2) the carried `[matrix]` fails to build `python-olm`, `facts.json` is never written, so every following `hermes update` runs `legacy_selection` again and fails the same way. Main gives no supported way out. With this PR, `--without matrix` is that way out.

### Review round (head 29b7c5be75a vs 1b1f005b0db, real runs, scratch homes)

| Sequence | 1b1f005b0db | 29b7c5be75a |
|---|---|---|
| First PM migration failed (old `venv/` holds matrix + fal, no `facts.json`), then `python -m pm.cli install --without matrix` | recorded `['all']`, fal_client **missing**, later updates stop re-scanning | recorded `['all', 'fal']`, fal_client installed, no mautrix. The next update sync keeps `['all', 'fal']` |
| `pm install --extra matrix` (A) with the update's sync (B) queued behind it, B starting while A clears the decline (clear widened to 5 s in the scratch tree) | B reads the stale decline: recorded `['all']`, mautrix **gone** | B waits for A's lock: recorded `['all', 'fal', 'matrix']`, mautrix installed |

## What changed

- `pm/extras.py`: `declined_extras()` / `record_declined_extras()` keep a per-install `installs/<key>/declined-extras.json` next to `facts.json` and the existing `declined-packages.json`. `legacy_selection` skips declined extras. `droppable_extras()` lists the extras `--without` accepts: declared extras that are not `all` and not pulled in by `[all]`.
- `pm/install.py`: a sync carries the recorded extras that are still declared and **not declined** (`_carried`, shared by `_target_selection` and `venv_is_current`, so both make the same decision). An extra the caller explicitly requests still wins, and a successful explicit sync takes it off the decline list (opt back in) while it still holds the dependency lock, so a sync queued behind it cannot publish without it. `decline_extras()` writes `--without` under the same lock. A lazy, non-explicit install of a declined extra is refused and points to `hermes pm install --extra NAME`.
- `pm/cli.py`: `--without NAME` now accepts a droppable extra as well as a default package. The bare install's own sync then builds the generation without it. Before any `facts.json` exists (a first migration that failed), the install's sync is seeded from the legacy scan with declines applied (`_first_selection`), so `--without matrix` keeps fal. If the scan finds nothing beyond `[all]`, the request is unchanged.
- `hermes_cli/main_install_repair.py`: the update's "install extras for configured platforms" step skips declined extras, so a Matrix block left in config cannot undo the opt-out.
- Docs: new `pm install --without EXTRA` row in `reference/package-management.md`.

**Is the legacy re-carry one-shot?** Only while `installs/<key>/facts.json` exists. The old in-tree `venv/` / `.venv` is never deleted (the `committed_venv` docstring says PM deletes it, but no code does). So the scan runs again for any data root without facts: a failed first sync (the loop above), a fresh `HERMES_HOME` that borrows the checkout, or a deleted `installs/` dir. The decline lives in the same per-install dir, so it applies to every one of those re-scans.

## Tests

`tests/pm/test_declined_extras.py` (3 tests, all red on `origin/main`, green here): `--without matrix` drops it from the next selection and from the legacy scan while `fal` stays, and a lazy install refuses it. `--extra` opts back in. `--without web` (inside `[all]`) is refused. Review round, 3 more: a bare sync queued behind an `--extra` opt-in keeps the extra, and a `--without` landing during an opt-in sync stays recorded. Both drive real `sync_venv` interleaves gated by events, and each goes red when its lock scope is reverted. The third covers `--without` after a failed first migration keeping fal (red on 1b1f005b0db). Existing `test_install_default_closure.py`, `test_extras.py` and `test_retired_agent_browser.py` pass unchanged. `scripts/check --only health` is clean.

### Review round 2 (head f8672c8993c vs e1a85a3266e)

Independent review: configured-platform repair (`main_install_repair._install_configured_features_missing_deps`) read the declines, then sent an `explicit=True` sync. A `--without feishu` completing in between was undone: the stale request rebuilt feishu and its opt-back-in clear emptied the decline. Fix: `sync_venv(..., automatic=[...])` names the extras Hermes chose on the user's behalf. Under the dependency lock a declined automatic extra is left out, and only the user-requested extras clear a decline. Callers classified: automatic = configured-platform repair, the update's/launch migration's legacy carry (`venv_sync`, `_update_takeover`), the container baseline restore (`pm.recovery`, whose gap list also skips declines now) and the carried part of `pm install`'s first selection; user requests = setup flows, `--extra NAME`, plugin/memory setup, CI.

| Reviewer's live probe (real configured Feishu detector, real PM worker + uv, `--without` scheduled after repair's decline read) | e1a85a3266e | f8672c8993c |
|---|---|---|
| final declined / recorded | `[]` / `['all', 'feishu']` | `['feishu']` / `['all']` |
| serial control | `['feishu']` / `['all']` | `['feishu']` / `['all']` |

New test `test_automatic_repair_never_undoes_a_without_that_landed_after_its_read` (deterministic interleave through the real repair function and `sync_venv`): red on e1a85a3266e, green here. Two main tests that pin `sync_venv`'s exact call kwargs gain the `automatic` entry (`test_baked_selection.py::test_refresh_restores_baked_extras_a_volume_lost`, `test_update_missing_configured_deps.py::test_update_installs_the_extras_configured_features_need`). 23 PM/update files, 359 passed.

NOT COVERED: if another recorded umbrella extra declares the same packages, they stay until that extra is dropped too (documented). The first-migration `--without` race the previous note named is closed by the same under-lock re-read.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0e8f8/1tfu3HuttgZUSRFuBH0wu_T1Znvgp8.png)

prs.title: fix(tools): gate Matrix E2EE lazy install on macOS hosts with CMake 4
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`platform.matrix` (Matrix E2EE) depends on `python-olm`, which ships no wheel — on every host it must build the bundled libolm 3.2.16 from sdist via `olm_build.py`. On macOS hosts where Homebrew provides CMake 4.x, that build can never succeed:

- libolm 3.2.16 declares `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4)`; CMake 4.0 removed compatibility with `< 3.5`
- `olm_build.py` invokes cmake unconditionally whenever cmake is on PATH — there is no make fallback for the cmake-present-but-failing case
- even with the compatibility policy relaxed, Apple Clang 21 rejects the const-pointer self-increment in `list.hh`

So on affected macOS hosts, `hermes update` reports the lazy install as **failed** on every run instead of cleanly skipping.

This PR mirrors the existing Windows gate for `platform.matrix` in `_unsupported_feature_reason`: a cached cmake major-version probe (`cmake --version`, shelling out once) and, on darwin with cmake ≥ 4, an "unsupported on this host" reason with actionable guidance. Installs then report `skipped` instead of `failed`, consistent with other platform-incompatible features.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/lazy_deps.py`: add `_macos_cmake_major_version()` (cached probe) and a darwin + cmake ≥ 4 branch in `_unsupported_feature_reason()` for `platform.matrix`

## How to Test

1. On macOS with Homebrew cmake 4.x installed (`cmake --version` → 4.x)
2. Run `hermes update` (or any lazy-install gate check) with `platform.matrix` pending
3. Before: install attempt fails in olm_build under CMake 4 → "failed"
4. After: feature is reported unsupported with a clear reason → "skipped", no build attempt

On Linux, Windows, or macOS with cmake 3.x, behavior is unchanged (gate returns None).

prs.title: fix(deps): let python-olm's vendored libolm configure under CMake 4
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Installing the `[matrix]` extra on Linux fails on hosts with CMake 4. Both `hermes update` and the lazy matrix install are affected. `mautrix[encryption]` pulls `python-olm==3.2.16`, which has no cp314 wheel, so uv builds its sdist. That sdist compiles a vendored libolm whose `CMakeLists.txt` declares `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4)`. CMake 4 removed compatibility with anything below 3.5, so the build stops at configure:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:1 (cmake_minimum_required):
  Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.
  ...
  Or, add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 to try configuring anyway.
```

This PR sets `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for the python-olm build only, via `[tool.uv.extra-build-variables]`. That variable is the escape hatch CMake's own error message recommends, and the issue thread already confirms it works as a manual workaround. It has to live in the project table because PM runs uv with an empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and drops non-index `UV_*` settings, so neither user uv config nor environment tweaks reach every sync reliably.

The separate missing-`clang++` failure (#122402) is out of scope. #130255 handles it.

## Related Issue

Fixes #122733

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pyproject.toml`: add `[tool.uv.extra-build-variables]` with `python-olm = { CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM = "3.5" }`. `uv.lock` is unaffected, and `uv lock --check` passes.
- `tests/test_project_metadata.py`: the test asserts the policy floor stays set while `[matrix]` still pulls `mautrix[encryption]`. It skips visibly once that premise is gone.

## How to Test

Tested on Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 with cmake 4.2.3, the managed Python 3.14.9 and uv 0.13.5. I went through PM itself, with a fresh uv cache so no previously built wheel could be reused:

1. On `main`: `CC=gcc CXX=g++ python -m pm.build_env --source . --out /tmp/v --cache /tmp/c --extra matrix` fails with `Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed`. `CC`/`CXX` only sidestep #122402 on a host without clang++.
2. On this branch, the same command succeeds and `/tmp/v/bin/python -c 'import olm'` works.
3. `pytest tests/test_project_metadata.py`: 7 passed. The new test fails if the pyproject table is removed.

prs.title: fix(pm): default a cmake policy floor into uv-driven source builds
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update`'s historical takeover can die building the carried `matrix` extra: `mautrix[encryption]` pulls `python-olm`, which publishes no wheel past cp312, so on the managed Python 3.14 uv compiles vendored libolm from source — and libolm's `CMakeLists.txt` declares `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4)`, which cmake 4.x refuses outright (compatibility below 3.5 was removed). The build fails at the configure step on a host whose toolchain is otherwise complete (clang++/gcc/cmake all present), which is exactly why the existing takeover preflight checks (#122429/#122434, CXX existence) do not catch it.

This PR defaults `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` into the environment of every uv child process started by `pm/environment.py`'s `PythonEnvironment._run` — the single choke point for pm-driven `uv sync`/`lock`/`export` (the takeover dependency-sync path included). The variable is cmake's official escape hatch: it only lifts the policy floor of declarations cmake would otherwise reject, and older cmake versions ignore it entirely. An explicit user-provided value still wins (`setdefault`), since `_base_environment` does not strip `CMAKE_*` names.

This complements #39816 (same idea on the `tools/lazy_deps.py` runtime path, a different code path that does not go through pm environments).

## Related Issue

Fixes #122733

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/environment.py`: after `_base_environment` filtering and the `UV_*` pinning in `PythonEnvironment._run`, `setdefault("CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM", "3.5")` so every uv-driven source build survives cmake 4.x (5 lines incl. comment)
- `tests/pm/test_environment_build.py`: regression test asserting the floor is injected by default and an explicit value is preserved

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/pm/test_environment_build.py -k cmake -q` → 1 passed (red without the fix: the injected env key is absent, green with it)
2. `pytest tests/pm/test_environment_build.py -q` → 19 passed, 15 errors; the 15 errors are a pre-existing local-environment baseline (shared venv is Python 3.11 while the repo pins `==3.14.*`; identical on clean `upstream/main`)
3. Observed result: the captured uv child environment contains `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` by default and keeps a caller-supplied `3.9` untouched
4. On an affected host (Ubuntu 24.04, cmake 4.x, managed Python 3.14), a takeover carrying `matrix` should pass the libolm configure step instead of failing with `cmake_minimum_required ... 3.4` rejection

prs.title: fix(lazy-deps): set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 for native builds
prs.body:
## Problem

On macOS 26 with cmake 4.x, `ensure("platform.matrix")` fails at the cmake *configure* step before it even gets to compile:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:1 (cmake_minimum_required):
  Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.
```

cmake 4.x dropped support for `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION < 3.5)`. `python-olm 3.2.16` bundles libolm source with `CMakeLists.txt` declaring `VERSION 3.4`.

## Fix

Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` in the build environment passed to uv/pip. cmake 4.x reads this env var and treats the project as though it declared the minimum as 3.5. One env key, no source patching, no platform gating.

## Relationship to #31354

#31354 fixes the C++ const-pointer compile error in `list.hh`. This fixes the cmake configure error that fires *before* compilation starts. On macOS 26 / cmake 4.3.x, both are needed. Without this change, #31354's patched source build still aborts at the configure step.

Note: the subprocess in `_python_olm_macos_install` (added by #31354) doesn't pass an explicit `env=`, so it'll also need this fix when that PR merges — either inherit it from the calling process or pass `env={**os.environ, "CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM": "3.5"}` directly.

## Testing

```
# Fresh hermes venv, cmake 4.3.3, Apple clang 21.0.0 (macOS 26)
uv pip uninstall python-olm mautrix
CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 uv pip install "mautrix[encryption]==0.21.0"
# → installs cleanly; previously failed at cmake configure step
```

prs.title: fix(pm): default a CMake policy floor into uv source builds so python-olm builds under CMake 4 (salvage #39816)
prs.body:
On a computer with CMake 4, installing Hermes' Matrix support fails because one of its libraries (python-olm) ships C code whose build file asks for a CMake older than 3.5, which CMake 4 refuses. PM now tells CMake "treat old build files as 3.5" for every package it builds from source, unless you already set that value yourself.

Salvages #39816 (earliest, by @MwC-Trexx; cherry-picked, authorship kept) with the identical `setdefault` from #122753 (@liuhao1024, `Co-authored-by`).

## Before / after (real `PythonEnvironment` install, this host)

CMake 4.2.3 at `/usr/bin/cmake`, PM's pinned interpreter `python-3.14.9+20261021`, fresh venv + fresh uv cache per leg, scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, `env -i` (no ambient `CMAKE_*`), `PYTHONPATH` at a `git archive` of each tree. Driver: `managed_environment(...).install_requirements([...])`.

| Leg | origin/main `45219aa35c2` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `python-olm==3.2.16` (sdist, vendored libolm `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4)`) | **BuildFailure**: `Command '['cmake', '.', '-Bbuild', '-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=NO']' returned non-zero exit status 1` | **INSTALL OK**; `import olm; olm.Account().identity_keys` → `['curve25519', 'ed25519']`; build's `CMakeCache.txt`: `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM:STRING=3.5` |
| same, user exported `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.10` | — | **INSTALL OK**, `CMakeCache.txt` records `3.10` (user value wins) |
| control: `docopt==0.6.2` (sdist, no CMake) | INSTALL OK | INSTALL OK |

The error uv's tail hides, from running the same configure on base's extracted sdist:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:1 (cmake_minimum_required):
  Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.
  ...
  Or, add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 to try configuring anyway.
```

## What changed

- `pm/environment.py` `PythonEnvironment._run`: `env.setdefault("CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM", "3.5")` on the uv child env, after `_base_environment()` (which keeps `CMAKE_*`) and the `--no-config` index filter. Every uv entry point (`sync`, `lock`, `pip install`, `export`) goes through `_run`, and PEP 517 backends inherit uv's env, so main install, `hermes update` sync, extras, plugin envs and the legacy `tools/lazy_deps` shim (now a PM redirect) all get it. CMake < 4 ignores the variable.
- `tests/pm/test_cmake_policy_floor.py` (from #39816): both install tiers (`sync`, `install_requirements`) get the floor (**red on main**: `KeyError: 'CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM'`); an ambient user value survives `managed_environment` (precedence control, green on both).
- `contributors/emails/`: mapping for the salvaged author's commit email.

### Why this mechanism over the alternatives in the cluster
- No maintainer ruling rejects the env approach: #127806 was closed by its author as a duplicate of #122753, not refused, and the sweeper review on #39816 only asked to move it onto the current install path (done here: it is now PM's single uv choke point).
- `[tool.uv.extra-build-variables]` (#143999) covers only `python-olm` inside Hermes' own project. It overrides a user's own value, and plugin environments and other old-CMake sdists stay broken.
- Gating Matrix off on CMake 4 (#63186, #90401) disables the feature instead of building it.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/test_cmake_policy_floor.py tests/pm/test_environment_build.py` → 2 + 34 passed (fake `HOME`, `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` set).
- Red on base: the floor test fails on an origin/main tree copy (`KeyError`).
- `python scripts/check --only health` → ok.

## Not covered

## Summary of Changes
The bug was that configuration backups were created using `shutil.copy2`, which preserves the source file's permissions. 4. Verify the backup file is created with mode `640` (or `600` if desired) instead of `644`.

prs.title: fix(config): keep config.yaml backups owner-only
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`backup_config()` copied `config.yaml` with `shutil.copy2`, which preserves the source file's mode. A `config.yaml` left at 0644 by an editor or a non-atomic writer therefore produced world-readable backups containing the user's credentials.

Each new backup now gets the same `_secure_file` policy that `config.yaml` itself already gets: 0600, skipped when managed (activation sets 0640 group-readable) or in a container. Reusing the existing helper keeps one permission policy for the config and its copies instead of hardcoding a second chmod.

## Related Issue

Fixes #148317

- `hermes_cli/config_backups.py`: call `_secure_file(dest)` right after the `shutil.copy2` in `backup_config()` (late import, matching how `config.py` late-imports this module).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_backups.py`: regression test: a 0644 `config.yaml` yields a 0600 backup.

prs.body:
## Owner submission: Media Scout 0.1.0

I own and maintain [dakshagrawa/hermes-workflows](https://github.com/dakshagrawa/hermes-workflows). This PR adds **one catalog entry**, pinned to the released commit `d444ad9e5508e40750164fd2ecf946aa558f81bd`, subdirectory `plugins/media-scout`.

[Experimental release and checksums](https://github.com/dakshagrawa/hermes-workflows/releases/tag/media-scout-v0.1.0) · [Pinned source/setup](https://github.com/dakshagrawa/hermes-workflows/tree/d444ad9e5508e40750164fd2ecf946aa558f81bd/plugins/media-scout) · [Qualification](https://github.com/dakshagrawa/hermes-workflows/blob/d444ad9e5508e40750164fd2ecf946aa558f81bd/plugins/media-scout/QUALIFICATION.md)

### What it does and the public surfaces used

Small, experimental Linux bookkeeping plugin for an owner-scoped Discord media workflow. It captures supported Instagram submissions after native admission, creates durable receipts/records, claims extraction, saves bounded evidence/coverage and prepares source-bound native Kanban reviews. A bundled skill guides actual media understanding and the separate reviewer's contract. It is not a downloader, second bot, replacement queue or core patch.

- `ctx.register_tool`: `media_scout`.
- `ctx.register_hook`: `post_gateway_admission`, returning no handling/rewrite directive.
- `ctx.register_skill`: `media-scout:workflow`.
- `ctx.register_command`: `/media-scout` for explicit owner stopped-writer claim recovery.
- `ctx.get_config`, profile-scoped `plugin_data_dir`/`plugin_db`, and `ctx.dispatch_tool("terminal", ...)` for fixed, safely quoted native Kanban CLI operations.
- No middleware, tool overrides, adapter/SDK handles, borrowed OAuth, gateway raw events or private registry access.

### Risk/effect disclosures

- Runs with native Python plugin host authority, not in a filesystem sandbox.
- Writes private source receipts, summary/evidence, claims and task references under `plugin-data/media-scout` in the active profile; does not migrate another profile or legacy library.
- Native terminal dispatch creates a blocked native task, binds/verifies notification/wake routing, persists/readbacks task identity and only then releases authorized work. Stable keys and source markers support recovery; this is not a transaction across the plugin DB and queue or an exactly-once claim.
- Reviewer work uses the configured native profile/model and can consume its quota. Native tools/transport may retrieve media or deliver notifications using the operator's existing credentials. The plugin has no direct HTTP/model client or credential-store reader and does not provision media tools/models.
- Automatic review and bounded registered-artifact cleanup are separate explicit opt-ins, disabled by default. Local-only/no-review directions override standing review. Installation/configuration changes, outreach, purchases and publication are not authorized by media submission or review consent.
- Cleanup is limited to registered owned cache/evidence, with exact-plan/state/hash checks and bounds of 100 files/50 MiB. Durable summaries survive. Native task bodies include a compact evidence copy with separate native retention; artifact cleanup does not erase queue/conversation copies.
- No custom daemon, direct subprocess runner, telemetry, self-updater, stored credentials or runtime core override. No UI/screenshots apply.

### Executed qualification

- Exact release source passed 59 portable tests and both required Ubuntu jobs (Python 3.10/3.13); native Hermes runtime tests use v0.22.6 on Linux.
- Actual native Plugin Doctor passed.
- `hermes plugins validate <pinned-plugin> --install-deps` passed: security **safe**, no warnings, declared registrations match, no core override, no Python dependencies declared. The final release ZIP also passed validation.
- Actual pinned Git installation was tested disabled in an isolated profile and source-file hashes matched the pinned commit.
- The real SDK/isolated native queue fixture exercised capture/replay, exclusive claim, saved evidence hash, blocked creation/subscription verification, persisted identity before release, retry reuse, synthetic operator completion and retained note.
- Independent bounded read-only review found no release-blocking findings; this is not a security certification.
- Current catalog structural validator passes this entry with no errors or warnings.

### Explicit limits

**Experimental, not production-qualified.** One owner/profile, one distinct supported Instagram item per submission, Linux, Hermes >=0.22.6. SDK evidence and task completion are labeled synthetic; no actual Discord/provider/media acceptance, model review, photo/carousel completeness, quota/outage/stress guarantee or proposed-skill installation cycle is claimed. The existing live deployment was not changed during packaging.

Please review this as a **community** plugin, not a Nous endorsement or pre-approved official listing. Maintainer admission remains a separate human gate.

prs.title: fix(plugins): skip dot-prefixed dirs in directory discovery
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A killed `hermes plugins update` leaves its staging tree behind at `plugins/.update-<rand>/` (the `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".update-", dir=target.parent)` in `plugins_transaction.py` cannot clean up when the process dies). Directory discovery then recurses one level into that manifest-less dot dir and registers the staged `plugin/` payload as a second package with the key `.update-<rand>/plugin` — `hermes plugins list` shows two rows for one plugin, and the Desktop Plugins page renders a duplicate row whose Desktop column is stuck on "copying…" forever (the app-level half can never pair with a slash-containing staging key).

This PR makes `scan_directory` skip dot-prefixed children, right next to the existing dunder-dir skip. Dot dirs under a plugins root are transaction staging (`.update-<rand>/`) and tool caches (`.git`, `.venv`) — never installable packages. One carve-out: `.hermes-plugin/` is the multi-harness manifest location (the Hermes-side counterpart of the already-skipped foreign-harness dirs `.claude-plugin`, `.codex-plugin`, …) and must stay discoverable, so it is explicitly exempted.

## Related Issue

Fixes #137974

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py`: skip dot-prefixed children in `scan_directory` (like the dunder skip), with `_HERMES_HARNESS_MANIFEST_DIR = ".hermes-plugin"` exempted so the multi-harness manifest convention keeps working.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_scan_dunder_dirs.py`: add `test_scan_skips_leftover_update_staging_dir` (a leftover `.update-<rand>/plugin/` tree must not surface as a second package) and `test_scan_still_finds_hermes_plugin_manifest_dir` (the `.hermes-plugin/` carve-out must keep discovering).

prs.title: Windows installer no longer gets stuck on a half-installed Git ("INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH")
prs.body:
On Windows, a file locked for a moment (usually by antivirus scanning it) while the installer moved the freshly unpacked Git into place left a half-copied Git that could not download over https, and every retry reused it ("INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH"). Now the installer spots that broken Git and replaces it, and the move itself is a single step that either moves everything or nothing, waiting out short locks.

The Windows installer no longer gets stuck on a half-installed Git.

## Changes
- `Get-PinnedGit` (scripts/install.ps1) keeps a cached Git only when `git --exec-path` still holds `git-remote-https`; otherwise it deletes the tree (clearing PortableGit's read-only files) and extracts again. A fresh extract without the helper is discarded, not cached. (@xxxigm)
- Git is extracted into `<store>\.staging-git-bootstrap-<pid>` beside its entry and moved with `[IO.Directory]::Move`, one rename on one volume, instead of `Move-Item`. Moves and deletes refused by a short hold retry for 1+2+4+8+16 s (like pm's `Store.publish`). A hold that never clears fails with a message naming the folder. The download still lands in `%TEMP%`, so rejected bytes never touch the store. `hermes pm gc` already reclaims leftover `.staging-*` dirs.
- The readiness check also accepts a suffixless `git-remote-https` (pwsh-driven installer tests on Linux plant the system git).

Root cause: Windows PowerShell's `Move-Item` falls back to a file-by-file copy when a directory rename is refused, and stops at the held file. `cmd\git.exe` lands first and `mingw64\libexec\git-core\git-remote-https.exe` (shipped in the PortableGit archive) never does.

## Before / after (real `Get-PinnedGit`, real PortableGit 2.53.0.3, windows-latest)
| Store state | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| reporter's tree (git-remote-https missing) | reused; `git ls-remote https://github.com/...` exit 128, "'remote-https' is not a git command" | "pinned git is incomplete; reinstalling"; https `ls-remote` exit 0 |
| same tree, `bash.exe` held open | reused; https exit 128 | fails: "cannot replace the incomplete git at …\git-2.53.0+3-win32-x64: … being used by another process. Close programs using files there, then retry." |
| `Move-Item` with one held file (PS 5.1, same volume and C:→D:) | destination has `cmd\git.exe`, no `git-remote-https` | not used; one rename, whole tree or nothing |

## Tests
- `tests/scripts/install/test_install_ps1_pinned_git_extract.py` (Windows): the pinned extract restores a deleted `git-remote-https`, and a held file never leaves a partial tree (permanent hold → nothing lands; 3 s hold → whole tree lands). Passed on Windows x64 and arm64 in CI.
- Full CI green on df524b3 (52 checks).

prs.title: fix(pm): re-seed from the checkout lock when the recorded generation lock is missing
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` crashed with a raw `FileNotFoundError` in the dependencies step when the venv fact's `resolved_lock` pointed at a generation `workspace/uv.lock` that was no longer on disk (e.g. after a partial restore/copy of `installs/`). `Venv.apply()` passed that path to `lock_and_sync()` as the seed without checking that it exists.

Now the update path only uses the recorded lock if it's actually a file. If it isn't, it logs a warning and seeds from the checkout's `uv.lock`. That's the same seed the repair rebuild uses (repair always seeds from `project / "uv.lock"`). Repair's own strict "recorded dependency lock is missing; refusing to drop plugins" check and `lock_and_sync()`'s strict handling of an explicit missing seed are unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #136694

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/packages.py`: `Venv.apply()` falls back to the checkout `uv.lock` (with a warning) when the recorded seed lock is missing.
- `tests/pm/test_update_seed_lock.py`: new regression tests. A missing recorded seed falls back to the checkout lock, and a recorded seed that exists is still used.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/pm/test_update_seed_lock.py -q`: the missing-seed test fails on main with the issue's `FileNotFoundError` and passes with this change.
2. I also ran a small script: a real `Facts` file whose `resolved_lock` points at a missing generation lock, a real `Venv.apply()` and the real `lock_and_sync()`, with only venv creation stubbed. On main it raises `FileNotFoundError`. With this change it logs the fallback warning and gets past the seed read.
3. `pytest tests/pm -q`: 917 passed, 34 skipped, 3 failed. The 3 failures (`test_plugin_survival_contract::test_update_sync_retries_a_fetch_failure_once_before_disabling` and two in `test_runtime_bootstrap_tls`) pass when run alone, both with and without this change, so they look like load flakes.
4. `ruff check` on the changed files is clean.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (not tested on Windows, where the issue was reported)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` (ran only `tests/pm`)
- [ ] `python scripts/check` (not run; ran ruff check only)

AI assistance: this fix, the tests and this description were written with help from an AI assistant (Grok Bot), and I reviewed them.

prs.title: fix(tests): stop the home guard refusing PM's payload probe
prs.body:
## What

`tests/home_io_guard.py` refuses filesystem access under the real Hermes root, with one carve-out for the checkout itself — `install.sh` checks the repo out INSIDE the home (`INSTALL_DIR=$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent`). On that same default layout, PM's payload detection probes `<checkout>/../manifest.json`, which **is** `<home>/manifest.json`:

```
pm/client.py:185: in ensure
pm/runtime.py:53:  in is_runtime
pm/runtime.py:61:  in _resident_runtime
    payload = project.parent if (project.parent / "manifest.json").is_file() else None
tests/home_io_guard.py:123: in guarded
E  AssertionError: TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home: /home/<user>/.hermes/manifest.json
```

(`pm/environments.py::store_root` has the twin probe.) In CI the checkout is not inside the guarded root, so this never fires there; on a default install it took out **35** `tests/pm` tests — all of `test_worker.py` (13), `test_security_consumers.py` (12), `test_startup_activation.py` (4), `test_worker_observers.py` (3), `test_worker_registry.py` (2), plus `test_build_operations.py`, `test_plugin_survival_contract.py`, `test_runtime_bootstrap_tls.py`, `test_venv_sync_ambient_config.py` — several of them silently, because the refusal surfaced inside a background thread's log and the test then failed on its own timeout/assertion ("worker never began transferring", "an in-flight first download is not a fault").

## Fix

Exempt the probe candidate only:

```python
} | {
    # PM's payload probes test ``<checkout>/../manifest.json`` to detect a packaged payload.
    # For a checkout that is a child of the home, the candidate IS ``<home>/manifest.json`` —
    # an existence probe of a packaging file, not a read of Hermes state.
    Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "manifest.json",
})
```

A real sibling (`config.yaml`, `state.db`) stays refused, and `test_real_home_tripwire.py::test_checkout_inside_a_guarded_root_is_not_hermes_state` still passes — it asserts exactly that the parent's `config.yaml` is refused.

The remaining failure in that area is a test, not the guard: `test_active_context_home_exported_to_wrapper_subprocess` calls `build_subprocess_env`, which decorates PATH with the resolved console-script dir; that resolver stats the interpreter's own `bin` — Hermes state by the guard's rule (`_INTERPRETER_PREFIXES` covers `sys.prefix` and its site-packages, not the PM generation venv). The test asserts HERMES_HOME propagation, so it pins the PATH decoration out of the way.

## How to test

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_real_home_tripwire.py          # 28 passed — the guard's own refusal contract
tests/pm/test_build_operations.py tests/pm/test_plugin_survival_contract.py \
tests/pm/test_runtime_bootstrap_tls.py tests/pm/test_security_consumers.py \
tests/pm/test_startup_activation.py tests/pm/test_venv_sync_ambient_config.py \
tests/pm/test_worker.py tests/pm/test_worker_observers.py tests/pm/test_worker_registry.py
```

Before: 37 failed / 66 passed. After: **103 passed**.

Whole `tests/pm` on the same machine: **828 passed, 2 failed** (from 620 passed / 101 failed before this and the sibling `pm/workspace.py` fix). The 2 remaining (`test_update_sync_retries_a_fetch_failure_once_before_disabling`, `test_pm_cli_verifies_tls_with_platform_trust`) fail identically on unmodified `main` and only in a full-suite run — order-dependent pre-existing failures, not touched here. (The TLS one is `truststore` calling `sslobj.get_unverified_chain()` on a `None` `_sslobj` inside a server-side `wrap_socket`; it passes in isolation.)

## Platforms

Tested on Linux (CachyOS), default install layout (checkout inside `HERMES_HOME`). Test-only change; no product code.
