# Hermes Agent v0.22.6

**Release Date:** November 2, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~776 PRs merged since v0.22.5 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.23.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `f0d94882e89`, the window since v0.22.5 contains **3,448 non-merge commits** across **4,316 changed files** (+248,579 / −94,077), **776 merged PRs** and **385 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: the Webapp served from the gateway's own listener (`hermes webapp`, a Desktop Web Access pane to open it on your network or your own URL behind Nous sign-in, and Desktop plugins loading in a browser tab), `/model reset` to clear a session's model pin without losing history, per-skill locks against autonomous writes (lockable from the Desktop Capabilities pane), opt-in prepared compaction (`compression.prepare_ahead`), `hermes cron cancel` plus a per-job missed-run policy and a Stop button in the Desktop cron editor, `/delegation` choices saved for the next session, `hermes migrate` and setup moving Grok Bot and OpenBot users over, opt-in OS-keychain storage for the vault key, the catalog's `requires_hermes` enforced at plugin install and update, agent-picked ElevenLabs voices in `text_to_speech`, a `pre_llm_call` hook that can block a turn before inference, Desktop group chat rename, disband, mentions and attachment paste, every profile shown as a Desktop sidebar section, Telegram video notes, Slack emoji reactions in thread context, and resumable downloads in the package manager.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.23.0**, which will document everything from v0.22.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.22.5...v0.22.6](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.22.5...v0.22.6)

prs.title: fix(telegram): pass the selected part of a partial quote to the agent
prs.body:
## Problem

In Telegram a user can select part of a message and reply to just that part. The fragment arrives in `message.quote`, but `extractReplyContext` ignored it. The agent saw the whole replied message in `<quoted_message>` and could not tell which part the user meant. Long agent answers made this frequent: reply "?" to one line and the agent answers about the whole message.

## Changes

- `extractReplyContext` (`src/channels/telegram.ts`) keeps `quote.text` as `replyTo.quote` (`ReplyContext.quote` is optional).
- A reply to a message from another chat (`external_reply`) has no `reply_to_message`. Its quote is now kept, with the origin's name as sender, instead of being dropped.
- In forum topics every message carries an implicit `reply_to_message` pointing at the topic's creation message. It is now ignored (it rendered nothing anyway because its text is empty).
- The runner's `formatReplyContext` adds `<quoted_part>` after `<quoted_message>` when the quote is only part of the message. Nothing changes for whole-message replies.

## Tests

- `src/channels/telegram-reply-context.test.ts`: plain reply, partial quote, forum topic creation reply, external reply, no reply.
- `container/agent-runner/src/formatter.test.ts`: `<quoted_part>` rendered, and omitted when the quote equals the whole text.
- Both suites fail when the change is reverted. Running in production since 2026-11-03.

prs.title: feat(router): defer expensive inbound content until an agent will receive it
prs.body:
## Problem

An adapter that has to do real work to produce a message's full content — a network fetch, a download — has nowhere to put it. `InboundMessage.content` must be complete before `routeInbound` ever sees it, so the work happens for **every** message that arrives: including the ones in chats no agent is wired to, and the ones that fail their wiring's engage test.

On a personal WhatsApp number that means every image, video and document across every chat the account is in, fetched from WhatsApp's CDN on arrival and thrown away moments later.

## Approach

An optional second view of the same message:

- **`content`** — the ROUTING view. Cheap, always present, complete enough for every routing decision: text to match an engage pattern against, sender, attachment metadata with no bytes.
- **`resolveContent()`** — the DELIVERY view. The same object with the expensive parts filled in.

The router calls the resolver at most once per message, and only from `deliverToAgent` — i.e. only once some agent is actually going to persist the message — then writes that result instead of `content`.

Details worth reviewing:

- **Memoized on the promise, not the value**, so a fan-out to several engaged agents shares one fetch rather than racing several.
- **Placement is deliberate.** After the command gate (a filtered or denied slash command shouldn't pull attachment bytes, and the gate only reads text, which both views share) and after `backfillNewSession` (which reads sibling sessions, never this message's content) — so the work sits behind everything that can still abort the write.
- **Fail-soft.** If the resolver rejects, the router logs and persists the routing view. The agent loses the bytes, not the message; the container formatter already renders metadata-only attachments as `[document: report.pdf]`.
- **`fanInboundMessage` and `dispatchSessionCreated` keep the routing view on purpose.** Session-echo rows and hook payloads want to know an attachment exists; they shouldn't each carry another copy of it.

## Compatibility

Adapters that leave `resolveContent` undefined are completely unaffected — `content` is delivered as-is. That is every adapter in trunk today, so this lands as a no-op for existing installs.

## Tests

`src/router-deferred-content.test.ts` covers the laziness contract itself, through the real `routeInbound` path:

- never resolved for a chat with no wiring at all
- never resolved when the engage test fails
- resolved exactly once across a fan-out to several engaged agents
- resolved on the accumulate path (that message is still persisted)
- falls back to the routing view when resolution throws

Full suite: 188 files, 2247 tests passing.

## Follow-up

The WhatsApp adapter is the first consumer — mmv/nanoclaw@`feat/whatsapp-lazy-media`, which I'll open against `channels` once this lands. It also fixes a `documentMessage.caption` omission that was dropping captioned PDFs outright.

## Note

I could not run the full suite on this machine (linux/arm64, Node v23.1.0) without temporarily pinning `better-sqlite3` back to 11.10.0 — the 13.0.3 prebuild loads but segfaults in `new Database()`, killing the vitest workers. That pin was local to verification only and is **not** in this diff.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, the barrel import, and five exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal` and no Proton DMARC verdict at all. Either way, the `From:` must be a single plain dot-atom address. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command, so duplicate labels can't shadow each other. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed (a terminal edit), or no longer holds a row for, refuses later replies, giving core's reason when it gave one ("that request has closed: ⏱️ Timed out — no response"). Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused (delivery fails) rather than pushing one out.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`) — core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received". If that acknowledgement fails to send, the answer still stands.
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required (it was opportunistic: a listener without STARTTLS received the bridge password in clear); certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter rather than falling back.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until a fixed 30 s after `setup()`, whatever the poll interval, so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing at startup. The inbound message id is chosen by the adapter (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID, which stays in `content` for threading. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts (a new agent's name, a rejection reason) get just the answer. A mail whose handling fails *inside the adapter* (fetch, parse, card lookup, sending a refusal notice) is retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`. **Routing failures inside the host are not retried**: `onInbound` hands the mail over and the host catches its own routing errors, so the mail is already marked read. Messages are fetched one at a time; mail over 40 MB is skipped.
- **Limits**: HTML-only mail uses mailparser's own text conversion. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300, and Message-ID and References are bounded. Attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. State lives under `STORE_DIR`; `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. Loops are stopped by the own-address check, by the inbound filter for bounces and auto-replies, and by a limit of 20 mails an hour from any one sender; beyond it mail is left unread. That limit is what stops two agents answering each other.
- **Message kinds**: the body comes before the subject, so a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743 — a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them, and Proton's clients offer none. Bridge takes `From` from Proton's sender record. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values, and if Proton stopped sending the header, internal mail would go back to being refused.
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, five deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` on this branch → clean
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/` → 746 passed, 19 skipped (68 files), run locally: CI does not run on PRs into `channels`. This includes:

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other. This covers ordinary chat and `/` admin commands as well as cards: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. An owner who writes from a Proton address is identified by mailbox, not by domain (below). For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, which means Proton authenticated the sending account; anyone with a free Proton account is therefore verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card. Approvals additionally need the per-card token, so only someone who can read the approver's mailbox can answer.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, so a stranger cannot park large events in `pending_channel_approvals`.
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Attachment filenames pass `isSafeAttachmentName`; bodies are capped at 50k characters; bounces, auto-replies, mailing lists and mail from the Bridge account's own address are dropped before the router.
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): read document captions, and stop downloading media nobody wants
prs.body:
> **Depends on #3711** (`InboundMessage.resolveContent` in trunk). Until that lands and `channels` re-syncs, the `resolveContent` field here is simply ignored and the adapter behaves exactly as it does today — it compiles and passes either way, it just isn't lazy yet.

## Two inbound bugs, both about attachments

### 1. Captioned documents never reached the agent

The text extraction read `conversation`, `extendedTextMessage.text`, and the image and video captions — but **not `documentMessage.caption`**.

A PDF captioned `@Bot ...` in a wired group arrived at the router with empty text, so a pattern-engage wiring could not match it and the whole message — attachment included — was dropped as `no_agent_engaged`. The same words typed on their own routed fine, which makes it a confusing one to report: the group works, the bot answers, but documents silently vanish.

Extraction moves into an exported `extractMessageText()` so the caption-bearing types are one reviewable list. A type missing from that list fails exactly this way — silently — so it's worth having in one place with the media list it must stay in sync with.

### 2. Media was downloaded before anyone wanted it

Every inbound image, video, audio and document was fetched from WhatsApp's CDN as it arrived: for every chat the account is in, whether or not any of them is wired to an agent, and before the engage test that drops most of what is left.

Attachment handling now splits into the two views #3711 adds — `content` is the routing view (text, sender, attachment metadata, no bytes), `resolveContent()` is the delivery view with the bytes fetched.

## Shape of the change

`downloadInboundMedia` splits in two:

- **`detectInboundMedia()`** — names attachments from the envelope alone, no network. The traversal guard on the attacker-controlled `documentMessage.fileName` moves here, since it belongs with naming rather than with the fetch. This is also what now answers *"does this message have media?"* for the empty-protocol-message guard, so that guard no longer depends on a successful download.
- **`fetchInboundMedia()`** — takes those refs and does the network part, unchanged otherwise (same `reuploadRequest` handling, same `DATA_DIR/attachments` destination, same `localPath` result).

`appendMediaFailureNote` moves onto the delivery view with the fetch. It used to run **before** routing, where a failed download could change the very text the engage pattern was about to match against.

## Tests

`src/channels/whatsapp-inbound-content.test.ts` — extraction per caption-bearing type (including the document caption that regressed), and detection: sender-supplied filenames, generated fallbacks, the traversal guard, and multi-attachment ordering.

All WhatsApp tests on this branch pass: 5 files, 72 tests. The change introduces no new type errors (28 before, 28 after — all pre-existing on `channels`, from `local-web`/`deltachat` against modules this branch doesn't carry yet).

prs.title: fix(cross-session-context): copy attachments onto echo and backfill rows
prs.body:
fix(cross-session-context): copy attachments onto echo and backfill rows

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Agents now see the files on messages copied in from the conversation's other threads (live echoes and dm/channel-timeline backfill). Before this, those copies carried text only.

- **Problem**: a copy of a message in another session kept only `text`. Its files stay in the source session's `inbox/`, and the target container mounts only its own session folder. Separately, `formatEchoMessage` never calls `formatAttachments`. Live-hit on Slack: a thread root with a screenshot reached the agent as `<channel-history …>see the screenshot</channel-history>`, with no file. Media-only messages (no text) were dropped from fan and backfill entirely (`if (!parsed.text) return 0`).
- **Fix (host)**: new `copyEchoAttachments` (`src/modules/cross-session-context/attachments.ts`) copies each staged file into the target session's `inbox/<echo-row-folder>/` and lists it on the row in the usual `attachments` shape. Used by `writeEcho` (fan) and `backfillSession`.
- **Fix (router)**: `writeSessionMessage` now resolves to the content as written (staged `localPath`, no base64). The router fans that version instead of the raw event, so the fan copies files from disk.
- **Fix (container)**: `formatEchoMessage` appends `formatAttachments(content.attachments)` inside `<dm-history>`, `<channel-history>` and `<cross-session-context>`, using the same format as `<message>`.
- **Media-only messages** now fan and backfill when they have attachments.
- **Guardrails**: at most 25 MiB of files are copied per echo row (`ECHO_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES`). A file past the cap, or one that can't be copied, stays on the row by name with no path (`[image: x.png]`), so the agent still knows it was there. One bad file never drops the row.
- **Out of scope**: files on the agent's own outbound posts (outbox `files`). Those echoes stay text-only, as before.

<details><summary>How the live case happens</summary>

In a per-thread room, an untagged message is stored in its thread's session. A later new session in the same conversation (another thread, or a reply that roots a new session) gets the conversation's top-level timeline through `backfillSession`, and live sibling messages through `fanInboundMessage`. Both wrote `{ text, sender, echo }` only.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue. Touches `deliverToAgent` next to #3711 (deferred inbound content). The two compose: this fans the content as written, so once #3711 lands, its resolved delivery view is what gets copied.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- The first commit adds only the tests. Each one failed on `main` before the fix:
  - `container/agent-runner/src/cross-session-echo.test.ts` › `attachments` (5 tests): files on dm-history, channel-history and cross-session-context rows; name-only files; XML escaping
  - `src/modules/cross-session-context/backfill.test.ts` › `backfillSession — attachments` (4): the copy lands in the target inbox; a media-only root is kept; a planted symlink is not followed; an `inbox/../` source path is refused
  - `src/modules/cross-session-context/fan.test.ts` › `fanInboundMessage` › `attachments` (3): per-sibling copy; media-only fan; size cap
  - `src/host-core.test.ts` › `a sibling thread's echo of a message with a file carries its own copy of the file`: end to end through `routeInbound`
- `pnpm test` → 4244 passed, 1 failed: `src/group-skills.test.ts` › `resolves the legacy shape…`. That test fails the same way on unmodified `main` in this environment, so it is unrelated.
- `bun test` (container/agent-runner, Bun 1.4.3) → 632 pass, 0 fail
- `pnpm run build`, `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `eslint` on touched files → clean
- Real install: Slack's API shows 38 messages with files over 2 weeks. Every original row had its files, and every text-only copy in other sessions (`dm-timeline`, `channel-timeline`, `dm-thread`) had none.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Agents now see images and files on messages from earlier in the conversation (channel/DM history and other threads), not just the text.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Both session folders are writable by containers, so the host reads the source inbox and writes the target inbox only through `AnchoredDir`: symlinked `inbox`/message folders are refused, and source files are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and must be regular files. The target is created exclusively, so no entry is followed or overwritten. Same pattern as `forwardAttachedFiles` (agent-route.ts).
- The source `localPath` must be exactly `inbox/<safe>/<safe>` (checked with `isSafeAttachmentName`). The target folder comes from `inboxFolderName(echoRowId)`.
- No new audience: echoes still go only to sessions of the same agent group and the same messaging group, which already received the text. The size cap limits disk use and is not a trust boundary, since both sessions belong to the same agent group.
- Tests: symlink planted in the source inbox; a traversal path.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep delivery ownership valid on allocation failure
prs.body:
## Summary

Scheduler delivery replacement now copies each string before releasing its old value, so an allocation failure cannot leave teardown owning freed memory.

- Apply allocate-before-free to channel, account, destination, peer, and thread strings in [src/daemon.zig](src/daemon.zig).
- Update each pointer and its ownership flag together, without a fallible operation after releasing its old value.
- Keep merge teardown and error propagation; a replacement-copy failure returns before saving the store.

Successful routing propagation, scheduling values, the store format, and retry policy are unchanged. Missing-job insertion is unchanged.

## Validation

With Zig 0.16.0, the focused `zig test` run filtered to `upsertSchedulerRuntimeJob` and `mergeSchedulerTickChangesAndSave` passed all six tests, with no failures or skips.

The new allocation-failure and store-preservation tests fail with the original replacement implementation. The store-preservation test reports `Double free detected`: the channel is first freed by `upsertSchedulerRuntimeJob`, then freed again by `freeJobOwned` during teardown. These tests check each replacement-copy failure, unchanged store bytes before saving, and scheduling and routing values after a successful retry. Additional coverage checks clearing delivery without allocation, externally added jobs, and runtime agent fields.

`zig build test --summary all` with Zig 0.16.0 succeeded: 13/13 steps, 7496 of 7510 tests passed, 14 skipped, no leaks. The only change from the base run (7493 of 7507) is the three new tests.

## Notes

Risks: The successful replacement path preserves behavior and adds no allocations. The behavior change is limited to allocation failure while replacing an existing job's delivery strings.

Occurrence under real memory pressure is unmeasured.

2 recorded checks pass with this change.

- Scheduler merge and delivery ownership tests
- Daemon formatting

prs.title: fix(http): route socks5 proxies through curl instead of silently ignoring them
prs.body:
## Problem

Both `config_types.zig` and the docs advertise `socks5://` proxy support, but the HTTP layer never implemented it:

```zig
// http_util.zig
var client = try initProxyClientWithOptionalProxy(allocator, proxy);   // -> std.http.Client.initDefaultProxies
```

`std.http.Client` only implements `Client.Proxy.Protocol` = `http` / `https`. Any other scheme is parsed to `null` and dropped **without an error and without a log line**, so the request goes out directly. A configured `socks5://` proxy therefore did nothing except mislead the operator.

## Observed

A Telegram long-poll channel with `"proxy": "socks5://127.0.0.1:10812"` set:

* `nullclaw channels` reported `bot net: ... direct`, while the same proxy worked for `curl -x socks5h://... https://api.telegram.org` (302 in <1s),
* the same proxy configured as `http://` produced a different failure (`TlsInitializationFailed` / plaintext-to-443), proving the proxy field was being applied at all only for http(s),
* net effect: silent direct connections over a filtered path, channel down, nothing in the logs pointing at the proxy.

## Fix

Route requests whose effective proxy is SOCKS (`socks5h://`, `socks5://`, `socks4a://`, `socks4://`, `socks://`, case-insensitive) to the existing secured curl request path, which speaks SOCKS natively. The effective proxy follows the same precedence as before: explicit `proxy` argument first, then the process proxy environment.

http(s) proxies keep using `std.http` — no behaviour change there.

Tradeoff: SOCKS proxies now require `curl` on `PATH` (the Android path already depends on it); the alternative is implementing the SOCKS handshake on top of `std.http`'s tunnel.

## Tests

Unit tests cover scheme detection (`isSocksProxyUrl`) and the selection helper (`socksProxyForUrl`), including http(s) proxies staying on the std path.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep restart budget when a restart is launched (hot restart loop)
prs.body:
## Problem

`ChannelManager.supervisionLoop()` calls `recordSuccess()` right after a restart has been *launched*:

```zig
self.spawnPollingThread(entry, rt) catch |err| { ... };
entry.supervised.recordSuccess();   // <-- resets restart_count and backoff_ms
```

`recordSuccess()` resets `restart_count = 0` and `backoff_ms = 1000`. So when a channel keeps failing *after* every restart, the supervisor

* logs `Restarting <channel> (attempt 1)` forever — the counter never advances,
* always sleeps the initial backoff (1000 ms) — no exponential growth,
* never reaches `gave_up`, so the channel silently stays down.

## Observed

A Telegram long-poll channel whose TLS handshakes were failing (transparent-proxy interference on the direct path) produced, over ~2 hours:

```
warning(channel_loop): Telegram poll error: error.TlsInitializationFailed
warning(channel_manager): telegram issue: health check failed
info(channel_manager): Restarting telegram (attempt 1)          <- x258, always "attempt 1"
```

No `gave up after max restarts` ever appeared, and pending updates piled up unanswered because the channel was stuck in the loop.

## Fix

Add `SupervisedChannel.recordRestartLaunched()`: a restart was launched, so the channel is up again but **not proven healthy**. It keeps the failure budget (and therefore the exponential backoff) and leaves the state as `restarting`; the existing `recordSuccess()` path on a healthy probe still resets everything.

Both restart sites (gateway-loop channels and polling channels) now use it, so a persistently failing channel escalates `1s → 2s → 4s → …` and eventually reports `gave up after max restarts` instead of hot-looping at attempt 1.

Adds a unit test covering the budget-preserving restart path.

## Verification

CI (zig build + tests) on this branch.

prs.title: ci(dependabot): stop unmergeable dependency PRs
prs.body:
## Summary

Recent Dependabot npm PRs (#2968–#2973, #2852, #2857) could not be merged as-is: they were major upgrades needing code migration, or single-package bumps of version-locked families. This change makes Dependabot only open PRs that are actually useful for this repo.

- `versioning-strategy: increase-if-necessary` — `package-lock.json` is gitignored, so updates inside a `^` range already install automatically; PRs that only raise the floor are noise.
- Ignore `semver-major` for all npm deps. Majors (vite 8, mermaid 12, Electron 45, js-x-ray 16, …) need migration work and should be deliberate PRs.
- Ignore `semver-minor` for the 12 `0.x` dependencies, where a minor bump is breaking and the major rule does not apply (e.g. katex 0.16 → 0.19 would split katex from `rehype-katex` and break mhchem `\ce`).
- Group `@univerjs/*` (34 packages pinned to one version) and `@docx-editor.dev/*` so they move together instead of producing mixed-version installs.
- Remove the `electron*` group (it bundled electron with electron-builder and electron-log) and the `@anthropic-ai/*` group (no such deps anymore).

The github-actions section is unchanged.

## Notes

- A grouped Univer PR will still need manual follow-up: Dependabot does not touch `overrides`, and `scripts/sheet-third-party-notices.cjs` must be regenerated.
- Major upgrades no longer get reminders. Electron 43 reaches EOL when 46 ships (~mid-December 2026) and needs a planned upgrade.
- Ignore rules may also suppress Dependabot security-update PRs; the weekly `npm audit` in `security.yml` remains (non-blocking).

## Testing

Validated the file against the SchemaStore `dependabot-2.0` JSON schema, and checked that every `0.x` dependency in `package.json` is covered and that the groups match 34 and 2 packages. No code changes.

prs.title: fix(web-search): keep bundled dist usable after copying and stop npm repairs that cannot work
prs.body:
## Summary
In packaged builds, the bundled `web-search` skill was judged "dist outdated" every time it was copied. Startup then ran `npm install` + `npm run build`, which can never succeed in a packaged copy, so the Web Search bridge server did not start. This PR fixes that check, removes npm repair paths that can't help packaged copies, and stops `WEB_SEARCH_FORCE_REPAIR` from deleting a healthy `iconv-lite`.

Evidence from a real packaged build (macOS, 2026.10.30), in `main-2026-11-02.log`:
```
[SkillServices] Repaired web-search runtime from bundled resources
[SkillServices] Installing/reparing web-search dependencies...
[SkillServices] Compiling web-search TypeScript...
[error] [SkillServices] Failed to start Web Search service: Error: Command failed: npm run build
```

Root causes:
- Copying resets mtimes: packaging (`prepareMacSkills` `fs.cpSync`, electron-builder), `syncBundledSkillsToUserData` and `repairWebSearchRuntimeFromBundled` all copy without preserving them. `readdir` order puts `dist/` before `server/`, so the `.ts` sources always end up newer than `dist/server/index.js`. The shipped `.app` bundle already has this order (~0.19 s), so preserving mtimes in `cpRecursiveSync` would not fix it.
- `npm run build` cannot work in a packaged copy: `electron-builder.json` filters `!**/tsconfig.json` out of `SKILLs`, so `tsc` only prints its help text and fails. Since d4ab92fa, Mac builds also no longer ship `typescript`.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- `skillServices.ts`: new `canRebuildWebSearchDist()` (not packaged, and `tsconfig.json` present). Source mtimes are compared only when it is true. `ensureWebSearchRuntimeReady` now fails fast with a clear error when a packaged copy is still unhealthy after the bundle restore. It no longer falls back to a blocking `execSync` npm install/build on the main process, and no longer runs npm inside `Resources` when the bundle itself is the only copy.
- `start-server.sh`:
  - same staleness rule (`can_rebuild_server`);
  - the build step moved into `ensure_server_build()`, which asks the user to restart LobsterAI instead of running npm in a packaged copy;
  - dependency checks moved into `ensure_dependencies()`;
  - `WEB_SEARCH_FORCE_REPAIR` no longer reinstalls `iconv-lite` unconditionally (that needed npm just to restart, and offline it deleted a healthy package);
  - `verify_iconv_runtime` now decodes once, so missing encodings (the `Cannot find module …encodings` errors that `search.sh` reacts to) are actually detected.
- web-search skill bumped to `1.0.3`, so existing installs get a clean copy with the new `start-server.sh`.
- Dev behavior is unchanged: a source checkout (with `tsconfig.json`) still runs install + build when sources change or `dist` is missing.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed (not yet run in a packaged app)

Details:
- New `src/main/skills/skillServices.webSearchDist.test.ts` (14 tests). It covers copying through `cpRecursiveSync`, the packaged startup/repair path (no `execSync`), dev rebuild, the legacy dist, and the `start-server.sh` build and dependency steps with a fake npm. Against the unfixed code, the copy, packaged and shell cases fail.
- `skillManager.bundledSync.test.ts`: a newer bundled web-search version clean-copies the skill and keeps `.env`.
- `npm test -- skill`: 280/280. ESLint (CI rules) is clean on the touched TS files. `npm run compile:electron` passes. `bash -n` passes on the script.
- Ran the old and new shell staleness checks read-only on the real installed `.app` bundle and userData copy: old = outdated, new = fresh.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)

## Additional Notes
- No IPC, storage, or OpenClaw config/restart changes.
- On upgrade, the 1.0.3 bump makes every existing install re-copy `web-search` once (`.env` / `accounts.json` are preserved).
- A full `npm test` run locally also shows failures in `windowsInstallerContract`, `sheetCommandPolicy` and `mcpLaunchResolverManager`. They come from files missing in this worktree's `node_modules` and from the local npm path, and are unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): keep sessions_spawn children off model-picked models
prs.body:
## Summary

Users reported subagents sometimes running on expensive models (e.g. Kimi) instead of the main agent's model.

Root cause in OpenClaw v2026.8.1:
- `sessions_spawn` accepts any `model` the LLM passes, and an explicit value always wins (upstream keeps this by design: openclaw/openclaw#90763, openclaw/openclaw#89522 closed as not planned).
- Same-agent children fall back to the agent's configured model, not the session's active model (`modelSelectionScope: 'session'` keeps session switches local). Upstream fixed only this part in v2026.9.5 (openclaw/openclaw#149036).

## Change

`lobster-model-routing` now rewrites the `sessions_spawn` model in `before_tool_call`:
- Same-agent spawn → the requesting run's selected model (recorded in `before_model_resolve`, before virtual presets resolve, so `yd-fast` children keep the preset).
- Cross-agent spawn → `'default'`, i.e. the target agent's own configured model.
- Unknown requester model → `'default'` (previous 8.1 behavior); ACP spawns untouched.
- Each rewrite logs `[lobster-model-routing] sessions_spawn model A -> B`.

No OpenClaw patch, IPC, storage, or config sync change. Takes effect after the gateway reloads the extension.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 761 files passed.
- ESLint (CI rules) on changed files: clean.
- E2E on a dev gateway: session pinned to `deepseek-flash-YoudaoInner`, LLM told to spawn with `kimi-k3.1-pro-YoudaoInner`:
  - self spawn → ran on `deepseek-flash-YoudaoInner`
  - cross-agent spawn → ran on target agent's `yd-fast`
  - zero Kimi requests in gateway logs.

prs.title: fix(packaging): stop shipping source maps, tsc output and unused runtime files
prs.body:
## Summary

The installer carries a lot of files the app never loads. This PR removes the ones that can be dropped without changing any dependency or runtime behavior. The largest is every renderer and main-process source map, which was shipped inside `app.asar`.

Root cause for the source maps: `electron-builder.json` lists `"!**/*.map"` at the top level of `files`, but that pattern only applies to the app-root matcher. The `dist` and `dist-electron` FileSets (`from`/`to`/`filter`) use only their own `filter: ["**/*"]`, so all `.map` files were packaged. The 2026.9.17 macOS build had 85 MB of maps in `app.asar`; the current build would ship about 160 MB.

## Changes

- **`electron-builder.json`**
  - `dist` and `dist-electron` FileSets exclude `**/*.map`.
  - `dist-electron` also excludes the tsc-emitted subtrees (`common`, `main`, `renderer`, `scheduledTask`, `shared`). `npm run compile:electron` emits them, but the app runs the Vite bundle `dist-electron/main.js` and nothing loads them.
  - `win.electronLanguages: ["en-US", "zh-CN", "zh-TW"]` drops the other Chromium `locales/*.pak` on Windows.
- **`scripts/prune-openclaw-runtime.cjs`**: new `RUNTIME_UNUSED_PATHS` step.
  - Removes `tree-sitter-bash/src` and `tree-sitter-bash/prebuilds`. OpenClaw only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` through `web-tree-sitter`.
  - Removes the type-only packages `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `bun-types` when present.
- **`src/renderer/assets/startup-credit-poster.png`**: downscaled from 5884×4136 to 1296×911 (5.9 MB → 1.4 MB), sRGB profile kept. It renders at most 432px wide, so 1296px still covers 3× displays.

## Size impact (uncompressed)

| Item | Removed |
|---|---|
| Source maps in `app.asar` | ~160 MB (current build) |
| tsc output tree in `dist-electron` | ~5–9 MB |
| Windows Chromium locales | ~40 MB (estimate, not measured on Windows) |
| `tree-sitter-bash` sources/prebuilds | 18 MB |
| Startup poster | 4.5 MB |

Source maps compress well, so the reduction in the dmg/installer is smaller than these numbers.

## Electron-specific notes

- **Packaging only.** No IPC, preload, storage or OpenClaw config changes.
- **Windows locales**: `app.getLocale()` reports `en-US` when the system locale's `.pak` is missing. First-run i18n only picks Chinese for `zh-CN` (`inferLanguageFromLocale`), so keeping `zh-CN` (and `zh-TW`) preserves the current language choice. A test guards that `zh-CN` stays in the list.
- **macOS locales are intentionally unchanged.** electron-builder only trims `Contents/Resources/*.lproj` on macOS, and those directories are empty. The 47 MB of Chromium locales live inside `Electron Framework.framework`, so `electronLanguages` would save nothing there and would only change `app.getLocale()`.
- **Runtime prune**: `buildScriptHash` changes, so the next `electron:dev:openclaw` may rebuild the runtime.

## Not included

- `typescript` in `SKILLs/web-search/node_modules` (Windows) stays. The runtime recompiles the skill when it thinks `dist` is stale, so removing it is not safe yet. That staleness check is being fixed separately.
- Renderer-only libraries packaged under `app.asar/node_modules` (about 370 MB in the current build, e.g. `@univerjs/*`, `mermaid`, `echarts`, `pdfjs-dist`) are left for a follow-up PR. The main process is bundled and does not require them, but `app.asar/node_modules` is on `NODE_PATH` for agent scripts, so this needs its own smoke test.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` on `tests/pruneOpenClawRuntime.test.ts`, `tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts`, `tests/skillMacDependencies.test.ts`, `tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts`, `tests/openclawRuntimePackaging.test.ts`, `tests/openclawWindowsPayload.test.ts` and `tests/openclawBundleAssets.test.ts`: 131 passed.
- New `tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts` runs electron-builder's own file matchers on a fixture. With the old filters the same check ships `.map` files and the tsc tree.
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on the touched test files: clean.
- Ran `npm run openclaw:prune` on the local mac-arm64 runtime: 18 MB freed. `web-tree-sitter` still loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` and parses `ls -la | grep foo && echo ok` without errors.
- Unsigned `electron-builder --mac --arm64 --dir` build: `app.asar` has 0 `.map` files and no tsc subtrees, and `dist-electron/main.js`, `dist-electron/preload.js` and `dist/index.html` are present.
- Not done: launching the packaged app, and a Windows build.

prs.title: fix(cowork): reconnect model streams that drop mid-reply
prs.body:
## Problem

Users increasingly see `⚠️ Agent couldn't generate a response. Note: some tool actions may have already been executed` (and, on the first call of a turn, "模型响应超时"). Local transcripts and user logs show the same cause every time: the model SSE stream is cut off mid-reply before any visible output.

- The token proxy aborts the downstream response when the upstream stream fails (`net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR`, `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED`) or ends without a terminal packet, so OpenClaw sees undici `TypeError: terminated`.
- OpenClaw v2026.8.1 can resume such drops after a settled tool batch, but only when the transport records a `provider_transport_failure` diagnostic. Only the ChatGPT Responses transport does that, so OpenAI-compatible completions (LobsterAI's own models) never resumed.
- First-call drops are never retried because `openclaw-skip-turn-replay-after-model-call.patch` closes the outer replay once a model call has started.

One user's 2026-10-30 logs show 6 drops in 30 minutes, all `ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR`; replying "继续" finished every turn.

## Changes

**OpenClaw patch** `zzz-openclaw-stream-drop-reconnect.patch` (documented in the v2026.8.1 patches README, strong validator added)
- Shared `assignTransportErrorDetails` records the diagnostic when a transient socket failure (undici `terminated`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, `ECONNRESET`, ...) left no visible text or tool call. Reasoning-only output still qualifies; errored turns are dropped from replay.
- `attempt-recovery` resumes from the committed transcript with a model-only continuation prompt, also for drops before any tool batch (once the user turn is persisted) and for a resumed attempt that fails again before output, including retryable HTTP failures such as the proxy's 502 while the network settles. Nothing is resubmitted and no tool reruns.
- Up to 5 consecutive continuations with ~1/2/4/8/16 s backoff (±20% jitter), abortable; tool progress restarts the budget.
- Emits `model_retry` agent events (`retrying` with attempt/max/delay/error/code, `exhausted`).

**Cowork / UI**
- New `modelReconnect.ts`; the adapter turns `model_retry` events into a reconnect system row: "连接中断，正在重新连接 n/5" → "已自动重连" / "自动重连 5 次未成功" / "已停止重新连接". It folds into the turn's process once done.
- When reconnects run out, the generic runtime error is replaced with a localized explanation; the technical detail keeps the raw error plus `reconnectAttempts=N/M streamError=... code=...`. The error card offers a **Continue** button.
- IM reply assembly does not treat the reconnect row as an inbound turn boundary.

## Electron-specific behavior

- OpenClaw runtime changes: rebuild the runtime (`npm run openclaw:runtime:host`); a running gateway keeps the old runtime until restarted.
- New agent event stream `model_retry`; new system message kind `model_reconnect`; new error metadata flag `modelStreamInterrupted`. No IPC, storage schema, or config changes.

## Testing

- OpenClaw: new transport, recovery, and full-entry `runEmbeddedAgent` integration tests; the full patch set applies cleanly to a fresh v2026.8.1 tree with strong validation. Embedded-runner and transport suites pass except `server-endpoint-compaction.test.ts`, which fails the same way without this patch.
- LobsterAI: `npm test` passes except patch checks that read a stale local `../openclaw` (pass with `OPENCLAW_SRC` pointing at a tree with this branch's patches); `tsc` (renderer + electron) and ESLint on changed files pass.
- End to end against the rebuilt runtime with a mock OpenAI-compatible server that cuts the socket mid-stream: first-call drop, drop after a tool (tool ran once), sustained 502 during recovery, and exhaustion after 5 retries.
- In the app with the mock as a custom provider: reconnect row recovered at 2/5 and the reply arrived; with constant drops, the row ended failed, the localized error and Continue button appeared, and Continue started a new turn.

Not covered: drops after visible text has streamed (resuming would duplicate text) keep the existing error. The server-side `ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR` resets still need investigation by trace id.

Bumps [@univerjs/find-replace](https://github.com/dream-num/univer) from 1.0.2 to 1.0.3.
Release notes

Sourced from @​univerjs/find-replace's releases.

🕶️ Release v1.0.3

New features

  • Pivot tables (Pro): Copy pivot tables together with worksheets.
  • Shape hyperlinks (Pro): Show hyperlink popups when hovering over shape text in Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Boards.
  • Notifications: Support custom CSS classes per notification.
  • Extensions: Expose the destination worksheet name to copy-sheet interceptors.

Improvements and fixes

  • Formulas: Improve conditional aggregate performance with array criteria.
  • Cell editing: Double-click a cell to select its editable content.
  • Sheets: Fix automatic row heights after paste, filter range updates, and formula editor focus and help positioning.
  • Docs: Preserve selections in long documents and improve paste controls.
  • Emoji picker: Support searching by localized names and keywords.
  • Networking: Fix interceptor disposal and completion handling for merged requests.
  • Cross-document formulas (Pro): Fix stale results after referenced sheets become available.
  • Embedded editors (Pro): Fix missing tools, scrolling behavior, and shape tool activation.
  • Boards (Pro): Avoid redundant undo entries for unchanged text styles.
  • Docs (Pro): Fix mobile editor dependencies and hide empty table menus.
  • Charts (Pro): Fix referenced data-source selection and activation.
  • Collaboration (Pro): Respect the offline-caching setting from startup.

Breaking changes and upgrading

Custom Pro chart integrations require updates:

  • Chart reference APIs moved from @univerjs-pro/engine-chart to @univerjs-pro/chart-embed. Register UniverChartEmbedPlugin when using referenced charts.
  • ChartReferencedDataSourceEditor was removed. Custom editors should use ReferencedDataSelector from @univerjs-pro/embed-unit-ui with host-specific controls.
  • ChartResourceRepository is now abstract and requires host-specific data-source decoding.
  • Saved chart resources no longer include a version field. Existing supported resources remain readable, but older SDK versions may reject newly saved resources.

Keep interdependent Univer and Univer Pro packages aligned at 1.0.3, including applications that read and write shared chart resources.

prs.body:
Bumps [@univerjs/find-replace](https://github.com/dream-num/univer) from 1.0.2 to 1.3.1.
Release notes

Sourced from @​univerjs/find-replace's releases.

🕶️ Release v1.3.1

Full changelog: v1.3.0…v1.3.1

🎃 Release v1.3.0

👻 Halloween is around the corner, and Univer 1.3.0 comes with a few treats 🎃 This release adds slicers, timelines, and expanded pivot grouping, alongside improvements to document editing, rendering performance, and everyday interactions.

New features

Slicers and timelines (Pro)

Filter tables and pivot reports with interactive slicers. Timelines provide date-range filtering for pivot tables and pivot charts, with year, quarter, month, and day views.

Three new packages provide the feature:

Package Purpose
@univerjs-pro/slicer Shared slicer and timeline models, rendering, and themes.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer Worksheet integration, data-source connections, commands, and Facade APIs.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer-ui Interactive controls, insertion menus, settings, and connection dialogs.

These plugins and the slicer Facade API are included in UniverSheetsAdvancedPreset. For direct plugin integrations, register the Sheets Slicer and Sheets Slicer UI plugins and load the corresponding styles and locales.

Expanded pivot grouping (Pro)

Group selected items manually, organize numbers into ranges, and group dates by calendar units. These capabilities work with connected slicers and timelines for interactive report filtering.

Code block fonts and table alignment (Pro)

Code blocks now support built-in and custom monospaced fonts on desktop and mobile. Fonts registered with FontCategory.MONOSPACE are available in the code block font picker.

Traditional documents also gain left, center, and right table alignment controls in the Ribbon.

Conditional formatting: Stop If True

Use “Stop If True” to prevent lower-priority formatting rules from applying when a rule matches. The rule editor and rule list now expose this setting.

Improvements and fixes

  • UI: Move overflowing Ribbon groups into a compact More menu, improve the color picker, and support resetting sheet tab colors.
  • Sheets: Preserve text values during formatting, correct number-format colors, and retain table borders after filtering.
  • Sheets: Improve mobile editing and row/column resizing, and support Format Painter on row and column headers.
  • Docs: Improve block dragging, pasting, and focus handling across embedded editors and multiple instances.
  • Bases (Pro): Improve view tabs, hierarchical rows, and selection interactions.
  • Performance (Pro): Improve PDF scrolling and zooming, and reduce rendering work for 3D charts.
  • Collaboration and export (Pro): Provide clearer license errors, expose server rejection reasons through CollaborationConflict.message, and fix formatting loss in generated collaboration snapshots.

Breaking changes and upgrading

Keep all @univerjs/* and @univerjs-pro/* packages on the same version.

🎃 Release v1.3.0

👻 Halloween is around the corner, and Univer 1.3.0 comes with a few treats 🎃 This release adds slicers, timelines, and expanded pivot grouping, alongside improvements to document editing, rendering performance, and everyday interactions.

New features

Slicers and timelines (Pro)

Filter tables and pivot reports with interactive slicers. Timelines provide date-range filtering for pivot tables and pivot charts, with year, quarter, month, and day views.

Three new packages provide the feature:

Package Purpose
@univerjs-pro/slicer Shared slicer and timeline models, rendering, and themes.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer Worksheet integration, data-source connections, commands, and Facade APIs.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer-ui Interactive controls, insertion menus, settings, and connection dialogs.

These plugins and the slicer Facade API are included in UniverSheetsAdvancedPreset. For direct plugin integrations, register the Sheets Slicer and Sheets Slicer UI plugins and load the corresponding styles and locales.

Expanded pivot grouping (Pro)

Group selected items manually, organize numbers into ranges, and group dates by calendar units. These capabilities work with connected slicers and timelines for interactive report filtering.

Code block fonts and table alignment (Pro)

Code blocks now support built-in and custom monospaced fonts on desktop and mobile. Fonts registered with FontCategory.MONOSPACE are available in the code block font picker.

Traditional documents also gain left, center, and right table alignment controls in the Ribbon.

Conditional formatting: Stop If True

Use “Stop If True” to prevent lower-priority formatting rules from applying when a rule matches. The rule editor and rule list now expose this setting.

Improvements and fixes

  • UI: Move overflowing Ribbon groups into a compact More menu, improve the color picker, and support resetting sheet tab colors.
  • Sheets: Preserve text values during formatting, correct number-format colors, and retain table borders after filtering.
  • Sheets: Improve mobile editing and row/column resizing, and support Format Painter on row and column headers.
  • Docs: Improve block dragging, pasting, and focus handling across embedded editors and multiple instances.
  • Bases (Pro): Improve view tabs, hierarchical rows, and selection interactions.
  • Performance (Pro): Improve PDF scrolling and zooming, and reduce rendering work for 3D charts.
  • Collaboration and export (Pro): Provide clearer license errors, expose server rejection reasons through CollaborationConflict.message, and fix formatting loss in generated collaboration snapshots.

Breaking changes and upgrading

Keep all @univerjs/* and @univerjs-pro/* packages on the same version.

prs.body:
Bumps [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid) from 10.9.8 to 12.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from mermaid's releases.

mermaid@12.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #8394 6ac38cb Thanks @​jackroberts236! - feat: Add opt-in mindmap coloring by hierarchy depth using mindmap.colorBy: depth and the existing theme palette.

Patch Changes

  • #8409 419ee68 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: size circle and double-circle nodes from their label instead of minNodeWidth, and trim neo circle padding

  • #8395 2fb3ff1 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: ELK no longer straightens an edge terminal when that would put a label over another edge, or an edge through a label

  • #8394 cbf89ab Thanks @​jackroberts236! - fix: Keep mindmap HTML labels readable in the neo look on themes that repaint node backgrounds

  • #8390 430ac9b Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: Centre mindmap node labels when htmlLabels is false

  • #8161 d7532ed Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix: scope a swimlane cluster's DOM id like every other cluster, so two diagrams on one page do not collide

  • #8270 ad8d61a Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(rendering): clip an edge for the layout engine that drew it, so a diagram pinning its own engine (bpmn, swimlanes) still renders when the configured default is another one

  • #8383 9d41c0f Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): split shared terminal lanes again after crossing cleanup, so an edge that detours around another lane no longer ends on the same attachment point as a neighbouring edge

  • #8384 6c67397 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): move a lane's title band clear of an edge that crosses it, in LR diagrams whose lanes carry no direction of their own and when the edge runs along the band's border

  • #8366 40124c3 Thanks @​SwastikTripathi! - fix: swimlane nodes with no edges keep their source order inside a lane instead of being sorted by ID

mermaid@12.1.0

Minor Changes

  • #8303 9140716 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - feat: add the elk.orientFeedbackEdges option, enabled by default. With the ELK layout, an edge from a node that a subgraph feeds back into that subgraph is now routed downstream instead of around the subgraph. This changes the layout of existing ELK diagrams that contain such edges; set elk.orientFeedbackEdges: false to keep the previous routing.

  • #8250 fd4f5f2 Thanks @​kartben! - feat: add a bitOrder option to packet diagrams. It defaults to ascending, which is the current behaviour, and descending mirrors every row so it reads from that row's highest bit down to its lowest. Fields are still declared lowest bit first and keep their width, so switching a diagram between the two conventions only means changing bitOrder.

Patch Changes

  • #8330 50c9e55 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: upgrade chevrotain to 13 so mermaid no longer pulls in vulnerable lodash-es@4.17.23

  • #8259 4c90f5c Thanks @​afonsojanu! - fix(sequence): allow whitespace between an actor name and its @{ ... } config object

    participant Bob@{ "type" : "database" } parsed fine, but adding a single space before the config object (participant Bob @{ "type" : "database" }) failed with a confusing parse error, even though the plain form without a config object tolerates trailing whitespace just fine.

  • #8339 c7fa1a5 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: keep ELK class-diagram cardinalities off namespace frames

  • #8334 d67331d Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix(class): place cardinality labels beside their relation ends on dagre's sides with ELK, centre dagre's end labels, and stop clipping their text

  • #8344 99a050b Thanks @​pbrolin47! - fix: with the ELK layout, an edge label could sit up to 16px beside its edge instead of centred on it, when the edge's terminal jog was straightened after the label's position was computed. The label is now re-projected onto the straightened route

... (truncated)

Bumps the electron group with 2 updates in the / directory: [electron](https://github.com/electron/electron) and [electron-builder](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/tree/HEAD/packages/electron-builder). Updates `electron` from 43.5.0 to 45.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from electron's releases.

electron v45.1.0

Release Notes for v45.1.0

Features

  • Added filtering options to session.registerPreloadScript - matches, excludeMatches, includeGlobs, excludeGlobs, matchOriginAsFallback. #55181 (Also in 44)

Fixes

  • Fixed a crash on Linux when a D-Bus method call was made on a disconnected bus. #55292 (Also in 44, 46)
  • Fixed a main process crash when onSendHeaders observed Blob uploads. #55169 (Also in 44)
  • Fixed extension chrome.webRequest events reporting a tabId of -1 and chrome.declarativeNetRequest rules restricted to tabs never matching. #55283 (Also in 46)
    • Fixed session.clearStorageData() unregistering the service workers of loaded extensions.
    • Fixed chrome.management methods and events being unavailable to extensions with the management permission.
    • Fixed __MSG_*__ placeholders not being localized in extension stylesheets.
    • Fixed extension service workers being stopped after 30 seconds while a WebSocket was active.
    • Fixed sandboxed extension pages being hosted in a process with extension API privileges.
    • Fixed extension service workers running an outdated script after an app restart when the extension's files changed without a version change.
    • Fixed chrome.alarms and content scripts registered with persistAcrossSessions not persisting across app restarts.
  • Fixed File System Access blocklist gaps for .git/hooks writes and hypervisor UNC shares. #55329
  • Fixed handling of malformed asar archives whose size fields do not match the file length. #55175 (Also in 43, 44)
  • Fixed inconsistent handling of asar archive paths between the main process and child processes. #55184 (Also in 43, 44)
  • Fixed Menu.popup() on macOS sometimes not showing a menu after another closed. #55326 (Also in 44, 46)
  • Fixed MV3 extension events not arriving to background service workers. #55154 (Also in 43, 44)
  • Fixed protocol.registerSource schemes not applying the same fetch rules as protocol.handle schemes. #55178 (Also in 44)
  • Fixed requests stalling when an extension used a blocking chrome.webRequest listener. #55271 (Also in 46)
  • Fixed utilityProcess not emitting an exit event when the app quit while the process was still launching. #55274 (Also in 43, 44, 46)

Other Changes

  • Updated Chromium to 156.0.8078.49. #55252
  • Updated Node.js to v24.22.1. #55163

prs.title: ci: bump actions/download-artifact from 4 to 8
prs.body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 4 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

v7.0.0

v7 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v7 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v6 had preliminary support for Node 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

prs.title: fix(data-migration): skip Chromium Partitions in backup and restore
prs.body:
## Summary
Restoring a data-migration backup from inside the running app fails and rolls back because the "clear old data" step hits `EBUSY` on `userData/Partitions`. The in-app browsers use persistent `persist:` partitions (`persist:lobster-artifact-browser`, `persist:lobster-agent-browser`), and the main process keeps their LevelDB/cookie files locked while they are open.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- Add `Partitions` to `SOURCE_EXCLUDED_TOP_LEVEL_NAMES`, so it is left out of migration archives. It is the same kind of machine-local Chromium storage as `Local Storage` / `Network` / `Cookies`, and on Windows its cookies are DPAPI-encrypted per machine, so they could not be decrypted elsewhere anyway.
- Add `Partitions` to `RESTORE_PRESERVED_TOP_LEVEL_NAMES`, so restore leaves the live partition data alone instead of trying to delete it. Archives exported by older builds that still contain `Partitions` are skipped by the same rule. Archive format and manifest validation are unchanged.
- Extend the existing archive and restore tests: `Partitions` is absent from the archive and the rollback archive, runtime partition files are kept, and source partition files are not restored.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/dataMigration/dataMigrationService.test.ts`: 19/19 pass. Without the source change, the 2 updated tests fail.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` / `-p electron-tsconfig.json`: clean. ESLint on the changed files with `--max-warnings 0`: clean.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
N/A

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)

- [ ] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes
Behaviour change: in-app browser partition data (logins/cookies) is no longer carried between machines by migration. It stays on the machine it was created on, the same as the default session's cookies and Local Storage already do.

While a config-driven gateway restart is deferred, starting a new session is rejected with "please try again later" even when the gateway is already idle.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- Root cause: after an MCP/config change that needs a restart, `scheduleDeferredGatewayRestart()` queues the restart until workloads drain (polled every 3 s). Meanwhile `waitForOpenClawConfigApply()` returned the pending/overdue status for every caller as long as `deferredRestartReason` was set, without checking whether the gateway was idle.
- How it is triggered: change MCP servers or config while a task is running (or right before starting a session). The restart is deferred, and the next session start bounces with the "applying configuration" message until the poller happens to fire.
- Fix: extract `admitPastDeferredGatewayRestart()` (`src/main/libs/openclawDeferredRestartAdmission.ts`) and use it in `waitForOpenClawConfigApply()`:
  - idle gateway (the same busy check the poller uses): apply the deferred restart immediately and continue;
  - active workloads: wait up to 45 s for the scheduled restart to land, then await the resulting config apply and continue;
  - still queued after the wait (or re-deferred): return the existing pending / overdue status unchanged;
  - a failed config sync is surfaced instead of the generic pending message (`executeDeferredGatewayRestart()` now returns the sync result).

## Summary
Re-importing a skill that is already installed (a newer ZIP of the same skill, a local folder, or the same GitHub repo) silently installs a second copy as `<id>-1`, `<id>-2`, ... prs.title: fix(media): check user intent before generating paid images and videos
prs.body:
## Summary
The media model selection stays active across messages, and the media generation callback only checks that a model is selected (`resolveMediaGenerationGate`, `src/main/mediaGenerationPolicy.ts`). The chat model can therefore start a paid image or video generation when the user did not ask for one. On a downstream build we saw a refusal ("No image is needed this turn. The user asked not to generate images…") passed as the prompt, rendered into a picture and billed. This PR checks the user's intent before a generate request is submitted, and tightens the per-turn media instruction.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- New `src/main/mediaGenerationIntentGuard.ts`, used by `handleMediaGenerationCallback` right after the existing selection gate and before any cost confirmation. It cancels a generate request (status `cancelled`, with a corrective tool result for the model) when:
  - the latest user message, or an earlier one that no newer message overrides, asks to stop or pause image/video generation. An explicit generation request or a follow-up on earlier media ("make the background red", "another one") lifts the pause.
  - the tool prompt is a refusal or meta instruction instead of a visual description. Negative visual constraints ("no text or watermark", "不要生成图片边框") are still allowed.
  - the assistant asked the user to confirm the media in this turn and has no answer yet. An answered `AskUserQuestion` call resolves it, so generation right after the answer is not blocked.
- Skin workflows (`SkinRuntimeController.hasActiveWorkflow`) only get the prompt check, because they drive their own generation steps.
- `buildMediaGenerationTurnInstruction`: generate only when the current message asks for media; stop requests persist; wait for answers to confirmation questions; the prompt must describe visual content; no simulated tool calls via shell/echo.

prs.title: feat(cowork): add Auto and Max model modes
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds two per-session model modes to Cowork. **Auto** picks a suitable model for every turn. **Max** runs a conversation on the model the user chose as their strongest. The routing policy is derived locally from the models the user can already use and can optionally be overridden in Settings. Nothing changes for users who don't pick either mode.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- **Auto classification** (pure heuristic; no extra model call, latency or tokens): image attachments → vision; roughly ≥6k estimated tokens of prompt plus selected text → long context; fenced code, source-file references or code keywords → code; everything else → general. Precedence: vision > long context > code > general.
- **Policy derivation** (`src/shared/cowork/autoModelRouting.ts`). Candidates are the enabled provider models plus server models that are accessible and pass the existing server run gate. Defaults:
  - general = the session / agent model;
  - code = general;
  - vision = general if it reads images, otherwise the first image-capable model (same provider preferred);
  - long context = the model with the largest known context window, only when it is strictly larger than the general model's.
  Overrides that point at a model that is no longer usable are ignored; anything unresolved falls back to the agent model.
- **Settings**: Settings → Agent Engine → "Auto / Max models" lets users override the general, code, vision and long-context models and choose the Max model. Stored in the Cowork config as `autoModelRouting`.
- **Visibility**: Auto is offered when at least two usable models exist. Max is offered only when a usable Max model is explicitly configured; it is never guessed. Neither is offered for IM-managed sessions.
- **Auto semantics**: stored as the reserved ref `lobsterai/__auto__` in `session.modelOverride` and re-resolved on every turn; the resolved model is patched for that turn only. The sentinel is never written back, never sent to the gateway (selecting Auto stores it locally without a `sessions.patch`), never appears in the outbound prompt, and is skipped by the run gate, thinking-level resolution, error details and the gateway model-echo sync. The selector shows a subtle "This turn: <model>" hint driven by the display-only `cowork:session:modelAutoResolved` event.
- **Max semantics**: a per-session flag that overlays the current selection (an explicit model or Auto). Turning it off restores the previous selection, because the selection itself is never modified.
- **New task**: the home / new-task selector supports Auto and Max for the task it starts; the agent's default model is never changed. Agent configuration and scheduled-task selectors are unaffected.
- **Persistence**: new `cowork_sessions.max_mode INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column added through a required migration following the `thinking_level` pattern; forks carry Auto and Max over. New IPC: `cowork:session:setMaxMode`.
