issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel plugin fails to activate with DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED when a hub plugin (aliyun-hub) has no dependency environment
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2

## Description

The `qq` channel plugin (`dependency_mode: shared`) fails to activate on startup. Activation aborts inside the shared-dependency audit:

```
DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED: qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.
Stop environment consumers before explicit repair and re-audit.
Source rollback does not restore dependency packages.
```

The QQ channel never comes online. The Console "repair dependencies" action returns **409 Conflict** every time, because the repair path re-runs the same failing audit — and its instruction ("stop environment consumers before explicit repair") is unsatisfiable, since `qq` itself is one of the consumers. That is a deadlock with no UI path out.

`aliyun-hub` is an unrelated built-in **hub**-type plugin (Aliyun Skill marketplace source). It has no Python requirements and provides no dependency environment, so it should not be able to block a channel plugin.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2** (PyPI `2.3.0b2`)
- Armbian aarch64 (TV box), Python 3.12.3
- One active agent, one workspace with the `qq` channel enabled
- Workspace plugins present: `aliyun-hub`, `qwenpaw-hub`, `clawhub-hub`, `modelscope-hub`, `memory-console`, `qq`
- `qq` channel: `enabled: true`, official QQ bot `app_id` + `client_secret` configured, previously working on 2.3.0b1

## Reproduction

1. Install 2.3.0b2 with the stock `aliyun-hub` plugin present in the workspace `plugins/` directory.
2. Enable the `qq` channel (`dependency_mode: shared`, `process_mode: runner_process`).
3. Restart qwenpaw.
4. Observe the activation failure above; the QQ channel stays offline.
5. Click "repair dependencies" in the Console → HTTP 409.

## Logs

```
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: aliyun-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qwenpaw-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qq
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: clawhub-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: modelscope-hub
INFO  plugins/registry.py:538 | Registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' from plugin 'qq' (priority=80)
INFO  plugins/api.py:1329 | Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' (priority=80)

ERROR plugins/loader.py:5002 | Failed to activate plugin 'qq': DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED:
      qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
      Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.

INFO  ... "POST /api/plugins/qq/repair-dependencies HTTP/1.1" 409 Conflict
```

There is no `channel_qq` startup line and no runner connection attempt after the failure.

## Root cause analysis (from reading 2.3.0b2 source)

**1. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `DependencyUsageRegistry.observe_host()`** only attaches an environment when an observation succeeded:

```python
self._host[token] = deepcopy(
    replace(
        declaration,
        active=True,
        origin="host",
        snapshot=snapshot,
        environment=(
            DependencyEnvironment.from_snapshot(snapshot)
            if observed and (previous is None or previous.environment is not None)
            else None
        ),
    ),
)
```

**2. `plugins/python_backend.py:963`** — when host dependency observation is inconclusive it explicitly records an unknown state:

```python
def unknown():
    if valid():
        usage.observe_host(token, None)
```

So a host plugin whose imports/requirements can never be resolved ends up in `_host` with `snapshot=None` and `environment=None`.

**3. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `snapshot()`** includes every `_host` entry in `uses` unconditionally:

```python
uses = [
    use for token, use in self._declarations.items()
    if use.pending or token is admission_token
] + list(self._host.values())
```

**4. `plugins/dependency_gate.py` — the audit loop** treats any use with `environment is None` as a hard failure:

```python
for use in uses:
    environment, evidence = use.environment, use.snapshot
    ...
    if environment is None:
        unsupported.append(f"{use.origin} {use.plugin_id}: environment evidence unavailable")
        continue
```

**5.** `unsupported` being non-empty yields `DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED` for the whole shared plan, so **every** `dependency_mode: shared` plugin in that environment is refused activation.

In short: a hub-type plugin with no dependency involvement is registered as a host dependency user, can never produce environment evidence, and that missing evidence is treated as a fatal condition for an unrelated channel plugin's shared plan.

## Suggested fix

Any one of:

- Do not register `type: hub` plugins in `_host` (they have no dependency environment by design); or
- In `snapshot()`, keep host entries with `environment is None` out of the audited `uses`; or
- In `dependency_gate.py`, treat `environment is None` for a use that declares no requirements as "no dependency involvement" instead of `unsupported`.

## Workaround

Moving the `aliyun-hub` plugin directory out of the workspace `plugins/` folder and restarting makes the QQ channel activate with zero errors:

```bash
mv <qwenpaw_home>/working/plugins/aliyun-hub /tmp/aliyun-hub.bak
systemctl restart qwenpaw
```

After this, `Failed to activate plugin 'qq'` disappears, `Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq'` runs, and the QQ bot connects normally.

Downside: the Aliyun skill marketplace source disappears from the Console until the plugin is restored.

issues.title: [Feature]: agent.json 配置热加载范围应覆盖 MCP、Skills 等更多配置项

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## 背景

当前 QwenPaw 的 `agent_config_watcher`（agent.json 文件监控）每2秒轮询一次，但仅监控 `channels` 和 `heartbeat` 两个配置项的 hash 变化（源码见 `app/agent_config_watcher.py`）：

```python
def _channels_hash(channels):
    return hash(str(channels.model_dump(mode="json")))

def _heartbeat_hash(hb):
    return hash(str(hb.model_dump(mode="json")))
```

在实际的使用过程中，存在通过agent访问mcp市场，拉取需要的mcp服务，通过这种方式修改的`mcp.clients`、`skills` 等配置项的修改不会被检测到，导致用户只能通过重启 QwenPaw 来使这些配置生效。

## 建议

扩展 `agent_config_watcher` 的监控范围，增加以下配置项的 hash 检测：

1. `mcp.clients` — MCP 客户端配置变更（增删改 MCP）
2. `skills` — Skills 配置变更
3. 其他高频修改的配置节

## 预期收益

- agent修改 MCP/Skills 配置后无需重启即可生效
- 减少因频繁重启导致的 agent记忆混乱等问题
- 提升 Agent 和用户的配置修改体验

## 备选方案

如果全量监控有性能考虑，也可以：

1. 提供一个 CLI 命令（如 `qwenpaw reload-config`）来手动触发热重载
2. 或者在 QwenPaw 控制台增加"重载配置"按钮

## 参考

当前 `agent_config_watcher.py` 已有完整的 workspace reload 机制（`MultiAgentManager.reload_agent`），只需要扩展触发条件即可。

issues.title: [Bug]: Plugin hot-install aborts when importlib.invalidate_caches() raises on distro-patched Python 3.11（我的插件被这个卡了））

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

## Description

The plugin loader calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally at three
sites (`loader.py:201`, `loader.py:465`, `loader.py:1094`). On Python builds where
this stdlib function itself raises (a real-world distro backport bug, see
Additional Notes), the exception propagates and aborts the entire plugin
install / hot-update.

Cache invalidation is best-effort by design — a failure here should not be fatal.

**Related PR(s):** N/A
**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (Lifsea 8 container, kernel 5.10.134-18.0.12.lifsea8)
- **Install method:** pip (venv)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11.15 (`libpython3.11-minimal 3.11.2-6+deb12u9`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On an affected Python build, verify the environment bug directly:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import importlib; importlib.invalidate_caches()"
   ```

   → `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`

2. With QwenPaw running, install any plugin whose `requirements.txt` contains a
   not-yet-satisfied dependency (Console upload or `qwenpaw plugin install`).
3. The install aborts with the TypeError above; the plugin directory is copied
   into `plugins/` but the plugin never loads.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The entire plugin install fails with `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`.
- **Expected:** A cache-invalidation failure degrades to a warning and the install proceeds.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
File ".../qwenpaw/app/routers/plugins.py", line 847, in upload_plugin
  record = await _load_plugin_with_optional_force_reinstall(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1179, in load_plugin_from_path
  record = await self._load_plugin_from_path_unlocked(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1316, in _load_plugin_from_path_unlocked
  await asyncio.to_thread(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 465, in _install_requirements_locked
  importlib.invalidate_caches()
File "/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/__init__.py", line 70, in invalidate_caches
  finder.invalidate_caches()
File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>", line 1409, in invalidate_caches
TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## Additional Notes

Root cause has two layers:

1. **Environment (not QwenPaw's fault):** this distro build backported the
   CPython 3.12 change "PathFinder.invalidate_caches also clears
   importlib.metadata caches" into 3.11's frozen bootstrap, but the backported
   `/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/metadata/__init__.py` (line 918) lost its
   `@classmethod` decorator:

   ```python
   def invalidate_caches(cls):      # ← @classmethod missing in backport
       FastPath.__new__.cache_clear()
   ```

   So **every** `importlib.invalidate_caches()` call raises. Reproduced with a
   bare interpreter, including under `python3 -S`. The same environment bug
   also breaks `pip`, `pytest`, etc., so QwenPaw cannot rely on the
   environment being fixed — it should tolerate the failure.

2. **QwenPaw side:** `loader.py:201` / `:465` / `:1094` call it unguarded.

**Suggested fix** — wrap all three sites:

```python
try:
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
except Exception:
    logger.warning("importlib.invalidate_caches() failed; continuing", exc_info=True)
```

**Workaround for plugin authors:** ship the plugin without `requirements.txt`
when all deps are already QwenPaw host dependencies — `loader.py:392` returns
early when the file is absent, bypassing the failing path entirely. (Verified:
`pyyaml>=6.0` is already a direct `Requires-Dist` of the `qwenpaw` package.)

labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2b3（桌面端，bundled backend，qwenpaw --version 输出）

## Description

在 Console「技能池 → 广播/下载到智能体」一个大技能（本例 ppt-master：12,994 个文件、解压后 80.1 MB）时，UI 总是在约 30 秒后报错：

Request timeout after 30000ms: POST /skills/pool/download
后端实际仍在执行复制，但最终技能永远无法落到目标工作区。叠加了三个问题：

前端 30 秒 AbortController 硬超时（console/assets/index-*.js 中 fetch 封装，超时即 abort 并抛出上述错误）。大技能的下载耗时远超 30 秒，前端必然放弃。
handler 在 async def 中同步执行整个复制流程，未卸载到线程池（qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py 的 @router.post("/pool/download") → download_pool_skill_to_workspaces，直接调用同步的 SkillPoolService.download_to_workspace，无 run_in_threadpool/asyncio.to_thread）。复制期间整个后端事件循环被阻塞，所有 API 无响应，桌面端表现为整体卡死。
复制中途被杀则前功尽弃：若后端在复制期间被重启（我们每次尝试后都观察到重启，具体是用户重启还是桌面端拉起未定论），进行中的复制被中断，%TEMP% 残留半成品 qwenpaw_skill_stage_<skill>_* 目录（启动时无清理），uvicorn access log 因请求无响应而缺失该次记录。
download_to_workspace 的实现是两轮全量目录复制 + 安全扫描：技能池 → %TEMP% staging（copy_skill_dir）→ scan_skill_dir_or_raise → staging → 目标工作区（第二次 copy_skill_dir）→ 写 manifest。对 13k 文件的技能即约 26,000 次文件操作。

实测（本机有终端 DLP 软件显著拖慢文件 I/O，仅 27~99 files/s）：一次完整下载需要 10 分钟量级。即便在无安全软件的机器上，万级文件技能的两轮复制 + 扫描也很容易超过 30 秒上限——即该 bug 不依赖本机的特殊环境。

Related PR(s): #（无）

Security considerations: 无（不涉及 auth / 敏感信息；仅本地文件复制与临时目录残留）

## Component(s) Affected

 [√]Core / Backend（app/routers/skills.py、agents/skill_system/pool_service.py）
 [√]Console（前端 30s 硬超时）
 [√]Skills（技能池 → 工作区下载路径）

## Environment

QwenPaw version: 2.2.2b3
OS: Windows 10（AMD64）
Install method: 桌面端安装包（D:\QwenPaw，bundled backend + console）
Python version: 捆绑运行时（backend 为 PyInstaller 打包）
补充：企业环境装有终端 DLP（E-SafeNet），文件 I/O 明显偏慢，放大了耗时；但如上所述，结构性问题在正常环境同样成立。

## Steps to Reproduce

在技能池安装一个大技能（如 12,994 文件 / 80 MB 的 ppt-master；或任何数千文件量级的技能目录）。
Console → 技能池 → 选择目标智能体广播（若某目标工作区已有同名技能，会先收到 409 conflict 弹窗，确认覆盖后继续——这一步本身是 all-or-nothing 设计，属正常）。
等待约 30 秒。
UI 报 Request timeout after 30000ms: POST /skills/pool/download；期间整个 Console/后端无响应；若等待期间后端被重启，%TEMP% 出现残缺 staging 目录，目标工作区最终拿不到技能。
（我们今天连续复现 4 次，全部失败。）

## Actual vs Expected

Actual:

- 30 秒后前端报 Request timeout，操作在 UI 层面失败；
  - 复制期间后端事件循环被阻塞，全部接口无响应，应用假死；
  - 复制被后端重启打断后，%TEMP% 残留 qwenpaw_skill_stage_ppt-master_* 半成品目录（我们残留了 6 个，单次最多复制到 7070/13152 项）；
技能从未成功落到任何目标工作区。
- Expected:
  - 大技能下载作为后台任务执行：POST 立即返回 202 + job id，前端轮询进度（已复制/总文件数），完成后刷新；
  - 复制不阻塞后端事件循环；
  - 中断/重启后能恢复或至少启动时清理孤儿 staging 目录。

## Logs / Screenshots

时间线（2026-09-29，同日 4 次尝试；日志来自 desktop.log / qwenpaw.log / %TEMP% 目录时间戳）：

尝试 预检请求(409 conflict) staging 开始 复制中断时进度 后端重启 1 08:58:29 08:58:45 3676/13152 08:59:54 2 09:00:25 09:00:34 6242/13152 09:04:27 3 09:05:33 09:05:48 6086/13152 09:07:26 4 09:08:14 09:08:56 7070/13152 09:10:17
关键佐证：

qwenpaw.log 在复制窗口内完全静默（09:00:32 → 09:04:28 无任何日志），与事件循环被阻塞一致；
uvicorn access log 仅有 409 的预检请求行，实际开始复制的请求无响应行（被杀）；
%TEMP% 残留 qwenpaw_skill_stage_ppt-master_6au3z2p2（3676 项）、_hl_dg_z7（6242）、_7k87z5pw（6086）、_f_in7_va（7070）等 6 个目录；
前端超时代码（console 打包产物）：instanceof DOMException && k.name==="AbortError" → new Error(`Request timeout after ${i}ms: ${n} ${e}`)，其中 i=30000；
路由 handler（2.2.2b3 本地核对）：@router.post("/pool/download") async def 内直接同步调用 hub_service.download_to_workspace(...)。

## Additional Notes

建议的修复方向（按性价比排序）：

下载改为后台任务 + 进度轮询（202/job id 模式），前端不再用 30s 硬超时等待长操作；
至少：handler 用 run_in_threadpool 卸载，避免阻塞事件循环；该端点的前端超时单独放宽或禁用；
后端启动时清理孤儿 qwenpaw_skill_stage_* 目录；
可选优化：池与工作区同盘时省掉 staging 中转（直接复制/重命名），文件操作减半。
Workaround：直接脚本调用 SkillPoolService.download_to_workspace（同一官方 API，无前端超时限制）。

相似但不重复的问题：#6635 / #6633（慢网络下 Console 加载 MB 级 skills 列表超时）——同属"前端对长耗时操作缺乏异步任务机制"这一类，但端点与流程不同。

issues.title: [Bug]: Scroll history synchronization blocks startup and rescans completed migrations

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: context and memory
labels.description: Issue related to context-and-memory

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Code review covers `v2.2.0`, `v2.3.0-beta.1`, and commit `0e2a7a543`.

The exact deployed build for the reported incident still needs confirmation. The startup dependency exists in both reviewed tags; this report does not claim that upgrading alone forces a full reimport or that a final 2.3.0 release has been verified.

## Description

Scroll history synchronization blocks application startup until all configured Scroll agents have been processed sequentially. In a reported deployment, server readiness took approximately **27 minutes**, almost all of which was covered by the history synchronization phase.

Previously synchronized sessions also incur work on subsequent starts. The implementation uses a per-file manifest rather than a durable per-agent migration-completion record. It reads registered session files in full to calculate hashes, attempts ownership updates, and may query the database before deciding to skip importing them.

Normal conversations update session files and write through to the history database, but do not update the migration manifest. Consequently, a changed file can be parsed and processed again even when it adds no history rows.

Expected behavior: history migration should be a one-time preparation step owned by each agent. Completed migrations should be skipped without scanning session files. The default agent should become ready independently of other agents' history, and remaining enabled agents should start with bounded concurrency.

**Security considerations:** This report contains only sanitized summaries and public code identifiers. Customer agent identifiers, workspace paths, absolute timestamps, organization details, endpoint URLs, credentials, and raw logs are intentionally omitted. Counts and timings below are rounded.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** Reported deployment build pending confirmation; reviewed versions listed above.
- **OS:** Not independently verified; no OS-specific root cause established.
- **Install method:** Not independently verified.
- **Python version:** Python 3.11, as indicated by the supplied runtime log paths.
- **Workload:** Approximately 40 agents, 55,000 session files, and 550,000 newly inserted history rows in the reported synchronization run.

## Steps to Reproduce

The following describes a controlled reproduction and validation workload, not a completed local reproduction of the customer environment:

1. Prepare multiple enabled Scroll agents with registered session files and a mixture of previously synchronized and unsynchronized history. Use isolated synthetic data at the approximate scale described above.
2. Start the application and measure history synchronization, HTTP availability, default-agent readiness, and remaining agent startup separately.
3. Observe that global startup awaits synchronization across agents before the existing agent startup scheduler runs.
4. After synchronization completes, restart with the same data. Instrument file enumeration, session-file reads, hashing, and per-session database operations.
5. Continue a conversation so its session file changes while normal Scroll write-through is active, then restart again. Observe that file changes can trigger synchronization processing even when the rows are already durable.

Total elapsed time depends on data size, storage, and database state; 27 minutes is an observed incident duration, not a guaranteed reproduction time.

## Actual vs Expected

**Actual:**

- Application lifespan awaits the global history synchronization helper.
- Offloading to a worker thread keeps the event loop free but does not release the startup dependency.
- Agents are processed sequentially by the synchronization loop, before prioritized agent startup.
- A manifest cache hit still incurs full-file hashing and database access.
- There is no durable agent-level completion state that retires a successful migration from ordinary startup.
- Normal database construction can perform integrity checks and FTS repair, potentially moving latency to agent initialization or the first conversation if only the global synchronization call is removed.

**Expected:**

- HTTP initialization does not await a global history migration.
- Each agent handles its own necessary migration before accepting work.
- The default agent has priority and does not wait for other agents' migration completion.
- Remaining enabled agents use the existing bounded startup queue, with a default concurrency of 5.
- A completed agent migration performs no session enumeration, content reads, hashing, or per-session database verification during ordinary startup.
- Integrity verification, repair, and retention maintenance have explicit execution paths separate from migration completion and normal database opening.

## Logs / Screenshots

Sanitized summary of the supplied logs; these are rounded measurements, not verbatim log lines:

| Measurement | Approximate value |
| --- | ---: |
| Server readiness | 27 minutes |
| Visible history synchronization span | 27 minutes |
| Additional time until core-agent readiness | 18 seconds |
| Scroll agents processed | 40 |
| Session files enumerated | 55,000 |
| Files classified as unchanged | 27,000 |
| Files entering synchronization | 23,000 |
| Newly inserted history rows | 550,000 |
| Unregistered files skipped | 5,000 |

One anonymized agent processed approximately 600 files and inserted zero rows; its completion log followed the previous agent's completion by roughly 100 seconds. This interval includes multiple possible phases and is not an exact per-function timing.

The newly inserted rows require separate investigation: the supplied logs do not establish whether they resulted from missing legacy history, database recovery, write-through gaps, or identity changes. Unchanged file hashes alone would not explain those insertions.

## Additional Notes

### Root cause and relevant code

- `src/qwenpaw/app/_app.py`: lifespan awaits `_sync_scroll_history_on_startup()`, which awaits `run_sync_io(sync_all_scroll_agents)`.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/sync.py`: `_sync_all_scroll_agents()` processes profiles sequentially; `sync_sessions_to_history()` hashes registered files and calls `claim_session()` before the skip decision.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/history.py`: ordinary initialization performs database integrity work and FTS checks/repair.
- `src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py`: an existing bounded startup scheduler already supports the required concurrency. Currently, default and built-in QA share a core-readiness barrier.
- `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py`: the proposed integration point for per-agent migration before business services start.

### Proposed remediation

#### 1. Move migration into agent startup

Remove the global synchronization call from application lifespan. Invoke a single-agent migration entry point from `Workspace.start()`, after configuration and required layout migration, but before channels, scheduled jobs, and other business services accept work.

Run blocking migration I/O in a worker thread and await it only within the corresponding agent's startup. An agent becomes RUNNING after its own migration and service initialization complete.

This deliberately means a default agent with a large, unfinished migration can still take time to become usable. The HTTP status surface should remain available; other agents' migration duration must no longer be added to that wait.

#### 2. Reuse bounded parallel startup

Start default first and publish readiness independently of built-in QA. Put QA near the front of the remaining agent queue.

Reuse `QWENPAW_CUSTOM_AGENT_STARTUP_CONCURRENCY` (default: 5). Each slot covers migration plus service initialization. Start the next queued agent as soon as a slot becomes available; do not impose a barrier between fixed batches.

Requests for an already queued agent must join its existing startup task rather than duplicate migration or bypass the limit. Disabled agents must not have their history scanned. Agents sharing a database path need serialized migration access to that database rather than competing writers.

#### 3. Persist a migration-completion record

Add a small metadata table inside `history.db`, logically keyed by `(agent_id, migration_key)` with a completion timestamp. The migration key identifies a specific data transformation, not the application release version.

- Completion exists: return immediately without reading the manifest or enumerating sessions.
- New, empty workspace: explicitly initialize completion as part of creation.
- Existing data without completion: run the agent's migration once.
- Successful migration: commit completion after all required work succeeds.
- Interrupted or failed migration: retain committed data and progress, but do not mark completion.
- Recreated database: the completion record is absent, so recovery can run.
- Normal conversations, restarts, and configuration reloads: do not invalidate completion.

Keep existing ownership, deduplication, registry, and retention semantics. Orphan files excluded by policy do not prevent completion; unreadable required files, an invalid registry, or failed writes must not be silently reported as success.

#### 4. Handle existing installations once

The existing manifest does not prove that the entire agent's migration finished. On first entry into the new lifecycle, reuse it for one successful reconciliation pass during that agent's startup, then persist completion. Interrupted runs may resume.

After completion, the manifest is no longer consulted on ordinary startup. Do not add a new legacy-format compatibility framework or recreate ongoing file synchronization under another name.

Explicit imports, transitions from native context management to Scroll, database replacement, and recovery must arrange their own necessary backfill. They must not rely on every subsequent startup rescanning all files. Real-time write failures should remain visible and be repaired at the affected-session boundary.

#### 5. Separate maintenance from ordinary database opening

Keep necessary connection and schema initialization, but move full `quick_check`, FTS verification, and rebuild work out of ordinary `HistoryStore` construction into explicit maintenance/recovery paths. Avoid shifting the delay to the first chat or recall request.

Retention cleanup must continue independently of migration completion: run due maintenance after agent readiness and periodically during long-running service, in bounded batches. Preserve the configured retention period and keep VACUUM outside normal startup.

#### 6. Make lifecycle and failures explicit

Reuse existing PENDING / STARTING / RUNNING / FAILED states and add migration phase/progress details where needed. A non-default agent's hard migration failure affects that agent, while the rest of the queue continues. Preserve existing default-failure readiness semantics.

Persist progress at safe boundaries and support cooperative stop checks between bounded transactions and file-processing steps. Cancelling the awaiting coroutine must not leave a worker writing after shutdown. Measure cancellation latency for unusually large files instead of promising an unverified fixed shutdown time.

Startup-time migration reduces normal chat races, but administrative deletion/import, hot reload, and other processes still require existing lifecycle/data-operation coordination. Recovery must also reestablish saved session references to history rows; removing a completion record alone is insufficient.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Remove the global history-migration startup dependency.
- [ ] Integrate single-agent migration before that agent's business services start.
- [ ] Default readiness does not wait for QA or other agents' migrations.
- [ ] Remaining startup work obeys the existing concurrency limit; queued access does not duplicate work.
- [ ] Persist completion in the history database only after successful migration.
- [ ] Completed-agent restarts perform zero session enumeration, content reads, hashing, or per-session verification.
- [ ] Normal conversation updates do not reactivate a completed migration.
- [ ] Legacy installations reconcile once successfully; interruptions resume without duplicate history rows.
- [ ] Disabled agents do not open or scan history during automatic startup.
- [ ] Non-default migration failures are isolated and visible.
- [ ] Ordinary database opening and first chat do not trigger full integrity scans or FTS rebuilds.
- [ ] Imports, strategy changes, hot reload, and recovery maintain correct completion semantics.
- [ ] Retention maintenance continues without gating readiness.
- [ ] Shutdown leaves no orphaned migration worker or false completion record.
- [ ] Adapt existing startup/history tests and add necessary lifecycle regression coverage; all relevant tests pass.
- [ ] Validate at the approximate reported scale, measuring HTTP availability, default readiness, all-agent readiness, disk I/O, memory, and cancellation latency separately.

### Review decisions and rollout

- Confirm that each agent waits for its own migration before becoming usable, including default on first migration.
- Confirm removing QA from default's readiness barrier.
- Confirm that hard migration failures fail the affected agent instead of being swallowed as warnings.
- Confirm the explicit maintenance/recovery entry point and retention scheduling owner.
- Verify downgrade behavior with the actual older package before claiming rollback support. Keep source sessions and existing manifests; rolling back to the old implementation can restore the old slow-startup behavior.

This is a remediation proposal, not an implemented fix. No startup-time SLA or linear speedup from five-way concurrency is claimed before measurement.

issues.title: [Bug]: Model config write path bypasses field validation — invalid thinking_budget / max_input_length are persisted and the provider silently disappears after restart
issues.body:
## Summary

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the per-model config write path never enforces those bounds, so an out-of-range value is accepted, persisted to disk, and then breaks every read path — after a restart the provider fails to load and silently disappears.

## The chain

1. `Provider.update_model_config` (`src/qwenpaw/providers/provider.py`) handles `thinking_budget` and `max_input_length` with a bare `int(...)` assignment. Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment (`validate_assignment` is not enabled), so the declared `ge` bounds in `src/qwenpaw/providers/model_info.py` are never checked on this path.
2. The HTTP layer has the same gap: `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/providers.py`) is the only numeric field in that model without a bound — `max_input_length` carries `ge=1000` and `generate_kwargs.max_tokens` has an explicit `>= 1` validator.
3. The invalid value is stored and persisted by `ProviderManager.update_model_config`.
4. Read paths re-validate: `resolve_model_info` runs `ModelInfo.model_validate(model.model_dump())` and raises `ValidationError`. After a restart, `load_provider` catches the validation failure and returns `None` — a custom provider silently disappears, and a built-in provider loses all persisted configuration, with no error pointing at the value that caused it.

## Reproduction (against current main)

```python
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": 1024})  # baseline OK
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": -5})
# -> returns True, stores -5 (declared ge=1)
provider.resolve_model_info("m1")
# -> ValidationError: thinking_budget Input should be greater than or equal to 1
OpenAIProvider.model_validate(provider.model_dump())
# -> ValidationError (1 error) -> load_provider returns None after restart
```

## Related: `thinking_budget_range` has no shape validation

`ModelInfo(thinking_budget_range=[8000])` constructs fine, but `Provider.thinking_control()` unpacks `low, high = info.thinking_budget_range` and raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack`. The newer `ThinkingControl` model (`src/qwenpaw/providers/thinking.py`) already validates that a budget range is complete and ordered; the legacy `List[int]` field has no equivalent check. A malformed range also poisons `list_provider_info`, which aggregates providers without isolating per-provider failures.

## Expected behavior

- Out-of-range `thinking_budget` / `max_input_length` values are rejected at write time (HTTP request validation and `update_model_config`), consistent with how `update_model_config` already rejects an invalid `model_type` or non-boolean `supports_*` values with `ValueError`, instead of being persisted.
- `thinking_budget_range` only accepts a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair.

I have a fix and regression tests ready and would like to work on this.

issues.title: Creator: the only bundled inspiration example (cat-perspective-0803) still cannot be opened on Windows in 2.0.4 — regression of #7291, which was closed as fixed in 1.1.2
issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw core | **2.2.2.post1** (latest stable, published 2026-10-22) |
| qwenpaw-creator | **2.0.4** |
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| OS | Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), x86_64 |
| Locale / TZ | zh-CN / Asia/Shanghai |

## Summary

`POST /api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open` fails with
`503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR`. The archive downloads fine and its checksum
verifies; the failure is in extraction, because one directory inside the
archive contains a `:` and Windows cannot represent it.

`backend/examples/manifest.json` ships **exactly one** example, so on Windows
the entire "inspiration examples" feature is dead — there is no example a
Windows user can open.

This is the same failure reported in #7291, which was closed as `completed`
on 2026-08-31 with the note:

> Both issues (the `os.fsync` failure during archive download and the
> extraction failure caused by Windows-illegal characters like `:` in archive
> paths) are **fixed in qwenpaw-creator 1.1.2**. Please upgrade the plugin and
> try again — feel free to reopen if anything still fails.

2.0.4 is much later than 1.1.2, and it still fails. So this looks like a
regression, or the fix never landed in the released line.

## Reproduction

1. Install QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 + qwenpaw-creator 2.0.4 on Windows.
2. Open Creator → home → inspiration examples → click "小猫视角"
   (`cat-perspective-0803`).
3. The download succeeds, then the request fails with 503.

Reproduced twice in a row (17:13 and 17:14 local), identical failure.

## Observed

Surfaced to the UI:

```
status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
method=POST path=/api/qwenpaw-creator/examples/cat-perspective-0803/open
error_id=error-999601b341b9492e925238c0ff9c2483
StorageIntegrityError: 灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803
```

The underlying exception, which is only visible in `creator.log`:

```
File ".../backend/api/example_routes.py", line 322, in _materialize_example
    _extract_example_archive(archive_path, extract_dir)
File ".../backend/services/project_files/archive.py", line 133, in extract_archive
    raise BadRequestError(
BadRequestError: archive path is not supported on Windows:
  'project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/';
  import on Linux or macOS to preserve its media references
```

Download and integrity are **not** the problem:

```
17:13:32  Downloading remote file | url=https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip max_bytes=2147483648 timeout=300s
17:13:49  Downloaded remote file | path=<data_root>/.example-staging/<uuid>/archive.zip, size_mib=106.2
17:13:50  Creator request failed ... status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
```

106.2 MiB in 17 s, and the sha256 check passed (a checksum mismatch would have
raised "校验失败" instead).

## Root cause, verified against the actual archive

I downloaded the archive independently and inspected it without extracting:

- `https://creator-store.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/example/cat-perspective-0803.zip`
- compressed `111,352,101` B, sha256 `e91955b3b44ae4e78c117519e8e83887f7e6fab41df00976a786ed17b1f64c7b`
  — **matches** the manifest
- 465 members, 122.6 MiB uncompressed, 83 directories
- members with Windows-illegal characters: **2**
- members hitting reserved names (`CON`/`NUL`/`COM1`…): **0**
- members with trailing space/dot: **0**
- members with a path longer than 240 chars: **0**
- the only illegal character present: **`:`**

The two offending members:

```
DIR   project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/
FILE  project-10ee251e37e45f64aaf560b1f5b5b09f/assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json
```

That file is 32,817 B. So a 122.6 MiB / 465-member project is rejected in its
entirety because of one 32 KB sidecar.

`extract_archive` raises on the **first** unrepresentable member and aborts the
whole extraction, discarding everything already unpacked (`.example-staging` is
left empty).

### What the sidecar is

It is a source-intelligence index for a 21 m 48 s cat-POV clip: `8` shots,
`15` semanticEntries, `8` entities, a summary, `2` modelRuns,
`id = source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170`.

Per the docstring on `SourceMemoryRef` in `schemas/assets.py`, this class of
artifact is *"Hydrated at read time from `runtime/source-intelligence/<index-id>/memory`;
never persisted inside the immutable index JSON"* — i.e. a derived cache, not
authoritative project data.

### How `project.json` references it

`source:cat_cam_1` occurs 4 times in `project.json` (86,832 B):

1. as a **dict key** under `sources.sources.items`
2. as the value of `"source_id"`
3. inside `"order": ["source:cat_cam_1"]`
4. as a **path**: `"relative_uri": "assets/source-intelligence/source:cat_cam_1/source-intelligence-5ee4da7fd8e35741bd8fc87189e3b170.json"` (with its own `sha256` and `file_id`)

Only **#4 is a filesystem path.** #1–#3 are logical identifiers that live
inside JSON and are legal on every platform.

Two facts that make a rename-based fix straightforward:

- The on-disk path is resolved **from the registry**, not derived from
  `source_id`:
  - `services/media/source_observation.py:401` → `Path(project_root, indexed.relative_uri)`
  - `services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:9384` → `(project_root / indexed.relative_uri).read_text(...)`
  - `services/project_files/assets.py:412` → `project_root / PurePosixPath(indexed.relative_uri)`
- `_validate_relative_uri` (`services/project_files/models.py:170`) rejects only
  empty/untrimmed values, `\`, NUL, absolute paths, `<2` parts, a first part
  other than `assets`, and traversal segments. It accepts a sanitized name
  just as readily as the colon form — which is also why `project.json` itself
  loads fine on Windows and only *extraction* fails.

The registry `sha256` covers file **content**, so renaming the containing
directory does not invalidate it.

## The promised sanitizing logic is absent from 2.0.4

`services/project_files/archive.py` has exactly two `sys.platform == "win32"`
branches:

- line 127 — the hard `raise BadRequestError(...)` shown above
- line 149 — the `\\?\` long-path prefix

Grepping the whole backend for `sanitize`, `sanitize_windows`, `windows_safe`,
`def _sanitize`, `rewrite` returns **no hits**. There is no code path that
maps an unrepresentable member name to a legal one, and nothing that rewrites
`relative_uri` to match.

## Suggested fix

Essentially what #7291 said would ship:

1. When materializing an archive on Windows, map illegal characters in member
   names to legal ones (`:` is the one that actually occurs here) instead of
   aborting.
2. Rewrite the affected `relative_uri` entries in `project.json` so the
   registry keeps pointing at the real on-disk path.
3. Leave logical identifiers alone — `source_id`, the `sources.items` dict key
   and the `order` array are JSON-internal and need no change.
4. Apply the same handling to **user-imported** archives, not just bundled
   examples.

Two additional points worth considering:

- **Don't fail the whole import over one unrepresentable member.** Here the
  member is a 32 KB derived cache that is documented as hydrated-at-read-time.
  Skipping it with a warning would yield a fully usable project; aborting
  throws away 122.6 MiB of good data. A per-member skip-with-warning (or at
  least an explicit "N members could not be represented on Windows" summary)
  would degrade far more gracefully than a 503.
- **The error message loses the only actionable hint.** `example_routes.py:324`
  re-raises the `BadRequestError` as
  `StorageIntegrityError("灵感示例归档无法解包: cat-perspective-0803")`, so the
  user sees a bare 503 while the useful text ("archive path is not supported
  on Windows … import on Linux or macOS") stays in the log. Chaining the
  original reason into the user-facing message would make this self-diagnosing.

## Possibly wider impact (inference — not yet verified)

`source_id` values are generated by the app with a literal colon prefix
(`services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:3197`:
`source_id = f"source:{uuid4().hex}"`, and the query expression
`("source:" + $logicalId) as $sourceKey` at `driver.py:10053` /
`services/project_files/agent_tools.py:562`).

If a project created on macOS/Linux materializes a source-intelligence
directory named after that id, then **any** such archive exported there and
imported on Windows would hit the same wall — not just the bundled example.
I have not verified this path end to end; flagging it because it would make
the fix worth prioritizing beyond the demo project.

## Minor: the #7184 cross-reference in #7291 does not resolve

The comment on #7291 says *"This is the same approach described in #7184 for
import archives"*, but #7184 is
"[Feature]: Add an Agent-level cross-session recall toggle for Scroll", which
is unrelated. Possibly a wrong issue number; mentioning it so the intended
prior art can be found.

## Workaround used while waiting

None needed for me — I do not require this example. Documenting the manual
route for anyone who does: fetch the archive, verify its sha256, extract the
463 representable members, rename `source:cat_cam_1` to a legal name, and
update the single `relative_uri` occurrence in `project.json` accordingly.
`source_id`, the dict key and `order` stay untouched.

issues.title: Session permanently broken after provider switch: file:// media URLs in history rejected with invalid_parameter_error
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.2b3**, Windows 10 (ARM64)
- Provider: `agentscope` (`https://platform.agentscope.io/v1`, OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- Models: `qwen3.8-max` and `qwen3.8-flash` — both fail identically (not model-specific)

## What happened

After switching the model provider, one **existing** console session started failing on **every** message with HTTP 400:

```
openai.BadRequestError: data: {"error":{"code":"invalid_parameter_error","param":null,
"message":"The provided URL does not appear to be valid. Ensure it is correctly formatted.",
"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

The session becomes permanently unusable — every subsequent turn re-sends the same poisoned history and gets the same 400.

## Root cause

That session's persisted state (`sessions/console/<agent>_<session>.json`) contains 52 `tool_result` data blocks produced by QwenPaw's **own tools** (`view_video`, `send_file_to_user`) and chat file attachments, e.g.:

```json
{"type": "data",
 "source": {"type": "url",
            "url": "file:///C:/Users/<user>/.copaw/workspaces/default/wan3_demo_cat.mp4",
            "media_type": "video/mp4"},
 "name": "wan3_demo_cat.mp4"}
```

After the provider switch, the capability auto-probe logged:

```
Auto-probe for agentscope/qwen3.8-max: image=True, video=True
Learned capability for agentscope:qwen3.8-max: rejects_media=False
```

so these `file://` URLs are passed through **verbatim** as media content parts in the chat-completions request. The remote endpoint validates URLs server-side and rejects the `file://` scheme → 400 on every request.

The previous provider apparently tolerated local file URLs (SDK-level upload or media stripped), so the pollution stayed dormant until the switch.

## Expected behavior

Any of:

1. **Sanitize before sending**: convert `file://` media to base64 data URIs where size permits, or downgrade to a text placeholder (e.g. `[local media file: name.mp4]`) for endpoints that don't accept local URLs.
2. **Graceful degradation on 400**: when the API returns `invalid_parameter_error` about an invalid URL, detect and strip the offending media block(s), then retry — instead of leaving the whole session bricked.
3. At minimum, document the limitation and/or expose a per-provider media-URL policy.

## Workaround (what I did)

Backed up the session file, replaced all 52 `data` blocks with text placeholders (keeping file name/path info as text), session works again.

## Additional notes

- New sessions are unaffected; only sessions whose history contains local media references break.
- Attaching a new local **video** in chat under this provider would likely re-trigger the same failure (videos are too large for base64, and `file://` is rejected). Images seem fine (sent as base64).
- The text of the conversation is preserved; only the media parts are the problem.

issues.title: [Bug]:Daily Paper fails silently when arxiv.org is unreachable — no proxy/endpoint config, error message hides real cause

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop v2.2.1-beta.2 (Windows 10 x64)
- Component: ReMe Daily Paper plugin (`reme_daily_paper`)

### Problem

The Daily Paper memory cron job fails every day with a misleading "completed with no returned content" message in the inbox, while the actual error is an `httpx.ConnectError` during TLS handshake to `arxiv.org`.

### Reproduction

1. Use QwenPaw Desktop in a network environment where arxiv.org TLS connections are reset (SNI-based filtering — common in mainland China without a VPN)
2. Wait for the Daily Paper cron to fire (or trigger it manually)
3. Inbox shows: `Daily Paper completed with no returned content` (status: error)

### Error log (desktop.log)

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "reme\components\job\base_job.py", line 74, in __call__
  File "reme\steps\base_step.py", line 148, in __call__
  File "reme_daily_paper\analyze.py", line 193, in execute
  File "reme_daily_paper\analyze.py", line 87, in _analyze_one
  File "reme_daily_paper\arxiv.py", line 77, in download
  File "contextlib.py", line 210, in __aenter__
  File "httpx\_client.py", line 1583, in stream
  ...
  httpx.ConnectError: [WinError 10054] An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.
```

### Root cause

TCP connection to `arxiv.org:443` succeeds, but the TLS handshake is reset (SNI field detected and RST'd by network filtering). Browsers with ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) support can bypass this, but `httpx` does not support ECH, so the Daily Paper plugin cannot connect.

### Two improvement requests

**1. Bug — error message hides the real cause (high impact)**

The inbox message "completed with no returned content" gives users zero diagnostic information. It should surface the actual exception, e.g.:

> `Daily Paper failed: ConnectError — arxiv.org unreachable (TLS handshake reset)`

This would save users from having to dig through `desktop.log` to understand why the feature stopped working.

**2. Feature — configurable arxiv endpoint / proxy support**

QwenPaw already provides `HF_ENDPOINT` for HuggingFace mirror configuration. A similar approach for the Daily Paper plugin would allow users in restricted network environments to point to an accessible arxiv mirror or proxy:

```bash
# Example: point to a mirror or proxy
ARXIV_ENDPOINT=https://mirror.example.com/arxiv
# or respect standard proxy env vars
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7890
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7890
```

This is especially relevant since QwenPaw is developed by a Chinese team (Alibaba/Qwen) and many users are in mainland China where arxiv.org connectivity is unreliable.

---

*This issue was drafted with the assistance of an AI agent (QwenPaw) and reviewed by the reporter before submission. [#4333]*

issues.title: [Performance]: Long-running qwenpaw-backend memory grows unbounded to 20GB+ (runtime accumulation, not startup leak)
issues.body:
## 现象

qwenpaw-backend 在连续运行约 2 天后（2026-08-21 03:18 启动 → 2026-08-23 23:00），进程内存从启动时的几百 MB 持续增长到 **20.7 GB**，最终拖慢整机。此问题与 #9（启动阶段 ReMe 内存泄漏）不同——**进程已成功启动且正常运行了 2 天，内存是在运行时逐步累积的**。

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/placeholder)

## 复现条件

- 持续使用 qwenpaw-backend 2 天以上，不重启进程
- 工作负载包含重度文件读写（大量 .md 策略文档）
- 多轮对话触发自动记忆重建

## 根因分析（4 个结构性问题）

### 1. auto_memory 每 N 轮全量重建 BM25 倒排索引，内存不释放

每次 `auto_memory_interval`（默认 5 轮）触发时，狍子会：
1. 读取 `mem_session/dialog/` 下所有历史对话 JSONL 文件
2. 在内存中重建 BM25 倒排索引
3. 调用 LLM 做摘要、推送到 inbox
4. **索引重建完成后，Python 进程的 RSS 堆不归还给 OS**

每重建一次就留下一块内存碎片，经多次累积后内存膨胀到 20GB。

**相关配置**：
```json
{
  "auto_memory_interval": 5,
  "embedding_model_config": {
    "max_cache_size": 10000
  }
}
```

### 2. dream_cron 每天 23:00 跑重度记忆整合任务

```json
{
  "dream_cron": "0 23 * * *",
  "dream_cron_enabled": true
}
```

这是一个后台内存整合任务，把所有记忆读入内存、做摘要、分类、合并。backend 运行 2 天至少触发 2 次 dream 任务，每次都是内存暴涨的推手。

### 3. .md 文件豁免上下文滚动裁剪

```json
{
  "tool_result_pruning_config": {
    "exempt_file_extensions": [".md"]
  }
}
```

用户日常工作大量读写 .md 文件，这些文件的内容**不会被上下文滚动机制裁剪**，全部常驻内存。豁免列表越长，累积内存越严重。

### 4. 没有内存压力阈值守卫

狍子 backend 在跑任何重度操作（记忆重建、dream 整合、索引重建）之前，**从来不检查当前进程内存占用**。20GB 的时候它还在继续重建索引，直到系统 OOM 或用户手动杀进程。

## 临时缓解方案

修改 `config.json` 中的以下参数可显著降低内存增长速率：

| 参数 | 原值 | 建议值 | 效果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `history_retention_days` | 30 | 7 | 旧对话索引快速清理 |
| `offload_retention_days` | 30 | 7 | 工具结果缓存保留缩短 |
| `auto_memory_interval` | 5 | 20 | 后台索引重建频率降低 4 倍 |
| `max_cache_size` | 10000 | 2000 | 缓存上限砍 80% |
| `goal.max_tokens` | 300000 | 128000 | 单会话 token 上限砍半 |
| `history_max_length` | 10000 | 4000 | 消息窗口上限砍半 |

## 建议修复方向

1. **加内存压力阈值**：在 auto_memory、dream、索引重建等重度操作前检查 `psutil.virtual_memory().percent`，超过阈值（如 80%）则跳过或推迟
2. **exempt 上限可配置**：对豁免文件加大小/数量上限，超过上限的自动裁剪
3. **auto_memory 索引重建用子进程**：重建完成后完全释放内存，不进主进程 RSS
4. **dream 整合任务显式触发 GC**：`gc.collect()` 后配合 `tracemalloc` 确认内存已归还

## 环境

- QwenPaw 版本：v2.1.0（桌面版，qwenpaw-backend.exe 125MB PyInstaller 打包）
- OS：Windows 11
- 运行模式：桌面端，本地工作区
- 工作负载：大量 .md 文件读写 + 长时间对话

prs.title: fix(tools): preserve line endings and encoding in edit_file (#8414, #8415)
prs.body:
Fixes #8414, #8415.

## What Problem This Solves

`edit_file` rewrote the whole file through a text-mode writer (`newline='\n'`, UTF-8). Two user-visible bugs followed:

- **CRLF files were converted to LF on every edit** (#8414, #8415) — a one-line change rewrote every line ending in the file, which shows up as a whole-file diff in git and can break files that require CRLF (Windows batch scripts, some configs).
- **Non-UTF-8 files were destroyed** — an ISO-8859-1 file with bytes outside ASCII was re-encoded (or failed) even when the edit itself touched nothing near them.

The fix writes the snapshot back byte for byte: `edit_file` now reads the raw bytes, decodes with the encoding the file actually uses (BOM detection first), applies the replacement, re-encodes, and hands the result to a new `_write_bytes_atomic` that writes a sibling temp file in binary and `os.replace()`s it into place. Line endings are normalised for *matching* only, then the file's own ending is re-applied to inserted text.

## Evidence

Unit tests in `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py` (all new, per file-ending/encoding case):

- `test_crlf_endings_survive_a_one_line_edit` — a CRLF file edited in the middle keeps CRLF everywhere; byte-comparing the whole file passes
- `test_lf_file_is_unchanged_in_shape` — an LF file is not rewritten into CRLF
- `test_iso_8859_1_bytes_are_not_destroyed` — a Latin-1 file with non-ASCII bytes around the edit point round-trips
- `test_utf8_bom_is_preserved` — the BOM is still there after editing
- `test_new_lines_in_new_text_follow_the_file_ending` — inserted text uses the file's ending, not a hardcoded `\n`

The atomic writer also keeps the target's mode: `shutil.copymode(target, temp)` when the file exists (which additionally preserves setuid/setgid bits that a `st_mode & 0o777` mask dropped), and the constant `0o644` for a brand-new file.

CI on this revision: pre-commit (black 23.3.0, flake8, mypy, pylint) clean, CodeQL clean, unit tests passing.

prs.title: fix(skills): offload pool skill download to a worker thread
prs.body:
## Summary

`POST /skills/pool/download` ran its whole pipeline inline in the async
handler: target preflight, rollback snapshots (`shutil.copytree` of the
existing skill), and the per-target copy itself. All of that is blocking
filesystem work that scales with the skill's file count, so downloading a
skill with thousands of files blocks the event loop for minutes — every
other API stops answering and the console's 30 s `AbortController` timeout
fires, so the operation fails in the UI even though the backend is still
copying.

This moves the blocking body into a sync helper and awaits it with
`asyncio.to_thread`, the same pattern `/pool/import-builtin` and
`/pool/{name}/update-builtin` already use.

Refs #8013

## What Problem This Solves

Downloading a large skill from the skill pool (e.g. 12,994 files / 80 MB)
freezes the whole backend. While the copy runs, the event loop is blocked
so no other request is served — the console looks hung, and the frontend's
hard 30 s timeout aborts the request even though the copy is still in
flight. Users see `Request timeout after 30000ms: POST /skills/pool/download`
and the skill never lands in the target workspace.

The reported reproduction is a large skill downloaded 4 times in a row,
each one failing at the 30 s mark with the backend unresponsive for the
whole copy window.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py`: extract `_download_pool_skills_blocking`
  (preflight + `preview_only` short-circuit + per-target download + rollback
  + backup cleanup, all unchanged) and call it from the handler via
  `asyncio.to_thread`.

## Behaviour

Unchanged: `preview_only`, the 400/404/409 conflict paths, the
`SkillScanError` → 422 payload, and the all-or-nothing rollback all still
run in the same order with the same semantics. Only the thread they run on
changes.

## Evidence

Regression test `tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py::test_pool_download_runs_off_the_event_loop`
patches the blocking helper with a 0.2 s `time.sleep` and runs a 10 ms
heartbeat task concurrently. The two waits must overlap:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py::test_pool_download_runs_off_the_event_loop
1 passed

# with the handler calling the blocking body inline instead of via to_thread:
assert elapsed < blocking_seconds * 1.5
E   assert 0.40799228847026825 < 0.3
```

Full validation:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_skills_router.py      # 14 passed
$ pytest tests/integration/test_skills_pool.py             # 18 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

`tests/unit/app/routers/test_git_router_endpoints.py` has 20 failures on
clean `main` in this environment (git-version dependent) — unrelated to
this change.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

**Related Issue:** No linked issue.

**Security Considerations:** Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials. Provider contexts remain provider-owned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Channels (Console streaming/reconnect)
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (replay verification tooling)

## Checklist

- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (changed-file checks passed; no all-files claim)
- [ ] Full default test configuration is green (see known failures below)
- [ ] Documentation published in this repository
- [ ] Ready for review / merge

## Testing

The latest local validation ran against the committed working tree in the project Conda environment. Groups overlap and should not be summed as unique coverage.

- Chat storage suite: **478 passed** after each of the three storage optimizations.
- Backend combined regression: **2337 passed, 1 platform skip**.
- HTTP integration retry (backup, checkpoints, conversation commands, PawApp context): **54 passed**, using the existing `QWENPAW_INTEGRATION_HTTP_TIMEOUT=180` setting after initial fixture startup timeouts.
- SDK lifecycle: **2 passed** with a 180-second test timeout after a 45-second dependency metadata scan timeout. Other plugin/SDK contracts: **147 passed**.
- TypeScript noEmit, changed-file pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Frontend full single-worker run: **657 files passed / 2 failed**; **8475 tests passed / 1 failed / 2 expected failures / 9 skipped**. This was not a green default full run.
  - JobDrawer JSON validation did not display its error within `waitFor`; the unchanged complete file passed on isolated retry (**29 passed**).
  - PawApp SDK session routing exceeded the default 10-second initialization hook timeout, also on isolated retry (**45 passed / 9 skipped**). With command-line `--hookTimeout=30000`, all **54 passed**. No source or test configuration was changed to hide this limitation.

## Evidence

Local terminal results retained from this validation:

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q
478 passed

Backend combined regression
2337 passed, 1 skipped

HTTP integration retry
54 passed

SDK lifecycle / other contracts
2 passed / 147 passed

vitest run --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 failed | 657 passed (659)
Tests       1 failed | 8475 passed | 2 expected fail | 9 skipped (8487)

Isolated JobDrawer retry: 29 passed
Isolated sessionRouting --hookTimeout=30000: 54 passed
```

Additional behavior checks:

- A database generated by the previous implementation containing four `block.committed` events was rebuilt twice: messages, runtime, and original events remained unchanged.
- Eight database command scenarios and sixteen Fork boundaries verified state preservation, with Codex/Qoder native reset failure protection probes.
- Console browser flow: create two Turns, fork the first, continue with the remembered first-Turn marker, fork again, and reload. Both forks closed the dialog, navigated automatically, and incremented the name. Long-history scrolling and the message directory also loaded.

## Additional Notes

Historical legacy runtime reconstruction can be approximate where exact snapshots were never stored. The latest browser smoke used the built-in agent; native-provider behavior was covered by automated adapters/probes, not a fresh five-Turn provider UI run in this validation. prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
path.write_bytes("姓名: 张三\n".encode("gbk"))
# read_file_safe previously returned ": \n"
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_search.py::test_walk_and_grep_matches_gbk_file -q
# 43 passed
```

Also re-ran the new GBK cases alone after rebase: 4 passed.

## Notes

- After a successful GBK decode, `edit_file` still writes with the existing suffix-based encoding (`.txt` → `utf-8-sig`). Chinese text is preserved; only the on-disk encoding may change to UTF-8, which matches the project’s Windows Excel/Notepad write path.
- CRLF whole-file rewrite and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer preserving the original GBK bytes on write as well.

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

- `OllamaProvider.fetch_models`: after listing models, probe:
  1. `GET /api/ps` — loaded runtime `context_length` (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`)
  2. `POST /api/show` — Modelfile `num_ctx`, then GGUF `*.context_length`
- Set `max_input_length_auto_detected` so existing resolution precedence applies (explicit user config still wins)
- Keep catalog opt-out; if probes fail or return nothing usable, behavior stays at the 128k default

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 78 passed
```

Coverage includes parser precedence (served → num_ctx → GGUF), fetch enrichment with mocked `/api/ps` + `/api/show`, catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer a different probe order or want this folded into a broader local-provider detection pass.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`edit_file` does not patch bytes in place. It reads a snapshot through `read_file_safe` (which normalizes every newline to `\n`) and then atomically replaces the file via `write_text_atomic` (`newline="\n"`). This is separate from #8234 (GBK/encoding fallback) and from #7091 (workspace editor CRLF). Only the agent `edit_file` tool path is changed here.

- Regression tests: CRLF stays CRLF; LF stays LF

## How to reproduce (before)

path = Path("app.py")
path.write_bytes(b'def hi():\r\n    return "old"\r\n')

- Truncation past `MAX_FILE_READ_BYTES` and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

prs.title: feat(loop): add optional Jev completion decisions
prs.body:
## Description

The optional Jev check can catch a text-only reply that promises work and ends the turn. It uses the decision model selected for the agent or the global default. Enable it in the standard completion check or in a custom qualitative rubric. Existing configurations keep their current behavior.

For each eligible response, one provider request asks whether the agent should continue and which reason applies. A probability above 0.5 triggers continuation. A sufficiently confident reason is appended to the existing rubric prompt for the agent to verify. An unavailable model, invalid decision, or four-second timeout falls back to the bounded agent self-check. Cancellation still propagates and a successful Jev intervention preserves the iteration budget.

The qualitative rubric stores that reason in its session state and returns the prompt through the existing `build_continuation()` hook. Goal mode keeps its own turn and budget rules. A probe of its handler with simulated probabilities of 0.1 and 0.9 found that both decisions used the same Goal prompt. Removing that integration avoids the unused provider request.

When enabled, the configured provider receives conversation text, tool inputs and results, available tool schemas, and completion criteria. Thinking blocks are omitted and media blocks are represented by text references.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Component(s) Affected

- Agent loop and configuration
- Console settings, with two new strings per locale
- English and Chinese loop documentation

## Evidence

Verified on Windows with Python 3.12, AgentScope 2.0.10, and TypeSafe SDK 0.7.5.

```text
pytest tests/unit/loop tests/unit/providers/test_typesafe_evaluation.py tests/unit/config/test_agent_config_persistence.py -q
101 passed

vitest run src/pages/Agent/Config/components/AgentLoopCard.test.ts src/pages/Agent/Config/components/AgentLoopCard.render.test.tsx src/pages/Agent/Config/useAgentConfig.test.tsx
3 files passed, 31 tests passed

tsc -b --noEmit
vite build
Exit code 0
```

Two loop regression tests cover letting a text-only reply through, sending tool evidence, forwarding the reason, reverting to the original prompt on missing configuration, and respecting the evaluation cap. They also check that tool iterations and opting out skip the provider. The existing TypeSafe suite covers the provider protocol. prs.title: fix(channels): keep control-command routing on the user's own text in quoted replies
prs.body:
## Description

Replying to a message with a control command such as `/stop` in Feishu, QQ, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, OneBot or Yuanbao never routed as a command. These channels prepend the quoted (replied-to) message before the user's own text, so the inbound text becomes:

```
[quoted message: Alice: quarterly report]
/stop
```

Three shared consumers classify or dispatch on that first text block:

- `manager.enqueue` -> `CommandRegistry.get_priority_level`: `/stop` received normal priority 20 instead of critical 0.
- `BaseChannel._consume_one_request` -> `CommandRegistry.is_control_command`: the reply took the normal tracked-message branch instead of the control branch.
- `Runtime.run` -> `SlashCommandRegistry.dispatch`: even when routed fast, the command was not resolved and reached the agent as plain chat text.

Root cause in all three: they must look at the user's own text, but see the quote-first rendering (source probes in #8342).

### Fix

Add one shared recognizer, `strip_quote_context_prefix()` (`src/qwenpaw/utils/quote_context.py`), that removes leading `[quoted ...]` context blocks (some channels stack more than one, e.g. `[quoted media: download failed]` before `[quoted message: ...]`), and apply it at the two extraction points those consumers share:

- `BaseChannel._extract_query_from_payload`: command classification, queue priority, and the ACL "first message" record now see the user's own text, for both dict and `AgentRequest` payloads.
- `Runtime.run` slash-command dispatch text.

Behavior contract (pinned by tests):

- Quote + own `/stop` -> classified and dispatched as the command.
- Command only inside the quoted text -> not a command (unchanged).
- Quote-only reply (no new text) -> no command.
- Normal quoted chat -> unchanged; quote-first input still reaches the model, and text without the prefix is extracted byte-identically.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8342

**Security Considerations:** None. Quoted content is not modified; only the text used for routing and classification is stripped. The full quoted message still reaches the model.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Testing

- New `tests/unit/utils/test_quote_context.py` (16 cases): prefix variants, stacked prefixes, multi-line quoted content, command-only-in-quote, quote-only reply, and safe degradation when quoted content contains `]`.
- New `tests/unit/runtime/test_runtime_command_dispatch.py` (3 cases): `Runtime.run` dispatches `/stop` (not the quoted context) for a quoted reply; plain command unchanged; normal quoted chat does not dispatch.
- `tests/unit/channels/test_base_core.py`: new `TestExtractQueryQuoteContext` (6 cases) covering dict and `AgentRequest` payloads through the real `CommandRegistry`.
- Regression check: with the source change stashed, 7 of the new cases fail on current `main` (`7 failed, 2 passed`); with the fix applied, all 25 pass.

prs.title: test: stop leaking unawaited coroutines from scheduling mocks
prs.body:
## Summary

Six unit tests leak a coroutine: a scheduling mock replaces the scheduler
without consuming what production handed it, or a test runs a production
path in the wrong execution context. The tests pass, but the
`RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited` noise hides real async
lifecycle defects (the issue cites #7857) and makes a clean test run
impossible to certify.

This fixes all six and tightens each test so it asserts the behaviour it
claims to cover.

Refs #7858

## What Problem This Solves

Running the affected files with `-X tracemalloc=5` emits **7**
unawaited-coroutine warnings. Six come from tests that pass for the wrong
reason, so a genuine async defect introduced nearby would be invisible in
the noise — the warnings are attributed to whichever test happens to
trigger the delayed GC, not the one that leaked.

Concretely, `test_download_attachment_exception` patched
`qq_channel._loop.run_coroutine_threadsafe` while production calls the
module-level `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, so the mock never fired
and the "returns None on failure" assertion was never exercising the
intended exception path. Similarly, `test_run_stream_forever` called the
sync thread entry point from inside a test coroutine, where `asyncio.run`
raises and the entry point's `except Exception` swallowed it — the test
asserted nothing about the stream loop at all.

## Changes

| Test | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_proactive_trigger_logic.py::TestEnableDisable::test_enable_stores_config_and_workspace` | `create_task` mock returned a stub task and left `_run_trigger_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_hub.py::TestClientLifecycle::test_aclose_hub_client_drain_timeout_warns` | fake `wait_for` raised `TimeoutError` without consuming the `Event.wait` coroutine | close it, and assert the warning the timeout path is supposed to log (was: `# must not raise`) |
| `test_dingtalk.py::TestDingTalkStreamMode::test_run_stream_forever` | async test called the sync thread entry point; `asyncio.run` failed inside the running loop and was swallowed | run it in a real thread and assert the stream loop actually executed |
| `test_qq.py::TestDownloadAttachmentSync::test_download_attachment_exception` | patched the loop's method; production uses the module-level function | patch `qwenpaw.app.channels.qq.channel.asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, assert it was scheduled on the channel's loop |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_creates_task` | `create_task` mock left `_typing_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_replaces_existing` | same | same |

No production code is touched — every defect here is in the tests.

## Evidence

The issue's reproduction command, before and after:

```
$ python -X tracemalloc=5 -m pytest -q \
    tests/unit/agents/acp/test_acp_service.py \
    tests/unit/agents/memory/test_proactive_trigger_logic.py \
    tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_hub.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_dingtalk.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py

# before: 755 passed, 38 warnings   → 7 unawaited-coroutine warnings
# after:  755 passed, 33 warnings   → 1 unawaited-coroutine warning
```

The one remaining warning is `ACPService.close_all_sessions`, which is the
separate production defect tracked in #7857 — the issue's acceptance
criteria explicitly asks for this PR to land before that one.

Wider runs (no new failures; the single failure is a pre-existing
network-dependent one):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/channels tests/unit/agents -q
1 failed, 5864 passed, 4 skipped
# tests/unit/agents/utils/test_file_handling.py::TestDownloadFileFromUrl::test_remote_download
# fails on clean main too (needs network)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)   # clean
```
