prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
  The field is **derived from the instance's per-file cap** when it is not
  set explicitly: `max(8 MiB, 4 × max_bytes)`. A raised per-file cap is
  therefore no longer undercut by a fixed total — with a 16 MiB per-file cap
  a 10 MiB file reaches the wire instead of being dropped by the total — and
  a lowered per-file cap never tightens the total below the 8 MiB default.
  An explicitly configured `max_total_bytes` always wins.
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- A base64 payload is measured **without its `=` padding**, for a
  `Base64Source` and for a base64 `data:` URL alike (one shared helper). The
  padding is not payload: a 512-byte image encodes to 684 characters, one of
  which is padding, so it is 512 bytes — not 513, which was enough to push a
  file sitting exactly on the per-file cap over it while the equivalent
  `Base64Source` was kept.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, but it is never
  sent, so it costs the budget nothing: the plan drops oldest occurrences only
  until the *deduplicated* payload — the distinct sources that actually reach
  the wire — fits the budget, and a folded copy is re-inlined when the budget
  dropped every earlier copy of its source (so A → B → A still keeps the
  newest A).
- **Video is bounded by the budget too.** Video never reaches a media hook:
  Anthropic routes it through `_format_anthropic_video_data_block`, and the
  OpenAI Chat / Responses / DashScope paths substitute it into the request
  around the formatter's `format()` call. The Anthropic path now caps the
  video before formatting it, and the OpenAI-family paths *mark* the video
  block (its `name` becomes the substitution placeholder) instead of
  replacing it, so the formatter's media hook still sees it and the budget
  can account for it at its own position in the wire order. A marked block is
  rendered as the substitution placeholder and resolved to the video wire
  dict afterwards, exactly as before. Assistant-role video is unaffected (it
  was never substituted and still is not).
- **A local PDF is prepared like any other media.** A `file://` PDF used to
  stay a `URLSource`: the asynchronous media preparation did not read it, so
  the formatter could not measure it and the base formatter inlined the whole
  file (with a blocking disk read) while formatting — three 512-byte PDFs
  fitted a 900-byte budget without a single budget placeholder. The
  preparation stage now reads local PDF attachments too, so they spend the
  per-request budget like every other media and obey the per-file cap (a
  local PDF above `max_bytes` becomes the same text placeholder an oversized
  image gets). Remote PDFs follow the same path for the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters, which have to download them anyway: the download
  moves out of the formatter into the bounded, non-blocking preparation
  stage.

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
89 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

`TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget` pins the video case on all five provider
paths through the production wrapper (three 312-byte `video/mp4` blocks, a
900-byte budget → two videos inlined, one dropped):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q -k TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget
9 passed
```

`TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget` pins the local-PDF case through the
production wrapper on the OpenAI Chat and Responses paths (three 512-byte
local PDFs, a 900-byte budget → the newest PDF inlined, two budget
placeholders), and the base64 padding case with
`test_data_url_size_matches_the_equivalent_base64_source` (a `data:` URL and
the equivalent `Base64Source` measure the same, padding excluded).

Without the fix the new cases fail:

```
FAILED test_data_url_size_matches_the_equivalent_base64_source[512]
FAILED test_data_url_image_at_the_per_file_cap_is_kept
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_openai_wrapper_caps_local_pdf_attachments
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_responses_wrapper_caps_local_pdf_attachments
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_local_pdf_over_the_per_file_cap_is_dropped
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failures below are pre-existing in this
environment (missing optional SDKs — `reme`, `typesafe` — and one
network-dependent download test) and are identical on the unmodified head
commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        23 failed, 5098 passed, 3 skipped
# unmodified head:    23 failed, 5086 passed, 3 skipped   (+12 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

**Yes — the budget is intentionally in raw (decoded) media bytes.** It is the
same unit as the per-file cap and as the file size the user sees, so one
number describes the media a request carries.

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

This is deliberate: the budget bounds the *media a request carries*, in the
same unit as the per-file cap and the file sizes reported to the user. The
alternative — budgeting encoded bytes — would mean the limit no longer
matches the number a user sees for a file, and it would still not track the
provider's own overhead on top of the media.

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or set `max_total_bytes` explicitly on the
model) to match their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- The per-request budget now covers **video** as well, on all five provider
  paths. One path is still outside it: the OpenAI-family / Gemini
  **tool-result video promotion** (`_promote_tool_result_videos`) injects the
  video after formatting, so it is capped per file but not per request. The
  Anthropic tool-result video goes through the media hook and is covered.
  Covering the promotion would mean moving it inside the budget's scope —
  worth a follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: fix(hub): restore running runtimes on startup
prs.body:
## Description
After a Hub restart, desired-running Local runtimes can remain stopped until a user accesses their personal runtime. Enabled cron jobs therefore miss execution even while the Hub is healthy.

Restore desired-running runtimes during Hub startup, after the model listener binds and before the control plane becomes ready. Recovery uses existing lifecycle locks, provisioner observations and capacity checks, runs outside the event loop, preserves explicit stops and administrator-disabled runtimes, and isolates individual failures with redacted logging.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8213

**Security Considerations:** No authentication, credential or sandbox changes. Administrator-disabled runtimes remain stopped. Provisioner exception messages are not written to startup logs because they may contain credentials.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected
- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist
- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes (baseline failures detailed below)
- [x] I ran relevant tests locally and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Ready for review

## Evidence
Retested locally on 2026-11-03 with Python 3.12.14 on macOS after merging upstream main `401662d8` into this branch (head `f946711b`). The remote merge tree matches the locally tested tree exactly. Installed editable `.[dev,test,full]` dependencies in a separate virtual environment.

```text
python -m pytest tests/unit/hub/test_service.py tests/unit/hub/test_control_app.py -q
93 passed in 25.21s

python -m pytest tests/unit/hub -q
2 failed, 461 passed, 3 skipped in 27.78s

python -m pytest --collect-only -q
18240 tests collected in 29.40s
```

A paired Hub lifespan experiment used the same persisted desired-running/stopped record and a fake provisioner, with zero personal-runtime requests: unchanged main left it stopped; this patch restored it to running. This verifies startup orchestration, not a native subprocess or live cron end-to-end test.

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the six changed files, including mypy, black, flake8 and pylint. Full-repository pre-commit passes every hook except pylint.

## Validation limitations
The full local gate is not entirely green. Each blocker was reproduced separately on unchanged upstream main `401662d8`:

- Both failing Hub tests are native macOS isolation tests: `test_macos_seatbelt_real_preflight` and `test_macos_sandbox_cli_can_reach_only_its_runtime`. Seatbelt's loopback connection fails with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. A native subprocess restart probe was blocked by the same preflight; isolation was not bypassed.
- Full-repository pylint reports E1120 at `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_elevated_sandbox.py:1766,1768` and `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_unelevated_sandbox.py:1711`. These files are unchanged by this PR. No checks were suppressed.
- The earlier full pytest collection mismatch and the earlier `runtime_boundary.py` pylint error did not recur on current main.

Regression coverage includes graceful restart, stale running metadata, explicit stop/disable, healthy-runtime idempotency, capacity limits, a concurrent administrator stop, failure isolation, redacted logging, listener ordering and execution outside the event loop.

## Additional Notes
Recovery restores future scheduling; it does not replay cron jobs missed during downtime. Recovery attempts are limited to startup, and failures remain observable through runtime state and Hub logs.

Earlier deployment evidence: a version-adapted mitigation on QwenPaw 2.2.0 restored two desired-running Local runtimes after a controlled Hub restart without personal-runtime traffic. Channels and three enabled cron schedules recovered; the disabled job and all job configurations stayed unchanged. That is historical evidence for the approach, not production execution of this exact main-branch patch. No business deployment was changed during this retest.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add approval notifications (#8460)
prs.body:
## Description

Introduces a unified system notification feature, ensuring users receive timely alerts—such as approval requests, completed responses, and background task updates—even when the application is running in the background.

Closed #8460

- Centralized notification management under "Settings → General," featuring a master toggle. Options for approval requests and completed responses include "Disabled," "Background Only," and "Always Enabled." Scheduled tasks, heartbeat signals, and email notifications can be configured individually.
- Supports browser-based notifications as well as native system notifications on macOS, Windows, and Linux. On desktop, a Rust-based background polling mechanism ensures alerts are received even when the application window is minimized to the system tray.
- Clicking a notification brings the application to the foreground and navigates directly to the relevant Agent, conversation, approval card, or inbox message. If an approval session is no longer valid, the user is redirected to the approval list.
- Implements notification deduplication, filters out initial snapshot history, automatically dismisses expired or already-processed approval requests, and includes retry logic for failed deliveries—all to minimize redundant or obsolete alerts.
- The backend now stores short-term, non-consumable notification event snapshots. Completion events are triggered only upon the successful finalization of a response, while empty "heartbeat" signals are filtered out.
- Enhanced permission management, including streamlined authorization access, automatic UI refreshes upon permission changes, and direct access to system notification settings. Maintains backward compatibility with legacy approval preferences; category-specific settings are preserved even when the master notification toggle is disabled.
- Added an approval access point in the system tray, with full support for multiple languages, narrow-screen layouts, and keyboard navigation.

prs.title: fix(providers): reject out-of-range model config values on the write path
prs.body:
Fixes #8549

## What Problem This Solves

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the write path never enforced those bounds: `Provider.update_model_config` assigned `int(...)` results directly (Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment), and `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` was the only numeric field in its model without a bound. An invalid value was accepted and persisted, then failed re-validation on every read — after a restart `load_provider` returned `None` and the provider silently disappeared.

## What changed

- `app/routers/providers.py`: add `ge=1` to `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget`, matching the existing `ge=1000` on `max_input_length`.
- `providers/provider.py`: `update_model_config` now raises `ValueError` for `thinking_budget < 1` and `max_input_length < 1000` before assigning, consistent with the existing `model_type` / `supports_*` validation in the same method.
- `providers/model_info.py`: `thinking_budget_range` gains a model validator requiring a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair (mirroring `ThinkingControl` in `providers/thinking.py`); previously `[8000]` constructed fine and `thinking_control()` crashed unpacking it.

## Evidence

New regression tests (10):

- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_config_validation.py` — `thinking_budget` of -5 / 0 and `max_input_length` of 500 are rejected and not stored; valid values round-trip and clearing with `None` still works; `thinking_budget_range` of length 1 / 3 or `low > high` is rejected, an ordered pair still drives `thinking_control`.
- `tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_config_request_validation.py` — `ModelConfigRequest(thinking_budget=-5 / 0)` fails request validation, `1` is accepted.

Red/green: with the fix reverted, the 8 rejection tests fail (the 2 valid-value guards pass both ways); with the fix, all 10 pass. The reproduction script that previously showed `update_model_config(..., -5)` returning `True` and poisoning reads now raises `ValueError: thinking_budget must be at least 1` at write time.

Broader subset `tests/unit/providers/` + the provider router tests: 1008 passed; the single failure (`test_typesafe_evaluation.py::test_as_model_injects_same_instance_and_preserves_host_headers`) fails identically on the unmodified baseline in this environment because the optional `reme` package is not installed.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): never write a sandbox ACE on a volume root
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, sandbox ACLs are **inheritable** and are written on the
workspace, on every mount (including the session project directory, which
is mounted writable) and on every deny path. A volume root has no parent,
so writing one there re-propagates it to every existing child of the
volume. When the root DACL is missing (a NULL DACL) it gets replaced with
a sandbox-only DACL, and SYSTEM / Administrators / the user vanish from
the subtree — the drive becomes inaccessible even to an elevated
Administrator, and the sandbox-only ACE has to be removed by hand.

This closes every path that could create that state:

1. **A volume root is never a sandbox grant root** — `SandboxConfig`
   collects them (`volume_root_paths`) across `workspace_dir`, any mount
   (read-only mounts get an inheritable ACE too) and any `deny_paths`
   entry, and warns. `create_sandbox` then downgrades such a config to
   `SandboxMode.NONE` and logs a warning, so **the command still runs**
   while the volume stays usable. One check covers the AppContainer,
   elevated and unelevated backends.
2. **Never fill a NULL DACL** — `_set_path_ace` and `_add_traverse_ace`
   refuse instead of letting `SetEntriesInAclW` produce a DACL that holds
   only the sandbox SID.
3. **Never rewrite a volume root's DACL** — both DACL-reset fallbacks
   (`icacls /reset` in the elevated backend and
   `_reset_dacl_to_inherited` in the unelevated one) skip volume roots.
4. **A second guard in `_set_path_ace`** — it is the single point where
   sandbox ACEs are written (the AppContainer and elevated backends both
   delegate to it), so no caller can reintroduce the write.

The console warns before the user picks such a directory
(`ProjectSelectModal`), so the loss of the sandbox is not silent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7943

**Security Considerations:** This tightens, rather than loosens, the
sandbox — no auth or config surface is added. Two judgement calls worth
flagging:

- **Fail-open on the volume root.** The sandbox is *skipped* rather than
  the session failing, because the reporter's expected behaviour is
  "command runs in the host / volume stays usable". That means a
  volume-root workspace runs **unsandboxed**; the backend logs a warning
  and the console asks the user first. If you would rather refuse
  outright (fail-closed), it is a two-line change — happy to switch.
- **The volume-root check is platform-independent**, so a POSIX
  `workspace_dir` of `/` also falls back. The ACL hazard is Windows-only,
  but "a volume root is not a usable workspace" holds everywhere. Happy
  to scope it to Windows if you prefer.

prs.title: fix(security): guard inline Office COM automation before unsandboxed fallback
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, with approval level `auto` and the security sandbox off, an
agent-authored inline Office COM command is executed instead of denied. The
Office COM servers (`PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`,
`Word.Application`, `Outlook.Application`) are single-instance, so `Quit()`
on an inline-constructed object terminates the user's already-open app.

The command matched no signature in `dangerous_shell_commands.yaml`, was
classified `SANDBOX_FALLBACK` by `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, and — with the
sandbox off — was rewritten to `ALLOW` by `ResourceGovernor`
("running unsandboxed"), so it ran silently.

This PR adds a CRITICAL detection rule (`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION`)
covering the inline-construction verbs against the four Office ProgIDs:

- `New-Object -ComObject <App>.Application` (PowerShell)
- `GetActiveObject(...)` / `[Marshal]::GetActiveObject(...)`
- `CreateObject(...)`
- `win32com.client.Dispatch` / `DispatchEx(...)`
- `[Type]::GetTypeFromProgID(...)` (used by `[activator]::CreateInstance`)
- `Activator` + `CreateInstance`

The CRITICAL finding surfaces in Phase 1, so the call is held for approval
*before* the unsandboxed fallback, instead of running silently.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8002

**Security Considerations:** Local impact only — a shell command the agent is
already allowed to run can no longer silently close the user's Office
process. Ordinary shell commands are unaffected.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest`) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

The new rule is matched through the real loader
(`load_rules_from_yaml` → `RuleBasedToolGuardian`) and through
`GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, not by re-declaring the patterns in the test.

Verified behaviour with a default policy (`execution_level` = smart / auto):

| command | decision | finding |
|---|---|---|
| `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `win32com.client.Dispatch('Word.Application').Quit()` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `echo hello` | SANDBOX_FALLBACK (unchanged) | — |

`ASK` maps to the approval card, so in `auto` + sandbox-off the command is
now held for the user instead of closing their PowerPoint.

## Evidence

```bash
$ pre-commit run --files \
    src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml \
    tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py
check python ast.........................................................Passed
check yaml...............................................................Passed
check docstring is first.................................................Passed
detect private key.......................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
mypy.....................................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py -q
41 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py \
         tests/unit/governance/test_policy.py -q
141 passed
```

## Additional Notes

Approval (`ASK`) rather than a hard `DENY` is deliberate. Per
`policy.py`, severity alone does not hard-deny — only rule IDs listed in
`resolve_auto_denied_rules()` do (default:
`SAFETY_CHECKS_DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND`). `ASK` is the right outcome here
because legitimate COM automation that drives a *private* instance should
remain approvable, while an accidental `Quit()` on the user's open app can
no longer slip through. If a hard deny is preferred, adding
`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` to the default auto-denied set is a
one-line follow-up — happy to do it if that's the intended policy.

prs.title: fix(skill): avoid scanner false positive in make-skill validator
prs.body:
## Description

The built-in `make-skill` is blocked by QwenPaw's own skill security scanner when it is imported into the skill pool or a workspace:

```
[CRITICAL] Dangerous code execution functions that can execute arbitrary code
(scripts/validate_skill.py:432) rule_id=COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL
```

The flagged line is the validator's syntax check for generated scripts:

```python
compile(path.read_bytes(), relative, "exec")
```

`compile()` only produces a code object, which is never executed here, so this is a false positive. However, `COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL` matches any bare `compile(` call. This PR replaces it with `py_compile.compile(..., doraise=True)`, writing to a temporary directory. It keeps the compile-stage checks, does not execute the script and leaves the Skill unchanged. The check moves into a small `_python_error` helper, applied identically to `make-skill-en` and `make-skill-zh`.

I chose to fix the skill rather than relax the scanner rule, since loosening a CRITICAL rule to let one built-in pass seems like the wrong trade.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8320 (same validator, different failure)

**Security Considerations:** The scanner rule is untouched. Generated scripts are compiled but never executed.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): skip completed startup migrations and snapshot live backups
prs.body:
## Description

Scroll history synchronization delays HTTP startup until every configured agent has been processed, even when its sessions were already synchronized. Move migration into each workspace's history initialization and record durable per-agent completion. Default alone gates readiness; QA and other agents use the existing bounded startup queue (default concurrency: 5).

Completed starts check the pending marker and migration metadata, without enumerating sessions, reading manifests, hashing files, or running integrity scans. Existing installations reconcile once, using bounded batches and atomic progress checkpoints. Ownership is claimed once per session. Explicit conversation imports reconcile only their imported files.

History lifecycle follows workspace ownership:

- One configuration predicate identifies runtimes that write Scroll history. Native and third-party backends record deferred reconciliation outside SQLite, so an inaccessible history database cannot block their operation.
- The manager drains outgoing writers before preparing a candidate whose history sink changed or needs reconciliation. This includes native-to-Scroll, third-party-to-QwenPaw, and database changes. In-request `/daemon restart` schedules reload and returns, allowing its final save to finish. Other agents remain available.
- Discarded candidates preserve pending reconciliation. Retention uses the candidate's captured policy and becomes active only after successful ownership handoff; preparation cannot replace a shared store's maintenance policy.
- Restored workspaces reconcile once before trusting completion metadata. Explicit invalidation ignores manifest completion proofs without hashing, while retaining legacy identity provenance.

Online backups stage workspace files in a subprocess. The archive process reads staged copies, avoiding ordinary opens/closes of live SQLite files even if their type changes after staging. SQLite snapshots are verified once, and their sidecars are excluded. Configured history additionally receives schema validation; external history paths and portable archive configuration remain supported. Snapshot failures abort, and cancellation/timeout terminates the worker.

`qwenpaw history check DATABASE [--repair-fts]` opens an existing validated history schema without initializing tables, changing the schema version, or enabling WAL. Normal startup does not perform proactive integrity scans or destructive quarantine; actual runtime database errors still trigger the existing recovery path.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8540

**Related PR:** Supersedes the backup-safety work in #7930, originally contributed by @niceIrene. The FTS probe cache is unnecessary because this PR removes ordinary startup scans.

**Security Considerations:** Only synthetic test data and sanitized findings are included; no customer logs, identifiers, paths, or credentials.

## Type of Change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)

Pre-commit checks cover changed files. Existing test fixtures/assertions were adapted; no new test cases or development documents were added for the review fixes.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context \
  tests/unit/app/test_scroll_startup_io.py \
  tests/unit/app/test_multi_agent_manager_startup.py \
```

**2,070 passed, 1 skipped in 53.95s.** The Linux-only DMS lock regression was skipped on macOS. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, Black, flake8, and pylint.

Disposable scenarios also verified:

- Scheduled in-request reload completes after native, old-database, and real HarnessSessionBridge final saves, including a target database with previous completion metadata.
- A discarded candidate keeps the committed 30-day retention policy and a 10-day-old row.
- Restore with an older database snapshot and newer session/manifest reconciles once without hashes; the next start performs no session scan.
- Both check and repair reject an unrelated SQLite database without changing bytes; a healthy check preserves schema, version, journal mode, and database bytes.
- A valid SQLite header with a corrupt B-tree fails snapshot verification.
- Archiving a staged file after its source becomes SQLite leaves the source writer lock intact.

The original synthetic migration benchmark used 41 agents, 55,001 session files, and 550,010 rows: default migration 0.045s; all initial migrations 43.405s with five workers; completed reopen/check 0.035s with zero session scans/hashes. These are local migration timings from the initial implementation, not end-to-end startup or customer-environment measurements.

## Additional Notes

A default agent with unfinished migration still waits for its own history. Relevant reloads wait for outgoing saves, and `/daemon restart` now reports scheduling rather than immediate completion. File staging adds temporary disk space and I/O during explicit backups; snapshot verification is confined to backup/maintenance. Restores incur one reconciliation. Ordinary completed startup keeps its fast path. Runtime checks were performed on macOS; Linux/Windows execution is left to CI.

prs.title: fix(plugins): report an unusable dependency state root at startup
prs.body:
## Description

On restricted POSIX deployments, an unusable passwd home can make QwenPaw fail during import with a bare filesystem exception. This change reports `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` during state-root selection, naming the source, reason and `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` remedy.

POSIX selection remains: explicit override → absolute passwd home → absolute `HOME` fallback. The deployment guide documents the override and requires every process sharing a dependency environment to resolve the same root.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8515 (diagnostics and documentation).

**Security Considerations:** The existing `HOME` fallback can still select different roots when no absolute passwd home is available. Restricted deployments should configure one shared absolute override.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy

## Changes

- Probe the proposed POSIX home-derived coordination directory before canonicalization and report unusable paths with actionable context.
- Accept an already prepared, writable coordination directory under a read-only home.
- Add four regressions: unusable passwd home, dangling coordination link, read-only home, and a prepared root under a read-only home.
- Document the override in `deploy/DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE.md`.

The probe is best effort; later writes can still fail because of filesystem changes, capacity limits or races. Explicit overrides and Windows are not probed.

## Checklist

- [ ] Full-repository `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [x] Relevant tests pass
- [x] Documentation updated

## Testing

Run `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -v -rs`, including a non-root run for permission-bit cases.

## Evidence

Linux, original PR-head source:

| Scope | Root / Python 3.12 | uid 65534 / Python 3.11 |
|---|---|---|
| `state_root` tests | 6 passed / 2 skipped | 8 passed |

prs.title: fix(agents): recover from rejected media URLs
prs.body:
## Description

When a provider returns HTTP 400 with “The provided URL does not appear to be valid” for a request containing media, an existing conversation can keep failing on every turn. The reasoning loop currently retries explicit media-capability rejections but does not handle this URL-validation error.

Retry this specific error once with media replaced by text placeholders in the formatted request. Keep the original saved messages and restore media handling after the retry, including when the retry fails. Do not record a model-wide media rejection for a URL error. Requests without wire media, unrelated validation errors, authentication/server errors, and content-policy rejections retain their existing behavior.

Adds regression coverage using deserialized tool-result history, the real formatter, and simulated OpenAI API errors, plus English/Chinese model documentation and README documentation entries.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7966

**Security Considerations:** Content-policy errors are excluded from this fallback. The change reuses existing request-time media normalization and does not introduce new file access or URL fetching.

prs.title: fix(console): persist market install provenance so 'Update All' covers third-party plugins (#8176)
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8176.

When a plugin is installed from the AgentScope plugin market, the install URL is discarded after download. The console later re-derives the market identity by string-matching the local `author` field against the market `owner`/`developer` logins. Real plugin.json `author` strings frequently differ from the market owner login (the issue's reporter has owner `onesix` but author `onesixth`), so third-party plugins never match, never enter the `updates` map, and the `Update All` button silently skips them.

Changes:

- Stamp a small `.qwenpaw-market.json` marker with the scoped market id (e.g. `@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task`) into the freshly extracted plugin tree before the loader copies it into the install directory. The marker rides through install, gets overwritten on update, and is removed with the plugin on uninstall.
- Expose `market_id` on every entry in `GET /api/plugins`, in both the loader path and the pre-loader disk-scan fallback.
- `marketPluginMatches` treats a recorded `market_id` as authoritative; the existing author heuristic is the fallback for legacy installs that have no provenance yet.

Non-market install sources (local paths, third-party hosts, uploads) are untouched — the marker is only written for official-market archive URLs that match `{host}/plugins/{owner}/{name}/archive/zip/{ref}`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8176

**Security Considerations:** None. The marker is derived from the install URL after the hostname is verified to match the official market; no user-supplied path or query is persisted. Local-path and third-party-host installs do not write the marker.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

- [ ] Refactoring

## Testing

- New backend: `TestMarketProvenance` (9 cases) covers URL parsing, marker writing, malformed-marker tolerance, and the disk-scan path surfacing `market_id`.
- Updated: `TestListPluginsRoute` accepts the new `market_id` field.
- New frontend: 3 cases in `marketPluginIdentity.test.ts` (provenance match, provenance authoritative over author, blank-falls-back).
- New frontend: 1 case in `usePluginManager.test.ts` that reproduces the reporter's exact plugin shape (`author: 'onesixth'`, owner `onesix`) and verifies `Update All` triggers `installPlugin`.

```bash
$ QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR=$(mktemp -d) pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_plugins_router_helpers.py tests/unit/app/routers/test_plugins_router_lifecycle.py tests/unit/plugins/ -q
...
```

## Evidence

Reproduction from issue #8176 (downloaded the reporter's actual market plugin):

```json
{
  "id": "qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task",
  "name": "Wait Agent Task",
  "version": "1.2.0",

}
```

vs. the corresponding market entry returned by the live market API:

```json
{
  "id": "@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task",

```

Before the fix, `marketPluginMatches` short-circuits at the author check (`onesixth` ≠ `onesix`), the third-party plugin is missing from the `updates` map, and the red "Update All (n)" badge only counts official plugins.

After the fix, `install_plugin_source` writes `.qwenpaw-market.json` with `@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task` into the install tree, `GET /api/plugins` returns that id on the installed record, and `marketPluginMatches` accepts the exact scoped id regardless of the free-form author — `Update All` now triggers the update for the third-party plugin.


## Additional Notes

- Marker file name `.qwenpaw-market.json` follows the existing `.qwenpaw-pawport.json` convention already used by the plugin loader for install-stage provenance.
- No migration is needed for existing installs: legacy plugins without the marker still get author-based matching. Re-installing from the market picks up the marker.
- Scope intentionally narrow — only the install provenance + matching path. Doesn't touch `fetchPluginCatalog` (official plugins), `installPluginSource`'s force-reinstall branch, or the conflict-resolution flow.

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

**Fork sync completed before opening this PR.** The head is the actual **`xuanrui-L:dev/creator`** branch at `df983dd5dc960e4e98f5a8dea421c00960f44a6a`. Latest upstream `main`, `c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`, was first merged through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/239 using a **merge commit**, preserving the upstream ancestry. The five conflicts caused by the previous squash baseline were resolved against the exact prior fork head and checked against a clean reference merge. Upstream's Docker/Node and Windows storage fixes are preserved, not overwritten.

**Scope:** **28 files under `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/`, +5,463 / −442**. The entire tree outside this plugin is byte-identical to the recorded upstream baseline. No host application, Console, other plugin, dependency declaration, or CI/release workflow change is contributed by this PR.

### What's new since 2.0.3

- **Provider-correct local media transport.** Local source images/videos, document pages, and extracted frames now use the configured VLM's transport rather than unconditionally going through DashScope temporary OSS. Non-DashScope gateways receive inline Base64; Bailian MaaS retains its supported upload path, while Token Plan credentials use inline media rather than an upload API they cannot authorize. Grounding verification carries the protocol of the credential it actually borrows, avoiding mismatched transport and wire format. Oversized decodable images step down a bounded JPEG ladder with EXIF orientation and transparency preserved appropriately; undecodable or still-oversized inputs retain a clear refusal. MIME handling respects recognizable image bytes and meaningful declarations instead of losing media behind `application/octet-stream`, including direct Anthropic/Gemini paths. Inline media is charged against the model-context budget by a bounded representative cost rather than its full Base64 text length, so normal media-bearing messages are not rejected locally before reaching the provider.
- **Connection tests report what they actually prove.** ASR tests now exercise the production-selected Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, or Fun-ASR route with one second of silent WAV audio, rather than treating a model-list or upload-policy response as transcription success. Responses are graded according to the production reader: empty/HTML/error-wrapped 2xx responses and malformed transcription structures no longer report success. A queued asynchronous task is not claimed to be a completed transcript. The optional `capability_verified` response field separates credential acceptance from verified capability; the model-settings UI shows an explicit bilingual warning for credential-only results and retains the existing success/error flows. **An operator-triggered ASR connection test can incur the provider's charge for the short sample.** No real provider calls were made during this release validation.
- **Saved credentials stay within their configured probe boundary.** A probe borrowing a saved key must target an operator-saved origin normalized by HTTPX's own scheme/host/port interpretation. LLM/VLM credential reuse follows the actual key owner; built-in default addresses are not silently treated as authorization. Probe transports filter credential-bearing GET values, do not follow redirects, reject unsupported schemes and embedded URL credentials, and apply cloud-metadata address checks including IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings. Destination checks also run before ASR sample-upload side effects and the relevant save-time probes. These are configuration-bound checks, not a restriction against legitimate operator-configured localhost/LAN model gateways.
- **Visual guidance no longer silently selects animation.** The Creator prompt and the two mandatory visual skills distinguish camera/layout language from rendering medium. Final visual variants and video prompts explicitly preserve the project/user's medium; narrative, micro-film, and documentary work without a declared style defaults to photographic texture rather than animation. Intermediate storyboard drawings retain their separately requested pencil/charcoal/etc. medium, without forcing that sketch appearance into the finished video. Existing assets are not automatically regenerated. The specialist-cancellation regression also uses the test file's existing bounded wait helper instead of a separate two-second wait; production behavior and the assertion are unchanged.

**Version and dependencies.** The existing fork version bump is included: `plugin.json`, `ui/package.json`, and both root package-lock version fields all read **2.0.4**. The host minimum remains **2.1.0**. No Python or npm dependency changes are introduced relative to current upstream. Publication still uses the unchanged version-driven main-branch workflow; this PR does not overwrite an already published artifact.

**Related Issue:** Release follow-up to https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8357. The source increments were integrated through https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/233, https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/234, and https://github.com/xuanrui-L/QwenPaw/pull/237.

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, user projects, runtime directories, or generated media are committed. Saved-key origin checks constrain credential reuse; request-supplied credentials and explicitly configured local gateways remain supported. Cloud-metadata literal checks happen before dispatch, while connected-peer checks inspect the response path; behind an HTTP proxy that peer is the proxy, so this is not claimed as complete DNS/proxy isolation. Existing secure media-materialization boundaries remain unchanged. Real provider probes may be billable as noted above; automated tests and browser smoke used synthetic fixtures, not production credentials or paid calls.

prs.title: fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels
prs.body:
## Description

The auto-memory-recall pipeline injected a synthetic `memory_search` tool interaction (`ToolCallBlock` + `ToolResultBlock`) into the LLM context. Two problems followed from that:

- models that observe a tool interaction in their own context tend to imitate it out loud in the next user-facing reply ("I'll check memory for relevant context…"), which leaks the internal recall flow to the user and to outbound channels;
- the payload had to be kept off the wire with a dedicated `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY` metadata flag plus a channel-renderer guard and a console tool-card guard — three cooperating layers, none of which was actually connected (see *Root cause*).

This PR carries the recall payload in a single `HintBlock` instead. Every provider formatter (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / DashScope / Ollama) turns a hint into a separate `role="user"` message, so the request never ends with an assistant turn; and the console / PawApp history converter skips hint blocks entirely, so the payload never reaches a transcript. Because the block type already covers both concerns, the hidden flag and the two guards are gone. The middleware recognises the message through the pre-existing `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_IDS_KEY`, which the block-cleanup path already uses, so the transient injection and cleanup behaviour are unchanged.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## Root cause

Two independent issues, both reproduced against the real converter and the real formatters before the change:

1. **Assistant prefill.** With the payload in a `TextBlock`, the Anthropic formatter emitted the recall as an assistant turn, so the request ended with `role="assistant"`. Anthropic reads a trailing assistant turn as a prefill continuation, which Claude 4.6+ rejects.
2. **The hiding logic was not connected.** `agentscope_msg_to_message()` nests the original metadata under `message.metadata["metadata"]`, while the renderer guard only checked the top level, so `_is_auto_memory_recall_message()` never fired and the recall text was rendered to the channel as an ordinary assistant message. The console guard did not help either: it lived on the tool-card path, which the payload no longer used, and the tool-card adapter did not forward the metadata the guard checked.

## Evidence

The two issues above were reproduced against the real converter and the real provider formatters before the change, and the same paths were re-checked after it. The payload never appears in an outbound message, and the model request never ends with an assistant turn.

### Before / after, against the real converter and formatters

Request tail, Anthropic:

```
before: [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # assistant tail -> prefill
after:  [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "user",     "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # no assistant turn
```

History conversion:

```
before: agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 1 message containing the payload
after:  agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 0 messages
```

The renderer guard before the change:

```
message.metadata = {"original_id": ..., "original_name": "memory_search",
                    "metadata": {"auto_memory_search_hidden": true, ...}, ...}
                                   ^ nested here
guard checks:    message.metadata.get("auto_memory_search_hidden")   # top level -> misses
=> rendered parts: 1  (full recall payload sent to the channel)
```

### Formatter coverage

The request ends with a `user` turn and contains no `assistant` turn for: Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope, Ollama (and DeepSeek / MiniMax, which share the OpenAI base formatter).

### Local verification evidence

- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_base_memory_manager.py` + `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` + `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` + `tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py`: **131 passed**
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`, `pylint` (repository pre-commit arguments): clean, **10.00/10**

### Regression tests added

`tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` — four test functions, ten execution cases:

- `test_final_request_carries_the_recall_as_a_user_turn` (parametrized over the six QwenPaw formatter wrappers — Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope and Ollama): the request ends with a `user` turn carrying the recall, the recalled text itself is present, and there is no `assistant` turn;
- `test_recall_is_injected_and_reused_from_the_cache`: the recall is injected right after the user turn without touching the agent context, and the same turn then reuses the serialized cache instead of searching again — the reloaded message is compared against the original payload (same hint text, same block id);
- `test_recall_is_omitted_from_the_converted_transcript`: the real conversion path (`agentscope_msg_to_message`) drops the recall — exactly the user message and the normal reply remain;
- `test_next_user_turn_replaces_the_cached_recall` (parametrized over a second turn with fresh results and with no results): the stale evidence disappears either way.

The two middleware tests that this supersedes — `test_search_result_only_updates_current_model_input` and `test_new_turn_replaces_search_cache` — are removed: they patched the extraction step out, while the new test drives the real path. The tool-call follow-up test and all six formatter variants are kept.

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py` | carry the recall payload in a `HintBlock` instead of a text/thinking/tool_call/tool_result quartet |
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/middlewares.py` | `_is_auto_memory_recall_msg` helper; memory-extraction filter accepts the recall message |
| `src/qwenpaw/constant.py` | remove the now unused `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_TEXT` / `_THINKING_PREFIX` |
| `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` | new regression tests (final request, conversion path, middleware injection path) |
| `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` | drop the two middleware tests that the new real-path test supersedes |

5 files, +345 / -127 lines. No new metadata flag and no renderer or frontend guard: the block type handles both, so the payload cannot reach a transcript even if a future channel renders messages directly.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass

prs.title: fix(agents): drop empty media blocks before formatting requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A media `DataBlock` whose base64 payload is empty (e.g. a tool returning a
zero-byte image) was serialized by the formatters as an empty data URI:

```json
{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}
```

Every provider rejects this — OpenAI answers with *"Image data cannot be
empty"*.

## Fix

- Add `_is_empty_media_block()`: a media/data block whose `base64` source has a
  zero-length `data` payload.
- Strip such blocks in `normalize_messages_for_model_request()` **before** the
  multimodal branching — no endpoint accepts an empty data URI, so this runs
  regardless of multimodal support.
- Reuses the existing strip machinery via a new `empty_only` mode, so tool-result
  nesting and the `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` fallback behave like the other
  media-stripping paths.
- URL sources are left untouched: their emptiness cannot be determined without
  fetching them.

## Evidence

Reproduced and verified locally:

- Before: a `Msg` with `DataBlock(source=Base64Source(data="", media_type="image/png"))`
  formats to `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}`.

prs.title: fix(matrix): recover cached sessions and missing device keys
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8365. Password-authenticated Matrix channels log in again on restart. If a homeserver loses a device's encryption keys while the local crypto store marks them as shared, startup does not restore the keys and the channel can appear healthy while decryption fails.

Adapt session recovery to main's native Matrix plugin and per-instance `channel_state/matrix` ownership. Reuse a session only for the same homeserver, login identity, device and password, then verify its canonical user/device pair with `whoami`. Fall back to password login only for `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`; preserve explicit tokens and main's atomic state writes and ownership checks.

Reconcile E2EE device keys at startup and re-upload a missing identity from the existing SQLite crypto store, preserving sessions. Refuse conflicting remote keys and distinguish query failure from deletion. Retry transient startup key-query failures up to three times, with a ten-second limit per query and a one-second interruptible delay. Permanent authorization failures and conflicting remote keys fail without retry. Run ongoing health probes in a separate background task once per minute, report failed key health to the plugin host, and keep routine sync/send maintenance independent of that result. Log the first undecryptable event at error level.

## Security considerations

Use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and the session token as salt for the password fingerprint, with an explicit format version. Legacy fast-hash fingerprints cannot authorize cache reuse and require a fresh password login. Passwords are not persisted. Conflicting remote identities are never overwritten.

## Evidence

Validated on Linux/Python 3.11 against main `c26d31c0`, using real matrix-nio HTTP calls, local aiohttp homeserver fixtures, python-olm and persisted SQLite crypto stores:

```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_matrix_recovery.py tests/unit/channels/test_matrix.py -q
With matrix-e2ee:    41 passed
Without matrix-e2ee: 27 passed, 14 skipped
```

The two runs explicitly checked `nio.crypto.ENCRYPTION_ENABLED=True` and `False`. E2EE-only tests skip when the optional backend is absent.

Cases cover transient HTTP errors, partial key-query failures, query timeouts, retry exhaustion without account mutation, permanent authorization rejection, cancellation during retry, background health failure/recovery, continued delivery of pending device messages after a failed health query, and repeated routine maintenance without extra health queries. Existing cases cover restart reuse, expired-token fallback, temporary authentication failure, changed credentials/server/device, localpart names, old unversioned fingerprints, explicit tokens, key loss, upload retry, conflicting identities, bounded health checks and the host's failed-state notification. Missing keys are restored using the original identity.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: ci(release): resolve desktop artifacts by id so duplicate names cannot break publish
prs.body:
> **Submitted by**: 秦琼·CIOps@QPQAT

## What this fixes

A release run that gets cancelled and then re-run keeps **every attempt's artifacts under the same name**. `scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` listed them with `--jq '.artifacts[] | ... | .name'` and appended each line to `selected[]` **without de-duplication**, then downloaded every entry into `--dir "$name"`.

With two copies of `QwenPaw-Desktop-Tauri-macOS-2.3.0b2` present, the helper downloaded that name **twice into one directory** and the second extraction aborted:

```
error downloading QwenPaw-Desktop-Tauri-macOS-2.3.0b2: error extracting zip archive:
error extracting "QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-macOS.zip": openat QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-macOS.zip: file exists
##[error]Desktop artifacts remained unavailable or corrupt after 2 attempts
```

Both publish jobs (`upload-release`, `upload-oss`) died on that step, so `finalize`, `deploy-website`, `promote-desktop` and `duty-issue` were all skipped and the draft release kept **zero desktop assets**. Real case: run [`41035310997`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/actions/runs/41035310997) attempt 3, draft `v2.3.0-beta.2` left at `assets=0`.

Retrying could never help: the attempt loop re-listed the same two copies and hit the same collision, and `cleanup_downloads` runs once per attempt rather than between names.

## Why not just de-duplicate the names

`gh run download` only accepts `--dir` / `--name` / `--pattern` — there is **no way to select one artifact by id**. So after de-duplicating we would still pass a bare name and `gh` would decide which copy to fetch, which can silently pick the **older** attempt's build. Turning a loud crash into a silently stale release is worse, so the copies are resolved explicitly instead.

## Changes

`scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` only (+123 / −23). Upload-side workflows are untouched.

1. **List by id, not by bare name** — `--jq '[.id, .created_at, .name] | @tsv'`.
2. **New `resolve_selection()`** keeps the newest copy per matching name (ISO-8601 UTC sorts lexicographically; numeric id breaks exact ties) and emits `<name>\t<id>` pairs. A dropped duplicate is reported as a `::warning::` so an unexpected extra copy stays visible in the job log instead of surfacing two steps later as a corrupt artifact.
3. **Download by id** through `gh api repos/<repo>/actions/artifacts/<id>/zip`, written to `${name}.zip.partial` and removed only on success, so a truncated transfer can never be mistaken for a complete artifact.
4. **New `extract_artifact()`** unpacks with python3: `testzip()` pre-check, **POSIX mode bits restored from `external_attr`**, and paths escaping the target directory are rejected. `python3 -m zipfile -e` silently drops mode bits (a `0755` entry comes back `0644`), which would strip the executable bit from the macOS `.app` payload while every step still reported green.
5. `cleanup_downloads()` now also removes `${name}.zip.partial`.

The two strings asserted by `tests/unit/tauri/test_desktop_workflows.py::test_download_helper_resolves_verifier_from_its_own_checkout` are preserved verbatim.

## Verification

CI cannot cover this change: `scripts/pack/**` matches none of the `paths` filters in `tests.yml`, so the unit test that asserts this script's content does not run when the script changes. Everything below was therefore run locally.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash -n` | pass |
| `tests/unit/tauri/test_desktop_workflows.py` — the 6 assertions touching this script/workflows | **6 passed, 0 failed** |
| Old selection logic fed the real duplicate listing from run `41035310997` | `selected` = `[macOS, macOS, Windows]` — reproduces the incident exactly |
| New `resolve_selection()` on the same input | selects macOS **once**, picks the newer id `12976234290`, warns about dropped `12971716292` |
| Negative control — listing **without** duplicates | new and old select the identical set |
| End-to-end with the real 955,499,745-byte Windows artifact | download RC=0, unpack RC=0, yields `QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b2-Windows-setup.exe` (959,765,766 bytes) + `.sha256` sidecar |
| `verify_desktop_artifacts.py --require windows` on the unpacked tree | **RC=0** — `verified windows artifact: … (959765766 bytes)` |
| Independent sha256 recomputation | `e307ebaab4cfd5043d47eca3d9551cdf148a41474d55ee170118185abfb09f20` matches the sidecar, so extraction is byte-identical |
| Mode-bit round trip (0755 / 0644 fixture) | `python3 -m zipfile -e` → both `0644` (bits lost); `extract_artifact` → `0755` / `0644` restored |
| `pre-commit run --files scripts/pack/download_desktop_artifacts.sh` | RC=0 — note 16 of 17 hooks report `no files to check` because `^scripts/pack/` is excluded in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`; only `detect-private-key` actually ran |

## Side effect: peak disk usage

Downloading to `${name}.zip.partial` keeps the archive and its extracted tree on disk at the same time, which the previous `gh run download --dir "$name"` path may not have (gh handles its own temporary storage internally; **its peak was not measured for comparison**).

Measured on the real artifacts of run `41035310997`, processing one platform at a time:

| Platform | archive | extracted | peak for that platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | 955,499,745 B (911 MiB) | 959,765,766 B (915 MiB) | **1.78 GiB** (`du` on the unpacked tree: 912M + 916M = 1.8G) |
| macOS | 1,227,545,728 B (1171 MiB) | not downloaded here (payload is an already-compressed `.app.tar.gz`, so ~1171 MiB) | ~2.28 GiB |

Names are processed serially and each archive is deleted right after its extraction succeeds (`rm -f -- "$zip_path"`), so the worst case is roughly *previous platform's extracted tree + current platform's archive + current extracted tree* ≈ **3.2 GiB** — well inside the 14 GB of a GitHub-hosted runner, but worth stating because the same job also handles `qwenpaw-docker-image` (2.0 GB).

There is no toggle: this helper is only ever invoked from the two desktop publish jobs, and a partial archive that is *not* cleaned up would be worse than the extra peak, since `cleanup_downloads` now removes `${name}.zip.partial` on every retry and on failure.

## Relationship to #7641

`download_desktop_artifacts.sh` and its verifier were introduced by #7641 ("fix(release): retry and verify desktop artifact downloads"), which addressed **partial downloads from network timeouts** — hence `--attempts`, `cleanup_downloads` and the sha256 sidecar checks.

This PR is not an alternative to that work; it builds on it. #7641's retry loop assumes a name maps to one artifact, which holds within a single attempt but not across attempts of a re-run release. The two changes compose: `--attempts` still guards against a truncated transfer of the *chosen* copy, while id-based selection guarantees there is exactly one chosen copy per name. `verify_desktop_artifacts.py` and its test are left untouched.

## Scope

Only the desktop publish helper is changed. No workflow, no product code, and no artifact is modified by this PR.

prs.body:
## Description

Automatic memory recall was represented as an assistant-authored thinking/tool-call/tool-result sequence. Models could imitate that synthetic trajectory and call `memory_search` again in the same turn.

This change represents automatic recall as transient, untrusted `TextBlock` reference data attached to a request-local copy of the current user message. The fixed system prompt and conversation history remain unchanged for cross-turn prompt-cache reuse. The request copy is not persisted, and explicit model-initiated `memory_search` calls are unchanged.

Persisted caches from the previous synthetic format are versioned out and searched again on restore. Evidence block IDs are retained on the request copy so repeated preparation is idempotent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8361

## Description

Resolves two related issues in `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_reranker.py`:

1. **Enablement requires non-empty credential:** `load_reranker_config()` previously evaluated enablement from `config.enabled and config.model_name` alone. prs.title: fix(backup): snapshot SQLite databases without releasing live locks
prs.body:
## Summary

Online workspace backups can release live SQLite locks on Linux when the application reads and closes database sidecar files, allowing another connection to truncate mapped SHM and trigger SIGBUS. Backups now identify and snapshot SQLite databases in a separate process using SQLite's Backup API, archive the snapshots at their original paths, and exclude WAL/SHM/journal sidecars. Snapshot failures abort the backup rather than falling back to raw copies; cancellation and timeouts remain supported.

History construction also reran the FTS integrity scan on every connection, even after the quick_check cache hit. That scan takes a writer lock and can stall another session's synchronous history append. Successful FTS checks are now cached by process, resolved path and file identity, independently of quick_check. Concurrent constructors share the existing coordination; contention defers the FTS check for a later retry. Replacement, index recreation, repair and reported corruption invalidate the relevant cache.

Open-database replacement tests are POSIX-only. Closed-connection replacement coverage remains cross-platform. Repeated backup filename cases are consolidated into one nested custom filename with URI-sensitive characters that are valid on Windows.

## Validation

- 349 related history, Scroll and backup tests passed; 1 Linux-only test skipped on macOS.
- Before the cache fix, the focused regressions fail with a repeated FTS scan and a competing append reporting `database is locked`; both pass after the fix.
- A local 40,000-row, 150-token-per-row synthetic database (~109 MB) reopened in 0.6–0.8 ms on cache hits, versus ~250 ms previously, with zero repeated FTS scans. A synchronous append during concurrent cached reopens took ~0.5 ms. These measurements are machine-specific.
- Original backup verification included a Linux container SIGBUS reproduction: the raw read-and-close path released locks, while the snapshot path preserved them.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

## Scope

Initial uncached FTS checks still scan the index and require a writer lock; this change removes repeated scans on ordinary opens, not all synchronous SQLite I/O. Windows portability changes were reviewed but not run on Windows. Snapshot staging requires additional temporary disk space. Attribution of every reported production crash remains unconfirmed.

issues.body:
### Summary

Treat the gateway WebSocket as a transport channel for an agent turn, not as the thing that owns the turn — client disconnects should not cancel in-flight turns.

### Problem statement

In the gateway web chat UI, an active agent turn is tied 1:1 to the WebSocket connection's lifetime. The chat WebSocket is owned by the `AgentChat` page component (`web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx`), so navigating to a different page in the left nav unmounts it, and closing the browser tab does the same. On the backend, `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs`'s mid-turn `tokio::select!` loop classifies any client disconnect (`Close`/`Err`/`None` from `receiver.next()`) the same way: it calls `cancel_token.cancel()`, which aborts the running turn. When the turn unwinds as cancelled, the gateway persists an assistant message with the `"[interrupted by user]"` marker (`turn-interrupted-by-user` i18n key) instead of the real response.

This means a routine SPA navigation or a brief network blip — not just an abandoned session — kills the in-flight turn. The user comes back to the chat (or reopens the browser) expecting their answer and instead sees "[interrupted by user]," even though the agent may have been seconds away from finishing.

This cancel-on-disconnect behavior was intentionally added to fix #6514 (the forward loop could hot-loop and make `/abort` and `/health` unresponsive after a client disconnected mid-turn). That fix correctly stops forwarding events to the dead socket, but it also conflated "stop forwarding to this socket" with "cancel the turn" — the two don't need to be the same action.

### Proposed solution

- On WS disconnect mid-turn, stop the event-forwarding loop (preserving the #6514 fix) but do **not** cancel `cancel_token` purely because the socket closed. Let `turn_fut` keep running to completion server-side.
- Keep accumulating `TurnEvent`s (or persist them incrementally) so a turn that finishes while no client is attached still lands in the session transcript normally — no `"[interrupted by user]"` marker for this case.
- On reconnect with the same `session_key`, let the client attach to a still-running turn (e.g., replay buffered events / resume streaming) or, if the turn already finished, simply load the persisted result — instead of only ever being able to observe a cancelled turn.
- Keep an explicit cancel path (e.g. `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` or `/abort`) as the only way to truly cancel a turn; a bare WS disconnect should no longer imply cancellation.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- No change to the explicit abort/delete-session cancellation path — that should still cancel immediately.
- No requirement to support multiple simultaneously-attached clients to the same running turn in v1.

### Alternatives considered

Keep current behavior and rely on session persistence (#6932) to recover transcript fidelity after the fact — rejected because the user-visible turn is still killed early; the agent doesn't get to finish its work, it's not just a presentation/storage gap.

### Acceptance criteria

- Switching nav pages or closing the tab mid-turn no longer cancels the running turn server-side.
- A turn that completes with no client attached is persisted as a normal assistant response, not `"[interrupted by user]"`.
- Reconnecting to the same session while a turn is still running can observe its progress/result; reconnecting after completion loads the real response.
- `/api/sessions/{id}/abort` and `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` still cancel turns promptly (regression coverage for #6514 preserved).
- Regression test: WS disconnects mid-turn, turn finishes server-side, session transcript shows the real assistant response.

### Architecture impact

`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs` (mid-turn select loop, `classify_client_msg`/`DisconnectAction`), `crates/zeroclaw-runtime` turn/cancellation plumbing, `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx` (WS reconnect/resume UX). Related: #6514, #6932.

### Risk and rollback

Medium risk — touches turn cancellation semantics shared with the abort path fixed in #6514. Rollback is reverting to "any disconnect cancels," i.e. current behavior; rollout should be additive/guarded so the explicit abort path is unaffected.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: [Task]: show a detached chat turn's answer when the socket reopens before the turn ends
issues.body:
### Task

When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running on the gateway, keep track of that turn and reload the transcript once it ends.

### Context

Follow-up from the review of #11965 (dashboard sign-in).

When a chat socket closes in the middle of a turn, the page stops showing the turn as running. The close can come from a session ending, a gateway reload or a network drop. The page then reloads the transcript once when a socket opens again (`resyncOnOpenRef` in `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx`).

The gateway keeps running the turn after its viewer goes, and saves it only when the turn ends. The new socket doesn't receive the turn's result.

So if the socket reopens before the turn ends, that one reload fetches a transcript without the answer. Nothing triggers another reload, so the page sits idle with the answer missing until the user reloads the page or switches conversations. Since #11571, the prompt itself stays on screen.

The existing test covers only a turn that ends before the socket reopens: "a socket closed mid-turn stops the turn and reloads the transcript when it reopens" in `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts`.

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` already reports whether a session's turn is still running. #9002 proposes the wider reconnect contract for detached turns: polling that state and keeping the composer locked while a turn runs. #9641 tracks browser tests for it. This task is the narrow case that the resync on reopen left open, and it should fit whichever of these lands first.

### Acceptance criteria

- If the socket reopens while the turn is still running, the page shows that the turn is running, and the answer appears once the turn ends, without a page reload.
- The watch stops when the turn ends, when the conversation changes and when the session ends. It never loops.
- Without session persistence the state route answers 404. The page then keeps today's single reload.
- A test covers a socket that reopens before the turn ends, next to the existing test.

### Likely files or areas

- `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx` (the socket close and open handlers, transcript hydration)
- `web/src/lib/api.ts` (a call for `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state`; the web client has none yet)
- `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts`

Related: #9002, #9641, #11571.

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet

### Risk notes

Low to medium. It is web only, but it touches chat hydration, which #11571 just changed: keep a prompt the gateway hasn't saved yet on screen.
