issues.title: [Bug]: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider with no context_window silently assumes 32,000, then rejects valid turns locally
issues.body:
### Affected component

provider

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Summary

When a custom OpenAI-compatible provider has no `context_window`, the runtime resolves the model capacity to a hard-coded **32,000** with `ModelContextWindowSource::CompatibilityFallback`. With `[tools] optional = ["*"]` the fixed prompt floor is already **~16k tokens**, so a brand-new conversation starts at ~50% of the assumed window and two or three tool calls make the turn fail.

The turn is rejected **client-side** (`provider_attempted: false`), and the error discards the capacity provenance, so the operator sees a generic "this request exceeds the selected model's context window" that points at the conversation instead of at the unconfigured model metadata. In this report the real model window is ~1,000,000 tokens, i.e. the guard enforces a window ~31x smaller than reality.

### Current behavior

Config (custom endpoint, no `context_window`):

```toml
[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]
model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"
uri = "https://<gateway>/v1"
api_key = "<redacted>"
```

Observed on a **fresh** conversation (after `/new`, `messages_count: 2`):

| Step | Input tokens |
|---|---|
| 1st request (system + one short user line, 49 tools) | **16,165** |
| after `web_fetch` + `web_search` | 24,994 |
| after 2 more `web_fetch` | 30,850 |
| next dispatch | rejected: `estimated_tokens: 39830` > `context_token_budget: 32000` |

Rejection event (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/mod.rs:1036`):

```json
{"message":"Provider-facing request exceeds the active model context window",
 "attributes":{"error_key":"context_window_exceeded","estimated_tokens":39830,
 "context_token_budget":32000,"model_context_window":32000,
 "model_context_window_source":"CompatibilityFallback","provider_attempted":false,
 "token_count_source":"calibrated"}}
```

With `[tools] optional = ["*"]`, 49 tool schemas are sent every turn; the measured floor on turn 1 is 16,165 tokens with a 4,567-character system prompt and a ~20-token user message.

### Expected behavior

1. **Do not silently present the 32k stub as model truth.** When a route resolves to `CompatibilityFallback`, this should be visible to the operator (startup, `doctor`, `status`) and, most importantly, in the failure itself.
2. **Make the failure actionable.** When the rejection is caused by an unconfigured capacity, the error should name the provider alias and the fix, e.g. "`context_window` is not configured for `providers.models.<type>.<alias>`; assuming 32,000 tokens. Set `context_window`, or raise `agent.max_context_tokens`."
3. Optionally, before falling back to 32k, consult bounded catalog metadata for models that are known (the models.dev data already used for listings in #9347) — or at minimum make the stub configurable/disableable.

### Root cause (v0.8.6 source)

1. `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:5440` — `pub const UNCONFIGURED_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FALLBACK: usize = 32_000;`
2. `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:4787-4822` — `resolved_model_context_window_for_route()` reads **only** `provider.context_window` for the selected alias/model. There is no catalog lookup on the runtime path; anything unset becomes `ResolvedModelContextWindow { tokens: 32_000, source: CompatibilityFallback }`.
3. `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:4020-4030` — the proactive budget defaults to `LEGACY_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET`, which is the same 32,000 constant (`schema.rs:3899`), so window and budget coincide.
4. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/mod.rs:1023-1056` — `context_window_exceeded_error()` builds `ContextWindowExceeded { estimated_tokens, model_context_window }` and therefore **drops `model_context_window_source`**, even though the log line records it.
5. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/outcome.rs:86-97` — `ContextWindowExceeded` has no provenance/provider field and renders a static string. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/locales/en/cli.ftl`:

   ```
   turn-context-window-exceeded-error = This request exceeds the selected model's context window. Reduce the request or enabled tools, or choose a model with a larger context window.
   ```

   Nothing here distinguishes a real 32k model from a 32k stub.

Note for whoever picks this up: an explicit `agent.max_context_tokens` **does** raise the fallback operand today (`schema.rs:4002-4008`, `bind_budget`), so the current workaround is a single config key — but that behaviour is undocumented at the point of failure, and the source still reports `CompatibilityFallback`.

### Proposed fix

Minimal (fixes the misleading failure):

- Add `model_context_window_source: ModelContextWindowSource` (or `provider: &str` + `source`) to `ContextWindowExceeded` and thread it through `context_window_exceeded_error()` and the channel/RPC error payload (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:11096`).
- Add a separate i18n key for the fallback case that names the provider alias and both remediation keys. Keep the current key for genuine windows.

Then:

- Emit a one-time startup/`doctor` warning for any agent whose route resolves to `CompatibilityFallback` (the `doctor` context-window autofill already exists; the gap is surfacing the unconfigured state without being asked).
- Optionally resolve known models from the bounded catalog before the stub, keeping `Configured` as the only value presented as model truth.

Verification: a config with no `context_window` should produce the fallback-specific message and no turn should be rejected at 32k when the operator has set a larger `max_context_tokens`; a route with a real `context_window` must keep the existing message and behaviour.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible provider without context_window
zeroclaw config set providers.models.<type>.<alias>.model "<model-id>"
zeroclaw config set providers.models.<type>.<alias>.uri "<base-url>"
```

```toml
[tools]
optional = ["*"]
```

2. Bind the provider to an agent with a channel (Telegram used here) and restart the daemon.
3. Start a new conversation (`/new`).
4. Send a request that triggers 2-3 `web_fetch` / `web_search` calls, e.g. "how safe is this repo? <url>".
5. Observe `context_window_exceeded` with `provider_attempted: false`.

### Impact

Affected users: anyone on a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenCode Zen, LM Studio, llama.cpp, DeepInfra, gateways, ...) whose model has more than 32k context and who has not manually set `providers.models.*.context_window`.

Frequency: deterministic for tool-using turns once roughly 16k of context is consumed; worse with `tools.optional = ["*"]`.

Consequence: the turn is dropped before the provider is called, so the model's real capacity is never used, and the message sends operators looking at the conversation instead of at model metadata.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
# fresh conversation, first request (2 messages, 49 tools)
{"message":"llm_request","attributes":{"iteration":1,"messages_count":2,"system_chars":4567,"tools_count":49,...}}
{"message":"llm_response","attributes":{"iteration":1,"input_tokens":16165,...}}

# after web_fetch + web_search
{"message":"llm_response","attributes":{"iteration":2,"input_tokens":24994,...}}
{"message":"llm_response","attributes":{"iteration":3,"input_tokens":30850,...}}

# rejection
{"message":"Provider-facing request exceeds the active model context window",
 "attributes":{"error_key":"context_window_exceeded","estimated_tokens":39830,
 "context_token_budget":32000,"model_context_window":32000,
 "model_context_window_source":"CompatibilityFallback","provider_attempted":false,
 "token_count_source":"calibrated"}}
```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.6

### Rust version

Prebuilt release binary (no local toolchain)

### Operating system

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (10.0.19045)

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest release (v0.8.6).
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.title: runtime: unknown model silently falls back to a 32k context budget (UNCONFIGURED_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FALLBACK) and fails turns that would fit the real window
issues.body:
## Problem

When a configured model is unknown to zeroclaw (no catalog entry, no `context_window` in the provider section), the turn budget silently becomes `UNCONFIGURED_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FALLBACK = 32_000` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:5442`, source `CompatibilityFallback`). Turns exceeding 32k estimated tokens fail BEFORE the provider call with `context_window_exceeded` — even when the real model window is far larger.

Production incident 2026-11-02 (NotaBene contour): after wiring an MCP server into the Researcher agent, every legal-research turn died with `Provider-facing request exceeds the active model context window` (estimated 34,403 tokens vs budget 32,000). The provider (`kimi-k2.8-preview-thinking`) actually accepts ≥200k tokens — measured by direct API probes (100k and 200k input tokens both returned 200). The agent worked on the previous zeroclaw release because the older binary resolved a larger window for the same setup, so the regression surfaced only after the upgrade + MCP adding tool schemas and discovery results.

## Ask

- Emit a startup/turn warning when `model_context_window_source == CompatibilityFallback` names the model and the configured fix (`context_window` in the provider section).
- Document `context_window` as REQUIRED for custom/unknown models in the provider config docs.
- Optionally: allow a global default context window setting so a whole fleet of custom providers doesn't need per-entry values.

## Workaround (applied)

Set `context_window = <real window>` in the `[providers.models.<...>]` section; validated by TOML parse + `config migrate`; restart required.

issues.title: [Feature]: hybrid (dense + BM25) recall for the Qdrant memory backend
issues.body:
### Summary

Hybrid (dense + BM25) recall for the Qdrant memory backend, plus keeping `importance`

### Problem statement

The SQLite memory backend ranks recall with a hybrid of vector similarity and keyword (FTS/BM25) scores, weighted by `memory.vector_weight` / `memory.keyword_weight`. The Qdrant backend only runs a dense cosine search. Two consequences:

- Exact names and rare terms (a person's name, a product code, "air filter") recall noticeably worse than on SQLite, because a short query's embedding is a weak signal for them.
- `store_with_agent` ignores `importance` and every Qdrant-backed entry comes back with `importance: None`, so the importance term of the recall rerank (`memory.importance_weight`) never contributes.

Qdrant itself supports keyword ranking: a sparse vector with `modifier: idf`, and since Qdrant 1.15 server-side BM25 inference (`{"text": ..., "model": "qdrant/bm25"}`), so a client needs no tokenizer.

### Proposed solution

- New `[storage.qdrant.<alias>] hybrid = true` (default `false`). When the backend creates the collection, it adds a `bm25` sparse vector (`modifier: idf`) next to the unnamed dense vector.
- Writes send the dense embedding plus `{"text": "<key>\n<content>", "model": "qdrant/bm25"}` for the sparse vector.
- Recall runs the existing dense search and a Query API BM25 search under the same filters (agent scope, session, time range), then merges them with the existing `vector::hybrid_merge` and the configured weights. Scores stay on the SQLite backend's 0-1 scale, so `memory.min_relevance_score` keeps its meaning (raw RRF fusion scores would not).
- `importance` is stored in the payload and returned from recall/list/get.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Converting existing dense-only collections (Qdrant cannot add a sparse vector to existing points; re-creating and re-storing is an operator step).
- Client-side tokenization or a configurable BM25 model.

### Alternatives considered

- Qdrant's own RRF/DBSF fusion in a single Query API call: simpler, but RRF scores are rank-based (~0.01-0.03) and would all fall under the default `min_relevance_score`; DBSF changes the score distribution relative to SQLite.
- Client-side BM25 tokenization: works on older Qdrant, but duplicates what the server already does and adds a tokenizer to keep in sync.

### Acceptance criteria

- Default (`hybrid = false`) behaviour and requests are unchanged.
- With `hybrid = true` on a new collection, points carry a `bm25` sparse vector and recall issues both searches with identical filters.
- Merged scores match `vector::hybrid_merge` for the same inputs.
- A failed BM25 leg degrades to dense-only recall instead of failing.
- `importance` round-trips; payloads written before the change deserialize with `importance: None`.

### Architecture impact

Contained in `zeroclaw-memory` (`qdrant.rs`, factory wiring in `lib.rs`) and one additive field on `QdrantStorageConfig`.

### Risk and rollback

Opt-in and additive. An existing collection is used as found (hybrid only if it already has the `bm25` vector). Rollback = set `hybrid = false` or revert.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Review of the accompanying PR.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: web_search_tool silently compiled out without tools-external — no TOOL_COMPILED_OUT warning
issues.body:
## Summary

Since #11221, `web_search_tool` registers only under `#[cfg(feature = "tools-external")]` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`). Builds without that feature (the common `--features gateway` build) silently drop the tool: no registration, no log entry, no validation warning — the agent simply never sees `web_search_tool`.

Unlike notion/jira, which got `warn_tool_compiled_out` in their `not(tool-*)` branch of the same commit, web_search has no `not(tools-external)` counterpart.

## Impact

- A config with `[web_search] enabled = true` (+ provider API key) validates cleanly in a build that can never run the tool.
- The `[tools] optional` wildcard path stays quiet by design (`EXTERNAL_TOOL_NAMES` only warns on explicit named entries; `optional = ["*"]` selects what the build carries), so the wildcard case — the default — gives no signal either.
- Diagnosing this in the field requires binary forensics (e.g. `strings zeroclaw | grep html.duckduckgo.com` → 0 hits); nothing in logs or `config validate` hints at it.

## Expected behavior

An enabled `[web_search]` section in a build without `tools-external` should produce a `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` validation warning (and ideally the same runtime `warn_tool_compiled_out` log line other opt-in tools emit), pointing at `tools-external` / the `tools-compat` bundle.

## Suggested fix

Add `WebSearch` to `OptInTool` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/opt_in_tools.rs`): section `web_search`, feature `tools-external`. That lights up the existing `collect_compiled_out_tool_warnings` path automatically; plus a `warn_tool_compiled_out` call in the runtime registry mirroring notion/jira.

Note: other `tools-external` adapters (weather, text_browser, browser, screenshot, pushover, image_gen, email_read/email_search) share the wildcard-silence gap via `EXTERNAL_TOOL_NAMES`; this issue scopes to web_search as the highest-traffic tool, but a uniform fix may be preferable.

### Affected component

tooling/ci

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior

Every source image build from `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.debian` and `Dockerfile.alpine` stops at the dependency pre-fetch:

```
error: failed to load manifest for workspace member `/app/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`
  failed to read `/app/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/Cargo.toml`
  No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

#11174 added `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer` to `[workspace] members`. Before the pre-fetch, the three Dockerfiles copy member manifests from three places:
- `crates/*/Cargo.toml`;
- `crates/*/tests/fixtures/*/Cargo.toml`;
- explicit lines for `apps/tauri`, `apps/zerocode`, `apps/zerorelay`, `tools/fill-translations` and `xtask`.

None of these matches a member at the top-level `tests/fixtures/`, so cargo cannot load the workspace. The Dockerfile comment says every fixture member lives at `crates/*/tests/fixtures/*/`, which is no longer true.

`.dockerignore` does not exclude `tests/`, so the file is in the build context; only the `COPY` is missing.

### Expected behavior

The pre-fetch stages every workspace member's manifest, and source image builds load the workspace as they did before #11174.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On master `03b29bcc68`, build any source image, for example `docker build -f Dockerfile .`.
2. The builder stage's dependency pre-fetch (`cargo build --release --locked … -p zeroclaw -p zerocode`) fails with the error above.

CI shows the same on #11218's "Docker Image PR Check" run 41564745835. All seven "Source Image Build (no push)" jobs fail at that step: `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.debian` and `Dockerfile.alpine`, amd64 and arm64, and the two WASM-feature variants.

### Impact

- **Every PR that touches a container file** (the Dockerfiles, `.dockerignore`, the compose files, the CI context script) runs these jobs and gets them red.
  - They are in their own workflow, "Docker Image PR Check", which "CI Required Gate" does not depend on, so they don't block merging.
  - #11174 did not run them: the workflow's path filter does not include `Cargo.toml` or `tests/`.
- **"Docker Publish" builds the same Dockerfiles from source**, on a tag push and from the release workflow. Its last run (2026-10-24, `4db7afdcfa`) predates #11174. The next one, for v0.9.0, would fail the same way.

### Logs / stack traces

From job "Source Image Build (no push) (Dockerfile, linux/amd64, …)" in run 41564745835:

```
#33 0.078 error: failed to load manifest for workspace member `/app/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`
#33 0.078   failed to read `/app/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/Cargo.toml`
#33 0.078   No such file or directory (os error 2)
#33 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c if [ \"$TARGETARCH\" = \"arm64\" ]; then … cargo build --release --locked --target \"$RUST_TARGET\" -p zeroclaw -p zerocode $ZEROCLAW_CARGO_FLAGS; … fi" did not complete successfully: exit code: 101
```

master `03b29bcc68` (since #11174, `6ac37f60f1`)

1.98 (the `rust:1.98-slim` builder image)

GitHub Actions Ubuntu runners, Docker BuildKit

Yes, it worked before
