prs.title: feat(zerocode): refresh the focused session without cancellation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Add F5 to refresh the focused Code or Chat session through the existing read-only session APIs. Keep local drafts, attachments, queues and interactions instead of invoking cancel-first recovery. Retain selection and reading position when their transcript entries still match; refuse replacement when they do not.
- **Scope boundary:** No polling, cancellation, automatic retries, cross-client streaming, new RPC method, authorization change or persistence migration.
- **Blast radius:** Shared ZeroCode Chat/ACP key handling, transcript projection and cached rendering. The daemon and other clients are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Refs #10695. This implements the manual-refresh slice.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode lets you keep several agent conversations open. Another authorized client can send a message to one of those sessions, but the already-open pane can keep showing its older transcript. Closing and reopening the session reloads it, at the cost of disrupting the local view.

With this change, press F5 in Code or Chat to read the focused session again. A completed exchange returned by the daemon is added to the view without sending another prompt or cancelling a turn. Your unsent draft, attachments and queued messages stay in the pane. If the session is busy, the read fails, or selected content cannot be matched safely, the existing view stays available with a notice.

This is an explicit, point-in-time refresh. It does not stream another client's response or keep the pane synchronized in the background.

Refresh rebuilds the stored transcript. Local-only transcript rows, such as notices, can disappear.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The daemon remains the history owner. Both panes use the existing shared Chat action and history projection. Most of the remaining client work matches transcript entries and preserves reading/selection anchors; calling recovery or resetting the pane would discard state that #10695 requires retaining. The diff also includes focused preservation regressions. Append-only histories reuse the existing rendered prefix. No new runtime or transport owner is introduced.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. I ran the two-client smoke myself (below); an independent run is welcome.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, Code/ACP and Chat.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run this branch's ZeroCode against a compatible daemon. Open a harmless dedicated session and keep it focused. A second authorized RPC client must be able to resume that same session.
- **Steps to run:** Leave an unsent draft and a paused queued message in the pane. From the second client, submit a harmless prompt to the same session and wait for completion. Select unchanged text in the existing pane, then press F5. Also press F5 once while the second client still has a turn running.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The completed exchange appears after refresh; the local draft, attachment ownership, paused queue, selection and reading position remain. Refresh during a running turn reports busy without cancellation.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** F5 has no focused-session refresh action. The already-open transcript can remain stale until the session is reopened.

### How I tested

Run on head `204ca052d` (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, the CI toolchain):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
cargo test --locked -p zerocode
  zerocode (lib)       52 passed; 0 failed
  zerocode (bin)       1566 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored  (10 session_refresh tests pass)
  terminal_disconnect  3 passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh          Comment hygiene gate passed.
bash scripts/ci/zerocode_no_zeroclaw_dep_gate.sh zerocode gate passed: no zeroclaw-* implementation dependencies.
```

The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on clean `master` on these machines and is not touched by this PR.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [`CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40932393331) passed on the current head `204ca052d`: Formatting, Lint, workspace Test, ZeroCode RPC-only, MSRV and platform checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** The focused suite drives the real Chat action, RPC request sequence, asynchronous result application and production renderer with controlled daemon responses. It does not submit a turn through a second real client or exercise daemon persistence.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A live two-client run on the current head `204ca052d` (Linux, daemon and both clients from one debug build, local stub provider; [manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/MANIFEST.txt)). Client B resumed client A's session and completed a turn. F5 in A then imported that exchange and kept the unsent draft and the `notes.txt` attachment. F5 while B's slow turn was running showed the busy notice and left the transcript unchanged. That turn completed without being cancelled, and a second F5 imported it. Earlier, a two-client smoke on the experiment build [`20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) ([commit](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/af67956b5e9d1b9a9f0521dab4a1f48c999d6e71); dogfood base [`0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d), which carries this change). A second client submitted a prompt to the focused session; F5 in the open pane imported the completed exchange and kept the unsent draft and attachment. F5 while the second client's turn was running showed the busy notice, and that turn completed normally without cancellation. I did not separately exercise the paused-queue or selection/reading-position cases live; the automated tests cover them. The tests cover preserved draft attachments, paused queue and selection, busy/failed/stale reads, pending interactions, removed or inserted selected rows, ACP enrichment and sent attachments, first-plan visibility, durable ACP recovery-notice anchors, and an append to 900 transcript entries.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real captures of the current head: [before refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R03-clientA-before-F5.png), [after F5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R04-clientA-after-F5-imports-exchange-keeps-draft.png), [busy notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R06-clientA-F5-while-busy-notice.png), [second client's turn not cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R07-clientB-turn-completed-uncancelled.png), and [after a second F5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R08-clientA-F5-after-completion.png). All eight are listed in the [manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/MANIFEST.txt). The earlier experiment-build screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11457#issuecomment-6232350070).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current head `204ca052d1a975cfe0269fc43b010539b93de2c9`: the tests above, plus the live two-client Chat run over local RPC (xfce4-terminal at 120×34, ffmpeg x11grab captures of the real windows).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See Visual interface evidence. After F5, the status line reads "Session refreshed. Local draft and queued messages were kept." While the other client's turn runs, it reads "This session is busy. Nothing was cancelled. Refresh again when the turn finishes."
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The automated F5 test imports a controlled completed exchange and observes its answer after final rendering while retaining local transient state.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Broad local workspace tests and platform builds are deferred to exact-head CI. Documentation translation refresh is deferred to the normal catalog pass; new application keys fall back to embedded English.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint or destination; refresh invokes existing authorized read-only session calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Refresh does not submit transcript content to the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Uses existing `session/state` and `session/messages` responses.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? The TUI adds the remappable `chat.refresh_session` keybinding action, bound to F5 by default. No environment or CLI change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No migration or daemon restart required for this client-only change; run the updated ZeroCode binary.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit or run the previous ZeroCode binary.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Refresh runs only when its action is invoked.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** F5 fails to import a completed exchange, loses local state, changes selected text, or reports a refresh error. The refusal path keeps the previous transcript. Refresh sends only existing session-read requests; it does not submit prompts or cancellation requests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not applicable. No PR is superseded.

prs.title: feat(dashboard): show OpenRouter credit balance
prs.body:
## Summary
Base branch: `master`.

Expose the selected OpenRouter account's credit balance through the authenticated dashboard, keeping provider credentials server-side and respecting configured proxy behavior.

This revision integrates current upstream and resolves conflicts while retaining the proposed behavior. Published history is preserved.

Supersedes #11231. Related #11204; account balance remains separate from per-request spend accounting.

## Testing

prs.title: fix(memory): keep owned-session subagent and pipeline memory private
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **`spawn_subagent` hands its child the owner's memory.** `child_run_overrides` set `memory: None`, so `agent::run` built the child's memory itself with an unscoped `create_memory_for_agent`, and a subagent of an owned session read and wrote the agent's shared plane. Once the parent session is pinned, the child is now started over the session's routed handle. The child run's SOP engine is built over that same handle: since #11174, a run's SOP engine is built over the run's memory, which is the caller's handle when one is given.
  - **`execute_pipeline` runs memory steps over the owner's memory.** The pipeline runs tools it captured when it was assembled. `rebind_memory_tools` replaces the registry's memory tools when a session is pinned, but it cannot reach the pipeline's captured copies. Once the session is pinned, a memory step now runs over the routed handle, in both sequential and parallel mode.
  - **One route per registry, pinned with the session.** The tool factory creates a `SessionMemoryRoute` and gives it to `spawn_subagent`. `assemble` gives it to the pipeline it mints, and the sealed registry keeps it. `route_memory_to_principal` first checks that the route can take the owner, then runs #11174's one-time rebind of the native memory tools, then pins the route, and only then swaps the session's memory. A routing the rebind refuses leaves the route unpinned. Skill wrappers that captured either tool hold the same instances, so they follow the pin as well.
  - **A cross-agent SOP step keeps the owner.** A SOP step naming another agent re-assembles that agent's execution, and the re-assembly built the step agent's memory from config, unscoped, whether the step ran from the owned session itself or from its subagent. The re-assembly handle now carries the owner of the memory the run is on: the session's routed handle, or the child's. The step agent's memory becomes the owner's plane for that agent, the plane `memory/*` serves for that owner and agent. An owned session whose memory handle does not report its owner refuses cross-agent steps instead. On current master, per-agent SQLite memory does not forward the principal-scoped calls, so such a step's memory writes are refused before any effect. The per-agent forwarding in #11225 turns them into writes on the owner's plane. A step re-assembled through the turn's supplied capabilities (#11174) gets those capabilities' memory, put on the owner's plane for the step agent. It is refused before assembly when the run's memory owner is not the principal those capabilities resolve for, because their provider credentials belong to that principal.
  - **A registry built over an owner's plane is pinned at birth.** The route was pinned only by `route_memory_to_principal`. A registry the factory builds over memory that is already an owner's plane never went through that call, so its spawner and pipeline saw an empty route and fell back to shared memory. That covers a subagent's run, a re-assembled SOP step, and #11225's independent delegate target. The factory now pins the route when the memory it is given reports an owner. `Memory::principal_scope` is the new trait method it reads (default `None`); the principal-plane wrapper reports its scope.
  - **An owned session's SOP runs are audited on its owner's plane.**
    - The SOP tools a session is built with capture the daemon's audit logger, which writes through the shared plane.
    - That logger recorded `sop_execute`'s run, including the caller's payload, and the step outputs of the run it queues. `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` recorded step results the same way, directly or through a pipeline allowed to run `sop_execute`.
    - The three tools now share the registry's session memory route. Once the session is pinned, each call audits through a logger over the owner's routed memory, and `sop_execute` hands that logger to the run it queues.
    - The daemon's shared logger itself is never changed. The operator-facing run views read the engine, not these rows, so nothing visible moves.
  - **An owned run keeps its owner across an approval.**
    - A run that parks for approval can resume away from the session that started it. The approval can come from RPC `sops/decide`, HTTP, WebSocket or a channel on the daemon's headless driver, or from another session's `sop_approve`.
    - Neither path knew the run's owner. The daemon's shared logger then audited the finished run, private payload included, and the resumed step ran on shared memory.
    - The run now records its owner (`SopRun.memory_owner`) when `sop_execute` starts it in a pinned session. It is persisted with the run, so it survives a daemon restart; runs persisted before it restore as unowned.
    - Every driver resolves the run's audit logger from that owner through `audit_for_run`. An unowned run keeps the logger. An owned run keeps its owner's logger, gets the shared logger re-scoped to its owner, and gets no logger when the logger belongs to another owner.
    - The headless driver also gives the resumed step turn the owner's memory for the step agent. If that memory cannot be built, the step fails.
    - A live driver in another session re-assembles the step agent under the run's owner, even for its own agent, and memoizes that execution apart from its own, keyed by the owner's whole scope (principal, agent, namespace and tenant). A step that names no agent runs as the driving session's agent and is attributed to it.
  - **An owned session's SOP tools act only on its own runs** (662acf5fae from #11411 by @Aarlington, adopted here as dd6f10d57c with its authorship kept).
    - `sop_advance`, `sop_approve` and `sop_status` read the session's owner from its route and check `SopRun::is_accessible_from` before they touch a run. An owned session sees and moves only runs recorded with its exact owner. Unowned runs, including runs persisted before this PR, are not visible to it. Unowned operator sessions keep full access.
    - `sop_status` also leaves other owners' runs out of its active and finished lists, and skips the metrics summary in an owned session, because the collector aggregates every owner.
    - `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` audit through `audit_for_run` with the run's recorded owner.
    - The SOP tools registered when no audit logger is configured, and `sop_status`, now take the session route too. Before, only the audited branch did.
  - **Refused where the owner cannot be carried.** A registry that holds a `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline` or SOP tool the runtime built, but has no route (one not assembled from the factory's tool set), refuses the pin, so the owned session fails to start instead of falling back to the shared plane. Only tools the runtime built count: a tool a source supplied keeps the memory handle it was built with, whatever its name, and a registry assembled only from a source's tools pins nothing, so routing changes only the agent's own memory there. A route pins once and refuses a different handle.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The `delegate` path is #11225's and is untouched: `delegate.rs`, `rebind_memory_tools`, and the skill-alias rebinding it introduces.
  - The existing memory tools are still rebound by `rebind_memory_tools`, as before; this PR only adds the route for the tools that start memory work of their own.
  - An unowned session is unchanged: it never pins the route, and both tools keep the agent's shared memory.
  - The delegation doctrine in `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md` is drafted separately (see the issue).
- **Blast radius:**
  - `rt/tools/spawn_subagent.rs`: the child's memory override.
  - `zeroclaw-tools` `pipeline.rs`: step resolution for sequential and parallel runs, plus a new `session_memory` module.
  - `rt/tools/mod.rs` and `rt/tools/scoped.rs`: a new `AllToolsResult.session_memory` field, and the route carried on `ScopedToolRegistry` with `check_session_memory_pin` and `pin_session_memory`. `NativeMemoryBinding` forwards `principal_scope()`.
  - `rt/agent/agent.rs`: the pin check and the pin in `route_memory_to_principal`, around #11174's one-time rebind and before the session's memory is swapped.
  - `rt/agent/loop_.rs`: the run's cross-agent step handle carries its memory's owner beside the bound capabilities.
  - `rt/agent/turn/mod.rs`: `SopStepReassembly.memory_owner`; `assemble_owned_execution_with_capabilities` wraps the step agent's memory, config-backed or from the turn's capabilities, in the owner's scope for that agent, and the live driver refuses a bound step whose owner is another principal.
  - `rt/agent/agent.rs`: the session's cross-agent step handle carries its owner, or is withheld when the owner cannot be read.
  - `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-memory`: `Memory::principal_scope`, reported by `PrincipalPlaneMemory`.
  - `rt/tools/sop_execute.rs`, `sop_advance.rs`, `sop_approve.rs`, `rt/sop/audit.rs`: the SOP tools take the session route, and `session_audit` picks the owner's logger once the session is pinned.
  - `rt/sop/types.rs`, `rt/sop/engine.rs`: `SopRun.memory_owner` and `SopEngine::start_run_for`. `activate_reserved_run` takes the owner, and every headless start passes `None`.
  - `rt/sop/audit.rs`, `rt/sop/executor.rs`, `rt/agent/turn/mod.rs`: `audit_for_run`, the headless driver's logger and step memory, and the live driver's run-owner handling.
  - `rt/tools/sop_advance.rs`, `sop_approve.rs`, `sop_status.rs`, `rt/sop/types.rs`: the run-ownership check (`SopRun::is_accessible_from`) and the route on `sop_status`.
  - `rt/locales/en/cli.ftl`: `cli-sop-run-unavailable`, `cli-sop-step-owner-principal-mismatch` and `cli-sop-step-owner-memory-unavailable`.
  - `docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-composition.md`: which registries an owned session can pin.
  - `rt/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`: the extra step-owner argument.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: `PrincipalScope` derives `Serialize`/`Deserialize` so a run can persist it.
  - `zeroclaw-channels`: its daemon SOP step handle passes the turn memory's owner (channel sessions are not principal-pinned today, so this is `None` there).
  - Every `AllToolsResult` literal gains the field. Since #11174 the test helpers in `zeroclaw-channels` and `parity.rs` build through `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`, so they need no change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11239. Related #11225, #11198, #11411, tracker #8290.
- **Co-authored:** 662acf5fae (here dd6f10d57c) and the `sop_advance` test update come from @Aarlington's #11411.
- **Labels:** (set after the labelers run)

### What this does, simply

A session that belongs to one user keeps that user's memories private. Two tools could still read and write the agent's shared memory from such a session: a helper agent the session starts, and a chain of tool calls run as one pipeline. Both now use the owner's private memory. A session whose tools cannot be pointed at the owner's memory refuses to start, rather than quietly using the shared one.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The regressions drive the real tool factory and `assemble` into an owned session and observe where rows land.

### How I tested

**Review fixes at ac9069f67e.** Three commits on 64d43dbaaa, one per review comment:
- 592046152d: when an unowned session approves an owned run whose step names no agent, the step agent is re-assembled as the session's own agent. The step's prompt and attribution assumed the step named that agent, and the prompt builder panicked. Both now use the alias the step was re-assembled as. Test: `another_sessions_driver_runs_an_owned_runs_unnamed_step_as_its_own_agent`.
- 4f43785fbe: the live driver memoizes the execution of a foreign-owned step by the owner's whole scope instead of the principal id alone, so runs of one principal in different namespaces or tenants never share an execution. The runtime's own sessions are scoped only by principal and agent, so this takes an embedder that routes with a namespace or tenant. Test: `owned_runs_in_different_scopes_never_share_a_step_execution`. `another_sessions_driver_runs_an_owned_run_under_its_owner` now finds the owner's execution without assuming the key's format.
- ac9069f67e: the bound-step refusal and the headless owner-memory failure come from Fluent keys through the runtime i18n helpers. `a_bound_cross_agent_step_refuses_a_foreign_memory_owner` checks the recorded output against the catalogue, and `an_unavailable_owner_memory_fails_the_step_in_the_catalogues_words` covers the headless failure.
- Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, at ac9069f67e:

  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` | 6024 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` | 1386 passed |

  | this PR's 32 runtime regressions, three runs | 32 passed each run |
  | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, CI's clippy lint command, comment hygiene, docs quality | clean |

  The test binaries ran with `TMPDIR` on a short path outside `/tmp`, because of the stray `/tmp/.git` described below.
- **Failing first.** With all three fixes switched back, which is 64d43dbaaa's behaviour, the three new tests and the extended refusal test fail: the unnamed step panics with `needs_reassembly implies a step agent alias`, the two scopes share one execution, and both failures read in their old English strings. Switching back one fix at a time, each fails only its own test: the alias for the prompt alone (the panic) and for the step's attribution alone (no agent recorded), the scope key, the refusal's catalogue string and the owner-memory failure's.
- The 13 revert checks below still fail their own tests at ac9069f67e, and all 16 pass with every fix in place.

**Refresh on master after #11174, at 64d43dbaaa.**

Every constructor carries it, the supplied-only one included. `SessionMemoryRoute::check_pin` answers without pinning (`a_route_check_matches_pin_without_pinning`).

A re-assembled step agent's memory comes from the capabilities and is then put on the owner's plane; the headless driver keeps its config-backed form. The live driver passes the run's audit logger and owner into both arms (new test `a_bound_cross_agent_step_of_an_owned_session_keeps_its_owner`).
  - `run_with_capabilities` builds the run's SOP engine over the run's memory, which is the caller's handle when one is given. This PR's `sop_memory` helper and its test `sop_engine_memory_follows_the_callers_memory` are gone.
  - `NativeMemoryBinding`, new in #11174, forwards `principal_scope()` as the `Memory` forwarding rule asks (`native_memory_binding_forwards_the_principal_scope`).

- Otherwise the diff is unchanged: 21 of the 29 files this PR touched carry identical changes against the new base, and the merge adds one argument in `supplied_only_traps.rs`. The resolutions are the ones I prepared against #11174's branch before it landed; replayed onto master, only `cli.ftl` needed a hand edit.
- Three commits on top cover what #11174's supplied capabilities make reachable:
  - 469c607826 judges the pin by where a tool came from, not by its name. A registry assembled only from a tool source's tools pins nothing. In a native registry, only tools the runtime built count. Test: `source_tools_named_like_memory_starters_do_not_refuse_the_pin`.
  - 70056b39a8 says which registries an owned session can pin, in `runtime-composition.md` and in the pin check's docs. A custom native recipe that builds these tools by hand without the route is still refused.
  - 64d43dbaaa refuses a cross-agent step re-assembled through bound capabilities when the run's memory owner is a different principal from the one those capabilities resolve for, or they resolve for none. The refusal comes before anything is assembled. Test: `a_bound_cross_agent_step_refuses_a_foreign_memory_owner`. Without the guard, an operator principal's step completes over the owner's memory.
- Each place #11174's capability-taking constructors build a subagent child, a pipeline or a SOP step either carries the session's route or the run's owner, or holds no tool the runtime built:
  - a session built from supplied capabilities;
  - `spawn_subagent`'s bound child and the child's own registry and SOP engine;
  - a run's step handle;
  - the live driver's bound arm.

**New tests:**
- `rt::agent::agent`. Each test assembles a session from the real `all_tools` and `assemble`, pinned to `user:alice`, over a shared SQLite memory:

- `rt::agent::loop_::sop_engine_memory_follows_the_callers_memory` (removed in the #11174 refresh, which builds the run's SOP engine over the caller's handle itself).
- `zeroclaw-tools`:
  - `pipeline::memory_steps_of_a_pinned_session_land_on_the_owners_plane` covers sequential and parallel runs.
  - `pipeline::memory_steps_of_an_unpinned_session_keep_the_shared_plane` is the control.
  - `session_memory::a_route_pins_once_and_refuses_another_plane` and `session_memory::only_memory_tools_are_rebuilt_over_a_handle`.

**Proof on master.** The three regressions that use only master's API (the tool factory, `assemble`, and `route_memory_to_principal`) were run on plain `upstream/master` e16fd898ba, without the fix, and then on this branch. The master run adds only the tests and the same `#[cfg(test)]` task-local that records the memory override `spawn_subagent` gives its child. - **#11225 overlap.** Both PRs change `route_memory_to_principal` in `agent/agent.rs`, so this PR lands after #11225 and I'll re-merge it then. milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(channels): allow inbound-only email channels without SMTP
prs.body:
Email config required `smtp_host` and `from_address`, so an IMAP-only mailbox could not be expressed: the section failed to parse and the read-only email tools never registered. Both fields are now optional, so an operator can grant mailbox access without granting outbound email.

- `EmailConfig::smtp_host` and `from_address` become `Option<String>`; blank values are treated as unset so legacy `field = ""` configs stay inbound-only instead of pointing SMTP at an empty host.
- `EmailChannel::send` refuses with `channels.email.<alias>: outbound email is disabled ...` while IMAP reading and flag updates keep running; `listen` logs one inbound-only warning at startup.
- `supports_outbound_send` mirrors the SMTP configuration, so surfaces that must genuinely deliver (SOP approval routes, no-reply notices, escalations, text polls) reject or skip an inbound-only channel up front instead of failing at send time.
- `Config::collect_warnings` raises `email_smtp_partially_configured` when only one half of the pair is set, instead of silently disabling sending.
- Tests cover enabled/disabled/blank configuration, the send refusal and its alias, the From-identity requirement, the half-configured warning, and a resilient config load of an alias without SMTP.
- Document inbound-only mode in the email channel guide.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `smtp_host` and `from_address` are now optional, so an IMAP-only mailbox can be configured at all. Before this, the section failed to parse unless both were present — even though the read-only `email_search`/`email_read` tools never use SMTP. Sending is now explicitly refused instead of being impossible to express, and a half-configured outbound pair is reported instead of silently disabling sending.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the main agent reply path (a bound inbound-only channel still attempts `send_final` and receives the refusal). Does not change the email tools' read-only behaviour (`BODY.PEEK`, no STORE) or add outbound email tooling. Does not change `doctor`/listener health; that is a separate follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** The email channel and its config schema (two fields become optional); delivery-dependent surfaces that consult `Channel::supports_outbound_send()` (SOP approval routes, no-reply notices, escalation alerts, text polls) now skip or refuse an inbound-only email alias; the email tools now register for configurations that previously failed to load.
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A
 
### What this does, simply

Email had no way to say "read my mail, but never send as me": both the SMTP relay and the From address were required, whether or not you wanted outbound mail. An operator who wanted the agent to search and read a mailbox had to configure a working SMTP identity they never intended to use — and a configuration with only IMAP settings was rejected as malformed, which also removed the email tools entirely.

This PR makes outbound SMTP optional. With both fields unset the channel loads, keeps reading mail and updating flags, registers the read-only tools, and refuses every send with an error that names the alias. A channel that cannot deliver also reports that through `supports_outbound_send()`, so features that must actually reach a human (approval routes, notices, escalations) skip it deliberately rather than discovering the failure at delivery time. Setting only one of the two fields still keeps sending disabled, and now raises a config warning that names the missing field, so an operator who *meant* to send finds out before wondering why replies never leave.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (config loading/warnings) and `channel` (email)
- **Setup / preconditions:** an enabled `[channels.email.<alias>]` block with `imap_host`, `username`, `password` and no `smtp_host`/`from_address`; bind it to an agent to exercise the channel, or leave it unbound to exercise the tools.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw config list --filter channels.email`
  2. Start the daemon with the alias bound; ask the agent to reply to an inbound mail (or drive `Channel::send` directly).
  3. Add only `smtp_host = "smtp.example.com"` and re-run `zeroclaw config validate` / look for `email_smtp_partially_configured`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** step 1 lists the full section with `smtp_host = <unset>` and `from_address = <unset>`; step 2 logs `Email channel is inbound-only: smtp_host/from_address are not configured...` once and the send fails with `channels.email.<alias>: outbound email is disabled because smtp_host and from_address are not both configured`; step 3 reports one warning pointing at `channels.email.<alias>.from_address`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** step 1 reports `config section channels.email.<alias> ... is malformed and was reset to defaults`, no email tools are registered, and the channel cannot be started at all.

### How I tested

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib email` — 93 passed (includes enabled/disabled/blank configuration, send refusal with alias, `build_email_message` requiring the From identity, `supports_outbound_send`, and the inbound-only startup path).
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib email` — 3 passed (new `email_smtp_partially_configured` warning test; resilient migration load of an alias without SMTP).
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration` — 99 passed.
- Manual smoke on an arm64 container: an IMAP-only alias loads after previously being rejected as malformed, the read-only tools work, and sending is refused with the alias-scoped message.
- **Known CI coverage gap / caveat:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on my local Rust 1.99.1 flags pre-existing `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` lints in `zeroclaw-providers` and `orchestrator/mod.rs`, untouched by this diff; the repository's pinned 1.98 toolchain in CI should not flag them. The two changed crates pass clippy with only those pre-existing lints allowed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No` — `smtp_password` stays `#[secret]`; only the two plaintext endpoint/identity fields change shape)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` for existing TOML configuration; Rust callers constructing `EmailConfig` must use `Some(...)` for the now-optional `smtp_host` and `from_address` fields.)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- Upgrade steps for existing users: none required. Existing configs keep working unchanged. To opt into inbound-only, omit or blank both `smtp_host` and `from_address`. Legacy `smtp_host = ""`/`from_address = ""` values are treated as unset, so they remain inbound-only rather than relaying to an empty host. New warning code: `email_smtp_partially_configured`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None` — setting `smtp_host` and `from_address` restores the previous outbound behaviour without a code change.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** startup warning `Email channel is inbound-only: ...`; send errors beginning `channels.email.<alias>: outbound email is disabled`; `config validate`/`doctor` warning `email_smtp_partially_configured`.

---

prs.title: fix(container): stage top-level fixture members during prefetch
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11174 added `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer` to `[workspace] members`. Before the dependency pre-fetch, `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.debian` and `Dockerfile.alpine` copy member manifests only from:
    - `crates/*/Cargo.toml`;
    - `crates/*/tests/fixtures/*/Cargo.toml`;
    - a few explicit app and tool paths.

    Cargo could not load the workspace, and every source image build stopped at the pre-fetch.
  - Each of the three now also copies `tests/fixtures/*/Cargo.toml` and stubs an empty `src/lib.rs` for each such member, as it already does for the crate fixtures. Cargo needs only a target to load the member; the pre-fetch builds `zeroclaw` and `zerocode` only.
  - The comment that said every fixture member lives under `crates/` now names both places.
  - The architecture test that guards nested members looked only under `crates/`, which is how this got through. It now covers `tests/fixtures/` members too.
  - A new architecture test checks that each of the three Dockerfiles stages the manifest of every `[workspace] members` entry before its pre-fetch, wherever the member lives. A small companion test pins how it reads `COPY` lines: globs, `--parents`, destinations, `--from`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No change to the build itself, the image contents, features or the release workflows.
  - `.dockerignore` already leaves `tests/` in the build context, so it is unchanged.
  - Containerfile, `demo/Dockerfile` and `apps/zerorelay/Dockerfile` copy the whole context and were not affected.
  - The "Docker Image PR Check" path filter, which doesn't run these builds when only `Cargo.toml` changes, is left as is.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The three source Dockerfiles' builder stages, and `tests/architecture/container_release.rs`.
  - "Docker Publish" builds these Dockerfiles from source on a tag push and from the release workflow, so this unblocks the next image publish.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12210. Related #11174, #9966 (the `crates/*/tests/fixtures/*` glob this extends), #11218 (whose Docker checks show the failure).

### What this does, simply

Our container images build the project in two steps. First they download and build all dependencies, using only each package's `Cargo.toml`, so that step can be cached. Then they build our own code.

For the first step to work, Docker has to copy in the `Cargo.toml` of every package in the workspace. A new test package was recently added in a place the Dockerfiles didn't look (`tests/fixtures/`), so every image build failed with "failed to load manifest".

This PR copies that package's `Cargo.toml` too, in all three Dockerfiles, and gives it the empty placeholder source the other test packages get. A test now fails if any workspace package is ever left out again, wherever it is added.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. CI's "Docker Image PR Check" runs the seven source image builds on this PR, because it changes the Dockerfiles.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** none at runtime; container builds only.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Docker with BuildKit (the Dockerfiles use `COPY --parents` under `dockerfile:1.7-labs`).
- **Steps to run:** `docker build -f Dockerfile .` (or `Dockerfile.debian`, `Dockerfile.alpine`).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the builder stage gets past the dependency pre-fetch.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the pre-fetch fails with `failed to load manifest for workspace member /app/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - "Docker Image PR Check" runs the full source-image matrix on this PR, because it changes the Dockerfiles: `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.debian` and `Dockerfile.alpine`, amd64 and arm64, and the two WASM-feature variants. That is the real BuildKit build.
  - The architecture tests run in the required test job.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - A change that only adds a workspace member doesn't trigger "Docker Image PR Check", which is how #11174 got through.
  - The new architecture test closes that gap for manifest staging, because it runs in the required test job on every PR.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Rust 1.98.0, at `0f249f87b5`:

  ```
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                  # exit 0
  $ git diff --check 03b29bcc68 0f249f87b5                                      # exit 0
  $ cargo nextest run --locked --test architecture -E 'test(/container_release::/)'
       Summary [   0.009s] 16 tests run: 16 passed, 67 skipped
  $ cargo nextest run --locked --test architecture
       Summary [  12.211s] 83 tests run: 83 passed, 0 skipped
  $ cargo clippy --locked --test architecture -- -D warnings                    # exit 0
  ```

  The two guard tests fail without the fix. With master's three Dockerfiles restored under the new tests:

  ```
       Summary [   0.010s] 16 tests run: 14 passed, 2 failed, 67 skipped
  Dockerfile must stage every workspace member manifest before its dependency pre-fetch; missing: ["tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/Cargo.toml"]
  Dockerfile must stage nested workspace manifest tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/Cargo.toml before prefetch
  ```

  Each also catches a partial fix:
  - Dropping only `Dockerfile.alpine`'s new stub loop fails with `Dockerfile.alpine must stub nested workspace target tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/src/lib.rs before prefetch`.
  - Dropping only `Dockerfile.debian`'s new `COPY` fails both tests, naming `Dockerfile.debian`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I replayed each Dockerfile's builder stage up to its dependency pre-fetch, on master and on this branch:
  - **Context:** `git archive` with `.dockerignore` applied. `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer/Cargo.toml` is in the context on both.
  - **Staging:** every `COPY` from the context, then the stub `RUN`, as written.
  - **Checks:** `cargo metadata --locked --no-deps`, `cargo fetch --locked` and `cargo metadata --locked` in the staged tree.

  | | Dockerfile | Dockerfile.debian | Dockerfile.alpine |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | master `03b29bcc68` | exit 101 on all three: `failed to load manifest for workspace member …/tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer` | same | same |
  | this branch | exit 0 on all three; the member is staged as `Cargo.toml` + `src/lib.rs` | same | same |

  I did not run a full image build locally. The available podman (4.9.3) rejects `COPY --parents`, which all three Dockerfiles already use, so this PR's "Docker Image PR Check" run is the real build evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no interface change)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `0f249f87b5`; container build inputs and the `architecture` test target.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A local full image build (see above), and the workspace-wide clippy and test runs, because only the Dockerfiles and one architecture test file change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`. Reverting brings back the pre-fetch failure in every source image build.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add durable task lifecycle foundation for Goal Mode [Goal V1 proposal 1/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> **V1 foundation proposal 1/12.** This supplies task/storage contracts, not a complete Goal feature or a request to merge. Current-head required GitHub CI passed. The local full-workspace Cargo test remains failed: its five failures were also reproduced on the exact upstream comparison revision. Neither result erases the other or the historical full-stack limitations below.

Selected slice **01**, head `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`, compared with pinned upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582`. This update merges that official upstream revision without rewriting published history. The 15-path Goal foundation delta is unchanged in substance; upstream conversation-binding, session-store safety, OIDC/plugin and CI changes remain upstream-owned. The first PR has no predecessor. Do not enable an incomplete Goal implementation.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Move the canonical task types into `zeroclaw-api`, preserving runtime re-exports and enum variants; add serde-defaulted session/epoch fields.
  - Replace unguarded Goal creation/pause/resume APIs with exact task/session/epoch-guarded transitions, pending-operation settlement and accounting-state contracts; generic task APIs reject Goal creation and session-Goal mutations.
  - Converge existing task databases transactionally to schema 13, including session uniqueness/fencing triggers and failure classification of invalid legacy Goal rows.
  - Reconcile dead-owner Goals before generic startup recovery; retain terminal session-Goal history during agent deletion and refuse the control-plane cleanup step while a live session Goal exists. That refusal is reported as a cascade warning, not a rollback of the already-published agent deletion.
  - Add file-backed control-plane and task-type compatibility tests; propagate SQLite iteration errors rather than silently returning partial task/settlement lists.
- **Scope boundary:** First incremental slice of an unmerged proposal stack. No complete Goal workflow, user entrypoint, later configuration/commands, policy/execution crate, or enabled-rollout claim. The upstream merge preserves this foundation delta; this is not a correctness audit of all incoming upstream changes.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal registry interfaces, SQLite schema/recovery, generic mutation/error paths, agent deletion and ordinary delegate/peer/subagent producers. Public record/trait compatibility changes and one-way migration limits are detailed below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 and tracker #10341, not closing either.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

The previous Goal registry did not bind its create/pause/resume operations to a durable session and execution epoch. This slice supplies those fences and the shared task/storage foundation so stale work cannot use ordinary task APIs to change a session Goal. It does not yet expose a complete Goal feature.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — no user-reachable Goal entrypoint or task-store CLI has a meaningful manual A/B path in this foundation slice. File-backed integration tests exercise storage/recovery; no manual or live-session execution is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 39905108375](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375), attempt 1, passed on head `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`. GitHub tested merge `9cf58a86c59c0fe3a7faf2e17d74ed7ff65166fb` against upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582`; its tree `115fc31a9583896b3236697005dd7ef750977d18` equals the locally validated tree. Test, all repeated parallel runtime/channel runs, required Windows selection/recovery/service/build checks, lint, selected feature/platform lanes, Security and CI Required Gate passed. Earlier-head results remain historical, including the cancelled Windows selection and failed aggregate at `1b64f2d0`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The terminal snapshot contains 46 successful checks and 10 skips, not 56 passes. Skips follow the unchanged path/event/opt-in conditions: targeted Windows Clippy, docs, Nix hash/evaluation, crates.io preflight, relay smoke, PR benchmarks, master-push debounce and the two advisory Windows jobs (no `ci:windows` opt-in). The required Windows jobs did execute and pass. The local full workspace run remains FAIL, as detailed below. No complete Goal controller, verifier, surface adapter or enabled-rollout behavior exists in this slice. Core/CODEOWNERS review and the scoped runtime exception remain outstanding.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local macOS validation on `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1:

| Command / check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | PASS |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` | FAIL, exit 101; stopped on the #11959 fixture |
| Same full workspace command with `--no-fail-fast` | FAIL, exit 101; five failed tests across two targets; reached final doc-tests |
| `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | PASS; all three runtime and all three channel repetitions, 16 threads |
| `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` | PASS; formatting, correctness Clippy and provider-dispatch scan |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `./scripts/ci/firmware_protocol_gate.sh` | PASS; formatting, strict Clippy and 28 tests |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` | PASS; 58 cases |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` | PASS |
| `cargo deny check` (0.20.2) | PASS with unchanged-policy warnings |
| `cargo audit` (0.22.2) | PASS with six allowed unmaintained-package warnings |

Relevant literal output:

```text
error: 2 targets failed:
    `-p zeroclaw-config --lib`
    `-p zeroclaw-providers --lib`

test result: ok. 5813 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 49.31s
test result: ok. 2015 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 14.50s
test result: ok. 28 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
58 passed, 0 failed
Comment hygiene gate passed.
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
warning: 6 allowed warnings found
```

The runtime/channel lines are excerpts from the first runtime and final channel repetition. All three runtime runs had 5,813 passed/zero failed/nine ignored; all three channel runs had 2,015 passed/zero failed/two ignored. The full candidate workspace run separately observed all 69 named regression cases passing, including all 26 file-backed Goal contract tests, canonical task-type/reaper/peer cases and the upstream conversation-binding/session-store/daemon intersection controls. These passes do not change its aggregate FAIL result.

**Full exact-upstream comparison:** One unfiltered `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast` run at upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582` used the same toolchain and sealed environment as the candidate. Both runs reached final doc-tests and failed these same five cases with matching error details (only panic thread IDs and random temporary-directory components normalized):

1. `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception` — OS error 17/AlreadyExists in the case-variant fixture (#11959). macOS filesystems may be case-sensitive or case-insensitive.
2. `grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant` — timeout waiting for the fake child’s PID file.
3. `openai::tests::responses_model_listing_carries_header_only_profile_and_surfaces_auth_failure` — response decoding, missing `data`.
4. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` — response decoding, missing `choices`.
5. `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` — four proxy hits versus two expected.

No candidate-only or upstream-only failure was observed in this comparison. The three affected source files are byte-identical between upstream and this candidate. That proves reproduction, not the precise provider-test interleaving or timeout cause. These are automated local fixtures, not failures of live provider accounts. The original fail-fast run and both comparison runs remain FAIL; no test, assertion, deadline or gate was weakened.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11959

Earlier results at `1b64f2d0` remain historical and are not relabeled. In particular, the earlier seven unmatched signatures were not observed in the current unfiltered candidate run; their absence here is not proof of their exact cause or a claim that this integration repaired them.

**Warnings retained:** Candidate and upstream comparison logs include the Apple linker `__eh_frame` size/performance warning. Deny reports six unmatched skips and two unused-wrapper exceptions; audit allows six unmaintained-package warnings (anymap2, nostr-relay-pool, proc-macro-error, zbus_names, zvariant and zvariant_derive). The lockfile, manifests, `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` equal the selected upstream revision. No advisory ignore or security-policy change is introduced.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Exact parent/tree identity, clean worktree, both-direction preservation of upstream and Goal-owned changes, and the complete public API/storage/recovery/caller diff. No manual runtime or live-room test, migration failpoint, or executed downgrade is claimed. Three direct guard cases remain untested: deletion with a pending operation, settlement with a mismatched operation ID/epoch, and limit updates on a terminal Goal. Their SQL predicates were inspected.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — this foundation slice changes no supported user-visible interface state.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`; local automated API/runtime/file-backed control-plane boundaries. Relevant literal output is above. No private local path is presented as a hosted attachment.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for presentation; command excerpts above are test evidence, not screenshots or final-interface proof.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Exact-task/session/epoch guards, schema convergence/reopen, valid-row preservation, generic-mutation rejection, boot reconciliation and ordinary producer compatibility exercised by the named tests.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Documentation gates are not applicable because the PR has no docs delta against the selected upstream revision. Container-only `dev/ci.sh all` and strict `ci-all`/feature lanes were not locally run. The selected current-head remote feature/platform lanes passed; that is not a claim that every possible feature combination was tested. No enabled-rollout footprint or end-to-end Goal surface claim is made.

### Current remote CI — separate from the local Cargo failures

The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375/job/120255167226) ran the workspace nextest suite: 19,360 passed and 42 skipped. Its separate hardware suite passed 189 with one skip; informational golden replay passed seven with five skips. The [parallel job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375/job/120255292193) completed all three runtime runs (5,809 passed, zero failed, nine ignored each) and all three channel runs (2,015 passed, zero failed, two ignored each). Both job logs confirm checkout `9cf58a86`.

Literal excerpts, with ANSI colour and runner timestamp prefixes removed:

```text
Summary [  97.345s] 19360 tests run: 19360 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 42 skipped
test result: ok. 5809 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 36.11s
test result: ok. 2015 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 11.07s
```

The one slow daemon-feedback test, two leaky child-process tests (MCP inherited stdout and ZeroCode inherited stderr), and the cache action's Node20-deprecation warning remain recorded. These Linux nextest/CI observations do not turn the failed local macOS Cargo run into a pass or establish the provider-fixture failure mechanisms. The earlier report-only risk workflow was cancelled under its per-PR `cancel-in-progress` policy and replaced by a successful current-head risk report; it is not a product-test failure or an unreported rerun. No validation gate was weakened.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this diff adds task lifecycle/persistence behavior without granting a new permission or filesystem scope.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No known real identity or secret is introduced; fixtures use test data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No — this slice does not add a model-visible prompt path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust consumers of the changed record literals or `GoalTaskRegistry` trait. Existing task enum variants and runtime import paths remain compatible, and legacy serialized records load with defaults. The persistent migration is forward-only; it does not preserve invalid legacy Goals as resumable work.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No in this slice.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No declared floor change in this slice.
- Exact upgrade steps:
  1. Update direct `TaskRecord` literals with `session_id`/`execution_epoch` (ordinary tasks use `None`/`0`). Update `GoalTaskRecord` literals with `pending_call_id`, `pending_call_epoch` and `accounting_state`, or use `..GoalTaskRecord::default()` where appropriate. No enum-match migration is needed. The new public `GoalAccountingState` and `GoalTransitionResult` distinguish accounting completeness from guarded transition outcomes.
  2. Migrate `GoalTaskRegistry` implementers/callers: `create_goal` becomes `create_or_replace_session_goal`; `pause_goal_task`/`resume_goal_task` become `pause_session_goal`/`resume_session_goal` with exact session/epoch arguments. `update_goal_objective` is removed without an in-place equivalent: objectives are supplied at creation, and replacement requires a fully settled terminal predecessor. The removed create/resume methods accepted a `continuation_context`; set it separately through the existing `set_continuation_context` method when migrating those callers. Implement the new current-session/terminal-reason queries, guarded finish/limit/disposal methods and pending-operation admit/settle methods. Handle `Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing` by reloading canonical state when required; do not bypass guards through the generic registry.
  3. Generic `TaskRegistry::create` now rejects every Goal. Generic heartbeat, progress, status/terminal, settlement, claim and timeout mutations reject session-bound Goals. Existing ordinary task producers still use that registry. Generic `reconcile_lost` returns `Ok(false)` for any Goal and the periodic sweep skips Goal rows, leaving their recovery to Goal-specific reconciliation. Task and settlement enumeration now propagates SQLite step errors instead of returning partial results; callers must handle those errors.
  4. Before first opening an existing control-plane database, preserve a consistent backup and validate against a disposable copy. The transaction converges released v8/v9/v10 and provisional schemas to v13, adds fields/triggers and replaces `idx_tasks_active_goal_context` with session-based uniqueness. Running/paused legacy Goals missing a session/objective or carrying an invalid epoch are marked failed (`legacy_goal_missing_session`, `legacy_goal_missing_objective`, `goal_invalid_execution_epoch`); this is not automatically undone by reverting the binary. No down-migration is supplied.
  5. Startup now reconciles Goal state before ordinary recovery: dead-owner running Goals without uncertain work pause; pending operations or incomplete accounting cause terminal classification under V1. Agent deletion retains terminal session-Goal rows; a running/paused session Goal refuses the whole control-plane deletion step and is reported as a cascade warning. prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **Integrated upstream:** Official `master` v0.8.7 (`5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9`) was incorporated by ordinary merge `d8f7fd7eea1b46e76e8f51ee7653fcdc596e7f11`. These nine imports are upstream work, not Goal implementation: plugin runtime-config refusal reporting ([#11811](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11811)); ctutils security updates ([#11998](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11998)); ctutils/tokio security updates ([#12010](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12010)); container CA-store updates after emSign distrust ([#11925](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11925)); SOP stale-copy protection ([#11861](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11861)); gateway stop admission/drain ([#11901](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11901)); saved provider-alias probing ([#10034](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10034)); owner-only lifecycle lock ([#11803](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11803)); and release 0.8.7 ([#12011](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12011)). This is not a release-only import or a claim to include later upstream changes. The sole manual integration resolution aligns the new `zeroclaw-goal` workspace dependency and lock record with version 0.8.7; it adds no separate dependency upgrade. The subsequent config-save repair is a separate commit.
- **What changed and why:** This remains Goal V1 proposal slice 3/12; the full `master`-to-candidate diff remains 36 paths, including the earlier stack work. The latest follow-up is limited to two files across `fa7136de529eb55076e04c162c43b1bb4b6ddc1b` → `afadb4058eb1c7395e63046c8bfa19b2e04f3e69`: canonical session-key checks at trusted ingress and a current-task fence for status projections.
  - Extract transport-neutral Goal task, ingress, host, controller, and response contracts into `zeroclaw-goal`, while keeping durable task and SQLite ownership in the existing API/runtime layers.
  - Enforce current-config validation before admission effects. Without explicit command limits, configured defaults are accepted when at least one dimension is positive, or when both token and cost defaults are explicitly zero (the explicit-unlimited choice). Absent defaults or a single zero paired with an unset dimension produce typed `GoalResponse::BudgetRequired` without creating a task; invalid config retains precedence.
  - Inherit the canonical task-type move to `zeroclaw-api`, compatibility re-exports, durable session/epoch fields, and schema-13 storage from the earlier stack slices; extend the Goal storage guards and contract/persistence tests in this slice.
  - Repair optional-number Web saves while preserving unset versus explicit zero, and reject gateway config writes that introduce invalid Goal settings without preventing unrelated saves with a pre-existing Goal error.
  - Isolate plain-HTTP loopback webhook-audit regression fixtures from the unused native TLS trust store, so those tests can validate audit delivery without platform trust-store initialization. This is test-only; production TLS, deadlines, and assertions are unchanged.
  At trusted ingress, directly constructed Matrix and ZeroCode session-key variants now receive the same canonical checks as constructor-created keys: malformed values are rejected while canonical keys keep their exact existing durable IDs. After loading a Goal extension for status, the controller rereads the current task and compares its ID, status and execution epoch before projecting; a missing or changed task follows the existing typed `Stale` path, while a missing extension remains an error if the original task is still current. This bounded fence does not promise an atomic snapshot. Regression tests cover invalid and valid keys, stable projections and task changes; the final test-fixture lifetime annotation does not change runtime behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** Proposal and policy-contract slice only. No production Goal driver/model executor, Matrix or ZeroCode adapter wiring, provider/model accounting loop, Goal renderer, or full rollout is added. The present-but-unwired master channel-only `/goal` command-catalogue entry was removed rather than advertised without a handler; no Fluent key depended on it. The complete channel crate is unchanged against the integrated `master`. The `webhook_audit.rs` change is limited to the plain-HTTP loopback test fixtures described above. The two follow-up commits add no public enum/trait/signature change, storage schema, scheduler/lock, retry loop, or production transport behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal contracts and imports; Goal config/admission and durable task lifecycle; optional-number Web configuration serialization; gateway/dashboard config-write validation, including writes to the enabled verifier's provider profile; and test fixture setup. Production Goal transport behavior and model execution remain with later slices. The upstream import also carries gateway, runtime, tools and workflow changes: integration/recovery and CI behavior are risk-bearing seams, checked on the integrated tree rather than assumed safe from a conflict-free merge. The follow-up affects trusted session-key admission and status-response consistency only; canonical session IDs and stable status projections retain their existing behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8303; Related #10341; Depends on #11879.
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  - https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11879

### What this does, simply

This proposal establishes typed rules and storage contracts for a future Goal feature. It gives the runtime a common representation for task ownership, session identity, budgets, and guarded lifecycle transitions, without claiming that a user can run a Goal through a production transport today.

Budget admission distinguishes absent values from explicit zero. For a start without command budget flags, at least one positive configured default is a budget; two explicitly configured zeros select unlimited operation. One zero plus one unset value, or both unset, is unconfigured and returns the typed `GoalResponse::BudgetRequired` response before task creation. That response is a non-admission outcome, not a config-validation error. Invalid current Goal configuration is validated first and keeps its error precedence. Explicit command budgets remain independent of absent defaults.

Dashboard/gateway PATCH, per-field PUT/DELETE and section initialization now reject a save that leaves the edited Goal inputs invalid, before disk or live-config publication. Enabling Goal without a valid verifier is rejected; selecting a valid verifier and enabling Goal in the same save works. An unrelated save can still preserve an existing Goal error with a warning. Edits to Goal settings or, while enabled, to the verifier's provider profile must leave Goal valid; those profile edits are not unrelated saves. Disabling Goal clears the enabled-verifier requirement, not other numeric/model validation. An existing Goal error no longer hides an invalid unrelated edit; an edit touching Goal inputs may still report the Goal error first. This repair changes save behavior and whole-config first-error ordering, not the wire schema or error codes; it adds `Config::goal_validation_input_paths` for shared validation-input ownership.

The follow-up also closes two edge cases: trusted ingress rejects malformed session keys even when a caller constructs the public key variant directly, while preserving canonical IDs; and status lookup rechecks the task after reading its Goal details, returning the existing stale response if its ID, status or execution epoch changed. It does not make the two reads atomic or enable a production Goal transport.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the config-save, host and persistence boundaries have automated regression coverage. This slice does not wire a production Goal transport; a live Matrix/ZeroCode trial would not test an implemented feature.

### How I tested

It stopped before the later suites. Their results below come from separate, full, unfiltered `--no-fail-fast` runs, not from that stopped run.

The last column records one full comparison run of upstream `master` v0.8.7 (`5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9`). - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes — typed capability contracts, not new grants.** Principal/session binding and current-config checks apply here; durable storage transitions use epoch guards. - Backward compatible? **No for Rust consumers of the changed public interfaces**, including removed-method callers, custom trait implementers, struct literals and exhaustive matches. Relative to integrated `master`, `TaskKind::Goal` already existed in the runtime registry; `TaskKind`, `TaskStatus`, and `TaskRecord` move to canonical `zeroclaw-api` definitions and remain re-exported at the existing runtime paths. `TaskRecord` adds `session_id: Option<String>` and `execution_epoch: i64` (Serde defaults `None` and `0`), so Rust struct literals must supply them; ordinary task records use those default values, while Goal creation goes through the guarded registry.
  The existing public `GoalTaskRegistry` and `GoalTaskRecord` move to `zeroclaw-goal::task`, retaining runtime re-exports but not full source compatibility. Removed trait methods are `create_goal`, `update_goal_objective`, `pause_goal_task` and `resume_goal_task`. Implementers must provide ten new required methods: `current_goal_for_session`, `terminal_reason_for_session_goal`, `create_or_replace_session_goal`, `pause_session_goal`, `resume_session_goal`, `finish_session_goal`, `admit_pending_operation`, `settle_pending_operation`, `update_session_goal_limits` and `delete_session_goal`. Session mutations require exact task/session/epoch predicates; handle `GoalTransitionResult::Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing` explicitly and reload authoritative state before deciding what to do after stale/missing outcomes. Objectives are immutable rather than updated in place.
  `GoalTaskRecord` adds public `pending_call_id: Option<String>`, `pending_call_epoch: Option<i64>` and `accounting_state: GoalAccountingState` fields; update literals or use its default. Generic `TaskRegistry::create` rejects `TaskKind::Goal`, and generic mutators reject session-bound Goals: migrate those callers to the controller or guarded session-Goal registry APIs instead of bypassing lifecycle guards.

Construct fresh settings from the current canonical config per operation. These host-settings/response APIs, unlike the existing Goal store interfaces above, are new relative to integrated `master`. The `zeroclaw-goal` crate now reports version 0.8.7 with the workspace; upstream's own compatibility changes follow upstream release notes.
  Compared with integrated `master`, `Config` gains a public `goal` field: Rust struct-literal consumers must provide it or use `Config::default()` and modify needed fields. The unused public command variants `BuiltinCommandId::Goal` and `CommandExecution::GoalAdmission` are removed; Rust callers must remove those matches or use the transport-neutral parser/controller contracts. No working Goal command handler or native transport is removed. The config-save repair itself adds the public `Config::goal_validation_input_paths` method without changing the wire schema or error codes.
  These two follow-up commits add no public enum variant, trait method, field, signature, serialized field, schema migration, or durable-ID format. They intentionally correct edge behavior: trusted ingress now rejects noncanonical session-key values even when callers construct the public enum variants directly, and status lookup returns the existing typed stale result if the task ID, status or execution epoch changed during the read. Valid canonical keys retain their exact prior values and durable IDs. This does not promise an atomic snapshot across task and Goal storage.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes — new Goal contracts/configuration compared with integrated `master`; no user-facing Goal command is wired.** Relative to earlier proposal revisions, missing budget defaults no longer count as unlimited consent: both defaults explicitly zero select unlimited, while absent defaults or one zero paired with an unset dimension produce `BudgetRequired`. Explicit command limits remain separately supported. No new environment key or runnable user command syntax is enabled by this slice. The removed channel-only `/goal` catalogue entry was present but unwired on integrated `master`; no production channel renderer consumed it and no Fluent key existed. Rendered help is unchanged; the public catalogue/API removals are the source-compatibility changes described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No declared floor change.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: The inherited task-store migration advances control-plane schema version 10 to 13 when the store is opened; it is not a manual migration requested here, and no live migration/deployment was performed. Keep a recoverable store backup. Rust consumers should update struct literals and exhaustive matches as above, use `GoalHostSettings::from_config` with the current config for each operation, and retain existing runtime type re-export paths or import the canonical API types. No automatic database downgrade is claimed; review data compatibility before reverting to an older binary.

**Legacy Goal data on upgrade:** On first store open, running or paused Goals created through the old session-less API are retained but marked failed, normally with `legacy_goal_missing_session` (an existing error is preserved), and receive a completion timestamp. They cannot be resumed as sessionless Goals; review the retained objective/state and recreate them as session-bound Goals through guarded admission. The same reconciliation fails active rows with a missing objective (`legacy_goal_missing_objective`); malformed legacy execution epochs have a separate `goal_invalid_execution_epoch` safety path. Completed Goal statuses and non-Goal data are preserved by this reconciliation. Old-record deserialization does not imply active-Goal resumability. Back up the store before opening it with the new version.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** To revert only this follow-up in a separately reviewed rollback change, first revert `afadb4058eb1c7395e63046c8bfa19b2e04f3e69`, which only adds the async test-fixture lifetime annotation; then revert `c716dd73af99c9565ae065c2323767d5001fefcd`, which contains the behavior change and regression tests. Reverting `c716dd73af99c9565ae065c2323767d5001fefcd` restores the prior invalid-direct-key admission and unfenced status-projection behavior. These commits add no persistent data or schema change. To undo only the config-save repair in a rollback PR, `git revert fa7136de529eb55076e04c162c43b1bb4b6ddc1b` restores the former save-with-warning behavior, including its defect; that is a separate reviewed decision. Before merging to master, undo the upstream integration with `git revert -m 1 d8f7fd7eea1b46e76e8f51ee7653fcdc596e7f11` through the same gates; later re-integration requires reverting that revert. To revert the entire slice, use `git revert <PR squash commit>` after reverting dependent Goal slices in reverse dependency order. Preserve the task database and usage ledger; do not delete them. No live rollback was performed.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** After this follow-up, a malformed direct session-key variant is rejected at trusted ingress, and a status request whose task changed during the read returns the existing stale response. Those are intentional outcomes, not new error codes or evidence of a production transport rollout. Configuration admission errors include `Goal configuration does not admit execution`; a legacy active Goal may instead be retained as failed with `legacy_goal_missing_session` or `legacy_goal_missing_objective` after upgrade. Opening newer-schema data emits `control-plane DB was created by a newer schema version` with `db_version` and `known_version`; that warning is not a safe-downgrade guarantee.
