prs.title: fix(cli): exit non-zero when get-paircode fetch fails
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The human-readable `gateway get-paircode` path printed a fetch failure then returned `Ok(())`, so the process exited 0.
  - After the existing guidance, the Err arm now exits with status 1 so scripts can detect the failure.
  - Uses `process::exit(1)` after printing so anyhow does not reprint the same error on top of the guidance.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `--json` (already uses `?` and fails on fetch Err). Does not change the `NoCode` success-path messaging/exit (still Ok with guidance). Related #11975 covers gateway-less builds separately and leaves standard-build fetch failures alone.
- **Blast radius:** CLI exit status for failed human-readable get-paircode only; automation that already checked stdout for ❌ may additionally see non-zero status.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11972. Related #11975.

### What this does, simply

If you ask the CLI for a pairing code and the gateway cannot be reached (or the admin token is missing), ZeroClaw already printed a clear error, but it still exited successfully. Scripts that check `$?` thought everything was fine. This change keeps the same message and exits with code 1 instead.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Standard build; no gateway running; fresh config dir.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```bash
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$(mktemp -d)" gateway get-paircode; echo "exit=$?"
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Failure message printed; `exit=1`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Same message; `exit=0`.

### How I tested

- Built `zeroclaw` from this branch and ran the repro above against a temp config dir with no gateway.
- Observed exit status 1 and the existing human-readable failure text (no duplicate anyhow line).
- Ran focused unit tests: `cargo test --bin zeroclaw gateway_get_paircode` → 2 passed.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required PR CI for the CLI binary / gateway paths.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the usual platform matrix.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```text
  ❌ Failed to fetch pairing code from gateway at 127.0.0.1:42617
     Error: No gateway admin token at …/data/gateway-admin.token. …
     Is the gateway running? Start it with:
       zeroclaw gateway start
  exit=1
  ```
  ```text
  test tests::gateway_get_paircode_cli_accepts_port_and_host_overrides ... ok
  test tests::gateway_get_paircode_rotate_flags_parse_and_conflict ... ok
  test result: ok. 2 passed
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Human-readable failure exit code. Did not re-test the `--json` success path on a live gateway.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (CLI stdout/stderr; no presentation-sensitive claim)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** head of this branch; `cli`; locale default; terminal width irrelevant
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see command tail above
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** failed get-paircode → exit 1
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` / clippy not re-run locally after a prior disk-full cleanup; relied on focused binary build + unit filter + CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`No` — intentional exit-status fix for failure cases that previously exited 0)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes` — exit code of failed human-readable `gateway get-paircode` only)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Scripts that relied on exit 0 despite a printed fetch failure should treat non-zero as failure (the intended contract). Successful fetches are unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this commit.

## Code understanding / AI assistance

AI tooling helped draft the change and PR text; every line was reviewed. Approach: keep the existing user-facing guidance, then `process::exit(1)` so the process status matches the failure without a second anyhow error line.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `desktop-check.yml` now runs `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-desktop` after clippy on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Every workspace test job excludes `zeroclaw-desktop` (`ci.yml`, `platform-tests.yml`, `windows-tests.yml`). Until now the desktop crate's tests (35 on macOS and Linux, 31 on Windows) were compiled by clippy but never run. They include the supervisor process-tree cleanup, readiness-frame, capability-probe, and webview-capability tests.
  - `tests/architecture/desktop_release.rs` gains a guard that keeps those tests running. The architecture suite fails if Desktop App Check:
    - stops triggering on pull requests that change `apps/tauri/**`;
    - drops macOS, Linux, or Windows from its matrix;
    - gains `continue-on-error`;
    - makes the test step conditional or changes its command (for example `--no-run`).
  - Docs: `ci-and-actions.md` gets a Desktop App Check section, and its pinned-action table now lists `desktop-check.yml` for the two actions it already used. The stale "CI matrix to add" note in `apps/tauri/TESTING.md` now describes the actual coverage.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No installer builds. Earlier revisions of this PR also added a per-PR "bundle dry run" workflow. That workflow is removed: the desktop jobs in Release Stable already build the installers on a stable tag.
  - The dashboard smoke script that came with the dry run moved to #11272, which is its only user.
  - Release Stable is not modified. There are no Rust product changes, and nothing is added to `CI Required Gate`.
- **Blast radius:** `desktop-check.yml` runs a bit longer, adding a test build of one crate on each OS. Its triggers are unchanged: PRs touching `apps/tauri/**` or the workflow itself, weekly, and manual dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11004
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0` (path and size labels are applied by the labelers)

### What this does, simply

The desktop app has tests, but CI never ran them, because the main test jobs skip the desktop crate. This PR runs those tests on Mac, Linux, and Windows whenever the desktop app changes, and adds a check that fails if the workflow ever stops running them.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Desktop App Check runs on this PR itself because it changes the workflow file.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Desktop App Check` runs the new test step on all three OS. It triggers on this PR through its own path.
  - The architecture suite in `Quality Gate` runs the new guard.
  - `Docs Style` covers the Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for the test step itself.
- **Follow-up (not in this PR):** the guard matches the literal matrix line, so a `strategy.exclude` entry that drops an OS would slip past it. Asserting there is no `exclude:` under `strategy` (or parsing the matrix) would close that.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

Architecture tests at this head, on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.98.0 (the CI toolchain), through a remote build of this exact tree:

```text
$ cargo test --locked --test architecture desktop_release
test desktop_release::desktop_app_check_runs_the_desktop_unit_tests ... ok
test desktop_release::windows_desktop_manifest_selects_common_controls_v6 ... ok
test desktop_release::macos_desktop_sidecar_embeds_the_web_artifact ... ok
test release_workflow::macos_desktop_release_notarizes_published_dmg ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 52 filtered out
```

The full architecture suite (`cargo test --locked --test architecture`) passes with `58 passed; 0 failed` on #11272's head, which contains this commit.

Mutation check of the new guard. Each edit was made to `desktop-check.yml`, `cargo test --locked --test architecture desktop_release::` was run against it, and the file was restored. Every mutant fails `desktop_app_check_runs_the_desktop_unit_tests`:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| test step removed | FAILED |
| test command gains `--no-run` | FAILED |
| `continue-on-error: true` added to the job | FAILED |
| test step gains `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` | FAILED |
| `windows-latest` dropped from the matrix | FAILED |
| `apps/tauri/**` dropped from the pull-request paths | FAILED |

Static checks:

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                     -> EXIT:0
$ git diff --check                                                               -> EXIT:0
$ actionlint .github/workflows/desktop-check.yml                                 -> EXIT:0
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh tests/architecture .github/workflows   -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo clippy --locked --test architecture -- -D warnings   (Rust 1.98.0)       -> EXIT:0, no warnings
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                                                -> Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh                                                  -> OK
```

Clippy and the docs gates ran on #11272's head, which contains this commit.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - This PR's CI at head `46f62539be`: `Desktop App Check` passed on all three OS. macOS and Linux ran 34 lib tests plus the capability test; Windows ran 30 plus the capability test, because the 4 Unix-only process-tree tests are excluded there. The same counts were seen at the earlier head `509d14ae11`.
  - `CI Required Gate` at `46f62539be` is red only because `Check (32-bit)` timed out installing its apt packages, before any compilation (`apt install: attempt 2/2 timed out (status: 124)`). Every other job passed. This failure is unrelated to the change.
  - No bundle dry-run check runs on this head; the workflow is gone.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-desktop` was not run outside hosted CI at this head. This PR does not change the desktop crate's code, and `Desktop App Check` runs it on all three OS.

- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(web): fit global header and page actions on phones
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** At 320px the global header title collapsed to zero width and overlapped the action cluster, and `PageHeader` action rows could force horizontal overflow (for example the Tools page at 627px). Tighten header padding/gaps, collapse non-essential labels below `sm`, and let `PageHeader` actions wrap to a full-width row on phones.
- **Scope boundary:** Global header and shared `PageHeader` only. This PR deliberately does **not** touch the chat header, `SessionPicker`, or agent/model pickers; #11933 already covers that separate row.
- **Blast radius:** Shared page chrome used by every dashboard route; changing wrapping can move actions to a second line on narrow screens but does not change their behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11933 (open PR covering the chat header). No linked issue for the global header/PageHeader overflow.

### What this does, simply

On a phone, the top bar had too many fixed-width controls for the title to fit. Section pages could also push their action buttons past the right edge. This PR makes the global header and page action rows responsive so they wrap and truncate instead of clipping.

## Testing (required)

- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`

### How I tested

```sh
npx tsc -b
```

prs.title: fix(web): correct personality editor copy for channels
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** the Personality editor intro claimed personality-file edits land on the next message on every surface and never need a daemon reload. Channel agents build their base system prompt once when the daemon starts (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`), so a dashboard edit never reaches a channel conversation until the daemon restarts or `/admin/reload` runs. The copy now states each surface's real behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** copy only. No runtime, channel, orchestrator, or personality-loading behavior changes; #11698 keeps ownership of the per-session snapshot work on the `Agent::turn` path.
- **Blast radius:** one English i18n value in `web/src/lib/i18n.ts`. The key exists only in the `en` table; the other locale tables have no entry for it and continue to fall back to English.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12175

### What this does, simply

The Personality editor told operators that editing a markdown file such as `AGENTS.md` would reach their channel agents on the next message. It does not: channels read those files once when the daemon starts, so a channel agent keeps using the old text. The panel now says dashboard and CLI sessions pick the change up on the next message, while channel agents need a daemon restart (or `/admin/reload`) before they see it.

One follow-up note: when #11698 lands, dashboard sessions move to a per-session snapshot as well, so the dashboard sentence will need a one-line refresh at that point. This PR matches the behavior on `master` today and the wording requested in #12175.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; this is a single localized string whose correctness is established by reading the change and the checks below, not by an interface flow.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (Personality editor intro text).
- **Setup / preconditions:** none.

### How I tested

Changed value and the consumer that renders it:

```console
$ git diff --stat
 web/src/lib/i18n.ts | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

$ grep -n "personality.editor_intro" web/src/lib/i18n.ts
819:    'personality.editor_intro': "These markdown files shape your agent's voice and context. Dashboard and CLI sessions pick up changes on the next message. Channel agents read them when the daemon starts — restart the daemon (or call /admin/reload) to push an edit to channels.",

$ grep -n "editor_intro" web/src/components/sections/PersonalityEditor.tsx
339:        {t('personality.editor_intro')}
```

No stale copy or duplicate locale entry remains:

```console
$ grep -rn "no daemon reload needed" . --exclude-dir=.git
$ grep -c "personality.editor_intro" web/src/lib/i18n.ts
1
```

The edited module still parses (esbuild, TypeScript loader inferred from the file):

```console
$ esbuild web/src/lib/i18n.ts --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null
  ../../dev/null  875.8kb
⚡ Done in 42ms
```

prs.title: fix(config): migrate retired keys at schema version 4 and warn on a missing schema_version
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Credit:** this builds on @singlerider's #8754, opened 2026-07-06, which first identified these inert keys and proposed the move to schema version 4. Its still-valid retirements, its version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and its version 4 fixture and tests are carried forward here, with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the retirement commits. This PR also folds #11217, which reads an unversioned config in the version 3 format as version 3.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11082 retired `[security.nevis]` but left `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at 3, so no migration ran. The table was discarded at load with a warning hidden unless `-v` was passed, and it stayed on disk with any plaintext `client_secret`. This PR bumps the schema to version 4 and adds a version 3 → version 4 step driven by a new `RETIRED_KEYS` table.
  - Each table entry names a key path, the version that retires it, and the reason shown to the operator, with a Fluent id so the CLI prints the reason in the operator's locale (logs and `--json` keep the English text). A retired key is removed with everything under it. A path segment `ANY_KEY` (`"*"`) matches every key at its level, so one entry retires a key in every `[agents.<alias>]` block or every runtime profile. Each concrete match is reported under its real path.
  - Retired keys are applied during migration and again on every load of a current-version config. A retired key that reappears in a version 4 file is dropped with a notice, not silently ignored by serde.
  - The same table also drives incremental saves. #11191 made `save_dirty` remove `[security.nevis]` from the on-disk document, since an incremental save rewrites only dirty paths and would otherwise carry a retired table and its secret forward. This PR replaces that Nevis-only helper with `apply_retired_keys_to_doc`, so `save_dirty` and migration share one retirement policy. Wildcard entries work there too, so the eight agent-inline tunables are removed from disk as well. The edit touches only retired keys, keeps comments and unrelated ciphertext byte for byte, and logs each removal only after the atomic write succeeds. #11191's tests are kept against the table-driven cleanup. A save first reads the version of the file on disk. A version 1 or version 2 file is not edited as it stands, because keys retired at version 3 (`[identity]`, an agent's `max_tool_iterations`) are still live inputs to its version 2 → version 3 step. An incremental save first carries the file on disk through the typed migration chain, then applies the dirty paths to the result, so those inputs are converted and keys another handle saved after this config loaded survive. A file whose version cannot be determined (an unversioned file that mixes layouts or reads both ways) or is newer than this binary is refused by both save paths, so a load that fell back to defaults cannot relabel it and write over it.
  - Containers a retirement leaves empty follow one rule on both paths. A literal container such as `[security]` or `context_compression` is dropped. A table matched by a wildcard is an operator-named alias such as `[agents.coder]` and is always kept, so a reference to it never dangles. `toml_edit` writes nothing for an empty implicit or dotted table, so an alias that existed only as a prefix of retired dotted keys (`runtime_profiles.slow.context_compression.summary_model = …`) is written back as its own `[runtime_profiles.slow]` header, or as `slow = {}` inside an inline table.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate` edits a file at version 3 or later in place: from version 3, reaching version 4 only retires keys and re-stamps `schema_version`, so quoting, number spelling and comments on untouched lines keep their exact bytes. Older files still take the structural rebuild.
  - A `ZEROCLAW_*` environment override naming a retired key is ignored with a notice instead of failing startup as an unknown property.
  - Every change is a `MigrationNotice` carrying key paths and reasons only, never values. Notices print on stderr after every config load, with a line saying `zeroclaw config migrate` writes them. `config migrate` prints them itself and returns them in `--json`.
  - The first time this binary rewrites a file of an older version (through `config migrate`, the dashboard's migrate, or any save), it keeps a copy of the original as `config.toml.v<version>.backup`. The copy is owner-only (0600 on Unix) whatever the source's mode, because it can hold the plaintext secrets of retired keys, and it is never replaced or removed. It is written and synced under a private name, then published with a hard link, which never replaces an existing path, so a file at that name is never an unfinished copy. An existing file there counts only when it holds exactly the bytes about to be rewritten; it is then synced and, if an older build left it readable by others, made owner-only, or the rewrite is refused. Anything else there is left alone and the copy goes to `config.toml.v<version>-<n>.backup`. Where the filesystem has no hard links, the synced copy is renamed to a name of its own, `config.toml.v<version>-<uuid>.backup`, so no writer counts on a copy another writer might still fail to finish. `config migrate` names the copy, and `--json` reports it as `version_backup_path`.
  - Master's built-in tool selector (`[tools] optional`) is carried across every migration route: a file that omits it is read and written with the full default selection, as on master.
  - A config with no `schema_version` is read by its layout, judged by definitions rather than guesses (folded from #11217 and extended).
    - Evidence of an older layout is a setting only the layouts before version 3 have. A table lists every setting the version 1 → version 3 chain reads, moves, renames or drops that the current schema does not read in place: version 1's top-level provider settings and the spellings it accepts for them, `[autonomy]`, `[swarms]`, `[storage.provider]`, `tunnel.provider` and the like. Added to it are the version 2 shapes a path cannot express: a provider or channel section holding fields directly, a value directly under `[providers]`, a version 2-only agent key, `[[cron.jobs]]` or a cron knob, and a route naming `provider`.
    - Evidence of the version 3 layout is a setting only it has that the version 1 reading would reshape or merge an older setting into:
      - an alias-keyed section of any provider category (`providers.models`, `providers.tts`, `providers.transcription`) or channel type, under `channels` or its accepted spelling `channels_config`;
      - a declarative `[cron.<name>]` job;
      - a child of a version 2 section that is not one of its fields with what it actually holds (an alias named `extra_headers` holding a float is an alias, not headers), probed under the family the migration files the section by (`grok` as `xai`, a `custom:` URL as `custom`);
      - a version 3-only setting the chain writes into: the risk and runtime profiles, peer groups, alias-keyed storage, `tunnel_provider`, `search_provider`, and a current agent's keys. None existed in version 2.
    - A file with only version 3 evidence is read as version 3. The version is fixed at 3, not the current version, so the file still runs the version 3 → version 4 step; it reports an `InferredV3` notice telling the operator to run `zeroclaw config migrate`, and the version 2 → version 3 filesystem relocation no longer runs for it.
    - A file with both is refused, with an error naming one setting of each and how to fix it, rather than read in a way that reshapes or drops part of it. When the older setting is one the current layout retires anyway (a stale `[identity]`), the error leads with the one-line fix, add `schema_version = 4`, and gives the retirement reason, which says where the setting lives now.
    - A child of an alias-keyed section that also reads as a field of a version 2 entry (`[providers.models.openai.extra_headers]` on its own, or an empty map-valued field) is refused the same way, asking for `schema_version = 2` or `3`. An agent holding no current agent setting (only `system_prompt` or `max_tool_iterations`, say) can only be a version 2 agent, so a file with nothing else to decide by is read as version 1, as on master: the agent is bound to profiles, and its iteration limit lands in its runtime profile, where version 2 read it.
    - Any other unversioned config is still read as version 1, as on master, and that assumption now prints a warning. Reading a file written for a newer version as version 1 is what this prevents: it folds hand-written channel aliases into `default`, the most likely cause of the "half my config is ignored" reports, and nests `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>]` one level too deep, stranding the model and URI. The warning names both effects.
    - Tests pin both sides, generating what must be listed from the types and the chain rather than from a reading of them:
      - Each table entry is moved by the chain and not read in place by the current schema.
      - No table entry is a key the current types accept, serde aliases included. The keys come from the field list serde's derive passes to `deserialize_struct`.
      - The top-level spellings an older typed lens also reads are listed, with how the detector tells the layouts apart for each.
      - For every leaf the chain writes from each older example, that example beside a different version 3 value there is refused.
      - Every key retired at version 4 either reads the same both ways or requires the version.
      - No section of the version 4 fixture, of the default config, or of a config with every exposed property and keyed section set, under any accepted spelling, counts as an older layout. In every one of those samples, a file with no evidence configures the same thing read either way. This is broad regression coverage, not a proof over every possible file.
      - Every older-layout example is also checked under each spelling its section accepts (`channels_config` for `channels`).
  - The version 2 → version 3 step keeps version 2's `[transcription]` settings where they are: the current schema and runtime still read them there, while the `[providers.transcription]` aliases spell some fields differently (`uri` for local Whisper's `url`, no Groq endpoint), so moving them lost the endpoint and failed strict loading. A version 2 `[tts.<type>]` block now merges into an existing `[providers.tts]` instead of replacing it.
  - An incremental save that carries an older file through the structural migration logs what the migration did once the file is replaced, as it logs retirements.
  - Saves keep one spelling of every setting the schema reads under two (its serde aliases: `channels_config` for `channels`, `dbURL` for a Postgres store's `db_url`, a heartbeat's `channel` for `target`, and the rest). Before an incremental or full save edits a current file, it retires keys (as loading does) and then renames such a key to the spelling the schema writes, keeping its value, the comments around it and its place among its siblings. An incremental edit used to write the second spelling beside the first, which the schema cannot read back. A file still holding two live spellings of one setting, its written spelling beside an alias or two of its aliases (a Postgres store's `dbURL` beside `database_url`), is refused before anything is written, and the message names the spellings it holds. A full save over an older file leaves the choice to its migration where the migration makes one (V1's `channels_config` over `channels`), and runs the same check on the migrated file to refuse a conflict the migration leaves, so a section the loaded config lacks is never written away. Retirements also apply under every accepted spelling: `channels.notion` covers `channels_config.notion`. A test checks the list against every `alias` in the crate's source, and checks each pair against serde's own duplicate-field error. Another takes every pair of spellings of each aliased key, in a version 1 and a version 2 file, through both saves: the value must survive where the migration chooses between them, and every other save must be refused with the file unchanged. Removing the check for any one spelling fails exactly that spelling's cases.
  - Retired at version 4:
    - `[security.nevis]`, which was added in #3651 and never implemented. Its schema field, load shim and validation warning are deleted.
    - Eight agent-inline runtime tunables in every `[agents.<alias>]` (`compact_context`, `max_tool_iterations`, `max_history_messages`, `max_context_tokens`, `memory_recall_limit`, `parallel_tools`, `tool_dispatcher`, `strict_tool_parsing`). ### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's config file carries a version number, so that when a setting is removed an upgrade can rewrite old files and say what it changed. Several settings had been removed without that happening, so they were quietly ignored. Some had been ignored from the start, like tuning knobs written under an agent instead of under its runtime profile. This PR adds a list of retired settings. The upgrade removes each one it finds and prints a plain warning saying why and what to use instead. One entry can cover a setting under every agent or every profile. The first entries are the removed Nevis login block, eight agent knobs that never did anything, and an old summary-model setting. A config file with no version number is no longer read as the oldest version when it is plainly written in the current shape, which used to silently merge your named channels into one called `default`. It warns either way.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits. #11191's Nevis-only save cleanup then returns with it. A config already migrated to `schema_version = 4` is then newer than the binary supports. A version 4 body is a subset of version 3, so setting it back to `schema_version = 3` by hand works; to restore the file as it was, use `config.toml.v3.backup` (or `.v1`/`.v2`). This binary writes that copy the first time it rewrites a file of that version, through `config migrate`, the dashboard's migrate, or a save, and never replaces it. `config.toml.backup` is not a reliable rollback copy: each `config migrate` replaces it, including a later retirement-only one of a version 4 file. The dashboard migrate's `config.toml.bak` is replaced by the next save.

prs.title: fix(memory): add per-agent attribution and scoping to the knowledge graph
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds mandatory agent ownership to the shared SQLite knowledge graph. `KnowledgeScope` is bound from trusted registration; writes keep caller ownership and directional `read_knowledge_from` grants widen reads only.
  - Makes legacy attribution explicit and fail-closed, with a sole-agent automatic path or configured `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` for ambiguous multi-agent upgrades.
  - Makes agent delete/rename recovery lifecycle-specific: delete probes exported memory while rename detects even an empty agent identity row; filesystem inspection errors retain residue; workspace/knowledge archives surface failures; cron and ACP rows are purged only after durable export.
  - Makes the fail-toward-residue rule uniform across surfaces. The gateway workspace mover and committed-rename probe no longer collapse a metadata error into absence, and the CLI deletion path archives through the shared helper instead of a hand-rolled copy that swallowed its errors.
  - Makes that fail-toward-residue rule platform-independent. A workspace whose parent is a file surfaces as an error on Unix and as an ordinary "not found" on Windows, so every surface now classifies a path through one shared `inspect_lifecycle_path` helper that re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe. An uninspectable workspace is residue on every supported platform, and the regressions assert that classification instead of the platform's error shape.
  - Gives every deletion archive an exclusively created leaf, so a duplicate delete inside the same clock second cannot adopt another attempt's directory, and writes the archive artifacts with `create_new` so a shared leaf could not replace a durable export even if one were reached.
  - Prevents shared inbound edges from suppressing the caller's own relation and requires a scope-visible anchor for every direct graph-neighbor query after grant revocation.
  - Validates lifecycle aliases before any recovery probe or filesystem path derivation, keeps unreadable RPC rename workspaces retryable, and serializes the global node cap across per-agent SQLite connections.
  - Boxes the RPC map-key delete future, which the master merge showed is needed to keep `process_line` inside the two-megabyte stack budget `master` now pins.
  - Resolves grants from live policy for each graph operation after acquiring the database connection. Purge verifies the archived snapshot in an immediate transaction, using durable edge generation identities to distinguish recreated relations.
  - Refuses to recreate an agent over a retired agent's knowledge on every config creation path. Explicit creation and property writes that would create the agent (`zeroclaw config set` and `config patch`, gateway PUT and PATCH, RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many`) share one admission rule: never the reserved `default` agent, and never an absent alias whose knowledge remains or whose store cannot be inspected without waiting. The refusal is a 400 `validation_failed` on HTTP (explicit creation previously reported it as 404) and a localized message on RPC and the CLI. The `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent`, which inserts agents directly, runs the same retirement check against the store the runtime opens; an agent defined by environment overrides is live and is not probed. The probe re-walks the ancestors of a store reported as missing, so a store under a regular-file parent is refused on Windows as on Unix.
  - Merges current `master` (`5d4b18d335`) and ports the knowledge-ownership paths onto its atomic live-config publication: the live knowledge scope reads a `LiveConfigHandle`, and agent delete and its committed-delete retry admit a `ConfigCommit` and publish only when config changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Knowledge ownership is per agent alias, not per authenticated principal; different principals using the same agent share its knowledge. The unwired Postgres graph is unchanged. Knowledge tool schema/shape is unchanged, but row visibility is intentionally narrowed by `KnowledgeScope`. Gateway and RPC can retry committed rename residue; CLI cannot yet, and #10373 owns that shared recovery follow-up. Lifecycle requests now enforce the canonical alias grammar before touching recovery state. #10149 owns durable recovery for a failed custom workspace archive. Not changed here, and predating this PR: an environment override that names a new agent is applied at config load without the retirement check (documented as an operator caveat), and the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` removes an agent without the owned-state cascade.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-memory`, tools/runtime registration, config, gateway/RPC/CLI alias lifecycle, SQLite knowledge/session/memory stores, cron and ACP cleanup, workspaces, and documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9647. Related #9646. Related #10149. Related #10373.

Agent aliases remain the canonical ownership key already used by configuration, workspaces, grants, and lifecycle operations. The storage API requires scope so foreign rows behave as absent even if a caller knows an ID. Disabled configured siblings remain valid explicit read sources; they do not become writers.

### What this does, simply

Agents previously shared the same knowledge graph. This change gives each row an owning agent and limits an agent to its own knowledge unless an operator grants read access to another agent's rows. Deletion archives owned knowledge before removing it, and rename moves its ownership. The latest repair makes revoked sharing take effect for retained tools and stops cleanup from purging rows that differ from its archive. If cleanup fails, creating that agent again through any config surface is refused until a retried delete removes the old knowledge, so a new agent with the same name never inherits it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` through the registered `knowledge` tool and alias lifecycle RPC/CLI paths.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Enable knowledge and configure neutral agents `agent_a` and `agent_b`.
- **Steps to run:** Capture a unique node as `agent_b`; search, inspect statistics, traverse, and relate by ID as `agent_a`; then add `read_knowledge_from = ["agent_b"]`, restart, and repeat. Exercise rename/delete once with a temporarily unavailable configured memory/workspace path, restore it, and retry. For the archive path, issue the same `agents delete` twice inside one second and inspect `<data_dir>/agents/_deleted`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign rows are absent before the grant; reads become visible after the directional grant while writes remain caller-owned. Failed lifecycle cleanup retains retryable residue. Creating the alias again, explicitly or through a property write such as `zeroclaw config set agents.<alias>.enabled true`, is refused while its knowledge remains or the store cannot be inspected, and is admitted once a retried delete converges. The duplicate delete lands in its own archive leaf and the first attempt's export is untouched.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Agents shared one unscoped graph, and several committed lifecycle failures could be mistaken for completed cleanup.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `e248cfe531`. `959cb698a3` merges `master` at `5d4b18d335`, and `e248cfe531` is the alias-recreation fix. Results below are from macOS arm64 at that head unless noted. Hosted CI was still running on this head when this was written.

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> no warnings
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 5951 tests run: 5951 passed, 9 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 727 tests run: 727 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component
    -> 263 tests run: 263 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 526 run: 525 passed; filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled
       timed out under full-suite load and passes alone
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 2531 run: 2530 passed; policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception
       fails identically on master on macOS (open PR #11646)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools -E 'test(/model_routing_config|knowledge/)'
    -> 56 tests run: 56 passed
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> no prose em-dashes; 0 errors
  ```

- **Not run as scripted here:** this machine's `rg` cannot load `libpcre2`, so `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` and the provider-dispatch step of `rust_quality_gate.sh` abort, and nine `content_search` tool tests fail for the same reason. The comment hygiene checker passed when given the same file set through `git ls-files`, and the fix adds no `ModelProvider` method calls. Hosted CI runs both gates.
- **Regression coverage for the blocker:** a failed knowledge purge followed by recreation is refused at each boundary: config unit (`auto_create_refuses_retained_knowledge_and_uninspectable_store`), gateway PUT, PATCH and explicit create (`property_writes_cannot_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many` after a real committed delete with a blocked store, then admitted after the retried delete converges (`config_set_cannot_recreate_agent_until_retired_knowledge_converges`), the CLI binary (`config_patch_refuses_to_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), and the `model_routing_config` tool (`upsert_agent_refuses_alias_with_retained_knowledge`, `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge`). Busy and uninspectable stores fail closed; the Windows-shaped not-found branch is driven directly (`missing_store_under_a_file_ancestor_is_uninspectable`).
- **Mutation checks:** restoring the old auto-create path (retirement check skipped, reserved check kept) makes the config, gateway, RPC, and CLI regression tests fail; probing the tool's env-free file config or skipping its probe fails the tool test; disabling the env-defined-agent check fails its test.
- **Known gap:** no Windows execution here; the gateway and RPC uninspectable fixtures rely on the new ancestor walk on Windows and are untested there until the advisory Windows job runs.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Previously reviewed head:** `be62e0b5160f65f3ddc937c427691395d968eb75`. The required [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36767407780/job/110069381765) passed. That re-review inspected source and regression assertions; it did not run local Cargo.
- **Historical validation below:** Commands, counts, and Windows results below were reported for `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`; they are not current-head execution claims.

- **Historical head under test:** `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, which merges `origin/master` (`46479bdca7`) into the branch and adds the two portability repairs described below.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `CI Required Gate` rollup plus the advisory Windows nextest job. This head exists to repair a Windows-only behavior, so the advisory Windows job is the one that actually exercises what changed; the required gate covers everything else.
- Hosted CI on this head (`4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34554821248.
- **Advisory Windows disclosure:** On historical head `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, [Windows job 103129316312](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34554821248/job/103129316312) ran the repaired unreadable-workspace, path-classifier, duplicate-archive, existing-export protection, and refused-move tests successfully. The job remains failed: its initial batch reported 13,163 tests run, 13,160 passed, 3 failed, and 20 skipped. The remaining failures are the architecture publish-contract test and two runtime PowerShell tests; none is one of the repaired lifecycle regressions. Subsequent scoped batches passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No Windows execution is available locally, so the Windows result for that historical head comes from the runner; what is proven here is that the shared classifier returns `Uninspectable` for the `Ok(false)` shape Windows reports and that every lifecycle surface routes through it. No live two-agent daemon A/B, and no live multi-process duplicate delete. The duplicate-archive regression drives two cascades of the same alias inside one clock second in-process, which is the interleaving the finding described, but it is not a two-daemon race. CLI committed-rename retry remains #10373.
- **Commands run and tail output (historical head `4291450ec`):**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean (exit 0)

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    -> No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
       (one pre-existing MD038 on an unchanged line of agents/internals.md, reported non-blocking)

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> 1 link collected, 0 errors

  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    -> fmt clean; workspace clippy --all-targets --features ci-all -D warnings clean;
       provider dispatch gate clean (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 4305 tests run: 4305 passed, 5 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 521 tests run: 521 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 383 tests run: 383 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 532 tests run: 532 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
    -> 15654 tests run: 15653 passed (2 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
    -> the single failure is zeroclaw-providers
       grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant,
       a known macOS-local timing flake unrelated to this change
  ```

  Both repairs were proven to fail before and pass after, on this machine.

  The Windows-shape defect was reproduced by reverting the new classifier to the
  pre-fix rule (`Ok(false)` means absent), which is exactly the path Windows
  takes:

  ```text
  # classifier temporarily reverted to `Ok(false) => Absent`
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --test-threads=1 --no-fail-fast \
    -E 'test(a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes) + ...'
    -> FAIL a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes
       panicked: a negative probe over a non-directory ancestor is not absence

  # after the fix, same command
    -> 5 tests run: 5 passed, 4270 skipped
  ```

  The cross-device failure was reproduced literally, by putting `TMPDIR` on a
  separate mount from the install root the pre-fix fixture reached into:

  ```text
  # pre-fix, TMPDIR on a separate filesystem
    -> FAIL duplicate_delete_cascades_cannot_share_an_archive_or_truncate_the_first_export
       ["workspace archive failed (<install-root>/agents/agent_a/workspace ->
         <tmpdir>/data/agents/_deleted/agent_a-<ts>-2/workspace): Cross-device link (os error 18)"]

  # after pinning config_path under the test's TempDir, same split-mount run
    -> 5 tests run: 5 passed, 4270 skipped
       and the install root was left empty, which is the property that was missing
  ```

- **Historical evidence (previous head `64d8944a4275a31aa39ce4094c5d655dce205ecf`):** the exact-head hosted rollup [run 34188562577](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34188562577) completed with 37 successful checks, 1 failure, and 3 skipped. The required `CI Required Gate` passed; the single failure was the advisory Windows nextest job described above. Local focused suites at that head passed, which is the asymmetry this head removes: the assertions they made were Unix-only. That head also needed one master-driven repair, kept here as history: `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` landed on `master` after the branch's previous head and aborted on the merged tree because the agent-delete branch of `handle_config_map_key_delete` left the owned-state cascade's future inline in the caller; it passed on `origin/master` alone, aborted on the merged head, and passed again after the delete future was boxed.

- **Historical evidence (earlier head `ab20806838a56a5ed9027e34c2517d4ee8af950e`):** the exact-head hosted rollup completed 38/38 successful check runs, including the required aggregate gate, strict lint, tests, Landlock, security, platform checks, MSRV, and the parallel runtime gate. Focused suites at that head were `zeroclaw-memory` knowledge_graph 30 passed, `zeroclaw-tools` knowledge 18 passed, `zeroclaw-config` knowledge 5 passed, `zeroclaw-runtime` `config_map_key_` 10 passed, and the gateway `agent_delete_`/`agent_rename_` suites 7 and 4 passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read the exact-head Windows job log rather than inferring the failures from the summary, and confirmed that five of its six failures are this PR's own `try_exists().is_err()` assertions and the sixth is the inherited packaging assertion. I re-audited every filesystem probe on the lifecycle surfaces so that all of them, including the deletion archive and the knowledge-database probe inside the residue predicate, now route through the one classifier. I mounted a separate filesystem locally to reproduce the reviewer's cross-device failure instead of taking it on faith, and confirmed after the fix that the test leaves the install root untouched. Earlier rounds established the master baseline for the stack regression in a separate worktree. I did not run a live daemon interaction, I did not exercise the duplicate delete across two operating-system processes, and I cannot execute Windows here.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no visual presentation changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo deny check` was not re-run locally; it is unchanged by this head and the hosted security job covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**; `read_knowledge_from` is an explicit directional read grant. It defaults empty, validates aliases, and never widens writes.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; output shape is unchanged and storage authorization reduces visible rows.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Trusted config is the only grant source; mandatory storage-layer predicates, foreign-as-absent results, and caller-owned writes constrain it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for ambiguous multi-agent legacy knowledge; it remains hidden until assigned. Single-agent upgrades are automatic.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**; adds `agents.<alias>.workspace.read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent`; alias lifecycle commands now cascade owned state and reject noncanonical/reserved aliases before recovery I/O. Explicit creation, rename, and property writes that would create an agent refuse retained knowledge or an uninspectable knowledge store, and the explicit HTTP create reports that refusal as 400 `validation_failed` instead of 404.
- Storage schema: Adds durable `edges.generation` identities and an insert trigger for archived-snapshot comparison.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Multi-agent operators with legacy knowledge set `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent = "<enabled-alias>"`, restart, verify ownership, then remove the migration setting. Add read grants only when deliberate.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable knowledge, back up its SQLite file, then revert the eventual PR landing commit. An old binary does not enforce ownership and may create unattributed rows, so rollback is containment only. The `edges.generation` column and insert trigger remain in the SQLite database across a binary downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[knowledge].enabled = false`; remove `read_knowledge_from` entries to revoke sharing.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `still owns knowledge` or `cannot inspect retired knowledge` refusals when recreating an agent (WARN `config.retired_agent_vivify_refused` for property writes), legacy-ownership ambiguity warnings, owned-state cascade warnings, retained cron/ACP rows after archive failure, `workspace inspection failed` warnings on a delete or rename result, or repeated delete/rename results reporting configured-but-unavailable residue.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. ### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

The deletion fix prevents an open WebSocket from recreating a session that RPC just deleted. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

Old Always responses fail closed without consuming strict requests. Unsupported/WASM adapters decline strict requests; ordinary approval remains available and WIT/WASM ABI is unchanged.
- ZeroCode Rust consumers constructing `SessionUpdate::ApprovalRequest` must supply `allow_always`; missing wire fields default to `true` for older ordinary producers. `RpcClient::session_kill` now returns `SessionKillResult { session_id, killed }`, not an untyped JSON value; callers must inspect `killed` before reporting an ended session. The channel prompt-building compatibility helpers are now test-only, but were already crate-private on master and create no external Rust migration.
- Add `TurnAttribution.session_id: Option<String>` for caller-visible identity separately from durable `session_key`. `rpc::turn::execute_turn` takes `session_prompts: Option<SessionPromptAdmission>` after `cost_context`; capture `{ backend, owner }` at primary Chat admission, never resolve a fresh owner after asynchronous preparation. Excluded execution uses `None`.
- Migrate queue `generation` use to `transcript_generation` or the separate async lifecycle-generation/lease APIs. `GatewayStarter` and gateway supervision constructors receive the shared coordination capability; `RpcContext` requires `gateway_sessions`. Share it across restart within a daemon generation, create a fresh coordination scope on reload, and do not share Chat coordination with ACP.
- `AppState.cancel_tokens` changes from upstream `Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<CancellationToken>>>>` to `Arc<Mutex<GatewayCancellationRegistry>>`. Direct constructors use the registry instead of a plain map; entries are `GatewayCancellationEntry { session_key, generation, token }`. Registration and deletion helpers carry the actual admitted queue key and lifecycle generation, not a queue reconstructed from a normalized abort ID. Wire/configuration/SQLite formats are unchanged by this correction. Do not invent generations outside the lifecycle.
- `SessionStore::insert_admitted` is removed. Use `insert_admitted_if_absent` with the matching session permit held through restoration; handle an existing successor without replacement. `insert` acquires admission itself and must not be called while holding that permit. `insert_for_prompt` requires matching cancellation registration. `SessionStore::register_cancel_token` is test-only/crate-private; external code must use RPC lifecycle rather than directly maintaining that registry. The separate public infra gateway registration helper remains the admission path for gateway tokens; do not bypass its latch/replacement checks with raw map insertion.
- Gateway `PendingApprovals` maps IDs to public `PendingApproval` entries with crate-private fields. Construct it with `new_pending_approvals()` and pass it to `WsApprovalChannel::new`; external manual insertion/resolution must be retired or replaced by a separately designed adapter API. `ApprovalPendingMap::register` now requires `strict_session_prompt_approval: bool`; its old `insert` helper is test-only. Use `insert_with_policy(..., false)` for ordinary approvals and explicit strict metadata for prompt mutations.
- Implement durable owner/reset/prompt operations for any `SessionBackend` supporting attachments. Unsupported key-set owned deletion fails closed. The default whole-reset implementation only clears messages and is insufficient for prompt support.

**Observable changes, including with attachments disabled:**

- `sessions_reset` invokes whole-session reset, clearing attachments and rotating incarnation atomically in SQLite. Its "already empty" wording still counts removed messages, not attachment removal. Message-only clear preserves attachments.
- Durable `/new` deletion failure keeps existing history and reports `channel-runtime-new-session-failed` instead of claiming success. Without a durable backend, ordinary ephemeral behavior remains.
- Chat RPC deletion attempts `<id>`, `rpc_<id>` and `gw_<id>` aliases, even without metadata, and coordinates live gateway cancellation/invalidation. Alias deletion is atomic in SQLite; non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them on failure. Unscoped callers no longer condition durable deletion on the live record's owner (master did). ACP deletion stays in its own recorded domain. Scoped callers return `FORBIDDEN` and retain live state when principal-bound durable deletion cannot be proved, including JSONL/unavailable backend. Queue admission can report `SESSION_BUSY`; old deleted WebSockets report `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` and must reconnect. Already-cancelled work is not resumed on rollback. Gateway deletion cancels only entries bound to the deleted queue and generation; a distinct dotted WebSocket queue survives an underscore-session deletion. RPC Kill captures the queue generation before waiting and prevents prompts queued behind that killed generation from entering the provider; it does not cancel a same-ID successor.
- Current-session views, strict previews, turn spans and delegate forensic principal identity use the canonical storage key. Public RPC/cost/OpenCode/shell identity remains separate; `ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID` prefers caller-visible identity. ACP identity is unchanged.
- The three session-prompt tool names are reserved for plugins/skills even when disabled, including prepared-skill registration. Rename conflicts. They also follow master's built-in selection: default full includes eligible prompt tools; minimal requires their explicit names in `[tools].optional` and a reload. This selection changes availability, not authorization or injection of already-stored prompts into an enabled primary Chat turn. Deferred MCP tools must use full `server__tool` names rather than conflicting bare suffixes. Indirect `unfiltered_tool_arcs` excludes prompt tools; use canonical direct calls.
- Native tool framing changes from 42 to 36 characters ("Use tools when this request needs it") for exact budget substitution, including feature-off turns. Native prompt fingerprints consequently change. Complete native/XML prompt framing is paired; nonempty attachment overflow fails closed without truncating host context.
- Strict mutation previews visibly encode Unicode 17 format/default-ignorable characters, including legitimate joiners and variation selectors. This can change how joined text and emoji look in the preview; stored text, content hashes and provider context keep the original bytes. This is display encoding, not a new restriction on valid prompt text.
- Channel retention preserves upstream selection after the last user-role row, including synthetic text-tool results. Text-protocol call/result exchanges are omitted from retained history; native-tool retention remains unchanged. Privacy projection scans the complete exchange before selection so host-marked results can identify sensitive calls. Provider working history is unchanged.
- Export recovery separately recognizes malformed JSON/XML/MiniMax prompt-tool material before ordinary diagnostic output; shared streamed detection retains master's name-based behavior. Recovery is best-effort, not approval or execution. Unrepresentable text media carriers are omitted only for marked sensitive rounds; ordinary media behavior remains upstream.
- Programmatic `HookHandler::before_llm_call` is skipped when the request or active scope carries private session-prompt content, including max-iteration summaries. Its transforms, cancellation and model selection do not apply to these requests; ordinary requests retain them. The classifier is deliberately conservative: parseable `session_prompt_*` envelopes can skip the hook even with the feature disabled. The feature guide documents this caveat; the short API rustdoc does not enumerate it. Observational input masking remains separate, and provider working history is never replaced with a masked hook projection.
- With single-tool rounds enabled, the host instruction is inserted before the private Session Prompts suffix. Diagnostic exports retain that instruction, and host protocol replacement leaves opaque attachment bytes unchanged. Trim reconstruction preserves the canonical host prompt before reapplying the transient instruction. Ordinary no-attachment and no-system behavior is preserved. The guide documents a reserved-heading limitation: host text (workspace files, skill/tool descriptions) with a standalone `## Session Prompts` after a blank line can be mistaken for the private suffix, leaving later tool-format/framing instructions unchanged and masking later host text in diagnostic/export views. Dispatch still rejects disallowed multi-tool calls; a failed turn may need a client retry. Use another heading in host text. This sync documents the limitation without changing runtime behavior.
- Independent child transcripts withhold attachment-bearing parent protocol scope, while same-agent inline SOP continues the primary transcript without attachment tools. Ordinary non-attachment child protocol inheritance is pre-existing and intentionally unchanged by this repair; this is not general child-context isolation.

The additive incarnation migration adopts valid unbound legacy attachments and removes mismatches/orphans. Historical legacy ownership cannot be proved retroactively; reset questionable old sessions. Feature-off does not delete stored attachments or scrub old histories. Downgrading and clearing history with an older binary can leave attachments that reappear after re-upgrade; reset affected sessions before downgrade and retain the backup.

`ToolResultMessage` adds the public `session_prompt_tool_result: bool` field.
Out-of-tree Rust struct literals must initialize it: use `false` for ordinary
results and preserve the host-derived value when replaying existing results.
Exhaustive patterns must bind the new field or use `..`; forwarding code must
preserve the flag.
The reserved key is exported as
`zeroclaw_api::model_provider::SESSION_PROMPT_HISTORY_RESULT_KEY`. Absent
serialized fields default to `false`; ordinary serialized results omit the
field. Marked results retain the existing native host key or text privacy
marker through Chat replay, including when a tool hook changed the original
call name. This is privacy provenance, not a capability or ACP prompt support.

The legacy public `SessionBackend::delete_session_owned` SQLite implementation retains master's two-autocommit deletion behavior. Runtime Chat now uses the transactional key-set replacement; external Rust consumers needing atomic owner/message/attachment deletion should use `delete_session_key_set_owned`. Retiring or transactionally repairing the legacy method is deferred to a separate follow-up.

The runtime loop facade additionally exposes `scope_required_session_prompt_section` for channel orchestration. This is an additive Rust API; it grants no tool capability or wire access.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Reset/delete affected sessions with this version first when stored attachments must be removed; back up SQLite and restore the previous known-good binary/client pair. Reverting this feature restores previous source behavior but does not retroactively clean stored data. Keep the backup for migration recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = false` and restart. This stops injection/tools, not attachment persistence, redaction of previously marked history or the feature-off lifecycle/retention changes described above. Reset/delete is required to remove attachments.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_BUSY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `channel-runtime-new-session-failed`, strict-preview refusal or prompt-budget errors before provider dispatch. Modifying-hook callbacks not firing for classified private requests is intentional; deployments relying on hook transforms/cancellation/model selection must account for this exclusion and conservative feature-off cases. Inspect lifecycle/approval metadata without dumping prompt bodies. An idle old WebSocket refusing after committed deletion is expected behavior, not a reason to bypass the owner fence.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
