prs.title: fix(memory): preserve owner in delegation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; refreshed through 6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserve the owned session's full principal scope when a delegate builds target-agent memory. The owner, namespace, and tenant remain fixed; only the target agent changes. The registered delegate and its nested/parallel instances retain that scope, and target construction refuses when it cannot preserve it.
  - Rebuild canonical memory tools and skill aliases over the owned handle, preserving names, schemas, restrictions, and locked arguments. Since #11174, this goes through master's one-time native memory binding: skill aliases over the registry's own memory tools follow the binding, so canonical tools and aliases move together. The delegate is bound to the owner only after that rebind succeeds, so a refused routing leaves nothing bound.
  - Forward principal-scoped operations through `AgentScopedMemory` and `RetrievalPipeline`. Private recalls bypass the cache whose keys lack an owner dimension. This also restores owned SQLite chat sessions' own memory tools, recall, and configured autosave.
  - Bind factory-built delegates from `Memory::principal_scope` before canonical tools or aliases can execute. Owned sessions, including administrators, refuse background delegation and every result-management action before accessing task rows or result files. Synchronous and parallel delegation remain available under existing policy.
  - Add regressions for owner/target isolation, alias reconstruction, nested factory construction, private-cache separation, and refusal of background creation, foreign results, legacy results, waits, and cancellation. Document the owned-session restriction in the authentication guide.
- **Scope boundary:** No new grants, memory schema, config keys, or RPC plane selection. Shared operator delegation retains its existing behavior. This does not migrate or remove existing result artifacts, nor establish isolation for every other tool: `spawn_subagent` and `execute_pipeline` remain tracked by #11239/#11266. Safe restoration of owned background tasks is tracked by #11995. The routing-order refinement discussed in #11174 remains separate; a routing error currently aborts owned RPC session creation/rehydration.
- **Blast radius:** Owned RPC sessions, including named administrators and restored sessions; direct, bounded, independent, nested, and parallel delegated memory; skill builtin wrappers; memory backend wrappers; runtime tool factories; external Rust consumers of `Tool`, `Memory`, and `AllToolsResult`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11198. Related #11239, #11266, #11174, #11409, #11995.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `agent`, `channel`, `memory`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `priority:p0`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `topic:identity-access`, `release:v0.9.0`.

### Issue and solution in plain terms

A signed-in user's session can ask another agent for help. Previously that helper received fresh memory tools pointing at shared storage, so it could read shared notes and save the user's notes there. The helper now uses that user's private memory for the target agent, including when a skill alias invokes the tool or delegation takes another hop.

Background task results still use an agent-based visibility boundary. The PR therefore refuses that route for owned sessions until task records and output files can enforce principal ownership. The refusal applies to administrators' owned sessions too; their private memory remains private.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: deterministic regressions exercise the actual delegate, factory, memory tools, and SQLite/task stores with synthetic owners. No additional manual browser or terminal rendering claim is made.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** 2595327a0ec8208800dd5c9acd9bfa58b86ce1e5, including the current `master` merge. The merge was conflict-free; the interaction in tool assembly preserves both the owner binding and master's host-name reservations.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39876483288) passed on this revision: 39 successful jobs, no failed jobs, and a successful `CI Required Gate`. `Test` ran the workspace suites, including the new runtime/memory/API regressions. `Parallel Runtime Test` exercised runtime and channels concurrently. `Lint`, `Format`, plugin-runtime checks, platform builds, and `Docs Style` also passed, covering the shared contracts, factory wiring, and documentation.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live authenticated browser/zerocode session or external model-provider acceptance was performed. The affected execution paths are covered with production tools and factories, real SQLite/task stores, and controlled providers; no frontend rendering or transport implementation changes.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The refreshed CI `Test` job reported 19,355 workspace tests passed (42 skipped); the additional test groups passed 189 and 7 tests respectively. Each named regression below appears as `PASS` in that job.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0; no output
  $ git diff --check origin/master...HEAD
  exit 0; no output
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source-traced both RPC owner-routing callers, the factory binding before tool publication, alias reconstruction, and the early background/management refusal. Session construction and rehydration return on routing failure. No production data, external provider, migration, or rollback rehearsal was used. Local Cargo test/clippy runs were not repeated; the refreshed required CI run supplies that coverage.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for visual rendering: no frontend, terminal layout, or rendering code changes. The new localized denial is checked at the production tool-result boundary by the refusal regressions below.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above; the `delegate` tool and skill-wrapper execution interface. The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39876483288/job/120163217120) exercises these regressions:
  - `owned_delegate_child_recalls_and_stores_only_in_owners_target_plane`, `owned_parallel_delegate_stores_only_in_owners_target_plane`, and `independent_delegate_alias_inherits_owner_before_nested_capture` check owner and target selection against shared, caller-agent, and other-owner sentinels.
  - `routing_rebinds_memory_skill_aliases_to_the_owners_private_plane` and `owned_bounded_delegate_memory_aliases_rebind_without_changing_parent` check alias restrictions and private writes.
  - `factory_delegate_inherits_private_memory_owner_before_any_action`, `owned_background_delegate_refuses_before_creating_shared_results`, and `owned_delegate_management_refuses_same_alias_and_legacy_results` check canonical/alias refusal, no provider/task/artifact creation, no foreign-result disclosure, and unchanged task status after denied cancellation. The fixture first proves the same artifacts are readable by the shared operator.
  - `cached_pipeline_keeps_private_recalls_per_owner`, `routed_session_memory_on_the_agent_stack_reaches_the_owners_plane`, `routing_rebinds_memory_skill_aliases_to_the_owners_private_plane` and `refused_routing_leaves_the_delegate_unbound` cover the cache, the real memory stack, skill aliases and the routing order.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The refusal tests assert `success: false`, empty output, and the English catalogue message: “Background delegation and task management are unavailable in principal-owned sessions until task results enforce principal ownership. Use synchronous delegation instead.” This is tool-result evidence, not a browser screenshot or live-client smoke test.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Owned background and management calls are denied before task or artifact access; synchronous/parallel writes land only in the owner's target plane. Existing shared-operator controls remain supported.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Duplicate local workspace builds were omitted in favor of the required CI matrix on the exact refreshed head. No runtime behavior was changed after that head was pushed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** No. Existing memory access is restricted to the owner, and unsafe owned background actions are refused.
- **New external network calls?** No.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** No.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No; regression data is synthetic.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** Yes. Delegated recall and restored owned-session recall can put the owner's private memory into provider context. Existing memory provenance applies; owner/tenant/namespace/agent predicates and cache bypass keep other scopes out. Owned background results are refused before publication or retrieval.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** No for owned background/task-management calls and external code constructing `AllToolsResult` with a struct literal. Shared operator behavior is preserved.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No config keys, environment variables, or CLI flags. The `delegate` tool now returns the localized refusal above for owned background/management requests; the authentication guide documents it.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Exact upgrade steps:** Use synchronous or parallel delegation for owned sessions; do not remove ownership or elevate permissions to restore background access. External Rust callers must use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools` instead of a struct literal. The new `Memory::principal_scope` method has a default, but private-memory views must preserve the documented scope contract.
- **Other behavior to account for:** On SQLite, owned chat sessions' configured autosave and recall now reach private memory through the wrapper stack; with autosave enabled this persists messages that previously failed to save. Backends without principal support refuse private operations. ACP/rehydrated sessions built with memory excluded retain that exclusion. Existing shared result artifacts are retained and are not migrated.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After landing, `git revert <landed-squash-commit>` restores the prior implementation. Reverting also restores the isolation defect; restrict affected owned-session/delegation access before rollback. Private rows remain stored and are not moved into shared storage.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Existing tool policy can remove delegation while investigating; keep owned background actions denied until #11995 is implemented and reviewed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** The intentional `delegate-owned-background-unavailable` message for owned background/management calls; “owned delegate memory requires target configuration” when a private target cannot be constructed; “memory alias ... cannot rebind its builtin target” for unsupported aliases; RPC session construction/rehydration refusing when memory routing fails.

The background containment and factory-owner changes from @Aarlington's #11409 retain their original commit authorship. This PR incorporates those focused changes and does not supersede that PR's broader prerequisite stack.

prs.title: ci(rust): bump routine toolchains to 1.99.1
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Upgrade routine CI, release, platform, audit, desktop, and development toolchain pins to Rust 1.99.1 so the build surfaces use the same compiler.
  - Pin the slim, Bookworm, and Alpine Rust builder images to 1.99.1 with matching registry digests in `dev/ci/container-base-images.toml`, the Dockerfiles it generates, and the local CI image. The current diff changes these three Rust builder images; other base-image digests are already on `master`.
  - Address Rust 1.99 diagnostics by removing needless closure borrows, replacing deprecated atomic `fetch_update` calls with `try_update`, and improving affected test assertions without new lint allowances. Restore original `is_empty()` assertions on maps, custom containers, and vectors whose elements do not implement `PartialEq`.
- **Scope boundary:** No `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changes. The declared MSRV remains Rust 1.96.0. Historical build records and fixed-version test fixtures retain their recorded versions.
- **Blast radius:** CI, release builders, local CI containers, demo/relay image builds, and Windows test scope contracts use the newer routine compiler. Runtime behavior, configuration, APIs, permissions, and security policy are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11834. Related #9527.

### What this does, simply

This moves ZeroClaw's routine builds and checks to Rust 1.99.1, including the pinned container images used to compile releases. It also handles the compiler and Clippy diagnostics exposed by the upgrade, so warnings can remain errors without adding exceptions. The minimum supported Rust version stays at 1.96.0; the replacement atomic API is available at that floor.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - this changes build tooling and compiler compatibility, with no user-facing workflow requiring manual verification.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On head `e6c3fe39c9`, [Quality Gate run 40807183769](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40807183769) passed Format, Lint, Test, the default/no-default/plugin/32-bit checks, MSRV, targeted Windows Clippy, Windows compilation and smoke/recovery checks, Installer Drift, and the feature-specific tests. These cover compiler compatibility, the declared floor, generated surfaces, and the affected test assertions. [Docker Image PR Check run 40807183439](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40807183439) passed all source-image builds, including amd64/arm64 and Wasm variants. [Desktop App Check run 40807183454](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40807183454) passed on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI is not entirely green. On this head, Security failed on `RUSTSEC-2026-0414` for `pulldown-cmark 0.13.4` in the unchanged lockfile, which also failed CI Required Gate. prs.title: fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11225 and #11234. This is the cumulative recut, including adopted containment and steering repairs; review its full owned delta, not only the latest test commit. The separately scoped SOP containment is #11220.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Withhold `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` from every non-admin RPC session, including wildcard selectors, because these tools do not enforce principal ownership. Keep `sessions_current`, which accepts no foreign target.
  - Withhold principal-unaware cron, schedule, peer-messaging and nested-executor paths, including captured skill aliases. Retained delegates carry the narrowing into bounded, parallel and independent descendants; an Agent without the concrete delegate handle drops that entry. The canonical delegate remains available only when its selectors and retained handle permit it.
  - Apply one complete tool posture to prompt admission and steering. Steering resolves authority when consumed and again after memory writes, so the next accepted steering applies current withholding. This does not add continuous revocation between every action. Narrowing is monotonic: a later grant does not restore withdrawn tools to that live Agent.
  - Authorize cron patches against the actual stored row after acquiring its SQLite write transaction, and retain current authority through the synchronous commit. A queued demotion, revoked grant, changed owner or changed job type cannot reuse an earlier decision.
  - Retain #11234's session-authority and error-handling repairs: immediate approval-channel refusal propagates, deferred installation logs a sanitized refusal, and a Chat running-state write failure preserves the session for retry while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery behavior. The latest commit serializes the deferred test's process-wide log capture using the existing writer-then-hook locks.
- **Source of truth:** current grants come from the existing authorization authority. The posture is derived at each applicable boundary; registry removal and shared delegate withholding are narrowing effects, not a second live grant policy.
- **Scope boundary:** this contains principal-unaware tools; it does not make their stores principal-aware, add shared-execution credential renewal, or propagate principal ceilings into SOP runs. #11220 owns the SOP entry/workshop containment. Scheduled work, channels, CLI turns and existing independent triggers are not converted into principal-owned execution by this PR. The #11225 routing integration and full current-parent integration remain separate gates.
- **Blast radius:** RPC Chat/ACP construction, prompts and steering, aliases and delegate descendants, cron patch commits, and the inherited session-authority/storage boundary. Non-admin sessions lose the listed tools even with wildcard selectors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11127; its containment closure also requires #11220 to land. Depends on #11225. Depends on #11234. Related #11220, #11410, #12046, #8290 and #12131.

### What this does, simply

Two people can use the same agent without owning each other's conversations. Until the cross-session tools check that ownership themselves, non-admin sessions cannot use them or regain them through the named contained cron, peer-message or nested-executor entry points exposed by that session. SOP entry and workshop containment remains in #11220. The same restrictions apply when a former administrator steers an existing turn after demotion. Ordinary tools and the current-session tool remain available when the caller's grants allow them.

The headless tool set withheld here is `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run`, `cron_list`, `cron_runs`, `cron_remove`, `schedule` and `send_message_to_peer`. The session tools, `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and aliases of the withheld tools or `delegate` are also removed. These restrictions are interim containment, not a claim that the OIDC isolation milestone is complete.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for an additional manual setup: dispatcher tests drive real session/store boundaries with synthetic principals, controlled demotion and competing writes. Live provider acceptance remains a separate milestone gate.

### How I tested

- **Current repair revision:** `0efa2558924e60fc3397720ffdf4f12e4459ec0a`. This retains the additive four-line log-test fix `9684cf3b5008fb64a17a2b3fc71650f4578f279d` and merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. The merge required no manual resolutions; the owned patch is unchanged, while the incoming master changes include persisted-log access containment. Both dependency files exactly match master.
- **Exact-revision local results:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::dispatch:: agent::turn::provider_call:: steering principal_scope principal_memory withhold --test-threads=8` passed all 642 selected tests with no failures or ignored tests. `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. These ran on macOS with jobs=2, incremental=0, debug=0 and an isolated Cargo target.
- **Validation retry:** the initial attempt reused another worktree's Cargo target and failed to see PR-specific trait methods already present in this source. The unchanged head passed after rebuilding in its own target directory; no source suppression or test bypass was added.
- **Current hosted evidence:** new-head checks remain required. The merge and test repair were independently checked. The unchanged dependency files adopt #12129's [successful Security and plugin matrix](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972); those feature suites were not repeated locally.
- **Historical hosted evidence on the preceding PR head:** d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158 passes [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534955), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202737438), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534799) and [Docs Style](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202723889). Test reports 19,572 passed and 42 skipped in its main group. The source-confirmed shared-log race was not an observed failure in this run.
- **Earlier failed gate:** [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534613) and the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124212229592) fail on the inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories, RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424. #12129 has merged the dependency repair; it was not integrated into this preceding head. These failures are not waived.
- **Boundary evidence:** hosted tests cover same-agent foreign-history/append refusal; wildcard and named selectors; canonical and aliased headless tools; descendant withholding; cron transaction contention; prompt admission after waits; and steering demotion both before consumption and during a memory write. Positive controls retain the caller's own session, allowed ordinary tools and unchanged administrator behavior.
- **Steering repair provenance:** dfe06dcf76b20533e622ba7a74b5b02b70335f65 is in the branch. [Its adoption check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#pullrequestreview-5706814602) links the exact earlier hosted steering regressions. The [session-error update](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#issuecomment-6528701580) records four passing focused tests, formatting and runtime all-target Clippy on d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158.
- **Beyond CI:** the earlier repair reports include negative controls; they are historical evidence on their named revisions, not new executions on this test-only commit.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: authorization/tool availability and error propagation are proved at dispatcher/store boundaries; this PR introduces no presentation-sensitive interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the linked hosted run covers d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158. Current integrated-head local results are recorded above; historical hosted results are not attributed to it.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the linked Test log records the named boundary regressions and their passing results.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** demotion or revocation during the tested waits denies the affected operation and preserves foreign data; unchanged permitted controls succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace, native Windows runtime suite and live IdP flows have not been rerun locally for this four-line test repair. Complete provider, migration and rollback acceptance is not claimed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The owned containment narrows tools and rechecks existing authority.
- New external network calls? No. The inherited #11225 slice places principal-scoped private recall in the existing provider context and restores private autosave; this containment slice adds no new payload type.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No in this slice; the existing authority supplies current decisions.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use synthetic roster identities.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes in inherited #11225: private recall reaches provider context under the existing provenance and owner/tenant/namespace/agent filters. This containment slice narrows the tool registry and adds no new text source.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: recalled memory remains untrusted context and must retain its ownership and provenance filtering. The containment risk is an omitted tool or a missed revocation boundary; foreign-data refusal, mutation preservation and allowed controls cover the specified paths. Related execution and storage work remains explicitly separate.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No. Non-admin RPC sessions, including wildcard accounts, lose the tools named above and their aliases. Previously narrowed live Agents do not regain tools on a later grant; a new or rehydrated session is needed after an authorized policy change. The inherited #11225 slice also refuses owned-background delegation and its task-management operations for owned principals, including named administrators.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new configuration or CLI option in this containment slice.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No toolchain-floor change. The public Rust `SteeringPosture` gains `withhold_principal_unaware_session_tools`; callers constructing it with struct literals must derive that field from their admission policy; the all-false default is unscoped. The inherited #11225 API requires former `AllToolsResult` struct-literal callers to use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`. The cumulative branch also carries the separately reviewed APIs from #11225 and #11234.
- Exact upgrade steps: operators must account for the restricted non-admin tool set and coordinate #11220's SOP containment and the declared parents. Single-operator and currently authorized administrator sessions retain their ordinary allowed tools. Principal-aware replacements and shared-execution renewal remain follow-up work; granting administrator access is a broad authority change, not an equivalent scoped replacement.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** after landing, `git revert <landed-PR-squash-commit>`, reconciling dependent PRs. There is no persisted migration in the owned containment slice. Reverting containment reopens the described foreign-session/headless access; keep affected tools unavailable through existing agent policy until a safe replacement is deployed. Reverting only 9684cf3b5008fb64a17a2b3fc71650f4578f279d restores the test race and does not undo containment.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** no new toggle. Existing agent tool policy can retain restrictions during rollback.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** non-admin `Unknown tool` responses for withheld capabilities are expected. A foreign transcript read/append, a queued cron mutation after revoked authority, or missing ordinary tools for an unchanged permitted control is a regression.

## Supersede Attribution

This is not a replacement PR. Adopted repairs from @Aarlington and @JordanTheJet retain their commit authorship and the prerequisite history. No contributor branch or published history was rewritten.

prs.title: fix(security): require administrator authority for SOP execution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require current administrator authority for `sops/run` and every `sops/decide` decision, including when a non-admin has wildcard selectors and `tools:execute`. SOP steps and their descendants do not carry a scoped caller's principal limits.
  - Retain that authority through synchronous start/approval storage effects after decision-model and engine waits; a contended store refuses immediately rather than holding authority while waiting for a writer.
  - Withhold `sop_execute`, `sop_approve`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, and their skill aliases from non-admin RPC sessions. Also withhold `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and delegate aliases that cannot carry the restriction.
  - Keep direct delegation for callers with unrestricted selectors, binding bounded, independent, background, parallel, and nested child builders to the originating credential's live authority resolver. The canonical policy remains `RpcInboundAuth`; no copied grant decision authorizes a child registry.
- **Scope boundary:** Cross-credential steering and combined permission checks with credential renewal remain separate work under RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; this branch does not implement them. This is interim containment, not principal propagation inside SOP steps; RPC SOP authoring and non-RPC triggers retain their existing policies. The cumulative diff includes the session-authority prerequisite from #11234 and current master; unrelated session-data and cron repairs from the supplemental drafts are not imported.
- **Blast radius:** Non-admin SOP execution, approval, workshop use, and unsafe nested tool exposure; administrators and the shared operator retain configured access, and ordinary admitted tools remain usable.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11123. Depends on #11234. Related #11408, #11410, #11230, and #11169.

### What this does, simply

A user could reach a procedure through a tool alias or an allowed agent and then run work outside that user's permissions. Until procedures can carry those permissions into every step, only administrators may start or decide them, and non-admin sessions do not receive tools that bypass that restriction.

```text
RPC run / decision ── current admin authority ── guarded storage effect
                         │ no
                         └───────────────────── FORBIDDEN

non-admin session ── ordinary tools / controlled delegate
                         └─ child registry rechecks live authority
                            └─ SOP entry tools and unsafe builders absent
```

The [earlier review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11220#pullrequestreview-5364022889) identifies the tool-entry and descendant gaps; this carries the SOP-specific repairs from [#11408](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408) and workshop regressions from [#11410](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410), retaining their authorship and adapting their delegate propagation pattern to live resolution.

### Landing and shared-helper reconciliation

Land #11234 before this PR; the supplemental drafts must drop the SOP changes carried here when they refresh. #11169 must rebase onto this admission contract: one `SopAdmissionCheck` returns a held `SopEffectGuard`, and execution must keep the administrator predicate and nonblocking storage boundary rather than restoring its older wildcard predicate or a check returning `()`.

An integration probe against #11169 at `908a035d3f6b3734fcdf471785def4f6c3a1ad00` reports conflicts in `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `sop/dispatch.rs`, `sop/executor.rs`, and `sop/mod.rs`; its new ingress/cancel methods and authenticated approver changes still require that rebase and combined validation before landing.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: compare the same scenarios with the previous head `ec5fc1c28760c63c9da9ea4d74e18379c146a2a8`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Local authenticated JSON-RPC and Chat/ACP tool dispatch used by CLI/TUI clients; model providers in the regressions are synthetic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A non-admin roster principal with `sops:execute`, `tools:execute`, wildcard selectors, and an approval-gated procedure; retain an administrator control.
- **Steps to run:** Request `sops/run` and an approval/denial through `sops/decide`; ask the session to invoke the direct SOP tools and a built-in skill alias, then repeat as administrator. The `sop_principal` tests also exercise a queued admin demotion and workshop persistence.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Non-admin RPC effects return `FORBIDDEN`; withheld tool calls return `Unknown tool` and leave runs/proposals unchanged; administrator controls and ordinary tools succeed.
- **Prior behavior (before):** Wildcard non-admins could pass the RPC guard, and model-facing SOP tools could enter procedures without the caller's principal ceiling.

### How I tested

#### Current revision: 0ddaef7c1a65aa9a934c03bbfbcef52591a4b65d

The latest change brings the existing writer-then-hook locks from #11234 into the copied deferred-approval log-capture test, keeping both guards through its asynchronous waits. It then additively merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. The owned production code is unchanged by this update; both dependency files exactly match master.

On this exact revision, all five selected tests passed together with `--test-threads=8`: deferred approval recheck, immediate approval refusal, provider payload capture, Chat state-write retry, and ACP checkpoint failure. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. The test command was `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume llm_request_payload_redacts_truncates_and_off_omits chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session --test-threads=8`.

The four-line repair and master integration were independently checked. New-head hosted checks remain required; the previous Wasmtime failure is addressed by the now-merged #12129 dependency files. The plugin feature matrix was not rerun locally; [#12129's successful run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972) is inherited dependency evidence. The full local workspace and live two-provider acceptance were not rerun. Shared-execution authority/renewal is the separate RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; #11169 integration remains a prerequisite.

#### Earlier integration: f09b08f749cba368959ae05cbbdf8a264b3f033f

This head incorporates the #11234 session-error repair and an additive merge of master at 1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29. Immediate approval-channel installation errors now fail the request; deferred installation remains nonblocking and logs a sanitized refusal. A Chat state-write failure preserves the live session for retry, while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery eviction. The Fluent merge preserves all SOP and turn-recovery entries.

Historical local validation on that exact combined revision:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session
# 853 passed; 0 failed; 1 existing live-model test ignored.
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Both passed.
```

[Hosted CI for that earlier head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41097867322) provides the remaining platform/workspace matrix. Security reports five inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424); the merged lockfile is identical to the pinned master. The hosted run is complete: Security and its aggregate required gate failed; the other required checks passed or were skipped as configured. A later metadata-only advisory risk-report job was cancelled; it is not source-validation evidence. The repair and merge were independently checked, but this is not whole-stack approval or resolution of the steering design and #11169 integration.

#### Earlier local validation: 137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2

The following results are preserved for this earlier revision, not attributed to the current head.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The historical local run below preceded hosted CI; current-revision evidence is listed above.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation is macOS with Rust/Cargo 1.97.1; cross-platform and full-workspace coverage remain with CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0

  1883 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored

  6 tests OK; no added links
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the registry/factory wiring and the #11169 merge probe; automated controls exercise real run/proposal persistence, SQLite writer contention, queued demotion, credential expiry/revocation, aliases, and all supported delegate construction paths. No external identity-provider or interactive TUI smoke test was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2`, local JSON-RPC/tool regressions; local logs in `tmp/oidc-11220-validation/` in the implementation worktree.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Runtime assertions verify `FORBIDDEN` or `Unknown tool: <name>` and unchanged durable/in-memory SOP state, with successful administrator controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A queued principal demotion prevents SOP/workshop effects; a queued config writer cannot deadlock a nested read; busy SQLite refuses before start/resume mutation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace/all-feature tests were not duplicated locally; the selected suites cover the changed boundaries. The existing two ignored runtime cases remain ignored.

The runtime test linker emits the pre-existing macOS `__eh_frame section too large (max 16MB)` warning; the same diagnostic was reproduced on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` during prerequisite validation, and both builds completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; this restricts existing access.
- New external network calls? **No**.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**; delegate builders retain the originating connection's non-secret authentication evidence in a live resolver, so current revocation/expiry and grants are checked rather than a stored admission decision; no bearer is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**; fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; unsafe tool capabilities are removed from the executable registry and its advertised surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A descendant must not inherit another later caller's authority; each child retains its originating resolver while current policy remains canonical in the auth layer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; non-admin wildcard SOP access is intentionally removed, including deny/amend/revise, and unsafe nested builders/aliases are withheld.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** new setting, flag, or wire method; existing methods have stricter authorization and localized refusal text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**.
- Exact upgrade steps: Use a trusted administrator/shared operator for SOP execution and decisions; adding `tools:execute` alone no longer restores access. Parent session tools narrow at the next prompt admission; recreate a session after promotion to regain removed tools, and retry busy-store requests once contention clears.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge/squash commit while retaining the #11234 prerequisite; no data migration is required, but reverting restores the unsafe non-admin paths.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; the restriction is deliberate and fails closed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `FORBIDDEN` on SOP run/decision, `Unknown tool` for withheld names, localized SOP storage-busy refusals, and matching RPC authorization-denied records.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(gateway): forward plugin webhooks to the core over RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11320** and **#11186** (`zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the gateway's core RPC seam). The branch merges #11320 at its current head `864b58d76e` (with #11319 `c352574198`, #11339 and #11165 `19e41b09fa` beneath it) and #11186 at its current head `ed92285a87` (restacked 2026-10-23 and refreshed 2026-10-29, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land. Review this PR's own commits: `d15729ebff` (the forwarder), `5926ddde14` (docs), `c02e5c0bac` (the in-process seam tests get a TUI signing key), `7702fe138c` (the forwarder's failure records keep the webhook path out) `c02417bfac` (change filter path restored after the restack) and `6d8ed835a8` (the forwarder ends a connection the daemon has stopped recognising, so the link dials again; from Greptile's review); `de5cd570ab` (the connector fix) is superseded by #11186's `535b43829a`.
- **Refresh of 2026-10-29 (`fee8af1cb8`):** merges #11320's new head, which brings master `5a51398dd5` (the one `rpc/types.rs` conflict against it was master editing a doc comment inside the block #11165 moved into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; the moved-out file stays and the doc line now lives on the proto copy) and #11320's admission re-check: the daemon re-resolves the forwarder's live grants at admission instead of trusting the binding its dispatch task copied, so a revoked or narrowed caller is refused and the forwarder answers 503 for it, as for any core refusal. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-10-29 (`6d8ed835a8`):** merges #11320's `864b58d76e` (`2f1fa249a4`: a rename or delete over the socket now refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; the forwarder connects as the shared operator and is not affected) and adds `6d8ed835a8`, from Greptile's review of this PR: when a policy change removes or revokes the gateway's identity while its connection is open, the daemon keeps the socket and answers `AUTH_REQUIRED`, and the link redialed only after a close, so webhooks stayed 503 after the operator restored access. The forwarder now ends the connection at the first such answer (record `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) and the redial is accepted once access is back, or refused into the slow backoff while it is not; `FORBIDDEN` stays on the connection. Two tests: the close seen from both sides, and the whole sequence over a local socket ending with a webhook served on the new connection.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`9138333811`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. The one conflict was the workspace `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`: this branch adds the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` and `zeroclaw-rpc-client` members and master appends `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`; both kept. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-11-03 (`364014755c`):** merges #11320's `d4517a7845` (`a0425fbf4c`, `4a099711c1`, `364014755c`), which records the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge in master's new runtime-composition policy and makes the two in-flight-cap tests hold the log writer's test lock, so their 1024-dispatch bursts cannot drop the persisted-log tests' records under the parallel runtime gate; both failures showed on this PR's run too. It also takes the cascade refusal's message from the catalog, from Greptile's review there. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Restack of 2026-10-23 (`bb5eb8a1ca`, `c02417bfac`, `54dc89c97f`):** #11165 and #11186 were refreshed onto master by their author on October 22, so this branch merges #11320's restacked head (which carries #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319) and then #11186 `ed92285a87`, and is mergeable with master again. The hand-resolved files against #11320 were the CI workflow registry, the CI guide, the plugin backend change filter (each side's lines kept; the filter's own test caught one path the first pass dropped, restored in `c02417bfac`), the root `Cargo.toml` (the rpc-client member, dependency, dev-dependencies and the two-process test target on top of #11320's) and the proto boundary test, taken from #11186's head, which already reconciles #11165's new wording with the rpc-client checks. Against #11186 only `inproc.rs` conflicted, and this branch takes #11186's file: its `535b43829a` is the connector fix this PR carried as `de5cd570ab`, so that commit is now redundant here and ownership sits in #11186 as asked, and its `e4bd5853e9` treats the in-process connection as remote in every local-only check, alongside this PR's `plugin-webhook/*` refusal arm.
- **Fix for #11186 on top of the merge** (`fix(rpc): release the in-process connector's context when its generation retires`): the daemon hands the gateway a clone of the generation's `InprocConnector` through its reload controls, and the connector kept the generation's `RpcContext` (its sessions and their lifecycle leases) until the last clone dropped. With #10621, a reload waits for that state to drain before it releases process ownership, so `reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership` failed 3 of 3 runs on the merge. Sealing admission now releases the context in the same critical section, `bind` leaves a sealed connector unbound, and a `connect` waiting for a bind gives up once the generation is sealed. Two new connector tests cover it, and the daemon test passes. It belongs in #11186: I asked for it there (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11186#issuecomment-5942108575; it cherry-picks cleanly onto `84f31b29cb`), and this branch drops it once #11186 has it.
- **Audacity88's review (both blockers):**
  - **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs.** Some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. `7702fe138c` drops the path from the five `plugin_webhook_core_*` records, which keep their error key and code. `core_failure_records_keep_a_secret_path_out` sends a secret-shaped path through each core failure and asserts no record contains it. The daemon-side part belongs to #11319 (`fc5f3e95b9`: the ingress's route-closed, reply-dropped and worker-answer records, plus the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record). It arrives here through #11320. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master.
  - **Removed-binding admission.** Merging #11320 at `d6ef5dc0af` (`853e49dfab`) brings its fail-closed fix `fcf4f6121c`: a route whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` binding a live config write removed is refused until reload retires it. #11320's `plugin_webhook_dispatch_refuses_a_published_route_once_its_binding_is_removed` proves that interval, and the forwarder answers that refusal 503 (`core_rpc_errors_map_to_503`). The two-process test still checks the state after reload.
- **#10621 and the standalone gateway:** a running daemon now owns its config state exclusively, so `zeroclaw gateway start` on the daemon's config dir exits with `config lifecycle is already owned`, on master too. Next to a daemon, the standalone gateway therefore runs on a config dir of its own and names the daemon's socket with `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`. The gateway API guide documents this, and the two-process test runs that way.
- **Channel scoping from #11320:** the forwarder connects as the shared operator, which is `admin`, so `allowed_channels` does not narrow it. A channel instance or agent with `accept_injected_webhooks = false` still refuses its dispatches: that path answers 503, logged `plugin_webhook_core_refused`, while the connection stays up and other paths keep forwarding. A connection the daemon has stopped recognising is different: its `AUTH_REQUIRED` answer ends the connection (`6d8ed835a8`, logged `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) so the link dials again. The gateway API guide lists both.
- **What changed and why:**
  - The standalone `zeroclaw gateway` is the separate gateway process that exists today. Its `/plugin/{path}` route used an empty in-process route table and answered 404 for every path. It now forwards each request to the running daemon over the local RPC socket through `plugin-webhook/dispatch`, so channel-plugin webhooks work across the process boundary. The daemon-supervised gateway keeps calling the core ingress in process.
  - Forwarding: shared request validation, base64 body under a process-unique `request_id`, strict result decoding with the reply bound re-checked, the same `outcome_response` mapping as the in-process path, and a best-effort `plugin-webhook/cancel` when the HTTP request is dropped. The daemon decides 404; while it is unreachable every path answers 503.
  - Daemon identity: on Unix the gateway forwards only to a socket whose peer uid equals its own effective uid, checked before any frame is sent. On Windows, where pipe names share one namespace and the server cannot be verified yet, forwarding stays off and the route keeps answering 404.
  - `core_rpc`: one maintain loop serves the in-process and local dialers; the forwarder owns its own `CoreRpc`, separate from the extension other routes can reach.
  - `plugin-webhook/*` are refused on in-process RPC connections as well as WSS (the arm the transport match needs once #11186 is in).
  - A two-process test runs the real daemon and the real standalone gateway binaries.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the supervised gateway's behavior, to vendor webhook handlers, WIT, or config. No gateway service identity (the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials; see Security). The standalone `zeroclaw-gw` binary is #11002.
- **Blast radius:** standalone `zeroclaw gateway` (start, restart, bare); gateway `core_rpc` seam from #11186; RPC transport refusal; CI plugin legs and path filters.
- **Changes to #11186's in-process seam (for its author):** after a lost connection the loop waits a backoff before redialing (it redialed immediately); logs only on state transitions with error keys `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused}` (and `core_rpc_untrusted_peer` for the local dialer); a FORBIDDEN refusal logs at INFO; `CoreRpc` stores a `CoreLink` (Disconnected, Connected, Refused) with `client()` and `is_connected()` unchanged; new public `CoreLink`, `CoreRpc::link()`, and Unix-only `attach_local` and `daemon_endpoint`. Refusals still end the in-process loop. `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)` returns a `Result`, because it builds the live config authority master now requires.
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** route `run_gateway` through `GatewaySupervision::standalone` or make it test-only, so an embedder does not get the old unrouted `/plugin/{path}` (#11568); a scoped service identity for the forwarder's connection, tracked in #11569 under #11002.
- **Merge-order note:** this PR carries the `TransportKind::Inproc` refusal arm and test that #11320's exhaustive match needs with #11186. If #11186 lands before #11320, move them into #11320. The arm must keep refusing `Inproc` with FORBIDDEN, never treat it like `Local`. #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` this arm uses, so if #11289 lands first the arm needs its `RpcDenialReason` (the variants are listed in #11320).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003 (acceptance: separate-process flow). Related #7432 (G4 transport; vendor migration stays under #8850). Related #11000. Related #11002. Depends on #11186.

### What this does, simply

You can run the web gateway on its own with `zeroclaw gateway`. Until now, webhooks meant for channel plugins did not work there, because the plugin routes live in the daemon. Now that gateway passes each plugin webhook to the daemon over the local socket and returns the daemon's answer, exactly as the built-in gateway would. If the daemon is down, senders get 503 so they retry, and nothing is forwarded to a socket owned by another user.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional (Unix).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP (`/plugin/{path}`) plus the local RPC socket.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with an installed channel plugin that claims a webhook path and an enabled agent routing it, plus an empty second config dir for the gateway (for example `~/.zeroclaw-gateway`).
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw daemon --port 0`, then `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET="$HOME/.zeroclaw/data/daemon.sock" zeroclaw --config-dir "$HOME/.zeroclaw-gateway" gateway start -p 18080`, then `curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/plugin/<path> ...` with the plugin's signature header; stop the daemon and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the plugin's normal answer while the daemon runs; 503 `webhook unavailable` while it is down; the answer again after it restarts; after a policy change that removes the gateway's identity, 503 until the operator restores it, then the answer again at the next redial.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 404 `webhook not found` from the standalone gateway for every path.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` runs `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (real binaries) and `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`; `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` runs the forwarder and handler tests and the golden frames; `Test` runs `core_rpc` and the runtime refusal tests; `Lint`; the filter and Windows-scope script tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows is not exercised (forwarding is off there by design); the `plugins cranelift runtime` leg's time against its 20-minute timeout needs measuring on hosted CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `c02e5c0bac`: this PR with #11320 `b5d9ebd577` and #11186 `84f31b29cb` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e   (x3)
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed (38.8s, 38.2s, 39.7s)
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 5 passed ; ok. 61 passed (includes plugin_webhook_boundary)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 650 passed ; test result: ok. 683 passed   (includes core_rpc::tests::inproc::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2) ; --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged) ; ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc:: ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
FAILED. 798 passed; 1 failed ; FAILED. 104 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock and a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below; reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership passes)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-client ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
ok. 14 passed ; ok. 31 passed ; ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, gateway, rpc-client, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and both e2e targets) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5483 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, Windows scope, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (#11320 lists the runs), and this stack does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` on macOS stops only on the pre-existing unused `std::sync::mpsc` import in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` (no lint in any changed runtime file).
- **Known residual risk:** the deadline test asserts the gateway did not log its own `plugin_webhook_core_timeout`, which fires one second after the core deadline, so a very slow runner could time out on the gateway side first. It passed every run so far, including under saturated CPU. If it flakes in CI, assert the daemon-side worker timeout record instead of the gateway log's absence.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Before the restack onto today's master, the two-process suite passed 13 consecutive runs, 3 of them with every CPU saturated; after it, all 4 runs passed. Mutations caught by the new tests: the cancel guard never firing, the stop guard removed, Inproc allowed, Inproc retrying refusals, redialing immediately after a loss, and trusting any peer uid.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Restack onto #11320 `f3364f9c67` and #11186 `ed92285a87` (head `0f5182fcf0`, 2026-10-23):** the whole suite again on `54dc89c97f` plus `0f5182fcf0`: rpc-client (16), proto (32), api and infra (339), gateway with and without `plugins-wasm`, the plugin webhook golden frames (5, x2, fixtures unchanged) and all 12 scenarios, runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` (107), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` (5), the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (3, passed twice after `0f5182fcf0`; before it, `the_reloaded_daemon_decides_who_owns_a_forwarded_path` failed on master's new refusal of a full save over an existing config file, which the test now replaces on purpose with `force_save`), architecture (85), `cargo generate openrpc --check` in sync, workspace check, `--no-default-features` with `-D warnings`, clippy on the touched crates, the root binary and both root e2e targets, and runtime clippy, the comment hygiene, change filter, Windows scope, docs and links gates, and the parallel runtime gate, all green.
- **Refresh for Audacity88's review (head `7702fe138c`):** the same suite again: gateway lib 33 plugin webhook tests with the new one, golden frames (x2 plus all 12), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`, the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (3 passed, x3), architecture (61), the OpenRPC check, workspace and no-default-features checks, and clippy on the touched crates and the root targets. The only failures are the pre-existing `configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload`, and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning, as on the old master base. Mutation check: putting the path back into a core-failure record fails the new test.
- **Second refresh of 2026-10-29 (head `6d8ed835a8`):** gateway lib `plugin_webhook` and `core_rpc` suites 48 passed (with the two new tests), the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` 3 passed, gateway clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean, workspace check, fmt, and the docs quality and link gates on `api.md`.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (head `9138333811`):** fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; workspace clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` and `core_rpc` suites with `plugins-wasm` 48 passed (both forwarder reconnect tests included); the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` 3 passed; `cargo generate openrpc --check`; the docs quality and link gates on this PR's docs files; cargo-audit 0.22.2 and `cargo deny check advisories` on the merged `Cargo.lock` (no vulnerabilities; RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 are gone with Wasmtime 48.0.8, the six pre-existing allowed unmaintained warnings and a yanked `async-executor 1.14.0` behind the optional AMQP feature remain, as on master); the runtime `rpc::` suite 884 passed at 16 threads
- **Second refresh of 2026-11-03 (head `364014755c`):** fmt; `rpc::dispatch::tests` 588 passed at 16 threads (the cascade test reads the refusal from the catalog); `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed, `dependency_boundary` included; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the two burst tests and the two persisted-log tests together at 4 threads, ten runs, no failure; the parallel runtime gate script itself (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6044 tests, and the channels suite, 2031 tests, at 16 threads) green on this tree, as it was on the unfixed tree: the drop only shows under CI's slower disk, so the fix rests on the writer queue's mechanism rather than a local reproduction
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The Windows cross-check could not run (the msvc target is not installed for the pinned toolchain); a macOS simulation that flipped the new `cfg(unix)`/`cfg(windows)` gates compiled clean with clippy `-D warnings`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: under the default policy (`security.trust_daemon_uid = true`) the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials as the shared operator, which holds every grant. Only the `/plugin/{path}` route uses that connection; it is separate from the core RPC extension other routes can reach.
- New external network calls? No (local socket only)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: webhook headers, including vendor signature headers, now cross the local socket to the daemon. Mitigation: on Unix the gateway verifies the socket's peer uid equals its own before sending anything; on Windows forwarding is off until the pipe server can be verified.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: messages reach the same plugin channel listener as before.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a publicly bound standalone gateway now exposes the daemon's plugin routes on that listener (same exposure as the supervised gateway on that address). The connection appears as a TUI client (`/api/tuis`) and keeps an `--ephemeral` daemon alive. A refused redial writes a daemon audit record, backed off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes. `zeroclaw gateway restart` first POSTs `/admin/shutdown` to the configured address, which stops a supervised gateway listening there (unchanged, now documented).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supervised gateway. Standalone gateway: `/plugin/{path}` changes from 404 for every path to forwarding (Unix); 503 for every path while the daemon is unreachable or the socket belongs to another user; 503 `plugin_webhook_core_unsupported` against an older daemon without the method. New error keys: `plugin_webhook_core_{unavailable,refused,identity_lost,unsupported,unexpected,timeout}`, `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused,untrusted_peer}`, `plugin_webhook_forwarding_disabled` (Windows). Rust API: `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)`; `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` is an optional gateway dependency behind `plugins-wasm`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The standalone gateway resolves the daemon socket like other local clients (`ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` or `<data_dir>/daemon.sock`); next to a running daemon it runs on its own config dir, so it needs `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the standalone gateway returns to answering 404 for plugin routes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** stop the daemon, or build without `plugins-wasm`; `security.trust_daemon_uid = false` without a `[users]` entry for the gateway's uid makes the daemon refuse the connection (webhooks then answer 503).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_core_*` and `core_rpc_*` error keys in the gateway log; 503 bursts on `/plugin/*` from a standalone gateway; `RPC authorization denied` records for the gateway's connection in the daemon log.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
