prs.title: feat(rpc): dispatch plugin webhooks over the core RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at its current head `c352574198` and #11165 at its current head `19e41b09fa` (restacked 2026-10-23, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants), `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test) and `1147d81ac2` and `2aeb57ae9b` (test adaptation to master: config edits go through `publish_test_config` on the read-only live config, `RpcContext::for_authority` sets the ingress handle, the WSS refusal test selects its audit record by reason too, and master's channel WebSocket e2e spreads the plugin channel default), `f3364f9c67` (the RPC socket guide says a rejection record carries the plugin name, channel alias and error key, not the path or the plugin's rejection text; from Greptile's review), `ad161acc03` (admission re-resolves the caller's live grants; from Greptile's and Audacity88's reviews), `13fd6a42e1` (the two denial-record tests drain past a lagged broadcast receiver instead of stopping at it) and `864b58d76e` (a rename or delete refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; from Greptile's review). **Needs the holding-crate exception from #11317 approved first.**
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`d2479d7f2f`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. The one conflict was the workspace `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`: this branch adds the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` member and master appends `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`; both kept. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Fixes after the refresh (`5d17864f14`, `d93d67f79c`, `d4517a7845`):** master's new `runtime-composition-consumer` fixture refuses any `zeroclaw-*` dependency of the runtime that its retained-dependencies policy does not name, and this branch carries #11165's `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge, so the policy gains that entry the way the relay wire contract is recorded (owner `rpc/types.rs`, which re-exports the wire-stable types; the reason names the dispatcher's import). #11165 will need the same line when it refreshes onto master. The parallel runtime gate then failed in master's `persisted_log_reads_refuse_a_scoped_principal`: the two in-flight-cap tests here send `MAX_PLUGIN_WEBHOOK_DISPATCHES_PER_CONNECTION` (1024) dispatches in a tight loop, each leaving a rejection record, and the log writer hands records to its disk worker through a bounded queue of the same size, dropping what it cannot take, whichever test emitted it. Under the gate's 16 threads those tests sort right after the persisted-log tests, so the four denial records that test reads back were dropped and the administrator's query found none. The two burst tests now hold the writer's test lock, which the persisted-log tests hold while they read their records back, so a burst never shares the writer with a test that reads it; the capture tests read the broadcast stream, whose channel is far larger than a burst, and are unaffected. From Greptile's review of this refresh, `d4517a7845` takes the cascade refusal's message from the catalog (`rpc-auth-config-cascade-write-denied`, with the refused path as a Fluent argument) instead of an English literal.
- **#11165 (restack of 2026-10-23, `534a7e41c3` and `82dc407331`):** #11165's head `19e41b09fa` merges master and moves #11132's `session/*` methods into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, so the master conflicts in `dispatch.rs`, `session.rs` and `types.rs` are resolved there and this branch merges it without conflict in those files. The hand-resolved files are the CI workflow, its gate registry, the CI guide and the plugin backend change filter, where master, #11165 and #11319 each add their own lines (every side's lines are kept), plus the regenerated OpenRPC document (`cargo generate openrpc`, 107 methods, `--check` clean). #11165's `session/prompt` fix (`SessionPromptAck`) comes along with its head. The branch is now mergeable with master.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Admission does not trust the grants the spawned dispatch task copied at the read loop's check (`ad161acc03`): `admit_plugin_webhook` re-resolves the caller's live grants with `recheck_authority_after_admission`, the same check `session/new` and `session/prompt` run after admission, so a credential revoked or a profile narrowed between the check and the task's admission refuses the delivery. `plugin_webhook_admission_rechecks_the_live_grants` narrows `allowed_channels` and then drops `channels:execute` after `spawn_handle` and asserts both refusals while the copied grants still allow.
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change. A caller does not reach a profile through that cascade (`864b58d76e`): the rename and the provider-model alias delete check every entry the cascade dirties against the caller's live config write grants and refuse the whole change, with nothing saved, when one of them is outside those grants, the write-set rule the gateway's config routes already follow (`config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`: a `channels.*` writer is refused FORBIDDEN naming `permission_profiles.ops`, then succeeds once `permission_profiles.*` is granted).
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #11165.

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 17 passed ; ok. 5 passed ; ok. 57 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; cargo check --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, config, gateway, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and e2e) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5466 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (two runs each), and this PR does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops only on the pre-existing macOS `unused import std::sync::mpsc` in `service/mod.rs`; no lint in any changed runtime file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutations caught by the new tests: releasing the permit before the send, shutdown not joining dispatch tasks, releasing the id after the send, allowing WSS, removing the send's race against connection cancel, and skipping the denial audit record.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Restack onto #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319 `c352574198` (head `2aeb57ae9b`, 2026-10-23):** the whole suite again on this head: proto (30, schema export 33), api and infra (339), config (1821 of 1822), channels listing (8), gateway with `plugins-wasm` and the plugin webhook golden frames (5, fixtures unchanged), runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` (104), plugin admission (34), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` (5), architecture (81), `cargo generate openrpc --check` in sync, workspace and root `plugins-wasm-cranelift` checks, `--no-default-features` with `-D warnings`, clippy on the touched crates, the root binary and e2e, and runtime clippy, the comment hygiene, change filter, docs and links gates, and the parallel runtime gate (runtime x3 at 16 threads, channels x3), all green. The one failure is `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, a master test that fails on macOS (PR 11646) and that this PR does not touch; the earlier pre-existing runtime failures no longer reproduce on this master.
- **Refresh for the #11322 review (head `d6ef5dc0af`):** the same suite again: `rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook` 27 passed (with the new test), and the only failures are the same three pre-existing runtime tests and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning described above. The new test fails if a missing binding is admitted.
- **The parallel-gate failure of `plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels` (`13fd6a42e1`):** the test reads its audit record from the process-wide log broadcast, and its drain stopped at the first lagged-receiver error, which the channel reports once a noisy neighbour floods the window between the subscription and the drain under 16 threads, so the record was never reached; the WSS refusal test had the same latent stop. Both now subscribe right before the call under test, drain past a lag with a two-second deadline for a late record, and report on a miss whether the capture layer was active and whether the broadcast hook changed since the subscription. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook -- --test-threads=16` x3 passes (28 tests); the parallel gate's result on this head is in CI.
- **The cascade write-set check (`864b58d76e`):** `rpc::` 865 passed at 16 threads, with `config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the docs quality and link gates pass on `authentication.md`, whose RPC selector bullet now says a cascade's rewrites are checked too.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (head `d2479d7f2f`):** fmt and `cargo metadata --locked` on this tree, with cargo-audit 0.22.2 and `cargo deny check advisories` on its merged `Cargo.lock` (no vulnerabilities; RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 are gone with Wasmtime 48.0.8). The build and test evidence for this merge ran on #11322's tree, which carries this branch's commits unchanged plus the gateway forwarder: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`, workspace clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`), the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` 3 passed, `cargo generate openrpc --check`, and the docs gates; the runtime `rpc::` suite 884 passed at 16 threads on that tree, which includes this branch's dispatcher unchanged
- **Fixes after the refresh (head `d4517a7845`):** on the #11322 tree that carries this head unchanged: fmt; `rpc::dispatch::tests` 588 passed at 16 threads (the cascade test reads the refusal from the catalog); `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed, `dependency_boundary` included; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the two burst tests and the two persisted-log tests together at 4 threads, ten runs, no failure; the parallel runtime gate script itself (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6044 tests, and the channels suite, 2031 tests, at 16 threads) green on this tree, as it was on the unfixed tree: the drop only shows under CI's slower disk, so the fix rests on the writer queue's mechanism rather than a local reproduction
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep a tool-result envelope intact when a follow-up turn follows it
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `normalize_cached_channel_turns()` no longer merges a `user` turn into a preceding `role=tool` turn. Tool content is a structured result envelope, so the merge produced invalid JSON; the OpenAI-compatible adapter then emitted `role=tool` without `tool_call_id`, and strict providers rejected the entire request (DeepSeek: `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`). Because the damaged pair is replayed from the persisted transcript, every later message in that conversation failed the same way.
  - The OpenAI-compatible adapter now recovers the id from the leading JSON value of a tool-result content string (tolerating trailing bytes) and falls back to the most recent assistant tool call, so one damaged envelope can no longer take down a whole request.
  - Two regression tests: `tool -> user` normalization keeps the envelope intact and keeps the user turn; the id recovery handles trailing content.
- **Scope boundary:** does not change the alternation merging added by #1057 for consecutive `user` / `assistant` turns, does not rewrite or drop the follow-up user turn, and does not touch the tool loop, persistence, or provider retry policy.
- **Blast radius:** channel cached-turn assembly (shared by all messaging channels) and OpenAI-compatible request serialization. ACP, ZeroCode, gateway sessions, and non-compatible provider adapters are untouched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12187

### What this does, simply

A channel keeps the recent turns of a conversation and replays them to the model. When a turn is interrupted, or hits the tool-iteration cap, the stored conversation can end up as `assistant asked for a tool -> tool result -> the user's message again`. The code that restores strict user/assistant alternation handled that by appending the later turn to the previous message. When the previous message was a tool result, prose was appended to a JSON object, and a strict provider answered `missing field 'tool_call_id'` — failing that message and every message after it in the same conversation, which looks like a credential or model problem to the operator.

This PR keeps the follow-up turn as its own message (providers accept `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user` directly), and adds a small safety net in the request builder: even if some other path hands over a damaged tool result, the id the result belongs to is read from the beginning of the object and included on the wire. No user or assistant text is dropped.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel`
- **Setup / preconditions:** any channel that keeps tool turns in its cached history (`keep_tool_context_turns`, default) plus a conversation whose stored history contains `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user`. A strict OpenAI-compatible provider makes the failure loud; this was reproduced against DeepSeek's official API (`https://api.deepseek.com`, model `deepseek-flash`).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`: obtain a conversation whose stored turns end with a tool result followed directly by the user's request (a tool-capped turn does this), then send a follow-up message.
  2. On this branch: replay the same conversation data and send the same follow-up message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the request carries the tool message with its `tool_call_id` intact and the follow-up user message as a separate turn; the provider answers 200.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the tool message content is `<envelope>\n\n<user text>`, the adapter emits `role=tool` with no `tool_call_id`, and the provider answers `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`; every later message in that conversation fails identically.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels normalize_cached_channel_turns
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers recover_leading_tool_call_id
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets
```

Tail of the runs that produced this branch:

```text
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_passes_through_tool_messages ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_merges_consecutive_assistant_turns ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_merges_consecutive_user_turns ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_keeps_tool_envelope_when_user_follows_tool ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2014 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

test compatible::tests::recover_leading_tool_call_id_tolerates_trailing_turn ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1983 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` lanes cover both crates; both regression tests are unit-level and run in the normal test job.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none specific to this diff. The end-to-end replay below adds provider-behavior coverage that unit tests cannot express.
- **Commands run and tail output:** shown above; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** With a local `webhook` channel instance (the same orchestrator path; no chat platform involved) against DeepSeek's official API:
  - Before: one request logged, in causal order, the merge into the tool turn (target 82 chars, incoming 54 chars), the envelope going invalid (82 -> 138 chars, exactly the appended `\n\n` plus the user turn), `role=tool` serialized without `tool_call_id`, and then `422 messages[N]: missing field 'tool_call_id'`.
  - After: the same stored transcript (still containing `tool -> user`) returned 200; the tool message kept its envelope and `tool_call_id`, the user turn arrived as its own message, and the turn completed with real tool calls.
  - Not verified: other channel transports and non-OpenAI-compatible adapters were not exercised individually (they share the same normalization function).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible layout, styling, or presentation state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head, `channel` path, evidence = the unit tests above plus the local replay logs (redacted).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** replay of a stored transcript with `tool -> user` adjacency; before = 422 on every message, after = 200.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` was not completed locally because this machine's toolchain (rustc 1.99.1) flags pre-existing lints outside this diff (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, a deprecated API in `zeroclaw-runtime`); with those allowed, the two affected crates report no warning attributable to this change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No` — the recovery path only reads an id the runtime itself wrote into the tool-result envelope; it adds no new text to the request and does not widen what the model can see)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` — existing transcripts still load; the only behavior change is that a follow-up turn is delivered as its own message instead of being concatenated into a tool result)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk change; rollback is `git revert 61b776f06 e640872da`.

prs.title: feat(providers): honor runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models and API/tool combinations absent from the capability table retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic. The GPT-5.x Chat Completions-with-tools entries are inferred from separately documented capabilities rather than verified by a live request; the remaining rejection risk is described under Testing.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates use their own profiles; bounded delegates inherit their caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Explicit raw-body overrides retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated mock HTTP regressions exercise the real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate paths and assert outgoing efforts; judging model answers manually would not verify the wire setting. The real CLI regression is reproducible with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact`.

### How I tested

Candidate `2872a677f3d03d7efb447eb9e091b01342cafee8` integrates upstream `master` at `03b29bcc68eadf8bd03905b93d6867d3af9d7b87`. The resolution retains both the profile's native-thinking scope and upstream supplied-capability/SOP bindings and `keep_tool_context_turns` propagation. The upstream repetition guard, supplied-only construction boundary and request-only history trimming remain intact. The public turn-loop futures also retain their explicit `+ Send` contracts.

The bounded runtime exception has [Core approval recorded in its row on PR #12057](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057#issuecomment-6502718792). That separate record must land before this implementation merges; owning human reviews remain required.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `2872a677f3d03d7efb447eb9e091b01342cafee8`, [Quality Gate run 41553064336, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41553064336) succeeded, including [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41553064336/job/125651428977), full workspace `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Test (CLI-only build)` and its artifact ratchet, lint/Rustdoc, security, MSRV, required Windows checks, platform/plugin builds and docs. Code Analysis also succeeded. All 57 head checks were terminal: 47 successful and ten conditionally skipped. The skips cover unchanged-version crates preflight, path-gated Windows task-owner/targeted Clippy, relay/Nix checks, the non-PR benchmark lane, master-push debounce, and the two label-gated advisory Windows jobs. Those skips do not supply executed coverage.

The exact-head [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41553064336/job/125645181500) reported:

```text
Summary [  98.133s] 19738 tests run: 19738 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 43 skipped
```

That Linux job explicitly passed the Gateway deadline, Telegram approval-route, Anthropic timeout and two configuration cases that failed locally. No additional base/candidate Gateway control was triggered. The local results below remain separate observations; successful CI does not turn those original local runs green.

The complete local battery below ran on integration `382c35a242af263a14affeb77da056d40a442715`, using Rust 1.98.1 on macOS, an isolated Cargo target, and disabled debug/incremental output. The final candidate adds only three one-shot test assertions; production and documentation are identical. After those assertions, the focused one-shot test, formatting and both comment gates passed again. The baseline assertions check global Responses `medium`, absent legacy Chat effort, and exactly three requests under an ambient `high` turn; the explicit one-shot request still sends `low` and restores the baseline afterward.

```text
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib native_thinking
12 passed; 0 failed
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib thinking

cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib codex -- --test-threads=4
58 passed; 0 failed

2 passed; 0 failed
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-api
321 passed; 0 failed; doctest: 1 passed
bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime, three 16-thread rounds: 6021 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored each
channels, three 16-thread rounds: 2033 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored each
cargo +1.98.1 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
cargo +1.98.1 doc --locked -p zeroclaw-api --no-deps
# exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh
58 passed, 0 failed

Comment hygiene gate passed.
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh

```

The strengthened final test executed successfully:

```text
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib openai_reasoning::tests::native_effort::legacy_one_shot_calls_read_only_the_delegate_carrier -- --exact
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2004 filtered out; finished in 0.57s
```

The broad local battery is **not uniformly green**:

```text
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --features schema-export
1838 passed; 2 failed
cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --no-fail-fast
library: 1995 passed; 6 failed; 4 ignored
Hailo integration: 60 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
remaining dispatch integration: 1 passed
cargo +1.98.1 nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
19729 tests run: 19724 passed (2 leaky), 5 failed, 43 skipped
RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.1 bash scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 8m 38s
# workspace Clippy --features ci-all --all-targets -- -D warnings passed
# provider-dispatch scanner failed on two unchanged test-helper calls
```

The two configuration failures are `native_build_rejects_bare_name_not_on_path` (an inaccessible host PATH entry changes the error) and `unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception` (`nul`/`NUL` collide on this filesystem). Their test/implementation files and the lockfile are byte-identical to the exact master base.

The provider library's failures include three same-process runtime-proxy races: `responses_model_listing_carries_header_only_profile_and_surfaces_auth_failure`, `responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config`, and `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults`. Concurrent unrelated requests received the proxy's Responses-shaped body, with missing `choices`/`data` errors and four hits instead of two. All three pass in the process-isolated workspace run. The other three are the Anthropic, OpenAI and Responses factory timeout fixtures; the two OpenAI cases pass in the workspace run, while the Anthropic deadline fails there too. New wire fixtures use the existing proxy guard; no unrelated proxy or timeout repair is included.

The completed workspace run's five failures were the two configuration cases above, Telegram's `routed_approval_times_out_when_prompt_delivery_exceeds_route_budget`, Gateway's `websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error`, and Anthropic's `anthropic_factory_forwards_timeout_to_native_provider`. The Telegram fixture passes all three complete channel rounds. The Gateway case expires on its three-second frame deadline before its behavior assertion; the default-profile level is `None`, and tracing found no changed await, I/O or retry on that path. These are fresh non-green observations, not a claim that current-base execution reproduced them. No executable base control was run for this candidate. The first workspace attempt was interrupted by SIGTERM. Its terminal summary reported `12528/19729 tests run: 12500 passed, 28 failed, 43 skipped`; 23 of those failure records are SIGTERM terminations, leaving five actual test failures and 7,201 tests unrun. In addition to the four overlapping failures above, `gateway_restart_hint_uses_gateway_bind_fallback_for_hostnames` failed its port-reservation expectation in that partial run (observed port 62517 versus expected 62516) and passed in the complete repeat. `src/main.rs` is unchanged from the base. The complete repeat above still has its own five failures, including the Anthropic timeout case; neither run is presented as green.

The strict script's dispatch scan flags two direct calls in `agent/safety_net_loop_recovery.rs`, a test-only module whose enclosing `cfg(test)` the per-file scanner does not recognize. Both the helper and scanner are byte-identical to the exact base. Workspace Clippy passed; the full strict script did not. The two leaky passes exercise inherited-child-output behavior in existing MCP and ZeroCode tests. The macOS linker emitted nonfatal unwind-table-size warnings; no current-base warning control was run. The docs gate reported an existing duplicate `See also` heading outside changed lines; optional external HTTP link validation was skipped because `lychee` is unavailable.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Required exact-head CI is complete. Local execution is macOS/Rust 1.98.1; CI uses Rust 1.98.0 and supplies platform/MSRV lanes. Live provider behavior, account entitlements and paid API calls were not tested. The non-green local runs, absent current-base execution controls and linker warning above remain explicit. Some sibling wire-temperature/default-stream controls rely on static tracing rather than an exhaustive wire-assertion cross-product.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Literal command results appear above. The earlier [ae3e8dbe integration report](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12059#issuecomment-6511128896) and [45e47dcd factory-follow-up report](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12059#issuecomment-6439318420) retain historical evidence at their own revisions; those results are not attributed to this candidate.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced request constructors/rebuilders, factory aliases, model fallbacks and scoped context through CLI, channels, Agent/RPC and delegates. Mock HTTP tests assert actual Responses/Chat/Codex efforts, opt-out/global controls, all levels, tools, deferred streams, fallback remapping, session resets and cache isolation. The pinned subscription catalog is checked as complete JSON, including all list-visible model effort sets and exclusion of client-only delegation levels. Public capability data remains documentation-derived, without live API probing. For GPT-5.x Chat Completions requests with tools, effort support is inferred from separately listed capabilities; that combination was not verified by a live request. An unsupported combination can be rejected by the provider; use the existing profile opt-out described under Rollback to restore the previous global/default path.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface or presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Broad battery on `382c35a242af263a14affeb77da056d40a442715`; focused one-shot test and unchanged-source gates cover `2872a677f3d03d7efb447eb9e091b01342cafee8`; real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate mock request paths, API/schema persistence, full workspace/parallel tests, lint/Rustdoc/docs/comment gates. Wire assertions are in `openai_reasoning_tests.rs` and the owning runtime/channel test modules.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Literal validation output above and outgoing-body assertions in those tests.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Opted-in profiles on one endpoint send their own efforts, model fallbacks remap the level, opt-out retains global/default behavior, and explicit native overrides bypass response-cache reuse. Single-call delegates retain their runtime prompt/temperature inputs; mapped non-`none` OpenAI efforts omit `temperature` on the wire for compatibility, as described below.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Desktop/UI and live/paid-provider checks are outside this change. Optional HTTP link validation was skipped because `lychee` is unavailable. No deployment or live account testing was performed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: bypassing response-cache reuse for an explicit native-thinking override can issue an existing model request where a cached result was previously returned. Requests use the same configured endpoints and authentication; tests use local mock servers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No: existing thinking-prompt selection is preserved.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Explicit overrides can increase model calls, latency and token cost. The existing `native_thinking` opt-in and rollback path control this behavior. Diagnostics include requested/effective effort, provider alias, model and mapping outcome; they exclude credentials, prompts, endpoint URLs and response bodies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust source constructing or exhaustively destructuring affected public structs. Existing TOML values, schema enum values, provider defaults and serialized configuration remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new key, environment variable or CLI option. Existing opted-in profile levels now affect supported OpenAI native requests.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No configuration migration. Downstream `ChatRequest` literals must initialize `thinking_level` (`None` for unrelated requests); rebuilders copy the original level, and exhaustive patterns add the field or `..`. `ThinkingLevel` remains available from its old configuration paths through a re-export. Callers of `default_budget_tokens()` through that path must import `zeroclaw_config::scattered_types::ThinkingLevelBudget`. Public runtime `ThinkingParams` literals need `native_level`; use the existing resolution helper where applicable. Recreate/reconnect Agent/RPC sessions after changing their profile defaults.

A successfully mapped non-`none` public OpenAI reasoning request omits optional `temperature`, as the verified models require. Existing runtime prompt/temperature policy, unmapped/global requests and other providers retain their behavior. Effort changes may affect latency and token usage; subscription model access still depends on the account's existing entitlements. Public API capabilities were checked against [official OpenAI model pages](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; subscription sets come from list-visible entries in the [Codex catalog at commit `126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json). Client delegation modes such as `ultra` are excluded and never sent as wire efforts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `native_thinking = false` on affected runtime profiles and apply it through the existing runtime reload or restart lifecycle, including recreating/reconnecting Agent/RPC sessions, to return OpenAI requests to the existing global/default effort path. For a full rollback, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if merged as separate commits, revert the complete feature commit range, including its API, config, provider and runtime changes together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `native_thinking` only. Disabling it on a mixed-provider profile also disables its existing native token budgets; revert the complete feature when those budgets must stay enabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upstream request rejection, unexpected latency/token use, an unmapped-level diagnostic, or an effort substitution inconsistent with the serving model. Inspect `requested_level`, `effective_effort`, provider/model and mapping outcome diagnostics without logging request bodies or credentials.

prs.title: feat(channels): add one-tap Matrix approval reactions
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Matrix approval prompts now arrive with ✅ and ❌ reactions seeded by the bot. An authorized operator taps ✅ to approve the call once or ❌ to deny it. Today the operator has to copy the 8-character token and type `<TOKEN> approve`, which is awkward on mobile clients.
  - The design follows the Mattermost one-tap approvals from #10358: the same emoji pair, the bot's own reactions ignored, and reaction decisions refused while the bot's identity is unknown. `always` stays typed-only, so a tap never grants more than one call.
  - Reactions use the typed path's authorization: the peer allowlist, `allowed_rooms`, the prompt's own room, and first decision wins. Matrix keeps its approvals in one private state in `matrix.rs`: live registrations, each with its prompt's event ID, plus the 64 most recently settled tokens. Resolution, timeout and cancellation retire a registration and its binding together, so a late tap does nothing.
  - A typed reply to one of those recently settled tokens is consumed instead of reaching the agent as ordinary chat. Without this, tapping ✅ and then typing `<TOKEN> always` sent the protocol text into a model turn. Older or unknown token-shaped text keeps its existing behaviour.
  - Reaction seeding runs alongside the wait for a decision. A slow or failing `/send/m.reaction` only logs at `WARN`; it never delays a typed answer or stretches `approval_timeout_secs`.
  - The homeserver can show the prompt before the bot learns its event ID, so a tap in that gap reaches sync before there is a binding. After binding, the bot reads the prompt's existing `m.annotation` relations, newest first, and runs each through the same decision path as a live reaction, so an early tap still counts. This runs alongside seeding, adds no state, and a failure only logs at `WARN`.
  - A tap on a live prompt that fails authorization logs at `INFO` with the sender, room, prompt event and reason. Reactions that are not approval answers stay unlogged.
- **Scope boundary:** Typed replies, approval routing and the runtime's approval policy are unchanged. No other channel's behaviour changes.
- **Blast radius:** Matrix only. The Discord, Signal, Slack and Telegram sources are unchanged. `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/util.rs` changes only by dropping `channel-matrix` from the `cfg` lists of the shared approval-map helpers, which Matrix no longer uses. Each Matrix registration carries an identity, so a stale guard or delayed send cannot touch a later registration that reuses the same token.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. Related #10358 (Mattermost approval prompts).

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw needs permission to run a tool, it asks in the Matrix room. Until now, the operator had to copy a code from the message and type it back with "approve" or "deny". With this change, the bot puts ✅ and ❌ under its own question, and the operator taps one. Only the same people who could type an answer can tap one, and the tap must be in the same room. Typing still works, and "always" still has to be typed, so a tap only ever approves one call.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. CI cannot cover a live homeserver or a real client.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `matrix`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Matrix channel alias with a peer group containing your account, in an encrypted room, and a risk profile that asks for some tool.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to use that tool, tap ✅ on the prompt, and repeat with ❌. Then react with another emoji, tap from an account outside the peer group, and tap after the prompt has been answered.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The prompt carries ✅ and ❌. Tapping ✅ runs the call once, ❌ denies it, and other emoji, outsiders and late taps do nothing. Typed replies still work.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The prompt has no reactions, and only typed replies answer it.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test, clippy and fmt jobs cover `zeroclaw-channels`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No test runs against a live homeserver or Element.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-matrix --lib matrix
test result: ok. 327 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; 0 measured; 870 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib
test result: ok. 2031 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo run -p xtask --bin fluent -- check
(exit 0)
```

  Before this change the Matrix filter reported 313 passed. With `--no-default-features --features channel-matrix`, clippy reports `function manager_from_snapshot is never used` on both `master` and this branch, so that finding predates this change.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests drive real matrix-sdk 0.19.1 sync dispatch through `MatrixMockServer`. They cover the bot's seeded reaction, another emoji, and an unauthorized sender (none resolve a prompt), plus emoji mapping with and without U+FE0F, binding to the prompt's event only, a stale registration that reuses a token, a failed seed with typed approval still working, and a reaction send stalled for 30 seconds while a typed answer or the timeout ends the wait on time (this test fails on an earlier revision that awaited seeding), an operator's ✅ already present on the prompt when the bot binds it, found on the second page of relations (this test fails with the catch-up disabled), the same for an unauthorized sender, a room excluded by `allowed_rooms` (this test fails with the room check removed), dropping a real in-flight approval request during a stalled seed, an unknown bot identity (no instruction line, no seed, no decision), a typed reply arriving after a tap settled the prompt, and late typed replies after a timeout, after a cancellation and from another room (these fail with retired-token consumption disabled, while ordinary chat in that room still dispatches). In matrix-sdk 0.19.1, successfully decrypted timeline events replace their encrypted form before handler dispatch, so `OriginalSyncReactionEvent` receives reactions from encrypted rooms. I did not verify this against a live encrypted homeserver or Element.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output. The prompt gains one Fluent line, `channel-approval-react-instruction`: "React ✅ to approve once or ❌ to deny." The other locales fall back to English through the documented workflow.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** This branch's head, `channel` = `matrix`, through the tests above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the Fluent line above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See "Beyond CI".
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all` was not run; the checks above cover the changed crate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The bot sends two `m.reaction` events to the homeserver it already uses, on its own prompt. This adds a new way to answer an approval prompt, so it applies the typed path's checks: the peer allowlist, `allowed_rooms`, the prompt's room, and first decision wins. It ignores the bot account's own reactions, and refuses reaction decisions while the bot's user ID is unknown, because the seeded ✅ returns through sync. Only ✅ and ❌ map to decisions, and neither maps to `always`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; typed approvals keep the same commands.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `matrix: failed to seed approval reaction` or `matrix: failed to catch up approval reactions` at `WARN` when the homeserver rejects those calls; `matrix: rejected approval reaction` at `INFO`, with the reason `sender_not_allowed`, `room_not_allowed` or `destination_mismatch`, when a tap is refused; `matrix: refusing to decide an approval without a trustworthy bot identity` at `WARN` when the bot's user ID is unknown.

prs.title: feat(providers): add Opper model provider
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add a typed provider slot `opper` for Opper, an EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible AI gateway. Operators select it by name, and ZeroClaw fills in the endpoint and bearer auth.
  - The endpoint lives in one constant, `OpperEndpoint::DEFAULT_URI`. The factory's `DEFAULT_URL` reads it, and a test guards the pair.
  - Opper is already on models.dev as `opper`, so the slot sets `MODELS_DEV_KEY = "opper"`. The model picker lists Opper models before a key is set, through the existing models.dev path. With a key, the shared client reads the live `/models`.
  - The API key comes only from the typed alias. A test checks that the constructor does not read `OPPER_API_KEY`.
- **Scope boundary:** No new client implementation, no `ModelProviderKind` variant, no context-window discovery, no alias shims, no `wire_api` handling. Other providers and existing configs do not change.
- **Blast radius:** The provider registry, the config schema (a new `providers.models.opper` map), the catalog source table, the generated "All slots" table and the provider list. The slot is inactive unless an operator configures it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11583. Related #8396.

### What this does, simply

Before this PR, an Opper user had to write a `custom` provider with the URL. Opper did not show in the provider list, and the model picker stayed empty until a key was pasted.

This PR adds a named `opper` slot. The operator sets `model` and `api_key`. ZeroClaw then sends Chat Completions requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat`. Model ids are bare names such as `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and Opper picks the route for each request. The slot is for chat only.

### Why a first-class family (not `providers.models.custom`)

- **Model list before a key is set.** Opper is already listed on models.dev as `opper`. The slot reuses the existing models.dev catalog path, as `vercel` and `synthetic` do. A `custom` alias has no catalog source, so its picker stays empty until a key is pasted.
- **Maintained defaults.** The endpoint and bearer auth come from one constant, so operators cannot mistype the base URL. The `/v3/compat` path is easy to get wrong by hand.
- **Discoverability.** Opper shows in the provider list and in the generated catalog next to the other gateways.
- **No new client code.** The slot is data on the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The intake decision is in #11583.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. You need an Opper key from https://platform.opper.ai.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:**

  ```toml
  schema_version = 3

  [providers.models.opper.default]
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
  api_key = "..."

  [agents.opper]
  model_provider = "opper.default"
  risk_profile = "default"

  [risk_profiles.default]
  level = "supervised"
  ```

- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default`
  2. `zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The model list loads and the agent replies. Without `api_key`, step 1 lists the models.dev `opper` catalog.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `opper` is not a known provider slot, so `model_provider = "opper.default"` does not resolve and config validation fails.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Check`, `Test` and clippy cover both changed crates. That includes the slot coverage tests `every_canonical_family_has_a_catalog_table_entry` and `listed_model_providers_match_canonical_slots`, and the 8 new tests. `Docs Style` covers `catalog.md`.
- **Mock request coverage (added in b488e30a5):** `opper_factory_sends_bearer_and_model_ids_to_compat_endpoint` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/factory.rs` points the Opper provider at a local mock server under `/v3/compat`. It asserts that chat requests go to `/v3/compat/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, that the pool name `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the pinned id `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` are sent unchanged, and that the model list goes to `/v3/compat/models` with the same header and returns both ids.
- **CI result on b488e30a5:** run 37914489616 concluded success with no failed jobs, including Format, Lint and Test, and the Test log shows the new test passing.
- **Live smoke from #11583 (run 2026-10-30):** tested commit `b488e30a5` (`zeroclaw 0.8.5 (b488e30)`), release build with rustc 1.98.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 (a GitHub Actions runner), the config above with a real Opper key in `api_key`, `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at it. Sanitized output:

  ```text
  $ zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider opper.default
    [opper.default]
      ✅ 1250 models
    Summary: 1 ok, 0 skipped, 0 auth/access, 0 errors
    opper.default      ok           1250     catalog fetched

  $ zeroclaw agent -a opper -m "hello"
  Hello! How can I help you today?
  ```

  1250 is the live `GET /v3/compat/models` list with the key. Without a key the same command lists the 55-model models.dev catalog.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI makes no live provider request; the live smoke above covers that once.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  git diff --check origin/master HEAD
  # exited 0, no output

  curl -s https://models.dev/api.json | jq -c '.opper | {id, api, env, models: (.models | length), has_default: (.models | has("claude-sonnet-4-6"))}'
  # {"id":"opper","api":"https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat","env":["OPPER_API_KEY"],"models":57,"has_default":true}

  curl -s "https://api.opper.ai/v3/models?limit=2000" | jq -c '[.models[] | select(.model == "claude-sonnet-4-6" and .pooled == true and .type == "llm")] | length'
  # 5
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The models.dev `opper` entry and the model id used in the tests and docs, shown above. The live chat and keyed model list are covered by the smoke above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendered interface changes. The new provider list entry is data from `list_model_providers()`.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` or `cargo test` locally, because this machine has no Rust toolchain. This PR relies on required CI for them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Only when an operator configures `providers.models.opper`, ZeroClaw sends requests to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat` through the shared OpenAI-compatible client. The keyless model list uses the existing models.dev fetch. Credentials stay on the typed alias `api_key` or the `ZEROCLAW_*` schema-mirror override.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: This adds the `providers.models.opper.<alias>` slot. It is additive. `ModelProviders` is a public exhaustive struct, so a downstream struct literal needs `..ModelProviders::default()` for the new `opper` field. Existing `custom` configs keep working. To move to the typed slot, create `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]`, set `model`, and set `api_key` directly or bridge it with `ZEROCLAW_providers__models__opper__<alias>__api_key="$OPPER_API_KEY"`. `opper-ai` and `opper_ai` are not runtime aliases.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` this commit, or remove the `opper` slot from `providers.rs`, `schema.rs`, `factory.rs`, `catalog.rs`, `lib.rs` and the catalog doc entry.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Without a configured `[providers.models.opper.<alias>]` entry, the provider is inactive.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Provider construction errors that mention `opper`, failed `/models` calls to `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat/models`, or chat errors from the compatible provider path.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? `No`
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A

Disclosure: Opper is my startup.

prs.title: fix(tools): report web_search as compiled out without tools-external
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Since #11221, `web_search_tool` registers only under `#[cfg(feature = "tools-external")]`, but — unlike notion/jira in the same commit — its `not(tools-external)` branch has no `warn_tool_compiled_out`, and `[web_search]` defaults to `enabled = true`, so a lean `--features gateway` build silently drops the tool with zero log or validation signal (issue #12203).
  - Add a `WebSearch` variant to `OptInTool` (section `web_search`, feature `tools-external`) and emit the standard `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` validation warning plus the runtime `warn_tool_compiled_out` log line when the section is enabled in a build without `tools-external`.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not move `web_search_tool` between inventory compilation groups and does not touch the other `tools-external` adapters (weather, browser, screenshot, etc.); `WebSearch` deliberately stays out of `OptInTool::ALL` to preserve the inventory opt-in invariant, and is reported by `collect_compiled_out_tool_warnings` directly. A full migration of `web_search_tool` from `External` to `OptIn` (with the cascade through `EXTERNAL_TOOL_NAMES` and SOP scope groups) is left as a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** `config validate` / `collect_warnings` consumers (`doctor`, gateway config API, channel orchestrator notices) now see one additional `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` warning for default configs in lean builds. No runtime registration behavior changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12203

### What this does, simply

A default ZeroClaw config has `[web_search] enabled = true`, but the common source build (`--features gateway`) compiles without `tools-external`, so the web search tool simply does not exist in the binary. Nothing says so: the agent never sees the tool, and neither logs nor `config validate` mention it. This PR makes the build say so — one `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` warning naming `web_search.enabled` and the `tools-external` feature, in both validation warnings and the runtime registry log, matching what notion/jira already do for their opt-in features.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by focused automated tests on both build configurations.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`config validate`), daemon log surface
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with the default `[web_search] enabled = true`
- **Steps to run:** build without `tools-external` (e.g. `cargo build --features gateway`), run `zeroclaw config validate` or start the daemon and inspect startup logs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** one `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` warning for `web_search.enabled` naming the `tools-external` feature; startup logs carry the matching `warn_tool_compiled_out` record.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no warning, no log line; the tool is absent and only binary forensics (`strings` for a tool-only string such as `html.duckduckgo.com`) reveal it.

### How I tested

Focused crate tests on the default (lean) feature set, where `OptInTool::WebSearch.compiled()` is false:

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools
```

New coverage: `web_search_section_reports_compiled_out_without_tools_external` asserts the warning appears in a lean build and is absent where the feature is compiled in; the inventory `opt_in_compilation_rows_cover_canonical_groups` and `external_compilation_rows_match_canonical_names` invariants still pass unchanged, confirming `WebSearch` stays consistent with the inventory's `External` filing.
