prs.title: fix(runtime): honour keep_tool_context_turns when building provider requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `keep_tool_context_turns` counts turns again. Since the history rip-out in #8196 removed `strip_old_tool_context`, the only consumer treated the key as a boolean (`> 0`), so the documented "number of recent turns whose full tool context is preserved" was never applied; `1`, `2`, `3` and the `unbounded` preset's `8` all behaved the same.
  - The tool loop now builds ordinary provider requests from a collapsed copy of the working history (`history_trim::collapse_tool_context_older_than`): turns older than the running one plus N prior are sent as their user prompt and closing assistant reply only, so user and assistant rows keep alternating on every provider; a turn that no reply closed (it ended on a call or a result) is sent as its prompt plus the existing `[Tool exchange: N tool call(s) — results collapsed]` summary marker, which then only ever follows a user row. The working history is never modified, so the channel sender cache, ACP transcript and CLI session file keep every row; raising the value later shows the rows again.
  - The value rides `ResolvedRuntimeKnobs` / `ResolvedAgentExecution` next to `max_tool_result_chars`, so channels, gateway, cron, delegate, subagent and the structured `Agent` engines get the same behaviour from the same resolved profile. Two nested loops that run on the caller's own history as part of the caller's turn are pinned to never collapse: live SOP steps and the skill-review fork (each step or review prompt is a user row, so the caller's turn would look older from inside them; `run_tool_call_loop_executes_queued_sop_steps_after_sop_execute` pins the SOP case).
  - Pairing-safe by construction in both native (`role=tool`) and prompt-mode (`[Tool results]` carrier) shapes; an assistant row is a tool-call carrier when it names a tool the loop can execute (the test the loop applies before it runs a call), answered or not, so an aborted exchange is summarised and a dangling call is never kept; a reply whose JSON merely contains a `tool_calls` array naming no such tool (a quoted API trace) executed nothing and is kept whole, since flat provider JSON cannot tell the two apart by shape. The loop hands the collapse the names of its registered tools, once per turn. Request rows keep a mapping to their history rows, so the existing trim-with-hook path (`prepared_source_rows`) stays correct.
  - Rows the loop itself appends inside a turn belong to the turn they interrupt and never open a retention turn: the parse-error feedback row and the prompt of each live SOP step (`[SOP: …]`, the marker `format_step_context` writes). A caller that resumes after its steps therefore still sends the tool round that opened its turn, at any retention value.
  - The malformed-protocol retry appends a user-role feedback row mid-turn (`[Tool call parse error]`; user-role because no tool call id exists to attach it to). Retention uses its own boundary predicate so that row does not open a turn: without it, a small value (`0`, or `1` after both retries) could push the running turn's own tool rows out of the retained window. The row is built from a shared prefix constant so text and predicate cannot drift; whole-turn trimming keeps its existing boundary rule.
  - A `Tool context collapsed` log record on a turn's first request reports the row and turn counts; no `HistoryTrimmed` event, because no turn is lost.
  - Docs: new "Tool context retention" section in `history-management.md`; schema doc comment and the setup guide say what the key now does. `N` is defined as prior completed turns (the running turn is always sent whole; `0` = running turn only), which is what the original #4840 stripping at persistence time amounted to.
- **Scope boundary:** terminal budget projection and the max-iteration final-summary request still use full history and remain follow-up work. No change to token-budget or turn-count trimming, to what channels persist (the `> 0` persistence gate stays), to `max_tool_result_chars`, to `history_pruning.*` (its `collapse_tool_results`/`keep_recent` fields have been inert since #8196 and are not revived here), or to any provider request shape beyond the rows sent. No new config keys; the default stays `2`.
- **Blast radius:** every deployment on the default now sends tool rows only for the running turn and the two before it (they were sent indefinitely, bounded only by whole-turn trimming). Operators who relied on older tool output staying visible should raise the key; presets already carry explicit values. Prompt size drops for tool-heavy sessions. On routes with prompt caching (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible) there is a trade-off: each time a turn ages out of the window, the request differs from the previous one starting at that turn, so the kept turns' tool output is re-sent uncached once per new turn even though the total is smaller; not measured either way. Post-turn skill creation (`extract_tool_calls_from_history`) reads the working history, which is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10781 (this implements the accepted disposition for `keep_tool_context_turns`: make the numeric semantics real; the other keys tracked there are untouched), Related #4840 (introduced the key), Related #8196 (removed its consumer).

### What this does, simply

An agent's conversation carries, for each turn, the user's message, the tool calls the model made, what those tools returned, and the model's final answer. Tool output is by far the bulkiest part and loses value fastest: three turns later the model rarely needs the raw file listing or search dump, only what it concluded from it. `keep_tool_context_turns` was introduced to keep that bulk only for the newest few turns. When the history pruner was replaced by whole-turn trimming, the code that applied the number was deleted and nobody noticed, because the key kept parsing and the tool rows simply stayed. This PR restores the documented behaviour at one chokepoint in the tool loop, so a setting of `2` means what it says on every path.

### Known limits

- **Internal rows are recognised by text.** The loop's parse-error feedback row and a live SOP step's prompt are told apart from user turns by the text the runtime writes (the parse-error prefix; the step header's `) — Step <n> of <m>]` and fixed last line, with the SOP name itself unparsed). A user message that reproduces one of those shapes would join the previous retention turn. History rows carry no provenance today; that is the proper fix and belongs with the session-event work.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, cheap A/B on any channel or CLI session.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` surface (also holds for any channel).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an agent with `keep_tool_context_turns = 1` in its runtime profile and any tool enabled (e.g. `shell` with `ls`).
- **Steps to run:** ask for three tool-using turns ("list the workspace", "list it again", "and again"), then inspect a provider request after the third turn’s tool result has been added. Use provider-request tracing; the durable transcript retains the full history.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the request carries full tool context for turns 2 and 3; turn 1 retains its user prompt and closing assistant reply, with its tool exchange collapsed. The collapse log reports one older turn collapsed and the newest two turns kept whole.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** all three turns' tool rows are sent, whatever the key says.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover the runtime and channels crates; Docs Style covers the two Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none identified.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Author-reported commands and results; see the revision details below.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                     # exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   # exit 0
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels   # exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
#   test result: ok. 1773 passed; 0 failed
bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh                                  # 3 runs, 16 threads
#   zeroclaw-runtime:  test result: ok. 5710 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored   (x3)
#   zeroclaw-channels: test result: ok. 1971 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored   (x3)
#   (new: history_trim ordinary_json_reply_is_kept_as_the_closing_reply, an_unanswered_call_to_a_known_tool_is_still_summarised,
#         sop_step_prompts_do_not_split_the_running_turn; turn resumed_parent_request_keeps_its_tool_round_across_sop_step_prompts)
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                        # Comment hygiene gate passed.
bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh                                             # OK (79 local targets checked)
markdownlint-cli2 (repo .markdownlint-cli2.yaml) on the two changed pages       # only a pre-existing MD001 on an unchanged os-tabs line, which the gate filters
```

The numbers above were measured at `2be8e99dc6`. The follow-up commit `a75ea6721b` (feedback rows do not split the running turn) was checked at its own head with `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests -- -D warnings` (exit 0), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (exit 0), the comment hygiene gate, and the `history_trim` + malformed-protocol retry tests (58 passed, 1 new: `runtime_feedback_rows_do_not_split_the_running_turn`); the full suite for that head is CI's.

At `ba1fdfbff9` (collapsed turns sent as prompt and reply; summary only where no reply closed the turn) and its master merge `2b499dc827` (master `e8d2e5fc81`): `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check` (exit 0); `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` (5811 passed; the collapse, SOP-step and resumed-parent suites 90 passed); `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --tests -- -D warnings` (exit 0); `cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime` with warnings denied (exit 0); comment hygiene gate passed.

`cargo check --workspace --tests` on this machine stops at `glib-sys`'s build script (a missing system library for an unrelated desktop crate); the runtime, channels and config crates are the ones this change touches and were checked with tests.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Provenance walk of the value from `RuntimeProfileConfig.keep_tool_context_turns` → `ResolvedRuntime` → `ResolvedRuntimeKnobs` → `ResolvedAgentExecution` → `run_tool_call_loop`, and a sweep of every `ResolvedRuntimeKnobs`/`ResolvedAgentExecution` constructor (production sites source the resolved profile; fixtures use `2`). Not verified: live channel sessions on a real provider.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (rows are removed, none added)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for config parsing and persisted sessions. Behavioural: the default `2` now takes effect (see blast radius).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>`; no schema or persisted-data change. Setting `keep_tool_context_turns` to a large value restores the previous effective behaviour without a rollback. Symptoms to watch for: provider errors about message role order, or the model losing track of tool output from more than N turns back; `grep 'Tool context collapsed'` in the runtime trace shows what each request dropped.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, true-rebased onto `6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback and their documentation. Dashboard sign-in remains in #11965. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. The existing gateway `rand` dependency moves from dev to normal dependencies; no new package or lockfile change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

### Current integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02

Current head: a0b660c198c9a8aef8f00b3a2c2096af671ce127. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 5 files.

The enrollment source, gateway manifest, locale loader and enrollment client are byte-identical to the previous head. The new master catalog keys are retained alongside the single enrollment error key, with no duplicate message keys. Focused rustfmt and whitespace checks pass. The callbacks, cookie parsing, consume-before-refusal and original-TTL capacity retry were traced again. Local Rust execution remains unavailable under Windows Application Control; the current-head upstream compilation and test results are recorded below. Earlier mock-provider/browser evidence remains historical and is not live-provider or combined dashboard evidence.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125581473661) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125571496498) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four browser-binding regressions. Parallel Runtime Test also passes. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier Fluent follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a`. Both new enrollment-start errors now use `get_required_cli_string("cli-oidc-browser-start-failed")`. The canonical English catalog keeps the exact existing text, `could not start sign-in`. Other locales inherit that English fallback until translated. This uses the existing runtime locale; it does not add per-request language negotiation.

Local `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. An exact inverse source comparison confirms that only the import, these two lookups and one English catalog entry changed. Status 500, the generic JSON error shape and early-return behavior remain. I traced the existing helper, catalog fallback and immediate JSON serialization; this was source validation, not a fresh gateway execution.

Historical CI on 1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Earlier rebase and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Earlier rebased head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. At that historical snapshot, its delayed-start browser-family finding was open. It is now repaired at 02314854b32eb45a55d9d9c004f0bd73bb7b51e8, as recorded in [the repair review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11965#pullrequestreview-5731811340). That dashboard repair is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. This PR does not contain or validate that combined integration.

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

The refreshed head now passes its required upstream CI; earlier results remain attached to their named revisions. This remains open for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. The default high-risk review requirement is two independent Core approvals. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.title: fix(install): prefer system glibc over an installed musl loader
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Prefer successful `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` or a glibc/GNU-libc `ldd --version` result before checking installed musl loaders. A glibc host can have musl installed for cross-compilation.
- **Scope boundary:** Installer libc detection and its existing target-test suite. The updater's separate target selection (#12156) is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** x86_64/aarch64 Linux archive and feature-target selection. Existing musl/distro fallbacks, unknown-host GNU fallback, ARM32, macOS and Termux rules remain.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12153.

### What this does, simply

Installing musl alongside glibc should not change which ZeroClaw archive a glibc host receives. The installer now checks the system libc first. Alpine still selects musl.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if a native Alpine or glibc-with-musl host is available.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, installer target selection.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A disposable host; use `--dry-run` to avoid installation.
- **Steps to run:** `sh install.sh --prebuilt --dry-run --skip-quickstart --no-modify-path`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** GNU on glibc even with a musl loader; musl on Alpine.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** The installed musl loader takes precedence over glibc.

### How I tested

### Current integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02

Current head: c47f963578fff87eb9a0410de15cced7ead201d7. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 2 files.

The installer and its test file are byte-identical to the previous head. The original author information is preserved, including @IftekharUddin's fixture repair. All 27 target/probe cases pass in WSL under ordinary, simulated Termux-present and simulated Termux-absent conditions. Both shell syntax checks and fixture syntax pass. Negative controls reproduce 24 passed / 3 failed with the old libc detector, and 18 passed / 9 failed with the old Termux mock. These temporary controls leave the real source unchanged; they are not native Alpine, ARM or Termux runs.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531179793/job/125583560216) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Installer Drift log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531179793/job/125571487189) records 27 target cases, three version-parser cases, nine offline entrypoint cases and the generated-installer check. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier fixture isolation follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `0af32c298576c4cd92f546096057fd8402e15341`. I adopted @IftekharUddin's two-line fixture repair with the original commit and authorship. The inner bracket mock now honors `mock_termux_dir`. Production `install.sh` is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Local WSL validation: all 27 target/probe cases pass on an ordinary host and with a controlled Termux-directory predicate. The original `5afea5fe` source passes 27 ordinary cases but fails exactly nine under the same simulation (18 passed, 9 failed). The shim changes only that host predicate; unrelated builtin controls also pass. `sh -n install.sh`, `bash -n install.sh`, `bash -n scripts/ci/install_target_triple_test.sh` and `git diff --check` pass. This is controlled host simulation, not native Termux execution.

Historical CI on 0af32c298576c4cd92f546096057fd8402e15341 failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

Three complete offline installer dry runs pass. Restoring only the old detector in a temporary source copy gives `passed: 24`, `failed: 3`, all glibc-with-musl cases. ## Summary
- Base branch: `master`.
- Implement native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO.
- Address the current reviews: supported recovery for completed inbox entries; terminal outcomes for deterministic pre-turn drops; bounded ping-response handling.

CI follow-up: pin Wasmtime 48.0.8 for the newly published advisories and replace the network-dependent Telegram test with a controlled local fixture.

- 64 XMPP tests and 5 durable-ingress tests passed locally.
- Four isolated interoperability scenarios passed: Direct TLS and STARTTLS, each with established sessions and first contact.
- Strict Clippy passed for the channel library and tests without warning suppressions.
- Current-head GitHub checks are authoritative; earlier approvals do not approve this revision.

## Security and Privacy
This changes the channel and ingress lifecycle described by the public diff. Uncertain work remains protected from automatic replay. No organization-specific infrastructure, credentials, messages or deployment information is included here.

## Compatibility
Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO is distinct from OMEMO v2. Existing-state and recovery boundaries are documented in the repository.

## Rollback
Revert the code changes subject to the state-compatibility limitations in the repository documentation. Do not treat an uncertain operation as completed.

## Supersede Attribution
None; #12015 remains a dependency.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(web): refresh config form after Save all
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Refresh mounted field forms after Save all so their saved baseline matches the value returned by the gateway.
  - Keep rows mounted during that refresh to preserve focus and row-local state.
  - Preserve edits made while a save or baseline refresh is in flight and ignore stale reload responses.
  - Clear loading state when the latest refresh finishes, including overlapping group and global saves.
  - Run the rendered regression test in the required web CI job.
- **Scope boundary:** Web dashboard configuration state, its regression test, and CI wiring; no API contract, config schema, or migration changes.
- **Blast radius:** The shared config draft provider and mounted configuration forms; each completed Save all triggers one existing config-list request per mounted form.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12021.

### What this does, simply

The Save all banner and each settings group keep related draft state. Save all persisted the shared draft and dismissed the banner, but the open group kept comparing its value with the old baseline, so it still looked dirty. The form now refreshes the saved value in the background, keeping its rows mounted while the request runs. Later edits use the refreshed baseline, and edits made during a pending save remain staged.

## Testing (required)

Local verification and the current CI snapshot are summarized below.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the same steps show the reported difference on `master` and this branch.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` dashboard.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run ZeroClaw with the web dashboard available and a config gateway; open Config → Channels → Global settings.
- **Steps to run:** Toggle “Show Tool Calls” from its current value, click the banner’s “Save all”, and inspect the Channels group. Then toggle it again to verify the group compares against the newly saved value.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The banner reports “No unsaved changes”, the group Save button is disabled, and another change shows as unsaved. During the background refresh, the field remains mounted and focused.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** After the same Save all action, the group still shows “1 unsaved change” and its Save button remains highlighted until the page or daemon is reloaded.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On parent commit `4699d1d9409d825fe4b079bc6f41c5b70f77b871`, the required `main` gate and `Web Permission Tests` job passed. That web job ran `cargo web check`, permission/catalog tests, `npm run test:config-draft-save-all`, context tests, and SOP tests. CI has restarted for current head `8ed6e7dd2c6115bb1a81ab4c82e11f42ee6959df`; results are pending. The regression test uses the real React DOM renderer with a mocked gateway in Happy DOM.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live-daemon or cross-browser smoke test; this PR’s regression test covers the form transition and focus behavior in Happy DOM.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `npm test` (Node v24.22.1) — passed; all suites passed, including `Save all refreshes the saved baseline and preserves in-flight edits`.
  - `npm run test:config-draft-save-all` — `# pass 1`, `# fail 0`.
  - `npm run test:permissions` — passed.
  - `npm run typecheck` (Node v24.22.1) — passed (`check:generated` and `tsc -b`).
  - `npm run build` (Node v24.22.1) — passed; Vite reported the repository’s existing chunks over 500 kB.
  - `git diff --check` — passed with no output.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Before the change, reproduced the issue on master commit `5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9` with a mock gateway. On this branch, the integration test clicks the switch and Save all, then observes the rendered status and group Save state. It delays the post-save config-list request and verifies the switch remains the same focused DOM node while an edit matching the old baseline stays staged until the new baseline arrives. It also switches sections during a pending save and overlaps a group save with global Save all to verify the spinner clears after the shared reload completes. Delayed successful and failed PATCH requests verify the latest input survives.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output from the React DOM renderer. The delayed-refresh regression verifies stable DOM identity and focus, preserved edits until the new baseline arrives, and no spinner after overlapping saves complete.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `8ed6e7dd2c6115bb1a81ab4c82e11f42ee6959df`, surface `web`; `web/src/lib/configDraftSaveAll.test.ts`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The final React DOM displays “No unsaved changes”; the group Save button is disabled and the switch has `aria-checked="true"`. During the delayed config-list refresh, the original switch remains the rendered node and retains focus; an edit back to the old value remains visible and dirty after the new baseline arrives. During an overlapping group/global save, the latest shared reload clears the spinner. Section changes during a pending PATCH preserve the latest draft; delayed success and failure cases also verify the newest input remains staged, with the failure error visible. Assertions are in `web/src/lib/configDraftSaveAll.test.ts`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Toggle “Show Tool Calls” → click “Save all” → the saved value becomes true and the banner/group are clean. Edit while the next save is pending → the latest value remains staged; on a failed save the dirty count and error remain visible for retry.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Rust formatting, clippy, and Rust tests were not run because this change modifies only the web dashboard.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes. After Save all completes, each mounted form requests the current configuration from the existing ZeroClaw gateway so it can update its baseline. This uses the configured gateway origin and introduces no third-party service.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual squash-merge commit with `git revert <merge-sha>`; no data migration or manual state repair is required.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A field group remains dirty after a successful Save all, shows a loading spinner after overlapping saves, loses field focus or row-local state, or drops an edit made while a save or background refresh is pending. The focused regression test covers these behaviors.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — this PR does not supersede another PR.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add capability-taking constructors for turn entry points
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Turn entry points take the capabilities they build from: `run_with_capabilities`, `process_message_with_capabilities`, `Agent::from_config_with_capabilities`, owned SOP steps, delegates, spawned subagents, peer turns and manual `cron_run` jobs. The old signatures stay as adapters over the config-backed set, so configured setups build exactly what they build today.
  - A supplied tool registry is now complete. `ToolSource::native_recipe` defaults to `Ok(None)`, and then the supplied vector is the whole registry: no native factory, skills, MCP servers, peripherals, pipeline, `tool_search` or post-turn skill work. The config-backed source opts into the native recipe explicitly. In that mode native names win over same-name source tools: native factory tools, peripheral and skill tools, MCP tools and MCP capability tools, and `execute_pipeline` and `tool_search` when the runtime builds them. Admitted source tools reach bounded delegates. In both modes a source vector that repeats a name keeps its first tool.
  - Bounded delegation keeps memory writes on the caller's policy. Every ancestor's policy is checked in order on Store, Forget and Purge, the target's tracker is charged once, and background and parallel workers carry the same chain. The background worker is still narrowed by the caller's tool-name filter (#11797). The delegate's inherited tools get the same memory/delivery context filter as the outer registry.
  - Merges current master. Effort-aware routing (#11516) now asks the capability source for its provider, with the route-scoped config, wherever the CLI loop or `process_message` chooses a route: at the CLI start, on each turn's re-route, and in `process_message`. The `Agent` path, which RPC sessions also use, still sends a selected route to the source's provider as a `hint:<name>` selector; `runtime-composition.md` says so, and #12092 tracks resolving it through the source.
  - A native recipe takes a `#[non_exhaustive]` `NativeRecipeInputs` struct with named fields, so the runtime can add inputs without breaking embedder recipes.
  - The interactive CLI now takes its session channel from the capability source's `cli` alias. The config-backed source maps it to the registered CLI channel factory as before; a supplied source with no `cli` channel makes the interactive CLI fail with "This agent has no channel for the CLI session" instead of falling back to the global factory.
  - CLI model switches now use `switched_model_provider`, the switch recipe `Agent` already used. For config-backed users this changes which credential wins when a matching `model_routes` entry has its own `api_key` (see Compatibility).
  - Adds an external consumer crate (`tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`) that depends only on the public runtime contract and checks, from outside the crate, that a supplied-only turn constructs nothing native and that an external recipe can select native compatibility. It came from #11526.
- **Scope boundary:** No application wiring: `DefaultCapabilities`, the daemon heartbeat, the cron scheduler and the gateway are not moved here (#11187). No new capability kind, config key, CLI flag or tool grant. The ADR-016 exception row for the widened paths is #11980, merged as 279188f0c3.
- **Blast radius:** Turn construction at every entry point listed above; tool registry assembly in `tools/scoped.rs` (construction mode, name precedence); bounded and independent delegation; vision and effort routing provider construction; `docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-composition.md`. Existing configs keep the native recipe through the config-backed adapters. One visible difference on that path: a child turn (delegate, subagent, peer) started from an adapter-built parent now reuses the parent's observer instead of creating its own.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10993, Related #7432. Contract lineage #11090. Supersedes #11526.

**Merge with #11851.** 74e016ce85 merges master with #11851. #11851's late host-name step and this PR's source retirement are one step now: peripheral and skill names are host names, so the same check refuses a same-name plugin tool and retires a same-name source tool (logged as `"kept": "reserved"`). #11851 reserves `mcp_resources` and `mcp_prompts` even when MCP is off, so in native compatibility mode a source tool with either name is always dropped. Peripherals now load at the start of assembly so their names can be reserved, still behind `connect_peripherals`, and still register after the guests. The reserved skill names are those of every declared skill tool, so a source tool is dropped even when that skill tool is later skipped. #11851's late-name test now uses this PR's shared peripheral trap, because the peripheral factory is a process-wide `OnceLock` and two tests registering different factories in one test process would break each other. Nothing else in this PR's delta changes; supplied-only registries are unaffected. ef6dbdff18 adds the docs lines in `runtime-composition.md`: the name-keyed `shell` approval exemption, the reserved MCP capability names, and plugin tool precedence.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's runtime has always built its own providers, memory and tools from config. This PR lets an embedder hand the runtime those pieces instead, and makes sure the runtime then uses only what it was given. If an application supplies three tools, the agent gets those three tools and nothing else: no built-in tools, no MCP servers started, no skills loaded or written. Before, the runtime quietly added its native set on top.

Running ZeroClaw from config is unchanged: the built-in config-backed source asks for the native set, and every existing entry point uses it.

Two smaller fixes come with it. A delegated agent can no longer write memory beyond what its caller's policy allows, even when the delegation runs in the background. And a supplied tool can no longer take the name of an MCP tool, the pipeline tool or `tool_search` and shadow it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The change is an embedder API with no user-visible surface for configured setups; the named tests below drive the real entry points.

### How I tested

The local runs below are on this head, c49912d42d (tree `ffb2794211`). It is ef6dbdff18 plus two commits, 8cc6ca6ab2 (a restored doc comment) and ff0502ab35 (the `Agent` route paragraph), merged with master f2b432db09. The runs used a Linux build with Rust 1.98, `--locked`, an isolated target directory, a throwaway `HOME` and `umask 022`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Lint` (clippy, `-D warnings`), `Check` (no default features, and default features with all targets) and `Test` (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`). `Test` runs the new tests that build without plugin features: the construction traps (`composition::supplied_only_traps`), the native-name precedence tests in `tools::scoped`, the skill-gating pair in `agent::loop_`, and the consumer crate. nextest runs each test in its own process, so the process-wide peripheral trap cannot leak between tests. `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` runs the `tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search_*` proofs against `tools/scoped.rs`. `Docs Style` covers `runtime-composition.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded as usual. The construction-trap module is Unix-only, because its MCP trap is a shell-script stdio server, so the Windows jobs do not run it. CI tests the consumer crate inside the workspace run, where features are unified with the root package; I ran it on its own as well (below), which shows it builds against the public API alone. #11982 tracks a CI step for that; this PR does not change workflows.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
    clean
cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    both: Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s); no warnings from workspace crates
cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
cargo +1.98.0 doc --locked --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh && bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    58 passed, 0 failed; Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -- --exact --test-threads=1 <77 named tests: capability construction, supplied-only traps, native-name precedence, delegation memory policy, model switches, skill gating> tools::tests::colliding_plugin_tools_taking_late_host_tool_names_are_refused_in_assembly
test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5999 filtered out
    one process, one thread: this PR's tests and #11851's late-name test share the peripheral trap
cargo +1.98.0 nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -E 'not test(late_tool_search)'
     Summary 6096 tests run: 6096 passed, 33 skipped
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -- tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search --include-ignored
    with both tool-fixture components built for wasm32-wasip2 and a fixture receipt written the way the CI job writes it
test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6054 filtered out
    each of the 23 wrote a passing case receipt bound to that fixture receipt
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus --doc
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p runtime-composition-consumer
test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh; bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh   (runtime-composition.md)
    Summary: 0 error(s); Checked 3 local docs link target(s).
cargo +1.98.0 nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop -E 'not test(late_tool_search)'
     Summary 19563 tests run: 19558 passed (2 leaky), 5 failed, 43 skipped
    the 5 failures come from my machine, not this PR: daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions
    needs `expect`, which is not installed here (CI installs it), and four zerorelay frontdoor_assets tests
    need Web Crypto in Node, where my system Node is 18. The same test binary with Node 24 passes all 13
    frontdoor_assets tests. The 2 leaky tests are in zeroclaw-tools and zerocode, outside this PR.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Revert checks on this head: each guard this PR adds was removed one at a time, and the tests named for it had to fail. All 23 did, and the source was restored exactly after each: peripheral, skill, MCP and repeated-name precedence; the `tool_search` claim and the pipeline reservation; the supplied-only parent filter; the skill creation and review gates; the forced native recipe at each of the five entry points; the same-hop, ancestor and hop-two memory policy carry; the SOP memory routes; the #11797 caller-name filter. After the merge, the peripheral and skill checks remove those names from the shared host-name step, and the MCP check fails two of its three tests: #11851 also reserves the MCP capability names, so the third is held by that reservation. Commits 8–11 each build on their own: `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p runtime-composition-consumer --all-targets` with the three plugin features above passes on each commit's tree; commit 12 is 1f7c1745c5, the last commit before the master merges.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** c49912d42d (tree `ffb2794211`), tested locally for every run above; the output tails are above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded from check and clippy because the build machine lacks `glib-2.0` 2.70 or newer.

### Follow-ups

- Bounded delegation refusals log one generic cause; logging a non-secret cause class (selection refused, missing runtime or memory, target memory failed) would make them easier to diagnose.
- Effort-aware routing through a supplied provider source has no direct test yet: a recording source at the CLI start, the per-turn re-route and `process_message`, and a config-backed case whose route excludes the agent's own alias.
- `Agent` turns send a selected route to the source's provider as a `hint:<name>` selector instead of asking the source for the route's provider and model; #12092 tracks it.
- The non-interactive `shell` approval exemption is keyed on the tool name; #11981 tracks keying it on the native shell tool.
- The consumer crate is tested inside the workspace run, where features are unified; #11982 tracks building it on its own in CI.
- The WARN logged when a native name retires a source tool does not name the agent; an `agent` field would tell registries apart in a shared log.
- Principal memory routing does not reach source-built tools (documented). Before RPC sessions run on supplied sources (#11187), either the source gets the session's principal scope at construction or routing is refused for supplied-only registries unless the source opts in.
- Native tool calls are recorded in history in a shape the skill creator's extractor does not read, so native-tool-call turns never auto-create skills. This is not new here.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. A supplied-only build constructs less than before; a source cannot widen what the policy allows.
- Name-keyed approval: approval still exempts a tool named `shell` on non-interactive turns without an approval back-channel, because the native shell enforces its own command policy. In a supplied-only registry a source tool can hold that name and gets the same exemption; `runtime-composition.md` says so, and #11981 tracks keying the exemption on the native shell tool.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for configs and existing entry points. Two changes affect existing users or embedders:
  - **CLI model switches (config-backed).** A switch now builds through the same switch recipe as `Agent`'s. A `model_routes` entry that matches the target provider and model and has an `api_key` now supplies the credential ahead of the target entry's own key. Bare-family switches would also take different runtime options, but `model_switch` rejects bare families, so a model cannot reach that path.
  - **Embedder APIs.** No in-tree users outside this PR, and no released consumer of the supplied-only contract:
    - a custom `ToolSource` now gets a supplied-only registry by default;
    - code outside the crate that builds `AllToolsResult` with a struct literal must use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`;
    - `DelegateTool::with_parent_tools` is no longer public (it is test-only). Nothing outside the crate used it, and it was the only public way to install a delegate parent view without provenance or the caller's policy chain.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - a custom `ToolSource` that relied on native tools being added must implement `native_recipe` and return `Ok(Some(&defaults::native_compat_registry))`, or wrap `defaults::NoSuppliedTools`;
  - replace `AllToolsResult { .. }` literals with `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools(tools)`, and set the public fields after;
  - code that called `with_parent_tools` should build the delegate through the tool factory, which installs the parent view itself. A trusted caller that adds tools to an existing delegate's parent list uses `parent_tools_handle()`. Tools added that way keep unknown provenance, as the contract requires;
  - CLI users who set a route `api_key` that differs from the target provider entry's key should check which one they want; the route's key now wins on a CLI switch.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an embedder's agent missing native tools it expected (source needs `native_recipe`); bounded delegations refusing with "Tools could not be prepared safely" when a supplied-only owner inherits native memory tools; provider construction errors on effort-routed turns that name the route's provider.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #11526 by @JordanTheJet
- Scope materially carried forward: the supplied-only registry boundary (reimplemented here as `native_recipe` instead of `uses_native_registry`) and the external consumer with its dependency ratchet (ported to the new selector). #11526's daemon lifecycle tests and the heartbeat MCP gate move to #11187.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: same author.

The design of this boundary owes a lot to review. Thanks to @tidux, @IftekharUddin and @Audacity88 for the findings on #11174, #11187 and #11526: the `cron_run` escape, pipeline and MCP shadowing, missing supplied tools in bounded delegates, post-turn skill work and heartbeat MCP outside the supplied registry, and the case for an external consumer.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(deps): bump pulldown-cmark to 0.13.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0433
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0433 was added to the RustSec advisory database on 2026-11-02 and matches `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.5 in `Cargo.lock`.
  - The `Security` job fails on every build, so `CI Required Gate` blocks every merge.
  - This moves `pulldown-cmark` from 0.13.5 to 0.13.6, the patched release, which came out on 2026-10-30.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Only `Cargo.lock` changes, in one package entry: its version and checksum.
  - The manifests don't change, and no other package moves. The entry's dependency list is unchanged.
  - No advisory ignores are added.
- **Blast radius:** `pulldown-cmark` renders Markdown in `zerocode`'s chat view, in the email channel's HTML part and in the orchestrator, and parses the book in `xtask`. With `channel-matrix`, it also reaches the Matrix channel through `ruma-events`. This is a patch release in the same 0.13 line, with the same dependencies, features and minimum Rust version.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12196. Related #12094 and #12095 (the same parser path, RUSTSEC-2026-0414, fixed by the move to 0.13.5).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw uses a Markdown library, `pulldown-cmark`, in the terminal chat, the email channel and the docs tooling. A second security advisory was published against the version in our lockfile, so the security check fails on every pull request again and nothing can merge. Like the last one, the flaw only affects an optional Markdown feature (wiki-style links), which ZeroClaw never turns on. This moves the library to its fixed release and changes nothing else.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this is a one-entry lockfile bump. The `Security` job is the check, and the build and test jobs compile and run against the new version.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Security` (cargo-deny) clears the advisory.
  - The Check, Test and Lint jobs build and run the workspace against `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.6.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, toolchain 1.98.0, cargo-deny 0.19.9 as pinned by the `Security` job; advisory database at 263a4d951a, the head of its `main` branch since 2026-11-02 11:45 UTC, which includes RUSTSEC-2026-0433):

```text
$ cargo deny check                                   # master 9dbb57231f
error[vulnerability]: Quadratic parsing of nested image wikilinks with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`
    ├ ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0433
advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok

$ cargo update -p pulldown-cmark --precise 0.13.6
    Updating pulldown-cmark v0.13.5 -> v0.13.6

$ cargo deny check                                   # this branch
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok

$ cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 >/dev/null     # exit 0
$ cargo verify-project && cargo fetch --locked              # exit 0
$ python3 scripts/ci/lru_advisory_scope_test.py             # exit 0

$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-email,channel-matrix
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 52s

$ cargo check --locked -p zerocode -p xtask
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 07s

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-email,channel-matrix --lib -- email_channel:: orchestrator::tests::sanitize_channel_response
test result: ok. 117 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2183 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- chat::tests::md_ markdown
test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1556 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p xtask -- mdbook::placeholders:: mdbook::protected::
test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 207 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new checksum matches the crates.io index entry for `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.6 (`3db2be46…bb7b`) and the downloaded crate. The release's dependencies, features and minimum Rust version (1.71.1) are the same as 0.13.5's.
  - No ZeroClaw code sets `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` or uses `Options::all()`:
    - `zerocode` enables tables, strikethrough and task lists;
    - the email channel enables tables and strikethrough;
    - the orchestrator uses no options;
    - `xtask` uses the defaults.
  - `ruma-events` 0.35.0 enables tables and strikethrough only.
  - So the vulnerable path isn't reachable on `master` either. The bump clears the advisory.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head; the commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **What the tests cover:**
  - the email channel's message builder with the HTML part on, which renders the body through `pulldown-cmark` (`build_email_message_*`), plus the rest of the email channel's unit tests;
  - the orchestrator's Markdown link-destination scan, which the outbound credential redaction in `sanitize_channel_response` relies on (`sanitize_channel_response_*`, 7 of them on Markdown links);
  - `zerocode`'s chat renderer (`md_*`, 31 tests: code blocks, tables, headings, quotes, links, lists, strikethrough, task lists);
  - `xtask`'s book placeholder and protected-literal parsing (`mdbook::placeholders`, `mdbook::protected`).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run a full local `cargo test`. This is a patch release with an unchanged dependency list; I ran the tests that exercise the Markdown paths, and the CI build and test jobs cover the rest.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. This removes an advisory match.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <merge sha>`. This brings the advisory match back, so `Security` fails again.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded RPC denial reason exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the stable RPC denial reasons and reason-keyed denial records in #11289 (which closes #11005). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #11289 (`src/rpc/auth.rs:97`, 2026-10-12), which found that no recorded exception covers RPC denial reporting.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11289 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `5740f15a35` (three files: `src/rpc/auth.rs`, `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`): the `RpcDenialReason` identifier type with `as_str`, its private `code` and `message_key` mappings and `From<DenyReason>`; on the existing `AuthDenied`, the private `reason` field and `reason()` accessor, the private `new`, `with_message` and `with_values` builders, the `quoted` helper, the 21 named `pub(crate)` constructors that replace `auth_required` and `forbidden` (with `from_deny_reason` rebuilt on the private `with_message` and the five other `auth.rs` functions named in the row building their denials through them), and `audit_attrs`, which gives the existing `RPC authorization denied` record its `method`, `reason`, `denial_message`, `code`, `principal_id` and `auth_provider` attributes; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `audit_denial` emitting those attributes, `RpcDispatcher::refuse`, the `authorize` gate and the 21 other refusal functions named in the row building their denials through the constructors or refusing through `refuse`, the gate attributing a denial after a failed revalidation to the principal whose binding it drops, the `steering_admission` closure's record changes (its ownership and remote local-capability refusals recorded under their own reasons, the latter with that reason's `-32003` on the record while the steer is still answered `-32012`; the refusals its binding checks record themselves recorded once rather than twice, so a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved leaves no denial record), the selectors' refusals of an uninitialized connection now recorded, the retired `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL` literal, the fourteen `rpc-auth-*` keys and their translator comment (thirteen replacing an inline literal, `rpc-auth-session-local-capabilities` feeding only the record), and focused tests. `RpcDenialReason`, `as_str` and `reason()` are `pub`; no other crate consumes them. `DenyReason`, the JSON-RPC error codes and the grants stay in `zeroclaw-api`, and the record sink in `zeroclaw-log`, so they need no runtime permission; the root `AGENTS.md` bullet and the `docs/book` section that #11289 adds are outside the holding crate. It excludes any identifier in a client response, recording a refused `initialize` handshake or the other refusals answered without an `AuthDenied`, and any new RPC method, grant source, config key, record kind, record sink, retained runtime state or non-English locale.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11005 and #11289 (head `5740f15a35`). #11289 lands after #11326, whose global-stream wording the row's key note reflects. Precedent: #11701, #12058, #11963, and the #11286 row already in the table, which covers `src/rpc/auth.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl` but is limited to roster-bound pairing tokens.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #11289 gives every RPC authorization refusal built through `AuthDenied` a stable identifier such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, writes that identifier into the denial record the daemon already emits (the refusal text moves to its own `denial_message` attribute), moves the refusals' inline English literals into the Fluent catalogue (the gate's grant refusal and the global-stream, SOP, session-environment and upload-ownership refusals as well as the selectors'), and keeps the principal and provider on the record when a policy change drops a connection's binding. Clients receive the same codes and English text as before (the global-stream refusal takes the wording #11326 gives it), and never the identifier. The set of recorded refusals changes slightly: the selectors' refusals of a connection that never initialized are now recorded, a steer refused by its agent, workspace or environment check is recorded once rather than twice, and a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved is no longer recorded. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the RPC authorization-gate and inbound-authentication owners in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

Why placement is right: every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. ## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the roster password verification in #11264 (the provider-only first slice of #8076). - **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11264 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime`: `PasswordAuthProvider` in `src/security/auth_provider/password.rs`, compiled from the roster entries that carry a `password_hash`, with one scrypt verification per attempt on the blocking pool, the same `BadCredential` denial for every miss (against a decoy when the name has no hash to check), and a match resolving to the entry's durable roster principal; the `Credential::Password` kind, redacted in `Debug`, and the `(Password, Roster)` provenance arm in `src/security/auth_provider/mod.rs`; registration in `AcceptedAuthState::from_config` in `src/rpc/auth.rs` only while `security.password_auth.enabled` is on and pairing is required, and `security.password_auth` joining the `auth_inputs` the accepted authorization state is compiled from; and, for whichever of #11264 and #11313 lands second, the `security.password_auth` arm of `is_auth_input_path` that #11265 carries in commit 9707c30981. The scrypt hash policy, the `password_hash` roster field and the `[security.password_auth]` switch live in `zeroclaw-config`, and `AuthMethod::Password` in `zeroclaw-api`, so they need no runtime permission. It excludes any transport that presents a password, login sessions, rate limits or lockout, principal sources beyond the `[users]` roster, new grant sources or operator-authority paths, and #11265's own runtime changes (its Fluent keys), which need their own decision.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge.

prs.title: feat(channels): opt-in voice transcription without mention in mention-only groups
prs.body:
## Problem

In a group with `mention_only = true`, a voice note without an explicit `@bot` mention is dropped by `check_media_mention_gate`. That is the right default — but voice notes essentially never carry a mention, and in groups where clients cannot address the bot directly (e.g. `join_to_send_messages` groups where typing `@bot` is blocked), it means voice can never be transcribed at all: the bot stays silent no matter what the sender does.

## Change

New opt-in channel flag `voice_without_mention` (default `false`, Telegram channel config). When `true`, `try_parse_voice_message` skips the mention gate for voice notes; the sender allowlist is still enforced before any download. Disabled-by-default keeps the existing spam-protection posture for everyone else.

Plumbed through `TelegramConfig` → both orchestrator listener factories → `TelegramChannel` (builder `with_voice_without_mention`).

## Tests

- `try_parse_voice_message_bypasses_mention_gate_when_configured` — full wiremock path (getFile → download → transcribe) yields `[Voice] …` in a `mention_only` group without a mention.
- `try_parse_voice_message_bypass_keeps_allowlist_mandatory` — non-allowlisted sender is still dropped with the flag on.
- `try_parse_voice_message_gate_drops_unmentioned_voice_by_default` — default behavior unchanged.

`cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib voice` — 66 passed, 0 failed; `cargo check -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels` clean.
